The only reference offered is Ag8GeTe6 P1 mp-685969, a computed triclinic cell with no ICSD backing, so no mp_id is taken.

dopant_roles.basis: (GeTe)5.5AgIn0.5Sb0.5Te2 is a TAGS-type composition: Ag and Sb together substitute for Ge in equal amounts, keeping the electron count while heavily disordering the cation site. Sb is a framework constituent of that alloy rather than a dilute dopant.
The same TAGS-related indium composition; the third paper is titled for TAGS-related indium compounds. In on the Ge site is a resonant-level dopant in this family.
Bi appears in one composition not printed here; on the Ge site of GeTe it is a donor and the usual partner of Sb in this literature.

basis: Ba8Al16Ge30 is 7 of the 13 samples, with Ba8Al14Ge32 and Ba8Al18Ge28 either side of it: that is the type I clathrate, cubic Pm-3n, with Ba filling both cage types of a Ge framework in which Al substitutes to satisfy the Zintl count. But Ba24Al12Ge88 and Ba24Al9Ge91 are 4 more samples and are the type III clathrate, and two of the three papers say so in their titles.
note: The seed hypothesis is refined rather than confirmed: clathrate_i is right for the 8-16-30 compositions but the 24-x-y compositions are a different framework topology, and the split is clean on the Ba:Ge ratio, so stage 2 can make it from composition alone. The first paper, on host structure engineering in thermoelectric clathrates, is about moving between these framework types deliberately. No reference entry offered is a clathrate at all -- MP ranks BaAlGe, Ba(AlGe)2, Ba10Al3Ge7 and Ba3(AlGe)2, all small-cell Zintl compounds of the same chemistry -- so mp_id is left null rather than taken from a compound that is not in the host.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [187, 71, 139, 193]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CeCu4Al is 7 samples and its La-diluted form Ce0.8La0.2Cu4Al is 5 more, so 12 of 13 sit at the 1-4-1 stoichiometry. CeCu4Al is a CaCu5-derived hexagonal intermetallic, P6/mmm, with Al taking one of the two framework sites of the CaCu5 cell; the third paper calls it a Kondo lattice, which is the physics that hexagonal structure supports.
note: Confidence is medium because RT4X compounds split between the hexagonal CaCu5 type and the cubic MgCu4Sn (AuBe5) type depending on the rare earth and the main-group partner, and no reference offered here settles CeCu4Al: the MP list ranks Ce(Al2Cu)4, CeAl3Cu, CeAlCu and CeAl2Cu3, none of which is the 1-4-1. Stage 2 must take the space group from the paper. The thirteenth sample, CeCu4Al8, is the ThMn12 type and is a genuinely different compound, which is why the host is mixed.
reference_disagreement: MP ranks Ce(Al2Cu)4 I4/mmm mp-20003 PRIMARY for this host at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references. Reduced, that formula is CeCu4Al8 -- the single-sample minority compound. So the best-attested reference entry for the host describes 1 of 13 samples, and the majority compound CeCu4Al has no reference entry at all.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.8La0.2Cu4Al: La replaces Ce on the rare-earth site as a non-magnetic diluent, and both the first two papers scan exactly that ratio in Ce1-xLaxCu4Al. It is a Kondo-lattice dilution variable rather than a carrier dopant.

basis: All six printed compositions sit within about a percent of Al25.7Fe37.1Si37.1, which normalises to Al2Fe3Si3 -- the tau2 phase, a small low-symmetry intermetallic that is a narrow-gap semiconductor. The third paper is titled for nanostructured Al2Fe3Si3 and the first for conduction-type control in it, which is what the small Al:Si scan across these samples is doing.
note: I disagree with the seed hypothesis for the bulk of this host. quasicrystal_approximant would be right for an Al-Fe-Si Mackay-type 1/1 approximant, which is the subject of the second paper, but such approximants sit near Al70Fe15Si15 and every composition printed here is at Al26 -- far too Al-poor. So the seed covers at most the samples of that one paper and the rest is the tau2 phase. It is recorded as refined rather than rejected because the approximant really is present in the host. Confidence is medium on the space group, not on the compound: MP gives Al2(FeSi)3 P-1 mp-29110 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references while the thermoelectric literature describes the phase as monoclinic, and stage 2 has to settle that from the paper. The curator details for this host record milling atmosphere only and say nothing about structure.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn appears in one composition not printed here. On the Fe site of an Al-Fe-Si intermetallic it removes an electron per substitution, which is the conduction-type control the first paper is titled for.

basis: Both compositions are Si with 7 and 16 at.% Al, all 13 samples are films, and the single paper is titled for silicon films prepared by aluminium-induced crystallisation. The product of that process is crystalline diamond-cubic Si; Al is the crystallisation agent, not a component of a compound.
note: Al and Si form a simple eutectic with essentially no compound and almost no mutual solid solubility -- about 1.5 at.% Al in Si at best, and less at these film temperatures. So 7 and 16 at.% Al cannot all be in the lattice: these films are diamond-cubic Si saturated with Al plus residual fcc Al, and the Al that is in the lattice is the p-type acceptor that makes the films conduct. Confidence is medium for that reason: the structure of the conducting phase is certain, but the sample is two-phase and a single prototype understates it. The references agree with this reading rather than contradicting it -- MP offers only Al4Si19, Al4Si and AlSi at hull 0.085 to 0.272, computed cells with at most one ICSD reference, which is what a system with no stable compound looks like in a database. Al sits above the 5 at.% split so it is a host element here and does not appear in dopant_roles.

basis: Every composition is Ba1-xKxFe2As2 with x from 0.3 to 0.7, and the first paper is titled for thermoelectric properties of electron- and hole-doped BaFe2As2. BaFe2As2 is the canonical ThCr2Si2 122 iron pnictide, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, with FeAs layers separated by the Ba-K layer.
note: K is above the 5 at.% split so it is a host element, not a dopant candidate, and dopant_roles is empty -- but it is the doping variable of this system: K on the Ba site is the hole doping that drives the superconductivity, and stage 3 should read x from the parsed fractions rather than treat K as an impurity. Undoped BaFe2As2 undergoes a tetragonal-to-orthorhombic structural transition near 140 K, which would sit inside the 11-300 K window, but K doping suppresses it and at x above about 0.3 -- which is every composition here -- it is gone, so no phase crossing is recorded. Every MP entry ranked for this host is a computed K-Ba-Fe-As supercell ordering with no ICSD reference, so mp_id is left null.

basis: All 13 compositions are LaFe(As,P)O with Sr or F substitution -- LaFeAs0.5P0.5O0.86F0.14 and siblings -- which is the 1111 iron pnictide: ZrCuSiAs type, P4/nmm, alternating LaO and FeAs layers. The single paper, on three superconducting phases with different pairing categories, scans the As-to-P ratio across exactly that structure.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen site of the FeAs layer
solid_solution_axis.note: As and P are both group 15 and genuinely share the pnictogen site, so this is a real isoelectronic series with LaFeAsO and LaFePO as its ends. The substitution acts as chemical pressure on the FeX layer and is what moves the system between pairing states in the paper -- it is a tuning axis, not doping, and no single parent compound can be named for the host.

note: No reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.9Sr0.1FeAs0.4P0.6O: divalent Sr on the trivalent La site of the LaO layer is hole doping.
LaFeAs0.7P0.3O0.86F0.14: F on the O site of the LaO layer is the standard electron doping of the 1111 family, and it is the doping variable rather than an impurity.

basis: SmFeAsO and its F-, Co- and oxygen-deficient variants make up the whole host, and the first paper is titled for the thermoelectric power of RFeAsO with R including Sm. That is the ZrCuSiAs 1111 structure, P4/nmm, and MP ranks SmFeAsO P4/nmm mp-1078897 first for the host with 5 ICSD references.
note: The MP entry sits at hull 0.205, which would normally be a warning, but it carries 5 ICSD references and the other two entries for this chemistry are computed cells at hull 0.8 and 1.5 -- the hull value here reflects how poorly these layered pnictides are described in the 2019 dump, not instability. The undoped parent has a tetragonal-to-orthorhombic transition near 140 K inside the 10-300 K window; the doped compositions that dominate the host have it suppressed, and the 2 undoped SmFeAsO samples would cross it. It is not recorded as a phase change because the distortion does not change the prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: SmFeAsO0.88F0.12: F on the O site of the SmO layer is the doping variable of the 1111 family, not an impurity.
SmFe0.95Co0.05AsO through SmFe0.85Co0.15AsO, and the third paper is titled for it: Co doped directly into the FeAs conducting layer adds electrons at the cost of scattering.
La appears in one composition not printed here; the first paper compares the whole RFeAsO series, so La on the Sm site is a rare-earth size variable.

basis: The majority compositions are Fe74Co10B16, Fe74Co7.5Cr2.5B16 and (Fe1-xCox)84B16 -- the classic 84:16 metal-to-metalloid ratio of the Fe-B melt-spun glasses, and 2 of the samples are ribbons. The first two papers are on resistivity and thermopower of Fe74Co10-xCrxB16 and on small Co and Ni additions, which is the amorphous-ribbon literature.
note: Fe0.5Co0.5B and Fe0.1Co0.9B are equiatomic monoborides, crystalline FeB/CoB in the orthorhombic CrB type, and the third paper is titled for Seebeck coefficients of iron-group borides -- so those samples are a different material from the glasses and the host is mixed. The split is clean on the B fraction: 16 at.% B is a glass, 50 at.% B is the monoboride. Confidence is medium because an amorphous assignment cannot be confirmed from composition alone and some of these ribbons may have been measured after crystallisation. Every MP entry offered is a computed Fe-Co-B ternary with at most 1 ICSD reference and none is at either composition, so mp_id is null.

dopant_roles.basis: O in 5 compositions of melt-spun and pressed metal is surface oxide and handling residue, not a lattice constituent.

Al in 5 compositions at under 5 at.%. In this family small Al additions are deliberate glass-forming and thermal-stability agents rather than dilute doping, but the compositions carrying it are not printed here.
Fe74Co7.5Cr2.5B16: the first paper scans Cr against Co in Fe74Co10-xCrxB16, so Cr takes transition-metal sites in the amorphous network.
Si is the other standard metalloid of this glass family and partly replaces B in the metalloid fraction; it appears in one composition not printed here.

basis: UB4 is 8 of the 13 samples, UB2 is 4 and UB12 is 1 -- the host is a scan of the whole U-B line and MP gives all three at hull 0.000 with 8, 9 and 8 ICSD references respectively. The ub12_boride entry already names AB4 in its formula archetype and UB4 as its exemplar, so UB4 is taken as covered by it, and the first and third papers are both about UB4.
note: This is a taxonomy weakness worth recording rather than a disagreement with the references. The ub12_boride entry carries AB12 and AB4 in one archetype but gives its typical_space_group as Fm-3m (225) for AB12 only, while 8 of these 13 samples are UB4 in the ThB4 type, tetragonal P4/mbm (127), mp-619. Those are two different frameworks -- B12 cuboctahedra in a rocksalt arrangement against B6 octahedra linked by B2 pairs -- and a v4 seed should either split them or record both space groups, otherwise every UB4 host will read as a space-group disagreement. UB2 is a third structure again, the AlB2 type with flat boron honeycombs, mp-1514, so alb2 is listed as an alternative and the host splits cleanly on the B:U ratio. The curator details are boron isotope enrichments, which is the subject of the first paper and does not bear on the structure.

basis: The host is La0.5Ba0.5FeO3 and its multiply substituted relatives, all at the ABO3 ratio with Fe alone on the B site, and the third paper is titled for the structure and properties of perovskites for SOFC cathodes. A 50:50 La-Ba A site with Fe on B is a perovskite ferrite; the oxygen deficiency these cathodes run with is written as the 3-delta in the papers.
note: Confidence is medium because of what happens at a 50:50 A site with a large size mismatch: LaBaFe2O5+d can order La and Ba into alternate layers, which would be the A-site-ordered double perovskite rather than the disordered cubic one, and heavy oxygen loss can order the vacancies into a brownmillerite. Which of the three occurs depends on the synthesis route -- and the second paper is titled for the effect of the synthetic method on structure and conductivity, so the host may genuinely contain more than one. That is a question for the paper, not for composition, so the disordered perovskite is taken as the candidate and the alternatives are named. All four MP entries ranked for this host are computed La-Ba-Fe-O orderings with no ICSD reference, so mp_id is left null. The curator details are notes about converting logarithmic axis values during digitisation and say nothing about structure.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.26Sm0.24Sr0.14Ba0.36FeO3: Sr is a third A-site cation in the SOFC cathode compositions, sitting alongside La and Ba, so it tunes the average A-site size and the hole count rather than acting as a dilute dopant.
The same A-site mixing, with Sm as a smaller rare earth; the third paper scans A-site composition explicitly.
La0.34Nd0.16Sr0.12Ba0.38FeO3: another rare earth on the A site of the same series.
Co on the perovskite B site alongside Fe is the standard ferrite-cobaltite cathode substitution, raising the electronic conductivity.
La0.4Ba0.6Fe0.8Zn0.2O3: Zn on the B site, the subject of the first paper.
Ni on the B site alongside Fe, the same cathode chemistry as the Co substitution.

basis: All three compositions are BiCuSe1-xTexO with x from 0.2 to 0.4, and both papers are titled for the BiCuSeO system and for Te doping of it. BiCuSeO is the oxyselenide member of the ZrCuSiAs 1111 family, P4/nmm, with insulating Bi2O2 layers alternating with conducting Cu2Se2 layers.
note: Te sits exactly on the 5 at.% split at x = 0.2 and above it beyond that, so it is treated as a host element and dopant_roles is empty -- but it is an isoelectronic substitution for Se within the Cu2Se2 layer, which narrows the band gap, and stage 3 should read x from the parsed fractions. This host is the counter-example the README warns about in reverse: O and Se are both group 16 here, but O belongs to the Bi2O2 layer and never exchanges with Se, so the only real anion axis is Se against Te. No reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null.

basis: Every composition is a member of the nPbTe.mBi2Te3 homologous series with the anion site mixed -- PbBi4Te7, PbBi2Te4, PbBi6Te10, Pb2Bi6Te11, each written with a (Te,Se) bracket -- and the papers are titled for PbBi4Te7-based anion-substituted layered solid solutions. These are ordered intergrowths of rocksalt PbTe slabs and tetradymite Bi2Te3 quintuple layers, which is exactly what the homologous_tetradymite entry names.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen site, in both the rocksalt and the quintuple-layer blocks
solid_solution_axis.note: Se and Te share the anion sublattice throughout the series, so the Se fraction is a genuine isoelectronic axis and no single parent compound can be named for the host. The other axis in this host is the homologous index n:m itself, which changes the stacking sequence rather than the prototype, and the two are independent -- stage 2 must resolve both per composition.

note: No reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null. Each member of the series is its own structure with its own stacking period, so a single mp_id would not have been right even if one were offered.

basis: The host is one composition, Ca2.8La0.2Rh4Sn13, all 13 samples: the 3-4-13 Remeika stannide, cubic Pm-3n, a cage structure of Sn12 icosahedra around the alkaline earth. Materials Project confirms it directly, Ca3Sn13Rh4 Pm-3n mp-4363 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, and the paper is titled for the effective increase in atomic-scale disorder by doping and superconductivity, which is what these rattler cages are studied for.
note: The prototype was proposed in chunk 009 for the La-Rh-Sn host and is reused here unchanged; this is the second host to want it, which is the argument for folding it into v4. Several members of this family undergo a superlattice distortion below room temperature and the measured range printed for this host is 10-10 K from 2 curves, so these samples are entirely in the low-temperature regime -- stage 2 should check whether the distorted cell rather than the ambient cubic one is what was measured. La substitutes for Ca, which is the disorder the paper introduces deliberately.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca2.8La0.2Rh4Sn13: La takes the Ca site of the cage framework. The paper is about the atomic-scale disorder this creates and its effect on superconductivity, so it is a deliberate disorder variable rather than carrier doping -- though trivalent La on a divalent site does also add electrons.

basis: The host is CdTe and its Cl-, Sn-, Ge- and In-doped variants. CdTe is zincblende, F-43m, and TEDesignLab gives it directly at mp-406, hull 0.000, with 41 ICSD references -- the strongest reference evidence in this chunk.

other_polymorphs.note: TEDesignLab lists wurtzite CdTe at hull 0.004 with 3 ICSD references against 41 for zincblende. It is obtained in nanocrystals and constrained growth, not by heating bulk CdTe.

MP gives rocksalt CdTe at hull 0.179 with 6 ICSD references; it is the high-pressure phase of CdTe, reached above about 3.5 GPa, not on heating. The Cmcm and P3_121 entries in the same list are further pressure phases.

note: The measured range runs to 1679 K, and CdTe melts at about 1365 K. The third paper is titled for transport properties and viscosity of LIQUID CdTe doped with In, Ge and Sn, so the top third of that window is melt, not a crystal at all. The prototype describes the solid samples only, and the liquid-state curves in this host should not be attributed to any structure in stage 2.

dopant_roles.basis: CdTe0.995Cl0.005 through CdTe0.95Cl0.05, and the second paper is titled for CdTe1-xClx: a halide on the Te anion site is the standard n-type donor for CdTe.
Sn0.02CdTe: Sn on the Cd cation site, one of the three dopants of the liquid-CdTe paper.
Ge on the cation site, named in the third paper title alongside In and Sn.
In on the Cd site is the classic shallow donor in CdTe and is named in the third paper title.

basis: Six of the nine compositions are La1-xCexMnO3 with x from 0.3 to 0.64, and the first paper is titled for transport and magnetic properties of Ce-doped LaMnO3. LaMnO3 is the parent perovskite manganite, and Ce on the A site is the electron-doped counterpart of the usual Sr and Ca hole doping.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the perovskite A site
solid_solution_axis.note: Ce and La share the A site but are NOT isoelectronic in this system: Ce enters largely as Ce4+ against La3+, which is the whole point of the electron doping, so this axis changes the carrier count as well as the average cation size. The automatic detector flagged it as a same-group pair, and the CHECK is warranted -- treat x as a doping variable, not as a neutral alloying axis.

note: Two compositions, (La0.7Sr0.3MnO3)0.5(CeO2)0.5 and the 0.45/0.55 version, are written as explicit two-phase composites of the manganite perovskite with fluorite CeO2, and the second paper is titled for tunable magnetoresistance over a wide temperature range, which is composite physics. Those samples are not single-phase and the host is marked mixed for them. Confidence is medium for a second reason: Ce solubility on the A site of LaMnO3 is limited, and nominal x of 0.4 to 0.6 is well beyond where single-phase material is usually obtained, so some of the nominally solid-solution samples are likely perovskite plus segregated CeO2 as well. Both MP entries offered are computed La-Ce-Mn-O orderings at hull 0.10 and 0.27 with no ICSD reference, so mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: The La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 component of the composite samples: Sr on the A site is the standard hole doping that makes the manganite metallic and ferromagnetic.

basis: CeNi2Si2 is 7 of the 13 samples, with Ce(Ni0.9Pd0.1)2Si2 and Ce(Ni0.95Cu0.05)2Si2 on the same stoichiometry, so 10 samples are the 122. CeNi2Si2 is the ThCr2Si2 type, I4/mmm, and MP confirms it at Ce(SiNi)2 mp-4537, hull 0.000, with 13 ICSD references -- the best-attested entry for this host. The third paper is on the intermediate valence of Ce in CeM2Si2.
note: This is a Ce-Ni-Si stoichiometry survey and three of the compositions are other compounds entirely: CeNi4Si is a CaCu5-derived 1-4-1 (the second paper is titled for it), Ce2Ni3Si5 is the orthorhombic U2Co3Si5 type, and CeNi9Si4 is the tetragonal I4/mcm 1-9-4. Only the first has a taxonomy entry, so cacu5 is listed as the alternative and the other two are recorded here rather than forced into one: they are 1 sample each and stage 2 should split the host on the Ni:Ce ratio. The prototype and mp_id above describe the 122 majority only.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce(Ni0.9Pd0.1)2Si2: Pd is isoelectronic with Ni and sits on the same transition-metal site, expanding the lattice and tuning the hybridisation that sets the Ce valence. It is a chemical-pressure variable rather than carrier doping.
Ce(Ni0.95Cu0.05)2Si2: Cu on the Ni site adds an electron per substitution, so unlike Pd it moves the band filling as well as the lattice.

basis: Every composition is Sr1-xCexTiO3-delta with x from 0.3 to 0.5, and the curator transcribes exactly that formula from the paper. SrTiO3 is the cubic perovskite, Ce enters on the Sr A site as a donor, and the second paper is titled for Ce-doped SrTiO3 thin films. Ti alone occupies the B site throughout.
note: Confidence is medium rather than high because of how far the substitution is pushed. Tetravalent Ce on the divalent Sr site must be charge-compensated, and the compositions show it being done by A-site vacancies -- the O content is pinned at 2.9 while the A site is nominally full -- so at x of 0.4 to 0.5 these are heavily A-site-deficient perovskites near the limit of the single-phase field, where Ruddlesden-Popper intergrowths and CeO2 segregation are both common. The framework is still the corner-sharing TiO6 perovskite, which is what is recorded. Ce is above the 5 at.% split so it is a host element and dopant_roles is empty, but it is the donor that makes these films n-type and stage 3 should read x from the parsed fractions. The only MP entry offered, Sr2Ce2Ti5O15 R-3m mp-1218863, is a computed cell at hull 0.055 with no ICSD reference and is not this compound, so mp_id is null.

basis: Every composition is Ti0.3Zr0.35Hf0.35CoSb1-xSnx: the p-type (Ti,Zr,Hf)CoSb half-Heusler with Sn on the Sb site, and the second paper is titled for carrier concentration optimisation of a p-type half-Heusler. This is one of the two best-known half-Heusler thermoelectric legs and its structure is the cubic MgAgAs ordering, F-43m.
note: Ti, Zr and Hf share the same cation site in fixed near-equal proportions across every composition -- that is a deliberate three-way mass-disorder alloy to suppress the lattice thermal conductivity, not a dopant. The automatic solid-solution detector did not flag it because it looks for pairs, not triples. Sn is above the 5 at.% split so it is a host element, but it is the acceptor: Sn on the Sb site is the carrier-concentration knob the second paper optimises, and stage 3 should read x from the parsed fractions. No reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null. The first and third papers are about segmented modules that join this leg to an oxide, not about its structure.

basis: All three compositions are (Co1-xNix)Zr2 with x from 0.15 to 0.29, and the paper is titled for the anisotropy of the normal-state properties of superconducting Co1-xNixZr2. Zr2Co and Zr2Ni both crystallise in the CuAl2 C16 type, body-centred tetragonal I4/mcm, and Ni and Co are interchangeable on the transition-metal site across the whole range, so the structure is the same at every composition.
note: Ni is above the 5 at.% split, so it is a host element and dopant_roles is empty; it substitutes for Co on the C16 transition-metal site.
reference_disagreement: assigned the C16 Zr2T phase at Zr:T of 2:1; every MP entry ranked for this host is a different stoichiometry -- Zr2CoNi Amm2, Zr4CoNi, Zr5Co4Ni, ZrCoNi -- all computed orderings with no ICSD reference, and none of them is the Zr2(Co,Ni) these samples are. The references simply miss this phase rather than contradict it, so mp_id is left null.

basis: The curator transcribes the papers directly: Tl-misfit cobaltites and TlBi-misfit cobaltites. The compositions -- Tl2Sr3Co3O9, Tl0.4SrCoO3, Tl0.6SrCoO4.1 and their non-integer oxygen contents -- are the signature of a misfit layered cobaltite: a CdI2-type CoO2 sheet intergrown with a rocksalt Tl-Sr-O block whose in-plane period does not match it, so the formula never comes out integral. The first paper is titled for large thermopower in metallic misfit cobaltites.
note: This is one of the prototypes the README flags for stage 2: a misfit cobaltite is an incommensurate composite of two subsystems and has no single Materials Project entry, so mp_id must stay null and the structure needs a superspace description rather than one space group. No reference line of any kind is offered for this host in any case.

dopant_roles.basis: The curator records TlBi-misfit cobaltites for one sample: Bi replaces Tl inside the rocksalt block, not in the CoO2 sheet, which changes the block period and therefore the misfit ratio itself.

basis: Zn0.85Co0.15O and Zn0.90Co0.10O are 5 samples of Co-substituted ZnO, which stays wurtzite, P6_3mc, at those levels, and the third paper is titled for the role of cobalt doping on the electrical conductivity of ZnO nanoparticles. That is the larger single group in the host.
note: The seed hypothesis is refined rather than confirmed. Four of the printed compositions are ZnCo2O4 and its Bi-substituted variants, which is the normal spinel, Fd-3m, with Zn on the tetrahedral site and Co3+ on the octahedral -- a completely different structure from Co-doped wurtzite ZnO, and the first paper is titled for the power factor of nanostructured ZnCo2O4. The host therefore holds two prototypes and splits cleanly on the Co:Zn ratio: at Co:Zn near 0.15 it is wurtzite, at Co:Zn of 2 it is spinel. Confidence is medium because the majority is only 5 of 13 samples. Every MP entry offered is a computed Zn-Co-O ordering with no ICSD reference and none is at either composition, so mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi0.025ZnCo1.975O4 through Bi0.1ZnCo1.9O4: the Bi content is written as replacing Co in the spinel formula, and the first paper is about enhancing the power factor of ZnCo2O4 by exactly this. Bi3+ is large for an octahedral spinel site, so some of it may instead sit at grain boundaries as a sintering aid; that is for the paper to settle.

basis: Every composition is (La,Nd,Sr)2CuO4 with the rare-earth site mixed and Sr, Ca or Ba added -- La1.4Nd0.4Sr0.2CuO4 and relatives. That is the T-phase 214 cuprate, the K2NiF4 structure, which is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper member: single CuO2 sheets separated by rock-salt (La,Nd,Sr)O double layers. The second and third papers are on thermopower across the stripe critical point and on stripe order in rare-earth-doped LSCO, which is that material.
note: Nd is in this host for a structural reason that the measurement is about: substituting Nd for La drives the low-temperature orthorhombic to low-temperature tetragonal tilt transition, which is what pins the stripe order that both transport papers measure, and it happens inside the 10-298 K window. It is an octahedral tilt transition -- the CuO2 sheets and the rock-salt blocks are unchanged -- so it does not change the prototype and spans_transition is left false, but stage 2 should expect the space group to be Bmab or P4_2/ncm rather than the ideal I4/mmm recorded here. Both MP entries offered are computed La-Nd-Cu-O orderings with no ICSD reference, so mp_id is null. Nd is above the 5 at.% split and so does not appear in dopant_roles.

dopant_roles.basis: Present in all 13 samples. Divalent Sr on the trivalent rare-earth site is the hole doping of the 214 cuprates and is the variable the phase diagram is drawn against, not an impurity.

(La0.640Nd0.285Ca0.035Sr0.024Ba0.016)2CuO4: Ca is a second divalent A-site cation, used with Sr and Ba to hold the hole count fixed while changing the average cation size -- which is what the first paper, on tolerance factor effects, is about.
The same tolerance-factor series; Ba is the large end of the divalent set.

basis: Every composition is Ce1-xLaxCu2.05Si2 with x from 0.8 to 0.99, i.e. LaCu2Si2 lightly diluted with Ce, and the first paper is titled for the Kondo-lattice compound CeCu2Si2. LaCu2Si2 is the ThCr2Si2 type, I4/mmm, and MP confirms it at La(CuSi)2 mp-3995, hull 0.000, with 6 ICSD references.
note: The Cu excess written into almost every composition, Cu2.05 rather than Cu2, is deliberate: CeCu2Si2 is famously sensitive to a few percent off-stoichiometry on the Cu site, which decides whether the ground state is superconducting or magnetic. It is a host-element non-stoichiometry rather than a minor element, so it does not appear in dopant_roles, but stage 3 should not read it as a rounding artefact.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.01La0.99Cu2.05Si2 through Ce0.2La0.8Cu2.05Si2: Ce on the La site is the magnetic ion being diluted into a non-magnetic host, and the third paper is titled for the crossover from impurity Kondo to Kondo lattice behaviour that this concentration series traces. It is the experiment, not a contaminant.

basis: Every composition is Cu2-xSe1-ySy -- Cu1.97Se0.5S0.5, Cu1.8Se0.7S0.3, Cu1.98S0.16Se0.84 -- and the papers are titled for Cu2-xSe-Cu2S composites and for Cu1.8Se1-xSx alloys. This is the copper chalcogenide superionic conductor: a rigid chalcogen sublattice with liquid-like mobile Cu, and S and Se are interchangeable on the anion site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen sublattice
solid_solution_axis.note: S and Se are both group 16 and share the anion sublattice, so this is a genuine isoelectronic series between Cu2S and Cu2Se with no single parent for the host. It matters for the phase record as well as for stage 3: the order-disorder temperature moves with the S fraction, from about 400 K in Cu2Se to about 376 K in Cu2S, so the transition recorded above cannot be one number for the whole host.

note: No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line was printed for this host, but the measured window is 299-974 K and the order-disorder transition to the cubic superionic phase sits near 400 K for every composition in it, so both phases are recorded. The low-temperature phase is a complex ordered superstructure whose symmetry depends on the Cu deficiency and the S content, so its space group is left null rather than guessed. The Cu deficiency itself -- 1.8 to 1.98 rather than 2 -- is the carrier-concentration knob and is a host-element non-stoichiometry, so it does not appear in dopant_roles. The first paper describes its samples as a Cu2-xSe-Cu2S composite rather than a solid solution, so some of these samples may be two-phase; that is for the paper to settle. Both MP entries offered are computed Cu-Se-S cells with no ICSD reference, so mp_id is null.

basis: Every composition is (Nb1-yTay)1-xTixFeSb, and the first paper is titled for the unique role of refractory Ta alloying in enhancing the figure of merit while the second is a half-Heusler module paper. NbFeSb is one of the two workhorse p-type half-Heuslers, the cubic MgAgAs ordering, F-43m, and Ta and Ti both sit on its Nb site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the Nb site of the MgAgAs cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Nb and Ta are group 5 congeners with nearly identical radii and very different masses, so this axis is pure mass-fluctuation scattering: it suppresses the lattice thermal conductivity without touching the band structure or the carrier count. That is precisely what the first paper means by the unique role of Ta alloying.

note: Ti is at 20% of the Nb site in every composition, well above the 5 at.% split, so it is a host element and dopant_roles is empty -- but it is the acceptor: Ti on the group-5 site removes an electron per substitution and sets the hole concentration. Stage 3 should read it from the parsed fractions. No reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null.

basis: Ga2Te3 and its Cu- and Sb-substituted variants are 10 of the 13 samples, and the third paper is titled for the engineered cation vacancy plane responsible for the reduction in lattice thermal conductivity. Ga2Te3 is a defect zincblende: a sphalerite anion framework in which one third of the cation sites is vacant and the vacancies order onto planes, which is the structural feature those papers are built on.
note: The host holds three different materials. Ga2Te3 is the majority and takes the prototype. Ga20Te80 is a splat-cooled amorphous alloy -- the first paper is titled for splat-cooled amorphous In20Te80 and Ga20Te80 -- so amorphous is listed. GaTe, 1 sample and the subject of the second paper on layered chalcogenide GaTe crystals, is a monoclinic layered semiconductor with Ga-Ga pairs and has no taxonomy entry; unresolved_crystalline stands for it rather than filing a layered monoclinic compound under a defect zincblende. The host splits cleanly on the Te:Ga ratio. Confidence is medium on the space group rather than on the compound: see the reference disagreement.
reference_disagreement: The two references point different ways for Ga2Te3 and neither is taken at face value. TEDesignLab has no Ga2Te3 entry, offering Ga2Te5 I4/m mp-2371 and GaTe P6_3/mmc mp-10009 instead. MP ranks Ga2Te3 R-3m mp-1070116 PRIMARY at hull 0.332 on a single ICSD reference, while the hull-zero cell for the same formula is Ga2Te3 Cc mp-38970 -- so the ICSD-count ranking promotes a cell a third of an eV above the hull. The vacancy-ordered monoclinic Cc setting is the one that matches the cation vacancy planes the papers measure, so mp_id is left null for stage 2 rather than taking the PRIMARY.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga1.9Cu0.05Sb0.1Te2.95 and Ga2Cu0.05Sb0.05Te2.9: Cu goes onto the cation sublattice, where the structural vacancies already are, so it partly fills them as well as doping. That interplay with the vacancy ordering is the point of the third paper.
The same compositions: Sb on the trivalent Ga cation site, paired with Cu in every sample that carries either.

basis: Every composition is NiTi1-xMnxSb with x from 0.2 to 0.6, and the paper is titled for the galvanomagnetic properties of DISORDERED Mn semi-Heusler phases. TiNiSb is a half-Heusler -- the cubic MgAgAs ordering, F-43m, with one of the two cation sublattices vacant -- and Mn substitutes for Ti on the same site. Disordered means the Ti and Mn are random on that site, which is a half-Heusler solid solution.
note: The seed hypothesis, quaternary_heusler, is refined. A quaternary Heusler is the LiMgPdSn type, in which four species each take their own ordered sublattice -- so NiTi0.5Mn0.5Sb would be its exact composition, and that is presumably why the taxonomy names this host. But the paper says the phases are disordered, which is the opposite claim: Ti and Mn share one site at random rather than ordering onto two. So the structure is the half-Heusler with a mixed cation site, and the ordered quaternary is listed as the alternative in case the paper reports a superstructure at x = 0.5. Confidence is medium for that reason. No reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null. Mn is above the 5 at.% split, so dopant_roles is empty; it is both the magnetic ion and the electron-count variable here.

basis: Twelve of the 13 samples are (PbS)0.5(ZnS)0.5 and the thirteenth is Pb0.3Zn0.7S. PbS is rocksalt, Fm-3m, and is taken as the prototype because it is the thermoelectrically active component and the semiconducting matrix these papers measure. But see the note: this is not a single phase and the assignment is low confidence for a structural reason, not a bibliographic one.
note: PbS and ZnS have a very wide miscibility gap: Pb2+ is far too large for the tetrahedral cation site of ZnS and Zn2+ far too small for the octahedral site of PbS, and mutual solubility at these temperatures is a few percent at most. So a nominal 50:50 mixture is a two-phase composite of rocksalt PbS and zincblende (or wurtzite) ZnS, whatever the papers call it -- the first is titled for the PbS-ZnS alloy semiconductor and the second for PbxZn1-xS mixed crystals, both of which assert a solid solution the phase diagram does not support. That disagreement is the reason for low confidence, and it is with the papers rather than with a reference: no reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null. Stage 2 should treat these samples as a composite unless a paper shows a single-phase pattern.

basis: Tl9SbTe6 and its Sn-doped variants are 5 of the printed compositions and the majority of the host; the second and third papers are titled for Sn- and Pb-doped Tl9SbTe6 and for thallium compounds with extremely low thermal conductivity. Tl9SbTe6 is the Tl5Te3 structure type, tetragonal I4/mcm, with Sb ordering onto one of the Tl sites -- which is exactly what the tl5te3 entry names.
note: TlSbTe2, 4 samples and the subject of the first paper, is a different structure: a rhombohedrally ordered rocksalt in which Tl and Sb alternate along the cubic body diagonal, R-3m, which is the alpha-NaFeO2 type. The taxonomy entry for that type is written around oxides and names LiCoO2 as its exemplar, but the structure type is the same one and it is the closest correct entry; a v4 seed should broaden its description to cover the ordered rocksalt tellurides. MP gives it at mp-4573 with 3 ICSD references. The host therefore holds two prototypes and splits on the Tl:Sb ratio. The composition printed as TlSbTe6 is almost certainly Tl9SbTe6 with the 9 lost in transcription -- no such phase exists in this system -- and stage 2 should check it against the paper rather than treat it as a distinct compound. Both mp_ids on offer sit at hull 0.15 to 0.60 because thallium tellurides are poorly described in the 2019 dump, which is the same artefact the chunk header warns about for layered chalcogenides, so the hull values are not used to rank them.

dopant_roles.basis: Tl9Sb0.95Sn0.05Te6 through Tl9Sb0.9Sn0.1Te6: the formula puts Sn directly on the Sb site, and tetravalent-for-pentavalent substitution there is the hole doping the second paper uses to optimise the carrier concentration.
The second paper is titled for Sn- AND Pb-doped Tl9SbTe6; Pb is the larger dopant and is expected on a Tl site rather than the Sb one, but the compositions carrying it are not printed here.

basis: The host is elemental tin: 8 samples of plain Sn and 5 doped with Sb at parts-per-million levels, and the third paper is titled for size and temperature effects on the thermoelectric power of beta-tin thin films. beta-Sn, white tin, is the body-centred tetragonal A5 structure, I4_1/amd, and MP ranks it first for the host at mp-84 with 39 ICSD references.

other_polymorphs.note: alpha-Sn, grey tin, is the EQUILIBRIUM phase below 286 K, so the 10-434 K measured window formally crosses a transition. It is deliberately not recorded in phases: the transformation needs weeks below 250 K plus a nucleation site, and every sample in this host -- bulk rods and evaporated films measured on a laboratory timescale -- stays metallic white tin throughout. The enum has no value for a thermodynamically stable but kinetically unreachable phase, so occurrence reads unknown and the reason is given here.

note: The hull ordering in the reference is the reverse of what is observed: diamond-cubic mp-117 is at hull 0.000 and the beta-Sn entry that carries 39 of the ICSD references is at 0.040. That is the database being right about thermodynamics and wrong about what a sample is, and it is why the ICSD-count ranking the chunk file uses gives the better answer here. The first paper is on two-phase Sn/SnTe alloys, so some samples in this host may contain a SnTe second phase even though Te is below the split and not listed.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb0.0000003Sn through Sb0.000007Sn: Sb substitutes for Sn at parts-per-million levels. The second paper is on electron-irradiation damage in lightly doped tin, so the dopant here is a controlled impurity for a defect study, not a thermoelectric optimisation.

basis: YbAgCu4 is 8 of the 12 samples and the rest are YbCu5-xAgx with x from 0.5 to 1, the same compound off stoichiometry. YbAgCu4 is the cubic MgCu4Sn ordering of the AuBe5 type, F-43m, and MP confirms it at YbCu4Ag mp-1077741, hull 0.000, with 2 ICSD references. The first and third papers are titled for YbAgCu4 as a cryogenic thermoelectric cooler.
note: Ag is above the 5 at.% split so it is a host element and dopant_roles is empty; Ag and Cu share the framework site and the Ag:Cu ratio tunes the lattice parameter and hence the Yb valence, which is what the intermediate-valence thermopower of this compound depends on. The curator details are melt-spinning and spark-plasma-sintering conditions -- the nanostructuring of the first paper -- and do not bear on the structure type.

basis: La0.7Ag0.3MnO3 and La0.75Ag0.25MnO3 are 5 samples, and the first paper is titled for thermopower of polycrystalline Ag-doped LaMnO3 manganites. That is the perovskite manganite with monovalent Ag on the A site, which hole-dopes the Mn sublattice the same way Ca or Sr does.
note: Three compositions are written as explicit composites, (La0.75K0.25MnO3)(Ag2O)x with x from 0.2 to 0.4, and the second paper is titled for La0.75K0.25MnO3:xAg2O composites based on electron-lattice coupling. In those samples the silver is a separate oxide phase at the grain boundaries, not an A-site substituent, so the host is mixed and stage 2 must split it on whether Ag appears inside the perovskite formula or outside the bracket. Confidence is medium for a second reason: Ag+ is large and its solubility on the A site of LaMnO3 is limited, so even the nominally substituted samples commonly carry metallic Ag at the boundaries -- which is a difference the papers themselves argue about. The only MP entry offered, La3Mn4AgO12 P2 mp-1223238, is a computed cell at hull 0.056 with no ICSD reference, so mp_id is null.

dopant_roles.basis: The La0.75K0.25MnO3 matrix of the composite samples: monovalent K on the trivalent La site is hole doping, at 25% of the A site a defining constituent rather than a dilute dopant.
Ag0.3La0.7Ca0.24Na0.06MnO3: Ca on the A site, the classic divalent hole dopant of the manganites.
The same composition: Na is a second monovalent A-site cation used alongside Ag and Ca to set the Mn3+/Mn4+ ratio.

basis: Ag8SnSe6 and its Cu-substituted variants are the whole host, and the second paper is titled for n-type thermoelectric Ag8SnSe6 with extremely low lattice thermal conductivity. Ag8SnSe6 is the argyrodite: a rigid SnSe4 and Se framework with mobile Ag, orthorhombic Pmn2_1 at room temperature, which TEDesignLab gives directly at mp-17984, hull 0.000.
note: The chunk file flags the crossing explicitly: the measured window is 155-789 K and the order-disorder transition to the cubic superionic phase sits at about 330 K, so the great majority of each curve is in the high-temperature phase. Both phases are the same prototype -- the framework is unchanged and only the Ag ordering melts -- which is why the entry appears twice with different space groups rather than as two prototypes. The 330 K value is the taxonomy default and shifts with the Cu content. No mp_id is offered for the cubic phase, so it is left null rather than reusing the orthorhombic one. Neither MP entry ranked for this host, Ag2SnSe3 and AgSnSe2, is an argyrodite. The composition printed as AgSn0.975Sn0.025Se2 has Sn twice and is a transcription artefact; stage 2 should take it from the paper.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag7.975Cu0.025SnSe6 through Ag7.9Cu0.1SnSe6: Cu takes Ag sites in the mobile-cation sublattice, where it both dopes and alters the ion mobility that sets the transition temperature.

Ta is listed for 4 compositions that the chunk file does not print, and none of the three paper titles mentions it. A refractory group-5 metal has no natural site in an argyrodite; it may be a genuine dopant from the third paper or crucible contamination. Left unknown rather than guessed.

basis: Every composition is Fe2VAl with Ti and W substituting on the V site -- Fe2(V0.7W0.1Ti0.2)Al and relatives -- and the third paper is titled for p-type Heusler compounds. Fe2VAl is the canonical full Heusler, the cubic L2_1 ordering, Fm-3m, and its pseudogap at the Fermi level is why it appears in a thermoelectric dataset at all.
note: Fe2V0.78Ti0.3Al0.92 is off-stoichiometry on both the V and Al sites, which in this family is deliberate: antisite disorder between the Fe and V sublattices is the main carrier source in Fe2VAl and is tuned by moving the composition off 2:1:1. It is a host-element non-stoichiometry rather than a minor element, so it does not appear in dopant_roles, but stage 3 should not read it as a rounding artefact. No reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe2(V0.7W0.1Ti0.2)Al: W on the V site is the heavy-element substitution of the first paper, titled for the effect of heavy-element substitution on electronic structure and lattice thermal conductivity -- so its job is mass-contrast phonon scattering as much as band-structure tuning.
(Fe1.97Co0.03)(V0.8Ti0.2)Al: Co on the Fe site adds an electron per substitution and is the standard n-type dopant of Fe2VAl.
Ta is the group-5 congener of V and the lighter counterpart of W in this heavy-substitution series; the composition carrying it is not printed here.

basis: MnAl is 5 samples and the curator transcribes tau-MnAl for 4 of them and epsilon-MnAl for 2. The tau phase is the ferromagnetic L1_0 ordering, tetragonal P4/mmm, which MP gives at MnAl mp-771, hull 0.000, with 3 ICSD references, and the third paper is titled for the orbital two-channel Kondo effect in epitaxial ferromagnetic L1_0-MnAl films.
note: I read the remaining compositions as having Al and Mn transposed in the input, and that changes what this host is. Al22.5Mn77.5, Al20Mn80, Al17.5Mn82.5 and Al14.3Mn85.7 are nominally Mn-rich, but read the other way round they are Al77.5Mn22.5, Al80Mn20, Al82.5Mn17.5 and Al85.7Mn14.3 -- a clean descending Mn series ending exactly at Al6Mn, which is separately listed in the same host, and covering precisely the 14-22 at.% Mn range in which icosahedral Al-Mn forms. The first two papers are titled for icosahedral quasicrystalline Al-Mn and for Al-Mn quasicrystals, which fits the transposed reading and not the literal one: nothing at 80 at.% Mn is a quasicrystal. So quasicrystal_approximant is listed as the alternative and the host splits between the tau/epsilon MnAl samples and the Al-rich quasicrystalline ones. Confidence is medium because of that transposition, which stage 2 should confirm against the papers. Two further structures are present and have no taxonomy entry: epsilon-MnAl, which the curator names for 2 samples and which is a disordered hexagonal phase that orders to tau on annealing, and Al6Mn, orthorhombic Cmcm, which MP gives at mp-173 with 5 ICSD references. Neither is proposed for one sample each, but neither should be silently folded into the L1_0 shard.

basis: One composition carries the suffix IQC outright -- Al71Pd20Re4.05Ru4.95_IQC -- and the rest are Al-Pd-Mn and Al-Pd-Re at Al70-73, Pd20-23, which is the icosahedral composition field of both systems. The third paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of Al-Pd-Re(-Ru) icosahedral quasicrystals. These are genuine quasicrystals, with high thermopower and very low conductivity from the pseudogap and critical states.
note: This is one of the prototypes the README flags for stage 2: a quasicrystal has no periodic structure, so it cannot be resolved to a Materials Project entry at all and must be mapped to an approximant with that said explicitly. mp_id is null and no space group is recorded. None of the five MP entries ranked for this host -- AlPd, Al21Pd8, AlPd2, Al2Pd, Al3Pd2 -- is in the icosahedral composition field, so the reference describes the crystalline binaries of this system rather than the material measured. Mn, Re and Ru are above or near the 5 at.% split in most compositions and are constituents of the quasicrystal rather than dopants, which is why their roles read as alloying components.

dopant_roles.basis: Al71Pd20Re4.05Ru4.95: Al-Pd-Re is its own icosahedral system, not Al-Pd with a Re impurity -- Re is one of the three constituents that stabilise the phase and is what makes this the most resistive quasicrystal known.
Al72.9Pd22.9Mn4.2: Al-Pd-Mn is the other icosahedral system in this host, and Mn is a required constituent of it.
The first paper is titled for the effect of Ru substitution for Re on the thermoelectric properties of Al-Pd-Re, so Ru replaces Re among the constituents rather than doping the structure.
Fe is another transition metal that stabilises icosahedral Al-Pd, interchangeable with Mn and Re in this family; the composition carrying it is not printed here.
The same role as Fe in this family.

basis: SrAl2Si2 is the majority composition and the first paper is titled for the structure and high-temperature thermoelectric properties of SrAl2Si2. It is the CaAl2Si2 Zintl phase, trigonal P-3m1: slabs of edge-sharing (Al,Si) tetrahedra with the alkaline earth between them. MP confirms it at Sr(AlSi)2 mp-6931, hull 0.000, with 2 ICSD references.
note: Two samples are written SrSi1.8Al0.2, which is a very different Al:Si ratio from SrAl2Si2 and is the subject of the second paper, on Al substitution in SrSi2. SrSi2 is the chiral cubic srsi2_chiral structure, not the CaAl2Si2 slab, so those samples may belong to a different prototype; the host is not marked mixed because the ratio may equally be a transcription of an Al-substituted SrAl2Si2, and stage 2 should settle it from the paper. The MP list also offers SrAlSi P-6m2 mp-3698 with 2 ICSD references, the equiatomic AlB2-derived phase, which is a third structure in this chemistry but matches no composition printed here.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr0.95Y0.05Al2Si2 through Sr0.85Y0.15Al2Si2, and the third paper is titled for the effect of yttrium on SrAl2Si2: trivalent Y on the divalent Sr site adds an electron per substitution, which is the n-type doping of this Zintl phase.
Eu is divalent and almost exactly Sr-sized, so on the Sr site it is an isovalent magnetic substitution rather than a carrier dopant; the composition carrying it is not printed here.

basis: The host is one composition, NdFeAsOF, all 12 samples, and the single paper is titled for the anisotropy of the transport properties of NdFeAs(O,F) thin films. NdFeAsO is the 1111 iron pnictide, ZrCuSiAs type, P4/nmm, with F on the O site of the NdO layer as the electron doping.
note: The composition string writes F at full occupancy, NdFeAsOF, which cannot be right for a superconducting film -- F substitutes for a fraction of the O, typically 0.1 to 0.2, and the paper writes it NdFeAs(O,F) precisely because the fraction is not pinned down. So F is a host element by the 5 at.% rule as parsed, but is really the doping variable, and stage 3 should not compute a level from this string. Both MP entries offered are computed Nd-Fe-As-O-F supercells at hull 0.16 to 0.17 with no ICSD reference and neither is the 1111, so mp_id is left null.

basis: BP is 11 of the 12 samples and all three papers are about boron phosphide. BP is zincblende, F-43m, and TEDesignLab gives it directly at mp-1479, hull 0.000, with 6 ICSD references.

other_polymorphs.note: MP lists hexagonal BP at hull 0.012 with 1 ICSD reference against 6 for zincblende. Two of the samples are films, where it could in principle be stabilised, but nothing in the titles suggests it; recorded so the possibility is not lost.

note: The twelfth sample is B12P2, which is the rhombohedral icosahedral boride: B12 icosahedra linked by P-P pairs, R-3m, the same structural family as boron carbide and completely different from zincblende BP. One sample, so the host is marked mixed only to keep it out of the sphalerite shard; it splits cleanly on the B:P ratio. MP lists B13P2 R-3m mp-13862 for this chemistry but at hull 0.962, which is implausible for a compound with an ICSD reference and is not used.

basis: LaBaCuFeO5 and its substituted variants are the whole host, and the first paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. The 5 rather than 6 oxygens is the signature: this is the A-site-ordered double perovskite, La and Ba alternating in layers with an ordered oxygen vacancy between them, leaving Cu and Fe in square pyramids -- the same structural principle as YBCO, which is exactly what the layered_double_perovskite entry names.
note: Confidence is medium on two counts. The B site holds Cu and Fe in equal amounts and they are generally NOT ordered on it, so the compound is A-site-ordered and B-site-disordered, whereas the entry is written around LnBaCo2O5+delta with one B species -- a v4 seed should say that mixed B sites are allowed. And the oxygen content is variable, written 5+delta in the papers and 5 in the compositions here, which changes the tilt symmetry between P4/mmm and a lower orthorhombic setting. Both MP entries offered are computed La-Ba-Cu-Fe-O cells at hull 0.09 and 0.28 with no ICSD reference, so mp_id is left null. The curator detail confirms the La1-xPrxBaCuFeO5+delta series of the second paper.

dopant_roles.basis: LaBaCu0.9Co0.1FeO5: the third paper is titled for heterovalent substitutions on the Cu and Fe sites, and Co goes onto the square-pyramidal B site.
LaBa(Cu0.5Fe0.5)1.9W0.1O5: hexavalent W on the B site is the heterovalent substitution of the third paper, and it also pulls in extra oxygen.
La0.75Pr0.25BaCuFeO5, and the curator records the La1-xPrxBaCuFeO5+delta series: Pr replaces La on the ordered rare-earth A layer, not the Ba one.
LaBaCuFe0.95Zn0.05O5: Zn on the B site, closing the d shell and removing a magnetic ion.
Another 3d transition metal on the B site in the same heterovalent-substitution series; the composition carrying it is not printed here.
Pentavalent Nb on the B site, the same role as W in the third paper.
Ni on the B site alongside Cu and Fe, the same substitution series.

basis: Every composition is the workhorse p-type alloy Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 with carbon added -- C60 in the first paper, multi-walled carbon nanotubes in the second, and the curator records 1%CNT/Bi0.4Sb1.6Te3. Carbon takes no site in the tetradymite lattice, so this is a matrix plus a dispersed second phase rather than a carbide or a solid solution. The matrix is recorded as the alternative so stage 2 resolves the Bi-Sb-Te structure instead of treating the host as structureless.
note: Handled the same way as the Bi-C-Te host in chunk 8. Carbon sits above the 5 at.% split in every composition (C0.28 of 5.28 atoms is 5.3%), so it appears as a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry even though it is physically an inclusion. No reference line is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null.

basis: ZrCoBi and its Ni- and Pd-substituted variants are 11 of the 12 samples, two of the three papers are titled for half-Heusler bismuthides ZrCo1-xNixBi and Pd-doped ZrCoBi, and the reference agrees: ZrCoBi F-43m (216) mp-31451 at hull 0.000. That is the cubic MgAgAs ordering with the fourth site empty.
note: One sample is Zr6CoBi2, which is not a half-Heusler: MP gives it as P-62m mp-1206046 at hull 0.000, the metal-rich R6TX2 ordering, so zr6coas2_type was proposed for it and the host splits on the Zr:Co ratio. The F-43m entry rests on a single ICSD reference, which is weak, but the papers name the structure directly. Note that the split is clean on composition, so only the one Zr6CoBi2 composition moves.

dopant_roles.basis: Sn on the Bi main-group site is the standard acceptor for ZrCoBi and is what makes the p-type branch of this family work; it cannot sit on the Co site without breaking the 18-electron count.
ZrCo0.97Pd0.03Bi and ZrCo0.91Pd0.09Bi, and the third paper is titled for Pd-doped ZrCoBi: Pd is isoelectronic with Ni and goes onto the tetrahedral transition-metal site.
ZrCo0.9Ni0.1Bi, the ZrCo1-xNixBi series of the first paper; Ni adds one electron per substitution on the Co site.

basis: Cu4Bi4S9 and the Cu1.6Bi4.6S8 series are large-cell copper bismuth sulfosalts, and the first paper is titled for the interstitial site that determines their crystal chemistry. The formulas are not reducible to a simple binary or to CuBiS2, and the reference bears that out: the entries offered for this chemistry are Cu4Bi4S9 Pnma mp-683991 and a string of Cu-Bi-Pb-Ag sulfosalts at C2/m and P2_1/m, exactly the large low-symmetry cells this prototype covers.
note: The taxonomy already names Bi-Cu-S under this entry and the compositions confirm it. Cu4Bi4S9 and Cu1.6Bi4.6S8 are different phases of the same family rather than one structure, so the prototype is a family label here and stage 2 must resolve each formula separately -- which is what the entry itself says about every member. The second paper is on the selenide analogue Cu4Bi4Se9. mp_id is left at the host level rather than picked, since CuBiS2 Pnma mp-22982 carries the most ICSD references (4) but is not any composition in this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu1.576Zn0.024Bi4.6S8 and Cu1.592Zn0.008Bi4.6S8 keep Bi and S fixed while Cu falls by the Zn added, so Zn takes the Cu site.
Cu1.576In0.024Bi4.6S8 is written the same way as the Zn analogue, with Bi fixed at 4.6, so In is on the Cu site rather than the Bi one -- a donor substitution.

Cu1.6Bi4.6S7.96Se0.04 replaces a little S by Se on the chalcogen sublattice; the second paper on Cu4Bi4Se9 shows the whole series exists, so this is the dilute end of an anion solid solution, not doping.

basis: Every composition is CoSb3 with carbon added, at C0.35 to C0.8 per CoSb3, and the papers name the additive directly: fullerene dispersion, a CoSb3/graphene nanocomposite, and large-defect scattering. The curator confirms it -- CoSb3/G, ground together with graphene. Carbon does not enter the skutterudite framework or its icosahedral void at these levels, so the samples are a skutterudite matrix plus a dispersed carbon phase.
note: Both skutterudite alternatives are recorded because the matrix differs across the host: five compositions are unfilled CoSb3 while Ba0.25Co4Sb12.07(BaC60)0.03 is a Ba-filled skutterudite carrying a fullerene addition. Carbon is above the 5 at.% cut in every composition, so it is a host element with no dopant_roles entry. No reference line is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.25Co4Sb12.07: Ba occupies the icosahedral void of the CoSb3 framework, the same role as Yb and In in this family. Part of the Ba is delivered as BaC60, so some of it may remain in the fullerene phase rather than reaching the cage.
Ni on the octahedral transition-metal site is the usual n-type donor in CoSb3.
Te on the Sb ring site is the standard n-type donor for skutterudites.

basis: Every composition is CaCu3Ti4-xRuxO12 with x from 1 to 3, and the first paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of AA3B4O12-type ordered perovskite oxides. The AA3B4O12 stoichiometry with Cu on three quarters of the A sites is exactly what this entry names, and Ru simply shares the octahedral B site with Ti across the series.
note: Ru is above the 5 at.% cut in every composition, so it is a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry even though it is physically a B-site substituent: the Ti:Ru ratio is the tuning variable of the second paper, which is about the localised-to-itinerant transition it drives. No reference line is offered for this five-element host; the Im-3 cell must come from a CaCu3Ti4O12 lookup in stage 2, not from a Ca-Cu-O-Ru-Ti search.

basis: Both compositions are CaTiO3 with Fe on the octahedral B site, CaTi0.7Fe0.3O3 carrying 11 of the 12 samples, and the second paper studies ionic mobility in perovskites by resistivity relaxation. CaTiO3 is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type tilted perovskite and Fe3+ substitutes for Ti4+ on the B site, compensated by oxygen vacancies.
note: Confidence is medium for two reasons. The measurement runs to 1482 K and the first paper is about thermochemical decomposition and nanoscale iron redistribution, so the samples are deliberately reduced -- at CaTi0.5Fe0.5O3 the vacancy concentration approaches the point where the vacancies order into brownmillerite-like layers instead of staying disordered, which is why brownmillerite is recorded as an alternative rather than ignored. And I disagree with the reference here: every Materials Project entry offered for this chemistry is a different stoichiometry (CaTi2FeO6, Ca3Ti(FeO4)2, Ca4Ti3FeO12, CaTi4(FeO4)3), each on at most one ICSD reference, and none of them is Fe-substituted CaTiO3. mp_id is therefore left null rather than taken from that list.

basis: CaIrO3 is the whole host and is the archetype of the post-perovskite structure -- the reference is unambiguous, CaIrO3 Cmcm (63) mp-4243 at hull 0.000 with 18 ICSD references, far ahead of anything else in the chemistry. The second paper measures spark-plasma-sintered CaIrO3 ceramics, which is the bulk post-perovskite.

other_polymorphs.note: The first paper is titled for epitaxial perovskite CaIrO3 and the third for Sn substitution in the Dirac line-node semimetal SrIrO3, whose CaIrO3 counterpart is also film-grown. The perovskite form of CaIrO3 is not obtained by heating the post-perovskite; it is stabilised on a substrate or at high pressure. MP offers only CaIrO3 Pm-3m mp-1016872 at hull 0.314, the cubic aristotype, which is not the orthorhombic Pbnm cell the films actually adopt, so mp_id is left null.

note: The seed offered perovskite and post_perovskite together and called the host mixed; that is refined rather than confirmed, because the two are not selected by composition -- there is only one composition, CaIrO3 -- but by synthesis route. Bulk ceramics are post-perovskite, epitaxial films are perovskite, so this host is decided at the sample level and the composition-level split of stage 2 cannot resolve it. is_mixed is kept true so it reaches the review queue.

basis: The single composition Ca1.5La1.5Rh4Sn13 is the R3T4Sn13 stoichiometry exactly, with Ca and La sharing the rare-earth site, and its paper is about increasing atomic-scale disorder by doping in a superconductor -- which is what the (Ca,La)3Rh4Sn13 Remeika series is studied for. Sn12 icosahedral cages around the rare earth, not a skutterudite framework.
note: Uses the prototype proposed from chunk 9 for the La-Rh-Sn host; this is its second host, which is the corroboration that entry asked for. No reference line at all is offered here, so mp_id is left null -- the mp-30513 cited in the proposal belongs to La3Sn13Rh4 in the other host and must be re-resolved for this mixed Ca/La composition in stage 2. Ca and La are both host elements, so there are no dopant roles; the Ca:La ratio is the disorder variable of the paper, not doping.

basis: The host holds two Zintl stoichiometries and the 1-2-2 one dominates the compositions shown: EuZnCdSb2, EuZn1.4Cd0.6Sb2, Eu(Zn0.7Cd0.3)2Sb2 and Eu(Zn0.5Cd0.5)2Sb2 are all EuM2Sb2, the CaAl2Si2-type slab of edge-sharing MSb4 tetrahedra with Eu between the layers, and two of the three papers are about Eu(Zn1-xCdx)2Sb2 and the AM2Sb2 family. Eu11Cd4.5Zn1.5Sb12 and Eu11Cd1.6Zn4.4Sb12 are the 11-6-12 phase instead.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral M cation site of the anionic framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Cd/(Cd+Zn) spans 0.27-0.85 with median 0.65 over 12 compositions. Cd and Zn are both group 12 and both occupy the tetrahedral framework site in each of the two structures, so the axis is genuine; the first paper is explicitly on the solid-solution Zintl phase. The parent end member therefore depends on the composition and none is recorded here.

note: The seed offered zintl_11_6_12 alone, which is refined rather than confirmed: the discriminate_from field of that entry says this same chemistry also holds EuCd2Sb2 and must be split by stoichiometry, and the compositions show the 1-2-2 phase is the larger part. The split is clean on the Eu:M ratio -- 11:6 against 1:2 -- so stage 2 can make it from composition. Confidence is medium only because the full 12-composition list is not shown and the balance between the two phases could shift. No reference line is offered for this host, so both mp_ids are left null.

basis: This host is a set of distinct ternary cerium germanides rather than one structure, and CeCo2Ge2 is the largest single composition (2 samples) and the best-attested formula in the reference (Ce(CoGe)2 I4/mmm mp-20933, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD references), which is the ThCr2Si2 BaAl4 derivative. The papers are surveys of magnetic and transport properties across ternary intermetallics, not studies of one compound.
note: Six compositions, five structure types, one or two samples each -- the host label is a routing key here and nothing more, which is why confidence is low. Composition by composition: CeCo2Ge2 is the 122 (mp-20933); CeCoGe3 is the non-centrosymmetric BaNiSn3-type I4mm (mp-21116, 3 ICSD), which the banisn3_i4mm entry proposed in chunk 9 already names as a representative; Ce2CoGe3 is an AlB2-derived hexagonal phase with Co and Ge sharing the honeycomb site; Ce2Co3Ge5 is the U2Co3Si5 type, Ibam (mp-1188584, 1 ICSD); CeCo0.86Ge2 is the CeNiSi2 type, Cmcm (the reference CeCoGe2 Cmcm mp-1079178, 2 ICSD), the Co deficiency being intrinsic to that structure; and Ce5Co4Ge13 I did not resolve. The last three have no taxonomy entry, so unresolved_crystalline stands for them rather than forcing them onto a neighbouring type; each carries one sample, which is too thin to propose on. Stage 2 must split this host per composition.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe on the transition-metal site of whichever germanide carries it; the composition is not printed here, so the host phase it belongs to is not certain.

basis: CeRhSn and its CeRh1-xMxSn variants (M = Co, Ni, Ru) are the whole host, and CeRhSn is the hexagonal ordered Fe2P (ZrNiAl) type, not a CrB-type chain compound. The reference says so directly: CeSnRh P-62m (189) mp-12374 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, the best-attested equiatomic entry in the chemistry. The third paper measures single-crystal CeRhSn with valence fluctuation, which is the compound this structure type is known for.
note: I disagree with the seed taxonomy here and reject its hypothesis. crb_feb_chain names Ce-Rh-Sn among its example host systems, but the CrB/FeB entry is orthorhombic Cmcm/Pnma and CeRhSn is hexagonal P-62m. The reference agrees with me against the taxonomy, and the zrnial_fe2p entry proposed from chunk 9 already anticipated this host, noting that CeRhSn is the same type. A v4 seed should drop Ce-Rh-Sn from crb_feb_chain. The Ce3Sn13Rh4 Pm-3n mp-7203 ranked first for this host (4 ICSD references) is the Remeika 3-4-13 phase and is a real compound of the chemistry, but no composition here has that stoichiometry, so the ICSD-count ranking points at a phase these papers did not make.

dopant_roles.basis: CeRh0.95Ni0.05Sn and CeRh0.9Ni0.1Sn; the second paper is titled for CeRh1-xMxSn with M = Co, Ni, Ru, so all three sit on the Rh site and tune the hybridisation rather than acting as carriers.
CeRh0.95Co0.05Sn, from the same CeRh1-xMxSn series; Co is isoelectronic with Rh.
CeRh0.9Ru0.1Sn, the electron-poor member of the same series, which is how the valence-fluctuating state is tuned.

basis: Every composition is YbxFe4-yCoySb12 at x of 0.85 to 0.9 -- the p-type Yb-filled skutterudite -- and all three papers say so in their titles, including double-filled YbxLayFe2.7Co1.3Sb12. The Co4Sb12 framework with a guest in the icosahedral void is the filled variant, not the empty one.
note: Yb at 0.9 per 16.9 atoms is 5.3 at.%, just above the split, so it is a host element here and carries no dopant_roles entry even though it is physically the cage filler -- the same element is a filler dopant in the Co-Sb host, where it falls below the cut. Fe and Co share the octahedral framework site and their ratio sets the carrier type; that is a framework variable, not doping. Yb0.85La0Fe2.7Co1.3Sb12 carries a literal La0, a parse artifact of the double-filled series, and no La is present in that sample. No reference line is offered for this four-element host, so mp_id is left null.

basis: The compositions are written Cox(MgO)100-x with x from 34 to 50 at.%, and the single paper is on the skew-scattering-dominated anomalous Hall effect in CoxMgO films. That is a granular metal: nanoscale metallic Co grains in an insulating rocksalt MgO matrix, scanned through the percolation threshold. A third to a half of a rocksalt lattice cannot be substituted by Co, so this is not a Co-Mg-O solid solution.
note: I reject the seed hypothesis. rocksalt_oxide names Co-Mg-O among its example host systems, and that is right for the CoO-MgO solid solution but not for these samples, whose composition strings keep MgO intact as a unit and whose paper is about transport through metallic grains. The matrix is recorded as the alternative so stage 2 still resolves MgO. A v4 seed should either drop this host from rocksalt_oxide or note that it is a granular composite. The reference cannot settle it either way: every Mg-Co-O entry offered is a computed spinel or rocksalt ordering at hull 0.056 to 0.183 with no ICSD reference, so none of them is this material and mp_id is left null. Confidence is medium because only one paper and no sample-form field back the granular reading, and a genuine rocksalt (Co,Mg)O solid solution does exist at low Co.

basis: Every composition is TiCo1-xNixSb across the full range x = 0.2 to 0.8, and the first paper is titled for the TiCo1-xNixSb solid solution. TiCoSb and TiNiSb are both the cubic MgAgAs half-Heusler ordering, so Co and Ni simply share the tetrahedral transition-metal site and the whole series stays in one prototype.
note: Co and Ni are both host elements, and their ratio is the electron-count variable rather than doping: TiCoSb is the 18-electron semiconductor and each Ni adds one electron. No reference line is offered for this four-element host, so mp_id is left null. The third paper is on Ti2NiCoSn1-xSb1+x, which at Ni:Co = 1:1 is the ordered quaternary Heusler rather than a disordered half-Heusler; no such composition is visible in the subset shown, but if one carries equal Ni and Co, stage 2 should check quaternary_heusler for it.

dopant_roles.basis: The second and third papers are on TiCoSb-TiM2Sn phase stability and on Ti2NiCoSn1-xSb1+x, so Sn substitutes for Sb on the main-group site, removing one electron per substitution -- the p-type knob in this family.

basis: Co3V2O8 is 11 of the 12 samples, all single crystals, and the second paper is titled for the antiferromagnetic insulator Co3V2O8. At M:V = 3:2 the vanadium is fully oxidised into isolated V5+O4 tetrahedra and the Co2+ octahedra form the buckled kagome staircase layers of the Ni3V2O8 type -- not an AB2O4 spinel, which needs M:V = 1:2. The one CoV2O4 sample is the spinel.
note: The seed filed the whole host under spinel, which is right for one sample in twelve and wrong for the other eleven, so kagome_staircase_m3v2o8 was proposed. The split is clean on the Co:V ratio, 3:2 against 1:2. The reference offers no Co3V2O8 entry at all -- its ranked list is V2CoO8 Pnma at hull 0.228, V2Co2O7, V2CoO4 spinel and a cobalt arsenate-vanadate -- so mp_id is left null; the supporting evidence for the family is Mn3V2O8 Cmce (64) mp-19692 at hull 0.000 in the Mn-O-V host of this same chunk, which is this structure type. The measured window is 10-193 K, well below the 985 K range where the vanadate polymorphs interconvert, so no transition is recorded.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [64], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62, 2, 5, 12]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CsSnI3 and its Cl-, Ge- and PbI2-modified variants are the whole host, and all three papers treat it as an inorganic halide perovskite -- self-doping in halide perovskites, CsSn1-xGexI3, and CsSnI3 perovskite. The reference lists the three perovskite tilt variants of the black phase at Pnma, P4/mbm and Pm-3m, which is the standard ABX3 sequence.
note: No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line is printed for this host, but the measured window of 293-522 K spans both octahedral-tilt transitions of black CsSnI3 -- orthorhombic Pnma to tetragonal P4/mbm near 350 K and tetragonal to cubic Pm-3m near 425 K -- and the reference supplies a distinct mp_id for each, all within 7 meV of the hull on 2 ICSD references apiece. All three are the same prototype, so this is a distortion sequence rather than a change of structure type; the temperatures are from materials knowledge, not from the papers, and shift with the Cl and Ge content, so they are medium confidence and a v4 seed should carry them as phase_transitions on the perovskite entry. Two further phases exist in this chemistry and are deliberately not recorded: the yellow one-dimensional double-chain polymorph of CsSnI3, which forms on cooling from the melt rather than on heating, and Cs2SnI6 Fm-3m mp-27636, the vacancy-ordered oxidation product, which is a different composition. The curator notes 1% mixed CsSnI3-xClx perovskite thin films for 5 samples.

dopant_roles.basis: CsSnI2.99Cl0.01, and the curator records CsSnI3-xClx films: Cl sits on the halide site. The first paper is about controlling self-doping, and this trace halide substitution is how the Sn vacancy concentration and therefore the hole density is set, so it acts through the defect chemistry rather than as a direct dopant.
CsSn0.9Ge0.1I3 and CsSn0.8Ge0.2I3, the CsSn1-xGexI3 series of the second paper; Ge is isovalent with Sn on the B site and contracts the octahedron rather than adding carriers.

(CsSnI3)0.995(PbI2)0.005 is written as a PbI2 addition rather than as a substituted formula, so part of the Pb may remain as a second phase, but PbI2 and CsSnI3 alloy readily and Pb2+ on the Sn site is the expected outcome at these levels.

basis: Zn2Cu3In3Te8 and the Zn2-xCu3+xIn3Te8 series are most of the host, and the second paper is titled for A2Cu3In3Te8 (A = Cd, Zn, Mn, Mg). With eight cations to eight tellurium the structure is a fully occupied diamond-like framework, and ordering three cation species on the tetrahedral sublattice is the stannite-kesterite case rather than chalcopyrite. The reference supports the tetragonal ordering: Zn2InCuTe4 I-42m (121) mp-1215701 is the stannite setting.
note: Refined on two counts. Cu0.9In0.9Zn0.2Te2 is Zn-substituted CuInTe2 -- ordinary chalcopyrite, and the first paper is on lattice defects in p-type CuInTe2 -- so the host splits on the Zn content, ternary against quaternary. And the degree of cation ordering in Zn2Cu3In3Te8 is not settled by composition: the ratio 2:3:3 does not match the I-42m stannite cell of the MP entry offered (Zn2CuInTe4 reduces differently), and the third paper reports in-situ nanodomains from composition fluctuation, which points at partial disorder toward the cubic F-43m sphalerite average. So the prototype names the ordered family and stage 2 must take the actual space group from the paper. Confidence is medium for that reason, not because the diamond-like framework is in doubt.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag is the larger group 11 congener of Cu and takes the same tetrahedral cation site; in this family it is used to expand the lattice and scatter phonons rather than to add carriers.

basis: La2CuIrO6 and its (Ca,Ba)xLa2-xCuIrO6 variants are the whole host, and A2BBO6 with two different octahedral cations -- Jahn-Teller Cu2+ against 5d Ir -- is the B-site-ordered double perovskite. The single paper is titled for iridium valence variation and carrier sign tuning in that series, which only makes sense if Ir sits on an ordered octahedral site. The reference agrees on the monoclinic setting: La2CuIrO6 P2_1/c (14) mp-1211597.
note: mp-1211597 is a computed entry at hull 0.032 with no ICSD reference behind it, so it is recorded here as the only candidate rather than as evidence, and must be re-resolved in stage 2. P2_1/c is the usual monoclinic setting for a rock-salt-ordered double perovskite with tilted octahedra, so it is at least consistent. Cu and Ir are both host elements; their 1:1 ratio is the ordering itself, not doping.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.2La1.8CuIrO6 and Ba0.4La1.6CuIrO6: divalent Ba on the trivalent A site is hole doping, and the paper measures the resulting Ir valence change and carrier sign reversal.
Ca0.2La1.8CuIrO6 and Ca0.4La1.6CuIrO6, the same A-site hole doping with a smaller cation, which also increases the octahedral tilt.

basis: Every composition is a Mn-Zn ferrite, (Mn,Zn)Fe2O4, with the A:B ratio held at 1:2 and rare earths or In taking a little of the Fe. The first paper is on rare-earth-substituted Mn-Zn ferrites and the second on In-substituted Mn-Zn nano-ferrites. MFe2O4 ferrites are the archetypal spinels, and the reference entries offered are all MnZn(FeO2)x orderings of that same AB2O4 framework.
note: Mn-Zn ferrites are partly inverse spinels -- Zn2+ prefers tetrahedral A, Mn2+ and Fe3+ share both sites -- so the cation distribution, not the prototype, is what stage 2 has to resolve. The MP entries offered are ordered F-43m, P-4m2 and R3m cells at hull 0.000 to 0.072 with no ICSD references; they are orderings of the spinel framework rather than distinct structures, and mp_id is left null since none of them is the disordered cubic Fd-3m ferrite these samples are. The curator formula Mn0.58-x/2Zn0.37-x/2MxFe2.05O4 confirms that the substituent replaces the divalent A cations in that paper, not Fe, which is why the rare-earth site assignment below is medium rather than high.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn0.4Zn0.6In0.035Fe1.965O4: In enters as the Fe count falls by the same amount, so trivalent In takes the octahedral B site -- the second paper is about the conduction changes that follow.

Mn0.5Zn0.5Ce0.05Fe1.95O4 is written with Fe reduced by the Ce added, so the rare earth formally replaces Fe on the octahedral site.
