The curator formula from the other paper instead subtracts from Mn and Zn, and rare earths are far too large for either site in quantity, so some of it segregates to grain boundaries.
Mn0.5Zn0.5La0.05Fe1.95O4, the same rare-earth-for-Fe substitution as Ce.
Mn0.5Zn0.5Tb0.05Fe1.95O4, same series.
Mn0.5Zn0.5Th0.05Fe1.95O4, same series; Th4+ is an unusual member and is likely to be the least soluble of them.
Part of the same rare-earth-substituted ferrite series of the first paper; the composition carrying it is not printed here.
Part of the same rare-earth-substituted ferrite series; the composition carrying it is not printed here.

basis: Every composition is FeSb2Se4 with Sn or In on the Sb site, and both papers treat it as a single ferromagnetic-semiconductor phase -- bipolar doping in FeSb2-xSnxSe4, and indium preferential distribution in magnetic FeSb2Se4. The MSb2X4 stoichiometry is a ternary framework of FeSe6 octahedral chains within an Sb-Se network, isostructural with MnSb2Se4, and no existing prototype covers it.
note: Confidence is medium because the space group is from the structure literature on MnSb2Se4 rather than from either reference, and the monoclinic C2/m assignment has to be confirmed in stage 2. The only MP entry offered for this host is FeSbSe P2_1/c mp-1103256 at hull 0.000 on one ICSD reference -- a 1:1:1 compound, not the 1:2:4 these samples are -- so mp_id is left null rather than taken from it. The curator detail, p-type ferromagnetic semiconductors, matches the family.

dopant_roles.basis: FeSb2-xSnxSe4 at x = 0.02 to 0.2 is the series of the first paper, whose point is that Sn2+ for Sb3+ is compensated by charge disproportionation rather than by a simple hole, so the doping is bipolar.

FeSb1.95In0.05Se4 is written with Sb reduced by the In added, so nominally In takes the Sb site; the second paper is titled for indium preferential distribution, meaning the site it actually occupies is the finding of the paper and should be taken from there in stage 2.

basis: LiMn2O4 and its slightly off-stoichiometric and Li-deintercalated forms (Li0.4Mn2O4 to Li1.03Mn1.97O4) are the whole host, both papers are about the LiMn2O4 cathode and its chemical and electrochemical deintercalation, and the reference is emphatic: LiMn2O4 Fd-3m (227) mp-25015 with 23 ICSD references, more than any other Li-Mn-O entry.
note: Removing lithium from the 8a tetrahedral site leaves the Mn2O4 spinel framework intact all the way to lambda-MnO2, so Li0.4Mn2O4 is the same prototype with an emptier A site, not a different structure -- the lithium content is the carrier-concentration and Mn-valence variable. Li is a host element throughout, so there are no dopant roles. Two things stage 2 should know: LiMn2O4 has a cubic-to-orthorhombic charge-ordering transition just below room temperature near 280 K, and the measured window here is 233-302 K, so it may straddle it; I have not recorded it as a phase because it is a Jahn-Teller distortion of the same framework and the 280 K figure is composition-sensitive, moving with the Li:Mn ratio that these samples deliberately scan. The layered LiMnO2 and Li2MnO3 entries in the reference are real phases of the chemistry but no composition here has their stoichiometry.

basis: Li2RuO3 with Ti or Ir on the Ru site is the whole host, and Li2MO3 is the honeycomb-ordered layered oxide -- Li[Li1/3Ru2/3]O2, a superstructure of the alpha-NaFeO2 O3 stacking in which one third of the transition-metal layer is lithium. The reference agrees on the monoclinic cell: Li2RuO3 C2/m (12) mp-4630 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in the chemistry. The first paper is on ruthenium oxide as a thermoelectric with unconventional behaviour, the second on its anisotropy with correlation and orbital effects.
note: No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line is printed, because the taxonomy had no entry for this family at all until now, but the 20-612 K window does cross one: Li2RuO3 dimerises below about 540 K, the Ru honeycomb forming Ru-Ru singlet pairs and the symmetry dropping from C2/m to P2_1/m. That is a distortion of one prototype rather than a change of type, so both phases carry the same id and differ only in space group, and the low-temperature cell has no mp_id in the reference. The 540 K figure is from materials knowledge, not from these papers, and Ti or Ir substitution suppresses the dimerisation -- which is what the second paper is about -- so it does not hold across the whole host. Confidence is medium on the prototype for the same reason it is a proposal: the honeycomb ordering is inferred from the Li2MO3 stoichiometry and the C2/m cell, not read from a paper.

dopant_roles.basis: Li2Ru1-xTixO3 at x = 0.05 to 0.3: d0 Ti4+ on the Ru site dilutes the honeycomb and breaks up the Ru-Ru dimerisation, which is the experiment rather than a carrier-doping exercise.
Li2Ru0.9Ir0.1O3 and Li2Ru0.8Ir0.2O3; Ir on the same honeycomb site moves the system toward Li2IrO3, so this is an isostructural alloying axis rather than doping.

basis: The host is MgO, with one alumina-added composition, and the reference is as strong as it gets in this dataset: MgO Fm-3m (225) mp-1265 at hull 0.000 with 54 ICSD references in TEDesignLab, against one or two for every other polymorph. MgO is the archetypal rocksalt monoxide.

other_polymorphs.note: TEDesignLab lists MgO at P6_3/mmc, Ibam and P6/mcc on one ICSD reference each at hull 0.040 to 0.113. These are high-pressure or thin-film curiosities, not phases reached by heating bulk MgO, which melts at 3125 K in the B1 structure. MgO2 Pa-3 and C2/m are a different composition, the peroxide.

note: The seed hypothesis was rocksalt, which is the same structure but the wrong shard. rocksalt_oxide exists, in its own words, so that the monoxides shard together, and it already names Cd-O, Ni-O and Co-Mg-O; leaving MgO itself under rocksalt with PbTe and SnTe would separate it from the Co-Mg-O host it belongs with. So this is a shard refinement, not a structural disagreement, and a v4 seed should move Mg-O across. Note also that most papers in this host do not study MgO as a thermoelectric at all -- they measure NaxCoO2 thin films and superconducting microbolometers, for which MgO is the substrate -- so the transport curves here may not belong to the material named. That is a data-quality flag for stage 2 rather than a structure question. The second MP reference list is not usable: it ranks MgO2 C2/m at hull 0.531 first and then a string of BaMg30AlO32-type computed cells.

dopant_roles.basis: (MgO)0.96(Al2O3)0.04 is written as an alumina addition, and MgO-Al2O3 does not form a rocksalt solid solution at 4 mol% -- it reacts to MgAl2O4 spinel. So the Al is in a second phase, not on the Mg site.

basis: Every composition is Sn1-xMgxTe with a Cu2Te addition, and both papers are explicitly about SnTe -- interstitial defects improving thermoelectric SnTe, and maximising transporting bands for high-performance SnTe alloy thermoelectrics. SnTe is rocksalt, and Mg2+ substituting on the cation site is the standard band-convergence alloying that widens the gap and lifts the light and heavy valence bands together.
note: Mg is a host element at 12 to 20 at.% of the cation site, so it carries no dopant_roles entry; note that MgTe on its own is wurtzite or NiAs, not rocksalt, so beyond the solubility limit a second phase appears -- at Mg0.2 these samples are at or past the usual limit and MgTe precipitates are likely, which stage 2 should expect. No reference line is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null; SnTe must be resolved as the rocksalt Fm-3m entry in stage 2 and not as the metastable zincblende form, which is a known trap in this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: Added as (Cu2Te)0.01 to 0.05 rather than substituted into the formula, and the first paper is titled for interstitial defects improving SnTe: Cu occupies interstitial sites in the rocksalt lattice, which is how it scatters phonons and donates carriers without simply filling Sn vacancies.
Sn0.8Ge0.05Mg0.2Te: Ge is isovalent with Sn on the cation site and continues the same band-convergence alloying as Mg, on the SnTe-GeTe line.

basis: Every composition sits on the AB2O4 line -- MnV2O4, Mn2VO4, Mn1.67V1.33O4 and the Cr- and Zn-substituted MnV2O4 -- and the first paper is titled for the Mott insulator MnV2O4, the third for its ferrimagnetism. MnV2O4 is a normal spinel with V3+ on the octahedral B site, and Mn2VO4 is the inverse arrangement of the same framework, so the whole host is one prototype at different cation distributions.
note: The reference does not cover this host usefully and I do not follow it: its ranked list is Mn2V2O7, Mn3V2O8 Cmce and two barium manganese vanadates, none of which is an AB2O4 spinel, and it offers no MnV2O4 entry at all -- so mp_id is left null. Mn3V2O8 Cmce (64) mp-19692 is a real phase of this chemistry and is the kagome staircase structure proposed for the Co-O-V host in this chunk, but no composition here has that 3:2 ratio. MnV2O4 has a cubic-to-tetragonal orbital-ordering transition at about 53 K and orders ferrimagnetically near 57 K; the measured window is 101-300 K, so it stays above both and no phases are recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn(V0.95Cr0.05)2O4 and Mn(V0.9Cr0.1)2O4 are written with Cr inside the B-site bracket; Cr3+ has no orbital degeneracy, so it dilutes the V3+ orbital order that these papers measure.
Mn0.95Zn0.05V2O4: divalent Zn replaces Mn on the tetrahedral A site, removing a magnetic ion from that sublattice.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12, 62, 205, 64]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every composition is Pb1-xMnxTe with 4% Na, x running from 0.12 to 0.36, so the matrix is Na-doped rocksalt PbTe with Mn alloyed onto the cation site. The single paper is titled for eutectic microstructures and the thermoelectric properties of MnTe-rich precipitates, which names both the matrix and what the excess Mn does.
note: Confidence is medium and is_mixed is deliberately false. Mn solubility in PbTe is only a few per cent, so at x = 0.12 to 0.36 every one of these samples is two-phase: a rocksalt (Pb,Mn)Te matrix plus NiAs-type MnTe-rich precipitates in a eutectic microstructure, which is the subject of the paper. nias is recorded as an alternative prototype because the second phase is real, but is_mixed is false because the two coexist inside every single composition -- there is no composition-level split that separates them, so marking it mixed would send stage 2 looking for one. The matrix structure is what the host label should mean. No reference line is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: Na0.04 in every composition: monovalent Na on the Pb site is the standard acceptor for p-type PbTe, and it is held fixed here while the Mn content is scanned.

basis: ScNiSb is 11 of the 12 samples and the remainder is ScNi0.86Sb, the same compound with nickel vacancies. All three papers are surveys of the ScMSb and YMSb 1:1:1 compounds, and the reference is unambiguous for the type: ScNiSb F-43m (216) mp-3432 at hull 0.000 -- the cubic MgAgAs ordering with the fourth site vacant.
note: ScNi0.86Sb is worth flagging for stage 3: the Ni deficiency is intrinsic non-stoichiometry on the tetrahedral site -- the first paper names ScNi0.86Sb in its title rather than ScNiSb -- and since Ni is a host element it does not appear in dopant_roles, so the vacancy would otherwise be invisible. The F-43m entry rests on 2 ICSD references, which is below the weak threshold, but the papers name the half-Heusler structure directly.

basis: The host is a single compound written two ways, YPtSb and PtYSb, and two of the five papers name the structure in their titles -- high-temperature thermoelectric properties of the half-Heusler compound PtYSb, and transport and optical properties of the gapless Heusler compound PtYSb. The reference agrees: YSbPt F-43m (216) mp-4964 at hull 0.000.
note: YPtSb is a zero-gap half-Heusler rather than a semiconducting one, which is why one paper calls it gapless; that is a band-structure property and does not change the prototype. The curator details record deposition at 500 to 800 degC, so some samples are films, and the 2 ICSD references behind mp-4964 make it a weak primary -- but the papers state the structure, so confidence stays high. Y5SbPt2 I4/mcm mp-1207703 is offered as a second entry with no ICSD backing and no composition here matches it.

basis: The host splits cleanly by stoichiometry and the larger part is YbRh3Si7 (7 of 12 samples), the low-carrier-density Kondo lattice of the Phys. Rev. X paper, which adopts the rhombohedral ScRh3Si7 type. The rest is YbRh2Si2, the ThCr2Si2-type 122 named in the first and third papers alongside beta-YbAlB4.
note: Confidence is medium because the reference covers only the minority phase: Yb(SiRh)2 I4/mmm mp-10626 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references is YbRh2Si2, and nothing at all is offered at 1-3-7, so the space group for the majority compound comes from the structure literature and mp_id is left null. The split is clean on the Rh:Si ratio, so stage 2 can make it from composition. Both dopant roles below belong to the 122 compositions, not to the 1-3-7 one.

dopant_roles.basis: Yb0.98La0.02Rh2Si2: nonmagnetic trivalent La on the Yb site dilutes the Kondo lattice, which is how the third paper follows the thermopower across the quantum critical point.
Yb(Rh0.94Ir0.06)2Si2: Ir is isoelectronic with Rh on the transition-metal site and applies negative chemical pressure, the standard tuning axis in the YbRh2Si2 family.

basis: Ten of the twelve samples are elemental Sb, which is the A7 rhombohedral semimetal -- the reference puts Sb R-3m (166) mp-104 at hull 0.000 with 13 ICSD references, twice the next entry -- and the third paper is on BiSb alloys for magneto-thermoelectric cooling, the same structure with a little Bi.

other_polymorphs.note: TEDesignLab ranks Sb Pm-3m mp-133 second with 7 ICSD references at hull 0.049, and Im-3m and P6_3/mmc below it. These are the high-pressure phases of antimony -- the A7 structure converts above about 8 GPa -- not phases reached by heating at ambient pressure, so they must not be read as a thermal sequence.

note: is_mixed is true but the split is at the SAMPLE level, not the composition level, which is why it needs flagging rather than a stoichiometry rule: the first paper is on the thermoelectric properties of AMORPHOUS antimony, so some of the samples whose composition string is simply Sb are vapour-deposited amorphous films and the rest are crystalline A7. Composition cannot separate them; only the paper can. The second paper adds Cu2O nanoparticles, making that sample a composite, hence the second alternative.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi1Sb90 is about 1 at.% Bi in Sb; Bi and Sb are the same group and both A7, fully miscible, and the third paper is about that alloy series, so this is the dilute end of a continuum rather than doping.
(Cu2O)0.15Sn0.4Ba0.4Sb11.6 -- the second paper is titled for the effect of Cu2O nanoparticle dispersion, so the Cu is in a deliberately added oxide phase, not in the Sb lattice.
The other half of the same Cu2O nanoparticle addition.

Sn0.4 of about 12.4 atoms in the Cu2O-dispersed sample, roughly 3 at.%; Sn is one group to the left of Sb and would act as an acceptor on its site, but the composition string is unusual and the paper is about the oxide dispersion, so the site is not certain.

Ba0.4 in the same single composition. Ba is far too large and too electropositive to sit comfortably in the A7 lattice and more likely forms an antimonide second phase; recorded as substitutional only for want of better evidence.

basis: The host is thorium metal with a few per cent of Ce or U dissolved in it -- Th96Ce4, Th98Ce2, Th99.5U0.5, Th97U3 -- and the papers are on the thermoelectric power of Th-Ce alloys and on superconductivity and normal-state properties of Th-U alloys. alpha-Th is face-centred cubic and the reference confirms it, Th Fm-3m (225) mp-37 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references, so these are dilute substitutional solid solutions in a close-packed elemental metal.

other_polymorphs.note: Th Im-3m mp-11343 at hull 0.130 on one ICSD reference is body-centred cubic beta-Th, which is real but only above about 1630 K -- far above the 10-297 K window measured here, so it is not part of this thermal sequence. The prototype id is the closest available label for a bcc elemental metal and should not be read as an ordered B2 compound.

note: Two of the three papers are about the Kondo effect and superconductivity rather than thermoelectric performance, which is why the measurement stops at 297 K. Ce in Th is the textbook dilute Kondo impurity system, so the samples exist to study single-impurity physics; the prototype is simply fcc Th throughout.

dopant_roles.basis: Th96Ce4 and Th98Ce2: Ce sits substitutionally on the fcc Th site as a dilute magnetic impurity, which is precisely what the second and third papers measure through the thermoelectric power.
Th99.5U0.5, Th98U2 and Th97U3: U on the Th site, the dilute alloy series of the first paper on superconductivity in Th-U.

basis: Every composition is a sodium cobaltite with silver added -- Na0.55Ag0.45Co2O4 and Na0.6Ag0.4Co2O4 written on the Na1-xAgxCo2O4 formula unit, plus Na1.7Ag0.5Co1.5O4 -- and all three papers are about Ag-doped NaxCo2O4. The CoO2 triangular layers with sodium between them are the NaxCoO2 prototype, and the Na content written per two Co is just the other convention for the same x.
note: Ag sits above the 5 at.% cut in every composition, so it is a host element with no dopant_roles entry -- but what it does is genuinely unsettled and the composition cannot settle it. The first paper mills Ag powder into the cobaltite, which normally leaves metallic Ag at the grain boundaries as a conductive second phase, while the other two write Na1-xAgxCo2O4 as a substituted formula. Ag+ is far too large for the Na site in quantity, so at x = 0.4 to 0.45 most of it is likely metallic, which is why composite_multiphase is recorded as an alternative. Stage 2 should read the XRD from the papers before accepting a solid solution. Na1.7Ag0.5Co1.5O4 additionally has Co below 2 per formula unit, so Ag may be partly on the Co site there. No reference line is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null.

basis: Every composition is Cu1-xAgxGaTe2, and the first two papers are titled for chalcopyrite-type CuGaTe2 with Ag substitution and for substitutional defects enhancing thermoelectric CuGaTe2. Both end members, CuGaTe2 and AgGaTe2, are I-III-VI2 chalcopyrites (I-42d), so the whole series stays in one prototype with Cu and Ag sharing the group 11 cation site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: group 11 cation site of the chalcopyrite lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: Ag/(Ag+Cu) spans 0.20-0.75 with median 0.35 over 8 compositions. Both are monovalent on the same tetrahedral site and both end members are chalcopyrite, so the parent compound depends on the composition and none is recorded at host level.

note: The one reference entry offered, Ga2CuAgTe4 I-4 (82) mp-1224861 at hull 0.009, is the ordered 1:1 Cu/Ag arrangement: ordering the two cations lowers the symmetry from I-42d to I-4. That is a superstructure of chalcopyrite rather than a different prototype, but it matters for stage 2, which should not assume I-42d across the whole axis -- the third paper, on ultralow thermal conductivity in diamondoid structures, is about exactly this kind of cation arrangement. No ICSD count is shown for it, so it is computed evidence only.

dopant_roles.basis: In is the group 13 congener of Ga and takes the trivalent tetrahedral site, moving the composition toward CuInTe2; at the trace level here it is the substitutional defect engineering of the second paper.

basis: Every composition is AgxMo9Se11 with x from 3.4 to 3.9, exactly the range of the first paper, and the third is titled for cage-shaped Mo9 chalcogenides as promising thermoelectric materials. The Mo9Se11 unit is a bioctahedral cluster -- two face-sharing Mo6 octahedra -- which is a step beyond the Mo6X8 Chevrel unit the taxonomy carries, so a new prototype was proposed for it.
note: I disagree with both references here and record it rather than matching them. TEDesignLab offers Ag(MoSe)3 P6_3/m mp-1105028, which is AgMo3Se3, the infinite-chain compound; Materials Project offers Ag(Mo3Se4)2 R-3 mp-1103642, which is AgMo6Se8, the Chevrel phase. Both are genuine compounds of the Ag-Mo-Se system and neither is the 3-4-13-like 9-11 stoichiometry every sample here has, so mp_id is left null and typical_space_group in the proposal is null too. This is the condensation series Mo6 - Mo9 - infinite chain appearing three times in one chemistry, which is why the discriminate_from entries matter. Confidence is medium because the structure comes from the cluster-chemistry literature rather than from a reference line.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag3.6Cu0.2Mo9Se11 keeps the total cation count at 3.8, and the second paper is titled for the influence of Cu insertion in Ag3.8Mo9Se11: Cu takes the partially occupied channel sites between the clusters that Ag otherwise fills.

basis: Every composition is Ba8(Al,Ga)16Ge30, the type-I clathrate at its exact Zintl electron count, and the first paper is titled for high-temperature transport in p-type Ba8Ga16-based clathrates. Eight Ba guests per 46-atom group 14 framework cage network is the defining stoichiometry of this entry, and Al simply shares the framework with Ga.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: trivalent framework site of the type-I clathrate cage network
solid_solution_axis.note: Al/(Al+Ga) spans 0.16-0.50 with median 0.24 over 9 compositions. Both are trivalent framework substituents for Ge and both are counted in the 16 that balance the 8 Ba2+ guests, so the axis is on the framework and the electron count is unchanged along it.

note: Al and Ga are both host elements, so the framework substitution does not appear in dopant_roles -- but it is the whole point of the series and stage 3 should read it from the host fractions rather than looking for a dopant. The third paper is on an order-disorder transition in inorganic clathrates controlling electrical properties; that is Al/Ga site ordering within the fixed cage framework, not a change of structure type, so it is not recorded as a phase transition. No reference line is offered for this four-element host, so mp_id is left null.

basis: Every composition is (Fe1-xCox)2TiAl across x = 0.2 to 0.8, and both papers name the structure -- thermoelectric properties of Fe2TiAl Heusler alloys, and of Heusler-type (Fe1-xCox)2TiAl. X2YZ with the X site filled twice over is the L2_1 full Heusler, and Fe and Co simply share that site.
note: The reference is worth reading carefully rather than following: TiAlFeCo F-43m (216) mp-998980 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference is the ORDERED QUATERNARY Heusler, in which Fe and Co occupy the two X sublattices separately and the symmetry drops from Fm-3m to F-43m. That is the right description only at (Fe0.5Co0.5)2TiAl, one of the seven compositions here; away from 1:1 the X site cannot be ordered and the alloy is a disordered L2_1 full Heusler. So quaternary_heusler is recorded as an alternative for the equiatomic composition and stage 2 should check whether the paper reports the F-43m superstructure there. Fe and Co are both host elements and their ratio is the electron-count variable.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [216]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions are Fe2V0.75Mo0.25Al, and both papers are about the Fe2VAl pseudogap system -- thermoelectric properties of Fe2VAl and Fe2V0.75M0.25Al (M = Mo, Nb, Ti), and doping effects on the pseudogap Fe2VAl system. Fe2VAl is the textbook L2_1 full Heusler semimetal and Mo simply replaces a quarter of the V on the Y site.
note: Mo at 0.25 of 4 atoms is 6.25 at.%, just above the split, so it is a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry -- but it is physically a substituent on the V site and acts as an electron donor, which is exactly the doping study the papers describe. Three neighbouring hosts in this chunk are the same experiment with a different substituent: Al-Fe-Nb-V, Al-Fe-Si-V and this one. No reference line is offered for any of them, so mp_id is left null; stage 2 should resolve Fe2VAl Fm-3m once and reuse it.

basis: Both compositions are Fe2V1-xNbxAl at x = 0.2 to 0.25, and the first paper is titled for the effect of Nb substitution for V on the thermoelectric properties of Fe2VAl. The L2_1 Heusler framework is unchanged; Nb is the heavier group 5 congener of V and takes its site, adding mass contrast without changing the electron count.
note: Nb at 0.2 to 0.25 of 4 atoms is 5 to 6 at.%, at or just above the split, so it appears as a host element with no dopant_roles entry even though it is a dilute isoelectronic substituent on the V site -- an example of the threshold landing inside what is physically one series, since the same experiment with Mo is the separate Al-Fe-Mo-V host. No reference line is offered, so mp_id is left null.

basis: Every composition is Fe2VAl1-xSix, and the first paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of quaternary Heusler alloys Fe2VAl1-xSix, the third for a high power factor near room temperature in full-Heusler alloys. Si substitutes for Al on the Z site of the L2_1 lattice and donates one electron per substitution, which is the n-type branch of the Fe2VAl family.
note: Si runs from 0.2 to 0.5 of the Z site, far above the 5 at.% split, so it is a host element and the substitution is recorded through the host fractions rather than in dopant_roles. At Fe2VAl0.5Si0.5 the Al and Si could in principle order on the Z sublattice, which would make it a genuine quaternary Heusler; the first paper calls the series quaternary for that reason, but no composition here is at a simple ordering ratio other than 1:1. Fe2.2V0.8Al0.6Si0.4 additionally moves Fe onto the V site, which is a second, independent off-stoichiometry axis. No reference line is offered, so mp_id is left null.

basis: Every composition is Al73Ir27 give or take a per cent, several carry an explicit IAC suffix in the composition string, and the second paper is titled for band engineering in Al-TM (TM = Rh, Ir) quasicrystalline approximants. The Al-rich Al-transition-metal complex metallic alloys with a pseudogap at the Fermi level are what this entry covers.
note: Confidence is medium because the reference and the composition do not meet. None of the three MP entries offered matches Al73Ir27: Al3Ir P6_3/mmc mp-2294 is 75 at.% Al, Al9Ir2 P2_1/c mp-12003 is 81.8 at.%, and AlIr Pm-3m mp-1885 is 50 at.%, so the samples sit between the first two and are slightly Ir-rich of Al3Ir. The first paper is titled for vacancy control in Al-Ir, which fits a structure carrying constitutional vacancies in that composition window. So the assignment rests on the approximant paper and the IAC labels rather than on a structure match, and stage 2 should identify which Al-Ir phase these actually are before taking any mp_id -- mp_id is left null here. If they turn out to be a small-cell Al3Ir-derived phase rather than a large-cell approximant, this host should move, the way Al-Fe-Si did in chunk 11.

dopant_roles.basis: Al72.3CuIr26.7 and Al71.3Cu2Ir26.7 hold Ir fixed at 26.7 while Al falls by exactly the Cu added, so Cu takes Al sites. The third paper is titled for the anomalous effects of Cu doping on the structural and thermoelectric properties of this system, so the effect on the structure is itself the finding.

basis: Y3Al5O12 is 6 of the 11 samples outright and is a component of three more, the curator records commercially available Ce-doped YAG, and the first two papers are on yttrium aluminium garnet thermal barrier coatings. The reference agrees: Y3Al5O12 Ia-3d (230) mp-3050 at hull 0.000 with 15 ICSD references.
note: Mixed because five of the eleven samples are not single-phase YAG. (Y3Al5O12)14.66(Al2O3)85.34 is 85 mol% alumina -- an alumina matrix with a garnet minority, which the curator confirms as Ce-doped YAG plus alpha-Al2O3 -- and the two (Y2O3)x(Al2O3)y compositions at 58:41 and 30:68 straddle the YAG and YAlO3 lines and will be multiphase coatings. The split is clean on the Y:Al ratio, so stage 2 can make it from composition. Note that TEDesignLab covers only YAlO3 Pnma mp-3792 (17 ICSD references), the perovskite YAP, not the garnet -- the two references cover different compounds of the same chemistry here, and the MP one is the relevant one. A pure YAlO3 composition would be a third prototype, but none appears in the list shown.

dopant_roles.basis: The curator names Ce-doped YAG directly, and the compositions write (CeO2)0.5 alongside the Y2O3-Al2O3 mixture. Ce3+ takes the eight-coordinate Y dodecahedral site, which is the standard YAG:Ce phosphor substitution.

basis: The single composition Cs2Mo3As3 is the A2Mo3X3 stoichiometry, and its paper is titled for the synthesis and superconductivity of a novel quasi-one-dimensional ternary compound. That family is built from Mo6 octahedra condensed by shared faces into infinite [Mo3As3] columns separated by the alkali, which is the Tl2Mo3Se3 type and has no existing taxonomy entry.
note: No reference line at all is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null and the P6_3/m cell comes from the A2Mo3X3 literature. It is corroborated sideways within this same chunk: TEDesignLab gives the isostructural AgMo3Se3 at P6_3/m mp-1105028 in the Ag-Mo-Se host. The measured range is 10-13 K for the 5th-95th percentile of 12 curves, with the full span reaching 283 K, so most of these curves are superconducting-transition measurements rather than thermoelectric characterisation -- worth knowing before the transport data is used.

basis: The single composition YbNi2B2C is the 1221 borocarbide itself, and the reference confirms the structure: YbNi2B2C I4/mmm (139) mp-6286 at hull 0.000. That is the ThCr2Si2-derived stack in which a C layer is inserted into the rare-earth plane, which is exactly what this entry names.
note: All 11 samples are single crystals of one composition, differing only in annealing (unannealed, or 950 degC for 20 to 150 hours) -- the paper is about drastic annealing effects on transport. So the variable here is defect concentration, not chemistry, and nothing in the composition distinguishes the samples. The mp entry rests on 2 ICSD references, which is technically weak, but YbNi2B2C is a well-known heavy-fermion superconductor and the structure type is not in doubt.

basis: SrB6 is 8 of the 11 samples and the rest are (Sr,Ba)B6 and (Ca,Sr)B6, and the papers are titled for the thermoelectric properties of alkaline-earth hexaborides and of metal hexaborides. The reference agrees: SrB6 Pm-3m (221) mp-242 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references -- the cubic CaB6 framework of B6 octahedra with the divalent cation in the cage.
note: Ca0.25B1.5Sr0.75B4.5 is a parse artifact: boron appears twice and sums to 6, so it is the same compound as Ca0.25Sr0.75B6 written with the B distributed over two terms. Stage 3 should not read it as two boron species. One film sample is present and the chunk file flags that a metastable polymorph could be reachable; SrB2 P6/mmm mp-1008755 at hull 0.533 is the only alternative offered and that hull value rules it out as anything but a computed structure, so no other polymorph is recorded. The second paper works at high pressure to densify solid solutions, which is a processing route rather than a phase change.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.25Sr0.75B6: CaB6 and SrB6 are the same structure, so Ca on the cage site is the smaller-cation end of an isostructural solid solution -- the alkaline-earth hexaboride series the papers scan.
Sr0.75Ba0.25B6, the larger-cation end of the same series; BaB6 is also cubic Pm-3m.

basis: GdBa2Cu3O7 is 10 of the 11 samples, and the papers are on the normal-state transport of RBa2Cu3O7-x and on ABa2Cu3O7-y with A = Y and Gd -- the Gd member of the YBCO 123 family, with the same ordered Y/Ba layer sequence and CuO chains. The reference confirms it: Ba2GdCu3O7 Pmmm (47) mp-19813 with 3 ICSD references.
note: Gd sits on the Y site of the 123 structure, so this is the same prototype and not a separate one. Two points for later stages: the oxygen content written as 7 here is really 7-delta and is the doping variable of this family, which the entry already records; and (GdBa2Cu3O7)0.8(Gd2O3)0.2 carries 20 mol% Gd2O3, a deliberate second-phase addition (the flux-pinning route), so that one composition is a composite. The measured window is 77-300 K, i.e. normal-state transport above the superconducting transition. The Pmmm entry is the orthorhombic ordered-oxygen cell, which is correct for the fully oxygenated composition.

basis: BaIrO3 is 9 of the 11 samples. The Ba2+ cation is far too large for a corner-sharing ABO3 perovskite network, so the AO3 layers close-pack hexagonally and the IrO6 octahedra condense into face-sharing Ir3O12 trimers -- the 9R polytype. The first paper measures a transition from a weak ferromagnetic insulator, which is the known behaviour of that phase.
note: I disagree with the reference and record it rather than following it. Materials Project ranks BaIrO3 Pm-3m (221) mp-5660 PRIMARY at hull 0.141 on 3 ICSD references, which is the cubic aristotype -- a cell BaIrO3 does not adopt at ambient conditions, the same failure mode the README describes for cubic ReO3 standing in for monoclinic WO3. mp_id is left null rather than taken from it. The host is mixed and splits cleanly on the Ba:Ir ratio: Ba2IrO4 (1 sample) is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper phase, and the reference does offer Ba2IrO4 I4/mmm mp-755117 for it. Ba2Ir3O9 (1 sample) is a third structure -- its own paper calls it a new 5d mixed-valence metallic oxide with the KSbO3-type structure -- which has no taxonomy entry, so it is parked under unresolved_crystalline rather than mislabelled; one sample is too thin to propose on. Confidence is medium because which hexagonal polytype forms depends on synthesis and must come from the paper.

basis: Every composition is Ba8NixSi46-x with x near 3, and the first paper is titled for the crystal structure and thermoelectric properties of the clathrate Ba8Ni3.5Si42. Eight Ba guests per 46-atom silicon cage framework is the type-I clathrate stoichiometry exactly, with Ni substituting on the framework.
note: The reference offers Ba8Si43Ni3 R32 (155) mp-1228480 at hull 0.003, which is a rhombohedral ordering of the type-I cage framework rather than a different structure type -- the ideal clathrate I cell is cubic Pm-3n, and lowering the symmetry is how a particular Ni arrangement on the framework is described. It carries no ICSD reference, so stage 2 should resolve the cubic parent and treat R32 as a possible superstructure. Ni is a host element (3.5 of 53 atoms is 6.6 at.%) so the framework substitution does not appear in dopant_roles; the Ni content is the electron-count variable and the compositions deliberately scan both it and the total atom count.

dopant_roles.basis: Pt is the heavier group 10 congener of Ni and takes the same framework site in the silicon cage network; like Ni it removes electrons from the framework, which is how the Zintl count is balanced against the Ba guests.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [63]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: BiCuOTe, written both ways round in the compositions, is the tellurium member of the BiCuChO family and adopts the same ZrCuSiAs 1111 structure as BiCuSeO -- alternating insulating Bi2O2 layers and conducting Cu2Te2 layers. The taxonomy entry is built on BiCuSeO and already names the Bi-Cu-O-Se host; the third paper is titled for improved thermoelectric performance of BiCuTeO.
note: The one reference entry offered, CuBi2Te2O P4/mmm mp-1213110 at hull 0.546, is a computed cell at a different stoichiometry and half an eV above the hull, so it is not evidence for anything; mp_id is left null and stage 2 should resolve BiCuOTe itself. Note for the solid-solution machinery that O and Te are both group 16 but never share a site here -- oxygen sits in the Bi2O2 layer and tellurium in the Cu2Te2 layer -- which is the BiCuSeO case the README uses as its example of why same-group pairs need a CHECK.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi1-xPbxCuOTe at x = 0.01 to 0.06, and the curator writes the series that way: divalent Pb on the trivalent Bi site of the oxide layer is the standard acceptor for this family, and the first paper is about the point-defect-assisted doping mechanism behind it.

basis: Every composition is K2Bi8Se13-xSx, and the first paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of hot-pressed beta-K2Bi8Se13-xSx. K2Bi8Se13 is the compound this entry is built on -- a large low-symmetry cell of Bi2Te3-like and NaCl-like blocks linked by Bi2Se3 rods with K in the tunnels -- and the sulfur simply substitutes on the chalcogen sublattice.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: chalcogen sublattice of the K2Bi8X13 framework
solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se) spans 0.31-0.62 with median 0.46 over 7 compositions, and the anion count stays at 13 throughout (Se7S6, Se9S4, Se5S8). Both are group 16 and both sit on chalcogen sites of the same framework, so the axis is genuine -- but the framework has several inequivalent chalcogen sites and sulfur is likely to prefer some of them, which stage 2 should check rather than assume random mixing.

note: The paper specifies the beta polymorph, which matters: K2Bi8Se13 has alpha and beta forms with different cell symmetries, so the prototype is a family label here and the polymorph must be taken from the paper. No reference line at all is offered for this four-element host, so mp_id is left null. K2Bi8Se7S6.002 and K2Bi8Se7S6.01 differ from K2Bi8Se7S6 in the third decimal place and are transcription variants of the same composition rather than a real series.

basis: Every composition is the Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 alloy with an oxide deliberately added -- Sb2O3 at 6 to 13 mol%, Ta2O5, Nd2O3, RuO2, ZrO2 and a dehydrated attapulgite clay -- and the paper titles say so directly (Bi-Sb-Te/Sb2O3 nanocomposites, the influence of RuO2 addition, dehydrated-attapulgite nanoinclusions). The curator confirms 4 wt% ZrO2 and 1.5 wt% D-ATP. None of these oxides dissolves in the tetradymite lattice, so the samples are a matrix plus dispersed oxide inclusions.
note: The same pattern as the Bi-C-Sb-Te host at rank 551 and Bi-C-Te in chunk 8, with an oxide instead of carbon. The matrix is recorded as the alternative so stage 2 resolves the Bi-Sb-Te structure. Oxygen is above the 5 at.% cut in these compositions and so appears as a host element rather than in dopant_roles, which is the right outcome here for once: it really is a separate oxide phase. The one reference entry offered for this host is a computed CuBi-free oxide cell of no relevance, so mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: (BiSbTe)87.89(RuO2)12.11 -- RuO2 is the added second phase of the second paper, a rutile oxide dispersed in the alloy.
(Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3)94.06(Ta2O5)5.94: an added oxide, written as a mole fraction of the oxide rather than as a substitution.
(Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3)88.72(Nd2O3)11.28: the same, an added rare-earth oxide.
The curator records BiSbTe alloy powder plus 4 wt% ZrO2, so the zirconium is in a dispersed oxide.

(Mg1.25Al0.75Si4O11H)0.03Bi0.42Sb1.58Te3 is attapulgite clay, a magnesium aluminium silicate, added as nanoinclusions in the first paper; all four of its elements are in that mineral phase, not in the tetradymite.
Part of the same attapulgite clay addition.
Part of the same attapulgite clay addition.
Structural hydroxyl left in the dehydrated attapulgite; not in the alloy in any form.
Most likely yttria-stabilised zirconia rather than a separate addition, given the ZrO2 sample the curator records; the composition carrying it is not printed here.

basis: TiC and its carbon-deficient forms TiC0.96, TiC0.93 and TiC0.88 are 8 of the 11 samples and are rocksalt with vacancies on the carbon sublattice, which MP backs at Fm-3m 225 mp-631, hull 0.000, 37 ICSD references. But C84Ti16 and C91.5Ti8.5 come from a doped-graphite paper and are carbon hosts carrying a little titanium, not carbides, so one label cannot cover the host.

other_polymorphs.note: Ti3C2 P6_3/mmc at hull 0.061 is the MXene sheet, a solution-processed 2D phase, not something the bulk TiC or the graphite samples here pass through.

basis: Every composition is Ca5In2Sb6 or a Zn- or Al-substituted form of it, and ref 1 gives Ca5(InSb3)2 at Pbam 55 mp-649479 on the hull -- the Ca5Al2Sb6 5-2-6 Zintl structure of corner-sharing InSb4 tetrahedral chains charge-balanced by Ca. The third paper title names the Zintl phase outright.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca5In1-xZnxSb6 across x = 0.02 to 0.2: Zn2+ for In3+ on the tetrahedral framework site is an acceptor and is the carrier-concentration knob of the two Zn-doping papers.

Ca5Al0.2In1.7Zn0.1Sb6 sits on the Ca5Al2-xInxSb6 solid-solution line named in the second paper title; Al and In are both group 13 on the same framework site, so this tunes the lattice rather than the carrier count.

basis: CdFe2O4 is the parent of 4 samples and every curator formula the chunk prints -- Li0.5-x/2CdxFe2.5-x/2O4, Cd1-xNixFe2O4, Mn1-xCdxFe2O4 -- is a spinel ferrite series; MP gives Cd(FeO2)2 Fd-3m 227 mp-24940 on the hull as primary, which is the spinel cell.

other_polymorphs.note: CdFeO3 Pnma at hull 0.078 is a different stoichiometry from anything measured here and carries no ICSD reference.

dopant_roles.basis: The curator formula Li0.5-x/2CdxFe2.5-x/2O4 is the lithium-cadmium ferrite line, where Li+ and extra Fe3+ jointly replace Cd2+ on the spinel cation sites; the lithium ordering on the octahedral site is what the second paper measures.
CdFe1.9Gd0.1O4: a large rare earth on the octahedral B site, which is the substitution the first paper title names.
Cd1-xNixFe2O4 from the curator: Ni2+ for Cd2+, and Ni has a strong octahedral site preference so it also redistributes the inversion.
Mn1-xCdxFe2O4 from the curator: the Mn-Cd ferrite solid solution.
The first paper is on Cu-Cd ferrites, so the copper is a second divalent A-site cation rather than an impurity.

basis: Ce3Cu3Sb4 is 8 of the 11 samples and is the cubic Y3Au3Sb4 type, a Th3P4-derived Kondo semiconductor, which MP confirms at I-43d 220 mp-1189165 on the hull. Ce5CuSb3 is a genuinely different structure -- the Cu-filled Mn5Si3 D88 type -- and has its own heavy-fermion paper, so the host holds two. Note the MP primary by ICSD count is CeCuSb2 P4/nmm, a formula no sample here matches.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce3Cu2.75Ni0.25Sb4: Ni on the Cu site of the 3-3-4 framework, which shifts the narrow gap that the first paper revisits.

basis: Ce(NixPd1-x)2Si2 at x from 0.2 to 0.7 is 8 of the 11 samples, and CeNi2Si2 and CePd2Si2 are both body-centred tetragonal ThCr2Si2, so the seed holds for the bulk of the host. The two Ce2(Ni,Pd)3Si compositions are a 2-3-1 stoichiometry that the 122 does not cover and that neither reference reaches, which is why this is medium and flagged mixed.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the transition-metal (Cr) site of the ThCr2Si2 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Ni and Pd are both group 10 and share the same site, so this is a clean isoelectronic series; what it tunes is the cell volume and hence the Kondo coupling, which is exactly what the heavy-fermion papers scan. No single parent compound is recorded at host level.

basis: CeSb is 9 of the 11 samples and MP gives Fm-3m 225 mp-387 on the hull with 15 ICSD references, the rocksalt rare-earth monopnictide. Ce4Sb3 is the anti-Th3P4 cubic phase at I-43d mp-20680, which the first paper names in its title, so the host holds both a rocksalt and a Th3P4 compound.

SmCoO3 and its Sr-, Ca- and Ni-substituted forms are every composition. MP makes the orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted Pnma 62 mp-24877 the primary on the hull, while the cubic aristotype Pm-3m mp-24865 sits 0.151 eV above it, so this is a tilted perovskite rather than the ideal cubic one -- which matters because the small Sm3+ radius is the variable the second paper scans.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm1-xSrxCoO3 at x = 0.1 and 0.2: Sr2+ on the A site is an acceptor that drives Co3+ toward Co4+ and is the main hole-doping route in these cobaltites.
Sm0.9Ca0.1CoO3: the same A-site acceptor with a smaller cation, so it also increases the octahedral tilt.
SmCo0.95Ni0.05O3, the Ln(Co,Ni)O3 series of the first paper title: Ni on the B site.

basis: Every composition is Sr2CoTiO6 or a La- or Ba-substituted form, an A2BBO6 arrangement with Co and Ti alternating on the B site; the first paper title is for the double perovskite outright and the third is a structure and transport study of SrTi1-xCoxO3. No reference line is offered, so the degree of B-site order is not corroborated here.

dopant_roles.basis: BaxSr2-xTiCoO6 at x = 0.1 and 0.15, the BaxSr series of the second paper title: Ba2+ for Sr2+ on the A site adds no carriers and works by enlarging the cell.
Sr2-xLaxCoTiO6 at x = 0.2 and 0.4: La3+ for Sr2+ is a donor on the A site.

basis: Both compositions are Ti0.7V0.3CoSb0.7Sn0.3 with or without Fe on the Co site, which is TiCoSb at the 1-1-1 MgAgAs stoichiometry with V on the Ti site and Sn on the Sb site; the first paper title is the Ti1-xVx half-Heusler series. The second paper reports full-Heusler TiCo2Sb segregating as a second phase, so that prototype is listed as an alternative even though no composition here is written at the 1-2-1 stoichiometry.

dopant_roles.basis: Ti0.7V0.3Co0.85Fe0.15Sb0.7Sn0.3: Fe on the Co site of the half-Heusler removes one valence electron, compounding the p-type Sn-for-Sb substitution. It falls under 5 at.% of the whole formula but is 15 percent of its own sublattice.

basis: CuxMo6Se8 at x = 1, 2 and 4 is 9 of the 11 samples: the Mo6Se8 octahedral cluster framework with copper in the channel sites between clusters. MP gives Cu(Mo3Se4)2 R-3 148 mp-1104894, which is that compound written per two formula units. The first paper title is for AgxMo9Se11, a different chemistry that does not belong to this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu1.38Fe0.66Mo6Se8: iron takes channel cation sites alongside copper rather than entering the Mo6Se8 cluster, so it changes the electron count donated to the cluster framework.

basis: YbCu2Si2 is 7 of the 11 samples and MP gives Yb(CuSi)2 at I4/mmm 139 mp-5934 on the hull with 3 ICSD references, so the seed holds for the dominant compound. The three Yb(CuxSi1-x)~1.88 compositions are Si-rich at Cu/Si near 0.15 and total only about 1.88 main-group atoms per Yb, which is an AlB2-type Yb(Cu,Si)2 rather than a 122 -- hence mixed and medium. The first paper listed, on rare-earth doped SrTiO3, is not about this chemistry at all.

Five of the six printed compositions are (Sn0.95Cd0.05Te)0.93(Cu2Te)0.07 or (SnTe)0.94(Cu2Te)0.06, which is rocksalt SnTe with Cu2Te added -- the first paper title attributes the transport to interstitial copper point defects, so the copper is in the SnTe lattice rather than forming a separate structure. Cu5Sn2Te7 is the exception: its own paper calls it a sphalerite superstructure, and MP gives C2 (5) mp-1103821 for it. Cu2SnTe3, which MP ranks first for this chemistry, matches no composition measured here.

other_polymorphs.note: Cu2SnTe3 Imm2 is the MP primary for the chemistry but no sample here is written at that stoichiometry; it may be the second phase the eutectoid-precipitate paper reports, which is worth checking against that paper.

dopant_roles.basis: Sn0.95Cd0.05Te: Cd2+ for Sn2+ on the cation site of rocksalt SnTe, the standard band-convergence substitution rather than a carrier dopant.
Iodine at 0.0025 to 0.015 per formula unit on the anion site is a donor, used here to compensate the intrinsic Sn-vacancy holes.

basis: MgFe2O4 is 6 of the 11 samples and the Li- and Sm-substituted formulas are the same magnesioferrite spinel; the third paper title names spark-plasma-sintered spinel directly. The reference disagrees and should not be followed: the MP primary here is Mg(FeO2)2 Pbcm 57 mp-630714 at hull 0.101 with a single ICSD reference, and no Fd-3m entry appears at all, which is a gap in the 2019 snapshot rather than evidence against the cubic spinel.

dopant_roles.basis: Li0.15Mg0.7Fe2.15O4 and its siblings follow the Li0.5-x/2MgxFe2.5-x/2O4 lithium-ferrite line, where Li+ plus extra Fe3+ replace Mg2+; the second paper is titled for magnesium-substituted lithium ferrites.
MgSm0.1Fe1.9O4: a large rare earth confined to the octahedral B site, which distorts the lattice and pins grain growth.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [57, 91]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Ref 1 ranks Ga2O3 C2/m 12 mp-886 first on the hull with 5 ICSD references, the curator records Ti3+:beta-Ga2O3 and a beta-(Al0.1Ga0.9)2O3/Ga2O3 superlattice, and both of those papers plus the Si- and Sn-doped samples are monoclinic gallia. The taxonomy had no entry for it, so beta_ga2o3 is proposed. The one exception is the Sn-doped alpha-Ga2O3 thin film of the third paper: alpha is the corundum polymorph, reachable only on a sapphire substrate, so the host is mixed.

other_polymorphs.note: alpha-Ga2O3 at hull 0.029 with 4 ICSD references. It is grown epitaxially on sapphire, as in the Sn-doped alpha-Ga2O3 thin-film paper here, and is not produced by heating bulk beta-Ga2O3 -- heating converts alpha to beta, not the reverse.
Ga2O3 Cmcm at hull 0.285 with one ICSD reference; a high-pressure form, far outside anything measured in this 14-451 K window.

dopant_roles.basis: Sn0.0002 to Sn0.01 per Ga2O3: Sn4+ on the octahedral Ga3+ site is the standard shallow donor for gallia and is the doping route of the third paper.
Si4+ on the tetrahedral Ga3+ site, the other common n-type donor; it appears in 5 compositions.
The curator gives Ti3+:beta-Ga2O3 at 0.182 at.%, so titanium is isovalent with Ga3+ here and is an optically active laser centre rather than a carrier dopant.
beta-(Al0.1Ga0.9)2O3 in the superlattice paper: Al3+ for Ga3+ widens the gap and is what reduces the thermal conductivity, with no change in carrier count.

basis: Ge1-xSnxTe across x = 0.2 to 0.9 is the whole host and the seed is right for the Ge-rich end: GeTe is rhombohedral R3m and converts to rocksalt Fm-3m near 700 K, which the 49-809 K window crosses. But the transition temperature falls steeply with Sn content -- SnTe itself is cubic at room temperature -- so Ge0.1Sn0.9Te and Ge0.2Sn0.8Te are already rocksalt across most of their measured range. The host is therefore mixed on composition as well as spanning a transition, and the 700 K value cannot stand for the whole series.

dopant_roles.basis: The curator records 5 mol% Bi2Te3 added to Sn0.2Ge0.8Te; bismuth enters the cation site as a donor rather than staying as a separate tetradymite phase, which is the usual outcome for small Bi2Te3 additions to GeTe.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge and Sn are both group 14 on the rocksalt cation site, so the substitution is isoelectronic; what it moves is the rhombohedral distortion, and with it the transition temperature itself. The transition temperature recorded in phases applies to the Ge-rich end only.

basis: LiH is the only composition and MP gives Fm-3m 225 mp-23703 on the hull with 20 ICSD references. It is a saline hydride -- H- as an anion on the rocksalt anion site -- not an interstitial_hydride, where hydrogen sits in the voids of a metal lattice. Both papers measure it as a light-atom model crystal for phonon thermal conductivity rather than as a thermoelectric.

Ni50Mn34In16 and Ni50Mn35In15 are 6 of the 11 samples and are off-stoichiometric Ni2MnIn L21 full Heusler with the excess Mn on the In site, which MP backs at Fm-3m 225 mp-22731 with 6 ICSD references. Two reservations keep this at medium. The four In46(Ni,Mn)54 samples come from the liquid-indium-alloy paper and are indium-rich melts, not a Heusler phase. And Mn-rich Ni-Mn-In of exactly this composition undergoes a martensitic transformation on cooling inside the measured 13-1433 K window; the chunk file prints no transition line and the martensite structure is not pinned here, so it is left for review rather than guessed into phases.

All four compositions are La1-xNaxMnO3 at x = 0.25 to 0.4, a monovalent-A-site-doped lanthanum manganite, and the paper titles say Na-doped lanthanum manganites directly. Sodium is 6 to 8 at.% of the formula so it lands above the host cut and is a host element here rather than a dopant. The reference does not help: MP offers only NaLa2Mn3O9 P-3m1 mp-1220767 at hull 0.042 with no ICSD backing, which is a computed ordered variant, not the A-site-disordered perovskite these papers sinter.

(LaS)1.14NbS2 and its La-content variants are every composition, and the curator states the subsystem split outright -- the NbS2 slab as subsystem 1 and the La2S2 block as subsystem 2 -- which is the definition of an incommensurate misfit composite. All three paper titles say misfit layered. MP reaches only La8Nb7S22 Ccc2 mp-28507, a commensurate ternary, because a two-subsystem composite has no single MP entry; that is expected for this prototype, not a disagreement.

The single composition is N2O measured from 10 to 139 K by two cryocrystal papers, one of them titled for solid nitrous oxide. Solid N2O is isostructural with dry ice -- cubic Pa-3, four linear molecules per cell, head-to-tail orientationally disordered -- and the taxonomy had no molecular-cryocrystal entry, so one is proposed. The reference is of no use here: every MP entry printed for the N-O chemistry is an NOx oxide at large positive hull and none of them is N2O.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [205], ICSD-backed references for this host report [14, 15, 19, 59]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every composition is Nb3SbxTe7-x with x from 1 to 6, the series of the two papers, centred on Nb3Sb2Te5. Neither reference covers the chemistry at all -- no TEDesignLab entry and no MP line is printed -- and I could not identify the structure type with enough confidence to name a prototype, so it is parked here rather than forced into a layered-dichalcogenide or chain entry it may not belong to. It is a single well-defined ternary line, not a composite or a glass, and deserves a taxonomy entry once the structure is read out of the 2006 paper.

Both papers are titled for a lead vanadate glass system, the compositions are written as oxide mole fractions -- (PbO)50(V2O5)50, (ZnO)x(PbO)y(V2O5)50, (Ag2O)5(PbO)45(V2O5)50 -- and the transport reported is small-polaron hopping between V4+ and V5+ in a glass network, so there is no crystalline prototype to assign. The MP list of crystalline lead vanadates is not relevant to these samples.

dopant_roles.basis: (ZnO)x(PbO)0.5-x(V2O5)0.5 at x = 0.05 to 0.15: ZnO substitutes for PbO as a network modifier at a mole fraction far above a doping level, which is what the first paper scans.
The second paper is on CdO- and Ag2O-substituted lead vanadate, so cadmium is a modifier oxide on the same footing as the zinc.
(Ag2O)5(PbO)45(V2O5)50: 5 mol% Ag2O as a modifier oxide; silver also adds ionic conduction in these glasses.

basis: Sr0.22Rh2O4 rewrites as Sr0.88Rh8O16 and Ba1.2Rh8O16 is already in AxM8O16 form, so all five compositions are the hollandite tunnel framework -- double chains of edge-sharing RhO6 corner-linked into square tunnels with the alkaline earth inside. The third paper calls SrxRh2O4 a doped band insulator, and the Sr content from 0.11 to 0.22 is that band-filling variable. MP reaches only the binaries Rh2O3 and RhO2 and does not cover the ternary tunnel phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Strontium occupies the hollandite tunnel, not a framework site. Its content from 0.11 to 0.22 per Rh2O4 is the electron count donated to the Rh4+ band and is the whole experimental variable of the third paper, so it is a compositional knob rather than an impurity. It falls under the 5 at.% cut only because the Rh8O16 framework is so large.
Ba1.2Rh8O16: the same tunnel site with a larger cation, which is the classic hollandite composition.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [87], ICSD-backed references for this host report [60, 62, 136, 61]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: RhSb3 and Rh4Sb12 are the same compound written per one and per four formula units and account for 5 of the 11 samples; the other 6 are InxRh4Sb12 from the indium-filled skutterudite paper. So the host holds both the binary CoAs3-type framework and its filled form, as Co-Sb does. MP ranks Sb2Rh and SbRh above it by ICSD count, but Sb3Rh Im-3 204 mp-2395 is the only entry matching any composition measured here -- the reference is describing the whole Rh-Sb phase diagram, not these samples.

dopant_roles.basis: InxRh4Sb12 at x = 0.05 to 0.2: indium is a guest in the icosahedral void of the Sb12 cage, rattling to suppress lattice thermal conductivity, not a substituent on Rh or Sb. The paper title says indium-filled outright.

basis: RuSb2 is 6 of the 11 samples and the rest are Fe-, Co- or Cr-substituted RuSb2. MP gives Sb2Ru at Pnnm 58 mp-20928 on the hull with 6 ICSD references, which is the marcasite cell, and two of the three papers compare the compound directly with FeSb2, the marcasite Kondo insulator whose colossal thermopower they are chasing.

other_polymorphs.note: SbRu Pnma at hull 0.051 is a different stoichiometry in the same binary, not a polymorph of RuSb2; listed only so it is not mistaken for one.

dopant_roles.basis: Ru1-xFexSb2 at x = 0.01 to 0.15: iron on the Ru site of the marcasite, which is an isostructural interpolation toward FeSb2 and tunes the hybridisation gap. At x = 0.15 this is closer to alloying than to dilute doping.
Co0.1Ru0.9Sb2: cobalt on the metal site adds an electron relative to Ru, an n-type substitution. It is 10 percent of its own sublattice but under 5 at.% of the whole formula.
Cr0.1Ru0.9Sb2: the same metal site on the hole-doping side.

basis: The single composition is written Zn6Sc_IAC_1_1 and the curator gives the nominal Zn85.5Sc14.5; the one paper is titled for a phase transition in the Zn6Sc 1/1 cubic approximant. That is a Tsai-type approximant -- a periodic Im-3 packing of the same icosahedral clusters that build the i-ZnSc quasicrystal -- so this is the one case where the prototype names a genuinely periodic structure. MP lists only simple ScZn binaries and does not reach the 1/1 cell.

ZnTe is 10 of the 11 samples and ref 1 makes F-43m 216 mp-2176 the primary with 27 ICSD references on the hull; zincblende is the ambient phase and the others are far behind it. Note the epitaxial films present here: wurtzite ZnTe is reachable on a suitable substrate but is not produced by heating bulk zincblende, so it is recorded as a polymorph and not as a phase.

other_polymorphs.note: One ICSD reference against 27 for zincblende, hull 0.006. Five of these samples are epitaxial films and four are nanowires, so the hexagonal stacking is plausible in those, but heating bulk ZnTe does not produce it.
Hull 0.288; the high-pressure phase of ZnTe, well outside the ambient-pressure 11-601 K window measured here.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn0.95Al0.05Te: Al3+ on the Zn2+ site is a donor. It sits right at the host cut, so it is nearer a dilute alloy end member than a trace dopant.

basis: ZrTe5 is 8 of the 11 samples, all single crystals, and MP gives Cmcm 63 mp-605 on the hull with 6 ICSD references -- the layered trigonal-prismatic ZrTe3 chains linked by zigzag Te into van der Waals sheets. The second paper measures ZrTe5 and HfTe5 side by side, which are the two members of the prototype, and the third names the transition-metal pentatellurides directly.

dopant_roles.basis: ZrTe4.75Se0.25: selenium for tellurium on the chalcogen sublattice, same group, so it compresses the lattice and shifts the resistivity peak without changing the carrier count.
Zr0.9Ti0.1Te5, the substitution the first paper title names. Ti and Zr are both group 4 and isovalent, so the effect is through the cell size and the band overlap rather than through doping.

basis: Every composition is AuxAlyGd14 at a fixed 14 at.% rare earth, and the first paper is titled for Tsai-type Au-Al-RE quasicrystals while the second probes the pseudogap in Au-Al-Gd. These are icosahedral quasicrystals rather than periodic approximants, so the prototype is used as its own notes direct -- there is no periodic structure and stage 2 must map to an approximant and say so. MP offers only GdAl7Au3 R-3c mp-22711, an ordinary crystalline ternary, which is not the icosahedral phase.

The curator writes two of the compositions as (ZrC)2Al3C2 and (ZrC)3Al3C2, which are Zr2Al3C4 and Zr3Al3C5 -- the (ZrC)nAl3C2 homologous series of rocksalt ZrC slabs interleaved with Al3C2 blocks -- and all the rest are those two with Si on the Al site. Both synthesis papers are titled for a new layered ternary carbide, and the third measures the isostructural YAl3C3. The taxonomy had no entry, so one is proposed. MP offers Zr2AlC P6_3/mmc mp-3886, which is the 211 MAX phase, a different compound; its Zr2Al3C4 entry is P-3m1 at hull 0.225 with no ICSD backing, so the space group needs confirming in stage 2.

dopant_roles.basis: Zr2Al3.56Si0.44C5 and the curator note 90.7 mol% (ZrC)3[Al3.56Si0.44]C3: silicon shares the Al site inside the Al3C2 block, which the bracket in the curator formula makes explicit. The same curator note records 9.3 mol% free ZrC alongside it, so a rocksalt second phase is present in that sample.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [194, 193]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions are Ce1-xLaxCu4Al at x = 0.4 and 0.6, the RCu4Al line, which is the hexagonal CaCu5 structure with Al ordering preferentially onto one of the two copper sites. Both papers scan the Ce/La dilution, so La at 40 to 60 percent of the rare-earth site is a host constituent, not a dopant. Medium rather than high because no reference line is offered for this host, so the cell is uncorroborated, and because the degree of Al/Cu order distinguishes plain cacu5 from the ordered PrNi2Al3-type variant that is also in the proposed taxonomy.

Al65Cu20Co15 is the classic decagonal quasicrystal and every composition here is that alloy with Si or Fe substituted; one composition string is labelled DQC outright, the third paper is titled for a decagonal phase and the first reports a new stable icosahedral quasicrystal in Al-Cu-Co-Fe. So these are aperiodic and the prototype is used as its notes direct. MP offers only ordinary crystalline ternaries such as Al12Co4Cu C2/m mp-17017, which are not the decagonal phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Al62Si3Cu20Co15: silicon takes aluminium positions and is used to stabilise the decagonal phase, adjusting the electron-per-atom ratio that sets the pseudogap.
Al65Cu20Co15-xFex in the second paper title: iron on the cobalt site, and at higher Fe the first paper reports the structure switching from decagonal to icosahedral.

basis: Every composition is LaFe1-xRuxAsO0.89F0.11, the F-doped 1111 iron pnictide of the single paper, which is the ZrCuSiAs type -- P4/nmm layers of edge-sharing FeAs4 tetrahedra alternating with LaO fluorite-like blocks. MP offers only computed La-Fe-Ru-As-O supercells such as La4FeAs4Ru3O4 P-42m mp-1223053, which are particular ordered Fe/Ru arrangements of that same 1111 structure rather than a different prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: O0.89F0.11 throughout: fluorine on the oxygen site of the LaO block is the electron-doping variable of the whole 1111 family, held fixed here while Fe/Ru is scanned. It is the doping knob, not an impurity.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the transition-metal site of the FeAs layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Fe and Ru are both group 8 and share the pnictide-layer metal site, so the substitution is isovalent; it acts by diluting magnetism and expanding the layer, which is why the paper tracks the superconducting transition across it.

basis: The host splits evenly. Five compositions are Co100-xBx at x = 20 to 40, measured as melt-spun ribbons, and come from the amorphous Co-B paper -- these are metallic glass. CoB is from the crystalline iron-group borides paper and is the FeB B27 type, orthorhombic Pnma, which MP gives at mp-20857 on the hull with 3 ICSD references. Five ribbon samples against five bulk, so neither dominates and the host must be split composition by composition.

dopant_roles.basis: Nickel on the transition-metal sublattice; in the amorphous ribbons it is a glass-forming addition rather than a lattice substituent, so the role holds strictly only for the crystalline boride compositions.
The second paper covers the iron-group borides as a family, so iron shares the metal site of CoB.

basis: FexNiyB10Si10 with the metalloid content held at 20 at.% is the classic metglas composition, and both paper titles say amorphous outright -- thermoelectric power singularities of FeNiBSi amorphous alloys, and thermopower of amorphous Fe-Ni-Cr-Mo-Si-B. There is no crystalline prototype to assign and no reference line is offered, as expected.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe40Ni40Mo2Si10B8: molybdenum at 2 at.% is a deliberate glass-stabilising and corrosion-resisting addition to the transition-metal fraction, named in the second paper title, not a dopant on a lattice site -- there is no lattice.
Fe38.5Ni38.5C3Mo2Si10B8: carbon at 3 at.% joins Si and B as a metalloid glass former. It is a composition variable here, not the milling or pressing residue that carbon usually is.

basis: Fe78Si9B13 is 7 of the 10 samples, a melt-spun ribbon whose paper is about nanocrystallising a magnetic amorphous ribbon, so the as-made state is a metallic glass. The other three are (FeSi2)1-x(TiB2)x composites at x = 0.1 and 0.125 -- semiconducting beta-FeSi2 with a dispersed diboride, the same material as the B-Fe-Si-Ti host at rank 637. Two unrelated materials share this element set, so the split has to be per composition.

dopant_roles.basis: Titanium appears only inside the TiB2 dispersoid of the (FeSi2)(TiB2) composites; it is a separate phase, not a substituent in either the ribbon or the silicide.

basis: Every composition is (FeSi2)1-x(TiB2)x at x = 0.15 to 0.3 from the two TiB2-addition papers, so the matrix is semiconducting beta-FeSi2 and the titanium diboride is a deliberately added conducting second phase. The seed naming both beta_fesi2 and composite_multiphase is right: the stoichiometry is written as a two-phase mole fraction, so the split is by which phase a question is about rather than by any element ratio.

BaCeO3 and its B-site-substituted forms are every composition, and MP gives the orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted Pnma 62 mp-3187 on the hull with 14 ICSD references. Two of the three paper titles printed here -- barium molybdate and strontium ruthenium oxide -- are for other chemistries; only the BaCe0.95Tb0.05O3 hollow-fibre membrane paper is about this host, and it names the composition directly.

dopant_roles.basis: BaCe1-xTbxO3 at x = 0.05 and 0.15, in 8 of the compositions: terbium on the octahedral B site is the acceptor that creates the oxygen vacancies these proton-conducting membranes rely on.
BaCe0.85Tb0.05Y0.1O3: trivalent yttrium on the B site, the other standard acceptor for barium cerate.
BaCe0.85Tb0.05Zr0.1O3: Zr4+ for Ce4+ is isovalent and is added to stabilise the perovskite against carbonation, not to dope it.
BaCe0.85Tb0.05Co0.1O3: a 3d transition metal on the B site, added as a sintering aid and mixed-conduction promoter.
The same B site; iron enters at the level of the other 10 percent B-site substituents in this series.
The same B site.

basis: YbBaCo4O7 accounts for 7 of the 10 samples once the BaYbCo4O7 spelling is folded in, and MP gives P31c 159 mp-25738 with 3 ICSD references -- the trigonal distortion of the P6_3mc swedenborgite framework of corner-sharing CoO4 tetrahedra in alternating kagome and triangular layers. The first paper is titled for BaRCo4O7 and the second for the triangular and kagome sublattices, which is that framework. YbBaCo4O8 is the oxygen-loaded form of the same structure, not a different prototype.

other_polymorphs.note: A Cc monoclinic variant of the same composition at hull 0.007 with one ICSD reference. Swedenborgites are known to lower symmetry on cooling through an orthorhombic or monoclinic distortion, so this may in fact be a low-temperature phase rather than a separate polymorph; the 56-855 K window would cross it. Left here rather than in phases because the chunk file flags no transition and the temperature is not established.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [159, 9]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every composition is BaxLa2-xCuIrO6 at x = 0.5 to 1.4 from the single paper, an A2BBO6 double perovskite with Cu and Ir alternating on the B site and Ba replacing La on the A site to tune the iridium valence -- which is what the paper title says it is doing. Medium rather than high: no reference line is offered for this host, so the cell is uncorroborated, and Cu/Ir B-site order in these iridates is often only partial, which would make it a disordered perovskite instead.

Every composition is Ba8Ga16Sn30 with Ge substituting part of the Sn, and the taxonomy already records the correction that matters here -- beta-Ba8Ga16Sn30 is clathrate type VIII, not type I, which is why the Ba-Ga-Sn seed was refiled. The same applies to this Ge-substituted host, so the type I seed is rejected in favour of type VIII. Medium, and with type I kept as an alternative, because Ba8Ga16Sn30 does also form a type I alpha phase and neither the chunk file nor a reference line says which of the two these papers grew.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the group-14 framework site of the clathrate cage
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge and Sn are both group 14 and both build the cage framework, so the substitution is isoelectronic and acts on the cage size and the guest rattling rather than on the electron count -- the electron count is set by the Ga content, which is held near 16 throughout. Germanium sits above the 5 at.% cut and so is a host element here, not a dopant.

basis: Ba0.98La0.02MnO3 is 5 of the 10 samples, and BaMnO3 is not a cubic perovskite -- the Ba2+ cation is too large, so the AO3 layers stack hexagonally and the MnO6 octahedra share faces. MP backs that with P6_3/mmc 194 mp-19156 at hull 0.008 with 5 ICSD references, the 2H polytype. The host holds at least two more structures: the three (La0.67Ba0.33MnO3)(BaMnO3) composites are the structurally phase-separated cubic-plus-hexagonal mixture of the second paper title, and Ba3Mn2O8 is a separate R-3m spin-dimer compound of isolated Mn2O8 pairs with no taxonomy entry.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.98La0.02MnO3: La3+ for Ba2+ on the A site is a donor that puts Mn into a mixed 3+/4+ valence. In the composite compositions the lanthanum instead belongs to a distinct La0.67Ba0.33MnO3 phase, so the role differs by composition.

basis: Sr0.5Ba0.5Nb2O6 is 7 of the 10 samples and SBN is the textbook tetragonal tungsten bronze -- a corner-sharing NbO6 framework with pentagonal, square and trigonal tunnels that Sr and Ba partially and disorderedly fill. BaSrNb4O12 and Ba3Sr3Nb10O30 are the same compound written per different formula units, the last of them in the canonical A6B10O30 bronze form. MP offers only computed Ba2Sr3Nb10O30 cells at P1 and P2 with no ICSD backing, which is a symmetry-lowered relaxation of that same framework.

dopant_roles.basis: BaSrNb4O12(TiC)0.05: the titanium arrives as 5 mol% of added titanium carbide, a dispersed conducting second phase, not as a B-site substituent.
The other half of the same TiC addition; carbon is not in the oxide lattice.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [100], ICSD-backed references for this host report [164]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: BeO is the only composition and ref 1 makes P6_3mc 186 mp-2542 the primary on the hull with 32 ICSD references -- bromellite, the wurtzite form, which is the ambient phase for the whole 10-1499 K window. The rocksalt, zincblende and rutile entries all carry far fewer references and are pressure-driven or computed. All three papers measure it as a high-thermal-conductivity ceramic, not as a thermoelectric.

other_polymorphs.note: Hull 0.482 with 7 ICSD references; the high-pressure phase of BeO, not reached by heating at ambient pressure.
Hull 0.007 with 6 ICSD references. Nearly degenerate with wurtzite, as always for a stacking variant, but it is a stacking polytype stabilised in films rather than a thermal phase.
Hull 0.012 with 2 ICSD references; another compressed form.

basis: Ca1-xBixMnO3 at x = 0.25 to 0.5 is 9 of the 10 samples, a Bi-substituted CaMnO3 orthorhombic perovskite, and all three paper titles name either Ca1-xBixMnO3-delta or manganese perovskites directly. Ca1.6Bi0.4MnO4 is the one exception, written at the A2BO4 stoichiometry of an n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper phase, so the host is flagged mixed for that single composition. MP offers only a computed Ca3Mn4BiO12 Pm cell with no ICSD backing.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi0.25Gd0.05Ca0.7MnO3: a trivalent rare earth on the A site alongside the Bi, acting as a donor and as a size perturbation on the octahedral tilt.

basis: Ce3Bi4Pt3 is 9 of the 10 samples once the La-diluted composition is included, and it is the cubic Y3Au3Sb4 type -- the Th3P4-derived lattice that makes it the archetypal Kondo insulator of the second and third paper titles. MP confirms I-43d 220 mp-1105392 on the hull. CeBiPt is a genuinely different structure, a half-Heusler at F-43m mp-1018162, and has its own paper, so the host holds two.

dopant_roles.basis: (Ce0.9La0.1)3Bi4Pt3: lanthanum is isostructural and trivalent like cerium but has no f electron, so diluting with it is how the second paper separates Kondo coherence from single-ion behaviour. A magnetic dilution rather than a carrier dopant.

basis: Pb5Bi6Se14, Pb7Bi4Se13, Pb5Bi12Se23, Pb5Bi18Se32 and K1.25Pb3.5Bi7.25Se15 are each effectively their own structure -- lillianite and pavonite homologues built from rocksalt-like slabs of differing width, which is exactly what the first two paper titles say and what the third calls modular construction. MP reaches only Bi4Pb7Se13 C2/m mp-1190436 with 2 ICSD references, so most of these homologues have no entry, which is the expected situation for this prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb5Bi6Se13.975I0.025: iodine on the chalcogen site is a donor, used at the 0.025 level to tune the carrier concentration of the lillianite homologue.

K1.25Pb3.5Bi7.25Se15 is the A1+xM4-2xM7+xSe15 phase of the third paper title, where potassium is a structural cation of that particular homologue rather than a dilute addition to Pb5Bi6Se14. It falls under the 5 at.% cut only because the formula unit is large.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [11], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The curator names most of these outright: polythiophene C4H2S, poly(3-methylthiophene) C5H4S, PVC and poly(nickel 1,1,2,2-ethenetetrathiolate), measured as free-standing films -- so organic_polymer carries the majority of the host. The two exceptions are C36H32Cl4GaS24 and C36H32AuBr2S24, which are (BEDT-TTF)4 radical-cation salts with GaCl4 and AuBr2 counter-anions: crystalline molecular conductors, not polymers, from the one-dimensional-conductor paper. A bedt_ttf_salt prototype is proposed for them and the host is flagged mixed. The MP entries printed for this chemistry are unrelated metal thiolate and thiocyanate complexes.

dopant_roles.basis: Chlorine is a backbone atom of the PVC in the three-component hybrid film and part of the GaCl4 counter-anion in the BEDT-TTF salt. In both cases it is a constituent of the molecule, not a dopant.
The curator gives PETT, C2S4Ni, poly(nickel 1,1,2,2-ethenetetrathiolate): the nickel is the coordinating metal centre of the polymer backbone itself, which is what makes that component conducting.
The GaCl4 counter-anion of C36H32Cl4GaS24; it sets the charge on the BEDT-TTF donors and forms its own sublattice.
The AuBr2 counter-anion of C36H32AuBr2S24, the same role in the other salt.
The other half of the AuBr2 anion.

basis: Every composition is (Ca0.85OH)1.16CoO2 or an Nd-substituted form, and the third paper is titled for the monoclinic phase of the misfit-layered cobalt oxide (Ca0.85OH)1.16CoO2. The 1.16 is the incommensurate ratio between the CaOH rocksalt-like block and the CdI2-like CoO2 layer, which is the definition of the prototype. No reference line is offered, as expected for a two-subsystem composite that has no single MP entry.

dopant_roles.basis: The curator formula (Ca0.85-xNdxOH)1.16CoO2 puts neodymium on the calcium site inside the hydroxide block, so it dopes the CoO2 layer indirectly by changing the charge transferred across the interface.

basis: Pr1-xCaxCoO3 at x = 0.3 and 0.5, some of it with Y or Sm partly replacing Pr, is every composition; these are orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted cobaltite perovskites and all three papers are about the metal-insulator transition in R1-xAxCoO3. MP offers only computed cells with no ICSD backing -- CaPr3(CoO3)4 Pm mp-1227199, an ordered A-site supercell of the same perovskite, and CaPrCoO4 I4mm mp-1227079, an n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper stoichiometry that matches none of these compositions.

dopant_roles.basis: (Pr1-yYy)0.7Ca0.3CoO3 at y up to 0.125: yttrium is trivalent like Pr, so it adds no carriers -- it shrinks the average A-site radius, which is precisely how the papers shift the metal-insulator transition temperature.
(Pr0.8Sm0.2)0.7Ca0.3CoO3, the RE = Sm member of the same A-site size series in the second paper title.

basis: Every composition is Ca2FeMoO6 with Sr or La partly replacing Ca. This is the ordered rock-salt alternation of FeO6 and MoO6 octahedra that defines the A2BB6 double perovskite, and all three papers treat it as such (Ca2-xSrxFeMoO6 for x up to 0.3, La-doped Ca2FeMoO6). MP gives Ca2FeMoO6 P2_1/c (14) mp-18783 at hull 0.001 with 1 ICSD reference: monoclinic tilting of the same ordered framework, not a different prototype.
