basis: Four of the six compositions are Ag(0.2-0.4)Bi0.5Sb(0.2-1.5)Te3 -- silver added to Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3, the workhorse p-type tetradymite alloy -- and the third paper is on quaternary Ag-Bi-Sb-Te alloys prepared by pressureless sintering. The other two are written as (Ag2Te)0.25 and (Ag2Te)0.5 of (Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3), i.e. 25 and 50 per cent silver telluride: at that level Ag2Te is a second phase and the sample is a tetradymite/Ag2Te composite, not a doped tetradymite, so the host is flagged mixed and those two split off in stage 2. Silver below its solubility takes a cation site as an acceptor; above it, it precipitates as Ag2Te, which is the whole subject of the Ag2Te doping paper. [ref 2] offers only Ag2BiSbTe4 I-4m2 mp-1229125 at hull 0.457 with no ICSD references, a computed ordered quaternary that is not the measured material, so no mp_id is recorded. The Bi/Sb ratio spans 0.25 to 0.71 across the host, so the parent tetradymite composition is per-composition work for stage 3, not a host-level label.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Bi/(Bi+Sb) over six compositions, median 0.31. Bismuth and antimony are isoelectronic and share the octahedral cation site of the tetradymite layer, so this is a genuine substitution axis; the structure is tetradymite across the whole of it, but the parent end member is not the same at x = 0.25 and x = 0.71.

basis: All six compositions are Ag10Te4Br3 with partial anion substitution -- Cl for Br, S or Se for Te -- from the Nilges paper on a conceptional approach to materials for resistivity switching and thermoelectrics. It is a silver-rich telluride bromide with mobile silver in a Te/Br anion substructure, which is neither an argyrodite (no central tetrahedral cation, different anion count) nor a simple binary silver chalcogenide, so ag10te4br3_type is proposed before use. [ref 2] has no entry at this composition: Ag5Te2Br Pnma mp-1215016 is the neighbouring 5-2-1 compound of the same family (the chloride analogue of which is the next host in this chunk) and Ag9Te4Br3 P1 mp-676260 at hull 0.062 is a computed silver-deficient variant with no ICSD backing. So no mp_id is recorded and the ambient space group is not settled by the references. Silver-ion order-disorder transitions are reported in this family and the measured window is 289-524 K, so the measurement probably crosses one; no temperature is established by either reference, so none is asserted here and the paper should be read.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag10Te4Br(3-x)Cl(x) for x = 0.2 to 0.6. Chlorine is the lighter halogen on the same anion site, adding no carriers and tuning the lattice by size and mass contrast. At up to a fifth of the halide sublattice this is closer to alloying than to dilute doping, and it falls under the cut only because the formula unit has seventeen atoms.
Ag10Te3.8S0.2Br3. Sulfur is group 16 like tellurium and takes chalcogen sites in the anion substructure.
Ag10Te3.9Se0.1Br3, the same anion-site substitution one row up the group from tellurium.

basis: All five compositions are Ag5Te2Cl with small anion substitutions (S or Se for Te, Br for Cl), and the lead paper is titled Reversible Property Switching, Thermoelectric Performance, and d10-d10 Interactions in Ag5Te2Cl. This is the 5-2-1 member of the same silver telluride halide family as the Ag-Br-Te host at rank 947, and a distinct structure from it, so a separate prototype ag5te2cl_type is proposed rather than merging two structure types under one id. Neither reference returns a line for the chloride; [ref 2] does carry the bromide analogue Ag5Te2Br Pnma (62) mp-1215016 at hull 0.005 in the neighbouring host, which is where the Pnma in the proposal comes from, and it is not recorded as an mp_id here because it is a different compound. The reversible property switching of the title is a structural or ionic transition and the measured window is 297-505 K, so the measurement probably crosses it; no temperature is given by the references, so none is asserted.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag5Te1.9S0.1Cl and Ag5Te1.7S0.3Cl, from the paper on the effects of partial anion substitution. Sulfur takes chalcogen sites, adding no carriers; at 15 per cent of the tellurium sublattice the larger of the two is alloying rather than doping.
Ag5Te1.8Se0.2Cl, the same anion-site substitution with selenium.
Ag5Te2Cl0.8Br0.2. Bromine on the halide site, which is also the direction of the sibling compound Ag5Te2Br, so this composition sits on the line between the two.

basis: One composition, AgCuS, across all six samples, and the paper is titled The effect of order-disorder phase transitions and band gap evolution on the thermoelectric behaviour. The ambient phase is ordered orthorhombic stromeyerite, with copper in trigonal and silver in near-linear coordination on distinct ordered sites: [ref 1] gives CuAgS Cmc2_1 (36) mp-1077811 and Cmcm (63) mp-8911 and [ref 2] gives CuAgS Pnma (62) mp-5014 flagged AMBIGUOUS, which are three settings of that same ordered structure, none with more than two ICSD references. The taxonomy had no stromeyerite entry, so stromeyerite_agcus is proposed before use. On heating the cations disorder in two steps inside the measured 291-542 K window -- to a hexagonal cation-disordered phase near 360 K, then to a cubic superionic phase near 440 K -- which is what the title means by order-disorder transitions, so the high-temperature phase is recorded as cu2se_superionic, whose entry already covers the Ag-Cu-Se and Ag-Cu-Te analogues. Both temperatures come from materials knowledge rather than from the chunk references, and the intermediate hexagonal step is folded into the second phase because the taxonomy has no id for it; the paper would pin both numbers.

Every composition is built on Ge0.62Ag0.11Sb0.13Pb0.12Te -- a TAGS-type GeTe alloy (the Ag and Sb in near-equal amounts are the AgSbTe2 half of TAGS) extended with lead and then with one per cent Bi and five per cent of Cd, Mn or Sn, from the Science paper on high figure-of-merit high-entropy GeTe-based thermoelectrics. The structure is the rhombohedral R3m ferroelectric distortion of rocksalt, which converts to cubic Fm-3m inside the 299-801 K measured window, so both phases are recorded. The transition is near 700 K in pure GeTe and every one of these substituents pushes it down -- that is what high entropy on the cation site does, and it is part of why the paper works -- so 700 K is an upper estimate for these compositions rather than a measured value. Neither reference covers this five-element system, so mp_id is null on both phases.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi0.01 on five of the six compositions. Bismuth on the cation site of a GeTe-based rocksalt-derived lattice donates an electron each, compensating part of the very large intrinsic hole concentration from germanium vacancies, which is the standard way this system is tuned towards optimal carrier density.

Cd0.05 in one composition, one of the three cations swapped in to raise the configurational entropy. Divalent cadmium is isovalent with germanium here, so it works on the band structure and the lattice rather than on the carrier count.
Mn0.05 in one composition. Divalent manganese on the germanium site is a well-established band-convergence agent in GeTe and also lowers the rhombohedral-to-cubic transition temperature.

Sn0.05 in one composition. Tin is group 14 like germanium and forms a complete solid solution with it in the telluride, so it adds no carriers; it is the mildest of the three entropy-raising substitutions.

Cu0.003 in a single composition, three parts in a thousand. At that level copper is a fine carrier-tuning addition on the cation site, though copper is small and mobile enough in telluride lattices that an interstitial position cannot be ruled out without the paper.

basis: All three compositions are Ag2S, two of them with a few per cent excess sulfur, and the papers are on superionic phase transitions in silver chalcogenide nanocrystals and on binary silver chalcogenides. The ambient phase is monoclinic acanthite, which [ref 2] carries as Ag2S P2_1/c (14) mp-610517 at hull 0.024 with 7 ICSD references as PRIMARY. I disagree with [ref 1] here: TEDesignLab offers only P2_12_12_1 (19) mp-1095694 with 2 ICSD references and P2_1 (4) mp-31053 with 1, and although the project precedence prefers TEDesignLab, neither of those is the acanthite structure that every study of Ag2S at room temperature reports, and the Materials Project entry carries more than three times the ICSD evidence. The taxonomy had no acanthite entry -- ag2se_naumannite is the orthorhombic selenide, a different ordered arrangement -- so acanthite_ag2s is proposed before use. Acanthite converts to the body-centred cubic silver-disordered argentite phase near 450 K, which is inside the measured 303-543 K window and is the subject of the lead paper, so both phases are recorded.

other_polymorphs.note: The naumannite-type setting TEDesignLab gives for Ag2S, with 2 ICSD references against 7 for monoclinic acanthite. It is not the ambient phase and heating produces argentite rather than this, so it is kept out of the thermal sequence.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag2S1.05 and Ag2S1.1: sulfur excess, equivalently silver deficiency, on the chalcogen sublattice. In a mixed ionic-electronic conductor this sets the carrier concentration directly, which is why the composition is varied at all; it is not a foreign impurity.

basis: Every composition is a SnTe or SnSe alloy with AgSbSe2 or AgSbTe2 in near-equal Ag:Sb ratio, and the two papers are on a SnTe/AgSbSe2 nanocomposite and on cubic SnSe-AgSbTe2 alloys. All four end members sit on the rocksalt lattice: SnTe is rocksalt outright, AgSbSe2 and AgSbTe2 are rocksalt with silver and antimony sharing the cation site, and SnSe is driven from its layered Pnma form into the cubic rocksalt structure by exactly this alloying, which is the point of the band-flattening paper. So the whole host is one prototype even though the parent compound differs across it. Neither reference block covers this five-element system and no mp_id is recorded. The Se/Te ratio spans 0.27 to 0.70, so which end member a given sample is closer to is stage 3 work, not a host-level label.

other_polymorphs.note: Pnma SnSe is the ambient structure of one end member, but in these alloys the cubic rocksalt form is stabilised at room temperature by the AgSbTe2 content, so the layered phase is not part of the measured sequence.

dopant_roles.basis: Cd0.05 in the two SnTe-based compositions. Divalent cadmium on the tin site of rocksalt SnTe is a standard band-convergence agent, isovalent with tin so it does not by itself add carriers.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) over six compositions, median 0.50. Both are group 16 and share the single anion site of the rocksalt lattice, so this is a genuine substitution axis; the structure is rocksalt across all of it, but the parent is SnTe-AgSbSe2 at one end and SnSe-AgSbTe2 at the other.

basis: All six compositions are Ba8(Ga,Al)xSi(46-x) with eight barium atoms to a 46-atom framework, which is the type I clathrate stoichiometry exactly, and both papers name the compounds as Ba8AlxSi(46-x) and Ba8Ga(x)Si clathrates. The framework is the silicon type I cage network with aluminium and gallium substituting on framework sites to set the electron count -- Ba8Ga16Si30 and Ba8Al16Si30 are the two charge-balanced end members and the compositions here lie between them. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded. The Al/(Al+Ga) ratio spans 0.16 to 0.49, so the framework composition is a per-composition variable rather than a host-level one.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Al/(Al+Ga) over six compositions, median 0.37. Both are trivalent and both substitute for silicon on the type I cage framework, so the axis is a framework substitution that leaves the electron count unchanged while altering the cage size and the guest rattling; neither is a dopant. Barium occupancy of the cages is fixed at 8 per cell throughout, so the axis is purely a framework one.

basis: One composition, Co2MnAl, across all six samples, and two of the three papers name it as a full-Heusler and a half-metallic ferromagnetic Heusler alloy. X2YZ with the 2:1:1 ratio is the L2_1 full-Heusler structure, and [ref 2] confirms it directly: MnAlCo2 Fm-3m (225) mp-3623 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references as PRIMARY. The third paper measures epitaxial L2_1 Co2MnAl films, so the same ordered structure is named there too. The Mn2AlCo F-43m (216) entry in the same reference block is the inverse-Heusler arrangement at a different composition and is not what these samples are.

other_polymorphs.note: Mn2AlCo F-43m, the inverse-Heusler arrangement of the same three elements at a different stoichiometry. Listed only because it appears in the reference block for this host; it is not a polymorph of Co2MnAl.

basis: The host key is a parse artifact. The single composition is written LiAl02 with the letter O typed as a zero, and the only paper is titled Effects of Fast Neutron Irradiation on Thermal Conductivity of Li2O and LiAlO2 -- so the material is lithium aluminate, the oxygen was lost when the string was parsed, and Al-Li is not a lithium aluminium alloy host at all. That makes both reference blocks irrelevant: [ref 2] returns LiAl Fd-3m mp-1067 with 26 ICSD references and four other Li-Al intermetallics, none of which describes the measured material, so no mp_id is recorded and the reference evidence is set aside rather than followed. The taxonomy had no LiAlO2 entry, so gamma_lialo2 is proposed before use: gamma-LiAlO2 is the tetragonal P4_12_12 tetrahedral-framework polymorph, the form used as a tritium-breeder ceramic and the one a 1988 fusion-materials irradiation study would have measured. Confidence is medium rather than high because the polymorph is inferred from the application rather than read from the paper; the alpha and beta forms are recorded as alternatives.

other_polymorphs.note: alpha-LiAlO2, the R-3m ordered-rocksalt layered polymorph with octahedral aluminium. It converts irreversibly to the gamma form on heating, so it cannot be present above a few hundred K, but it cannot be ruled out for the as-received material without the paper.
beta-LiAlO2, the wurtzite-derived Pna2_1 polymorph. Also a possible starting material and also converts to gamma on heating.

basis: Three of the six samples are MgAl2O4 outright and a fourth is Mg0.73Fe0.33Al1.93O4, an iron-substituted spinel, and [ref 1] gives MgAl2O4 Fd-3m (227) mp-3536 at hull 0.000 with 28 ICSD references as PRIMARY -- as clean a spinel assignment as this project gets. The host is nevertheless mixed: the remaining two compositions are written (MgO)0.92(Al2O3)0.08 and (MgO)0.88(Al2O3)0.12, from the paper on MgO-based ceramics with high dielectric breakdown strength, which is rocksalt MgO with an alumina addition of 8 to 12 mole per cent, not a spinel. At that ratio the alumina is beyond the solubility limit in MgO and the material is an MgO matrix with spinel at the grain boundaries, so those two split off in stage 2. The Materials Project block for this host is unusable -- every entry in it is a computed off-stoichiometry phase at hull 0.08 to 0.49, including an AMBIGUOUS Mg16Al12O -- and is not followed; TEDesignLab has the real structure.

other_polymorphs.note: MgAl2O4 Pnma at hull 0.099 with 3 ICSD references, the CaTi2O4-type post-spinel phase that forms above about 25 GPa. Not reached by heating at ambient pressure.

dopant_roles.basis: Mg0.73Fe0.33Al1.93O4. Iron enters the spinel as Fe2+ on the tetrahedral magnesium site, and as Fe3+ it would take octahedral aluminium sites instead -- MgFe2O4 and MgAl2O4 form a continuous spinel solid solution, so the site split depends on the oxidation state and cannot be fixed without the paper. At 4.7 at.% it falls just under the host cut but is really the dilute end of that solid solution.

basis: All six compositions cluster tightly around Al65Rh27Si8 and the only paper is titled Electrical resistivity of the Al65Rh27Si8 2/1 cubic approximant -- the structure is named in the title. A 2/1 approximant is a large-cell cubic crystal whose local order reproduces the icosahedral quasicrystal, which is exactly what this prototype covers. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, which is expected: approximants have hundreds of atoms per cell and are poorly represented in both snapshots. The 13-296 K measured window is the low-temperature resistivity regime where approximants show their characteristic negative temperature coefficient.

Two samples are AlSb and four are Al(1-x)MgxSb with x from 0.005 to 0.02, and [ref 1] gives AlSb F-43m (216) mp-2624 at hull 0.000 with 10 ICSD references as PRIMARY. AlSb is the standard III-V zincblende semiconductor, so this is unambiguous. The P6_3mc (186) wurtzite entry in [ref 2] carries 1 ICSD reference and is the nanowire polytype rather than a bulk phase, and the Pa-3 and Cmcm entries at hull 0.113 and 0.191 are high-pressure or computed structures; none of them is reached on heating in the 306-858 K window.

other_polymorphs.note: AlSb P6_3mc at hull 0.008 with 1 ICSD reference against 10 for zincblende. The hexagonal polytype of a III-V is normally a nanowire or thin-film form, and these samples are bulk.

dopant_roles.basis: Al(1-x)MgxSb for x = 0.005 to 0.02, from the paper on improving the thermoelectric properties of AlSb by incorporation of magnesium. Divalent magnesium on the trivalent aluminium site is an acceptor, so this is p-type doping on the cation sublattice.

basis: The host holds two stoichiometries and two structures. Three compositions are (Yb,Sc)Al3, which is the Cu3Au L1_2 structure -- YbAl3 is this prototype exemplar and ScAl3 is isostructural -- and three are (Yb,Sc)Al2, which is the cubic C15 MgCu2 Laves phase, both YbAl2 and ScAl2 adopting it. The two papers split the same way, one on the YbAl3 system and one on Yb(1-x)ScxAl2 alloys. A single label would be wrong, so the host is flagged mixed and splits cleanly on the Al:(Yb+Sc) ratio, 3 against 2. [ref 2] offers only a computed YbScAl4 F-43m mp-1215458 at hull 0.036 with no ICSD references -- an ordered quaternary that is not either of the measured phases -- so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Sc/(Sc+Yb) over six compositions, median 0.70. Scandium and ytterbium share the single rare-earth site in both the L1_2 and the Laves structure. They are not isoelectronic in the usual sense -- the point of the substitution is that scandium is trivalent while ytterbium is intermediate-valent, so the axis tunes the f-level occupancy and hence the thermopower, which is what the chemical-pressure paper measures. Recorded as an axis rather than as doping because it runs the full range.

basis: Three different structures sit in this host and the split is by composition, not by dopant. Three samples are RTi2Al20 cage compounds -- LaTi2Al20 twice and PrTi2Al20 once, from the two papers on RT2Al20 thermoelectric power -- which is the CeCr2Al20 structure, Fd-3m with the rare earth inside a 16-atom aluminium Frank-Kasper cage; [ref 2] confirms both, La(TiAl10)2 and Pr(TiAl10)2 Fd-3m at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference each. The other three are Ti-rich binary alloys -- Ti94Al6, Ti89Al11 and Ti0.67Al0.33 -- from the paper on electrical conduction in concentrated disordered transition metal alloys, which are hcp titanium solid solutions at 6 and 11 per cent aluminium and an ordered or partly ordered Ti-Al intermetallic at 33 per cent. I give the cage compounds the host label because they are the thermoelectrically meaningful half, but the record is medium confidence precisely because it covers only half the samples, and the host must be split in stage 2.

dopant_roles.basis: LaTi2Al20. Lanthanum is not a dopant despite falling under the 5 at.% cut -- one atom in twenty-three is the full stoichiometric occupancy of the AB2C20 cage site. The cut lands here only because the formula unit is so large.

PrTi2Al20, the same stoichiometric cage site. The non-Kramers doublet of Pr3+ in the cubic cage is the subject of the thermoelectric power anomaly paper, so the guest is the physics rather than an impurity.

basis: Four of the six samples are binary Al-Zn alloys spanning 15 to 89 per cent zinc, from two papers on the solid-liquid interfacial energy of Al-Zn solid solutions and of the eutectoid beta phase. Across that range the material is fcc aluminium-rich solid solution, hcp zinc-rich solid solution, or a two-phase mixture of them below the eutectoid at 550 K -- all of it random substitution on a close-packed lattice, which is what this prototype covers. The remaining two samples are not an alloy at all: Zn0.91Al0.07Ni0.02 comes from the paper on Al and Ni co-doped ZnO films, so the real material is wurtzite ZnO and the oxygen was lost when the composition string was parsed. The host is therefore flagged mixed and those two split off to wurtzite in stage 2. [ref 2] returns only computed Al2Zn and Al3Zn line compounds at hull 0.024 and 0.043 with no ICSD references; the Al-Zn system has no stable intermetallic, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Ni0.02 in the two Zn0.91Al0.07Ni0.02 samples, which are Al and Ni co-doped ZnO films rather than Al-Zn alloy. Nickel substitutes for zinc on the wurtzite cation site alongside aluminium; the paper reports room-temperature ferromagnetism, which is the usual reason for a transition-metal substitution in ZnO. The role applies to the wurtzite half of this host only.

basis: All four compositions are BaFe(2-x)CoxAs2 with x from 0.25 to 0.34, single crystals, from the paper on thermoelectric properties of electron- and hole-doped BaFe2As2. BaFe2As2 is the parent 122 iron pnictide, ThCr2Si2-type I4/mmm with FeAs layers of edge-sharing tetrahedra separated by barium, and cobalt substitution on the iron site leaves that structure intact. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host. The parent compound has a tetragonal-to-orthorhombic structural transition at about 140 K, which would sit inside the measured 10-299 K window, but cobalt suppresses it rapidly and at 12 to 17 per cent of the iron site these crystals are well past the doping where it survives -- so spans_transition is false, deliberately, and the reason is recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered.

dopant_roles.basis: BaFe(2-x)CoxAs2 for x = 0.25 to 0.34. Cobalt on the iron site of the FeAs layer is the electron-doping variable of the 122 pnictides -- it is what suppresses the spin-density wave and drives superconductivity -- so it is the tuning knob of the whole series rather than an impurity. It sits above the 5 at.% cut and so is part of the host key, but the role is recorded because the doping level is the point of the paper.

basis: One composition, BaPd2As2, across all six samples, from the paper on high-pressure effects on isotropic superconductivity in the iron-free 122 pnictide. The 1:2:2 stoichiometry with a late transition metal and a pnictogen is the ThCr2Si2 family, and [ref 2] gives Ba(AsPd)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-6962 at hull 0.020 with 1 ICSD reference, which is that structure. I record a disagreement with the reference ranking: the PRIMARY entry is Ba(AsPd)2 P4/mmm (123) mp-8237 with 2 ICSD references, and P4/mmm is not the ThCr2Si2 setting. Two references against one is a thin margin either way, and BaPd2As2 is known in a CaBe2Ge2-type variant as well as the ThCr2Si2 one -- same formula, same layer count, different stacking of the PdAs layers -- so the P4/mmm listing may be a reduced-symmetry description of that variant rather than a separate compound. The 122 assignment is made on the chemistry and marked medium until the paper settles which stacking was grown; no mp_id is asserted.

Every composition is Cd3(P,As)2 and the curator composition details confirm them as mol per cent mixtures of Cd3P2 and Cd3As2 prepared as solid solutions, from a 1970 paper on the physical and electronic properties of semiconducting solid solutions of those two compounds. Cd3As2 and Cd3P2 are isostructural -- the tetragonal antifluorite-derived structure with one quarter of the anion-coordinated cation sites ordered vacant -- and form a complete solid solution, so the whole host is one prototype. [ref 2] offers only a computed CdAsP I2_12_12_1 mp-1226754 at hull 0.035 with no ICSD references, a 1:1:1 ordered phase that is not this composition, so no mp_id is recorded. Cd3As2 does pass through further order-disorder steps, but they begin above 500 K and the measured window here stops at 373 K.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: As/(As+P) over six compositions, median 0.50, and the curator details give the same series as 20 to 80 mol per cent Cd3P2. Both are group 15 and share the single pnictogen site of the antifluorite-derived lattice, so this is a genuine substitution axis; the structure is unchanged across it while the band gap opens from the inverted, essentially zero-gap Cd3As2 towards semiconducting Cd3P2, which is what the paper measures.

basis: Four samples are LuAs and two are La(0.05-0.09)Lu(0.91-0.95)As, and [ref 2] gives LuAs Fm-3m (225) mp-2017 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references as PRIMARY. Rare-earth monopnictides are rocksalt as a family, and the paper on electron transport and magnetic properties of semimetallic LuAs describes the standard rocksalt semimetal with compensated electron and hole pockets. The Pm-3m entry at hull 0.502 is a computed CsCl-type alternative, not a phase these samples pass through.

other_polymorphs.note: LuAs Pm-3m at hull 0.502 with 1 ICSD reference. Rocksalt to CsCl is the standard high-pressure transition of the rare-earth monopnictides; it is not reached by heating at ambient pressure.

dopant_roles.basis: LaxLu(1-x)As for x = 0.05 and 0.09, from the paper on the temperature dependence of the electrical resistivity of LaxLu(1-x)As. Lanthanum takes the lutetium site of the rocksalt lattice; both are trivalent, so it adds no carriers and acts as a mass-and-size disorder scatterer -- the resistivity of the alloy is the measurement.

basis: Four samples are Th3As4 outright, and the lead paper is titled Some X-Ray and Thermoelectric Studies on Cubic Th3X4 Compounds -- the structure is named in the title and confirmed by [ref 2], which gives Th3As4 I-43d (220) mp-382 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references as PRIMARY. This is the anti-Th3P4 body-centred cubic structure the prototype is named for, and the same one that makes La3Te4 a thermoelectric: the cation sublattice tolerates vacancies, which is how carrier concentration is set in this family. The ThAs Fm-3m and ThAs2 P4/nmm entries in the same block are different compounds in the same binary, not polymorphs of Th3As4.

dopant_roles.basis: Th3(As0.95Sb0.05)4. Antimony is the next pnictogen down the group and takes arsenic sites in the anion framework, adding no carriers; Th3Sb4 is isostructural, so this is the dilute end of a complete solid solution rather than doping.

(Th0.94U0.06)3As4, from the paper on electronic properties of Th3As4-U3As4 solid solutions. Uranium takes the thorium site and U3As4 is isostructural, so this too is one end of a full solid solution; unlike the antimony substitution it changes the f-electron count, which is what the paper is about.

basis: One composition, CeIr2B2, across all six samples, from the paper on ferromagnetic ordering in CeIr2B2. The compound is certain; its structure type is not. Many RT2B2 borides are ThCr2Si2-type, but [ref 2] gives the only entry at this exact composition as Ce(BIr)2 Fddd (70) mp-8680 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is orthorhombic and not the 122 tetragonal structure, so filing this under thcr2si2_122 would assert something the reference contradicts. Since the taxonomy had no non-ThCr2Si2 RT2B2 entry, ceir2b2_boride is proposed before use. Confidence is low rather than medium on purpose: two ICSD references is below the threshold this project treats as weak, the structure has not been read out of the paper, and the other three entries in the reference block are different stoichiometries of the same ternary (CeB2Ir3, Ce(BIr)4, Ce2B2Ir5), which shows the Ce-Ir-B system is crowded enough for a mis-indexed phase to be plausible. This one belongs in the review queue.

The compositions are Fe40Ni40B20, Fe20Ni60B20 and (Fe,Ni)84B16 -- the classic metal-metalloid glass-forming compositions around 80 per cent transition metal and 20 per cent boron -- the sample form is Ribbon, which means melt spinning, and all three papers say so in their titles: thermoelectric power in Fe-based amorphous alloys, additives in amorphous ribbons, and transport properties of Fe-Ni glasses. There is no crystal structure to assign. [ref 2] returns five computed Fe-Ni-B line compounds at hull 0.03 to 0.06, one of them flagged AMBIGUOUS and none with more than 1 ICSD reference; they are what the material would crystallise into if annealed, not what was measured, so no mp_id is recorded. The 61-526 K window is below the crystallisation temperature of these glasses, so the amorphous state holds throughout.

One composition, PrB6, across all six samples, and both papers measure RB6 single crystals -- one explicitly on the thermal conductivity of RB6 for R = Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd. [ref 2] gives PrB6 Pm-3m (221) mp-12762 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references as PRIMARY, the CaB6 structure of boron octahedra with the rare earth in the cube-centre cavity. The PrB4, Pr2B5 and PrB12 entries in the same block are other line compounds of the binary, not polymorphs of the hexaboride. The 10-25 K window is the low-temperature magnetic regime where PrB6 orders antiferromagnetically; that is a magnetic transition, not a structural one, so no phases are recorded.

All four compositions are TmB12 or Tm(1-x)YbxB12, and the third paper is titled Thermal conductivity of metal dodecaborides with a UB12 structure -- the prototype is named there. [ref 2] gives TmB12 Fm-3m (225) mp-1104905 at hull 0.000, the cuboctahedral B12 cage framework of the UB12 type, although with only 1 ICSD reference, which this project flags as weak evidence. The TmB2 P6/mmm entry with 3 ICSD references that heads the block is the AlB2-type diboride, a different compound of the same binary rather than a better-attested polymorph, so the ranking is not followed here. The 10-301 K window covers the antiferromagnetic instability and metal-insulator behaviour the first paper studies; those are electronic and magnetic, and the cooperative Jahn-Teller distortion reported in this family is a subtle lattice instability rather than a prototype change, so no phase sequence is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Tm(1-x)YbxB12 for x = 0.05 to 0.3, from the paper on the antiferromagnetic instability and metal-insulator transition. Ytterbium takes the thulium site inside the B12 cage framework; YbB12 is isostructural and is the Kondo-insulator member of the family, so the substitution drives the host across that instability rather than merely adding carriers. At x = 0.3 it is alloying rather than doping.

basis: Four samples are BaBiTe3 and two are BaBiTe3 with a little selenium, and the lead paper is titled Oligomerization Versus Polymerization of Te(x)n- in the Polytelluride Compounds -- BaBiTe3 is one of the Kanatzidis alkaline-earth bismuth polytellurides, a low-symmetry orthorhombic structure built from BiTe slabs with tellurium-tellurium oligomers filling the space between them. That is precisely what the bi_chalcogenide_complex entry is for: module-built bismuth chalcogenides with large cells where each composition is effectively its own structure and stage 2 has to resolve it individually. It is not a tetradymite -- the resonant-bonding paper is about how its multiband transport differs from the Bi2Te3 family -- and it is not the 3-14-12 copper polytelluride either. Neither reference block returns anything for this host, so no mp_id and no space group are recorded; confidence is medium because the family label is secure while the specific structure rests on the paper title rather than on a database entry.

dopant_roles.basis: BaBiTe2.95Se0.05 and BaBiTe2.9Se0.1, from the paper on resonant bonding and native defects. Selenium is group 16 like tellurium and takes chalcogen sites; at 2 to 3 per cent of the anion sublattice it is dilute, and in a structure with tellurium-tellurium bonding the site it prefers is a real question for stage 2 rather than a formality.

basis: Every composition is La0.33Ba(0.47-0.67)Gd(0-0.2)Co0.7Fe0.3O3 -- an ABO3 stoichiometry with a mixed rare-earth and alkaline-earth A site and a mixed cobalt-iron B site, which is the standard perovskite cathode chemistry the paper works in. Two things rule out the A-site ordered variant: the La:Ba ratio is 1:2 rather than the 1:1 that LnBaB2O5+d ordering requires, and the oxygen content is written as 3 rather than as 5+delta per two B sites. So this is a disordered perovskite, cubic or rhombohedrally tilted depending on the exact A-site mix, rather than a layered double perovskite. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded. Oxygen non-stoichiometry is certain to be present in a cobaltite of this composition but is not captured by the composition strings.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.33Ba(0.67-x)GdxCo0.7Fe0.3O3 for x = 0.05 to 0.2, and the paper is titled Impacts of A-site gadolinium doping. Gadolinium takes the A site, replacing barium: it is trivalent where barium is divalent, so it lowers the hole count on the cobalt-iron sublattice, and being much smaller it also increases the octahedral tilting. At x = 0.2 the larger substitutions are alloying rather than dilute doping.

basis: Five of the six samples are SmBaCuFeO5 or Sm(1-x)LaxBaCuFeO5, and the second paper names the family directly: layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. The structure is the A-site ordered double perovskite -- samarium and barium in alternating layers, copper and iron sharing the B sites, and one oxygen vacancy per formula unit ordered into the rare-earth layer, which gives the tetragonal P4mm cell that [ref 2] returns as BaSmFeCuO5 mp-1214324 at hull 0.000. That entry has no ICSD reference, so the space group is supported by the chemistry rather than by measured evidence, but the A-site ordering itself is not in doubt at a 1:1 Ln:Ba ratio with O5 rather than O6. The sixth sample is a 20 weight per cent silver composite of the same ceramic; the matrix structure is unchanged, so the host is not flagged mixed, but stage 2 should treat that one as a composite.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm(1-x)LaxBaCuFeO5 for x = 0.2 to 0.4, from the paper on the thermoelectric properties of that series. Lanthanum takes the samarium layer of the A-site ordered structure; both are trivalent, so the substitution works through size -- the larger lanthanum reduces the tilting and the A-site size mismatch that drives the ordering. At 20 to 40 per cent of the site this is alloying rather than doping.

(SmBaCuFeO5)80(Ag)20, from the paper on SmBaCuFeO5+delta/Ag composite ceramics. Silver is added as a metallic second phase to raise the electrical conductivity of the ceramic; it is not in the perovskite lattice at all, which is why the sample is a composite rather than a doped oxide.

basis: All six compositions are YBaCuFe(1-x)NixO5, from a single paper on that solid solution. This is the yttrium member of the same LnBaCuFeO5 layered ferrocuprate family as the Sm host at rank 973: yttrium and barium order into alternating A-site layers, copper and iron share the B sites, and the single ordered oxygen vacancy per formula unit gives the tetragonal P4mm cell. I disagree with the reference here, though there is little to disagree with: [ref 2] offers only Ba4Y2FeCu5O14 C2/m (12) mp-1228213 at hull 0.066 with no ICSD references, which is a different stoichiometry -- five coppers to one iron rather than one to one -- and a monoclinic cell, so it is not the measured compound and no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: YBaCuFe(1-x)NixO5 for x = 0.025 to 0.3. Nickel takes the iron half of the shared B site; the paper treats the whole range as a solid solution, so the x = 0.2 and 0.3 members are alloying rather than dilute doping, and only the 0.025 and 0.05 ones are doping in the usual sense.

basis: The host holds two distinct structures. Four samples are BaCu2S2 or K-substituted BaCu2S2, which the two papers call beta-BaCu2S2 and describe as having a natural superlattice structure -- the orthorhombic Pnma form with puckered CuS layers between barium, which [ref 1] carries as Ba(CuS)2 Pnma (62) mp-5970 at hull 0.002 with 2 ICSD references. The other two are BaCu4S3 and BaCu3.96S3, a copper-richer layered compound with a different connectivity, from the paper on BaCu4S3 as a p-type thermoelectric with high band degeneracy; the taxonomy had no entry for it, so bacu4s3_layered is proposed and the host is flagged mixed. Two disagreements to record. First, [ref 1] makes Ba(CuS)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-4255 with 5 ICSD references PRIMARY over the Pnma entry, but I4/mmm is the ThCr2Si2-type form and the layered superlattice the papers measure is the Pnma one, so the primary is not followed. Second, the taxonomy entry itself says beta-BaCu2S2 is the I4/mmm variant and alpha the Pnma one, which is the opposite of the naming these papers use for the material they measure; the structure assigned here is the Pnma layered one either way, and the alpha/beta labelling in the taxonomy note should be checked rather than propagated.

other_polymorphs.note: Ba(CuS)2 I4/mmm at hull 0.017 with 5 ICSD references, the ThCr2Si2-type polymorph of the same formula. It is a real phase of this chemistry but not the layered form the thermoelectric papers report, and the relationship between the two on heating is not established by the references.

dopant_roles.basis: K(0.05-0.1)Ba(0.9-0.95)Cu2S2, from the paper on potassium-doped beta-BaCu2S2. Monovalent potassium on the divalent barium site between the CuS layers is an acceptor, so it is the p-type doping variable of this compound.
BaCu3.96S3 against nominal BaCu4S3: a one per cent copper deficiency on the framework, which in a copper chalcogenide sets the hole concentration directly rather than acting as an impurity.

basis: Two samples are BaRuO3, which [ref 2] gives as R-3m (166) mp-5773 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references as PRIMARY -- the 9R polytype, face-sharing RuO6 trimers linked by corners, exactly the structure this prototype is named for. The other four are Ba4Ru3O10, which [ref 2] gives as P2_1/c (14) mp-1200068 at hull 0.001 with 1 ICSD reference and which the antiferromagnetic-order paper studies. Ba4Ru3O10 is not a separate family: it is built of the same face-sharing Ru3O12 trimers, corner-linked in a different sequence, so it sits inside the hexagonal-perovskite polytype series rather than beside it, and the host is not flagged mixed. Confidence is medium because the prototype entry describes the ABO3 polytypes and the 4-3-10 member is an intergrowth of that motif at a different stoichiometry; if stage 2 wants the two separated, the split is on the Ba:Ru ratio. The alkaline-earth ruthenate paper prepared these by spark plasma sintering, so both compositions are bulk polycrystals.

One composition, Ba8Zn7Si39, across all six samples, and the paper is titled Clathrates Ba8{Zn,Cd}xSi46-x, x about 7: synthesis, crystal structure and thermoelectric properties -- eight guests to a 46-atom framework is the type I clathrate stoichiometry and the paper reports the crystal structure. Zinc substitutes on the silicon cage framework, the same role gallium plays in Ba8Ga16Si30, and at x = 7 the compound is electron-rich rather than charge-balanced, which is why this series is measured. The reference block is no help and is not followed: it returns Ba(ZnSi)2 I4/mmm and BaZnSi P6_3/mmc, both 1 ICSD reference, which are ordinary line compounds of the ternary at completely different stoichiometries, not clathrates. No mp_id is recorded.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [139, 194]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every sample is an inorganic-organic composite, and the curator composition details say so explicitly: five are Bi2Te3 with 2 to 7 per cent PEDOT:PSS by weight and one is Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 with AgBi3S5 and polypyrrole. There is no single structure here -- the material is tetradymite grains in a conducting-polymer matrix, and the whole point of the three papers is the interface between them, energy filtering and selective carrier transport. So the host is composite_multiphase with tetradymite and organic_polymer as the constituents, flagged mixed so stage 2 splits it rather than assigning one lattice. Neither reference block returns anything, as expected for a composite. The carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, sulfur and nitrogen in the composition strings are the polymer written out as a formula, not elements in a crystal.

dopant_roles.basis: The sulfur of PEDOT:PSS, C14H14O5S2, and of the AgBi3S5 filler. It belongs to the polymer and to the sulfosalt inclusion, not to the tetradymite lattice.
The oxygen of the PEDOT:PSS repeat unit. Not a substituent on the chalcogen site and not processing residue either -- it is part of the polymer that was deliberately added.
The nitrogen of polypyrrole, C4H2NH, in the single Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 composite.
AgBi3S5 added as an inclusion in the BiTeSe-based composite, a distinct sulfosalt phase rather than silver dissolved in the tetradymite.
Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 is the n-type tetradymite alloy the composite is built on; selenium shares the chalcogen site with tellurium. It is a property of the inorganic matrix, not of the composite.

basis: All six compositions are BiCuSe(1-x)SxO and the paper is titled Structure and Transport Properties of the BiCuSeO-BiCuSO Solid Solution. BiCuSeO is the standard oxyselenide thermoelectric and adopts the ZrCuSiAs 1111 structure -- alternating insulating Bi2O2 layers and conducting Cu2Se2 layers, P4/nmm -- and BiCuSO is isostructural, so the whole solid solution is one prototype. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded. Note that the sulfur-selenium axis is a genuine shared site while the oxygen is not part of it: oxygen sits in the Bi2O2 layer and never exchanges with the chalcogen of the Cu2X2 layer, which is exactly the case the project flags when it warns that same-group elements need not share a site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: chalcogen site of the Cu2X2 layer
solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se) over six compositions, median 0.50, a complete solid solution between BiCuSeO and BiCuSO. Both are group 16 and both take the chalcogen site of the copper layer; the oxygen of the Bi2O2 layer is group 16 as well but is not on this axis and does not exchange with it.

basis: The compositions are written Bi2Sr2Cu6.04 through Bi2Sr2Cu6.48 and the paper is titled Evidence for Antiferromagnetic Order in Bi2Sr2CuO6 Phase with Stoichiometry -- so the material is Bi-2201, the single-CuO2-layer member of the BSCCO cuprate family, and the composition strings are a parse artifact: the oxygen subscript 6.04 to 6.48 was attached to copper and the element symbol dropped, which is why the host key has no oxygen in it. Read correctly the series is Bi2Sr2CuO(6.04-6.48), a fixed cation ratio with the oxygen content varied. That variation is the doping variable of the cuprate, tuning hole count on the CuO2 plane from the antiferromagnetic side of the phase diagram, which is what the paper measures over its 11-300 K window. [ref 2] returns only SrCuBi P6_3/mmc mp-30451, an oxygen-free ternary intermetallic that follows from the broken composition string rather than from the material, so it is disregarded and no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: The 6.04 to 6.48 in the composition strings is the oxygen content of Bi2Sr2CuO(6+delta), misparsed onto copper. Interstitial oxygen in the BiO layers is the hole-doping variable of every BSCCO phase, so this is the tuning knob of the series rather than an impurity; it is recorded here even though the parser left oxygen out of the host key.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [139], ICSD-backed references for this host report [194]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: All five compositions are Er2O(1.2-1.8)Bi(1.2-1.8), and the paper is titled Superconductivity in Anti-ThCr2Si2-type Er2O2Bi -- the structure is named there. Er2O2Bi is I4/mmm with fluorite-like Er2O2 slabs separated by square nets of bismuth, and [ref 2] confirms it as Er2BiO2 I4/mmm (139) mp-1069613 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY. The id is a judgement call between two entries that describe the same arrangement from opposite directions. Bi2O2Se is the M2O2X archetype -- a fluorite-like M2O2 slab with a square anion net between -- and Er2O2Bi differs only in which element plays which part, so bi2o2se_layered is the closer structural match; thcr2si2_122 is recorded as the alternative because the anti-ThCr2Si2 description the paper uses refers to the same I4/mmm topology with cation and anion roles exchanged. Confidence is medium for that reason, not because the structure is in doubt. The compositions are off-stoichiometric on both the oxygen and the bismuth side, which for a compound built on a bismuth square net is likely to be real rather than a rounding artefact.

dopant_roles.basis: Er2O(1.2-1.8)Bi(1.2-1.8): the oxygen and bismuth contents are varied in opposite directions across the series, so the composition is moved along the Er2O2Bi line rather than doped. In a compound whose conduction comes from the bismuth square net, that ratio sets the band filling, which is presumably why the superconductivity paper varies it.

basis: Five of the six samples are ErPdBi, the 1:1:1 stoichiometry of the half-Heusler structure -- three interpenetrating fcc sublattices with one of the four Heusler sites empty -- and the lead paper is titled Thermoelectric and thermophysical properties of ErPdX (X = Sb and Bi) half-Heusler compounds. [ref 2] gives ErBiPd F-43m (216) mp-1206953 at hull 0.000, with no ICSD reference, which is the expected space group. The sixth sample is ErPd2Bi, the 1:2:1 stoichiometry, which is the full Heusler with that fourth site occupied; it is a different structure and a different compound, so the host is flagged mixed and splits cleanly on the Pd:Er ratio. The two are closely related -- the paper on unusual features of erbium-based Heusler phases studies both -- but one label cannot cover them.

One composition, GdPdBi, across all six samples, and the lead paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties of Half-Heusler Type LaPdBi and GdPdBi. [ref 2] gives GdBiPd F-43m (216) mp-1076916 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY, the half-Heusler space group. This is the same RPdBi family as the Er host at rank 982 and has no second stoichiometry in it, so unlike that host it is not mixed. The 12-955 K window contains no structural transition for this family; the low-temperature end is where the antiferromagnetic ordering and the topological-semimetal behaviour of RPdBi are studied.

Every composition is Ge(Bi,Sb)4Te7 and the paper is titled Single-crystal growth and thermoelectric properties of Ge(Bi,Sb)4Te7. GeBi4Te7 is the n = 1, m = 2 member of the (GeTe)n(Bi2Te3)m series: a GeTe rocksalt block stacked with two Bi2Te3 quintuple layers, giving the P-3m1 twelve-layer cell. That is what the homologous_tetradymite entry covers, and its exemplar GeBi2Te4 is the neighbouring member of the same series. gst_homologous is the antimony-block sibling and is not used even though antimony is present here, because the Bi/(Bi+Sb) ratio runs from 0.25 to 0.80 with bismuth dominating in four of five compositions -- the blocks are Bi2Te3 with antimony substituting into them, not the other way round. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation site of the quintuple layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Bi/(Bi+Sb) over five compositions, median 0.75. Bismuth and antimony are isoelectronic and share the octahedral cation site of the Bi2Te3 blocks; the homologous stacking is unchanged along the axis, but the end members are GeBi4Te7 and GeSb4Te7 and the parent has to be assigned per composition.

basis: Five of the six samples are Mn0.85Bi2.1Te4, which is MnBi2Te4 with a little manganese-bismuth site mixing, and [ref 2] gives Mn(BiTe2)2 R-3m (166) mp-1077840 at hull 0.009 with 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY. MnBi2Te4 is the septuple-layer member of the (MnTe)(Bi2Te3)n series -- a MnTe rocksalt layer inserted into the middle of a Bi2Te3 quintuple layer -- so it belongs to the homologous tetradymite family rather than to tetradymite proper, which has no inserted block. The sixth composition is written Bi2MnTe5; no standard member of the series has that formula, so it is either a tellurium-rich variant or a transcription of one of the neighbouring members, and confidence is medium partly for that reason. The papers -- one on a new layered chalcogenide and its nanostructuring, one on the candidate antiferromagnetic topological insulator -- both concern the same septuple-layer compound. The manganese-bismuth antisite disorder recorded below is intrinsic to it and is the subject of the second paper.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn0.85Bi2.1Te4 rather than MnBi2Te4: manganese deficient and bismuth in excess by the same amount, which is manganese-bismuth antisite mixing, not a foreign dopant. It is intrinsic to the compound and controls both the carrier type and the magnetic order, which is what the chemistry paper on the candidate antiferromagnetic topological insulator examines. Manganese is a host element here, so this entry records the off-stoichiometry rather than a doping role.

basis: The compositions run Bi2Te(1-2)S(1-2) and the lead paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of the tetradymite-type Bi2Te2S-Sb2Te2S solid solution -- tetradymite is literally the mineral Bi2Te2S, so this host is the prototype compound rather than an analogue of it. [ref 2] confirms Bi2Te2S R-3m (166) mp-27910 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY, the quintuple-layer structure with sulfur ordered onto the central chalcogen site. The second paper studies the Bi2Te3-Bi2Se3-Bi2S3 system, and along the tellurium-sulfur line the tetradymite structure persists while the sulfur content rises; the sulfur-richer Bi2Te1S2 end approaches the limit of that solid solution, which is part of why the S/(S+Te) axis is recorded rather than a single parent. The other entries in the reference block -- Bi3Te2S at hull 0.168, R3m and C2/m settings of Bi2Te2S at hull 0.19 and 0.22 -- are ordering variants and computed alternatives, not phases reached on heating.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi2Te2S0.94Cl0.06. A halogen on a chalcogen site of a bismuth chalcogenide is the standard n-type donor -- the same role chlorine, bromine and iodine play in Bi2Te3 -- so this is genuine dilute doping rather than alloying.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Te) over six compositions, median 0.37. Sulfur and tellurium share the anion sites of the quintuple layer, but not equally: in ordered Bi2Te2S the sulfur takes the central site and tellurium the outer ones, so the axis is a site-ordering question as well as a composition one and the sulfur-rich end is where the tetradymite solid solution runs out.

basis: Three samples are CH3NH3PbI3 and three are the same with 1, 3 and 5 per cent BiI3 substituted into the lead iodide, from two papers on doping optimization of the organic-inorganic hybrid perovskite MAPbI3 and on bismuth doping-induced stable Seebeck effect in MAPbI3. The structure is the hybrid halide perovskite -- corner-sharing PbI6 octahedra with the methylammonium cation in the A cavity -- for which the taxonomy had no entry, so halide_perovskite_hybrid is proposed before use rather than filing it under the ABO3 oxide archetype. MAPbI3 has three settings of that one framework and the measured 30-401 K window crosses both boundaries: orthorhombic Pnma below about 162 K, tetragonal I4/mcm between about 162 and 327 K, cubic Pm-3m above about 327 K. All three are recorded as phases of the same prototype, in the same way the taxonomy handles the WO3 distortion series. The temperatures come from materials knowledge, not from the papers or the references, and both shift somewhat with bismuth content. [ref 2] returns only computed hydrogen-ordered approximants -- mp-995214 Pnma, mp-1194995 Aea2 and similar, each with one or no ICSD reference -- which freeze a cation that is really rotating, so no mp_id is recorded. Four of the six samples are films, where a setting can be held that bulk material would not keep.

dopant_roles.basis: (CH3NH3I)100(PbI2)(100-x)(BiI3)x for x = 1, 3 and 5, so bismuth enters on the lead site of the octahedral framework. Trivalent bismuth on a divalent site is a donor, and it is also isoelectronic with lead in the sense that both have a lone pair contributing to the band edges, which is why the paper reports a stabilised rather than merely shifted Seebeck coefficient.

basis: The composition is written W(CO)6, tungsten hexacarbonyl, which is a molecular precursor rather than a thermoelectric sample -- and the paper says so: it is titled Focused-Ion-Beam Direct-Writing of Ultra-Thin Superconducting Tungsten films. In focused-ion-beam deposition the W(CO)6 gas is decomposed by the beam and what lands is an amorphous tungsten-carbon-oxygen deposit, typically around half tungsten with the carbon and oxygen carried over from the ligands. So the measured material is amorphous, the composition string records the precursor stoichiometry rather than the deposit, and neither is a crystal. [ref 2] returns five computed W-C-O phases at hull 0.58 to 1.61, one flagged AMBIGUOUS and none with an ICSD reference -- hull values that high mean these are not real compounds -- so the reference block is disregarded and no mp_id is recorded. Confidence is medium because the amorphous state is inferred from how the samples were made rather than from a structural measurement.

dopant_roles.basis: The carbon of the six carbonyl ligands of the precursor. Some of it ends up in the deposit, but the amount in the composition string is the precursor formula rather than the measured film, so the number cannot be used as a composition.
The oxygen of the same carbonyl ligands, and the same caveat: the string describes W(CO)6 gas, not the tungsten-carbon film that was measured.

basis: All three compositions are ZnO with 14 to 24 per cent carbon and two of them also carry 2 per cent aluminium, from papers on ZnO/graphene oxide molecular hybrids and on orientation-dependent transport in ZnO. The oxide itself is wurtzite ZnO, which is unambiguous from the 1:1 Zn:O ratio, and the carbon is graphene oxide added as a second phase -- it is a hybrid, not a carbon-substituted oxide, since carbon does not enter the wurtzite lattice at anything like these levels. So the structure of the host is wurtzite and the carbon is a distinct phase alongside it; composite_multiphase is listed as an alternative for stage 2 rather than as the host label, because unlike the Bi2Te3/PEDOT:PSS host at rank 978 the matrix here is a single well-defined crystal and the additive is a two-dimensional filler at the grain boundaries. [ref 2] returns zinc carbonates -- ZnCO3 R-3c mp-9812 and relatives -- which is what the element set looks like to a database but not what was made, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn0.98Al0.02O in two of the three compositions. Trivalent aluminium on the divalent zinc site is the standard n-type donor in ZnO and the basis of AZO; at 2 at.% it is genuine dilute doping.

Graphene oxide added to form the hybrid, 14 to 24 per cent of the formula. It sits between ZnO grains rather than in the lattice, and it is deliberate rather than residue -- the point of the first paper is the ZnO/graphene-oxide interface. Carbon is a host element by the 5 at.% rule here, which is a case where the threshold routes a composite additive into the host key.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12, 15, 167]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: All three compositions are Nd(1-x)CaxCoO3 for x = 0.25, 0.375 and 0.5, and the paper is titled Transport and Magnetic Properties of R(1-x)AxCoO3 for R = La, Pr and Nd -- an ABO3 perovskite series with the rare earth partly replaced by an alkaline earth, orthorhombically tilted in the Pnma setting at these tolerance factors. I disagree with the reference: [ref 2] gives CaNdCoO4 I4mm (107) mp-1227058 at hull 0.044 as PRIMARY and flags it AMBIGUOUS, with a Cmcm alternative, but CaNdCoO4 is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper phase with four oxygens per cobalt, and every composition measured here has three. The reference describes a compound that exists in this chemistry, not the one these samples are, so the perovskite assignment is made on the composition and no mp_id is recorded. Calcium substitution is the hole-doping variable and drives the cobalt spin-state and metal-insulator behaviour the paper measures over 10-347 K; those are electronic transitions, not structural ones.

Four samples are CaCu3Ru4O12 and two are CaCu3Ti0.5Ru3.5O12, and one of the papers is titled Thermoelectric properties of the AA-prime-3B4O12-type ordered perovskite oxides -- which is this prototype by another name. The 1:3:4:12 stoichiometry is the A-site ordered perovskite in which calcium and copper order over the A sites in a 1:3 ratio, the copper taking square-planar coordination and the octahedral tilting becoming a fixed part of the structure; [ref 2] confirms CaCu3(RuO3)4 Im-3 (204) mp-6036 at hull 0.025 with 3 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is the right space group. This is the ruthenate member, a correlated metal, and its partner host at rank 992 is the titanate member; the two papers span both, which is how the pair should be read.

dopant_roles.basis: CaCu3Ti0.5Ru3.5O12, so titanium takes the octahedral B site from ruthenium. Both are tetravalent here, so it adds no carriers; what it does is dilute the Ru 4d band and push the compound from the itinerant towards the localised side, which is precisely the electronic phase transition between localized and itinerant states that the third paper studies across this pair of hosts.

basis: Three samples are CaCu3Ti4O12 and three are CaCu3Ti3.5Ru0.5O12, and [ref 2] gives CaTi4(CuO4)3 Im-3 (204) mp-22592 at hull 0.054 with 15 ICSD references as PRIMARY -- the best-attested entry in this whole chunk, and the compound the prototype is named for. CCTO is the giant-dielectric-constant A-site ordered perovskite; the thermoelectric paper on its conduction mechanism measures the same ceramic. The Im-3m entry at hull 0.430 with 1 ICSD reference is the untilted aristotype and is not a phase reached on heating within the 11-1072 K window -- the CuO4 square-planar coordination requires the tilt. This host is the titanate partner of the ruthenate at rank 991 and the two share two of their three papers.

other_polymorphs.note: CaTi4(CuO4)3 Im-3m at hull 0.430 with 1 ICSD reference, the untilted cubic aristotype of the A-site ordered structure. The square-planar copper coordination depends on the tilt, so this setting is not reached by heating.

dopant_roles.basis: CaCu3Ti3.5Ru0.5O12, the mirror image of the titanium substitution in the ruthenate host at rank 991. Ruthenium on the octahedral B site is isovalent with titanium but brings a partly filled 4d band, so it drives the insulating titanate towards the metallic ruthenate -- the substitution is the tuning axis between the two hosts rather than dilute doping.

basis: Every composition is Ca(1-x)EuxZn2Sb2 and the first paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties of Zintl Phase Compounds of Ca(1-x)EuxZn2Sb2. Both end members adopt the CaAl2Si2 structure -- trigonal P-3m1, with anionic Zn2Sb2 slabs of edge-sharing ZnSb4 tetrahedra separated by layers of the divalent cation -- and they form a complete solid solution, so the whole host is one prototype. The third paper on single parabolic band transport in p-type EuZn2Sb2 measures the x = 1 end of the same line. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation layer between the Zn2Sb2 slabs
solid_solution_axis.note: Eu/(Eu+Ca) over five compositions, spanning 0.3 to 0.7 with no end member measured. The chunk file did not flag this host as a solid-solution series because the detector pairs elements of the same periodic group and calcium and europium are not one; chemically they are interchangeable here, both divalent and of nearly equal ionic radius, which is why the solid solution is complete. The axis is recorded by hand for that reason, and stage 3 should treat neither element as a dopant.

basis: All five compositions are Ca5Ga2Sb6 or Ca5Ga(2-x)ZnxSb6, from the paper on improved thermoelectric properties in Zn-doped Ca5Ga2Sb6. The 5-2-6 Zintl stoichiometry builds chains of corner-sharing GaSb4 tetrahedra with Sb-Sb bonds between them, charge balanced by the calcium cations, and [ref 2] confirms Ca5(GaSb3)2 Pbam (55) mp-17985 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY -- the expected orthorhombic space group for this family. The second paper compares the aluminium, gallium and indium members of the same 5-2-6 structure, which is the family this prototype covers. The Ca11GaSb9 entry in the same block is a different Zintl compound of the same ternary, not a polymorph.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca5Ga(2-x)ZnxSb6 for x = 0.05 to 0.3. Zinc takes the gallium site inside the tetrahedral chain of the polyanion: divalent where gallium is trivalent, so it removes one electron per substitution from a charge-balanced Zintl phase and dopes it p-type. That is the standard way this family is tuned, and it is framework substitution in the structural sense even though the carrier effect is what the paper is after.

basis: One composition, KCa2Nb3O10, across all six samples, and the paper is titled Transport properties of Li intercalated KCa2Nb3O10. This is the n = 3 Dion-Jacobson layered perovskite: three-octahedron-thick Ca2Nb3O10 perovskite slabs with a single potassium layer between them, which is what makes the alkali exchangeable and the slab exfoliable and is exactly what the paper exploits by intercalating lithium. The taxonomy had no Dion-Jacobson entry -- ruddlesden_popper is the other layered-perovskite family, with offset slabs and a rocksalt double layer between them rather than a single alkali layer -- so dion_jacobson_perovskite is proposed before use. [ref 2] gives KCa2Nb3O10 Cmc2_1 (36) mp-1223594 at hull 0.012 but with no ICSD reference, so the composition is corroborated while the setting is not; the assignment rests on the formula and the paper title, both of which are unambiguous.

dopant_roles.basis: Lithium does not appear in any composition string but is the subject of the paper: it is intercalated into the interlayer gallery alongside or in place of the potassium, and the transport is measured as a function of how much went in. Recorded as interstitial because the guest enters an existing gallery rather than taking a lattice site; stage 3 should treat the intercalation level as a compositional variable of the interlayer, like x in NaxCoO2, not as doping on a perovskite site.

basis: Both compositions are CaV(0.6-0.7)Ti(0.3-0.4)O3, an ABO3 perovskite with calcium on the A site and vanadium and titanium sharing the octahedral B site. CaVO3 and CaTiO3 are both orthorhombically tilted perovskites in the Pnma setting and form a continuous solid solution, so the intermediate compositions measured here are one prototype throughout. The paper is an X-ray diffraction, magnetic and transport study of lattice instabilities in this series -- the instabilities in question are the tilt and orbital-ordering distortions within the perovskite framework and the metal-insulator crossover that comes with band filling as vanadium d1 is diluted by titanium d0, not a change of prototype -- so no phase sequence is recorded. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: octahedral B site
solid_solution_axis.note: Ti/(Ti+V) over the two compositions, 0.3 and 0.4. Titanium and vanadium are adjacent rather than same-group, so the chunk file did not flag this as a series, but both are tetravalent on the B site here and the substitution is isovalent -- what it changes is the d-electron count, from d1 towards d0, which is the point of the measurement. The recorded range covers only the two compositions in this host and is not the extent of the CaVO3-CaTiO3 solid solution.

basis: All three compositions are Ca(1-x)YbxZn2Sb2 for x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, and the first paper is the Snyder group Zintl phases paper on tuned transport in exactly this series. CaZn2Sb2 and YbZn2Sb2 both adopt the CaAl2Si2 structure -- trigonal P-3m1, anionic Zn2Sb2 slabs separated by the divalent cation layer -- and are mutually soluble, so the host is one prototype throughout. It is the ytterbium counterpart of the europium series at rank 993 and shares its second paper with it. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation layer between the Zn2Sb2 slabs
solid_solution_axis.note: Yb/(Yb+Ca) over three compositions, 0.25 to 0.75, with neither end member measured. As with the europium series at rank 993 the chunk file did not flag this because calcium and ytterbium are not the same periodic group; divalent ytterbium substitutes for calcium freely and the axis is recorded by hand. Ytterbium is the heavier of the two, so the substitution lowers the lattice thermal conductivity as well as shifting the band structure, which is what the tuned-transport paper is about.

basis: Every composition is Cu(1-x)CdxFe2O4 with x from 0.4 to 0.6, and the papers are on cadmium-substituted copper ferrites and on gadolinium-substituted Cu-Cd ferrites. AB2O4 ferrites are spinels: iron on the octahedral and tetrahedral sites of a cubic close-packed oxygen array, with copper and cadmium distributing between them -- cadmium strongly prefers the tetrahedral site, which is why substituting it inverts the cation distribution and changes the transport, the subject of the second paper. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded. One caveat worth carrying forward: CuFe2O4 is tetragonally distorted below about 700 K by the Jahn-Teller effect of Cu2+ and becomes cubic above it, which would fall inside the 305-687 K window, but cadmium substitution at 40 to 60 per cent of the A site suppresses the distortion, so no phase sequence is recorded. The distortion would not change the prototype in any case.

dopant_roles.basis: Cd0.4Cu0.6Fe1.9Gd0.1O4, from the paper on thermoelectric power in Gd3+-substituted Cu-Cd ferrites. Trivalent gadolinium replaces iron on the octahedral B site -- it is far too large for the tetrahedral one -- and being isovalent with Fe3+ it works through lattice distortion and magnetic dilution rather than by adding carriers.

basis: All six compositions are Cu(2.09-2.15)Cd(0.88-0.95)Ge(0.90-1.0)Se(4.0-4.09), which is Cu2CdGeSe4 with a few per cent excess copper, from the paper on the effect of copper addition on the thermoelectric properties of Cu2CdGeSe4. [ref 1] gives CdCu2GeSe4 I-42m (121) mp-10967 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references as PRIMARY -- the stannite structure, an ordered superstructure of sphalerite in which copper, cadmium and germanium fill the cation sites of a tetrahedral selenide framework. The Pc (7) entry in [ref 2] at hull 0.020 has no ICSD reference and is a computed lower-symmetry ordering variant, not a thermally reached phase. Note that this quaternary is the one the taxonomy calls A2BCX4, distinct from the BaAg2SnSe4-type 1-2-1-4 compounds proposed in chunk 019, where a large non-tetrahedral cation sits outside the framework.

dopant_roles.basis: Copper runs from 2.09 to 2.15 against the nominal 2.0 while cadmium and germanium fall slightly below 1.0 -- copper added on top of the stoichiometric quaternary, which is the variable the paper sweeps. Excess copper on cation antisites or interstitials is the hole-concentration knob in this family; it is off-stoichiometry of a host element, not a foreign dopant.

basis: Every composition is Cu(2.0-3.0)Cd(0.5-1.0)Sb(0.94-1.0)Se4 -- cadmium-substituted Cu3SbSe4 -- and the paper is titled The reduction of thermal conductivity in Cd and Sn co-doped Cu3SbSe4-based thermoelectrics. Cu3SbSe4 is famatinite, the I-42m tetragonal ordered sphalerite superstructure with copper and antimony on the cation sites, and cadmium substituting for copper leaves that framework intact. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded. Cadmium sits above the 5 at.% cut and so is part of the host key rather than a dopant candidate, but it is substitutional on the copper site throughout and reaches a quarter of it; the real doping variable in the set is tin.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb0.94Sn0.06 in three of the six compositions. Tin takes the antimony site of the famatinite framework; it is tetravalent where antimony is pentavalent, so each substitution removes an electron and dopes the compound p-type, which is the standard carrier-tuning route in Cu3SbSe4 and what the paper means by co-doping alongside cadmium.

basis: All three compositions are Hg(1-x)CdxTe with x between 0.175 and 0.212, the classic MCT infrared alloy, and the papers are on transport and the figure of merit of n-type Hg1-xCdxTe and on arsenic implantation into it. HgTe and CdTe are both zincblende and mutually soluble over the whole range, so the alloy is a single disordered F-43m phase with mercury and cadmium sharing the cation site. I disagree with the reference block here: [ref 2] returns only CdHg3Te4 P-43m, CdHg4Te5 Immm and CdHgTe2 R3m, which are computed cation-ordered superstructures of that same zincblende lattice at fixed rational Cd:Hg ratios. None of them is the phase measured -- a random solid solution at x = 0.2 has no long-range cation order -- and none carries an ICSD reference, so no mp_id is recorded rather than adopting an ordering the samples do not have.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral cation site of the zincblende lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: Cd/(Cd+Hg) across the three compositions. Cadmium sits above the 5 at.% cut because the cation site is only half the formula, so the host key carries both elements even though this is one narrow slice of a continuous alloy. The slice is the physically important one: x near 0.2 is where the gap closes to a few tens of meV, which is why these samples were measured from 18 to 300 K. Structure does not change along the axis, only the band gap.

basis: The single composition is Cd2Re2O7, an A2B2O7 pyrochlore with cadmium on the A site and the rhenium-oxygen octahedral network as the B framework, and all three papers name it as such. [ref 2] gives Cd2Re2O7 Fd-3m (227) mp-16783 at hull 0.044 with a single ICSD reference, which is the cubic aristotype and agrees with the assignment; the reference is thin, flagged weak by the chunk rules, but the compound is not in doubt. The 11-507 K window crosses the two structural transitions this material is known for and the third paper is titled after them, so they are recorded in phases even though no MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line was printed -- the taxonomy carries no phase_transitions for pyrochlore, so nothing flagged them automatically. Both are symmetry-lowering distortions of the pyrochlore framework rather than changes of prototype, in the same sense as the WO3 distortion series, and the mp_id is recorded only on the cubic phase because that is the only one the references contain.

Every composition is SrCd2Sb2 with sodium substituting for strontium from 0.1 to 2 per cent, and the paper is on manipulating hole concentration and band structure in SrCd2Sb2. The 1-2-2 stoichiometry with a divalent cation and a trielide-free pnictide framework is the CaAl2Si2 structure: trigonal P-3m1, corrugated Cd2Sb2 anionic slabs with strontium in the layer between them. [ref 2] confirms it directly, Sr(CdSb)2 P-3m1 (164) mp-7432 at hull 0.000. I disagree with [ref 1]: TEDesignLab supplies Sr11(CdSb2)6 C2/m (12) mp-3195, which is Sr11Cd6Sb12, a different Zintl compound at a different stoichiometry, not a polymorph of SrCd2Sb2, so the project precedence that would normally let TEDesignLab pick the polymorph does not apply -- it is not describing the same material.

dopant_roles.site: the divalent cation layer between the Cd2Sb2 slabs
dopant_roles.basis: Sr(1-x)NaxCd2Sb2 for x from 0.001 to 0.02. Monovalent sodium on a divalent site removes one electron per substitution and dopes the compound p-type; this is the hole manipulation of the title, and the series is a clean doping sweep of one element over five levels.

basis: Every composition is CeFe4P12 with lanthanum replacing part of the cerium. The 1-4-12 stoichiometry is the filled skutterudite: an Fe4P12 framework of corner-sharing octahedra with square P4 rings, and the rare earth in the icosahedral void that the binary skutterudite leaves empty. [ref 2] gives Ce(FeP3)4 Im-3 (204) mp-16272 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which is that structure and agrees. The I4/mmm entry beside it is CeFe2P2, a different compound in the same chemistry rather than a polymorph. Note the second paper is on CeFe4As12 rather than the phosphide -- the arsenide is the same prototype, so it does not change the assignment, but the host key does not contain arsenic and the sample count for this host should not be read as all-phosphide.

dopant_roles.site: the 2a icosahedral void of the Im-3 framework
dopant_roles.basis: Ce(1-x)LaxFe4P12 for x from 0.001 to 0.1. Lanthanum does not enter a new site: it dilutes the cerium already occupying the cage. The point of the series is that trivalent lanthanum has no f electron where cerium is mixed-valent, so the substitution turns the Kondo lattice off site by site while leaving the framework and the filling fraction untouched. Recorded as cage_filler rather than substitutional because the site it occupies is the structural cage, which is how stage 3 should treat its concentration.

basis: Three different compounds sit in this host and it has to be split. CeNiIn, four of the six samples and the subject of two of the papers on Kondo and valence-fluctuation behaviour, is the equiatomic RTX compound in the ZrNiAl structure, an ordered Fe2P derivative in P-62m; [ref 2] confirms it as CeInNi P-62m (189) mp-21492 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in the block. Ce2Ni2In is the R2T2X Mo2FeB2 type, ordered U3Si2, and [ref 2] gives Ce2InNi2 P4/mbm (127) mp-640108 at hull 0.000 to match. CeNi4In is the AB5-derived CaCu5 type with indium ordered onto one of the nickel sites, which I take from the RNi4In series rather than from the references -- the reference block contains no CeNi4In at all, only CeIn2Ni9, a different stoichiometry -- so that third prototype is the least secure of the three and sets the medium confidence for the record as a whole. The primary id is the ZrNiAl type because it carries two thirds of the samples.

The single composition is CeIrSi3 and the paper measures thermoelectric power in a single crystal of it. RTX3 cerium compounds of this kind adopt the BaNiSn3 structure, tetragonal I4mm, which is the non-centrosymmetric ordered variant of ThCr2Si2 -- the same layer stacking without the inversion centre, which is exactly why CeIrSi3 and CeRhSi3 are studied as non-centrosymmetric heavy-fermion superconductors under pressure. [ref 2] contains CeSi3Ir I4mm (107) mp-1068906 at hull 0.000 and agrees on both the composition and the setting, though with a single ICSD reference. The I4/mmm entry ranked above it is CeIr2Si2, a different compound rather than a polymorph, and is the sort of case where taking the highest ICSD count in the block instead of matching the formula would give the wrong structure.

Every composition is CeTiO3 or Ce(1-x)SrxTiO3, and the paper is on electronic states of perovskite-type titanates across a metal-insulator transition. ABO3 with a rare earth on the A site and titanium octahedrally coordinated is the perovskite prototype; at the cerium tolerance factor it is strongly tilted and orthorhombic, the GdFeO3 setting in Pnma, not cubic. I disagree with the reference block on that point: [ref 2] does return CeTiO3 but only as Pm-3m (221) mp-754524 at hull 0.087 with no ICSD reference, which is the untilted aristotype and is not what a cerium titanate adopts at any temperature in this window. The entries ranked above it -- Ce2Ti2O7 pyrochlore, CeTi2O6 and Ce2TiO5 -- are other compounds of the Ce-Ti-O system, not polymorphs of CeTiO3, and are a good illustration of a reference block describing a chemistry rather than a sample. No mp_id is recorded. CeTiO2.85 is the same perovskite with ordered or disordered oxygen vacancies; oxygen is a host element here so it is not listed as a dopant role, but the vacancy level is the carrier-concentration variable and stage 3 should read it that way.

dopant_roles.site: the 12-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: Ce(1-x)SrxTiO3 for x of 0.01, 0.02, 0.03 and 0.1. Divalent strontium on a trivalent A site removes an electron from the titanium t2g band, so the series walks the filling from the d1 Mott insulator towards the metal, which is the metal-insulator transition the paper is about. Strontium is a perfectly ordinary A-site substituent in a perovskite and does not disturb the framework.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62, 167, 221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12, 15]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: All six compositions are Ce(Pb(1-x)Snx)3 and the paper measures thermoelectric power across that series. CePb3 and CeSn3 both crystallise in the cubic AuCu3 structure, Pm-3m, cerium at the corners and the p-block element on the face centres, and they form a continuous solid solution, so the whole axis is one prototype. The chemistry is the reason the series was made: CeSn3 is an intermediate-valence compound and CePb3 an antiferromagnetic Kondo lattice, and the alloy moves between them without the lattice changing. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the 3c face-centre site of the AuCu3 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Pb/(Pb+Sn) as the chunk file reports it, spanning 0.20 to 0.90 with neither end member measured.
