Lead and tin are the same group and isovalent on this site, so the substitution is isoelectronic and the parent compound genuinely depends on the composition rather than on the host; every sample sits in the middle of the axis, which is where the valence crossover between the two end members happens.

basis: The compositions are (CuCl)x(Cu2Se)(1-x) mixtures and the paper is titled Electrical properties of molten CuCl-Cu2Se mixtures. The measured range is 1102-1453 K, which is above the melting point of both components -- copper chloride melts near 700 K and copper selenide near 1400 K, and the mixture is liquid across the whole window -- so there is no crystal structure to assign and the prototype is the non-crystalline melt entry. [ref 2] returns CuSe2Cl P2_1/c, a ternary solid that is neither of the two components and is not present at these temperatures; it is disregarded and no mp_id is recorded. Worth keeping visible for stage 2, which cannot resolve this host to a Materials Project entry and should not try.

Both papers embed sodium chloride in lead telluride to scatter phonons -- artificial nanostructures in one, embedded NaCl in the other -- so this host is a two-phase composite rather than a compound, with NaCl running from 0.12 to 0.64 formula units against the PbTe. It is assigned to rocksalt rather than to composite_multiphase because both phases are rocksalt: PbTe and NaCl are the same prototype with different cations, which makes the structural answer unambiguous even though the microstructure is not single-phase. The transport is carried by the PbTe matrix; the salt is a dispersed insulating inclusion, immiscible with it, which is the whole point of the design. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded. Sodium here is emphatically not the usual Na-for-Pb acceptor of doped PbTe -- it arrives as its chloride and stays as a separate phase -- which is why it sits above the 5 at.% cut and in the host key rather than in dopant_roles.

Every composition is Cu(12-x)CoxSb4S13 with x between 1.5 and 2, and all three papers say tetrahedrite outright -- Co substituted synthetic tetrahedrite, the mineral tetrahedrites Cu10Tr2Sb4S13 series, and the synthetic tetrahedrite performance paper. This is the cubic I-43m sulfosalt framework with the copper site split between trigonal-planar and tetrahedral coordination and the antimony lone pair pointing into the cage; cobalt takes the tetrahedral copper site. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded, but the assignment does not rest on the databases: x = 2 is the electron count at which the framework becomes a closed-shell semiconductor, which is why that stoichiometry recurs across the whole tetrahedrite family in this chunk.

Both compositions are Sr2.4Dy0.6Co2O(7-delta) and the paper names the phase in its title: the Sr2.4Dy0.6Co2O7 Ruddlesden-Popper phase. A3B2O7 is the n = 2 member -- two perovskite layers of cobalt-oxygen octahedra separated by a rocksalt AO double layer, with strontium and dysprosium sharing the A sites. The two compositions differ only in oxygen content, 5.90 against 6.67, which is the variable the paper sweeps. I disagree with [ref 2], which returns SrDyCoO4 Cmcm (63) mp-1218284 at hull 0.128 with no ICSD reference: that is the n = 1 member of the same family at a different cation ratio, so it supports the family but not the layer count, and taking its mp_id would assert the wrong n. No mp_id is recorded. Layered cobaltites at this oxygen deficiency order their vacancies into cobalt-oxygen polyhedra of mixed coordination, so stage 2 should expect a vacancy-ordered superstructure rather than the ideal 327 cell.

All six compositions are (NiyCo(1-y))xFe(3-x)O4 with x near 1 and the paper measures p-type transport in exactly that sintered series. AB2O4 ferrites are spinels: a cubic close-packed oxygen array with iron, nickel and cobalt distributed over the tetrahedral and octahedral cation sites, Fd-3m. Both NiFe2O4 and CoFe2O4 are inverse spinels and fully miscible, so the nickel-cobalt ratio changes the cation distribution and the transport without changing the prototype, and the deliberate off-stoichiometry in x -- 0.9, 1.0 and 1.1 against iron -- shifts the Fe2+/Fe3+ ratio on the octahedral site, which is what carries the hopping conduction. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

All three compositions are FexNiyCo(1-x-y)Sb3 with iron and nickel added in equal amounts, and the first paper is titled for that series. The MSb3 stoichiometry is the binary skutterudite framework, Im-3, corner-sharing octahedra enclosing square Sb4 rings, and the void stays empty here -- nothing in these compositions could fill it. Iron and nickel sit well above the 5 at.% cut and substitute directly for cobalt on the octahedral site; taking them in equal proportion is charge compensation, one electron short and one electron over, which keeps the compound near the semiconducting electron count while mass fluctuation on the metal site scatters phonons. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

The single composition is Ce0.09Fe0.67Co3.33Sb12(FeSb2.1Te)4 and both the curator note and the paper title say what it is: a multilayer of thin equidistant layers of Ce0.09Fe0.67Co3.33Sb12 against FeSb2Te. That is two distinct structures stacked, not one compound -- a lightly cerium-filled iron-substituted skutterudite on one side and an FeSb2-based marcasite with tellurium substituted onto the antimony site on the other -- so the record is a composite and the two constituents are carried in alt_prototype_ids. Splitting by composition cannot separate them because both are inside every sample; separating them needs the layer, not the formula. No reference entry exists for this host and no mp_id is recorded. Stage 2 should resolve the two constituents separately rather than looking for a single Materials Project entry for the parsed formula, which describes no real phase.

dopant_roles.site: the 2a icosahedral void of the skutterudite constituent
dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.09 against Co4Sb12, a filling fraction of nine per cent in the skutterudite layers only -- it has nothing to do with the FeSb2Te layers. The iron substitution on the cobalt site is what makes room for it: each Fe-for-Co takes an electron out, and the cerium guest puts it back while rattling in the cage. Its apparent dilution to under 5 at.% is an artefact of averaging over both layers of the multilayer, so stage 3 must not compute its level against the whole formula.

basis: The series is Fe(2-2x)Co2xTiSn, named as such in the first paper, running from Fe1.8Co0.2TiSn to the equiatomic point. Fe2TiSn is the cubic full Heusler, Fm-3m, two interpenetrating iron sublattices with titanium and tin ordering on the remaining sites, and cobalt substitutes for iron across the series. At the equiatomic composition, which two of the six compositions reach -- written both as FeCoTiSn and as CoFeTiSn -- the four sublattices carry four different elements, and if iron and cobalt order onto their own sites rather than sharing one, the structure becomes the LiMgPdSn-type quaternary Heusler in F-43m. The second paper is explicitly about the quaternary Heusler, so both descriptions are present in this host and it is marked mixed rather than forced to one. The split is by composition and it is sharp: only the 1:1 members can be quaternary. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

Every composition is Co4Sb12 with germanium substituted onto the antimony framework and a guest in the void: In0.5Co4Sb11Ge1 in one paper, Yb0.46-0.65Co4Ge~1Sb~11 in the other, which is titled Yb-filled Ge-compensated CoSb3. The framework is the skutterudite Im-3 lattice throughout and the filling is the point of both papers, so the filled entry is the right one rather than the binary. Germanium sits above the 5 at.% cut in these formulas and so appears in the host key; structurally it is a framework substitution on the Sb4 ring, tetravalent against antimony pentavalent, which compensates the electrons the filler donates -- the compensation named in the title. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.site: the 2a icosahedral void
dopant_roles.basis: Yb0.46 to Yb0.65 per Co4Sb12, a partial filling of the cage rather than a substitution on any framework site. Ytterbium is the heavy rattler that suppresses the lattice thermal conductivity and donates electrons; the germanium co-substitution is there to take those electrons back.

dopant_roles.site: the 2a icosahedral void
dopant_roles.basis: In0.5Co4Sb11Ge1. Indium fills the same void as ytterbium does in the companion compositions. It is a small filler for the cage and is known to partly form InSb secondary phase at higher nominal loadings, but at 0.5 per formula unit it is taken as occupying the void.

basis: Every composition is HfCoSb with tin substituted for part of the antimony, some with titanium or zirconium on the hafnium site, and all three papers say half-Heusler in their titles. HfCoSb is the 18-electron F-43m half Heusler, one of the four fcc sublattices left empty, and it is the standard p-type member of the family. Tin at 0.2 to 0.3 of the antimony site is the acceptor that makes it p-type, and the phase separation the first paper tunes is within the (Ti,Zr,Hf) cation sublattice, not a change of prototype. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.site: the group 4 cation site of the half-Heusler cell
dopant_roles.basis: Ti0.15Hf0.85 and Hf0.9Ti0.1. Titanium is isovalent with hafnium and adds no carriers; it is there for the mass and size contrast, which scatters phonons and drives the nanoscale phase separation the first paper is about. Its sublattice fraction is 0.1 to 0.15, far above dilute, so it is an alloying substitution rather than doping even though the whole-formula fraction falls under the 5 per cent cut.

dopant_roles.site: the group 4 cation site of the half-Heusler cell
dopant_roles.basis: Zr0.10Hf0.90CoSb0.7Sn0.3, one composition. Same role as titanium: isovalent on the same site, contributing mass contrast rather than carriers. Zirconium and hafnium are nearly identical in size, so this one mainly changes the mass.

basis: Both papers are on CoSb3-based skutterudites -- Co(4-x)MnxSb(12-y)Sny in one, calcium-filled CoSb3 in the other -- and every composition keeps the Sb12 or Sb(12-y)Sny framework with manganese substituting for cobalt on the octahedral site. Two of the six carry Ca0.3 in the icosahedral void, so the filled entry stands as the alternative and the host is marked mixed; the split is by composition and is unambiguous, since the calcium is either present or not. I disagree with [ref 2] here, which returns only MnCoSb in half-Heusler and Heusler settings -- P4/nmm, Fm-3m, F-43m -- at the 1:1:1 and 1:2:1 stoichiometries. Those are real compounds of the Co-Mn-Sb system but they are not what these samples are: the formulas carry twelve antimony atoms to four metal ones, which is the skutterudite ratio, and the papers name it. This is the reference block describing a chemistry rather than a sample, and no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.site: the 2a icosahedral void
dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.3 in two compositions, from the paper on calcium-filled CoSb3-based skutterudites. Calcium is a light, cheap filler that donates two electrons and rattles in the void; its presence is what makes those two compositions filled skutterudites rather than binary ones.

dopant_roles.site: the 24g antimony ring site
dopant_roles.basis: Sb(11.6-11.8)Sn(0.2-0.4) in two compositions. Tin on the antimony ring is tetravalent against pentavalent, so it removes electrons and compensates the manganese substitution on the metal site; it is a framework substituent that sets the carrier count, not a rattler.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [129, 216, 225]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: All three compositions are (Zr,Nb)(Ni,Co)Sn at matched ratios -- 0.25/0.75, 0.5/0.5, 0.75/0.25 -- and the paper is on solid solution behaviour and thermoelectric properties of half-Heusler alloys. The two end members ZrNiSn and NbCoSn are both 18-electron half Heuslers in F-43m, and the coupled substitution of niobium for zirconium with cobalt for nickel keeps the electron count at 18 all the way across, which is exactly why the two cation sites are varied together rather than independently. It is one prototype with a continuous solid solution between two members of it. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the 4b cation site of the half-Heusler cell, varied jointly with Ni/Co on the 4c site
solid_solution_axis.note: Nb/(Nb+Zr) over the three compositions, mirrored by Co/(Co+Ni) at the same fractions. This is not an isoelectronic axis in the usual sense -- niobium has one electron more than zirconium and cobalt one fewer than nickel -- but the two substitutions are made in lockstep so that the total stays at the 18-electron semiconducting count. Stage 3 should treat the pair as a single compositional variable, not as two independent dopants.

basis: All three papers add zinc oxide to a cobalt antimonide skutterudite as a second phase -- embedded ZnO, ZnO inclusions, ZnO nano-inclusions -- and the curator records the samples as a mixture. The oxide is not a dopant here: the compositions put it at 31 to 42 weight or mole per cent against the skutterudite, so both phases are structurally present in quantity and the sample has two prototypes at once, wurtzite ZnO dispersed in a skutterudite matrix that is itself indium-filled in half the compositions. It cannot be split by composition because both phases are in every sample. I disregard [ref 2], which returns Zn3Co4(SbO6)2 P-1 with no ICSD reference: that is a quaternary oxide the reference block found by element matching, and nothing in these papers makes one. No mp_id is recorded. This is the case the project README warns about from the other direction -- normally a composite additive must not be allowed to relabel its host, but here the additive is too abundant to call an inclusion in a single-phase material.

dopant_roles.site: the 2a icosahedral void of the skutterudite constituent
dopant_roles.basis: In0.2Co4Sb12 in two compositions. Indium fills the skutterudite cage and is the standard n-type filler for this matrix; it has nothing to do with the zinc oxide phase. Its whole-formula fraction falls under 5 per cent only because the oxide dilutes the denominator, so stage 3 must compute its level against Co4Sb12 alone.

basis: All six compositions are Co(1-x)RuxSb2 and the paper is on structural and electrical properties of exactly that series. MSb2 with antimony pairs is the marcasite family. The two end members differ only by a distortion within it: RuSb2 is the undistorted orthorhombic marcasite in Pnnm, while CoSb2 is the monoclinic arsenopyrite variant in P2_1/c, where the extra d electron drives metal-metal pairing along the octahedral chain and doubles the cell. Substituting ruthenium for cobalt walks the compound from one setting to the other, which is the structural half of what the paper reports. The taxonomy has no separate arsenopyrite entry and does not need one -- its cosbs_paracostibite entry already describes the marcasite and arsenopyrite as one family -- so the whole series is filed under marcasite, with the distortion recorded here rather than as a second prototype. FeSb2, the colossal-Seebeck member named in the taxonomy entry, is the same structure. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the octahedral metal site of the marcasite chain
solid_solution_axis.note: Ru/(Ru+Co) over the six compositions, 0.2 to 0.7, with neither end member measured. Cobalt and ruthenium are not the same group, so the chunk file did not flag this as a series, and the substitution is not isoelectronic -- it is the d-electron count that decides whether the lattice pairs its metal atoms, so this axis changes the space group even though it does not change the prototype.

basis: Co2TiSn carries four of the six samples and two of the three papers, both on the half-metallic ferromagnet Co2TiZ family. It is the cubic full Heusler in Fm-3m, and [ref 2] agrees emphatically: TiCo2Sn Fm-3m (225) mp-21467 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references, the strongest entry in the block. But CoTiSn at 1:1:1 is the half Heusler, F-43m with one of the four sublattices vacant, which [ref 2] also carries as TiCoSn F-43m (216) mp-1216949 with 2 ICSD references, and the third composition TiCo1.5Sn sits between the two -- the half-Heusler lattice with its vacant site half occupied by cobalt, which is how these two structures interconvert. So the host holds both prototypes and splits cleanly on the Co:Ti ratio. The P4/mmm TiCo2Sn entry at hull 0.143 with no ICSD reference is a computed tetragonal variant, not a phase these samples reach.

Both compositions are Cr2Ge2Te6 and the first paper is titled for it. This is the M2X2Te6 layered van der Waals telluride the taxonomy entry describes, rhombohedral R-3: honeycomb sheets of chromium octahedra with Ge-Ge dimers standing in the honeycomb centres, stacked with no bonding between the slabs. [ref 2] gives CrGeTe3 R-3 (148) mp-1078220 at hull 0.005 with 4 ICSD references, the same structure written at half the formula unit, and agrees. The taxonomy entry names silicon in its formula archetype with the exemplar Sb2Si2Te6; germanium substitutes for silicon in the dimer without changing anything else, and Cr2Ge2Te6 is in fact the parent the family is named after, so this is a straightforward member rather than a stretch. The second paper measures the low thermal conductivity that follows from the soft interlayer bonding, and both are worth reading against the ferromagnetic ordering near 60 K, which falls inside the measured window but is magnetic rather than structural.

Both compositions are Mn3CuN, written once in each order, and the second paper is titled for the antiperovskite carbides and nitrides. The structure inverts the perovskite: nitrogen at the body centre, manganese on the face centres and copper at the corners, cubic Pm-3m. [ref 2] returns Mn3CuN Pm-3m (221) mp-1070242 with 1 ICSD reference and agrees on the structure; its hull energy of 1.908 eV per atom is not a statement about the compound but an artefact of referencing a nitride against elemental nitrogen in the 2019 dump, and should not be read as instability. A magnetostructural cubic-to-tetragonal distortion is reported near 140 K in stoichiometric Mn3CuN, which would fall inside the 13-347 K window, but it is strongly suppressed by the nitrogen deficiency that the first paper varies -- its films are Mn3CuNy -- and it lowers the symmetry without changing the prototype, so it is noted here rather than recorded as a phase sequence. That same suppression is what flattens the resistivity and gives the nearly zero temperature coefficient of the second title.

Every composition is Cu(12-x)MnxSb4S13 with x from 1.5 to 1.8, and all three papers name tetrahedrite, one of them specifically a manganese-substituted synthetic tetrahedrite. The cubic I-43m sulfosalt framework is unchanged by the substitution; manganese takes the tetrahedral copper site, as cobalt, nickel and zinc do in the neighbouring hosts of this chunk. [ref 2] gives Mn2Cu10Sb4S13 I-42m (121) mp-1222021 at hull 0.032 with no ICSD reference, which is the same framework computed with the manganese ordered onto one particular copper site -- the ordering lowers I-43m to its I-42m subgroup. The real samples have manganese distributed over the site rather than ordered, so the parent symmetry is the right description and no mp_id is recorded.

Both compositions are Cu(12-x)NixSb4S13 at x = 1.5 and 2, and all four papers are tetrahedrite papers, including one on co-doping to raise the figure of merit. Same cubic I-43m framework as the cobalt, manganese and zinc hosts alongside it, with nickel on the tetrahedral copper site. I disagree with [ref 2], which returns CuNiSbS3 P2_12_12_1 (19) mp-1191203: that is a quaternary orthorhombic sulfide at a completely different stoichiometry -- one antimony to three sulfurs rather than four to thirteen -- and is not a tetrahedrite at all. The reference block matched on elements, not on formula, and adopting it would discard the structure the papers actually report. No mp_id is recorded.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [217], ICSD-backed references for this host report [19]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions are Cu(12-x)ZnxSb4S13 at x = 1.5 and 2, and the papers are the earth-abundant tetrahedrite performance paper and the synthetic and mineral tetrahedrite series. Zinc-bearing tetrahedrite is the mineral sphalerite-free end of that series and is the best studied substitution in the family, because zinc is divalent and fills the tetrahedral copper site cleanly, driving the framework to the closed-shell electron count at x = 2. [ref 2] gives Zn2Cu10Sb4S13 I-42m (121) mp-1215797 at hull 0.042 with no ICSD reference; as in the manganese host, that is the I-43m framework with the substituent ordered onto one site, so it corroborates the structure while describing a cation order the samples do not have. No mp_id is recorded.

All six compositions are DyxGd(5-x)Si2Ge2 and both papers are on that series. The 5-2-2 stoichiometry is the R5T4 slab family the taxonomy entry describes: two-dimensional slabs of rare earth and tetrelide joined by Si-Ge dimer bonds that break and reform at the transition, which is what makes these compounds giant magnetocaloric and what the second paper means by a martensitic transition. Dysprosium and gadolinium are both trivalent and interchangeable on the rare-earth sites, so the whole axis is one prototype. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded. The 19-299 K window crosses the magnetostructural transition for every composition in the series, so the two settings are recorded in phases even though no MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line was printed -- but see the note there, because the temperature moves by two hundred kelvin along the dysprosium axis and no single value describes the host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the rare-earth sites of the R5T4 slabs
solid_solution_axis.note: Dy/(Dy+Gd) as the chunk file reports it, 0.20 to 0.90. The two are isovalent and the substitution does not change the prototype, but it moves the magnetostructural transition hard: Gd5Si2Ge2 orders near 275 K and the dysprosium-rich members near 70 K. The 200 K written into the phases array is a placeholder midpoint chosen so the sequence is not left without one, not a measured or even a representative value, and both phase entries are marked low confidence for that reason. Whoever reads these papers should replace it per composition.

basis: Every composition is EuxNbO3 with x between 0.68 and 0.90 and a slight oxygen excess, and the paper is titled Electrical properties of divalent europium niobium bronzes. That is the perovskite-type bronze: the NbO3 corner-sharing octahedral framework with the A site only partly occupied by europium, the niobium taking mixed valence to balance it, exactly as sodium does in NaxWO3. The taxonomy entry covers this under its AxMO3 archetype and cubic bronze space group, so no new prototype is needed, but the entry conflates two different frameworks -- the tetragonal tungsten bronze of its exemplar Sr0.5Ba0.5Nb2O6 has pentagonal and triangular tunnels and is not the same thing as a cation-deficient perovskite. This host belongs to the second branch, and the confusion is worth resolving when the taxonomy is folded into v4. [ref 2] gives EuNbO3 Imma (74) mp-1078341 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which is the fully occupied stoichiometric end of the series in a tilted setting; it supports the framework but not the vacancy level that makes these samples bronzes, so no mp_id is recorded. Confidence is medium because the assignment turns on which branch of a mixed taxonomy entry this is, not because the structure is in doubt.

Every composition is PbxEu(2-x)Ru2O7 and the paper is titled for the metal-insulator crossover in Pb-Ru based oxides with pyrochlore-type structure. A2B2O7 with the ruthenium-oxygen octahedral network as the B framework and the large cations on the A site is the pyrochlore prototype, Fd-3m. The series is instructive as to why it was made: Pb2Ru2O7 is metallic with lead nominally divalent and the ruthenium pushed to mixed valence, while Eu2Ru2O7 with trivalent europium is a Mott insulator, so walking the A site from one to the other walks the compound across the transition the title names. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the 16d A site of the pyrochlore lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: Pb/(Pb+Eu) over the six compositions, 0.3 to 0.7 of the A site. This axis is not isoelectronic and must not be treated as one: lead enters as Pb2+ and europium as Eu3+, so the substitution changes the ruthenium valence and the band filling, which is the whole mechanism of the metal-insulator crossover. Recorded here because the chunk file does not flag non-isovalent pairs.

basis: The host is RbMnF3 with four samples carrying a few tenths of a per cent of another cation, and the paper measures thermal conductivity of antiferromagnetic RbMnF3 from 10 to 41 K. Fluoride perovskites are the textbook undistorted case: rubidium is large enough that the tolerance factor sits almost exactly at one, so RbMnF3 stays cubic Pm-3m down to the lowest temperatures with no octahedral tilting, which is precisely why it is the model isotropic Heisenberg antiferromagnet these measurements are about. I disagree with [ref 2], which returns Rb2MnF6, RbMnF4, Rb2MnF5, Rb2MnF4 and Rb3MnF7 and no RbMnF3 at all: those are the higher fluorides and layered phases of the Rb-Mn-F system, reflecting a manganese oxidation state above two, and none is a polymorph of the samples here. No mp_id is recorded. The measured window lies below and across the 83 K Neel temperature, which is magnetic rather than structural and is not recorded as a phase.

dopant_roles.site: the 12-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: (RbMnF3)90K10 -- ten parts of potassium against ninety of the host, written as a mixture rather than a formula. Potassium is isovalent with rubidium and merely smaller, so it perturbs the tolerance factor rather than the carrier count. In a thermal conductivity experiment at 10-41 K that is the point: a substituted cation is a point-mass defect that scatters phonons.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: (RbMnF3)99.69Ni0.31. A few tenths of a per cent of a divalent 3d cation on the manganese site -- an isovalent magnetic impurity, again a phonon and magnon scatterer rather than a carrier dopant. The same reading applies to the cobalt and iron samples.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: (RbMnF3)99.82Co0.18. Isovalent divalent impurity on the manganese site, at 0.18 per cent.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: (RbMnF3)99.81Fe0.19. Isovalent divalent impurity on the manganese site, at 0.19 per cent.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62, 167, 221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [225, 14]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: This host key is a parsing accident and the curator note says so: FP stands for fission product, not fluorine and phosphorus. The compositions are (UO2+x)(FP O2+x) and the paper is on the effect of oxidation on the thermal conductivity of (U,M)O2 pellets -- uranium dioxide nuclear fuel carrying simulated fission-product cations, measured to 2090 K. Uranium dioxide is the fluorite prototype, Fm-3m, a cubic uranium lattice with oxygen filling every tetrahedral hole, and it stays fluorite as it takes up excess oxygen into interstitial clusters, which is the hyperstoichiometry the paper varies from UO2.0 to UO2.2. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, unsurprisingly, since the element set is not real. No mp_id is recorded. The host key should be corrected upstream rather than annotated around, and both spurious elements are recorded as parse artefacts below so that stage 3 does not compute a doping level for them.

dopant_roles.basis: The F of the curator abbreviation FP, fission product. There is no fluorine in these pellets; the parser read a two-letter placeholder as two element symbols.

The P of the curator abbreviation FP, fission product. There is no phosphorus in these pellets. What the placeholder actually stands for is a mixture of lanthanide and transition-metal cations substituting on the uranium site of the fluorite lattice, which is what the (U,M)O2 of the paper title means.

basis: This host holds two layered iron oxide families and has to be split. Four of the six compositions are GdSr(1+x)Gd(1-x)FeO4 written as GdSrFeO4 through Gd0.7Sr1.3FeO4 -- the A2BO4 ratio, which is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper member, a single layer of iron-oxygen octahedra between rocksalt AO layers, and the second paper is on the structural and physical effect of increasing strontium content in exactly that series. The other two are ABO3 at Gd0.33Sr0.67FeO3 and Gd0.5Sr0.5Fe0.8Cu0.2O3, ordinary orthorhombically tilted perovskites, and the first and third papers treat them as such -- small-polaron hopping in Gd1/3Sr2/3FeO3 and a cobalt-free perovskite cathode. The split is by the A:B ratio and is sharp. [ref 2] returns Sr2Gd(FeO3)3 and SrGd2(FeO3)3, neither of which has an ICSD reference and neither of which is at either stoichiometry measured here, so no mp_id is recorded. Confidence is medium because the primary id rests on a four-to-two composition count with one sample each, not on a real majority of the transport data.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Gd0.5Sr0.5Fe0.8Cu0.2O3, from the cobalt-free perovskite cathode paper, where copper is substituted for iron on the B site to raise the electronic conductivity and lower the sintering temperature without using cobalt. At a fifth of the B site this is a substantial alloying substitution rather than dilute doping; it sits under the 5 at.% cut only because the perovskite formula has five atoms.

basis: Five of the six samples are FeGe1.52 or the same thing written as Fe39.5-39.8Ge60.2-60.5, and the curator note spells out the equivalence -- gamma = 1.52, nearly equal to Fe39.7Ge60.3. A transition metal with a tetrel at a ratio near 1:1.5, written with a non-integer gamma, and a paper titled for glass-like lattice thermal conductivity is the Nowotny chimney-ladder signature: the metal atoms form a fourfold helix, the germanium atoms a second helix with an independent and incommensurate repeat, and the mismatch between the two is what makes the thermal conductivity glass-like. The composition is Fe2Ge3 in integer form. The sixth sample is stoichiometric FeGe from a thin-film magnetotransport paper, which is a different structure -- the cubic B20 phase, the helimagnet, and the taxonomy has an entry for it -- so the host is marked mixed. I part company with [ref 2] on both counts: its primary FeGe2 I4/mcm with 9 ICSD references is the CuAl2-type compound at a different composition, and its FeGe P6/mmm with 5 references is the B35 hexagonal polymorph rather than the B20 one that films grow in. The chimney-ladder phase is simply absent from the 2019 snapshot. No mp_id is recorded, and confidence is medium because the chimney-ladder identification comes from the gamma notation and the paper title rather than from any reference entry.

other_polymorphs.occurrence: FeGe2 in the CuAl2 type is the best-attested Fe-Ge compound in Materials Project with 9 ICSD references, but it sits at a different composition from anything measured here. It is listed so that a later reader does not mistake it for the phase these samples are, and it is not reached by heating them.

basis: The single composition is (Si0.8Ge0.2P0.02)0.9(FeSi2)0.1 and both the paper title and the curator note describe it the same way: a multiphase nanostructure of phosphorus-doped Si0.8Ge0.2 with ten atomic per cent of Fe0.98Co0.02Si2 added. Two prototypes are present at once -- the diamond-cubic silicon-germanium matrix that carries the transport, and beta-FeSi2 as a dispersed second phase whose purpose is to scatter phonons and, at ten per cent, to be structurally significant rather than an impurity. It cannot be split by composition, since both are in every sample. I disregard [ref 2], which returns FeSiGe Cmce at hull 0.149 with one ICSD reference: a ternary line compound the reference block found by element matching, which is not what a silicide dispersed in SiGe forms. No mp_id is recorded. Note that the cobalt the curator records in the silicide is not in the parsed formula at all.

dopant_roles.site: the diamond-cubic lattice site of the SiGe matrix
dopant_roles.basis: P0.02 per SiGe formula unit. Phosphorus is the standard n-type donor in silicon-germanium, one electron per substitution, and it is what makes this an n-type material as the title says. It belongs to the matrix phase only, not to the silicide, so stage 3 should compute its level against the SiGe fraction rather than the whole formula.

basis: Every composition is Sm(1-x)SrxFeO3 with various substitutions on both sites, and the papers are on Ln0.5M0.5FeO3 perovskite characterisation, on La1-xSrxFeO3-type conductors and on a dual-phase ceramic membrane -- all perovskite ferrite work. ABO3 with a rare earth and an alkaline earth sharing the A site and iron octahedrally coordinated on the B site is the perovskite prototype, orthorhombically tilted at these tolerance factors and oxygen-deficient at the stated half-and-half A-site charge, which is what the delta in the paper titles refers to. [ref 2] returns Sr3Sm(FeO4)2 Amm2 at hull 0.018 with no ICSD reference, a Ruddlesden-Popper-related phase at a different stoichiometry from anything measured here, so no mp_id is recorded. The measured range reaches 1173 K, well into the region where these ferrites lose oxygen reversibly and the vacancies can order into a brownmillerite superstructure; that is a real possibility at the top of the window but it is not reported in these titles and is not recorded as a phase.

dopant_roles.site: the 12-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: La0.05Sm0.45Sr0.32Ba0.18FeO3. Barium is divalent like the strontium it joins, so it adds no carriers beyond what the strontium already does; it is there for its size, which raises the tolerance factor and reduces the octahedral tilting. At 0.18 of the A site this is alloying, not doping.

dopant_roles.site: the 12-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: La0.05 in the same composition. Trivalent and isovalent with samarium, differing only in size; the paper series compares lanthanum, neodymium and samarium at this site.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Sm0.6Sr0.4Co0.2Fe0.8O3. Cobalt on the iron site at a fifth of the B site -- a substantial alloying substitution that raises both the electronic conductivity and the oxygen mobility, and the reason the companion paper advertises a cobalt-free alternative.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Sm0.5Sr0.5Fe0.8Cu0.2O3, the cobalt-free cathode composition, the same one that appears in the gadolinium host at rank 1034. Copper substitutes for iron on the B site.

dopant_roles.site: the 12-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: Sm0.5Sr0.45K0.05FeO3. Monovalent potassium on a site otherwise shared by trivalent and divalent cations removes further electrons, so unlike the other four this one genuinely changes the carrier count -- an acceptor that pushes the iron valence higher or creates more oxygen vacancies.

basis: The single composition is Fe2TiSi and the papers name it: experimental realisation of a semiconducting full-Heusler compound, and thermoelectric properties of single-phase full-Heusler Fe2TiSi films. X2YZ with two iron sublattices interpenetrating the titanium and silicon ones is the cubic full Heusler in Fm-3m, and the interest in this particular member is that at 24 valence electrons it has a gap, unlike the metallic Heuslers around it. [ref 2] carries it as TiFe2Si Fm-3m (225) mp-866141 at hull 0.000, which agrees on both formula and setting, although with no ICSD reference -- the compound is difficult to make in bulk, which is exactly why two of the six samples are films and why the first paper frames itself as a realisation. The other entries in the block, TiFeSi2 and TiFeSi, are different compounds of the same three elements and would be the wrong answer. No mp_id is recorded. The film flag is worth carrying: the bulk samples may well contain the competing TiFeSi phases while the films need not.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [55, 46]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The single composition is La2Ga6Ge40 and the paper is titled Hosting of La3+ guest ions in type-I Ge clathrates. The framework count is the giveaway: 6 gallium plus 40 germanium is 46 atoms, which is exactly the type-I clathrate cage framework of two dodecahedra and six tetrakaidecahedra per cell, with the lanthanum guests filling 2 of the 8 available cages. Gallium substitutes into the framework rather than sitting in a cage, and at 6 per 46 it balances the 3 electrons each of the 2 trivalent guests donates. Gallium is above the 5 at.% cut and so lands in the host key, which is why this host reads as a gallium-germanium binary when it is really a filled clathrate. I disregard [ref 2], which returns Ga3Ge, GaGe and GaGe3 in various settings at hulls from 0.09 to 0.26: those are hypothetical binary orderings, none with an ICSD reference, and none of them is a clathrate. No mp_id is recorded. Note that the paper is first-principles, so nothing here is even a synthesised sample, let alone a confirmed structure.

dopant_roles.site: the 2a and 6d cages of the type-I framework
dopant_roles.basis: La2 per Ga6Ge40, so 2 guests in the 8 cages of the cell -- a partial filling, and the quantity the paper computes. Lanthanum here is the rattler and the electron donor, not a substituent: it never takes a framework site. Its whole-formula fraction of 4 per cent puts it under the cut and out of the host key, which for a clathrate is misleading, since the guest is the reason the compound exists.

basis: Every composition is Re6GaxSeyTe(15-y) and the paper sweeps exactly that formula. Six rhenium atoms to fifteen chalcogens is the Re6Ch15 cluster compound the taxonomy entry describes, with its exemplar Re6Se4Te10 sitting in the middle of this very series: octahedral Re6 clusters capped and bridged by chalcogen, packed as discrete units in Pbca, which is why the lattice thermal conductivity is so low. Gallium enters as an additional cation between the clusters and is above the 5 at.% cut, so it appears in the host key; the series varies it from 1.5 to 2 alongside the selenium-tellurium ratio. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the capping and bridging chalcogen sites of the Re6 cluster
solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) as the chunk file reports it, 0.16 to 0.50, never reaching the selenide end. The two are isovalent and interchangeable on the chalcogen positions, though not necessarily at random: in Re6Se4Te10 the lighter chalcogen prefers the sites capping the cluster face over the ones bridging between clusters, so the sublattice fraction alone does not say which site is being filled. Stage 2 should expect site preference rather than a uniform mix.

basis: Five of the six samples are R5T4 compounds -- Gd5(Si0.1Ge0.9)4 in four and Gd5Ge4 in one -- which is the slab intermetallic family the taxonomy entry describes, with Gd5Ge4 in the germanium-rich Sm5Ge4 setting of Pnma. [ref 2] supports it directly: Gd5Ge4 Pnma (62) mp-1198083 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references, the strongest entry in the block. The sixth sample is Gd5Ge3, a different prototype at a different stoichiometry -- the hexagonal Mn5Si3 D88 type -- and the first paper is titled for the RE5X3 compounds, so the host is marked mixed and splits cleanly on the Ge:Gd ratio. The third paper measures thermopower near the martensitic transition, which in this family is the shear between the two orthorhombic settings where the Si-Ge dimer bonds between slabs break and reform. It is a distortion within the prototype and both settings are Pnma, so recording it as a phase sequence would add a temperature and nothing else; since no paper here states that temperature, it is described rather than recorded.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrel sites of the R5T4 slabs, including the interslab dimer
dopant_roles.basis: Gd5(Si0.1Ge0.9)4 -- a tenth of the tetrel site, which is far from dilute even though it falls under the 5 at.% whole-formula cut, since the tetrel site is only four of nine atoms. Silicon is isovalent with germanium and adds no carriers; what it does is strengthen the interslab dimer bond, which is what sets the temperature of the magnetostructural transition. That is the reason the composition is held at exactly 0.1 rather than being swept.

basis: The compositions are (GdN)x(UN)(1-x) mixtures at 15, 20 and 48 per cent, and the paper is on the thermal conductivity of gadolinium-added uranium mononitride fuel pellets. Uranium mononitride and gadolinium nitride are both rocksalt, Fm-3m, and gadolinium is added to nitride fuel as a burnable neutron absorber; whether it dissolves into the UN lattice or stays as dispersed GdN grains, both phases are the same prototype, so the assignment is unambiguous either way. I disagree with [ref 2], which returns GdUN2 R-3m mp-1224527 with no ICSD reference: that is a computed ordered 1:1:2 compound, not the solid solution or two-phase mixture a fuel pellet contains, and no ordering of that kind is claimed in the paper. No mp_id is recorded.

Three different things are in this host. GdTiO3 and the two Gd(1-x)SrxTiO3 compositions are ABO3 perovskites, strongly tilted at the gadolinium tolerance factor, and two of the papers are on them -- the structural, magnetic and electronic properties of GdTiO3 and the metal-insulator transitions in epitaxial Gd1-xSrxTiO3 films, where strontium substitution dopes holes into the d1 Mott insulator. The (Gd2O3)50(TiO2)50 and (Gd2O3)45.5(TiO2)54.5 mixtures are at the Gd2Ti2O7 ratio, which is the pyrochlore, and [ref 2] backs that with Gd2Ti2O7 Fd-3m (227) mp-5302 at hull 0.008 and 7 ICSD references. The (Gd2O3)15.8(TiO2)84.2 mixture is far past pyrochlore towards titania and would be pyrochlore plus rutile as a two-phase ceramic; that third paper is on burnable absorbers, where the material is a phase mixture by design rather than a compound. The host is marked mixed with all three ids present. The primary is perovskite on a three-to-two composition count with one sample each, which is thin, hence medium confidence -- a reader who wanted the pyrochlore to lead would have a fair case, and the reference block would support them.

dopant_roles.site: the 12-coordinate A site of the perovskite compositions
dopant_roles.basis: Gd0.960Sr0.040TiO3 and Gd0.870Sr0.130TiO3, the epitaxial film series. Divalent strontium on the trivalent A site removes electrons from the titanium t2g band and drives the Mott insulator metallic, which is the transition the paper measures. It has nothing to do with the pyrochlore or absorber compositions in the same host.

basis: Every composition is PrPt4Ge(12-x)Sbx with x from 1 to 5, and the paper investigates the superconducting and normal-state properties of the filled skutterudite series. PrPt4Ge12 is the germanide filled skutterudite: a Pt4Ge12 framework of corner-sharing octahedra enclosing Ge4 rings, in Im-3, with praseodymium in the icosahedral void -- the same topology as CoSb3 with a platinum-germanium framework instead of a cobalt-antimony one. It is an unconventional superconductor near 8 K, below the 12-282 K measured window. Antimony substitutes into the framework rings and is above the 5 at.% cut, so it appears in the host key rather than as a dopant candidate; the substitution is the electron-count knob that suppresses the superconductivity. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

The two compositions are IIDT and IIDDT, which are not chemical formulas at all but polymer abbreviations -- isoindigo-based conjugated polymers -- and the paper is on Seebeck effects in n-type and p-type polymers, measured on films at 303-353 K. The host key is a parsing accident: the I of the acronym was read as iodine, and the D and T almost certainly as deuterium and tritium, both of which normalise to hydrogen, which is how two letters of an abbreviation became an H-I binary. The material is a semicrystalline conjugated polymer with no periodic crystal structure to assign, which is what the taxonomy entry is for. [ref 2] returns HI and HI3, hydrogen iodide and its polyiodide -- structures for a compound that is not present in the experiment in any form. No mp_id is recorded, and stage 2 should skip this host rather than resolve it.

dopant_roles.basis: The D and T of IIDT and IIDDT, read as deuterium and tritium and normalised to hydrogen. The polymer does contain hydrogen, but not in any quantity these letters describe.
The II of IIDT and IIDDT, which abbreviates the isoindigo repeat unit, not iodine. There is no iodine in these films.

basis: The compositions are TiHx for x from 0.82 to 2 and both papers measure electrical and thermal properties of titanium hydrides. This is the metal hydride entry of the taxonomy: hydrogen absorbed into the interstices of a metal lattice rather than forming a compound with its own anion sublattice. [ref 2] agrees strongly, TiH2 Fm-3m (225) mp-24161 at hull 0.002 with 11 ICSD references. One correction to the taxonomy entry, which calls the family rocksalt-derived with hydrogen on the octahedral sites as in PdH: the titanium dihydride is fluorite-derived, with hydrogen filling both tetrahedral holes of the face-centred metal lattice, which is what allows x to reach 2 at all. Two structural caveats that the composition range makes real. Near x = 2 the cubic phase distorts tetragonally to I4/mmm below roughly room temperature, at the bottom edge of the 293-768 K window. And TiH0.82 is below the lower phase boundary of the hydride, so that sample is a two-phase mixture of hydrogen-saturated hexagonal titanium metal and the cubic hydride rather than a single phase. Neither is recorded as a thermal phase sequence, since both are composition effects rather than something every sample passes through on heating.

All three compositions are Ti0.4Hf0.6Ni(1+z)(Sb,Sn) and the paper is on nanoscale interface engineering in this half-Heusler system. The MNiX 18-electron half Heusler in F-43m is not in doubt. But the curator note contradicts the parsed formula and I take the curator: the paper writes Ti0.4Hf0.6Ni1+zSn0.975Sb0.025, that is a tin-based half Heusler with antimony as the dilute donor, while the parsed composition has them the other way round as Sb0.975Sn0.025. TiNiSn with a little antimony is one of the best known n-type half Heuslers and TiNiSb is not a stable 18-electron compound at all, so the curator reading is also the chemically sensible one. This matters downstream: the two readings disagree about which element is the host anion and which is the dopant, and the dopant roles below are written for the curator version, with the parsed version noted. The other variable is the nickel excess z, which is the interface engineering of the title -- excess nickel on the vacant fourth sublattice, precipitating full-Heusler nanoinclusions at the grain boundaries. Neither reference block returns an entry for this host, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.site: the main-group 4a site
dopant_roles.basis: Recorded as the parsed composition has it, Sb0.975Sn0.025, so that the ledger matches the composition strings this host was keyed from. On the curator reading it is the reverse and tin is the host species while antimony is the 2.5 per cent donor, one electron per substitution, which is the standard n-type route in TiNiSn. Either way the element pair sits on the same site and the doping level is 0.025 of it; only the sign and the identity of the dopant differ, and that should be settled from the paper.

dopant_roles.site: the vacant fourth fcc sublattice of the half-Heusler cell
dopant_roles.basis: Ni1.005, Ni1.01 and Ni1.03 -- the variable z of the paper, and the only thing that differs between the three compositions. Excess nickel enters the sublattice that the half Heusler leaves empty, which is the same site it occupies in the full Heusler; past its solubility it precipitates full-Heusler inclusions, and the nanometre-scale interfaces those create are what the title claims boosts performance. It is off-stoichiometry of a host element on a structurally defined void, so interstitial rather than substitutional or non_stoichiometry.

basis: Four of the five compositions are (Zr,Hf)3Ni3Sb4 written as Zr2HfNi2.9Co0.1Sb4 and the like, and the first paper is titled for the electronic transport analysis of Zr3Ni3Sb4. The 3-3-4 stoichiometry is the Y3Au3Sb4 structure, cubic I-43d -- a body-centred framework related to the anti-Th3P4 arrangement, which is a distinct prototype from the half Heusler even though both are cubic ZrNi-antimonides and both are 18-electron-like narrow-gap semiconductors. The fifth composition, Hf0.75Zr0.25NiSb0.99Sb0.01, is at the 1:1:1 ratio and belongs with the half Heuslers of the second paper on ZrNiPb-based materials; its formula is also visibly malformed, listing antimony twice with the fractions summing to one, which suggests a second element was lost in transcription. The host is marked mixed. Neither reference block returns an entry, so no mp_id is recorded, and the medium confidence reflects the malformed composition and the absence of any reference support rather than doubt about the 3-3-4 phase.

dopant_roles.site: the transition-metal site of the 3-3-4 framework
dopant_roles.basis: Ni2.9Co0.1 in two compositions, a thirtieth of the site. Cobalt has one electron fewer than nickel, so this is acceptor doping of a narrow-gap semiconductor and the obvious way to tune its carrier concentration without touching the framework.

dopant_roles.site: the transition-metal site of the 3-3-4 framework
dopant_roles.basis: Ni2.7Cu0.3 in two compositions, a tenth of the site. Copper has one electron more than nickel, so it dopes in the opposite direction to the cobalt samples -- the pair of substitutions brackets the intrinsic composition, which is how the transport analysis of the first paper separates the two carrier types.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the group 4 cation site, shared by both the 3-3-4 and half-Heusler compositions
solid_solution_axis.note: Hf/(Hf+Zr) as the chunk file reports it. The two are isovalent and nearly the same size, so this axis contributes mass contrast for phonon scattering and almost nothing else electronically; it does not change the prototype and it crosses the mixed-prototype boundary in this host, which is why the axis and the split are independent of one another.

basis: All six compositions are In5SnSbO12 with gallium replacing up to a tenth of the indium, and the paper is on densification and thermoelectric performance of In5SnSbO12. Nothing in the taxonomy covered it, so m7o12_delta_fluorite is proposed in prototypes_proposed.jsonl and used here. The identification rests on the cation-to-anion ratio rather than on any reference, since neither block returns an entry for this host: seven cations to twelve oxygens is the delta-phase ratio, and In4Sn3O12 is the established rhombohedral R-3 phase of the In2O3-SnO2 system at exactly that ratio -- a fluorite with one anion in seven removed and the vacancies ordered along the rhombohedral axis. In5SnSbO12 replaces two of its tin atoms with one indium and one antimony, which preserves both the ratio and the charge balance, since In3+ plus Sb5+ is two Sn4+. Confidence is medium for that reason: the reasoning is sound and the parent compound is real, but no reference here tests it, and it should be checked against the diffraction pattern in the paper. No mp_id is recorded. Stage 3 should not read the sub-fluorite oxygen count as a tunable vacancy concentration -- those vacancies are ordered and part of the structure.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral cation sites of the M7O12 framework
dopant_roles.basis: In(5-y)Gay for y from 0.05 to 0.5, five of the six compositions. Gallium is isovalent with indium and much smaller, so it adds no carriers; it contracts the lattice and, on the paper title, improves densification, which is a sintering effect as much as an electronic one. At the top of the range it takes a tenth of the indium, so the upper compositions are alloying rather than dilute doping.

basis: The host is lanthanum metal with cerium added from 0.03 to 5 atomic per cent, and both papers are on thermopower of dilute cerium in lanthanum -- the canonical dilute Kondo impurity experiment, which is why the series runs over three decades of concentration and is measured from 11 to 295 K. Lanthanum metal in that window is the double hexagonal close-packed alpha phase, P6_3/mmc, which becomes face-centred cubic near 580 K and body-centred cubic near 1140 K, both well above the measurement. [ref 2] carries all three -- La Fm-3m mp-156 with 6 ICSD references, La P6_3/mmc mp-26 with 4, La Im-3m mp-10023 with 2 -- and ranks the cubic one first on reference count, which for an elemental metal counts entries rather than temperatures and does not mean the samples were cubic. Following the precedent already set in this ledger for elemental metal hosts, the prototype is the solid solution alloy entry rather than a specific close-packed stacking. No mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.site: the close-packed metal sites
dopant_roles.basis: Ce from 0.0003 to 0.05 per lanthanum. Cerium is trivalent like its host and nearly the same size, so it is not a dopant in the carrier-concentration sense at all: what it brings is a localised f electron, and the giant low-temperature thermopower peak the papers measure is single-ion Kondo scattering from it. The concentration is swept precisely to show the effect is per impurity rather than collective, so stage 3 should record the level but not interpret it as doping.

basis: All six compositions are La0.7Sr0.3Mn(1-x)RuxO3 with x running from 0.25 to 0.70, and the paper is on the effects of Ru substitution for Mn on La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 perovskites. La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 is the canonical hole-doped manganite, an ABO3 perovskite with the rhombohedral R-3c tilt system at this Sr content, and ruthenium enters the octahedral B site as a continuous solid solution with manganese. I disagree with [ref 2], which ranks SrLaMnRuO6 R3 (146) mp-39239 at hull 0.000: that is the B-site ordered double perovskite at exactly x = 0.5, and only one of the six compositions sits at that ratio. The series is continuous and nothing in a substitution study claims rock-salt ordering of Mn and Ru, so the disordered single perovskite is the right label and double_perovskite is recorded as an alternative rather than taken as the answer. Sr and Ru are both above the 5 at.% cut and so appear in the host key rather than as dopant candidates; the Mn-Ru pair is not flagged as a solid-solution axis because the two are not in the same group and the substitution changes the electron count rather than being isoelectronic.

The single composition is Li2O and the paper is on the effects of fast neutron irradiation on the thermal conductivity of Li2O, which is a tritium breeder ceramic rather than a thermoelectric. Lithium oxide is the antifluorite: a face-centred cubic array of oxide ions with lithium filling all eight tetrahedral holes, Fm-3m, the anti-arrangement of CaF2. [ref 2] agrees directly -- Li2O Fm-3m (225) mp-1960 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references, the strongest entry in the block. The other entries are peroxides and superoxides (Li2O2, LiO2, LiO3), which are different compounds at different oxygen contents rather than polymorphs of Li2O, so none of them belongs in other_polymorphs. The taxonomy entry names Mg2Si as its exemplar; Li2O is the oxide member of the same structure type and needs no new id.

The single composition is LuSb and the paper is on Fermi surface topology and magnetotransport in semimetallic LuSb. The rare-earth monopnictides are rocksalt B1 without exception at ambient pressure, and [ref 2] confirms it: LuSb Fm-3m (225) mp-516 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references. The compensated semimetal band structure that gives the extreme magnetoresistance in that paper is a property of the rocksalt cell, so the assignment and the physics agree. The LuSb Pm-3m (221) entry mp-1009007 at hull 0.330 with 2 ICSD references is the CsCl-type form these compounds take under pressure, not a phase reached by heating, and is recorded as such; LuSb2 and LuSb3 are different compositions, not polymorphs.

other_polymorphs.note: The B1 to B2 transition is the standard high-pressure behaviour of the rare-earth monopnictides. The 12-299 K measurement is at ambient pressure and never reaches it.

basis: Four of the six samples carry an explicit _IQC suffix on the composition string and all three papers are on quasicrystals -- electronic transport in Cd-Yb and Y-Mg-Zn quasicrystals, low-temperature thermal conductivity of a single-grain Y-Mg-Zn icosahedral quasicrystal, and growth of large-grain R-Mg-Zn quasicrystals from the ternary melt. Y8.7Mg34.6Zn56.8 is the face-centred icosahedral Zn-Mg-RE phase, a Tsai-type quasicrystal built from rare-earth-centred icosahedral clusters, and Y12Mg29Zn59 sits in the same primary field. I disagree with [ref 2] as a structure source here: it returns ordinary crystalline line compounds of the ternary system -- YMgZn P-62m mp-6908, Y2Mg3Zn4, Y2(MgZn)3 and so on -- and none of them is the icosahedral phase, because the icosahedral phase is aperiodic and has no Materials Project entry to return. No mp_id is recorded, and per the taxonomy note this host must be mapped to an approximant in stage 2 with that substitution stated rather than silently made.

dopant_roles.site: the rare-earth site at the centre of the Tsai-type icosahedral cluster
dopant_roles.basis: Y6.03Tb2.97Mg42Zn57, and the curator records the series as (Y1-xTbx)-Mg-Zn with the Mg and Zn ratios unspecified. Terbium takes a third of the rare-earth site, so this is alloying rather than dilute doping even though it falls under the 5 at.% whole-formula cut. Terbium and yttrium are both trivalent and nearly the same size, which is why the icosahedral phase forms across the whole R-Mg-Zn series; what terbium adds that yttrium does not is a 4f moment, so the substitution is isoelectronic for the band structure while changing the magnetism entirely.

basis: All four compositions are Mn(31-x)RexSi63.4 with rhenium at 6 to 8 atomic per cent, which puts the silicon-to-metal ratio at about 1.73, and the three papers are on a supersaturated Re solid solution of higher manganese silicide, the effect of Re substitution on the phase stability of complex MnSi-gamma, and Re substitution effects in the same system. That ratio is the definition of the higher manganese silicide: a Nowotny chimney-ladder in which a tetragonal beta-Sn-like manganese sublattice and a helical silicon sublattice are mutually incommensurate, so the composition is fixed near MnSi1.73 to 1.75 rather than at a simple stoichiometry and the commensurate approximants Mn4Si7, Mn11Si19, Mn15Si26 and Mn27Si47 are all descriptions of the same material. Neither reference block returns anything for this host, so no mp_id is recorded and the assignment rests on the composition and the paper titles. Rhenium sits above the 5 at.% cut and therefore appears in the host key rather than in dopant_roles; what it does is substitute for manganese on the chimney sublattice, adding one valence electron per atom, which is how these papers tune the carrier concentration of an otherwise fixed-composition phase. The taxonomy flags this prototype for special handling in stage 2 because the incommensurate composite has no single Materials Project entry; that flag applies here.

All six compositions are MnSe with sodium from 0.1 to 3 per cent of the manganese site, and the paper is on the thermoelectric properties of p-type MnSe. Alpha-MnSe is rocksalt, and [ref 1] is unambiguous: MnSe Fm-3m (225) mp-972 with 19 ICSD references as PRIMARY, against 2 or fewer for every other setting. The zincblende, wurtzite and NiAs forms in the two blocks are the beta and gamma polymorphs, which are obtained by epitaxy on suitable substrates or by precipitation inside a host matrix and revert to rocksalt on warming -- they are not steps in a thermal sequence, so they go in other_polymorphs and the 297-749 K window crosses no structural transition. The magnetic ordering of this antiferromagnet does lie in the window in the sense that the Neel temperature near 150 K is below it, but a magnetic transition is not a structural one and nothing is recorded for it.

other_polymorphs.note: beta-MnSe, 2 ICSD references against 19 for rocksalt. Stabilised epitaxially or as inclusions; not reached by heating alpha-MnSe.
gamma-MnSe, 1 ICSD reference.
1 ICSD reference; the NiAs-type setting reported for thin films rather than for bulk on heating.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral cation site of the rocksalt cell
dopant_roles.basis: Mn(1-x)NaxSe with x swept from 0.001 to 0.03 across five of the six samples, the sixth being undoped MnSe. Monovalent sodium on a divalent cation site removes one electron per substitution, which is the acceptor doping that makes the p-type MnSe of the title; the series is a straightforward carrier-concentration sweep and stage 3 can read the level directly from the fractions.

basis: All three compositions are Mo(3-x)RuxSb7 with x of 0.5 or 0.8, one of them additionally tellurium-substituted, and the three papers are on the beneficial influence of Ru on the thermoelectric properties of Mo3Sb7, on the crystal structure and high-temperature thermoelectric properties of the same, and on transport and magnetic properties of Mo2.5Ru0.5Sb7-xTex. Mo3Sb7 is the Ir3Ge7 type in Im-3m and is the exemplar of that taxonomy entry, so the host needs no interpretation beyond reading the stoichiometry. Ruthenium substitutes for molybdenum and supplies the extra electrons that open the pseudogap at the Fermi level, which is what the first paper means by beneficial. I disagree with the only entry [ref 2] returns, Sb28(Mo3Ru)3 Cm (8) mp-1219530 at hull 0.000: that is a computed monoclinic ordering of ruthenium onto specific molybdenum sites with no ICSD reference behind it, whereas the substitution in these papers is a random solid solution that leaves the cubic symmetry intact. No mp_id is recorded from it.

dopant_roles.site: the antimony framework, which in this structure includes both isolated Sb atoms and Sb4 square units
dopant_roles.basis: Mo2.5Ru0.5Sb6.75Te0.25, the single composition from the third paper, which sweeps x in Sb7-xTex. Tellurium has one electron more than antimony, so it dopes the framework in the same direction as the ruthenium substitution on the metal site; using both at once is how that paper separates the effect of band filling from the effect of disorder.

basis: The five compositions are VN and VNx down to x = 0.76, and the paper is on the phonon and electron contributions to the thermal conductivity of VNx -- a nitrogen-vacancy series, which is precisely what this taxonomy entry exists for. Delta-VN is rocksalt with vanadium on the metal sublattice and nitrogen on the octahedral sites, and the vacancies that make x less than one are the variable being swept. Here I disagree with the reference precedence. [ref 1], TEDesignLab, is normally preferred, but the only VN entry it carries is F-43m (216) mp-1001826 at hull 0.328 with 2 ICSD references -- a zincblende setting that is 0.33 eV per atom above the hull -- while [ref 2] gives VN Fm-3m (225) mp-925 with 28 ICSD references. Twenty-eight references against two, and a nitride that every account of the vanadium-nitrogen system describes as B1, decide it against the preferred reference. The V2N, V8N and V32N3 entries are lower nitrides at different compositions, not polymorphs of VN.

other_polymorphs.note: The TEDesignLab entry for VN, at hull 0.328 with 2 ICSD references. Not the ambient bulk structure and not reached by heating; recorded here so the disagreement with the preferred reference is visible rather than silently dropped.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral anion site of the rocksalt cell
dopant_roles.basis: VN0.93, VN0.88, VN0.84 and VN0.76 against stoichiometric VN. These are ordered or disordered vacancies on the nitrogen sublattice, not an impurity and not a second element, and they are the independent variable of the paper: the vacancies scatter both phonons and electrons, which is how the two contributions to the thermal conductivity are separated. Stage 3 should read 1 minus x as a vacancy concentration rather than as a doping level.

basis: The curator states plainly what this is -- clear, bronze, gray and green float glass -- and the paper is on thermal conductivity measurements of float glass at high temperatures. It is ordinary soda-lime-silica window glass and has no crystal structure to assign. The composition string (SiO272)3.47(Al2O3)4.14(Na2O)44.3(K2O)2.24(MgO)15.72(CaO)30.13 is a list of oxide mole percentages that the parser has read as stoichiometric subscripts, and the damage is specific: the 72 of the leading SiO2 term has been absorbed into the formula as an oxygen count, so silicon -- about three quarters of the glass -- falls under the 5 at.% cut and lands in the dopant candidate list, which is how a silicate glass acquired the host key Na-O. Neither reference block describes the material: the sodium oxides, peroxides and superoxides they return are crystalline compounds that do not occur in a float glass. No mp_id is recorded and stage 2 should skip this host. The 302-1173 K window runs through the glass transition and into the softening range, but a glass transition is not a structural phase transition and nothing is recorded in phases.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral network-forming site of the silicate glass
dopant_roles.basis: Silicon is the majority network former of a float glass at roughly 72 mole per cent SiO2, not a minor element at all. It appears under 5 at.% only because the parser swallowed the 72 into the oxygen subscript. Every fraction in this host is unreliable for the same reason, so stage 3 must not compute a level from them.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral network-forming site
dopant_roles.basis: About 1 mole per cent Al2O3 in a typical float glass. Aluminium substitutes for silicon in the network as a tetrahedral former, charge-compensated by the alkalis, and is added for durability rather than to change any electronic property.

dopant_roles.site: network-modifier site in the interstices of the silicate network
dopant_roles.basis: The lime of soda-lime glass, around 8 mole per cent. Calcium breaks bridging oxygen bonds and lowers the melt viscosity; it is a constituent of the glass rather than a dopant in it.

dopant_roles.site: network-modifier site
dopant_roles.basis: Magnesia partially replaces lime in float glass to widen the working range. Same structural role as calcium.

dopant_roles.site: network-modifier site
dopant_roles.basis: A small potassium fraction alongside the soda, again a modifier. The bronze, gray and green tints named by the curator come from iron, cobalt and selenium additions at levels far below anything this composition string records, so the colour differences between the six samples are not visible in the formula at all.

basis: The paper settles it in its title -- electrical resistivity and thermoelectric power of amorphous niobium-nickel -- and the three compositions Ni0.50Nb0.50, Ni0.52Nb0.48 and Ni0.36Nb0.64 sit in the deep-eutectic band where melt-spun Ni-Nb ribbons are the textbook binary metallic glass. There is no crystal structure to assign. [ref 2] returns the equilibrium crystalline line compounds of the system -- NbNi3 Pmmn mp-1451 with 7 ICSD references, Nb7Ni6 R-3m, NbNi2, Nb3Ni -- which are what these ribbons would become if they crystallised, not what was measured, so no mp_id is recorded. One thing worth flagging for review rather than recording as a phase: the measured window reaches 945 K and Ni-Nb glasses crystallise somewhere near 900 K. If the top of the range crossed crystallisation, the sample above that point is a different material, but crystallisation is irreversible and one-way and is not a thermal phase sequence, so phases is left empty and spans_transition false.

The single composition reads (Pr4.76Nd95.24)0.44Fe2Co2Sb12, which is a partially filled skutterudite written with the rare-earth mixture in per cent: the filler is 0.44 formula units of a rare earth that is 95 per cent neodymium and 5 per cent praseodymium, and the framework is Fe2Co2Sb12. The paper is on changes of thermoelectric properties and hardness after high-pressure torsion processing, which is a microstructure study of exactly this class of material. The host key is a casualty of that notation: because the 4.76 and 95.24 are percentages rather than atom counts, the parser inflated neodymium to about seventy per cent of the formula and deflated iron and cobalt below the 5 at.% cut, so a cobalt-antimony skutterudite was keyed as Nd-Sb and its framework metals were offered as dopant candidates. [ref 2] returns the Nd-Sb binaries -- NdSb rocksalt mp-1586 and so on -- none of which is present in the sample; no mp_id is recorded. Stage 3 must not read any fraction in this host literally.

dopant_roles.site: the icosahedral void of the Sb12 cage framework, the 2a site
dopant_roles.basis: Five per cent of the rare-earth filler, which is itself only 0.44 per formula unit. Praseodymium and neodymium are adjacent trivalent rare earths and both rattle in the cage; the mixture is almost certainly a didymium feedstock rather than a deliberate co-filling experiment, so stage 3 should treat the two together as one filler species.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedrally coordinated transition-metal site of the framework
dopant_roles.basis: Fe2Co2 -- half the framework metal site, which is not doping in any sense. Iron has one electron fewer than cobalt, so replacing half the cobalt creates the electron deficit that the trivalent rare-earth filler compensates; this is what allows a filling fraction as high as 0.44 when unsubstituted CoSb3 accepts almost none. The prototype and the filling fraction are set by this ratio together.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedrally coordinated transition-metal site of the framework
dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt is the parent framework metal of the skutterudite, not a dopant. It is listed as a candidate only because the percentage notation deflated every fraction in the formula. Recorded so that the Fe-Co pair is read as one framework sublattice rather than as two impurities.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [225, 64, 123, 139]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: All six compositions are Nd(3-x)Te4 with x from 0 to 0.22 and the paper is on the synthesis and characterization of vacancy-doped neodymium telluride for thermoelectrics. This is the case the taxonomy entry already describes for La(3-x)Te4: the Th3P4 structure in I-43d tolerates a continuous range of cation vacancies between the 3-4 and 2-3 limits, and that vacancy concentration is the carrier-concentration knob rather than a defect. [ref 2] supports the structure at the measured composition -- Nd3Te4 I-43d (220) mp-2204 at hull 0.024 with 4 ICSD references. The block ranks NdTe Fm-3m mp-570 first on 8 references, but that is the rocksalt monotelluride, a different composition that no sample here is at, so the ranking is answering a question about the chemistry rather than about these samples. The 58-1286 K window is wide but no structural transition is established for the rare-earth sesquitelluride Th3P4 phase within it.

dopant_roles.site: the 12a cation site of the Th3P4 framework
dopant_roles.basis: Nd2.78Te4 through Nd3Te4 -- up to 7 per cent of the cation site left empty. Each vacancy removes three electrons from the conduction band, carrying the compound from a metal at Nd3Te4 towards a semiconductor at Nd2.67Te4, so this is the doping variable itself and the vacancy-doped of the paper title. It is a host-element deficiency, not a foreign atom, which is why it is recorded as non_stoichiometry rather than as a dopant.

basis: The single composition is Sr1.7Ce0.3NiO4, and the A2BO4 ratio is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper member -- the K2NiF4 structure, a single NiO2 perovskite sheet between rock-salt SrO double layers -- which is where the nickelate at that stoichiometry belongs. The paper record carries no title, so the composition is nearly all there is to go on, and [ref 2] offers no support at all: it returns Sr(NiO2)4, SrNiO2 and a set of large Sr-Ni-O chain and mixed-valence compounds, and nothing at the A2BO4 ratio. That absence is itself informative rather than contradictory, because strontium-only Sr2NiO4 is difficult to make at ambient pressure and the K2NiF4 nickelates are normally lanthanum-based; the cerium here is what makes the composition accessible. Confidence is medium for that reason: the stoichiometry names the prototype clearly but nothing independent confirms the phase was obtained, and a reader who suspected a mixture of a Ruddlesden-Popper phase with the Sr-Ni-O chain compounds the reference block prefers would not be unreasonable. No mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.site: the nine-coordinate A site in the rock-salt layer of the n = 1 block
dopant_roles.basis: Sr1.7Ce0.3NiO4 -- 15 per cent of the A site, which is alloying rather than dilute doping. Tetravalent cerium on a divalent site adds two electrons per substitution to the NiO2 sheet, reducing the nickel oxidation state; this is electron doping of a layered nickelate, the counterpart of the hole doping usually done with strontium on a lanthanum site. It is also the likely reason a strontium-rich 214 nickelate could be made at all.

basis: Two samples are stoichiometric YbNiSb and the remaining four are off-stoichiometric variants around it, and the second paper is titled Discovery of YbNiSb-Based Half-Heusler Alloys as Promising Thermoelectrics while the first is on the observed properties and electronic structure of RNiSb compounds. The RNiSb rare-earth half-Heuslers are the MgAgAs type in F-43m: three interpenetrating face-centred sublattices with the fourth left vacant, which is what gives the family its narrow gap and its tolerance for the wide off-stoichiometry seen here, Yb1.3Ni0.9Sb0.8 and Yb0.78Ni1.2Sb0.95 among them. The only entry [ref 2] returns is Yb2NiSb2 R3m (160) mp-1215858 at hull 0.075 with no ICSD reference, a computed compound at a different stoichiometry; it does not bear on the assignment and no mp_id is recorded. Ytterbium in this family sits between divalent and trivalent, which is the reason for both the heavy-fermion behaviour of the first paper and the thermoelectric interest of the second, but it does not change the structure type.

dopant_roles.site: the rare-earth site of the half-Heusler cell
dopant_roles.basis: Ta at 0.01, 0.03 and 0.07 across three compositions, and the site follows from the trend rather than from assumption: tantalum rises as ytterbium falls across Yb1.28Ta0.01, Yb0.95Ta0.03 and Yb0.78Ta0.07, while nickel and antimony move the other way. Pentavalent tantalum on a divalent-to-trivalent rare-earth site is heavy electron doping, which suits an n-type half-Heusler. The anticorrelation is only three points in a host where every composition is off-stoichiometric in several places at once, so the site is recorded at medium confidence and the paper should settle it.

basis: Five compositions, five different structure types -- this is one of the most genuinely mixed hosts in the set and a single label would be simply wrong. UNiSn, with two samples and the third paper on anomalous magnetic, transport and thermal properties of the half-metal, is the MgAgAs half-Heusler in F-43m and [ref 2] carries it at mp-21425 with 3 ICSD references; it is taken as the primary on sample count and because it is the compound the host is best known for. U2Ni2Sn, the subject of the first paper on magnetoresistance and thermoelectric power, is the Mo2FeB2 ordered U3Si2 type in P4/mbm, mp-22813 with 3 references. UNi2Sn is the full Heusler, Fm-3m, mp-672374. UNi4Sn is the MgCu4Sn type, F-43m, mp-22197 with 4 references -- the ordered derivative of the cubic Laves phase in which tin takes a quarter of the magnesium sites, which is why it is filed under laves_phase rather than under either Heusler. U3Ni3Sn4 is the Y3Au3Sb4 type in I-43d, the same 3-3-4 framework recorded for Hf-Ni-Sb-Zr in chunk 021. All four alternatives are listed and the host must be split per composition. One thing described rather than recorded: UNiSn distorts tetragonally at its antiferromagnetic ordering near 43 K, inside the 10-308 K window, but that is a magnetostructural distortion within the half-Heusler prototype rather than a change of prototype, and no paper here states the temperature, so it is not entered in phases. The UNiSn C2/m mp-1217516 entry at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference is a computed distortion of the same compound and is not evidence of a separate phase.

All six samples are RbOs2O6 and both papers name the family explicitly -- chemical trends of superconducting properties in pyrochlore oxides, and high-pressure effects on the superconductivity of beta-pyrochlore oxides. The AB2O6 stoichiometry is the beta or defect pyrochlore: the corner-sharing Os2O6 octahedral network of an ordinary pyrochlore with the interpenetrating A2O-prime sublattice removed, leaving a single rubidium ion loose in an oversized cage. The taxonomy carried only the A2B2O7 parent, whose formula archetype this does not match, so beta_pyrochlore_ab2o6 is proposed in prototypes_proposed.jsonl and used here. [ref 2] supports the framework directly -- Rb(OsO3)2 Fd-3m (227) mp-5050 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references, by far the strongest entry in the block.
