Two of those come from the paper on TiOxNy thin-film selective surfaces. That is three of the five samples and it is why rocksalt_nitride_carbide is the label. But (TiO2)0.8(TiN)0.2, from the paper on phases and thermoelectric properties of TiO2-TiN compacts, is written as a mixture and is a two-phase composite of a titanium dioxide polymorph with TiN; and N0.2TiO2, from the paper on the physical properties of NxTiO2 prepared by a sol-gel route, is nitrogen-doped TiO2, which from a sol-gel route is anatase. So the host contains a rocksalt oxynitride, a composite, and a doped dioxide, and the MO2 and MO stoichiometries are genuinely different compounds rather than variants. Low confidence, marked mixed, with anatase, rutile and composite_multiphase as alternates; the split is on the anion-to-metal ratio and is straightforward but has to be made per composition. I disagree with the whole reference block, which returns Ti(NO3)4, Ti17(NO4)6, Ti2N2O, Ti3N2O3 and Ti3NO4 -- nitrates and computed nitride-oxides at hull values up to 0.053, most without ICSD backing. None of them is an oxynitride solid solution or a doped dioxide, and none should be attached. No mp_id is recorded.

The single composition is Na2Ti2Sb2O and the paper is on the physical properties of the layered pnictide oxides Na2Ti2Pn2O with Pn = As and Sb. The structure is body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm and is built from a Ti2O sheet -- a square lattice of titanium with oxygen at the centre of each square, which is the anti-configuration of a CuO2 plane -- capped above and below by antimony, with sodium between the slabs. [ref 2] is exceptionally strong here: Na2Ti2Sb2O I4/mmm (139) mp-6328 at hull 0.000 with 20 ICSD references, the best-attested single entry anywhere in this chunk, and it is the only entry returned for the host, so there is no competing polymorph to weigh. The taxonomy had no entry for this family, so I have proposed na2ti2sb2o_oxypnictide rather than force it into one of the neighbouring layered oxide-pnictide entries: bi2o2se_layered and zrcusias_1111 both put the oxygen in a separate fluorite-type block from the pnictogen, whereas here the oxygen and the antimony are in the same slab, and the d1 titanium square lattice this produces is a distinct electronic system that shows a density-wave anomaly rather than a gap. The 10-297 K window is the low-temperature transport that anomaly lives in; the 349 K figure in the full span is an outlier.

All three compositions are members of NaPbmSbTem+2 -- NaPbSbTe3 at m = 1, NaPb6SbTe8 at m = 6, and Na1.10Pb5.90Sb0.85Te8 as a slightly off-stoichiometric version of the latter -- and the paper title settles the structural question directly: absence of nanostructuring in NaPbmSbTem+2, solid solutions with high thermoelectric performance. This is the SALT family, the sodium analogue of LAST, and it is a rocksalt solid solution at Fm-3m: tellurium fills the anion sublattice and sodium, lead and antimony share the cation sublattice, with Na+ and Sb3+ charge-compensating each other. The paper is worth reading carefully because it is arguing against exactly the reading a composition like NaPb6SbTe8 invites -- these are homogeneous solid solutions, not nanostructured composites with precipitated second phases -- so composite_multiphase would be the wrong call here even though the formula looks like a mixture, and the record says so explicitly. No reference block is returned for this host, which is expected for a three-cation solid solution, and no mp_id is recorded. No dopant candidates fall below the cut: every element is a constituent of the solid solution, and the Na:Sb ratio near one is the charge-balance condition rather than a doping level.

Niobium-substituted titanium dioxide, but across a range wide enough that it stops being one material. Nb0.2Ti0.8O2 and Ti0.80Nb0.20O2 are heavily Nb-doped TiO2, and the second paper is on carrier generation and transport in heavily Nb-doped anatase -- anatase is the label because that paper names it, because the first paper works from chemically tuned TiO2 nanoparticles where anatase is what a nanoparticle route gives, and because Nb-doped anatase is the well-known transparent conducting oxide this chemistry is studied for. Rutile is the genuine alternate: the third paper sinters and reduces TiO2 ceramics at elevated temperature, and anatase converts irreversibly to rutile on heating above roughly 900 K, so the sintered samples in a host measured to 1057 K are very likely rutile rather than anatase. That conversion is not recorded in phases because it is a one-way transformation during processing rather than a reversible transition the measurement sweeps through, and because which polymorph a given sample is depends on its history, not on its temperature during the measurement. The third structure is the reason for medium. Ti0.60Nb0.40O2 and Ti0.40Nb0.60O2 carry far more niobium than any doped dioxide accommodates; in the TiO2-Nb2O5 system that composition range is where the Wadsley-Roth crystallographic shear phases form, which the taxonomy carries as block_shear_niobate. [ref 2] points the same way, returning Ti5Nb2O14 Cmmm, Ti3NbO8 P-1, Ti15NbO32 and TiNb3O6 R-3 -- mostly computed, mostly at low hull, and all of them ordered ternary line compounds rather than doped dioxides. Marked mixed and left for a composition-level split on the Nb:Ti ratio. No mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: One composition, Ti0.83Nb0.17(O0.955N0.045)2, and the curator note records that the nitrogen-to-oxygen ratio was estimated at the surface. Nitrogen substitutes for oxygen on the anion site of the dioxide; in TiO2 it is the standard visible-light sensitiser, narrowing the gap by raising the valence band edge. The surface qualifier in the note is a real caveat -- a nitrogen content measured by a surface technique may not be the bulk value -- so the level stage 3 computes from this formula should be treated as nominal.

basis: This is a case where the reference and the paper genuinely disagree and the paper wins. The single composition is NdNi5 and [ref 2] gives NdNi5 P6/mmm (191) mp-1824 at hull 0.000 with 10 ICSD references, which is the CaCu5 structure and is the correct crystalline structure of this compound. But the one paper here is on the magnetotransport and magnetic properties of amorphous NdNi5 -- the samples are the amorphous form, and assigning a crystalline prototype would attach long-range order they do not have. So metallic_glass is the label, with cacu5 recorded as the alternate because it is what the same composition is when crystallised and because a review pass reading the paper may well find crystalline reference samples measured alongside. Medium confidence for that reason: the structural call follows from a single word in a title, and the title is the only evidence available. This is precisely the situation the project README describes -- a reference describes which phases exist in a chemistry, not which phase a paper made -- and the disagreement here is real rather than an artefact of polymorph selection. No mp_id is recorded, since an amorphous alloy has no periodic structure to point at. The other reference entries, NdNi2 Fd-3m with 5 references, Nd2Ni7, NdNi3 and NdNi, are the other line compounds of this binary and none matches the 1:5 stoichiometry.

The single composition Nd2SbO2 is the neodymium member of the rare-earth pnictide oxide family, better written Nd2O2Sb, and the second paper is the review of (RE,Ca)mPnnOm crystal chemistry that also covers the gadolinium and erbium analogues annotated above. The structure is layered: fluorite-like Nd2O2 slabs alternating with square nets of reduced antimony, which is the Bi2O2Se arrangement with the rare-earth oxide layer in place of Bi2O2. The first paper, on decoupling electrical conductivity from the Seebeck coefficient in this family, is the thermoelectric motivation. Here the reference does contain the compound, unlike the gadolinium case: [ref 2] gives Nd2SbO2 Pmmn (59) mp-1105626 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference. That is an orthorhombic setting rather than the tetragonal I4/mmm parent, and I read it as a distortion within this prototype rather than a different structure -- the antimony square net is prone to dimerising, which lowers the symmetry without changing the layer stacking. Medium because the entry rests on a single ICSD reference and because the orthorhombic distortion is asserted rather than confirmed. The other entries returned, Nd3Sb5O12 I-43m, Nd3SbO7 Cmcm, NdSbO4 P2_1/c and the NdSbO3 Pm-3m at hull 0.768, are oxide-rich chemistry with antimony in a high oxidation state and belong to a different family. No mp_id is recorded.

Five compositions spanning most of the praseodymium nickelate phase diagram, and the host has to be split. Pr2NiO4 is the n=1 Ruddlesden-Popper member, the K2NiF4 structure, and Pr4Ni3O10 is the n=3 member; Pr2Ni0.75Cu0.25Ga0.05O4 is the n=1 member again with copper and gallium on the nickel site, from a solid-oxide-cell electrode paper. That is three of the five samples and is why ruddlesden_popper is the label -- the RP series is one prototype with n as its index, in the same way the InMO3(ZnO)n host above is one entry. The third paper, on the synthesis, structure and properties of Ln4Ni3O10, covers the n=3 member directly. The other two are different structures. Pr0.82Sr0.18NiO3 is the n=infinity end, the orthorhombic perovskite PrNiO3, which [ref 2] attests best of anything here at PrNiO3 Pnma (62) mp-25590, hull 0.000, 14 ICSD references, with a rhombohedral R-3c setting at mp-19170 also ICSD-backed. And Pr0.82Sr0.18NiO2 is the infinite-layer nickelate -- the topotactically reduced form with square-planar Ni1+, which is the superconducting phase, and the second paper is the pressure-enhancement-of-Tc work on exactly that. The oxygen stoichiometry is the whole difference between those last two, O3 against O2, and it is not a doping level but a reduction step. Marked mixed with perovskite and infinite_layer_cuprate as alternates; the split is clean on the Ni:O ratio. Medium because the label covers three of five samples and because the reference block, which returns Pr2NiO4 Cmce mp-19434 at a single ICSD reference against 14 for the perovskite, is weighted towards the phase that is not the label.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr0.82Sr0.18NiO3 and Pr0.82Sr0.18NiO2 both carry strontium on the rare-earth A site at 18%. Sr2+ for Pr3+ is an acceptor; in the infinite-layer nickelate it is the hole doping that produces superconductivity, and 0.18 sits squarely in the superconducting dome. This is the doping variable of the second paper, not an incidental impurity.

Pr2Ni0.75Cu0.25Ga0.05O4 puts copper on the nickel octahedral site of the n=1 Ruddlesden-Popper layer at a quarter occupancy -- substantial alloying rather than dilute doping. In an electrode material the purpose is to tune the oxygen interstitial content and the mixed conductivity. The paper describes the composition as B-site cation-excess, so the site sum exceeding one is deliberate.

The 0.05 of gallium in the same composition also sits on the B site. Ga3+ is fixed-valence and Jahn-Teller inactive, so it acts as a stabiliser of the octahedral layer rather than as an electronic dopant.

basis: Every composition is ZrNi1-xPdxSn with antimony from 0 to 0.01 on the tin site, and all three papers name the family: substitution effects on the thermoelectric properties of ZrNiSn-based half-Heuslers, the effects of partial substitution of Ni by Pd, and thermoelectric properties of ZrNiSn-based half-Heusler compounds. ZrNiSn is the canonical n-type half-Heusler, MgAgAs type at F-43m, an 18-electron semiconductor with one of the four fcc sublattices vacant. Palladium and nickel are both group 10 and both take the tetrahedral T site, so the substitution is isovalent and the structure is preserved across the whole 0.5 to 0.8 range recorded here. No reference block is returned for this host, which is expected for a quaternary substituted solid solution, and no mp_id is recorded; the assignment rests on the stoichiometry, which is unambiguously 1:1:1 with one mixed site, and on three paper titles that agree. The 294-1006 K window crosses no transition -- half-Heuslers of this family are stable to well above it, which is much of their appeal.

dopant_roles.basis: Three compositions carry Sb0.01 against Sn0.99. Antimony has one more valence electron than tin, so on the main-group site of an 18-electron half-Heusler it is the standard n-type donor for ZrNiSn, and 1% is a typical optimised level. It is genuine dilute doping, unlike the Ni/Pd substitution which is alloying on a different site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral T site of the half-Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: Ni/(Ni+Pd) spans 0.50-0.80 over four compositions, median 0.80. Both are group 10 and both occupy the same tetrahedral site, so the substitution is isovalent and the valence electron count stays at 18 -- no carriers are added, which is why the antimony is there to do that job separately. What the palladium changes is the mass contrast for phonon scattering and, more subtly, the band effective mass, which is what the second paper is measuring. The parent compound is a per-composition question and the series is continuous, so no single end member is recorded at host level.

basis: Two uranium antimonides, both well characterised, and the host holds both. U3Ni3Sb4 and U3Ni2.9Co0.1Sb4, three of the five samples, are the Y3Au3Sb4 structure type -- cubic I-43d, a filled-Th3P4 derivative -- which the taxonomy carries and which is the family the semiconducting and small-gap members like Ce3Bi4Pd3 belong to. That is the label. UNi0.5Sb2, the other two samples and the subject of the first paper on its low-temperature transport hysteresis, is the HfCuSi2 type: tetragonal P4/nmm with a square antimony net and a half-occupied nickel layer, and [ref 2] gives UNiSb2 P4/nmm (129) mp-1080551 at hull 0.027 with one ICSD reference, confirming both the stoichiometry family and the space group. The alternate uses hfcusi2_112_square_net, which is a pending proposal rather than a seed entry; it is the right description and was proposed for exactly this structure. Marked mixed and split on the U:Sb ratio, 3:4 against 1:2. Medium because the label covers three of five samples and because the reference block returns nothing for U3Ni3Sb4 itself -- its only other entry is U2NiSb4 P-4m2 mp-1216654, a computed phase with no ICSD backing at a stoichiometry no sample has. The second paper, on uranium-based materials for thermoelectric applications, is the survey that puts both compounds in the set. No mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: U3Ni2.9Co0.1Sb4 replaces about 3% of the nickel with cobalt. Co has one fewer d electron than Ni, so on the transition-metal site of a narrow-gap Y3Au3Sb4-type compound this shifts the Fermi level -- hole doping of a material that sits close to a gap, which is the usual way these are optimised. A single composition against the undoped parent, so it reads as a doping trial rather than an alloy series.

basis: All four compositions sit in the Ti-Zr-Ni icosahedral field -- Ti45Zr38Ni17, Ti53Zr27Ni20, Ti54Zr26Ni20 and one with copper -- and the papers say what they are three times: preparation and transport properties of a bulk icosahedral quasicrystal, superconductivity of TiZrNi alloys containing quasicrystals, and a measurement of the thermoelectric properties of quasicrystalline Al-Pd-Re as the comparison system. Ti-Zr-Ni near Ti45Zr38Ni17 is one of the few stable icosahedral quasicrystals outside the aluminium-based families, and it is the composition the first paper is built on. The taxonomy entry is the right one and its caveat applies in full: there is no periodic structure here, so stage 2 has to map this to a crystalline approximant -- the 1/1 W-phase of this system -- and say that it has done so rather than record an mp_id as if it described the sample. [ref 2] illustrates the problem rather than solving it: it returns ZrTi2Ni9 R-3m mp-1095547 with one ICSD reference and a set of computed Amm2 and R3m entries, none of which is at the quasicrystalline composition and one of which, Zr12Ti4Ni8O at hull 0.907, is not a real phase at all. No mp_id is recorded. The second paper is a reminder that these samples may be partly crystalline -- it says containing quasicrystals, not single-phase -- which is worth a look at review but does not change the prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Ti45Zr35Ni17Cu takes one atomic per cent from the zirconium and adds copper alongside the nickel. In a quasicrystal-forming alloy a late transition metal addition of this size is composition tuning of the electron-per-atom ratio, which is what sets whether the icosahedral phase forms at all; copper substitutes on the nickel sites of the icosahedral clusters. The role is recorded with the caveat that site assignment in an aperiodic structure is not a Wyckoff question and stage 2 cannot fill in a site here.

basis: The single composition is Te2P2O9 and the paper is on the Czochralski growth and characterisation of it as a novel nonlinear optical crystal. [ref 2] confirms the compound exists and gives its symmetry: Te2P2O9 Cc (9) mp-1193939 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, which matches the formula exactly and whose non-centrosymmetric space group is consistent with a nonlinear optical material. So the structure is known, and the assignment is nevertheless unresolved_crystalline, because Te2P2O9 is a tellurium phosphate with its own structure type and the taxonomy has no entry that covers it. I have not proposed one: it is a single composition from a single paper, the structure would be described entirely from the space group in the reference rather than from anything I can state about its connectivity, and a one-member prototype built on that is not worth adding to a taxonomy that has to be reviewed. Parking it here is the documented alternative and keeps the fact that the compound is crystalline and identified, which amorphous or unresolved would lose. The other entries in the block -- Te3P2O11, Te2PO7, Te4P2O13 and Te2(PO4)3 -- are neighbouring compounds of the same binary oxide join and confirm it is a rich system, but none is this formula. No mp_id is recorded at host level; mp-1193939 is noted here for whoever picks this up.

All five compositions are (Y1-xYbx)2SiO5 -- YbYSiO5 is the x = 0.5 member written without the bracket -- and both papers name the family: tailoring the thermal properties of multi-component rare-earth monosilicates, and improved thermophysical properties of rare-earth monosilicates for environmental barrier coatings. RE2SiO5 has two polymorphs, X1 for the larger rare earths from lanthanum to about terbium and X2 for the smaller ones from dysprosium to lutetium including yttrium, and both Y and Yb are on the X2 side of that boundary, so the whole solid solution is X2 monoclinic C2/c. That is the taxonomy entry and its exemplar is Y2SiO5 itself. I disagree with the reference and the disagreement is a stoichiometry error rather than a polymorph question: [ref 2] returns only Yb3Y(Si2O7)2 P1 (1) mp-1215859 at hull 0.010 with no ICSD backing, which is a disilicate RE2Si2O7, not a monosilicate. RE2SiO5 and RE2Si2O7 are different compounds with different structures and different thermal expansion -- the distinction is the whole point of the coatings literature these papers come from -- so that entry should not be attached. No mp_id is recorded. Neither paper is a transport study in the usual sense: both are measuring thermal conductivity for thermal and environmental barrier coatings, which is why the window is 293-1274 K and why there is no dopant.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Y/(Y+Yb) spans 0.20-0.80 over five compositions, median 0.50 -- a full alloy series with no dilute end, which is deliberate: the papers are engineering thermal conductivity downward by mass-contrast point-defect scattering on the rare-earth site, and the minimum sits mid-series. Both are trivalent and both occupy the two inequivalent rare-earth sites of the X2 structure, so the substitution is isovalent and does not change the polymorph; yttrium and ytterbium have almost the same ionic radius, which is why the series is continuous and why the scattering is from mass rather than strain.

basis: The single composition is ZrW2O8 and the paper is on the unusual thermal conductivity of the negative thermal expansion material. This is a well-defined structure type and the taxonomy had no entry for it, so I have proposed zrw2o8_type rather than park it: cubic P2_13, a framework of corner-linked ZrO6 octahedra and WO4 tetrahedra in which each tetrahedron has one terminal, singly coordinated oxygen. That free corner is the whole story -- it is what permits the transverse vibrational modes responsible for the negative thermal expansion, and it is also why the thermal conductivity is anomalously low and glass-like, which is what the paper measures. [ref 2] agrees and is the best-attested entry for the host: Zr(WO4)2 P2_13 (198) mp-18778 with 7 ICSD references. Its hull value of 0.074 should not be read as instability in the usual way -- ZrW2O8 is metastable against the binary oxides below about 1380 K and is recovered by quenching, so it is expected to sit above the hull. The alpha to beta order-disorder transition of the WO4 orientations near 430 K does not change the prototype and in any case lies above the measured 10-386 K window, so no phase sequence is recorded. The other two reference entries, Zr9W4O3 at hull 0.588 and ZrW2O11 at hull 0.439, are computed-only and are not candidates. No mp_id is recorded at host level, per project convention; mp-18778 is the one stage 2 should resolve to.

Two of the three papers are on bulk black phosphorus -- its thermoelectric power, and the large anisotropic thermal transport observed in bulk single crystals -- and between them they account for the single-crystal and bulk samples. Black phosphorus is the A17 structure, orthorhombic Cmce, a stack of puckered honeycomb layers held by van der Waals forces, and the anisotropy both papers are measuring is the direct consequence of that layering and of the armchair-zigzag distinction within a layer. The taxonomy had no entry for it, so I have proposed black_phosphorus_a17. The existing a7_rhombohedral entry is not a substitute and the reference block shows why: it separates P Cmce mp-157 with 25 ICSD references from P R-3m mp-130 with 4 and P Pm-3m mp-53 with 5, and the latter two are high-pressure phases of phosphorus, not what a bulk crystal at ambient pressure is. The hull ordering in that block is misleading in the way the chunk header warns about -- the triclinic P-1 entry sits at hull 0.000 with 2 references while Cmce sits at 0.030 with 25 -- and the ICSD count is the right signal, not the hull. Medium, and marked mixed, because the third paper does not belong to this material at all: thermoelectric power in reticulate doped polymers, which is where the fifth sample and the composition string PP come from. PP reads as polypropylene rather than as two phosphorus atoms, so that sample is a polymer and organic_polymer is the alternate. No mp_id is recorded.

other_polymorphs.note: The A7 grey-arsenic-type form of phosphorus, reached above roughly 5 GPa. 4 ICSD references against 25 for Cmce, and not produced by heating at ambient pressure, so it is not in the thermal sequence.

The simple cubic high-pressure phase of phosphorus, mp-53 at hull 0.141 with 5 ICSD references. The taxonomy has no simple-cubic elemental entry and b2_cscl would be wrong, since B2 is an ordered binary bcc structure and this is elemental, so the id is left neutral; the point of the record is only that this is a pressure phase and not a thermal one.

basis: Three of the five samples are FePb4Sb6S14 or its tin-substituted variants, and that formula is jamesonite, a lead antimony sulfosalt mineral: monoclinic, built from SbS3 ribbons cross-linked by lead in irregular high-coordination sites and by iron in its own octahedral site. The second paper is on high-performance thermoelectrics from earth-abundant materials in exactly this chemistry, and the first is on the electronic structure and thermoelectric properties of the thioantimonates. The taxonomy had no entry, so I have proposed jamesonite_fepb4sb6s14 rather than park a named mineral structure in unresolved_crystalline. Neither reference returns jamesonite itself, and that is the reason for medium. [ref 1] gives Sb6Pb4S13 P1 (1) mp-27907 -- the same cation ratio, one sulfur short, no iron -- and Sb2Pb2S5 at space group 62; [ref 2] gives the iron-free sulfosalts Sb8(PbS5)3, Sb8Pb7S19 and Sb4Pb5S11 plus MnSb6(Pb2S7)2. That last one is the useful corroboration: it is the same structural family with manganese in place of iron, which supports the octahedral divalent-cation site without naming the iron member. The space group in the proposal comes from materials knowledge and should be checked at v4 review. The fifth sample, Pb0.9Cl0.1Sb2S3, is a different material -- chlorine-doped lead-substituted Sb2S3, closer to the stibnite ribbon structure or to boulangerite -- so the host is marked mixed with stibnite as the alternate and splits on the Fe content. No mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Iron is not a dopant here at all and stage 3 must not compute a doping level for it. It is a full stoichiometric site of the jamesonite formula FePb4Sb6S14, occupying a distinct octahedral position, and it falls below the 5 at.% host cut only because the formula has 25 atoms -- 1 in 25 is 4%. alloying_component is the least wrong term available, and it is still wrong: the vocabulary has no role for a stoichiometric constituent pushed under the threshold by formula size, which is a gap worth closing, since the same problem produced the langasite silicon entry earlier in this chunk.

Sn0.04FePb4Sb5.96S14 and Sn0.08FePb4Sb5.92S14 replace a little antimony with tin, and the second paper is on enhancing the properties by exactly this. Sn2+ for Sb3+ removes an electron per substitution, so it is an acceptor on the ribbon site -- hole doping of a compound that is otherwise a poorly conducting semiconductor. Two levels against the undoped parent is a carrier-concentration trial.

Pb0.9Cl0.1Sb2S3 only, the composition that is not jamesonite. Chlorine on the sulfur site has one more valence electron, so it is an n-type donor in an antimony sulfide; the lead here is on the antimony site and would be an acceptor, so the two are being used together. Recorded against the second composition and not against the jamesonite structure.

basis: Four of the five samples are U2Ru2Sn -- one of them with a stray tab character in the composition string, which is a transcription artefact and not a different material -- and the first paper asks whether it is a new Kondo insulator, with the third reporting its magnetic, thermodynamic, NMR and transport properties as a heavy-fermion system. U2Ru2Sn is the Mo2FeB2 type, the ordered ternary derivative of U3Si2, tetragonal P4/mbm, and [ref 2] confirms it at U2SnRu2 P4/mbm (127) mp-20705 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference. The R2T2X family is exactly what the taxonomy entry covers and its exemplar Ce2Ni2Ga is the same structure. Medium rather than high because of the fifth composition, URuSn3, which is a single sample and is not this phase: the second paper is on new uranium compounds U3Sn5 and USn3, so a 1:1:3 uranium ruthenium stannide is plausibly a real distinct compound rather than a typo, and I cannot fix its structure from the formula. I have not marked the host mixed, because doing so would assert a second prototype I cannot name; it is flagged here instead so that a review pass can decide whether that sample needs a composition-level record. Note also the reference block returns USnRu P-62m mp-19811 with 6 ICSD references, the ZrNiAl-type equiatomic compound -- better attested than the 2:2:1 phase but at a stoichiometry no sample here has, which is a good example of the block describing the chemistry rather than the samples. No mp_id is recorded.

Four of the five samples are ZnS and the fifth is Al0.02ZnS, so the host is zinc sulfide. Cubic sphalerite F-43m is the ambient form and [ref 1] makes it primary at mp-10695, hull 0.000 with 26 ICSD references, against 3 references for the 2H wurtzite polytype and 1 each for the R3m and P3m1 stackings. The measured window is 180-334 K, far below the roughly 1290 K at which wurtzite becomes the equilibrium phase. Both papers measure thin films - an Al-implanted film and a photo-Seebeck study - and evaporated or sputtered ZnS films often retain some 2H, which is why the wurtzite polytype is recorded below rather than dismissed. ZnS2 Pa-3 in the reference block is the disulfide, a different compound, not a polymorph of what is measured here.

other_polymorphs.note: 2H ZnS at hull 0.001 with 3 ICSD references. It is the equilibrium phase only above about 1290 K, far above the 180-334 K window, so heating inside the measurement does not produce it; it is listed because it is routinely retained in deposited films, which is what both papers measure.

dopant_roles.basis: Al0.02ZnS, from a paper on the electrical conductivity of Al-implanted ZnS films: trivalent Al on the divalent Zn site is the standard n-type donor in II-VI sulfides.

basis: All five samples are USbTe single crystals, and this is the family the taxonomy entry was built on - its exemplar is UAsSe, the selenide analogue measured alongside USbTe in the first paper. UAsSe and USbTe are the ferromagnetic uranium members of the tetragonal P4/nmm MXY family, and [ref 2] returns USbTe P4/nmm (129) mp-7935 as primary with 2 ICSD references, the right space group. The hull value of 0.142 is not evidence against it: these are single crystals of a known compound and the 2019 snapshot handles actinide f electrons poorly. The other two papers are on ferromagnetism and Kondo behaviour of structural defects, which are statements about the electronic state of the same compound, not about a different structure.

Four of the five samples are elemental zirconium and the fifth is Zr97.5Er2.5, so this is hcp alpha-Zr (A3, P6_3/mmc), which [ref 2] gives as mp-131 at hull 0.000 with 17 ICSD references, well ahead of every other entry. It follows the treatment already given to the elemental metal hosts in the ledger - Ti, Nb, W, Fe, Ni, Mg and the rest are all filed under this entry for the A1, A2 and A3 close-packed metals. The papers are on high-melting-point metals, uranium-zirconium alloys and Zr-Er alloys, so the zirconium is the matrix in each case.

other_polymorphs.note: beta-Zr, bcc Im-3m, is the equilibrium phase above about 1136 K. The robust measured range stops at 1024 K, so no phases entry is warranted, but the full span including outliers reaches 1592 K, which means at least one curve in this host sits above the transition. Worth revisiting if those high-temperature curves are used.

dopant_roles.basis: Zr97.5Er2.5, from a paper on the phase state and thermal and mechanical properties of Zr-Er alloys. Erbium is added to zirconium as a neutron absorber, but its solubility in alpha-Zr is small, so a good part of the 2.5 at.% is likely a second phase rather than in solution. Recorded as substitutional because that is where the soluble fraction goes, at low confidence because the formula cannot separate the two.

basis: All four samples are Mg-Al-Ag at a fixed 15 at.% Ag with aluminium running from 10 to 50 at.%, and the single paper is titled New Icosahedral and Amorphous Phases in the Mg-Al-Ag System Prepared by Liquid Quenching - so which of the two a given composition forms is the subject of the paper, not something the host label can settle. [ref 2] supports the quasicrystalline reading structurally: its primary entry Mg32Al36Ag13 Im-3 (204) mp-31506 is the Mg32(Al,Zn)49 Bergman type, which is the 1/1 cubic approximant of the icosahedral phase in exactly this chemistry. Filed here with metallic_glass as the second prototype and marked mixed, because the paper asserts both are present across this composition range; the split has to be made per composition by reading it.

All four samples are BaAgAs with a dilute substituent on the arsenic site, and the paper is titled Exceptional Performance Driven by Planar Honeycomb Structure in a New ... - the planar honeycomb is the [AgAs] layer of the ZrBeSi type, the ordered AlB2 or Ni2In derivative this entry covers, whose exemplar CaAgSb is the same alkaline-earth coinage-metal pnictide family. [ref 2] returns BaAgAs P6_3/mmc (194) mp-7359 at hull 0.000, which is that space group. BaAgAs is also discussed as a topological nodal-line semimetal, and the flat honeycomb layer is the reason in both literatures.

dopant_roles.basis: BaAgAs0.97S0.03: sulfur carries one more valence electron than arsenic, so on the pnictogen site of the honeycomb layer it is an n-type donor.
BaAgAs0.95Sb0.05: same group as arsenic, so it tunes the band structure and the lattice thermal conductivity through mass and size contrast without changing the carrier count.
BaAgAs0.95Bi0.05: the heavy isovalent member of the same series, used for mass contrast and spin-orbit coupling rather than for doping.

basis: All four samples are AgPbBiSe3 with a dilute halide, which is the 1:1 line between PbSe and AgBiSe2 - the selenide analogue of the LAST rocksalts AgPbmSbTe2+m. Averaged over the Ag, Pb and Bi cations that is a single face-centred cubic cation sublattice against a selenium sublattice, and the paper, on bonding heterogeneity and lone-pair-induced anharmonicity, presumes the cubic rocksalt average with local distortion rather than a different framework. Medium rather than high because the AgBiSe2 end member orders into trigonal and rhombohedral cation-ordered forms below roughly 470 and 580 K, and the formula alone cannot tell me whether any ordered superstructure survives at the 296 K end of the window at this PbSe content. No reference block was returned for the host, so nothing external tests it either way.

other_polymorphs.note: The AgBiSe2 end member has cation-ordered low-temperature forms in which Ag and Bi separate onto alternating layers of the rocksalt lattice. Alloying with PbSe suppresses the ordering, so this is recorded as a possibility at the cold end of the window rather than as a thermal phase of the measured composition.

dopant_roles.basis: AgPbBiSe2.98Br0.02: a halogen on the chalcogen site is the standard n-type donor in rocksalt chalcogenides.
AgPbBiSe2.97I0.03: same donor mechanism as Br, on the selenium site.
AgPbBiSe2.97Cl0.03: same donor mechanism, the smallest of the three halogens used here.

basis: The curator composition details settle this outright: all four samples are Ca3Co4O9-Ag composites at 5, 7.5, 10 and 15 vol% silver, and the paper is on the fabrication and thermoelectric properties of Ca3Co4O9/Ag composites. The host is therefore the misfit-layered cobaltite Ca3Co4O9, the incommensurate [Ca2CoO3][CoO2] intergrowth this entry covers, with metallic silver added as a second phase to improve intergrain conduction. Silver appears in the host key only because the composite loading pushes it past the 5 at.% cut - it is not in the cobaltite lattice and does not substitute for calcium or cobalt, so no prototype is recorded for it. Every sample is nominally two-phase, which is worth carrying into stage 2, but composite_multiphase is not used as the label because the thermoelectric phase is unambiguous.

All four samples are AgCr1-xMgxO2 with x from 0.04 to 0.16, and the paper is explicitly on p-type delafossite Ag-based transparent conductors made by chemical solution synthesis. [ref 2] confirms the parent at CrAgO2 R-3m (166) mp-19378, hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references - the 3R delafossite stacking - with the 2H R3m polytype mp-1096875 behind it at hull 0.092. The curator detail says thin film for all four, so which polytype was actually grown is not settled by the composition; both are this prototype. The CrAgO4 and Cr2Ag2O7 entries in the block are different oxidation states at stoichiometries no sample here has.

other_polymorphs.note: The 2H (R3m) delafossite polytype at hull 0.092. Same prototype, different stacking of the same layers; a solution-deposited film can contain either, which is why it is recorded rather than ignored.

dopant_roles.basis: AgCr0.84Mg0.16O2: divalent Mg on the trivalent Cr site is the acceptor that makes these films p-type. At 16% of the chromium site in the most heavily doped sample it is a heavy acceptor alloy rather than dilute doping, even though the whole-formula fraction keeps it under the 5 at.% cut.

basis: All four samples are Ag6Ge10P12 within a small phosphorus excess, and the paper is on the origin of high thermoelectric performance in this earth-abundant phosphide. [ref 2] returns Ag3Ge5P6 I-43m (217) mp-17862 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, which is the same compound written at half the formula unit and gives the space group. No taxonomy entry covered a cubic silver germanium phosphide framework of this kind - it is not a sphalerite superstructure, not an ordered vacancy compound and not an argyrodite - so ag6ge10p12_type was proposed first and is used here.

dopant_roles.basis: The four samples run Ag6Ge10P12, P12.03, P12.05 and P12.1 - deliberate phosphorus excess over the stoichiometric formula, used to compensate phosphorus loss and tune the carrier concentration. It is excess on a host site, not a foreign species.

basis: Three compositions are GeAgxSbxSe2-2x and the fourth is written (GeSe)0.85(AgSbSe2)0.15, which is the same alloy line stated two ways. The first paper is titled High Thermoelectric Performance of New Rhombohedral Phase of GeSe stabilized ... - AgSbSe2 alloying is what pulls GeSe out of its ambient orthorhombic Pnma layered form into the rhombohedral R3m distortion of rocksalt, and that R3m phase is what this entry describes for GeTe. The GeSe analogue is isostructural, so the entry is used here rather than layered_ges. Medium because no reference block was returned for this host and the stabilisation depends on the AgSbSe2 content, which varies across the samples; the low-content end may still be orthorhombic.

other_polymorphs.note: Pnma GeSe is the ambient structure of the unalloyed parent. At the AgSbSe2 contents measured here the rhombohedral phase is the one the paper reports, so this is recorded as what the host reverts to at low alloying rather than as a thermal phase.

basis: Two closely related materials, both rhombohedral GeQ. (GeTe)75(AgSbTe2)18.75(AgSbSe2)6.25 is TAGS, the GeTe-AgSbTe2 pseudobinary with part of the tellurium replaced by selenium, whose ambient phase is the R3m rhombohedral distortion of rocksalt GeTe. GeSeAgxSbxTe1-x from the second paper is the same AgSb-stabilised rhombohedral GeQ approached from the selenide side, and it is the same research line as the Ag-Ge-Sb-Se host one rank below. Both land on this prototype even though the anion changes across the host. Medium because the anion axis below spans 0.10 to 0.77 in Se/(Se+Te): the R3m to cubic Fm-3m transition temperature moves with that ratio and with the AgSbQ2 content, so no single transition temperature can be given for the host and no phases array is recorded despite the window reaching 755 K. That is a limitation of the host level, not evidence that the measurements stay in one phase.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) across four compositions, median 0.71. Both are group 16 and share the chalcogen sublattice of the rhombohedral GeQ lattice, so the axis is genuine; the parent is GeTe-based at one end and GeSe-based at the other, and the rhombohedral to cubic transition temperature shifts along it.

basis: All four samples are Pd1-xAgxHy with x from 0.14 to 0.39 and y from 0.2 to 0.71, from a paper on the influence of hydrogen on electron transport of palladium alloyed with silver. Pd and Ag form a continuous face-centred cubic solid solution, and hydrogen occupies the octahedral interstices of that lattice - which is exactly this entry, whose exemplar is PdH0.66 and whose space group is Fm-3m. Silver sits in the host key because it is far above the 5 at.% cut, but structurally it is substitutional on the metal sublattice and does not change the prototype; the hydrogen is the interstitial and the variable the paper scans. No reference block was returned, which is expected for a non-stoichiometric hydride.

All four samples are KAg3Se2 and the paper title states the structural point: Ag2Se to KAg3Se2, Suppressing Order-Disorder Transitions via Reduced Dimensionality. Inserting potassium cuts the three-dimensional Ag2Se framework into anionic silver selenide layers, which is why the superionic transition of the parent is gone. [ref 1] gives KAg3Se2 C2/m (12) mp-9782 at hull 0.000 as primary. The taxonomy had ag2se_naumannite for the parent but nothing for this layered derivative, so kag3se2_layered was proposed first and is used here. Note that the 10-823 K window would cross the Ag2Se order-disorder transition near 400 K if this were the parent compound - the compound exists precisely so that it does not, so no phases array is recorded.

All four samples are silver with 7.4 to 14.6 at.% Mn, from the classic paper on the thermoelectric power and electrical resistivity of dilute alloys of Mn in the noble metals - the Kondo and spin-glass system. Manganese dissolves substitutionally in the face-centred cubic silver lattice at these levels and no Ag-Mn compound is involved; no reference block was returned for the host, which is consistent with there being no stable ordered phase to return. Filed with the other A1 metal solid solutions, as the Au-Mn host in this same chunk is.

All four samples are AgSbO3 and the first paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of AgSbO3 with defect pyrochlore structure, so the structure is named in the source: the corner-sharing Sb2O6 octahedral network of pyrochlore with the O-prime site empty, Ag2Sb2O6 rather than A2B2O7, in Fd-3m with a cell near 10.2 A. The taxonomy carried only the full pyrochlore and the KSbO3-type framework, and this is neither, so defect_pyrochlore_a2b2o6 was proposed first. I disagree with [ref 2] and do not follow its ranking: it puts Ag3SbO4 P4_122 mp-1202934 first on a single ICSD reference, its one AgSbO3 entry is a computed monoclinic C2 (5) structure mp-860791, and its Fd-3m entry mp-1214924 is written AgSbO12 at hull 1.047. None of those is the cubic defect pyrochlore both papers report, so no mp_id is recorded here.

All four samples are AgxTiS2 with x from 0.32 to 0.98, and the paper is on thermoelectric power in solid-solution electrodes - silver intercalated electrochemically into the van der Waals gap of 1T TiS2. The host lattice is the CdI2-type TiS2 slab stack this entry covers; the silver is a guest between slabs, not a replacement for titanium, and it appears in the host key only because at these loadings it is far above the 5 at.% cut. [ref 2] returns Ti3AgS6 R-3 mp-1217143 and Ti6AgS12 C2/m mp-675920, which are silver-ordered superstructures of the same intercalated stack at x = 1/3 and 1/6; they corroborate the intercalation picture rather than contradicting it. At x near 1 the silver ordering becomes a superstructure question, not a different prototype.

All four samples are SrAgSb at or just above stoichiometry, and the paper is titled Promising Zintl-Phase Thermoelectric Compound SrAgSb. Alkaline-earth coinage-metal pnictides at this 1:1:1 stoichiometry take the hexagonal ZrBeSi type, the ordered AlB2 derivative with planar [AgSb] honeycomb layers between strontium planes - the same structure assigned to BaAgAs twelve ranks earlier in this chunk, and the same family as the exemplar CaAgSb. [ref 2] does return SrAgSb P6_3/mmc (194) mp-11217, which is that space group, but ranks Sr(Ag2Sb)2 R-3m mp-1077980 above it on hull energy. I do not follow that ranking: the 1:2:2 CaAl2Si2-type phase is a different stoichiometry from every composition measured here, and a 0.211 hull value on the 1:1:1 entry is a statement about a calculated convex hull, not evidence against a compound the paper synthesised and measured. The Sr1.01 to Sr1.03 spread is deliberate cation excess used to tune carriers, not a second element.

Both compositions are Au49Al36Tm15 and Au49Al34Tm17, and the two papers name the phase directly: thermoelectric properties of Tsai-type Au-Al-RE quasicrystals and approximants, and localised electron magnetism in the icosahedral Au-Al-Tm quasicrystal. This is the aperiodic entry, whose own note says to map to an approximant in stage 2 because there is no periodic structure to resolve. [ref 2] returns only the ordinary intermetallics TmAl7Au3 R-3c, TmAlAu Pnma and TmAlAu2 Fm-3m, none of which is the Tsai-type cluster phase - exactly what a database of periodic structures can be expected to say about a quasicrystal.

Both compositions are CePd1-xNixAl at x = 0.2 and 0.4, single crystals, from a paper on the thermoelectric power of CePd1-xNixAl single crystals. CePdAl is the ZrNiAl type - the ordered Fe2P structure, hexagonal P-62m - and CeNiAl is the isostructural end member, so the substitution series stays on one prototype throughout. The parent is attested in the neighbouring Al-Ce-Pd host of this same chunk, where [ref 2] gives CeAlPd P-62m (189) mp-21158 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references. No reference block was returned for the quaternary host itself. Nickel is above the 5 at.% cut here and so is not in the dopant list, but it is substitutional on the palladium site and the series is a chemical-pressure scan of the Kondo lattice.

Two of the four samples are CePdAl and two are CePd0.9Ni0.1Al, the x = 0.1 member of the series that makes up the neighbouring Al-Ce-Ni-Pd host. [ref 2] returns CeAlPd P-62m (189) mp-21158 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, the ZrNiAl ordered Fe2P type this entry covers; the block leader CeAl3Pd2 P6/mmm mp-4785 has more references but is a different stoichiometry from anything measured here. CePdAl is a well known geometrically frustrated Kondo lattice, the frustration coming from the distorted kagome cerium sublattice of that structure, which is what a thermopower study of it is about.

dopant_roles.basis: CePd0.9Ni0.1Al: nickel takes the palladium site of the ZrNiAl structure, CeNiAl being the isostructural end member. The substitution applies chemical pressure and tunes the ratio of Kondo to RKKY energy scales rather than adding carriers.

basis: All four samples are Al65Cu20Co15-xFex with x from 5 to 10, and the first paper is titled Electron transport in Al65Cu20Co15-xFex quasicrystals. Al65Cu20Co15 is the classic decagonal quasicrystal composition and iron substitution for cobalt runs along it; the second paper is on Al-Pd-Mn icosahedral quasicrystals, the same class of material. No reference block was returned for the host, which is what an aperiodic phase produces.

All four samples are Ni2CuCrFeAlx with x from 0.5 to 2.5 - the AlxCoCrCuFeNi family with cobalt left out - and the paper is on the thermoelectric behaviour of a high-entropy alloy. This entry is exactly that multi-principal-element solid solution. Aluminium content is the variable that drives these alloys from face-centred cubic at low x towards body-centred cubic and B2 ordering at high x, with a two-phase region between, so no single space group can be attached to the host; the prototype absorbs that, which is why the host is not marked mixed. No reference block was returned.

All four samples are Al-Cu-Fe-Si near Al65Cu8Fe17Si10, and both papers name the phase: low thermal conductivity of Al-based icosahedral quasicrystals, and the extremely small thermal conductivity of the Al-based Mackay-type approximant. The curator nominal compositions Al67Cu7Fe17Si9 through Al65Cu7Fe17Si11 sit in the Mackay-type approximant field rather than in the Al-Cu-Fe icosahedral field. Both the quasicrystal and its approximants are this entry, which is why it is named for the pair; the fourth sample, Al53Cu25.5Fe12.5Si9, is the outlier in composition but comes from the same two papers.

All four samples are UCu4+xAl8-x with x from 0 to 1.75, and the paper is on non-Fermi-liquid behaviour in UCu4+xAl8-x. That 1:12 stoichiometry is the ThMn12 type, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, with copper and aluminium sharing the three transition-metal sites - x is literally the redistribution between them, which is why the series exists. [ref 2] returns U(Al2Cu)4 I4/mmm (139) mp-7248 at hull 0.011 with 2 ICSD references, the same formula and space group; its other entries are unrelated stoichiometries, one of them at hull 0.455.

Two unrelated materials share this host. Three samples are Al72.5Mn21.5Fe6.0, from a paper on the anisotropic transport properties of the Al13TM4 and T-Al-Mn-Fe complex metallic alloys - the Taylor phase, a large-cell decagonal approximant, which is this entry. The fourth is Fe2MnAl, from a paper on half-metallic ferromagnetic Heusler alloys, which is the full Heusler L21 structure; [ref 2] gives MnAlFe2 Fm-3m (225) mp-31185 at hull 0.000 for it. One label would be wrong for one of them, so the host is marked mixed and must be split in stage 2 on the aluminium fraction - the approximant sits at 72 at.% Al, the Heusler at 25 at.%. Medium confidence on the majority label because complex metallic alloys in this system cover several large-cell phases and the composition alone does not fix which one.

All four samples are NiAlxFe2-xO4, which the curator composition detail confirms as the NiAlxFe2-xO4 series, and the paper is on electrical conduction in Ni-Al ferrites. NiFe2O4 is an inverse spinel and Al3+ substitutes for Fe3+ across the series while the AB2O4 framework is unchanged; x reaches 1.6 here, which is heavy substitution towards NiAl2O4 but still spinel at both ends. No reference block was returned for the host. Aluminium is in the host key rather than the dopant list because it is far above the 5 at.% cut; it is substitutional for iron, with the usual complication that the Al3+ and Fe3+ redistribute between tetrahedral and octahedral sites as x rises, which changes the inversion degree but not the prototype.

The compositions are written (Hg3Se)1-x(Al2Se3)x with manganese at the 0.1% level, from a paper on the electrical and optical properties of manganese-doped (3HgSe)(Al2Se3). [ref 1] gives the ordered ternary of that line directly: Al2HgSe4 I-4 (82) mp-3038 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, the defect chalcopyrite, with the cation-disordered Fd-3m defect zincblende form mp-1103510 behind it. HgAl2Se4 is a textbook ordered vacancy compound - one cation site in three empty in an ordered pattern - so the entry fits. Medium rather than high because the samples sit at (Hg3Se)0.5(Al2Se3)0.5 and 0.7/0.3 rather than at the HgAl2Se4 point, so what is measured is a mercury-rich section of the pseudobinary in which the vacancy ordering may be partial or absent; [ref 2] returning Al2Hg5Se8 P1 mp-685952 is a sign of exactly that intermediate region.

other_polymorphs.note: The cation-disordered defect zincblende form of Al2HgSe4 at hull 0.048 with 2 ICSD references: the same tetrahedral framework with the vacancies randomised instead of ordered. A quenched mercury-rich composition is as likely to show this as the ordered I-4 form, which is the reason confidence on the main label is medium.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn at 0.001 to 0.0015 per formula unit, from a paper on manganese doping of this pseudobinary: Mn2+ replaces Hg2+ on the tetrahedral cation site, the standard dilute magnetic semiconductor substitution in mercury chalcogenides.

basis: All four samples are written Mg5Al2Sb6, which is exactly the A5M2Pn6 stoichiometry of the Ca5Al2Sb6 Zintl phase this entry covers, and it charge balances the same way - five Mg2+ against an [Al2Sb6]10- chain polyanion. That is the reason for the assignment, and it is the only reason. The paper is titled Thermoelectric and mechanical properties of Mg-Al-Sb alloys, which does not assert a single phase, and [ref 2] contains no Mg5Al2Sb6 at all: its entries are unrelated stoichiometries at hull values from 0.041 to 0.233. A two-phase Mg3Sb2 plus AlSb mixture would give the same nominal formula, and Mg2+ is small for the A site of this structure type. Low confidence, with both alternatives recorded; this host should be checked against the paper before the label is used.

All four samples are TaAlN, from a paper on fabricating high-TCR TaAl-N thin films by reactive sputtering. Reactively sputtered Ta-Al-N is normally either a face-centred cubic (Ta,Al)N solid solution on the rocksalt TaN lattice or X-ray amorphous, depending on nitrogen flow and substrate temperature, and the rocksalt nitride entry covers the crystalline case. I disagree with [ref 2] here: its only entry is Ta4AlN3 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1188888 at hull 0.185, a MAX-type layered ternary nitride that is made by hot pressing at high temperature and is not what reactive sputtering at a nominal 1:1:1 ratio produces. Low confidence and amorphous recorded as the alternative: with one film composition, a 306-772 K resistive measurement and no diffraction named in the title, the two readings are about equally likely and the paper would settle it.

All four samples are Al-Si-Ru near Al67Si9Ru24, two of them with copper, and the first paper is titled Experimental realization of a semiconducting quasicrystalline approximant - the Al-Si-Ru 1/1 approximant, one of the few members of this family with a real gap, which is why it is measured thermoelectrically at all. The second paper is on the effects of Cu doping on the thermoelectric properties of the same Al-Si-Ru semiconductor, and the _IAC_1_0 suffix on three composition strings is the curator recording that 1/1 approximant. [ref 2] returns only AlSiRu2 Fm-3m mp-862778, a small Heusler-like cubic cell rather than the large approximant cell, which is the usual blind spot of a database of simple periodic structures.

dopant_roles.basis: Al67.5Si7.5Cu2Ru23 and Al65.6Si8.1Cu4.1Ru22.1, from the paper on Cu doping of the Al-Si-Ru approximant. Copper comes at the expense of aluminium while ruthenium stays near 23 at.%, so the aluminium-rich cluster shells are where it goes; it shifts the Fermi level within the pseudogap.

basis: The compositions are written (AlSb)1-x(Zn4Sb3)x with x from 0.1 to 0.3, and the papers are on composite fabrication to improve the thermoelectric properties of AlSb and on improving AlSb by incorporation of a second phase. That is a two-phase composite by construction: the matrix is zincblende AlSb, this entry, and the additive is beta-Zn4Sb3, which has its own entry. Marked mixed and given both, with AlSb as the primary label because it is 70 to 90% of every sample. No reference block was returned for the host. Medium confidence because the composite is deliberate and neither phase can be called the structure of the sample on its own.

dopant_roles.basis: (Al0.995Mg0.005Sb)0.9(Zn4Sb3)0.1: divalent Mg on the trivalent Al site of zincblende AlSb is an acceptor, and the second paper title, truncated at Incorporation of M, is most plausibly about this magnesium addition.

basis: Three of the four samples are YAl2, the cubic MgCu2 C15 Laves phase, and [ref 2] gives YAl2 Fd-3m (227) mp-2322 at hull 0.000 with 18 ICSD references - the best attested entry in the block by a wide margin. The papers are on transport in spin-fluctuation systems and in RAl2 and RCo2 compounds, which is the RAl2 Laves series. The fourth sample is YAl3, a different structure: [ref 2] puts it at R-3m (166) mp-2451 with 7 ICSD references, the rhombohedral BaPb3-type nine-layer close-packed stacking of the AB3 family. The taxonomy has no entry for that stacking variant, so cu3au_l12 is recorded as the nearest AB3 relative and flagged here as an imperfect fit - it is not a claim that YAl3 is cubic L12. Mixed, and cleanly separable on the Al:Y ratio in stage 2.

All four samples are Cu-As-Te at a fixed 55 at.% Te, made as melt-spun ribbons, and the paper is titled Chalcogenide Glasses as Prospective Thermoelectric Materials. Ribbon form plus a glass-forming Cu-As-Te composition plus a measurement that stops at 299 K is the glass, not a crystalline phase. [ref 2] offers only CuTeAs Pnma mp-1184180 at hull 0.027 with no ICSD reference - a computed crystalline ternary, which is roughly what the melt would crystallise to if it were allowed to, and not a description of these ribbons. Filed under amorphous rather than metallic_glass because the network is covalent chalcogenide, not a glass-forming metal eutectic.

All four samples are LaFeAsO1-xFx at x = 0.2 and 0.225, the 1111 iron pnictide, and both papers say so in their titles. The ZrCuSiAs type, P4/nmm, with [La2O2] layers alternating with [Fe2As2] layers, is exactly this entry, and the taxonomy already records F-for-O in LaFeAsO1-xFx as the doping variable of the prototype. Fluorine lands in the host key rather than the dopant list only because at x = 0.2 it is exactly 5 at.% of the formula; it is the doping variable, not an alloying end member. No reference block was returned. The 10-299 K window crosses superconducting and magnetic transitions, which are electronic rather than structural; the tetragonal-to-orthorhombic distortion of the undoped parent near 150 K is suppressed at this doping level, so no phases array is recorded.

All four samples are SmFeAsO0.8F0.2, written two ways by different curators - the samarium member of the 1111 family, the same ZrCuSiAs P4/nmm structure as the lanthanum host one rank above, and the compound that carries the highest transition temperature of the pnictide 1111 series. Both papers are on RFeAsO1-xFx. I disagree with [ref 2]: its only entry is Sm6Fe6As6O5F P2_1/m mp-697821 at hull 0.169, which is not a distinct structure but the same 1111 lattice in a supercell with one fluorine placed at a chosen site so that a calculation can be run on an ordered cell. Taking it as the structure of the host would be an artefact of how doped compounds have to be modelled.

All four samples are LaFeAsO1-xHx at x = 0.25 to 0.30, two of them with phosphorus on the arsenic site, from a paper on three superconducting phases in heavily hydrogen-doped LaFeAsO. Hydride doping replaces O2- with H- in the [La2O2] layer of the same ZrCuSiAs 1111 structure and reaches electron concentrations fluorine cannot, which is how that paper maps two superconducting domes; the lattice itself is unchanged. Hydrogen is in the host key because 0.25 per formula unit is above the 5 at.% cut, and it is the doping variable - the hydride analogue of the F-for-O substitution the prototype notes already name. Note the first composition is transcribed as LaFeAs1O0.75H0.25, where the As1 is a transcription of stoichiometric arsenic rather than a separate species.

dopant_roles.basis: LaFeAs0.9P0.1O0.75H0.25 and LaFeAs0.8P0.1O0.90H0.30: phosphorus is the same group as arsenic and takes the pnictogen site, compressing the FeAs layer. It applies chemical pressure rather than adding carriers, and in this paper it is used alongside the hydrogen content to move between the superconducting domes.

basis: All four samples are (K,Ba,Sr)Fe2As2 - KFe2As2 itself, K0.87Sr0.13Fe2As2 and two Ba-K members - which is the 122 iron pnictide family, the ThCr2Si2 type in I4/mmm. [ref 2] confirms K(FeAs)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-675576 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. The second paper is on electron- and hole-doped BaFe2As2, the same structure with the alkaline earth on the A site, and the taxonomy already names K-for-Ba in Ba1-xKxFe2As2 as the doping variable of this prototype; these samples approach the same axis from the potassium end. The measured 12-300 K window covers superconducting and spin-density-wave transitions, which are electronic.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.2K0.8Fe2As2 and Ba0.1K0.9Fe2As2: divalent Ba on the monovalent alkali site removes holes from the FeAs layer. This is the Ba1-xKxFe2As2 axis the prototype notes describe, entered from the potassium-rich end, so it is the doping variable rather than an impurity.
K0.87Sr0.13Fe2As2: the strontium version of the same hole-count variable, and the first paper is on the phase diagram of KxSr1-xFe2As2.

basis: All four samples are LaFe1-xMnxAsO with x from 0.2 to 0.8, from a paper on impurity doping and NMR in the La 1111 system, so the structure is the ZrCuSiAs 1111 lattice throughout: manganese substitutes iron inside the [Fe2As2] layer across the whole range and LaMnAsO is the isostructural end member, so the type does not change. One thing to flag rather than fix: every composition is transcribed with a second iron term, O0.89Fe0.11, which cannot be right - iron already occupies the transition-metal layer, and the oxygen-site substituent in this family and in this paper series is fluorine. It is almost certainly F0.11 mis-parsed into Fe0.11, and it inflates the apparent iron content of every sample in this host. The prototype is unaffected either way, but the parsed fractions here should not be used for stage 3 without checking.

All four samples are the dilute magnetic semiconductor (Ga,Mn)As, from a paper on resistivity minima and the Kondo effect in ferromagnetic GaMnAs films. These are molecular-beam-epitaxy films of zincblende GaAs with a few per cent of Mn2+ substituting for Ga3+ - the zincblende lattice is what makes them epitaxially compatible with a GaAs substrate in the first place, and the ferromagnetism depends on the manganese staying substitutional rather than interstitial. Note that the composition string GaMnAs is a name, not a stoichiometry: parsed literally it reads as an equiatomic ternary, which is what put manganese into the host key, while the real x in Ga1-xMnxAs is of order 0.05. No reference block was returned. The structure is not in doubt here; the manganese content is.

Three of the four samples are GeAs and the fourth is Sn0.08Ge0.92As, and the paper is titled GeAs: Highly Anisotropic van der Waals Thermoelectric Material. [ref 2] gives GeAs C2/m (12) mp-9548 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references - the layered monoclinic GeAs type, whose slabs contain Ge-Ge dimers, which is where the anisotropy in the title comes from. The taxonomy had no entry for it: layered_ges is the orthorhombic Pnma GeS type, a different arrangement with no metal-metal bonds, so geas_layered_c2m was proposed first and is used here. The block is led by GeAs2 Pbam mp-17524 on 3 ICSD references, but that is a different compound, not a polymorph of what is measured.

dopant_roles.basis: Sn0.08Ge0.92As: tin is the heavy group 14 neighbour of germanium and takes its site. At 8% of the germanium site it is a light isovalent alloy for band and lattice tuning rather than a carrier dopant.

basis: Two samples are Re3GeAs6 and two Re3Ge0.6As6.4, from two papers on new ternary arsenides for high-temperature thermoelectrics. The stoichiometry is what makes the assignment: Re3(Ge,As)7 is the A3X7 archetype of the Ir3Ge7 or Mo3Sb7 type, body-centred cubic Im-3m, with germanium and arsenic sharing the X positions - and Re3Ge0.6As6.4 is precisely a Ge/As ratio tuned within a fixed 3:7 framework, which is what that structure allows. Medium rather than high because [ref 2] does not contain the compound: its only entry is a computed ReGeAs C2/m mp-1219536 at a different stoichiometry with no ICSD reference. The type therefore comes from the formula and materials knowledge, not from a reference line, and should be checked against the papers at review.

All four samples are As14Ge14Se57-66Sb6-15 bulk glasses, from a paper on semiconducting quaternary chalcogenide glasses as new potential thermoelectric materials. Ge-As-Se is one of the best known glass-forming systems and antimony is added to it here to raise the carrier concentration; the 300-450 K measurement stays below crystallisation. The As/Sb axis reported for this host is recorded below, but with shared_site null: in a glass this is substitution between network-forming pnictogens, not occupancy of a crystallographic site, and reading it as a site fraction would be wrong.

solid_solution_axis.note: As/(As+Sb) over four compositions, median 0.61. Both are three-coordinate pnictogens bonded to selenium in the glass network, so the substitution is real, but there is no crystallographic site to assign it to; raising the antimony content lowers the glass transition and pushes the material towards crystallisation.

basis: All four samples are La1-xSrxZnAsO with x from 0 to 0.075, and the paper is on the thermoelectric properties of that series. LaZnAsO is the ZrCuSiAs 1111 type, P4/nmm, with [La2O2] layers alternating with [Zn2As2] layers - the same framework as the LaFeAsO hosts above it in this chunk, but with zinc in place of iron, which makes it a wide-gap p-type semiconductor rather than a pnictide superconductor. I disagree with [ref 2] here: it returns only La2ZnAs2O and LaZn2AsO2 at hull 1.373 and 1.150, neither of which is the 1:1:1:1 compound measured, and both at energies that mark them as computed curiosities rather than candidate structures for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.925Sr0.075ZnAsO: divalent Sr on the trivalent La site of the oxide layer is the acceptor that makes this series p-type, the same aliovalent A-site substitution used throughout the 1111 family.

basis: All four samples are NaZn4-xCuxAs3 and the paper title states the phase: NaZn4-xCuxAs3 crystallised in the rhombohedral system. [ref 2] returns NaZn4As3 R-3m (166) mp-1078703 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, matching both the formula and the symmetry. That layered rhombohedral Zintl pnictide - charge balanced as Na+ plus four Zn2+ against three As3- - had no taxonomy entry, and [ref 1] offers only NaZnAs P4/nmm mp-13097, the PbFCl-type 1:1:1 compound, which is a different stoichiometry and a different stacking; the F-43m NaZnAs entry behind it at hull 0.130 is neither. So nazn4as3_type was proposed first and is used here. The block description in that proposal is tentative and flagged for v4 review; the formula and space group are not.

dopant_roles.basis: NaZn3.98Cu0.02As3 through NaZn3.94Cu0.06As3: the paper series is written NaZn4-xCuxAs3, so copper is explicitly on the zinc site. Monovalent Cu replacing divalent Zn is an acceptor and is the carrier-tuning knob of the study.

basis: All four samples are NdO0.8F0.2Sb1-xAsxSe2, and the paper is on the crystal structure and thermoelectric transport of As-doped NdOSbSe2. This is the LaOBiS2 family with antimony in place of bismuth and selenium in place of sulfur: alternating fluorite-like [Nd2O2] layers and [SbSe2] square-net layers in P4/nmm, which is what this entry covers. No reference block was returned for this five-element host. Note that the As:Sb ratio is 0.4 to 0.6 across the samples, so the pnictogen site is genuinely mixed rather than dilutely doped, whatever the title calls it; the axis is recorded below even though the chunk file did not flag one, since only two distinct compositions exist here.

dopant_roles.basis: NdO0.8F0.2: fluorine on the oxygen site of the [Nd2O2] layer is the electron-doping variable of the whole LaOBiS2 family, not an impurity - the undoped parent is barely conducting and is not measured here at all.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: pnictogen site of the [SbSe2] layer
solid_solution_axis.note: As/(As+Sb) across the two compositions. Not flagged in the chunk file, presumably because two compositions are too few for the detector, but it is a genuine isovalent mix of the pnictogen site at close to 50:50 rather than doping.

basis: All four samples are Th3(As1-ySby)4 and the paper is on X-ray and thermoelectric studies of cubic Th3X4 compounds, so both the type and the cubic symmetry are named in the source. Th3P4, I-43d, is this entry, and the taxonomy already names cation vacancies in Th3-xX4 as the carrier-concentration knob of the prototype. The As/Sb axis runs the full 0.10 to 0.90 across the anion site, so the host is one continuous solid solution between Th3As4 and Th3Sb4 - both the same structure, which is why a single prototype is correct here even though no single parent compound is. [ref 2] returns only a computed Th3(SbAs)2 I2_13 mp-1217386 at a different stoichiometry, so no mp_id is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: As/(As+Sb) over four compositions, median 0.75. Th3As4 and Th3Sb4 are both Th3P4-type, so the whole axis stays on one prototype and the end member assigned per composition in stage 3 changes the lattice parameter and the band gap, not the structure.

basis: Two compounds, two structures, two samples each. U3As4 is the Th3P4 type, cubic I-43d, and [ref 2] gives U3As4 I-43d (220) mp-606 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references; the first paper is on giant anisotropic magnetoresistance and magnetothermopower in cubic 3:4 uranium pnictides. UAs2 is the tetragonal P4/nmm anti-Fe2As or Cu2Sb type, mp-1657 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, which is the same P4/nmm MXY arrangement the PbFCl entry covers - that entry names anti-Fe2As and Cu2Sb as related in its own prototype field, and it is what USbTe was assigned earlier in this chunk. Marked mixed and split on the As:U ratio: 4:3 is the cubic phase, 2:1 the tetragonal one. Note the block is led by rocksalt UAs mp-2104 on 14 ICSD references, a third compound that no sample here has - a clean instance of the reference describing the chemistry rather than the samples.

The composition string AuFe is a name, not a stoichiometry: the paper is on the absolute thermoelectric power of AuFe alloys between 0.01 K and 7 K, which is the classic dilute Kondo system - parts per million to a few at.% iron in face-centred cubic gold, the material AuFe thermocouples are made of. Gold and iron have a wide miscibility gap and form no stable compound, and [ref 2] agrees in its own way: every entry it returns is a computed structure at hull 0.137 to 0.247 with no ICSD reference at all. Medium confidence because the parsed formula cannot tell me the iron concentration, only that the matrix is fcc gold; no measured temperature range is recorded for this host either, which is consistent with a sub-kelvin study the digitiser could not place.

All four samples are gold with 6.8 to 18.6 at.% Mn, from papers on the thermoelectric power and resistivity of dilute manganese in the noble metals - quenched face-centred cubic Au(Mn), the spin-glass and Kondo system, the same series as the Ag-Mn host in this chunk. Medium rather than high for one reason: Au81.4Mn18.6 is within a point of Au4Mn, which orders into the tetragonal MnAu4 structure that [ref 2] lists at I4/m (87) mp-12565 with 2 ICSD references, so whether that sample is a disordered solid solution depends on its thermal history rather than on its composition. The other three sit well below any ordered stoichiometry. MnAu2 I4/mmm leads the block on 4 references but is far from every composition measured here.

other_polymorphs.note: MnAu4, I4/m, the ordered superstructure the 18.6 at.% sample would adopt if annealed rather than quenched. Recorded under unresolved_crystalline because the taxonomy has no entry for this ordered AB4 tetragonal variant and filing it under the disordered solid solution would assert the opposite of what it is.

basis: Two samples are BaB6 and two are Ca0.25Ba0.75B6 and Sr0.25Ba0.75B6, and the papers are on high-pressure densified solid solutions of alkaline earth hexaborides and on the thermoelectric properties of divalent hexaborides. That is the CaB6 type outright: a simple cubic Pm-3m framework of B6 octahedra with the divalent cation in the cage. [ref 2] confirms BaB6 Pm-3m (221) mp-954 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references; its other two entries, Ba3NaB24 and Ba3SmB24, are different borides at stoichiometries no sample here has.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.25Ba0.75B6: calcium takes a quarter of the barium cage sites. Same valence, so it changes the cage occupancy and the rattling rather than the electron count, and the paper treats these as alkaline earth hexaboride solid solutions. It falls under the 5 at.% cut only because the formula carries six borons.
Sr0.25Ba0.75B6: the strontium member of the same alkaline earth solid-solution series, on the same cage site and for the same reason.

basis: Every composition is (Bi0.48Sb1.52Te3)72.83B27.17, i.e. the workhorse p-type Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 alloy with boron added, and the paper is titled Synergistic effects of B-In codoping in zone-melted Bi0.48Sb1.52Te3-ba[sed ...]. Zone-melted Bi0.48Sb1.52Te3 is tetradymite R-3m outright. Boron reaches the host key only because the composition is written as a molar mixture of two components: the 27.17 is mol percent of elemental B against 72.83 mol percent of a five-atom formula unit, so the real atomic fraction is far smaller and boron is a dopant or a dispersed second phase, not a host constituent. The Bi:Sb ratio is fixed at 0.24 across all four compositions, so this is a single parent rather than a series.

dopant_roles.basis: In goes on the group 15 cation site of the tetradymite at 0.003 to 0.007 per two Bi+Sb, and the paper calls it codoping with boron. In Bi2Te3-type alloys indium is the standard resonant-level dopant on that site.

Boron is named as the second codopant in the title, but nothing in the composition fixes where it sits: it is too small to substitute comfortably for Bi, Sb or Te, and in zone-melted tetradymites boron additions are usually reported as a dispersed phase or a grain-boundary scavenger rather than as a lattice substituent. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed. Note also that its 27.17 is a molar coefficient of the second component, not an atomic percentage, so the parsed fraction that put B into the host key overstates it by roughly a factor of five.

basis: All four samples are YNi2B2C and the paper is Thermal conductivity of RNi2B2C (R=Y,Ho) single crystals. That is the LuNi2B2C borocarbide exactly -- the taxonomy entry is seeded on B-C-Ni-Yb, and yttrium is the same 1-2-2-1 compound with the same I4/mmm cell of NiB tetrahedral layers separated by R-C sheets. [ref 2] confirms YNi2B2C I4/mmm (139) mp-6576 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in the block; its other two, YNiBC P4/nmm and TbY3Ni8(B2C)4 P4/mmm, are different stoichiometries that no sample here has.

All four samples are B6S0.599 to B6S0.628 and the paper is titled An alpha-rhombohedral boron-related compound with sulfur: Synthesis, struc[ture ...]. B6S0.6 is B12S1.2 per icosahedron, which is the B12X2 family -- the alpha-rhombohedral B12 icosahedral array with the inter-icosahedral site occupied by a heavier main-group atom, as in B12P2 and B12As2 -- and the structure type is named in the paper title rather than inferred. The taxonomy had only boron_carbide, which folds B4C and beta-rhombohedral boron together and whose inter-icosahedral species is a covalent C-B-C chain; b12x2_alpha_boron is proposed here for the two-atom and single-atom variants. Confidence is medium rather than high because [ref 2] is unhelpful: it leads with B2S3 I4_1/a mp-1199451 and BS2 P2_1/c mp-1200183, which are molecular thioborates at a different chemistry, and carries B12S R3m (160) mp-1228640 at hull 0.076 with no ICSD reference at all.

dopant_roles.basis: Sulfur is a host constituent, not a dopant, but the four compositions differ only in its occupancy -- 0.599, 0.609, 0.620, 0.628 per B6 against 1.0 for a filled inter-icosahedral site. That partial occupancy is the carrier knob of the series and is the variable the paper sweeps, the same role the carbon content plays across the B4C homogeneity range. Stage 3 should read it as non-stoichiometry rather than as a doping level.

basis: The host element set is wrong and the curator settles it. The parsed compositions read Bi1.6Pb0.4Ba2Ca2O10, but composition_details transcribed from the paper reads Bi1.6Pb0.4Ba2Co2O plus 1, 3 or 5 wt percent Ag, and the paper is titled Improved thermoelectric performances in textured Bi1.6Pb0.4Ba2Co2Oy/Ag[ composites]. Every Ca in this host is a Co: the routing key should be Ba-Bi-Co-O. Bi1.6Pb0.4Ba2Co2Oy is the barium member of the Bi-based misfit layered cobaltites, a [Bi,Pb,Ba,O] rocksalt block stacked incommensurately on CoO2 sheets, the same family as Bi2Sr2Co2Oy. I therefore disagree with [ref 2] in full: its Ba2CaBiO6 Fm-3m mp-1214698, Ba3CaBi2O9 Immm mp-1228277 and Ba4Ca(BiO4)3 Im-3m mp-1147549 are real Ba-Ca-Bi oxides but they answer a question about a chemistry that is not the one measured here. Confidence is medium only because the assignment rests on the curator string overriding the parsed formula.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb0.4 against Bi1.6 in the rocksalt block. Pb-for-Bi is the standard hole-doping substitution in the Bi-based misfit cobaltites and in the Bi cuprates, and it also stabilises the intergrowth; it is a fixed part of the parent formula here rather than a swept variable.

The curator string gives it as plus 1, 3 or 5 wt percent Ag and the paper title says composites. Silver is added as a metallic second phase to improve conductivity and texture, not dissolved into the cobaltite lattice.

basis: The two compositions are TlBaSrCaCu2O7 and TlBaSrCa2Cu3O9, and the paper is Systematic thermopower measurements of the thallium cuprates Tl(Ba,Sr)[...]. A single Tl-O charge-reservoir layer with (Ba,Sr) on the adjacent site makes these the Tl-1212 and Tl-1223 members, which is the ABa2Ca(n-1)CunO(2n+2+d) single-reservoir series that this entry names explicitly among its representative materials. The two homologues differ only in n, so the host is not mixed: n is a member index within one prototype, not a second structure. The double-Tl-layer alternative tl_2212_cuprate is excluded by the single Tl per formula unit. [ref 2] offers only BaSrCa2Tl(CuO3)3 Pm (6) mp-1227794, which is the 1223 composition in a computed low-symmetry cation-ordered decoration; the parent symmetry is P4/mmm and the Pm setting is an artefact of ordering Ba against Sr in the calculation rather than a distinct phase.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site of the charge-reservoir block, between the Tl-O and CuO2 layers
solid_solution_axis.note: Both compositions sit at exactly Ba1Sr1, so no range is sampled here, but the paper title Tl(Ba,Sr) states that Ba and Sr are being varied on one site across the wider study. Recorded so the site sharing is not later mistaken for two independent host elements. The chunk file did not flag this axis because Ba and Sr enter at equal fixed amounts.

basis: Every composition is written as a molar mixture of two named compounds, (NdBaCoFeO5)x(Ce0.8Sm0.2O1.9)y, and the paper is Improved electrochemical performance and thermal expansion compatibili[ty ...] for a dual-phase SOFC electrode. So this is a deliberate two-phase composite, not one compound: NdBaCoFeO5+d is an A-site ordered layered double perovskite of the NdBaCo2O5+d type with Co and Fe sharing the octahedral site, and Ce0.8Sm0.2O1.9 is samarium-doped ceria, a fluorite oxide. I record the perovskite as the primary because it is the electronically active phase the transport is attributed to, with is_mixed set so stage 2 splits the two rather than forcing one label. composite_multiphase was considered and rejected: that entry exists for materials whose phases cannot be resolved, whereas here both are named in the composition string with their molar ratio, so naming them loses nothing.
