dopant_roles.basis: Sm sits on the cerium site of the ceria component, at the fixed 20 percent of Ce0.8Sm0.2O1.9 that defines SDC. It is an aliovalent acceptor creating the oxygen vacancies that make that phase an ionic conductor, and it never enters the perovskite. Its role is a property of the second phase, not of the host prototype.

basis: Identical to Ba-Ce-Co-Fe-Nd-O with praseodymium in place of neodymium: every composition is (PrBaCoFeO5)x(Ce0.8Sm0.2O1.9)y from the same paper, a dual-phase SOFC electrode of an A-site ordered layered double perovskite PrBaCoFeO5+d mixed with samarium-doped ceria. The perovskite is recorded as primary because it carries the electronic transport, with the fluorite as the second phase and is_mixed set for a stage 2 split.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm is the fixed 20 percent acceptor on the cerium site of the Ce0.8Sm0.2O1.9 component, generating oxygen vacancies in the ceria. It belongs to the second phase and does not enter the perovskite.

basis: Both compositions are BaCe0.5Fe0.5O3 with and without Ni on the B site, from a paper titled Novel dual-phase symmetrical electrode materials for protonic ceramic [fuel cells]. BaCe0.5Fe0.5O3-d is the well-known self-assembling dual-phase composition: it separates on firing into a cerium-rich orthorhombic BaCeO3-type proton conductor and an iron-rich cubic BaFeO3-type electronic conductor. Both products are simple ABO3 corner-sharing perovskites, so unlike the Ba-Ce-Co-Fe hosts above the two phases share one prototype and the host is not mixed; what varies between them is only the tilt system and the oxygen vacancy content. Confidence is medium because the split itself is inferred from the word dual-phase in the title together with the known BaCeO3-BaFeO3 miscibility gap, not read from a diffraction pattern. No reference entry is offered for this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: BaCe0.5Fe0.4Ni0.1O3: nickel takes a fifth of the iron content on the octahedral B site. It is an aliovalent B-site substituent tuning the electronic conductivity and the vacancy concentration of the iron-rich phase, and it partitions with the iron rather than with the cerium.

basis: All four compositions are GdBaCo2-xFexO5 with x from 0.6 to 1.0, and the papers are Thermoelectric properties of GdBaCo2-xFexO5+d ceramics and Synthesis and properties of LnBaFeCoO5+d (Ln = Nd, Sm, Gd). LnBaB2O5+d with a trivalent lanthanide and barium alternating along the c axis is the A-site ordered double perovskite this entry names, with the oxygen vacancies ordering into the lanthanide plane; the taxonomy already seeds the entry on Ba-Co-Nd-O and Ba-Co-La-O, and gadolinium is the same compound. Fe and Co share the octahedral B site and both exceed the 5 at. percent cut, so neither is a dopant candidate; the Fe content is the swept variable.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: octahedral B site of the double perovskite
solid_solution_axis.note: Fe/(Fe+Co) runs from 0.30 at GdBaCo1.4Fe0.6O5 to 0.50 at GdBaCoFeO5, which is the series the first paper sweeps. Not isoelectronic -- Fe3+ against Co3+ changes the d count and the spin state, and the spin-state crossover is what the transport in these cobaltites is about -- so this is recorded as a shared site rather than as an isoelectronic alloy. The chunk file did not flag the axis because Co and Fe are not in the same periodic group.

basis: The host holds two different cobaltates in equal measure and must be split. Two samples are HoBaCo2O5.5, which is the A-site ordered layered double perovskite of the LnBaCo2O5+d type, and two are BaHoCo4O7 and HoBaCo4O7, which are the swedenborgite -- a trigonal P6_3mc framework of corner-sharing CoO4 tetrahedra in alternating triangular and kagome layers, an entirely different structure that shares only the elements. The papers split the same way: two of the three are on BaRCo4O7 and RBaCo4O7 for R = Dy, Ho, Er, and the third is Thermoelectric Power of HoBaCo2O5.5. I record the swedenborgite as primary because [ref 2] makes it the best-attested phase in the chemistry, BaHoCo4O7 P6_3mc (186) mp-19620 at hull 0.022 with 6 ICSD references, and because the 1-1-4-7 composition is unambiguous; the reference block also contains Ba2Ho2Co4O11 Pmma mp-25731 with 4 references and BaHo(CoO3)2 at Pmmm and P4/mmm with one each, which are the double-perovskite side of the same host. Confidence is medium because the split is 2 samples against 2, so neither label describes the host on its own.

All four compositions are SmBaCo2O5 with Sr or Ca replacing part of the barium, and both papers name the structure: Ca and Fe co-doped SmBaCo2O5+d layered perovskite and Electrical, thermal and electrochemical properties of SmBa1-xSrxCo2O5+d. SmBaCo2O5+d is the A-site ordered double perovskite exactly as this entry defines it, with Sm and Ba alternating along c and the oxygen vacancies ordering in the Sm plane. [ref 2] agrees on the structural family even though it cannot rank it well: BaSm(CoO3)2 is listed at Pmmm mp-1188886 and P4/mmm mp-1205695, which are the two standard settings of the ordered double perovskite depending on whether the vacancy ordering doubles b, and its hull minimum BaSm2CoO5 Immm mp-19248 is a different compound with a different Co content.

dopant_roles.basis: SmBa0.9Sr0.1Co2O5 and SmBa0.7Sr0.3Co2O5 are the x = 0.1 and x = 0.3 members of the SmBa1-xSrxCo2O5+d series named in the second paper title. Sr2+ for Ba2+ is the same valence on the same A site, so it works by shrinking the cell and raising the oxygen content rather than by adding carriers. It falls under the 5 at. percent cut only because the formula carries eight atoms.

SmBa0.75Ca0.25Co2O5 is the calcium member of the same alkaline-earth A-site series, on the same site and for the same reason; the first paper calls it Ca co-doping. Ca2+ is the smaller cation again, so the effect is a larger tolerance-factor change than Sr gives.

basis: The compositions are GdBaCuFeO5 and its La-substituted relatives Gd0.6Ba0.4CuFeO5 and Gd0.5Ba0.5CuFeO5, and the papers are Thermoelectric properties of layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+d and Electrical and Thermal Conduction Behaviors in La-Substituted GdBaCuFe[O5]. LnBaCuFeO5 is the oxygen-deficient A-site ordered double perovskite: Ln and Ba alternate along c, the CuO5 and FeO5 square pyramids share the apical oxygen across the Ba layer, and one oxygen per formula unit is absent from the Ln plane. That is the LnBaB2O5+d archetype of this entry with Cu and Fe on the B site instead of two cobalts. I disagree with [ref 2]: it offers only BaGdFeCuO5 P4mm (99) mp-1206575 at hull 0.710, and both the polar P4mm setting and a hull distance of 0.7 eV mark that as a computed decoration rather than the observed phase, which is reported in the centrosymmetric P4/mmm parent. Note also the measured range printed as 293-2578 K: the upper figure is a digitisation artefact, not a real measurement, and no transition should be read from it.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site, but only in the disordered compositions
solid_solution_axis.note: Gd/(Gd+Ba) is 0.5 in GdBaCuFeO5 by construction and drops to 0.375 and 0.333 in the two compositions written Gd0.6Ba0.4CuFeO5 and Gd0.5Ba0.5CuFeO5, which carry excess barium. This is not an isoelectronic axis -- Gd3+ against Ba2+ is aliovalent, and the whole point of the structure is that the two cations order onto distinct layers. Recorded to flag that extra Ba forces some A-site disorder and therefore some loss of the layer ordering, which is what the second paper studies. Treat with caution; the chunk file did not flag an axis here.

basis: All four compositions are Ba2HoCu3-xCoxO6 with x from 0.3 to 0.6, and the paper is Thermoelectric and structural characterization of Ba2Ho(Cu3-xCox)O6+y. Three coppers per two bariums and one rare earth is the 123 phase, HoBa2Cu3O6+y, which is the YBCO structure with holmium on the yttrium site -- the CuO2 bilayer sandwiching the rare earth, the BaO layers, and the CuO chain plane whose oxygen content y is the doping variable. I disagree with the ranking in [ref 2], though not with its contents: it makes Ba2Ho(CuO2)4 Cmmm mp-6205 primary on 5 ICSD references, which is the 124 double-chain phase, and puts Ba2HoCu3O7 Pmmm mp-6616 second on 2. The compositions here total exactly three coppers, so they are 123 and not 124; the reference is describing which phases exist in the Ho-Ba-Cu-O chemistry, not which one this paper made.

dopant_roles.basis: Co replaces 0.3 to 0.6 of the three coppers. In the 123 structure cobalt substitutes preferentially on the Cu(1) chain site rather than in the CuO2 planes, because it prefers a higher oxygen coordination than the two-fold chain copper; that is what converts the orthorhombic chain order to a tetragonal cell and suppresses the hole count, and it is the variable the paper sweeps. The plane site is where it would have to go to affect transport directly, and it largely does not.

basis: Both compositions are the 123 phase with substitutions on three different sites: YBa1.2Sr0.8Cu3O6.95 is Sr-for-Ba, and Y0.8Ca0.2Sr1Ba1Cu2.7Ga0.3O7 adds Ca-for-Y and Ga-for-Cu. The papers confirm it -- Strain effect on the thermoelectric power of YBa2-xSrxCu3O7 names the compound outright, and the other is on carrier concentration determined by structural and electr[ical means] in the same family. Three coppers, two large alkaline earths and one rare earth per formula unit is YBa2Cu3O7-d, the CuO2 bilayer plus CuO chain structure of this entry. [ref 2] is of no use here: all four of its entries are computed Ba-Sr-Y-Cu oxides at stoichiometries none of these samples has, none carries an ICSD reference, and the 123 phase itself is absent from the block.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga0.3 against Cu2.7. Gallium is a closed-shell trivalent ion that goes onto the Cu(1) chain site, where it takes tetrahedral coordination and breaks the chains into isolated units; it removes chain copper from the conduction problem and reduces the hole count transferred to the planes. It does not enter the CuO2 planes.

Ca0.2 against Y0.8 in Y0.8Ca0.2Sr1Ba1Cu2.7Ga0.3O7. Ca2+ for Y3+ is the standard overdoping substitution in the 123 phase: it sits between the CuO2 planes and adds holes to them directly, which is how the paper on carrier concentration compensates for the holes the gallium removes.

Sr is above the 5 at. percent cut and so is a host element here, but its role is the same in both compositions: Sr2+ for Ba2+ on the alkaline-earth site, same valence, acting through chemical pressure. That is exactly the strain effect the second paper measures. Recorded despite not being listed as a dopant candidate, because otherwise the host key would suggest Sr is an independent constituent.

basis: Three of the four samples are Ba8Cu16P30 and the papers are explicit about the structure: Thermoelectric properties of a clathrate compound Ba8Cu16P30, then Twisted Kelvin Cells and Truncated Octahedral Cages in the Crystal Str[ucture ...], then Unconventional Clathrates with Transition Metal-Phosphorus Frameworks. The 8-16-30 ratio is the type-I clathrate stoichiometry, but the second and third titles say directly that the framework is not a conventional clathrate type -- truncated octahedra, the Kelvin cell, are not among the cages of types I, II, VIII or IX -- so clathrate_i would be wrong despite the formula match, and ba8cu16p30_clathrate is proposed for it. I have left its space group null rather than assert one: [ref 2] contains no Ba8Cu16P30 entry at all, only other Ba-Cu-P phosphides at one ICSD reference each, so there is no database support for a setting here. The fourth sample, BaCu2P4, is a separate phosphide that this entry does not cover and that I cannot place, so the host is mixed.

All four compositions are BaInFe3.7Co0.3Sb12.72 to Sb13.92 and the paper is Effects of Excess Sb on Thermoelectric Properties of Barium and Indium [filled skutterudites]. Four transition metals to twelve antimonies is the CoSb3 skutterudite framework -- corner-sharing MSb6 octahedra with Sb4 rings and two icosahedral voids per cell -- and Ba and In occupy those voids as double fillers, which is what makes this the filled entry rather than the unfilled one. Barium and indium are above the 5 at. percent cut and so enter the host key, but structurally they are guests in the cage, not framework atoms; the framework itself is Fe/Co-Sb. The excess antimony beyond Sb12 per four metals is the variable the paper sweeps and is accommodated as a secondary Sb phase and as filling-fraction compensation rather than in the framework.

dopant_roles.basis: Co0.3 against Fe3.7 on the octahedral framework metal site. Fe-based skutterudites are electron-deficient and need the filler charge to balance; substituting cobalt for iron adds electrons to the framework and is used together with the filling fraction to set the carrier concentration. It is a framework substitution in the ordinary sense -- same site, same coordination -- not a cage guest.

Antimony runs from 12.72 to 13.92 against the ideal 12 per four framework metals, and excess Sb is the title variable of the paper. It is not a dopant: it is deliberate off-stoichiometry that compensates antimony loss during synthesis and leaves a minor free-Sb phase. Sb is a host element here, recorded only so stage 3 does not read the excess as a doping level.

basis: All four compositions are BaGa2-xZnxSb2 with x from 0 to 0.1, and the paper is Thermoelectric Enhancement in BaGa2Sb2 by Zn Doping. The 1-2-2 formula invites caal2si2_zintl, and that is the trap: CaAl2Si2 is trigonal P-3m1, whereas [ref 2] puts Ba(GaSb)2 at Pnma (62) mp-29938, hull 0.000, with an ICSD reference behind it. Barium is too large for the trigonal slab and the gallium antimonide anion condenses into a three-dimensional framework of corner- and edge-sharing GaSb4 tetrahedra with the barium in its channels. Since the taxonomy had no orthorhombic AM2Pn2 entry, baga2sb2_pnma_zintl is proposed rather than forcing the trigonal one. The other entries in the reference block -- Ba3GaSb3 Pnma mp-28296, Ba7Ga4Sb9 Pmmn mp-28314 -- are other Ba-Ga-Sb Zintl stoichiometries, not polymorphs of this one.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn replaces up to 0.1 of the two galliums on the tetrahedral site of the anionic framework. Zn2+ for Ga3+ removes one electron per substitution from the polyanion, so it is an acceptor that sets the hole concentration directly rather than a dilute impurity -- exactly the case the role vocabulary reserves framework_substitution for, as with Ga-for-Ge in the clathrates. It is the only variable across the four compositions and is the enhancement the paper title refers to.

basis: Two samples are elemental Be and two are commercial-purity beryllium, Be98.7 with about 1.2 percent BeO and tenths of a percent of Al, Ni, Mn and Si; the papers are Low-Temperature Transport Properties of Commercial Metals and Alloys and Plasma-sprayed beryllium for ITER. Beryllium metal is hexagonal close packed, and [ref 2] confirms Be P6_3/mmc (194) mp-87 at hull 0.000 with 15 ICSD references, by far the best-attested entry in its block. solid_solution_alloy is the taxonomy entry for the close-packed elemental metals and dilute alloys, and its own note asks for the lattice to be recorded: hcp. The remaining reference entries -- Be22Mo, Be22W, LaCeBe26, ThUBe26 -- are beryllides of elements that appear in no composition here.

dopant_roles.basis: The composition writes it as (BeO)1.18 and (BeO)1.2, an explicit oxide fraction. Beryllium oxide is insoluble in the metal and is present as dispersed BeO particles at grain boundaries, which is the normal microstructure of powder-consolidated and plasma-sprayed beryllium. It is not dissolved oxygen.

Al at 0.044 and 0.056 percent is a residual impurity of the ore and reduction route, at a level low enough to sit in solid solution or at grain boundaries. Treated as a dilute substituent in the hcp lattice; it is not deliberately added.

Ni at 0.014 to 0.016 percent, the same residual-impurity case as Al. At these levels the impurities matter for the low-temperature resistivity and hence for the electronic thermal conductivity, which is why the commercial-metals paper lists them at all.
Mn at about 0.01 percent, a residual impurity from the reduction route, as above.
Si at 0.035 percent in one composition only, again a residual impurity rather than an addition.

basis: The one composition is Be12.01Ni0.19Co0.19Cu87.6, which is beryllium copper: about 2 wt percent Be in copper, with the standard Ni plus Co addition, and the paper is Zirconium Copper - a New Material for Use at Low Temperatures, a comparison of low-temperature conductor alloys. At 87.6 at. percent copper this is an fcc copper solid solution, age-hardened by fine gamma-CuBe precipitates, not a compound. I therefore disagree with [ref 2], which offers BeCu Pm-3m (221) mp-2323 with 3 ICSD references and Be2Cu Fd-3m mp-2031 with 2. Those are the ordered equiatomic and 2:1 Be-Cu intermetallics; they describe which line compounds exist in the binary, not the copper-rich alloy that was measured, and the 5 at. percent split put Be into the host key only because 2 wt percent of a light element is 12 at. percent. The taxonomy note for this entry asks for the lattice: fcc.

dopant_roles.basis: Ni at 0.19 at. percent is part of the alloy specification for beryllium copper, where nickel plus cobalt at a few tenths of a percent refine the grain size and control the precipitation of the beryllide phase during ageing. Deliberate, not a contaminant, and in solid solution in the fcc matrix.
Co at 0.19 at. percent, the companion addition to Ni in the same specification and for the same purpose.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [194, 225, 229], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 227]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: All four samples are UBe13 across four papers, all of them on the heavy-fermion superconductor -- Spin gap in heavy fermion compound UBe13 and two calorimetry and thermal conductivity studies. UBe13 is the NaZn13 type: uranium on the corners and face centres of a cubic cell, each surrounded by a snub cube of 24 beryllium atoms, with the remaining beryllium forming icosahedra. [ref 2] fixes it without inference at UBe13 Fm-3c (226) mp-1163, hull 0.000, 11 ICSD references, the dominant entry in its block; U2Be25Cu, U2Be25Ga and U4Be51B are quaternary derivatives of no relevance here. The taxonomy had no AB13 entry, so nazn13_type is proposed rather than defaulting to solid_solution_alloy, which would be wrong for a line compound this well attested.

Three of the four samples are HoPdBi and one is HoPd2Bi, and the three papers name both: Physical properties of rare-earth-based Heusler phases REPdZ and REPd2Z, and two on the half-Heusler REPdBi phases. The 1-1-1 and 1-2-1 stoichiometries are the two halves of the same structural relationship -- HoPdBi is the C1b half-Heusler in F-43m with one of the two tetrahedral sites empty, HoPd2Bi fills it and becomes the L2_1 full Heusler in Fm-3m -- so the host genuinely holds both and must be split on the Pd:Ho ratio. [ref 2] confirms the majority phase directly: HoBiPd F-43m (216) mp-1009132 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference. Its other entries, Ho5Bi2Pd Pnma and Ho5BiPd2 I4/mcm, are rare-earth-rich phases at stoichiometries no sample here has.

All four compositions are Bi2-xSrxIr2O7 with x from 0.6 to 0.9, and the paper is On the electrical properties of the Bi2-xSrxIr2O7 pyrochlore solid solu[tion], which names the structure. A2B2O7 with a tetravalent B cation is the pyrochlore archetype exactly: a corner-sharing IrO6 octahedral network interpenetrated by a Bi2O-prime chain sublattice. No reference entry is offered for this chemistry, so the assignment rests on the formula and the paper title, both of which are unambiguous.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr runs from 0.6 to 0.9 of the two A sites and is the only variable in the series. Sr2+ for Bi3+ is aliovalent, so it dopes holes into the iridate network and drives the insulator-to-metal behaviour the paper measures; it is above the 5 at. percent cut and so is a host element, but it is functionally the doping variable. The A site in a pyrochlore is eight-coordinate and scalenohedral, which is why the large Sr2+ is accommodated there rather than on the Ir site.

basis: The single composition La2BiLiMn4O12 divides by four to (La0.5Bi0.25Li0.25)MnO3: one manganese per three oxygens with the A site summing to exactly one. That is a simple ABO3 manganite with a mixed A site, and the paper is Effect of bismuth doping on the physical properties of La-Li-Mn-O mang[anites], which names the family. Lithium is on the A site rather than the B site in the La1-xLixMnO3 manganites -- it is the hole-doping substituent that raises the Mn4+ fraction -- so there is no B-site ordering and this is not a double perovskite. No reference entry is offered for this chemistry.

Both compositions, Bi0.25La0.25Sr0.5MnO3 and La0.45Bi0.25Sr0.3MnO3, are ABO3 with the A site summing to one and a single manganese on the B site. The papers put it beyond doubt -- Electrical, thermal and magnetic properties of Bi doped La0.7-xBixSr0.[3MnO3], plus a magnon-drag thermopower study and one on the Bi3+ lone-pair effect on the charge-ordering state. These are the canonical mixed-valence manganites: orthorhombic or rhombohedral corner-sharing MnO6 with the Sr content setting the Mn3+/Mn4+ ratio. No reference entry is offered for this chemistry.

Every composition is LixBi2Se0.3Te2.7 or LixBi2Se0.3Te2 with x from 0.24 to 0.8, and the paper is Structural modifications and non-monotonic carrier concentration in Bi[2Te3-based ...]. Bi2Se0.3Te2.7 is n-type Bi2Te3 with a little selenium on the anion sublattice, which is the tetradymite R-3m quintuple-layer structure outright. Lithium is intercalated into the van der Waals gap between quintuple layers; that is what the structural modifications of the title are, and it does not change the prototype. Neither Li nor Se is listed as a dopant candidate because both clear the 5 at. percent cut on a five-atom formula, but both are chemically minor and are recorded below so the host key is not read as a four-component compound. No reference entry is offered for this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: Li is intercalated into the van der Waals gap between the Te-Bi-Te-Bi-Te quintuple layers rather than substituting on any site. It is an electron donor there, and the non-monotonic carrier concentration of the title is the signature of intercalation competing with the defect chemistry rather than of simple substitutional doping. It is above the 5 at. percent cut only because the formula unit is small.

Se0.3 against Te2.7 or Te2 is 10 to 13 percent of the anion sublattice. Same group, same site, so it tunes the gap and scatters phonons without adding carriers -- the standard Bi2Te3-xSex n-type composition. Its share of the shared anion site is well above the dilute band, so stage 3 should treat it as an alloying fraction and not as a doping level.

basis: The single composition is Sr5BiNi2O9.6 and the paper is Synthesis, crystal structure and physico-chemical properties of the ne[w ...], i.e. the compound was new when it was reported. [ref 2] backs it with Sr5Ni2BiO10 I4/mmm (139) mp-1189753 at hull 0.059 and 3 ICSD references, so the phase is real, tetragonal and crystalline, and the oxygen deficiency to 9.6 is genuine rather than a parse artefact. What I cannot do is name a prototype: A5B3O10 in I4/mmm does not match any entry in the taxonomy. It is not Ruddlesden-Popper, whose n = 3 member is A4B3O10 and would need one fewer strontium; it is not a perovskite or a double perovskite at this A:B ratio. Filed as unresolved_crystalline rather than forced into the nearest layered-perovskite label, with the mp_id noted here so stage 2 can start from the structure file and settle it.

All four compositions are (Bi1-xSbx)2S3 and the paper is Thermoelectric Properties of (Bi1-xSbx)2S3 with Orthorhombic Structure, which names the symmetry in the title. Bi2S3 bismuthinite and Sb2S3 stibnite are isostructural in Pnma and form a complete solid solution, so every member of this series is the stibnite type. [ref 2] agrees, giving BiSbS3 Pnma (62) mp-1227486 at hull 0.003 -- the same space group, as an ordered 1:1 model of the mid-series composition.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Bi/(Bi+Sb) spans 0.20 to 0.80 across the four compositions, a genuine pseudobinary alloy series across its whole middle. Both end members are Pnma and isostructural, so the prototype is the same everywhere on the axis and only the parent formula changes; stage 3 should pick the end member per composition rather than call either one doped.

basis: The single composition Fe0.693C0.0966Si0.0180Mn0.0459Cr0.0776V0.0693 is not a compound, it is a steel: 69 at. percent iron with 9.7 percent carbon against 7.8 percent chromium and 6.9 percent vanadium as carbide formers, plus manganese and silicon. The paper is Improvement of thermoelectric power of n-type earth-abundant iron rich [alloys]. Carbon at that level is far beyond its solubility in iron, so the material is necessarily at least two phases -- a body-centred iron solid-solution matrix with vanadium MC and chromium M7C3 carbides dispersed in it -- and no single crystal structure describes the sample. That is what composite_multiphase exists for. I have not set is_mixed, because the multiphase label is correct at host level and there is only one composition to split; the two constituents are recorded here instead. Confidence is medium because the carbide types are inferred from the alloy chemistry, not reported. No reference entry is offered.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn at 4.6 at. percent is fully soluble in iron and sits substitutionally in the matrix, where it stabilises austenite and raises the resistivity. It is an alloying addition rather than a dopant in the semiconductor sense.

Si at 1.8 at. percent is in substitutional solid solution in the iron matrix. In iron-rich thermoelectric alloys silicon is the usual addition for raising the thermopower, so it is deliberate here rather than residual.

basis: Both compositions are Cu55Ni45 with carbon added, at 10.6 and 16 parts per 100 of alloy, and the paper is Enhancing the thermoelectric performance of Cu-Ni alloys by introducin[g ...]. Cu55Ni45 is constantan: copper and nickel are completely miscible and the alloy is a disordered fcc solid solution across the whole range, which is the prototype here. The carbon is what is being introduced -- it has essentially no solubility in either metal, so it is a dispersed second phase rather than a constituent, and it reaches the host key only because the 5 at. percent split counts it in the formula. The material is therefore a metal-matrix composite, but unlike C-Cr-Fe-V the matrix that carries the transport is a single well-defined structure, so the alloy label is kept and the carbon recorded as a second phase. Confidence is medium for that reason. No reference entry is offered. Record the lattice as fcc, per this entry own note.

dopant_roles.basis: One selenium per 100 metal atoms, about 0.8 at. percent. Selenium has negligible solubility in fcc Cu-Ni and reacts readily with copper, so it will be present as copper selenide precipitates at grain boundaries rather than dissolved on a lattice site. Whether those precipitates are the intended phonon scatterers or an incidental product is not settled by the composition alone.

Carbon at 10.6 and 16 parts per 100 is the variable the paper sweeps and the thing being introduced. It is insoluble in both copper and nickel and is present as a dispersed carbon phase. Recorded despite being above the 5 at. percent cut, because it is the reason the host key has three elements and it is not part of any lattice.

basis: All four compositions are ZnFe3 with carbon from 1.2 to 1.5, i.e. ZnFe3C with a carbon excess, and [ref 2] gives exactly ZnFe3C Pm-3m (221) mp-10266 at hull 0.021 with an ICSD reference. That is the metallic antiperovskite: zinc at the cube corners, iron at the face centres forming a Fe6C octahedron, carbon at the body centre -- cation and anion roles inverted relative to an oxide perovskite, which is what this entry defines, and the same arrangement as the Co3SnC it is seeded on. The paper is The magnetic, electrical transport and thermal transport properties of[ ...], consistent with the itinerant-magnetic antiperovskite carbides.

dopant_roles.basis: Carbon runs 1.2 to 1.5 against the ideal 1.0 per ZnFe3, and it is the only variable across the four compositions. The body-centre site cannot hold more than one carbon, so the excess is either a batching surplus that leaves free graphite or a measure of how completely the body-centre site is filled -- in these carbides the site is routinely sub-stoichiometric and the filling fraction sets the carrier count. Either way it is off-stoichiometry on a host site, not a foreign dopant. C is a host element here; recorded because it is the swept variable.

basis: All three compositions are Si80Ge20 with carbon added at 6, 15 or 30 parts per 100, the curator recorded 5-10wt percent C from the paper, and the paper is Transport properties of nanocomposite thermoelectric materials based o[n SiGe]. Si80Ge20 is the classic high-temperature thermoelectric alloy: silicon and germanium are completely miscible and the alloy keeps the diamond-cubic Fd-3m structure across the whole range. The carbon is the nanocomposite addition, insoluble in SiGe at these levels and present as a dispersed phase and as SiC at the interfaces; it reaches the host key only through the 5 at. percent split. The Si:Ge ratio is fixed at 80:20 across every composition, so there is no series to record. No reference entry is offered.

dopant_roles.basis: Carbon is the nanocomposite additive the paper studies, at a curator-recorded 5-10 wt percent. Its equilibrium solubility in silicon is parts per million, so it is not on a lattice site: it is dispersed carbon and interfacial SiC whose purpose is to scatter phonons. Above the 5 at. percent cut and therefore a host element by the split, recorded here because it is not part of the structure.

basis: The compositions are written as the batched mixture (ZrC)1-y(ZrH2)y with y from 0.1 to 0.4, but the paper is Densification, mechanical and thermal properties of ZrC1-x ceramics fab[ricated ...], so what was measured is single-phase sub-stoichiometric zirconium carbide. The hydride is a reactive-sintering precursor: it decomposes and the hydrogen leaves, and the ZrH2 fraction is simply how the carbon vacancy content x is set. ZrC is the rocksalt carbide of this entry, Fm-3m, with carbon on the octahedral anion site and vacancies there as the carrier knob. I disagree with [ref 2], which offers Zr2HC P3m1 mp-1215471 and Zr3HC2 P-3m1 mp-1215581: both are computed ordered hydride-carbides with no ICSD reference behind them, and neither survives the firing that produces the ceramic.

dopant_roles.basis: Hydrogen enters only as ZrH2 in the starting powder and is driven off during sintering; it is not present in the measured ceramic. It is in the host key because the composition string records the batch rather than the product. Any that remains is trapped residue, not a lattice species.

The whole point of the series is that the extra zirconium supplied as ZrH2 leaves carbon vacancies, giving ZrC1-x with x rising as the hydride fraction rises from 0.1 to 0.4. Vacancies on the host anion site, which in the rocksalt carbides set the electron count and are the intended variable, not an impurity.

basis: Three compositions are Mg3Sb2 with carbon added at 0.32 to 0.66, the fourth is Mg3Sb1.8Bi0.2 with the same, and the paper is Graphene boosts thermoelectric performance of a Zintl phase compound. Mg3Sb2 is the CaAl2Si2-type Zintl antimonide, trigonal P-3m1, with an Mg2Sb2 tetrahedral slab and octahedral Mg between the slabs -- one of the best-known entries in this family. The graphene is an additive, not a constituent. I disagree with [ref 2] entirely: its Mg14SbC Amm2 mp-1026465 at hull 0.239, Mg6SbC Amm2 mp-1017117 at hull 0.442 and Mg14SbC P-6m2 mp-1026411 at hull 0.313 are computed magnesium carbide-antimonides with no ICSD support and hull distances of a quarter to half an eV; they exist in the block only because carbon is in the host key, and none of them is what was made.

dopant_roles.basis: Mg3Sb1.8Bi0.2C0.3: bismuth takes a tenth of the antimony sublattice. Same group, same site, so it narrows the gap and lowers the lattice thermal conductivity without adding carriers -- the Mg3Sb2-Mg3Bi2 series is continuous and is the main composition axis of this material family. Only one composition here carries it, at 10 percent of the shared site.

Carbon is the graphene of the title, added at 0.32 to 0.66 per formula unit and dispersed at the grain boundaries. It is above the 5 at. percent cut and so is a host element by the split, but it is not in the lattice; recorded here to keep it out of any structural claim.

basis: All four compositions are TiC1-xNx with x from 0.3 to 0.7, and the paper is Titanium carbonitride-based cermets: processes and properties. TiC and TiN are both rocksalt Fm-3m and form a complete solid solution, so every carbonitride in this range is the same structure with carbon and nitrogen sharing the octahedral anion site -- which is exactly this entry, whose own note points at TaN0.89-type non-stoichiometry as the carrier knob. I disagree with [ref 2]: it lists only Ti2CN, Ti4C3N, Ti4CN3 and Ti5CN4, all R-3m and all at hull 0.000 or 0.001, which are computed layered orderings of carbon against nitrogen on that same anion site. They are ordered decorations of the rocksalt parent, not observed phases -- none carries an ICSD reference -- and a sintered cermet is a disordered solid solution.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: octahedral anion site of the rocksalt lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: N/(C+N) spans 0.30 to 0.70 across the four compositions, covering the whole middle of the TiC-TiN join. Recorded as a shared site, NOT as an isoelectronic one: carbon and nitrogen are in different groups, so each nitrogen adds an electron and the substitution moves the Fermi level as well as the lattice parameter. The chunk file did not flag an axis for exactly that reason. Stage 3 must not treat the minority component as a doping level -- at these fractions both are alloy constituents.

basis: Two different materials and a genuinely uncertain call on the larger one. Three samples are Ca1.55Na0.45Co2O5 from Preparation and characterization of the new oxides Ca2-xNaxCo2O5. Ca2Co2O5 is CaCoO2.5, an ABO2.5 oxygen-deficient perovskite, and the standard ordering of that vacancy content is brownmillerite -- alternating layers of CoO6 octahedra and CoO4 tetrahedra -- so that is what I record. Confidence is low because this is inference from stoichiometry alone: the paper calls them new oxides and I have not seen the structure, and the alternative is a misfit cobaltite, which is what nearly every other Ca-Co-O thermoelectric turns out to be. If the paper reports an incommensurate cell this should become misfit_cobaltite. The fourth sample is unambiguous and different: (Ca3Co4O9)2.2(Na0.75CoO2)3.2 is written as a two-component mixture of the Ca3Co4O9 misfit and NaxCoO2, from Improved environmental stability of thermoelectric ceramics based on i[ntergrowths], so the host carries three prototypes in all and must be split per composition.

dopant_roles.basis: In Ca2-xNaxCo2O5 sodium replaces up to 0.45 of the two calciums on the A site. Na+ for Ca2+ is aliovalent, so it oxidises the cobalt and is the doping variable of that series. Its role is different in the fourth composition, where the sodium belongs to a separate NaxCoO2 phase and is a compositional variable of that phase rather than a substituent -- another reason the host has to be split before this is used.

basis: All four compositions are Y0.7Ca0.3Cr1-xZnxO3 with x from 0 to 0.15, and the paper is Stable, easily sintered Ca-Zn-doped YCrO3 as novel interconnect materi[al]. YCrO3 is an orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted ABO3 perovskite, corner-sharing CrO6 with the rare earth in the distorted twelve-coordinate cavity, and both substitutions here stay on their respective sites without changing that. The A site sums to one and there is one B cation per three oxygens, so there is no ordering and no layered variant. No reference entry is offered for this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn replaces 0.05 to 0.15 of the chromium on the octahedral B site and is the only variable across the series. Zn2+ for Cr3+ is an acceptor, which both raises the p-type conductivity and, as the title says, improves sinterability; calcium on the A site does the same electronically but is fixed at 0.3 here and is a host element.

basis: Both compositions are La2-xCa1+xCu2O6 at x = 0.10 and 0.15, and the paper is Evidence for magnetic-field-induced decoupling of superconducting bila[yers]. La2CaCu2O6 is the 0212 cuprate: an A3B2O7 Ruddlesden-Popper n = 2 block with the apical oxygens between the two CuO2 planes removed, giving A3B2O6 and a pair of square-pyramidal CuO5 layers sharing the calcium plane, separated by rocksalt La-O double layers. That is the bilayer the paper studies. [ref 2] agrees on symmetry and stoichiometry, offering CaLa2Cu2O7 I4/mmm mp-1213978 and Ca2La2Cu3O8 I4/mmm mp-1214137 -- both tetragonal I4/mmm, which is the Ruddlesden-Popper space group, though with the oxygen content written for the fully stoichiometric parent rather than for the oxygen-deficient phase that is actually made. Confidence is medium because the entry as written is the full An+1BnO3n+1 series and this is the vacancy-ordered member; record n = 2 and the missing apical oxygen alongside the id.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site, but they order -- La in the rocksalt layer, Ca between the CuO2 planes
solid_solution_axis.note: La/(La+Ca) moves only from 0.633 to 0.617 between the two compositions, i.e. x = 0.10 to 0.15 in La2-xCa1+xCu2O6. This is not an isoelectronic alloy axis: La3+ against Ca2+ is aliovalent and is the hole-doping knob, and the two cations occupy crystallographically distinct A positions rather than sharing one. Recorded to make that ordering explicit so the host key is not read as a disordered La-Ca site. The chunk file did not flag an axis here.

basis: All four compositions are Ca2-xLaxFeMoO6 with x from 0.5 to 0.8, and the paper is Disorder induced magnetism and electrical conduction in La doped Ca2Fe[MoO6]. A2BB-primeO6 with iron and molybdenum alternating on the octahedral sites is the Sr2FeMoO6-type double perovskite, and the disorder of the title is antisite mixing between those two sites, which only makes sense if the structure is the ordered one. I disagree with the detail of [ref 2]: its single entry Ca3LaFe2(MoO6)2 P1 (1) mp-1228602 at hull 0.184 is a triclinic computed model with no ICSD reference, and P1 at 0.18 eV above the hull is what a supercell decoration of a La-Ca mixed site looks like in a database, not the observed monoclinic or tetragonal double perovskite.

dopant_roles.basis: La replaces 0.5 to 0.8 of the two calciums on the A site and is the only variable in the series. La3+ for Ca2+ is aliovalent electron doping, which fills the Mo 4d band and is what drives the change in conduction the paper reports. It is above the 5 at. percent cut and so appears in the host key, but functionally it is the doping variable named in the title.

basis: All four compositions are CaHf1-xScxO3 with x from 0 to 0.2, and the paper is Influence of Sc concentration on transport properties of CaHf1-xScxO3-alpha. CaHfO3 is an orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted ABO3 perovskite and [ref 2] confirms it outright: CaHfO3 Pnma (62) mp-754853 at hull 0.000. I disagree with [ref 1]: TEDesignLab covers this chemistry only as Ca2Hf7O16 R-3 (148) mp-27221, a hafnium-rich pyrochlore-related oxide on one ICSD reference, which is a different compound and not one any sample here has. The cubic CaHfO3 Pm-3m mp-1016873 in the reference block sits 0.154 eV above the hull and is the untilted aristotype, not what is formed at these temperatures.

dopant_roles.basis: Sc replaces 0.1 to 0.2 of the hafnium on the octahedral B site. Sc3+ for Hf4+ is an acceptor that is charge-compensated by oxygen vacancies -- the alpha in the CaHf1-xScxO3-alpha of the title is exactly that vacancy count -- so the substitution creates the ionic and protonic conduction the paper measures rather than adding electronic carriers. It is the only variable across the series.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62, 167, 221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [148]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The three compositions are Ca0.95La0.05, Ca0.78La0.22 and Ca0.30La0.70, and the paper is Thermoelectric power of Nd1-xLax and Ce1-xLax alloys. Those x values are the Ce1-xLax series of the title, so the Ca in this host is almost certainly a transcription of Ce: the routing key should be Ce-La. Either reading gives the same structural answer -- La with Ca, and La with Ce, are both close-packed metals that form continuous substitutional solid solutions with no ordered phase in the composition range sampled -- so solid_solution_alloy stands regardless. Record the lattice as dhcp or fcc depending on composition and temperature, per this entry own note. I disagree with [ref 2], whose only entry is CaLa P-6m2 mp-1183602 at hull 0.088 with no ICSD reference: a computed equiatomic line compound is not what a thermopower study of a dilute alloy series measured, and none of these three compositions is equiatomic.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the single metal site of the close-packed lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: La fraction spans 0.05 to 0.70, so the series runs from dilute solute to majority component and no single parent compound describes the host -- stage 3 must pick the end member per composition. If the Ca is read as Ce, as the paper title indicates, the axis is Ce-La, two adjacent light rare earths on one site, which is as close to isoelectronic as a metallic alloy gets. The chunk file did not flag the axis because Ca and La are not in the same group.

basis: All three compositions are (La,Ca)(Ti,Mn,Ni)O3 with the A site summing to one and the B site summing to one against three oxygens: La0.7Ca0.3Ti0.5Mn0.4Ni0.1O3 and the two La0.4Ca0.6Ti1-xMnxO3 members. The papers are Manganese-doped lanthanum calcium titanate as an interconnect for flat[ SOFC] and A-site cation influences on performance, structure and conductivity of[ ...], both of them straightforward doped-titanate perovskite work. Three cations share the octahedral B site at fractions that give no ordered arrangement, so this is a disordered ABO3 perovskite and not a double perovskite. I disagree with [ref 2] as a structural statement: its Ca9LaTi4Mn6O30, Ca9LaTi6Mn4O30, Ca9LaTi8Mn2O30 and Ca9LaTi9MnO30 are all P1 or Pm thirty-oxygen supercells, which is how a database represents a disordered B site -- they are ordering decorations of the same perovskite, not distinct phases, and they carry no ICSD references.

dopant_roles.basis: Ni0.1 on the octahedral B site alongside Ti0.5 and Mn0.4 in the two rod-shaped samples. Ni2+ or Ni3+ against Ti4+ is an acceptor that is compensated by oxygen vacancies, added on top of the manganese to raise the mixed conductivity of an SOFC interconnect. It shares the site with Ti and Mn rather than taking one of its own.

basis: All four compositions are La1-xCaxTiO3 with x from 0.3 to 0.6, one of them with manganese on the B site, and the papers are Development of Perovskite-type Cobaltates and Manganates for Thermoele[ctrics] and Manganese-doped lanthanum calcium titanate as an interconnect for flat[ SOFC]. The first names the structural family in its own title. La1-xCaxTiO3 is a GdFeO3-tilted ABO3 perovskite with the two large cations disordered on the A site; the aliovalent La3+ against Ca2+ ratio sets the Ti3+/Ti4+ mixed valence and hence the electron count. [ref 2] again answers a different question: Ca9LaTi10O30 P1 mp-686651 and the Mg-containing supercells are ordering models of a disordered A site, and Ca2La4Ti5O18 R-3m mp-1227811 is a layered intergrowth at a stoichiometry no sample here has.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.4Ca0.6Ti0.8Mn0.2O3 is the one composition that carries it: manganese takes a fifth of the octahedral titanium site. Mn is the doping element named in the second paper title, added to raise the p-type conductivity of the titanate under the oxidising side of an interconnect. Same site, same coordination, no ordering at this fraction.

basis: All four compositions are La3-xCaxTe4 with x from 0.5 to 2.1, and the paper is Mechanochemical synthesis and high temperature thermoelectric properti[es]. La3-xTe4 is the textbook Th3P4-type thermoelectric: a cubic I-43d framework of eight-coordinate cations and tetrahedrally coordinated tellurium in which the cation site is partly vacant, and the vacancy concentration is the carrier knob -- which is exactly what this entry own note records. Substituting divalent calcium for trivalent lanthanum is the same knob reached chemically instead of by vacancies. [ref 2] offers Ca(LaTe2)2 I-42d (122) mp-36031 at hull 0.015; I read that as an ordered-cation tetragonal distortion of the same Th3P4 framework at the specific 1:2 Ca:La ratio rather than as a different structure, and note that the parent symmetry of the disordered phase is cubic I-43d, not I-42d.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca runs from 0.5 to 2.1 of the three cation sites and is the only variable in the series. Ca2+ for La3+ removes one electron per substitution from the conduction band, which is the same effect the cation vacancies of undoped La3-xTe4 have and is how the carrier concentration is set here. It is well above the 5 at. percent cut and so is a host element, but functionally it is the doping variable.

basis: This host is two unrelated materials joined by a parsing failure, and neither label covers it alone. Two samples are plain CaO, from Thermal Conductivity of 2CaO.SiO2 Bearing Solid Solution -- and note that even there CaO is likely a truncation of the 2CaO.SiO2 cement notation rather than lime itself, which would move those samples to Ca-O-Si. The other two read Ca3O4O9 and Ca3O3.9Re0.1O9, which are Ca3Co4O9 and Ca3Co3.9Re0.1O9 with every Co mis-parsed as O: the paper is Structure and transport properties in Ca3Co4-xMxO9 (M=Re and Pt) ceramics, so those two are the Ca3Co4O9 misfit layered cobaltite and belong in a Ca-Co-O host. I record rocksalt_oxide as primary because [ref 1] backs CaO Fm-3m (225) mp-2605 at hull 0.000 with 14 ICSD references and because it is at least the literal reading of the composition string, with misfit_cobaltite as the alternate and is_mixed set. Confidence is low: the host key itself is wrong and this should be revisited at the source rather than resolved here. [ref 2] is not usable -- its primaries CaO2 P-3m1 mp-1062228 at hull 0.483 and CaO10 P4/mcc mp-1182382 are peroxides and a computed ozonide, and Ca3SiCSO24 and Ca3MnCSO25 at hull 0.9 and 0.8 are artefacts of the block.

dopant_roles.basis: The composition reads Ca3O3.9Re0.1O9 but the paper is Ca3Co4-xMxO9 with M = Re and Pt, so rhenium takes 0.1 of the four cobalts. In the Ca3Co4O9 misfit that substitution goes into the CoO2 conducting sheet, where a high-valent 5d cation tunes the carrier concentration and scatters phonons. The role belongs to the cobaltite half of this host, not to the CaO half.

basis: Three of the four compositions are Ca1-xSrxRuO3 with x from 0.4 to 0.6, from Thermoelectric properties of Ca1-xSrxRuO3 compounds prepared by spark [plasma sintering], and those are ABO3 perovskite ruthenates -- SrRuO3 and CaRuO3 are both GdFeO3-tilted perovskites and are fully miscible, the tilt angle increasing as calcium replaces strontium. The fourth, Ca1.5Sr0.5RuO4, is a different structure: A2BO4 is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper, the Sr2RuO4 type, and its paper is Quasi-Two-Dimensional Mott Transition System, i.e. the Ca2-xSrxRuO4 series. One extra A cation per formula unit separates them cleanly, so the host splits on the A:Ru ratio. Confidence is medium because the primary label covers three of four samples rather than all of them.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site
solid_solution_axis.note: Ca/(Ca+Sr) spans 0.40 to 0.75. Isoelectronic -- both divalent on the same A site -- so the substitution works through ionic radius and octahedral tilting rather than through carrier count, which is precisely why it drives the ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic change in the perovskites and the Mott transition in the n = 1 member. The parent compound depends on the composition and stage 3 must pick the end member per composition; note also that the axis runs across both structures in this host, so it cannot be applied before the perovskite and Ruddlesden-Popper samples are separated.

basis: Two unrelated materials again, and the split is 3 to 1. Three compositions are belite solid solutions -- (Ca2SiO4)0.86(Ca3P2O8)0.14 and (Ca2SiO4)0.84(Ca3P2O8)0.1(Fe2SiO4)0.05 -- from Thermal Conductivity of 2CaO.SiO2 Bearing Solid Solution, where 2CaO.SiO2 is cement notation for Ca2SiO4. That is an orthosilicate of isolated SiO4 tetrahedra and had no entry in the taxonomy, so larnite_ca2sio4 is proposed for it; [ref 1] supports it well, with Ca2SiO4 P2_1/c (14) mp-4180 primary on 19 ICSD references and Ca2SiO4 Pnma (62) mp-4481 at hull 0.000 on 12. The fourth composition, Ca3SiO, is not a silicate at all: its paper is Thermoelectric properties of inverse perovskites A3TtO (A = Mg, Ca; Tt[ = Si, Ge, Sn]), which names the structure, and silicon there is the anion. So the host holds a silicate and an antiperovskite and must be split. Confidence is low for the host as a whole because of that, and because the phase sequence recorded below is materials knowledge rather than anything the paper states.

other_polymorphs.note: gamma-Ca2SiO4, Pnma (62), mp-4481, hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references. It is the thermodynamically stable low-temperature form, so it is not metastable in the usual sense, but heating these samples does not produce it: the phosphate component is there precisely to stabilise beta against the beta-to-gamma inversion on cooling, and on heating beta converts upward to alpha-prime instead. Recorded here rather than in phases so the hull minimum is not read as a thermal phase of this measurement.

dopant_roles.basis: The composition writes it as a Ca3P2O8 component at 10 to 14 mol percent of the solid solution. Phosphate substitutes for silicate on the tetrahedral site with the charge balanced by calcium vacancies, and this is the standard beta-stabilising additive in belite -- it is the reason the samples are the P2_1/c form at room temperature at all, so it is a structural stabiliser as much as a solute.

One composition carries an (Fe2SiO4)0.05 component. Fayalite is an orthosilicate of the same anion type, so the iron enters the large-cation site of the belite rather than the tetrahedral one. At 5 mol percent it is a solid-solution component of the cement phase, not a dopant in the electronic sense.

basis: All four compositions are Sr0.5Ca0.5VO3 with the oxygen content varied from 3.010 to 3.023, and the paper is Structure and electrical properties of Sr0.5Ca0.5VOy. SrVO3 and CaVO3 are both ABO3 perovskites -- correlated metals with a d1 vanadium on the octahedral site -- and the 50:50 A-site mixture is the standard way of tuning the octahedral tilt between them. The A site sums to one against one vanadium and three oxygens, so there is no layered or ordered variant here. I disagree with [ref 2]: its Sr3CaV4O12 Pmmm mp-1218542, SrCa3V4O12 Pm mp-1218581 and SrCaV2O6 Pmc2_1 mp-1218467 are computed supercell orderings of the mixed A site with no ICSD references, which is a database representation of the disorder, not a distinct phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Oxygen runs 3.010 to 3.023 against the ideal 3.000 and is the only variable across the four compositions -- the y in the Sr0.5Ca0.5VOy of the title. Excess oxygen in these vanadates is accommodated as cation vacancies rather than as interstitials, and it oxidises the vanadium away from d1, which is what the paper measures. O is a host element; recorded so stage 3 does not read the excess as a doping level.

basis: All three compositions are Ce(Cu1-xCox)2Ge2 with x from 0.2 to 0.6, and the paper is Non-Fermi-liquid behavior at the antiferromagnetic quantum critical po[int]. CeCu2Ge2 and CeCo2Ge2 are both ThCr2Si2-type, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm with cerium layers alternating with M2Ge2 slabs of edge-sharing MGe4 tetrahedra, and they are isostructural so the whole series is one prototype. This is the canonical heavy-fermion 122 family, and tuning the transition metal to reach a quantum critical point is what that entry is for. No reference entry is offered for this chemistry.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal site of the M2Ge2 slab
solid_solution_axis.note: Co/(Co+Cu) spans 0.2 to 0.6 across the three compositions. Not isoelectronic -- copper and cobalt differ by three d electrons, and it is exactly that change in band filling and in cell volume that moves the system through the antiferromagnetic quantum critical point of the title. Recorded as a shared site so neither metal is read as a dilute dopant; the chunk file did not flag it because they are not in the same group.

basis: Two of the four samples are CeCo2Si2 and [ref 2] fixes that phase without inference: Ce(CoSi)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-3437 at hull 0.000 with 10 ICSD references, the dominant entry in the block. Two of the papers are on CeM2Si2 and on intermediate-valent cerium intermetallics, so the 122 is what the host is mostly about. The other two samples are different compounds and the host must be split. CeCo0.8Cu0.2Si3 is RTX3 rather than RT2X2 -- one transition metal to three silicons -- which is the non-centrosymmetric BaNiSn3 type that the taxonomy already carries with CeCoGe3 among its representative materials, so I list banisn3_i4mm as an alternate. Ce2Co3Si I cannot place: it matches no entry, [ref 2] has nothing at that stoichiometry, and it is filed under unresolved_crystalline rather than forced into the 122.

dopant_roles.basis: CeCo0.8Cu0.2Si3: copper takes a fifth of the transition-metal site. That site belongs to the RTX3 sample rather than to the 122 phase, and the substitution adds d electrons and expands the cell, which in intermediate-valent cerium compounds shifts the f level relative to the Fermi energy -- the subject of the papers. Confidence is limited by the fact that this one composition is also the one whose structure is least certain.

basis: Three of the four compositions are Ce(Ni1-xCux)2Si2 with x from 0.25 to 0.75, and the paper is Competing energy scales in the compounds Ce(Ni1-xCux)2(Si2), which names the series. CeNi2Si2 and CeCu2Si2 are both ThCr2Si2-type in I4/mmm and are isostructural, so the whole substitution series is one prototype -- and CeCu2Si2 is the original heavy-fermion superconductor, which is what the competing energy scales of the title are about. The fourth composition, Ce2Ni2.5Cu0.5Si, is a 2-3-1 stoichiometry that matches no entry in the taxonomy and that [ref 2] does not carry either -- its only entry is CeCuSi2Ni I-4m2 mp-1226605, a computed quaternary at yet another stoichiometry with no ICSD reference -- so it is filed under unresolved_crystalline and the host is marked mixed. Confidence is medium for that reason rather than from any doubt about the 122 samples.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal site of the M2Si2 slab
solid_solution_axis.note: Cu/(Cu+Ni) spans 0.25 to 0.75 across the three 122 compositions, the whole middle of the CeNi2Si2-CeCu2Si2 join. Not isoelectronic: nickel and copper differ by one d electron, and the series works by moving the hybridisation strength between the intermediate-valent nickel end and the heavy-fermion copper end. Both are alloy constituents at these fractions, not dopants. The chunk file did not flag the axis because they are not in the same group.

basis: All four compositions are Mn0.58Zn0.37CexFe2-xO4 with x from 0.4 to 1.0, and the paper is Thermoelectric power studies of cerium substituted Mn-Zn ferrites. Mn-Zn ferrite is the archetypal mixed spinel: MnFe2O4 and ZnFe2O4 are both cubic Fd-3m with zinc strongly tetrahedral and manganese and iron distributed over both sites, and the AB2O4 stoichiometry of every composition here matches. Neither reference covers this host. The cerium content is the one thing that is not a spinel statement: Ce3+ and Ce4+ are far too large for either the tetrahedral or the octahedral site of a ferrite, the solubility limit is a few percent at most, and at x up to 1.0 a CeO2 second phase is the expected outcome, so the spinel label describes the matrix rather than the whole nominal formula.

dopant_roles.basis: Nominally substituting for iron, but at x from 0.4 to 1.0 it is far past what a spinel site can accept for an ion this large; fluorite CeO2 precipitating at the grain boundaries is the usual result and is what the transport is likely responding to. Recorded as a second phase rather than as substitutional for that reason, at medium confidence because only the paper can settle it.
Zinc shares the tetrahedral A site with manganese across the whole Mn-Zn ferrite series; at 0.37 per formula unit it is an alloying constituent, not a dopant.

basis: All four compositions are CeTi1-xNixGe3 with x from 0.30 to 0.45, and the paper is on ferromagnetic quantum critical behaviour in these heavy-fermion compounds. CeTiGe3 is the BaNiO3-type 2H hexagonal perovskite in P6_3/mmc: chains of face-sharing TiGe6 octahedra running along c with cerium between them, which is what gives the compound its quasi-one-dimensional magnetic behaviour. Neither reference covers this host. Confidence is medium for one reason only, and it is a taxonomy problem rather than a structural doubt: hexagonal_perovskite_polytype is written with an ABO3 archetype and oxide exemplars, while this is an intermetallic germanide with the same face-sharing octahedral topology. The structure type is right; a v4 review should decide whether the entry is widened or a non-oxide sibling is split off.

dopant_roles.basis: Nickel takes the octahedral B site from titanium at 30 to 45 percent of that site, which is an alloying level rather than doping. It is not isoelectronic: nickel brings eight more d electrons than titanium, and moving the band filling is precisely how the series is driven to its ferromagnetic quantum critical point.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: octahedral B site of the face-sharing chain
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the nickel fraction of the B site. The chunk file did not flag this axis because titanium and nickel are not in the same group, and that is the point: the substitution changes the electron count rather than only the lattice, so the end members are not interchangeable and the series should not be treated as isoelectronic.

basis: Ce0.5Y0.5MgNi4 is a member of the RMgNi4 series, which takes the MgCu4Sn ordering of the C15b AuBe5 type in F-43m: the rare earth on one cubic site, magnesium on the other, and nickel forming the tetrahedral network. That is the aube5 entry, whose exemplar YbAgCu4 is the same ABC4 arrangement. Confidence is medium because the second composition, CeYMgNi2, does not balance to that stoichiometry; it comes from two broad rare-earth alloy survey papers rather than a structural study, and is most likely the same 1:1:4 phase transcribed differently. [ref 2] gives CeY(MgNi4)2 R3m (160) mp-1226870 at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference; that is a computed rhombohedral ordering of cerium and yttrium over the single rare-earth site of the same cubic type, not a distinct structure, so its space group is reported rather than followed.

dopant_roles.basis: Yttrium and cerium share the rare-earth site at 1:1. Trivalent yttrium is the non-magnetic and non-f analogue of a trivalent lanthanide, which is the standard way to dilute a cerium lattice while leaving the structure alone.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth site of the ordered C15b cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Only the 1:1 point is present, so there is no spread to fit, but the site really is shared and stage 3 should treat yttrium as an alloy constituent rather than a dopant. Cerium in these intermetallics is not always cleanly trivalent, so the substitution is isovalent by intent rather than by measurement.

basis: All four compositions are Th0.2-0.3(Nd,Ce)0.7-0.8Pd3 and the paper is Modification of the thermoelectric properties of CePd3 by the substitution of thorium and neodymium. CePd3, NdPd3 and ThPd3 are all Cu3Au-type L12 in Pm-3m, palladium on the face centres and the large cation on the corners, so the whole substitution field is a single prototype and the assignment does not depend on which end member dominates. Neither reference covers this host. I disagree with the ISOELECTRONIC SERIES line the chunk file prints for Ce/(Ce+Th): thorium is tetravalent in ThPd3 while cerium is trivalent to intermediate-valent in CePd3, so thorium substitution changes the band filling as well as diluting the 4f lattice, and that is what the paper is measuring. Neodymium for cerium is the substitution here that is close to isovalent.

dopant_roles.basis: Thorium takes the L12 corner site at 20 to 30 percent. Tetravalent, so it adds an electron relative to trivalent cerium as well as removing a 4f moment; an electron-count substitution at alloy concentration, not a dilute dopant.

Trivalent neodymium on the same corner site, replacing cerium at 42 to 56 percent of it. Isovalent in the formal sense, though it exchanges an intermediate-valence 4f1 ion for a stable 4f3 one, which is not electronically neutral.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: corner A site of the APd3 L12 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Bounds are the Ce/(Ce+Th) range quoted in the chunk file. Three species share one site here, not two, and the pair the chunk flagged is the one pair that is not isoelectronic: thorium is tetravalent. The parent compound is CePd3 throughout, diluted rather than alloyed toward a second end member.

basis: Every composition is Ce1-xSrxZnSbO with x from 0 to 0.10, and the curator detail transcribed from the paper says exactly that. CeZnSbO is the ZrCuSiAs 1111 type in P4/nmm: fluorite-like [Ce2O2] layers alternating with antifluorite-like [Zn2Sb2] layers, the same construction as LaZnAsO and BiCuSeO, which is why the paper calls these materials formed between an intermetallic and an oxide. [ref 2] agrees at CeZnSbO P4/nmm (129) mp-22620, hull 0.029; it rests on only 2 ICSD references and is flagged weak, but the composition and the layer chemistry settle it independently of that.

dopant_roles.basis: Divalent strontium on the trivalent cerium site of the oxide layer is an acceptor: it takes electrons out of the conducting ZnSb layer, which is the standard hole-doping route in the 1111 oxypnictides and is the variable x of the reported series.

basis: Both compositions are SrCeO3 with a few percent thulium and, in one case, twenty percent zirconium on the cerium site, and the paper is on hydrogen permeation through strontium cerate. SrCeO3 is an orthorhombic GdFeO3-distorted perovskite in Pnma, and acceptor-doped SrCeO3 is the original high-temperature proton conductor, which is what the 973 to 1173 K measured window is about. [ref 2] agrees and is well attested: SrCeO3 Pnma (62) mp-22428 at hull 0.008 with 14 ICSD references. Its other entries, Sr2CeO4 in Pbam and SrCe2O4 in Pnma, are different stoichiometries that no composition in this host matches.

dopant_roles.basis: Trivalent thulium on the tetravalent cerium B site is an acceptor, compensated by oxygen vacancies. Those vacancies are what hydrate to give proton conduction, so this is the functional dopant of the material rather than an impurity.

Tetravalent zirconium on the tetravalent cerium site adds no carriers; SrZrO3 is the isostructural end member and the join is continuous. It is added for chemical stability against CO2 and water, and the paper is about what that costs in permeation.

basis: The single composition is Sr(Ce0.6Zr0.4)0.85Y0.15O3, an yttrium-doped member of the SrCeO3-SrZrO3 join, and the paper is on its proton conduction and hydrogen permeation. Both end members are orthorhombic GdFeO3-distorted perovskites in Pnma and the solid solution between them is continuous, so the whole B-site field is one prototype; this is the same chemistry as the Ce-O-Sr host at rank 1356 with zirconium promoted above the 5 percent cut. Neither reference covers this host, but SrCeO3 Pnma mp-22428 with 14 ICSD references is carried on the neighbouring host and applies here.

dopant_roles.basis: Trivalent yttrium on the tetravalent B site, occupying 15 percent of it. The acceptor charge is compensated by oxygen vacancies, which hydrate to carry protons; this is the doping variable of the material, not a trace addition.
Tetravalent zirconium taking 40 percent of the cerium site. Isovalent, so it adds no carriers; it is there to stabilise the cerate against carbonation, at the cost of conductivity.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: octahedral B site of the perovskite
solid_solution_axis.note: Only one point of the SrCeO3-SrZrO3 join is present. Both end members are Pnma perovskites, so the axis changes the lattice parameters and the basicity but never the prototype.

basis: Three of the four samples are CePdSn, the Kondo-lattice antiferromagnet, which takes the TiNiSi type, the ordered Co2Si arrangement in Pnma. [ref 2] fixes that without inference: CeSnPd Pnma (62) mp-21490 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, the only well-attested entry in the block. The fourth sample is Ce2Pd2.05Sn0.95, the 2-2-1 phase, which is the Mo2FeB2 ordered U3Si2 type in P4/mbm and a genuinely different prototype, so the host is mixed and separates cleanly on stoichiometry. The remaining MP entries, Ce(SnPd)2 in P4/nmm, CeSn3Pd2 in Pbcm and Ce4Sn25Pd12 in Im-3, carry one ICSD reference each and match no composition measured here.

All four compositions are (Ce,Y)Pd3 spanning Ce/(Ce+Y) from 0.22 to 0.78, and the paper is a thermoelectric power investigation of the (Ce,Y)Pd3 system. CePd3 and YPd3 are both Cu3Au-type L12 in Pm-3m and form a continuous solid solution, so every composition on the join is the same prototype and no end member has to be chosen. [ref 2] offers CeYPd6 P4/mmm (123) mp-1226462 at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference; that is a computed 1:1 ordering of cerium and yttrium over the L12 corner site, which is the same structure made ordered for the calculation. The real alloys are disordered on that site, so the tetragonal cell is reported rather than adopted.

dopant_roles.basis: Yttrium and cerium share the corner site across the full range. Formally isovalent and nearly the same size, but yttrium has no f electron at all, so the series works by diluting the cerium lattice toward the non-magnetic limit while leaving the structure untouched.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: corner A site of the APd3 L12 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Ce/(Ce+Y). Isoelectronic in the formal sense and structurally continuous, but not electronically neutral: CePd3 is an intermediate-valence compound and YPd3 an ordinary metal, and the interest of the join is the crossover between them. No parent compound is assigned at host level.

basis: All four compositions are Ce(Rh1-xRux)2Si2 with x from 0.20 to 0.40, and the paper is a resistivity and thermopower study of that series. CeRh2Si2 and CeRu2Si2 are both ThCr2Si2-type in I4/mmm and isostructural, so the entire join is one prototype; the series is interesting because it moves between the antiferromagnet and the heavy-fermion metamagnet without changing the structure. [ref 2] offers only CeSi2RuRh I-4m2 (119) mp-1226491 at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference. I-4m2 is a subgroup ordering of the same 122 slab with rhodium and ruthenium made to alternate for the calculation, not a separate structure type, so it is noted rather than followed.

dopant_roles.basis: Ruthenium takes 20 to 40 percent of the transition-metal site of the T2Si2 slab. Not isoelectronic: it has one d electron fewer than rhodium, and shifting the band filling is how the series tunes the balance between Kondo screening and RKKY magnetism.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal site of the T2Si2 slab
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the ruthenium fraction of that site. The chunk file did not flag this axis because rhodium and ruthenium are in adjacent groups rather than the same one, which is exactly why it is not an isoelectronic series: the end members differ by one electron per transition metal.

basis: All three compositions are CeSe2 or a lightly substituted version of it. The light rare-earth diselenides belong to the PbFCl and ZrSSi family: fluorite-like [CeSe] slabs alternating with planar square nets of selenium, ideally tetragonal P4/nmm. In the cerium case the square net pairs up into Se2 dumbbells and the cell drops to a monoclinic superstructure, which is what [ref 2] carries as CeSe2 P2_1/c (14) mp-1320 at hull 0.040 with 4 ICSD references. The MP primary for this host is rocksalt CeSe Fm-3m mp-906175 with 7 references, but no composition measured here is the monoselenide, so the primary is reported and not followed. Confidence is medium because pbfcl_matlockite is written at the ideal undistorted MXY archetype while these are square-net-paired binaries.

other_polymorphs.note: CeSe is the well-attested monoselenide of this chemistry and the MP primary on 7 ICSD references, but it is a separate compound rather than a polymorph of CeSe2, and no composition in this host is at 1:1. Listed so the primary is not mistaken for a competing structure for the measured material.

dopant_roles.basis: The paper writes the series as CeSe2-xSnx, which puts tin on the selenium site, and the selenium square net is the site that can accept it. Tin on an anion sublattice is unusual enough that this should be checked against the paper; the alternative reading, tin on the cerium site with a selenium deficiency, would change the carrier sign.

Ce0.9Cu0.1Se2 writes the deficiency on cerium, so copper takes the rare-earth site. The companion paper is about controlling the localised f band by d-p hybridisation, which is consistent with a substitution that perturbs the cerium environment directly.

basis: Three of the four samples are CeSi2 and the paper naming them is Thermoelectric properties of the solid solutions based on ThSi2-type CeSi2, which states the structure type directly. CeSi2 is the alpha-ThSi2 type in I4_1/amd, a three-dimensional net of three-connected silicon atoms with cerium in the channels, and [ref 2] confirms it at CeSi2 I4_1/amd (141) mp-1072078, hull 0.000, 11 ICSD references. The taxonomy had no ThSi2 entry, so alpha_thsi2 is proposed rather than defaulting to alb2, which is the competing hexagonal RSi2 arrangement and would be the wrong half of that pair for a light rare earth. The fourth sample is Ce3Si2, the U3Si2 type in P4/mbm, confirmed by [ref 2] at mp-1079007 with 3 ICSD references, so the host is mixed and splits on stoichiometry. Note that CeSi2 is stable over a wide silicon deficiency and distorts to Imma when depleted, which is a composition effect rather than a thermal one.

The single composition is Cu9.1Te4Cl3 and the paper is titled after that compound. It is a well-defined crystalline thermoelectric, not a mixture, but the taxonomy has no entry for a copper-rich telluride halide and the references do not supply one: [ref 2] carries only CuTe2Cl P2_1/c (14) mp-30971 with a single ICSD reference, which is a different stoichiometry and a different connectivity and settles nothing about this material. The non-integral copper count of 9.1 points to a partially occupied and probably mobile copper substructure, the same feature that gives the copper chalcogenide superionics their low thermal conductivity and is consistent with the low thermal and high electrical conductivity of the title. That is a hypothesis about the compound, not a structure type I can name, so it is parked in unresolved_crystalline rather than forced onto a neighbouring prototype. The paper reports the crystal structure and would settle this in a single reading; it should be queued for exactly that.

Three samples are Cm2O3 and one is CmO2. The dioxide is straightforward: CmO2 is a fluorite oxide, and the paper measuring it covers NpO2, AmO2 and CmO2 together, all of them fluorite. The sesquioxide is not: Cm2O3 has the standard rare-earth and actinide sesquioxide polymorph problem, cubic C-type bixbyite in Ia-3 at low temperature, monoclinic B-type in C2/m in between, and hexagonal A-type in P-3m1 near the melt, and for curium specifically the alpha decay damages and can transform the lattice of a stored specimen, so which form a given sample is in depends on its history as much as its temperature. The C-type is taken as primary because it is what is normally obtained at room temperature, but confidence is low and the host belongs in the review queue. The 297 to 1277 K window may well cross the C to B transition, which is quoted near 1100 K for neighbouring actinide sesquioxides, but I will not put a number on it for curium, so no phases are recorded. Neither reference covers this host, which is expected for a transuranic.

Two of the four samples are elemental cobalt and the curator details say beta-Co, which is the hcp form. Cobalt is P6_3/mmc up to about 695 K and Fm-3m above it, and the 14 to 762 K window crosses that, so both are recorded as phases. [ref 2] ranks Co P6_3/mmc mp-54 and Co Fm-3m mp-102 at 10 ICSD references each, which is the two-phase situation appearing as a tie rather than a disagreement. The other two compositions are not cobalt at all: Rb3Co60 and K3Co60 are Rb3C60 and K3C60, the alkali fullerides, with C60 mis-parsed into an element symbol plus a count. They are recorded under fulleride_a3c60 and the host is flagged mixed for that reason, but this is a parsing artefact rather than a real two-phase chemistry, and stage 2 should route those two compositions out of this host rather than split it. Following the precedent set for elemental Ni, Cu, Fe and Cr, the cobalt itself is filed under solid_solution_alloy because the taxonomy has no separate entry for a close-packed elemental metal.

other_polymorphs.note: Cubic Fd-3m cobalt at hull 0.207 with 2 ICSD references, along with the P6_3mc and P4_2/mnm entries at one reference each. These are special preparations and computed cells, not steps in the hcp to fcc sequence.

dopant_roles.basis: Rb3Co60 is Rb3C60 with the fullerene mis-parsed. Rubidium is a genuine intercalant in the fulleride, filling the octahedral and tetrahedral voids of the C60 lattice, but it has nothing to do with cobalt metal and should not be read as a dopant of this host.
K3Co60 is K3C60, same mis-parse. The composition belongs to fulleride_a3c60, not to elemental cobalt.

basis: All four compositions are CoCrxFe2-xO4 with x from 0.5 to 1.0, and the paper is Thermoelectric power studies of Co-Cr nano ferrites. Both end members are cubic Fd-3m spinels, CoFe2O4 inverse and CoCr2O4 normal, and the join between them is continuous, so the prototype holds across the whole range even though the cation distribution over the tetrahedral and octahedral sites shifts with x. That redistribution is what the thermopower is measuring. [ref 2] gives only CrFeCoO4 Imma (74) mp-1226366 at hull 0.065 with no ICSD reference; an orthorhombic cell at this composition is a computed cation ordering of the same spinel framework, a way of making a three-cation disordered structure calculable, and not a phase these samples are in. I record the cubic spinel against it.

dopant_roles.basis: Chromium replaces iron at 25 to 50 percent of the B2 positions. Trivalent like the iron it replaces, so it adds no carriers, but its very strong octahedral site preference forces iron onto the tetrahedral site and inverts the cation distribution, which is the actual mechanism of the series.

basis: The four compositions run from Co15Cu85 to Co30Cu70 and the paper is on granular Co-Cu thin films. Cobalt and copper are essentially immiscible: the equilibrium phase diagram has no intermetallic and a solubility of well under a percent at room temperature, and granular is the standard description of what forms instead, nanoscale cobalt particles in an fcc copper matrix. That is a two-phase composite, not a compound, so composite_multiphase is the honest label. [ref 2] offers Co3Cu I4/mmm mp-1183752 at hull 0.124 with no ICSD reference; a computed ordered compound 124 meV above the hull is evidence for the immiscibility rather than against it, and I do not take it as a structure. solid_solution_alloy is kept as an alternative because films deposited far from equilibrium can retain a supersaturated fcc solution and some of these may be partly in that state, which is a question for the paper.

All four compositions are LaCo1-xCuxO3 with x from 0.25 to 0.50, two of them also carrying manganese, and the papers cover copper substitution in LaCoO3 and the LaMnO3-LaCoO3-LaCuO3 quasi-ternary. LaCoO3 is a rhombohedral R-3c perovskite and LaMnO3 an orthorhombic one; copper enters the same B site. The copper-rich end is the only complication: stoichiometric LaCuO3 requires high oxygen pressure, so at x near 0.5 these samples carry oxygen deficiency and the distortion that goes with it, which changes the space group but not the prototype. [ref 2] returns only computed multi-cation cells, La3Co2CuO9 in P-3c1 at hull 0.014 and a set of samarium-bearing quaternaries with no ICSD references and no relevance to these compositions; they are B-site orderings of the same perovskite framework.

dopant_roles.basis: Copper on the octahedral B site at 25 to 50 percent. It is the variable of the study rather than a dilute dopant, and because it does not reach the formal trivalent state easily it brings oxygen vacancies with it, which is how the carrier concentration actually moves.
Manganese on the same B site at 5 to 10 percent of it, coming from the LaMnO3 corner of the quasi-ternary the second paper maps. An alloying constituent of that join rather than an impurity.

basis: The two compositions are Cu2CoTi3S8 and Cu2Co1.5Ti2.5S8, and the paper is a comparative study of the thermoelectric thiospinels Cu2TrTi3S8 with Tr = Co and Sc, which names the family. Six cations to eight sulfur is the spinel ratio written on a doubled formula unit: copper tetrahedral, titanium and cobalt octahedral, cubic Fd-3m. [ref 2] gives Ti3Co(CuS4)2 R-3m (166) mp-1217164 and TiCoCuS4 Imma (74) mp-1216991, both computed and both without ICSD references. Rhombohedral and orthorhombic cells at this composition are the usual symmetry-lowered cation orderings used to make a multi-cation spinel tractable in a calculation, not competing phases, so I record the cubic thiospinel against them.

dopant_roles.basis: Moving from Cu2CoTi3S8 to Cu2Co1.5Ti2.5S8 puts extra cobalt on the octahedral titanium site. Cobalt and titanium differ in both valence and d-electron count, so this is the carrier-concentration knob of the series rather than an isovalent swap.
