basis: All four compositions are (Ti,Zr,Hf,V,Nb,Ta)(Fe1-xCox)Sb with the six early transition metals at an equal 0.167 share, and the paper is Synthesis and thermoelectric properties of high-entropy half-Heusler materials. The 1:1:1 stoichiometry with antimony is decisive: this is the half-Heusler F-43m structure with a six-component M sublattice, not a disordered high-entropy alloy. The point of the design is that six different M atoms on one crystallographic site scatter phonons hard while the three-sublattice ordering keeps the band structure of a half-Heusler intact, so calling it high_entropy_alloy would describe the disorder and lose the structure. Neither reference covers a nine-element host, and nothing at this composition could be expected in either. The Fe to Co ratio from 0.7:0.3 to 0.4:0.6 is the valence-electron-count knob that moves the material through the 18-electron semiconducting point.

dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt replaces iron on the tetrahedral T site from 30 to 60 percent. One electron more than iron, so the ratio sets the valence electron count directly and with it the carrier type and density; this is the doping variable of the series, applied at alloy concentration.

Vanadium, niobium and tantalum are one group and titanium, zirconium and hafnium another, and all six share the M site in equal parts. Within each group the substitution is isovalent and serves only mass and size contrast for phonon scattering; between the two groups it also shifts the electron count.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: M site of the half-Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: Six elements at an equal share of one site, which is the definition of the high-entropy design rather than a two-end-member join. No parent compound exists to assign; stage 3 should treat the M site as a six-component mixture and the Fe to Co ratio as the separate doping axis.

basis: Every composition is La(Fe,Co,Si)13. LaFe11.05Co0.91Si1.04 and LaFe10.5Co1.0Si1.5 each sum to thirteen iron, cobalt and silicon atoms per lanthanum, and Ce0.05La0.95Co10Fe2Si does the same with cobalt taking most of the thirteen. These are NaZn13-type cubic compounds in Fm-3c: lanthanum enclosed in a snub cube of 24 atoms, the remainder forming icosahedra. The nazn13_type prototype was proposed in chunk 027 for UBe13, and this host is independent confirmation that it was needed, since La(Fe,Si)13 is the giant-magnetocaloric material and one of the papers here is on the maximal cooling power of magnetic and thermoelectric refrigerators. Silicon is not a dopant: binary LaFe13 does not exist, and a minimum silicon content is what makes the NaZn13 type form at all. Neither reference covers this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Cerium takes 5 percent of the lanthanum site. Trivalent and nearly the same size, so it is a light chemical-pressure adjustment rather than a carrier dopant; in the magnetocaloric literature it is used to move the Curie temperature.

Silicon sits on the icosahedral 96i iron positions and is a required stabiliser, not an impurity: LaFe13 is not a stable compound and the NaZn13 type only forms once silicon reaches about one atom per formula unit. Its content is the main lever on the lattice parameter and the transition temperature.

Cobalt substitutes for iron on the same positions, from a little under one atom per formula unit up to ten in the Co10Fe2Si compositions. One electron more than iron; in this family it is the standard way of raising the Curie temperature toward room temperature.

basis: The single paper is titled Band-filling dependence of thermoelectric properties in B20-type CoGe and every composition is CoGe with a few percent nickel or iron on the cobalt site, so the structure is stated rather than inferred. B20 is the FeSi type, cubic P2_13, a chiral non-centrosymmetric arrangement with no inversion centre. I disagree with [ref 2] here and say so: its primary for the 1:1 formula is CoGe C2/m (12) mp-21237 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, which is the equilibrium ambient monoclinic phase. B20 CoGe is not the ground state; it is made under several GPa and retained metastably at ambient pressure, which is why the monoclinic form carries the hull minimum. The measured material is the B20 phase, so that is what is recorded, and the monoclinic phase is listed under other_polymorphs rather than allowed to override the paper.

other_polymorphs.note: Monoclinic C2/m CoGe at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references is the ambient equilibrium phase of this composition, but it is not what the samples are: the B20 form is synthesised under pressure and retained. Recorded so the reference disagreement is visible rather than silently resolved. The monoclinic phase has no prototype entry of its own in the taxonomy.

dopant_roles.basis: Nickel on the cobalt site at 4 to 8 percent, one electron more than cobalt. Together with iron it is how the paper moves the band filling across the narrow gap of B20 CoGe, which is the entire subject of the measurement.
Iron on the cobalt site at 4 percent, one electron fewer. The hole-doping half of the same band-filling series, and FeGe is itself a B20 compound so the substitution is structurally seamless.

basis: All three compositions are AxCoO2 layered cobaltates: H0.3CoO2 from the paper on the weakly correlated triangular lattice metal HxCoO2, and two hydrated sodium potassium cobalt oxyhydrates Na,K(H2O)yCoO2 from the thermopower and Co K-edge study. The CoO2 slab of edge-sharing octahedra on a triangular lattice is the same in all of them; what changes is the guest between the slabs and the interlayer spacing it sets. The hydrated sodium cobaltate is the family that superconducts near 4.5 K when the water content is right, which is why the measurements run to low temperature. [ref 2] offers CoHO2 R-3m (166) mp-31526 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference; that is heterogenite CoOOH, the fully protonated end of the same layered stacking, so it supports the layer topology while not matching any composition here. The Co(OH)2 entries are a different compound and are not relevant.

dopant_roles.basis: Sodium occupies the gallery between CoO2 slabs, not a cobalt or oxygen site. Its content is the compositional variable that sets the cobalt valence, exactly as x does in NaxCoO2, so it is not a dopant in the impurity sense.
Potassium shares the same interlayer gallery with sodium and water. Being larger it expands the spacing, which is one of the things the paper is comparing.

basis: All four compositions are Zr0.5Hf0.5(Co1-xRhx)Sb1-ySny and both papers are explicitly about p-type Zr0.5Hf0.5CoSb half-Heuslers with rhodium substitution. The 1:1:1 stoichiometry is exact once the site mixtures are collapsed: zirconium and hafnium share the M site, cobalt and rhodium the T site, and tin substitutes on the antimony site. F-43m throughout. [ref 2] offers HfZrCoSb2Rh R3m (160) mp-1224248 at hull 0.692 with no ICSD reference; a rhombohedral cell 692 meV above the hull is what comes of forcing four species onto a small ordered cell for a calculation, and it says nothing about the real material, so it is reported and rejected.

dopant_roles.basis: Tin on the antimony site at 1 to 15 percent, one electron fewer, which takes the valence electron count below 18 and makes the material p-type. This is the doping variable of both papers.

Rhodium is directly below cobalt in group 9, so it adds no carriers when it takes 20 to 60 percent of the T site. It is there for mass and size contrast, which lowers the lattice thermal conductivity, and RhSb-based half-Heuslers are stable in their own right so the join is continuous.
The fixed 50:50 Zr/Hf mixture on the M site is the standard mass-disorder trick for this family; isovalent, so it affects phonons and not carriers.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral T site of the half-Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Co/(Co+Rh) as the chunk file reports it. Genuinely isoelectronic, so both end members are half-Heuslers and no composition-dependent prototype choice arises; the parallel Zr/Hf mixture on the M site is fixed at 50:50 and is the same kind of substitution.

basis: Three of the four samples are Co2HfSn, the L21 full Heusler in Fm-3m, which [ref 2] confirms without inference at HfCo2Sn Fm-3m (225) mp-20730, hull 0.000, 5 ICSD references. The fourth is HfCo1.5Sn, which the companion paper introduces as a three-quarter Heusler, the same cubic cell with the second tetrahedral site half occupied rather than full or empty. That is a different prototype, so the host is mixed and separates on the cobalt count; three_quarter_heusler is proposed in this chunk for it. Worth noting for stage 2: [ref 2] also carries HfCoSn P-62c (190) mp-22315 with 2 ICSD references, a hexagonal 1:1:1 ternary that is not a Heusler at all, so a composition near MTX in this chemistry cannot be assigned cubic on stoichiometry alone.

All four compositions are Co3InSnS2-xSex, which is Co3Sn2S2 shandite with indium taking one of the two tin sites and selenium sharing the chalcogen site. Shandite is R-3m, kagome layers of cobalt sandwiched between the main-group and chalcogen atoms, and Co3Sn2S2 is the well-known half-metallic ferromagnet; the paper here is on the effect of simultaneous substitution on the electronic band structure, which is what the indium and selenium are for. Neither reference covers this five-element host, but the parent is fixed on the neighbouring Co-S-Sn host at rank 1389: Co3(SnS)2 R-3m (166) mp-19807, hull 0.000, 13 ICSD references.

dopant_roles.basis: Indium takes one of the two tin positions in every composition, a fixed 50 percent of that site rather than a variable. One electron fewer than tin, so it moves the Fermi level down through the half-metallic band structure, which is half of the simultaneous substitution of the title.
Selenium on the chalcogen site from 20 to 50 percent of it. Same group as sulfur, so it adds no carriers; it expands the lattice and adds mass contrast, the other half of the substitution.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: chalcogen site of the shandite
solid_solution_axis.note: x is S/(S+Se) as the chunk file reports it. Isoelectronic and structurally continuous, so the prototype is the same at every point; only the lattice parameter and the phonon spectrum move. The indium for tin substitution is fixed at 50 percent and is not isoelectronic, so it is recorded as a role rather than as an axis.

basis: Every composition is an indium-filled CoSb3 skutterudite: In1.2Co4Sb12, In0.9Fe0.5Co3.5Sb12 and two written explicitly as composites, (InSb)0.4In0.5Co4Sb12 and (InSb)0.5In0.5Co4Sb12. The framework is the CoSb3 corner-sharing octahedral network of the skutterudite with indium in the icosahedral void, which is a cage filler and not a substituent. The nominal indium content is the reason confidence is medium and the host is flagged mixed: the filling fraction limit for indium in CoSb3 is only about 0.2 per formula unit, so indium of 0.9 to 1.2 cannot all be in cages, and the third paper says as much in its title, Enhanced thermoelectric properties of In-filled Co4Sb12 with InSb nanoinclusions. These samples are filled skutterudite plus zincblende InSb as a deliberate second phase. [ref 2] is consistent with a low filling fraction rather than with the nominal formula: its entries are In(CoSb3)16 and In(CoSb3)20 in C2/m at hull 0.007 and 0.009, one indium per sixteen or twenty formula units.

dopant_roles.basis: Indium enters the icosahedral void of the CoSb3 framework as a rattler, donating electrons and scattering phonons. Only about 0.2 per formula unit fits; the excess in these compositions leaves the cages and forms InSb inclusions, so the same element is both filler and second phase in one sample.

In0.9Fe0.5Co3.5Sb12 puts iron on the framework cobalt site, one electron fewer, which compensates the donated electrons from the filler and is the standard way of holding the carrier concentration while raising the filling fraction.

basis: All four compositions are LixNayCoO2 with both alkalis present and the paper is on the magnetic and thermoelectric properties of layered LixNayCoO2. The CoO2 slab of edge-sharing octahedra is not in question; where the lithium sits is. In NaxCoO2 the alkali occupies trigonal prismatic sites between the slabs in the P2 stacking, while lithium prefers octahedral coordination and LiCoO2 takes the O3 alpha-NaFeO2 stacking instead, so a mixed lithium sodium cobaltate can be a single P2 phase with both guests, or an intergrowth of two stackings. That is a genuine caveat on the Li/(Li+Na) axis the chunk file prints: the two alkalis are formally isovalent but need not share a site, which is the same warning the project raises about oxygen and selenium in BiCuSeO. Recorded as naxcoo2_layered at medium confidence with alpha_nafeo2_layered as the alternative, and queued for the paper. [ref 2] gives only Na2Li2CoO4 in P2_1/c and P1, computed quaternaries at twice the alkali to cobalt ratio of these samples and not layered cobaltates at all; they are reported and rejected.

dopant_roles.basis: Sodium in the interlayer gallery of the CoO2 stack. Its content sets the cobalt valence and is a compositional variable of the material rather than a dopant.

Lithium is also an interlayer guest, but at medium confidence only: it may take the octahedral sites of an O3 stacking rather than the prismatic sites sodium uses, and a small amount of lithium can also enter the CoO2 slab itself on the cobalt site, which would make it substitutional instead. The paper would settle this.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: interlayer alkali gallery, subject to the stacking caveat
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Li/(Li+Na). Formally isovalent, but unlike a true anion-site series the two guests differ enough in size and coordination preference to change the stacking, so this axis may carry a prototype change rather than only a lattice parameter change. Treat it as a CHECK rather than an assertion.

basis: All four compositions are LiNi1-yCoyO2 with y from 0.2 to 0.75, and the papers are on transport in the LiNi1-yCoyO2 system and on LiCo1-xMxO2 thermoelectrics. LiCoO2 and LiNiO2 are both the O3 alpha-NaFeO2 structure, the rhombohedral R-3m cation-ordered rocksalt superstructure with alternating lithium and transition-metal layers, and they form a continuous solid solution, so the entire join is one prototype. [ref 2] returns only large computed supercells at odd stoichiometries, Li10Co3Ni7O20 in P-1 and Li10CoNi9O20 in P1 among them, three of the five flagged AMBIGUOUS; these are cation-ordering models of the same layered structure and their low-symmetry cells should not be read as competing phases. One of them, Li2Co3NiO8 in P4_332, is a spinel-type ordering, which is a real possibility for a lithium-deficient member but not for these LiMO2 compositions.

dopant_roles.basis: Nickel and cobalt are both trivalent on the transition-metal layer, so the substitution adds no carriers and the structure is continuous across the join. It is not electronically inert, though: low-spin Co3+ is a filled t2g shell while Ni3+ is Jahn-Teller active, which is why the transport changes so much along the series.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal layer of the O3 stacking
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Co/(Co+Ni) over the four compositions. The chunk file did not flag this as an axis, but it is the whole design of the series and both end members are the same prototype, so nothing about the structure assignment depends on where a composition sits on it. Note that the measured window reaches 1181 K, where lithium loss becomes a real concern for these oxides; that is a stability issue rather than a phase transition and no phases are recorded for it.

basis: All four compositions are Co2Mn1-xTixSn with x from 0.2 to 0.8. Co2MnSn and Co2TiSn are both L21 full Heuslers in Fm-3m and both half-metallic ferromagnets, so the entire join is one prototype. The paper is titled Phase-separation-induced changes in the magnetic and transport properties, and that separation matters for stage 2 without changing the label: it is a miscibility gap between manganese-rich and titanium-rich regions of the same Heusler structure, not a decomposition into two different prototypes, so the host is not flagged mixed. Neither reference covers this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Titanium takes 20 to 80 percent of the Y site from manganese. Three electrons fewer, so the valence electron count falls from 29 toward 27 across the series and the Fermi level moves through the half-metallic gap; it is also what opens the miscibility gap the paper reports.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: Y site of the L21 full Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the titanium fraction of the Y site. Not isoelectronic, and not a simple solid solution either: the paper reports phase separation into manganese-rich and titanium-rich Heusler regions, so a composition on this axis may be two Heuslers rather than one.

basis: All four compositions are CoNb1-xTixSn with x from 0.2 to 0.8, and the papers are High temperature thermoelectric properties of CoNb1-xMxSn half-Heusler compounds and a study of niobium vacancies and p-type doping in the NbCoSn-NbCoSb half-Heusler system, so the structure is named by both. NbCoSn is the 18-electron half-Heusler in F-43m, three interpenetrating sublattices with the fourth tetrahedral site empty, and titanium simply takes the niobium site. Neither reference covers this host. The titanium-rich end, CoNb0.2Ti0.8Sn, approaches TiCoSn at 17 valence electrons, which is metallic rather than semiconducting but structurally the same prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Titanium on the niobium M site from 20 to 80 percent of it. One electron fewer than niobium, so it takes the count below 18 and makes the material p-type; this is the doping variable of the first paper, applied at alloy concentration rather than dilutely.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: M site of the half-Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the titanium fraction. Not isoelectronic: niobium and titanium are adjacent groups and the electron count is what the series is varying, so the position on this axis sets the carrier concentration even though it never changes the prototype.

basis: All four compositions are NiCo2O4 with 0 to 5 mol percent calcium, and the curator detail transcribed from the paper says exactly that. NiCo2O4 is a cubic spinel in Fd-3m, largely inverse, with nickel and cobalt distributed over the tetrahedral and octahedral sites; it is the well-known conducting spinel of the cobaltite family. [ref 2] gives Co2NiO4 Imma (74) mp-38683 at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference plus four other computed cells, two of them flagged AMBIGUOUS; the orthorhombic, monoclinic and rhombohedral entries are cation-ordering models of the same spinel framework and are not competing phases. One caution for stage 2 rather than for the label: NiCo2O4 decomposes to the rocksalt monoxides above roughly 670 K in air, and the measured window runs to 1074 K, so the high-temperature end of these curves may not be on a spinel at all. That is a decomposition, not a polymorphic transition, so no phases are recorded for it.

dopant_roles.basis: Calcium at 1 to 5 mol percent, which the curator detail states as the doping level. Divalent like the nickel it replaces, so its effect is through size and site preference rather than through added carriers; at this level it is genuine dilute doping, unlike most of the substitutions in this chunk.

basis: The compositions are TiNiCoxSn with x of 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, and the papers are on metal distributions and n-type doping in TiNiSn and on controlling half-Heusler properties through the lattice. TiNiSn is the half-Heusler: F-43m with the second tetrahedral 4d site empty. Cobalt here is not replacing nickel but filling that vacant site, which walks the material from the half-Heusler toward a filled Heusler, and at x = 0.75 it is three quarters of the way there. Whether a given sample is a single phase with a partly occupied site or a nanoscale intergrowth of half-Heusler and full Heusler is exactly the question the first paper is asking, so the host is flagged mixed and confidence is medium. [ref 2] is unhelpful: Ti2CoNiSn2 R3m at hull 0.689 and Ti8Co3NiSn4 R-3m at hull 0.242 are computed orderings far above the hull, and only TiCoNiSn F-43m mp-1216950 at hull 0.050 is sensible, that being the fully filled end where cobalt and nickel share the two tetrahedral sites.

dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt occupies the vacant tetrahedral 4d site of the half-Heusler rather than substituting for nickel, which is why the formula is written TiNiCoxSn with nickel held at one. It is an electron donor in that position and an efficient phonon scatterer while the site is only partly filled; at x approaching one the structure is a filled Heusler instead.

basis: All four compositions are Co3-xRuxO4+d with x from 0.5 to 0.7, and the paper reports synthesis, crystal structures and high-temperature thermoelectric properties. Co3O4 is a normal spinel in Fd-3m with divalent cobalt tetrahedral and trivalent cobalt octahedral, and ruthenium substitutes on the octahedral site, so the framework is a spinel throughout. Confidence is medium because of the oxygen count: 4.3 to 4.47 oxygen per three cations is more than a spinel lattice can hold, so either the formulae are normalised from a refinement that included a second phase such as rutile RuO2, or the samples carry cation vacancies, and the difference matters for the carrier concentration. [ref 2] gives Co2RuO4 Imma (74) mp-34586 at hull 0.029 flagged AMBIGUOUS and several other computed cells with no ICSD references; as elsewhere in this chunk these are symmetry-lowered cation orderings of the cubic spinel rather than distinct phases.

dopant_roles.basis: Ruthenium takes the octahedral cobalt site at 0.5 to 0.7 atoms per formula unit. It is stable as Ru4+ where cobalt is Co3+, so the substitution adds electrons as well as a much more extended 4d orbital, and that is what turns an insulating spinel into a measurable thermoelectric.

The oxygen counts of 4.3 to 4.47 exceed the AB2O4 formula. In a spinel that is expressed as cation vacancies rather than interstitial oxygen; it may also be an artefact of the reported formulae. Recorded so the excess is not read as a separate element doping the lattice.

basis: Every composition is a CoSb3 skutterudite with an oxide dispersed in it: (CoSb3)0.9(ZrO2)0.1 twice, (ZrO2)0.1(CoSb3)0.9 written the other way round, and (CoSb3)92.17(Al2O3)7.83. All three papers say so in their titles, two on nano ZrO2 and CoSb3 composites and one on nano alumina dispersion. The matrix is the unfilled binary skutterudite, Im-3 with corner-sharing CoSb6 octahedra and Sb4 rings, and the oxide is a deliberate second phase added to scatter phonons at the grain boundaries. The zirconium, aluminium and oxygen are therefore not dopants of the skutterudite at all, and the host is not a ternary oxide: [ref 2] lists genuine cobalt antimonates, Co(SbO2)2 in P4_2/mbc and Co(SbO3)2 in P4_2/mnm among them, and none of them is what these samples are. That reference line is reported and rejected.

dopant_roles.basis: Present as nanoscale ZrO2 particles dispersed in the skutterudite, not in the lattice. The composite is the point of the paper.
Present as nano alpha-Al2O3, again a dispersed second phase rather than a substituent.
Oxygen belongs entirely to the dispersed ZrO2 and Al2O3 and does not enter the skutterudite framework.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [135, 136, 143, 227]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: All three compositions are the same material written three ways, (CoSb3)0.7(ZrO2)0.3, and they share two of their papers with the Co-O-Sb host at rank 1385. The matrix is the unfilled CoSb3 skutterudite in Im-3 and the zirconia is a dispersed second phase, so the prototype is the same as at rank 1385; what separates the two hosts is only that 30 mol percent zirconia pushes zirconium above the 5 at. percent cut. Confidence is medium for that reason: at 30 percent the zirconia is no longer a minor dispersoid but a major volume fraction, and stage 2 should carry this host as a genuine two-phase composite of skutterudite and zirconia rather than resolve it to a single structure. Neither reference covers this host.

dopant_roles.basis: ZrO2 at 30 mol percent, dispersed in the skutterudite rather than dissolved in it. Nanoscale zirconia is usually retained tetragonal rather than the monoclinic baddeleyite form stable in the bulk, which is a question for stage 2 if the second phase is ever resolved to a structure.
Oxygen is entirely in the zirconia and does not enter the CoSb3 framework.

basis: Three of the four samples are SrTbCoO4, which is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper member, the K2NiF4 structure: single CoO2 sheets of corner-sharing octahedra separated by rock-salt SrO and TbO layers, with strontium and terbium sharing the nine-coordinate A site. The fourth sample is Sr0.7Tb0.3CoO3-d, a simple perovskite, and the second paper is on the design of Sr0.7R0.3CoO3-d cathodes, so the host holds two prototypes and splits cleanly on the Co to A-site ratio. Confidence is medium because the perovskite member is strongly oxygen deficient and the Sr0.7Ln0.3CoO3-d cobaltites are known to order their oxygen vacancies into tetragonal or brownmillerite-like superstructures depending on preparation, which the label perovskite does not capture. Neither reference covers this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Terbium shares the A site with strontium in both members, at 50 percent of it in SrTbCoO4 and 30 percent in the perovskite. Trivalent against divalent strontium, so it reduces the cobalt valence and drives the oxygen deficiency; a compositional variable of the material rather than a dilute dopant.

basis: The single composition is CoS2, which is cattierite, the pyrite-type disulfide: cubic Pa-3 with cobalt octahedrally coordinated and S2 dimers on the anion positions. It is a well-studied itinerant ferromagnet, which is what the second paper on densified CoS2 ceramic is measuring. [ref 2] agrees at CoS2 Pa-3 (205) mp-2070, hull 0.000, 19 ICSD references. Two reference points are reported rather than followed. [ref 1] TEDesignLab covers only Co9S8 and Co3S4 for this chemistry, neither of which is the measured composition, so the usual precedence of TEDesignLab over Materials Project does not apply here. And the MP line also carries CoS2 Pbca (61) mp-850049 at hull 0.016 with 20 ICSD references, one more than the pyrite: an orthorhombic ambient CoS2 with more references than cattierite is not credible, and I read that count as mis-attribution within the 2019 snapshot rather than as evidence for a competing ambient phase.

other_polymorphs.note: The Pbca CoS2 entry at hull 0.016 with 20 ICSD references. Pbca is not the marcasite setting either, so the prototype given here is the nearest relative rather than a claim; an orthorhombic CoS2 could in principle be stabilised in the one film sample in this host, but the count is more likely a database artefact. Recorded so the disagreement with the pyrite assignment is visible.

basis: All four compositions are Co3Sn2S2 with indium on tin and iron on cobalt, and both papers are on this compound, one on the interplay of metal-atom ordering and Fermi level tuning and one on double substitution in the shandite. Co3Sn2S2 is the shandite structure, R-3m, with kagome nets of cobalt; it is the magnetic Weyl semimetal that has made this family prominent, and the thermoelectric interest follows from the same band structure. [ref 2] confirms it at Co3(SnS)2 R-3m (166) mp-19807, hull 0.000, 13 ICSD references, the only entry in the block and a well-attested one.

dopant_roles.basis: Indium on the tin site at 10 to 15 percent of it, one electron fewer than tin. It lowers the Fermi level through the band structure, which is the Fermi level tuning of the first paper title.

Iron on the kagome cobalt site at about 11 percent, again one electron fewer. Together with indium it is the double substitution of the second paper, acting on the magnetic sublattice rather than the spacer.

basis: The single composition is UCo0.5Sb2, measured on single crystals, and the paper is on the weak localisation effect in the strongly ferromagnetic Kondo compound UCo0.5Sb2. The UTSb2 ternaries take the HfCuSi2 type in P4/nmm: [USb] layers alternating with planar square nets of antimony, with the transition metal in the site between them and typically only half occupied, which is precisely why the formula carries Co0.5 rather than Co. That prototype was proposed in an earlier chunk with SrZnSb2 as its exemplar and fits this compound without stretching. Confidence is medium because no reference supports it here: [ref 2] offers only U3Co3Sb4 I-43d (220) mp-1188905 with 2 ICSD references, which is the Th3P4-type 3-3-4 compound at a quite different composition, so it is reported and rejected rather than used.

dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt is a framework element of the 112 structure, not a dopant, but its site is only half occupied and the vacancy level is what the formula records. In this family the transition-metal occupancy varies continuously and controls the magnetic ordering, so it should be treated as a structural variable rather than as an impurity level.

basis: Three of the four samples are Co2ZrSn, the L21 full Heusler in Fm-3m, which [ref 2] confirms at ZrCo2Sn Fm-3m (225) mp-914303, hull 0.000, 7 ICSD references. The fourth is ZrCo1.5Sn, the three-quarter Heusler of the companion paper, the same cubic cell with the second tetrahedral site half occupied, so the host is mixed and separates on the cobalt count. This is the zirconium twin of the Co-Hf-Sn host at rank 1375 and the two papers are shared between them. As there, note that [ref 2] also carries ZrCoSn P-62m (189) mp-30563 with 2 ICSD references, a hexagonal 1:1:1 ternary that is not a Heusler, so stoichiometry alone does not put an MTX composition in this family into the cubic structure.

The single composition is Co0.76Te, measured on single crystals and polycrystals. The cobalt tellurides between CoTe and CoTe2 are all NiAs derivatives in which cobalt is removed from alternate metal layers, and 0.76 is within rounding of the 0.75 that gives Co3Te4, the composition at which those vacancies order into the Cr3S4 type, monoclinic C2/m or I2/m. That is why cr3s4_defect_nias is taken over plain nias, which is kept as the alternative: whether this particular crystal has ordered or randomly distributed vacancies is a question only the paper can settle, and the difference matters because vacancy ordering changes the superstructure and the transport anisotropy. [ref 2] brackets the composition without covering it: CoTe P6_3/mmc mp-788 with 3 ICSD references is the filled NiAs end, CoTe2 Pnnm mp-9945 with 8 is the marcasite-type other end, and Co5Te6 R-3 mp-1226090 at hull 0.049 is exactly the kind of vacancy-ordered NiAs derivative this composition belongs to.

dopant_roles.basis: The 24 percent cobalt deficiency is the structure rather than an impurity: vacancies sit on alternate metal layers of the NiAs parent and their ordering is what defines the phase. Stage 3 should not read 0.76 as a doping level.

basis: The host holds two different silicides. Three of the four compositions are Fe1-xCrxSi at x from 0.10 to 0.15, and their paper is on the metal to insulator transition and impurity band conduction in Fe1-xCrxSi; FeSi is the archetypal B20 compound, cubic P2_13, and CrSi is isostructural, so that join is one prototype. The fourth, written (Fe0.9Cr01Si2)0.995Cu0.005, is a disilicide with a typographical slip in the chromium subscript, and its paper is on p- and n-type beta-FeSi2, the semiconducting orthorhombic Cmce phase. Those are different prototypes at different stoichiometries, so the host is mixed and splits on the silicon to iron ratio. [ref 2] matches neither: CrFe2Si Fm-3m mp-1018068 with one ICSD reference is a Heusler-like full-cubic ternary, and CrFe11Si4 and CrFeSi2 are computed cells with none, so the reference line is reported and not used.

dopant_roles.basis: Copper at 0.5 percent in the beta-FeSi2 composition only. At that level it is genuine dilute doping of the semiconductor; the paper is about making p-type and n-type legs, and copper is also used in this system as a sintering aid, so which of the two it is doing should be checked against the paper.

Chromium takes the iron site in both phases but does different work in each. In B20 Fe1-xCrxSi it removes an electron per substitution and drives the metal to insulator transition the paper is measuring; in beta-FeSi2 it is the standard acceptor for p-type legs. At 10 to 15 percent it is an alloying constituent rather than a dilute dopant.

basis: The single composition is (LaS)1.20CrS2 and the paper is Microstructural Control and Thermoelectric Properties of Misfit Layered sulfides. The 1.20 is the signature of the structure rather than a stoichiometry: two mutually incommensurate subsystems stacked along one axis, rock-salt LaS slabs and CdI2-like CrS2 slabs, whose in-plane periods do not share a common multiple. [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives LaCrS3 Pnma (62) mp-10328 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference; that is the commensurate 1:1 approximant of the same layer stacking, and although the project precedence would normally prefer TEDesignLab, a commensurate cell cannot represent an incommensurate composite, so it is recorded as an approximant and not adopted. This is one of the prototypes the project already flags as having no single Materials Project entry, and stage 2 will need the two subsystems separately.

All four compositions are Cr(N1-xOx) with x from 0.11 to 0.45 and the paper is on changes in the electrical resistivity of CrN after oxygen dissolution, so the material is rocksalt CrN with oxygen taken onto the nitrogen site. Fm-3m, cubic, the standard interstitial-compound rocksalt of the nitride prototype. I disagree with [ref 2] outright and record that: every entry it returns is a chromium nitrate or nitrite molecular salt, CrN3O4 at hull 2.24, CrN3O8 at 2.06, Cr(NO2)2 at 0.79, up to 2.2 eV above the hull. Those are compounds of the NO3 and NO2 anions, not a nitride with dissolved oxygen, and matching on element set alone is what produced them. The measured window of 76 to 291 K also crosses the CrN Neel transition near 280 K, at which the paramagnetic cubic phase distorts to an orthorhombic Pnma antiferromagnet; that is a magnetostructural distortion of the same rocksalt framework rather than a change of prototype, so both phases are recorded under the same prototype id. Oxygen dissolution is known to suppress that transition, so the temperature is composition-dependent here in particular.

dopant_roles.basis: Oxygen dissolves onto the nitrogen site of the rocksalt lattice, which is the subject of the paper. It brings one more electron than nitrogen, so it dopes as well as alloys; at x = 0.11 that is doping, while at x = 0.45 the material is halfway to an oxide and the word dopant no longer applies. This is emphatically not milling or pressing residue.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion site of the rocksalt
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the oxygen fraction of the anion site. Not isoelectronic: oxygen and nitrogen differ by one electron, and that is the whole mechanism of the paper. The chunk file did not flag this axis because the two are not in the same group.

basis: All four compositions are (CrO2)x(SnO2)1-x and the paper is on magnetic and magnetotransport properties of half-metallic CrO2-SnO2 composites. This is the rare case where a composite needs no splitting: CrO2 and SnO2 are both rutile in P4_2/mnm, so both phases of every sample are the same prototype and the host label is true of all of it. The mutual solubility is limited, so these are two-phase mixtures rather than a solid solution, but that does not change the structure assignment. Neither reference covers this host. One point for stage 2 rather than for the label: CrO2 is metastable with respect to Cr2O3 above about 670 K in air, which would matter for a high-temperature measurement but not here, where the window stops at 300 K.

dopant_roles.basis: SnO2 is the second phase of the composite, deliberately added, at 20 to 70 percent by formula. It is isostructural with the CrO2 matrix, which is why the prototype is unaffected, but it is a separate phase rather than a substituent on the chromium site.

basis: All four compositions are Cr1-xVxSi2 with x from 0.2 to 0.74 and the paper is Thermoelectric and magnetic properties of Cr1-xVxSi2 solid solutions. CrSi2 and VSi2 are both the C40 hexagonal disilicide in P6222 and form a continuous solid solution, so every composition on the join is the same prototype regardless of which end it is nearer. CrSi2 is the narrow-gap semiconductor of the pair and vanadium substitution moves it metallic, which is what the series measures. [ref 2] contributes nothing usable: V(CrSi3)2 in C222, V2(CrSi)3 in Ibam, V3Cr3Si2 in R32 and the rest are computed cells at stoichiometries that are not disilicides at all and carry no ICSD references, so the whole line is reported and rejected.

dopant_roles.basis: Vanadium on the chromium site from 20 to 74 percent of it. One electron fewer than chromium, so it empties the band that makes CrSi2 semiconducting; the substitution is an alloying axis rather than doping at these levels, and it is also what carries the magnetic behaviour of the series.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: metal site of the C40 disilicide
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Cr/(Cr+V) across the four compositions. Both end members are C40, so no composition-dependent prototype choice arises, but the electron count changes along the axis and the parent semiconductor is CrSi2 only at the chromium-rich end. The chunk file did not flag this axis because chromium and vanadium are in adjacent groups.

basis: All four compositions are TlSr2(Er1-ySry)Cu2O7-d and the paper names the structure in its title, Thermopower and Resistivity of 1212-Type Phase TlSr2(Er1-ySry)Cu2O7-d. The 1212 phase is exactly the archetype of this prototype with n = 2: a single Tl-O charge reservoir layer, two CuO2 planes, and a cation layer between them, tetragonal P4/mmm. Strontium stands in for barium on the reservoir-adjacent site and erbium for calcium between the planes, which is a chemical substitution within the family rather than a different structure. Neither reference covers this five-element host, which is usual for the cuprates in this dataset.

dopant_roles.basis: Strontium replaces erbium on the interplane site at y = 0 to 0.3, which is the variable of the paper. Divalent on a trivalent site, so it removes electrons from the CuO2 planes; this is the hole-doping knob of the cuprate and is what moves the sample across the underdoped to overdoped range that the thermopower reflects. Strontium also occupies its own separate site in the TlSr2 block, where it is a framework element rather than a dopant.

basis: The compositions are Cu3ErTe3 with up to 0.3 silver replacing copper, and the two papers are Cu3ErTe3: a new promising thermoelectric material and Ternary Compounds Cu3RTe3 (R = Y, Sm, and Dy): A Family of New Thermoelectric materials, so the family is established rather than a single composition. The taxonomy had no entry for it, so cu3rte3_type is proposed here. [ref 2] supplies the structure: Er(CuTe)3 Pmn2_1 (31) mp-640885 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, which is this compound in Materials Project element ordering; the rhombohedral R-3 entry at hull 0.048 and the ErCuTe2 entries are different or higher-energy phases and are not taken. Confidence is medium for two reasons: the space group comes from a single ICSD reference rather than from independent knowledge of the type, and the fourth composition, Cu2ErTe3, is a full copper short of the others. At Cu2ErTe3 the cations cannot balance three tellurium, so it is either a transcription slip for Cu3ErTe3 or a strongly copper-deficient sample; it is flagged here rather than split off into a second prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Silver on the copper site at 3 to 10 percent of it. Same group and the same monovalent state, so it adds no carriers; it is there for the size and mass contrast, and in copper chalcogenides it also tends to slow copper migration. Whether the reported series intends it as a dopant or as a stabiliser is worth checking against the paper.

basis: The single composition is Cu22Fe8Ge4S32 and the paper is Structure, microstructure and thermoelectric properties of germanite-type Cu22Fe8Ge4S32, which names the structure type directly. Germanite is a cubic P-43n superstructure of sphalerite with 32 sulfur atoms per cell and copper, iron and germanium ordered over the cation positions, the mineral being nominally Cu26Fe4Ge4S32 and the synthetic thermoelectric pushing iron up to eight at the expense of copper. The taxonomy had colusite but nothing for germanite, and the two are close enough that filing this under colusite would misstate the cation chemistry rather than round it, so germanite_type is proposed here. The references split without settling it: [ref 1] TEDesignLab has only FeCu2GeS4 I-42m mp-917359 with 5 ICSD references, which is the stannite-type quaternary at a completely different stoichiometry, and [ref 2] offers Fe2Cu13(GeS8)2 P-43m (215) mp-1227624 at hull 0.017 with no ICSD reference, which is at the right composition and a closely related cubic symmetry and is probably a computed relative of the germanite cell.

dopant_roles.basis: Iron at eight per cell against the four of mineral germanite, taken from the copper count. That exchange is the carrier-concentration variable of this family: copper is monovalent and iron is not, so the cation ratio sets the hole count in the sulfur framework.

basis: Cu2Zn(1-x)Fe(x)GeSe4 across the series, which is the quaternary A2BCX4 tetrahedral framework. [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives FeCu2GeSe4 I-42m (121) mp-1087471, the stannite setting, and agrees. The listed CuFeGeSe4 is almost certainly Cu2FeGeSe4 with one copper lost in transcription, since the paper works the Cu2Zn(1-x)Fe(x)GeSe4 solid solution and the other three compositions all carry Cu2.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn(II) and Fe(II) both sit on the B site of the A2BCX4 framework, so exchanging them changes mass, size and magnetism but not the electron count. The paper title -- phonon scattering through a local anisotropic structural disorder -- says the point of the substitution is lattice thermal conductivity, not carriers.

note: The Zn/Fe exchange is a genuine full-range solid solution in the paper (x from 0 to 1), but only the Fe-rich members fall in this host and the chunk file does not flag an axis, because Zn and Fe are not in the same periodic group. No axis is recorded.

basis: CuFeS2(1-x)Se2x throughout, which is chalcopyrite with selenium on the anion site; the paper title states the series and its solubility limit. [ref 2] offers only FeCuSeS I2_12_12_1 (24) mp-1224989 at hull 0.139 with no ICSD backing, and I do not follow it -- that is a computed ordered cell for the 1:1 midpoint, while the ambient structure of CuFeS2 and of its Se-substituted members is the tetragonal I-42d chalcopyrite superstructure of sphalerite. A hull of 0.139 with no ICSD reference is not evidence of an ambient phase.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: x is S/(S+Se). Every composition sits on the sulfur-rich side, so these are Se-substituted CuFeS2 rather than a symmetric pseudobinary, and the parent compound is chalcopyrite CuFeS2 for all four.

basis: Gd2CuO4 is the n=1 A2BO4 layered cuprate. The taxonomy entry itself states that Nd2CuO4 and Pr2CuO4 take the T-prime variant under this same id, and Gd2CuO4 is that same T-prime structure -- fluorite-like Gd2O2 blocks and square-planar CuO2, rather than the rocksalt blocks and apical oxygen of T-phase La2CuO4. [ref 2] agrees on the cell: Gd2CuO4 I4/mmm (139) mp-4860 with 4 ICSD references. The papers are titled Thermoelectric properties of layered rare earth copper oxides.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce held at a fixed 0.15 per formula is the electron-doping variable of the T-prime cuprates, exactly as in Nd(2-x)Ce(x)CuO4: Ce(IV) on a trivalent rare-earth site adds electrons to the CuO2 planes. It is the knob, not an impurity.
Pr(III) for Gd(III) on the rare-earth site at 0.1 to 0.3 per formula; same valence, so it changes the lattice parameter and the 4f moment without altering the carrier count set by Ce.

note: Variant: T-prime (Nd2CuO4 type). Recorded under ruddlesden_popper because the taxonomy entry explicitly directs T-prime cuprates there; the variant is worth carrying forward to stage 2, because the T and T-prime forms share a space group but differ in oxygen positions and in the sign of the carriers.

basis: Gd(1.85-x)Pr(x)Ce0.15CuO4 from a single paper, which is the same T-prime A2CuO4 layered cuprate as the Cu-Gd-O host at rank 1403; only the rare-earth mix changes, and Ce is held at 0.15 throughout. The two hosts are one series split by the 5 at.% cut. No reference is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce(IV) at a fixed 0.15 on the rare-earth site is the electron-doping variable of the T-prime cuprates, held constant while the Gd/Pr ratio is swept.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth A site of the T-prime A2CuO4 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Gd/(Gd+Pr). Both are trivalent on the same site, so this is a lattice-parameter and 4f-moment series at fixed electron count rather than a doping axis.

note: Variant: T-prime (Nd2CuO4 type), as for Cu-Gd-O.

basis: Two of the four compositions, Cu15Ge7.5Te77.5 and Cu20Ge5Te75, are atomic-percent Te-rich melt-quenched chalcogenide glasses -- the paper is titled Conducting glasses as new potential thermoelectric materials: the Cu-Ge-Te system -- and carry no periodic structure at all. The other two, Cu0.10Bi0.05Ge0.85Te and the (GeTe)0.96(Bi2Te3)0.04 compact with 28 at.% Cu, are Cu- and Bi-doped GeTe, rhombohedral R3m at room temperature. One label cannot cover both, so the host is mixed. [ref 2] offers only Cu2GeTe3 polymorphs, a crystalline ternary at a stoichiometry none of these four compositions has, and is not followed.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi at 0.05 per formula in Cu0.10Bi0.05Ge0.85Te, and as Bi2Te3 in the (GeTe)0.96(Bi2Te3)0.04 pseudobinary. Bi(III) on the Ge(II) site is a donor and is the carrier-density control the second paper is about.

note: No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line was printed for this host, but the measured window reaches 770 K and the GeTe R3m to Fm-3m transition sits near 700 K, so the sequence is recorded anyway. It applies only to the two GeTe-based compositions; the glasses have no transition of this kind. Heavy Cu and Bi content moves the temperature, so 700 K is the taxonomy default and is approximate here.

basis: CuIn(1-x)Fe(x)S2 with x up to 0.15, plus the parent CuInS2. [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives InCuS2 I-42d (122) mp-22736 at hull 0.000 with 13 ICSD references, which is chalcopyrite and settles it. The In2CuS4 spinel and In5CuS8 entries in [ref 2] are other phases of the chemistry, not what this series is; the paper title, structure-property relationships along the Fe-substituted CuInS2 series, names the parent directly.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe(III) for In(III) on the trivalent cation site. It is isovalent, and the other end member CuFeS2 is itself a chalcopyrite, so this is a solid-solution series rather than carrier doping -- what it changes is the magnetism and the gap, not the electron count.

basis: Every composition resolves as n SnTe plus one CuInTe2: CuSn7InTe9 is 7 + 1, CuSn5InTe7 is 5 + 1, CuSn2InTe5 is 2 + 1 and CuSnInTe3 is 1 + 1. The paper is a strategy to optimise the overall thermoelectric properties of SnTe by compositing it with CuInTe2, so this is a two-phase rocksalt SnTe matrix carrying a chalcopyrite CuInTe2 second phase, not a single quaternary compound. SnTe dominates in three of the four, so rocksalt is primary and the host is mixed. No reference is offered for this host.
note: The split is by phase fraction within each sample rather than by composition, so stage 2 cannot separate these the way it separates a mixed host into single-phase compositions. Each sample genuinely contains both structures.

basis: Two different compounds share this host. YInCu2 and its Ce-substituted members are the Heusler L21 type -- the RInCu2 series crystallises in the Cu2MnAl structure -- and [ref 2] carries YInCu2 Fm-3m (225) mp-19946 with an ICSD reference, which is that cell. YInCu4 is the C15b AuBe5 type, F-43m, and [ref 2] carries YInCu4 F-43m (216) mp-1071645 with an ICSD reference; the second paper is titled Transport properties of RInCu4 with C15b-type structure and names it outright. Three of the four compositions are the 1:1:2 Heusler, so that is taken as primary and the host is mixed.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce at 0.05 to 0.10 for Y in Ce(x)Y(1-x)InCu2. The paper studies the dilute Kondo regime, so cerium is a magnetic 4f substituent on the rare-earth site rather than a carrier dopant; yttrium is the non-magnetic reference lattice it is diluted into.

note: The two compounds separate cleanly on the Cu:In ratio -- 2:1 for the Heusler, 4:1 for the C15b -- so this host should split on composition in stage 2.

basis: CuIrRhS4 is Cu(Ir0.5Rh0.5)2S4, the AB2S4 thiospinel: copper on the tetrahedral A site, iridium and rhodium sharing the octahedral B site, cubic Fd-3m. Both end members CuIr2S4 and CuRh2S4 are thiospinels, so the 50:50 member is one too. No reference is offered for this host.
note: CuIr2S4 undergoes a metal-insulator transition near 230 K with Ir(III)/Ir(IV) charge ordering and a symmetry-lowering distortion away from cubic, which would sit inside the measured 13-300 K window. At 50 at.% Rh on the octahedral site that transition is suppressed, which is why the paper can report smooth thermodynamic and electrical behaviour across the range, so no phase sequence is recorded. That is judgement from the chemistry of the end members, not something read out of this paper, and is worth confirming.

basis: La1.85Sr0.15Cu(1-x)Mg(x)O4 with x of 0.4 and 0.5 is the n=1 K2NiF4 layered cuprate La2CuO4 with magnesium diluting the CuO2 plane; the paper title names the La1.85Sr0.15Cu(1-x)Mg(x)O4 system. This is the T phase, with rocksalt La2O2 blocks and apical oxygen, unlike the T-prime Gd2CuO4 at rank 1403. Mg at 0.4 to 0.5 per formula is a host constituent of the B site, not a dopant. No reference is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr(II) for La(III) at a fixed 0.15 per formula is the hole-doping variable of La(2-x)Sr(x)CuO4, held at optimal doping while magnesium dilutes the plane. It is the doping knob of the family, not an incidental substituent.

basis: LaCuOSe is the ZrCuSiAs 1111 type, P4/nmm, with alternating (La2O2) and (Cu2Se2) layers; the paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of layered oxyselenides La(1-x)Sr(x)CuOSe. [ref 2] carries no LaCuOSe entry at all -- its four candidates are a La2Cu(SeO3)4 selenite, La2CuSe2O and LaCu2SeO2 at hulls above 1.0, and a cubic La4Cu3SeO12 -- so the reference set simply misses the ambient phase here and none of it is followed.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr(II) for La(III) in the (La2O2) layer is the hole-doping variable of this family and is what the paper sweeps from x=0 to x=0.15. The carriers land in the (Cu2Se2) layer, so the dopant and the conducting layer are separated -- the modulation-doping feature this family is studied for.

note: The curator records two thin-film and two polycrystalline samples. Both forms are the same P4/nmm phase, so the host is not split on that.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [129], ICSD-backed references for this host report [14]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Copper with 5.5 to 9.5 at.% manganese, from two papers on the thermoelectric power and resistivity of dilute alloys of Mn in copper. These are the classic Kondo dilute alloys: manganese substitutes randomly on the fcc copper lattice and no ordered phase forms at these concentrations. [ref 2] offers only Mn4Cu R-3m at hull 0.133 and MnCu3 P6_3/mmc at hull 0.098, both computed with no ICSD backing and neither at these compositions; I disagree with taking either, because below 10 at.% Mn the material is a disordered fcc terminal solid solution and there is no compound to point at.
note: Manganese sits at 5.5 to 9.5 at.%, just above the 5 at.% split, so it is treated as a host element and gets no dopant_roles entry. Physically it is a dilute magnetic solute on the Cu site, which is the whole subject of both papers.

basis: TlSr2(Er(1-y)Sr(y))Cu2O7-delta, and the paper title states 1212-type phase outright. That is the single-TlO-layer 1212 cuprate: a TlO charge reservoir, two SrO layers, two CuO2 planes and the Er/Sr site between them where calcium sits in the canonical compound. [ref 2] offers Sr2TlCuO5 P4/mmm (123) mp-620290, which is the 1201 member with one CuO2 plane, and Sr4CaLaTl2(Cu2O7)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-1218536, which is 1212 but at a different cation set; neither is this composition, so no mp_id is taken.

dopant_roles.basis: Er occupies the interlayer site between the two CuO2 planes, the calcium site of the canonical 1212 cuprate, and y is the doping variable: replacing trivalent Er with divalent Sr there adds holes to the planes. Er runs from 0.3 to 0.6 of that site, so it is an end member of a substitutional series rather than dilute doping, and it falls under the 5 at.% cut only because the formula has twelve atoms.

basis: Cu3P(1-x)Ge(x)S4 with x up to 0.3, plus the parent Cu3PS4. The paper is titled Enargite Cu3PS4, naming the type directly, and [ref 2] agrees on the cell: Cu3PS4 Pmn2_1 (31) mp-3934 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, ranked first for the formula. The taxonomy carries famatinite for the tetragonal I-42m Cu3BX4 polymorph but nothing for the orthorhombic wurtzite-derived enargite polymorph. These are genuinely different structures at one stoichiometry -- enargite and luzonite are exactly that pair for Cu3AsS4 -- so filing this under famatinite would assert the wrong anion stacking rather than round it. enargite_cu3ps4 is proposed here.

dopant_roles.basis: Ge(IV) for P(V) on the group-15 site of the Cu3BX4 framework is an acceptor, and it is the hole-doping knob of the series -- the parent Cu3PS4 is a wide-gap insulator and x is swept from 0 to 0.3 to make it conduct.

basis: Cu(6-x)WSnSe8 with copper taken deliberately from 6.00 down to 5.91. The stoichiometry is the selenide analogue of the mineral kiddcreekite, Cu6SnWS8, and it charge-balances exactly as Cu(I)6 Sn(IV) W(VI) Se(-II)8; the cell is a cation-ordered 2x2x2 superstructure of sphalerite in the germanite-colusite group. The taxonomy has colusite but nothing at this cation set, and a colusite label would assert a group-5 metal and six group-14 atoms per 32 anions that are not present here, so kiddcreekite_type is proposed. The alternative reading, an ordered famatinite Cu3(W0.5Sn0.5)Se4 with the B site shared equally by W(VI) and Sn(IV) to average the Sb(V) of Cu3SbSe4, describes the same tetrahedral framework at a smaller cell and is recorded as the alternative. No reference is offered for this host, so nothing here is checked against a database.
note: The copper content is the variable here: 6.00, 5.97, 5.94, 5.91 per formula. Copper vacancies are the carrier-concentration knob, which is non-stoichiometry rather than doping, and the paper title -- the charge localization deteriorating the thermoelectric properties -- is about what those vacancies do. Copper is a host element, so no dopant_roles entry is made for it and stage 3 should read the deficiency off the parsed fractions.

basis: Three of the four compositions are copper with 5.2 to 8.4 at.% silicon, from a paper on the thermoelectric power and resistivity of dilute alloys of Si in copper -- a disordered fcc terminal solid solution, as for the Cu-Mn host at rank 1412. The fourth, LaCu20.5Si2, matches no standard stoichiometry in this system; the nearest real compound is LaCu2Si2, the ThCr2Si2 122 type, and the string looks like a digitisation of that. [ref 2] offers the Cu15Si4, Cu3Si and Cu7Si2 line compounds, none of which forms below about 9 at.% Si, so none is taken.

dopant_roles.basis: La at 4.3 at.% belongs entirely to the separate LaCu20.5Si2 entry, not to the dilute Cu-Si alloys that make up the rest of the host. It is a constituent of its own intermetallic rather than a dopant in copper, and the composition string is not trustworthy enough to say which site it takes.

note: The LaCu20.5Si2 composition should be checked against its paper (Phys. Rev. B 64, 195106) before the alt prototype is relied on. If it is LaCu2Si2 the alt is right; if the 20.5 is real then neither prototype here covers it.

basis: Three unrelated compounds across four samples. CuTl9Te5, which carries two of the samples, is the Tl-rich end; [ref 2] carries Tl4CuTe3 I4/mcm (140) mp-34765 with an ICSD reference, which is the Tl5Te3 type with copper on a thallium site, and that is the nearest attested phase. I flag that the match is not clean: Tl9CuTe5 has a metal-to-tellurium ratio of 2:1 against the 10:6 of Tl5Te3, so the composition is either off-stoichiometric or two-phase. TlCu2Te2 is the ThCr2Si2 / BaAl4 layered type, I4/mmm, as TlCu2Se2 is. TlCu3Te2 is a third structure again, monoclinic Pc in mp-1217029 at hull 0.051, and has no taxonomy entry at all. With three structures over four samples the host label is weak whichever one is chosen.
note: Needs review. The three compositions separate cleanly on the Tl:Cu ratio, so a composition-level split is possible, but the TlCu3Te2 branch has nowhere to go in the current taxonomy and the CuTl9Te5 stoichiometry does not sit on the Tl5Te3 line. All three papers report the structure, so reading them would settle this.

basis: Mn0.58Zn0.37Er(x)Fe(2-x)O4 with x from 0.4 to 1.0 is a Mn-Zn ferrite, the AB2O4 cubic spinel Fd-3m, with erbium substituted for iron on the octahedral B site; the paper is titled Thermoelectric power studies of erbium substituted Mn-Zn ferrites. No reference is offered for this host.
note: Confidence is medium rather than high because Er(III) is far too large for the octahedral B site of a spinel and its solubility there is at most a few atomic percent. At the nominal x of 0.8 and 1.0 the samples very likely carry an ErFeO3 orthoferrite second phase, so the higher-x compositions are unlikely to be single-phase spinel. Settling that needs the diffraction pattern in the paper. The same caveat applies to the Fe-Gd-Mn-O-Zn host at rank 1421.

basis: EuNiO3 throughout, the GdFeO3-distorted orthorhombic perovskite. [ref 2] agrees: EuNiO3 Pnma (62) mp-32341 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references; the Pm-3m entry mp-1076460 at hull 0.037 is the undistorted cubic aristotype, which is not the observed form at any temperature here.
note: No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line was printed, because the prototype does not change -- EuNiO3 is a perovskite on both sides. The space group does change. Below its metal-insulator transition near 460 K the structure is monoclinic P2_1/n with two inequivalent nickel sites from Ni(III) charge disproportionation; above it the symmetry rises to orthorhombic Pnma and the compound is metallic. The measured window is 217-483 K, so it straddles that point, and the paper -- a d-band electron correlated thermoelectric thermistor established in EuNiO3 -- is about exactly this feature. The 460 K value comes from general knowledge of the RNiO3 series, not from the paper, and no mp_id exists for the monoclinic phase in the reference set.

basis: Eu(1-x)Yb(x)Zn2Sb2 across the full range. AZn2Sb2 with a divalent A cation is the CaAl2Si2 trigonal P-3m1 Zintl structure, with (Zn2Sb2) slabs and A between them; both EuZn2Sb2 and YbZn2Sb2 are that type, and both papers call these Zintl compounds. No reference is offered for this host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A cation site between the (Zn2Sb2) slabs
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Eu/(Eu+Yb) as written in the compositions. Both are divalent on this site, so it is an isoelectronic mass and size series tuning lattice thermal conductivity rather than a doping axis. The chunk file did not flag an axis because Eu and Yb are not in the same periodic group, but on this site they behave as one; it is recorded here anyway.

basis: Mn0.58Zn0.37Gd(x)Fe(2-x)O4 with x from 0.4 to 1.0, the same Mn-Zn ferrite series as the Er host at rank 1418 with gadolinium in place of erbium; the paper is titled Thermoelectric power studies of gadolinium substituted Mn-Zn-Gd ferrites. AB2O4 cubic spinel, Fd-3m. No reference is offered for this host.
note: Same caveat as rank 1418: Gd(III) is far too large for the octahedral B site of a spinel and its solubility there is a few atomic percent at most, so the nominal x of 0.8 and 1.0 compositions very likely carry a GdFeO3 orthoferrite second phase and are not single-phase spinel. The diffraction pattern in the paper would settle it.

basis: FeV(1-x)Hf(x)Sb with x of 0.2 and 0.3, written both as FeV0.8Hf0.2Sb and Fe(V0.8Hf0.2)Sb. FeVSb is the 18-electron half-Heusler, F-43m, and all three papers say so -- transport and thermoelectric properties of Hf-doped FeVSb half-Heusler, optimizing the thermoelectric performance of FeVSb half-Heusler compounds. No reference is offered for this host.
note: Hafnium sits at 0.2 to 0.3 of the three-atom formula, well above the 5 at.% split, so it is a host constituent and gets no dopant_roles entry. Chemically it is the acceptor: Hf(IV) for V(V) takes the count below 18 electrons and sets the hole concentration, which is what all three papers vary.

basis: In0.4Yb0.6Fe(Zn,Mg)O4 is the m=1 member of the InMO3(ZnO)m homologous series -- the YbFe2O4-type layered structure, with InO6 octahedral layers alternating with trigonal-bipyramidal (Fe,M)O blocks. The paper is Thermal and mechanical properties of Yb and Mg co-doped InFeZnO4, which names the parent. Ytterbium at 0.6 of the In site is a host constituent here rather than a dopant, and it is the natural one: YbFe2O4 is itself the archetype of this structure type. No reference is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn(II) and Mg(II) are both divalent on the tetrahedral-to-bipyramidal M site of the (Fe,M)O block, so exchanging them changes size and mass but not the electron count. In this host Mg dominates that site and Zn is the minor partner; the companion host Fe-In-O-Yb-Zn at rank 1425 is the same series worked from the other end.

note: This host and Fe-In-O-Yb-Zn are one Zn/Mg series from a single paper, split across two host keys only because the 5 at.% cut falls in the middle of it. Confidence is medium because the m of the homologue is inferred from the 1:1:1:4 stoichiometry rather than read off a diffraction pattern, and because Yb on the In site at 0.6 is a large substitution whose single-phase range is not established here.

basis: (In0.8Mo0.05Fe0.15)2O3 is In2O3 with iron and molybdenum on the cation site, so the host is the C-type cubic sesquioxide, bixbyite Ia-3. The paper is about oxygen vacancies, ferromagnetism and transport in bulk Fe-doped In2O3, a dilute magnetic oxide. [ref 2] ranks InFeO3 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-24934 first with 2 ICSD references and In(FeO2)2 R-3m second; I do not follow it. Those are the ordered indium ferrites at 1:1 In:Fe, while this composition is 0.8 indium to 0.15 iron -- iron is a substituent in an In2O3 lattice here, not half the cation content.

dopant_roles.basis: Mo at 0.05 of the cation site. Mo(VI) or Mo(V) on an In(III) site is a donor, and it is the carrier-density knob here alongside the oxygen vacancies the paper studies.

note: Iron at 0.15 of the cation site sits above the 5 at.% split so it is treated as a host element, but chemically it is a dilute substituent. Whether all of it dissolves in the bixbyite lattice or some of it forms an InFeO3 second phase is precisely what the dilute-magnetic-oxide literature argues about, and it cannot be settled from composition -- hence medium rather than high.

basis: In0.4Yb0.6FeZn(1-x)Mg(x)O4 with x from 0 to 0.3, the Zn-rich half of the same series as the Fe-In-Mg-O-Yb host at rank 1423 and from the same paper. The m=1 member of the InMO3(ZnO)m homologous series, the YbFe2O4-type layered structure. No reference is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Mg(II) for Zn(II) on the M site of the (Fe,M)O block; same valence, so the exchange alters size and mass and not the carrier count. Here Zn dominates the site and Mg is the minor partner, the mirror image of rank 1423.

note: One series, two host keys, split only by where the 5 at.% cut lands. Same medium-confidence caveats as rank 1423.

basis: Three compositions are simple ABO3 perovskites with iron and manganese disordered over the B site -- LaFe0.4Mn0.6O3, LaFe0.25Mn0.75O3 and the cathode composition (La0.8Sr0.2)0.95Fe0.6Mn0.3Co0.1O3 -- orthorhombic, GdFeO3-distorted. The fourth, La2FeMnO6, is written as the ordered double perovskite and the paper reporting it is about double perovskites, so B-site ordering is claimed there. Disordered LaFe0.5Mn0.5O3 and ordered La2FeMnO6 are the same composition with and without that ordering, which is exactly the case a single host label cannot carry, so the host is mixed. [ref 2] offers only Sm-containing La-Mn-Fe-O cells at hulls of 0.07 to 0.14, none of which is any of these compositions, so no mp_id is taken.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr(II) for La(III) on the A site of (La0.8Sr0.2)0.95Fe0.6Mn0.3Co0.1O3 is the standard hole doping for manganite and ferrite perovskites, and in that composition it also comes with a deliberate A-site deficiency of 5%.

Co at 0.1 of the B site in the same cathode composition. It is a third B-site transition metal in a deliberately three-component B site rather than a dilute impurity; the paper it comes from screens LaM0.25Mn0.75O3 with M = Fe, Co, Ni, Cu.

note: Whether La2FeMnO6 is genuinely rock-salt ordered or is disordered LaFe0.5Mn0.5O3 written in double-perovskite notation cannot be decided from the formula. Fe(III)/Mn(III) ordering is weak because the charge and size difference is small, so this record needs the diffraction data before the double_perovskite branch is relied on.

basis: Pr0.9Sr0.1Mn(1-x)Fe(x)O3 with x from 0.3 to 0.7 -- an ABO3 perovskite manganite with iron on the B site, orthorhombic and GdFeO3-distorted at this tolerance factor. The paper title says perovskite-type Pr0.9Sr0.1Mn(1-x)Fe(x)O3 outright. No reference is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr(II) for Pr(III) at a fixed 0.1 per formula is the A-site hole-doping variable, held constant while the B site is swept from Mn-rich to Fe-rich. It sets the Mn(IV) fraction and hence the double-exchange conduction.

basis: Sr2FeNbO6 and Sr2FeMo(1-x)Nb(x)O6 are the A2BB-prime O6 rock-salt-ordered double perovskite; the paper is titled Thermoelectric Property of Nb-doped Sr2FeMoO6 Double Perovskite Oxide. [ref 2] agrees on the cell: Sr2NbFeO6 Fm-3m (225) mp-1218741 at hull 0.000, with the P4/mmm variant mp-1218744 at 0.025 as the tetragonally distorted setting of the same ordering.

dopant_roles.basis: Mo at 0.2 to 0.4 of the B-prime site. The paper starts from Sr2FeMoO6 and replaces Mo with Nb, so within this host Mo is the minority partner; Mo(VI)/Mo(V) against Nb(V) sets the electron count on the Fe-O-B-prime network, which is the doping variable.

basis: Fe2Pd2Sb12 is exactly the M4X12 skutterudite stoichiometry with iron and palladium sharing the eight metal sites, and the paper is a synthesis, crystal structure and thermoelectric study of the ternary compound. I record a disagreement with [ref 2] rather than following it: its only entry at this formula is FeSb6Pd C2/m (12) mp-1224896 at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference, a monoclinic ordered cell rather than cubic Im-3. Fe/Pd ordering over the metal sites of a skutterudite cell would lower the symmetry in exactly that way, so the two readings may be the same Sb4-ring framework described at different levels of order, but which one the paper reports cannot be settled from the composition alone.
note: Reference disagreement recorded rather than resolved. The paper title promises a crystal structure, so reading it would settle whether this is cubic Im-3 or the ordered monoclinic variant.

basis: Two compounds, two samples each. Ru(1-x)Fe(x)Sb2 at x of 0.25 and 0.5 is the MX2 marcasite, Pnnm -- FeSb2 is the Kondo-insulating marcasite with the colossal low-temperature thermopower the first paper is about, and RuSb2 is isostructural with it. Ce(Fe3.6Ru0.4)4Sb12 and Ce(Fe3.5Ru0.5)4Sb12 are cerium-filled skutterudites, an entirely different structure at M4Sb12 with a guest in the cage. The host therefore holds two prototypes. No reference is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Cerium fills the icosahedral void of the CoSb3-type cage in Ce(Fe3.6Ru0.4)4Sb12 and Ce(Fe3.5Ru0.5)4Sb12. It is a guest, not a substituent, and its presence is what makes those two compositions filled skutterudites rather than marcasites -- the Fe-rich M4Sb12 framework needs the filler for charge balance.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal site
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Fe/(Fe+Ru). The axis is real within each structure separately -- FeSb2/RuSb2 marcasite at the low-x end, Ce(Fe,Ru)4Sb12 skutterudite at the high-x end -- but it does NOT run continuously across the host, because the two ends of the reported range are different structure types. Stage 3 must split on structure before using this axis.

basis: Fe(1+y)Te(1-x)S(x) throughout, which is the anti-PbO tetragonal P4/nmm layered structure that FeSe and FeTe share; the papers are on Fe1+yTe1-x(Se,S)x and on sintered FeTe1-xSx. [ref 2] offers only Fe4Te3S P4mm (99) mp-1225166 at hull 0.075 and an Amm2 variant at 0.109, both computed ordered supercells with no ICSD backing at a 4:3:1 stoichiometry that none of these samples has; neither is taken.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: x is S/(S+Te). Every composition is Te-rich, so these are S-substituted FeTe and the parent is FeTe throughout; the substitution is isoelectronic on the chalcogen site and acts by chemical pressure.

note: Fe1.06Te carries 6% excess iron on the interstitial site between the layers, which is a non-stoichiometry knob for this family rather than an impurity; it gets no dopant_roles entry because iron is a host element. Pure Fe1+yTe also undergoes a tetragonal-to-monoclinic distortion with its magnetic ordering near 70 K, inside the measured 10-300 K window, but sulfur substitution suppresses and broadens it and three of the four compositions carry 10 at.% S or more, so no single phase sequence covers this host and spans_transition is left false.

basis: Fe2TiSn(1-x)Sb(x), with the same composition written both ways round (TiFe2Sn0.8Sb0.2 and Fe2TiSn0.8Sb0.2). Fe2TiSn is the 24-electron full Heusler, Fm-3m L21, and the papers say so -- Sb-doped TiFe2Sn Heusler, and thermoelectric properties of chemically substituted full-Heusler compounds. No reference is offered for this host.
note: Antimony runs from 0.2 to 0.5 of the Z site, which is 5 to 12.5 at.% of the formula and above the split, so it is treated as a host constituent and gets no dopant_roles entry. Chemically Sb(V) for Sn(IV) is the electron-count variable that moves the Fermi level through the pseudogap, which is what all three papers are doing.

basis: (Ta,Ti,V)FeSb is the 18-electron half-Heusler, F-43m; the paper is titled Discovery of TaFeSb-based half-Heuslers with high thermoelectric performance. Titanium is held at a fixed 0.16 of the Ta site across all four compositions and is the acceptor that sets the hole count. No reference is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: V at 0.05 to 0.15 of the Ta site. Vanadium and tantalum are both group 5, so the exchange is isovalent: it substitutes mass and size without changing the 18-electron count that Ti already sets, which is a lattice-thermal-conductivity move rather than a doping one.

basis: Fe2TiSn(1-x)Si(x) across x = 0.2 to 0.8 -- the same Fe2TiSn full Heusler L21 as the Fe-Sb-Sn-Ti host at rank 1432, with silicon rather than antimony on the main-group Z site. The paper is on the preparation and thermoelectric properties of Fe2TiSn(1-x)Si(x). No reference is offered for this host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: main-group Z site of the L21 full Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Si/(Si+Sn). Both are group 14, so the exchange is isoelectronic and holds the 24-electron count; it tunes the lattice parameter and the position of the pseudogap rather than the carrier count. The range is squarely in the middle, so these are genuine alloys with no single parent compound.

basis: Two structures across four samples. FeTe2 and Fe0.9Co0.1Te2 are the MX2 marcasite, Pnnm, and [ref 2] ranks FeTe2 Pnnm (58) mp-19880 first at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references; the first paper is on sintered Fe(1-x)Co(x)Te2. FeTe and Fe1.04Te are the anti-PbO tetragonal P4/nmm layered phase, [ref 2] FeTe P4/nmm (129) mp-21273 with 4 ICSD references. Two samples each, so the host is mixed; marcasite is taken as primary because it is the ground state of the chemistry and carries the better-attested cell.

other_polymorphs.note: FeTe2 Pa-3 at hull 0.046 with a single ICSD reference against 8 for the Pnnm marcasite. Marcasite and pyrite are the standard polymorph pair for a 3d MX2 dichalcogenide, but the pyrite form of FeTe2 is not what sintering at these temperatures produces, so it is not in the thermal sequence.

dopant_roles.basis: Co at 0.1 for Fe in Fe0.9Co0.1Te2. The paper sweeps x in Fe(1-x)Co(x)Te2, so cobalt is an electron donor on the marcasite metal site and is the carrier-concentration variable.

note: The two structures separate cleanly on the Te:Fe ratio -- 2:1 for the marcasite, 1:1 for the layered phase -- so this host should split on composition in stage 2.

basis: Every stoichiometry here is GenSb2(Te(1-x)Se(x))(n+3) with n = 7 or 12: Ga7Sb2Te5Se5 is n=7 at x=0.5, Ga7Sb2Te8Se2 is n=7 at x=0.2, Ga12Sb2Te7.5Se7.5 is n=12 at x=0.5 and Ga12Sb2Te12Se3 is n=12 at x=0.2. The paper is titled Enhancing the Thermoelectric Properties of Germanium Antimony Tellurides by substitution with selenium in compounds GenSb2(Te1-xSex)n+3. So the element recorded as Ga is Ge -- there is no gallium in this work, and four exact stoichiometric matches on both n and x is not coincidence. I assign the GeTe-Sb2Te3 homologous series and flag the host key itself as wrong rather than inventing a gallium chemistry to fit it.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Se/(Se+Te), which is the same x as in the paper formula GenSb2(Te1-xSex)n+3.

note: DATA ERROR FLAGGED: the host key Ga-Sb-Se-Te should read Ge-Sb-Se-Te, and the four composition strings should have Ge in place of Ga. The key is left exactly as recorded here so the ledger still joins to df_host_systems.parquet, but this should be corrected upstream in the composition parsing. Confidence is medium for that reason, not because the structural call is doubtful. The measured window is 322-725 K; the long-period GST homologues do disorder toward the cubic rocksalt average structure on heating, but the temperature depends on n and on the Se content and no phase sequence is recorded from a composition that carries the wrong element symbol.

basis: Sr3GaSb3 with zinc substituted for gallium. The paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of Sr3GaSb3, a chain-forming Zintl compound, and A3MPn3 built from chains of corner-sharing MPn4 tetrahedra is the Ca3AlSb3 type, Pnma, which is what the taxonomy entry names. No reference is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn at 0.02 to 0.07 of the Ga site, which is inside the anionic (GaSb3) chain rather than on a cation sublattice. Zn(II) for Ga(III) removes one electron from the polyanion and is the carrier-concentration knob of this compound, so it alters the framework electron count -- framework substitution, not simple cation doping.

basis: SmGa2 only, as single crystals, from a paper on transport properties of RGa2 (R = La, Ce, Sm). RGa2 is the AlB2 type, P6/mmm, with graphitic gallium layers and the rare earth between them. [ref 2] agrees: SmGa2 P6/mmm (191) mp-477 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, ranked first.

LaGd(1+x)S3 with x from 0 to 0.03. LnS1.5, that is Ln2S3, is the gamma sesquisulfide, which is the cation-deficient Th3P4 type I-43d -- the same structure as the La(3-x)Te4 thermoelectrics, with vacancies on the cation site setting the carrier count. Excess gadolinium fills those vacancies, which is exactly what the x in LaGd(1+x)S3 does, and that non-stoichiometry only makes sense in the gamma phase. The paper is Preparation and Thermoelectric Properties of LaGd1+xS3 and SmGd1+xS3. No reference is offered for this host.
note: Confidence is medium because the rare-earth sesquisulfides have alpha (Pnma), beta and gamma (Th3P4) forms and which one is obtained depends on the synthesis temperature. The gamma form is the thermoelectrically interesting one and the one the LaGd(1+x)S3 non-stoichiometry argues for, but nothing here confirms it. La and Gd are both host elements, so the cation excess is not recorded in dopant_roles; stage 3 should read it off the parsed fractions as a vacancy filling.

basis: Gd7Pd3 only, as single crystals. R7T3 is the Th7Fe3 type, hexagonal P6_3mc, and that is the standard structure for the rare-earth-rich 7:3 palladides and rhodides this paper studies. [ref 2] carries no Gd7Pd3 entry at all -- it offers GdPd3, GdPd and Gd3Pd2 -- so the reference set misses this phase entirely and no mp_id is taken. That is an absence, not a contradiction.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 63, 127]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Gd7Rh3 only, as single crystals, from the same paper as the Gd7Pd3 host at rank 1440. R7T3 is the Th7Fe3 type, hexagonal P6_3mc. [ref 2] carries no Gd7Rh3 entry -- it offers GdRh, GdRh2 and GdRh3 -- so again the reference set misses the 7:3 phase rather than contradicting it, and no mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 227, 194]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Tl2HgGeTe4 with three separate ultra-dilute dopants. The paper is Tl2AXTe4 (A = Cd, Hg, Mn; X = Ge, Sn): Crystal Structure, Electronic Structure and Thermoelectric Properties, which establishes the family and reports its structure. The A2BCX4 stoichiometry is that of stannite, but the A cation here is Tl(I) with a 6s2 lone pair, far too large for a sphalerite cation site, so filing this under stannite_kesterite would assert a tetrahedral thallium sublattice that is not there. tl2axte4_type is proposed, with stannite_kesterite recorded as the alternative in case the paper shows otherwise. Neither reference offers anything at all for this host.
