dopant_roles.basis: I0.001 written against Te3.999, so iodine takes a tellurium site. A halide on a chalcogen site is a donor, and at one part in four thousand of the formula this is a deliberate n-type carrier-concentration step.
Pb0.001 written against Tl1.999, so lead takes a thallium site. Pb(II) on a Tl(I) site is a donor, the cation-site counterpart of the iodine step.
As0.001 written against Ge0.999, so arsenic takes the germanium site of the framework. Arsenic against Ge(IV) is the aliovalent step on the group-14 site.

note: All three dopants sit at 0.001 per formula unit, one part in a thousand of their site. That is a deliberate carrier-concentration sweep around a very lightly doped narrow-gap semiconductor, not contamination. The proposed prototype carries an unverified space group -- read the crystal structure section of the paper before v4 review.

basis: K8Li(1-2)Ge(43.5-44) and its four-times supercell writing K32Li2Ge175.5. The paper is Synthesis and Thermoelectric Properties of the Clathrate-I Phase K8LixGe46-x, which names the type. That is the type I clathrate, Pm-3n, with a 46-atom sp3 germanium framework per cell and potassium in the two cage types. [ref 2] agrees once the formula is reduced: K4Ge23 Pm-3n (223) mp-27800 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference is K8Ge46 written at half scale, i.e. the type I cell. The K3Ge17 Fd-3m entry mp-1196998 is the type II clathrate and is a different member of the family.

dopant_roles.basis: Lithium replaces germanium in the sp3 framework -- the paper formula is K8LixGe46-x, and 46 minus x is exactly the 43.5 to 44 germanium seen here. It changes the framework electron count rather than filling a cage; potassium is the cage guest and is a host element in this host.

basis: The composition string Ge0.6Pb0.3Sn0.1 carries no chalcogen, and as written it is a ternary of three group-14 metals that are not mutually soluble. Two things say the tellurium was lost in curation rather than absent from the sample. First, the measurement runs to 773 K, well above the melting points of tin (505 K) and lead (601 K), which no elemental Ge-Pb-Sn compact would survive. Second, (Ge0.6Pb0.3Sn0.1)Te is a known spark-plasma-sintered pseudoternary telluride and the parenthesised composition in the paper title is the notation that family uses. Read that way the host is GeTe-rich, so rhombohedral R3m at room temperature with a PbTe-rich cubic phase alongside it -- hence mixed. No reference is offered for this host.
note: Needs the paper. Confidence is low because an element is missing from the record, not because the chemistry is obscure. If the telluride reading is right, the rhombohedral-to-cubic transition of a GeTe-rich pseudoternary falls somewhere inside the measured 323-773 K window, but it moves strongly with Pb and Sn content and no phase sequence is recorded from a composition string that is missing an element. If the reading is wrong and these really are Ge-Pb-Sn metal compacts, the right label is composite_multiphase, which is why it is listed as an alternative.

basis: Y3Ru4Ge13 with cobalt substituted for ruthenium. R3T4X13 is the Remeika phase, cubic Pm-3n, and [ref 2] agrees: Y3Ge13Ru4 Pm-3n (223) mp-704462 at hull 0.023 with 2 ICSD references. The paper is Thermoelectric properties of rare earth-ruthenium-germanium compounds. The other [ref 2] entries -- Y(GeRu)2 I4/mmm and Y2Ge5Ru3 Ibam -- are other line compounds of the system at different stoichiometries.

dopant_roles.basis: Co at 0.4 to 0.8 of the four ruthenium sites in Y3Ru(4-x)Co(x)Ge13. Cobalt and ruthenium are both group 9, so the substitution is nominally isovalent and works through mass contrast and cage size on the rattling germanium sublattice rather than through the carrier count. At x = 0.8 it is an alloying level rather than dilute doping.

basis: Sn(1-x)Ge(x)Se across x = 0.1 to 0.8, plus one Ag-doped member. Both SnSe and GeSe are the layered GeS (herzenbergite) type, orthorhombic Pnma, so the whole series is one structure and the papers -- Giant Seebeck effect in Ge-doped SnSe, and Thermoelectric properties of GeSe -- sit at the two ends of it. [ref 2] offers only SnGeSe2 Pmc2_1 (26) mp-1218835 at hull 0.009 with no ICSD reference, a computed ordered 1:1 cell; the real materials are disordered solid solutions of the Pnma parent, so it is not taken.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag0.01 in Ge0.79Ag0.01Sn0.2Se. Ag(I) on the divalent group-14 cation site is an acceptor and is the standard p-type dopant for the SnSe and GeSe family.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Ge/(Ge+Sn). Both are divalent group-14 lone-pair cations on the same site, so the exchange is isoelectronic; the parent is SnSe at the low-x end and GeSe at the high-x end, with no single parent for the host.

note: The measured window tops out at 701 K, below the roughly 800 K Pnma-to-Cmcm transition of SnSe, and germanium alloying raises that temperature further, so no transition is crossed and spans_transition is false.

basis: Mg2NiH at 0.7, 1.3, 3.5 and 4. Mg2NiH4 is not an interstitial hydride: it is a salt of discrete tetrahedral [NiH4](4-) anions and Mg(2+) cations, monoclinic C2/c at room temperature, with the metal-metal bonding gone and a wide gap. [ref 2] ranks it first -- Mg2NiH4 C2/c (15) mp-697331 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references. Mg2NiH0.7 is the other thing entirely: the alpha solid solution of hydrogen in the Mg2Ni intermetallic, where hydrogen genuinely does sit interstitially, and Mg2NiH1.3 lies in the alpha-plus-beta two-phase field. The existing taxonomy entry interstitial_hydride (exemplar PdH0.66, described as rocksalt-derived MHx) covers only the dilute end, so complex_hydride_mg2nih4 is proposed for the beta phase and the host is recorded as mixed.
note: The hydrogen content separates the two structures cleanly -- H below about 1 is alpha, H near 4 is beta -- so this host should split on composition in stage 2, with Mg2NiH1.3 flagged as two-phase rather than forced to either. Mg2NiH4 also has a well-known order-disorder transition near 510 K to a cubic high-temperature form; no measured temperature range is printed for this host, so whether the measurement crosses it cannot be judged here and spans_transition is left false.

basis: Tl2HgSnTe4 with three ultra-dilute dopants, the tin member of the same Tl2AXTe4 family as the Ge-Hg-Te-Tl host at rank 1442 and from the same paper. Same reasoning: A2BCX4 stoichiometry, but Tl(I) is a 6s2 lone-pair cation that cannot sit on a sphalerite cation site, so stannite_kesterite would assert a framework that is not there and is recorded as the alternative instead. Neither reference offers anything for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: I0.001 written against Te3.999, so iodine takes a tellurium site; a halide on a chalcogen site is a donor.
Pb0.001 written against Tl1.999, so lead takes a thallium site. Pb(II) on a Tl(I) site is a donor.

Ga0.001 is written against Te3.999, which as recorded would put gallium on the anion site. That is not chemically sensible for Ga(III), and the far more likely reading is an acceptor on the Sn(IV) site of the framework. Recorded as such, with the discrepancy noted rather than copied.

note: The gallium composition string is internally inconsistent -- it reduces tellurium to balance a cation-forming element -- so the substitution site given here is inference, not transcription. The proposed prototype also carries an unverified space group; read the crystal structure section of the paper before v4 review.

basis: HgTe in three samples plus HgS0.045Te0.955. The ambient structure of HgTe is cubic zincblende, F-43m, and [ref 2] ranks it first at hull 0.000 with 28 ICSD references, mp-2730. I depart from the project precedence here and do not follow [ref 1]: TEDesignLab offers only HgTe P3_121 (152) mp-358 and P3_221 (154) mp-1071269, which are the trigonal cinnabar polymorph, with 3 and 1 ICSD references. Cinnabar HgTe is the high-pressure phase, formed above roughly 1.4 GPa, and no ambient-pressure Seebeck measurement from 91 to 397 K is made on it. Twenty-eight ICSD references for zincblende against three for cinnabar says the same thing.

other_polymorphs.note: HgTe Fm-3m at hull 0.153 with 5 ICSD references; the second high-pressure phase, above the cinnabar field. Not reached by heating at ambient pressure.

dopant_roles.basis: S at 0.045 of the anion site in HgS(x)Te(1-x). The paper is on HgSxTe1-x solid solutions, so this is the dilute end of an isoelectronic anion series: it widens the gap of the semimetal without adding carriers, which is the point of the work.

note: There is no taxonomy id for the cinnabar HgS structure type, so the two [ref 1] trigonal polymorphs are argued about in the basis rather than listed in other_polymorphs, where they would need one. A cinnabar entry is worth adding at v4 review -- it is the ambient form of HgS and the high-pressure form of both HgSe and HgTe.

basis: Mo3Sb7 with iodine substituted for antimony at 0.75 to 1.5 per formula. Mo3Sb7 is the Ir3Ge7 type, Im-3m, which is precisely what this taxonomy entry names -- Mo3Sb7 is its exemplar and its only representative material. The paper is Beneficial influence of iodine substitution on the thermoelectric properties of Mo3Sb7. No reference is offered for this host.
note: Iodine runs from 7 to 13 at.% of the formula, above the 5 at.% split, so it is treated as a host constituent and gets no dopant_roles entry. Chemically it is an electron donor on the antimony site and is the carrier-concentration variable of the paper: Mo3Sb7 is two electrons short of a filled band, and iodine substitution is one of the ways that deficit is made up.

basis: InN in four film samples. The ambient structure of indium nitride is wurtzite P6_3mc and [ref 2] ranks it first, mp-22205 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references. The second paper is about In-polarity versus N-polarity, which is a property only a wurtzite film has -- the polar c axis is the whole subject -- so the papers themselves confirm the prototype.

other_polymorphs.note: InN Fm-3m at hull 0.210 with 2 ICSD references. The wurtzite-to-rocksalt transition of InN is near 12 GPa, and the first paper -- pressure cycling of InN to 20 GPa with in situ transport -- goes through it deliberately. The transport reported at ambient is still the wurtzite phase, so this is recorded here rather than in phases.
InN F-43m at hull 0.010 with 5 ICSD references. Reachable only by epitaxy on a cubic substrate, never by heating.

note: The measured window is 16-573 K and crosses nothing at ambient pressure. The transition this host does cross is a pressure one, which the ledger has no field for; it is recorded in other_polymorphs with the paper named so it is not lost.

basis: All four compositions are M2O3 once the cations are added up -- In1.2Ni0.4Sn0.4O3, InNi0.5Sn0.5O3, In1.4Ni0.3Sn0.3O3 and In0.9Ni0.55Sn0.55O3 each carry exactly 2.0 cations per 3 oxygen -- so this is the cubic C-type sesquioxide, bixbyite Ia-3, which is the structure of In2O3. The paper is enhancement of the thermoelectric performance of In2O3 by a coupled substitution, and the Ni:Sn ratio is held at 1:1 throughout, which is the signature of a charge-compensated pair: Ni(II) plus Sn(IV) averages the In(III) it replaces, so the lattice stays a sesquioxide at every composition. Neither reference offers anything for this host.
note: Nickel and tin run from 15 to 27 at.% of the cations, far above the 5 at.% split, so neither gets a dopant_roles entry even though both are substitutional on the indium site. At the In0.9Ni0.55Sn0.55O3 end this is a genuine ternary oxide rather than doped In2O3, and whether the bixbyite solubility limit is actually reached is a question for the paper. Stage 2 should watch for a second phase at the high-substitution end.

basis: Four compositions of the form In12Ti10(Al,Ga)2(Mg,Zn)O42 from a phase-stability and dielectrics study of a quaternary oxide system. The arithmetic is clean and the identification is not. Charge balances exactly with In(III), Ti(IV), Al(III) or Ga(III) and Mg(II) or Zn(II): 36 plus 40 plus 6 plus 2 is 84, against 84 for O42. The cation-to-oxygen ratio is 25:42, an O:M of 1.68, which sits between bixbyite In2O3 at 1.50 and fluorite at 2.00 and within rounding of M3O5 at 1.667. It also decomposes exactly as seven (In,Al)2TiO5 plus four (Ti,Mg)O2, which reads as an A2BO5 titanate with excess rutile. I cannot choose between those readings from a composition string: In2TiO5 has its own orthorhombic structure type that is not in this taxonomy, pseudobrookite M3O5 is proposed in this chunk and would fit the ratio, and a paper reporting phase stability and microstructure in a four-component oxide system may simply have made multiphase ceramics. Neither reference offers anything at all for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Al(III) for In(III) on the trivalent site, paired one-for-one with Ga in the sister compositions. Isovalent, so it is a size and field-strength substitution rather than a carrier one.
The other member of the Al or Ga pair, same trivalent site, same reasoning.
Mg(II) on the tetravalent site, paired with Zn in the sister compositions. The oxygen count of the formula only balances if this is where it sits.
The other member of the Mg or Zn pair, same site, same reasoning.

note: Filed as unresolved_crystalline deliberately rather than forced to a prototype. The 2x2 design -- Al or Ga against Mg or Zn on a fixed In12Ti10 backbone -- is a dielectrics study varying two sites independently, and the paper will name the phase in its first figure. This host is cheap to settle by reading and should be near the top of the review queue.

basis: Two of the four compositions are In4(Se,Te)3 -- In4Se0.5Te2.5 and In4(Se0.83Te0.17)3 -- which is the layered Pnnm In4Se3 Zintl phase with tellurium on the chalcogen site, and two of the three papers are explicitly on In4Se3-xTex and on spark-plasma-sintered In4Se3-In4Te3. The other two compositions are In2(Te0.90Se0.10)5, which is In2Te5 and a different compound entirely -- a layered indium polytelluride, not an In4X3 framework -- so the host holds two structures and is recorded as mixed. The taxonomy has no In2Te5 entry, so the alternative is recorded as unresolved_crystalline rather than forced onto a neighbour. Neither reference offers anything for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.05 written against In1.95 in Fe0.05In1.95(Te0.90Se0.10)5, so iron takes an indium site of the In2Te5 member. The paper is about tailoring at the In and Te sites together, so this is a deliberate cation-site substitution rather than contamination.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Se/(Se+Te). Both are group-16 anions on the same chalcogen site in both structures present, so the exchange is isoelectronic. There is no single parent: the In4X3 members run from In4Se3 at high x to In4Te3 at low x, and the In2Te5 members sit at the tellurium-rich end with a little selenium. The split itself is on the composition, not on this host.

note: The In4X3 and In2X5 compositions must be separated in stage 2; the In:chalcogen ratio does it cleanly, 4:3 against 2:5. An In2Te5 entry is worth adding at v4 review.

basis: Na3Ir3O8 and Na3.6Ir3O8 measured on single crystals, with the paper on thermal conductivity across the metal-insulator transition. These are sodium-deficient Na4Ir3O8, the hyperkagome iridate: a B-site ordered spinel in which sodium and iridium share the octahedral sublattice one-to-one, leaving the iridium on a three-dimensional net of corner-sharing triangles. Sodium content is the variable that drives the metal-insulator transition the paper measures across, which is why both compositions sit below Na4. No taxonomy entry existed, so na4ir3o8_hyperkagome is proposed in this chunk. I disagree with [ref 2] here: it offers Na2IrO3 C2/m, Na4IrO4 I4/m and NaIrO3 Cmcm, each on a single ICSD reference and none at this stoichiometry, so it is describing other compounds of the chemistry rather than this one.
note: Sodium runs from 3.0 to 3.6 per three iridium, well above the 5 at.% split, so it takes no dopant_roles entry; chemically it is the carrier-concentration knob, exactly as the O content is in YBa2Cu3O6+delta. Measured 11-291 K, so any transition here is electronic rather than structural and spans_transition stays false.

basis: ZrNiSn with iridium added, at close to the 1:1:1 ratio in every composition -- Zr30.1Ni27.4Ir11.5Sn31.1 and its neighbours are ZrNiSn with iridium at 6 to 12 at.%, and the fourth is written ZrNiIr0.2Sn outright. Both papers name the family: vacancy site occupation by Co and Ir in half-Heusler ZrNiSn, and ordered structures and thermoelectric properties of MNiSn. The half-Heusler F-43m cell has an empty 4d site, and the first paper is precisely about iridium going into it, which converts the structure locally towards the full Heusler. Neither reference offers anything for this host.
note: Iridium is above the 5 at.% split in all four compositions so it gets no dopant_roles entry, but its role is the point of the work: it occupies the vacant 4d interstitial site of the half-Heusler cell rather than substituting on the Ni or Zr sublattice. If stage 2 needs a site label this is the case to record it for. full_heusler is listed as the alternative because at high enough iridium filling the distinction stops being clean.

basis: A single composition, Ir0.71V0.29O2. IrO2 and VO2 are both rutile dioxides and they form a substitutional solid solution on the cation site, so an iridium-rich member is rutile P4_2/mnm throughout. I do not follow [ref 2] here: its only entry for this host is VIrO3 Pm-3m mp-972116 at hull 1.228 with no ICSD reference, a computed cubic perovskite more than an electronvolt per atom above the hull, which is not a real phase and is not the measured stoichiometry either.
note: Vanadium is 29 per cent of the cations, which is 9.7 at.% of the formula and above the 5 at.% split, so it takes no dopant_roles entry. spans_transition is false but the reason is worth stating: pure VO2 undergoes the monoclinic-to-rutile transition at 340 K, inside the 19-323 K measured window, and vo2_monoclinic would be the right label at the vanadium-rich end of this line. At 71 per cent iridium the transition is suppressed and the rutile phase is stable to the lowest temperature, which is what makes the enhanced correlation the paper reports measurable at all.

basis: A single composition, Ru0.8Ir0.2Se2, and the paper is on enhanced thermoelectric power and electronic correlations in RuSe2. RuSe2 is a pyrite-type diselenide, cubic Pa-3, with Se2 dumbbells and octahedral ruthenium; IrSe2 substitution on the metal site keeps that framework. Neither reference offers anything for this host.
note: Iridium is 6.7 at.% of the formula, just above the 5 at.% split, so it takes no dopant_roles entry; it is a substitutional hole dopant on the ruthenium site and at 20 per cent of that site it is an alloying level rather than dilute doping. marcasite is recorded as the alternative only because it is the orthorhombic polymorph of the same MX2 chemistry; nothing here suggests it, and there is no reference for this host either way.

basis: The composition strings K1Ni4, K1Ni5, K1Ni10 and K1Ni14 carry no carbon and no sulfur, which no real potassium-nickel binary does either, and the paper is Boosting the Seebeck Coefficient for Organic Coordination Polymers. These are poly(nickel-ethenetetrathiolate) samples: a metal-dithiolene coordination polymer in which nickel is chelated by tetrathiolate ligands and potassium is the counter-ion that sets the redox level. The K:Ni ratio is therefore the doping variable and the strings are what is left after the organic ligand was lost in parsing. organic_polymer is the taxonomy entry for semicrystalline and non-crystalline polymeric conductors and is the honest label; poly(Ni-ett) is poorly crystalline and is not solved as a three-dimensional structure. Neither reference offers anything for this host, which is itself consistent with the compound not being a binary.

dopant_roles.basis: Potassium is real and is the counter-ion, but its apparent stoichiometry here is meaningless because the carbon and sulfur of the ligand are missing from the string, so the ratio is computed against nickel alone. The chemically meaningful quantity is potassium per nickel-dithiolene repeat unit, which the paper gives and this record cannot.

note: conductive_mof_2d is listed as the alternative because poly(Ni-ett) is a coordination polymer and could reasonably be filed with the two-dimensional conductive frameworks. I did not choose it because that entry is for crystalline porous hexagonal frameworks such as Ni3(HITP)2, and poly(Ni-ett) is a one- to two-dimensional ladder polymer with no pores and no solved framework. This host cannot be resolved further without the paper.

basis: La3LiMn4O12 is (La0.75Li0.25)MnO3 written over four formula units: four A cations, four B cations, twelve oxygen. That is a lithium-substituted lanthanum manganite, and the substitution is a standard way of setting the Mn(III)/Mn(IV) ratio -- three lanthanum at 3+ plus one lithium at 1+ gives an average A charge of 2.5, so manganese sits at 3.5+ -- which is exactly the mixed-valence condition of the colossal-magnetoresistance manganites. The paper title, on bismuth doping of La-Li-Mn-O manganites, uses the word manganite. I depart from [ref 2] here: it offers LiLa2Mn3O9, LiLa3MnO7, LiLa4MnO8 and LiLa6Mn3O14, none of which is at the measured 3:1:4:12 stoichiometry and none of which carries an ICSD reference, so it is listing computed phases of the chemistry rather than the compound made.
note: Lithium is 5 per cent of the atoms in the formula and sits on the A site; it is a host constituent at this level rather than a dopant, and the dopant the paper actually studies -- bismuth -- does not appear in any composition string for this host, so the four samples here are presumably the undoped reference. Measured 10-400 K. Manganites of this family are rhombohedral R-3c or orthorhombic Pnma depending on tolerance factor and oxygen content; which one applies needs the paper, so no space group is asserted.

basis: All three compositions are (RE0.7Sr0.3)MnO3 with the rare-earth site shared between lanthanum and neodymium -- (La0.5Nd0.5)0.7Sr0.3MnO3, Nd0.4La0.3Sr0.3MnO3 and La0.35Nd0.35Sr0.3MnO3 are the same thing written three ways. This is the canonical hole-doped manganite at x = 0.3, the composition with the highest Curie temperature and the strongest magnetoresistance, and the first paper is on A-site cation disorder, which is exactly what mixing two rare earths of different size on one site produces. Neither reference offers anything for this host.
note: Nothing here is below the 5 at.% split, so dopant_roles is empty; strontium at 30 per cent of the A site is the doping variable of the family and lanthanum against neodymium is an isoelectronic exchange on the same site used to tune the A-site radius and its variance. Measured 27-373 K, which brackets the ferromagnetic-metal to paramagnetic-insulator transition near 300-360 K for this composition. That is a magnetic and electronic transition accompanied at most by a small structural distortion, not a change of prototype, so spans_transition is false.

basis: LaRuO3 and LaRu1-xCrxO3 at x = 0.02, 0.05 and 0.10. LaRuO3 is an orthorhombic GdFeO3-distorted perovskite and [ref 2] carries it directly, LaRuO3 Pnma (62) mp-20472 at hull 0.048 with one ICSD reference. The other [ref 2] entries -- La2RuO5, La3RuO7, La3Ru3O11 -- are the neighbouring line compounds of the La-Ru-O system at other stoichiometries, not polymorphs of this one. The papers are on rare-earth ruthenates and on Ru-doped material, and the ABO3 stoichiometry is unambiguous in every composition.

dopant_roles.site: B site
dopant_roles.basis: Cr is written against Ru in LaRu1-xCrxO3, so it takes the octahedral B site. Cr(III) for Ru(III) is nominally isovalent, so the effect is on bandwidth and on the 4d-3d exchange rather than on carrier count; at x = 0.10 it is an alloying level rather than dilute doping.

note: Measured 345-1273 K, a wide high-temperature window. Ruthenate perovskites lose oxygen and can decompose at the top of that range in air, so the high-temperature data may not be on the same phase as the low-temperature data; that is a sample question for the paper rather than a phase transition of the prototype, and spans_transition is left false.

basis: A single composition, LaRu4Sb12, which is the filled skutterudite exactly: a Ru4Sb12 framework of corner-shared octahedra with lanthanum rattling in the icosahedral void, cubic Im-3. [ref 2] agrees, La(Sb3Ru)4 Im-3 (204) mp-1188603 at hull 0.000, and the second paper is titled transport properties in the filled-skutterudite compounds RERu4Sb12. The third paper, on CeRu4Sb12, is the cerium member of the same series.
note: Lanthanum is 5.9 at.% of the formula, just above the split, so it takes no dopant_roles entry even though its role is the defining one for this prototype: it is a cage filler in the icosahedral void, not a substituent, and its rattling is what the first paper measures. skutterudite is recorded as the alternative because the filled and unfilled entries describe the same framework; the void here is occupied, so the filled entry is correct. Measured 10-292 K, no structural transition.

basis: La3-xTe4 with ytterbium substituted for lanthanum, which is what the paper says in its title: optimizing thermoelectric efficiency in La3-xTe4 via Yb substitution. La3-xTe4 is the Th3P4 type, cubic I-43d, and the cation vacancies on that lattice are the carrier-concentration knob -- La3Te4 is metallic and La2.67Te4 is a semiconductor, with everything useful in between. The compositions bear this out: La2.2Yb0.52Te4 and La1.58Yb1.63Te4 are both cation-deficient against the 3:4 ideal, and Yb0.079La0.348Te0.574 and Yb0.086La0.34Te0.574 are the same thing normalised to one. Neither reference offers anything for this host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: x is La/(La+Yb). Both are rare earths on the single Th3P4 cation site, but the exchange is NOT isoelectronic in the way the generic axis label implies: lanthanum is trivalent throughout while ytterbium is divalent or mixed-valent, so substituting Yb for La removes electrons as well as changing the mass and size. That is the point of the paper -- it is a second carrier knob alongside the vacancy concentration -- and it means the two ends of this axis are not two parent compounds of the same kind.

note: Both ytterbium and lanthanum are well above the 5 at.% split, so dopant_roles is empty; the chemistry that matters here is recorded in solid_solution_axis and in the basis instead. Measured 296-1264 K with no structural transition in Th3P4 rare-earth tellurides over that range.

basis: The composition string is Li20, and I read that as Li2O with the oxygen misread as a zero, not as twenty lithium atoms. Three things say so. The measured range is 463-1163 K, and lithium metal melts at 454 K, so a lithium-metal sample would be molten over the entire window and no thermal diffusivity of a porous solid could be measured on it. The paper is a 1980 Journal of Nuclear Materials study of the porosity dependence of thermal diffusivity and thermal conductivity, which is the standard characterisation done on sintered ceramic pellets -- and Li2O is the classic lithium-ceramic tritium breeder material that such studies were done on. And a bare Li20 stoichiometry is not a compound at all. Li2O is the antifluorite structure, Fm-3m, with lithium in the tetrahedral sites of an fcc oxygen lattice. I therefore disagree with [ref 2], which lists five polymorphs of elemental lithium: it is answering the host key it was given, and the host key is wrong.
note: Confidence is medium because the reading corrects the composition string rather than following it. If the string really is elemental lithium then solid_solution_alloy is the right label -- bcc Im-3m, mp-135, 13 ICSD references -- and the record should be swapped, but the melting point makes that reading hard to sustain against the printed temperature range. This host should be checked against the paper, and if the reading holds, the composition parser should be looked at for other O-as-zero cases: the host key would need to become Li-O and this record would move with it.

basis: A single composition, LuNiSb, at 1:1:1. [ref 2] ranks LuNiSb F-43m (216) mp-20185 first at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which is the half-Heusler cell, and all three papers name the family -- high-temperature power factor of half-Heusler phases RENiSb, effect of secondary LuNiSn phase on half-Heusler, and thermoelectric performance of the half-Heusler phases. The other [ref 2] entry, Lu5Ni2Sb I4/mcm, is a different line compound of the system.
note: One of the papers is specifically about a secondary LuNiSn phase in these samples, so a second phase is present by the authors own account even though the composition string is clean. That is a sample-purity matter rather than a second prototype for the host, so is_mixed stays false, but stage 2 should expect a two-phase microstructure. Measured 11-994 K with no structural transition; half-Heuslers are stable to well above that.

basis: Three of the four compositions are MgTi2O5, twice as a deliberate composite with TiN -- MgTi2O5(TiN)0.359 and MgTi2.67O6.34(TiN)0.455 -- and once bare. MgTi2O5 is karrooite, the magnesium end of the pseudobrookite M3O5 family, and [ref 2] confirms the cell: MgTi2O5 Cmcm (63) mp-28232 at hull 0.000. The taxonomy had no pseudobrookite entry, so pseudobrookite_m3o5 is proposed in this chunk. The fourth composition, Ti0.73Mg0.27O, is a different material altogether -- magnesium-substituted titanium monoxide, a rocksalt -- from the second paper, on Mg-doping enhanced superconductivity and ferromagnetism in Ti1-xMgxO, so the host is mixed. I do not follow [ref 1]: TEDesignLab offers MgTiO3 R-3 (148) mp-3771 with 30 ICSD references as the primary, and that is geikielite, the ilmenite titanate, which is neither of the compounds measured here. It is the best-attested phase in the chemistry, not the phase in these samples.

dopant_roles.basis: Nitrogen appears only as the TiN of MgTi2O5/TiN composites and is a deliberate conductive second phase, not a dopant on the oxide lattice and not milling residue. The taxonomy warns that composite additives must not be allowed to relabel their host, and that applies here: the host prototype is the pseudobrookite matrix, with TiN recorded as what it is.

note: Three prototypes touch this host and the compositions separate them cleanly: MgTi2O5 by its 3:5 cation-to-oxygen ratio, the TiN second phase by the presence of nitrogen, and Ti0.73Mg0.27O by its 1:1 ratio. Split on composition in stage 2. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the primary label is a prototype proposed in this same chunk and its space group, although reference-backed for MgTi2O5, has not been checked against a structure file here. Measured 11-973 K; pseudobrookite is cation-disordered and the degree of order is quench-dependent, but no change of prototype occurs in that window.

basis: Three of the four compositions are Mg2Si0.7Sr0.3, Mg2Si0.8Sr0.2 and Mg2Si0.75Sr0.25, from a paper on high-performance p-type magnesium silicon thermoelectrics. Mg2Si is the antifluorite, Fm-3m, and those three read as the Mg2Si parent with a second element on the silicon site. But I doubt the element is strontium. Mg2Si0.7Sn0.3, Mg2Si0.8Sn0.2 and Mg2Si0.75Sn0.25 are the standard Mg2Si-Mg2Sn solid solutions and are among the most studied thermoelectric compositions there are, whereas 10 to 13 at.% strontium on the silicon site of Mg2Si has no solubility basis at all -- Sr is a large divalent cation and cannot sit on an anionic silicon site. An Sn-read-as-Sr transcription explains all three at once. The assignment is robust to which reading is right, because Mg2Si, Mg2Sn and the whole solid solution between them are the same antifluorite structure. The fourth composition, Sr2Mg4Si3, is genuinely strontium-bearing and comes from the other paper, on hexagonal A-Mg-Si Zintl phases with A = Sr and Ba, so it is a different structure and the host is recorded as mixed.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: uncertain
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Mg/(Mg+Sr) as computed by the pipeline. I do not think this is a real substitution axis. Magnesium and strontium are both group 2 but they do not share a site in either structure present: in Mg2Si magnesium is the tetrahedral cation and there is no strontium site at all, and in the hexagonal Sr-Mg-Si Zintl phase strontium is the large electropositive cation outside a magnesium-silicon polyanion. The axis is an artefact of pooling two papers into one host, compounded by the probable Sn-for-Sr transcription.

note: Confidence is low because the dominant reading requires correcting the composition string. The alternatives are the two candidate structures for the real strontium phase: caal2si2_zintl if it is the trigonal AMg2Si2, which is what hexagonal A-Mg-Si usually means, and tinisi_co2si because [ref 1] attests SrMgSi Pnma (62) mp-15642 with 2 ICSD references at a different stoichiometry. Sr2Mg4Si3 matches neither exactly and was not identified here. Read both papers before stage 2 splits this host.

basis: The composition string says it outright: Tb8.7Mg34.6Zn56.8_IQC, where IQC is icosahedral quasicrystal. Both papers are on R-Mg-Zn icosahedral quasicrystals grown from the ternary melt, and the second measures magnetic and transport properties of single-grain specimens. R-Mg-Zn with R a heavy rare earth is one of the best-established stable face-centred icosahedral systems. There is no periodic structure to assign, so this entry is the correct one and stage 2 must map it to an approximant and say which. I note that [ref 2] offers TbMgZn2 Fm-3m mp-1187349 with no ICSD reference: that is a computed Laves-type line compound, not the quasicrystal, and it is not what was measured.

dopant_roles.basis: Y1.08 against Tb7.92 in Y1.08Tb7.92Mg42Zn57, and the curator note records the series as (Y1-xTbx)-Mg-Zn. Yttrium and terbium are both trivalent and nearly the same size, so the substitution changes the magnetic moment on the rare-earth site while leaving the quasilattice alone -- which is the experiment, since Y-Mg-Zn is the non-magnetic reference for the Tb-Mg-Zn magnetism.

note: Measured 10-297 K. No transition of prototype; the transitions of interest in this system are the spin-glass freezing of the rare-earth moments, which is magnetic rather than structural.

basis: TiNiSn with manganese on the titanium site. Three compositions are written explicitly that way -- Ti0.967Mn0.163Ni0.98Sn1.04, Ti0.984Mn0.19Ni1.01Sn1.013 and Ti0.855Mn0.20Ni1.06Sn0.98, all close to 1:1:1 once Ti and Mn are added together -- and the fourth, Ti6.2Ni33.9Mn36.4Sn30.9Bi0.4, is the same family at high manganese in atomic per cent. Both papers name it: thermoelectric behaviour of p- and n-type Ti-Ni-Sn half Heusler alloys, and optimized thermoelectric performance of the n-type half-Heusler material. Manganese on the Ti site is the standard route to p-type in this family. I disagree with [ref 2], whose only entry is TiMn(Ni2Sn)2 R-3m mp-1217085 at hull 0.044 with no ICSD reference: that is a computed rhombohedral ordering of a full-Heusler-like cell, not the cubic half-Heusler these papers make.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi0.4 in Ti6.2Ni33.9Mn36.4Sn30.9Bi0.4, 0.4 at.% and written next to tin, so it takes the main-group site. Bismuth has one more valence electron than tin, so on that site it is a donor and is the standard n-type dopant for MNiSn half-Heuslers.

note: Nickel runs slightly above one per formula unit in three of the four compositions, up to Ni1.06. In this family excess nickel occupies the vacant 4d interstitial site of the half-Heusler cell, producing local full-Heusler regions and in-gap states, and that is a known and deliberate feature of Ti-Ni-Sn rather than a weighing error. It is not recorded in dopant_roles because nickel is a host element, but stage 2 should carry it. full_heusler is the alternative for the same reason.

basis: Pr0.67Pb0.33MnO3 and Pr0.7Pb0.3MnO3, plus one lanthanum-substituted member. ABO3 exactly, with the A site shared between trivalent praseodymium and divalent lead at close to the x = 1/3 that gives the mixed Mn(III)/Mn(IV) valence of the colossal-magnetoresistance manganites. The first paper is thermopower studies of the Pr0.67D0.33MnO3 manganite system, where D is the divalent A-site cation, and the second is on magnetoresistive oxides. Lead-substituted praseodymium manganite is a standard member of the family. I note that [ref 2] offers only Pr3Mn4PbO12 Pm (6) mp-1220019 at hull 0.023 with no ICSD reference -- a computed cation-ordered supercell of the same chemistry at 3:1 rather than 2:1 on the A site. It does not contradict the perovskite assignment so much as refine the cation ordering, which these disordered samples will not have.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: La0.2 against Pr0.5 in La0.2Pr0.5Pb0.3MnO3, 4 at.% of the formula. Lanthanum and praseodymium are both trivalent rare earths on the twelve-coordinate A site, so the exchange does not change the manganese valence; it raises the average A-site radius and so the tolerance factor and the Curie temperature. That is A-site radius engineering, not doping.

note: Measured 42-299 K, which spans the ferromagnetic-metal to paramagnetic-insulator transition of this composition near 200-260 K. That transition is electronic and magnetic and carries at most a small distortion within the same perovskite prototype, so spans_transition is false and no phases are recorded.

basis: Four compositions written as (SnTe)y(MnO2)1-y with the MnO2 fraction running from 14.5 to 25.4 mol per cent, from a paper on a facile route to high-performance SnTe-based thermoelectric materials. SnTe is the rocksalt and it is the matrix in every sample, so the host prototype is rocksalt. MnO2 is a separate oxide, not a solute: in this chemistry it reacts during processing, manganese enters the SnTe cation site while the oxygen leaves as a tin oxide, so what is measured is a doped rocksalt with an oxide second phase rather than a single quaternary compound. The host is therefore recorded as mixed. [ref 2] offers only Mn3Sn3(TeO8)2 Cm mp-772482 at hull 0.060 with no ICSD reference, a computed tellurite, which is not a phase anyone makes by sintering SnTe with MnO2.
note: Answering the CHECK marker the chunk prints on the O/(O+Te) axis: no, oxygen and tellurium do not share a site here, and this is not a substitution axis. Tellurium is the anion of the rocksalt matrix and oxygen belongs to the MnO2 additive; the two are in different phases, not on different sites of one phase. The axis figure of 0.25 to 0.40 is an artefact of the additive fraction and should not be read as a solid-solution composition, which is why solid_solution_axis is left null. rutile is listed as an alternative because beta-MnO2 is rutile-structured; whether any MnO2 survives sintering unreacted is a question for the paper. Measured 300-874 K. SnTe has no structural transition in that window -- its rhombohedral distortion occurs below about 100 K and is suppressed by the high intrinsic hole concentration anyway.

basis: TbMnO3 and three aluminium-substituted members. TbMnO3 is the orthorhombic Pnma perovskite -- the well-known type-II multiferroic -- and [ref 2] ranks it first, TbMnO3 Pnma (62) mp-25030 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references. The other [ref 2] entries, TbMn2O5 Pbam and Tb2Mn2O7 Fd-3m, are the neighbouring manganite line compounds at other stoichiometries, not polymorphs. The paper is on the effect of Al-doping on the electrical and thermoelectric response, and every composition keeps the ABO3 ratio.

dopant_roles.site: A site as written; probably the B site in fact
dopant_roles.basis: The compositions are written Tb1-xAlxMnO3 with x = 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20, which puts aluminium on the twelve-coordinate A site. I record the site as written but do not believe it: Al(III) has an ionic radius of about 0.54 Angstrom in six-fold coordination and is one of the smallest trivalent cations there is, while the A site of a rare-earth manganite hosts Tb(III) at about 1.04 Angstrom in eight-fold coordination. Aluminium is far too small for that site. The chemically sensible outcomes are aluminium on the octahedral Mn site, which is isovalent and common, or aluminium exsolving as an Al2O3 second phase. Both leave the perovskite prototype intact, which is why the assignment is unaffected, but the site label here is transcription and not chemistry.

note: The A-site reading of the aluminium substitution is recorded as a disagreement rather than quietly corrected, because the composition string is what the curator transcribed and the paper is what would settle it. Measured 10-379 K, which contains the antiferromagnetic ordering near 41 K and the ferroelectric transition near 27 K of TbMnO3. Both are magnetic and electric orderings within the Pnma perovskite, not changes of prototype, so spans_transition is false.

basis: Zn0.89Mn0.1Al0.01O and Zn0.88Mn0.12O, both at the 1:1 cation-to-oxygen ratio of ZnO, and the second paper is titled n-type Zn1-xMnxO: a dilute magnetic semiconductor. Manganese-substituted ZnO at 10 to 12 per cent of the cation site is within the reported solubility limit for the wurtzite phase, so this is Mn-substituted wurtzite ZnO, P6_3mc. I depart from [ref 2] deliberately. It lists Mn2ZnO4 I4_1/amd with 3 ICSD references as the primary, plus four further Mn-Zn-O spinels and oxides, none of them ZnO. That is the Al-O-Zn situation the taxonomy warns about: the reference describes which phases exist in the Mn-Zn-O chemistry, while nearly every sample in this host is substituted wurtzite ZnO. Spinel ZnMn2O4 is what forms if the solubility limit is exceeded, so it is recorded as the alternative rather than as the answer.

dopant_roles.basis: Al0.01 in Zn0.89Mn0.1Al0.01O, and the first paper is on Mn-Al co-doped ZnO. Al(III) on the Zn(II) site is the standard n-type donor for ZnO and is what makes these samples conducting enough to be thermoelectrics at all; manganese alone would not.

note: Manganese is 5 to 6 at.% of the formula and so sits above the split as a host constituent; its role is substitutional on the zinc site, where it adds a magnetic moment and scatters phonons but does not dope. Measured 107-1020 K. The risk at the top of that range is not a phase transition of ZnO but precipitation of the spinel from a supersaturated solid solution, which stage 2 should watch for.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [148, 141]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Four members of the Pb-Sn-Mn-Te pseudoquaternary, written two ways -- Pb0.60Mn0.15Sn0.25Te and Pb0.65Mn0.10Sn0.25Te from one paper, (Sn0.8Pb0.2)0.88Mn0.12Te and (Sn0.8Pb0.2)0.85Mn0.15Te from the other. PbTe, SnTe and MnTe in its metastable rocksalt form all share the Fm-3m cation-anion lattice, and the cation site is shared by all three metals at a fixed 1:1 ratio against tellurium in every composition. The papers are on Pb0.75-xMnxSn0.25Te alloys and on enhanced thermoelectric properties of Sn0.8Pb0.2Te by Mn substitution. Neither reference offers anything for this host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Pb/(Pb+Sn). Both are divalent group-14 lone-pair cations on the rocksalt cation site, so the exchange is isoelectronic, and the samples sit at both ends -- two are Pb-rich PbTe with tin, two are Sn-rich SnTe with lead. The parent compound is therefore a per-composition matter. This axis also moves the band structure strongly: the Pb-Sn-Te system passes through a band inversion, which is part of why these alloys are studied.

note: Manganese is 10 to 15 per cent of the cation site, far above the 5 at.% split, so it takes no dopant_roles entry. Its role is substitutional on that site, where it acts as a band-convergence agent rather than as a carrier dopant. MnTe is hexagonal NiAs-type on its own and is only rocksalt as a dilute solute here, so the solubility limit matters: above it, NiAs-type MnTe precipitates. Measured 295-725 K with no structural transition of the rocksalt matrix.

basis: All three compositions are RE2Mo2O7 with the rare-earth site shared -- (Nd0.8Er0.2)2Mo2O7, (Nd0.95Yb0.05)2Mo2O7 and (Nd0.9Yb0.1)2Mo2O7 -- and both papers say pyrochlore in the title: thermoelectric power of RE2Mo2O7 pyrochlores, and electrical properties of Ln2Mo2O7 pyrochlores. A2B2O7 with trivalent rare earth and tetravalent molybdenum is the pyrochlore, cubic Fd-3m. I disagree with [ref 2] on the cell: it gives Nd2Mo2O7 I4_1/a (88) mp-690122 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, a tetragonal cell, and its remaining entries are molybdate double salts such as KLiNd2(MoO4)4 that have nothing to do with this host. A single ICSD reference behind a tetragonal cell does not outweigh two papers that call the material a pyrochlore, and the taxonomy precedence puts the thermoelectric judgement first.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: Er0.2 of the rare-earth site in (Nd0.8Er0.2)2Mo2O7. Erbium and neodymium are both trivalent, so the substitution changes the A-site radius rather than the electron count. In the RE2Mo2O7 series the A-site radius is the control parameter: the large rare earths are ferromagnetic metals and the small ones spin-glass insulators, and substituting a smaller rare earth into Nd2Mo2O7 walks the sample towards that boundary. That is the experiment.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: Yb at 0.05 and 0.10 of the rare-earth site, the same substitution with a still smaller rare earth. Ytterbium can be mixed-valent in some hosts, so a small departure from purely isoelectronic behaviour is possible and would have to come from the paper.

note: Measured 11-301 K, which contains the ferromagnetic ordering of Nd2Mo2O7 near 90 K. That is a magnetic transition inside one prototype, not a structural one, so spans_transition is false.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [15, 14, 2, 12]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Four quaternary compositions given in atomic per cent -- Mo35Ru31Rh9Pd25, Mo30Ru43Rh14Pd13, Mo20Ru54Rh15Pd11 and Mo43Ru34Rh12Pd11 -- from a paper on the thermophysical properties of Mo-Ru-Rh-Pd alloys. These are the so-called white inclusion alloys, the metallic fission-product precipitates that form in irradiated nuclear fuel, and they are hexagonal close-packed solid solutions based on the epsilon phase of ruthenium, with molybdenum, rhodium and palladium dissolved in it. Nothing here is a line compound: the compositions wander over a wide field with no fixed stoichiometry, which is the signature of a substitutional solid solution. I do not take [ref 2], whose only entry is MoPdRuRh P3m1 (156) mp-1221443 at hull 0.089 with no ICSD reference -- a computed equiatomic ordered cell, which is not what a melted and annealed quaternary alloy at these off-equiatomic compositions is.
note: Confidence is medium for two reasons. The hcp epsilon field in this system does not extend to arbitrary molybdenum content -- above roughly 35 to 40 at.% Mo a bcc molybdenum-rich phase appears -- so Mo43Ru34Rh12Pd11 may well be two-phase, which is why composite_multiphase is listed as an alternative. And a four-component alloy at these fractions is close to what the high_entropy_alloy entry covers; solid_solution_alloy is chosen because the taxonomy entry is explicitly Cu A1 / W A2 / Mg A3 random substitution and the hcp A3 lattice is the right parent here, but the two entries are hard to separate for this host. Measured 286-1273 K.

basis: Three of the four samples are the Chevrel phase: Mo6Se8 twice, and Mo3Se4 once, which is the same compound written at half the formula unit. Chevrel phases are rhombohedral R-3 built from Mo6 octahedral clusters in a selenium cage, and [ref 2] carries it -- Mo3Se4 R-3 (148) mp-21021 with 7 ICSD references as its primary. Two of the papers are explicitly on Chevrel phases, one titled a new Chevrel phase. The remaining sample is MoSe2, the 2H layered dichalcogenide, which is a different structure, so the host is mixed. [ref 1] ranks MoSe2 P6_3/mmc first with 7 ICSD references, which is right for that one composition and not for the other three.
note: The split is clean on the Mo:Se ratio: 3:4 or 6:8 is the Chevrel phase, 1:2 is the dichalcogenide. mo9se11_cluster is listed as a second alternative because both references carry Mo9Se11 entries -- Cmcm mp-299 at 2 ICSD references in [ref 1] and P6_3/m mp-638048 in [ref 2] -- so that cluster phase exists in this chemistry, but no composition here is at 9:11 and it is not assigned. The Chevrel phases in the papers are the filled ternaries such as Ti0.3Mo6Se8, where the filler sits in the cavity between clusters; the bare Mo6Se8 recorded in these compositions is the empty host framework. Measured 101-1088 K, no structural transition.

basis: Two compositions from two quite different papers. NbON0.17 is niobium monoxide with nitrogen in it, and the paper is vacancy filling effect in thermoelectric NbO: NbO is not a rocksalt with defects but an ordered-vacancy structure, Pm-3m, with a quarter of both the cation and the anion sites systematically empty, which leaves square-planar NbO4 units and direct Nb-Nb bonding. The nitrogen the paper adds goes into those vacancies, so the ordered vacancies are the subject of the work and a prototype that does not carry them cannot describe it. No taxonomy entry existed and nbo_ordered_vacancy_rocksalt is proposed in this chunk. The other composition, Nb0.36Ru0.04O0.52N0.07, is a combinatorially sputtered film from the second paper, which is titled enhanced thermoelectric performance of amorphous Nb based oxynitrides, so it is not crystalline at all and the host is mixed. [ref 2] offers NbNO P2_1/c (14) mp-7596 with 3 ICSD references and a set of computed Nb-N-O cells at high hull; none of them is NbO and none is taken.

dopant_roles.basis: Ru at 4 at.% in Nb0.36Ru0.04O0.52N0.07, the sputtered film composition. Ruthenium is added as a metal-site substituent to raise the carrier concentration of the oxynitride. In an amorphous film site is not a meaningful label, so this is a nominal cation-site substitution rather than a crystallographic one.

note: The two compositions separate cleanly: the bulk NbON0.17 is the crystalline ordered-vacancy monoxide and the ruthenium-bearing sputtered film is amorphous. Split on composition in stage 2. rocksalt_nitride_carbide is the third alternative because it is the nearest existing entry and because a reader who does not know the NbO structure would file it there; the difference is that its vacancies are random and NbO ones are ordered. Nitrogen in NbON0.17 is 8 at.% by the curator note, above the split, so it takes no dopant_roles entry even though it is the doping variable.

basis: Two sputtered film compositions, Nb0.38Ru0.06O0.48N0.07 and Nb0.29Ru0.07O0.58N0.06, both with the curator note combinatorial reactive sputtering, from a paper titled enhanced thermoelectric performance of amorphous Nb based oxynitrides. The paper states the phase in its title and the deposition method is the one that produces it. Neither reference offers anything for this host, which is consistent with there being no crystalline phase to offer.
note: Ruthenium is 6 to 7 at.% and so above the split; it is the metal-site substituent that sets the carrier concentration, the same role it plays in the ruthenium-bearing film of the N-Nb-O host at rank 1479. These two hosts are the same material from the same paper, separated only by whether ruthenium fell above or below the 5 at.% cut, and they should be reviewed together. Measured 334-927 K: an amorphous film held at the top of that range will crystallise, so whether the high-temperature data are still on the amorphous phase is a question for the paper. No prototype change is recorded because crystallisation of an amorphous film is a sample history, not a phase sequence of a structure.

basis: Two compositions, ZnO0.42N0.30 and ZnO0.48N0.27, from a paper titled thermoelectric properties of amorphous ZnOxNy thin films at room temperature. The paper names the phase, and the sub-stoichiometric anion totals -- 0.72 and 0.75 anions per zinc -- are what a reactively sputtered amorphous film gives rather than a crystalline compound. I disregard [ref 2] entirely here: every entry it offers is a zinc nitrate or oxynitrate salt, Zn(NO6)2, Zn(NO4)2, Zn5(N2O7)2 and the like, at hulls from 0.21 to 0.90. Those are molecular-anion salts matched on element set alone and have nothing to do with a sputtered ZnOxNy film.
note: wurtzite is listed as the alternative because ZnOxNy films crystallise to substituted ZnO on annealing and because nitrogen-rich films in this system are often reported as nanocrystalline rather than fully amorphous; which applies to these particular films needs the paper. Measured 11-297 K, so no annealing happened during measurement.

basis: Na1-xSrxNbO3 at x = 0.3, 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6, from a paper on the conduction mechanism in polycrystalline Na1-xSrxNbO3 niobium bronzes. The stoichiometry is ABO3 with a full A site shared between sodium and strontium, which is a perovskite. The word bronze in the title is the older usage for a mixed-valence perovskite oxide of this kind -- the same sense as in the perovskite tungsten bronze NaxWO3 -- and does not mean the tetragonal tungsten bronze framework the tungsten_bronze entry covers; substituting Sr(II) for Na(I) is what puts niobium into mixed Nb(IV)/Nb(V) valence and makes these conducting. I do not take [ref 2]: it offers NaSr3NbO6 R-3c with 2 ICSD references and three computed Na-Sr-Nb-O cells, none of them at the 1:1 A-to-B ratio measured here.
note: tungsten_bronze is recorded as the alternative only because the paper uses the word, and the disagreement is stated here rather than resolved silently: the composition is a perovskite by stoichiometry and the terminology in the title is the historical one. Nothing is below the 5 at.% split so dopant_roles is empty; the Na-to-Sr ratio is the doping variable, not an impurity. Measured 15-277 K. NaNbO3 itself has a long sequence of ferroelectric and antiferroelectric distortion transitions, but they lie above room temperature and heavy strontium substitution changes them entirely, so none is asserted here.

basis: Sodium-doped lead sulfide, from a paper on thermoelectrics with earth abundant elements and high-performance p-type PbS. PbS is galena, the rocksalt Fm-3m, and sodium on the lead site is the standard acceptor. Neither reference offers anything for this host.
note: The composition strings are internally inconsistent and I record that rather than work around it. Pb0.98Na0.2S, Pb0.975Na0.25S, Pb0.97Na0.3S and Pb0.96Na0.4S each have a lead deficit of 0.02 to 0.04 against a sodium content of 0.2 to 0.4, ten times larger, so the cation site does not balance. Read as written, sodium is 9 to 18 at.% of the formula, which is why it sits above the 5 at.% split and takes no dopant_roles entry. Read as intended -- Pb0.98Na0.02S through Pb0.96Na0.04S, a 1 to 2 per cent sodium series, which is the range this paper works in and which balances the lead deficit exactly -- sodium is a dilute substitutional acceptor on the lead site and the host would carry it as a dopant. The second reading is almost certainly right and a factor-of-ten transcription is the likely cause, but the record follows the string and flags it. The prototype is unaffected either way: 20 at.% sodium would exceed the solubility limit in PbS and precipitate a sodium sulfide second phase, but the matrix stays rocksalt.

basis: A single composition, NbSi2, measured as thin films. NbSi2 is the C40 hexagonal disilicide, P6_222, the same structure type as CrSi2 and VSi2 that this taxonomy entry names. [ref 2] confirms it: NbSi2 P6_222 (180) mp-2478 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references as the primary. The remaining [ref 2] entries -- Nb5Si3 I4/mcm, Nb3Si P4_2/n and Nb3Si2 P4/mbm -- are the other line compounds of the Nb-Si system at metal-rich stoichiometries, not polymorphs of the disilicide.
note: Measured 178-635 K, no structural transition. These are thin films, so a silicon-rich or metal-rich interfacial phase is possible at the substrate, but the film itself at NbSi2 stoichiometry is C40.

basis: A single composition, Nd2PdO4, grown by molecular beam epitaxy. The A2BO4 stoichiometry with a square-planar d8 cation is the T-prime variant of the K2NiF4 layered structure -- the same arrangement as Nd2CuO4, tetragonal I4/mmm, in which the B cation is four-coordinate square planar and the oxygen that would cap it sits in the rare-earth block instead. Pd(II) is a d8 ion and square-planar coordination is what it always takes, so the T-prime arrangement is the one that fits. [ref 2] does carry Nd2PdO4 I4/mmm (139) mp-1025319, which is that cell, but at hull 0.369 and with no ICSD reference, and it also carries Nd2PdO4 Fd-3m at hull 0.487. Its hull-zero entries for this chemistry, Nd(PdO2)2 I4_1/a and Nd2Pd2O5 P4_2/m, are different stoichiometries.
note: Confidence is low for a specific reason worth keeping. A hull of 0.369 eV per atom is very high, no ICSD reference backs the cell, and the sample is an MBE film -- which is exactly the combination in which a compound exists only because the substrate stabilises it. The chunk warns that film samples may reach polymorphs bulk synthesis never does, and that may be the whole story here. So ruddlesden_popper records the structural family the stoichiometry and the d8 coordination imply, not a confirmed structure; the T-prime variant is a distinct arrangement within that family and the taxonomy does not separate it. Read the paper before stage 2, and consider a T-prime entry at v4 review since it is the structure of the electron-doped cuprates as well.

basis: NdO0.8F0.2SbSe2 and its arsenic-substituted member. This is the REOBiS2 family with antimony for bismuth and selenium for sulfur: alternating REO fluorite-like blocks and BiS2-type square-net chalcogenide layers, tetragonal P4/nmm. Fluorine for oxygen in the rare-earth block is the doping mechanism that family is defined by, and it is present here at exactly the usual x = 0.2. The paper is on the crystal structure and thermoelectric transport properties of As-doped material in this system. Neither reference offers anything for this host.

dopant_roles.site: rare-earth oxide block
dopant_roles.basis: F at x = 0.2 on the oxygen site of the NdO block. This is the doping variable of the whole REOBiS2 and REOBiSe2 family, not an impurity: fluorine carries one more electron than oxygen, so it transfers electrons into the chalcogenide layer and turns an insulating parent into a conductor. Same mechanism as F-for-O in LaFeAsO1-xFx.

dopant_roles.site: chalcogenide layer
dopant_roles.basis: As0.2 written against Sb0.8 in NdO0.8F0.2Sb0.8As0.2Se2. Arsenic and antimony are both group 15 on the same site of the square-net layer, so the substitution is isovalent and works through size and through the lone-pair chemistry of the layer rather than through carrier count. That is the subject of the paper.

note: zrcusias_1111 is listed as the alternative because the two families share the same fluorite-block plus square-net building principle and the same F-for-O doping, and the boundary between them is which layer sits between the blocks. Measured 298-672 K, no structural transition.

basis: Three of the four compositions are Nd1-xAxTiO3 with A divalent -- Nd0.8Ca0.2TiO3, Nd0.9Ca0.1TiO3 and Nd0.6Sr0.1TiO3 -- from a paper on the band-filling dependence of the electrical transport of Nd1-xAxTiO3 and one on neodymium-strontium titanate. NdTiO3 is an orthorhombic Pnma perovskite and [ref 2] carries it, NdTiO3 Pnma (62) mp-3119 at hull 0.042 with 3 ICSD references; substituting a divalent cation on the A site is band filling within that structure, which is what the first paper measures. The fourth composition, Ba3.45Nd9.7Ti18O54, is a different structure from a different paper -- the Ba6-3xNd8+2xTi18O54 tungsten bronze, as its title says -- so the host is mixed. The other [ref 2] entries, Nd2TiO5 Pnma and Nd2Ti2O7 P2_1, are further line compounds of the system at other stoichiometries.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: Ca at x = 0.1 and 0.2 of the A site in Nd1-xCaxTiO3. Ca(II) for Nd(III) removes an electron from the titanium 3d band, so it is the band-filling variable the paper sweeps, not a dilute impurity.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: Sr at 0.1 of the A site, the same substitution with the larger alkaline earth, from the neodymium-strontium titanate paper.

dopant_roles.site: tunnel site of the bronze
dopant_roles.basis: Ba3.45 in Ba3.45Nd9.7Ti18O54. Barium is not a dopant here at all: it is a framework constituent of the tungsten-bronze phase, occupying the large pentagonal tunnels of the Ti18O54 network alongside neodymium. It falls below the 5 at.% cut only because that cut is taken against the whole 85-atom formula.

note: Two prototypes, separable by stoichiometry: A-to-B ratio of 1 is the perovskite, the Ba-Nd-Ti-O composition at 18 titanium and 54 oxygen is the bronze. Split on composition in stage 2. Nd0.6Sr0.1TiO3 is A-site deficient as written, with only 0.7 A cations per titanium; A-site vacancies are real in this family but 30 per cent is a lot, so that string may also be incomplete.

basis: A single composition, YNiO3, and [ref 2] gives exactly one entry for the host: YNiO3 Pnma (62) mp-19242 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references. The rare-earth nickelates RNiO3 are orthorhombic GdFeO3-distorted perovskites, and the paper -- a d-band electron correlated thermoelectric thermistor -- is about the correlated transport that family is known for.
note: YNiO3 has a charge-ordering metal-insulator transition at about 580 K, at which the structure changes from orthorhombic Pbnm to monoclinic P2_1/n with two distinct nickel sites. The measured window here is 219-483 K, entirely below it, so the samples stay in the charge-ordered monoclinic phase throughout and spans_transition is false. That is worth recording because the same host measured to 700 K would cross it and would need two phases. The reference cell, Pnma, is the high-temperature setting; the low-temperature monoclinic cell is not in the reference list and no mp_id is asserted for it.

basis: Four compositions of NiSi3-xBxP4 with x from 0 to 0.2, and the paper is thermoelectric properties of polycrystalline NiSi3P4. [ref 2] carries the compound directly, Si3NiP4 I-42m (121) mp-8311 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, and the two neighbouring entries -- Si2NiP3 Imm2 and Si2Ni5P3 Pbca -- are other line compounds of the Ni-Si-P system rather than polymorphs. There is no taxonomy entry for this structure, so nisi3p4_type is proposed in this chunk rather than forcing the composition into stannite_kesterite, which shares the I-42m space group but is a 2:1:1:4 quaternary with a distinct cation and anion sublattice and does not describe a 1:3:4 silicophosphide.

dopant_roles.basis: B at 0.02, 0.1 and 0.2 written against silicon in NiSi3-xBxP4, so boron takes a silicon site. Boron has one fewer valence electron than silicon, so on that site it is an acceptor, and the series is a p-type carrier sweep on an otherwise lightly doped semiconductor.

note: Confidence is medium because the prototype is proposed in this chunk and because its structural description -- a tetrahedral diamond-like framework -- is inferred from the space group, the main-group stoichiometry and the semiconducting transport, not read from a structure file. The space group and mp_id themselves are reference-backed. A single ICSD reference makes it a weak primary by the chunk criterion, but it is also the only entry at this stoichiometry and it matches the measured compound exactly. Measured 10-795 K, no transition known.

basis: The host key itself is a parsing failure and has to be read through. The four composition strings are CeTiO33.1, SrCo0.8Nb0.1NiO30.1, SrCo0.7Nb0.1NiO30.2 and SrCo0.6Nb0.1NiO30.3, in which an oxygen count of 30 to 33 has been produced by running the 3 of an O3 suffix together with a following decimal: CeTiO3 with something at 3.1, and SrCo1-x-yNbxNiyO3-delta with the deficiency digits absorbed. Every cation then falls below 5 at.% against that enormous oxygen count, which is why all six cations were binned as dopant candidates and the host collapsed to bare oxygen. Both papers are perovskite papers -- electronic states of perovskite-type systems with a metal-insulator transition, and a cathode for oxygen reduction in an intermediate-temperature fuel cell, where SrCoO3-based perovskites are the standard cathode material -- and both underlying compositions are ABO3. So the prototype is perovskite. [ref 1] and [ref 2] both answer with polymorphs of solid molecular O2, which is the correct answer to the host key they were given and no answer at all to the question.

dopant_roles.basis: The A cation of CeTiO3. It appears as a minor element only because the oxygen count of that string is wrong by a factor of ten.
The B cation of CeTiO3, minor for the same reason.
The A cation of the SrCo1-x-yNbxNiyO3-delta cathode compositions, minor for the same reason.
The principal B cation of the cathode compositions.

A genuine B-site substituent at 0.1 per formula unit in the cathode compositions -- niobium stabilises the cubic perovskite against the brownmillerite ordering -- but its apparent fraction here is meaningless.
The other B-site substituent of the cathode series, at 0.1 to 0.3 per formula unit. Also genuine, also mis-scaled.

note: This record exists to keep the host from being silently dropped and to say why it cannot be used as it stands. Two unrelated materials from two unrelated papers were pooled into one host by a parsing error, and nothing downstream should treat host O as a chemistry. Both are perovskites, so the prototype is not in doubt, but the host key is wrong and the dopant fractions are unusable, which is why every cation is recorded as parse_artifact. brownmillerite is listed as the alternative because oxygen-deficient SrCoO3-delta orders into it at delta near 0.5, which is exactly the regime a fuel-cell cathode operates in. The fix belongs in the composition parser, not in this ledger.

basis: A single composition, Pr2Zr2O7, and both papers work on the A2Zr2O7 series -- electrical and thermal conductivities of rare-earth A2Zr2O7 with A = Pr and Nd, and thermal and oxygen transport properties of complex pyrochlores. A2B2O7 with a trivalent rare earth and zirconium is the pyrochlore, cubic Fd-3m, and praseodymium is well inside the radius ratio range where the ordered pyrochlore is stable rather than the disordered defect fluorite. I disregard [ref 2] here: its single entry is PrZrO14 Fd-3m mp-1210241 at hull 0.619 with no ICSD reference, a formula that is not even charge-balanced as a zirconate and is 0.6 eV per atom above the hull.
note: fluorite_oxide is recorded as the alternative because the pyrochlore-to-defect-fluorite boundary is the live question in this family: as the rare earth gets smaller the cation and vacancy ordering is lost and the structure becomes a disordered fluorite, which is why these compositions are studied as thermal barrier coatings. Praseodymium is large enough to be ordered, so pyrochlore is the assignment, but a partially disordered sample is possible and only a diffraction pattern would settle it. Measured 293-873 K, with the full span reaching 1072 K; no transition of prototype in either window.

basis: ZnRh2O4 and three variants of it. AB2O4 with octahedral Rh(III) and tetrahedral Zn(II) is the normal spinel, and [ref 2] confirms it, Zn(RhO2)2 Fd-3m (227) mp-5146 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. The first paper is on the synthesis and thermoelectric properties of a novel A-site deficient rhodate, which is what Zn0.5Rh2O4 and Li0.25Zn0.5Rh2O4 are -- half the tetrahedral A site emptied, with lithium partly refilling it -- and the second is on Mg substitution effects in new thermoelectric Rh oxides, which is ZnRh1.8Mg0.2O4. Vacancies and substitutions on either site leave the spinel framework standing. The other [ref 2] entry, ZnRhO3 Pm-3m at hull 0.766, is a computed perovskite and is not taken.

dopant_roles.site: tetrahedral A site
dopant_roles.basis: Li0.25 in Li0.25Zn0.5Rh2O4, filling a quarter of an A site that is half vacant. Li(I) on a site that held Zn(II) is an acceptor and, with the vacancies, is how the paper sets the hole concentration of an A-site deficient rhodate.

dopant_roles.site: octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Mg0.2 written against Rh1.8 in ZnRh1.8Mg0.2O4, so magnesium takes the octahedral site. Mg(II) for Rh(III) is an acceptor substitution on the conducting rhodium sublattice, which is the subject of the second paper.

note: Two of the four samples are films, where the chunk warns a metastable polymorph may be reachable. ZnRh2O4 is a robust spinel and nothing here suggests otherwise, but the A-site deficient Zn0.5Rh2O4 is the kind of composition that is easier to stabilise as a film than in bulk. Measured 11-873 K, no structural transition.

basis: A single composition written Sc0.67WO4, which is Sc2W3O12 written per tungsten -- the defect-scheelite way of writing it, with one third of the A sites vacant. The ambient compound is the orthorhombic Pbcn A2M3O12 negative-thermal-expansion framework, corner-linked ScO6 octahedra and WO4 tetrahedra, and [ref 2] attests it: Sc2(WO4)3 Pbcn (60) mp-19588 at hull 0.008 with 5 ICSD references. There was no taxonomy entry for this family and sc2w3o12_type is proposed in this chunk. But the paper is high-pressure synthesis, crystal and electronic structures of a NEW scandium tungstate, so the sample measured is probably not the ambient Pbcn form, and the assignment records the family rather than the phase.

other_polymorphs.note: Sc2(WO4)3 P2/c at hull 0.025 with no ICSD reference. Offered as a candidate for the denser high-pressure form the paper reports, NOT as a confirmed identification -- the paper may have made a defect scheelite instead, which would be a different framework and not a polymorph within this type at all. Not reached by heating at ambient pressure either way.

note: Confidence is low because the paper explicitly reports a new high-pressure phase and the prototype assigned is the ambient one. This is the only host in the chunk where the reference is well attested and I still expect the sample not to match it, so it is worth flagging rather than letting the 5 ICSD references carry it. The measured range is also suspect: the robust window is 19-304 K but the full span reaches 598 K, so the curve set is inhomogeneous. Several A2M3O12 members hydrate reversibly at room temperature and change cell when they do, which is one more reason to read the paper before stage 2 resolves a structure.

basis: The compositions are written (ZnO)a(SiO2)3.3 with a running from 4.2 to 6.3, and the paper is structure and electrical properties of (ZnO/SiO2)25 thin films -- a stack of twenty-five ZnO and SiO2 bilayers, not a compound. The varying ZnO fraction against a fixed SiO2 fraction is the layer-thickness ratio of the stack. So the sample is two phases by construction: nanocrystalline or textured ZnO layers alternating with amorphous silica. I do not take either reference. [ref 2] ranks Zn2SiO5 Imm2 at hull 0.435 first and then willemite Zn2SiO4 R-3 mp-3789 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, and [ref 1] offers five further Zn2SiO4 polymorphs. Willemite is the compound that exists in the ZnO-SiO2 chemistry, and it is not what a room-temperature-deposited multilayer contains; forming it would need firing above 1000 C.
note: This is the clearest reference disagreement in the chunk and it is the Al-O-Zn case again in a sharper form: the databases describe the thermodynamics of the ZnO-SiO2 join while the sample is a deposited multilayer that never reached equilibrium. The two constituent prototypes are recorded as alternatives -- wurtzite for the ZnO layers, amorphous for the silica -- and the transport measured across a stack belongs to neither alone, which is why composite_multiphase is the host label. The taxonomy marks composite_multiphase for skipping in stage 2 structure resolution and that is the right treatment here. Measured 73-296 K.

basis: A single composition, SmO, and both papers are on samarium monoxide itself -- transport properties of SmO, and samarium monoxide epitaxial thin film as a possible heavy-fermion compound. SmO is the rocksalt monoxide, Fm-3m, and [ref 2] carries it, mp-1611 with 2 ICSD references. The interest in it is that samarium is intermediate-valent in this structure, which is a rocksalt property and not a sesquioxide one.
note: [ref 2] ranks Sm2O3 Ia-3 mp-218 first, at hull 0.000 with 10 ICSD references, against SmO at hull 0.112 with 2. That ranking is correct about the chemistry and wrong about these samples: the C-type sesquioxide is the stable samarium oxide in air, and SmO is a metastable monoxide made under pressure or as an epitaxial film, which is exactly how both papers make it. The reference describes which phase exists, not which phase was measured, and the disagreement is recorded rather than followed. Measured 12-298 K.

basis: One composition, (Zn0.993Al0.007O)85.86(ZrO2)14.14, from a paper titled a self-forming nanocomposite concept for ZnO-based thermoelectrics. The matrix is aluminium-doped ZnO at 86 mol per cent -- wurtzite P6_3mc -- with 14 mol per cent zirconia as a deliberate second phase that precipitates during sintering; the curator notes name two different commercial ZrO2 powders used as the starting material, which confirms that the zirconia is added rather than formed in solution. The host is therefore mixed, with the wurtzite matrix carrying the transport. [ref 2] offers only ZrZnO3 Pm-3m mp-1016883 at hull 0.759 with no ICSD reference, a computed perovskite that does not exist; it is not taken.

dopant_roles.basis: Al0.007 per zinc, the standard donor doping of ZnO. Al(III) on the Zn(II) site supplies the electrons that make aluminium-doped ZnO a thermoelectric at all; the zirconia is there to scatter phonons, not to dope.

note: fluorite_oxide is listed as the alternative for the zirconia phase, with a caveat: pure ZrO2 is monoclinic baddeleyite at room temperature, not cubic fluorite, and only becomes tetragonal above about 1400 K or cubic above 2600 K unless stabilised. Nanoscale ZrO2 inclusions are often tetragonal by size stabilisation instead. Which form these are needs the paper, so fluorite_oxide records the family rather than the phase. Measured 423-1223 K; the wurtzite matrix has no transition there.

basis: A single composition, Zn3P2. [ref 2] ranks Zn3P2 P4_2/nmc (137) mp-2071 first at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references. That is the alpha-Zn3P2 structure: an antifluorite-derived tetragonal cell in which a quarter of the cation sites are systematically vacant and the vacancies are ordered, which is the same building principle as Cd3As2 and is what this taxonomy entry names. I depart from the project precedence and do not use [ref 1] for the assignment: TEDesignLab offers only ZnP2 and ZnP4 for this host, which are different compounds at different stoichiometries, so it has no entry for the material measured and [ref 2] is the only reference that does.

other_polymorphs.note: Zn3P2 Ia-3 at hull 0.027 with 1 ICSD reference, a cubic vacancy-disordered form. Zn3P2 does have an order-disorder transition to a cubic phase, but it lies near 1120 K, well above the 79-793 K measured window, so it is recorded here rather than in phases.

note: The taxonomy entry gives I4_1/acd (142), which is the Cd3As2 cell; alpha-Zn3P2 is P4_2/nmc (137). Both are ordered-vacancy antifluorite superstructures of the same A3B2 family and differ in how the vacancies are stacked, so the prototype is right and the space group should be taken from the reference rather than from the entry. Worth noting in the entry at v4 review. Two of the four samples are films and the paper on them grows Zn3P2 by a vapour method; nothing suggests a metastable polymorph.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [142], ICSD-backed references for this host report [137, 92, 14, 96]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Three of the four samples are elemental lead, measured as a thermoelectric reference standard -- the papers are on the thermal conductivity, electrical resistivity and thermoelectric power of lead, and on thin gold wires as a reference for thermopower measurements. Lead is face-centred cubic, Fm-3m, and [ref 2] ranks it first, mp-20483 at hull 0.000 with 14 ICSD references; the four other entries it lists are high-pressure and computed polymorphs at 1 to 3 ICSD references each. The fourth composition, Pb99.975TeNa0.025, is not elemental lead at all: it is sodium-doped PbTe with the tellurium left at 1 while the lead and sodium were scaled by a hundred, so the real formula is Pb0.99975Na0.00025Te and the paper is on the heavy hole effect in highly doped p-type PbTe. The host is therefore mixed, with rocksalt as the second prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Tellurium is not a dilute additive to lead metal. It is the anion of a PbTe composition whose cation counts were written in per cent while the anion was left at 1, which made it look like a trace element. Its true fraction is one half of the formula.

Sodium is a real dopant but at the wrong scale: in the intended Pb0.99975Na0.00025Te it is 0.025 at.% on the lead site, the standard p-type acceptor for PbTe. Recorded as substitutional rather than parse_artifact because the role is unambiguous even though the fraction printed here is a hundred times too large.

note: Split on composition in stage 2: the bare Pb string is the metal, the Te-bearing string is rocksalt PbTe. Measured 20-550 K robust, full span to 688 K. Lead melts at 600 K, so the top of the full span is above the melting point of the elemental samples and those points must belong to the PbTe composition; that is one more sign the host pools two materials. No solid-state transition of fcc lead occurs in the window.

basis: A single composition, YPdSb, at 1:1:1, and all three papers name the family -- thermoelectrical properties of the compounds ScMSb and YMSb, physical properties of rare-earth-based Heusler phases REPdZ, and magnetic and transport properties of the rare-earth-based Heusler phases. REPdSb at 1:1:1 is the half-Heusler, cubic F-43m, with the 4d site empty. I take that over the [ref 2] ranking. [ref 2] does list YSbPd F-43m (216) mp-1215892, which is the right cell, but at hull 0.532 and with no ICSD reference, and it ranks four other Y-Pd-Sb line compounds above it. A half-electronvolt-per-atom hull for a compound that three papers synthesise and measure is not credible; YPdSb is a well-established half-Heusler and the MP entry is the one at fault.
