note: full_heusler is recorded as the alternative because two of the papers study REPdZ and REPd2Z together and samples in this family commonly carry some YPd2Sb as a second phase. Measured 12-398 K, no structural transition.

basis: Ru2Si3, in three undoped samples and one with manganese. Ru2Si3 is a Nowotny chimney-ladder phase: the Si-to-metal ratio of 1.5 is exactly what the valence-electron-count rule of that family gives for a group-8 metal, the silicon atoms form the helical ladder threading a tetragonal beta-Sn-like metal chimney, and the semiconducting gap that makes it a thermoelectric is a consequence of that electron count. [ref 2] confirms the ambient cell, Si3Ru2 Pbcn (60) mp-22192 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, which is the orthorhombically distorted low-temperature form. The remaining [ref 2] entries -- SiRu P2_13, SiRu2 Pnma, Si2Ru P4/mmm, Si3Ru5 Pbam -- are the other line compounds of the Ru-Si system, not polymorphs of this one. All three papers are on Ru2Si3 as a thermoelectric.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn0.01 per Ru2Si3 formula unit, from the paper on Mn-doped Ru2Si3. Manganese has three fewer valence electrons than ruthenium, so on the metal site of a chimney-ladder phase whose gap is set by the electron count it is an acceptor and shifts the Fermi level into the valence band. That is a stronger lever here than in an ordinary semiconductor, because the electron count is what opens the gap in the first place.

note: Ru2Si3 transforms from the low-temperature orthorhombic Pbcn form to a tetragonal P-4c2 form near 1000 K. It is a distortion within the same chimney-ladder prototype, not a change of family. spans_transition is set false because the robust measured window is 11-872 K, below it -- but the full span reaches 1268 K, so the highest-temperature curves in this host are in the tetragonal phase and the two should not be averaged. The taxonomy entry for this prototype describes the family as incommensurate and says stage 2 must pick an approximant; Ru2Si3 is one of the commensurate members, so for this host an exact cell does exist and mp-22192 is it.

basis: One composition, V5S8, in four single crystals. V5S8 is a metal-deficient NiAs derivative: it is VS2 with an extra quarter of a vanadium per formula unit inserted into the van der Waals gap, equivalently a NiAs lattice with one quarter of the metal sites empty and the vacancies ordered into alternate layers. That ordering is exactly the construction this prototype is defined by, and V3S4 -- the half-vacancy member of the same series -- is already one of its representative materials. [ref 1] gives V5S8 C2/m (12) mp-690772 at hull 0.005 with 6 ICSD references, which is the monoclinic cell of that vacancy ordering. The paper is on intercalation of van der Waals layered materials, which is the same picture read from the other direction.
note: One qualification on the prototype. V5S8 is usually given in I2/m as the V5S8 type, with a quarter of the metal sites vacant; Cr3S4 has half of them vacant and is set in C2/m. They are different members of one ordered-vacancy series rather than the same structure, and the taxonomy entry names the series by its half-vacancy member. [ref 1] reports the C2/m setting for V5S8, so the two agree on the cell even though the vacancy fraction differs. cdi2_1t is the alternative because V5S8 can equally be read as self-intercalated 1T-VS2, which is the reading the paper takes; the sibling host Se-V, where no vanadium is intercalated, is assigned cdi2_1t outright. Measured 12-296 K. V5S8 orders antiferromagnetically near 32 K and shows a metal-insulator-like anomaly around 100 K, both inside the window, but neither changes the structure type.

basis: Three of the four compositions are written as (YbTe)x(YbSb)1-x across x = 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8, from a paper on the YbTe-YbSb system. Both end members are rocksalt -- YbTe is Fm-3m and YbSb is Fm-3m -- and they share the ytterbium cation site, so the pseudo-binary is a single rocksalt solid solution with Sb and Te sharing the anion site, not a line compound. The fourth composition, YbSb2Te4, is a different material: it is (YbTe)(Sb2Te3), the ytterbium member of the (MX)n(Sb2Te3)m tetradymite homologous series, built from septuple Te-Sb-Te-Yb-Te-Sb-Te layers. The host therefore holds two prototypes and is split on composition.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: Only the three (YbTe)x(YbSb)1-x compositions lie on this axis. Sb and Te are adjacent groups rather than the same group, so this is not isoelectronic substitution: replacing Te by Sb on the anion site of YbTe removes one electron per substitution and is the carrier-concentration knob the paper is using. Recorded as an axis because the composition varies continuously across it, not because the two species are equivalent.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] here and record it rather than following it. The only two Materials Project entries offered are Yb(SbTe2)2 I-42d (122) mp-675892 at hull 0.836 and Yb3(Sb7Te12)2 P1 (1) mp-675683 at hull 0.966, both with no ICSD reference and both nearly an electronvolt per atom above the hull. Those are computed orderings, not the measured materials, and neither is the rocksalt solid solution nor the septuple-layer YbSb2Te4. mp_id is left null for both prototypes. Splitting rule for stage 2: a composition written as a YbTe-YbSb mixture is rocksalt, YbSb2Te4 is homologous_tetradymite. Measured 287-827 K, no structural transition known in that window for either.

basis: Th3Sb4 in three samples and Th3(As0.05Sb0.95)4 in one, and the paper is titled as X-ray and thermoelectric studies on cubic Th3X4 compounds, which names the structure type in the title. Th3Sb4 is the anti-Th3P4 arrangement, body-centred cubic I-43d, the same cation-deficient framework that carries La3-xTe4 -- the prototype this taxonomy entry is built on. [ref 2] confirms it directly: Th3Sb4 I-43d (220) mp-552 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. The other entries it lists -- ThSb Fm-3m, ThSb2 P4/nmm, Th2Sb3 -- are the neighbouring line compounds of the Th-Sb system, not polymorphs of Th3Sb4, and none of them is in the compositions.

dopant_roles.basis: Th3(As0.05Sb0.95)4: arsenic and antimony are both group 15 and both sit on the pnictogen site of the Th3X4 framework, so 5 per cent As adds no carriers. It shrinks the cell and scatters phonons, which is what a single substituted sample in an otherwise binary series is testing. The paper studies the Th3X4 compounds as a family, so this is a deliberate step along the As-Sb line rather than a contaminant.

note: In this structure the carrier count is set by cation vacancies on the Th site, as it is in La3-xTe4, so a nominal Th3Sb4 and a slightly thorium-deficient one are different materials electronically while sharing a space group. Nothing in the composition strings records that, and the measured window is wide -- 102-1218 K -- so the spread across the three nominally identical samples may be a vacancy spread rather than scatter. Worth reading the paper for the refined thorium occupancy.

basis: A single composition, VSe2, in four samples including a single crystal, with papers on bulk VSe2 with layered structure and on intercalation of van der Waals layered materials. VSe2 is the canonical 1T dichalcogenide: octahedrally coordinated vanadium in single CdI2-type sheets stacked across a van der Waals gap, trigonal P-3m1. [ref 2] gives exactly that, VSe2 P-3m1 (164) mp-694 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, the top-ranked entry.
note: [ref 1] does not cover this material and I am not following it. TEDesignLab lists VSe P6_3/mmc, V2Se9 C2/c and VSe P4/nmm for this chemistry but has no VSe2 entry at all, so on the project precedence the ICSD-backed source is simply silent here and [ref 2] decides. VSe2 has a charge-density-wave transition near 110 K, inside the measured 10-700 K window. It is a periodic lattice distortion within the 1T structure rather than a change of prototype, so spans_transition is left false, but transport across 110 K should not be treated as one regime. The third paper is on interstitial vanadium in ferecrystals, which is the same self-intercalation that makes V5S8 in the sibling host S-V; if any sample here is V1+xSe2 rather than VSe2 it belongs with cr3s4_defect_nias instead.

basis: A single composition, WSe2, in four samples. WSe2 is the 2H polytype: trigonal-prismatic coordination of tungsten, two layers per hexagonal cell, P6_3/mmc, and a real band gap near 1.2 eV that is why it appears in thermoelectric work at all. [ref 1] gives WSe2 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1821 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references and nothing else, which is as clean a call as this chunk offers.

other_polymorphs.note: The 1T octahedral polymorph [ref 2] lists at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference. In tungsten diselenide the 1T form is not reached by heating bulk 2H material; it appears in exfoliated or chemically treated monolayers. Listed here so the zero hull value is not mistaken for evidence that it competes with 2H.
P-6m2 is the 1H single-layer setting of the same trigonal-prismatic coordination -- a monolayer model rather than a distinct bulk phase. Same prototype, different stacking, no ICSD reference.

note: Measured 101-673 K, no structural transition. One of the papers adjusts the layer alignment to decouple thermal and electrical conductivity, so texture and stacking disorder vary between samples within the one prototype; that is a microstructure axis, not a second structure.

basis: Elemental tantalum, measured as a reference metal -- the papers are on the intrinsic thermoelectric power of the group VB metals, on the thermoelectric properties of high-melting metals, and on tantalum-tungsten alloys. Tantalum is body-centred cubic Im-3m, and [ref 2] ranks that first with 11 ICSD references, mp-50 at hull 0.000. The same prototype was used for the elemental hosts W and Ni earlier in this ledger, so an unalloyed metal is filed consistently.

other_polymorphs.note: The tetragonal beta-Ta phase, P-42_1m, which [ref 2] carries at hull 0.005 with 5 ICSD references. It is real and well attested, but it forms in sputtered thin films and converts irreversibly to bcc on heating; it is not a thermal phase of bulk tantalum. The samples here are bulk, so it is recorded as metastable rather than as a second phase.
fcc tantalum at hull 0.246. Together with the P4_2/mnm and P6_322 entries above 1.2 eV per atom, these are computed or high-pressure structures, not phases of the measured material.

note: The robust measured range is 15-373 K but the full span reaches 1563 K. bcc tantalum has no solid-state transition anywhere in that range -- it is bcc from cryogenic temperatures to its 3290 K melting point -- so the wide span costs nothing structurally. One paper is on Ta-W alloys; any Ta-W composition would route to a two-element host, so the samples pooled here should be the unalloyed end member. solid_solution_alloy is a slightly awkward label for a pure element, but it is what this taxonomy uses for elemental metals and changing that is a v4 question, not a per-host one.

basis: A single composition, WTe2. WTe2 does not take the 2H structure its selenide sibling does: it is the Td phase, orthorhombic and polar, Pmn2_1, with the tungsten atoms displaced into zigzag metal-metal chains within octahedrally coordinated layers. That distortion closes the gap and makes it a semimetal, which is the whole reason it is measured separately from WSe2. [ref 2] ranks Te2W Pmn2_1 (31) mp-22693 first at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references. The proposed prototype names WTe2 explicitly among its representative materials.

other_polymorphs.note: 2H WTe2 at hull 0.025 with a single ICSD reference. The 2H form is the ground state for WS2 and WSe2 but not for the telluride, where Td wins; one reference against five is the evidence gap to read here.

The undistorted 1T parent, plus the P-6m2 monolayer model at mp-1025573. Neither carries an ICSD reference; the undistorted 1T is the structure the Td phase is the Peierls distortion of, so it is a reference point rather than a competing phase.

note: Measured 201-497 K. The Td to 1T-prime transition in WTe2 sits well above that, near 570 K, so the measurement stays in the polar orthorhombic phase throughout and spans_transition is false. The same paper supplies the WSe2 samples in the sibling host Se-W; the two hosts are deliberately different prototypes and the contrast between them is the point of that review.

basis: One composition, Au49Cu26.9Ag5.5Pd2.3Si16.3, and the paper is titled as thermoelectric properties of Au-based metallic glass at low temperatures. This is the classic Au-Cu-Ag-Pd-Si bulk-glass-forming composition: five elements at deeply eutectic proportions with a metalloid at 16 per cent, which is the standard recipe for suppressing crystallisation. There is no periodic structure to assign and neither reference offers an entry for the host.

dopant_roles.basis: Pd at 2.3 atomic per cent is below the host threshold but is not a dopant. In gold-based bulk metallic glasses palladium is a deliberate glass-forming addition: it broadens the supercooled liquid region and raises the critical casting thickness. There is no lattice site for it to substitute on, so the role is recorded as an alloying component of the amorphous network rather than as substitutional.

note: mp_id is null and must stay null -- an amorphous alloy has no Materials Project entry, and the README already flags metallic_glass as a stage 2 skip. Measured 12-392 K. The glass transition of this family is near 400 K, at the very top of the full span, so the highest points may approach the supercooled liquid region; crystallisation would show as an irreversible jump rather than a reversible transition and would make those samples a different material entirely.

basis: Three compositions of the form Bi2Ba2-xAgxCo2O9 at x = 0.5, 1 and 1.5. That formula is the barium member of the misfit layered cobaltite family: a rocksalt-type Bi2Ba2O4 block stacked incommensurately on CoO2 layers of the CdI2 type, the same construction as Bi2Sr2Co2O9 and Ca3Co4O9. The paper reports a narrow band contribution with Anderson localization in a silver-doped layered cobaltite, which names the layering. Silver substitutes on the barium site of the rocksalt block, so the CoO2 sheets that carry the transport are left intact and only the carrier count changes.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag is a host element here by the 5 per cent rule, not a dopant candidate, but what it does is worth recording because it is the variable the paper sweeps. Monovalent silver replacing divalent barium in the Bi2Ba2O4 rocksalt block removes one electron per substitution and hole-dopes the CoO2 sheets. It is not entering the cobalt oxide layer.

note: This prototype is flagged in the README as needing special handling in stage 2: a misfit cobaltite is an incommensurate composite of two subsystems with independent lattice parameters, so there is no single Materials Project entry for it and mp_id stays null. Neither reference printed any line for this host, so the assignment rests on the formula and the paper. Measured 11-338 K, entirely below any structural transition of this family.

basis: The three compositions are written explicitly as mixtures, (Ag2O)x(YBa2Cu3O7)1-x, at x = 41.8, 55.2 and 65.7 per cent, and the paper is on the possibility of Ag2O plus YBa2Cu3O7-x ceramics for low temperature thermoelectrics. At those fractions silver oxide is not an additive to a superconductor, it is the majority phase in two of the three samples. Two structures are present in every sample -- the oxygen-deficient 123 cuprate and cuprite-type Ag2O -- and neither one describes the material, so the host is a composite and must be split rather than labelled.
note: The two constituents are named as alternatives so stage 2 has them: YBa2Cu3O7-x is ybco_cuprate, orthorhombic Pmmm, and Ag2O is cuprite, cubic Pn-3m -- the taxonomy entry for Cu2O covers the isostructural silver oxide. Measured 11-260 K, which straddles the 92 K superconducting transition of the 123 phase; that is an electronic transition, not a structural one, so spans_transition is false, but Seebeck data above and below it are not one regime. A caution for stage 2: Ag2O decomposes to silver metal and oxygen near 570 K, so a sintered ceramic of this kind may contain metallic silver rather than the oxide depending on the processing, which the composition string cannot tell us.

basis: The curator transcription settles this one outright: the three samples are (Bi1.6Pb0.4Sr1.6Ca2Cu3Oy) with 10, 20 and 50 weight per cent silver added, and the paper is on thermoelectric power studies of the BPSCCO system with silver addition. Bi1.6Pb0.4Sr1.6Ca2Cu3Oy is the lead-substituted 2223 member of the Bi-Sr-Ca-Cu-O family, the phase lead is added to stabilise in the first place. The silver is a metallic addition made for grain connectivity and is not in the cuprate lattice.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb0.4 per formula unit on the bismuth site of the double Bi-O rocksalt block. Lead substitution is what makes the 2223 phase form at all in this chemistry: it widens the stability field of the three-CuO2-layer member against the 2212 member, and it also alters the incommensurate modulation of the Bi-O layers. Not a dilute impurity despite sitting under 5 atomic per cent of the whole formula.

Metallic silver at 10 to 50 weight per cent, added to the ceramic rather than dissolved in it. Silver has negligible solubility in the BSCCO lattice; it sits at grain boundaries where it improves intergrain coupling and lowers resistivity. Recorded here even though it is a host element by the 5 per cent rule, because treating it as part of the structure would be wrong.

note: At 50 weight per cent silver the highest sample is arguably a composite rather than a doped cuprate, and a case could be made for composite_multiphase as the sibling host Ag-Ba-Cu-O-Y received. I kept bscco_cuprate because the silver is a discrete unreactive metal phase rather than a second oxide competing for the same elements, so the cuprate structure is unchanged and the host still has one crystal structure to resolve. Measured 102-299 K; the 2223 superconducting transition is near 110 K, at the bottom of that window, and is electronic rather than structural.

basis: Three compositions, AgBi3S5-xClx at x = 0.8, 1.65 and 2.5, from a paper on high thermoelectric performance in electron-doped AgBi3S5 with ultralow thermal conductivity. AgBi3S5 is the mineral pavonite: a monoclinic C2/m sulfosalt built from alternating thin and thick NaCl-type slabs meeting across a mirror plane, with the silver in the thin slab. That is a defined structure type with a name, not a one-off, so it is proposed as its own prototype rather than dropped into the complex-bismuth-chalcogenide bucket.

dopant_roles.basis: Chlorine on the sulfur site is the doping variable the paper is built on, not an impurity, even though at x = 2.5 it reaches half the anion count. A halide replacing a chalcogenide donates one electron per substitution, which drives an intrinsically p-type sulfosalt n-type and is exactly the electron doping named in the title. Recorded as substitutional rather than isoelectronic because the whole point is that it changes the electron count.

note: Confidence is medium rather than high because neither reference covers this host -- no TEDesignLab entry and no Materials Project line was printed -- so nothing independent confirms the C2/m pavonite cell for the measured samples, and mp_id is left null rather than guessed. A second caution for stage 2: at x = 2.5 the chlorine is a quarter of all anions, which is far past what a dilute substitution can be assumed to leave structurally intact. The paper reports the series as single phase, but whether the pavonite framework survives to x = 2.5 or whether the chloride-rich samples order differently is a question for the paper, not for the composition string. Measured 299-802 K.

basis: Three compositions of BiCu1-xAgxSeO at x = 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4, and the paper is on enhanced low temperature thermoelectric performance of Ag-doped BiCuSeO. BiCuSeO is the thermoelectric workhorse of the ZrCuSiAs 1111 type: insulating Bi2O2 layers alternating with conducting Cu2Se2 layers, tetragonal P4/nmm. Silver replaces copper within the Cu2Se2 layer and is isovalent, so the layer stacking is untouched.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag for Cu at 20 to 40 per cent of the copper site. Silver and copper are both group 11 and both monovalent here, so no carriers are added; what silver does is expand the Cu2Se2 layer and soften the lattice, which lowers the thermal conductivity. The carrier increase these samples show comes from copper vacancies that accompany the substitution rather than from the silver itself. Ag is a host element by the 5 per cent rule, recorded because the substitution is the variable being swept.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation, within the Cu2Se2 conducting layer
solid_solution_axis.note: The site is worth stating explicitly because this host is the exact case the README warns about: oxygen and selenium are both group 16 but in BiCuSeO oxygen sits in the Bi2O2 layer and never substitutes for selenium, so an automatic same-group axis detector would produce a wrong O-Se axis here. The real shared site is the copper one.

note: No reference line was printed for this host, so the P4/nmm assignment rests on the compound being a very well known one and mp_id is left null. Measured 12-301 K, no structural transition. Note that the silver content here, 20 to 40 per cent of the copper, is alloying rather than doping; a stage 3 treatment that reports it as a dilute dopant level would misdescribe it.

basis: Two of the three compositions are Ag5Te2Cl1-xBrx at the 5:2:1 ratio -- Ag5Te2Cl0.6Br0.4 and Ag5Te2Cl0.4Br0.6 -- which is the Ag5Te2Cl type already proposed from the Ag-Cl-Te host. The third, Ag10Te4Br1.6Cl1.4, is the 10:4:3 compound, the sibling type proposed from Ag-Br-Te. The two are distinct structures in the same chemistry and the same publications, so this host pools both and has to be split on the Ag:Te:X ratio. The papers are on partial anion substitution in these silver telluride halides and on materials for resistivity switching, both of which treat the two stoichiometries as separate compounds.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: halide
solid_solution_axis.note: Chlorine and bromine are both group 17 and share the halide site in both stoichiometries, so this is genuine isoelectronic substitution and the papers describe it as partial anion substitution. It tunes the cell size and the silver-ion mobility without changing the electron count.

note: Splitting rule for stage 2: Ag5Te2X is ag5te2cl_type, Ag10Te4X3 is ag10te4br3_type. [ref 2] offers one line, Ag10Te4BrCl P2_1/c (14) mp-1229222 at hull 0.008 with no ICSD reference, which matches the 10:4:3 composition rather than the 5:2:1 one and so belongs to the alternative prototype, not the primary. Confidence is medium because neither proposed type has a settled space group -- the 5:2:1 entry infers Pnma from the bromide analogue and the 10:4:3 entry records its cell as unsettled. Both families are silver-ion conductors that disorder to a higher-symmetry silver-mobile phase on heating; the measured window is 302-499 K, which is where such transitions commonly sit in silver chalcogenide halides, so spans_transition is left false only because no temperature is established for either compound. Worth reading the papers for it.

basis: The three compositions are Ag2Te with two, five and nine carbon per formula unit, and the paper is on an n-type carbon nanotube and silver telluride nanohybrid buckypaper. Carbon is the majority element in every sample and it is nanotube, not a lattice constituent of the telluride. So the material is two phases in contact -- Ag2Te particles decorating a carbon nanotube network -- and the carbon fraction is the mixing ratio of the composite, not a stoichiometry. No single prototype describes it.

dopant_roles.basis: Carbon nanotubes forming the buckypaper scaffold. It is the majority element by count and a host element by the 5 per cent rule, but it is a separate phase: it carries the current and the mechanical integrity while the Ag2Te supplies the n-type character. Recorded so a stage 3 pass cannot read C5 or C9 as a stoichiometric coefficient.

note: Two matters to carry forward. First, the telluride component: I name acanthite_ag2s rather than ag2se_naumannite for it, because Ag2Te hessite is monoclinic P2_1/c and the acanthite entry was proposed precisely to separate the monoclinic ambient phase from the orthorhombic P2_12_12_1 naumannite one. That disagrees with the earlier Ag-Te record in this ledger, at chunk 3 rank 125, which predates the acanthite proposal and used ag2se_naumannite; the two should be reconciled at v4 review rather than left to differ silently. Second, the transition: Ag2Te converts from the monoclinic ambient phase to the cubic superionic one near 418 K, and the measured window here is 324-539 K, so the telluride component does cross it. spans_transition is recorded false because the host label is a composite and a phase array hung off composite_multiphase would attribute the transition to the wrong object; the crossing is stated here instead and should be picked up once the composite is split. Note also that the taxonomy files the high-temperature phase as bcc_superionic, whereas Ag2Te above 418 K is face-centred cubic rather than body-centred.

basis: A single composition, CeAgSb2, in three samples including two single crystals, with papers on the thermoelectric power of RAgSb2 for R = Y, La, Ce and Dy and on Kondo lattice behaviour in CeTSb2 compounds. RAgSb2 is the HfCuSi2 112 type: tetragonal P4/nmm, rare-earth and silver-antimony slabs alternating with flat square nets of antimony, and it is those square nets that produce the linearly dispersing bands and the large magnetoresistance these papers measure. The same paper supplies the LaAgSb2 and YAgSb2 samples in two other hosts in this chunk, and all three are the same structure type.
note: I do not follow [ref 2] here. Its only entry for this host is Ce2(AgSb)3 P4/mmm (123) mp-1206228 at hull 0.962 with no ICSD reference -- a computed 2:3:3 ordering that is neither the measured composition nor a credible phase at nearly one electronvolt per atom above the hull. CeAgSb2 itself is absent from the snapshot, which is why mp_id is null. The sibling hosts Ag-La-Sb and Ag-Sb-Y do have the right P4/nmm entries, mp-20271 and mp-1078739, and those confirm the structure type for the family even though not for the cerium member. Measured 10-295 K. CeAgSb2 orders ferromagnetically near 9.6 K, at the very bottom of the window; that is magnetic, not structural.

basis: Three compositions of Ag1-xCuxTlTe at x = 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4, from a paper on enhancing the figure of merit of AgTlTe by tuning the carrier concentration. The material is a definite ternary line compound, AgTlTe, and it is crystalline -- but I do not know its structure type with enough confidence to name one, and neither reference printed any entry for this host. Rather than force it into a silver chalcogenide or a thallium telluride entry on the strength of the elements alone, it is parked as unresolved crystalline and flagged.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu for Ag at 20 to 40 per cent of the silver site. Both are group 11 and monovalent, so the substitution adds no carriers directly; the paper describes it as tuning the carrier concentration, which in a compound of this kind happens through the vacancy population on the silver site rather than through the copper valence. Cu is a host element by the 5 per cent rule and is recorded because it is the swept variable.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: monovalent cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Assumed rather than confirmed: without the structure type I cannot state that silver and copper occupy one crystallographic site, only that they are interchangeable in the formula.

note: This is the weakest assignment in the chunk and should go to the review queue. What is known: AgTlTe is a narrow-gap semiconductor studied by the same group that worked on Tl9BiTe6 and TlBiTe2, thallium chalcogenides are prone to low-symmetry cells with stereochemically active lone pairs, and the analogous Tl5Te3 and Tl2Te families each have their own taxonomy entry. What is not known to me is which of those, if any, AgTlTe belongs to, so tl5te3 is deliberately not offered as an alternative -- the stoichiometry does not match it and guessing would put a wrong space group into the ledger. One paper and one structure refinement would settle it. Measured 300-563 K.

basis: Three compositions of AgInxSb1-xTe2 at x = 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6, from a paper on a high-pressure route to thermoelectrics with low thermal conductivity. This is the AIST chemistry, the phase-change family, and its thermoelectrically interesting form is the cation-disordered rocksalt: silver, indium and antimony share one face-centred cubic cation site at random against a tellurium anion lattice. That is the same call already recorded in this ledger for the parent host Ag-Sb-Te, where AgSbTe2 was assigned rocksalt because every ordered Materials Project ternary sat far above the hull -- the expected signature of a disordered phase rather than evidence against it. High-pressure synthesis favours the dense cubic form over the tetrahedral one.
note: The alternative is named because the two end members of this pseudo-binary do not share a structure: AgSbTe2 is the disordered rocksalt, but AgInTe2 is tetragonal chalcopyrite, I-42d, with ordered tetrahedral coordination. Somewhere along the line the structure changes, and these samples sit at x = 0.4 to 0.6, in the middle where it could go either way -- which is why confidence is medium rather than high and why is_mixed is left false only on the grounds that all three samples sit in the same narrow band. Indium and antimony are not isoelectronic, group 13 against group 15, so no solid-solution axis is recorded: substituting In for Sb removes two electrons per substitution and is a doping axis, which is plausibly what the paper is using it for. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null. Measured 11-300 K.

basis: One composition, marked IQC in the string itself -- Ag42In42Yb16 is the Tsai-type icosahedral quasicrystal, and the paper is on the electrical and thermal transport properties of icosahedral and decagonal quasicrystals. Ag-In-Yb is the textbook stable binary-like i-phase, built from Tsai clusters with ytterbium at the cluster shell, and it is the one quasicrystal whose surface and bulk structure are best determined. There is no periodic cell.
note: The README flags this prototype as one where stage 2 must map to an approximant and say so, and that applies here. [ref 2] offers YbInAg2 Fm-3m (225) mp-865789 at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference; that is a Heusler-like 1:1:2 cubic ordering, not an approximant of the Tsai i-phase, and it is not what was measured. The genuine periodic relative is the YbCd6-type 1/1 cubic approximant, Im-3, into which Ag-In-Yb also forms at a nearby composition. mp_id is left null rather than filled with the mp-865789 entry. Measured 11-303 K, which is the range where the characteristic quasicrystalline transport -- resistivity rising as temperature falls -- is seen.

basis: A single composition, LaAgSb2, in three single crystals, from the same RAgSb2 thermoelectric power study as the cerium and yttrium hosts in this chunk. [ref 2] confirms the type directly: LaAgSb2 P4/nmm (129) mp-20271 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, top-ranked. That is the HfCuSi2 112 structure -- alternating LaSb and AgSb slabs separated by flat square nets of antimony -- and LaAgSb2 is the best-studied member, the one whose square-net Dirac bands and charge-density-wave order are mapped in detail.
note: The second [ref 2] entry, La2AgSb3 P4/mmm (123) mp-1206475 at hull 3.031, is a computed ordering three electronvolts per atom above the hull and is disregarded. One caveat on spans_transition: LaAgSb2 has charge-density-wave transitions near 207 K and 186 K, both inside the measured 12-292 K window. They are periodic lattice distortions that superstructure the antimony square net rather than changes of prototype, so spans_transition stays false, but they produce clear anomalies in the thermopower and the data across them are not one regime. This is the kind of case where a structural transition flag would be misleading and a transport-regime flag would not exist.

basis: The compositions are written as Agx(TaN)1-x at x = 0.25, 0.27 and 0.30, the curator transcription records a sputtering power in watts per square centimetre for the silver rather than a chemical formula, and the paper is on the resistivity and temperature coefficient of resistance of co-sputtered TaN-(Ag, Cu) films. Co-sputtering silver with a nitride does not make a ternary: silver has no solubility in TaN and precipitates as metal, so these are metal-ceramic nanocomposite films -- silver grains in a rocksalt TaN matrix at a quarter to a third by atom count. Two phases, no single structure.

dopant_roles.basis: Metallic silver precipitated as a separate phase during co-sputtering. The curator detail gives the silver target power rather than a composition, which is the tell that the silver fraction is a deposition parameter and not a lattice occupancy. It is a host element by the 5 per cent rule and is recorded here so it is not read as a nitride constituent.

note: The two constituents are named as alternatives for stage 2: TaN is rocksalt_nitride_carbide, cubic Fm-3m, and the silver is face-centred cubic metal. Neither reference printed a line for this host. Two cautions. First, TaN as sputtered is commonly substoichiometric, TaN1-x, and the nitrogen vacancy content is the carrier knob for that phase -- the taxonomy entry itself notes this for TaN0.89 -- so the nominal 1:1 in these strings should not be trusted. Second, sputtered tantalum nitride also forms a hexagonal phase, so even the ceramic component may not be the rocksalt one; these are films, and a metastable polymorph is reachable here that would not form in bulk. Measured 186-367 K, and the paper is about the temperature coefficient of resistance rather than about a thermoelectric figure of merit.

basis: The three compositions are near-equal lead and tellurium with silver and oxygen alongside -- Pb0.374Te0.357Ag0.143O0.126 and two similar -- and the paper is on enhancing the thermoelectric power of PbTe thin films by silver ion implantation. Stripping the silver and oxygen leaves Pb:Te at very close to 1:1, so the host is PbTe, cubic rocksalt Fm-3m, and the other two elements are implanted silver and film oxidation rather than constituents of a quaternary compound.

dopant_roles.basis: Implanted silver. In PbTe silver on the lead site is a monovalent cation replacing a divalent one and acts as an acceptor, which is the p-type enhancement the paper reports. Silver also enters lead telluride interstitially, where it donates instead, and implantation produces both; the substitutional channel is recorded as the dominant one but stage 2 should not assume the interstitial population is zero. The 5 to 14 atomic per cent quoted here is an implanted near-surface concentration, not a bulk solubility -- silver dissolves in PbTe only to well under one per cent at equilibrium, so much of it is likely precipitated.

Oxygen at 12 to 14 atomic per cent in a thin film. PbTe has no oxygen site; this is surface and grain-boundary oxidation of the film, picked up by whatever analysis produced the composition. It is a host element by the 5 per cent rule only because the measured fraction is high, which is itself a sign the film is substantially oxidised.

note: No reference line was printed for this host, but PbTe rocksalt is not in doubt and mp_id is left null for stage 2 to resolve from the Pb-Te host rather than from this quaternary string. Measured 290-401 K, well below any transition of PbTe. The oxygen fraction is worth a second look: at this level the samples are as much lead and tellurium oxide as telluride, and a thermopower measured on such a film is not a bulk PbTe number.

basis: A single composition, YAgSb2, in three single crystals, from the same RAgSb2 study as the lanthanum and cerium hosts here. [ref 2] gives YAgSb2 P4/nmm (129) mp-1078739 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference, which is the HfCuSi2 112 cell. Yttrium is the non-magnetic member of the series, which is why it is measured alongside the rare earths -- it isolates the square-net band structure from the 4f magnetism.
note: The single ICSD reference behind mp-1078739 is below the threshold this chunk file calls weak, so the database match is thin on its own. It is not carrying the assignment: the structure type is established by the family -- LaAgSb2 at mp-20271 has five references in the same P4/nmm setting -- and by the paper treating all four RAgSb2 members as isostructural. The second entry, Y2AgSb3 P4/mmm mp-1206111 at hull 3.079, is a computed ordering and is disregarded. Measured 10-294 K; YAgSb2 has a charge-density-wave anomaly in the same region as LaAgSb2, which is a lattice modulation within the prototype rather than a transition out of it.

basis: All three compositions are tin telluride with a tenth of an atom of silver and a small third element -- Sn0.94Gd0.06Ag0.11Te, Sn0.85In0.05Ag0.10Te, Sn0.82In0.06Ag0.12Te -- and the papers are on promoting SnTe as an eco-friendly replacement for p-type PbTe and on solvothermally synthesised doped SnTe. SnTe is cubic rocksalt Fm-3m, the tin analogue of PbTe, and every substituent here sits on the cation site of that lattice.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag at about a tenth of an atom per formula unit, a host element by the 5 per cent rule but functionally a dopant. Monovalent silver on the divalent tin site is an acceptor, and in SnTe -- which is already heavily p-type from intrinsic tin vacancies -- silver is used together with a donor to bring the carrier concentration back down and to introduce band convergence. Silver also promotes AgSnSe2-like nanoscale precipitates in these alloys, so some of it may not be in solution.

In at 5 to 6 atomic per cent on the tin site. Indium in SnTe is the standard resonant-level dopant: its impurity state sits inside the valence band and distorts the density of states there, which raises the Seebeck coefficient at fixed carrier concentration. That is a different mechanism from ordinary acceptor doping and is why indium and silver are used together rather than either alone.

Gd at 6 atomic per cent on the tin site. Trivalent gadolinium replacing divalent tin is a donor, which compensates the intrinsic tin vacancies; rare-earth substitution in SnTe is also used to converge the light and heavy valence bands. One sample only.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] here. Its single entry is AgSnTe2 P4/mmm (123) mp-1229006 at hull 0.052 with no ICSD reference -- a computed tetragonal ordering of a 1:1:2 compound that is not what these samples are. The samples are SnTe with roughly a tenth of an atom of silver, not a silver tin telluride line compound, so mp_id is left null and the rocksalt cell should be resolved from the Sn-Te host in stage 2. Measured 300-824 K, no structural transition -- the rhombohedral distortion of SnTe occurs on cooling below about 100 K and heavy doping suppresses it further, so it is nowhere near this window.

basis: One composition written as (InAs)33.4(AlSb)31.8, from a paper on nanoscale heat transfer and nanostructured thermoelectrics. InAs and AlSb are both zincblende III-V semiconductors and their lattice parameters differ by about 1.3 per cent, which is precisely why the pair is used together: it is the standard nearly lattice-matched system for superlattices grown to study cross-plane phonon transport. Both components are the same prototype, so the composite formula does not create a second structure.
note: is_mixed is false but the material is still two distinct compounds: an InAs and AlSb superlattice is not an (InAlAsSb) alloy, and the near-equal fractions in the string are the layer thickness ratio, not a stoichiometry. Stage 2 should resolve two separate zincblende cells, InAs and AlSb, rather than one quaternary entry -- the same prototype twice. Neither reference printed a line for this host and mp_id is null. Measured 81-299 K, the range where superlattice thermal conductivity reduction is measured. Nothing here is a bulk thermoelectric.

basis: The arithmetic settles it. K10Ba14Al35Ga4Sn97 has a framework of 35 + 4 + 97 = 136 atoms and 10 + 14 = 24 guests; K9Ba15Al38Sn98 has 136 framework atoms and 24 guests. A24E136 is the type II clathrate cell exactly -- sixteen small dodecahedral cages and eight large hexakaidecahedral ones per unit cell -- and one of the two papers is titled on the preparation and thermoelectric properties of sintered type-II clathrates. Aluminium and gallium substitute into the tin framework to set the electron count against the guest charge.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga4 out of 136 framework sites in one of the two compositions, alongside 35 aluminium. Gallium and aluminium are both trivalent and both replace tetravalent tin in the covalent cage framework, each removing one electron; the total trivalent count is what balances the charge donated by the potassium and barium guests and decides whether the clathrate is metallic or semiconducting. This is framework substitution, not doping, and reporting it as a dilute impurity would hide the electron-counting rule it belongs to.

note: Potassium and barium are the cage guests rather than framework atoms, and their split -- roughly 10 potassium to 14 barium, or 9 to 15 -- matters as much as the framework substitution does, because the two contribute one and two electrons respectively. Type II clathrates also differ from type I in that the guest sites can be partially empty, so the guest count is a variable rather than a fixed 24; here it happens to be full. Neither reference printed a line for this host and mp_id is null. Measured 100-637 K, no structural transition. The second paper predicts ground-state guest and framework orderings computationally, so an ordered model may exist in the literature even though the measured material is likely disordered on both sublattices.

basis: The three compositions are written as (Al2O3)x(Cr3C2)1-x at 20, 30 and 40 per cent carbide, and the paper is on the heat conduction of composites and its dependence on the microstructure. Alumina and chromium carbide are mutually insoluble at these proportions -- an oxide and a carbide with no common structure -- so these are two-phase ceramics deliberately made to vary the second-phase fraction. The whole point of the paper is the microstructure, which is another way of saying the material is not one phase.
note: Both constituents already have entries, so stage 2 has somewhere to send them: Al2O3 is corundum, rhombohedral R-3c, and Cr3C2 is the orthorhombic Pnma carbide proposed earlier in this annotation as cr3c2_orthorhombic. Neither reference printed a line for this host. Measured 297-871 K; neither component transforms in that range. This host is a thermal-conductivity study rather than a thermoelectric one, which is worth knowing before any figure of merit is computed from it.

basis: The compositions are written as (TiC)x(Ni3Al)1-x at 77, 60 and 36 per cent carbide, and the paper is on the densification and thermal properties of TiC-Ni3Al composite materials. This is a cermet: titanium carbide particles bonded by a nickel aluminide metal phase, the standard binder system for TiC. The two are separate phases by design -- the Ni3Al is there to sinter and toughen the carbide, not to dissolve in it -- so no single prototype applies.
note: Both constituents are named for stage 2: TiC is rocksalt_nitride_carbide, cubic Fm-3m, and Ni3Al is the L1_2 ordered face-centred cubic gamma-prime phase, cu3au_l12, Pm-3m. Two cautions. TiC in a cermet is almost always carbon-deficient, TiC1-x, and the carbon vacancy content is what sets its electronic structure -- the nominal 1:1 in the composition string should not be trusted. And titanium carbide does dissolve some nickel and aluminium at sintering temperature, so the interface region is a graded solid solution rather than a sharp boundary; the composition string cannot show that. Measured 290-1316 K, a very wide window. Ni3Al stays L1_2 up to its melting point, so nothing transforms structurally, but the upper end is above where a nickel-based binder softens.

basis: The three compositions are cobalt-rich to the point of excluding any stoichiometric oxide -- Co63Al13O24, Co66Al11O23, Co74Al8O18 -- with two to five times more cobalt than aluminium and far too little oxygen to oxidise the cobalt. The paper is on the transport properties of ferromagnetic granular Co-Al-O films, and granular is the operative word: these are metallic cobalt nanograins embedded in an amorphous aluminium oxide matrix, the standard tunnelling-magnetoresistance film system. The oxygen is bound to the aluminium, the cobalt is metal.
note: I disagree with [ref 2] on this host and record it rather than following it. Every entry it offers is a cobalt aluminate: Al2CoO4 Fd-3m (227) mp-36447 with one ICSD reference, then AlCoO3 and three further Al2CoO4 orderings. Spinel CoAl2O4 is a real compound and is what this chemistry makes at equilibrium with enough oxygen -- but it has two aluminium per cobalt and four oxygen, and these films have the cobalt-to-aluminium ratio the wrong way round by a factor of five and nowhere near enough oxygen. This is the Al-O-Zn situation the chunk header warns about, in a sharper form: the reference describes which phase exists in the chemistry, not what was sputtered. Assigning spinel here would be flatly wrong. Stage 2 should resolve metallic cobalt, hexagonal close-packed or face-centred cubic, plus an amorphous alumina matrix, and mp_id stays null for the matrix. Measured 10-59 K only, a very narrow low-temperature window.

basis: Three compositions of Co2TiAl1-xSix at x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, and the paper is on tuning the carrier concentration for thermoelectric application in a Heusler system. Co2TiAl and Co2TiSi are both full Heusler compounds, L2_1 ordered, cubic Fm-3m, with cobalt on the two tetrahedral sublattices, titanium and the main-group element alternating on the octahedral ones. The entire series is one structure; only the valence electron count moves.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: main-group site of the L2_1 cell, the 4b position
solid_solution_axis.note: Aluminium and silicon are adjacent groups, 13 and 14, so this is NOT isoelectronic substitution and the axis should not be labelled as such. Each silicon for aluminium adds one valence electron per formula unit, taking Co2TiAl from 25 to Co2TiSi at 26 -- and 26 is where the Slater-Pauling rule puts the half-metallic gap for this family. Sweeping x is sweeping the Fermi level across that gap, which is precisely the carrier-concentration tuning in the title.

note: Neither reference printed a line for this host, so mp_id is null. Measured 10-1034 K. Full Heuslers of this family do not change structure over that range, but two things do vary within the prototype and matter for stage 2: the degree of L2_1 against B2 antisite order, which these alloys lose progressively on heating and which controls the half-metallic gap, and whether the samples are single phase at intermediate x. No transition is recorded because antisite disordering is a continuous process without a defined temperature here.

basis: All three composition strings carry the IAC marker and sit at Al66-68, Cu5-7, Ir26.7, with the iridium fraction held fixed while copper replaces aluminium. The paper is on the anomalous effects of copper doping on the structural and thermoelectric properties of an Al-Ir phase, and the Al-Ir system at roughly Al73(TM)27 is one of the standard aluminium-transition-metal approximant regions -- large cubic or orthorhombic cells built from the same icosahedral clusters as the quasicrystal, with a periodic lattice. The sibling host Al-Ir-Rh in this same chunk is the same chemistry and the same marker.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu at 5 to 7 atomic per cent, increasing while aluminium decreases and iridium is held constant, which is the signature of a substitution on the aluminium sublattice rather than an addition. Copper has a different electron count from aluminium, so in a Hume-Rothery phase like this it moves the electron-per-atom ratio and with it the position of the pseudogap at the Fermi level -- which is what the paper means by anomalous effects on the thermoelectric properties. Cu is a host element by the 5 per cent rule.

note: I do not follow [ref 2] here. It offers Al2CuIr Cmme (67) mp-1079890 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, which is a genuine ternary line compound -- but at Al50Cu25Ir25, and these samples are Al67Cu6Ir27. The copper content is off by a factor of four and the aluminium by a third, so mp-1079890 is a different material in the same chemistry, not the measured one. mp_id is left null. The README already flags this prototype as one where no exact structure may exist; here the specific approximant of the Al-Ir system has to be identified from the paper before any cell is attached. Measured 363-962 K, a high-temperature window where approximant phases can order or transform between related superstructures -- the paper reports structural effects of copper doping, so that should be read rather than assumed absent.

basis: All three compositions are AB2O4 with the oxygen fixed at four: Mg0.4Al0.8Li0.30Fe1.50O4 and Mg0.5Al1.0Li0.25Fe1.25O4 are magnesium- and aluminium-substituted lithium ferrite, and Mg0.75Fe0.41Al1.85O4 is iron-substituted magnesium aluminate. Lithium ferrite Li0.5Fe2.5O4, MgFe2O4, MgAl2O4 and Fe3O4 are all spinels, and the cations here total 3 per 4 oxygen in every case. The first paper is on thermoelectric power of magnesium- and aluminium-substituted lithium ferrites, and the second measures the thermal conductivity of MgAl2O4 and Fe3O4 among others.

dopant_roles.basis: Li at 0.25 to 0.30 per formula unit. This is not an impurity: it is the defining constituent of lithium ferrite, Li0.5Fe2.5O4, where monovalent lithium and trivalent iron order on the octahedral site in a 1:3 pattern that lowers the symmetry from Fd-3m to P4_332. The lithium content falling under 5 atomic per cent of the whole formula is an artefact of oxygen and iron dominating the atom count, not a sign of dilution. Stage 3 must not report it as a doping level.

note: I disagree with the [ref 2] ranking. Every entry it offers is magnesium-rich and non-spinel -- Mg14AlFeO16 Pmmm mp-1036658, Mg30AlFeO32 P4/mmm mp-1038379, Mg6AlFeO8, MgAlFeO4 Imma mp-1222041, none with an ICSD reference -- which are computed substitutional orderings in a rocksalt MgO supercell, not the spinel these samples are. The cation-to-oxygen ratio is the discriminant: 3 to 4 here, 1 to 1 in those entries. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should resolve MgAl2O4 and the lithium ferrite cell directly. One structural caution: the ordered lithium ferrite is P4_332 rather than Fd-3m and it disorders to the Fd-3m spinel near 1030 K, above the 14-677 K window here, so the samples should be in the ordered form throughout. Whether the substituted compositions retain that ordering at these Mg and Al levels is a question for the paper.

basis: Three compositions of Ru2-xFexNbAl at x = 0.25, 0.38 and 0.50, and the paper names the family in its own title -- physical properties of the full Heusler-type Ru2-xFexNbAl. The formula is X2YZ with ruthenium and iron sharing the X sublattice, niobium on Y and aluminium on Z: the L2_1 ordered cubic Fm-3m cell. Ru2NbAl is a 24-valence-electron full Heusler, the count at which this family opens a gap, which is why it appears in thermoelectric work.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the X sublattice of the L2_1 cell, the two tetrahedral 8c positions
solid_solution_axis.note: Iron and ruthenium are both group 8, so this is isoelectronic on the group count -- but it is not electronically neutral in a Heusler, because the 3d and 4d states hybridise differently with the niobium and aluminium and the gap width follows. x is given here as the iron share of the two X sites, 0.25 to 0.50 iron atoms out of two.

note: Neither reference printed a line for this host, so mp_id is null. Measured 11-298 K only, a low-temperature window. The property to watch in stage 2 is the site order rather than the space group: substituting iron onto the ruthenium sublattice of a full Heusler commonly drives partial B2 or A2 disorder, and in this family the gap and hence the thermopower depend on that order. The composition string cannot show it.

basis: Three compositions of Al1-xSbxFeO3 at x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, from a paper on the influence of Sb3+ cations on the structural, magnetic and electrical properties of the material. The formula is a stoichiometric ABO3 oxide and the samples are crystalline, but I am not confident which structure type it is, and neither reference printed any entry for this host. Rather than assert one, it is parked and flagged.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the A site of the ABO3 formula, unconfirmed
solid_solution_axis.note: Aluminium and antimony are not the same group and Sb3+ carries a stereochemically active lone pair while Al3+ does not, so although both are trivalent they are very unlikely to be comfortable on one site. That mismatch is probably the reason the paper is about the structural influence of the antimony, and it is also why the axis is recorded with the site unconfirmed.

note: What I can say and what I cannot. The parent AlFeO3 is not a perovskite and not corundum: it takes the GaFeO3 or kappa-Al2O3 structure, orthorhombic Pna2_1, which is a polar corundum-derived framework with mixed tetrahedral and octahedral cation sites. That is my best candidate for x near zero and it is offered as a lead, not as an assignment -- it is not in the taxonomy and I will not propose a prototype on a guess about which parent the paper actually made. At x = 0.75 the material is antimony-dominated on the A site and there is no reason to expect the same framework at all. Three things would settle it: the reported space group, whether the series is single phase across x, and whether the antimony is trivalent throughout as the title asserts. This host belongs in the review queue. Measured 200-398 K.

basis: One composition, Fe2V0.8W0.2Al, in bulk and film samples. Fe2VAl is the best-known full Heusler thermoelectric: L2_1 ordered, cubic Fm-3m, a 24-valence-electron pseudogap semimetal whose thermopower is tuned by moving off that count. Tungsten substituting for vanadium is the heavy-element version of that tuning, adding electrons and mass. Both papers name the Heusler structure -- one on the thermoelectric performance of a metastable thin-film Heusler alloy, the other on stoichiometric and off-stoichiometric full Heusler compounds.

other_polymorphs.note: The chunk file flags film samples in this host, and the Nature paper is titled on a metastable thin-film Heusler alloy -- the whole claim is that epitaxial growth reaches a phase, and a power factor, that bulk synthesis of the same composition does not. So the film and the bulk samples here are not interchangeable even though they share a composition string. The metastable variant is recorded as a distinct structure of the same prototype family rather than as a separate prototype, because what differs is the site occupancy and strain state rather than the structure type. Space group and mp_id are left null: naming one from memory is exactly what this field is meant to prevent.

dopant_roles.basis: W at 0.2 per formula unit on the vanadium site, a host element by the 5 per cent rule. Tungsten is in the same group as vanadium in the older numbering but has five more core d electrons and roughly four times the mass; in Fe2VAl the effect is to add carriers and to scatter phonons strongly through the mass contrast, both of which raise the figure of merit. It is the substitution the two papers are built around.

note: Neither reference printed a line for this host and mp_id is null throughout. Measured 11-818 K for the robust range. The bulk material stays L2_1 across that window, but the degree of antisite order does not, and in Fe2VAl the pseudogap is destroyed by disorder -- so annealing history matters more here than in most hosts. Stage 2 should keep the film and bulk samples separable; sample_form is the only field that currently distinguishes them.

basis: All three composition strings carry the IQC marker and sit at Al61-65, Pd20.7, Mn8.4 with gallium replacing aluminium at 6, 8 and 10 per cent. Al-Pd-Mn near Al70Pd21Mn9 is the archetypal stable face-centred icosahedral quasicrystal, and the paper is on structural, tribological and resistivity studies of gallium-substituted Al-Pd-Mn. The curator transcription confirms it directly: one sample is described as a nearly single phase face centred icosahedral phase. There is no periodic cell.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga at 6 to 10 atomic per cent, rising exactly as the aluminium falls, so it is a substitution on the aluminium positions of the icosahedral structure. Gallium is isoelectronic with aluminium -- both group 13 -- which is why it can be pushed this far without destroying the quasicrystal; what it changes is the atomic size and the electron density, and with them the stability field. Recorded as substitutional rather than isoelectronic_substitution because in a quasicrystal there is no single crystallographic site to be isoelectronic on, and because the curator detail shows the substitution is destabilising the phase rather than merely tuning it.

note: The important finding for this host comes from the curator, not from me, and it outranks any inference from the formula: two of the three samples are recorded as containing intermetallic phases in addition to the icosahedral quasicrystal, and only one as nearly single phase. So two thirds of this host is a mixture. is_mixed is left false because I cannot name the second phase -- the Al-Pd-Mn system has several crystalline approximants and line compounds near this composition, and asserting one would be a guess -- but the record should not be read as a claim that these samples are single phase. Transport measured on a two-phase quasicrystal is not a quasicrystal measurement. The README already flags this prototype as having no periodic structure; mp_id is null and stage 2 must map to an approximant and say so. Measured 19-247 K.

basis: Three compositions of Mn2.7Cr0.3Si4Al2-yIny at y = 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0, from a paper on structural investigation and indium substitution in a thermoelectric manganese silicide-aluminide. The parent stoichiometry is Mn3Si4Al2 -- a definite ternary line compound, crystalline, with the indium clearly substituting on the aluminium site -- but I cannot name its structure type with confidence, and neither reference printed an entry for this host. It is parked rather than forced.

dopant_roles.basis: Cr0.3 against Mn2.7, held constant across all three samples while the indium is varied. A fixed minor constituent that does not move is a deliberate part of the parent composition rather than a doping series: chromium has one fewer valence electron than manganese, so it sets the carrier concentration and is then left alone while the second substitution is swept. Recorded as substitutional on the transition-metal site.

In from 0.6 to 1.0 per formula unit, rising exactly as the aluminium falls from 1.4 to 1.0. Indium and aluminium are both group 13, so this adds no electrons; it is a size and mass substitution, which in a thermoelectric is aimed at the lattice thermal conductivity. In is a host element by the 5 per cent rule and is the variable the paper is named for.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: main-group site, unconfirmed
solid_solution_axis.note: Both group 13 and genuinely isoelectronic, so this is a clean solid-solution axis, expressed here as the indium share of the two main-group positions per formula unit. Whether they share one crystallographic site cannot be confirmed without the structure type.

note: Two candidates I considered and rejected as assignments, recorded so the next pass does not have to rediscover them. hms_chimney_ladder: the higher manganese silicides sit at MnSi1.73, and (Si+Al+In) per Mn here is 2.0, which is outside that family. al2fe3si3_tau2: the tau2 phase is at Al26Fe37Si37 against Al22Mn33Si44 here, close in spirit -- a low-symmetry transition-metal aluminide-silicide -- but a different stoichiometry and a different transition metal, and that entry is already recorded as having an unresolved space group of its own. Neither is offered in alt_prototype_ids because an alternative should be a structure the host might actually hold, not the nearest thing in the file. This host needs the paper, which is titled as a structural investigation and so will state the answer. Measured 298-898 K.

basis: All three compositions are Al73.3(Rh,Ir)26.7 with the IAC marker, the rhodium and iridium exchanging while the total transition-metal content is held exactly fixed, and the paper is titled on band engineering in Al-TM quasicrystalline approximants for TM = Rh and Ir. Al73.3TM26.7 is a well-defined approximant composition in these systems -- a periodic crystal built from the same icosahedral clusters as the quasicrystal, with a pseudogap at the Fermi level that band engineering is aimed at. The title names the family outright.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the transition-metal positions of the approximant cluster
solid_solution_axis.note: Rhodium and iridium are both group 9 and the substitution is complete and continuous from one to the other at fixed total transition-metal content, which is as clean an isoelectronic axis as this chunk contains. x is the rhodium share of the transition metal. The band engineering in the title works through the 4d against 5d hybridisation with the aluminium sp states rather than through electron count.

note: I do not follow [ref 2]. Its only entry is Al2IrRh Fm-3m (225) mp-862694 at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference -- a Heusler-like 2:1:1 cubic ordering at Al50Ir25Rh25, whereas these samples are Al73.3 with the transition metals at 26.7 together. The aluminium content is off by nearly half, so that entry is a different compound in the same chemistry. mp_id is left null and the specific approximant has to come from the paper. Measured 299-903 K.

basis: Two of the three compositions are SrLaAlO4, written once in each element order, which is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper member: a single perovskite LaAlO3 layer alternating with a rocksalt SrO layer, tetragonal I4/mmm, the standard K2NiF4 structure and a common epitaxial substrate. The third, (La0.7Sr0.3)(Al0.8Fe0.2)O3, is a straight ABO3 perovskite with no rocksalt layer at all. The host holds both and must be split on the Sr-to-La ratio and the oxygen count.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.2 on the B site of the (La,Sr)(Al,Fe)O3 perovskite, one composition only. Iron replacing aluminium turns an insulating band-gap perovskite into a conducting one: aluminium contributes no d states near the Fermi level and iron does, so the substitution creates the transport the paper measures. That paper is on temperature-independent sensors based on perovskite-type oxides, so the iron content is the working variable, not an impurity.

note: Splitting rule for stage 2: an AO4 composition with Sr and La in a 1:1 ratio is ruddlesden_popper; an ABO3 composition is perovskite. I also disagree with the [ref 2] ranking on the first of those. It gives SrLaAlO4 I4mm (107) mp-1218184 at hull 0.017, a polar tetragonal setting, whereas SrLaAlO4 is centrosymmetric I4/mmm (139) in every experimental report and is used as a substrate precisely because that cell is well characterised. mp-1218184 has no ICSD reference; it is a computed cation-ordering model. The other entries offered -- Sr2LaAlO5, SrLa2Al2O7 I4/mmm mp-1218238, SrLaAl3O7 -- are different stoichiometries, though SrLa2Al2O7 is worth noting as the n = 2 Ruddlesden-Popper member of the same series. mp_id is left null. Confidence is medium because the host pools three different papers and one composition is a thin film, where the substrate fixes the strain state and can stabilise a cell the bulk does not take. Measured 13-348 K robust, full span to 1263 K.

basis: Two compositions. LuAl3, in two samples, is the L1_2 ordered face-centred cubic phase, Pm-3m, the AuCu3 type -- and [ref 2] confirms it, LuAl3 Pm-3m (221) mp-2805 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references. LuAl2, in one sample, is a different structure entirely: the cubic C15 Laves phase, Fd-3m, given at mp-1234 with 6 ICSD references. The papers are on RAl3 solid solutions, on the intermediate valence compound YbAl3 and on nonmagnetic reference compounds, so the trialuminide is the object of interest and the dialuminide the comparison.
note: Splitting rule for stage 2 is simply the Al-to-Lu ratio: 3 gives cu3au_l12 at mp-2805, 2 gives laves_phase at mp-1234. Both are unambiguous in [ref 2] with four and six ICSD references respectively, so this is one of the cleaner mixed hosts -- two well-attested line compounds rather than an ambiguity. The remaining entries, LuAl Pbcm, Lu3Al2 and Lu3Al, are the other binaries of the system and are not in the compositions. Measured 10-300 K, no transition in either phase. Lutetium is the filled-4f member and is measured here as the nonmagnetic reference against which the ytterbium intermediate-valence behaviour in the sibling hosts Al-Lu-Yb and Al-Sn-Yb is read.

basis: Three compositions of Yb1-xLuxAl3 at x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of Yb1-x(Er,Lu)xAl3 solid solutions. Both end members are L1_2 ordered cubic trialuminides, Pm-3m: YbAl3 is the intermediate-valence thermoelectric and LuAl3 is confirmed by [ref 2] in the sibling host Al-Lu at mp-2805 with 4 ICSD references. Lutetium and ytterbium substitute freely on the rare-earth corner of that cell, so the whole series is one structure.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the rare-earth corner of the L1_2 cell, the 1a position
solid_solution_axis.note: Both are late rare earths and both trivalent in the usual counting, so structurally this is a clean substitution -- but electronically it is anything but isoelectronic. Ytterbium in YbAl3 is in an intermediate-valence state between 2+ and 3+ and lutetium is a filled-4f trivalent ion with no such physics, so x dilutes the Kondo lattice. Recorded as an axis because the composition varies continuously; it should not be read as a neutral substitution.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] here and record it rather than following it. Its only entry is YbLuAl4 F-43m (216) mp-1215433 at hull 0.023 with no ICSD reference -- a computed 1:1:4 ordering of the two rare earths on a Heusler-like cell, which is a plausible DFT model of the x = 0.5 composition but is not the same thing as a disordered L1_2 solid solution. The measured samples are a random alloy on the rare-earth site, not an ordered ternary, so mp_id is left null and stage 2 should resolve YbAl3 and LuAl3 separately. Measured 80-300 K, no structural transition. The thermopower here is dominated by the Kondo resonance of the ytterbium, so a substitution series is being used to move the characteristic temperature rather than to change the lattice.

basis: Two compositions, and they are different structures. UNiAl, in two single crystals, is 1:1:1 and takes the ZrNiAl type -- the ordered ternary derivative of Fe2P, hexagonal P-62m -- which [ref 2] gives directly as UAlNi P-62m (189) mp-1079086 with 7 ICSD references. UNi2Al3, in one sample, is the heavy-fermion superconductor and takes the PrNi2Al3 type, an ordered CaCu5 derivative, hexagonal P6/mmm, which [ref 2] carries as UAl3Ni2 P6/mmm (191) mp-2903 with 5 ICSD references. Both are well attested and both are in the taxonomy, so the host is mixed and splits on the Ni-to-U ratio.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] also lists UAlNi in Amm2 (38) at hull 0.172 with 7 ICSD references -- the same reference count as the P-62m entry it ranks first. Two settings of one formula each carrying seven references is a sign the ICSD holds both an ordered and a differently-described refinement rather than two distinct phases; the P-62m ZrNiAl description is the one the physics literature uses for UNiAl. Recorded so the parity in reference counts is not read as evidence for a second phase.

note: Splitting rule for stage 2: Ni:U of 1 is zrnial_fe2p at mp-1079086, Ni:U of 2 is prni2al3_ordered_cacu5 at mp-2903. Note that both [ref 2] entries sit well above the hull, at 0.158 and 0.108, despite carrying seven and five ICSD references between them. That is the expected signature of actinide compounds in a DFT database rather than evidence against the phases -- 5f states are poorly described by the functionals used for the snapshot -- and the ICSD counts are what should be believed here. Measured 12-283 K. UNi2Al3 orders antiferromagnetically near 4.6 K and superconducts below 1 K, and UNiAl orders near 19 K; all are electronic or magnetic, none structural, and the lower ones are below the window anyway.

basis: Two compositions, and neither is in either reference. YbNi0.8Al4.2, in two samples, is close to RTAl4 and is named in its own paper as a novel intermetallic compound with an enhanced thermoelectric power; that stoichiometry is the YNiAl4 type, orthorhombic Cmcm, proposed here as ynial4_cmcm. YbNi3Al9, in one sample, is a different compound at 1:3:9 -- the ErNi3Al9 type, trigonal and chiral in R32 -- and the paper for it describes YbNi3Al9 as a heavy fermion chiral magnet, which only makes sense in a Sohncke space group. Both are proposed in this chunk and the host splits on the Ni-to-Yb ratio.
note: I disagree with [ref 2] on this host, and the disagreement is the reason two prototypes had to be proposed. It offers Yb4Al23Ni6 C2/m mp-18482, YbAl2Ni Cmcm mp-12782, YbAlNi P-62m mp-1078733 and Yb2AlNi2 Immm mp-1207023, each with at most one ICSD reference, and not one of them is either measured composition -- the closest, YbAl2Ni, is 1:2:1 against 1:4.2:0.8 here. Taking mp-12782 because it shares a space group with the type I am assigning would be exactly the kind of nearest-formula substitution the project forbids, so mp_id is null for both prototypes. Confidence is medium rather than high for the same reason: the Cmcm setting of YbNi0.8Al4.2 rests on the YNiAl4 structure type rather than on an entry for this formula, and stage 2 should confirm it before attaching a cell. The off-stoichiometry, Ni-poor and Al-rich against ideal YbNiAl4, is the homogeneity range of that family rather than a doping level and must not be reported as one. Splitting rule: Ni:Yb near 1 is ynial4_cmcm, Ni:Yb of 3 is erni3al9_chiral. Measured 10-300 K; the third paper grows YbNi3Al9 as a thin film, where the chirality can be fixed by the substrate.

basis: One composition, URu2Al10, and the paper is on the crystal structure and physical properties of a new intermetallic compound of that formula. RT2Al10 is the YbFe2Al10 type, orthorhombic Cmcm, in which the rare-earth or actinide atom sits inside a closed twenty-aluminium cage -- the same structure as CeRu2Al10 and CeOs2Al10, which are the exemplar and a representative material of this taxonomy entry. The ruthenium member of the uranium series is the direct analogue. [ref 2] supports it: U(Al5Ru)2 Cmcm (63) mp-1193796 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference is URu2Al10 written with the aluminium grouped differently, and the space group is the right one.
note: The mp_id is taken from the ref line rather than from memory, but it should be checked in stage 2: U(Al5Ru)2 and URu2Al10 are the same composition, and the space group and hull value both fit, yet the formula grouping is unusual enough that the identity should be confirmed rather than assumed. The other [ref 2] entry, UAlRu P-62m (189) mp-1080013 at hull 0.084 with 2 ICSD references, is the 1:1:1 ZrNiAl-type compound of the same system -- the same structure the sibling host Al-Ni-U takes -- and is not in these compositions. Measured 10-289 K. The interest in CeRu2Al10 and CeOs2Al10 is an unusual magnetic ordering near 27 K driven by the cage environment; if URu2Al10 shows an anomaly in that region it is magnetic, not structural.

basis: Three compositions of YbAl3-xSnx at x = 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5, from a paper on the influence of tin substitution on the thermoelectric properties of YbAl3. YbAl3 is the L1_2 ordered cubic trialuminide, Pm-3m, the same structure as the LuAl3 confirmed by [ref 2] at mp-2805 in the sibling host Al-Lu, and it is one of the classic intermediate-valence thermoelectrics. Tin substitutes on the aluminium corner of that cell and the structure is unchanged.

dopant_roles.basis: Sn from 0.2 to 0.5 per formula unit on the aluminium site, a host element by the 5 per cent rule at the upper end. Tin is group 14 against aluminium group 13, so each substitution adds one valence electron; in YbAl3 that shifts the Fermi level relative to the narrow ytterbium 4f resonance that produces the large thermopower, which is exactly what the paper is tuning. It is not isoelectronic and should not be recorded as alloying.

note: Neither reference printed a line for this host, so mp_id is null and the L1_2 cell should be resolved from YbAl3 in stage 2. Measured 299-674 K, no structural transition -- but the physics does change across it, because the intermediate-valence state of ytterbium crosses over to a local-moment one on heating through its characteristic temperature, which for YbAl3 is around 500 to 600 K and so is inside this window. That is an electronic crossover with no change of space group, which is why spans_transition is false; it is recorded here because averaging transport across it would be wrong.

basis: One composition, written with its blocks already separated: (Fe2As2)Ca4(Mg0.25Ti0.75)3O8. That is the 42622 member of the perovskite-blocked iron pnictide family -- an anti-PbO Fe2As2 layer alternating with a three-octahedron-thick Ca4M3O8 perovskite block -- and the paper is on the thermoelectric properties of FeAs-based superconductors with thick perovskite blocks, which names the construction directly. The taxonomy entry already lists Ca4Al2O6Fe2As2 and Sr4V2O6Fe2As2 as representative materials; this is the titanium analogue.

dopant_roles.basis: Mg at a quarter of the three B sites in the perovskite block, not in the FeAs layer. Divalent magnesium replacing tetravalent titanium removes two positive charges per substitution from the block, and since the block is the charge reservoir for the Fe2As2 layer that is precisely how carriers are delivered to the conducting sheets. So the magnesium is the doping variable of the compound rather than a dilute impurity, even though it falls under 5 atomic per cent of the whole formula. Stage 3 should treat it that way.

note: Neither reference printed a line for this host, so mp_id is null. The perovskite-blocked family is built from two subsystems with an in-plane lattice mismatch that is accommodated by tilting rather than by incommensuration, so unlike the misfit cobaltites a single periodic cell does exist and stage 2 can resolve one -- the practical difficulty is that these compounds are recent and sparsely represented in the 2019 snapshot. Measured 11-299 K, which spans the superconducting transition of this family, near 40 K in the best members. That is electronic, not structural.

basis: Three compositions, one sample each, and they are three different structures -- this is a binary phase diagram sampled rather than one material. CoAs3 is the skutterudite, cubic Im-3 with the four-membered As4 rings and the icosahedral void, and [ref 2] gives it at mp-452, hull 0.000, 8 ICSD references. CoAs2 is the safflorite type, monoclinic P2_1/c, a distorted marcasite, at mp-2715 with 5 references. CoAs is the MnP type, orthorhombic Pnma, at mp-583 with 9 references. The skutterudite is taken as the primary because it is the thermoelectric member and one of the papers is on the thermoelectric properties of CoSb3 and related alloys, of which CoAs3 is the arsenic analogue.
note: Splitting rule for stage 2 is the As-to-Co ratio alone: 3 gives skutterudite at mp-452, 2 gives marcasite at mp-2715, 1 gives mnp_b31 at mp-583. All three are well attested, with 8, 5 and 9 ICSD references, so this is a clean split. One qualification on the middle member: CoAs2 is safflorite, which is the monoclinically distorted derivative of the orthorhombic Pnnm marcasite rather than marcasite itself, so the prototype names the family and not the exact space group -- P2_1/c, not Pnnm. The prototype is a fair description of the family; the cell is not the aristotype one. The remaining [ref 2] entries, Co2As P-62m and Co5As2 P6_3cm, are further binaries of the system and are not in these compositions. Measured 11-874 K across the three, but since each composition is one sample the pooled range cannot be attributed to any one structure.

basis: One composition, Cu10.0Zn1.8Fe0.2As2.7Sb1.3S13, and the S13 with Cu10M2X4 is the tetrahedrite formula exactly -- Cu10(Zn,Fe)2(As,Sb)4S13, cubic I-43m. With arsenic dominating the pnictogen site this is tennantite, the arsenic end of the tetrahedrite-tennantite series, and the paper is on the solvothermal synthesis of tetrahedrite for thermoelectrics. The 13 sulfur rather than 12 is the diagnostic: the extra sulfur sits at the centre of the cation cage and is what distinguishes this family from an ordinary sulfosalt.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb1.3 against As2.7 on the four trivalent pnictogen sites. Antimony and arsenic are both group 15 and the tetrahedrite-tennantite series is continuous between them, so no carriers are added; the substitution changes the lone-pair geometry and the lattice thermal conductivity. At a third of the site this is alloying rather than doping, and calling it a dilute dopant would misdescribe it -- Sb falls under 5 atomic per cent only because sulfur and copper dominate the atom count.

Fe0.2 against Zn1.8 on the two divalent cation sites of the cage. Iron and zinc both substitute there in natural and synthetic tetrahedrites, but they are not equivalent: zinc is fixed at 2+ and closes the shell, while iron can be 2+ or 3+ and so acts as the carrier-concentration knob for the family. A small deliberate iron content alongside a large zinc one is the standard way of setting the hole count in a tetrahedrite thermoelectric.

note: I do not follow [ref 2]. Its single entry is Zn3Cu6(AsS3)4 P1 (1) mp-1215617 at hull 0.010 with no ICSD reference, which is a triclinic computed structure of a different stoichiometry -- no S13 cage sulfur, a different Cu:Zn ratio and no antimony. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should resolve a genuine tetrahedrite or tennantite cell in I-43m. Measured 87-721 K. Tetrahedrites have a low-temperature structural and electronic transition near 85 K in the copper-rich unsubstituted compound, at the very bottom of this window, but zinc substitution suppresses it and at Zn1.8 it should be gone. Worth a check if anything odd appears at the cold end.
