dopant_roles.basis: Carbon appears only in the two compositions written with an explicit (SiC) term, at 0.79 and 2.42 formula units. Silicon carbide is the nanocomposite second phase the paper title refers to; it is inert against the clathrate framework and does not enter the cages or substitute on the framework. The parser splits it into elements, but it is one additive.

note: Confidence is medium because I doubt the guest element. Bismuth in the cages of a silicon clathrate would be remarkable -- the guests in this family are alkali or alkaline-earth metals, which is what the framework needs to balance its charge, and a group 15 element cannot play that role. The same paper contributes Ba8Cu5Si6Ge32Sn3 to this chunk, and Ba8Cu4.8Si41.2 is a known compound with exactly these framework numbers. So the likeliest reading is that this is barium and the Bi is a transcription error somewhere upstream. I have assigned clathrate_i because the framework arithmetic is unambiguous whatever the guest turns out to be, but the host key may be wrong and I would check the paper before trusting the element list. Neither reference printed anything; mp_id is null. Measured 422-773 K.
annotator_note: Bi8Cu4.8Si41.2 is very likely Ba8Cu4.8Si41.2. If confirmed, this host should merge into Ba-Cu-Si and this record should be withdrawn rather than corrected in place.

basis: EuMg2Bi2, written twice with a stray space in one composition string. The paper is on the thermoelectric transport properties of CaMg2Bi2, EuMg2Bi2 and YbMg2Bi2, which is the 1-2-2 Zintl series in the CaAl2Si2 structure: trigonal P-3m1, with anionic Mg2Bi2 slabs of edge-sharing MgBi4 tetrahedra separated by layers of the divalent cation. Europium is divalent here, which is what lets it sit on the calcium site.
note: The two composition strings EuMg2 Bi2 and EuMg2Bi2 are the same compound and should be deduplicated upstream; the space is a transcription artifact. Neither reference printed anything for this host; mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the P-3m1 cell. Measured 10-600 K over 19 curves. Europium in this compound orders antiferromagnetically below about 7 K, at the very bottom of that window, so the lowest points may sit in the ordered state -- worth knowing for anyone fitting the low-temperature thermopower, though it does not touch the structure.

basis: La1-x-yBixSryFeO3 with bismuth running from 0.3 to 0.5 on the A site, and the paper is titled on bismuth-doped lanthanum ferrite perovskites as cathodes. LaFeO3 is an orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskite, Pnma, and bismuth and strontium substitute on the lanthanum site without changing that -- the A site accommodates all three cations and the FeO6 octahedral network is untouched. All three compositions keep the A:B ratio at 1:1 and the oxygen at 3.

dopant_roles.site: the perovskite A site
dopant_roles.basis: Sr fixed at 0.2 of the A site in all three compositions. Divalent strontium for trivalent lanthanum is the standard hole doping of a lanthanum ferrite: it raises the iron valence towards Fe4+ or creates oxygen vacancies, and it is what turns an insulating parent into a mixed conductor usable as a cathode. Being constant across the series it is part of the base composition rather than the variable being studied -- that variable is the bismuth content, which is a host element here.

note: Bismuth at 0.3 to 0.5 of the A site is a host element by the threshold and is the substitution the paper is actually about. Its role is A-site substitution: Bi3+ is isovalent with La3+ so it adds no carriers, but it carries a 6s lone pair, which distorts the local coordination, lowers the tolerance factor and reduces the sintering temperature. I do not follow [ref 2]. Its entries, LaFe4(BiO4)3 Pm mp-1222983 and LaFe5Bi4O15 P1 mp-1223162, are computed cells in P1 and Pm with no ICSD references and cation ratios nothing like 1:1 -- these are hull-generated compounds, not the doped ferrite perovskite the paper made. mp_id is null. Measured 823-1073 K, a narrow high-temperature window typical of a cathode conductivity study.

basis: The paper is on a ternary Bi2Te3-In2Te3-Ga2Te3 n-type thermoelectric film, so the intended material is a bismuth telluride matrix alloyed with the two group 13 sesquitellurides. Bi2Te3 is tetradymite, R-3m, and n-type transport in this system belongs to it, so that is the host prototype. But the samples are films and the compositions do not sit at M2Te3: tellurium runs from 41.6 to 54.3 atomic per cent against the 60 per cent a sesquitelluride needs, so all three are cation-rich relative to any of the three end members.
note: Confidence is medium and the tellurium deficit is why. A co-sputtered or co-evaporated film that is 10 to 18 atomic per cent short of its nominal stoichiometry is not a single-phase alloy: the excess metal will be present as elemental bismuth, as a lower telluride, or as a disordered amorphous fraction. In2Te3 and Ga2Te3 are defect zincblende structures with a third of the cation sites vacant, which is a different lattice from the layered tetradymite, and the two do not form a continuous solid solution across the whole range. So the host is marked mixed, but it is mixed within each film rather than between compositions, and none of the three compositions is a clean member of either prototype. The chunk file flags that film samples may reach metastable polymorphs unavailable in bulk, which applies here directly. Neither reference printed anything; mp_id is null. Measured 288-368 K, a narrow room-temperature window consistent with a flexible-substrate device.
annotator_note: I would not use this host for training a structure-property model. The composition is off-stoichiometry, the samples are films and the phase content is unknown.

basis: GdBi is a rare-earth monopnictide and those are rocksalt without exception -- cubic Fm-3m, with the rare earth and the pnictogen on interpenetrating face-centred lattices. [ref 2] confirms it: GdBi Fm-3m (225) mp-614481 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, first on evidence. The paper is on extreme magnetoresistance in magnetic rare-earth monopnictides, which names the family.
note: The two GdBi3 entries, P6_3/mmc mp-1184501 and I4/mmm mp-1184536, sit at hulls of 0.066 and 0.072 with no ICSD references and are flagged AMBIGUOUS in the reference; they are irrelevant to a 1:1 composition. Measured 13-47 K robust, with the full span reaching 97 K -- an extremely cold and narrow window, which fits a magnetotransport study rather than a thermoelectric one. GdBi orders antiferromagnetically near 28 K, in the middle of that window, so the transport crosses the Neel transition; spans_transition is left false because the magnetic ordering does not change the crystal structure. This host is in the set because the samples carry transport curves, but nobody is proposing GdBi as a thermoelectric.

basis: La3Te3.20Bi0.80 and La3Te3.35Bi0.65 are La3Te4 with bismuth on the tellurium site, and the Physical Review B paper is on electron and phonon scattering in the high-temperature thermoelectric La3-xTe4 family. That compound is cubic Th3P4, I-43d, and its rare-earth vacancy concentration is the carrier-concentration knob the taxonomy already records for this entry. The third composition, La22.9Bi34.0Te43.1, belongs to the other paper -- solvothermal synthesis of lanthanum-containing bismuth telluride -- and at a Bi:Te ratio of 0.79 it is a Bi2Te3-based material, so tetradymite is recorded alongside.
note: Two papers on two unrelated materials, and the host cannot carry one label. The split is clean on the La:Te ratio -- 3:4 for the Th3P4 compositions, far lower for the telluride -- so stage 2 can separate them on composition. Bismuth plays opposite roles in the two: a tellurium-site substituent tuning the electron count in La3Te4-zBiz, and a cation-forming host element in lanthanum-containing Bi2Te3. Neither reference printed anything for this host and mp_id is null. Measured 294-1273 K over 11 curves, which is the high-temperature range the La3Te4 work uses.

basis: Mg2Si with bismuth substituting on the silicon site, from a paper titled on enhancing the figure of merit by doping Bi in Mg2Si. Mg2Si is the antifluorite structure, Fm-3m: a face-centred silicon lattice with magnesium filling every tetrahedral hole. Bismuth on the silicon site is the standard n-type donor for this material.
note: [ref 2] agrees more than it first appears. Mg64Si32Bi Pm-3m mp-1194936, Mg63Si32Bi P-43m mp-1194890 and Mg64Si31Bi mp-1195280 are all antifluorite supercells of 32 Mg2Si formula units carrying one bismuth atom; their hulls of 0.06 to 0.09 are the energy cost of the dopant, not evidence of a competing structure. None of them is the parent phase, so mp_id is left null. The nominal bismuth content is very high -- Mg2Si0.5Bi0.5 puts bismuth at a sixth of the atoms, against a solubility limit of around one atomic per cent -- so these samples almost certainly contain Mg3Bi2 as a second phase. The prototype named here is the matrix, not the whole sample. Bismuth is above the 5 at.% cut in all three compositions, so it is recorded as a host element rather than in dopant_roles, which does not change what it is doing.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 215]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: MnBi4S7-7xSe7x, a single line compound with selenium substituting for sulfur, from a paper on the n-type MnBi4S7-7xSe7x solid solution. MnBi4S7 is a module-built bismuth sulfide -- manganese-centred octahedra inside a framework assembled from rocksalt-like and Bi2S3-like blocks -- which is the class this entry covers.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion
solid_solution_axis.note: Selenium fraction of the chalcogen site, from Se/(S+Se) across the three compositions. Both are group 16 and both sit on the same anion framework, so the substitution is isovalent and tunes the lattice thermal conductivity rather than the carrier count.

note: Confidence is medium because I can place the family but not the structure type from composition alone. MnBi4S7 is monoclinic and most probably a pavonite homologue in C2/m; if the paper confirms that, a dedicated MBi4X7 entry belongs in v4 rather than this catch-all, which the taxonomy itself describes as one structure per composition. It is not the mnsb2se4_type entry: that is fixed at MX2X4 with a 1:2 metal ratio and this is 1:4. Neither reference printed anything for this host and mp_id is null. Measured 317-774 K.

basis: Bi3Os3O11, the osmium member of the pair the paper measures -- transport, thermal and magnetic properties of Bi3Os3O11 and Bi3Ru3O11. That is exactly the KSbO3-derived Bi3M3O11 framework this entry names, a three-dimensional network of edge- and corner-sharing MO6 octahedra with bismuth in the channels.
note: No reference line at all for this host, so mp_id is null and stage 2 must resolve the cell from the structure literature on the ruthenium analogue, which is the better-studied of the two. Measured 15-395 K over three curves: a low-temperature study of a metallic oxide, and the interest is in its magnetism rather than in thermoelectric performance.

basis: Two of the three compositions are Y2O2Bi -- written once as Y2O2Bi and once as Y2O1.6Bi1.5 -- and the JACS paper is on two-dimensional superconductivity at a monatomic Bi2- square net in layered Y2O2Bi. That compound is the anti-ThCr2Si2 type: I4/mmm with fluorite-like Y2O2 slabs alternating with flat bismuth square nets, the same atomic arrangement as ThCr2Si2 with cation and anion roles exchanged. [ref 2] puts Y2BiO2 I4/mmm mp-1070510 first at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference. The third composition, Bi0.95Sr0.05YO3, comes from a different paper on Sr-doped BiMO3 perovskites and is a BiYO3 perovskite.

dopant_roles.site: the perovskite A site
dopant_roles.basis: Bi0.95Sr0.05YO3: divalent strontium on the trivalent bismuth A site of the BiYO3 perovskite, which is hole doping, and the structure-property study of that substitution across M = Mn, Fe, Y is what the paper is about. It applies to one composition only and has no bearing on the two Y2O2Bi samples.

note: The host is mixed and splits cleanly on stoichiometry, A2O2Bi against ABO3. I file Y2O2Bi under thcr2si2_122 because that is the atomic arrangement, but it is the anti-type and I want the disagreement on record: the taxonomy separates inverse_heusler from full_heusler for exactly this reason, and an explicit anti-ThCr2Si2 oxypnictide entry would be better, since an oxide slab stacked with a bismuth square net has nothing in common with CeCu2Si2 beyond the site topology. Y2O1.6Bi1.5 is an off-stoichiometric transcription of the same phase rather than a distinct compound. The third paper listed, on ThCr2Si2-type magnetotransport, is presumably the same material again. mp_id for the perovskite composition is null; the remaining [ref 2] entries are bismuth-rich oxides at other ratios.

basis: (Bi0.2Sb0.8)2Te3 with PbTe or (Pb0.7Sn0.3)Te added at 30 to 77 mole per cent. The matrix is the p-type (Bi,Sb)2Te3 alloy -- tetradymite, R-3m -- and the second component is a rocksalt lead telluride, present as inclusions in one paper and as the other half of a functionally graded couple in the second. Both compositions are two-phase by construction, so rocksalt is recorded alongside.

dopant_roles.basis: (Pb0.7Sn0.3Te) in the graded-material composition: tin on the lead site of the rocksalt phase, isovalent, used to shift the band alignment of that leg. It is a constituent of the second phase rather than a dilute dopant of the tetradymite matrix, which is why the atomic fraction understates it.

note: A composite rather than a compound, and the two components do not dissolve into one another: layered R-3m (Bi,Sb)2Te3 and cubic Fm-3m lead telluride are separate phases in every sample. The README warns that composite additives must not relabel their hosts; the reverse caution applies here, because at 30 to 77 mole per cent the lead telluride is not an additive to be ignored. Composition cannot split this host -- both compositions contain both phases -- so the split is per sample or not at all. Neither reference printed anything and mp_id is null. Measured 298-623 K.

basis: NaBr, the textbook rocksalt halide, Fm-3m. [ref 2] gives NaBr Fm-3m mp-22916 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references and offers nothing else for the chemistry.
note: The taxonomy entry is written around rocksalt chalcogenides, but the structure is the same one and an alkali halide is its original case. This is not a thermoelectric measurement: the paper is on tunnelling of substitutional fluoride ions in NaBr and the curve is the low-temperature thermal conductivity of an insulator with defect scattering, 12-87 K. The fluorine that the study is actually about does not appear in the composition string at all, so nothing in this record captures it. Worth excluding from a thermoelectric training set.

basis: CuCl2.2((CH3)2SO), copper(II) chloride with two dimethyl sulfoxide ligands, measured as single crystals in a paper on the low-temperature thermal conductivity of an antiferromagnetic S = 1/2 chain material. This is a molecular coordination crystal: copper-chloride chains with the DMSO molecules completing the coordination sphere and separating the chains. The taxonomy had no entry for that class, so one is proposed.
note: Confidence is medium on the space group, not on the class: that this is a molecular crystal built from a copper coordination complex is not in doubt, but which setting it takes is not something composition settles, and no reference line was printed for this host. Materials Project does not index molecular crystals of this kind, so mp_id is null and stage 2 will need the crystallographic literature. Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and sulfur are all constituents of the DMSO ligand; the 5 at.% split happens to place them in the host, which is correct here, but stage 3 must not read any of them as a dopant. No temperature range was printed for this host.

basis: CuGaTe2 with carbon added at 0.25 to 0.5 per formula unit, from a paper on enhanced thermoelectric performance of CuGaTe2-based composites incorporating a carbon phase. CuGaTe2 is chalcopyrite, I-42d: the ordered diamond-like superstructure of zincblende with copper and gallium alternating on the cation site. The carbon is the composite addition, not a lattice constituent.
note: Carbon sits above the 5 at.% threshold and so counts as a host element, but it is not in the lattice: it is a deliberately added second phase at the grain boundaries, there to scatter phonons. The prototype named is that of the matrix. This is precisely the case the README flags -- a composite additive that could relabel its host -- and it is recorded rather than acted on. dopant_roles is empty because the threshold put carbon in the host; if a later pass moves it, its role is secondary_phase_or_contaminant by design rather than by contamination. No reference line for this host; mp_id is null. Measured 281-876 K.

basis: TiS2 with organic species intercalated between the layers -- hexylammonium, tetrabutylammonium, DMSO and water -- from the two papers on flexible n-type thermoelectrics by organic intercalation of layered TiS2 and on hybrid inorganic-organic superlattices. TiS2 is the 1T CdI2-type disulfide, P-3m1, with titanium octahedrally coordinated, and intercalation expands the van der Waals gap without altering the slab.

dopant_roles.site: the van der Waals gap
dopant_roles.basis: Nitrogen is the head atom of the hexylammonium and tetrabutylammonium cations intercalated into the gap. Read it as molecular intercalation, not as an atom in a void -- interstitial is the closest the role vocabulary offers. The charge transfer from these cations to the TiS2 slab is what makes the films n-type, so this is the doping mechanism even though the species is a molecule.

dopant_roles.site: the van der Waals gap
dopant_roles.basis: Oxygen of the co-intercalated dimethyl sulfoxide and water. A gap-filling solvent species rather than a lattice constituent or milling residue; it sets the interlayer spacing and the flexibility the papers are after.

note: Films and multilayer films, so the chunk metastable-polymorph warning applies in principle, but 1T is the stable TiS2 form and intercalation chemistry only works on it, so there is no competing polytype to weigh here. No reference line for this host; mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the P-3m1 host lattice, remembering that the measured c axis of these hybrids is the expanded superlattice, not that of the parent. Measured 299-413 K over 19 curves, a near-room-temperature flexible-device study.

basis: HfC and the substoichiometric HfC0.67 and HfC0.98. Hafnium carbide is the rocksalt carbide, Fm-3m, with carbon in the octahedral holes of a face-centred hafnium lattice, and [ref 2] puts HfC Fm-3m mp-21075 first on evidence at hull 0.000 with 28 ICSD references.
note: I do not follow [ref 1]. TEDesignLab offers HfC F-43m (216) mp-1002124 at hull 0.642 with a single ICSD reference; that is a zincblende arrangement more than half an electronvolt per atom above the hull, and it is not what a sintered refractory carbide is. Project precedence prefers TEDesignLab, and this is the case where it has to be overruled: 28 ICSD references against 1, with a hull difference of that size. Carbon vacancies are the defining feature of these carbides -- HfC0.67 leaves a third of the carbon sublattice empty -- and that is non-stoichiometry on a host site, not doping; the rocksalt lattice survives it down to about HfC0.6. The papers are on refractory ceramics and their thermal and oxidation properties rather than on thermoelectrics. Measured 296-1095 K.

basis: Ta1-xHfxC at x = 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8, from a paper on the low-temperature densification of Ta1-xHfxC solid solutions. TaC and HfC are both rocksalt carbides, Fm-3m, and they form a continuous solid solution on the metal site while the carbon sublattice is untouched.
note: The two [ref 2] entries, HfTaC2 R-3m mp-1224285 at hull 0.000 and HfTa3C4 P-3m1 mp-1224369, are ordered cation superstructures of the same rocksalt lattice generated for the hull; neither carries an ICSD reference, and a real (Ta,Hf)C ceramic is a disordered Fm-3m solid solution. mp_id is null. Hafnium and tantalum are not isoelectronic -- replacing group 5 tantalum with group 4 hafnium removes a valence electron per formula unit and moves the Fermi level -- so this is a valence-changing alloy rather than the isovalent case solid_solution_axis is written for, and that field is left null deliberately. Ta0.8Hf0.2C is the composition with the highest known melting point of any material, which is why this system is studied. Measured 297-1274 K.

basis: (ZrC)x(Mo)1-x with molybdenum at 29 to 53 atomic per cent, from a paper on liquid-phase sintered ZrC-Mo cermets. This is a two-phase ceramic-metal composite rather than a compound: rocksalt ZrC grains bonded by body-centred cubic molybdenum metal, which is what liquid-phase sintering with a metal binder produces by design.
note: Molybdenum at up to half the atoms cannot be treated as an additive to a carbide host, so the composite label is the honest one and the carbide is recorded as the alternative present. [ref 2] offers Zr4MoC5 R-3m mp-1215358 and ZrMoC2 R-3m mp-1215218, both computed ordered ternary carbides with no ICSD references; a sintered cermet is not a ternary carbide and I do not follow them. mp_id is null. The README lists composite_multiphase among the prototypes stage 2 should skip, which is the right outcome here -- there is no single structure to resolve. Measured 426-1278 K; the study is on thermal shock resistance, not thermoelectric performance.

basis: (TiC)x(ZrC)y with 2 per cent Cr3C2 added, from a paper on the microstructural evolution and thermal properties of TiC-ZrC ceramics. TiC and ZrC are both rocksalt carbides, Fm-3m, and they form a solid solution on the metal site; [ref 2] offers ZrTiC2 R-3m mp-1215182, which is an ordered cation superstructure of that same rocksalt lattice.

dopant_roles.basis: Cr3C2 is held at 2 per cent in all three compositions as a sintering aid and grain-growth inhibitor. It is added as its own carbide phase and stays largely at the grain boundaries; it is not chromium substituting on the titanium or zirconium site, and its constancy across the series shows it is part of the processing recipe rather than the variable being studied.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the metal site of the rocksalt carbide
solid_solution_axis.note: Titanium fraction of the metal site, Ti/(Ti+Zr), across the three compositions. Both are group 4 and both are tetravalent in the carbide, so the substitution is isovalent; TiC and ZrC are fully miscible at the sintering temperature though they can unmix on slow cooling.

note: The R-3m and P4/mmm entries in [ref 2] are computed cation orderings with no ICSD references. A hot-pressed TiC-ZrC ceramic is a disordered Fm-3m solid solution, so mp_id is null. Measured 297-1274 K; a structural-ceramic study rather than a thermoelectric one.

basis: UC, uranium monocarbide, a rocksalt carbide in Fm-3m. [ref 2] gives UC Fm-3m mp-2489 at hull 0.000 with 23 ICSD references, first on evidence and well ahead of everything else in the binary.
note: UC2 I4/mmm mp-2486 and U2C3 I-43d mp-2625 are also on the hull with 12 and 9 ICSD references, and one of the three papers is explicitly on uranium dicarbide, but which of them forms is set by the carbon-to-uranium ratio rather than by temperature, so they are not a thermal sequence and are not recorded as phases. All three compositions here are the monocarbide. The measured span, 22-2571 K, is a nuclear-fuel thermal-property compilation spliced from several sources -- UC melts near 2800 K -- and the papers are on carbide fuels for supercritical water reactors. Not a thermoelectric, and the low-temperature end and high-temperature end almost certainly come from different measurements on different samples.

basis: CaCd2Sb2, written three ways across the three compositions, with the two papers on the Zintl phase Yb1-xCaxCd2Sb2 and on the synthesis and properties of CaCd2Sb2 and EuCd2Sb2. This is the 1-2-2 CaAl2Si2 structure: trigonal P-3m1, anionic Cd2Sb2 slabs of edge-sharing CdSb4 tetrahedra with a layer of divalent calcium between them. [ref 1] confirms it -- Ca(CdSb)2 P-3m1 mp-7430 at hull 0.000.

dopant_roles.site: the divalent cation layer
dopant_roles.basis: Yb0.2Ca0.8Cd2Sb2 is the calcium-rich end of the Yb1-xCaxCd2Sb2 series the first paper scans; the rest of that series forms the neighbouring Ca-Cd-Sb-Yb host. Ytterbium is divalent here and shares the calcium layer, so the substitution adds no carriers and works through mass and size contrast instead.

note: [ref 1] also lists Ca2CdSb2 in space group 62, which is a different Zintl phase of the same chemistry and has its own taxonomy entry, zintl_2_1_2_a2cdsb2. No composition here is at that stoichiometry, so the host is not mixed -- but it is worth knowing the phase exists next door if a 2-1-2 composition turns up later. Measured 296-651 K over 14 curves.

basis: Yb1-xCaxCd2Sb2 at x = 0.4 to 0.6, the middle of the series whose calcium-rich end forms the neighbouring Ca-Cd-Sb host. YbCd2Sb2 and CaCd2Sb2 are both CaAl2Si2-type 1-2-2 Zintl phases, P-3m1, and they form a continuous solid solution on the cation layer, so the structure holds across the whole range.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the divalent cation layer of the CaAl2Si2 structure
solid_solution_axis.note: Calcium fraction of the cation layer. Both cations are divalent, so no carriers are added; the paper induces its property changes through mass and size contrast and through the band-structure shift that follows. The parent compound depends on the composition, so none is assigned at host level.

note: This host and Ca-Cd-Sb are the same study split by the 5 at.% threshold: the compositions with ytterbium above the cut land here, the one below lands there. That is the routing key working as designed rather than two different materials, and stage 2 should treat the two hosts together. No reference line for this host; mp_id is null and the P-3m1 cell should be resolved from either end member. Measured 298-652 K over 15 curves.

basis: CaFe4-xCoxSb12 at x = 1 to 2, from a paper on rare-earth-free p-type filled skutterudites and their mechanisms for low thermal conductivity. The framework is the skutterudite one -- corner-sharing (Fe,Co)Sb6 octahedra with two icosahedral voids per cell -- and calcium fills those voids, which is what makes this the filled entry rather than the binary one.
note: The filling fraction is one in every composition -- the formula is written CaFe(4-x)CoxSb12, not CayFe4Sb12 -- so calcium is a structural constituent rather than a dilute rattler, even though its rattling is what suppresses the lattice thermal conductivity. Iron-for-cobalt is what allows the filling: each Fe removes an electron from the framework and the divalent calcium guest returns two, which is also why the material is p-type. Both are host elements by the threshold, so dopant_roles is empty. No reference line for this host; mp_id is null. Measured 11-789 K over 19 curves.

basis: La2-xCaxCoMnO6, and both papers name the family -- one on the magnetic, transport and magnetocaloric properties of double perovskites, the other on magnetic frustration and structural disorder in the same. Cobalt and manganese alternate on the B site of an ABO3 perovskite, doubling the cell, while lanthanum and calcium share the A site.
note: Calcium is a host element at a quarter to a half of the A site, and that substitution sets the Co/Mn valence balance and thereby the degree of B-site ordering that the second paper is about. The caveat worth carrying to stage 2 is that B-site order in this family is rarely complete: the disordered limit is an ordinary perovskite with Co and Mn randomly mixed, not a double one, and the two samples sharing the LaCaMnCoO6 composition are a single crystal and a polycrystal, which typically differ in exactly that respect. No reference line for this host; mp_id is null. Measured 47-296 K.

basis: CaCr2O4 and Na0.25Ca0.75Cr2O4, two of the three compositions, with one paper on the electronic, thermoelectric and magneto-dielectric properties of the Ca1-xNaxCr2O4 series. AM2O4 with calcium cannot be a spinel -- calcium is far too large for the tetrahedral site -- and instead takes the CaFe2O4-type post-spinel structure, Pnma, with double chains of edge-sharing CrO6 octahedra enclosing tunnels of eight-coordinate calcium. The taxonomy had no entry for that type, so one is proposed.

dopant_roles.site: the eight-coordinate tunnel site
dopant_roles.basis: Na0.25Ca0.75Cr2O4: monovalent sodium on the divalent calcium site of the tunnel, which raises the mean chromium valence and hole-dopes the CrO6 chains. It falls below the 5 at.% cut only because the formula has seven atoms; at a quarter of the calcium site it is the variable the paper scans, not a dilute impurity.

note: The third composition, Ca2CrO4, is at a different stoichiometry and comes from the high-pressure, high-temperature synthesis paper. A2MO4 with a divalent A and a tetravalent transition metal is normally the K2NiF4-type Ruddlesden-Popper n = 1 phase, as Sr2CrO4 is, which is why that is recorded as the alternative -- but I have not confirmed it for the calcium member and it is the weak part of this record, which is why confidence is medium. [ref 2] is no help: its five entries are chromates, an oxychloride and Ca5Cr3O12, none at either stoichiometry present here, so mp_id is null throughout. Stage 2 can split the host on the Cr:Ca ratio, which is 2 for the post-spinel compositions and 0.5 for Ca2CrO4. Measured 11-381 K.
annotator_note: The Ca2CrO4 composition needs the high-pressure paper read before its Ruddlesden-Popper assignment can be relied on.

basis: (Sr0.7Ca0.3)0.9CuO2, from a paper on the synthesis of carrier-doped infinite-layer films. ACuO2 with A = Sr, Ca is the infinite-layer structure: flat CuO2 sheets alternating with bare alkaline-earth layers in P4/mmm, the simplest cuprate there is and the parent of every other one.
note: The A-site deficiency -- the 0.9 in (Sr,Ca)0.9CuO2 -- is the carrier doping the title refers to: cation vacancies hole-dope the CuO2 sheet. It is non-stoichiometry on a host site, and stage 3 should treat it as the doping variable rather than looking for a foreign dopant. Calcium and strontium share the A site, both divalent, and the 0.3 calcium fraction sets the lattice parameter and thus the Cu-O distance. [ref 2] is unusable here: Sr3Ca(CuO2)4, Sr3Ca(CuO3)2, the thallium-lead cuprates and Sr6Ca4Cu17O29 are computed multi-cation cells with no ICSD references, and none is the infinite-layer phase. mp_id is null. Measured 11-298 K.

basis: Ca5-xSrxIn2Sb6 across the full range, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties and electronic structure of the Zintl phase A5In2Sb6. That is the 5-2-6 structure this entry names: Pbam, with infinite ribbons of corner-sharing InSb4 tetrahedra and the alkaline-earth cations between them.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the alkaline-earth cation site between the InSb4 ribbons
solid_solution_axis.note: Calcium fraction of the cation site. Both are divalent, so the series is isovalent and the paper is tuning the lattice and the band structure rather than the carrier count.

note: No reference line for this host; mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the Pbam cell from the Ca5In2Sb6 end member. These 5-2-6 Zintl phases are valence-precise semiconductors with intrinsically low lattice thermal conductivity, which is what brings them into the set. Measured 291-778 K.

basis: CaMn1-xNbxO3 at x = 0.25 to 0.3, with both papers on Nb-substituted CaMnO3. CaMnO3 is a GdFeO3-distorted orthorhombic perovskite, Pnma, and niobium substitutes on the octahedral B site, donating electrons and making the material n-type.
note: The niobium content is far above what a dopant study would normally use -- a quarter to nearly a third of the B site -- so these sit well into the solid-solution regime, and B-site ordering towards a double perovskite becomes a real possibility at that level. [ref 2] hints at it with Ca2MnNbO6 P2_1/c mp-1227519 at hull 0.012, the 1:1 ordered double perovskite, but it carries no ICSD reference and no composition here is at 1:1, so I stay with the simple perovskite and leave the alternative in this note rather than marking the host mixed. mp_id is null. Niobium is a host element by the threshold, so dopant_roles is empty; its role is B-site donor substitution. Measured 332-1101 K.

basis: Ytterbium-substituted CaMnO3, from a paper on the effect of Yb substitutions on the thermoelectric properties of CaMnO3. The structure is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-distorted perovskite, Pnma, in all three compositions; rare-earth substitution electron-dopes it without changing the framework.
note: I do not read the composition strings the way they are written, and that is the disagreement worth recording. CaMn0.7Yb0.3O3, CaMn0.6Yb0.4O3 and CaMn0.5Yb0.5O3 place ytterbium on the manganese site at up to half occupancy. Yb3+ is a rare-earth cation of roughly calcium size and it substitutes on the A site -- Ca1-xYbxMnO3 -- which is the standard electron doping of this material and what the paper title implies. Half of a manganite B site occupied by a rare earth would destroy the MnO6 network and the compound with it. The most likely explanation is that the transcription lost the site assignment. The prototype is unaffected either way, but stage 3 must not compute a B-site doping level from these strings, and even on the A site x = 0.4 and 0.5 are beyond the usual solubility limit, so a second phase is likely in those two samples. [ref 2] offers only CaYb3Mn4O12 Pm mp-1227162, a computed cell with no ICSD reference at a quadruple-perovskite stoichiometry none of these compositions has, and I do not follow it. mp_id is null. Measured 304-1057 K.
annotator_note: For the review queue: the Yb site assignment in the composition strings contradicts both the chemistry and the paper title, and the doping level cannot be computed until it is resolved.

basis: CaMnZnP2 with copper substituting for zinc, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of light-element-containing Zintl compounds. Ca(Mn,Zn)2P2 is the 1-2-2 CaAl2Si2 structure, P-3m1: manganese and zinc share the tetrahedral site of an anionic (MnZn)P2 slab, with the calcium layer between slabs. CaMn2P2 and CaZn2P2 are both of this type, so the 1:1 mixed-metal composition sits on a continuous line between them.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral site of the anionic slab
dopant_roles.basis: CaMnZn0.9Cu0.1P2 and CaMnZn0.8Cu0.2P2: copper on the zinc tetrahedral site. Monovalent copper for divalent zinc removes one electron per substitution, which is the p-type doping knob of this series and the variable the paper scans.

note: No reference line for this host; mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the P-3m1 cell. One caveat for the transport reading rather than the structure: manganese carries a local moment on the tetrahedral site in this family, so these are not simple band semiconductors and their thermopower has a magnetic contribution. Measured 81-976 K over 11 curves.

basis: Two of the three samples are Ca3N2, which is anti-bixbyite -- the cubic C-type sesquioxide framework in Ia-3 with the cation and anion roles exchanged -- and [ref 2] confirms it with Ca3N2 Ia-3 mp-844 at hull 0.000 and 5 ICSD references. The third sample is Ca2N, a layered subnitride and a two-dimensional electride, which is a different structure and a different material; it gets the anti-CdCl2 entry proposed here.

other_polymorphs.note: The paper is titled on beta-Ca3N2, a metastable nitride in the Ca-N system, so one of the two Ca3N2 samples is very likely that form rather than the cubic alpha one. [ref 1] lists Ca3N2 R-3c mp-1047 at hull 0.014 with 3 ICSD references, and R-3c is the corundum setting, which is consistent with an anti-corundum beta form -- but I am inferring the correspondence from the space group rather than knowing it, and which sample is which is not recoverable from the composition strings. Recorded as a metastable polymorph with that uncertainty stated, not as a thermal phase.

note: Confidence is medium because the host holds two unrelated compounds and because the alpha-beta question above is unresolved. The split is clean on stoichiometry, 3:2 against 2:1, so stage 2 can separate them. The physics differs completely between them: Ca3N2 is a wide-gap insulating nitride, while Ca2N is metallic, with one electron per formula unit sitting in the interlayer gap as the anion -- the reason the new entry was proposed rather than folding it into a layered-halide prototype. [ref 2] gives Ca2N R-3m mp-2686 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references. [ref 1] also lists CaN6 Fddd mp-676, a calcium azide, which is not present in any composition here. mp_id is null for both, per the taxonomy rule. Measured 17-327 K.
annotator_note: Which Ca3N2 polymorph the two samples are -- alpha or the metastable beta the paper is about -- needs the paper.

basis: Ca3PbO with bismuth substituting for lead, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of the antiperovskite calcium oxides Ca3PbO and Ca3SnO. The structure is a perovskite with the charges inverted: oxygen at the B site octahedrally coordinated by six calcium, lead at the corners as a formal anion, Pm-3m. [ref 2] confirms it -- Ca3PbO Pm-3m mp-20273 at hull 0.000.

dopant_roles.site: the corner anion site
dopant_roles.basis: Ca3Pb0.9Bi0.1O and Ca3Pb0.8Bi0.2O: bismuth on the lead site. It carries one more valence electron than lead, so it acts as a donor and is the carrier-tuning knob for this Dirac-electron system, which is what the paper varies.

note: [ref 1] is not usable here and I do not follow it. TEDesignLab offers Ca2PbO4 Pbam mp-21137 and CaPbO3 Pnma mp-20079, ordinary calcium plumbates in which lead is the cation and oxygen the anion; the antiperovskite has the opposite polarity, with formally Pb4- anions, and is a different material. Project precedence prefers TEDesignLab, and this is the second case in this chunk where it has to be overruled -- [ref 2] has the right compound. mp-20273 carries a single ICSD reference, which the chunk header would call weak evidence, but it is the only entry at the right stoichiometry and the paper names the structure in its title. Measured 15-297 K.

basis: CaSO4 and Dy0.002CaSO4, from a paper on the crystal growth and electrical properties of CaSO4:Dy single crystals. Anhydrite is Cmcm: chains of alternating eight-coordinate CaO8 polyhedra and discrete SO4 tetrahedra. [ref 2] puts CaSO4 Cmcm mp-4406 first on evidence at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references. The taxonomy had no sulfate entry, so one is proposed.

dopant_roles.basis: Dy0.002CaSO4: dysprosium on the calcium site at 0.2 per cent, the activator that makes this material work as a thermoluminescent dosimeter. Trivalent dysprosium on a divalent site needs charge compensation, normally by calcium vacancies, so the defect chemistry rather than the substitution alone is what the electrical measurement sees.

note: Not a thermoelectric: CaSO4:Dy is a dosimeter phosphor and the curves are electrical conductivity and thermally stimulated current from 301 to 529 K. The remaining [ref 2] entries -- CaSO6, Ca2S2O9, Ca(SO5)2, Ca2S2O7 -- are peroxo and pyro compounds at hulls of 0.17 to 0.52 and have nothing to do with anhydrite. The hydrated calcium sulfates, gypsum and bassanite, are different structures; these crystals are the anhydrous form. mp_id is null per the taxonomy rule.

basis: Cd1-xCoxS films grown by chemical bath deposition, from a paper on the surface morphology and transport properties of such films. CdS is a tetrahedral II-VI semiconductor whose stable bulk form is hexagonal wurtzite, P6_3mc, with cobalt substituting for cadmium on the cation site.

other_polymorphs.note: Cubic zincblende CdS is routinely what low-temperature chemical bath deposition produces, on its own or mixed with the hexagonal stacking. It is not reached by heating -- heating converts cubic to hexagonal -- so it belongs here rather than in phases, and it cannot be ruled out for these samples without the diffraction pattern.

note: Confidence is medium and the deposition method is why: chemical bath deposition at low temperature gives cubic CdS or a cubic-hexagonal mixture at least as often as phase-pure wurtzite, and nothing in the composition settles which. The cobalt content is also very high -- Co0.5Cd0.5S is half the cation site -- and cobalt sulfide adopts neither tetrahedral structure, so the cobalt-rich films are likely to contain a separate CoS phase; the prototype named is the matrix. [ref 2] offers only Cd4CoS5 Cm mp-1226929 at hull 0.114 with no ICSD reference, a computed ordered cell that I do not follow, so mp_id is null. Measured 302-437 K.

basis: CdCr2-xSbxSe4, from a paper on the n-p phase transition in that series. CdCr2Se4 is a normal spinel, Fd-3m: tetrahedral cadmium, octahedral chromium, cubic close-packed selenium. [ref 1] confirms it -- Cr2CdSe4 Fd-3m mp-22605 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: CdCr2-xSbxSe4 at x = 0.05 to 0.08: antimony on the octahedral chromium site. It is the only variable across the three compositions and it is what drives the conduction from n-type to p-type, which is the subject of the paper.

note: The n-to-p transition in the title is a change of carrier type with antimony content, not a structural one, so spans_transition is false. CdCr2Se4 is a ferromagnetic semiconductor with a Curie temperature near 130 K, below the measured 275-472 K window, so these single crystals are paramagnetic throughout the measurement.

basis: Cu2Cd1-xZnxSnSe4 at x = 0.5 to 0.6, and the paper is on the crystal structure and thermoelectric properties of that solid solution. Cu2CdSnSe4 is stannite, I-42m, and Cu2ZnSnSe4 is kesterite, I-4; both are ordered diamond-like quaternary derivatives of zincblende and they form a continuous series, which this entry holds together.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the divalent cation site of the diamond-like framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Cadmium fraction of the divalent cation site. Both are group 12 and divalent, so the substitution is isovalent; what it changes is the cation-ordering variant and the lattice thermal conductivity, not the carrier count.

note: The stannite-to-kesterite change across this series is a cation-ordering change inside the same diamond-like framework -- which is exactly what the paper title says it measured -- and it is compositional rather than thermal, so it is not recorded as a phase transition. The taxonomy keeps the two variants in one entry, which is right for routing but means stage 2 has to resolve which ordering applies per composition; all three compositions here sit near the middle of the join, where the answer is least obvious. No reference line for this host; mp_id is null. Measured 298-721 K over 15 curves.

basis: Three compositions with exactly three cations per four tellurium atoms, from a paper on silver indium telluride semiconductors and their solid solutions. That cation deficit is the defining count of an ordered-vacancy compound: CdIn2Te4 is the defect chalcopyrite, I-4, in which one in four cation sites of the zincblende lattice is systematically empty. [ref 1] confirms it -- Cd(InTe2)2 I-4 (82) mp-21374 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references.

dopant_roles.site: the cation sublattice, partly filling the ordered vacancy
dopant_roles.basis: The compositions sit on the CdIn2Te4-AgInTe2 join: silver enters the cation sublattice together with extra indium and partly fills the ordered vacancy. It is an end member of a solid solution that happens to fall below the 5 at.% cut, not a dilute dopant, and its level tracks the cadmium and indium content rather than varying independently.

note: The cation-to-anion ratio is what settles this: 3:4 is the defect chalcopyrite count, against the 4:4 of an ordinary chalcopyrite such as AgInTe2, so these are ordered-vacancy compounds however much silver is present. [ref 2] offers Cd3(InTe3)2 C2 mp-1226986 at hull 0.016, a computed monoclinic cell with no ICSD reference at a different ratio, and I do not follow it. Measured 324-675 K.

basis: YbCd2-xMgxSb2 at x = 0.4 to 0.8, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of YbCd2Sb2 doped by Mg. YbCd2Sb2 and YbMg2Sb2 are both CaAl2Si2-type 1-2-2 Zintl phases, P-3m1, so magnesium and cadmium share the tetrahedral site of the anionic slab across a continuous series and the structure is not in doubt.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the tetrahedral site of the anionic slab
solid_solution_axis.note: Magnesium fraction of the tetrahedral site. Both are divalent, so no carriers are added despite the word doped in the title; the gain comes from mass contrast and the band shift that follows.

note: Magnesium is well above the 5 at.% cut and is a host element, not a dopant, which is why dopant_roles is empty here while the neighbouring Ca-Cd-Sb host records ytterbium. At x = 0.4 to 0.8 out of two cadmium atoms this is alloying on the tetrahedral site. No reference line for this host; mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the P-3m1 cell from YbCd2Sb2. Measured 299-651 K.

basis: Cd3P2 and Cd3(P0.9As0.1)2. Cd3P2 is isostructural with Cd3As2 -- the tetragonal antifluorite derivative with a quarter of the cation sites ordered vacant -- and [ref 2] gives Cd3P2 P4_2/nmc mp-2441 with 7 ICSD references, first on evidence for the host.

other_polymorphs.note: Cd3P2 Pn-3m at hull 0.214 with 2 ICSD references is the vacancy-disordered antifluorite aristotype of the same composition -- the idealised parent of the ordered tetragonal cell rather than a separate phase reached by heating in this window. Recorded here so it is not mistaken for a thermal phase.

dopant_roles.basis: The curator transcribed this composition as 90 mol per cent Cd3P2 with 10 mol per cent Cd3As2, so arsenic is a solid-solution end member on the pnictogen site rather than a dopant. Cd3As2 is isostructural with Cd3P2, the two are miscible, and the substitution narrows the gap towards the Dirac semimetal limit without adding carriers.

note: I do not follow [ref 1]. TEDesignLab lists CdP2 in two tetragonal settings and CdP4, which are different compounds of the same binary system, not polymorphs of Cd3P2; the 3:2 stoichiometry of every composition here is unambiguous and none of those is it. Cd3P2 is the phosphide analogue of the Dirac semimetal Cd3As2 and the 1964 paper is on its preparation and semiconducting properties. Measured 71-526 K robust, 71-619 K including outliers.

basis: Elemental cerium, measured in both of its low-temperature allotropes -- the paper is on the thermoelectric power of alpha- and beta-cerium. An element has no ordered prototype, so this is the close-packed elemental metal entry the taxonomy reserves for exactly that; the lattice is face-centred cubic for the gamma and alpha forms and double-hexagonal close-packed for beta. [ref 2] gives Ce Fm-3m mp-28 at hull 0.000 with 17 ICSD references, first on evidence, and Ce P6_3/mmc mp-20372 with 4.
note: Cerium is the awkward element of the lanthanides and the 10-294 K window covers its whole low-temperature history. Gamma-Ce is face-centred cubic at room temperature; on cooling it collapses near 100 K to alpha-Ce, which is also Fm-3m -- an isostructural volume collapse driven by the 4f electron, not a change of structure type -- and beta-Ce, the double-hexagonal close-packed allotrope, forms sluggishly below about 260 K and coexists with the cubic phase in any real sample. So the two allotropes the paper separates are one prototype and one stacking variant of it, and spans_transition is left false deliberately: the transition the measurement crosses does not change the structure type. The remaining [ref 2] entries fit the rest of the phase diagram -- Cmcm mp-64 is the high-pressure alpha-prime form and Im-3m mp-10024 the body-centred cubic delta form above 1000 K -- and neither is reached here. One taxonomy gap worth recording: there is no entry for the double-hexagonal close-packed A3-prime stacking of the light rare earths, which the solid_solution_alloy note asks to be recorded as a lattice rather than as a prototype. That is being done here, but a v4 entry would be better.

basis: CexY1-xInCu2, from a paper on the thermopower of that series and of CeInCuyAg2-y. CeInCu2 crystallizes in the cubic Heusler structure, Fm-3m, the MnCu2Al type, with cerium and indium on the two ordered cation sublattices and copper on the tetrahedral sites.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the rare-earth site of the Heusler cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Cerium fraction of the rare-earth site. Yttrium and cerium are both trivalent and close in size, so this dilutes the magnetic 4f lattice at nearly constant lattice parameter -- the standard way to separate single-ion Kondo behaviour from lattice coherence -- rather than doping it.

note: Confidence is medium because there is no reference line at all for this host: the structure comes from the heavy-fermion literature rather than from a database, and nothing here can check it. The caveat that matters for stage 2 is that indium-copper ordering in this family is reported to be incomplete; a partially disordered CeInCu2 tends towards a different cell from the fully ordered Heusler one, so the ordering should be confirmed before a structure file is taken. Measured 10-294 K.

basis: Ce1-xLaxCu6, from papers on the dense Kondo substitution series and on the heavy-fermion state in CeCu6. CeCu6 is the orthorhombic Pnma structure this entry is named after, and lanthanum substitutes for cerium on the rare-earth site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the rare-earth site
solid_solution_axis.note: Cerium fraction of the rare-earth site. Both are trivalent, so this is an isovalent dilution of the 4f lattice; lanthanum is slightly larger, so the cell expands a little across the series.

note: [ref 2] offers only LaCeCu12 Pmc2_1 mp-1223412 at hull 0.007, a computed ordered 1:1:12 cell with no ICSD reference -- that is the 50:50 alloy written as an ordered superstructure. The real material is a random substitution on the rare-earth site of the CeCu6 lattice, so I do not take it and mp_id is null. One thing worth knowing for the low-temperature end: CeCu6 undergoes an orthorhombic-to-monoclinic distortion near 200 K, inside the measured 10-277 K window, but that is a symmetry lowering within the same prototype and its temperature falls rapidly with lanthanum content, so it is not recorded as a phase change.

basis: Ce(Pd1-xCux)2Si2 across most of its range. CePd2Si2 and CeCu2Si2 are both ThCr2Si2-type, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, and palladium and copper share the transition-metal layer, so the structure holds across the join. [ref 2] supports it obliquely with CeCuSi2Pd I-4m2 mp-1226625 at hull 0.000, an ordered 50:50 variant of the same layer stack.
note: The mp entry is the ordered cell at x = 0.5 with no ICSD reference; a real alloy is disordered on the transition-metal site, so mp_id is null. This host is the CeCu2Si2 to CePd2Si2 line, which runs from the first heavy-fermion superconductor found to an antiferromagnet that superconducts under pressure, and the paper measures low-temperature thermoelectric power across it. Copper and palladium are not isoelectronic, so the substitution changes the band filling as well as the cell volume; the axis is not recorded as a solid solution for that reason. Both are host elements, so dopant_roles is empty. Measured 10-298 K.

basis: Ce1-xYxCu2.05Si2, the yttrium-diluted CeCu2Si2 series. CeCu2Si2 is the archetypal ThCr2Si2-type heavy-fermion superconductor, I4/mmm, and yttrium substitutes for cerium on the A site of that structure.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the A site of the ThCr2Si2 structure
solid_solution_axis.note: Cerium fraction of the A site. Both are trivalent, so the series dilutes the 4f lattice without doping it; yttrium is the non-magnetic analogue used to isolate the single-ion contribution to the thermopower.

note: No reference line for this host, so mp_id is null -- though the closely related Ce-Cu-Si host is already an example host system of this prototype, which is as close to independent support as this record gets. The copper excess, 2.05 rather than 2.00, is deliberate rather than a transcription error: CeCu2Si2 is famously sensitive to its exact copper content, which decides whether the ground state is superconducting or magnetic, so it is non-stoichiometry on a host site and stage 3 should not round it away. Measured 10-303 K on polycrystals.

basis: Ce3-xEuxS4 at x = 0.4 to 0.8, from a paper on the preparation and thermoelectric properties of ternary rare-earth sulfides. The gamma-Ce2S3 to Ce3S4 line is the Th3P4 structure, cubic I-43d, with a continuous range of rare-earth vacancies between the two limits, and europium substitutes on that rare-earth site.
note: The rare-earth vacancy concentration of the Th3P4 lattice is the carrier-concentration knob of this family, exactly as the taxonomy records for La3-xTe4 -- and the Bi-La-Te host at the top of this chunk is the telluride version of the same idea. Europium adds a second knob, since it can be divalent or trivalent here and so changes the electron count at fixed vacancy content; which valence it takes is not decidable from the composition and should be read from the paper. No reference line for this host; mp_id is null. Measured 298-674 K.

basis: Three different compounds, one sample each, from three different papers. CeRh2Ga2, the subject of the Kondo-lattice heavy-fermion paper, is an RT2X2 phase of the ThCr2Si2 family and is the nearest thing this host has to a majority call. Ce2Rh3Ga9 belongs to the ternary Ce2T3X9 family the second paper names and is the Y2Co3Ga9 type proposed here, Cmcm, supported by Ce2(Ga3Rh)3 Cmcm mp-1213907 at hull 0.000 in [ref 2]. The third composition, CeRh2Ga, I cannot place.
note: Confidence is low and this host should not be used as a single label. Two separate caveats. First, CeRh2Ga is at a stoichiometry I have no structure for: it is not the 1:1:1 CeGaRh Pnma mp-1102417 that [ref 2] lists with an ICSD reference, and an RT2X gallide of this chemistry is not something I can assign from composition, so unresolved_crystalline stands for it. Second, CeRh2Ga2 itself is not certain: several CeT2Ga2 compounds with a 4d or 5d transition metal adopt the CaBe2Ge2 ordering, P4/nmm -- the same layer sequence with the transition metal and the trielide exchanged in alternate layers, which removes the inversion centre -- and the taxonomy has no CaBe2Ge2 entry. I have filed it under the 122 family and flagged the variant rather than proposing a structure type I cannot confirm. All three compositions need their papers read. mp_id is null for all three. Measured 10-309 K.
annotator_note: Three compounds, one sample each, two of them unresolved. A clear candidate for the review queue, and a CaBe2Ge2 entry is probably missing from the taxonomy.

basis: Ce(Ga1-xSnx)2 at x = 0.1 to 0.3, from a paper on thermoelectric power and resistivity in the Kondo-lattice system. CeGa2 is the AlB2 structure, P6/mmm: flat gallium honeycomb nets with cerium between them, and tin substitutes into those nets.
note: No reference line for this host; mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the P6/mmm cell from CeGa2. Tin is not isoelectronic with gallium -- it brings an extra valence electron into the honeycomb net -- and that band filling is what drives the Kondo behaviour the paper follows, so this is a substitution series on a host site rather than an isovalent alloy, and solid_solution_axis is left null for that reason. CeGa2 is reported to develop a slight orthorhombic distortion of the AlB2 cell at low temperature in some studies; that is a distortion within the prototype, not a phase change, and it is not recorded. Measured 10-262 K.

basis: CePdGe, from papers on the thermoelectric power of CeTGe compounds with T = Ni, Pd, Pt and on CeTX magnetism. Equiatomic RTX compounds of this kind take the TiNiSi structure -- an ordered ternary Co2Si type in Pnma -- and [ref 2] confirms it directly: CeGePd Pnma mp-21647 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference.
note: The other [ref 2] entries are different stoichiometries of the same ternary system -- Ce(GePd)2 I4/mmm mp-13467, CeGePd2 Pnma mp-1188948, Ce3Ge5Pd14, Ce3(Ge3Pd10)2 -- and no sample here is at any of those ratios, so the choice among them is not in question. One of the three papers is titled on YbPdGe and YbPtGe rather than the cerium compound; since all three samples in this host are CePdGe, it presumably carries a cerium reference curve. Worth noting for this family that the orthorhombic TiNiSi type and the hexagonal ZrNiAl type compete across the RTX series -- the neighbouring CePdIn and CePtIn hosts in this chunk take the hexagonal one -- so the Pnma assignment rests on the reference rather than on the stoichiometry. Measured 11-299 K.

basis: CeIn3, the cubic AuCu3 type in Pm-3m: cerium at the cube corners, indium at the face centres. [ref 2] gives CeIn3 Pm-3m mp-20369 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references, first on evidence.
note: CeIn3 is the three-dimensional parent of the CeTIn5 and CenTmIn3n+2m heavy-fermion families that appear in the two neighbouring hosts of this chunk, which is why the same RIn3 block keeps recurring: those structures are built by intergrowing it with transition-metal layers. The other [ref 2] entries, Ce3In Pm-3m mp-20984 and Ce2In P6_3/mmc mp-19733, are different compounds of the binary system and no sample here is at their stoichiometry. CeIn3 orders antiferromagnetically near 10 K, at the very bottom of the 11-295 K window, so the measurement is essentially all paramagnetic. One of the three papers is on the anomalously large thermoelectric cooling figure of merit of a Kondo system, which is why this sits in a thermoelectric set at all.

basis: Three compounds, one sample each. CePdIn, from the Kondo-compound paper, is the hexagonal ZrNiAl type, P-62m, and [ref 2] backs it with CeInPd P-62m mp-991729 at hull 0.000 and 5 ICSD references -- the best-attested entry in the host, which is why it is the host-level call. Ce2PdIn8 is the 2-1-8 member of the CenTmIn3n+2m homologous series proposed here, P4/mmm, supported by Ce2In8Pd P4/mmm mp-1102172 at hull 0.000. Ce6Pd12In5 is a third structure again, matching Ce6In5Pd12 P6_3/mcm mp-641689.
note: Three distinct structures with one sample each, so the host cannot carry a single label and confidence is medium at best; the split is clean on stoichiometry and stage 2 should make it. Ce2PdIn8 is the material the thermoelectric quantum-criticality paper is about and it is a heavy-fermion superconductor; its stacking is one CeIn3 block more than the CeTIn5 structure the taxonomy already holds as hocoga5_115, which is why the proposed entry cross-references that one and suggests merging them in v4. Ce6In5Pd12 has its reference cell in [ref 2] but no prototype is assigned for it here -- it is a 6-12-5 phase I cannot place in a named family, and it is left to stage 2. mp_id is null at host level. Measured 11-299 K.

basis: The same pattern as the neighbouring palladium host. CePtIn is the hexagonal ZrNiAl type, P-62m, and [ref 2] backs it with CeInPt P-62m mp-640922 at hull 0.000 and 3 ICSD references, the best-attested entry here. Ce3PtIn11 is a further member of the CenTmIn3n+2m homologous series -- three CeIn3 blocks to one PtIn2 layer -- and Ce3Pt4In13 is a 3-4-13 phase of the Yb3Rh4Sn13 Remeika family with indium in place of tin.
note: Three compounds, three structures, one sample each; split on stoichiometry in stage 2. Ce3PtIn11 and Ce3Pt4In13 are both recent multi-site quantum-critical cerium compounds and the second paper covers them together. [ref 2] confirms the chemistry but not those two phases -- it lists CeIn7Pt2, Ce12InPt7, Ce(InPt)2 and Ce2In8Pt, each with a single ICSD reference, and nothing at 3-1-11 or 3-4-13 -- so both of those mp_ids are null and the assignments rest on the structure literature. The Remeika reading of Ce3Pt4In13 in particular should be confirmed in stage 2; the 3-4-13 stoichiometry is what suggests it. Measured 13-308 K on two curves only.

basis: Ce1-xLaxPd2Si2, from a paper on the thermoelectric power of that series. CePd2Si2 is ThCr2Si2-type, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, and lanthanum substitutes for cerium on the A site, diluting the Kondo lattice at nearly constant cell volume.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the A site of the ThCr2Si2 structure
solid_solution_axis.note: Cerium fraction of the A site. Both are trivalent, so this is an isovalent dilution of the 4f lattice rather than doping -- the standard method for separating single-ion Kondo scattering from lattice coherence in the thermopower.

note: [ref 2] offers LaCe(SiPd)4 P4/mmm mp-1222952 at hull 0.009, the ordered 50:50 cell, with no ICSD reference; the real alloy is a random substitution on the rare-earth site, so I do not take it and mp_id is null. The same situation arises in the Ce-Cu-Pd-Si and Ce-Cu-La hosts in this chunk: Materials Project represents a substituted alloy as an ordered superstructure, and none of those entries should be read as a distinct phase. Measured 10-285 K.

basis: (Ce1-xNdx)Ru2, from a paper on the transport properties of (Ce1-xRx)Ru2 with R = La, Nd. CeRu2 is a cubic C15 Laves phase, the MgCu2 type in Fd-3m, and neodymium substitutes on the rare-earth site without changing it.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the rare-earth site of the C15 Laves cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Cerium fraction of the rare-earth site. Cerium in CeRu2 is close to tetravalent and non-magnetic while neodymium carries a full moment, so this substitution is not electronically neutral despite both elements being rare earths -- it drives the compound from a superconductor towards a magnet, which is what the transport measures.

note: No reference line for this host; mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the Fd-3m cell from CeRu2. Both elements sit on the same site throughout, so the structure is constant across the series even though the ground state is not. Measured 10-289 K on polycrystals.

basis: CeRu4P12 with lanthanum substituting for cerium, from a paper on the La doping effect in the thermoelectric properties of skutterudite compounds. CeRu4P12 is a filled skutterudite: a RuP3 framework of corner-sharing RuP6 octahedra with cerium occupying the icosahedral void. [ref 2] confirms it -- Ce(P3Ru)4 Im-3 mp-10069 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, Im-3 being the LaFe4P12 filled-skutterudite space group.

dopant_roles.site: the filled icosahedral void
dopant_roles.basis: La0.025Ce0.975Ru4P12 and La0.1Ce0.9Ru4P12: lanthanum replaces cerium on the filler site, which is already occupied, so this is substitution on a host site and not cage filling. Lanthanum is trivalent with no 4f electron, so it dilutes the hybridization that opens this compound gap -- the paper calls it doping and that is what it does electronically.

note: The filling fraction is one, so this is the filled entry rather than the binary skutterudite one; the void is occupied by design. CeRu4P12 is a Kondo insulator with a small hybridization gap, which is where its large thermopower comes from, and diluting the cerium sublattice is a direct attack on that gap. The other [ref 2] entry, Ce5P12Ru19 P-62m mp-1203369, is a different phase of the same ternary system at a stoichiometry none of these compositions has. Measured 91-652 K.

basis: CePdSb, a ferromagnetic Kondo compound measured in two papers on large thermoelectric power in metallic cerium compounds. Equiatomic CePdSb does not take the usual orthorhombic TiNiSi structure: it is hexagonal, the CaIn2 type or its ordered LiGaGe variant, with a puckered honeycomb PdSb net and cerium between the layers. The taxonomy had no entry for that type, so one is proposed.
note: Confidence is medium because there is no database support at all: [ref 2] prints nothing at 1:1:1 for this host -- CeSb3Pd, Ce2(SbPd3)3, Ce(SbPd)2, Ce3Sb5Pd6 and Ce8SbPd24, each with a single ICSD reference -- so mp_id is null and the assignment rests entirely on the intermetallic literature. The competing possibility is the orthorhombic TiNiSi type that most RTX compounds take and that the Ce-Ge-Pd host in this chunk does take, which is why the new entry discriminates against it explicitly. Which of the two hexagonal settings applies, the centrosymmetric CaIn2 one or the ordered polar LiGaGe one, is also unresolved and matters: the ordered variant has no inversion centre. CePdSb orders ferromagnetically near 17 K, at the bottom of the 11-494 K window, so the lowest points are in the ordered state -- magnetic, not structural, so spans_transition stays false.

basis: CeRu2 with a tenth of the cerium replaced by lanthanum or neodymium, from the same paper on the transport properties of (Ce1-xRx)Ru2 that produced the Ce-Nd-Ru host in chunk 033. CeRu2 is the cubic C15 MgCu2 Laves phase and [ref 2] is unambiguous about it: CeRu2 Fd-3m mp-607 at hull 0.000 with 16 ICSD references, far ahead of Ce7Ru3, Ce3Ru and Ce4Ru, none of which matches these compositions.

dopant_roles.site: the rare-earth site of the C15 cell
dopant_roles.basis: (Ce0.9Nd0.1)Ru2: neodymium replaces cerium on the 8a site. Both are trivalent rare earths so the cell is barely disturbed, but cerium in CeRu2 is close to non-magnetic while neodymium carries a full moment, so the substitution is not electronically neutral -- it is how the paper tunes between superconductivity and magnetism.

dopant_roles.site: the rare-earth site of the C15 cell
dopant_roles.basis: (Ce0.9La0.1)Ru2: lanthanum on the same site, trivalent with no 4f electron, which dilutes the 4f lattice without adding a moment. Contrasting it against the neodymium series is the point of the paper.

note: This host is the dilute end of the same series as Ce-Nd-Ru at rank 1648 in chunk 033, which sits at 40 to 80 percent cerium; both were assigned laves_phase and the structure is constant across the whole range. Measured 14-294 K on polycrystals, so nothing structural is crossed.

basis: All three compositions are CeTe2 with antimony substituting on tellurium, from a paper on the dimensional crossover of the charge density wave in this compound. CeTe2 is the Cu2Sb or anti-Fe2As type in P4/nmm: CeTe slabs alternating with a flat square net of tellurium, and it is that square net that carries the CDW the paper measures. The taxonomy entry for that three-site tetragonal stack is pbfcl_matlockite, whose own prototype field names the anti-Fe2As and Cu2Sb relatives explicitly.

dopant_roles.site: most likely the planar square net rather than the slab
dopant_roles.basis: CeTe1.95Sb0.05 and CeTe1.9Sb0.1. Antimony is a pnictogen replacing a chalcogen, so this removes an electron per substitution rather than being isovalent, and the square net is the site where that matters -- it is the band the CDW gaps.

note: [ref 2] disagrees with the compositions and I do not follow it. It lists CeTe Fm-3m mp-1525 with 7 ICSD references, Ce3Te4 I-43d mp-22422 with 5, then Ce10Te19, Ce2Te5 and Ce2Te3 -- and prints nothing at all at CeTe2, which is what every composition in this host is. That is the reference describing a chemistry rather than the phase these single crystals are, so mp_id stays null and stage 2 should resolve the P4/nmm CeTe2 cell directly. Confidence is medium for the same reason: the structure type rests on the rare-earth ditelluride literature and not on a database entry. Note also that the ditellurides are commonly reported with a superstructure or an orthorhombic distortion of the square net rather than the ideal P4/nmm cell, which is precisely the CDW the paper is about. Measured 100-299 K.

basis: The paper is titled Thermoelectric power of Gd4(Co1-xCux)3 compounds, which names a rare-earth-rich R4T3 phase; Gd4Co3 exists in the Gd-Co system and takes the hexagonal Ho4Co3 type in P6_3mc. The taxonomy had no R4T3 entry, so one is proposed. Copper substitutes for cobalt across 10 to 30 percent of that site, which is band filling rather than doping.
note: I disagree with the recorded compositions and say so rather than matching them. All three parse as Gd(Co1-xCux)3, a rare-earth to transition-metal ratio of 1:3, while the paper title is Gd4(Co1-xCux)3, a ratio of 4:3. Those are two different compounds: RT3 is the rhombohedral PuNi3 type in R-3m, an ordered stacking of CaCu5 and Laves blocks, while R4T3 is the hexagonal Ho4Co3 type. I follow the authors formula because it is their own and both phases are real in the Gd-Co diagram, but confidence is low and this host should be settled by reading the paper. If the composition strings are the correct ones then the PuNi3 type is the answer, and the taxonomy lacks an entry for that too -- a v4 file should add one. No reference line was printed for this host, so there is no database evidence either way and mp_id is null. Measured 10-298 K on three curves.
annotator_note: Composition strings and paper title give different stoichiometries; the prototype follows the title.

basis: Na(Co0.8Cu0.2)2O4 is NaCo2O4, which is gamma-Na0.5CoO2: edge-sharing CoO2 sheets with sodium disordered on the interlayer site. The paper is on the influence of partial substitution of Cu for Co on its thermoelectric properties, so copper sits on the cobalt site of that sheet.
note: The second composition is written Na0.6Cu0.4Co2O4, which reads as copper on the sodium layer with the CoO2 sheet left intact, while the first is written Na(Co0.8Cu0.2)2O4, which is copper on the cobalt site. Both come from papers about substituting Cu for Co, so I take the cobalt site for both and treat the second string as a transcription that lost the bracket; the curator detail x = 0.4 matches the substitution level rather than a sodium content. Worth a glance in stage 2 because the two readings put copper in different layers. In this structure the sodium content is itself the compositional variable, not a dopant, which is what the taxonomy entry records for stage 3. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. Measured 573-1074 K.

basis: Co1-xFexGe at x = 0.12 to 0.30, from a paper titled Band-filling dependence of thermoelectric properties in B20-type CoGe. CoGe in the B20 FeSi structure, P2_13, is the host and iron substitutes for cobalt to move the Fermi level -- the band filling of the title.
note: [ref 2] disagrees and I do not follow it. Its entries are the Heusler and half-Heusler cubic phases of this ternary -- FeCo2Ge Fm-3m mp-22300 with 2 ICSD references, Fe2CoGe Fm-3m mp-30044, Fe3Co3Ge2 R3m, FeCoGe P6_3/mmc -- and none of them is at the 1:1 metal-to-germanium ratio every composition here has. The paper names the structure in its own title, which outranks a database list of neighbouring stoichiometries, so mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve B20 CoGe itself. B20 CoGe is metastable and is normally made under pressure or by rapid quenching, which is worth carrying forward. Iron is 12 to 30 percent of the metal site, an alloying level rather than doping, so no dopant role is recorded. Measured 12-291 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [198], ICSD-backed references for this host report [225]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Co2.5Fe0.5Sn2-yInyS2 is Co3Sn2S2 with iron on the cobalt kagome site and indium on the tin site, and the paper is titled Improved Thermoelectric Performance through Double Substitution in Shandite. Both substitutions are at alloying level, which is the point of the study: iron is the hole doping and indium tunes the tin sublattice.
note: No reference line was printed for this five-element host, so mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve the parent Co3Sn2S2 in R-3m and treat these as substituted cells. Co3Sn2S2 is a magnetic Weyl semimetal with a kagome cobalt layer, and iron substitution suppresses that ferromagnetism as well as moving the Fermi level, so the transport is not a simple rigid-band story. Measured 297-626 K.

basis: La(Co0.25Fe0.25Ni0.25Mn0.25)O3 with strontium on the lanthanum site, from a paper on a medium-entropy perovskite oxide. Four transition metals share the single octahedral B site at equal fractions, which is a disordered ABO3 perovskite and not an ordered double perovskite -- ordering needs two species in a 1:1 ratio, not four in a 1:1:1:1 one.

dopant_roles.site: the twelve-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: La0.9Sr0.1 and La0.8Sr0.2 against the undoped LaCo0.25Fe0.25Ni0.25Mn0.25O3. Divalent strontium on a trivalent site is the standard acceptor doping of these perovskites; charge compensation is shared between B-site oxidation and oxygen vacancies.

note: No reference line was printed and mp_id is null; a random four-way B site has no single Materials Project entry in any case, and stage 2 should resolve the parent LaMO3 rather than an ordered supercell. The likely setting is rhombohedral R-3c or orthorhombic Pnma rather than the ideal cubic aristotype, which is normal for lanthanum perovskites and does not change the prototype. Measured 923-1073 K on rod-shaped samples, all well inside the perovskite field.

basis: Pr2CoFeO6 with strontium substituting for praseodymium, and the paper is titled Double perovskite Pr2CoFeO6 thermoelectric oxide. Cobalt and iron are present in an exact 1:1 ratio on the octahedral B site, which is the condition for rock-salt B-site ordering, so this is the A2BBO6 double perovskite rather than a disordered ABO3.

dopant_roles.site: the A site
dopant_roles.basis: Pr1.8Sr0.2CoFeO6 and Pr1.6Sr0.4CoFeO6 against undoped Pr2CoFeO6. Divalent strontium for trivalent praseodymium is acceptor doping, and the paper title makes the role of Sr doping one of its two subjects.

note: No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null. How complete the Co and Fe ordering actually is should be checked in stage 2: cobalt and iron are close in size and charge, so these 3d-3d double perovskites are often only partially ordered and are reported in Pnma as often as in the fully ordered setting. The assignment follows the paper, which names the structure outright. Measured 301-777 K.

basis: Co0.5Zn0.5CrxFe2-xO4 is a mixed cobalt-zinc ferrite: three metals per four oxygen in the AB2O4 ratio, with chromium replacing iron on the octahedral B site. The paper measures structural and electromagnetic properties of that ferrite series.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Cr goes from 0.1 to 0.3 formula units against Fe from 1.9 to 1.7. Cr3+ has a very strong octahedral site preference, so it takes B-site iron and not the tetrahedral A site, which changes the A-B superexchange and hence both the magnetism and the hopping conduction.

note: [ref 2] does not help and I do not follow it. Every entry it prints is a computed ordered Zn-Fe-Co-O supercell -- Zn3Fe12(CoO12)2 Imm2, Zn3Fe8CoO16 P-4m2, ZnFe4CoO8 F-43m, ZnFe8Co3O16 P-4m2 -- all without ICSD references and none containing chromium. Those are ordering approximants of the same cation-disordered spinel, not distinct phases, so mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the parent CoFe2O4 or ZnFe2O4 cell in Fd-3m. The cation distribution between tetrahedral and octahedral sites is the real unknown here: CoFe2O4 is inverse, ZnFe2O4 is normal, and a 50:50 mixture is somewhere between, which is a stage 2 question. The third composition string, Co0.5Zn.5Cr0.3Fe1.7O4, has a malformed zinc subscript and should read Zn0.5. Measured 303-479 K.

basis: Fe7-xCoxS8 at x = 2.8, 4.2 and 5.0, from a paper on spark plasma sintered Fe7-xCoxS8. The 7:8 metal-to-sulfur ratio is pyrrhotite exactly -- a NiAs parent with one metal vacancy in eight ordered onto alternate layers -- and the taxonomy had no entry for it, so one is proposed. The host is flagged mixed because cobalt has no stable M7S8 phase, so the cobalt-rich members are likely to be pentlandite instead.
note: Two prototypes are proposed from this one host and the split between them is by composition. Fe4.2Co2.8S8 is iron-rich and should stay pyrrhotite; Fe2.0Co5.0S8 is five parts cobalt to two iron and is where the pentlandite field takes over, since Co9S8 is the stable cobalt sulfide near this ratio and Co7S8 is not a phase. Fe2.8Co4.2S8 sits between them. [ref 2] leans the same way: its primary is Fe(CoS)8 Fm-3m mp-1188182 at hull 0.002 with one ICSD reference, which is a mixed-metal M9S8 at the pentlandite space group rather than anything at M7S8, and its other entries -- FeCo3S8 R-3, FeCoS2 P-3m1, FeCoS4 P2_1/c -- carry no ICSD reference at all. So the reference does not support the pyrrhotite stoichiometry the paper writes, and neither assignment gets an mp_id. Confidence is low and this host needs the paper diffraction pattern; with only three samples it is cheap to settle. Measured 322-573 K, which also crosses the pyrrhotite vacancy-disordering range, so even the iron-rich member may not be the ordered superstructure at the top of the window.
annotator_note: Two new prototypes proposed; the pyrrhotite-to-pentlandite boundary across this series is a guess from the phase diagram, not from the paper.

basis: Fe44.6Co44.4Zr7.3B3.7Cu1 is HITPERM, and the paper is a thermoelectric and electrical resistivity study of Hitperm alloys published in the Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids. These are melt-spun amorphous ribbons, so the structure at the low-temperature end of the measurement is a metallic glass, not any crystalline prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Boron at 3.7 percent is a glass-forming addition, not a dopant: it is what makes the melt-spun ribbon amorphous in the first place, and it stays in the residual amorphous matrix once the bcc grains nucleate.

Copper at 1 percent is the nucleating agent of this alloy family. It is insoluble in the bcc phase and clusters on annealing, seeding the nanocrystals; recording it as a dopant on a lattice site would be wrong.

One of the three ribbons swaps a unit of zirconium for niobium and another for hafnium, against a baseline with neither. All three are early transition metals playing the same role -- slowing grain growth and stabilising the amorphous precursor -- so niobium is taken as sitting in the zirconium position of the formula.
The same swap in the third ribbon, Fe44.6Co44.4HfZr7.3B3.7Cu1. Hafnium and zirconium are chemically almost interchangeable here.

note: The measurement runs 349-1029 K, which takes these ribbons through their crystallisation. HITPERM is designed to nanocrystallise into ordered B2 alpha-prime FeCo grains in a residual amorphous matrix at around 750 to 800 K, so the upper half of the window is not a glass at all. That is an irreversible transformation rather than a reversible thermal phase sequence, so spans_transition stays false and phases is left empty rather than asserting a transition temperature the paper would have to supply; b2_cscl is recorded as an alternative prototype instead.
