[ref 2] is no help and is not followed: it prints Zr2FeCo Immm at hull 3.410, Zr2FeCo3 R-3m, Zr4FeCo I422 and ZrFeCo Imma, all computed Zr-Fe-Co intermetallics with no ICSD reference and none of them the phase an amorphous ribbon of this composition contains. mp_id is null throughout.

basis: LaCo1-xGaxO3 at x = 0.3 to 0.7, from a paper on the electrical conductivity and thermoelectric power of that series. Both LaCoO3 and LaGaO3 are ABO3 perovskites and gallium and cobalt are close enough in size to form a continuous solid solution on the octahedral B site, so the whole range is one prototype.
note: The third composition is written LaCo0.93Ga0.7O3, whose B-site total is 1.63 rather than 1; read against the paper series it is almost certainly LaCo0.3Ga0.7O3 and the 0.93 is a transcription slip. It does not change the prototype. [ref 2] offers only La2GaCoO6 R-3 mp-1223269 at hull 0.064 with no ICSD reference, which is the 50:50 member drawn as a rhombohedrally ordered double perovskite. I do not take it as a distinct phase: Ga3+ and Co3+ have the same charge and similar radii, which is the case where B-site ordering does not happen, and the series is continuous across x rather than special at 0.5. mp_id is null. The likely real setting is rhombohedral R-3c, as for LaCoO3 itself. Measured 322-1048 K; LaCoO3 has spin-state crossovers inside that window but they are electronic, not structural.

basis: A single composition, ThCoGa4, measured on single crystals in a paper on its crystal structure, transport and thermodynamic properties. [ref 2] gives ThGa4Co Cmcm mp-22767 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, and Cmcm at the RTX4 stoichiometry is the YNiAl4 type, the entry proposed for this family in chunk 031.
note: This reuses ynial4_cmcm, which is still pending review: it was proposed in chunk 031 for the aluminide YbNi0.8Al4.2 and its formula_archetype names aluminium only. Using it here extends it to a gallide with an actinide on the R site. That extension is reasonable -- gallium and aluminium are the usual pair of trielides across this structure type, and the space group and stoichiometry both match -- but whoever reviews the proposal should widen the archetype wording deliberately rather than have it widened by use. Confidence is medium for that reason and because the single ICSD reference behind mp-22767 is thin. The paper reports the crystal structure in its own title, so stage 2 has a direct source for confirming it.
annotator_note: Extends a still-pending chunk 031 proposal from aluminides to gallides; the proposal wording should be widened at review.

basis: Co4Sb8Ge1.9Te2.1 and Co4Sb9Ge1.4Te1.6 are CoSb3 written as Co4X12 with germanium and tellurium replacing antimony in the pnictogen rings in balanced pairs, which is exactly the double substitution the second paper is titled for. The third composition is a deliberate heterostructure of a skutterudite with a germanium antimony telluride, so the host holds two prototypes and is flagged mixed.
note: The split is clean by composition. The two Co4Sb(8-9)GeTe strings are unfilled skutterudites -- the void stays empty, which is why this is skutterudite and not filled_skutterudite. The string (CoSb2Ge0.5Te0.5)2(GeTe)10.5Sb2Te3 is a composite written as its two components: a skutterudite phase and a GeTe-Sb2Te3 homologue of the GST family, from a paper explicitly about heterostructures of the two. Germanium and tellurium enter in near-equal amounts on purpose: Ge is one electron short of Sb and Te is one over, so the pair is close to isoelectronic on the ring site and acts as a phonon scatterer rather than a carrier donor. That is why no dopant role is recorded for either -- both are well above 5 percent and both are framework substitutions rather than doping. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. Measured 296-776 K.

basis: One composition, Co2TiGe, in three papers on the half-metallic ferromagnet Co2TiZ with Z = Si, Ge, Sn. Co2YZ is the full Heusler L2_1 structure and [ref 2] confirms it directly: TiCo2Ge Fm-3m mp-4612 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, ahead of everything else in the ternary.
note: The half-Heusler TiCoGe P-62m mp-22769 that [ref 2] lists second is a different stoichiometry and none of these compositions is at it, so the host is not mixed. Co2TiGe is a half-metallic ferromagnet with a Curie temperature near 380 K, and the measured window is 10-885 K, so the transport crosses that magnetic transition -- magnetic and not structural, so spans_transition stays false, but the anomalous Hall and magnetoresistance papers here are measuring exactly that crossing. One of the three papers is on sputter-deposited films rather than bulk.

basis: Zr0.5Hf0.5Co0.4Rh0.6Sb1-xSnx keeps the 1:1:1 half-Heusler ratio across all six elements -- one unit of group 4 metal, one of group 9, one of main group -- and the paper is titled for the thermoelectric performance of that exact p-type composition. Every substitution is on one of the three sublattices of the MgAgAs cell.
note: Three separate alloying axes run at once and none is dilute doping: Zr and Hf split the group 4 site 50:50, Co and Rh split the group 9 site 40:60, and Sn replaces 20 to 40 percent of the Sb. Only the last changes the valence electron count -- eighteen electrons per formula unit is the semiconducting condition for a half-Heusler, and Sn for Sb is what takes it below that and makes the material p-type. The Zr-Hf and Co-Rh substitutions are isovalent mass disorder aimed at the lattice thermal conductivity. No reference line was printed for this six-element host and mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve ZrCoSb in F-43m as the parent. Measured 269-775 K.

basis: IFexCo4-xSb12 from a paper on iodine-filled FexCo4-xSb12 polycrystals. The CoSb3 framework is intact at Co4Sb12 and iodine occupies the icosahedral void, so this is the filled entry rather than the binary one; iron substitutes for cobalt on the framework to compensate the charge the filler adds.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral framework metal site
dopant_roles.basis: IFe0.3Co3.7Sb12 through IFe0.7Co3.3Sb12. Iron on the cobalt site removes an electron per substitution and is what offsets the electrons donated by the filler; the two are tuned against each other in this paper, which is why the iron content is varied and the iodine content is not.

note: Iodine is an unusual filler and worth flagging for stage 3. Almost every filled skutterudite in this dataset has an electropositive guest -- a rare earth, an alkaline earth, In or Tl -- that donates electrons to the framework. A halogen in the same void is the opposite case, and the taxonomy notes for this prototype describe the filler as a rattler in the icosahedral void without addressing the sign of its charge transfer. [ref 2] offers only Co5Sb15I C2/m mp-1226477 at hull 0.064 with no ICSD reference, which is a computed ordered iodine-containing cell in a monoclinic setting rather than the body-centred cubic Im-3 filled skutterudite. I do not take it; mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve the Im-3 cell. Measured 296-601 K.

basis: CoTi1-y(Nb,Ta)ySb1-xSnx from a paper titled High temperature thermoelectric properties of CoTiSb half-Heusler compounds. The 1:1:1 ratio holds in every composition: one cobalt, one unit of Ti plus Nb plus Ta, one unit of Sb plus Sn.
note: Nb and Ta together track the Sn content exactly across the three samples -- Ti0.6Nb0.2Ta0.2 with Sb0.6Sn0.4, then 0.4/0.3/0.3 with Sb0.4Sn0.6, then 0.2/0.4/0.4 with Sb0.2Sn0.8 -- so the two substitutions are deliberately balanced. Group 5 Nb and Ta on the group 4 titanium site each add an electron and group 14 Sn on the group 15 antimony site each remove one, keeping the eighteen-electron count roughly fixed while the mass disorder rises. This is alloying across nearly the whole composition range, not doping, so no dopant role is recorded for any of the four. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null; the parent to resolve is CoTiSb in F-43m. Measured 40-937 K.

basis: Co39Ni61, Co71Ni29 and Co24Ni76, measured as single electrodeposited nanowires. Cobalt and nickel are mutually soluble in all proportions and form a disordered substitutional alloy on one metal site rather than an ordered compound, so the prototype is the solid solution.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the single metal site of the close-packed lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: Cobalt fraction. These two are adjacent in the periodic table rather than in the same group, so this is not an isoelectronic axis -- each cobalt for nickel removes an electron and the moment rises across the series, which is what the magneto-thermopower measures. It is recorded here anyway because it is a genuine continuous substitution on one site with no parent compound at the host level.

note: Confidence is medium because the packing is not settled by composition alone. Nickel-rich CoNi is fcc, cobalt-rich CoNi can be hcp, and the boundary near room temperature sits around 70 percent cobalt -- which is exactly where Co71Ni29 falls. Electrodeposited nanowires complicate it further: the deposition conditions and the template diameter influence which phase grows, and mixed fcc-hcp wires are common. So fcc or hcp is a per-sample question, not a per-host one. [ref 2] is not followed: Co3Ni Pm-3m mp-1008349 and CoNi Pm-3m mp-1006883 are ordered L1_2 and B2-like cells with a single ICSD reference each, and an ordered phase is not what electrodeposition at these compositions produces. mp_id is null. Measured 56-288 K.

basis: SrCo1-xScxO3 at x = 0.3 to 0.5, from a paper on the effect of scandium doping concentration on strontium cobaltite. SrCoO3-delta is an ABO3 perovskite and scandium substitutes on the octahedral cobalt site; scandium is added in these materials precisely to stabilise the cubic perovskite against the ordered oxygen-vacancy alternatives.
note: Confidence is medium and brownmillerite is carried as an alternative for a reason. SrCoO3-delta is the textbook case where the oxygen content decides the structure: fully oxidised it is the cubic perovskite, reduced to SrCoO2.5 it is the ordered brownmillerite with alternating octahedral and tetrahedral layers, and a slowly cooled sample lands in between. The compositions here are all written as stoichiometric O3, which for a strontium cobaltite is a nominal formula rather than a measured one. Scandium at 30 to 50 percent of the B site is very high for this family -- the well-known cathode compositions sit near 10 percent -- so how much of it the perovskite field actually accommodates is itself a question for the paper. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. Measured 575-1173 K, high enough that the cubic form is the more likely one at temperature whatever the room-temperature structure is.

basis: (CoSi)1-x(SiO2)x at x = 0.075 to 0.15, written as its two components by the curator. The matrix is CoSi, the B20 FeSi structure in P2_13, and the silica is a deliberate second phase added to scatter phonons in a hot-pressed compact. The prototype is the matrix, not the additive.

dopant_roles.basis: Oxygen is about 14 percent of the atoms at x = 0.15, but all of it belongs to the SiO2 particles rather than to the CoSi lattice -- oxygen has no solubility in a B20 silicide. It is well above the 5 percent dopant threshold and is recorded here anyway because the threshold would otherwise make it look like a major host element.

note: This is the composite-additive case the project already has a regression check for, and it is recorded that way: the silica is separate, not dissolved, so the host keeps the CoSi prototype. [ref 2] reads it the other way and I do not follow it -- every entry it prints is a cobalt silicate, Co2SiO4 Pnma mp-25474 with 8 ICSD references, CoSiO3 Pbca, CoSiO4 Pna2_1, and a quaternary silicate -- which is what a Co-O-Si element set looks like as a chemistry but not what a hot-pressed CoSi plus SiO2 compact is. mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve B20 CoSi. The silica itself is amorphous or cristobalite depending on the pressing, and is not worth a prototype of its own. Measured 298-982 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [198], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62, 74, 61]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, CoSe, from a paper titled Frustrated magnetism in the tetragonal CoSe analog of superconducting FeSe. The paper names the structure outright: this is the anti-PbO layered form, P4/nmm, built from edge-sharing CoSe4 tetrahedra in the same layer FeSe has, and not the hexagonal NiAs-type CoSe.

other_polymorphs.note: Hexagonal NiAs-type CoSe, mp-426 with 8 ICSD references, is the thermodynamically stable form of this formula and is what both references put forward. It is kept out of phases because it is not what this sample is: the tetragonal analogue is made by deintercalating potassium from KCo2Se2 at low temperature and does not convert to or from the hexagonal form over the 10-12 K window measured here. The occurrence code is unknown rather than metastable because it is the assigned phase that is metastable, not this one.

note: Both references disagree with the assignment and I record that rather than matching them. [ref 1], the TEDesignLab entry, gives Co9Se8 Fm-3m mp-22745 and Co3Se4 Fd-3m mp-20456, neither of which is CoSe at all. [ref 2] gives CoSe2 Pa-3 mp-22309 with 9 ICSD references as its primary and CoSe P6_3/mmc mp-426 with 8 as the best-attested entry at the right formula. The reference is right about which phases exist in the Co-Se chemistry; it is wrong about which one this crystal is, and the paper title settles it. This is a textbook instance of the reference describing a chemistry rather than a sample. mp_id is null because the tetragonal form is not offered by either reference. Measured 10-12 K on three curves -- essentially a single low-temperature point, so this host carries very little weight.
annotator_note: Assignment deliberately contradicts both reference lines; the paper title names the tetragonal form explicitly.

basis: Co4Sn6Se6 is Co4X12 with the pnictogen rings built from equal parts tin and selenium, and the paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties of Co4Sn6Se6 Ternary Skutterudites. Tin and selenium flank the pnictogens on either side, so the pair together supplies the same electron count antimony would, which is how a skutterudite framework can be made with no group 15 element in it at all.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral framework metal site
dopant_roles.basis: Co3.6Ru0.4Sn6Se6. Ruthenium is isovalent with cobalt in group 9 and much heavier, so this is mass disorder on the framework aimed at the lattice thermal conductivity rather than carrier doping.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral framework metal site
dopant_roles.basis: Co3.8Ni0.2Sn6Se6. Nickel is one group to the right of cobalt, so it donates an electron to the framework and is n-type doping proper.

note: The void is empty in all three compositions, so this is the unfilled entry rather than filled_skutterudite. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve the Im-3 ternary cell, in which the Sn and Se are expected to order within the four-membered rings rather than sit at random, and whether that ordering lowers the symmetry below Im-3 is worth checking. Measured 301-804 K.

basis: One composition, YCo2, in three papers on transport in RCo2 spin-fluctuation compounds. YCo2 is the cubic C15 MgCu2 Laves phase and [ref 2] is decisive: YCo2 Fd-3m mp-1077486 at hull 0.000 with 28 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in the whole binary.
note: The other [ref 2] entries -- YCo3 R-3m with 27 ICSD references, YCo5 P6/mmm with 21, Y3Co Pnma, Y2Co17 R-3m -- are the neighbouring phases of the Y-Co system and are well attested, but none of these samples is at those stoichiometries, so the host is not mixed. YCo2 is an exchange-enhanced paramagnet on the edge of magnetic order, which is what all three papers measure through the thermopower. Note that the third paper listed is on a CeCo2 single crystal rather than YCo2; the two are the same structure type and the linkage is presumably through a shared figure. The robust measured range is 11-496 K against a full span to 996 K, so the higher points are sparse.

basis: MgFexCr2-xO4 across x = 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5: three metals to four oxygen in the AB2O4 ratio, magnesium on the tetrahedral A site and iron and chromium sharing the octahedral B site. MgCr2O4 and MgFe2O4 are both spinels and form a continuous solid solution, so the whole series is one prototype.
note: [ref 2] gives nothing usable and is not followed. Its entries -- Mg14CrFeO16 Pmmm, Mg30CrFeO32 P4/mmm, Mg3Cr8FeO16 R3m, Mg6CrFeO8 P4/mmm, MgCr4FeO8 F-43m -- are all computed dilute-substitution supercells with no ICSD reference, mostly at magnesium contents far above anything here, and several are rocksalt-derived rather than spinel. They are artefacts of how a quaternary oxide is sampled in the database, not phases. mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve MgCr2O4 or MgFe2O4 in Fd-3m. The real stage 2 question is the inversion parameter: MgCr2O4 is normal because Cr3+ will not leave the octahedral site, MgFe2O4 is largely inverse, so the site distribution shifts across the series and the hopping conduction shifts with it. Measured 322-697 K.

basis: FeCr2S4 with copper substituting for iron, from two papers on chalcogenide spinel crystals and on electrical transport in FeCr2S4-CuCr2S4 spinels. [ref 1], the TEDesignLab entry, confirms it: Cr2FeS4 Fd-3m mp-21019 with 16 ICSD references, the thiospinel with iron on the tetrahedral site and chromium on the octahedral one.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral A site
dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.94Cu0.06Cr2S4 and Fe0.86Cu0.14Cr2S4, the dilute end of the FeCr2S4-CuCr2S4 line the second paper is titled for. Copper enters the spinel as Cu+ rather than Cu2+, so each substitution removes an electron from the chromium band -- it is hole doping and not an isovalent swap, which is why a few percent changes the transport so much.

note: This host is a clean demonstration of why the chunk header says not to rank by e_above_hull. The correct answer, mp-21019, sits at hull 0.096 with 16 ICSD references, while [ref 2] leads with computed supercells at lower hull and no ICSD support at all -- Cr12Fe3S20 P-1, Cr8Fe2CuNiS16 R3m, Cr8Fe3NiS16 R3m, CrFeS2 P-3m1, CrFeS4 Imma. The ICSD count picks the real phase and the hull does not. Note that cr3s4_defect_nias names a monoclinic form of FeCr2S4 among its representative materials, but that is the high-pressure or defect variant and the cubic thiospinel is what these crystals are. FeCr2S4 orders ferrimagnetically near 170 K, inside the 10-494 K window, and has an orbital-ordering structural distortion below about 10 K -- at the very bottom of the range and on only three curves, so spans_transition stays false.

basis: Si0.8Ge0.2B0.016(CrSi2)0.091, from a paper comparing p-type nanostructured bulk SiGe alloys. The host is the Si0.8Ge0.2 solid solution in the diamond structure, boron is the acceptor, and the CrSi2 is a dispersed second phase added for phonon scattering rather than anything dissolved in the lattice.

dopant_roles.site: the single diamond-lattice site shared by Si and Ge
dopant_roles.basis: Boron at 1.6 percent of the formula is the standard p-type dopant for SiGe thermoelectrics: a group 13 acceptor on the group 14 site. At this level it is above the solubility limit for a clean substitutional picture, so some of it is likely precipitated, but its purpose is doping.

All the chromium is in the (CrSi2)0.091 term -- roughly 7 percent of the atoms, and so just above the dopant threshold. Chromium has negligible solubility in silicon and the paper adds CrSi2 as a nanoinclusion, so none of it should be treated as a dopant on the diamond lattice.

note: Only one composition and it is fixed at Si0.8Ge0.2, so there is no spread to record as a solid-solution axis even though Si and Ge share the site isoelectronically -- the whole series here is at a single point. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. The CrSi2 inclusions are the C40 hexagonal disilicide, the same phase the Cr-Mo-Si host at rank 1678 is made of, but they are a minority additive here and the host keeps the diamond prototype rather than being flagged mixed. Measured 293-1142 K.

basis: Cr1-xMoxSi2 at x = 0.2 to 0.3, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of that series. CrSi2 is the C40 hexagonal disilicide in P6_222 and molybdenum substitutes for chromium; at these contents the C40 structure is retained, since the changeover to the MoSi2 C11b tetragonal type happens much closer to the molybdenum end.
note: Molybdenum is 20 to 30 percent of the metal site, which is alloying rather than doping, so no dopant role is recorded; it is isovalent with chromium in group 6, so the effect is on the band widths and the lattice thermal conductivity rather than on the carrier count. [ref 2] offers nothing at this stoichiometry and is not followed -- Cr3Si2Mo3 R32 mp-1226248 and CrSiMo Amm2 mp-1226241 are both computed ternaries with no ICSD reference and neither is an MSi2 disilicide. mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve CrSi2 in P6_222. Worth noting that C40 and C11b are close in energy across this system and that the transition is composition-dependent, so a sample near the upper end of the range should have its space group confirmed rather than assumed. Measured 320-1070 K.

basis: The single composition string is Si NCs, which is silicon nanocrystals written in words, and the paper is on pseudo-direct bandgap transitions in silicon nanocrystals. The material is silicon in the diamond structure; caesium and nitrogen are not in it.

dopant_roles.basis: The letters Cs in the abbreviation NCs, meaning nanocrystals, were read as the element caesium by the composition parser.

The letter N in the same abbreviation, read as nitrogen. Between them Cs and N account for two thirds of the parsed atoms, which is why neither appears in the dopant candidate list -- the parser gave each an implied coefficient of one.

note: The host key itself is wrong: these samples belong in the elemental Si host, not in a Cs-N-Si ternary. Worth carrying back to generate_annotation_data.py as a parser case -- an uppercase letter followed by a lowercase one inside an abbreviation is exactly the pattern element symbols use, so NCs, MPs, NWs and NPs will all do this. The structural assignment is unaffected: silicon nanocrystals are diamond-cubic silicon, with the quantum confinement and surface chemistry rather than the lattice being what the paper is about. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. Measured 321-449 K.
annotator_note: host_system is a parser artefact -- Si NCs read as Cs plus N plus Si. The samples are elemental silicon.

basis: One composition, Cs8Na16Si136, and two papers on the synthesis and transport properties of type II clathrates. The Si136 framework with 8 large and 16 small cages filled is the defining stoichiometry of the type II clathrate, and [ref 2] matches it exactly: CsNa2Si17 Fd-3m mp-4877 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references is the same formula divided by eight, in the type II space group.
note: Both guests are above the 5 percent threshold and neither is a dopant: caesium fills the sixteen-vertex cages and sodium the twenty-vertex ones, and the cage occupancies are the compositional variables of this material rather than doping levels. That distinction matters for stage 3, which should treat them the way the taxonomy treats x in NaxCoO2. The other [ref 2] entry, Cs7NaSi8 Pa-3 mp-1199908, is a Zintl silicide with isolated Si4 tetrahedra and not a clathrate, so it is not an alternative here. Measured 10-301 K.

basis: RuSr2EuCu2O8 is the Ru-1212 ruthenocuprate and RuSr2Eu1.5Ce0.5Cu2O10 is the Ru-1222, and the papers name both by those labels. Each stacks a RuO2 sheet against CuO2 bilayers in place of the copper-oxide charge reservoir of an ordinary cuprate, which is exactly what this prototype covers, so both compositions fall under one entry.

dopant_roles.site: the fluorite block between the CuO2 bilayers
dopant_roles.basis: RuSr2Eu1.5Ce0.5Cu2O10. The cerium is not dilute doping of the 1212 compound -- it is what builds the 1222 structure: replacing a quarter of the rare earth by tetravalent cerium expands the single rare-earth layer into a fluorite-type Eu-Ce-O block and adds two oxygens per formula. It falls below the 5 percent threshold only because the formula has 16 atoms.

note: The two compositions are different members of the same family rather than different prototypes, so the host is not flagged mixed, but stage 2 still has to separate them: Ru-1212 is P4/mmm with a single rare-earth layer and Ru-1222 is I4/mmm with a fluorite block, so they need different structures even though the prototype label is the same. That split is clean on the Ce content. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. These are magnetic superconductors -- ferromagnetic order in the RuO2 layer coexisting with superconductivity in the CuO2 bilayers -- which is what both papers are about; measured 11-257 K, so the transport is entirely in that regime.

basis: Two of the three compositions are Sr1-xEuxCuO2 at x around 0.21, which is the infinite-layer cuprate: CuO2 sheets separated only by a bare alkaline-earth layer, with europium substitution providing electron doping. The third is (Nb0.5Cu0.5)Sr2EuCu2O8, a 1212 cuprate with a mixed Nb-Cu charge reservoir, so the host holds two different cuprate structures and is flagged mixed.

dopant_roles.site: the charge-reservoir layer of the 1212 stack
dopant_roles.basis: (Nb0.5Cu0.5)Sr2EuCu2O8, from a paper on new Nb-based cuprates. Niobium shares the reservoir site with copper in a 1:1 ratio and is what makes this a distinct compound rather than a doped one; it is below the threshold only because the formula has 14 atoms.

note: The split is clean by composition: two Sr-Eu-Cu-O2 strings against one A-site-heavy 1212 string. The 1212 member is filed against hg_tl_1212_cuprate because that entry describes the stacking -- two CuO2 sheets around a rare-earth layer with a charge reservoir between blocks -- and not because there is any mercury or thallium here; the reservoir cation is what differs and a v4 file may want a broader 1212 entry that does not name specific reservoir elements. Confidence is medium for that reason. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. The infinite-layer members are electron-doped, which is the rarer side of cuprate physics, and the second paper measures percolative superconductivity in them. Measured 11-300 K.
annotator_note: hg_tl_1212_cuprate is used for a Nb-based 1212 compound; the entry name is narrower than the structure it describes.

basis: Cu2Zn1-xFexGeSe4 at x = 0.4 to 0.6. The I2-II-IV-VI4 quaternary with two copper, one divalent metal, one group 14 element and four chalcogens is the stannite and kesterite family, a cation-ordered superstructure of sphalerite, and the paper is on phonon scattering from local structural disorder in that compound.
note: Zinc and iron split the divalent site nearly 50:50 across all three samples. They are isovalent as Zn2+ and Fe2+ but they are not in the same periodic group, so the generator solid-solution detector will not have flagged this axis and none is recorded here; it is a genuine substitution series on one site all the same, and the local ordering it creates is the anisotropic disorder the paper measures. Cu2ZnGeSe4 is normally reported in the stannite setting I-42m and Cu2FeGeSe4 likewise, so the end members agree, but which of stannite and kesterite a mixed crystal takes is a stage 2 question and the two differ only in how the copper and divalent cations are arranged. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. Measured 299-677 K.

basis: SrFe0.7Cu0.3O3 and SrFe0.6Cu0.3W0.1O3, from papers on copper-doped SrFeO3-delta perovskites as solid-oxide fuel cell cathodes. SrFeO3-delta is an ABO3 perovskite and copper and tungsten both substitute on the octahedral iron site.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: SrFe0.6Cu0.3W0.1O3, against SrFe0.7Cu0.3O3 with the same copper content and no tungsten -- so tungsten is the varied element and it displaces iron. W6+ is a high-valence donor on a site otherwise carrying Fe3+ or Fe4+, added to stabilise the cubic perovskite and suppress the oxygen-vacancy ordering that plagues SrFeO3-delta.

note: [ref 2] gives SrFe4(CuO4)3 Im-3 mp-1105138 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references, which is the A-site-ordered quadruple perovskite SrCu3Fe4O12 -- a real and well-attested compound, but at a copper-to-iron ratio of 3:4 where these samples are at 3:7, and requiring high-pressure synthesis rather than the ceramic route a cathode study uses. I do not take it; mp_id is null and the reference is recorded as disagreeing. As with the Co-O-Sc-Sr host, the compositions are written as stoichiometric O3 when SrFeO3-delta is always oxygen-deficient, and the vacancy content decides whether the sample is cubic perovskite or the ordered brownmillerite-like Sr4Fe4O11 variant. Measured 370-1072 K, hot enough that the disordered cubic form is the likely one at temperature.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62, 167, 221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [204]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CuxZn1-xFe2O4 at x = 0.4 to 0.6, from papers on thermoelectric power of zinc-substituted copper ferrites. Three metals to four oxygen in the AB2O4 ratio with copper and zinc sharing the divalent site: this is the copper-zinc ferrite spinel series.
note: [ref 2] offers only ZnFe4CuO8 R3m mp-1215656 at hull 0.041, a computed ordered supercell with no ICSD reference and in a rhombohedral setting rather than Fd-3m. It is an ordering approximant of the disordered spinel, not a phase, so mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve CuFe2O4 or ZnFe2O4 directly. The real subtlety is that CuFe2O4 is tetragonally distorted to I4_1/amd by the Jahn-Teller activity of Cu2+ on the octahedral site, while ZnFe2O4 is cubic and normal, so this series runs between two different settings of the same prototype and the boundary is near the compositions studied here -- worth confirming per composition rather than assuming cubic. The same paper also produced the Co-Fe-O-Zn host at rank 1659. Measured 303-483 K on the robust range.

basis: Cu2ZnGeSe4-xSx across x = 1, 2 and 3, from a paper on the effect of isovalent substitution on the thermoelectric properties of that quaternary. The I2-II-IV-VI4 composition is the stannite and kesterite family and sulfur simply replaces selenium on the anion site throughout.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the anion site of the tetrahedral framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Sulfur fraction of the anion site, from Cu2ZnGeSe3S through Se2S2 to Se1S3. Both are group 16 and both sit on the same tetrahedral anion position, so this is the isoelectronic case the schema describes -- it tunes the band gap and the lattice thermal conductivity without changing the carrier count, which is what the paper title means by isovalent substitution. There is no end member at the host level and stage 3 should assign one per composition.

note: [ref 2] prints the 50:50 member twice and flags it ambiguous: ZnCu2Ge(SeS)2 Pmn2_1 mp-1215417 at hull 0.006 and the same formula in Fmm2 mp-1215643 at hull 0.015, neither with an ICSD reference. Pmn2_1 is the wurtz-stannite setting, built on a hexagonal rather than a cubic close-packed anion lattice, which is a real alternative for this family and not just an ordering variant -- Cu2ZnGeSe4 is usually reported as tetragonal stannite in I-42m but wurtz-stannite forms are known. So the reference does not settle the packing and mp_id is null; the prototype covers both orderings of the cubic-packed form and stage 2 will have to pick the setting. Measured 298-676 K.

basis: One composition, YbCu2Ge2, in papers on the Yb valence and the Fermi surface of high-quality single crystals. The RT2X2 stoichiometry with a rare earth is the ThCr2Si2 type, and [ref 2] confirms it: Yb(CuGe)2 I4/mmm mp-13401 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, I4/mmm being the ThCr2Si2 space group.
note: The other [ref 2] entries -- YbCuGe P6_3/mmc, Yb3(CuGe)4 Immm, Yb2CuGe6 C2/m -- are neighbouring phases of the ternary at stoichiometries none of these samples has, so the host is not mixed. The interesting physics is the ytterbium valence, which is intermediate and temperature-dependent and drives a chemical expansion of the cell over the 16-350 K window, but that is a continuous crossover rather than a structural transition, so spans_transition stays false. The first paper listed, on rare-earth doping of SrTiO3, has nothing to do with YbCu2Ge2 and appears to be a linkage artefact in the sample table rather than a source for this host.

basis: Cu2HgSnSe4-xTex across the middle of the range, from a paper on the Cu2HgSnSe4-Cu2HgSnTe4 solid solution. Both end members are I2-II-IV-VI4 quaternaries of the stannite family and tellurium replaces selenium on the anion site, so one prototype covers the whole series.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the anion site of the tetrahedral framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Selenium fraction of the anion site, from Se0.8Te3.2 through Se2Te2 to Se3.2Te0.8. Isoelectronic on one site, so it tunes the gap and the lattice thermal conductivity rather than the carrier count; the parent compound depends on the composition and stage 3 should assign it per composition rather than at host level.

note: No reference line was printed for this five-element host and mp_id is null. Both end members are reported in the stannite setting I-42m, so the prototype is safe, but Cu2HgSnTe4 is the less well characterised of the two and the tellurium-rich members are worth confirming. Mercury on the divalent site makes these narrow-gap and close to semimetallic, which is why the series is studied. Measured 295-576 K.

basis: One composition, UCu5In, from a single-crystal study of it as a dense Kondo antiferromagnet. At AB6 with the B site split five to one between copper and indium, the natural structure is the CeCu6 type ordered onto that split, and [ref 2] agrees on the setting: UInCu5 Pnma mp-1208657, the CeCu6 space group.
note: Confidence is medium and mp_id is left null because the single [ref 2] entry carries no ICSD reference and sits at hull 0.029, so it is a computed structure rather than an observed one. The competing possibility is worth stating: the neighbouring compound UCu4In is cubic AuBe5-type in F-43m, the taxonomy aube5 entry, and these two stoichiometries sit one copper apart in the same ternary. If the real phase is UCu4In with excess copper rather than a line compound at UCu5In, the prototype is aube5 and not cecu6. The Pnma setting the reference gives is what tips it to the CeCu6 reading, since AuBe5 is cubic. Note also that the cecu6 entry in the seed taxonomy is thin -- no representative materials and a single discriminate_from line -- and this is the first use of it outside its own Ce-Cu host, so a v4 file should fill it out with the ordered CeCu5Au-type derivatives this assignment relies on. Measured 11-299 K on single crystals.
annotator_note: Prototype rests on the Materials Project space group for a computed entry with no ICSD reference; AuBe5 is a live alternative.

basis: La0.8Sr0.2Cu0.3Mn0.7O3 and LaCu0.25Mn0.75O3, from fuel-cell cathode studies. Both are ABO3 with lanthanum and strontium on the A site and copper and manganese sharing the octahedral B site, so the prototype is the simple perovskite.

dopant_roles.site: the twelve-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: La0.8Sr0.2 in two of the three samples. Divalent strontium on the trivalent lanthanum site is acceptor doping, compensated by Mn4+ and by oxygen vacancies -- the standard hole doping of the lanthanum manganites.

note: Two of the three papers call this a double perovskite in their titles and I do not follow them. B-site rock-salt ordering needs the two cations in a 1:1 ratio and at comparable size contrast; here copper to manganese is 0.3 to 0.7 and 0.25 to 0.75, so a disordered B site is much the likelier structure and the label in those titles is loose usage. [ref 2] points at a third possibility, LaMn4(CuO4)3 Im-3 mp-1211392 at hull 0.024 with no ICSD reference, which is the A-site-ordered quadruple perovskite LaCu3Mn4O12. That is a real compound with a genuine thermoelectric literature, but it requires copper at 3:4 against manganese where these are at 1:3, and it is a high-pressure phase. Neither reading is taken; mp_id is null and confidence is medium because two independent sources disagree with the plain reading of the formula. Measured 323-1428 K, the widest window in this chunk.
annotator_note: Paper titles say double perovskite and the reference suggests a quadruple perovskite; the Cu:Mn ratio supports neither, so the simple perovskite is assigned.

basis: Cux(TaN)1-x at x = 0.25 to 0.35, from a paper on the electrical resistivities and temperature-coefficient behaviour of co-sputtered TaN-Ag and TaN-Cu films. Copper and TaN are mutually insoluble, so a co-sputtered film at a quarter to a third copper is a two-phase composite of metallic copper in a TaN matrix, not a ternary compound.
note: The matrix prototype is recorded as an alternative because it is real and resolvable -- TaN in the rocksalt nitride structure, Fm-3m, usually substoichiometric as TaN1-x when sputtered -- but the host is given composite_multiphase rather than that, because copper at a third of the atoms is a majority-scale second phase and not an additive. That is the opposite call from the Co-O-Si and Cr-Ge-Si hosts in this chunk, where the second phase is under 15 percent and the matrix keeps the label; the boundary is a judgement about scale and it is stated here so it can be reviewed. is_mixed is false because each composition is itself the composite -- there is nothing to split per composition. [ref 2] offers TaCuN2 R-3m mp-8927 at hull 0.127 with one ICSD reference, an ordered layered ternary nitride, and I do not take it: a reactively sputtered film at 300 K does not assemble an ordered ternary, and the hull value says it is not the stable arrangement anyway. mp_id is null. The curator composition details are sputtering power densities rather than composition information. Measured 274-373 K.

basis: Sr2-xNaxCuO3 at x = 0.5, 0.7 and 1.0, from a paper on the preparation and electrical and magnetic properties of that series. Sr2CuO3 is not a layered cuprate at all: it is the one-dimensional chain compound, Immm, built from corner-sharing CuO4 squares running in a single direction with no bridging oxygen between chains.
note: Sodium runs from a quarter to a half of the alkaline-earth site, far above any doping threshold, so no dopant role is recorded; monovalent sodium on a divalent site is heavy hole doping of the chains, which is what the paper measures. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve Sr2CuO3 in Immm. Sr2CuO3 is the textbook spin-half Heisenberg chain and its transport is strongly anisotropic, so a polycrystalline measurement is an average over directions -- worth carrying forward, since the same caveat will apply to every member of this prototype. Measured 36-279 K.

basis: One composition, Tl3CuNb2Se12, from the paper titled Exploring Thallium Compounds as Thermoelectric Materials: Seventeen New Thallium Chalcogenides. It is a new quaternary reported in that survey and I cannot place it in any prototype the taxonomy carries, so it is parked rather than guessed at.
note: What the formula does say is worth recording for whoever picks this up. Niobium to selenium is 1:6, which in a niobium selenide means NbSe6 trigonal-prismatic units -- either condensed into chains by face sharing, as in NbSe3, or isolated as Nb2Se11 bioctahedral or biprismatic clusters with Se-Se dimers, as in the alkali-metal niobium polyselenides. Thallium and copper would then be counter-cations between those units, with thallium as Tl+ and copper as Cu+. That points at a low-dimensional chain or cluster structure, which is why these compounds are in a thermoelectric survey at all. But nbse3_chain assumes the specific NbSe3 chain and I have no basis for asserting it here, and a prototype cannot be proposed without a structure to name, so unresolved_crystalline is the honest entry. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. The Chem. Mater. paper reports crystal structures for all seventeen compounds, so this is settleable by reading one table. Measured 80-301 K.
annotator_note: Structure not identified; the paper itself reports it and would settle this host immediately.

basis: The paper is titled for R2-xSrxNi1-yCuyO4+delta, which is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper phase -- the K2NiF4 structure of single NiO2 sheets alternating with rock-salt A2O2 blocks. Copper substitutes for nickel in the sheet and strontium for neodymium in the rock-salt block.
note: The recorded compositions do not balance and I follow the paper instead. All three are written Nd1.6Sr1.4Ni1-yCuyO4, which puts three A-site cations against one B-site cation and four oxygen -- not a stoichiometry any Ruddlesden-Popper member has. The paper formula R2-xSrxNiO4 with x = 1.4 gives Nd0.6Sr1.4NiO4, an A-site total of 2, which is the K2NiF4 composition exactly; the curator appears to have written 1.6 where 0.6 was meant. That is a transcription error in the digits and does not touch the prototype, but stage 3 will compute the wrong substitution levels from the strings as they stand. [ref 2] offers only Sr5Nd5Cu(NiO5)4 P1 mp-743818 at hull 0.161, a triclinic computed cell with no ICSD reference, which is not a phase; mp_id is null. The oxygen excess delta on the interstitial site is the doping variable in this family, not an impurity. Measured 13-296 K.
annotator_note: Composition strings give Nd1.6 where the paper formula requires Nd0.6; the A-site total does not balance as recorded.

basis: Yb(Ni1-xCux)2Si2 at x = 0.375 to 0.875, from a paper on the thermopower of ytterbium heavy-fermion compounds under pressure. Both YbNi2Si2 and YbCu2Si2 are ThCr2Si2-type in I4/mmm and nickel and copper share the transition-metal site across the whole range, so the structure is constant.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the transition-metal site of the ThCr2Si2 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Copper fraction of the transition-metal site. Not isoelectronic -- copper brings one more d electron than nickel -- and that is the point: the substitution moves the ytterbium between nearly trivalent and nearly divalent, tuning the Kondo temperature chemically in the same way the paper tunes it with pressure. Recorded as an axis because it is a genuine continuous one-site substitution with no parent compound at host level, not because it is isovalent.

note: No reference line was printed for this quaternary and mp_id is null; the parents to resolve are YbNi2Si2 and YbCu2Si2, both I4/mmm. Ytterbium valence in this family is intermediate and temperature-dependent, so the cell parameters change over the 10-298 K window without any change of structure. Measured 10-298 K on polycrystals.

basis: One composition, SrOCuSbSe2, from a Chem. Mater. paper reporting a high Seebeck coefficient and low thermal conductivity in it. The formula is clearly a layered oxyselenide -- an oxide layer built on strontium alongside a copper antimony selenide layer -- but it matches no prototype in the taxonomy and I will not force it into one.
note: The obvious candidate is zrcusias_1111, the BiCuSeO family, and it does not fit. That structure is MOCuCh with one chalcogen per formula and a fluorite-type M2O2 layer; this formula has an extra antimony and a second selenium, so the anion block is larger and differently built. Two readings are plausible and I cannot choose between them: an intergrowth of a rocksalt-like SrO layer with a CuSbSe2 chalcostibite-like layer, or a 1111-derived stack in which a CuSbSe2 slab replaces the simple Cu2Se2 one. Either way it is a new layered oxychalcogenide and the paper that reports it will name the space group. Note also the warning in the project README about oxygen in a mixed-anion host: the axis detector will see O and Se as group 16 partners, and they are not on the same site here any more than they are in BiCuSeO. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. Measured 140-851 K on both polycrystals and a single crystal, which is an unusually wide window for a host this small.
annotator_note: Structure not identified; a new layered oxyselenide, and the source paper reports its structure.

basis: Both compositions are written as (Cu2Se)a(Cu2O)b, and the paper is titled The electrical properties of Cu2Se plus Cu2O composites. These are two-phase mixtures of superionic Cu2Se and cuprite Cu2O with the oxide as the majority component at 68 to 77 mol percent, so neither single prototype describes the sample.
note: Both constituent prototypes are recorded as alternatives since both are genuinely present and both are already in the taxonomy. is_mixed is false because the two phases coexist inside each composition rather than separating between compositions -- there is nothing for a composition-level split to do. The Cu2Se minority component has its superionic transition near 400 K, inside the 309-579 K measured window, so the composite does change structurally partway through the measurement; I leave spans_transition false and phases empty rather than assert a phase sequence for a composite whose majority phase is unaffected, but it is the reason the transport data will have a step in it and stage 2 should not be surprised by one. [ref 2] is not followed: every entry it lists is a copper selenite or selenate -- CuSeO3 Pnma mp-22414, CuSe2O5 C2/c, Cu4Se3O10 -- oxidised ternaries in which selenium is bonded to oxygen, which is what a Cu-O-Se element set looks like as a chemistry and not what a sintered mixture of two binaries is. mp_id is null.

basis: One composition, Cu7PSe6, which the argyrodite entry already names among its representative materials: a framework of PSe4 tetrahedra and selenium with mobile copper distributed over partially occupied sites. The paper is titled Thermoelectric Transport in Cu7PSe6 with High Copper Ionic Mobility, which is the argyrodite behaviour exactly.
note: The measured range starts at 305 K and runs to 575 K, which puts the order-disorder transition of this argyrodite just inside the bottom of the window. Below it the copper is ordered in the low-symmetry Pna2_1 cell that [ref 2] gives as Cu7PSe6 mp-29823; above it the copper sublattice melts into the cubic high-temperature form, which [ref 2] also lists as Cu7PSe6 P2_13 mp-1201955. Both phases are recorded with their own mp_id and both are the same prototype, since argyrodite is defined across the order-disorder pair. The transition temperature is approximate and from general knowledge of this compound rather than from the paper -- the ordering temperature of Cu7PSe6 is reported in the 250 to 330 K region and varies with stoichiometry -- so transition_basis is llm_materials_knowledge and the phase confidences are medium even though the prototype is high. [ref 2] also lists a third Cu7PSe6 setting, P1 mp-676863 at hull 0.079 with no ICSD reference, which is a computed distortion and not a thermal phase; it is left out of both arrays as an artefact rather than a polymorph. Cu3PSe4 Pmn2_1 mp-5756, its primary at 3 ICSD references, is a different compound in the same ternary.

basis: Cu2ScxTi4-xS8 at x = 1 to 2, from a paper comparing thermoelectric Cu2TrTi3S8 thiospinels with Tr = Co and Sc. Six metals to eight sulfur is the AB2X4 spinel ratio doubled, with copper on the tetrahedral A sites and scandium and titanium sharing the octahedral B sites, and the paper calls them thiospinels outright.
note: Scandium runs from 1 to 2 of the four B-site metals, alloying rather than doping, so no dopant role is recorded. Scandium is trivalent and titanium is nominally tetravalent here, so varying their ratio is how the paper sets the carrier concentration without leaving the spinel field -- the composition is the doping knob, which is worth carrying into stage 3. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve CuTi2S4 or Cu2ScTi3S8 in Fd-3m. Measured 301-752 K.

basis: Cu2S1-xTex at x close to 0.5, from the paper titled Ultrahigh Thermoelectric Performance in Mosaic Crystals. Cu2S and Cu2Te are both Cu2X superionic conductors with a rigid anion sublattice and liquid-like mobile copper, and this prototype is the taxonomy entry for that family; the mosaic crystal of the title is a Cu2S-Cu2Te intergrowth with the copper mobile through it.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the anion sublattice
solid_solution_axis.note: Sulfur fraction of the anion site, spanning only 0.50 to 0.54 across the three compositions -- a very narrow slice deliberately placed at the middle of the Cu2S-Cu2Te line, which is where the mosaic intergrowth forms. Sulfur and tellurium are both group 16 and share the anion sublattice, so the substitution is isoelectronic, but they are far enough apart in size that the two binaries do not form a simple continuous solution, which is the point of the paper.

note: The measurement runs 296-1012 K and this material is not one structure across that window. Cu2S alone goes from monoclinic low chalcocite to the hexagonal form near 376 K and to cubic near 700 K, Cu2Te has its own sequence of superstructures, and the mixed mosaic crystal will have transitions of its own that do not have to match either binary. I record two phases -- an ordered low-temperature form and the superionic high-temperature one -- with a nominal 400 K boundary from general knowledge of Cu2S, and flag the whole thing as uncertain: the low-temperature phase confidence is low because I cannot say which ordered superstructure a 50:50 mosaic crystal adopts, and no space group or mp_id is asserted for either. No reference line was printed for this host. What is not in doubt is that the copper is mobile over most of the window, which is what gives these crystals their thermoelectric performance and also what makes them degrade under current.
annotator_note: Phase boundary at 400 K is a nominal value carried from Cu2S; the actual sequence for a Cu2S-Cu2Te mosaic crystal is not established here.

basis: Two of the three compositions sit at Zn:Sb near 1:1 once Cu is counted with the zinc -- ZnSbSn0.02Cu0.15 and Cu0.8Zn2.4Sb2.2 -- which is orthorhombic ZnSb, and the third, Zn3.6Cu0.4Sb3, is the Zn4Sb3 stoichiometry with copper on the zinc site. The third paper is titled Thermoelectric efficiency of intermetallic compound ZnSb, so ZnSb is named outright for at least one of them.

dopant_roles.basis: Present at 2 at. percent in ZnSbSn0.02Cu0.15 only. Tin is the usual substituent on the antimony site in ZnSb, where it acts as an acceptor; the alternative of tin on zinc cannot be ruled out from a composition string, so the site is recorded at low confidence.

note: Copper is above the 5 at. percent cut in two of the three compositions and so is not listed as a dopant candidate, but chemically it is doing the same job in all three: the two papers that name it are titled Effects of a Cu-contained compound on the microstructures and thermoelectric properties and Thermoelectric properties of Cu-added Zn-Sb based alloys with multi-phase, so copper is added deliberately and the second paper says in its title that the result is multi-phase. This host is flagged mixed for that reason: the Zn-Sb binary has ZnSb and beta-Zn4Sb3 as neighbouring line compounds, both are thermoelectric, and copper addition is known to leave Cu-Sb or Cu-Zn second phases behind as well. Which composition is which separates cleanly on the Zn:Sb ratio, so stage 2 can split this without reading the papers. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null. beta-Zn4Sb3, if present, has its own order-disorder transition near 250 K and a decomposition above roughly 700 K, close to the top of the 297-721 K measured window; I do not record a phase sequence because I cannot say which sample is Zn4Sb3.

basis: All three compositions are Cu2SexTe1-x at x = 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, and the paper is titled Enhanced seebeck coefficient and low thermal conductivity of Cu2SexTe1-x. Cu2Se and Cu2Te are both Cu2X superionic conductors with a rigid chalcogen sublattice and liquid-like mobile copper, which is exactly this prototype.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen sublattice of the antifluorite-like Cu2X framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Selenium fraction of the anion site, sampled at 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7 -- the whole width of the pseudobinary rather than a dilute doping series, so no single parent compound can be named at host level. Selenium and tellurium are both group 16 and share the anion site, so the substitution is isoelectronic; what it changes is the lattice thermal conductivity and the superionic transition temperature, not the carrier count.

note: The 309-500 K measured window brackets the order-disorder transition of Cu2Se, which sits near 400 K in the pure selenide, so two phases are recorded: an ordered low-temperature form and the cubic superionic form above it. The transition temperature is the weak part of this record. It is taken from Cu2Se by general knowledge rather than from the paper, and alloying with tellurium moves it -- Cu2Te has its own and quite different sequence of superstructures -- so on a solid-solution axis this wide a single number cannot be right for all three compositions. transition_basis is llm_materials_knowledge and the low-temperature phase is recorded at low confidence because I cannot say which ordered superstructure a 50:50 Cu2(Se,Te) adopts. [ref 2] is not followed: its only entry is CuTeSe P2_13 mp-1225744 at hull 0.048, a 1:1:1 copper chalcogenide, which is a different compound from Cu2(Se,Te) and not what the paper made. mp_id is null throughout.
annotator_note: Transition at 400 K is a nominal value carried from Cu2Se and will shift with the Se:Te ratio; worth checking against the paper.

basis: Both compositions are Dy1-xEuxMnO3 at x = 0.3 and 0.5 and the paper is titled Modification of low temperature magnetic interactions in Dy1-xEuxMnO3. The rare-earth manganites RMnO3 with R from La through Dy are orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskites, Pnma, with cooperative Jahn-Teller distortion of the MnO6 octahedra.

other_polymorphs.note: The hexagonal P6_3cm manganite structure taken by the smallest rare earths, Ho through Lu and Y. Dysprosium sits right at the boundary: DyMnO3 is orthorhombic when made by ordinary solid-state synthesis but a hexagonal form can be stabilised by soft chemistry or thin-film growth. Europium substitution increases the average A-site radius and pushes further into the orthorhombic field, so the orthorhombic assignment is the right one for these samples.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the perovskite A site
solid_solution_axis.note: Europium fraction of the A site. Both are trivalent rare earths and the substitution is isovalent, so it adds no carriers; what it changes is the average A-site radius and therefore the octahedral tilt angle, which is how the paper tunes the magnetic exchange. Not one of the same-group pairs the automatic axis detector looks for, but it is the same kind of continuous isovalent series and the parent compound depends on the composition.

note: Measured 182-235 K across the robust range, 182-305 K including outliers, so the whole measurement is in the orthorhombic phase; the transitions in this material over that window are magnetic, not structural. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null. Stage 2 should look for DyMnO3 or EuMnO3 in Pnma rather than at the mixed formula.

basis: One composition, DyNiO3, a rare-earth nickelate. [ref 2] gives DyNiO3 Pnma (62) mp-19265 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references as the primary, which is the GdFeO3-type orthorhombic perovskite, and the paper is on a d-band electron correlated thermoelectric thermistor, that is on the correlated nickelate itself.
note: One nuance worth recording against [ref 2]. The RNiO3 nickelates are metallic in orthorhombic Pbnm, equivalently Pnma, and on cooling through their metal-insulator transition they distort to monoclinic P2_1/n with two inequivalent nickel sites, the breathing distortion that opens the gap. For DyNiO3 that transition is near 560 K, above the 299-483 K measured window, so these samples are in the monoclinic insulating phase throughout and the reference structure mp-19265 in Pnma is the high-temperature metallic setting rather than the one measured. Both are GdFeO3-type perovskites so the prototype is unaffected, and spans_transition is false because the window does not reach 560 K -- but stage 2 should take the monoclinic entry if one exists. DyNiO3 also requires high oxygen pressure to synthesise, which is why so few ICSD references exist for it.

basis: All three compositions are ErNi1-xPdxSb at x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, the 1:1:1 RETSb stoichiometry, and the paper is titled Substitution effect on the thermoelectric properties of p-type half-Heusler. ErNiSb and ErPdSb are both MgAgAs-type half-Heuslers in F-43m and form a continuous series between them.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the transition-metal 4c site of the half-Heusler cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Palladium fraction of the transition-metal site, spanning the middle of the ErNiSb-ErPdSb join. Nickel and palladium are both group 10 and isovalent, so the substitution does not change the 18-electron count that makes these compounds semiconducting; it expands the lattice and scatters phonons, which is the point of the paper. No single parent compound can be named at host level.

note: No reference line was printed for this host, so mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve ErNiSb and ErPdSb separately in F-43m and interpolate. The half-Heusler antimonides of the heavy rare earths are notorious for second phases -- full-Heusler ErNi2Sb and free antimony both appear in this system -- so a paper-level check on phase purity is worth doing before the transport data are used, but that affects the sample, not the prototype.

basis: One composition, Er2Zr2O7, from a paper on the electrical and thermal conductivities of rare-earth A2Zr2O7 zirconates. Whether an A2Zr2O7 is the ordered pyrochlore or the disordered anion-deficient fluorite is set by the A to Zr radius ratio, and erbium at about 1.39 is below the roughly 1.46 boundary, so the erbium zirconate falls on the defect-fluorite side.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists Er2Zr2O7 Fd-3m mp-756545 at hull 0.082, the ordered pyrochlore. It is kept here rather than in phases because the order-disorder relationship in the rare-earth zirconates is a function of composition and synthesis temperature rather than a transition that heating reliably produces, and because erbium is on the disordered side of the radius-ratio boundary. If the paper reports superlattice reflections, this is the entry to take instead.

note: The reference is weak here and I am not following its ranking. [ref 2] marks Er2Zr2O7 C2/m mp-1178353 primary and flags it AMBIGUOUS, and not one of its five entries carries an ICSD reference count -- they are all computed orderings of a structure that is experimentally disordered, which is exactly the case where a hull-ranked list is least useful. The C2/m and Pmma entries are computed cation orderings, the Fd-3m entry is the pyrochlore, and the true ambient structure of Er2Zr2O7 is a cubic Fm-3m fluorite with erbium and zirconium mixed on one cation site and one eighth of the anion sites vacant. That is what makes these zirconates useful as thermal-barrier coatings and why their thermal conductivity is low, which is what the paper measures. mp_id is left null rather than pointing at a computed ordering. The paper title names A = Pr, Nd and others, so the series it covers spans the pyrochlore-to-fluorite boundary even though the erbium member here does not.
annotator_note: Pyrochlore versus defect fluorite for Er2Zr2O7 is a genuine judgement call on the radius ratio, not a database lookup; confidence is medium for that reason.

basis: All three compositions are binary Zr with 5 to 14 at. percent Er, written as element percentages, and the paper is titled Phase State and Thermal and Mechanical Properties of Zr-Er Alloys. Both metals are hexagonal close packed at ambient temperature, so the alloy is an hcp A3 matrix however the erbium is distributed.
note: The reason confidence is medium rather than high is solubility, not structure. Erbium is much larger than zirconium and its equilibrium solubility in alpha-Zr is small, so at 5 to 14 at. percent these samples are most likely two-phase, a zirconium-rich hcp matrix with erbium-rich particles, which is presumably why a paper on the phase state of these alloys exists at all. Both phases are still hcp close-packed metal, so solid_solution_alloy remains the right prototype either way and I have not flagged the host mixed. Zirconium transforms hcp to bcc at about 1136 K, well above the 299-673 K measured window, so nothing structural is crossed. [ref 2] offers only ErZr P-6m2 mp-1225381 at hull 0.075, a computed 1:1 line compound with no ICSD reference and no counterpart in the assessed Zr-Er phase diagram; it is not followed and mp_id is null. Erbium in zirconium alloys is normally there as a burnable neutron absorber, which fits a paper in a nuclear engineering journal.

basis: One composition, EuGa4, across three single crystals, from a paper titled Transport and Magnetic Properties of EuAl4 and EuGa4. [ref 2] gives EuGa4 I4/mmm (139) mp-21884 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, which is the BaAl4 tI10 structure -- the binary aristotype of the ThCr2Si2 and BaNiSn3 orderings the taxonomy already carries.
note: baal4_type is new and is defined in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl. The taxonomy had both ordered derivatives of this cell -- thcr2si2_122 in I4/mmm and banisn3_i4mm in I4mm -- but not the binary parent, and putting a binary AB4 under a ternary ordered entry would assert an ordering that cannot exist with only one B species. [ref 2] also lists EuGa2 Imma mp-22317 with 5 ICSD references as its top primary; that is a real neighbouring compound in the same binary but not this composition, and the EuGa4 entry directly below it is the one that matches. Measured 10-299 K on single crystals: the transitions in that window are magnetic, EuGa4 ordering antiferromagnetically near 16 K, and are not structural, so phases is empty. The companion compound EuAl4 named in the same paper does have a charge-density-wave transition near 140 K with a small orthorhombic distortion, but that is a different host system.

basis: All three compositions are Eu1-xSrxMnO3 at x = 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5, and the paper is titled Structural, electrical, magnetic and thermal studies on Eu1-xSrxMnO3. These are hole-doped manganite perovskites, orthorhombic Pnma at the europium-rich end and approaching the cubic aristotype as strontium and the average A-site radius increase.
note: Strontium is above the 5 at. percent cut and so is a host element rather than a dopant candidate, but it is worth saying explicitly for stage 3 that it is the doping variable: Sr2+ for Eu3+ on the A site puts holes on the manganese, driving the Mn3+ to Mn4+ ratio from 30 to 50 percent across these three samples, and that is what the paper is varying. This is not an isovalent axis, so solid_solution_axis is left null. Measured 12-297 K, a low-temperature window in which the events are magnetic and charge-ordering rather than structural; Eu0.5Sr0.5MnO3 in particular is a phase-separated charge-ordered system, but that is electronic phase separation, not two crystallographic prototypes. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null.

basis: All three compositions are Nd1-xEuxNiO3 at x = 0.25, 0.30 and 0.35 and the paper is titled Magnetothermopower in Nd1-xEuxNiO3 compounds. The rare-earth nickelates are GdFeO3-type perovskites; substituting the smaller europium for neodymium increases the octahedral tilt and raises the metal-insulator transition temperature, which is what the series is built to do.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the perovskite A site
solid_solution_axis.note: Europium fraction of the A site. Both are trivalent, so the substitution is isovalent and adds no carriers; it works purely through the average A-site radius and the Ni-O-Ni bond angle. This is also why the transition temperature in the phases array cannot be a single number for the host -- it moves by tens of kelvin across these three compositions.

note: The measured window is 11-392 K and this host does cross a structural transition inside it. The metal-insulator transition of the RNiO3 nickelates is first order and structural: above it the compound is orthorhombic Pbnm, equivalently Pnma, with one nickel site, and below it the NiO6 octahedra breathe into two inequivalent sizes and the symmetry drops to monoclinic P2_1/n. NdNiO3 has that transition at about 200 K and EuNiO3 at about 460 K, so at x = 0.25 to 0.35 it falls somewhere near 280 K, right in the middle of the measurement -- and measuring transport through it is what the paper is doing. Both phases are the same prototype, a GdFeO3-type perovskite, so only the space group changes. The 280 K value is interpolated from the two end members by general knowledge rather than taken from the paper, so transition_basis is llm_materials_knowledge and both phases are recorded at medium confidence. No reference line was printed for this host and both mp_ids are null.
annotator_note: Transition temperature interpolated between NdNiO3 and EuNiO3; the paper reports it and would settle the value.

basis: One composition, Sm0.75Eu0.25NiO3, from the same d-band electron correlated thermoelectric thermistor paper as the DyNiO3 host. Rare-earth nickelates are GdFeO3-type perovskites; the europium substitution on the samarium A site is the standard way of tuning the octahedral tilt and with it the metal-insulator transition temperature.
note: The 299-483 K window crosses the metal-insulator transition of this compound, which in the nickelates is also a structural one: monoclinic P2_1/n with two inequivalent breathing-distorted nickel sites below, orthorhombic Pbnm with a single nickel site above. SmNiO3 has it at about 400 K and EuNiO3 at about 460 K, so Sm0.75Eu0.25NiO3 sits near 415 K, which is why this composition is useful as a thermistor -- the paper is exploiting the steep resistivity change at the transition. Both phases are the same GdFeO3-type perovskite prototype, so only the space group changes. The 415 K value is interpolated between the two end members from general knowledge, not read from the paper, so transition_basis is llm_materials_knowledge and both phases are medium confidence. Europium at 0.25 of the A site is 4 percent of the whole formula but a quarter of the site, so it is an isovalent alloying substitution rather than a dopant; it is not listed as a dopant candidate because the parser kept it above the cut. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null.

basis: The compositions are Eu2Ru2O7 and its lead-substituted members Pb0.2Eu0.8Ru2O7 and Pb0.4Eu0.6Ru2O7, the A2B2O7 pyrochlore stoichiometry, and the paper is titled Metal-insulator Crossover in Pb-Ru Based Oxides with Pyrochlore-type Structure. [ref 2] gives Eu2Ru2O7 Fd-3m (227) mp-637431 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which is the pyrochlore.

dopant_roles.site: the 16d A site of the pyrochlore
dopant_roles.basis: Lead is only 2 to 4 at. percent of the whole formula, which is what put it under the dopant cut, but it is 20 to 40 percent of the A site -- the classic case where the denominator is the formula and the substitution is on a sublattice. Pb2Ru2O7 is itself a well known metallic pyrochlore, so these samples are members of the Eu2Ru2O7-Pb2Ru2O7 join and lead is an end member, not an impurity. Replacing trivalent europium with divalent lead is also what drives the insulator-to-metal crossover the paper reports.

note: Lead is formally divalent and europium trivalent here, so the join is not isovalent and solid_solution_axis is left null even though the series behaves like an alloy series; the charge change is the physics of the paper. [ref 2] also lists Eu3RuO7 Cmcm mp-22365 and a computed cubic EuRuO3 at hull 0.114; neither matches the 2:2:7 stoichiometry of these compositions. Measured 18-246 K, low-temperature transport, with nothing structural crossed -- Eu2Ru2O7 orders magnetically near 20 K but that is not a prototype change.

basis: One composition, La1.4Sr1.6Mn2O7F2, and the paper is titled Electrical properties of fluorine-intercalated layered manganite. The A3B2O7 cation ratio is the n = 2 Ruddlesden-Popper member, the bilayer manganite (La,Sr)3Mn2O7, with fluorine taken into the rocksalt block.
note: Fluorine is 14 at. percent of the formula so the parser kept it in the host, but its role is the whole point of the paper and should be carried forward: the parent La1.4Sr1.6Mn2O7 is a bilayer manganite and low-temperature fluorination inserts F into the (La,Sr)2O2 rocksalt layer without breaking up the perovskite bilayer, which reduces the manganese valence and is a topochemical electron-doping route rather than a change of structure type. The unit cell stays I4/mmm and expands along c. [ref 2] is not followed: every entry it lists is a computed P1 oxyfluoride supercell at hull 0.07 to 0.18, none with an ICSD reference, plus a SrLaMnO4F in P4/nmm which is the n = 1 rather than the n = 2 member. These are enumerated orderings of fluorine and oxygen, not a measured structure, and mp_id is left null. Measured 148-295 K, so nothing structural is crossed; the transitions in that window are the magnetic and charge-ordering ones this family is studied for.

basis: All three compositions have exactly three cations per four oxygens -- Li0.7Ge0.4Fe1.9O4, Li0.8Ge0.6Fe1.6O4, Li0.9Ge0.8Fe1.2O4 -- which is the AB2O4 spinel ratio, and they charge-balance to 8 with Li+, Ge4+ and Fe3+. This is the lithium ferrite spinel Li0.5Fe2.5O4 with germanium substituted in and lithium raised to compensate, a well known Li-Ge ferrite series.
note: [ref 2] is not followed and the disagreement is clear-cut. Its primary is LiFe(GeO3)2 P2_1/c mp-645305 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references, a lithium iron germanate pyroxene at LiFeGe2O6, and its other entries are an olivine-like Li2FeGeO4 and a garnet Li3Fe2(GeO4)3. All are legitimate compounds of this element set, but none has three cations to four oxygens, and the compositions here plainly do. The germanium content runs from 0.4 to 0.8 per formula unit, far too high for these to be doped versions of the germanate phases and exactly right for a Li-Ge ferrite. Lithium ferrite is ordered inverse spinel, P4_3 32 rather than Fd-3m, with lithium and iron ordered over the octahedral sites, and it disorders to Fd-3m above about 1030 K -- well above the 310-420 K measured range, so nothing is crossed. Stage 2 should look for the ordered form. The paper title is empty in the chunk file and the DOI is a 2002 Kluwer journal entry, so there is no title evidence to weigh; the assignment rests on the stoichiometry and the charge balance. mp_id is null.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [14, 15]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The compositions are written in the curator two-component form (Fe)x(I2O3)1-x at x = 45 to 67 mol percent, which describes a metal plus an oxide rather than a single compound, and the paper is titled Abnormal Resistance and Magnetoresistance Temperature Dependence in Fe-something. A metal-rich mixture of iron with a semiconducting oxide, measured for magnetoresistance, is a granular composite.
note: I2O3 is not a real compound. Iodine forms I2O5 and a few metastable lower oxides, none of them I2O3, and no phase (Fe)(I2O3) exists to be made at 45 to 67 mol percent metal. The reading that does work is that the oxide is In2O3 and the letter n has been lost somewhere between the paper and the composition string: Fe-In2O3 granular films are a standard system for tunnelling magnetoresistance, the composition range is right for one, and abnormal resistance and magnetoresistance temperature dependence is exactly what is reported for granular metal-oxide films near the percolation threshold. On that reading the sample is bcc iron particles in a bixbyite In2O3 matrix, which is why both are listed as alternatives. I have not renamed the host or invented an element -- the record says what the string is and what I think it should be. [ref 2] offers Fe(IO3)3 P6_3 mp-24993 with 2 ICSD references, taking the formula at face value as an iron iodate; iron iodate is a real compound but it is an iodine-rich insulator and cannot be what a 67 mol percent iron sample is, so the reference is not followed. mp_id is null and confidence is low. Measured 16-159 K robust, 16-300 K full span.
annotator_note: The element set Fe-I-O is very likely a corruption of Fe-In-O. This host should be checked against the paper before any structure is attached to it, and if confirmed it belongs with the other In2O3 hosts rather than here.

basis: All three compositions are In0.4Yb0.6FeZn1-yMgyO4 and the paper is titled Thermal and mechanical properties of Yb and Mg co-doped InFeZnO4. InFeZnO4 is the m = 1 member of the InMO3(ZnO)m homologous series, the YbFe2O4-type layered oxide in R-3m, with InO6 octahedral layers alternating with trigonal-bipyramidal (Fe,Zn)O layers.
note: No element falls under the 5 at. percent cut, so dopant_roles is empty, but the substitutions are worth stating for stage 3 because they are on different sublattices. Ytterbium replaces indium on the octahedral site at 60 percent of it -- which is more than substitution, since YbFe2O4 is the archetype of this very structure type and the ytterbium-rich end is a real compound rather than a doped indium one. Magnesium replaces zinc in the bipyramidal layer at 40 to 60 percent of that site, again isovalent and again near an end member. The paper calls both co-doping; at these levels the sample is better described as a quaternary member of the YbFe2O4 family. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve InFeZnO4 or YbFe2O4 in R-3m. Measured 299-1273 K, a wide window, but this structure type has no transition in it -- what it does have, and what an InGaZnO-style layered oxide is prone to, is cation redistribution between the two layers at high temperature, which changes site occupancies rather than the prototype.

basis: Two of the three samples are La1.5Sr0.5Ni0.5Fe0.5O4, the A2BO4 K2NiF4 stoichiometry, which is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper member, and the paper names it as La1.5Sr0.5Ni1-xFexO4+delta. The third sample, La0.7Sr0.3Ti0.1Fe0.6Ni0.3O3, is ABO3 and a simple perovskite, so the host holds two structures.

dopant_roles.site: the perovskite B site
dopant_roles.basis: Titanium appears only in La0.7Sr0.3Ti0.1Fe0.6Ni0.3O3, at 0.1 of the B site, alongside iron and nickel. Tetravalent titanium on the B site of an SOFC electrode perovskite is added for redox stability rather than as a carrier dopant, and it takes the same octahedral site as the iron and nickel it sits beside.

note: Flagged mixed on the A to B cation ratio, which separates the two cleanly: 2:1 for the Ruddlesden-Popper member and 1:1 for the perovskite. Both papers are electrochemistry rather than thermoelectrics -- one on a cathode and one on a fuel-electrode material -- so these are conductivity measurements on SOFC electrode oxides that have landed in the transport set. The oxygen excess written as O4+delta in the first paper is a real structural feature and not a rounding artefact: the K2NiF4 rocksalt layer takes interstitial oxygen, which is how these cathodes conduct oxide ions, so stage 2 should expect a non-stoichiometric oxygen content rather than exactly four. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null. Measured 383-1073 K.

basis: All three compositions are La(Fe,Si)13 -- LaFe11.5Si1.5, LaFe11.40Co0.52Si1.09 and La(Fe0.88Si0.12)13 -- one lanthanum to thirteen transition metal and silicon atoms, which is the NaZn13 AB13 stoichiometry in Fm-3c. Both papers are on La(FexSi1-x)13 magnetic refrigerants, the best known compounds of that structure type.

dopant_roles.site: the 96i iron site of the NaZn13 cell
dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt appears only in LaFe11.40Co0.52Si1.09, at about 4 percent of the formula and 4 percent of the thirteen-atom B sublattice. Cobalt for iron is the standard way of raising the Curie temperature of La(Fe,Si)13 towards room temperature and softening the first-order character of its magnetic transition, and it sits on the iron site.

note: nazn13_type is in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl, proposed from chunk 27 for UBe13, and its notes already name La(Fe,Si)13 as a member. Silicon is above the cut and is not a dopant: it is what stabilises the NaZn13 structure at all, since binary LaFe13 does not exist, so at 1.1 to 1.6 atoms per formula unit it is a structural constituent. [ref 2] is not followed. Its primary is La(FeSi)2 I4/mmm mp-4088 with 3 ICSD references, a ThCr2Si2-type 1:2:2 compound, and its other entries are LaFe9Si4 and LaFeSi2; all are real phases of this ternary but none is AB13, and every composition here is unambiguously AB13. The NaZn13 phase is simply absent from the block the reference drew on. mp_id is null; stage 2 should look for LaFe11.5Si1.5 or LaFe13-xSix in Fm-3c. One thing to know when the transport numbers are used: La(Fe,Si)13 has a first-order itinerant-electron metamagnetic transition near 190 to 210 K with a volume change of over one percent, and the 26-343 K measured window runs straight through it. That transition is isostructural -- NaZn13 on both sides, no symmetry change -- so it is not recorded in phases and spans_transition is false, but it will put a large step in the transport data, and it is the reason these compounds are magnetocaloric and the reason a thermoelectric-refrigeration comparison paper measured them.
annotator_note: The 190-210 K isostructural metamagnetic transition is inside the measured window. It changes no space group, so it is deliberately not in phases, but it is not an artefact either.

basis: Three binary Fe1-xMnx alloys at x = 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of Fe-Mn-Si alloys. There is no line compound anywhere near these compositions; they are close-packed substitutional solid solutions of manganese in iron.
note: Confidence is medium because the lattice is not the same across the three samples even though the prototype entry is. The Fe-Mn binary at room temperature goes from bcc alpha-iron at low manganese, through a region where hcp epsilon-martensite and fcc gamma-austenite coexist from roughly 10 to 27 at. percent, to retained fcc austenite above that -- so Fe0.9Mn0.1, Fe0.8Mn0.2 and Fe0.7Mn0.3 plausibly have three different answers, and the exact one depends on the quench as much as on the composition.
