The solid_solution_alloy entry covers A1, A2 and A3 alike, which is why the host is not flagged mixed, but stage 2 cannot assume one structure for all three. [ref 2] is not followed: its entries are Mn3Fe Pmmm, MnFe P4/mmm and MnFe3 P4/mmm, each with a single ICSD reference and each a computed ordered superstructure on a close-packed lattice rather than a phase that forms at these compositions. mp_id is null. All three curves are single points at 300 K, so no temperature range is at issue.

basis: All three compositions are Nd2(Fe1-xMnx)2Se2O3, the curator records that formula from the paper, and the paper is titled Synthesis, structure and properties of new layered oxyselenides Nd2(Fe,Mn)2Se2O3. Written as Nd2O2M2OSe2 the structure is plain: a fluorite Nd2O2 slab alternating with an anti-CuO2 [M2O] square net whose apices are selenium.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the single transition-metal site of the [M2O] anti-CuO2 layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Manganese fraction of the transition-metal site, from 0.25 to 0.5. Both metals are divalent in this structure so the substitution is isovalent and adds no carriers; what it changes is the magnetic exchange and the degree of correlation in the layer, which is what the paper is after. Not a same-group pair, so the automatic axis detector will not have flagged it, but it behaves as one.

note: ln2o2m2ose2_oxychalcogenide is new and is defined in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl. The taxonomy had zrcusias_1111 for LnCuOSe, which shares the fluorite Ln2O2 slab, but the transition-metal block is quite different: 1111 has an antifluorite Cu2Se2 layer of corner-sharing tetrahedra, while this family has a planar Fe2O square net with selenium above and below, an anti-CuO2 arrangement that makes these compounds two-dimensional Mott insulators. That difference is the reason for a separate entry rather than a stretch of an existing one. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null; stage 2 should search La2O2Fe2OSe2 in I4/mmm and its neodymium analogue rather than the Nd2Fe2Se2O3 formula string. Measured 72-324 K, so the events in the window are magnetic ordering rather than structural.

basis: All three compositions are Fe2Ti1-xMnxSi at x = 0.23, 0.41 and 0.58. Two iron to one Y-site metal to one silicon is the L2_1 full-Heusler stoichiometry, Fm-3m, and Fe2TiSi is a well-studied 24-electron full Heusler semiconductor with a flat valence band, which is why it appears in a thermoelectric dataset at all.
note: I disagree with the paper title here and want that on the record. The chunk file gives the title as Probing local distortion around structural defects in half-Heusler thermoelectric materials, but a half Heusler is XYZ with one quarter of the cell empty, and every composition in this host is X2YZ with no vacant sublattice. Fe2TiSi is a full Heusler. Two readings are possible: the paper covers both families and these particular samples are the full-Heusler ones, or it treats the Fe2TiSi structure as a pair of interpenetrating half-Heusler blocks, which is a legitimate way to describe L2_1 and is how the double-half-Heusler literature talks. Either way the stoichiometry is what decides the prototype and it is unambiguous, so confidence stays high. Manganese is above the 5 at. percent cut and is not a dopant candidate, but its role should be carried to stage 3: it substitutes for titanium on the Y site at 23 to 58 percent of it, and because manganese brings three more valence electrons than titanium this is how the paper moves the valence electron count off the semiconducting 24 and dopes the compound heavily n-type. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null. Measured 10-380 K.
annotator_note: Paper title says half-Heusler; the compositions are Fe2(Ti,Mn)Si, which is full Heusler. Flagged rather than matched.

basis: The single composition is written (Fe2O3)NaTaO3, two oxides in a one-to-one molar ratio, and the paper is titled SPS-sintered NaTaO3-Fe2O3 composite exhibits enhanced Seebeck coefficient. The paper calls it a composite and the composition string is written as one.
note: Both constituents are recorded as alternatives because both are real and both are already in the taxonomy: NaTaO3 is an orthorhombic perovskite and alpha-Fe2O3 is hematite, a corundum. is_mixed is false because the two phases coexist inside the one composition rather than separating between compositions -- there is nothing for a composition-level split to do. At a 1:1 molar ratio neither is a minority additive, so no single prototype describes the sample and mp_id is null. Spark plasma sintering of this pair at the temperatures implied by a 566-1047 K measurement can produce interfacial reaction products, and the enhanced Seebeck coefficient of the title is most likely an interface effect rather than a property of either oxide, so stage 2 should not silently resolve this host to one structure. No reference line was printed.

basis: All three compositions are YbxFe3NiSb12 or its close variant Yb0.89Fe2.98Ni1.02Sb12, the RyT4Sb12 stoichiometry, and all three papers say skutterudite in their titles -- p-type skutterudites YbxFe3.5Ni0.5Sb12 and Thermoelectric Transport Properties of RyFe3NiSb12. Twelve antimony to four transition metals is the [T4Sb12] cage framework with ytterbium in the void.
note: Ytterbium is just above the 5 at. percent cut -- 0.95 of 16.95 atoms -- so it is not listed as a dopant candidate, but it is a cage filler and nothing else: it sits in the icosahedral void of the [Fe,Ni]4Sb12 framework, rattles there, and scatters phonons. Nickel is likewise not a dopant but a framework substituent; replacing one iron with nickel adds an electron to the framework and is how a p-type filled skutterudite is charge-balanced at a filling fraction near unity. Both are worth carrying to stage 3 even though neither falls under the threshold. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve YbFe4Sb12 in Im-3. Measured 11-799 K with no structural transition in it.

basis: All three compositions are M3O5 -- Fe2TiO5, FeTi2O5 and the midpoint Fe1.5Ti1.5O5 -- which is the pseudobrookite stoichiometry exactly, and the paper title begins Structural, electronic, magnetic and thermoelectric properties of pseudo, plainly pseudobrookite. Fe2TiO5 and FeTi2O5 are the two mineral end members of that structure type.
note: pseudobrookite_m3o5 was proposed from chunk 030 for the Mg-O-Ti host and already lists Fe2TiO5 and FeTi2O5 among its representative materials; this host is the one it was really waiting for. I do not follow the [ref 2] ranking. Its primary is TiFeO3 R-3 mp-19417 with 23 ICSD references, which is ilmenite -- a genuine and much better attested phase of the Fe-Ti-O system, but at M2O3, not M3O5, and no composition here is M2O3. This is the case the chunk instructions describe: the reference says which phases exist in a chemistry, not which one the paper made. The entries that do match are further down the same list, TiFe2O5 Cmcm (63) mp-24977 at hull 0.022 with 2 ICSD references for Fe2TiO5 and Ti2FeO5 Cmcm (63) mp-31857 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference for FeTi2O5, both in the pseudobrookite space group; stage 2 should take those two and interpolate for the midpoint. Iron is trivalent in Fe2TiO5 and divalent in FeTi2O5, so the join is not isovalent and solid_solution_axis is left null, but it is a continuous solid solution and the composition sets the iron valence. Pseudobrookites are strongly cation-disordered over the 4c and 8f octahedral sites with a quenching-rate-dependent degree of order; FeTi2O5 has an order-disorder transition above roughly 1000 K, above the 299-801 K window, so nothing is crossed.

basis: PrFe4Sb12 and PrFe3.5Co0.5Sb12: one rare earth to four transition metals to twelve antimony, the RT4X12 filled-skutterudite stoichiometry, and one paper is titled Preparation and thermoelectric properties of p-type PrzFe4-xCoxSb12 while the other is on fully filled skutterudites.

dopant_roles.site: the 8c transition-metal site of the [T4Sb12] framework
dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt appears only in PrFe3.5Co0.5Sb12, at 0.5 of the four framework metals. Cobalt for iron adds one electron per substitution to the covalent framework and is the standard way of moving a p-type filled skutterudite towards charge balance, so it alters the framework electron count rather than doping a fixed lattice.

note: [ref 2] has nothing that matches and is not followed. Its five entries are Pr6Fe13Sb, PrFeSb2, PrFeSb3, Pr(FeSb3)5 and Pr5Fe2Sb, none of them at RT4X12 and none of them a skutterudite; the filled skutterudite is simply missing from the block the reference drew on, which is a gap in the snapshot rather than evidence against the assignment, since PrFe4Sb12 is a heavily studied compound. mp_id is null and stage 2 should resolve PrFe4Sb12 in Im-3. Praseodymium is above the 5 at. percent cut so it is not a dopant candidate, but it is the cage filler and should be read that way in stage 3; PrFe4Sb12 is close to fully filled, which is what an all-iron framework requires. Measured 298-824 K with no structural transition.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [129, 140, 57]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, SrFe4Sb12, the RT4X12 filled-skutterudite stoichiometry with an alkaline earth in the cage, and [ref 2] gives Sr(FeSb3)4 Im-3 (204) mp-1188542 at hull 0.000 -- the same formula in the filled-skutterudite space group. One paper is on fully filled skutterudites and the other on rattling in magnetic and thermoelectric properties, rattling being what the strontium in the cage does.
note: The reference and the assignment agree here, which is worth saying because it is not the usual case in this chunk: mp-1188542 in Im-3 (204) is the body-centred cubic filled-skutterudite cell and the formula matches the composition exactly. It carries only 1 ICSD reference, so by the chunk file conventions it is a weak primary, but the structure is not in doubt for this compound. Stage 2 should take mp-1188542. Strontium is above the 5 at. percent cut and is not a dopant candidate; it is the cage filler and gives its name to the rattling in the second paper title. Measured 10-800 K, a very wide window, with no structural transition -- what happens at the low end is the spin-fluctuation and magnetic behaviour the first paper is about.

basis: All three compositions are InxGa1-xN at x = 0.17, 0.30 and 0.36, and two of the three papers are titled for InGaN alloys. GaN and InN are both wurtzite at ambient conditions and form a continuous wurtzite alloy, which is the basis of the entire nitride optoelectronics industry.

other_polymorphs.note: Cubic zincblende GaN and InGaN can be stabilised by epitaxy on cubic substrates. The chunk file flags this host as containing film and epitaxial samples, so the possibility is real and is recorded here rather than ignored; but the thermoelectric InGaN literature is almost entirely on c-plane wurtzite films grown on sapphire or on GaN templates, so wurtzite remains the assignment.
Wurtzite nitrides convert to rocksalt above roughly 40 GPa. Not reachable in a transport measurement.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the cation sublattice of the wurtzite cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Indium fraction of the cation site. Gallium and indium are both group 13 and isovalent, so the substitution adds no carriers; it narrows the band gap from 3.4 to 0.7 eV across the full range and is what the papers are optimising. No single parent compound can be named at host level.

note: [ref 2] lists only ordered supercells -- In3GaN4 P6_3mc mp-1120750 at hull 0.023 and several P3m1 orderings -- with no ICSD references on any of them. P6_3mc is the wurtzite space group, so the top entry is consistent with the assignment even though it is a computed cation ordering rather than the random alloy these films actually are; the P3m1 entries are alternative orderings of the same lattice. mp_id is left null rather than pointing at one ordering of a disordered alloy. One thing stage 2 should know: InGaN above about 20 percent indium has a miscibility gap and films in this composition range are prone to compositional inhomogeneity and indium clustering. That is a microstructure problem, not a second prototype, so the host is not flagged mixed. Measured 295-875 K.

basis: All three compositions are (GaxIn1-x)2Te3 at x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, and the paper is titled Thermoelectric Characterization of (Ga,In)2Te3 with Self-Assembled Two-dimensional vacancy planes. Both Ga2Te3 and In2Te3 are M2X3 defect zincblendes in which one third of the cation sites are vacant, and the ordering of those vacancies into planes is exactly what the title names.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the occupied two thirds of the cation sublattice
solid_solution_axis.note: Gallium fraction of the cation site, across the whole width of the Ga2Te3-In2Te3 join. Both are group 13 and trivalent, so the substitution is isoelectronic and the one third vacancy concentration is fixed by stoichiometry rather than by the alloying; what changes with x is the ordering of those vacancies, which is the phonon-scattering mechanism the paper exploits.

note: [ref 2] does not match and is not followed. Its primary is InGaTe2 I4/mcm (140) mp-20408 at hull 0.039 with 3 ICSD references, which is a TlSe-type chain compound at M(I)M(III)X2 with gallium and indium in two different valence states -- a real phase of this ternary, but at a different stoichiometry from every composition here, all of which are M2X3. mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve Ga2Te3 and In2Te3 separately. The vacancy ordering is the thing to record there: In2Te3 has a low-temperature ordered form and a disordered high-temperature form with the transition somewhere near 900 K, close to the top of the 300-869 K window, and Ga2Te3 has its own ordering behaviour. I have not put that in phases because the transition temperature on this join is composition dependent and I cannot place it within the window with any confidence, but a step near the top of the measurement would not be surprising.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [9, 216], ICSD-backed references for this host report [140]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: K8Ga8Si38 is the type-I clathrate composition exactly: 46 framework atoms per cell as Ga8Si38, eight potassium guests in the two dodecahedral and six tetrakaidecahedral cages, and the electron count balanced by one gallium per potassium. Both papers name it -- Synthesis, Structure, Thermoelectric Properties, and Band Gaps of Alkali clathrates, and Synthesis and thermoelectric properties of the quaternary type-I Si clathrate.

dopant_roles.site: the Ga and Si framework sites of the type-I cage network
dopant_roles.basis: Aluminium appears only in K7.5Ga5.5Al2.2Si38.8, where gallium has been reduced by almost exactly the amount of aluminium added, keeping Ga plus Al near 7.7 against 7.5 potassium. It is a trivalent framework substituent that holds the Zintl electron count while changing the cage size and the phonon spectrum -- the quaternary clathrate of the second paper title -- not a dilute dopant, even though it falls under the 5 at. percent cut.

note: No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve K8Ga8Si38 in Pm-3n (223). The potassium content is slightly under eight in two of the three compositions, 7.4 and 7.5, and the gallium tracks it; in a type-I clathrate that is a real and deliberate degree of freedom rather than a weighing error, since the guest count sets the carrier concentration. Stage 3 should read the vacancy on the guest site that way. Measured 10-554 K with no structural transition.

basis: The three compositions are Ga3InSn5O16, Ga3InSn4TiO16 and Ga3InSn4.5Ti0.5O16 -- nine cations to sixteen oxygens, charge-balancing exactly with Ga3+, In3+ and Sn4+ or Ti4+. That is a definite stoichiometry in the In2O3-Ga2O3-SnO2 system, but M9O16 does not match any structure type I can identify with confidence, so I would rather say so than name one.

dopant_roles.basis: Indium is 4 percent of the formula, just under the cut, but it is present at exactly one atom per formula unit in all three compositions, unchanged while the tin and titanium vary. That is a fixed structural constituent, not a dopant.

Titanium enters at 0.5 and 1.0 per formula unit and tin falls by the same amount, so it takes the tin site. Both are tetravalent, so the substitution is isovalent and adds no carriers -- it is presumably there to change the lattice thermal conductivity, which fits a thermoelectric paper.

note: What I can say positively: the cation-to-oxygen ratio of 9:16 is between bixbyite M2O3 at 1:1.5 and fluorite MO2 at 1:2, which is where the anion-excess bixbyite-derived phases of the In2O3-SnO2 system sit -- rhombohedral In4Sn3O12 is the best known of them, at M7O12 in R-3, and the taxonomy carries a proposed m7o12_delta_fluorite entry for that motif. There is also a reported layered phase Ga3-xIn5+xSn2O16 in this exact ternary whose oxygen count matches these strings and whose gallium content is the same Ga3, but its cation total is ten rather than nine, so it is not the same compound. Either would make this a bixbyite-derived or fluorite-derived cation-ordered oxide, which is why bixbyite is listed as the alternative, but choosing between them from a composition string would be guessing. [ref 2] is no help and is not followed: its single entry is GaSnO3 Pm-3m mp-1184243 at hull 0.575, a hypothetical cubic perovskite more than half an electronvolt per atom above the hull with no ICSD reference, which is what Materials Project returns when nothing real matches. mp_id is null. Measured 772-1273 K, a high-temperature window; the samples are bulk polycrystals.
annotator_note: M9O16 in the Ga-In-Sn-O system could not be identified with confidence. The paper reports the structure and would settle it; this host is a good candidate for the review queue.

basis: The curator transcribes the paper directly: a Ga-Sn-Zn eutectic alloy with a composition of 90.15 Ga, 6.64 Sn and 3.21 Zn. That eutectic melts near 290 K and the entire 307-908 K measured window is above its melting point, so what was measured is a melt, not a crystal.

dopant_roles.basis: Zinc is 3.21 at. percent, under the cut, but the curator note names it as one of the three components of the eutectic composition. It is there to depress the melting point, not as a dilute impurity, and there is no lattice site for it to occupy in a liquid.

Sodium is added deliberately at three levels, 0.16, 0.32 and 1.57 at. percent, and the paper is titled Potential cooling agents for fast nuclear reactors: Sodium influence on the properties of the melt. It is the variable of the experiment -- a solute in a liquid alloy -- so alloying_component is the nearest role; substitutional would assert a crystal site that does not exist here.

note: The host key Ga-Sn understates what this is: zinc is a third eutectic component that happens to fall under the 5 at. percent threshold, so the routing key lost it. Anything downstream should read the curator composition detail rather than the host name. No structure can be attached and mp_id is null -- liquid_metal is one of the prototypes the project README lists as skipped in stage 2. [ref 2] is not followed: its entries are computed Ga3Sn and GaSn3 orderings at I4/mmm, Fm-3m and Pm-3m with no ICSD references, which are hypothetical crystalline intermetallics in a system that has none at these compositions and certainly none at the measurement temperature. Freezing of the melt is the one structural event in play and it is below the measured window, so spans_transition is false.

basis: Elemental gadolinium. [ref 2] gives Gd P6_3/mmc (194) mp-155 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references as the clear primary, which is the hexagonal close-packed A3 structure, and the solid_solution_alloy entry is the taxonomy home for the A1, A2 and A3 close-packed metals -- the same call made for the other elemental hosts in this set.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists Gd R-3m mp-1076915 at hull 0.018 with 3 ICSD references and Gd Fm-3m mp-614502 with 2. The samarium-type rhombohedral and face-centred cubic forms of the heavy rare earths are high-pressure phases, reached above roughly 2 and 6 GPa respectively, not on heating.

Body-centred cubic gadolinium, mp-11421 with 1 ICSD reference, is the genuine high-temperature phase above about 1535 K. It is left out of the thermal sequence only because the measurement stops at 320 K, nowhere near it.

note: Three papers, all on magnetic refrigeration -- gadolinium is the reference magnetocaloric material and is being measured here as a benchmark alongside the La(Fe,Si)13 compounds that appear in the Fe-La-Si host of this same chunk. The 11-320 K window brackets the ferromagnetic Curie temperature of 293 K, which is the entire reason these papers measure it, but that is a magnetic transition, not a structural one: the lattice stays hcp through it. spans_transition is therefore false and phases is empty. Anyone reading the transport data should still expect a large anomaly at 293 K. Stage 2 should take mp-155.

basis: SmGd1+xS3 at x = 0, 0.02 and 0.06, from a paper titled Preparation and Thermoelectric Properties of LaGd1+xS3 and SmGd1+xS3. A rare-earth sesquisulfide with a controlled excess of metal above the 2:3 ratio is the gamma-Ln2S3 to Ln3S4 series, which is Th3P4-type cubic I-43d with cation vacancies, and the excess is how the carrier concentration is set.
note: The deliberate 1+x on the gadolinium is the signature. In the Th3P4 framework the cation sublattice has one third of its sites vacant at Ln2S3 and none vacant at Ln3S4, so filling them progressively is a continuous carrier-concentration knob -- the same mechanism the taxonomy already records for La3-xTe4 under this prototype -- and a paper that writes its formula as Gd1+x is using it. Two percent of a gadolinium atom is not a dopant and is not listed as one. I do not follow [ref 2]. It gives SmGdS3 Pnma (62) mp-1219055 at hull 0.000 as a primary, with no ICSD reference shown; Pnma at Ln2S3 is the alpha or U2S3-type ordered form, which is the low-temperature phase of the rare-earth sesquisulfides. The gamma Th3P4 phase is what forms at the high temperatures these materials are sintered at and is the one the thermoelectric literature works with, so the reference is describing a different member of the same chemistry. Its other entries, Sm(GdS2)2 I-42d and SmGdS2 R-3m, are at LnS2 and are different compounds again. mp_id is null; stage 2 should look for a gamma-Gd2S3 or Gd3S4 in I-43d. Measured 294-974 K.

basis: LaIr4Ge3Sb9 is RT4X12 exactly: four iridium and twelve pnicogen-site atoms as Ge3Sb9, with lanthanum in the cage. One paper is titled Effect of partial La filling on high-temperature thermoelectric properties, which says filling outright, and germanium-for-antimony substitution is the standard way of charge-balancing a fully filled iridium skutterudite.
note: Germanium is above the 5 at. percent cut so it is not a dopant candidate, but its role should be carried forward: it substitutes for antimony on the X12 framework ring site, and because germanium has one fewer valence electron than antimony, three of them per formula unit is what lets a trivalent lanthanum fill the cage without over-doping the framework. That is framework substitution, not doping of a fixed lattice. The second paper title says partial La filling, so the filling fraction is itself a variable across these samples even though both composition strings are written at unity. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve LaIr4Sb12 in Im-3 and treat the germanium as site substitution on it. Measured 298-951 K with no structural transition.

basis: Three compositions, three different compounds, one sample each: LaPdGe3 is the BaNiSn3-type ternary at RTX3, La2PdGe6 is the Ce2CuGe6 type, and LaPd2Ge is an RT2X compound. The second paper is titled Crystal structure and physical properties of LaPd2Ge and a novel compound, which says plainly that more than one structure is in play.
note: This host holds three prototypes for three samples and separates perfectly on stoichiometry, so stage 2 can split it without reading anything. LaPdGe3 is the polar I4mm ordering of the BaAl4 cell, already in the taxonomy as banisn3_i4mm, and is taken as the primary only because it is the best-established of the three; nothing makes it dominant. La2PdGe6 at R2TX6 needs ce2cuge6_type, which I have proposed in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl for this host -- it is a real and sizeable family of rare-earth germanides and the taxonomy had nothing at that stoichiometry. LaPd2Ge at RT2X is filed against ypd2si_ordered_cementite, the existing entry for ordered-Fe3C RT2X compounds with R a rare earth, T = Pd and X = Ge or Si, which is the right family by composition; the paper calls it a novel compound, so its setting should be taken from the paper rather than assumed. proposed_prototype is left null because the primary prototype_id is a seed id; the new entry enters through alt_prototype_ids. [ref 2] covers none of the three: La(GePd)2 I4/mmm mp-21033 is a 1:2:2, La3(GePd)4 is a 3:4:4, and LaGePd C2/m is a 1:1:1. mp_id is null for all three compositions. Measured 10-299 K, low-temperature transport on polycrystals.
annotator_note: Three compositions, three prototypes, one sample each -- a clean composition-level split, and worth doing rather than collapsing to one label.

basis: All three compositions are (Ge0.8Pb0.2)1-xMnxTe at x = 0.10 to 0.18 -- GeTe with a fifth of the germanium replaced by lead and a further tenth or so by manganese. GeTe is rhombohedral R3m at ambient temperature and both substituents sit on its cation site; the paper is titled Effects of Mn substitution on the phases and thermoelectric properties.
note: The 297-726 K window crosses the rhombohedral-to-cubic transition, which is why two phases are recorded. Pure GeTe converts at about 700 K; both substituents here push that down, lead by diluting the lone-pair-driven distortion and manganese rather strongly, so at 20 percent lead and 10 to 18 percent manganese the transition should sit somewhere near 550 to 600 K. The 570 K value is my estimate from that reasoning and not from the paper, so transition_basis is llm_materials_knowledge and both phases are medium confidence; the paper says phases in its title and would give the real number. The transition is displacive and continuous, so the two structures are the same rocksalt topology with and without the rhombohedral shear, and is_mixed is false -- this is one material measured through its own transition, not two materials in one host. Manganese solubility in GeTe is limited and MnTe precipitates are common in this system; that would be a second phase rather than a second prototype and does not change the assignment. No reference line was printed and both mp_ids are null.
annotator_note: Transition at 570 K is an estimate from the lead and manganese content, not a measured value.

basis: All three compositions are (Mo,Ru)Ge1.769, and 1.769 is 23 over 13 exactly -- the Mo13Ge23 stoichiometry. The paper is titled Tuning valence electron concentration in the Mo13Ge23-Ru2Ge3 pseudobinary, and both end members are Nowotny chimney-ladder phases: a tetragonal beta-Sn-like metal sublattice with the main-group atoms spiralling through it.
note: The Ge to metal ratio is the thing to notice: chimney-ladder phases exist over a range of X to T ratios and the ratio is set by the valence electron count, which is exactly what the paper title says it is tuning. Ru2Ge3 is at 1.5 and Mo13Ge23 at 1.769, and holding the germanium fixed at 1.769 while sweeping Mo:Ru from 0.4:0.6 to 0.8:0.2 moves the electron count across the stability field. The taxonomy flags this prototype for special handling in stage 2 because chimney-ladder phases are incommensurate composites -- the metal and germanium sublattices have different periodicities along c -- so only approximants exist in Materials Project and no single entry is the structure. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null. Molybdenum and ruthenium are both above the cut and neither is a dopant; their ratio is the experimental variable. Measured 298-973 K.

basis: Ge30.6P15.4Se8 splits cleanly into a 46-atom framework, Ge30.6P15.4, and eight guests, Se8 -- the type-I clathrate cell exactly -- and the paper is titled Synthesis, Structure, and Transport Properties of Type-I Derived Clathrates. The eight guest atoms per 46 framework atoms is the signature and it is met to within rounding.
note: This is an unusual member of the family and the word derived in the paper title is doing work. The common type-I clathrates have an electropositive guest -- an alkali or alkaline earth -- donating electrons to a group 14 framework. Here the guest is selenium, an anion, and the framework is charge-balanced instead by phosphorus substituting for germanium: fifteen phosphorus atoms against eight selenium guests is close to the two-to-one the electron count requires. Selenium is 15 at. percent of the formula so it is above the cut and not listed as a dopant candidate, but its role is cage_filler and stage 3 should read it that way rather than as an alloying element. Phosphorus is framework substitution. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null; stage 2 should look for Ge46-xPxSe8 in Pm-3n (223) or a lower-symmetry derivative of it, since guest and framework ordering commonly reduces the symmetry in these substituted clathrates. Measured 326-662 K.

basis: The single composition is recorded as the string NiTPP, which is not a formula but the standard abbreviation for nickel(II) tetraphenylporphyrin, and the paper is titled Polaron activation energy of nano porphyrin nickel(II) thin films. That is a molecular crystal of a square-planar nickel ion in a tetrapyrrole macrocycle, not an inorganic phase.
note: metalloporphyrin_molecular is new and is defined in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl. The host key is a trap and should be treated as unreliable: H-Ni-P looks like a hydrogen-bearing nickel phosphide, but it is what the composition parser made of the abbreviation NiTPP, and the P in it is the last letter of porphyrin rather than phosphorus. The carbon and nitrogen that make up most of the real molecule are missing from the element set entirely. Nothing downstream should read H or P here as elements present in a lattice, and no dopant role should ever be assigned to them. assignment_basis deliberately omits composition, because the composition string carries no usable information in this case. Confidence is medium rather than high for the structure, not for the chemistry: the compound is certain, but the samples are evaporated nano thin films, and metallomacrocycle films are frequently a metastable polymorph or largely amorphous rather than the bulk crystal, so no single structure can be asserted. The measurement, an activation energy from 300-380 K resistivity, is consistent with hopping transport in a disordered molecular film. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null.
annotator_note: Element set H-Ni-P is a parse of the abbreviation NiTPP and does not describe the material. Worth a curation fix upstream.

basis: The single composition is the string PTVT2T, a polymer acronym rather than a formula, and the paper is titled Two soluble polymers with lower ionization potentials: doping and thermoelectric properties. A soluble doped conjugated polymer is the organic_polymer prototype.
note: Same parsing problem as the H-Ni-P host and the same warning applies. H-P-V is what the composition parser made of PTVT2T: the P and the V are letters of the acronym, not phosphorus and vanadium, and the carbon and sulfur that the polymer is actually built from are absent from the element set. assignment_basis omits composition for that reason. Nothing structural can be attached -- conjugated polymers are semicrystalline at best, with the transport set by chain packing and doping level rather than by a unit cell -- so mp_id is null and organic_polymer is one of the prototypes stage 2 skips. The doping the title refers to is molecular charge-transfer doping, which will not appear in the parsed element fractions at all, so stage 3 should not expect to find a dopant here. Measured 281-380 K.
annotator_note: Element set H-P-V is a parse of the polymer acronym PTVT2T and does not describe the material.

basis: Two of the three compositions are Hf3Ni3Sb4 with a small substitution on the nickel -- Hf3Ni2.9Co0.1Sb4 and Hf3Ni2.7Cu0.3Sb4 -- which is the A3M3X4 Y3Au3Sb4 type, and the first paper is titled Thermoelectric properties and electronic transport analysis of Zr3Ni3Sb4, the zirconium analogue. The third composition, Hf6NiSb2, is a different compound entirely.

dopant_roles.site: the transition-metal site of the Y3Au3Sb4 framework
dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt appears only in Hf3Ni2.9Co0.1Sb4, at 0.1 of three nickel atoms. Cobalt has one fewer valence electron than nickel, so substituting it on that site dopes the semiconducting 3-3-4 compound p-type; it is a genuine dilute dopant and not an alloying end member.

dopant_roles.site: the transition-metal site of the Y3Au3Sb4 framework
dopant_roles.basis: Copper appears only in Hf3Ni2.7Cu0.3Sb4, at 0.3 of three nickel atoms, and has one more valence electron than nickel -- the n-type counterpart to the cobalt substitution in the neighbouring sample. Taking the nickel site is unambiguous since the nickel content falls by exactly the copper added.

note: Flagged mixed, and it splits on the Hf:Ni ratio with nothing left ambiguous: 1:1 for the 3-3-4 phase and 6:1 for Hf6NiSb2, which is the Zr6CoAs2 type in P-62m -- an Fe2P-derived structure and a completely different family. [ref 2] confirms that member directly, Hf6NiSb2 P-62m (189) mp-15297 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference, so stage 2 should take mp-15297 for it. The 3-3-4 phase is not in the reference list at all; its nearest entries, Hf3NiSb7 Pnma and HfNi2Sb P6_3/mmc, are different stoichiometries, so mp_id is null there and stage 2 should look for Hf3Ni3Sb4 or Zr3Ni3Sb4 in I-43d. Confidence is medium because it is the host label that is uncertain, not either individual compound. Measured 10-861 K.

basis: The composition string is HfO, but the only hafnium oxide there is at ambient conditions is HfO2, and [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives HfO2 P2_1/c (14) mp-352 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references as a clear primary -- monoclinic baddeleyite. The paper is on the Seebeck effect in an oxide resistive switching memory, that is on a hafnia film.

other_polymorphs.note: Tetragonal P4_2/nmc hafnia, the genuine high-temperature phase above roughly 2000 K. Far outside the 80-301 K measurement and listed only so it is not mistaken for something reachable.

Polar orthorhombic Pca2_1 hafnia, mp-685097 at hull 0.029 in [ref 2]. This is the ferroelectric phase that made hafnia a memory material, and it exists only as a thin film stabilised by dopants, strain and electrode confinement. It is worth flagging precisely because these samples are memory-device films: if the paper reports a polar phase, this is the entry, but it is not something heating produces.

note: baddeleyite_mo2 is new and is defined in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl; the taxonomy had only cubic fluorite_oxide, which is the wrong ambient structure for hafnia and zirconia both. Confidence is low and the reason is the sample rather than the chemistry. Resistive-switching hafnia is deposited by atomic layer deposition or sputtering and is usually amorphous as grown, and the switching filament is a sub-stoichiometric HfO2-x -- which is probably what the composition string HfO is reflecting, an oxygen-deficient film rather than a 1:1 compound, since no HfO phase exists. So the crystalline assignment follows the reference precedence and the alternative is recorded as amorphous. [ref 2] is odd for this host and I do not follow it: it ranks Hf6PbO18 and Hf8PbO24 C2/m first, both at hull above 0.4 and both containing lead, which is not in the element set and is presumably an artefact of how the block was assembled. [ref 1] is the one to use here, as the project precedence says. mp-352 is the entry for stage 2 if the film turns out to be crystalline.
annotator_note: A resistive-switching memory film is quite likely amorphous; the assignment follows [ref 1] rather than the processing, and both readings are recorded.

basis: One composition, HoNiSb, and [ref 2] gives HoNiSb F-43m (216) mp-4174 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references as the primary -- the MgAgAs half-Heusler space group. All three papers name it: High-temperature power factor of half-Heusler phases RENiSb, and Observed Properties and Electronic Structure of RNiSb Compounds.
note: Reference and assignment agree and the composition is a single stoichiometric compound, so this is as clean as an assignment gets in this chunk; stage 2 should take mp-4174. [ref 2] also lists four neighbouring phases with one ICSD reference each -- Ho(NiSb)2, Ho5NiSb2, Ho5Ni2Sb and HoNiSb2 -- which are real compounds of the ternary and a reminder that the RE-Ni-Sb systems are crowded. That matters for sample quality rather than for the assignment: the heavy rare-earth half-Heusler antimonides are hard to make single phase, and the measured 11-994 K range being so wide suggests data combined from several studies. Nothing structural is crossed in that window.

basis: InO0.82N0.86 has 1.68 anions per indium, and Al0.02In0.98O1.14N0.49 has 1.63. No crystalline In-N-O phase can hold that: InN is 1:1, In2O3 is 1:1.5, and no mixture of the two exceeds 1.5 anions per indium. These are reactively sputtered films with a non-equilibrium anion excess, which is the signature of an amorphous or heavily disordered oxynitride.

dopant_roles.basis: Aluminium appears at 2 at. percent in one composition and the second paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of Al1-xInxN and InOxNy prepared by reactive sputtering, so aluminium is on the cation site as the dilute end of an AlInN series. Isovalent with indium, so it changes the band gap rather than the carrier count.

note: The two alternatives are what the film would be if it were crystalline: wurtzite InN with oxygen dissolved in it, which is what the III-oxynitride framing of the first paper title implies, or a nanocomposite of wurtzite InN with bixbyite In2O3, which is what sputtered films in this composition range usually turn out to be. I have put amorphous first because the anion arithmetic rules out any single crystalline phase and because reactive sputtering at these oxygen fractions is a classic route to an amorphous oxynitride -- but the anion excess could equally be a film-composition measurement artefact, which is why confidence is low. [ref 2] offers In3NO3 R-3m mp-778848 at hull 0.040 with no ICSD reference, a computed ordered oxynitride at 1.33 anions per indium; it is closer than anything else but still does not match, and it is not followed. mp_id is null. If the paper reports diffraction, this host should be reassigned from it rather than from the composition. Measured 299-957 K.
annotator_note: Anion-to-cation ratio of 1.6 to 1.7 exceeds what any crystalline In-N-O phase allows; the film is either amorphous or its composition is mis-measured. Needs the paper.

basis: Sb1.6In0.4Te3 is Sb2-xInxTe3 at x = 0.4 exactly, and one of the three papers is titled Valence-band changes in Sb2-xInxTe3 and Sb2Te3-ySey by transport and Shubnikov-de Haas measurements. Sb2Te3 is the tetradymite layered chalcogenide and indium substitutes on its antimony site; the other two papers are on antimony telluride thermoelectrics.
note: Two of the three composition strings do not balance and should be treated with suspicion rather than read literally: Sb1.9In0.5Te3 gives 2.4 cations to 3 tellurium and Sb1.85In1.5Te3 gives 3.35, where the tetradymite ratio is 2:3. Only Sb1.6In0.4Te3 is exact. Cation excess on this scale is not a real solubility -- indium in Sb2Te3 is limited to a few atomic percent before In2Te3 or InSb precipitates appear -- so these look like transcription or digitisation slips in the composition strings, and the paper titles all describe In-doped or In-substituted Sb2Te3. The prototype is unaffected. [ref 2] is not followed and has nothing usable: In10Sb9Te, In3SbTe2, In3SbTe4 and In4SbTe3 at hulls from 0.19 to 0.46, all computed, none with an ICSD reference and none at the 2:3 chalcogenide stoichiometry. The In-Sb-Te ternary does contain real phases of that kind -- the phase-change materials around In3SbTe2 -- but they are not what these samples are. mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve Sb2Te3 in R-3m, and the chunk header warns that its e_above_hull is unusable for this family. Measured 15-643 K.
annotator_note: Two of three composition strings have physically impossible cation excess for a tetradymite; flagged as probable transcription error rather than fitted to.

basis: All three compositions are In0.9Si0.1Se with a little tellurium, and the paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties of Te-doped In0.9Si0.1Se with Enhanced Effective mass. InSe at 1:1 is the layered III-VI semiconductor: Se-In-In-Se tetralayers with an indium-indium bond through the middle, stacked by van der Waals contact.

dopant_roles.site: the chalcogen site of the InSe tetralayer
dopant_roles.basis: Tellurium enters at 0.03 and 0.07 of the selenium site. The paper calls it doping, and it does raise the effective mass as the title says, but tellurium and selenium are both group 16 and isovalent, so it adds no carriers -- it perturbs the band structure and scatters phonons. Recorded as isoelectronic_substitution with the sublattice fraction rather than as a dopant level.

note: inse_gase_layered is new and is defined in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl. The taxonomy carried layered_in2se3 for In2Se3 and in4se3 for the indium-rich Zintl phase but had nothing for InSe itself, which is the most studied member of the III-VI layered semiconductors; assigning this host to either of those would have been a different compound with different bonding. Silicon is above the 5 at. percent cut so it is not listed as a dopant candidate, but it is the more consequential substitution of the two: tetravalent silicon on the trivalent indium site is a donor, so the 10 percent silicon is what makes this material n-type, and stage 3 should read it that way rather than as an alloying component. The polytype is the open question for stage 2 -- InSe is usually the gamma rhombohedral R3m form but the beta hexagonal one is also common, and they differ only in tetralayer stacking. No reference line was printed and mp_id is null. Measured 102-690 K.

basis: One composition, ZnIn2Se4, three cations to four selenium -- one cation site in four is vacant, which is the ordered-vacancy defect-chalcopyrite stoichiometry. [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives Zn(InSe2)2 I-4 (82) mp-22607 at hull 0.000 as its primary, and I-4 is the ordered-vacancy tetragonal cell.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists Zn(InSe2)2 Fd-3m mp-1001017 at hull 0.058, which is the vacancy-disordered cubic parent -- the same atoms with the vacancies randomised instead of ordered. It is the aristotype rather than a phase that heating reliably produces at these temperatures, so it is kept out of the thermal sequence.

note: [ref 1] and the assignment agree, and by the project precedence [ref 1] selects the entry: stage 2 should take mp-22607 in I-4 rather than the I-42m entry mp-34169 that [ref 2] puts at a nearly identical hull of 0.001. The two settings differ in how the zinc, indium and vacancy are ordered over the cation sites, which is exactly the thing this compound is known to be sensitive to, so the ICSD-backed one is the right choice. [ref 1] is a weak primary by the chunk file convention, with only 1 ICSD reference, but it is the only ICSD-backed entry available. The vacancy is the structural feature that matters downstream: a quarter of the cation sublattice is empty and ordered, which is what gives this material its low thermal conductivity and is presumably why a paper titled Novel n-type thermoelectric material of ZnIn2Se4 exists. Measured 294-847 K; an order-disorder transition to the cubic form is reported for several ordered-vacancy selenides at high temperature but I cannot place one inside this window, so phases is left empty.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [111], ICSD-backed references for this host report [82]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, La0.4Sr0.6Mn0.6Ir0.4O3, which is ABO3 with a mixed (La,Sr) A site and a mixed (Mn,Ir) B site. That is a perovskite; the paper on emergent insulating ferrimagnetism and perpendicular magnetic anisotropy is a thin-film study of exactly this kind of B-site mixed manganite-iridate.
note: The judgement here is whether the B site is ordered. At Mn:Ir of exactly 1:1 a manganese-iridium perovskite would be a strong candidate for rock-salt B-site ordering, that is a double perovskite; at 0.6:0.4 it cannot be fully ordered, and in a thin film grown on a substrate partial or no ordering is the more likely outcome. So the simple perovskite is taken as the primary with double_perovskite as the alternative, and confidence is medium because short-range B-site order would not show up in the composition at all. [ref 2] gives one entry, Sr4La2Mn3(IrO6)3 P-3m1 mp-1218666 at hull 0.062 with no ICSD reference, which is a computed ordered hexagonal variant at a 1:1 Mn:Ir ratio -- a hint that ordering is energetically favoured in this chemistry, but not evidence about this composition, and not followed. mp_id is null. Measured 53-300 K; the transitions there are magnetic, and the perpendicular anisotropy of the title is a strain effect of the film, neither of them structural.

basis: Both compositions are Pr2Ir2O7, the A2B2O7 pyrochlore stoichiometry, and the first paper is titled Metal-Insulator Transition in Pyrochlore Iridates Ln2Ir2O7. The rare-earth iridates at 2:2:7 are cubic Fd-3m pyrochlores with interpenetrating corner-sharing tetrahedral networks of praseodymium and iridium.
note: The two composition strings differ only by leading whitespace on one of them, so this is one compound across three samples, not two. [ref 2] is not followed: its single entry is Pr3IrO7 Cmcm mp-5322 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, a 3-1-7 praseodymium iridate with a quite different structure -- one-dimensional chains of IrO6 octahedra, not a pyrochlore network -- and a different stoichiometry from every composition here. The 2:2:7 pyrochlore is absent from the block the reference drew on. mp_id is null; stage 2 should resolve Pr2Ir2O7 in Fd-3m (227). Worth knowing about the metal-insulator transition the first paper title names: it runs through the Ln2Ir2O7 series as the rare earth gets smaller, and praseodymium is the member that does not undergo it -- Pr2Ir2O7 stays metallic down to the lowest temperatures and is studied as a candidate chiral spin liquid, which is presumably why the second paper measures its resistivity and thermopower together. Either way that transition is electronic and not structural: the pyrochlore lattice is unchanged through it, so phases is empty and spans_transition is false. Measured 13-292 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [63]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Three binary platinum alloys at 5.8, 7.8 and 9.8 at. percent iridium. Both metals are face-centred cubic and iridium is fully soluble in platinum at this end of the system, so these are A1 substitutional solid solutions -- the standard Pt-Ir thermocouple and reference alloys.
note: Iridium is above the 5 at. percent cut in all three, so nothing is listed as a dopant candidate and the alloy is treated as the host, which is right: these compositions are chosen as alloys, not doped. [ref 2] is not followed. It gives IrPt R-3m mp-1223665 at hull 0.087 and IrPt3 Pm-3m mp-1184759 at hull 0.080, neither with an ICSD reference; both are computed ordered superstructures on the fcc lattice, and the Pt-Ir system has a miscibility gap at lower temperatures rather than ordered compounds. mp_id is null. The paper is a comment on the thermoelectric power of ThCe alloys with an alternative interpretation, measured 20-118 K -- low-temperature thermopower on dilute alloys, where the interest is in phonon drag and impurity scattering rather than in a compound.

basis: Elemental potassium, one composition with three samples from a single paper on the thermomagnetic and thermoelectric properties of potassium. Potassium is body-centred cubic (A2, Im-3m) from low temperature to its melting point at 337 K, so it belongs in the elemental close-packed entry, which covers A1, A2 and A3.
note: [ref 2] is not followed on its ranking. It puts K I4/mcm (140) mp-1078640 first on 10 ICSD references at hull 0.160, but a tetragonal potassium is a high-pressure or strain-stabilised cell, not the ambient metal; Im-3m mp-58 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references is the ambient structure and is what stage 2 should take. The Pnma, Fm-3m and P6_3/mmc entries are likewise pressure or computed polymorphs. mp_id is left null here per project convention. Nothing crosses a transition: the paper measures a normal bcc alkali metal, and the interest is phonon drag and the Nernst-Ettingshausen effect rather than a compound.

basis: The single composition KOs2O6 is the beta-pyrochlore osmate: the corner-sharing Os2O6 octahedral network of a pyrochlore with the O-prime site empty and only one A cation in two present, sitting loosely in an oversized cage. Both papers are explicitly on pyrochlore osmates -- chemical trends of superconducting properties in pyrochlore oxides, and fine features of the density of states in their transport.
note: [ref 2] supports this directly and is followed: K(OsO3)2 Fd-3m (227) mp-4788 at hull 0.012 with 7 ICSD references is PRIMARY and is the beta-pyrochlore itself. Everything else in the block is a different stoichiometry -- K2OsO6, K2OsO5, and a computed cubic perovskite KOsO3 Pm-3m mp-1185009 which is not this compound. The R3m K(OsO3)2 mp-675028 at the same hull is a rhombohedral distortion with no ICSD reference and is not recorded as a phase. The prototype id was proposed in chunk 022 for the O-Os-Rb host and is reused unchanged; KOs2O6 is the potassium member and the one with the highest superconducting Tc in the family, and the rattling of the underbonded K is the low lattice thermal conductivity mechanism. The measured window 11-680 K contains no structural transition; the reported first-order anomaly near 7.5 K in KOs2O6 is below it.

basis: KVO3 with Cs and Li taking a fifth of the alkali site. The alkali metavanadates AVO3 are built from infinite chains of corner-sharing VO4 tetrahedra with the alkali cations between them, and the paper measures the thermoelectric power of ferroelectric potassium vanadate and caesium vanadate, which is that family.

dopant_roles.basis: (K0.80Cs0.20)VO3: Cs+ for K+ on the interchain alkali site, same valence, so it changes the chain separation and the phonon spectrum rather than the carrier count. At 20 percent of the alkali site it is a solid-solution member, not dilute doping; it falls below the 5 at. percent cut only because the alkali is one atom in five.

(K0.80Li0.20)VO3: Li+ for K+, same valence and the same 20 percent of the alkali site. LiVO3 takes a different setting of the chain structure from KVO3, so this composition may be distorted or two-phase rather than a clean solid solution.

note: [ref 2] is followed for the structure but not for the ranking. It puts KV3O8 P2_1/m (11) mp-19172 first on 5 ICSD references, which is a layered vanadium bronze at a different stoichiometry and not what was measured; KVO3 Pbcm (57) mp-18815 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references is the compound and is the entry for stage 2. Note the space group disagrees with the taxonomy: the metavanadate_chain entry names C2/c (15), which is the LiVO3 setting, while KVO3 is Pbcm (57). The structure type -- VO4 tetrahedral chains with interchain alkali -- is the same in both, so this is a setting difference within one prototype rather than a wrong assignment, but the taxonomy entry would be better written as a range of settings. The three other reference entries, KV6O11, KV4O8 and K2V3O8, are all reduced vanadates of a different chemistry.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [15], ICSD-backed references for this host report [11, 57, 14, 12]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: La1/3NbO3 is an A-site-deficient perovskite: a complete corner-sharing NbO6 octahedral network with only a third of the A sites occupied by lanthanum and the rest vacant and ordered into alternating layers. The paper is titled Metallization of La1/3NbO3 by lithium incorporation, and both compositions, La0.33Li0.59NbO3 and La0.33Li0.44NbO3, are that host with lithium inserted into the empty A sites.
note: Lithium is the doping variable here rather than an impurity: it enters ordered A-site vacancies and donates its electron to the Nb 4d band, which is the metallization in the title. It sits at about 12 at. percent of the formula so it is above the 5 percent cut and the chunk lists no dopant candidate, which is why dopant_roles is empty; stage 3 should treat the Li content as the carrier-concentration knob in the same way as the oxygen content of YBa2Cu3O6+delta. [ref 2] is not followed. Every entry it returns is a computed Li-La-Nb-O ordering with no ICSD reference -- Li2LaNb6O18 Pmmm mp-1210870, Li4La3Nb12O36 C2/m mp-762374, Li5La3Nb14O42 C2/m mp-768083, Li5La3Nb2O12 P1 mp-761986 and a titanium-bearing quinary -- and none is the A-site-deficient perovskite. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should look for La1/3NbO3 itself and expect an orthorhombic vacancy-ordered superstructure rather than the cubic aristotype.

basis: La(1-x)Sr(x)Mn(1-y)Ti(y)O3 at two points, y = 0.5 and y = 0.3: a simple ABO3 perovskite with La and Sr disordered on the A site and Mn and Ti disordered on the B site. The papers are on neutron structural characterisation and transport of oxide perovskites and on magnetism and giant magnetoresistance in La0.7Sr0.3MnO3-derived material, both of which are the substituted manganite perovskite.
note: [ref 2] is not followed. All five entries are computed supercells of the same disordered perovskite -- Sr3La7Ti2Mn8O30 P1 mp-694976, Sr3La7Ti3Mn7O30 P1 mp-694908, Sr6La14Ti3Mn17O60 P1 mp-1173230 and two others -- with no ICSD reference among them; they are ordering enumerations, not distinct phases, and mp_id is left null. Two of them, SrLaTiMnO6 P2/c mp-691117 and Sr3LaTi2Mn2O12 R-3m mp-1218525, would be B-site-ordered double perovskites, and at Mn:Ti of exactly 1:1 that ordering is at least conceivable. It is recorded as the alternative prototype rather than the assignment because Mn3+ and Ti4+ differ little in size and rock-salt B-site ordering is not reported for randomly substituted La-Sr manganite-titanates; the La0.7Sr0.3Mn0.7Ti0.3O3 composition cannot be ordered at all. The measured window 108-1173 K crosses the orthorhombic-to-rhombohedral and rhombohedral-to-cubic octahedral tilt changes these manganites undergo, but those are distortions within the perovskite prototype and are not recorded as phase changes.

basis: Nd(1-x)La(x)NiO3 at x = 0.3, 0.4 and 0.6: the rare-earth nickelate perovskite, an orthorhombically or rhombohedrally tilted ABO3 with La and Nd sharing the A site and Ni3+ on the B site. The paper is on the metal-insulator transition in composition-tuned nickel oxide films, and tuning the mean A-site radius is exactly how that transition is moved in RNiO3.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A-site rare earth
solid_solution_axis.note: La/(La+Nd) across the three compositions. Both are trivalent so this adds no carriers; it changes the A-site radius, the Ni-O-Ni bond angle and hence the bandwidth, which is the tuning variable for the metal-insulator transition.

note: No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed. Stage 2 should look for LaNiO3 in R-3c and NdNiO3 in Pbnm rather than for anything at a mixed-A formula; the solid solution interpolates between them and the tilt system itself changes with x, which is a further reason the parent has to be assigned per composition. The measured window 18-297 K brackets the metal-insulator transition these films are grown to show, but in the nickelates that transition is electronic -- a bond-disproportionation and charge-order instability -- and involves at most a small continuous distortion within the same perovskite prototype, so it is not recorded in phases. Nickelate films are also epitaxially strained, which shifts the transition and can suppress it entirely; that is a sample-level fact no composition-level record can carry.

basis: Two different compounds in one host and composition separates them completely. LaO with two samples comes from a paper on the transport properties of SmO, where the rocksalt monoxide of a trivalent rare earth is the subject; La2O3 with one sample is the A-type sesquioxide, trigonal P-3m1 with seven-coordinate lanthanum, from a paper determining its thermal conductivity. Rocksalt LaO carries the label because it has two of the three samples, not because it is the better-attested structure.
note: [ref 1] is followed for the sesquioxide: La2O3 P-3m1 (164) mp-1968 at hull 0.024 with 13 ICSD references is the A-type structure and is the entry for that composition; its settings at space groups 12 and 150 are alternative descriptions of the same layer stacking. [ref 2] is not followed on its ranking -- LaO3 P6_3/m mp-1078452 leads on 11 ICSD references at hull 0.388, which is a peroxide-like computed cell rather than an oxide of lanthanum in the ordinary sense, and LaO2 mp-1206559 is likewise not a phase of this chemistry. Two of its entries are useful: LaO Fm-3m mp-1206710 at hull 0.027 is the rocksalt monoxide, and La2O3 Ia-3 mp-2292 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references is the C-type sesquioxide, which is the stable polymorph for the small rare earths but not for lanthanum, where A-type is the ambient form -- a clear case of the reference describing the chemistry rather than the sample. Confidence is medium because rocksalt LaO is only obtained as a film or under pressure and is not a bulk equilibrium phase, so the two-sample majority rests on a structure that is itself uncertain. The full span to 1386 K belongs to the La2O3 thermal conductivity measurement; the robust window 12-302 K is the LaO transport.

basis: LaOs4Sb12, three samples and one composition: the lanthanum-filled osmium antimonide skutterudite, an Os4Sb12 framework of corner-shared OsSb6 octahedra enclosing Sb4 rings, with La in the icosahedral void, in Im-3. Both papers are on the ROs4Sb12 series and on rattling and spin fluctuations in it, with LaOs4Sb12 serving as the non-magnetic reference for the heavy-fermion superconductor PrOs4Sb12.
note: [ref 2] gives exactly one entry and it is the compound: La(Sb3Os)4 Im-3 (204) mp-1106066 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which agrees with the filled skutterudite assignment. Lanthanum is a framework constituent at full void occupancy, not a dopant -- the composition is stoichiometric LaOs4Sb12 rather than La(x)Os4Sb12 -- so dopant_roles is empty; this is the difference between the filled_skutterudite entry and a partially filled R(x)Co4Sb12 in the skutterudite entry. The single-crystal sample and the 11-291 K window are low-temperature transport looking for the rattling phonon mode, not a high-temperature figure of merit.

basis: Two structures in one host. LaPd2Si2 and Ce0.1La0.9Pd2Si2, two of the three samples, are the ThCr2Si2 type -- body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm with La layers alternating with PdSi4 tetrahedral slabs -- and the first paper measures thermopower on the Ce(1-x)La(x)Pd2Si2 series, which is that 122 phase diluted with lanthanum. La2Pd3Si5, the third sample, is a different compound at a different stoichiometry and needs its own prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.1La0.9Pd2Si2: cerium on the rare-earth site of the 122 structure. It is not isoelectronic in any useful sense -- the whole point of the Ce(1-x)La(x)Pd2Si2 series is that Ce carries a 4f moment that hybridises with the conduction band while La does not, so the substitution tunes the Kondo lattice and the single-impurity thermopower, and the lanthanum end is the non-magnetic reference.

note: u2co3si5_type is proposed in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl in this chunk for La2Pd3Si5; the taxonomy had no R2M3X5 entry, so the alternative would have been unresolved_crystalline or a wrong 122 label. Its space group is not settled: the U2Co3Si5 type is orthorhombic Ibam while the closely related Sc2Fe3Si5 type is tetragonal P4/mnc, the composition cannot decide between them, and the proposal says so. [ref 2] is followed only in part. La(SiPd)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-4954 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references is the 122 phase and is the entry for the two majority compositions. Its other two entries are computed and unrelated to what was measured -- La3(Si3Pd10)2 Fm-3m mp-1211466 and LaSiPd P2_1/c mp-1211246 -- and there is nothing at the 2-3-5 formula, so no mp_id is proposed for La2Pd3Si5. Confidence is medium because the host label covers two prototypes at a 2:1 sample split; stage 2 should split it by stoichiometry, which is unambiguous here.

basis: LaRuSn3, three polycrystalline samples: the RERuSn3 compounds are cubic Pm-3n phases of the Yb3Rh4Sn13 or Remeika type, in which Sn12 icosahedra and RuSn6 trigonal prisms build a cage framework around the rare earth, and the ideal formula is RE3Ru4Sn13 rather than RERuSn3. Both papers are on the RERuSn3 series and the heavy-fermion behaviour of its cerium member, with the lanthanum compound as the non-magnetic reference.
note: [ref 2] supports this and is followed, with a caveat worth recording. It returns both LaSn3Ru Pm-3n (223) mp-30756 and La3Sn13Ru4 Pm-3n (223) mp-1196992, each at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references -- the same cubic framework written at the nominal 1-1-3 and the structurally correct 3-4-13 stoichiometry, which is characteristic of this family and not a genuine pair of polymorphs. Stage 2 should prefer the 3-4-13 entry, mp-1196992, because it is the one that describes the real cage framework; the 1-1-3 formula is how the papers label the sample. La(Sn3Ru2)2 I-42m mp-1206665 and La2Sn4Ru Amm2 mp-1223248 are computed entries at other stoichiometries and are not recorded as polymorphs. The measured 10-298 K window is low-temperature transport on the non-magnetic member, so there is no structural transition in it.

basis: Two compounds, separated cleanly by stoichiometry. La4Sb3 with two samples is the anti-Th3P4 structure, cubic I-43d, and the first paper is titled High-temperature transport properties of complex antimonides with anti-Th3P4 structure, which names it outright. LaSb with one sample is the rocksalt monoantimonide, and its paper is on Weyl fermions in the related Kondo system CeSb.
note: [ref 2] is followed and covers both phases independently: La4Sb3 I-43d (220) mp-1223 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, and LaSb Fm-3m (225) mp-1065 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references. Both are ambient equilibrium phases of the La-Sb system, so this is a genuine two-prototype host rather than a reference artefact, and stage 2 splits it by the Sb:La ratio without ambiguity. Its La2Sb I4/mmm mp-759, LaSb2 Cmce mp-1101942 and La5Sb3 P6_3/mcm mp-1106084 are further real La-Sb compounds but none of them was measured. The rocksalt rare-earth monoantimonides are semimetals studied for extreme magnetoresistance, while La4Sb3 is the anti-Th3P4 phase whose cation-vacancy tolerance -- La(3-x)Sb-type non-stoichiometry -- is the carrier-concentration knob; the high-temperature window to 874 K belongs to the La4Sb3 samples.

basis: La3Te(4-x)Sb(x) at x = 0.6, 0.65 and 0.8: the anti-Th3P4 lanthanum telluride, cubic I-43d, with antimony substituting on the chalcogen site. The paper is on electron and phonon scattering in the high-temperature thermoelectric La3Te4-based system, which is the anti-Th3P4 family whose La vacancies set the carrier concentration.
note: [ref 2] disagrees with this assignment and is not followed. It returns only LaSbTe compounds: P4/nmm (129) mp-1018747 at hull 0.053 with 2 ICSD references as PRIMARY, a Pnma setting mp-1185210, and a computed La4SbTe7. LaSbTe is a real compound -- a ZrCuSiAs-related layered square-net telluride -- but it is a 1:1:1 phase and the compositions here are La3Te(4-x)Sb(x) with La:(Te+Sb) near 3:4, which is the anti-Th3P4 stoichiometry and not LaSbTe. The reference describes what else exists in the La-Sb-Te chemistry, not what was made. No mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should look for La3Te4 or La3-xTe4 in I-43d. Antimony sits at about 11 at. percent so it is a host element and no dopant candidate is listed, but its role is worth recording for stage 3: Sb3- for Te2- on the anion site is an acceptor that compensates the electron doping from the La3-xTe4 vacancies, which is how this paper separates electron and phonon scattering.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [220], ICSD-backed references for this host report [129]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Li0.33MoO3, three single-crystal samples from one paper titled Anisotropic transport in the quasi-one-dimensional semiconductor Li0.33MoO3. The stoichiometry is the red bronze one, A0.33MoO3, and a small-gap quasi-one-dimensional semiconductor is the red bronze electronic signature; the blue bronze A0.30MoO3 is a metal with a Peierls transition near 180 K, which this is not.
note: red_bronze_a033moo3 is proposed in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl in this chunk. The taxonomy carried blue_bronze_a03moo3, itself proposed in chunk 011, but that entry is explicitly A0.3MoO3 with A = K, Rb, Tl in C2/m, so it covers neither the 0.33 stoichiometry nor a lithium guest nor a semiconductor, and it is recorded as the alternative rather than the assignment. Confidence is medium for a specific reason: the P2_1/c red bronze setting is carried over from the potassium and caesium members, and lithium is small enough that a different cluster condensation or stacking is possible -- the lithium member is the least well characterised of the family. Stage 2 should confirm the space group before accepting it. [ref 2] is not followed and offers nothing usable: LiMoO2 R-3m mp-19338, Li2MoO4 R-3 mp-25080, Li12Mo5O17 P-1 mp-1199885, Li4Mo3O8 R-3m mp-690551 and Li4MoO5 P-1 mp-19117 are all ordinary lithium molybdates with one to three ICSD references each, none of them a bronze at this stoichiometry, so mp_id is left null. Lithium is above the 5 at. percent cut so dopant_roles is empty, but it is the intercalated guest that donates electrons into the Mo 4d band and is the compositional variable of the family rather than an impurity.

basis: (Nd0.55Li0.36)TiO3 with 0, 5 and 10 percent Nb on the Ti site. This is the lithium lanthanide titanate A-site-deficient perovskite: a complete corner-sharing TiO6 network with Nd, Li and vacancies sharing the A site, the same family as the Li-ion conductor La(2/3-x)Li(3x)TiO3. The paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of Nb-doped (Nd0.55Li0.36)TiO3 bulk ceramics.

dopant_roles.basis: (Nd0.55Li0.36)(Ti(1-x)Nb(x))O3 at x = 0.05 and 0.10: Nb5+ for Ti4+ on the perovskite B site, an electron donor that populates the Ti 3d conduction band. It is the standard n-type donor in titanate perovskites, the same role Nb plays in SrTiO3, and here it is the carrier-concentration knob the paper turns.

note: [ref 2] is not followed. Its entries are layered lithium neodymium titanates at other stoichiometries -- LiNdTi2O6 Pmc2_1 mp-1105497 with 2 ICSD references, LiNdTiO4 P4/nmm mp-10520 with 1, and two further LiNdTi2O6 settings -- and LiNdTiO4 in particular is a Ruddlesden-Popper-type single-layer phase, not the three-dimensional A-site-deficient perovskite that was measured. The composition settles it: Nd + Li = 0.91 A-site atoms per TiO3 unit with the remainder vacant, which is the deficient perovskite, whereas the reference formulas have Li:Nd:Ti ratios of 1:1:2 or 1:1:1. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should look for La(2/3-x)Li(3x)TiO3-type structures, which are orthorhombic or tetragonal with A-site vacancy ordering along one axis. Lithium is above the 5 at. percent cut so it is not listed as a dopant candidate, but like the lanthanum in La1/3NbO3 it is an A-site species rather than an impurity.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62, 167, 221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [26, 6, 129]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Mg(2-x)Mn(x)Si at x = 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4, from a paper correlating the magnetic and thermoelectric properties of the Mg2-xMnxSi series. The matrix is antifluorite Mg2Si, Fm-3m, with Si on the fcc site and Mg filling all tetrahedral holes, and Mn is intended to substitute for Mg.
note: Confidence is medium and composite_multiphase is recorded as the alternative for a chemical reason, not a bookkeeping one: the equilibrium solubility of Mn in Mg2Si is only a few atomic percent, so nominal x of 0.2 to 0.4 will almost certainly be antifluorite Mg2Si plus a manganese silicide second phase -- MnSi, Mn5Si3 or a higher manganese silicide -- rather than a single-phase solid solution. The paper is looking for a magnetic signal, which a dispersed second phase would also produce. Stage 2 or a reading of the paper should decide whether the nominal composition is the phase. [ref 2] supports this reading and is not followed as a structure: Mg14MnSi Amm2 mp-1028099 at hull 0.123, Mg6MnSi Amm2 mp-1023005 at hull 0.232 and Mg14MnSi P-6m2 mp-1028096 at hull 0.131 are all computed Mn-in-Mg2Si supercells with no ICSD reference and high hull energies, which is what a low-solubility substitution looks like in a hull calculation. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should take Mg2Si Fm-3m for the matrix. Manganese is above the 5 at. percent cut so dopant_roles is empty; its intended role is substitutional on the Mg site.

basis: Mg(~2)Sn(1-x)Sb(x) at x = 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 with the Mg content varied between 1.94 and 2.06. The host is antifluorite Mg2Sn, Fm-3m, with Sb substituting on the Sn site; the paper is on thermodynamic criteria for thermoelectric performance enhancement in the Mg2Sn system, where Sb is the standard n-type donor and the Mg excess or deficit is the second variable.
note: Both non-Mg2Sn variables in these compositions are worth passing to stage 3 even though neither appears as a dopant candidate. Antimony is at 5 to 10 at. percent of the formula, so it sits above the chunk cut, and it is a donor rather than an isoelectronic partner: Sb is group 15 and Sn group 14, so Sb on the anion site adds one electron each. Twenty to forty percent of the anion site is a very high nominal donor level for Mg2Sn, well past the solubility at which Mg3Sb2 begins to appear as a second phase, so the true Sb content in the antifluorite lattice is probably lower than nominal. The Mg stoichiometry, 1.94 against 2.06, is the other knob -- Mg interstitials and Mg vacancies are the intrinsic donors and acceptors in Mg2X and are non_stoichiometry rather than doping. [ref 2] is not followed: Mg14SnSb P-6m2 mp-1026621, Mg6SnSb Amm2 mp-1021391 and Mg14SnSb Amm2 mp-1026644 are computed Sb-in-Mg2Sn supercells with no ICSD reference at hulls of 0.04 to 0.10, not distinct phases. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should take Mg2Sn Fm-3m.

basis: YbMg2Sb2, one composition and three samples, from a paper on the Zintl phase compounds AM2Sb2 with A = Ca, Sr, Ba, Eu, Yb and M = Zn, Cd and their thermoelectric properties. The AM2X2 antimonides of that series take the CaAl2Si2 structure, trigonal P-3m1: a tetrahedral [Mg2Sb2] polyanionic slab alternating with layers of octahedrally coordinated Yb2+.
note: [ref 2] returns exactly one entry and it agrees: Yb(MgSb)2 P-3m1 (164) mp-10996 at hull 0.000. It carries no ICSD reference, so this is a computed structure rather than a measured one, but the space group is the CaAl2Si2 one and the family is well established experimentally, so the agreement is worth having. Ytterbium is a full framework cation, not a filler or a dopant, so dopant_roles is empty. The 298-650 K window contains no transition. Note for stage 2 that Yb valence, not structure, is the open question in this compound -- YbMg2Sb2 is usually treated as Yb2+ and a closed-shell semiconductor, and mixed valence would change the carrier count without changing the prototype.

basis: NiMnSb with two samples and NiTi0.1Mn0.9Sb with one. NiMnSb is the archetypal half-Heusler, F-43m, and is the compound in which half-metallic ferromagnetism was first predicted; the paper is on the galvanomagnetic properties of disordered Mn semi-Heusler phases, semi-Heusler being the same structure under another name.

dopant_roles.basis: NiTi0.1Mn0.9Sb: Ti on the Mn site of the half-Heusler. The paper studies disorder in Mn semi-Heusler phases, and substituting a non-magnetic early transition metal for Mn dilutes the magnetic sublattice and lowers the valence electron count from 22, which is what the galvanomagnetic measurement is sensitive to.

note: [ref 2] is followed: MnNiSb F-43m (216) mp-600124 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references is PRIMARY and is the half-Heusler. Its second entry, MnNi2Sb Fm-3m (225) mp-5124 at hull 0.067 with 3 ICSD references, is the full Heusler obtained by filling the vacant site, and it matters here as a hazard rather than a phase: excess Ni in a nominally half-Heusler NiMnSb sample fills that site and produces full-Heusler inclusions, which is one of the disorder mechanisms the paper is about. It is not recorded in other_polymorphs because the compositions here are stoichiometric 1:1:1 and it would be a second phase rather than a polymorph. The remaining entries, Mn2NiSb, Mn3Ni4Sb and MnNiSb2, are computed and unmeasured. The 270-300 K window is essentially room temperature only.

basis: SrMoO(3-x)N(x) at three nitrogen contents from 1.05 to 1.27, from a paper on the synthesis, Mo valence state, thermal stability and thermoelectric properties of that oxynitride. These are perovskite oxynitrides: the SrMoO3 perovskite framework with N3- replacing part of the O2- on the anion site, which raises the Mo oxidation state and is what the valence-state study is about.
note: [ref 2] disagrees and is not followed. It returns a single entry, Sr4MoN4O P2_1/m (11) mp-19649 at hull 0.175 with 2 ICSD references, which is a nitridomolybdate built from discrete MoN4 units with an entirely different Sr:Mo ratio -- 4:1 against 1:1 here -- and is not a perovskite. The composition settles it: Sr:Mo:(O+N) of 1:1:3 is the ABX3 perovskite ratio exactly. No mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should look for SrMoO3 in Pm-3m or its tilted setting and expect mixed O/N occupancy of the anion site, which no ordered structure file will carry. Confidence is medium rather than high because anion ordering in perovskite oxynitrides is real -- cis-ordering of the nitride is common in the family and lowers the symmetry -- and because at N of 1.2 per formula unit the Mo valence is pushed high enough that the phase may not be a simple single-phase perovskite. Nitrogen is a host element here, above the 5 at. percent cut and constitutional rather than residue, which is the opposite of the usual reading of N in a milled sample.

basis: Sc(1-x)Nb(x)N at x = 0.13, 0.18 and 0.25, from a paper on reducing the thermal conductivity of the thermoelectric material ScN. ScN is a rocksalt semiconductor and NbN in its cubic form is rocksalt as well, so Nb-for-Sc substitution gives a rocksalt solid solution on the cation site -- which is precisely the alloy-scattering mechanism the title describes.
note: [ref 2] disagrees and is not followed. Its only entry is ScNbN P-3m1 (164) mp-1219256 at hull 0.312 with no ICSD reference -- a computed trigonal ordering of a 1:1:2 composition, at a hull energy that marks it as unstable, and neither the stoichiometry nor the symmetry of what was measured. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should take ScN Fm-3m as the parent and treat these as substituted films, since the Nb content is a continuous variable and no ordered ternary is involved. Niobium sits at 6 to 12 at. percent so it is a host element rather than a dopant candidate, but its role is twofold and worth passing on: it is an isoelectronic-like size and mass contrast that scatters phonons, and because Nb is group 5 against Sc group 3 it also donates two electrons per substitution, so these films are heavily n-type degenerate rather than lightly doped.

basis: (UN)(NpN) solid solutions at three mixing ratios, from a paper titled Thermal conductivity of actinide mononitride solid solutions. UN and NpN are both rocksalt mononitrides, Fm-3m, and they are completely miscible on the cation site, so the whole series is one rocksalt phase -- which is why the paper can treat it as a solid-solution thermal conductivity problem.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: U/(U+Np) across the three compositions. Both are trivalent-to-tetravalent actinides of nearly equal radius on the same rocksalt cation site, so the series is continuous and the parent compound depends on the composition.

note: No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should resolve UN and NpN separately in Fm-3m and interpolate, since no mixed-actinide nitride structure will exist in Materials Project. The composition strings are written as mole percentages of the two end members rather than as atomic fractions, so stage 3 must read them as (UN)0.25(NpN)0.75 and not as a formula with subscripts of 25 and 75. The measured window 760-1628 K is nuclear-fuel territory; the mononitrides stay rocksalt to the melt, so nothing crosses a transition, but nitrogen loss and hyperstoichiometry become real at these temperatures and would change the carrier concentration without changing the prototype.

basis: TaON in three samples from one paper titled High-Mobility Electron Conduction in Oxynitride: Anatase TaON. The structure is named in the source: an anatase-type TiO2 framework with Ta on the cation site and ordered O/N on the anion site, grown as a film. The curator detail -- annealed at 800 C under base pressure in the growth chamber -- confirms a thin-film synthesis, which is how the anatase polymorph of TaON is stabilised.
