other_polymorphs.occurrence: The bulk ambient phase of TaON is beta-TaON, the monoclinic baddeleyite-type structure in P2_1/c, and it is what [ref 2] ranks first: TaNO P2_1/c (14) mp-4165 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references. It is not reached from the anatase form by heating -- anatase TaON is the metastable film polymorph and would convert irreversibly to baddeleyite, not cycle with it -- so it is recorded here rather than in phases.

note: This is a deliberate disagreement with [ref 2]. The reference is right about the chemistry and wrong about this sample: monoclinic baddeleyite beta-TaON at 6 ICSD references is the bulk phase, and its C2/m setting mp-5813 carries 5 more, but the paper states in its title that it made and measured the anatase polymorph, and a paper-reported structure outranks an inference from a reference block. This is the same pattern as Al-O-Zn, where the best-attested structure for the chemistry is spinel while nearly every sample is wurtzite ZnO. The remaining reference entries -- Ta2N3O P6/mmm mp-1019262 at hull 0.969 and TaN3O8 I-42m mp-1208577 at hull 2.165 -- are computed and physically implausible. No mp_id is proposed for the anatase form; stage 2 should look for TaON in I4_1/amd or a lower-symmetry anion-ordered subgroup of it, and should expect that MP may not hold it at all. The prototype id anatase names the TiO2 framework; here it is an oxynitride on that framework, and the anion ordering is what gives it a band gap suitable for a transparent conductor.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [141], ICSD-backed references for this host report [14, 12, 8, 191]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Ta(1-x)Si(x)N0.56 at x = 0.086, 0.11 and 0.13, from a paper on the electrical and optical properties of Ta-Si-N thin films deposited by reactive sputtering. At this low nitrogen content, N:Ta near 0.56, a reactively sputtered Ta-Si-N film is normally a substoichiometric face-centred-cubic TaN(x) lattice with silicon in solution or segregated at grain boundaries, so the rocksalt nitride entry is the best available reading.
note: Confidence is low and this record should be treated as a placeholder for a reading of the paper. Sputtered Ta-Si-N is the textbook nanocomposite diffusion barrier: depending on the nitrogen flow it comes out as nanocrystalline TaN in an amorphous Si3N4 matrix, as a single-phase amorphous alloy, or as substoichiometric cubic TaN(Si). Composition alone cannot tell which, and both amorphous and composite_multiphase are recorded as alternatives for that reason. The clue that favours a crystalline cubic nitride is the low nitrogen content -- there is not enough N to form Si3N4 and a stoichiometric nitride both -- but it is a weak one. [ref 2] is not followed: its single entry, Ta5Si3N P6_3/mcm mp-1208335 at hull 0.036 with no ICSD reference, is a computed silicide nitride at a quite different stoichiometry and is not what a sputtered film would be. mp_id is left null. Silicon at 9 to 13 at. percent is a host element here, not a dopant candidate; nitrogen at N:Ta of 0.56 is constitutional and substoichiometric, which in this prototype is non_stoichiometry -- the vacancy concentration on the anion site is what sets the resistivity.

basis: ThN, one composition and three samples from three papers -- thermophysical properties of thorium mononitride from 298 to 1700 K, reactor performance of ThN-UN fuel, and the electrical properties of thorium nitrides. Thorium mononitride is rocksalt, Fm-3m, like every actinide mononitride, and it is a metallic conductor rather than a semiconductor.

other_polymorphs.occurrence: Th3N4 R-3m mp-467 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references and Th2N3 P-3m1 mp-1940 with 4 are real higher nitrides of thorium and the phases a nitrogen-rich ThN sample would contain as inclusions. They are separate compounds rather than polymorphs of ThN and neither has a taxonomy entry, so they are parked here rather than named. Heating ThN does not produce them.

note: [ref 2] agrees emphatically and is followed: ThN Fm-3m (225) mp-834 at hull 0.000 with 24 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in this chunk. Its ThN2 Fm-3m mp-1072204 at hull 0.622 is a computed fluorite dinitride and not a phase of the system. The measured window is reported as 76-860 K robust with a full span to 1701 K, the latter from the thermophysical-properties paper, and rocksalt ThN is stable throughout -- nothing crosses a transition. What does change at those temperatures is stoichiometry: the mononitride tolerates nitrogen vacancies, so the same nominal ThN can differ in carrier concentration between samples, which is non_stoichiometry rather than doping and is the likely source of any spread between the three papers.

basis: (ThN)(UN) solid solutions at three mixing ratios, from the paper on reactor performance and safety of ThN-UN fuel concepts. ThN and UN are both rocksalt mononitrides with closely matched lattice parameters and are fully miscible on the cation site, so the series is a single rocksalt phase.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Th/(Th+U) as written in the composition strings, which give mole percentages of the two mononitride end members. The two actinides share the rocksalt cation site, so the parent compound depends on the composition and is assigned per composition in stage 3.

note: [ref 2] is not followed. Its single entry, ThUN2 P4/mmm (123) mp-1217284 at hull 0.077 with no ICSD reference, is a computed tetragonal cation-ordered 1:1:2 cell -- the ordered ground state a hull calculation finds for an equimolar mixture -- while a real (Th,U)N fuel is a disordered rocksalt solid solution, and two of the three compositions here are not equimolar in any case. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should resolve ThN mp-834 and UN separately in Fm-3m. This host shares its paper with N-Np-U and N-Th, and the same caution applies: the composition strings are mole percentages of end members, not subscripts. No measured range is printed for this host.

basis: Both compositions are rocksalt PbTe with cations substituted. Pb0.90Na0.10Te is Na-substituted PbTe from a paper titled Sodium Substitution in Lead Telluride, and Na1.06Pb7.94Sb0.85Te10 is a member of the NaPb(m)SbTe(m+2) series whose paper is titled Absence of Nanostructuring in NaPbmSbTem+2: Solid Solutions -- the point of that title being that these are single-phase rocksalt solid solutions rather than the nanostructured composites they were once thought to be.

dopant_roles.basis: Na1.06Pb7.94Sb0.85Te10: Sb3+ on the rocksalt cation site alongside Na+. In the NaPb(m)SbTe(m+2) family Na+ and Sb3+ substitute for Pb2+ in roughly equal numbers, so the pair is self-compensating on charge and the net carrier concentration comes from the small excess of one over the other -- here Na 1.06 against Sb 0.85, a p-type excess. Sb also contributes most of the band-structure modification and point-defect phonon scattering.

note: No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should take PbTe Fm-3m as the parent for both compositions. The first composition string, Pb0.90Na0.10Te0.450, has an anion subscript of 0.45 against a cation total of 1.00, which is not a physical rocksalt stoichiometry and looks like a digitisation or transcription error in the source table -- most likely Pb0.90Na0.10Te with a stray figure, or a Te deficiency written per two formula units. It does not change the prototype, but stage 3 should not compute a doping level from that string without checking it. Sodium is above the 5 at. percent cut in that composition so it is not listed as a dopant candidate; its role is the same as Sb, substitutional on the Pb site, and it is the standard heavy p-type acceptor in PbTe.
annotator_note: Composition string Pb0.90Na0.10Te0.450 has an implausible Te subscript; flagged for curation rather than assumed.

basis: NaSn(m)SbTe(m+2) at m = 3, 4 and 5, from a paper titled Contrasting SnTe-NaSbTe2 and SnTe-NaBiTe2 Thermoelectric Alloys. These are SnTe-NaSbTe2 pseudobinary alloys: rocksalt SnTe with Na+ and Sb3+ co-substituting on the Sn2+ cation site, the tin analogue of the NaPb(m)SbTe(m+2) lead series.
note: No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should take SnTe Fm-3m as the parent. Both Na and Sb are above the 5 at. percent cut at these ratios, so the chunk lists no dopant candidates and dopant_roles is empty, but the chemistry is the same as in Na-Pb-Te: Na+ and Sb3+ replace Sn2+ in equal numbers as a self-compensating pair, and here they are exactly equal in every composition, so the carrier concentration is set by Sn vacancies rather than by the substitution. That is why a SnTe-based alloy of this kind stays heavily p-type -- Sn vacancies are the intrinsic acceptor in SnTe -- and it is a non_stoichiometry effect stage 3 cannot read off the nominal formula. The measured window 301-873 K is high-temperature figure-of-merit work; rocksalt SnTe undergoes a rhombohedral distortion but only below about 100 K and only in stoichiometric material, so nothing crosses a transition here.

basis: Two structurally unrelated compounds. NbTe2 with two samples is the distorted-octahedral layered ditelluride, monoclinic C2/m, and one of its papers is titled Structural, electrical, and thermoelectric properties of distorted 1T-NbTe2, which names the structure. Nb3Te4 with one sample is not layered at all -- it is a hexagonal framework of face-sharing NbTe6 octahedra forming Nb chains along c with open channels between them -- and its paper is on a quasi-one-dimensional Nb3Te4 single crystal.
note: nb3te4_chain is proposed in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl in this chunk; the taxonomy had no entry for the M3X4 hexagonal cluster-chain framework, and the nearest existing one, ta4site4_chain, is a different orthorhombic structure that needs a third element. mote2_1t_prime was proposed in chunk 019 and already names NbTe2 with C2/m in its space group field, so it is used unchanged. [ref 2] is followed for both compounds but not for its ranking: it puts NbTe4 P4/mcc (124) mp-20196 first on 14 ICSD references, and that is the tetratelluride -- a real and much-studied charge-density-wave chain compound, but not one of the two measured here. NbTe2 C2/m (12) mp-11675 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references and Nb3Te4 P6_3/m (176) mp-7564 at hull 0.000 with 2 are the right entries, and stage 2 should split the host by the Te:Nb ratio, which separates them without ambiguity. The third paper, on a rich structural phase diagram of layered tellurides, is a reminder that the Nb-Te system has several further phases; none of the others appears in these compositions.

basis: Sm0.75Nd0.25NiO3, one composition and three samples, from a paper on a d-band electron correlated thermoelectric thermistor. This is a rare-earth nickelate perovskite with Sm and Nd sharing the A site -- the same RNiO3 family as the La-Nd-Ni-O host in this chunk, moved to smaller A cations, which raises the metal-insulator transition temperature into the useful range for a thermistor.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A-site rare earth
solid_solution_axis.note: Only one composition is present, at Nd/(Nd+Sm) = 0.25, so the axis is recorded for continuity with the La-Nd-Ni-O host rather than as a measured range. Both are trivalent, so this tunes the A-site radius and the Ni-O-Ni angle, not the carrier count.

note: No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should resolve SmNiO3 and NdNiO3 separately, both in the orthorhombic Pbnm tilt system, and interpolate. The measured window 299-483 K sits squarely on the metal-insulator transition of Sm-rich RNiO3, which is what makes this a thermistor, but that transition is electronic -- bond disproportionation and charge order -- and involves at most a small continuous distortion within the perovskite prototype, so it is not recorded in phases. SmNiO3 also needs high oxygen pressure to synthesise and can lose oxygen on heating in air, which would change the Ni valence without changing the prototype.

basis: (Yb2Zr2O7)(Nd2Sn2O7) solid solutions at 40, 50 and 60 percent stannate, from a paper on the low thermal conductivity of rare-earth zirconate-stannate solid solutions. Nd2Sn2O7 is an ordered A2B2O7 pyrochlore and at 40 to 60 percent of it the mixture should retain the pyrochlore superstructure; Yb2Zr2O7, the other end member, is a disordered defect fluorite because Yb3+ is too small for the pyrochlore A site.
note: Confidence is medium because the pyrochlore-to-defect-fluorite boundary is exactly what these compositions straddle, and it cannot be placed from composition alone. The two structures are not different prototypes in any deep sense -- pyrochlore is the cation- and anion-ordered superstructure of the same fluorite framework -- but the order parameter is continuous and is measured by the superlattice reflections, so which side of the boundary a 50:50 mixture falls on is a diffraction result and not an inference. fluorite_oxide is recorded as the alternative for that reason, and the neighbouring hosts O-Yb-Zr and O-Sm-Sn-Yb-Zr from the same paper are assigned consistently with this reading: the Yb2Zr2O7-rich end goes to fluorite_oxide and the stannate-rich mixtures to pyrochlore. No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should resolve Nd2Sn2O7 in Fd-3m and Yb2Zr2O7 separately. The four cations all sit above the 5 at. percent cut in these compositions, so dopant_roles is empty -- this is a four-cation solid solution on two sublattices, and the deliberate mass and radius disorder on both is the low-thermal-conductivity mechanism the paper is about.

basis: Nd(1-x)Sr(x)TiO3 at x = 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, from a paper on the band-filling dependence of the electrical transport of Nd(1-x)A(x)TiO3. This is the ABO3 titanate perovskite with Nd3+ and Sr2+ disordered on the A site; varying their ratio varies the Ti 3d band filling continuously between Mott-insulating NdTiO3 and metallic SrTiO3, which is exactly what the title says is being measured.
note: [ref 2] is not followed. Its single entry, SrNd2Ti4O12 P4/mmm (123) mp-1218162 at hull 0.099 with no ICSD reference, is a computed A-site-ordered supercell of the same perovskite at one particular Sr:Nd ratio, not a distinct phase, and none of the three measured compositions matches it. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should take SrTiO3 Pm-3m and NdTiO3 in its orthorhombic Pbnm tilt setting as the two end members and interpolate, noting that the tilt system itself changes across the series -- NdTiO3 is strongly tilted and SrTiO3 is cubic, so the space group varies with x even though the prototype does not. Sr and Nd are both far above the 5 at. percent cut, so this is a band-filling solid solution rather than a doped compound; no solid_solution_axis is recorded because Nd3+ and Sr2+ are not isoelectronic, which is the whole point -- the substitution changes the carrier count, it does not merely scatter phonons.

basis: The composition string reads Nd0.5Pr0.5, but the only paper in this host is titled Magnetic-field induced multiple topological phases in pyrochlore iridates, and the measured window is 10-18 K. Read together, Nd0.5Pr0.5 is almost certainly the rare-earth site of a (Nd,Pr)2Ir2O7 pyrochlore iridate with the Ir and O lost from the composition string, not a binary rare-earth metal alloy: a 10-18 K measurement on Nd/Pr iridates is the temperature range of the all-in-all-out magnetic ordering those papers study.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A-site rare earth
solid_solution_axis.note: Nd/(Nd+Pr) at the single composition. If the pyrochlore reading is right this is the A site of (Nd,Pr)2Ir2O7, where substituting Pr for Nd tunes across the metal-insulator boundary between antiferromagnetic Nd2Ir2O7 and metallic Pr2Ir2O7.

note: This is a deliberate disagreement with [ref 2], stated rather than hidden. The reference is internally consistent with the literal composition -- PrNd P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1219716 at hull 0.000 is the double-hexagonal-close-packed solid solution the two light rare earths would form, and Pr3Nd and PrNd3 I4/mmm are computed orderings of it -- and if the composition string is taken at face value then solid_solution_alloy in the A3 dhcp setting is the right answer, which is why it is recorded as the alternative. It is not taken at face value because the paper decides it: nothing in a pyrochlore-iridate study would involve a Nd-Pr metal alloy, and a rare-earth metal measured only between 10 and 18 K makes no sense as a sample either. Confidence is low and this host needs the paper read before it is trusted; no mp_id is proposed under either reading.
annotator_note: Composition string appears truncated -- the rare-earth site only of a pyrochlore iridate (Nd,Pr)2Ir2O7, with Ir and O missing. Assigned pyrochlore on the strength of the paper title, at low confidence. If curation confirms the string is literal, reassign to solid_solution_alloy (dhcp) and move the host to Nd-Pr as a genuine binary alloy. Flagged for the review queue.

basis: Ni(x)(SiO2)(1-x) at x = 0.22, 0.26 and 0.55, from a paper titled Resistivity minimum in granular composites and thin metallic films. These are granular metal-insulator composites: nickel grains dispersed in an amorphous silica matrix, spanning the percolation threshold, and the resistivity minimum in the title is a transport signature of that granularity rather than of any compound.
note: [ref 2] disagrees and is not followed. It ranks Si(NiO2)2 Fd-3m (227) mp-18766 at hull 0.024 with 16 ICSD references as PRIMARY, and a Pnma setting mp-19072 with 8 more; these are nickel orthosilicate Ni2SiO4, spinel and olivine respectively, which is a real and well-attested compound but not what was made. A granular composite is metallic nickel plus glassy SiO2 with no reaction between them, and the compositions are written as a metal fraction and an oxide fraction precisely because they are two phases. The remaining reference entries are computed quaternary silicates. mp_id is left null, and per the project README composite_multiphase is a prototype that stage 2 skips rather than resolves. Neither Ni nor Si is a dopant in any sense here, so dopant_roles is empty -- the composition is a mixing ratio between two phases.

basis: Zr3Ni(2.3-1.7)Pt(0.6-1.2)Co0.1Sb4 in three samples, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties and electronic transport of Zr3Ni3Sb4-based material. Zr3Ni3Sb4 is the Y3Au3Sb4 structure type, cubic I-43d -- an ordered ternary filling of the anti-Th3P4 framework -- and Pt here substitutes for Ni on the transition-metal site. The taxonomy entry names Zr3Ni3Sb4 in its notes and Ni-Sb-Zr among its example hosts, so this is that host with platinum added.

dopant_roles.basis: Co0.1 on the transition-metal site in every one of the three compositions, at a fixed level while Ni and Pt are varied. Co is one electron short of Ni, so at this fixed small level it acts as an acceptor tuning the carrier concentration of the Zr3Ni3Sb4 semiconductor; its constancy across the series shows it is a deliberate dopant rather than a compositional variable.

note: No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should look for Zr3Ni3Sb4 in I-43d and expect Pt on the Ni site as a substitution rather than as a separate ordered phase. Platinum is above the 5 at. percent cut and its levels -- 0.6, 0.6 and 1.2 of four transition-metal atoms against Ni at 2.3, 1.7 and 1.7 -- make it a substitutional alloying partner for Ni rather than a dopant; note also that the Ni + Pt + Co total is 3.0 in the first and third compositions but only 2.4 in the second, Zr3Ni1.7Pt0.6Co0.1Sb4, so that sample is transition-metal deficient -- vacancies on the Ni site, which this anti-Th3P4-derived framework tolerates and which is itself a carrier-concentration variable that stage 3 should read as non_stoichiometry rather than as a doping level. Pt is isoelectronic with Ni, so it changes mass and size contrast and the lattice thermal conductivity without changing the electron count, which is the standard reason to put it there.

basis: Sc(1-x)Tm(x)NiSb at x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, from a paper titled Enhanced thermoelectric power factor of half-Heusler solid solution Sc(1-x)Tm(x)NiSb. Both ScNiSb and TmNiSb are 18-electron half-Heusler semiconductors in F-43m, Sc and Tm are both trivalent and both sit on the same site, so the whole series is a single half-Heusler phase with a mixed cation sublattice.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: half-Heusler 4b cation site
solid_solution_axis.note: Sc/(Sc+Tm) across the three compositions. Both are group 3 and trivalent, so the substitution adds no carriers and leaves the 18-electron count intact; it is mass and radius contrast for phonon scattering, which is how the power factor and the figure of merit are improved.

note: No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should resolve ScNiSb and TmNiSb separately in F-43m and interpolate. This is a clean isoelectronic solid solution with no dopant of any kind -- every element is above the 5 at. percent cut and dopant_roles is empty. The measured window 13-917 K is wide but half-Heuslers are stable throughout; what can appear at the high end is a full-Heusler second phase from excess Ni filling the vacant 4d site, which is a synthesis issue rather than a transition.

basis: NpPdSn, one composition and three polycrystalline samples, from a paper on the magnetic and electronic properties of NpPdSn. Equiatomic RPdSn and AnPdSn stannides are overwhelmingly orthorhombic TiNiSi-type, Pnma -- an ordered Co2Si derivative in which Pd and Sn build a puckered honeycomb net and the actinide sits between -- so that is the best available reading from the composition.
note: Confidence is low and this record should be checked against the paper. The 1:1:1 stannides of the rare earths and actinides split between three closely related structures that composition cannot distinguish: the orthorhombic TiNiSi type in Pnma, the hexagonal ZrNiAl or Fe2P type in P-62m, and the GaGeLi type that UPdSn itself adopts, which is an ordered variant of the same puckered-net principle. TiNiSi is the most common outcome for RPdSn and is assigned on that basis; zrnial_fe2p is recorded as the alternative, and the GaGeLi ordering that the uranium analogue takes is a third possibility with no taxonomy entry. No reference line is printed for this host, so there is no independent evidence at all and no mp_id is proposed -- stage 2 should look for NpPdSn directly or, failing that, for the UPdSn and PuPdSn analogues, and should not assume the space group. The 10-296 K window is low-temperature magnetic and transport characterisation of a transuranic compound, with no structural transition expected in it.
annotator_note: Structure assigned from the general behaviour of the RPdSn family, not from any evidence specific to NpPdSn. Low confidence; needs the paper.

basis: Pb2Ru2O7, Pb2Ru2O6.5 and Pb1.8Eu0.2Ru2O7: the lead ruthenate pyrochlore, A2B2O7 in Fd-3m, with a corner-sharing RuO6 octahedral network and an interpenetrating Pb2O-prime sublattice. Both papers name the structure -- one on the metal-insulator crossover in Pb-Ru based oxides with pyrochlore-type structure, the other on flux growth of pyrochlore Pb2Ru2O6.5 single crystals.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb1.8Eu0.2Ru2O7: Eu3+ on the pyrochlore A site in place of Pb2+, which in this family is the way the Ru 4d band filling and the metal-insulator crossover named in the paper title are tuned. It is a genuine aliovalent substitution on a fully occupied site, not a filler.

note: Pb2Ru2O6.5 is worth flagging for stage 2 and stage 3. It is not a defective version of Pb2Ru2O7 by accident: the O-prime site of the lead ruthenate pyrochlore is systematically half empty, giving the composition Pb2Ru2O6.5 with Pb2+ rather than the Pb4+ that a stoichiometric A2B2O7 would need, and the single-crystal paper is explicit about the 6.5 stoichiometry. That is an anion non_stoichiometry on a named crystallographic site, not a parse error, and the two compositions in this host are chemically distinct even though both are pyrochlores. [ref 2] is not followed: Ru4Pb4O13 F-43m mp-674149 at hull 0.000 is a computed cell that is arguably the same 6.5 stoichiometry written differently -- Pb2Ru2O6.5 doubled is Pb4Ru4O13 -- but it has no ICSD reference, and RuPbO3 Pm-3m mp-974337 at hull 0.177 is a computed perovskite that this is not. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should look for Pb2Ru2O7 and Pb2Ru2O6.5 in Fd-3m, and mp-674149 is worth a look as the O-prime-deficient cell.

basis: Rb0.83V2Te2O, one composition and three samples, from a paper on the weak metal-metal transition in the vanadium oxytelluride. The AxV2Te2O oxytellurides are the same structure type as Na2Ti2Sb2O: an anti-CuO2 [V2O] square sheet with oxygen at the centre of every V4 square, capped above and below by tellurium, with the alkali metal between the slabs in I4/mmm.
note: The prototype id was proposed in chunk 025 for the Na-O-Sb-Ti host and is reused here, but its formula_archetype is written narrowly as A2Ti2Pn2O with A = Na or Ba and Pn = As or Sb, which does not literally cover Rb(0.83)V2Te2O: the transition metal is vanadium, the capping anion is a chalcogen rather than a pnictogen, and the alkali site is only partly occupied. The defining feature -- the anti-CuO2 M2O square net -- is identical, so this is the right prototype and the proposed entry should be widened to A(x)M2X2O with M = Ti or V and X = As, Sb or Te when it is reviewed for v4. That widening is recorded here rather than assumed. No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should look for the AxV2Te2O family in I4/mmm, where the alkali deficiency is intrinsic and sets the vanadium d-electron count. The 11-300 K window contains the weak metal-metal transition the paper is named for, which is a density-wave instability of the vanadium square lattice rather than a change of structure type, so it is not recorded in phases; rubidium is above the 5 at. percent cut and its sub-unity occupancy is non_stoichiometry on a host site, not doping.

basis: Two different silicates, separated cleanly by composition. Yb2SiO5 with two samples is the rare-earth monosilicate in the X2 polymorph, monoclinic C2/c, which is the form the small rare earths take; Yb2Si2O7 with one sample is the disilicate in the thortveitite structure, C2/m. The papers are on the thermal properties of rare-earth monosilicates for environmental barrier coatings, which is the X2 family.
note: [ref 2] is followed and covers both phases, with a ranking that has to be set aside. Yb2Si2O7 C2/m (12) mp-4300 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references is PRIMARY and is the thortveitite disilicate; Yb2SiO5 C2/c (15) mp-17702 appears further down at hull 0.197 with 1 ICSD reference, and its C2/c setting matches the X2 monosilicate exactly, so the space groups agree even though the hull energy and reference count favour the disilicate. That ordering reflects which silicate is thermodynamically favoured in the Yb-Si-O system, not which one this paper made, and two of the three samples are the monosilicate. The other reference entries -- BaYb6Si7O24, SrYb4Si5O17, Yb5Si3SO12 -- are unrelated quaternaries. Stage 2 splits this host by the Si:Yb ratio, which separates 1:2 from 1:1 without ambiguity. Both compounds are studied here as thermal barrier and environmental barrier coatings rather than as thermoelectrics, which is why the measurement is thermal conductivity to 1272 K.

basis: (Yb2Zr2O7)(Sm2Sn2O7) solid solutions at 40, 50 and 60 percent stannate, from the same paper on low thermal conductivity in rare-earth zirconate-stannate solid solutions as the Nd-O-Sn-Yb-Zr host. Sm2Sn2O7 is an ordered A2B2O7 pyrochlore, and at 40 to 60 percent of it the mixture should keep the pyrochlore superstructure; the Yb2Zr2O7 end member is a disordered defect fluorite because Yb3+ is too small for the pyrochlore A site.
note: Assigned consistently with Nd-O-Sn-Yb-Zr, which is the same experiment with samarium in place of neodymium, and with O-Yb-Zr, the zirconate-rich end of the same series, which goes to fluorite_oxide. Confidence is medium for the same reason as the neodymium host: pyrochlore is the cation- and anion-ordered superstructure of the fluorite framework, the ordering is a continuous order parameter measured by superlattice reflections, and which side of the boundary a 40 to 60 percent mixture falls on cannot be inferred from composition. Sm3+ is slightly smaller than Nd3+, so if anything this series sits marginally closer to the disordered side than the neodymium one does, which is worth a diffraction check rather than an assertion. No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should resolve Sm2Sn2O7 in Fd-3m and Yb2Zr2O7 separately. All four cations are above the 5 at. percent cut, so dopant_roles is empty and the two-sublattice disorder is the intended phonon-scattering mechanism.

basis: SrTi(1-x)V(x)O3 at x = 0.33, 0.5 and 0.67, grown as thin films according to the curator detail, from a paper on the metal-insulator transition in SrTi(1-x)V(x)O3. Both end members are cubic ABO3 perovskites -- SrTiO3 a d0 band insulator and SrVO3 a d1 correlated metal -- and V substitutes for Ti on the B site, so the whole series is one perovskite with a mixed B sublattice.
note: No reference line is printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed; stage 2 should take SrTiO3 and SrVO3 separately in Pm-3m and interpolate, since the lattice parameters are close and no ordered ternary is involved. Vanadium is far above the 5 at. percent cut so dopant_roles is empty, but the substitution is not isoelectronic: V4+ is d1 against Ti4+ d0, so x is the band-filling variable and the metal-insulator transition in the title is driven by it. The films are epitaxially strained, which shifts the transition and is a sample-level fact no composition-level record carries. The 10-298 K window contains that transition; it is a correlation-driven electronic transition, not a change of structure type, so it is not recorded in phases.

basis: Yttria. Y2O3 with two samples is the cubic C-type sesquioxide, bixbyite in Ia-3, which is the ambient structure for yttrium and the small rare earths; the first paper measures the thermal diffusivity of Y2O3 sintered bodies. The third composition, (Y2O3)99.5(CeO2)0.5, reads as Ce-doped yttria on the same structure.

dopant_roles.basis: (Y2O3)99.5(CeO2)0.5: Ce on the yttrium site at half a mole percent, the standard luminescent activator level. Ce4+ in the precursor is reduced to Ce3+ in the host, which substitutes isovalently for Y3+; the interest is optical rather than electronic, so it is not a carrier dopant. See the annotator note -- the host of this particular composition may not be yttria at all.

note: [ref 1] disagrees with the assignment and is not followed. TEDesignLab gives Y2O3 P-3m1 (164) mp-13061 at hull 0.071 with 3 ICSD references and Y2O3 Pnma (62) mp-1178770 at hull 0.122 with 1; these are the high-pressure A-type and B-type sesquioxide polymorphs, which exist for yttria but are not the ambient phase and are not what a sintered body or a phosphor host would be. [ref 2] settles it in favour of bixbyite and is followed: Y2O3 Ia-3 (206) mp-2652 at hull 0.000 with 44 ICSD references, the single best-attested entry in this chunk by a wide margin. Its YO2 and YO3 entries are computed and not phases of the system, and the Y15TmO24 and SmY15O24 C2 entries at hull 0.001 are rare-earth-substituted yttria supercells, which is incidental support for the substitutional reading of Ce. The measured range reaching 2078 K is the sintered-Y2O3 diffusivity work; bixbyite yttria is stable to roughly 2600 K, so nothing crosses a transition.
annotator_note: The second paper is on YAG:Ce-Al2O3 colour converters, and YAG is Y3Al5O12 garnet, not yttria. The composition string (Y2O3)99.5(CeO2)0.5 carries no aluminium, so either it is a precursor ratio for a garnet that lost its Al in transcription, or a genuine Ce-doped yttria reference sample. Assigned bixbyite because that is what the composition as recorded says, with garnet as the alternative; confidence reduced to medium and flagged for curation. The two plain Y2O3 samples are unaffected.

basis: Yb2Zr2O7 and the same compound with 20 percent of a rare-earth stannate mixed in, from the paper on low thermal conductivity of rare-earth zirconate-stannate solid solutions. Yb2Zr2O7 is a disordered defect fluorite rather than an ordered pyrochlore: the Yb3+ to Zr4+ radius ratio is below the roughly 1.46 threshold at which the pyrochlore superstructure is stable, so the cations and the anion vacancies are randomly distributed on the fluorite lattice.

dopant_roles.basis: Present in two of the three compositions as 20 percent of a Nd2Sn2O7 or Sm2Sn2O7 end member mixed into Yb2Zr2O7, so Sn4+ takes the Zr4+ B site. It falls below the 5 at. percent cut only because it is a fifth of one cation sublattice in a five-element formula; it is a solid-solution end-member constituent, not a dilute dopant.

(Yb2Zr2O7)0.8(Nd2Sn2O7)0.2: Nd3+ on the A site as part of the stannate end member. Trivalent like Yb3+ and much larger, so it pushes the radius ratio back towards the pyrochlore-stable side while adding A-site mass and size disorder.
(Yb2Zr2O7)0.8(Sm2Sn2O7)0.2: the same role as Nd in the samarium version of the series.

note: Assigned as the zirconate-rich end of the same three-host series as Nd-O-Sn-Yb-Zr and O-Sm-Sn-Yb-Zr, which take pyrochlore at 40 to 60 percent stannate; at 0 and 20 percent the defect fluorite should still hold, which is why this host and those two are assigned differently from one composition set. Confidence is medium because the ordered-to-disordered boundary is a continuous order parameter measured by superlattice reflections and not an inference from composition, and because 20 percent of a large-A stannate is already a step towards the ordered side. [ref 2] is not followed as a structure but is consistent with the disorder reading: Yb2Zr2O7 Pmma (51) mp-676382 at hull 0.132, Yb2Zr8O19 P-4m2 mp-676389 and Yb4Zr3O12 P-1 mp-675744 all have no ICSD reference and are computed ordered cells of a phase that is experimentally disordered -- exactly what a hull calculation returns when the real material is a random solid solution. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should use a fluorite cell with mixed cation occupancy rather than any of these.

basis: Three different compounds, one sample each, and no single label is right. U3Pd3Sb4 is the Y3Au3Sb4 type, cubic I-43d, an ordered ternary filling of the anti-Th3P4 framework and the same structure as Ce3Bi4Pd3 named in that taxonomy entry; the paper on uranium-based materials for thermoelectric applications is about that family. UPdSb is the hexagonal 1:1:1 compound and UPd2Sb is a third phase at a third stoichiometry. U3Pd3Sb4 carries the label because it is the thermoelectrically relevant one, not because it is a majority.
note: [ref 2] is followed for all three and it is the reason each alternative is named rather than guessed. U3Sb4Pd3 I-43d (220) mp-1189990 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference is the Y3Au3Sb4-type phase. USbPd P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1077418 at hull 0.005 with 1 ICSD reference is the hexagonal equiatomic compound, and P6_3/mmc for an ABX 1:1:1 is the ZrBeSi ordered AlB2 or Ni2In setting, which is why zrbesi_ordered_alb2 is the alternative for it. USbPd2 Fm-3m (225) mp-1207137 at hull 0.070 is the full Heusler ordering for UPd2Sb, though at that hull energy and with no ICSD reference it is a computed structure rather than an attested one. Note that the block ranks USb2Pd P4/nmm mp-4207 first on 2 ICSD references; that is the 1:2:1 diantimonide and was not measured. Confidence is low because three prototypes are being asserted on one sample each from single-reference computed entries, and because the ZrBeSi entry is classed in the taxonomy as a Zintl polyanion, which is not a natural description of a uranium intermetallic even when the setting matches. Stage 2 must split this host composition by composition; the three stoichiometries separate it without ambiguity.
annotator_note: Three prototypes over three samples, each resting on a single ICSD reference or a computed entry. Queued for review; the equiatomic and 1:2:1 assignments in particular need the papers.

basis: Pd58.8U20.6Si20.6 in three samples, from two papers whose titles say what the samples are: Transport and magnetic properties of icosahedral and glassy Pd-U-Si alloys, and Low-temperature thermal conductivity of glassy and icosahedral Pd-U-Si alloys. So the host holds both an icosahedral quasicrystal and an amorphous alloy of the same composition, made by different quenching and annealing routes, and no periodic structure describes either.

dopant_roles.basis: The composition string Pd58.8SU20.6Si20.6 has a bare S wedged between the Pd and U subscripts, in a pair of compositions that are otherwise identical to Pd58.8U20.6Si20.6. No sulphur belongs in a Pd-U-Si metallic glass, and the pattern -- a stray single letter at a subscript boundary -- is characteristic of a transcription slip rather than a real constituent.

note: This host cannot be resolved to a structure and is flagged as such per the project README, which lists quasicrystal_approximant among the prototypes needing special handling in stage 2: there is no periodic structure, so an approximant has to be named and the substitution said out loud, and metallic_glass is skipped outright. Both are present here, which is why is_mixed is true; the split is not by composition but by sample preparation, so it is one that composition can never make -- the two papers measure the same nominal alloy in two states. [ref 2] is not followed and its entries are for the crystalline equilibrium phases of the chemistry: U(SiPd)2 I4/mmm mp-4793 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references is the ThCr2Si2-type 122 silicide, U3(Si3Pd10)2 Fm-3m mp-630265 has 2 references, and USiPd Pnma mp-21191 has 1. Those are what this alloy would crystallise into on annealing, not what was measured. mp_id is left null.
annotator_note: Composition string Pd58.8SU20.6Si20.6 contains a stray S; treated as a transcription artefact, not a constituent. Split here is by preparation state (icosahedral against glassy), which no composition-level rule can make -- needs the samples.

basis: Zr70Pd30, one composition and three samples, from a paper titled Influence of quasicrystalline phase on transport processes in Zr70Pd30. Zr70Pd30 is a well-known binary bulk metallic glass, and the title says the samples are the glass with a quasicrystalline phase in it -- Zr-Pd is one of the few binaries in which an icosahedral phase nucleates from the amorphous state on annealing, which is why it is studied at all.
note: The glass is named as the prototype and the icosahedral phase as the alternative because the paper studies the influence of the latter on the former -- the matrix is amorphous and the quasicrystals are a dispersed nucleated phase whose volume fraction depends on the anneal. That makes the host mixed by preparation and thermal history rather than by composition, as in Pd-Si-U. The measured window 308-948 K is the reason the distinction matters: it runs straight through the glass transition and the crystallisation sequence of Zr70Pd30, so a single sample changes state during the measurement -- amorphous, then icosahedral, then the equilibrium crystalline phases. That is a genuine transformation but not one the phases field can carry, because the low-temperature state is a glass with no prototype and the sequence is irreversible rather than a thermodynamic phase boundary. [ref 2] describes the crystalline endpoint and is not followed: Zr2Pd I4/mmm mp-266 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references is the equilibrium intermetallic nearest this composition, with ZrPd3, ZrPd, Zr3Pd4 and ZrPd2 also real phases of the system. Those are what the sample becomes at the top of the window, not what it is. mp_id is left null; metallic_glass is skipped in stage 2 per the README.

basis: Elemental platinum and two dilute Pt-Ir alloys at 2 and 3.9 at. percent iridium. Platinum is face-centred cubic (A1, Fm-3m) and iridium is fully soluble in it at this end of the system, so all three compositions are the A1 close-packed structure -- pure metal and substitutional solid solution on the same lattice. These are the standard Pt-Ir thermocouple and reference alloys.

dopant_roles.basis: Pt98Ir2 and Pt96.1Ir3.9: Ir on the fcc lattice site in place of Pt. Not isoelectronic -- Ir is group 9 against Pt group 10 -- so it is a genuine impurity scatterer and a valence perturbation, which is what a low-temperature thermopower measurement on a dilute noble-metal alloy is designed to see. At 2 to 4 at. percent this is dilute substitution rather than alloying.

note: [ref 2] gives exactly one entry and it agrees: Pt Fm-3m (225) mp-126 at hull 0.000 with 22 ICSD references. This host is the dilute-Ir counterpart of the Ir-Pt host at rank 1750 in chunk 035, where iridium is above the 5 at. percent cut and the same alloys are treated as the host rather than as doped platinum -- the two records describe one continuous series split by the threshold, and the first paper is shared between them. The robust window 10-117 K with a full span to 797 K reflects that: the low-temperature thermopower work is on the dilute alloys, and the second paper, on phonon and electron contributions to the thermal conductivity of VN(x), uses platinum as a reference metal to higher temperature. Nothing crosses a transition; platinum is fcc to the melt.

basis: ReSi1.75 and two Al-substituted versions, ReSi1.7125Al0.05 and ReSi1.675Al0.10, from a paper titled Tuning Crystal Structures and Thermoelectric Properties through Al Doping in ReSi1.75. ReSi1.75 is Re4Si7, a Nowotny chimney-ladder phase -- a tetragonal transition-metal subcell with a helical silicon ladder threading it at an incommensurate period -- which is the same structural principle as higher manganese silicide and is what this prototype covers.

dopant_roles.basis: Al on the silicon ladder in place of Si. The role is framework_substitution rather than plain substitutional because in a chimney-ladder phase the main-group count is the structure: the valence electron concentration fixes the ladder period and hence which member of the homologous series forms, so Al for Si changes the crystal structure and not only the carrier count. The paper says exactly this in its title -- tuning crystal structures through Al doping -- and stage 3 should treat the Al level as a structure variable as well as a doping level.

note: [ref 2] is followed only as background. ReSi2 I4/mmm (139) mp-12605 at hull 0.130 with 5 ICSD references is PRIMARY, and that is the disordered high-temperature C11b aristotype of this compound rather than the ordered chimney-ladder superstructure that the 1.75 stoichiometry names -- so the space group disagrees with the assignment in the same way the cubic ReO3 aristotype disagrees with monoclinic WO3. Re4Si7 is a tetragonal superstructure of it with ordered silicon and a much larger c axis; mp_id is left null and stage 2 should look for Re4Si7 rather than ReSi2. ReSi P2_13 mp-7948 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references is the B20 monosilicide, a genuine phase of the system but a different compound, and Re5Si3, Re2Si and Re3Si are further silicides not measured here. Per the README, this prototype is one of those needing special handling in stage 2: the structure is an incommensurate composite, so only approximants exist as structure files.

basis: Re6Te15, Re6Ga0.5Te15 and Re6GaTe15, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of Re6Ga(x)Se(y)Te(15-y). Re6Te15 is the archetype of this prototype by name: octahedral Re6 clusters bridged by tellurium into a three-dimensional cluster framework, with Te2 dimers and large voids, which is why the family has such low thermal conductivity.

dopant_roles.basis: Re6Ga(x)Te15 at x = 0.5 and 1. Gallium does not replace either Re or Te -- the Re6Te15 framework is complete at x = 0 and the series runs to x = 2 in the paper -- so it enters the voids of the cluster framework, donating electrons to the cluster and scattering phonons. Whether those voids count as genuine cages in the skutterudite sense is not settled from the composition, so interstitial is recorded rather than cage_filler.

note: [ref 2] is not followed and offers nothing for this compound: ReTe P6_3mc mp-974469 at hull 0.899 and ReTe2 P-1 mp-1102447 at hull 0.059, neither with an ICSD reference and neither at the Re6Te15 stoichiometry. The taxonomy entry names Pbca (61) as the typical space group and Re6Se4Te10 as its exemplar, which is the same family with selenium partly replacing tellurium -- the paper here spans that too, with y running from 0 to 7.5, though only the y = 0 end appears in this host. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should look for Re6Te15 in Pbca. This is a cluster compound rather than a layered or framework chalcogenide, and its interest is entirely the intrinsically low lattice thermal conductivity that the cluster-plus-void architecture gives.

basis: RuSe2 with two samples and Ru0.9Ir0.1Se2 with one, from a paper titled Enhanced thermoelectric power and electronic correlations in RuSe2. RuSe2 is a pyrite-type diselenide, cubic Pa-3, with Ru in octahedral coordination and Se2 dimers -- the same structure as FeS2 pyrite -- and it is a correlated narrow-gap semiconductor, which is what the title is about.

dopant_roles.basis: Ru0.9Ir0.1Se2: Ir on the octahedral cation site of the pyrite structure. Ir is one electron richer than Ru, so this is an n-type donor substitution that fills the narrow d band the paper is measuring; at 10 percent of the cation site it is heavy doping rather than a dilute impurity.

note: [ref 1] agrees and is followed: TEDesignLab gives RuSe2 Pa-3 (205) mp-1922 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is the pyrite structure and an ICSD-backed one. This is the strongest single piece of reference support in the chunk after Y2O3 and ThN. Note that the RuSe2 family also has a marcasite-type polymorph in some related diselenides; none is offered here and nothing in the composition suggests it, so no other_polymorphs entry is recorded. The measured window 10-1026 K is wide and pyrite RuSe2 is stable across it.

basis: All three compositions are written as (US)x(ThS)1-x at x = 0.75, 0.50 and 0.25, and the paper is on the thermoelectric properties of uranium monosulfide and thorium monosulfide. US and ThS are both NaCl-type monosulfides, and U and Th are close enough in size and both tetravalent-capable on that site that the 1:1 monosulfide solid solution is continuous. So this host is a (U,Th)S rocksalt series rather than a distinct ternary compound.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: U and Th share the single cation site of the rocksalt monosulfide. The three compositions sample it at a quarter, a half and three quarters, which is a deliberate series rather than doping, so no parent compound is recorded at host level.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] here and am recording it rather than following it. Materials Project offers ThU2S5 Pna2_1 mp-1217436 and ThUS2 R-3m mp-1217311 as PRIMARY, but both sit at a metal-to-sulfur ratio near 1:2, while every composition in this host is at 1:1. Those are real entries for a different part of the Th-U-S phase field, not for the monosulfides the paper measured. None of them carries an ICSD reference count in the chunk file either. No mp_id is taken, since neither US nor ThS appears in the returned set and the README forbids inventing one.
annotator_note: Confidence is medium rather than high only because no reference in the chunk corroborates the rocksalt call; the composition and the paper title are both unambiguous.

basis: One composition, Tl4TiS4, across all three samples, from a paper on the effect of nonstoichiometry on its thermoelectric properties. The 4:1:4 stoichiometry is an ortho-thiotitanate: isolated TiS4 tetrahedra balanced by four monovalent Tl cations, which is a different building principle from the layered TiS2 that a Ti-S composition normally implies.
note: The two references disagree with each other and I follow [ref 1], as the project precedence directs. TEDesignLab returns Ti(TlS)4 in space group 14 as PRIMARY, an exact formula match at the monoclinic setting reported for this structure type. [ref 2] Materials Project has no 4-1-4 entry at all: it offers Ti(TlS2)2 Pbca mp-14441 on 1 ICSD reference and Ti5TlS8 C2/m mp-1101049, which are layered thiotitanates at Tl:Ti ratios of 1:1 and 1:5 against the 4:1 measured here. No mp_id is taken, because the only formula-correct reference is the TEDesignLab one and it carries no mp_id in the chunk file.
annotator_note: New prototype tl4tis4_type proposed in prototypes_proposed.jsonl before use.

basis: One composition, U3ScSb5. The U3TSb5 family with T a small early transition metal is built as a U3Sb5 hexagonal framework with T filling the octahedral interstitial site, which is the filled Mn5Si3 arrangement, and the paper on anisotropic transport in ternary uranium antimonides is a study of exactly that series. The Sc and Ti members in this chunk are the same structure.
note: [ref 2] agrees: ScU3Sb5 P6_3/mcm mp-13243 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, an exact formula match at the space group the filled Mn5Si3 type takes. One ICSD reference is thin, so the support is weak in the sense the chunk header describes, but the reference and the structural reasoning point the same way. mp-13243 is taken from the ref line, not supplied from memory. The measured window is 11-295 K, entirely below anything that would change the structure.
annotator_note: The taxonomy entry is written for the unfilled A5B3 Mn5Si3 type; the filled 3-1-5 variant is the same space group with the 2b site occupied, and v4 review may want to note that explicitly on the entry.

basis: Three compositions written as ZnxSb2-xTe3 at x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, but the paper is titled optical and thermoelectric properties of Sb2Te3/ZnTe nanostructured composites, so the Zn is not on the Sb site of a single phase: these are Sb2Te3 with ZnTe precipitated in it. The stoichiometry looks substitutional only because the parser split Zn and Sb across the same two-atom slot.
note: is_mixed is false deliberately, following the Bi-C-Te precedent from chunk 8: every composition in this host contains both phases, so there is nothing for a composition-by-composition split to separate. The two constituent structures are recorded as alternatives instead, so stage 2 resolves tetradymite Sb2Te3 for the matrix and zincblende ZnTe for the inclusions rather than treating the host as structureless. No reference block was returned for this host at all.
annotator_note: At x = 0.75 the ZnTe fraction is high enough that the matrix may no longer be the majority phase; that cannot be settled from the composition string.

basis: One composition, U3TiSb5, from the same paper on anisotropic transport in ternary uranium antimonides as the Sc member. Same U3Sb5 hexagonal framework with the transition metal on the interstitial octahedral site, which is the filled Mn5Si3 type.
note: [ref 2] agrees: U3TiSb5 P6_3/mcm mp-21227 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, exact formula and the expected space group. mp-21227 is taken from the ref line. Measured window 10-295 K, no transition in range.

basis: Elemental selenium with indium at three levels spanning six orders of magnitude, from 6.5 parts per million to 3.3 at.%, and one paper on the electrical conductivity and thermoelectric power of liquid selenium doped with indium. The measurement is on the melt, so the record describes a covalent chain liquid rather than the trigonal crystal the element forms at room temperature.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives Se P3_121 mp-14 at hull 0.006 on 27 ICSD references, the helical-chain trigonal structure. It is the correct description of solid selenium and it is recorded here rather than in phases because the paper measures the liquid, above the 494 K melting point. It is filed as unknown rather than metastable because it is the stable ambient solid and simply outside the measured state.

[ref 2] also returns Se in Pm-3m mp-7755 at hull 0.180, Im-3m mp-119 at hull 0.589, Cmcm mp-1009757 at hull 0.156 and Fd-3m mp-12771 at hull 0.509. Hulls of that size mean high-pressure or computed cells; none is reached by heating selenium at one atmosphere, and none of them has a taxonomy entry.

dopant_roles.basis: Se0.9667In0.0333 and two far more dilute compositions. In a melt there is no lattice site to substitute onto, so none of the crystallographic roles applies. Physically indium cross-links and terminates the selenium chain fragments, which is how it changes the conductivity, but the vocabulary has no term for that and unknown is the honest entry rather than a guessed substitutional.

note: The chunk file shows no measured range line for this host, so I could not check the temperature window against the 494 K melting point from the data. The assignment rests on the paper title, which says liquid selenium explicitly, and confidence is held at medium because of that. If stage 2 finds the curves are actually on solid selenium, the alternative trigonal_te is the correct answer and this record should flip.
annotator_note: New prototype chalcogen_chain_melt proposed before use, following the molten_salt precedent from chunk 025.

basis: Two compositions and two different structures: U3Sn5 with two samples, from the paper reporting it as a new uranium compound, and USn3 with one, from a survey of thermoelectric power in uranium intermetallics. USn3 is the cubic AuCu3 type; U3Sn5 is the orthorhombic Pu3Pd5 type usually assigned to that stoichiometry in actinide intermetallics. The majority composition sets the host label and the other is recorded as an alternative.
note: This host separates cleanly on stoichiometry, so stage 2 should split it: U3Sn5 to pu3pd5_type, USn3 to cu3au_l12 with mp-20336. [ref 2] covers only the second of those. It gives USn3 Pm-3m mp-20336 at hull 0.000 on 9 ICSD references, which is solid support for the cubic phase, but it has no U3Sn5 entry at all -- the computed U3Sn7, U5Sn4, USn and USn2 cells it returns are all different stoichiometries with no ICSD backing. So the prototype carrying the host label is the one the references cannot check, which is why confidence is low.
annotator_note: The Pu3Pd5 assignment for U3Sn5 is from materials knowledge alone. Stage 2 should read the space group out of the 1990 paper, which is a structure report.

basis: Elemental strontium, one composition, from the same paper on the electrical resistivity and thermoelectric power of Ca and Sr above room temperature that supplied the Ca host in chunk 18. Strontium is face-centred cubic at ambient conditions and transforms to body-centred cubic at about 830 K, which the 288-899 K measured window crosses, so both phases are recorded rather than one label. Both fall under this prototype, whose display name already spans A1 and A2.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists Sr P6_3/mmc mp-867202 at hull 0.005 on 3 ICSD references. An intermediate hexagonal strontium phase between fcc and bcc was reported in older work and is now generally regarded as impurity-stabilised rather than an equilibrium phase of the pure metal. It is recorded as a polymorph rather than inserted into the thermal sequence, and the occurrence is unknown because the question is genuinely unsettled.

[ref 2] also returns Sr P6/mmm mp-19858 at hull 0.225 and I4_1/amd mp-10617 at hull 0.262. Strontium has a well-populated high-pressure sequence and those hulls place these cells in it, not in an ambient-pressure resistivity measurement.

note: [ref 2] marks Sr Fm-3m mp-76 PRIMARY but AMBIGUOUS, on 5 ICSD references against 4 for Im-3m mp-95 and 4 for P6/mmm. That spread is what a metal with several accessible polymorphs looks like in a reference count and is not a reason to doubt the fcc ground state. The mp_ids are taken from the ref line. The 830 K transition temperature is from materials knowledge, not from the paper, and is marked as such.
annotator_note: Modelled on the Ca record from chunk 18, which is the same paper and the same argument one row up the group.

basis: TaTe2 with two niobium-substituted variants, all single crystals, from a paper titled structural, electrical and thermoelectric properties of distorted 1T-TaTe2. TaTe2 is a layered transition-metal ditelluride whose 1T octahedral layers are distorted by metal-metal clustering into double zigzag chains, lowering the symmetry to monoclinic C2/m while keeping the 1T layer topology.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] also returns TaTe4 P4/mcc mp-22817 on 4 ICSD references and TaTe4 P4/ncc mp-202 on 2. TaTe4 is a real and well-studied chain compound with a charge-density wave, but it is a different composition from the TaTe2 measured here and has no taxonomy entry of its own.

dopant_roles.basis: Ta0.94Nb0.06Te2 and Ta0.9Nb0.1Te2: Nb is directly above Ta in group 5, so it takes the same octahedral metal site with the same valence electron count. It adds no carriers; what it does is perturb the metal-metal clustering that defines the distorted 1T structure, which is what a paper on the distortion would want to vary. At 6 and 10 percent of the metal site this is dilute on the sublattice but it is an alloying axis, not doping.

note: [ref 2] supports the assignment: TaTe2 C2/m mp-1967 at hull 0.000 on 5 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is the monoclinic distorted 1T cell. mp-1967 is taken from the ref line. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the taxonomy entry cdi2_1t is written for the undistorted trigonal 1T parent and does not name the monoclinic clustered variant; v4 review may want to widen it or split off a TaTe2 entry.
annotator_note: Nb is listed as a dopant candidate by the 5 at.% split but it reaches 10 percent of the metal sublattice, so it is recorded as an isoelectronic axis rather than as a dopant.

basis: Elemental uranium, three samples of polycrystalline metal across two papers on electrical resistivity and thermoelectric power. Uranium has three ambient-pressure phases and the measurement runs through them: orthorhombic alpha below about 941 K, tetragonal beta to about 1049 K, then body-centred cubic gamma to the melt. The robust window is 297-1019 K and the full span reaches 1374 K, so all three are recorded.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] gives U P4_2nm mp-43 on 4 ICSD references. That is the alpha-1 charge-density-wave distortion of alpha-U, which sets in below about 43 K -- far below the 297 K start of the measured window, so it is not in the thermal sequence. It is the same prototype in a distorted setting rather than a separate structure.
[ref 2] also returns U Pmma mp-1197206 at hull 0.370 on 2 ICSD references. A hull that high is a high-pressure or computed cell, not an ambient-pressure thermal phase.

note: [ref 2] supports the ambient phase strongly: U Cmcm mp-44 at hull 0.000 on 21 ICSD references, far ahead of everything else. It ranks Im-3m mp-108 at 6 references above P4_2/mnm mp-93 at 4, but reference counts do not order a thermal sequence and beta genuinely sits between alpha and gamma. All three mp_ids are taken from the ref line. The two transition temperatures come from materials knowledge, not from either paper, and are marked llm_materials_knowledge. The second paper is on uranium-zirconium alloys, which is where the full span up to 1374 K comes from; the pure-U samples are the ones recorded here.
annotator_note: Two new prototypes proposed before use: alpha_u_a20 and beta_u_sigma_tp30. Gamma-U goes to the existing solid_solution_alloy entry, following the bcc half of the Ca record from chunk 18.

basis: One composition, Zr65Al7.5Ni10Cu7.3Fe0.2Ag10, from a paper on Moessbauer and transport studies of amorphous and icosahedral Zr-based alloys. Zr65Al7.5Ni10Cu17.5 is the textbook Zr-based bulk metallic glass former and this is that alloy with Ag substituted for most of the Cu; the composition is a five-component deep eutectic chosen for glass formation, not a line compound.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.2 at 0.2 at.% in a Moessbauer study. At that level in that experiment iron is the resonant probe nucleus, deliberately added so the local environment of the late transition metal can be read; it sits where Ni and Cu sit in the glass. It is a probe rather than a carrier dopant, but substitutional on the transition-metal population is the right structural description and there is no probe role in the vocabulary.

note: The paper title names two states of the same alloy: the amorphous ribbon and the icosahedral quasicrystalline phase that forms from it on annealing. Both are real for this composition, so quasicrystal_approximant is recorded as an alternative. is_mixed stays false because the two states are not separable by composition -- it is one composition measured in two conditions -- so a composition-level split would have nothing to split on. Only sample-level information could tell which of the two samples is which. No reference block was returned for this host.
annotator_note: Both metallic_glass and quasicrystal_approximant are flagged in the README as needing special handling in stage 2; neither resolves to a single MP entry.

basis: Ag0.89Au0.11 and Ag0.92Au0.06Pd0.02, from papers on the thermal and electrical properties of Ag-Au and Ag-Cu alloy tapes for magnet and superconductor applications. Silver and gold are both face-centred cubic with nearly identical lattice parameters and form a continuous disordered solid solution at every composition; these are dilute alloy tapes, not intermetallics.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag0.92Au0.06Pd0.02: Pd is face-centred cubic and fully miscible with Ag, so it takes a site in the same disordered fcc lattice. In a tape alloy it is there for mechanical strength and resistivity rather than as an electronic dopant.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Ag and Au share the single fcc site. Only the dilute end is sampled here, at 6 and 11 percent gold, so both compositions are silver with gold in it rather than a half-and-half alloy.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] and record it rather than following it. Materials Project returns Ag3Au I4/mmm mp-1183214, AgAu R-3m mp-1229092 and AgAu3 P6_3/mmc mp-985287, all PRIMARY, all AMBIGUOUS, all at hull 0.000 and none with any ICSD reference count shown. Those are computed ordered superstructures on the fcc lattice -- the arrangements a calculation finds when it is asked to order a solid solution -- and Ag-Au is famous for not ordering: it is a continuous disordered fcc solution across the whole range. No mp_id is taken, because the physically right answer here is a disordered lattice that Materials Project has no single entry for.
annotator_note: Ag and Au both already appear as elemental hosts in the ledger under solid_solution_alloy, which this is consistent with.

basis: Both compositions are europium-substituted BaAgSb, from a paper on a point-defect approach to the thermoelectric performance of a Zintl phase. The AAgSb 1-1-1 Zintl phases with a large divalent A cation are built as planar honeycomb AgSb layers alternating with A layers, which is the ZrBeSi ordering of the AlB2 parent; Eu is divalent and substitutes Ba on the cation layer.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Eu2+ and Ba2+ share the interlayer cation site. The parsed fractions are not trustworthy here -- see the note -- so x_min and x_max are the Eu share of the stated cation content as written and should not be used for stage 3 arithmetic without re-parsing.

note: Confidence is low for two reasons. First, no reference block was returned for this host at all, so nothing checks the call. Second, the composition strings do not balance: Ba0.95Eu0.3AgSb and Ba0.96Eu0.2AgSb put 1.25 and 1.16 cations against one Ag and one Sb, which is not a 1-1-1 phase as written. That looks like a parse or transcription problem on a series that was probably Ba1-xEuxAgSb. Separately, the choice between the planar ZrBeSi ordering and the puckered LiGaGe variant in P6_3mc is genuinely open for AAgSb; a large cation like Ba favours the planar form, which is why that is the one recorded, but stage 2 should read the space group from the paper.
annotator_note: The malformed cation sum is worth flagging upstream -- it will produce wrong doping levels in stage 3 if taken at face value.

basis: Cs1.2Ag0.6Bi3.4S6 and Cs0.6Ag0.8Bi2.2S4, from a paper on a homologous series of two-dimensional Cs-Ag-Bi-Q chalcogenides with ion-exchange properties. Two non-integer compositions at different Cs:Bi ratios from one homologous series is exactly the situation this prototype exists for: large cells built from bismuth chalcogenide slabs of varying width with alkali cations between them, where each member is effectively its own structure.
note: The taxonomy entry already lists Ag-Bi-S among its example host systems, so this is the same family with caesium added rather than a new one. [ref 2] returns only CsAg2BiS3 P2_1/c mp-1193928 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference. That is a related quaternary and it does confirm the chemistry is real and monoclinic, but it matches neither composition measured here, so no mp_id is taken. The README flags this prototype as one where every composition is effectively its own structure and stage 2 must resolve them individually; that applies here, and the two compositions are different members of the series.
annotator_note: determined_at should probably read composition for this host once stage 2 looks at it, since the two members are different structures.

basis: Bi85Sb10Ag5 and Bi85Sb8Ag7, from a paper on the thermoelectric performance of ternary Bi-Sb-Ag alloys prepared by mechanical alloying. Both are 85 at.% bismuth with a little antimony, which is the Bi-Sb solid solution -- the arsenic-type A7 rhombohedral structure that Bi and Sb share continuously -- and the silver is a minor third component added by milling.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Bi and Sb share the single A7 site and are continuously miscible. Only the bismuth-rich end is sampled, at 9 to 11 percent Sb of the Bi-Sb pair, which is the composition range where the Bi-Sb alloys have their semimetal-to-semiconductor gap.

note: Confidence is low because of the silver, not because of the Bi-Sb matrix. Ag sits at 5 and 7 at.%, just above the split, so it is treated as a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry -- but silver has very little equilibrium solubility in bismuth, and in a mechanically alloyed powder it is more likely to be a dispersed metallic or Ag-Sb second phase than a substituent. That is why composite_multiphase is recorded as an alternative. No reference block was returned for this host, so nothing settles it; stage 2 should look for whether the paper reports a second phase in the diffraction.

basis: One composition, AgBi0.5Sb0.5Se2, from a paper on solid-solutioned homojunction nanoplates with a disordered lattice. AgBiSe2 and AgSbSe2 are both I-V-VI2 ternaries built on the rocksalt lattice with Ag and the pnictogen sharing the cation site; a fifty-fifty Bi-Sb mixture on top of that cation disorder is precisely the disordered lattice the title refers to.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Bi and Sb are both trivalent and share the pnictogen half of the rocksalt cation site. Only the fifty-fifty point is sampled, so this is the alloy midpoint rather than a doped end member.

note: I part company with [ref 2] and record it. Materials Project returns Ag2BiSbSe4 I-4m2 mp-1229120 at hull 0.046 as PRIMARY with no ICSD reference count shown. That is the same composition written as an ordered tetragonal superstructure -- a calculation choosing one arrangement of Ag, Bi and Sb on the cation sublattice -- and the paper is explicitly about the lattice being disordered. The cubic disordered solution is the physically right description and Materials Project has no entry for it, so no mp_id is taken. One genuine caveat: pure AgBiSe2 has ordered low-temperature phases that convert to the cubic form on heating, within the 300-551 K measured window, but half-substituting Sb suppresses that ordering and AgSbSe2 is cubic throughout, so no transition is recorded.
annotator_note: Confidence is medium rather than high because of the AgBiSe2 ordering question, not because the rocksalt framework is in doubt.

basis: CeInCu1.8Ag0.2 and CeInCu1.5Ag0.5, from a paper on the thermopower of CexY1-xInCu2 and CeInCuyAg2-y. CeInCu2 is a cubic Heusler-type heavy-fermion compound -- the MnCu2Al arrangement with Ce and In on the two ordered cation sublattices and Cu on the tetrahedral sites -- and this host is that compound with silver progressively replacing copper on the Cu sublattice.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: Heusler 8c tetrahedral site
solid_solution_axis.note: Ag and Cu are both group 11 and share the tetrahedral Heusler site. The series runs from 10 to 25 percent silver on that site here, and the paper name shows it is a deliberate y axis rather than doping.

note: [ref 2] returns CeInCuAg F-43m mp-1226682 at hull 0.027 as PRIMARY with no ICSD reference count. F-43m at a 1:1:1:1 composition is the fully ordered quaternary Heusler, which is what a calculation gives when Cu and Ag are placed on separate sublattices. Neither composition here is at 1:1 Cu:Ag -- they are at 9:1 and 3:1 -- so that ordering cannot apply, and the disordered Cu/Ag occupation of the Fm-3m parent is the right description. No mp_id is taken. quaternary_heusler is recorded as an alternative because at the 1:1 end of this series the ordered structure does become the right answer.
annotator_note: The related Ag-Ce-In host one row down is the y = 2 end member of the same paper and goes to the same prototype with reference support.

basis: One composition, CeInAg2, from the same paper on the thermopower of CeInCuyAg2-y as the Cu-containing host above; this is the y = 0 end member. CeInAg2 is the cubic Heusler-type X2YZ arrangement with Ag on the tetrahedral sublattice and Ce and In ordered on the other two, the silver analogue of the well-studied CeInCu2 heavy fermion.
note: [ref 2] agrees exactly: CeInAg2 Fm-3m mp-672191 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY. Fm-3m at an X2YZ composition is the full Heusler space group, so the reference and the structural reading give the same answer, and mp-672191 is taken from the ref line. The other entry it returns, Ce2InAg P4/mmm mp-1227262 at hull 0.054, is a computed cell at a different stoichiometry. Measured window 10-295 K, no transition.

basis: Ag5Te1.4Se0.6Cl and Ag5Te1.6Se0.4Cl, from a paper on the effects of partial anion substitution on the thermoelectric properties of the parent compound. The 5:2:1 metal-chalcogen-halide stoichiometry is the Ag5Te2Cl structure already in the proposed taxonomy, and this host is that compound with selenium substituted for part of the tellurium.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: chalcogen
solid_solution_axis.note: Se and Te are both group 16 and share the chalcogen site; the chloride sits on its own halide site and is not part of this axis. Selenium takes 20 to 30 percent of the chalcogen sublattice across the two compositions, which is the partial anion substitution the paper title refers to.

note: No reference block was returned for this host, so the assignment rests on the composition and the existing proposed entry rather than on any measured space group. Confidence is medium for that reason. Selenium sits above the 5 at.% split so it is a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry, which is correct: it is an alloying axis, not a dilute dopant.
annotator_note: ag5te2cl_type was proposed in an earlier chunk and is still pending review; this is a second host using it, which strengthens the case for folding it into v4.

basis: One composition, CsAg5TeS2, from a paper on two-dimensional CsAg5Te3-xSx semiconductors. That is the x = 2 member of the sulfur-substituted CsAg5Te3 series, so the structure is the CsAg5Te3 framework -- an ordered silver chalcogenide network with caesium in tunnels -- with sulfur on two thirds of the chalcogen sites.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: chalcogen
solid_solution_axis.note: S and Te share the chalcogen sublattice. Only the x = 2 point of the CsAg5Te3-xSx series is sampled in this host, at two thirds sulfur; the x = 0 end member is the separate Ag-Cs-Te host in this same chunk.

note: No reference block was returned for this host. The space group is inherited from the tellurium end member, where [ref 2] gives CsAg5Te3 P4_2/mnm mp-9206 on 1 ICSD reference, and no mp_id is recorded here because that entry is for a different composition. Confidence is medium: the family assignment is secure from the paper title, but two thirds sulfur substitution is a large perturbation and whether the tetragonal framework survives it unchanged is not something the composition can settle.
annotator_note: New prototype csag5te3_type proposed before use; it covers this host and the Ag-Cs-Te host together.

basis: One composition, CsAg5Te3, from the paper reporting concerted rattling in CsAg5Te3 leading to ultralow thermal conductivity. This is the parent of the CsAg5Te3-xSx series and the compound the prototype is named for: a tetragonal silver telluride framework with caesium in open tunnels, where the low lattice thermal conductivity comes from correlated rattling of the Cs and Ag rather than from superionic diffusion.
note: [ref 2] gives CsAg5Te3 P4_2/mnm mp-9206 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY, an exact formula match at the expected tetragonal setting; mp-9206 is taken from the ref line. A single ICSD reference is a weak primary by the chunk header rule, but it is the only structure reported for the formula and the paper is a structure-and-phonons study that describes it, so confidence is high. The other entry, CsAg3Te2 C2/m mp-1213692, is a computed cell at a different stoichiometry. The 292-761 K window is wide but this compound has no reported transition in it; note that silver-rich tellurides often do become superionic on heating, which stage 2 should check against the paper.

basis: One composition, DyAgSb2, single crystals, from a paper on the thermoelectric power of RAgSb2 for R = Y, La, Ce and Dy in zero and applied field. The RAgSb2 series is the classic HfCuSi2-type 112 structure: rare-earth and Ag-Sb slabs alternating with a square net of antimony, and it is the square net that gives these compounds their Dirac-like bands and large magnetothermopower.
note: [ref 2] agrees: DyAgSb2 P4/nmm mp-10965 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY, and P4/nmm is the HfCuSi2 space group. mp-10965 is taken from the ref line. The second entry it returns, Dy2AgSb3 P4/mmm mp-1206934, sits at hull 3.071 -- a hull that large means a computed cell that is nowhere near stable and should be ignored entirely. Measured window 11-296 K.
annotator_note: hfcusi2_112_square_net was proposed in an earlier chunk and is still pending; this host is further support for it.

basis: Ag9Ga(Se0.85Te0.15)6 and Ag9Ga(Se0.83Te0.17)6, from the paper on high thermoelectric performance of Ag9GaSe6 enabled by a low cutoff frequency. Ag9GaSe6 is an argyrodite: a close-packed selenium framework with GaSe4 tetrahedra and nine silver atoms distributed over many partially occupied sites, which is the origin of both the ultralow thermal conductivity and the low cutoff frequency the title names.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: chalcogen
solid_solution_axis.note: Te and Se are both group 16 and share the close-packed chalcogen framework of the argyrodite. Tellurium takes 15 to 17 percent of it, written explicitly as a bracketed anion mixture in the composition string, which is a deliberate alloying axis rather than doping.

note: [ref 2] does not cover this composition and I do not follow it. It returns Ga2Ag2TeSe3 C2 mp-1224849 and GaAgTeSe I2_12_12_1 mp-1224853, both computed entries with no ICSD references at a 1:1 Ag:Ga ratio, while every composition here is at 9:1. Those are different compounds in the same chemistry, so no mp_id is taken. Tellurium is above the 5 at.% split and carries no dopant_roles entry, which is right: it is an alloying component on the anion sublattice. Measured window 299-849 K; argyrodites commonly have an order-disorder transition on heating and stage 2 should check whether Ag9GaSe6 has one inside that range.

basis: One composition, (GeTe)5.5AgInTe2, from a paper on TAGS-related indium compounds and their thermoelectric properties. TAGS materials are (GeTe)x(AgSbTe2)1-x pseudobinaries that stay in the rhombohedrally distorted rocksalt structure of GeTe as long as GeTe dominates; this is the indium analogue at x = 5.5, which is TAGS-85 composition, well inside the rhombohedral field.
note: No reference block was returned for this host. The measured window is 10-399 K, entirely below the rhombohedral-to-cubic transition of GeTe near 700 K, so no transition is recorded and spans_transition is false -- which is the one thing that would otherwise need care for a GeTe-based material. Confidence is medium because alloying AgInTe2 into GeTe lowers that transition temperature, but not to anywhere near 399 K, and because the Ag and In fractions here are large enough that the cation sublattice is heavily substituted.

basis: One composition, YbAgGe, single crystals, from a paper on thermoelectric power investigations of YbAgGe across its quantum critical point. YbAgGe is the standard example of an equiatomic 1-1-1 in the hexagonal ZrNiAl structure, where the Yb atoms form a distorted kagome lattice -- the geometric frustration of that lattice is what makes it a field-tuned quantum critical system and is the reason the paper exists.
note: [ref 2] agrees: YbAgGe P-62m mp-9776 at hull 0.000 on 2 ICSD references as PRIMARY, and P-62m is the ZrNiAl space group. mp-9776 is taken from the ref line. The other entry, Yb2AgGe Fm-3m mp-865630, is a computed cell at a different stoichiometry with no ICSD backing. Measured window 10-347 K.

basis: One composition, Ag3In2Mo15Se19, across both papers on its crystal and electronic structure and its ultralow lattice thermal conductivity. The Mo15Se19 cluster compounds are built from alternating Mo6Se8 and Mo9Se11 cluster units in the same framework, with the silver and indium cations in the channels between them, so this sits in the Mo9 cluster family rather than in the pure Chevrel one.
note: The taxonomy entry mo9se11_cluster is written for the AxMo9X11 formula, and Mo15Se19 is strictly a hybrid: it contains both the Mo6 octahedral cluster of the Chevrel phases and the Mo9 bioctahedral cluster of that entry, in a 1:1 ratio per formula unit. Neither existing entry covers it exactly, so chevrel is recorded as an alternative and confidence is medium. I chose not to propose a separate M15Se19 entry because the Mo9 unit is the distinguishing one and the two families are already discriminated in the taxonomy; v4 review may reasonably decide otherwise. No reference block was returned for this host, so nothing external checks it.
