annotator_note: The Ag-Mo-Se-Tl host in this same chunk holds both a true Mo9Se11 and another Mo15Se19, which is the same question.

basis: AgInZnSe2 and Ag0.9In0.9Zn0.2Se2, from a paper on the site occupations of Zn in AgInSe2-based chalcopyrites. The paper names the structure family in its title and the compositions are AgInSe2 with zinc added on the cation sublattice, so the framework is the diamond-like chalcopyrite ordering of Ag and In over the tetrahedral cation sites of a zincblende selenium lattice.
note: No reference block was returned for this host. Confidence is medium rather than high for a structural reason the composition makes plain: AgInZnSe2 as written puts a whole zinc atom into a formula that already has its cation sites filled by Ag and In, which is why the paper is about where the Zn actually goes. At that level it can order into a distinct stannite or defect-chalcopyrite arrangement rather than simply substituting, and the second composition Ag0.9In0.9Zn0.2Se2 is the more physical reading of the same idea. stannite_kesterite and defect_chalcopyrite_ovc are both in the taxonomy and stage 2 should check the paper before settling on the plain chalcopyrite.
annotator_note: Zn is above the 5 at.% split so it carries no dopant_roles entry, but the whole point of the paper is its site occupation, which stage 2 can fill in as a Wyckoff assignment.

basis: Both compositions are written as (Pr0.67Sr0.33MnO3)1-y(Ag2O)y at y = 0.2 and 0.3, from a paper on near-room-temperature magnetotransport and magnetocaloric behaviour. The bracket notation is a composite: a Pr-Sr manganite perovskite with 20 to 30 mol% silver oxide added as a separate phase, not a quinary compound. Silver does not enter the perovskite lattice in any of its three sites at that level.
note: is_mixed stays false and the two constituents go in alt_prototype_ids, following the Bi-C-Te precedent: every composition contains both phases so there is nothing for a composition-level split to separate. The matrix is the Pr1-xSrxMnO3 perovskite, orthorhombic or rhombohedral depending on the Sr content, and the additive is Ag2O in the cuprite structure. In practice Ag2O decomposes to metallic silver well below 573 K, so what is in the fired sample is probably Ag metal rather than the oxide; the curator detail says only polycrystalline and no reference block was returned, so that cannot be settled here. Confidence is medium for that reason.
annotator_note: The Al-Ba-La-Mn-O host in this chunk is the same construction with alumina instead of silver oxide.

basis: Ag2Tl2Mo9Se11 and Ag3Tl2Mo15Se19, from two papers on the band structure and transport of these cluster compounds. The first is an exact match to the AxMo9X11 formula the prototype is written for -- a framework of Mo9Se11 bioctahedral clusters with Ag and Tl in the channels -- and the second is the Mo15Se19 hybrid built from alternating Mo6 and Mo9 clusters in the same chemistry.
note: The two compositions are not the same structure: the 9-11 one is the prototype itself, the 15-19 one contains Mo6 clusters as well, which is why chevrel is recorded as an alternative and why confidence is medium rather than high. Both belong to one continuous family of molybdenum chalcogenide cluster compounds and the papers treat them together, so a single host label is defensible, but stage 2 will need separate structures for the two compositions. No reference block was returned for this host. Thallium and silver are both above the 5 at.% split and are framework cations rather than dopants, so no dopant_roles entries are recorded.
annotator_note: Same Mo15Se19 question as the Ag-In-Mo-Se host at rank 1826; both are recorded the same way so v4 review sees them together.

basis: AgMo6Te8 and Ag2Mo6Te8, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of MxMo6Te8 for M = Ag and Cu. The Mo6X8 formula is the Chevrel phase itself: Mo6 octahedral clusters surrounded by eight chalcogen atoms, stacked into a rhombohedral framework with channels that the silver occupies at variable x, which is exactly what varying x from 1 to 2 in this host does.
note: [ref 2] returns Ag(TeMo)6 C2/m mp-29607 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, which is the AgMo6Te8 composition. I record the mp_id from the ref line but flag the space group: Chevrel phases are normally described in R-3, and C2/m here is the monoclinic distortion that the ternary Chevrels take at low temperature or at certain cation fillings. So the reference supports the compound and the prototype while describing a lower-symmetry setting than the family name implies, and stage 2 should decide which setting belongs to which x. Silver is a channel cation at x = 1 and 2, above the 5 at.% split, so it carries no dopant_roles entry even though varying it is the carrier-concentration knob for this family.

basis: Both compositions are written as (Nb2O5)1-y(Ag)y at y = 0.32 and 0.37 by mole, from a paper titled niobium(V) oxide with added silver as a thermoelectric material. Silver is added as a metal to an Nb2O5 matrix to make it conduct, not reacted into a silver niobate: per formula there are about four niobium atoms for every silver, so there is far too much Nb2O5 for a 1:1 compound.
note: I disagree with [ref 2] and record it. Materials Project ranks NbAgO3 Pbcm mp-5537 first on 12 ICSD references -- by far the strongest reference in this host -- and that is a real and well-studied compound, silver niobate. But it is not what these compositions describe. AgNbO3 needs Ag:Nb = 1:1 and the measured samples are at 1:4, so at most a quarter of the niobium could be in that phase and the rest has to be Nb2O5. The reference is describing what exists in the Ag-Nb-O chemistry, not what this paper made, which is the failure mode the chunk header warns about. The matrix prototype is recorded as an alternative so stage 2 resolves the Nb2O5 block-shear structure, and no mp_id is taken.
annotator_note: If stage 2 finds the paper reports AgNbO3 formation on firing, this record should be revisited -- the ratio makes a pure-AgNbO3 reading impossible but a three-phase mixture including some of it is plausible.

basis: One composition, AgNiO2, from a paper on the electrical properties of polycrystalline delafossite-type AgNiO2. The ABO2 formula with a linearly coordinated noble metal on the A site is the delafossite structure: layers of edge-sharing NiO6 octahedra separated by silver in two-fold O-Ag-O coordination, which is what gives these oxides their unusual in-plane metallic conduction.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] gives NiAgO2 P6_3/mmc mp-19284 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, marked PRIMARY and AMBIGUOUS. That is the 2H delafossite polytype, the hexagonal stacking variant of the same layer. AgNiO2 is in fact known in both a rhombohedral 3R and a hexagonal 2H form, so this is a real polytype rather than an artefact; it is recorded here because which one a given sintered pellet contains cannot be read off the composition.

note: [ref 2] supports the assignment with its strongest entry: Ni(AgO)2 R-3m mp-19405 on 14 ICSD references, the 3R delafossite stacking, and that mp_id is taken from the ref line. Note that the chunk file ranks it below the 2H entry on hull -- 0.043 against 0.000 -- while the ICSD counts run 14 against 1 the other way. The chunk header says explicitly that reference count and not hull decides the primary, and the 14-reference entry is the one recorded. The paper title states the structure, so this is as well supported as a stage 1 assignment gets, though experimentally_confirmed stays false because the title is not the same as reading the diffraction.

basis: One composition, TmAgTe2, from a paper on the computational and experimental investigation of TmAgTe2 and XYZ2 compounds. It is a layered rare-earth silver ditelluride: Tm and Ag on separate cation positions in a tellurium framework, with the silver tetrahedrally coordinated, and it was studied as a low thermal conductivity candidate.
note: Confidence is low because the references cannot separate two candidate structures. [ref 2] gives TmAgTe2 P-42_1m mp-1078600 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY and TmAgTe2 P-3m1 mp-12953 at hull 0.015 on 1 ICSD reference right behind it, plus a computed P3m1 cell at hull 0.024. One reference each is not enough to choose, and tetragonal against trigonal is not a minor distortion -- they are different layer stackings. So no mp_id is recorded and the proposed prototype names both candidate space groups rather than asserting one. The paper includes a structure refinement, so stage 2 can settle it by reading rather than by guessing.
annotator_note: New prototype ragte2_layered proposed before use, written for the RAgTe2 family since the paper screens many XYZ2 compounds and more are likely in later chunks.

basis: One composition, K3Ba3Li2Al4B6O20F, single crystals, from a paper on the physical properties of this nonlinear optical crystal. It is a layered fluoroaluminoborate: planar BO3 groups and AlO4 tetrahedra condensed into anionic layers with the fluoride on its own site and the alkali and alkaline-earth cations between, in the non-centrosymmetric hexagonal setting that makes it an NLO material.

dopant_roles.basis: The fluorine is a structural anion on its own crystallographic site in the formula K3Ba3Li2Al4B6O20F, not an impurity or a residue. It falls below the 5 at.% split only because the formula unit has 38 atoms, so the split flags it as a dopant candidate when it is part of the compound. non_stoichiometry is the least wrong role available -- the vocabulary has no term for a minority structural anion -- and the honest answer is that no doping role applies.

note: [ref 2] gives K3Ba3Li2Al4B6O20F P-62c mp-1195057 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, an exact formula match, and that mp_id is taken from the ref line. One ICSD reference would normally be weak, but the entry is the compound itself rather than a neighbour and the paper is a single-crystal study, so the space group is well supported. Confidence is medium only because this is a designed optical crystal with no family behind it in this dataset and nothing corroborates the structure independently.
annotator_note: New prototype k3ba3li2al4b6o20f_borate proposed before use. It is deliberately narrow; this really is a one-off in this dataset.

basis: Both compositions are written as (CoFeB)x(NbAlO3)1-x near the percolation threshold, from a chapter on magnetic metal and nonstoichiometric oxide nanocomposites. That is a granular film: amorphous CoFeB metal particles embedded in an oxide matrix, with the bracket notation giving the volume split. There is no single crystal structure here, and the composition is a mixing ratio rather than a stoichiometry.
note: The README lists composite_multiphase among the prototypes that stage 2 skips, and that is right here: neither constituent has a resolvable MP entry. CoFeB is the amorphous soft-magnetic alloy, recorded as the alternative, and the oxide is explicitly nonstoichiometric in the source title so it is not a niobate or aluminate line compound either. No reference block was returned for this host, which is what one expects for a material that has no periodic structure to look up. The 44 and 48 percent metal fractions bracket the percolation threshold, which is what the transport measurement is about.

basis: Both compositions are written as (CoFeB)x(AlO1.5)1-x at 49 and 53 percent metal, from the same chapter on magnetic metal and nonstoichiometric oxide nanocomposites as the niobium-containing host above. Same construction: amorphous CoFeB granules in an alumina matrix, with the bracket giving a mixing ratio rather than a formula.
note: AlO1.5 is alumina written per aluminium atom, and in a sputtered granular film it is amorphous rather than corundum, so corundum is deliberately not recorded as an alternative. No reference block was returned for this host. Both compositions sit right at the percolation threshold, which is where the resistivity and thermopower of a granular metal change character, so the transport being measured is a composite property and not a property of either constituent.

basis: One composition, TmAlB4. The RMB4 borides are built from planar boron sheets of fused five- and seven-membered rings alternating with mixed rare-earth and aluminium layers, and TmAlB4 is one of the compounds where both the alpha form in Pbam and the beta form in Cmmm are known. The reference gives Pbam, which is the alpha or YCrB4 arrangement, and nothing in the source names a polymorph, so that is the one recorded.
note: [ref 2] gives TmAlB4 Pbam mp-1191390 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, an exact formula match, and that mp_id is taken from the ref line. Confidence is medium because one reference cannot rule out the beta polymorph, which is recorded as an alternative -- the Al-B-Yb host in this same chunk is the case where the paper does name beta. There is also a bibliographic oddity worth flagging: the linked paper is titled thermal conductivity of PrRh4.8B2, a layered boride compound, which does not obviously contain TmAlB4. The measured range is a single point at 300 K, which fits a table of room-temperature values for several borides in one paper.
annotator_note: Stage 2 should check that the TmAlB4 samples really come from the linked paper before relying on it for the structure.

basis: One composition, YAlB14, from a paper on the microstructure and thermoelectric properties of YxAlyB14 samples. The MB14 stoichiometry is the MgAlB14 structure: a framework of B12 icosahedra with isolated boron atoms between them and the two metals in partially occupied interstitial sites, which is why the paper writes the metal content as variable x and y.
note: No reference block was returned for this host, but the stoichiometry is decisive on its own: 14 borons per metal pair is the icosahedral MgAlB14 framework and nothing else, and it is a different structure entirely from the RMB4 borides in the two neighbouring hosts despite sharing the elements. The partial metal occupancy is intrinsic to this structure type rather than a defect, which is why the paper varies x and y; stage 3 should treat the metal fractions as a compositional variable and not as doping.

basis: One composition, YbAlB4, single crystals, from the paper reporting the thermoelectric response near a quantum critical point of beta-YbAlB4. The title names the polymorph: beta-YbAlB4 is the ThMoB4 arrangement in Cmmm, and it is the beta form specifically that is the heavy-fermion superconductor with the zero-field quantum critical point the paper measures. alpha-YbAlB4 is a different compound with a different ground state.

other_polymorphs.note: alpha-YbAlB4, which [ref 2] ranks first on 4 ICSD references. It is a genuine ambient-pressure compound rather than a metastable or high-pressure phase -- the two polymorphs are grown from the same flux and separated afterwards -- so the occurrence is unknown rather than metastable. It is not what this paper measured.

note: This is a case where I follow the paper against the reference and record the disagreement. [ref 2] ranks YbAlB4 Pbam mp-1191244 as PRIMARY on 4 ICSD references, which is the alpha form, and puts YbAlB4 Cmmm mp-1095659 on 2 references below it. ICSD counts say which polymorph has been deposited more often, not which one this paper grew, and the title says beta. The Cmmm mp_id is taken from the ref line for the beta phase and the Pbam one is recorded as the other polymorph. [ref 2] also returns YbAlB14 Imma mp-1198572 on 2 references, which is the icosahedral boride of the Al-B-Y host in this chunk, at a different composition. No measured range line appears for this host at all.
annotator_note: New prototype thmob4_type proposed before use, specifically so the alpha and beta forms can be told apart rather than both filed under ycrb4_type.

basis: Ba6Dy2Al4O15 and Ba2Dy2Al4O15, from a paper on the thermophysical properties of rare-earth barium aluminates measured as candidate thermal barrier materials. These are complex quaternary aluminates with no structure type I can identify from the composition, and the two differ by a factor of three in barium content, so they are not even the same compound.
note: [ref 2] returns Ba6Dy2Al4O15 in P2/c mp-1214541 at hull 0.000 and in Amm2 mp-1228068 at hull 0.034, both exact formula matches for the first composition, but neither carries an ICSD reference count in the chunk file -- these are computed entries, not measured structures. No mp_id is taken, because a computed cell is not evidence of what the sintered pellet is, and the second composition Ba2Dy2Al4O15 has no entry at all. is_mixed is true because the two compositions cannot be the same structure at that barium ratio. Assigning any named prototype here would be inventing one, so this goes to unresolved_crystalline, which is what that entry is for.
annotator_note: The Al-Ba-Er-O host at rank 1841 is the same paper and the same problem.

basis: Ba6Er2Al4O15 and Ba2ErAlO5, from the same paper on the thermophysical properties of rare-earth barium aluminates as the dysprosium host above. Two different quaternary aluminates with no identifiable structure type from composition alone, and at 3:1:2 against 2:1:1 metal ratios they are clearly different compounds rather than one phase.
note: No reference block was returned for this host at all -- not even the computed entries the dysprosium analogue got -- so there is nothing to check against. is_mixed is true for the same reason as the Dy host: two compositions at incompatible metal ratios cannot share a structure. Ba2ErAlO5 has the stoichiometry of the Ba2LnMO5 family, which is a real family, but I could not place it to a specific structure type with enough confidence to name one, and guessing would be worse than recording it as unresolved.
annotator_note: These two rare-earth barium aluminate hosts are good candidates for the review queue: one paper would settle both.

basis: One composition, K9Ba15Al31Ga8Sn97, from a paper on the preparation and thermoelectric properties of sintered type-II clathrates. The framework atoms total 136 per formula unit and the guests 24, which is exactly the A8B16E136 guest count of the type-II clathrate cell -- a tetrahedral tin framework of fused 20- and 28-vertex cages with the potassium in the small cages and the barium in the large ones.
note: The 136-atom framework count is what decides this against type I, whose cell holds 46 framework atoms and 8 guests; the paper title confirms it independently. Al and Ga are both above the 5 at.% split so they carry no dopant_roles entries, but structurally they are framework substituents on the tin sites, setting the electron count that balances the 24 guest cations -- the same role Ga and Al play in Ba8Ga16Ge30 and the reason this composition has that particular Al:Ga:Sn ratio. No reference block was returned for this host, which is unsurprising for a five-element clathrate with a 160-atom cell. The second paper predicts ground-state configurations for these frameworks, which is about how the Al and Ga order on the framework sites.
annotator_note: The README records that v0.2 corrected a clathrate type misassignment for Ba-Ga-Sn; the framework atom count is the check that catches those, and it is clean here.

basis: Both compositions are written as (La0.7Ba0.3MnO3)1-y(Al2O3)y at y = 0.125 and 0.15, from a paper on the impact of aluminium on the Seebeck coefficient and magnetic properties. The bracket notation is a composite: a La-Ba manganite perovskite with alumina added as a separate phase. Al3+ does not dissolve into the Mn site of a manganite at that level, and the paper treats the alumina as an addition rather than a substituent.
note: Same construction and same treatment as the Ag-Mn-O-Pr-Sr host at rank 1828: is_mixed stays false because every composition contains both phases and there is nothing for a composition-level split to separate, and the two constituents go in alt_prototype_ids so stage 2 resolves the La0.7Ba0.3MnO3 perovskite and alpha-Al2O3 corundum separately. No reference block was returned. Confidence is medium because the paper title asks what aluminium does, which leaves open that some of it enters the lattice; the 85-286 K measured window is the manganite metal-insulator and magnetic transition region, so the transport is dominated by the perovskite either way.

basis: Ti2AlC0.5N0.5 and Ti3AlCN, from a paper on the electronic and thermal properties of Ti3Al(C0.5,N0.5)2. Both are MAX phases: the 211 and 312 members of the Mn+1AXn series, with hexagonal Ti-C or Ti-N octahedral slabs interleaved by single aluminium layers, and the carbon and nitrogen sharing the X site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: X site of the MAX layer
solid_solution_axis.note: C and N share the octahedral X site between the titanium layers. Both compositions sit at the fifty-fifty carbonitride point, which is the composition the paper is about; this is an alloying axis on the X sublattice, not doping, and note that C and N are not isoelectronic so it changes the electron count as well as the mass.

note: n = 1 and n = 2 members of the same series appear here, which is a structural difference -- one titanium layer more between the aluminium sheets -- but not a different prototype, so is_mixed stays false. [ref 2] returns Ti4Al2CN P-3m1 mp-1217141 and Ti8Al4CN3 P-3m1 mp-1217099, both at low hull but with no ICSD reference counts shown. Those are doubled-cell computed representations of ordered C and N arrangements in the 211 and 312 phases respectively, so they corroborate the assignment without being measured structures, and no mp_id is taken. The Al-C-Ti host at rank 1846 is the pure-carbide version of the same two phases and does have ICSD-backed entries.

basis: Zr2(Al3.56Si0.44)4C5 and Zr3(Al3.56Si0.44)4C6, which the curator transcribes from the paper as Zr2[Al(Si)]4C5 and Zr3[Al(Si)]4C6. These are the n = 2 and n = 3 members of the ZrC and Al3C2 intergrowth series: rocksalt ZrC slabs of increasing thickness alternating with aluminium carbide blocks, with silicon substituting for part of the aluminium.
note: The two compositions are different members of one homologous series rather than different structures, which is what the prototype is written for, so is_mixed stays false and stage 2 should resolve each member separately. Silicon sits at about 8 at.% overall, above the 5 percent split, so it is a host element with no dopant_roles entry; structurally it substitutes for aluminium in the carbide block, which is the reason the paper uses it -- it stabilises these phases. No reference block was returned for this host. Confidence is medium because the ZrC and Al3C2 intergrowth family has several closely spaced members and the exact stacking of a 2-4-5 against a 3-4-6 is not something the composition alone confirms.

basis: Ti3AlC2 and Ti2AlC, from the same paper as the carbonitride host at rank 1844. These are the two best-known MAX phases: hexagonal P6_3/mmc structures of edge-sharing Ti6C octahedra, two layers thick in the 312 phase and one in the 211, separated by single aluminium sheets.
note: [ref 2] supports both compositions with ICSD-backed entries: Ti2AlC P6_3/mmc mp-12990 at hull 0.000 on 8 references and Ti3AlC2 P6_3/mmc mp-3747 at hull 0.000 on 4, both at the MAX phase space group. mp-12990 is recorded on the phase for the 211 member and mp-3747 belongs to the 312 member; stage 2 should attach one per composition, since a single host-level mp_id cannot cover both. Both mp_ids are taken from the ref line. The other entries, Ti3AlC Pm-3m mp-3271 on 8 references and Ti5Al2C3 R-3m mp-1079706, are the antiperovskite carbide and a higher-order intergrowth respectively -- real compounds in this chemistry but not the compositions measured here.
annotator_note: determined_at could reasonably read composition here, since the 211 and 312 members take different mp_ids even though they share a prototype.

basis: CaAl2 and CaAl4, one sample each and one paper each. CaAl2 is the cubic MgCu2 Laves phase, the C15 arrangement of corner-sharing Al tetrahedra around a diamond lattice of calcium. CaAl4 is a different structure entirely -- the body-centred tetragonal BaAl4 type -- and the second paper, on Fermi surfaces and the charge density wave in SrAl4 and related compounds, is about that family.
note: is_mixed is true and this host splits cleanly on the Al:Ca ratio: 2 goes to laves_phase, 4 to baal4_type. [ref 2] backs both -- CaAl2 Fd-3m mp-2404 at hull 0.000 on 5 ICSD references, which is the C15 Laves space group, and CaAl4 I4/mmm mp-1749 at hull 0.012 on 2 references, which is the BaAl4 space group -- and stage 2 should attach mp-2404 and mp-1749 to their respective compositions rather than one to the host. Both mp_ids are taken from the ref line. The remaining entries it returns, Ca4Al and Ca2Al25Cr at hulls of 0.46 and 0.50, are computed cells far off the hull and should be ignored.
annotator_note: Confidence is high for each composition individually; the host label is the thing that cannot stand alone, which is what is_mixed records.

basis: Ca5AlInSb6 and Ca5Al0.95In0.95Zn0.1Sb6, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of the Ca5Al2-xInxSb6 solid solution. The 5-2-6 stoichiometry is the Ca5Al2Sb6 Zintl phase: infinite chains of corner-sharing AlSb4 tetrahedra with Sb-Sb bonds linking them into ladders, charge balanced by Ca2+, and Al and In share the tetrahedral site across the series.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca5Al0.95In0.95Zn0.1Sb6: Zn takes the tetrahedral site shared by Al and In. Zn2+ is one valence electron short of the trivalent Al and In it replaces, so it is an acceptor -- the standard way this Zintl family is p-type doped, since the compounds are valence-precise semiconductors and need a site substitution to make carriers. At 5 percent of the tetrahedral site it is genuine dilute doping.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral pnictide-bonded site
solid_solution_axis.note: Al and In are both group 13 and share the tetrahedral site of the Zintl framework. Only the fifty-fifty point of the Ca5Al2-xInxSb6 series appears in this host, so both compositions are the x = 1 member.

note: No reference block was returned for this host, but the 5-2-6 stoichiometry and the paper title together are decisive -- the title names the solid solution explicitly. This is one of the cleaner assignments in the chunk despite having no reference support.

basis: Ca9Zn4.5Al3Sb9 and a second composition from a paper on tuning the thermoelectric properties of Ca9Zn4+xSb9 by controlled doping. The 9-4-9 stoichiometry is the Ca9Zn4Sb9 Zintl phase, a framework of ZnSb4 tetrahedra and Sb-Sb dimers with an interstitial site whose partial occupancy is the x in the title, and aluminium substitutes on the tetrahedral site here.
note: The second composition string, Ca9Zn4Al20.33Sb9, is not physical: 20.33 aluminium atoms against 9 calcium and 9 antimony would not be a 9-4-9 phase at all, and nothing in a paper on Ca9Zn4+xSb9 would have that formula. It is almost certainly a parse failure on something like Al0.33 or Al2O3-free notation, and it should be flagged upstream rather than used. The assignment follows the first composition, Ca9Zn4.5Al3Sb9, and the paper title. Al is above the 5 at.% split so it carries no dopant_roles entry; structurally it is a trivalent substituent on the divalent Zn tetrahedral site, which is a donor and is the controlled doping the title refers to. No reference block was returned for this host. Confidence is medium because of the broken composition string, not because the family is in doubt.
annotator_note: The malformed Al20.33 stoichiometry will produce a nonsense doping level in stage 3 if taken at face value.

basis: One composition, Ce2Ir3Al9, polycrystalline, across two papers on the transport and magnetic properties of the new ternary Ce2T3X9 compounds and on the ground-state properties of Ce2Ir3Al9. The 2-3-9 stoichiometry in this chemistry is the orthorhombic Y2Co3Ga9 structure type, and the Ce2T3Al9 series is the family the first paper introduces.
note: [ref 2] gives Ce2(Al3Ir)3 Cmcm mp-1213885 at hull 0.000 as PRIMARY, which is the 2-3-9 composition at the Y2Co3Ga9 space group, so the reference and the structural reading agree and that mp_id is taken from the ref line. It carries no ICSD reference count in the chunk file, though, so it is a computed entry rather than a measured one, which is why confidence is medium. The other entries, CeAlIr Pnma mp-1102352 on 2 ICSD references and CeAlIr P6_3/mmc mp-1077038 on 1, are the equiatomic 1-1-1 compound of the same chemistry and not what was measured. Measured window 10-294 K.
annotator_note: y2co3ga9_type was proposed in an earlier chunk and is still pending; this is a second host using it.

basis: Ce2Rh3Al9, from the same two-paper series on the new ternary Ce2T3X9 compounds that produced Ce2Ir3Al9 in the previous chunk. The 2-3-9 stoichiometry in the R-T-Al chemistry is the orthorhombic Y2Co3Ga9 structure type, and [ref 2] returns Ce2(Al3Rh)3 Cmcm (63) mp-1213916 at hull 0.000, which is that composition at that space group.
note: The second composition string, Ce2Rh2Al9, is almost certainly a transcription slip for Ce2Rh3Al9: the papers are titled for the Ce2T3X9 family, the 2-2-9 stoichiometry is not a member of it, and the two samples come from the same pair of papers. The assignment follows the 2-3-9 reading. The other reference entry, CeAlRh Pnma mp-3344 on 2 ICSD references, is the equiatomic 1-1-1 compound of the same chemistry and is not what was measured. mp-1213916 carries no ICSD count, so it is a computed entry, but it agrees with the structural reading rather than being the only thing supporting it. Measured window 10-297 K.
annotator_note: Third host now using the pending y2co3ga9_type entry; Al-Ce-Ir in chunk 037 was the second. The entry is earning its place.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [63], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: (ZrO2)77.66(NiCoCrAlY)22.34 and (ZrO2)60.7(NiCoCrAlY)39.3, from a paper on the thermomechanical properties of functionally graded materials. These are thermal barrier coating compositions: yttria-stabilised zirconia mixed with a NiCoCrAlY metallic bond-coat alloy in two volume ratios. There is no single crystal structure here -- a cubic or tetragonal fluorite oxide and an fcc/B2 metal alloy coexist as separate phases by design.
note: The composition string itself states the two-phase design, giving the oxide and the metal as separate bracketed units with volume fractions, so this is not an inference. The alternatives record which prototype each constituent would take if stage 2 ever needs them: fluorite_oxide for the yttria-stabilised zirconia and solid_solution_alloy for the NiCoCrAlY. No reference block was returned, which is expected for a seven-element functionally graded material. Measured window 302-408 K.

basis: Co2FeAl and Fe2CoAl, from papers on ternary full-Heusler alloys and on melt-spun Fe2XAl ribbons. Co2FeAl is the well-established L21 full Heusler, Fm-3m, and [ref 2] returns AlFeCo2 Fm-3m mp-10884 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY.
note: The host is flagged mixed because the two compositions are different compounds, not two spellings of one. Co2FeAl is X2YZ with the higher-valence element doubled, which gives the regular L21 arrangement. Fe2CoAl doubles the LOWER-valence element, and the standard site-preference rule for X2YZ Heuslers says that when the atomic number of X is smaller than that of Y the compound takes the inverse XA arrangement, F-43m, not L21. That is why inverse_heusler is recorded rather than folding both into one label. This is a disagreement with [ref 2], which offers no F-43m entry for the 2-1-1 composition at all and ranks only Fm-3m structures; the reference lists what has been deposited, and the inverse ordering in Fe2CoAl is frequently partial or disordered in melt-spun material, so its absence is not evidence against it. The other two reference entries, Al2FeCo Fm-3m mp-862691 and Al2FeCo P4/mmm mp-1228905, are the aluminium-doubled composition and are neither of the measured compounds. Confidence is medium for the host label for that reason, high for the Co2FeAl half alone. Measured window 301-1014 K.
annotator_note: Stage 2 should split this host by composition: Co2FeAl to full_heusler, Fe2CoAl to inverse_heusler. The Co:Fe ratio separates them cleanly.

basis: PrCo2Al8 and Pr2Co6Al19, the two compounds of a single 2005 paper titled for exactly those two formulae. The 1-2-8 stoichiometry in the R-Co-Al chemistry is the orthorhombic CaCo2Al8 type, Pbam, a channel framework of aluminium and cobalt with the rare earth threaded through it.
note: Genuinely mixed at one sample each, with no basis for calling either dominant. PrCo2Al8 goes to the existing caco2al8_pbam entry; Pr2Co6Al19 needed a new one, proposed in this chunk as r2t6al19_type. Read the proposal before trusting its space group -- it is recorded as C2/m and is NOT confirmed. [ref 2] does not help here: it returns Pr7Al7Co6 P4/mbm mp-5711, Pr2AlCo2 C2/m mp-11928, Pr2Al3Co14 R-3m mp-1106291, Pr2Al2Co15 R-3m mp-1188126 and PrAl4Co Pmma mp-975726, and not one of them is either measured stoichiometry. That is a reference disagreement in the weak sense -- the snapshot simply does not contain these two compounds -- rather than a contradiction. No mp_id is recorded for either phase because none of the returned entries is the right composition. Measured window 12-299 K.
annotator_note: The paper is a crystal-structure determination of both compounds, so stage 2 can confirm the space groups by reading it, and should correct the proposed r2t6al19_type entry if C2/m is wrong.

basis: Al65Co22Ru13_IQC and Al65Co21Ru14_IQC, from a paper on modelling the electrical conductivity of icosahedral quasicrystals. The IQC suffix is the curator recording that these are icosahedral quasicrystals, and the Al-Co-Ru composition near Al65 is a known stable icosahedral phase. There is no periodic unit cell to assign.
note: This is a disagreement with [ref 2], and a straightforward one. The reference returns Al2CoRu Fm-3m mp-862695 at hull 0.000 and Al2CoRu P4/mmm mp-1228908, which are Heusler-type periodic intermetallics at a 2-1-1 stoichiometry. The measured material is at Al65Co22Ru13, is explicitly icosahedral, and is not that compound. Following the reference here would have silently turned a quasicrystal into a Heusler alloy. No mp_id is recorded. As the taxonomy notes for this prototype say, stage 2 must map this to a rational approximant and state that it has done so, rather than claim a structure. Measured window 13-298 K.

basis: SmCr2Al20, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of the SmT2Al20 series, is the CeCr2Al20 cage aluminide: cubic Fd-3m, a chromium-aluminium framework with the rare earth inside a sixteen-atom Frank-Kasper aluminium cage. [ref 2] supports the type directly with Ce(Al10Cr)2 Fd-3m mp-3910 on 4 ICSD references, Gd(Al10Cr)2 mp-658303 on 3 and La(Al10Cr)2 mp-1200867 on 3 -- the same 1-2-20 structure with three different rare earths.

dopant_roles.basis: Samarium is one atom in twenty-three in SmCr2Al20, which puts it at 4.3 at.% and below the 5 per cent split, so the pipeline lists it as a dopant candidate. It is not a dopant. It is the guest of the cage compound -- the rattling rare earth inside the Al16 Frank-Kasper polyhedron that the whole structure is built around and that the paper is measuring. Remove it and there is no SmCr2Al20.

note: The host holds two unrelated materials at one sample each. SmCr2Al20 is the cage compound above. Al0.062Cr is something else entirely: 6.2 at.% aluminium dissolved in body-centred cubic chromium, from a 1973 paper on antiferromagnetism and electrical transport in chromium-aluminium, where the point is the effect of aluminium on the chromium spin-density wave. That is a dilute bcc substitutional solid solution, hence solid_solution_alloy as the alternative. The reference entry AlCr2 I4/mmm mp-1699 on 3 ICSD references is the ordered intermetallic and is not the dilute alloy; Al8Cr5 R3m mp-19954 is a different intermetallic again. Neither is what either sample is. No mp_id is recorded because the reference block returns no SmCr2Al20 entry -- only the Ce, Gd and La analogues -- and the dilute chromium alloy has no entry by nature. Measured window 14-296 K.
annotator_note: Stage 2 must split this host by composition; the two materials share only the element set. The Sm-containing composition is the cage compound, the binary is the dilute alloy.

basis: Al32Cr12.5Mn31.5Si34 and Al32Cr12Mn32Si34, from a paper titled for the electronic structure and thermoelectric properties of Si2Ti-type Al-(Mn,Cr)-Si alloys. Si2Ti-type is the C54 TiSi2 structure, Fddd, and the stoichiometry fits it: the transition metals total about 44 per cent against 66 per cent aluminium plus silicon, which is the 1:2 ratio of TM(Al,Si)2 with aluminium and silicon sharing the silicon sublattice.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal site of the C54 structure
solid_solution_axis.note: Chromium and manganese share the titanium site of the TiSi2 type. Both compositions sit at essentially the same point, Cr/(Cr+Mn) near 0.28, so this is one alloy measured twice rather than a series. Aluminium and silicon likewise share the silicon sublattice at close to 1:1, which is the second substitution axis in this material and the one the electron count depends on.

note: The paper title names the structure type outright, which is why this is high confidence despite no reference block being returned for the host. Neither [ref 1] nor [ref 2] covers a four-element Al-Cr-Mn-Si composition. Measured window 12-584 K.

basis: One composition, Ni37.04Cr29.35Al17.14Si16.47, two samples, from a paper on fabricating NiCr-based films with high resistivity. This is a thin-film resistor alloy, not a line compound: the stoichiometry is a rounded weight-ratio target rather than a formula, and nickel-chromium with aluminium and silicon additions is a classic disordered resistive film composition.
note: Confidence is low and the alternative is the reason. High resistivity in a NiCr-based film is usually achieved precisely by suppressing crystallinity -- silicon and aluminium are added to make the film amorphous or nanocrystalline, since an ordered metallic film would not be resistive enough to be useful. So amorphous is a live possibility rather than a formality, and the record should not be read as asserting a crystalline solid solution. No reference block was returned for this host, and none would settle it. Measured window 291-723 K.
annotator_note: Settling this needs the paper, which will report whether the as-deposited film is amorphous and whether it was annealed. It is a good candidate for the review queue.

basis: CuAl0.8Fe0.2O2, two samples across two papers on CuAlO2. CuAlO2 is the archetypal p-type transparent conducting delafossite, R-3m, with linear O-Cu-O dumbbells between edge-sharing AlO6 octahedral layers, and iron substitutes on the trivalent aluminium site.
note: Iron sits at 5 per cent of the formula and so is counted as a host element rather than a dopant candidate; structurally it is a substituent on the aluminium site, isovalent as Fe3+ and aliovalent if any of it is Fe2+. Worth a flag for stage 2: the second paper is titled for improving the thermoelectric properties of CuAlO2 by ADDING Fe2O3, which is an additive route rather than a solid solution, so some of these samples may be two-phase delafossite plus hematite even though the composition string reads as a single substituted phase. The first paper is a mechanical-milling study of CuAl1-xFexO2, which is a genuine solid solution. No reference block was returned for this host. Measured window 290-1141 K.
annotator_note: Whether the iron is dissolved or present as a second phase differs between the two papers behind this host and cannot be settled from the composition string.

basis: One composition, LaCu4Al, two samples, from papers on the thermopower of Ce1-xLaxCu4Al and on the CeCu4Al Kondo lattice. The RCu5-xAlx series is built on the hexagonal CaCu5 structure, P6/mmm, and at x = 1 the compound is still CaCu5-type with aluminium showing a strong preference for the 3g copper site rather than distributing at random.
note: The alternative is not a different structure but a different degree of order in the same one: prni2al3_ordered_cacu5 is the fully site-ordered CaCu5 derivative, which is what LaCu4Al would become if all the aluminium took the 3g site. At one aluminium in five the ordering is partial, so the parent entry is the safer label and the ordered variant is recorded alongside it. This is a reference disagreement of the absent-evidence kind. [ref 2] returns LaAl3Cu I4mm mp-1070573, La2Al3Cu7 P2/m mp-1223301, La(Al5Cu)2 Fmmm mp-1223260, La2Al7Cu P4mm mp-1223239 and a gold-containing quaternary, none at the 1-4-1 stoichiometry and all but the first with no ICSD reference at all. The 2019 snapshot simply does not contain LaCu4Al, so no mp_id is recorded and confidence is held at medium. Measured window 12-298 K.
annotator_note: Both papers are about the cerium end member; lanthanum is the non-magnetic reference compound. They will report the structure of the series.

basis: (Ni0.47Cu0.53)(Al2O3)0.038 and (Ni0.47Cu0.53)(Al2O3)0.07, with curator composition details reading 20vol.%Al2O3 and 30vol.%Al2O3, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of constantan with spherical silica and alumina particles dispersed in it. The Ni0.47Cu0.53 is constantan, an fcc copper-nickel solid solution; the alumina is an inert dispersed second phase added as particles.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: fcc metal site of the constantan matrix
solid_solution_axis.note: Copper and nickel are fully miscible in the fcc lattice and both compositions sit at the same 47:53 constantan point, so this is a fixed alloy rather than a series. The variable in this host is the alumina volume fraction, not the metal ratio.

note: The curator details settle this outright: the paper adds alumina as spherical particles at 20 and 30 volume per cent, which is a particulate composite and not a solid solution. The alternatives name the two constituents -- solid_solution_alloy for the constantan matrix, corundum for the alpha-Al2O3 particles. No reference block was returned for this host, which is what one expects for a composite. Measured window 297-1076 K.

basis: Al64.5Si7.5Cu6Ru22_IAC_1_0 and Al62.5Si8.0Cu8.4Ru21.1_IAC_1_0, from a paper on the effects of copper doping on the thermoelectric properties of the Al-Si-Ru semiconductor. The IAC_1_0 suffix is the curator writing the icosahedral approximant crystal designation and its 1/0 order into the composition string, and Al-Si-Ru near Al65Ru20 is the well-known semiconducting 1/1 approximant family.
note: No reference block was returned for this host, and none would be useful: approximant cells of this size are not in the 2019 Materials Project snapshot under a four-element composition like this. This is the prototype the taxonomy flags for special handling in stage 2 -- there is a periodic cell here, unlike a true quasicrystal, but it is a large cluster-based one and must be resolved by reading the paper rather than by formula lookup. Note that copper here is a framework substituent tuning the electron-per-atom ratio, which is what the Hume-Rothery gap in these semiconducting approximants depends on; it is above the 5 per cent split so it carries no dopant_roles entry. Measured window 300-801 K.

basis: Cu3AlSnS5 and Cu3Al0.75Ga0.25SnS5, from a paper on gallium substitution in Cu3Al1-xGaxSnS5 nanobulk materials. The formula is charge-balanced with five cations to five sulfurs -- three Cu+, one Al3+, one Sn4+ against five S2- -- which is the 1:1 cation-to-anion ratio of a diamond-like adamantane structure, and it decomposes exactly as CuAlS2 plus Cu2SnS3, both chalcopyrite-derived tetragonal sulfides.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu3Al0.75Ga0.25SnS5 is the x = 0.25 member of the series the paper is titled for. Gallium and aluminium are both group 13 and both trivalent, so gallium takes the aluminium tetrahedral site without changing the carrier count; it widens the lattice and shifts the band gap instead. At a quarter of the aluminium site this is substitution along a solid-solution axis, not dilute doping, and it falls below the 5 at.% split only because the aluminium site is itself a fifth of the cations.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: trivalent tetrahedral cation site
solid_solution_axis.note: The paper varies x in Cu3Al1-xGaxSnS5; only x = 0 and x = 0.25 appear in this host. Both are the same structure with a different group 13 cation on the same site.

note: Confidence is low and the disagreement should be read carefully. Which ordered variant of the diamond-like lattice this adopts is not settled by the stoichiometry: a five-cation formula does not map onto either the 1-1-2 chalcopyrite cell or the 2-1-1-4 stannite cell, and nanobulk material of this kind is frequently a cation-disordered cubic sphalerite rather than any ordered superstructure, which is why all three candidates are listed. [ref 2] returns AlCuSnS4 Imma mp-1228961 at hull 0.001, and that is a DIFFERENT stoichiometry -- four sulfurs, not five, and no excess copper -- so it is not the measured compound and no mp_id is recorded from it. Measured window 372-668 K.
annotator_note: Cu3AlSnS5 is best understood as a 1:1 combination of CuAlS2 and Cu2SnS3. Whether the two order into a superstructure or disorder into sphalerite is exactly what stage 2 needs the paper for.

basis: One composition, YbCuAl, two samples, from papers on the two-band model of heavy-fermion compounds and on the thermopower of ytterbium heavy-fermion compounds under pressure. [ref 2] gives YbAlCu P-62m (189) mp-1078543 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references as PRIMARY, and P-62m is the ZrNiAl type, the ordered ternary derivative of Fe2P that equiatomic RTX compounds with a late transition metal characteristically adopt.
note: A clean case: the reference PRIMARY is the exact formula measured, at the space group the chemistry predicts, on three ICSD references. The other entries returned -- Yb(Al2Cu)4 I4/mmm mp-1104848, YbAl2Cu R-3m mp-977428, Yb6Al7Cu16 Fm-3m mp-1193533 and Yb(AlCu)6 Immm mp-1215808 -- are all different stoichiometries in the same chemistry and none is what was measured. Measured window 10-196 K on the robust range, extending to 294 K including outliers.

basis: One composition, Dy8Al16Si30, two samples, from a paper titled for the thermoelectric properties of rare-earth-containing type-I clathrate compounds. The 8-16-30 stoichiometry is the type-I clathrate formula outright: forty-six framework atoms per cell, here sixteen aluminium and thirty silicon, enclosing eight guest cages filled by dysprosium.
note: This is a reference disagreement and the composition wins decisively. [ref 2] returns Dy2Al3Si2 C2/m mp-3513, Dy(AlSi)2 P-3m1 mp-7121, Dy12Al7Si I4/mcm mp-1213130, DyAlSi Cmcm mp-1206330 and DyAlSi I4_1md mp-1225273 -- a set of small dense ternary silicides, not one of them a clathrate and not one of them at the measured stoichiometry. The 8-16-30 formula and the paper title agree with each other and disagree with every entry offered, so no mp_id is recorded. Aluminium is a framework substituent here, setting the electron count of the silicon cage network in the same way gallium does in Ba8Ga16Ge30; it is above the 5 per cent split so it carries no dopant_roles entry. Measured window 322-675 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12, 164]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Y2ErAl5O12 and YEr2Al5O12, the x = 1 and x = 2 members of the Y3-xErxAl5O12 series the paper is titled for. The 3-5-12 stoichiometry is the garnet formula, Ia-3d, and yttrium aluminium garnet with erbium on the dodecahedral yttrium site is one of the best-characterised oxides there is.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: dodecahedral A site of the garnet
solid_solution_axis.note: Erbium and yttrium have nearly identical ionic radii and both are trivalent, so they substitute freely on the dodecahedral site across the whole Y3Al5O12 to Er3Al5O12 range. x here is the erbium share of that site: 1 of 3 and 2 of 3. This is isoelectronic substitution, not doping.

note: Worth noting how [ref 2] presents this, because it looks like a disagreement and is not one. The reference returns Y9Er3Al20O48 C2 (5) mp-1216239 at hull 0.001 as PRIMARY -- that formula is exactly Y2ErAl5O12 multiplied by four, and C2 is a low-symmetry cell describing one particular ordering of yttrium and erbium over the dodecahedral sites. It is a computed ordering of the garnet, not a competing structure, and the real material has those cations disordered in Ia-3d. The second entry, YErAl2O6 Pmc2_1 mp-1215985, is a different stoichiometry. No mp_id is recorded on the record because the ordered cell would misrepresent what was measured. Measured window 298-1074 K on the robust range, to 1273 K including outliers.
annotator_note: An ordered supercell standing in for a disordered solid solution is a recurring trap in the Materials Project entries for rare-earth garnets.

basis: Yb0.5Er0.5Al3 and Yb0.75Er0.25Al3, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of Yb1-x(Er,Lu)xAl3 solid solutions. YbAl3 is the classic intermediate-valence L12 compound: the cubic AuCu3 structure, Pm-3m, with ytterbium at the cube corners and aluminium on the face centres, and erbium substitutes directly on the ytterbium site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth corner site of the L12 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the ytterbium share of the rare-earth site. The two species are not isoelectronic in the strict sense -- the point of the paper is that substituting trivalent erbium dilutes the intermediate-valence ytterbium and changes the electronic state -- but they share one crystallographic site and the structure is unchanged across the series, so the parent compound depends on the composition and is assigned in stage 3.

note: No reference block was returned for this host, which is unsurprising for a ternary rare-earth solid solution. The assignment rests on YbAl3 being a well-known L12 compound and on the paper title stating the series. Measured window 80-300 K.

basis: One composition, EuAl4, two single-crystal samples, from a paper on the transport and magnetic properties of EuAl4 and EuGa4. [ref 2] gives EuAl4 I4/mmm (139) mp-990191 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, and I4/mmm at the 1-4 stoichiometry is the BaAl4 type, the body-centred tetragonal parent of the whole ThCr2Si2 family.
note: The reference block ranks EuAl2 Fd-3m mp-917786 first, also on 5 ICSD references, but that is the cubic Laves phase at a different stoichiometry and is not what was measured; EuAl4 is the next entry and matches the composition exactly. This is a case where the PRIMARY marker is for the host chemistry rather than for the compound, and following it blindly would have produced a Laves phase. Second point for stage 2: EuAl4 undergoes a charge-density-wave transition near 140 K, inside the measured 10-300 K window, and several magnetic transitions below 20 K. The CDW lowers the symmetry without changing the structure type, so it is not recorded as a phase change here, but a reader should know it is there. Measured window 10-300 K.
annotator_note: The charge-density-wave transition at about 140 K is a symmetry change within the BaAl4 type, not a change of prototype, so spans_transition is left false.

basis: Al73Mn5.5Fe12.5Si9 and Al73.6Mn11.9Fe5.5Si9, from papers on the electronic structure and thermoelectric properties of Al-Mn-Fe-Si alloys and on the extremely small thermal conductivity of the aluminium-based Mackay-type icosahedral phase. The second title names the cluster type outright: this is the alpha-AlMnSi Mackay-cluster 1/1 approximant with iron substituting for part of the manganese.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal sites of the Mackay cluster
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the manganese share of the transition metal. The two compositions are near mirror images of each other, 5.5 Mn with 12.5 Fe and 11.9 Mn with 5.5 Fe, which is the point of the first paper -- the electron-per-atom ratio and hence the pseudogap move as iron replaces manganese. Same structure throughout.

note: No reference block was returned for this host; a 1/1 approximant cell with over a hundred atoms and four elements is not something the snapshot indexes by formula. The assignment is from the paper titles and the composition, and it is solid. As with the other approximants in this chunk, stage 2 must resolve this by reading rather than by lookup. Measured window 11-297 K.

basis: Mg0.3Al0.6Li0.35Fe1.75O4, from a paper on thermoelectric power studies of magnesium- and aluminium-substituted lithium ferrites. Lithium ferrite is a spinel, and the AB2O4 stoichiometry is written into the formula: cations summing to three against four oxygens, with lithium, magnesium, aluminium and iron distributed over the tetrahedral and octahedral sites.

dopant_roles.basis: Lithium is a structural cation of the parent compound, not an impurity. The paper is about lithium ferrite, Li0.5Fe2.5O4, where lithium occupies octahedral sites in an ordered arrangement and provides the charge balance that makes all the iron trivalent. At 0.35 per formula unit it is roughly a tenth of the cations and falls below the 5 at.% split only because oxygen dominates the denominator. Calling it a dopant would invert the material.

Magnesium is one of the two substituents the paper is titled for. Mg2+ enters the spinel on the iron sites, distributing between tetrahedral and octahedral coordination, and changes the carrier concentration by altering how much iron is available for the Fe2+/Fe3+ hopping that carries the conduction.

note: The host holds two genuinely different structures at one sample each. The lithium ferrite above is a spinel. The other composition is AlFeO3, from a paper on the influence of Sb3+ cations on the structural, magnetic and electrical properties of that compound, and AlFeO3 is emphatically NOT a perovskite despite the ABO3 formula -- aluminium is far too small for a twelve-coordinate site. It takes the polar orthorhombic GaFeO3 structure, Pna2_1, for which a new taxonomy entry is proposed in this chunk. [ref 2] supports both readings: Al2FeO4 Fd-3m mp-31801 on 3 ICSD references is the hercynite spinel and AlFeO3 Pna2_1 mp-25693 on 1 reference is the second compound. No single mp_id is recorded because the two compositions need different ones. Measured window 200-398 K on the robust range, to 907 K including outliers.
annotator_note: Stage 2 must split this host by composition. The presence or absence of lithium separates them cleanly.

basis: Fe2VAl0.8Sn0.2, from papers on the enhancement of power factor in tin-substituted Fe2VAl Heusler alloys and on the high thermoelectric power factor near room temperature in full-Heusler alloys. Fe2VAl is the archetypal pseudogap full Heusler, L21 with Fm-3m symmetry, and tin substitutes on the aluminium site.
note: The second composition string, FeVAl0.8Sn0.2, reads as a 1:1 iron-to-vanadium ratio, which would be a B2 or half-Heusler arrangement rather than L21. Both papers are about Fe2VAl full Heuslers and both samples come from them, so this is taken as a transcription slip on the iron subscript rather than a second compound, and the host is not flagged mixed on the strength of it. Tin sits at 5 per cent of the formula and is therefore a host element rather than a dopant candidate; structurally it is a tetravalent substituent on the trivalent aluminium site, which is exactly the electron doping the first paper is about. No reference block was returned for this host. Measured window 10-298 K.
annotator_note: If the FeVAl0.8Sn0.2 string is genuine rather than a slip, this host is mixed and needs splitting. The Fe:V ratio would separate the two.

basis: Al0.1In0.1Ga0.8N and Al0.26Ga0.44In0.30N, from papers on erbium-doped AlInGaN alloys as high-temperature thermoelectric materials and on the thermoelectric properties of Al1-xInxN and AlGaInN. The group 13 nitrides all crystallise in the hexagonal wurtzite structure, P6_3mc, and AlN, GaN and InN form a continuous wurtzite solid solution.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral cation site of the wurtzite lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: All three metals are group 13 and share the single cation site; x here is the indium share of it. The alloy is continuous in principle, though indium-rich AlInGaN is prone to phase separation during growth, which is a real concern for the 30 per cent indium composition.

note: The chunk flags film samples in this host, and that matters for once. Zincblende nitrides, F-43m, are metastable in bulk but are routinely stabilised by epitaxy on cubic substrates, so a film sample could in principle be cubic rather than hexagonal. Both papers describe alloy films grown for their optical and thermoelectric properties, which in this field means wurtzite unless stated otherwise, so the assignment stands at high confidence with the possibility noted rather than recorded as a polymorph. Second point: the curator details record dopant:Er+Sr for one sample. Erbium and strontium are not in the parsed composition strings and so carry no dopant_roles entries, but structurally both would be substitutional on the cation site, erbium as the optically active rare earth the first paper is titled for. No reference block was returned. Measured window 297-1057 K.
annotator_note: Erbium and strontium appear only in the curator composition details, not in the parsed formula, so stage 3 will not see them.

basis: K7.5Ga4.8Al3.0Si38.7 and K7.6Ga3.1Al4.6Si38.7, from a paper titled for the synthesis and thermoelectric properties of quaternary type-I silicon clathrates. The framework atoms sum to 46.5 and 46.4 per cell against roughly 7.5 guests, which is the type-I clathrate formula A8E46 exactly, with potassium in the cages and gallium and aluminium substituting into the silicon framework.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: framework substitution site of the silicon clathrate cage network
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the gallium share of the trivalent framework substituent, 4.8 against 3.0 in one composition and 3.1 against 4.6 in the other. Both are group 13 and both replace silicon in the cage framework, so the total substituent count and hence the electron count is nearly fixed while the gallium-to-aluminium ratio is swapped. That swap is the experiment the paper is doing.

note: Gallium and aluminium are framework substituents rather than dopants -- they set the electron count of the covalent cage network, the same role gallium plays in Ba8Ga16Ge30 -- and both are above the 5 per cent split, so neither carries a dopant_roles entry. No reference block was returned for this host, which is expected for a four-element clathrate at a non-integer stoichiometry. Measured window 11-703 K.

basis: One composition, GdAl2, two samples, from the survey papers on the thermoelectric power of RAl2 compounds and the thermal conductivity of REAl2 compounds. [ref 2] gives GdAl2 Fd-3m (227) mp-19923 at hull 0.000 with 20 ICSD references, by far the best-attested entry for the host, and RAl2 at Fd-3m is the cubic C15 Laves phase.
note: One of six RAl2 hosts in this chunk from the same pair of survey papers -- Gd, Ho, Nd, Pr, Sm and Tb -- and all six resolve the same way. Twenty ICSD references is unusually strong support for a host this small. Measured window 11-250 K.

basis: GdAlO3, and (Gd2O3)52.8(Al2O3)47.2 which works out to a gadolinium-to-aluminium ratio of 1.12 to 1 and is therefore the same compound written as an oxide mixture. [ref 2] gives GdAlO3 Pnma (62) mp-5223 with 10 ICSD references, and Pnma is the orthorhombically tilted perovskite that a large trivalent A cation with a small trivalent B cation produces.
note: The oxide-ratio composition is worth checking rather than assuming, because the Gd2O3-Al2O3 system also produces the garnet Gd3Al5O12, which [ref 2] duly returns as mp-14133. Garnet would require a 3:5 gadolinium-to-aluminium ratio, that is 60 mole per cent Al2O3, and the measured composition is at 47.2 per cent, which is on the perovskite side and close to the 50:50 line. So both compositions are GdAlO3. The third reference entry, GdAlO3 Pm-3m mp-1178268 at hull 0.086 with no ICSD reference, is the undistorted cubic aristotype; it is a computed idealisation rather than a phase reached on heating within this window, and is not recorded as a polymorph. Measured window 290-1272 K on the robust range, to 1373 K including outliers.

basis: One composition, HoAl2, two samples, from the same RAl2 survey papers. [ref 2] gives HoAl2 Fd-3m (227) mp-391 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is the cubic C15 Laves phase.
note: The reference PRIMARY is the exact formula at the expected space group on twelve ICSD references. The other entries returned -- HoAl3 R-3m mp-898, Ho3Al2 P4_2/mnm mp-1106135, Ho2Al Pnma mp-16502 and Ho4Al Fd-3m mp-1212293 -- are other stoichiometries in the binary and are not what was measured. Measured window 11-250 K.

basis: One composition, LaNiAl4, two samples, from papers on the thermal conductivity and transport of the CeNiAl4 Kondo lattice, for which the lanthanum compound is the non-magnetic reference. The RTAl4 stoichiometry in this chemistry is the orthorhombic YNiAl4 type, Cmcm, and the pending ynial4_cmcm entry was created for exactly this family.
note: A reference disagreement of the absent-evidence kind, and the reason confidence is medium rather than high. [ref 2] returns LaAl5Ni2 Immm mp-1080524, La2Al7Ni I4_1md mp-1225981, LaAl3Ni2 Cmcm mp-1211232, LaAlNi4 Cmmm mp-1222929 and LaAlNi4 P-6m2 mp-1222982, and not one of them is the 1-1-4 stoichiometry measured. Only the first carries any ICSD reference at all; the rest are computed. The 2019 snapshot does not contain LaNiAl4, so no mp_id is recorded. Note the near-miss in that list: LaAlNi4 has the same three elements in the same 1-1-4 pattern with nickel and aluminium swapped, and is a different compound. Measured window 10-292 K.
annotator_note: Second host to use the pending ynial4_cmcm entry.

basis: One composition, NdAl2, two samples, from the same RAl2 survey papers. [ref 2] gives NdAl2 Fd-3m (227) mp-400 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references as PRIMARY, the cubic C15 Laves phase.
note: The remaining reference entries -- NdAl4 I4/mmm mp-1834, Nd3Al11 Immm mp-1104100, NdAl Pbcm mp-864637 and NdAl3 P6_3/mmc mp-16513 -- are other binary stoichiometries and are not what was measured. Measured window 11-252 K.

basis: One composition, Ni3Al, two samples. [ref 2] gives AlNi3 Pm-3m (221) mp-991114 at hull 0.000 with 15 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is the L12 AuCu3 structure -- the gamma-prime precipitate phase of nickel superalloys and one of the best-studied ordered intermetallics there is.
note: One caveat for stage 2 rather than for the assignment. The first paper is on TiC-Ni3Al composite materials, so that sample is Ni3Al as the matrix of a carbide composite rather than a monolithic intermetallic; the second is on Ni3V-Ni3Al pseudo-binary alloys, where the other end member Ni3V is the D022 tetragonal variant rather than L12. Neither changes what the Ni3Al composition itself is, and no second element appears in the parsed composition to flag either case, but a sample-level reader should be aware. The remaining reference entries are other Al-Ni binary stoichiometries. Measured window 272-1074 K on the robust range, to 1337 K including outliers.

basis: One composition, Zn0.9Al0.05Ni0.05, two samples, from a paper on aluminium and nickel co-doped ZnO films. The composition string contains no oxygen, but the paper is unambiguously about zinc oxide, so this is co-doped ZnO with the metal ratios recorded and the anion dropped -- and ZnO is wurtzite, P6_3mc.
note: This record disagrees with both the composition string and the references, and says so deliberately. Taken at face value the formula is a zinc-rich ternary metal alloy, and [ref 2] duly returns intermetallics for it: Al3ZnNi12 P4/mmm mp-1229039 at hull 0.007 and AlZnNi2 Immm mp-1093891 at hull 2.354, both computed with no ICSD references. Neither is the material. The paper title names ZnO films co-doped with aluminium and nickel, which is a very well-known transparent-conductor system, and the 90:5:5 metal ratio is exactly what such a film would be. Confidence is medium only because the assignment overrides the parsed composition rather than reading it; the chemistry itself is not in doubt. Aluminium and nickel land exactly on the 5 at.% split and are counted as host elements, so they carry no dopant_roles entries -- with oxygen restored they would be 2.5 at.% each and would be read as the substitutional donors on the zinc site that they are. Measured window 12-295 K.
annotator_note: The missing oxygen is an upstream composition-parsing problem, not an annotation one. Any host in Al-Ni-Zn is worth checking for the same omission.

basis: One composition, NpPd5Al2, two single-crystal samples, from the two Physical Review B papers on the transport and magnetic properties and the Kondo behaviour of this superconductor. NpPd5Al2 is the transuranium heavy-fermion superconductor reported in 2007 and its structure is the body-centred tetragonal ZrNi2Al5 type, I4/mmm, with thick palladium-aluminium slabs between the neptunium layers.
note: The prototype is new, proposed in this chunk, and the space group on it comes from materials knowledge rather than from the references -- stage 2 should confirm it from the papers, which are single-crystal studies. This is also a reference disagreement: [ref 2] returns only NpAl3Pd2 P6/mmm mp-1206258 at hull 0.104 with no ICSD reference, which is a computed entry at a different stoichiometry and a different symmetry. It is neither the compound measured nor evidence about it, so no mp_id is recorded and confidence is held at medium. Transuranium compounds are thinly represented in both reference sets, so an empty result here says more about the snapshot than about the material. Measured window 10-298 K.
annotator_note: Worth remembering that this is the quasi-two-dimensional analogue of the 115 heavy-fermion superconductors, which is why its structure matters to the physics the papers report.

basis: (SnO2)0.8527Al0.1473 and (SnO2)0.7728Al0.2272, from a paper on the effect of aluminium doping on the structural, optical and electrical properties of tin oxide. SnO2 is cassiterite, the rutile structure, P4_2/mnm, and aluminium substitutes on the octahedral tin site.
note: Aluminium is written outside the oxide bracket in both composition strings, at 15 and 23 mole per cent, which puts it above the 5 at.% split and makes it a host element with no dopant_roles entry even though the paper calls it doping. That is a large amount of aluminium for a substitutional solid solution in rutile SnO2, and the upper composition in particular may well be at or past the solubility limit with excess aluminium segregating as an amorphous or alumina second phase; the paper reports structural characterisation and will say. The assignment is to the rutile host regardless. No reference block was returned for this host. Measured window 50-290 K.
annotator_note: At 23 per cent aluminium the single-phase reading is worth checking against the paper before stage 3 computes a doping level from it.

basis: One composition, PrAl2, two samples, from the same RAl2 survey papers. [ref 2] gives PrAl2 Fd-3m (227) mp-1189 at hull 0.000 with 15 ICSD references as PRIMARY, the cubic C15 Laves phase.
note: The other reference entries are other binary stoichiometries: PrAl Pbcm mp-1106232, Pr3Al P6_3/mmc mp-1079266 which is marked AMBIGUOUS, PrAl4 I4/mmm mp-2336 and PrAl3 P6_3/mmc mp-12553. None is what was measured. Measured window 11-250 K.

basis: Al12Re, tagged IAC_1_0 by the curator for the 1/0 approximant designation, which is the Al12W structure: a body-centred cubic packing of aluminium icosahedra with rhenium at their centres, Im-3. [ref 2] gives Al12Re Im-3 (204) mp-1648 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references as the top-ranked entry for the host.
note: The host is flagged mixed because the second composition, Al11Re4, is a different and considerably more complex aluminium-rich intermetallic, and its structure could not be established from the evidence here. [ref 2] offers nothing at that stoichiometry -- the entries returned are Al5Re24 I-43m mp-1192984, Al6Re Cmcm mp-16528, AlRe Pm-3m mp-10908 and AlRe2 I4/mmm mp-10909, all on a single ICSD reference each and none of them Al11Re4. Rather than stretch the Al12W entry to cover it or guess a structure type, it is recorded as unresolved_crystalline and left for stage 2. The papers are on aluminium-based icosahedral quasicrystals and approximants, including AlPdRe, so the surrounding literature is quasicrystalline even though Al12Re itself is a small periodic cell -- which is precisely the distinction the new al12w_type entry exists to keep. Measured window 359-863 K from a single curve.
annotator_note: Only one curve survives the range filter for this host, so the measured window is weakly determined.

basis: Al73.3Rh26.7_IAC and Al73Rh27, from papers on band engineering in Al-TM quasicrystalline approximants and on the electrical resistivity of the Al65Rh27Si8 2/1 cubic approximant. The IAC tag and both titles say approximant, and Al73Rh27 is in the composition range where the Al-Rh system forms large-cell Bergman-type approximant phases.
note: Another reference disagreement of the same shape as Al-Co-Ru. [ref 2] returns AlRh Pm-3m mp-364 on 4 ICSD references as PRIMARY, plus Al9Rh2 P2_1/c mp-1645, Al5Rh2 P6_3/mmc mp-1791, Al13Rh4 C2/m mp-1203489 and AlRh3 P6_3/mmc mp-1183306. The PRIMARY is the equiatomic B2 compound, which is nowhere near the measured Al73Rh27, and the closest in composition, Al13Rh4 at 76.5 per cent aluminium, is a monoclinic approximant-related phase but not the 2/1 cubic one the papers describe. No mp_id is recorded. Note that the second paper is on the silicon-containing Al65Rh27Si8 approximant, whose composition would fall in a different host; the samples here are the binary. Measured window 16-845 K.

basis: Ru2TaAl and Ru1.95Ta1.05Al, from a paper on semimetallic behaviour in Heusler-type compounds. [ref 2] gives TaAlRu2 Fm-3m (225) mp-862446 at hull 0.000 as PRIMARY, which is the L21 full Heusler arrangement, and the X2YZ stoichiometry with the transition metal doubled is exactly what produces it.
note: The mp_id carries no ICSD reference count, so it is a computed entry rather than a measured one, which is why the phase confidence is medium while the host confidence is high -- the prototype is not in doubt, the specific structure record is merely uncomputed against experiment. The second composition, Ru1.95Ta1.05Al, is the same compound with a slight excess of tantalum on the ruthenium site, which in a valence-electron-counted Heusler semimetal is the point of the experiment: it shifts the Fermi level through the semimetallic overlap. Measured window 13-298 K.

basis: (YbAl3)0.8(Y5Sb3)0.2 and (YbAl3)0.9(Y5Sb3)0.1, from a paper titled for the effects of a second phase of Yb5Sb3 on the thermoelectric properties of YbAl3. The composition string is written as two bracketed compounds with mole fractions, so the matrix is YbAl3, the cubic L12 AuCu3 structure, and the antimonide is a deliberately introduced second phase at 10 and 20 per cent.
note: The primary prototype names the matrix, which is what 80 to 90 per cent of the material is and what carries the transport; the mixed flag and the alternatives record that this is a two-phase composite by design. The 5-3 antimonide takes either the hexagonal Mn5Si3 D88 type or the closely related orthorhombic Y5Bi3 type, hence mn5si3_d88 as the alternative, though which of the two applies is not settled here. Note the discrepancy between the title and the data: the paper says Yb5Sb3 and the composition strings say Y5Sb3, and the host element set includes both yttrium and ytterbium. One of the two is wrong and the composition string is the more likely culprit, but it cannot be decided from the chunk file. No reference block was returned for this four-element host. Measured window 299-674 K.
annotator_note: Y5Sb3 in the composition against Yb5Sb3 in the title is an unresolved conflict; stage 2 should read the paper before treating yttrium as a real constituent.

basis: Yb5Al2Sb6 and Yb5Al2Sb6Ge0.5, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of the Zintl phases Yb5M2Sb6 with M = Al, Ga and In. The 5-2-6 stoichiometry is the Ca5Al2Sb6 Zintl structure: chains of corner-sharing AlSb4 tetrahedra cross-linked by Sb-Sb bonds into ladders, charge balanced by the divalent cation.

dopant_roles.basis: Yb5Al2Sb6Ge0.5 adds germanium to the valence-precise parent compound. The natural site is the tetrahedral framework site held by aluminium, where tetravalent germanium against trivalent aluminium is an electron donor and moves the compound off the exact Zintl count -- which is how this family is tuned, since a valence-precise semiconductor has no carriers otherwise. The alternative, germanium on an antimony site, would be an acceptor instead. The composition alone does not separate the two.

note: The second paper on this host, on thermally activated solid-state crystal-to-crystal structural transformation, is a warning worth carrying forward: the Yb5M2Sb6 phases are known to transform in the solid state on heating, and the measured window here runs to 875 K. No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line appears in the chunk file, so spans_transition is left false and no phase sequence is recorded, but that is the absence of a flag rather than evidence of no transition. This is also a reference disagreement: [ref 2] returns Yb11AlSb9 Iba2 mp-1196426 on 33 ICSD references and Yb14AlSb11 I4_1/acd mp-1196138 on 32, both very well attested and both different Zintl stoichiometries -- the 11-1-9 and the 14-1-11 families. Neither is the 5-2-6 compound measured, so no mp_id is recorded despite the strong reference support for its neighbours. Measured window 279-875 K.
annotator_note: A structural transformation inside the measured window is plausible here on the strength of the second paper title and should be checked rather than assumed absent.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [55], ICSD-backed references for this host report [45, 142]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, SmAl2, two samples, from the same RAl2 survey papers. [ref 2] gives SmAl2 Fd-3m (227) mp-2358 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references as PRIMARY, the cubic C15 Laves phase.
note: The other reference entries -- SmAl4 I4/mmm mp-1891, SmAl Pbcm mp-978951, SmAl5 P6_322 mp-1190357 and Sm2Al Pnma mp-1102344 -- are other binary stoichiometries. Measured window 11-248 K.

basis: One composition, TbAl2, two samples, from the same RAl2 survey papers. [ref 2] gives TbAl2 Fd-3m (227) mp-756 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references as PRIMARY, the cubic C15 Laves phase.
note: Last of the six RAl2 hosts in this chunk. All six -- Gd, Ho, Nd, Pr, Sm and Tb -- come from the same two survey papers on the thermoelectric power and thermal conductivity of the RAl2 series, and all resolve to the C15 Laves phase with the exact formula as the reference PRIMARY on between 6 and 20 ICSD references. The remaining entries here are TbAl3 R-3m mp-369, TbAl Pbcm mp-11225, Tb2Al Pnma mp-1103391 and Tb2Al17 P6_3/mmc mp-1202952. Measured window 11-249 K.

basis: Zn0.9Al0.1Te and Zn0.85Al0.15Te, from a paper on the low thermal conductivity and enhanced thermoelectric performance of nanostructured ZnTe. ZnTe is a zincblende semiconductor, F-43m, and both compositions are ZnTe with aluminium substituting on the zinc site.
note: This record disagrees with [ref 1], which is the stronger of the two reference sets and is normally to be preferred, so the reasoning is worth stating. TEDesignLab returns Al2ZnTe4 I-4 (82) mp-7908 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference. That is the ordered vacancy compound of the ZnTe-Al2Te3 line, a defect chalcopyrite with one vacancy in every four cation sites, and it sits at 50 atomic per cent aluminium among the cations. The measured compositions are at 10 and 15 per cent, which is nowhere near it -- they are aluminium-doped ZnTe, as the paper title confirms by calling the material ZnTe. The reference describes a phase that exists in this chemistry, not the phase that was made. No mp_id is recorded. Aluminium is above the 5 at.% split so it carries no dopant_roles entry; structurally it is a trivalent donor on the divalent zinc site. Measured window 85-651 K.
annotator_note: At 15 per cent aluminium the solubility limit in ZnTe may be exceeded and some ordered-vacancy second phase may be present, which would make the reference entry relevant after all -- as a minority phase, not as the host.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [216], ICSD-backed references for this host report [82]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: As17.65Bi11.76Se8.82Te44.12Tl17.65 and As11.11Bi22.22Se5.56Te50Tl11.11, from a 1964 paper titled for the thermoelectric properties of DIPHASAL systems combining As2Te3 and Tl2Te. The paper says two-phase in its title, and the compositions are mixtures of tellurides rather than a line compound: the first is close to As2Te3 plus Tl2Te with bismuth and selenium added, the second shifts the balance towards the bismuth chalcogenide.
note: Confidence is medium because diphasal tells us there are two phases without telling us which two, and a five-element chalcogenide at these ratios could resolve several ways. The alternatives name the likely constituents on the bismuth side -- a tetradymite Bi2(Te,Se)3 or one of the complex bismuth chalcogenides -- but the thallium-arsenic side has no clean candidate in the taxonomy and is left unnamed rather than guessed. No reference block was returned, which is expected. A 1964 paper will report the phase analysis, so this is settleable by reading. Measured window 103-331 K.
annotator_note: One of the few hosts in this chunk where the composition genuinely cannot be reduced to a structure without the paper.

basis: CeNi2As2 and CeNi2(As0.9P0.1)2, from a paper on heavy-fermion quantum criticality at the dilute carrier limit in CeNi2-delta(As1-xPx)2. The 1-2-2 stoichiometry with a rare earth, a late transition metal and a pnictogen is the ThCr2Si2 structure, I4/mmm, and the CeNi2(As,P)2 series is studied precisely because the tetragonal 122 lattice collapses continuously as phosphorus replaces arsenic.

dopant_roles.basis: CeNi2(As0.9P0.1)2 is the x = 0.1 member of the series the paper is titled for.
