Phosphorus and arsenic are both group 15 and both occupy the pnictogen site of the 122 lattice, so the substitution adds no carriers; it acts as chemical pressure, shortening the interlayer pnictogen-pnictogen distance and driving the collapse of the tetragonal cell that the quantum criticality depends on. At a tenth of the pnictogen site it is a solid-solution variable rather than dilute doping.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: pnictogen site of the ThCr2Si2 lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: x is the phosphorus share of the pnictogen site. Only the arsenic end member and x = 0.1 appear in this host; the full series in the paper runs further.

note: I disagree with the reference ranking here and record it rather than following it. [ref 2] marks Ce(NiAs)2 P4/nmm (129) mp-610645 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references as PRIMARY, and lists Ce(NiAs)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-21006 at hull 0.016 with an equal 2 ICSD references below it. P4/nmm at this stoichiometry is the CaBe2Ge2 type, which stacks two different tetrahedral layers rather than repeating one, and it is a real alternative for ANi2X2 compounds. But the quantum-criticality literature this host comes from works with the ThCr2Si2 structure, and the whole framing of the experiment -- collapsed versus uncollapsed tetragonal phase under chemical pressure -- is a 122 ThCr2Si2 phenomenon. Two ICSD references each is not enough to separate the two on evidence, so the mp_id recorded is the I4/mmm one and confidence is medium at both levels. The other entries returned, Ce2Ni12As7 P-6 mp-1191623, CeNiAs P-6m2 mp-1061766 and Ce6Ni20As13 P-6 mp-1214373, are different stoichiometries. Measured window 11-283 K.
annotator_note: ThCr2Si2 against CaBe2Ge2 for CeNi2As2 is a genuine open question in the references and should be read out of the paper in stage 2.

basis: CeOs4As12, from a paper titled for the filled skutterudite CeOs4As12 as a hybridisation-gap semiconductor. The 1-4-12 stoichiometry is the filled skutterudite formula outright, and [ref 2] gives Ce(As3Os)4 Im-3 (204) mp-1189855 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference, which is that composition at the skutterudite space group.
note: Composition, paper title and reference all agree, which is rare this far down the tail. Note that this is an arsenide skutterudite rather than the usual antimonide: the cerium fills the icosahedral void of an Os4As12 framework. Cerium is above the 5 at.% split so it carries no dopant_roles entry, and it would not be a dopant in any case -- it is the filler the compound is named for. The two composition strings differ only by a trailing space. Measured window 10-287 K.

basis: Yb0.13Co3.0Fe1.0Sb9As2.9 and Yb0.23Co2.8Fe1.0Sb9As2.9, from a paper on the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of p-type skutterudites. Both are the CoSb3 skutterudite framework with iron substituting for cobalt and arsenic for antimony -- the pnictogen count is 11.9 against a framework metal count of 4, which is the 4-12 skutterudite ratio -- and ytterbium filling the cage.

dopant_roles.basis: Ytterbium occupies the icosahedral void of the Co4Sb12 framework at 13 and 23 per cent filling. It is the rattler: it donates electrons to compensate the iron substitution and scatters heat-carrying phonons without entering the covalent framework. This is the canonical cage_filler case the taxonomy cites for the skutterudite prototype.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: pnictogen ring site of the skutterudite framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Arsenic replaces about a quarter of the antimony in the pnictogen rings, identically in both compositions. Both are group 15 and isoelectronic, so the substitution tunes the lattice thermal conductivity and the band structure without changing the carrier count. Arsenic is above the 5 at.% split and is therefore a host element, which is why it appears here rather than in dopant_roles.

note: Iron is the acceptor here rather than a filler: substituting Fe for Co in the framework makes the compound p-type, and the ytterbium filling partly compensates it. Both are above the split so neither carries a dopant_roles entry, but the roles are worth recording for stage 2 to pick up. No reference block was returned for this four-element host. Measured window 319-816 K.

basis: (SrF)2Ti2As2O, from a paper titled for the structure and physical properties of the layered pnictide-oxides. The Ti2As2O layer is a titanium-oxygen square net with arsenic above and below -- an anti-perovskite Ti2O sheet capped by pnictogen -- which is the Na2Ti2Sb2O structural family, and the SrF blocks are the charge reservoir between them. [ref 2] gives Sr2Ti2As2OF2 I4/mmm (139) mp-1079747 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference, the exact formula at the expected space group.
note: The second composition string, (SrF)2TiAs2O, has one titanium where the first has two. A 1-2 titanium-to-arsenic ratio would break the Ti2O square net that this structure is built on, and the paper is a structural study of the (SrF)2Ti2As2O compound, so this is taken as a transcription slip rather than a second phase and the host is not flagged mixed. Fluorine here is a structural anion in the SrF block, not a dopant, even though it is a light element that a role-assignment pass might mistake for one. Measured window 11-444 K.
annotator_note: Second host to use the pending na2ti2sb2o_oxypnictide entry, and the first with a fluoride rather than an alkali charge reservoir.

basis: One composition, TbFeAsO0.85, two samples, from a paper on the crystal structure and the electronic and thermal properties of TbFeAsO0.85. The 1111 oxypnictide stoichiometry is the ZrCuSiAs structure, P4/nmm, alternating TbO and FeAs layers, and [ref 2] gives TbFeAsO P4/nmm (129) mp-1079887 with 1 ICSD reference.
note: The oxygen deficiency is the point of the compound and not an impurity: removing oxygen from the TbO layer dopes electrons into the FeAs layer, which is the standard route to superconductivity in the 1111 iron pnictides and is the variable the paper title carries. Oxygen is a host element here, so it takes no dopant_roles entry, but stage 3 should read the 0.85 as the doping variable rather than as a stoichiometry error. The reference entry sits at hull 0.180, which looks poor, but that is for the stoichiometric parent in a snapshot where magnetic rare-earth pnictide energetics are unreliable, and it carries the ICSD reference. Measured window 10-299 K.

basis: One composition, LaNiAsO, two samples, from a comparative study of the thermoelectric effect of parent oxypnictides. LaNiAsO is the nickel analogue of LaFeAsO and takes the same ZrCuSiAs 1111 structure, P4/nmm, with LaO and NiAs layers alternating. [ref 2] gives LaNiAsO P4/nmm (129) mp-1079362 with 2 ICSD references as PRIMARY.
note: The reference PRIMARY sits at hull 0.548 and the second entry, La2NiAs2O P4/mmm mp-1213453, at 1.795. Those are large numbers and would normally be a warning, but the chunk header is explicit that hull energies in the 2019 dump are unusable for layered pnictides and chalcogenides, and the ICSD reference count is what carries the evidence here -- two references on the exact formula at the structure the compound is known for. The composition is the undoped parent, which is what the paper is about. Measured window 15-300 K.

basis: One composition, LaOs4As12, two samples, from papers on the crystal structure, NMR and transport properties of the arsenic-based filled skutterudites and on CeOs4As12. The 1-4-12 stoichiometry is the filled skutterudite formula, and [ref 2] gives La(As3Os)4 Im-3 (204) mp-1105556 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference.
note: The non-magnetic lanthanum counterpart of the As-Ce-Os host five ranks earlier, from an overlapping pair of papers, and it resolves identically. Lanthanum is the cage filler and is above the 5 at.% split, so it carries no dopant_roles entry. Measured window 11-300 K.

basis: One composition, MnAs, two samples. [ref 2] gives MnAs P6_3/mmc (194) mp-610 with 11 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is the hexagonal NiAs B81 structure -- the type compound of the prototype, with manganese in octahedral holes of a hexagonal close-packed arsenic array.
note: The chunk file shows no MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line for this host, but it should: MnAs undergoes a first-order transition at about 318 K from the ferromagnetic hexagonal NiAs-type to the paramagnetic orthorhombic MnP-type, and the measured window is 29-325 K, which crosses it by a few degrees. That transition is the reason MnAs is a magnetocaloric material at all, and it is why both papers here are about magnetic refrigerants -- MnAs appears as the comparison compound alongside La(Fe,Si)13. The phase sequence is recorded on that basis, with the transition temperature from materials knowledge rather than from the papers or the taxonomy, since the nias prototype carries no phase_transitions field that would have flagged it. On further heating, above roughly 400 K, the NiAs structure returns; that is outside the measured window and is not recorded. No mp_id is available for the orthorhombic phase -- the reference block returns Mn2As P4/nmm mp-610522, Mn3As Cmcm mp-2668, Mn4As3 C2/m mp-9305 and Mn3As2 C2/m mp-28916, all different stoichiometries. Measured window 29-325 K.
annotator_note: This is a case the automated flag missed. The 318 K transition sits just inside the measured range, so a host that looks single-phase in the chunk file is not.

basis: One composition, NaSn2As2, two polycrystalline samples from the paper on axis-dependent carrier polarity. The 1-2-2 alkali tin arsenide is the layered van der Waals Zintl phase built from puckered [Sn2As2] bilayers with sodium in the gap, and [ref 2] gives Na(SnAs)2 R-3m (166) mp-9378 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference.
note: NaSn2As2 is one of the goniopolar materials, whose Seebeck coefficient has opposite sign along and across the layers, so the layered prototype is the subject of the measurement rather than a detail of it. The other entry [ref 2] returns for the host, Na5SnAs3 P2_1/c mp-5248, is a different stoichiometry and is not the compound measured. Sodium is above the 5 at.% split and is a structural constituent, not a dopant, so dopant_roles is empty. Measured window 302-369 K.

basis: One composition, ThAs1.23S0.77, two plate samples from the paper on anomalous transport in thorium arsenosulphide crystals. ThAsS is the tetragonal PbFCl (matlockite) type, and [ref 2] gives ThAsS P4/nmm (129) mp-1019358 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference. The taxonomy entry was proposed for the uranium members of exactly this MXY series and names UAsS among its representative materials.
note: The recorded As:S ratio of 1.23 to 0.77 is anion off-stoichiometry on the two anion sheets of the PbFCl stack, the same variable the As-Se-U host scans on the uranium side of this family, and not an impurity. Both anions are above the 5 at.% split so nothing appears in dopant_roles. The second reference entry, Th2AsS2 P4/mmm mp-1207041 at hull 2.147, is a computed structure two electronvolts above the hull with no ICSD backing and is not a competing phase. Measured window 12-321 K.

basis: One composition, UAsS, two samples. UAsS is named in the taxonomy entry as a representative material, and [ref 2] gives UAsS P4/nmm (129) mp-4374 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references as the top-ranked entry for the host. Four references on the exact composition is strong attestation for a uranium ternary.
note: U2AsS R-3m mp-1216688 and U2AsS2 P4/mmm mp-1206491 are also returned but both are different stoichiometries with no ICSD backing, and the second sits 1.66 eV above the hull. Uranium and both anions are above the 5 at.% split, so dopant_roles is empty. Measured window 14-296 K, which is the low-temperature Kondo range the paper is about.
annotator_note: The composition and the paper title disagree and the record follows the composition. The curator recorded UAsS, but the linked paper is titled for UAsSe, a Kondo-like thermoelectric power study of the selenide ferromagnet. UAsS and UAsSe are both PbFCl-type members of the same UXY series, so the prototype is unaffected either way, but if the samples are in fact UAsSe they belong to the As-Se-U host annotated in chunk 10 and this host is a transcription artefact. Worth one look at the paper.

basis: One composition, As2SeTe2, two samples, from a Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids paper on the effect of gamma-irradiation on non-linear current-voltage behaviour. An As-Se-Te ternary at this stoichiometry is a bulk chalcogenide glass, and the non-linear switching behaviour the paper measures is a property of the glass rather than of any crystalline phase. Neither reference returns any entry for the host.
note: Arsenic chalcogenide glasses are the classic switching and memory-effect materials and are always quoted by nominal composition, which is why the formula looks like a line compound. There is no structure for stage 2 to resolve. Measured window 300-313 K, essentially room temperature.

basis: Two compositions, Ba8Au4Ga4Ge38 and Ba8Au3Ga7Ge36, from the paper on the thermoelectric properties of Au-containing type-I clathrates Ba8AuxGa16-xGe30. The Ba8 guest count against a 46-atom framework is the type-I clathrate formula, and the paper names the type in its title.
note: Gold and gallium both sit above the 5 at.% split here, so neither is listed in dopant_roles, but both are framework substituents on the germanium sublattice and the Au:Ga:Ge ratio is what sets the Zintl electron count. Stage 3 should read them that way rather than as doping. Neither reference returns an entry for this host, so the space group is the standard type-I Pm-3n from materials knowledge. Measured window 10-771 K.

basis: Two compositions, Ba8Au4Ga4Si38 and Ba8Au3Ga7Si36, from the paper on the effect of Au substitution on the thermoelectric properties of silicon clathrates. Same Ba8 guest count on a 46-atom framework as the germanium host one rank above, with silicon replacing germanium.
note: The silicon and germanium type-I clathrates are the same structure, and these two hosts are a deliberate pair from one research programme. As on the germanium side, gold and gallium are framework substituents above the split rather than dopants. No reference entry for the host. Measured window 302-871 K.

basis: Two ways of writing one compound, YbCu4Au and YbAuCu4, from two low-temperature papers on the Hall effect and thermopower of YbCu4Au and of the YbMCu4 series. The YbMCu4 compounds are cubic C15b, the ordered AuBe5 derivative in F-43m, and [ref 2] confirms it with YbCu4Au F-43m (216) mp-1077165 at hull 0.000.
note: The two composition strings are the same material with the elements in a different order, so this host is one compound and not a mixture. YbCu4Au is an intermediate-valence Kondo compound and the papers are about that; the M site in YbMCu4 runs Ag, Au, Pd across the second paper, which is why the neighbouring Yb hosts look similar. Only one ICSD reference backs the MP entry, which is thin but consistent with the structure literature on the series. Measured window 10-276 K.

basis: Two compositions, YbAu2 and YbAu3, one sample each, from one paper on the thermal conductivity and thermoelectric power of the Yb-Au system. They are two different intermetallics and the host is mixed. YbAu2 is the body-centred tetragonal MoSi2 C11b type, which [ref 2] supports as YbAu2 I4/mmm (139) mp-1668 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, the best-attested entry for the host. YbAu3 is the hexagonal D0_19 ordered close packing, which [ref 2] returns as YbAu3 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-979985 at hull 0.012 with no ICSD reference.
note: The split is clean on stoichiometry, one sample each: YbAu2 to mosi2_c11b and YbAu3 to ni3sn_d019. Confidence is medium for the host as a whole because the YbAu3 half rests on a computed entry with no ICSD backing, while the YbAu2 half is well attested. The paper surveys the Yb-Au system rather than one compound, so more phases of it may appear further down the tail. Measured window 10-269 K.

basis: Two compositions, (B4C)85.25(TiO2)14.75 and (B4C)81.26(TiO2)18.74, from the paper on the in-situ preparation of B4C-TiB2 composites. The matrix is boron carbide at over 80 mol per cent; the titania is a reactant that is consumed in situ to form TiB2, so the host is a boron carbide with a boride second phase and not a ternary oxide.

dopant_roles.basis: Added as TiO2 and reacted with the boron carbide to precipitate TiB2, the deliberate second phase named in the title. It does not enter the B4C lattice, so it is a composite constituent rather than a dopant, and the oxygen leaves as boria during hot pressing.

note: is_mixed is left false rather than true because the second phase is a deliberate additive in a composite, not a competing structure the host label is hiding; the README warns against letting composite additives relabel their hosts. alb2 is carried as the alternative because the TiB2 that forms is an AlB2-type diboride and stage 2 will need it if the composite is ever modelled as two phases. No reference entry for the host. Measured window 294-1073 K.

basis: Two compositions, (SiC)0.28ZrB2 and a La2O3-doped version of it, from the paper on the thermal properties of La2O3-doped ZrB2- and HfB2-based ultra-high-temperature ceramics. The matrix is ZrB2, the hexagonal AlB2-type diboride, with silicon carbide as the standard oxidation-resistant second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: La2O3 is a sintering aid added at 0.7 mol per cent, named in the paper title. It scavenges the surface zirconia and sits at grain boundaries rather than entering the ZrB2 lattice.
The oxygen of that same La2O3 addition, plus the native oxide on the diboride powder.

note: ZrB2-SiC is the workhorse ultra-high-temperature ceramic and the measurement runs to 2170 K, the highest window in this chunk by a wide margin, which is what these materials are made for. Silicon carbide is a major constituent at roughly 16 at.% rather than a dopant, so sic_polytype is recorded as the alternative; as with the B4C-TiB2 host one rank above, is_mixed is left false because this is an engineered composite rather than a hidden second structure. No reference entry for the host. Measured window 295-2170 K.

basis: One composition, UB2C, two samples, from the paper on electron correlation effects and ferromagnetic order in beta-UB2C. [ref 2] gives UB2C R-3m (166) mp-11332 at hull 0.051 with 2 ICSD references, the only entry it returns at this stoichiometry. The paper names the beta polymorph, so the compound is polymorphic and the form measured is identified even though the reference does not label which form R-3m is.
note: Confidence is medium, not high, because the alpha-beta polymorphism is real and the reference does not say which polymorph its R-3m entry is; the paper does say beta, and reading it would settle both that and the space group. [ref 2] ranks UBC Cmcm mp-5816 above it on 3 ICSD references, but UBC is a different compound in the same ternary rather than a competing structure for UB2C. Measured window 10-292 K, the range in which the ferromagnetic order the paper reports sets in.

basis: Both compositions are Ca0.5Sr0.5B6, the second written with the six borons split across the two cations. The metal to boron ratio of 1 to 6 is the cubic hexaboride formula, a framework of B6 octahedra with the alkaline earth in the cavity, and both papers are explicitly about alkaline-earth hexaboride solid solutions.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: CaB6 and SrB6 form a complete solid solution on the cavity site and every sample here sits at the midpoint. Mixing the two cation sizes is the mechanism the second paper uses to scatter phonons and cut the thermal conductivity, so the alloying is the experiment rather than incidental.

note: Calcium and strontium are each about 7 at.% of the formula, above the 5 at.% split, so both are host elements and dopant_roles is empty. Neither reference returns an entry for the host; the cubic Pm-3m cell is from materials knowledge. Measured window 289-1074 K, with the full span running to 1121 K.

basis: Two compositions, CeCrB6 and Y0.05Ce0.95CrB6, from one Physical Review B paper on the thermoelectricity and electronic properties of the compound. The ycrb4_type entry, proposed in chunk 032, explicitly covers the RMB6 member of the same family alongside RMB4: a planar boron net of six- and seven-membered rings with the large rare earth in the seven-ring and the smaller transition metal in the smaller ring. A ternary rare-earth chromium boride at this boron count belongs there rather than with the hexaborides.

dopant_roles.basis: Y0.05Ce0.95CrB6 dilutes the cerium sublattice with a non-magnetic ion of similar size, the standard way to test whether a property is single-ion or cooperative. It takes the large-cation site of the boron ring net.

note: The references do not support the recorded stoichiometry and this record says so rather than following either side quietly. [ref 2] returns Ce(CrB3)2 Immm (71) mp-2873 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which is CeCr2B6, and CeCrB4 Pbam (55) mp-1191927 with 1 reference. Neither is a 1-1-6 compound. The Pbam entry is the YCrB4 type itself, so the reference does place this chemistry in the assigned family; what it does not confirm is the boron count. Either the composition should read CeCr2B6, in which case the Immm entry applies and this assignment is wrong, or CeCrB6 is the RMB6 ring compound the taxonomy entry anticipates. Confidence is medium for that reason and the space group is recorded as the RMB4 Pbam value, which the RMB6 member need not share. Reading the paper would settle it in one line.
annotator_note: The ycrb4_type entry closes by saying that if a later chunk turns up RMB6 compositions on their own, splitting them out would be reasonable. This is that chunk: both compositions here are RMB6 and neither is RMB4. Flagging it for the v4 review rather than pre-empting it.

basis: Two compositions, Ni0.1Co0.9B and Ni0.5Co0.5B, from a paper measuring the Seebeck coefficients of the iron-group element borides. At the 1-to-1 metal-to-boron ratio the iron-group monoborides adopt the FeB and CrB chain structures, boron in zigzag chains through a metal framework, and CoB is the FeB-type orthorhombic member.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: The paper walks Ni across the Co site of CoB, so these are two points on a (Co,Ni)B substitution line rather than a doped compound and an alloy. CoB and NiB are both monoborides, though the boron chain motif differs between the CrB and FeB settings, which is the thing to watch if the series is extended.

note: Nickel is 5 and 25 at.% in the two compositions, well above the split, so it is a host element rather than a dopant and dopant_roles is empty. Neither reference returns an entry for this host, so the Pnma FeB setting is from materials knowledge; the CrB and FeB settings, Cmcm and Pnma, are two arrangements of the same chain motif and stage 2 should take the choice from a pattern rather than the formula. Measured window 438-948 K.

basis: The host string is a parsing artefact. Both compositions read Ce0.1Fe0.7Co3.3SB12 and Ce0.05Yb0.05Fe0.14Co3.86SB12, which are the filled skutterudites Ce0.1Fe0.7Co3.3Sb12 and (Ce,Yb)0.1Fe0.14Co3.86Sb12 with the antimony formula Sb12 split into a sulphur and a B12. Both papers confirm it: one is on Ce0.09Fe0.67Co3.33Sb12 multilayers, the other on the thermoelectric properties of the (Ce-Yb)yFexCo4-xSb12 skutterudites. The 1-4-12 stoichiometry with a rare-earth filler is the filled skutterudite formula.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe-for-Co on the skutterudite framework site is what creates the holes that the rare-earth filler compensates; the Fe:Co ratio and the filling fraction are a single tied variable in this family, not two dopants.
Rare-earth guest in the icosahedral void of the Sb12 framework, the rattler that suppresses the lattice thermal conductivity.
The second filler of the double-filled composition; mixing two guest species of different mass is the point of the (Ce-Yb)y paper.

note: Recorded under the host key the pipeline produced, since that is the routing key the sample table uses, but nothing about this host is a boride or a sulphide. The sulphur and the boron here are not present in the material at all.
annotator_note: A parse artefact worth fixing upstream rather than only annotating around. Sb12 has been read as S + B12, which puts real filled-skutterudite samples into a B-Co-S host that does not exist, and the same failure would hit any composition string where an element symbol is followed by a two-digit subscript that can be re-split. Worth grepping df_compositions for other Sb, Si, Se and Sn strings that came out as S plus something. The two samples are correctly assigned here, but they belong in Co-Sb.

basis: One composition, CrB, two samples, from a paper on the thermophysical and mechanical properties of CrB and FeB. CrB is the type compound of the prototype, and [ref 2] gives CrB Cmcm (63) mp-260 at hull 0.010 with 7 ICSD references.
note: The Cr-B binary is rich and [ref 2] returns five phases for it, CrB2, CrB, Cr3B4, Cr5B3 and CrB4, each with four or more ICSD references. The composition picks CrB unambiguously, so the others are neighbouring compounds rather than candidate polymorphs and are not listed in other_polymorphs. The robust measured range collapses to a single point at 293 K because only the endpoints of two curves survive the percentile filter; the full span runs to 1222 K and is the range the paper actually covers.

basis: Two compositions, Fe74Co2.5Cr7.5B16 and Fe74Cr10B16, both as ribbons, from a paper on the electrical resistivity and thermoelectric power of the Fe74Co10-xCrxB16 series. A metal-metalloid composition at 16 at.% boron produced as a ribbon is a melt-spun amorphous alloy of the Metglas type; the ribbon form and the boron content together are the signature.

dopant_roles.basis: In the Fe74Co10-xCrxB16 series cobalt and chromium are exchanged against each other at a fixed total, so the 2.5 at.% cobalt here is one point of a substitution series rather than dilute doping. There is no lattice site to occupy in a glass.

note: [ref 2] returns three computed Cr-Fe-B orderings, none with an ICSD reference, and they describe crystalline phases this material does not have. They are what the ribbons would crystallise into on annealing, which is a different question from what was measured. Measured window 312-602 K; the upper end approaches the crystallisation range of these glasses, so the transport above about 550 K may be of a partly relaxed or devitrified ribbon and that is worth checking against the paper.

basis: One composition, (Fe57Cr15Nb4B20Si4)0.12(Y2O3)0.2(ZrO2)0.8, as films, and the curator transcribes the paper directly: composite coating (amorphous plus ceramic) and amorphous coating. The paper is on a novel Fe-based amorphous composite coating with a unique interfacial layer. The material is an iron-based metallic glass sprayed together with yttria-stabilised zirconia, so it has two constituents and one of them has no structure at all.

dopant_roles.basis: The Y2O3 in the ceramic fraction is the stabiliser of yttria-stabilised zirconia: yttrium takes the zirconium site of the fluorite lattice and the charge imbalance creates the oxygen vacancies that keep the cubic phase down to room temperature. It is a constituent of the ceramic, not an impurity in the glass.
Part of the Fe-Cr-Nb-B-Si glass-forming composition, present to widen the supercooled liquid region. No lattice site in an amorphous phase.
The other metalloid of the glass former, alongside boron.

note: is_mixed is true here, unlike the B4C-TiB2 and ZrB2-SiC hosts earlier in this chunk, because the two constituents are not matrix and additive: the composition is 88 mol per cent ceramic and the paper is about the interface between the two. The ceramic fraction is 0.8 ZrO2 to 0.2 Y2O3, which is far more yttria than the usual 3 to 8 mol per cent and would give a fully cubic fluorite. Neither reference returns an entry, which is expected for a sprayed coating. Measured window 374-873 K.

basis: One composition, CuBO2, two samples, and the first paper names the structure in its title: the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of delafossite CuBO2. CuBO2 is the boron member of the CuMO2 delafossite series, layers of linearly coordinated Cu(I) between BO2 layers, and it is studied as a transparent p-type conductor for exactly that reason.
note: The reference disagrees and is not followed. [ref 2] returns no CuBO2 at all: its five entries for the host are Cu(BO2)2, Cu2BO6, two boracites and Cu3(BO3)2, which are copper(II) borates, a different oxidation state and a different structural family. CuBO2 is the smallest delafossite and has been hard to make phase-pure, which is a plausible reason for its absence from the 2019 snapshot, and the paper reports making it. No mp_id is recorded rather than borrowing one of the borate entries. The rhombohedral 3R polytype R-3m is assumed; delafossites also occur as the 2H polytype P6_3/mmc and stage 2 should take the choice from the pattern. Measured window 306-973 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [166], ICSD-backed references for this host report [122, 62, 219]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, DyB12, two samples, from two papers on the transition and rare-earth element dodecaborides and on the thermal conductivity of metal dodecaborides with the UB12 structure. The second title states the structure. [ref 2] gives DyB12 Fm-3m (225) mp-1103476 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference, the cubic cage of B12 cuboctahedra around the rare earth.
note: [ref 2] ranks DyB4 and DyB2 above DyB12 on ICSD counts, but those are the neighbouring borides of the same binary rather than polymorphs of this composition, and the composition names the dodecaboride. The robust measured range is 10-67 K while the full span reaches 1025 K; the low-temperature end is where the dodecaboride thermal conductivity peak the second paper is about sits. Rank 1922, B-Ho, is the same pair of papers on the holmium member.

basis: One composition, written PBFDO, and the curator transcribes what it stands for: poly(benzodifurandione). This is the n-type conducting polymer of the 2022 Nature paper on a solution-processed n-type conductor with ultrahigh conductivity, measured again in the printed generator paper. The element set is the polymer backbone and its dopant counterions, not a compound.
note: The host key is an artefact of running an elemental parser over a polymer name: B, F, H, O and P here come from the repeat unit and the tetrafluoroborate-type counterion rather than from a stoichiometric formula, so no element ratio in this host means anything and dopant_roles is left empty rather than guessing at roles for parser output. PBFDO is the current record-holder among n-type organic conductors, which is why it appears twice. Films as well as bulk. Measured window 10-482 K.

basis: One composition, HoB12, two samples, from the same two papers as the dysprosium host at rank 1920, one of which names the UB12 structure in its title. [ref 2] gives HoB12 Fm-3m (225) mp-1104585 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference.
note: The dodecaborides exist only for the smaller rare earths, roughly Tb through Lu plus Y, Zr and U, so Dy and Ho appearing together in one survey is the series being sampled rather than a coincidence. The robust measured range is 10-28 K against a full span to 1033 K; as with the dysprosium host the percentile filter keeps only the low-temperature cluster. Ho is above the split, so dopant_roles is empty.

basis: Two compositions, (K2O)20(B2O3)80 and (K2O)30(B2O3)70, from the paper on the thermal conductivity of molten Li2O-B2O3 and K2O-B2O3 systems, measured between 1073 and 1273 K. These are potassium borate melts and the reported quantity is a liquid thermal conductivity, so there is no crystal structure to assign.
note: The molten_salt entry was written for ionic melts such as molten nitrates. A borate melt is a network liquid, held together by a covalent B-O framework with the alkali modifying it, so the transport mechanism is not the same as in a nitrate melt even though both are liquids. The entry is still the right home in the sense that matters here, that the material has no periodic structure at the measurement temperature, and this is flagged so the v4 review can decide whether network oxide melts deserve their own entry. [ref 2] returns five crystalline potassium borates; none of them is what was measured. Measured window 1073-1273 K.

basis: Two compositions, (Li2O)30(B2O3)70 and (Li2O)20(B2O3)80, from the same paper as the potassium host one rank above, the two halves of one study of molten alkali borates. Measured from 1123 K, far above the liquidus, so the samples are melts.
note: Same caveat as B-K-O: this is a network oxide melt rather than an ionic salt melt. [ref 2] returns well-attested crystalline lithium borates, Li2B4O7 I4_1cd mp-4779 with 23 ICSD references among them, and that entry is a real and much-studied piezoelectric crystal. It is not this sample. This is the failure mode the README describes in the other direction: the reference describes which phases exist in the chemistry, and here none of them exists at the measurement temperature. Measured window 1123-1273 K, full span to 1473 K.

basis: Two compositions, Mo2B5 and MoB4, one sample each, from the 1979 paper on the physical properties of the higher borides of molybdenum and tungsten. They are two adjacent phases of the Mo-B system and the host is mixed. [ref 2] backs both: B5Mo2 R-3m (166) mp-7229 with 4 ICSD references and B4Mo P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1106346 with 3.
note: The split is clean on stoichiometry, one sample each: Mo2B5 to w2b5_type and MoB4 to wb4_type. Both prototypes are proposed in this chunk and cover this host and B-W at rank 1930 together. Confidence is medium because both MP entries sit far above the hull, 0.450 and 0.536, while carrying several ICSD references each; these are long-known refractory phases whose boron sublattices are partially occupied, which an ordered computational cell represents badly. [ref 2] ranks B2Mo R-3m mp-2331 first on 8 references, but MoB2 is a third compound of the binary and not a polymorph of either composition here. Measured window 300-1212 K.

basis: One composition, Mo5SiB2, two bulk samples, from the paper on the electrical and thermal properties of single-crystalline Mo5X3 phases. Mo5SiB2 is the T2 phase of the Mo-Si-B system, the tetragonal Cr5B3 type, and [ref 2] returns exactly one entry for the host, SiB2Mo5 I4/mcm (140) mp-4984 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references.
note: One composition, one reference entry, hull zero and four ICSD references pointing at the same space group is about as clean as this tail gets. Silicon and boron are both above the 5 at.% split and are structural constituents of the T2 phase, so dopant_roles is empty. The T2 phase is a principal constituent of Mo-Si-B ultra-high-temperature alloys, which is why single crystals exist to measure. Measured window 12-1062 K.

basis: Two compositions, NbB2 and (NbB2)87.09(SiC)12.91, from the paper on the effects of SiC and SiC-graphene additions on the mechanical properties and oxidation resistance of niobium diboride. NbB2 is the hexagonal AlB2 type and [ref 2] confirms it: NbB2 P6/mmm (191) mp-450 with 14 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in this chunk.

dopant_roles.basis: Added as SiC particles, the standard oxidation-resistance additive for a diboride ultra-high-temperature ceramic. It forms a separate phase and does not enter the NbB2 lattice.
The carbon of that same SiC addition, plus graphene nanoplatelets in the companion samples.

note: The same composite pattern as B-C-Si-Zr at rank 1910, from the same corner of the ultra-high-temperature ceramics literature, and handled the same way: matrix prototype on the record, additive as the alternative, is_mixed false. One of the two compositions is plain NbB2 with no additive at all. Measured window 303-573 K.

basis: One composition, (TiB2)9.7(ZnO)90.3, from the paper on the preparation and thermoelectric properties of ZnO-TiB2 composites. The matrix is ZnO at 90 mol per cent, which is hexagonal wurtzite, with TiB2 dispersed in it as a conductive second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Present as TiB2 particles added before sintering. Titanium does not substitute into the ZnO lattice here; the boron it is bound to is the rest of the same second phase.

note: This is the Al-O-Zn case the README uses as its warning, in a sharper form. [ref 2] returns only zinc borates for this host, Zn4B6O13 I-43m mp-4812 with 6 ICSD references at the top, and every one of them is a compound that does not exist in this sample. The reference is describing which phases the Zn-B-O chemistry can form; the sample is a mechanical mixture of ZnO and TiB2 that was never meant to react. Boron is about 9 at.% of the formula and so counts as a host element, but all of it is in the second phase, which is why the host key names an oxide-boride that is not a compound. Measured window 179-843 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [217, 61, 161, 29]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, Si92B8, two bulk samples, from the paper on the thermoelectric properties of a Si/SiB3 sub-micro composite prepared by milling. The matrix is elemental silicon in the diamond-cubic structure and the excess boron forms SiB3 particles in it, as the title states.
note: Boron is 8 at.%, above the split, so it is a host element and dopant_roles is empty, but its role is worth stating: the solubility of boron in silicon is far below 8 at.%, so a little of it is a substitutional acceptor in the matrix and the rest is the SiB3 second phase the paper is about. Two alternatives are carried because SiB3 is a boron-icosahedral compound and the taxonomy has two entries in that area, boron_carbide for the B4C-type icosahedron-plus-chain structure and b12x2_alpha_boron for the alpha-rhombohedral derivatives. Which one SiB3 belongs to should be settled in the v4 review rather than guessed here. Neither reference returns a useful entry: [ref 2] offers SiB6 Pm-3m mp-7700 at hull 0.477 and two rare-earth borocarbides at the wrong chemistry entirely. Measured window 286-1069 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Two compositions, W2B5 and WB4, one sample each, from the same 1979 paper on the higher borides of molybdenum and tungsten that supplies B-Mo at rank 1925. The host is mixed in the same way and splits on the same boundary. [ref 2] gives B5W2 R-3m (166) mp-8079 with 1 ICSD reference and B4W P6_3/mmc (194) mp-29651 with 3.
note: Split one sample each: W2B5 to w2b5_type and WB4 to wb4_type. Confidence is medium for the same reason as on the molybdenum side, hull values of 0.547 and 0.599 against real ICSD deposition, which reflects partial boron occupancy rather than instability. [ref 2] ranks BW I4_1/amd mp-7832 and BW2 I4/mcm mp-1113 above both on 5 references each, but those are the lower borides of the binary and neither composition here is one of them. WB4 is separately studied as a superhard material. Measured window 364-1191 K, full span to 1267 K.

basis: Two compositions, Ba0.4Bi0.6Ti0.4Fe0.6O3 and Ba0.6Bi0.4Ti0.6Fe0.4O3, from a paper on the structural evolution and electrical properties of the series. Both are ABO3 with a full A site of Ba and Bi and a full B site of Ti and Fe, which is the (1-x)BaTiO3-xBiFeO3 solid solution, one of the best-known perovskite-perovskite pseudobinaries.
note: No space group is recorded because the symmetry of this series is exactly what the paper set out to determine and it changes across the join: BaTiO3 is tetragonal P4mm at room temperature, BiFeO3 is rhombohedral R3c, and the intermediate compositions pass through a pseudocubic region whose true symmetry is contested. Asserting one cell from the formula would be the error the chunk header warns about. The substitution is coupled and aliovalent, Ba2+ with Ti4+ against Bi3+ with Fe3+, so it is not an isoelectronic axis and solid_solution_axis is left null. [ref 2] returns only two computed orderings, neither ICSD-backed, at compositions that do not match. Measured window 463-543 K.

basis: Two compositions, Ba0.7Bi0.3Ti0.7Mn0.3O3 and Ba0.6Bi0.4Ti0.6Mn0.4O3, from a paper on the synthesis, structural refinement and physical properties of novel perovskites. The same coupled A-site and B-site substitution as the iron host one rank above, with manganese in place of iron: BaTiO3 alloyed with BiMnO3.
note: Space group left null for the same reason as the iron host: the paper is a structural refinement, so the symmetry is its result and not an input. The only reference entry, BaTiMnBiO6 F-43m mp-1227378 at hull 0.166 with no ICSD backing, is a computed rock-salt-ordered double perovskite at a 1-1-1-1 stoichiometry; these compositions are not at that ratio and there is no evidence of B-site ordering, so it is not followed. Manganese is about 6 at.% and titanium 12 at.%, both above the split, so dopant_roles is empty. Measured window 293-383 K.

basis: Two compositions, YBa0.8Ca1.2Cu3O7 and YBaCaCu3O7, as pellets, from the paper on the metal-insulator transition in the YBa2-xCaxCu3O7-d system. The 1-2-3 cation ratio with the calcium sharing the barium total is the YBa2Cu3O7 structure with calcium substituted into it, and the paper names the series.
note: Calcium is at 1.0 and 1.2 per formula unit, roughly 8 at.%, so it is a host element rather than a dopant and dopant_roles is empty; its role is still the point of the paper, since Ca2+ for the trivalent or divalent site is what drives the system across the metal-insulator boundary. Where calcium sits, on the yttrium site or the barium site, is contested in this literature and the nominal formula here puts it on barium. The orthorhombic Pmmm setting is recorded, but calcium substitution drives YBCO towards tetragonal P4/mmm as the chain oxygen disorders, so the setting should come from the paper. [ref 2] returns two computed quinary orderings with no ICSD backing and neither is the 123 structure. Measured window 63-302 K.

basis: Two compositions, BaCa0.33Nb0.42Fe0.25O3 and BaCa0.33Nb0.34Fe0.33O3, from the paper on the role of dopants in fine-tuning the electrical and catalytic properties of these materials. The B site is one third calcium and two thirds pentavalent or trivalent cation, which is the Ba3CaNb2O9 stoichiometry, the 1:2 B-site ordered complex perovskite known as BCN18 and used as a proton conductor. Iron is substituted onto the niobium site in the same series.
note: Confidence is medium because the iron content is high, a quarter to a third of the B site, and heavy substitution of that kind degrades the 1:2 cation order that defines the prototype. At BaCa0.33Nb0.34Fe0.33O3 the niobium no longer outnumbers the calcium two to one and the ordered description may have broken down entirely, which is why perovskite is carried as the alternative rather than as a footnote. Iron sits at exactly 5 at.% of the formula, on the boundary of the host split, so it appears as a host element and dopant_roles is empty even though its role is substitutional on the niobium site. Neither reference returns an entry for this host. Measured window 573-1173 K. Rank 1935 is the same paper and the same family with the iron dilute enough to be a dopant.

basis: Two compositions, BaCa0.33Nb0.5Fe0.17O3 and BaCa0.33Nb0.57Y0.1O3, from the same paper as rank 1934. The Ca:Nb ratio of one to two on a full B site is the Ba3CaNb2O9 (BCN18) 1:2 ordered complex perovskite, and here the substituents are dilute enough that the parent structure is intact. [ref 2] supports it with Ba3CaNb2O9 P-3m1 (164) mp-1214569 at hull 0.000, its only hull-zero entry for the host.

dopant_roles.basis: Acceptor on the pentavalent B site of BCN18. Substituting Fe3+ for Nb5+ creates oxygen vacancies, which is how proton uptake and mixed conduction are tuned in this family, so it is a deliberate dopant rather than an impurity.
The other acceptor in the same series, playing the same aliovalent role. Y3+ is large and could in principle take the calcium position instead; the site should be confirmed in stage 2.

note: The reference entry has no ICSD reference attached in the 2019 snapshot, so the space group rests on the agreement between a hull-zero computed structure and the known 1:2 ordering of BCN18 rather than on deposition. The three other entries returned, Ba5Ca2Nb3O15, Ba8Ca3Nb5O24 and Ba2CaNbO6, are different stoichiometries and none matches the 1:1 A:B ratio of these compositions. Measured window 573-1174 K.

basis: Two orderings of one composition, BaDyCo4O7 and DyBaCo4O7, from two papers on the structural and thermoelectric properties of BaRCo4O7 and the transport of RBaCo4O7 for R = Dy, Ho, Er. The 1-1-4-7 stoichiometry is the swedenborgite structure, corner-sharing CoO4 tetrahedra in alternating kagome and triangular layers, and [ref 2] confirms it: BaDyCo4O7 P6_3mc (186) mp-18804 with 2 ICSD references.
note: The two composition strings differ only in the order of Ba and Dy and are the same material, so this host is one compound. [ref 2] ranks BaDy2CoO5 Pnma mp-19364 above it on equal ICSD references and hull zero, but that is the 1-2-1-5 brownmillerite-adjacent compound of the same ternary, not a polymorph of BaDyCo4O7, and the composition here is unambiguous. The swedenborgite cobaltites undergo a structural distortion below roughly 300 K in several members; the measured window starts at 300 K, so nothing is recorded as crossed, but the low end sits right at it. Measured window 300-997 K.

basis: Two orderings of one composition, BaErCo4O7 and ErBaCo4O7, from the same two papers as the dysprosium host at rank 1936, which cover R = Dy, Ho and Er together. The stoichiometry is the swedenborgite one and the erbium member sits in the middle of the series the papers survey.
note: The reference does not cover the compound and is not followed. [ref 2] returns only BaEr2CoO5 in two settings, Pnma mp-25677 and Immm mp-18746, which is a different stoichiometry; there is no BaErCo4O7 entry in the snapshot at all, even though the isostructural dysprosium compound is present as mp-18804. That is an absence in the reference rather than evidence against the phase, and the assignment rests on the composition and on the companion host one rank above. No mp_id is recorded rather than borrowing the 1-2-1-5 entry. Measured window 297-995 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62, 71]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Two orderings of one composition, NdBaFeCoO5 and NdBaCoFeO5, from papers on the synthesis and properties of LnBaFeCoO5+d and on its electrochemical performance as a cathode. LnBaB2O5+d with a rare earth and barium in a 1:1 ratio is the A-site ordered double perovskite: Ln and Ba alternate in layers along c and the oxygen vacancies order in the lanthanide layer.
note: The O5+d oxygen content is the doping variable of this family, not a fixed stoichiometry, and the taxonomy entry says so; the curator has recorded it as O5 exactly, so no oxygen non-stoichiometry can be read out of the composition string here. Iron and cobalt share the B site in equal parts and both are above the split, so dopant_roles is empty. The P4/mmm setting is recorded at medium confidence because the cell depends on how the vacancies order, which varies with delta and gives the Pmmm superstructure in many members. [ref 2] returns three computed orderings, none ICSD-backed, at stoichiometries that do not match. Measured window 300-1068 K, full span to 1122 K.

basis: Two compositions, SmBaFeCoO5 and SmBa0.75Ca0.25CoFeO5, from the same LnBaFeCoO5+d synthesis paper as the neodymium host at rank 1938 and from a paper on a Ca and Fe co-doped SmBaCo2O5+d cathode. Same A-site ordered double perovskite, with samarium as the lanthanide.

dopant_roles.basis: SmBa0.75Ca0.25CoFeO5 replaces a quarter of the barium in the A-site ordered layer with the smaller isovalent Ca2+. The second paper names it as one half of a Ca and Fe co-doping strategy, so it is deliberate substitution on the barium layer rather than an impurity, and being isovalent it acts through size and lattice strain rather than by adding carriers.

note: Neither reference returns any entry for this host, so both the prototype and the P4/mmm setting rest on the composition and the papers. The same caveat as rank 1938 applies to the oxygen content: O5+d is the real formula and the recorded O5 hides the doping variable. Measured window 146-1023 K, full span to 1073 K.

basis: Two compositions, Y0.5Ca0.5BaCo3.2Ga0.8O7 and Y0.5Ca0.4In0.1BaCo3.2Ga0.8O7, from the paper on the phase stability and electrochemical performance of the Y0.5Ca0.5-xInxBaCo3.2Ga0.8O7 series. The 1-1-4-7 stoichiometry with a mixed R site and gallium sharing the tetrahedral site is the swedenborgite YBaCo4O7 structure with the standard gallium stabilisation.

dopant_roles.basis: Yttrium is the parent R-site cation of YBaCo4O7 itself, not a dopant, and it only falls below the 5 at.% split because half of that site is calcium and the formula unit has thirteen atoms. Stage 3 should not compute a doping level for it.

Ca2+ for Y3+ on the R site is aliovalent and oxidises the cobalt, which together with the gallium substitution is what stabilises the swedenborgite phase against decomposition. It is half the R site, so it is an end member rather than a dilute dopant.
The x in Y0.5Ca0.5-xInxBaCo3.2Ga0.8O7, the variable the paper scans. It replaces calcium on the R site.

note: Gallium at 0.8 per formula unit is above the split and so is not in dopant_roles, but its role matters: Ga3+ substitutes for Co on the tetrahedral framework site and is added precisely to widen the temperature range over which the swedenborgite structure survives, which is what the phase-stability paper is about. The only reference entry, Ba6Ga2Co11O26 P-3m1 mp-642047 at hull 0.076 with no ICSD backing, is a computed structure at a different stoichiometry and is not followed. Measured window 572-1172 K.

basis: Two compositions, La0.25Ba0.749Sb0.001Co0.5Ti0.5O3 and La0.35Ba0.6494Sb0.0006Co0.7Ti0.3O3, from a paper on resistivity control by solid-state reaction of perovskite-type oxides. Both are ABO3 with lanthanum and barium on the A site and cobalt and titanium sharing the B site, a simple substituted perovskite.

dopant_roles.basis: Present at 0.001 and 0.0006 per formula unit, a few parts in ten thousand. At that level it can only be a deliberate donor dopant, Sb5+ on the tetravalent titanium site, which is consistent with a paper about controlling resistivity. The A site sums to 0.999 and 0.9994 in the two formulas, exactly the amount of the antimony, so the curator may have transcribed it as an A-site substituent instead; the site should be checked in stage 2.

note: The cobalt to titanium ratio is 1:1 and 7:3, neither of which is the 1:2 that would give the ordered complex perovskite, and there is no evidence of rock-salt ordering either, so the disordered aristotype is the right description. The cubic Pm-3m setting is recorded at medium confidence since substituted cobaltite-titanates of this kind commonly show octahedral tilting. Neither reference returns an entry. Samples are rod-shaped. Measured window 296-513 K.

basis: Two compositions, La0.2Ba0.8Co0.7Nb0.3O3 and La0.2Ba0.8Co0.6Nb0.4O3, sintered pellets, from a paper on the effect of Nb5+ content on the high-temperature properties of a mixed conductor. Full A site of Ba and La, full B site of Co and Nb: a disordered substituted perovskite.

dopant_roles.basis: La3+ for Ba2+ on the A site is a donor substitution, fixed at 0.2 across both compositions while the niobium is scanned. It sets the average cobalt valence together with the niobium content.

note: Both B-site ordered alternatives are carried because [ref 2] returns them and the chemistry can reach them: Ba3Nb2CoO9 P-3m1 mp-600864 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference is the 1:2 ordered compound and Ba2NbCoO6 Fm-3m mp-1228382 is the 1:1 double perovskite. Neither matches these compositions. Both ordered phases are cobalt-poor relative to niobium or exactly equal to it, while these samples are cobalt-rich at 7:3 and 6:4, which is the wrong side of both ordering ratios, so the disordered cubic phase is the reasonable reading. Measured window 299-1177 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [164]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, Ba3CoSb2O9, two single crystals measured along the ab plane and the c axis, from the paper on thermal conductivity in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Ba3CoSb2O9. [ref 2] returns exactly one entry for the host, Ba3CoSb2O9 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-19337 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which is the 6H hexagonal perovskite: face-sharing Sb2O9 dimers alternating with CoO6 octahedra that form the triangular lattice the paper is about.
note: The A3BB2O9 formula is the same 1:2 B-site stoichiometry as the BCN18 hosts at ranks 1934 and 1935, and that entry is carried as the alternative, but the two realise it differently: BCN18 keeps a fully corner-sharing network in the trigonal P-3m1 setting, while here the large barium and the Sb5+ dimer force face sharing and the 6H stack. The distinction is the one the hexagonal_perovskite_polytype entry was written for. This is a quantum magnetism sample rather than a thermoelectric one, measured from 11 to 99 K on single crystals in two orientations to separate magnon from phonon heat transport, and stage 2 should not expect carrier transport.

basis: Two compositions, Ba8.12Cu3.05Ga7.19Ge35.64 and Ba8.11Cu4.12Ga4.06Ge37.71, from the paper on the effect of copper substitution on the thermoelectric properties of germanium clathrates. Eight barium guests against a framework of roughly 46 atoms is the type-I clathrate formula, and the refined occupancies show it is a measured composition rather than a nominal one.
note: Copper and gallium are both above the split and both are framework substituents on the germanium sublattice; between them they set the electron count, which is what the paper varies. The barium excess above 8 is refinement scatter rather than an extra guest, since the type-I cage count is fixed at eight. No reference entry for the host. The measured range collapses to a single point at 300 K, so only room-temperature values are in this host.

basis: Two compositions, Ba8Cu3Zn3Ge40 and Ba8Cu3Zn3Ga1Ge39, from a theoretical and experimental study of Ba8-based clathrates. Eight barium guests on a 46-atom framework is the type-I formula, with copper and zinc substituted into the germanium framework.

dopant_roles.basis: One gallium per 54-atom formula unit, below the split but doing the same job as the copper and zinc above it: taking a germanium framework site and changing the Zintl electron count. It is a framework substituent, not an interstitial or a dilute impurity, and stage 3 should read its fraction against the framework rather than the whole formula.

note: The only reference entry, Ba4Zn2CuGe20 Ama2 mp-1229043 at hull 0.000 with no ICSD backing, is a computed ordering at half the formula size and in a polar orthorhombic cell. It is not the type-I clathrate and is not followed; ordered computational cells of substituted clathrates routinely come out in low symmetry because the substituents have to be placed somewhere. Measured window 323-474 K.

basis: Two compositions, Ba0.7K0.3Cu2Se2 and Ba0.65K0.35Cu2Se2, from the paper on enhancing the thermoelectric properties of BaCu2Se2 by potassium doping. BaCu2Se2 is named in the taxonomy entry as a representative material of the ACu2X2 type, the orthorhombic alpha-BaCu2S2 structure with puckered CuSe layers between the large cations.
note: Potassium is the dopant the paper is named for, K+ for Ba2+ on the cation site, which is an acceptor substitution that raises the hole concentration. It sits at about 6 at.% of the formula and so is above the host split and does not appear in dopant_roles; stage 3 should still treat it as the doping variable rather than as a host constituent, which is the kind of case the 5 at.% threshold gets wrong for a compound with only five atoms per formula unit. The alpha and beta forms of ACu2X2, Pnma and the I4/mmm ThCr2Si2 type, are both known and the choice is synthesis-dependent, which is why the space group is medium confidence and thcr2si2_122 is carried as the alternative; the taxonomy entry raises the same caveat. Neither reference returns an entry. Measured window 301-836 K.

basis: One composition, Li1.625YBa2Cu3O7, two samples, from the paper on the influence of lithium on the electronic structure of YBa2Cu3O7-d. The YBa2Cu3O7 part of the formula is the 123 cuprate exactly, and the paper treats it as YBCO with lithium added.
note: The lithium content is the problem with this record. At 1.625 per formula unit lithium would be about 12 at.%, more than half a cation site, and no 123 phase survives that much substitution; the literature on Li in YBCO works at a few per cent on the chain-copper site. The number is more likely a series label or a different quantity transcribed into the formula than a real stoichiometry. Because it is above the split it is treated as a host element and does not appear in dopant_roles, which understates the problem, so it is flagged here instead. The prototype itself is not in doubt. [ref 2] returns two computed quinary orderings with no ICSD backing and neither is a 123 structure. Measured window 77-297 K, liquid nitrogen to room temperature, which is the range a superconductivity paper of this vintage would use.
annotator_note: A composition worth checking against the paper before stage 3 computes anything from it: Li1.625 in a 123 cuprate is not a physically reasonable site occupancy, and whatever stage 3 derives from that fraction will be wrong even though the structure assignment is right.

basis: One composition, BaCuSi4O10, two single crystals, from the paper on the heat capacity, thermal expansion and heat transport in Han Blue. The reference agrees once the formula is rewritten: [ref 2] gives BaCu(Si2O5)2, which is BaCuSi4O10, in P4/ncc (130) as mp-6127 with 4 ICSD references, the gillespite structure of silicate sheets around isolated square-planar CuO4 units.
note: Han Blue is the ancient Chinese pigment and CaCuSi4O10 is the Egyptian Blue analogue; both are now studied for the isolated Cu(II) square lattice rather than the colour, and that lattice is why a heat transport measurement was made on single crystals. The other four entries [ref 2] returns are different barium copper silicates of the same ternary and none matches the composition. The compound is an insulator with no carrier transport for stage 2 to model. Measured window 11-295 K.

basis: Two compositions, SmBaSrCu3O7 and SmBa1.2Sr0.8Cu3O7, from the paper on the thermoelectric power of the SmBa2-xSrxCu3O7-d system. The 1-2-3 cation ratio with samarium on the rare-earth site and strontium sharing the barium total is the 123 cuprate, and the paper names the series.
note: Strontium is at 0.8 and 1.0 per formula unit, roughly 6 to 8 at.%, so it is a host element and dopant_roles is empty. Its role is isovalent substitution for barium: Sr2+ is smaller, so the substitution compresses the cell and changes the chain oxygen ordering rather than adding carriers, which is what shifts the thermopower the paper measures. Samarium sits on the yttrium site of the parent structure. [ref 2] returns four computed quinary orderings, all without ICSD backing and none of them the 123 structure, so no mp_id is recorded. Measured window 81-290 K.

basis: Two compositions, Y0.4Pr0.6Ba1.2Sr0.8Cu3O7 and Y0.4Pr0.6BaSrCu3O7, from the paper on inducing superconductivity in the Y0.4Pr0.6Ba2-xSrxCu3O7 system. The 1-2-3 cation ratio is the 123 cuprate, here with the rare-earth site shared between yttrium and praseodymium and the barium site between barium and strontium.

dopant_roles.basis: Yttrium is the parent rare-earth cation of the 123 structure, not a dopant. It falls below the 5 at.% split only because the formula unit has thirteen atoms and the site is shared with praseodymium, so stage 3 should not compute a doping level for it.

Praseodymium on the yttrium site is the substitution that suppresses superconductivity in YBCO, uniquely among the rare earths, and this paper is about recovering it by strontium substitution on the barium site. At 0.6 of the site it is an end member of the Y1-xPrxBa2Cu3O7 series rather than a dilute dopant.

note: Strontium is above the split at about 6 to 8 at.% and so is absent from dopant_roles, but it is the variable the paper scans: Sr2+ for Ba2+ is isovalent and acts through size. This host and rank 1949 are the same experiment on two different rare earths, and both are 123 cuprates measured below room temperature for superconductivity rather than for thermoelectric performance. [ref 2] returns five barium strontium cuprates and cobalt-cuprates, none of them a 123 phase and none ICSD-backed, so no mp_id is recorded. Measured window 10-275 K.

basis: Two compositions, YbBaSrCu3O7 and YbBa1.2Sr0.8Cu3O7, from the paper on structure and superconductivity in LnBa2-xSrxCu3O7 with Ln = Yb. The 1-2-3 cation ratio with ytterbium on the rare-earth site and strontium sharing the barium total is the 123 cuprate, and the paper names the series.
note: This is the third host in as many ranks running the same experiment on a different rare earth: chunk 039 ranks 1949 and 1950 were the samarium and the yttrium-praseodymium versions of LnBa2-xSrxCu3O7. Strontium is at 0.8 to 1.0 per formula unit, roughly 6 to 8 at.%, so it is treated as a host element and dopant_roles is empty; its role is isovalent substitution for barium, acting through ionic size on the chain oxygen ordering rather than by adding carriers. [ref 2] returns one computed quinary ordering, Ba8Sr2Yb5(Cu3O7)5 in Pm (6) at hull 0.036 with no ICSD backing. That formula is five 123 units with the cations distributed, so the reference is describing the same chemistry, but a P1-derived ordering of a disordered site is not the structure and no mp_id is carried. Measured window 55-259 K, which is a superconductivity measurement rather than a thermoelectric one.

basis: One composition, BaCu2SnSe4, two bulk samples, and the second paper is titled origins of ultralow thermal conductivity in 1-2-1-4 quaternary selenides. BaCu2SnSe4 is named as a representative material of the ba_1214_chalcogenide entry proposed from chunk 019 for the silver analogue.
note: [ref 1] carries BaCu2SnSe4 as PRIMARY in Ama2 (40) at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference and, unusually for TEDesignLab, an mp_id, mp-12364. That is a different setting from the I222 (23) the same reference gives for BaAg2SnSe4, which is what the proposed entry warned about when it said the setting has to be confirmed per compound; the copper and silver members are not in the same space group. The first paper, an exploratory synthesis of new heavy main group chalcogenides, is where the compound was first made, and the second measures it, so both samples are the same material at two dates. The large barium sits in cavities of the Cu2SnSe4 tetrahedral framework and its rattling-like motion is what the ultralow thermal conductivity is attributed to.

basis: One composition, BaCu5.9SeTe6, ten curves from the paper on the thermoelectric properties of the quaternary chalcogenides BaCu5.9STe6 and BaCu5.9SeTe6. No taxonomy entry covers a BaCu6Te6Q quaternary, so bacu6te6q_type is proposed for it rather than forcing it into the Ba3Cu14-dTe12 polytelluride entry, which has a different Cu:Te ratio and no third chalcogen.
note: The confidence is medium because the compound is identified with certainty but its structure is not. [ref 2] returns BaCu6Te6Se as P2 (3) at hull 0.053 with no ICSD reference, which is the composition but almost certainly not the symmetry: a P2 cell of a quaternary telluride is what Materials Project produces when it orders a partially occupied site by hand. No space group is recorded and no mp_id is carried, and stage 2 has to take the structure from the paper. The copper deficiency in Cu5.9 is intrinsic to the phase rather than a doping choice, and it is where the low lattice thermal conductivity is thought to come from, so stage 3 should read the missing 0.1 Cu as non-stoichiometry on a host site. Measured window 303-618 K.

basis: Two compositions from the paper titled thermoelectric properties of double perovskite (Sr, Ba)2(Fe, Mn)(Mo, V)O6, which states the structure in its title. The A site is shared by strontium and barium, the B site by iron and manganese and the B-prime site by molybdenum and vanadium, which is the A2BB-prime O6 rock-salt cation ordering.

dopant_roles.basis: Vanadium sits on the B-prime site with molybdenum at a fixed 0.2 to 0.8 ratio across both compositions. It is isovalent with neither Mo6+ nor Mo5+ in general, so it acts on the electron count of the Mo 4d conduction band that carries the transport, which is what the paper varies.

note: Neither reference returns anything for this six-element host. Sr2FeMoO6 is the well-known half-metallic parent of this family and the manganese and vanadium here are substitutions on its two B sites. The space group is recorded as the ideal cubic Fm-3m (225) at medium confidence: these compounds very commonly order into tetragonal I4/m or monoclinic P2_1/n depending on tolerance factor and on how complete the B-site ordering is, and a mixed A site of Sr and Ba makes that more likely rather than less. Measured window 373-973 K.
annotator_note: The transcribed stoichiometries do not balance and should be checked against the paper before stage 3 computes anything from them. Sr2BaFeMnMo0.8V0.2O6 has three A cations to 2.8 B cations, and Sr1.4Ba0.6Fe1MnMo0.8V0.2O6 has two A to three B, where a double perovskite needs two of each. The neighbouring host at rank 1955, from the same paper, is written correctly as Sr1.4Ba0.6Fe0.8Mn0.2Mo0.8V0.2O6, which suggests the iron and manganese subscripts here are the ones that went astray. The prototype is not in doubt; the numbers are.

basis: Two compositions, Sr1.4Ba0.6Fe0.8Mn0.2Mo0.8V0.2O6 and Sr1.4Ba0.6Fe0.9Mn0.1Mo0.8V0.2O6, from the paper titled thermoelectric properties of double perovskite (Sr, Ba)2(Fe, Mn)(Mo, V)O6. Both balance exactly as A2BB-prime O6 with 2.0 A cations, 1.0 on the B site and 1.0 on the B-prime site.

dopant_roles.basis: Manganese at 0.1 and 0.2 per formula unit shares the B site with iron. It is the variable this pair of samples scans, and it changes the B-site magnetic moment and the degree of B-site ordering rather than adding carriers directly.

Vanadium is fixed at 0.2 on the B-prime site alongside molybdenum in every composition from this paper, so it is part of the parent formula being studied rather than a dilute dopant, and it acts on the Mo 4d band filling.

note: This host and rank 1954 are the same paper and the same series, separated only because the manganese fraction falls below the 5 at.% split in these two compositions and above it in the other two. Sr2FeMoO6 is the parent. Neither reference returns anything for this five-element host. The cubic Fm-3m setting is the ideal aristotype and is recorded at medium confidence; tetragonal I4/m and monoclinic P2_1/n are the usual real symmetries of this family and depend on tolerance factor and B-site order. Measured window 374-972 K.

basis: Two compositions of the series the paper names, (SrBa)1-xPrx(CuTi)0.2Fe0.8O3-d. A single ABO3 formula with the A site shared by strontium, barium and praseodymium and the B site mostly iron with a fifth of it copper and titanium, which is a simple perovskite with heavily substituted sites rather than an ordered double perovskite.

dopant_roles.basis: Copper at 0.2 per formula unit is on the B site with iron and titanium. In a ferrite of this kind Cu2+ is an acceptor relative to Fe3+ and also lowers the sintering temperature, and the paper treats CuTi as a fixed pair.

Titanium at 0.2 per formula unit is on the B site. Ti4+ is a donor relative to Fe3+ and is paired with the copper so that the two roughly compensate, which is a common way to stabilise the perovskite while tuning the oxygen vacancy content.

note: The paper is a solid-state-ionics study of a cathode material with an oxygen deficiency d, so the oxygen content is a variable and the real formula is oxygen-deficient; the vacancies can order into a brownmillerite at high deficiency, which is why brownmillerite is worth a look in stage 2 if the paper reports a superstructure. The transcribed compositions do not balance well, with 1.6 A cations to 1.2 B cations in both, so the subscripts are approximate. The praseodymium content is what the series scans and it is above the split, so it is a host element here. Neither reference returns anything. Measured window 573-1073 K.

basis: Two compositions from two different papers, Sm1.875Ba3.125Fe5O15 and Sm0.5Ba0.5FeO3. Both reduce to the same (Sm,Ba)FeO3 perovskite stoichiometry, the first written over five formula units because the first paper describes it as a quintuple perovskite, the second as a single unit.
note: Confidence is medium because the perovskite framework is certain but the cation order over it is not, and that is what separates the two entries considered. A quintuple perovskite, the term the first paper uses, means the rare earth and barium order into a five-layer sequence along one axis, which is a layered A-site-ordered perovskite rather than a random one; SmBaFe2O5 and the LnBaCo2O5 family are the archetypes, hence layered_double_perovskite as the alternative. Sm0.5Ba0.5FeO3 from the second paper is the same 1:1 cation ratio and may be either ordered or disordered depending on synthesis. Both papers are SOFC cathode studies, so the samples are oxygen-deficient by design and the deficiency is the variable. I do not follow [ref 2] here: it gives Ba2Sm2Fe4O11 in Cmmm (65) at hull 0.020, which is an oxygen-vacancy-ordered orthorhombic phase at O2.75 per formula unit, well below the O3 the compositions state, so it describes a more reduced member of the chemistry than the samples as transcribed. Measured window 316-1124 K.

basis: One composition, La0.7Ba0.3Ti0.5Mn0.4Ni0.1O3, from a paper on A-site cation influences on the performance, structure and conductivity of a perovskite. A single ABO3 unit with lanthanum and barium on the A site and titanium, manganese and nickel sharing the B site.

dopant_roles.basis: Nickel at 0.1 per formula unit shares the B site with titanium and manganese. Ni2+ or Ni3+ against Ti4+ is an acceptor substitution and, in an SOFC anode material of this kind, is also there to produce catalytically active metal on reduction.

note: Three species on the B site with a mixed A site means the true symmetry is almost certainly a tilted orthorhombic or rhombohedral variant rather than the ideal cubic aristotype recorded here; the cubic setting is the family label, not a measured space group. The paper is a fuel-cell electrode study, so the sample is measured hot, 723-1123 K, and oxygen non-stoichiometry is expected. Neither reference returns anything for this five-element host.

basis: One composition written explicitly as a two-phase mixture, (Pr0.67Ba0.33MnO3)0.7(PdO)0.3, from a paper on the magnetotransport, magnetization and thermoelectric power of Pr2/3Ba1/3MnO3 with PdO added. At 30 per cent the palladium oxide is a major second phase, not a dispersion, so a single prototype would be wrong.
note: The matrix is the hole-doped manganite Pr2/3Ba1/3MnO3, a perovskite that is orthorhombic or rhombohedral rather than cubic and that carries a ferromagnetic metal to paramagnetic insulator transition inside the measured 12-285 K window. That transition is magnetic and electronic, not structural, so it is not recorded in phases, but it is why the thermopower is measured over that range and stage 2 should not read any anomaly in it as a phase change. The second phase, PdO, is tetragonal P4_2/mmc in the cooperite arrangement of square-planar PdO4 units and has no taxonomy entry; it is not proposed as one, because it is here as an additive and a single occurrence. Neither reference returns anything for this five-element host.

basis: One composition, BaMoO3, and the first paper is titled thermoelectric properties of perovskite type barium molybdate. BaMoO3 is the cubic ABO3 perovskite of corner-sharing MoO6 octahedra, and it is a metallic conductor, which is why it was measured.

other_polymorphs.note: BaMoO4, the scheelite that [ref 2] ranks first in this host with 9 ICSD references at hull 0.000. It is not a polymorph of BaMoO3 but a different, fully oxidised compound, and it is what BaMoO3 turns into if heated in air. Recorded here so the reference disagreement is visible rather than dropped.

note: I do not follow the ranking in [ref 2], and the reason is worth stating. The reference lists BaMoO4 in I4_1/a first because it is the best-attested barium molybdate in ICSD, but the composition measured is BaMoO3, which the same reference also carries, as Pm-3m (221) mp-19322 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference. The one-oxygen difference is the whole physics: BaMoO4 is a wide-gap scheelite insulator and BaMoO3 is a metallic d1 perovskite. Composition decides here and the reference is describing a different compound. The second paper, on strontium ruthenium oxide, is the same group measuring the analogous SrRuO3 perovskite, which supports reading this as a deliberate perovskite-metal study. The measured window, 285-1275 K in air or an inert atmosphere, is where oxidation to BaMoO4 becomes a real risk, and that is worth checking in the paper. Measured window 285-1275 K.

basis: Two compositions from two papers, one sample each. Ba3Os2O9 is a 6H hexagonal perovskite built on face-sharing Os2O9 dimers, and the paper reports its synthesis, crystal structure and magnetic properties. BaOsO3 is the cubic corner-sharing perovskite and its paper is titled high-pressure synthesis of 5d cubic perovskite BaOsO3 at 17 GPa. Two structures, one per sample, so the host is mixed.
note: The split is by composition and is clean: Ba3Os2O9 to the hexagonal polytype, BaOsO3 to perovskite with mp-781625 in Pm-3m (221), which [ref 2] carries at hull 0.086 with one ICSD reference. The high hull for a compound that exists is the signature of a high-pressure phase, and the title confirms it was made at 17 GPa, so the cubic perovskite here is a recovered high-pressure product rather than the phase a normal synthesis would give. The 6H setting P6_3/mmc (194) is the usual one for a Ba3M2O9 face-sharing-dimer polytype, recorded at medium confidence since 6H compounds of this family sometimes refine in lower symmetry. I do not use the entry [ref 2] ranks first, BaOsO9 in Pnma at hull 0.541, which is not a plausible composition. These are 5d magnetism studies measured from 19 K, not thermoelectric optimisation.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [194], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62, 221]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Two compositions of the series the paper names, La-doped Ba1-xSrxSnO3, written (Ba0.6Sr0.4)0.95La0.05SnO3 and (Ba0.4Sr0.6)0.95La0.05SnO3. BaSnO3 and SrSnO3 are both ABO3 stannate perovskites of corner-sharing SnO6 octahedra and form a continuous solid solution.

dopant_roles.basis: La3+ on the divalent A site of a stannate is the standard n-type donor, and it is what the paper is titled for. It is fixed at 0.05 in both compositions while the Ba to Sr ratio is the variable, so the doping level is constant and the band structure is what is being tuned.

note: BaSnO3 is cubic Pm-3m and SrSnO3 is the tilted orthorhombic Pbnm variant, so the true symmetry across this series depends on x and passes through a tilt transition somewhere in the middle of the composition range; at Ba0.6 and Ba0.4 the samples sit either side of where that is usually placed. That is a composition-driven symmetry change within one prototype, not a thermal transition, so it is not recorded in phases, but stage 2 should not expect both samples in the same space group. The cubic aristotype is recorded at medium confidence for that reason. Five computed Ba-Sr orderings are returned by [ref 2], none ICSD-backed and all of them artificial supercells of the solid solution, so no mp_id is carried. Measured window 368-1069 K.

basis: Two compositions, (Ba0.9Sm0.1)(Zr0.52Ti0.48)O3 and (Ba0.8Sm0.2)(Zr0.52Ti0.48)O3, from a paper on samarium-substituted barium zirconium titanate. BaZrO3 and BaTiO3 are both ABO3 perovskites and BZT is their B-site solid solution, here with samarium on the A site.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm3+ on the divalent Ba site is a donor and is the substitution the paper scans, from 0.1 to 0.2. In a titanate it is compensated by cation vacancies or by Ti3+, and it is what produces the negative temperature coefficient of resistance the paper reports.

note: [ref 2] gives Ba2ZrTiO6 in Fm-3m (225) at hull 0.005 with two ICSD references, which is the 1:1 B-site-ordered double perovskite. I do not carry that as the prototype: at Zr 0.52 to Ti 0.48 the ratio is right for it, but BZT is normally a disordered solid solution rather than a rock-salt-ordered double perovskite, and the paper describes a nanocrystalline ceramic, where long-range B-site ordering is unlikely. If the paper reports a superlattice reflection, double_perovskite would be the better call and this record should be revisited. Barium titanate itself has a tetragonal-to-cubic transition near 393 K that would sit inside the measured 312-672 K window, but zirconium substitution at this level suppresses it into a diffuse relaxor crossover rather than a sharp structural change, so no phases are recorded. Measured window 312-672 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [225]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, BaUO3, and both papers are titled for it, one on its thermoelectric and one on its thermophysical properties. BaUO3 is the ABO3 perovskite of corner-sharing UO6 octahedra with U4+ on the B site.
note: The reference and the composition disagree and I follow the composition. [ref 2] ranks BaUO4 in Pbcm (57) first with five ICSD references, and returns four further barium uranates, but not BaUO3 itself, which is absent from the 2019 snapshot.
