BaUO4 is the layered U6+ uranate and is a different compound, not a polymorph: it is what BaUO3 oxidises to, and since these are nuclear fuel studies measured to 1255 K the oxidation state of the sample is the thing to check in the papers. No mp_id is carried because the reference has no entry for the composition measured. The cubic aristotype is recorded at medium confidence; BaUO3 is usually described as slightly distorted orthorhombic through octahedral tilting. This host is in the set because uranate thermophysical data was digitised, not because anyone proposed it as a thermoelectric.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [57, 74, 141]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition, BaWO4, two polycrystals, from a paper on the thermal and mechanical properties of BaWO4 crystal. BaWO4 is the scheelite structure of isolated WO4 tetrahedra with eight-coordinate barium, and [ref 2] attests it directly as I4_1/a (88) mp-19048 with 11 ICSD references at hull 0.000, the best-attested entry in the host.
note: The scheelite structure type was missing from the taxonomy and is proposed here as scheelite_awo4; the gap was already noticed from chunk 030, where the discriminate_from block of sc2w3o12_type says in as many words that scheelite is not in the taxonomy. [ref 1] returns Ba3W2O9 in R-3c, a different compound of the same ternary and not the composition measured, so TEDesignLab does not settle this one and Materials Project does. BaWO4 is a wide-gap insulator grown as a Raman laser and scintillator crystal; this sample is in the set because thermal conductivity was measured on it, and stage 2 should expect no carrier transport to model. Measured window 297-563 K.

basis: One composition, BaOs4Sb12, which is the filled skutterudite formula exactly: an Os4Sb12 framework of corner-sharing OsSb6 octahedra with barium in the icosahedral void. [ref 2] confirms it as Ba(Sb3Os)4 in Im-3 (204) mp-1106056 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference.
note: Barium is a host constituent here rather than a filler fraction: the cage is fully occupied at one Ba per Os4Sb12, so there is no filling fraction for stage 3 to compute. The paper is about the roles of spin fluctuations and rattling in the magnetic and thermoelectric properties of this family, and the rattling in question is the barium motion inside the cage, which is exactly the physics the filled_skutterudite entry is for. Measured mostly from 10 to 286 K, which is the low-temperature regime these filled osmium and ruthenium antimonides are studied in; the full span reaches 482 K.

basis: One composition, BaRu4Sb12, the ruthenium analogue of the previous host and the filled skutterudite formula exactly. [ref 2] confirms it as Ba(Sb3Ru)4 in Im-3 (204) mp-9976 at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references, and it comes from the same paper on spin fluctuations and rattling.
note: The cage is fully filled at one barium per Ru4Sb12, so there is no filling fraction to compute. The second entry [ref 2] returns, Ba(SbRu)2 in I4/mmm at hull 0.031, is the ThCr2Si2-type 122 phase of the same ternary and a different compound; it is not a polymorph of the skutterudite and is not recorded as one. BaRu4Sb12 is a superconductor below about 1 K, well outside the 12-292 K window measured here. Measured window 12-292 K, full span to 498 K.

basis: One composition, Bi6Cu2Se3BrO6, two bulk samples. The formula is two BiCuSeO units plus two Bi2O2Se units with one selenium replaced by bromine, which is the commensurate BiCuSeO and Bi2O2Se intergrowth rather than either parent, so bicuseo_bi2o2se_intergrowth is proposed rather than filing it under zrcusias_1111.
note: Confidence is medium because the stoichiometric argument is strong and independent verification is absent. [ref 2] returns Cu3BiSe2BrO8 mp-628637, a copper-rich oxyselenide bromide of the same five elements and not the composition measured, so no mp_id and no space group are carried and stage 2 must read the structure out of the paper. The bromine is the point of the compound: BiCuSeO is a p-type conductor and this paper reports an n-type material, which is what substituting Br- for Se2- on the chalcogen site would do. Bromine is above the 5 at.% split so it does not appear in dopant_roles, but stage 3 should treat it as the doping variable rather than as a host constituent. Measured window 295-875 K, which is the usual BiCuSeO range.

basis: One composition, BiTeBr, and both papers name it against BiTeI. It is the polar layered trihalide-chalcogenide structure, P3m1 (156), with Te-Bi-Br trilayers stacked so that the two anion layers alternate, and [ref 2] carries BiTeBr in P3m1 mp-33723 at hull 0.000.

other_polymorphs.note: Bi(TeBr2)2 in P-1, which [ref 2] ranks first on its one ICSD reference. It is a different compound of the same ternary, not a polymorph of BiTeBr, and the ranking here is an artefact of BiTeBr having no ICSD entry in the snapshot.

note: This is a case where the PRIMARY flag has to be argued with rather than followed: the reference ranks Bi(TeBr2)2 above BiTeBr because ICSD reference counts drive the ranking and BiTeBr carries none in the snapshot, but the compositions are unambiguous and the mp-33723 entry sits at hull 0.000. These compounds are studied for the giant Rashba spin splitting that follows from the polar stacking, and the single crystals measured from 10 to 296 K here are galvanomagnetic and thermoelectric characterisations of that state.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [156], ICSD-backed references for this host report [2]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: One composition written as a two-component mixture, (Bi2Te3)67.58(C4H2NH)32.42, and the curator detail names polypyrrole with its CAS number and gives the masses. At a third of the material by formula the polymer is a genuine second phase, so an inorganic prototype alone would be wrong.
note: The inorganic component is ordinary tetradymite Bi2Te3 in R-3m and the organic component is polypyrrole, an amorphous or semicrystalline conducting polymer with no crystal structure to resolve; the paper is about the interface between them, so neither phase can be dropped. The curator detail says the sample was sintered at 400 degrees, which is above where polypyrrole decomposes, so what survives in the measured sample may be carbonised rather than intact polymer. That is a question for the paper and it is flagged rather than decided. The hydrogen and nitrogen in the host key are the polymer backbone, not impurities, which is the opposite of the usual reading of H and N in this data set. Measured window 299-476 K.

basis: Two compositions, Bi2(Se0.15Te0.85)3C0.6 and Bi2Te2.4Se0.6C0.3, and both curator details name carbon nanotubes added to Bi2(Se,Te)3. The matrix is n-type Bi2Te3-xSex, which is tetradymite; the carbon is a dispersed additive and does not change the host structure.

dopant_roles.basis: Carbon nanotubes dispersed in the matrix, named as such in both curator details. They are a deliberate second phase added to scatter phonons and are not in the tetradymite lattice, so no site or level should be computed for them.

note: Carbon is above the 5 at.% split, at about 11 per cent of the formula in the first composition, so it appears in the host key and pulls these samples out of the main Bi-Se-Te host. That is the composite-additive case the project README warns about, and the rule applied here is the same one: the additive does not relabel the host. It is recorded in dopant_roles anyway, even though it is a host-key element, because leaving it out would let stage 3 treat it as a constituent. Selenium sits on the tellurium site of the tetradymite as an isoelectronic alloying component in both compositions and is above the split. Measured window 296-545 K.

basis: One composition, Bi2(Te0.91Se0.09)3SiC, from a review of the progress from thermoelectric bulk to nanomaterials in Bi2Te3. The matrix is Bi2Te3-xSex, a tetradymite, and SiC is a dispersed ceramic second phase written as a unit in the formula.

dopant_roles.basis: Se on the Te site at 0.09 of the anion sublattice, the standard n-type Bi2Te3-xSex alloy composition. It is isovalent, so it tunes the gap and the lattice thermal conductivity rather than adding carriers, and the fraction to record is the anion-site one, not the atomic one.

note: Silicon and carbon are in the host key only because SiC is written at one formula unit per Bi2Te3, which is a large nominal addition; whether the real sample contains that much SiC or whether the formula is nominal is worth checking in the paper. Either way the SiC particles are a separate cubic or hexagonal ceramic phase, covered by sic_polytype if stage 2 needs to name them, and they do not enter the tetradymite lattice. The matrix assignment is not affected. Measured window 303-469 K.

basis: Two compositions from two papers, one sample each. Ca14AlBi11 is the A14MPn11 structure exactly, the bismuth analogue of Ca14AlSb11 named in the taxonomy entry, and its paper calls it a new Zintl phase from earth-abundant elements. Ca16Bi11 is a different compound with two more calcium and no group 13 element, so the host holds two prototypes.

dopant_roles.basis: Aluminium is the M cation of the 14-1-11 structure, at the centre of the AlBi4 tetrahedron, so it is a host constituent and not a dopant. It falls below the 5 at.% split only because the formula unit has 26 atoms and there is one of it, and stage 3 should not compute a doping level for it.

note: The split is by composition and is clean: Ca14AlBi11 to yb14mnsb11_zintl, Ca16Bi11 to the proposed ca16sb11_type. The two are related by replacing the AlBi4 tetrahedron with two more calcium, which is a different structure rather than a substitution, so forcing one label would be wrong. Neither reference covers either composition: [ref 1] returns Ca2Bi, which is not present in this host at all, and [ref 2] returns Ca5Bi3, Ca11Bi10 and CaBi2, all different calcium bismuthides. Ca11Bi10 in particular is close enough in stoichiometry to Ca16Bi11 to be mistaken for it and is a different structure type. No mp_id is carried. The I4_1/acd (142) setting on the phase is the standard one for A14MPn11 and is recorded at medium confidence since the bismuthide has not been checked against a reference here. Measured window 12-941 K, which spans two very different papers.

basis: One composition, (Bi0.5Pb0.5)2(Ca0.8Pr0.2)2Co2O7, which is the Bi-Ca-Co-O misfit cobaltite written as its ideal formula: a rock-salt [Bi2Ca2O4] block alternating with CoO2 layers in the ratio the paper works with, with lead on the bismuth site and praseodymium on the calcium site.

dopant_roles.basis: Praseodymium at 0.2 of the calcium site in the rock-salt block. A trivalent cation on a divalent site reduces the hole count in the CoO2 layer, which is the standard way this family is tuned, and the paper is about developing Bi-based cobaltites.

note: This is an incommensurate composite: the rock-salt block and the CoO2 layer have different in-plane periods along one axis and there is no single periodic cell, which is why the misfit_cobaltite entry is flagged for special handling in stage 2 and why no space group or mp_id is recorded. Lead is above the 5 at.% split and is a host element; its role is substitution for bismuth in the rock-salt block, which is the usual way this family is made single-phase, so stage 3 should not read it as a dopant either. Neither reference returns anything for this five-element host. Measured window 107-954 K.

basis: Two compositions, Bi2Sr1.3La0.9Ca0.8Cu2O8 and Bi2Sr1.1La0.8CaCu2O8, from a paper on the in-plane thermoelectric properties of heavily underdoped high-temperature superconductor single crystals. Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8 with lanthanum sharing the strontium site is Bi-2212 exactly.
note: Lanthanum is above the 5 at.% split, so dopant_roles is empty, but it is the doping variable the paper is built on: La3+ for Sr2+ removes holes from the CuO2 planes and is how Bi-2212 is driven into the heavily underdoped regime these crystals are grown for. The curator details give the intended cation ratios directly and they match the formulas. The I4/mmm setting is the idealised average structure and is recorded at medium confidence; real Bi-2212 has an incommensurate supermodulation along b that is usually refined in an orthorhombic or superspace setting. Neither reference returns anything for this six-element host. Measured window 12-210 K.

basis: Two compositions, Bi0.8Ca0.2CuSeO and Bi0.7Ca0.3CuSeO, and the paper is on the oxidation states of elements in pure and Ca-doped BiCuSeO thermoelectrics. BiCuSeO is the ZrCuSiAs 1111 structure of alternating Bi2O2 and Cu2Se2 layers.
note: Calcium is at 0.2 and 0.3 per formula unit, five to seven per cent of the atoms, so it sits above the split and dopant_roles is empty; its role is substitution for bismuth in the Bi2O2 layer, where a divalent cation on a trivalent site is an acceptor and raises the hole concentration in the conducting Cu2Se2 layer. That is the doping variable of the paper and stage 3 should treat it as one rather than as a host constituent. Neither reference returns anything for this host even though BiCuSeO itself is well covered elsewhere in the set. Measured window 120-929 K.

basis: One composition, CaMnBi2, two single crystals, from a paper on the large magnetothermopower effect in the Dirac materials (Sr/Ca)MnBi2. CaMnBi2 is named as a representative material of the hfcusi2_112_square_net entry proposed from chunk 022, and [ref 2] carries CaMnBi2 in P4/nmm (129) mp-611153.

other_polymorphs.note: Ca(MnBi)2 in P-3m1 at hull 0.365, the trigonal CaAl2Si2-type arrangement of the same formula. It is a distinct compound rather than a phase this sample passes through, and the very high hull makes it unlikely to be what was grown.

note: The reference ranks Ca9Mn4Bi9 first on two ICSD references, but that is a different compound of the ternary and not the composition measured; the entry that matters, mp-611153, is the composition exactly and in the P4/nmm setting the 112 family is known in. Its hull of 0.179 should not be read as instability, since this is the family the proposed entry was written for and the compounds are grown as single crystals routinely. The bismuth square net between the MnBi slabs carries the Dirac dispersion the paper measures, and it is exactly the feature that keeps this out of zrcusias_1111. Measured window 11-346 K.

basis: One composition, Bi2Sr2Ca0.2Cd0.8Cu2O8, from a paper on the structural characterization and transport properties of an HTc Bi2Sr2 cuprate. The 2-2-1-2 cation ratio with cadmium taking most of the calcium site is Bi-2212 with a substituted spacer layer.

dopant_roles.basis: Calcium is the parent cation of the 2212 spacer site, not a dopant. It reads as a minor element here only because cadmium has taken 0.8 of its site, so stage 3 should treat the pair as one site shared between Cd and Ca rather than computing a calcium doping level.

note: The interesting substitution is the one that is above the split: Cd2+ for Ca2+ is isovalent and larger, so it acts on the spacing between the CuO2 planes rather than on the carrier count, and the paper pairs a structural characterisation with transport for that reason. Whether 0.8 cadmium really enters the spacer site or whether some segregates is the kind of thing the structural part of the paper would settle. The I4/mmm setting is the idealised average structure at medium confidence, as for rank 1975; real 2212 carries an incommensurate supermodulation. Neither reference returns anything. Measured window 10-200 K, full span to 300 K.

basis: Two compositions, (Ce0.75La0.25)3Bi4Pt3 and (Ce0.5La0.5)3Bi4Pt3, single crystals, from a paper on substitutional effects on the electronic transport of a Kondo semiconductor. Ce3Bi4Pt3 is the cubic Th3P4-derived Y3Au3Sb4-type lattice and is the archetypal Kondo insulator of this family.
note: The 3-4-3 stoichiometry is the ordered ternary variant of Th3P4, in which the platinum fills the sites that are vacant in the binary; the taxonomy keeps that variant as y3au3sb4 and the two entries describe the same I-43d framework, so both are recorded, th3p4 as the prototype and y3au3sb4 as the alternative. Stage 2 should use the ternary description for the structure file. Lanthanum substitutes for cerium at 0.25 and 0.5 of the rare-earth site and is the variable of the paper: it dilutes the cerium 4f lattice and closes the Kondo gap, so these are two points on a doping series and not two materials. Both are above the split, so dopant_roles is empty. Neither reference returns anything. Measured window 15-299 K.

basis: Two compositions, Gd12Co5Bi and Gd12Co5.3Bi, from an inorganic chemistry paper reporting the compounds themselves. The 12-5-1 stoichiometry is a structure type of its own in the R12Co5Bi series and no taxonomy entry covers it, so r12co5bi_type is proposed rather than forcing it into a Zintl or Laves entry.
note: Confidence is medium because the compound and its stoichiometry are certain from the paper while the space group is not established here, and neither reference returns anything for this ternary. The pair differs only in the cobalt content, 5.0 against 5.3, which is partial occupancy of a cobalt site rather than doping, and stage 3 should read the excess as non-stoichiometry on a host site. The gadolinium sublattice orders magnetically, so an anomaly in the thermopower inside the measured 12-874 K window is more likely magnetic than structural and should not be read as a phase transition without evidence. The paper title was not captured in the chunk file, only the DOI.

basis: One composition, LaBiMn1.33Co0.67O6.02, from a paper on the enhancement of ferromagnetism by cobalt and nickel substitution in a perovskite. Two A cations and two B cations per six oxygens is the A2BB-prime O6 double perovskite formula, here La and Bi on the A site and Mn and Co sharing the B sites.
note: Confidence is medium and the reason is the B-site ratio. La2MnCoO6 is the ordered ferromagnetic double perovskite this composition is closest to, and its ordering is what the ferromagnetism in the title comes from, but here the ratio is 1.33 to 0.67 rather than 1 to 1, which cannot be fully rock-salt ordered; the real material is likely partially ordered, with antisite disorder that is itself the variable such papers report. If it turns out to be disordered it is a plain perovskite, hence the alternative. The P2_1/n setting is the usual one for a monoclinic ordered manganite-cobaltite and is recorded at low confidence. Bismuth on the A site with its lone pair is what drives the tilting and can push the structure off any ideal setting. Neither reference returns anything. Measured window 112-320 K, full span to 400 K, which is a magnetism measurement.

basis: One composition written as a two-phase mixture, (La0.7Sr0.3CoO3)85(SrBi4Ti4O15)15, and the paper is titled for a colossal Seebeck coefficient in an Aurivillius phase and perovskite oxide composite. The two components are named in the formula and neither can be dropped.
note: The 85 per cent component is La0.7Sr0.3CoO3, the rhombohedral R-3c metallic cobaltite perovskite, and the 15 per cent component is SrBi4Ti4O15, an m = 4 Aurivillius phase of Bi2O2 layers alternating with four-octahedron perovskite blocks and an insulator. The point of the paper is the interface between a metal and a ferroelectric insulator, so the composite is the material and a single prototype would destroy the claim. This is the same reading as rank 1959 and rank 1970: a second phase at tens of per cent is a composite, while a few per cent dispersion leaves the host label alone. Neither reference returns anything for this six-element host. Measured window 297-805 K.

basis: One composition, BiCoO3, from a paper on the synthesis, characterization and thermoelectric properties of an electrospun material. BiCoO3 is an ABO3 perovskite, but a strongly tetragonal PbTiO3-type one rather than a cubic or tilted orthorhombic one, with square-pyramidal cobalt and a very large c to a ratio.
note: Two things hold the confidence down. First, bulk BiCoO3 is normally made under high pressure, and this sample is electrospun, so what the fibres actually contain may be a different or poorly crystalline phase; the P4mm (99) setting recorded here is the known high-pressure structure, not a measured result. Second, [ref 2] agrees only loosely: CoBiO3 in Pnma at hull 0.117 is the entry with the single ICSD reference, and the four other entries are bismuth-rich cobalt bismuthates at other stoichiometries, none of them the tetragonal phase. The curator details say one sample is boron-undoped and one boron-doped, but no boron appears in either composition string, so the boron content is missing from the transcription rather than absent from the experiment. Measured window 10-295 K.
annotator_note: The boron the curator records is not in the composition strings, so the two samples are indistinguishable in this data set even though the paper treats them as a doped and an undoped pair. Anything computed per composition will silently merge them.

basis: Two compositions, CsPbBi3Te6 and CsPb2Bi3Te7, one sample each, from the paper that reports both as new thermoelectric compounds with low-dimensional structures. They are caesium-separated rocksalt-type slabs of Pb, Bi and Te and are not the CsBi4Te6 structure, which is held together by Bi-Bi bonds, so csmbi3te6_layered is proposed for the pair.
note: Confidence is medium because the compounds are certain and the structures are not resolved here: neither reference returns either composition, so there is no space group and no mp_id, and stage 2 must take both from the paper. The two stoichiometries differ by one PbTe layer in the slab, so they are consecutive members of a homologous series rather than two unrelated phases, and a stage 2 that resolves one should be able to build the other. They are grouped as one prototype for that reason rather than split. The measured window, 79-350 K, is the regime CsBi4Te6 is optimised for, which is why the family was made at all.

basis: Two compositions that are the same material written two ways, Bi0.80Pb0.20OCuSe and Bi0.80Pb0.20CuSeO, from two papers on the synthesis and thermoelectric properties of lead-substituted BiCuSeO. The 1111 structure of alternating Bi2O2 and Cu2Se2 layers is unchanged by the substitution.
note: Lead is above the 5 at.% split and so does not appear in dopant_roles, but it is the doping variable: Pb2+ for Bi3+ in the Bi2O2 layer is an acceptor and is the standard route to high hole concentrations in BiCuSeO, which is what both papers are about. Stage 3 should treat it as such. [ref 2] returns Cu4Bi3Pb(SeO)4 mp-1225836 in I4mm at hull 0.000, which is Bi0.75Pb0.25CuSeO written as an ordered supercell; it is the right chemistry but it is a computed ordering of a random site with no ICSD backing, so no mp_id is carried and stage 2 should resolve the parent BiCuSeO structure instead. The two composition strings differ only in the order the elements are written and should be merged downstream. Measured window 100-673 K, full span to 873 K.

basis: Two compositions built on PbBi4Te7, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of cation-substituted solid solutions. PbBi4Te7 is a member of the (PbTe)m(Bi2Te3)n homologous series, one rocksalt PbTe layer between Bi2Te3 quintuple layers, which is what homologous_tetradymite covers.

dopant_roles.basis: Cadmium at 0.02 and 0.04 per formula unit is the cation substitution the paper is titled for. A divalent cation on the trivalent bismuth site is an acceptor, and at this level it is dilute doping rather than alloying.

note: Confidence is medium because of the copper, not the structure. Neither reference returns anything for this quaternary, and no temperature range is recorded for these samples at all, which is unusual and suggests the curves are sparse. The P-3m1 setting is the usual one for PbBi4Te7 and is recorded at medium confidence.
annotator_note: The copper content is almost certainly a transcription error and should be checked before stage 3 uses it. Both compositions read (PbBi3.96Cd0.04Te7)0.999Cu1, which puts copper at about eight per cent of the atoms, more than the lead. The 0.999 multiplier on the bracket points at an intended 0.001 of copper, that is a tenth of a per cent dopant, which is the level at which copper is actually added to these tellurides. As written, copper is a host element and the record treats it as one, which is wrong if the intended formula was (PbBi3.96Cd0.04Te7)0.999Cu0.001.

basis: Two compositions, Cu0.36Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 and Cu0.6Bi2Te2.7Se0.3, from a paper on the transport properties of copper nanoprecipitates embedded in Bi2Te2.7Se0.3. The matrix is the standard n-type Bi2Te3-xSex tetradymite and the copper is a deliberate second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: The paper title says nanoprecipitates, so the copper is metallic inclusions rather than dissolved in the lattice. It is above the 5 at.% split and is recorded here anyway so that stage 3 does not compute a doping level from it.

note: Some copper almost certainly does dissolve: copper intercalates readily between the quintuple layers of Bi2Te3 and acts as a donor there, so the real material is likely a mixture of intercalated copper and metallic precipitates, and the split between the two is what the paper would have to settle. The role is recorded as the second phase the title names, with the intercalation noted here rather than asserted. Selenium at 0.3 of the anion site is the standard n-type alloy composition and is above the split. Neither reference returns anything for this quaternary. Measured window 301-484 K.

basis: Two compositions, ErNiSb0.8Bi0.2 and ErNiSb0.4Bi0.6, from a paper on the observed properties and electronic structure of RNiSb compounds. RNiSb is the MgAgAs half-Heusler, and bismuth simply shares the pnictogen site with antimony.
note: Bismuth is at 0.2 and 0.6 of the pnictogen site, far above the split, so dopant_roles is empty; its role is isoelectronic substitution for antimony, which tunes the gap and scatters phonons without changing the electron count. The chunk file prints no solid-solution axis line for this host, but Sb and Bi share one site here and the two compositions sit at opposite ends of it, so stage 3 should treat the parent compound as composition-dependent rather than fixed. The erbium 4f moments order at low temperature and the measurement runs from 15 K, so magnetic rather than structural anomalies are expected in the curves. Neither reference returns anything for this quaternary. Measured window 15-298 K.

basis: Two compositions, Bi1.7Er0.3Se3 and Bi1.6Er0.4Se3, from a paper on decoupling the Seebeck coefficient and the electrical conductivity. Both are Bi2Se3 with erbium on part of the bismuth site, and Bi2Se3 is the R-3m tetradymite quintuple-layer structure.
note: Erbium is at 0.3 and 0.4 per formula unit, six to eight per cent of the atoms, so it is above the split and dopant_roles is empty. Its role is isovalent substitution for Bi3+ on the cation site, which adds local moments and scatters phonons rather than adding carriers; at this level it is more likely to be at the solubility limit than in true solid solution, so a second phase is worth checking for in the paper. Bi2Se3 itself is missing its ambient phase from the 2019 reference snapshot, which the chunk header warns about, and nothing is returned for this ternary here. Measured window 297-480 K.

basis: Two compositions built on SmMg2Bi2, from a paper on achieving high-performance p-type SmMg2Bi2 thermoelectrics. The 1-2-2 formula with an alkaline-earth-like rare earth is the trigonal CaAl2Si2 structure of corrugated Mg2Bi2 slabs separated by the large cation.
note: All three rare earths, samarium, ytterbium and europium, share the single large-cation site and all are above the split, so dopant_roles is empty. Their role is not doping but entropy: the paper is about mixing the cation site to lower the lattice thermal conductivity, and the three compositions listed are two points on that mixing series. Europium and ytterbium are divalent in this structure while samarium may be mixed-valent, which is a real question for the carrier count and one the paper would address. The bismuth deficit in Bi1.99 is intentional non-stoichiometry on the anion site rather than a rounding artefact. Neither reference returns anything for this five-element host. Measured window 305-778 K.

basis: Two compositions, LaO0.75F0.25BiS2 and LaO0.5F0.5BiS2, from a paper on the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of novel layered bismuth sulphides. This is the REO1-xFxBiS2 formula archetype of the taxonomy entry exactly, with LaOBiS2 as the parent.
note: Fluorine is at 0.25 and 0.5 of the oxygen site, well above the split, so dopant_roles is empty, but it is the doping variable of the whole family: F- for O2- in the LaO blocking layer donates electrons into the BiS2 layers and turns an insulator into a metal and a superconductor. Stage 3 should treat it that way rather than as a host constituent, which is the same case the taxonomy already records for F in LaFeAsO1-xFx. [ref 2] returns two computed quinary orderings, La2Bi2S4OF and La4Bi4S8O3F, neither ICSD-backed and both artificial orderings of the O and F site, so no mp_id is carried. Measured window 23-738 K, which is unusually wide for this family and spans both the superconducting regime and a high-temperature thermoelectric measurement.

basis: One composition, La0.5Sm0.5O0.5F0.5BiS2, from a paper on the enhancement of superconductivity in La1-xSmxO0.5F0.5BiS2. The same REO1-xFxBiS2 layered bismuth sulphide as rank 1991, with the rare-earth site shared equally between lanthanum and samarium.
note: Samarium substitution for lanthanum is isovalent and works through chemical pressure: the smaller rare earth compresses the blocking layer and raises the superconducting transition temperature, which is what the paper reports. Both rare earths are above the split so dopant_roles is empty, and fluorine at half the oxygen site is again the electron-doping variable rather than a host constituent. This host and rank 1994 are the two ends of the same series from the same paper, separated only by which rare earth falls below the split. No measured range is recorded for these samples and no reference returns anything for this six-element host.

basis: Two compositions, LaO0.6F0.4BiSe2 and LaO0.5F0.5BiSe2, from a paper on the synthesis and physical properties of LaOBiSe2 and its fluorine-substituted forms. LaOBiSe2 is the selenide analogue of LaOBiS2 and is isostructural with it in P4/nmm.
note: The taxonomy entry is written for the sulphide, CeOBiS2 and LaOBiS2, with the archetype REO1-xFxBiS2, so recording a selenide against it is a small extension rather than an exact match; the layer topology and space group are the same and the selenide is always described as the BiS2-type analogue, so it does not warrant a separate entry. If a reviewer disagrees, the fix is to widen the chalcogen in the existing entry rather than to split it. Fluorine at 0.4 and 0.5 of the oxygen site is the electron-doping variable, above the split, so dopant_roles is empty. Neither reference returns anything. Measured window 16-299 K.

basis: One composition, La0.2Sm0.8O0.5F0.5BiS2, from the same paper on La1-xSmxO0.5F0.5BiS2 as rank 1992. The REO1-xFxBiS2 layered bismuth sulphide, here samarium-rich.

dopant_roles.basis: Lanthanum at 0.2 of the rare-earth site, the dilute end of the La1-xSmxO0.5F0.5BiS2 series. It is isovalent with samarium, so it acts through ionic size on the blocking layer rather than on the carrier count, and the fraction that matters is its share of the rare-earth site, not of the whole formula.

note: This host exists separately from rank 1992 only because lanthanum falls below the 5 at.% split at x = 0.2 while samarium does not, which is the sublattice-versus-formula problem the project README describes: the rare-earth site is one fifth of the atoms, so a fifth of that site reads as four per cent of the formula. The two records are one series and should be read together. No measured range is recorded for these samples and no reference returns anything for this five-element host.

basis: Two compositions, Mn50Fe5Bi45 and Mn47Fe8Bi45, from a paper on the structural, magnetic and electron transport properties of MnBi:Fe thin films. At roughly 1:1 Mn to Bi the phase is MnBi, which is the hexagonal NiAs structure, with iron added.
note: Iron is at five and eight per cent of the atoms, so it is a host element here and dopant_roles is empty; its role is substitution for manganese in the NiAs lattice, which is what the paper varies, though in a thin film some of it may also sit as a separate iron-rich phase. MnBi has a well-known low-temperature to high-temperature phase change near 630 K, above which it is a distorted NiAs, but the measurement runs from 13 to 290 K and does not approach it, so nothing is recorded in phases. The samples are thin films, so the phase actually formed depends on deposition and anneal rather than on the bulk phase diagram alone. Neither reference returns anything for this ternary.

basis: Two compositions written as a Bi0.88Sb0.12 alloy with barium hexaferrite added, Bi0.88Sb0.12(BaFe12O19)0.04 and the 0.025 version, from a paper on percolation conduction in a hybrid thermoelectric material. A hexaferrite formula unit carries 32 atoms, so even at 0.04 it is more than half the atoms in the string, and the paper is about conduction through the mixture.

dopant_roles.basis: Barium is present only as the large cation of the BaFe12O19 particles, which are a separate magnetic oxide phase dispersed in the bismuth-antimony matrix. It is not in the matrix lattice and no doping level should be computed for it.

note: The matrix is Bi0.88Sb0.12, the A7 rhombohedral bismuth-antimony alloy that is the classic low-temperature thermoelectric, and the second phase is M-type barium hexaferrite, an insulating hard magnet. The word percolation in the title is the reason this is a composite rather than a doped alloy: the transport is through a mixture whose connectivity is the variable. By mass the ferrite is roughly a fifth of the sample. I do not use [ref 2], which returns Fe2BiSbO7 in Imma at hull 0.314, a computed pyrochlore-like quaternary oxide that is neither phase present. Measured window 10-341 K, which is the range Bi-Sb alloys are used in.

basis: Two compositions given in atomic per cent, Bi35.34Se57.33Fe7.33 and Bi33.87Se56.49Fe9.63, from a paper on enhancing the thermopower and tuning the resistivity in Bi2Se3 with iron. Both are Bi2Se3 at the 40:60 cation to anion ratio with iron added, and Bi2Se3 is the R-3m tetradymite.
note: Iron is at 7 and 10 at.%, above the split, so dopant_roles is empty. Its role in Bi2Se3 is the interesting question and the paper is built on it: iron can substitute for bismuth in the quintuple layer or intercalate into the van der Waals gap, and the two give different carrier effects and different magnetism. At these levels part of it is likely a second phase as well. Stage 2 should not assume a single site. Bi2Se3 is one of the compounds whose ambient phase is missing from the 2019 reference snapshot, and nothing is returned for this ternary here. Measured window 12-300 K.

basis: Two compositions, Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 with Ga2O3 at 0.15 and 0.23 formula units, from a paper on the effect of Ga2O3 nanoparticle dispersion on the microstructure and thermoelectric properties. The matrix is Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3, the workhorse p-type tetradymite, and the oxide is a dispersed additive.

dopant_roles.basis: Gallium is present only as Ga2O3 nanoparticles dispersed in the matrix, which the paper title states. It is above the 5 at.% split and is recorded here anyway so that stage 3 does not read it as a substitutional dopant on the antimony site.
Oxygen belongs to the same Ga2O3 particles. This is the one case in this chunk where oxygen is neither a host constituent nor milling residue but a named additive.

note: Ga2O3 is about three per cent of the sample by mass even at 0.23 formula units, so this is a nanoparticle dispersion rather than a composite, and the host label stays with the matrix. That is the rule the project README sets out for additives, and it is the opposite call from rank 1996, where the second phase is a fifth of the mass and the paper is about percolation through it. The dispersed phase is beta-Ga2O3 if stage 2 needs to name it. Bismuth and antimony share the cation site as an isoelectronic solid solution at the fixed workhorse ratio. Neither reference returns anything for this five-element host. Measured window 299-501 K.

basis: Two compositions from two papers on the same pseudo-binary, (Ga2Te3)0.2(Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3)0.8 and Ga0.4Bi0.5Sb1.1Te3, and the curator detail gives the series as GaxBi0.5Sb1.5-xTe3. Written the second way the gallium sits on the antimony site of the tetradymite matrix, so the host structure is tetradymite in both.
note: Confidence is medium because the two papers describe the same material in two incompatible ways and the data set keeps both. One writes it as a pseudo-binary of Ga2Te3 with Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3, which implies two phases in equilibrium, and the other writes it as gallium substituting for antimony in a single phase. At 20 mol per cent Ga2Te3 a defect-zincblende second phase is quite possible, which is why ga2te3_defect_zincblende is carried as the alternative, but the tetradymite matrix is present either way and dominates the transport, so the host is not marked mixed. If stage 2 finds a second phase in the microstructure images these should be split. Gallium is above the split in both compositions so dopant_roles is empty. Measured window 316-497 K.

basis: Two compositions, Ho2BiO3 and Ho2Sn0.2Bi0.8O3, from a review of the crystal chemistry of the rare-earth pnictide oxides (RE,Ca)mPnnOm with Pn = Sb or Bi. These are fluorite-like Ho2O2 layers alternating with a square net of bismuth, not a bismuth oxide, and no taxonomy entry covers that, so re2o2pn_square_net is proposed for it.

dopant_roles.basis: Tin at 0.2 of the bismuth site enters the pnictogen square net. Substituting a group 14 element into a group 15 square net changes the electron count of the net directly, which is the carrier-tuning knob in this family rather than a conventional acceptor on a cation site.

note: The reference supports the structure but not the stoichiometry, and I record the disagreement rather than resolving it: [ref 2] gives Ho2BiO2 in I4/mmm (139) mp-1067937 at hull 0.000 with three ICSD references, which is the square-net oxide bismuthide, while both compositions here are written with three oxygens. Ho2BiO3 with all the bismuth in a square net does not balance, so either the transcription carries an extra oxygen or the material is something else. No mp_id is carried for that reason and the I4/mmm setting is recorded at medium confidence from the reference rather than from the compositions. The alternative reading, that this is a holmium-stabilised cubic bismuth oxide, is ruled out by the paper, which is a pnictide-oxide crystal chemistry review and treats the bismuth as a pnictide anion rather than as part of the oxide sublattice. Measured window 10-398 K.
annotator_note: Ho2BiO3 as transcribed does not balance for a RE2O2Bi square-net oxide, which needs two oxygens. Worth checking the paper before stage 2 resolves a structure: the choice is between a transcription error in the oxygen count and a genuinely different phase.

basis: Ho2Sb0.6Bi0.4O3 and Ho2Sb0.4Bi0.6O3 come from the same review of the rare-earth pnictide oxides (RE,Ca)mPnnOm with Pn = Sb or Bi that produced the Bi-Ho-O host in chunk 040, and this is the mixed-pnictogen member of it: fluorite-like Ho2O2 layers alternating with a flat square net that here carries antimony and bismuth together. It is not a rare-earth-stabilised bismuth oxide and not a holmium antimonate, because the pnictogen is the anionic net rather than part of the oxide sublattice.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen square net
solid_solution_axis.note: Both compositions sit near the middle of the Sb-Bi join, so this is an alloyed net rather than a doped one. Antimony and bismuth are both group 15 and both hypervalent in a square net, so the substitution is isoelectronic and tunes the band overlap rather than the carrier count.

note: No reference line is offered for this host, so no mp_id is carried. The same stoichiometry problem as Bi-Ho-O applies and I record it rather than resolving it: a RE2O2Pn square-net compound needs two oxygens, and both compositions here are transcribed with three. Ho2(Sb,Bi)O3 with the pnictogen in a net does not charge balance, so either the oxygen count carries a transcription error or the material is a different phase from the one the paper reviews. Measured window 10-394 K, all of it well below any transition in this family.
annotator_note: Worth settling with the paper before stage 2: the choice is between an extra oxygen in the transcription and a genuinely different compound. The judgement recorded here follows the paper, which treats these as pnictide oxides.

basis: The single composition is transcribed Bi1.4Rh3I9 and is Bi14Rh3I9, the compound the paper names in its title as a weak topological insulator with an ultralow thermal conductivity. That structure is an alternation of a cationic honeycomb slab of edge-sharing RhBi8 cubes with an anionic [Bi2I8]2- spacer, which no taxonomy entry covers, so bi14rh3i9_layered is proposed for it.
note: No reference line is offered for this host, so no mp_id is carried and the C2/m setting is recorded at medium confidence on the phase from the published crystal chemistry rather than from a database entry. Filing this under bii3_layered_trihalide, which is the only other bismuth iodide in the taxonomy, would have been wrong in the way that matters: the iodine here is an insulating spacer and the transport happens in the intermetallic slab. Measured window 10-552 K.

basis: The composition is transcribed Bi0.62K0.38BiO3 but the paper is titled for thermoelectric power of superconducting Ba-K-Bi-O crystals, so the A-site cation is barium and the material is Ba0.62K0.38BiO3, the cubic bismuthate perovskite. At x = 0.38 that composition is past the breathing-distortion boundary and sits in the simple Pm-3m field, which is the prototype recorded.
note: I disagree with the reference line and say so rather than following it. [ref 2] offers only potassium bismuth oxides -- KBiO2 C2/c mp-30988, KBiO3 Pn-3 mp-29799, K8BiO3, K3BiO3, K3BiO4 -- because the host string contains no barium. None of those is what was measured: the paper is on BKBO single crystals, whose superconductivity at 30 K is the reason the thermopower was measured at all. No mp_id is carried for that reason. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the assignment rests on reading the barium back into a composition string that records bismuth twice.
annotator_note: Host key Bi-K-O is itself a consequence of the transcription; the sample belongs with Ba-Bi-K-O. Worth flagging upstream rather than fixing in the ledger.

basis: The single composition is written (La0.7Sr0.3MnO3)86(SrBi4Ti4O15)14 and the paper is titled for a colossal Seebeck coefficient in an Aurivillius phase-perovskite oxide composite. Each sample is two crystalline phases by design -- a manganite perovskite matrix with 14 percent of a four-layer Aurivillius titanate -- so no single prototype describes a sample, which is what composite_multiphase is for.
note: Both constituents are in the taxonomy and both are named as alternatives: La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 is the orthorhombic manganite perovskite and SrBi4Ti4O15 is the m = 4 Aurivillius phase, Bi2O2 layers alternating with perovskite titanate blocks. is_mixed is left false because the two phases are present together in every sample by design and the host cannot be split per composition -- there is only one composition. The interface between the two is the point of the paper, so the composite label is the physically honest one. No reference line is offered for this host. Measured window 299-805 K.

basis: LaPdBi is the only composition and both papers name it directly, the first as a half-Heusler type LaPdBi. The reference agrees: LaBiPd F-43m (216) mp-1206717 at hull 0.000 is the C1b half-Heusler, a filled zincblende with the rare earth and bismuth forming the rocksalt sublattice and palladium in half the tetrahedral holes.
note: LaBiPd2 Immm mp-1093906 sits at hull 1.734 with no ICSD support and is not a competing phase for a 1:1:1 composition; it is not recorded as a polymorph. Measured window 300-958 K with no transition known in this family.

basis: The host holds two different structures at two different stoichiometries. LaBiPt is the C1b half-Heusler, F-43m (216) mp-1018136 at hull 0.000, and La3Bi4Pt3 is the cubic I-43d (220) 3-4-3 phase mp-1189173, which is the Y3Au3Sb4 type -- the same Th3P4-derived framework that makes Ce3Pt3Bi4 a Kondo insulator. One composition each, so the host must be split per composition rather than carrying one label.
note: The split is clean on stoichiometry: 1:1:1 is the half-Heusler, 3:4:3 is the y3au3sb4 entry. Both compositions are single crystals from Kondo-semiconductor studies, so neither is a minority impurity of the other. The prototype_id field carries the half-Heusler because the first paper is titled for LaBiPt, but the record is marked mixed and stage 2 should take the alternative for La3Bi4Pt3. Measured window 13-292 K.

basis: Bi80Li20 and Bi86Li14 are bismuth with lithium added, and the paper is titled for lithium as an interstitial donor in bismuth and bismuth-antimony alloys. The host lattice is therefore the A7 rhombohedral bismuth structure and the lithium enters its interstitial voids; the nominal atomic percentages describe how much lithium was charged, not a line compound.
note: I do not follow the reference line and record why. [ref 2] offers the line compounds Li3Bi Fm-3m mp-23222 and LiBi P4/mmm mp-22902, both at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references, and at 14-20 at.% lithium those are indeed the equilibrium phases -- the solubility of lithium in rhombohedral bismuth is far below that. But the paper measures interstitial lithium donors in a bismuth matrix at 22-297 K, so the nominal charge is not the phase content, and a sample of Li3Bi would not show the bismuth semimetal transport being reported. Confidence is medium for exactly that reason: a second lithium bismuthide phase is likely present alongside the bismuth. Lithium is above the 5 at.% cut and so is a host element with no dopant_roles entry, but its role in the measured material is interstitial.

basis: LuPdBi is the only composition and the first paper is titled for tunable magnetoresistance in half-Heusler RPtBi and RPdBi phases. The reference agrees: LuBiPd F-43m (216) mp-1207185 at hull 0.000 is the C1b half-Heusler, the same 18-electron RPdBi family as LaPdBi, NdPdBi and YPdBi elsewhere in this chunk.
note: Lu5BiPd2 I4/mcm mp-1210532 and the full-Heusler LuBiPd2 Fm-3m mp-1185495 are other compounds in the same chemistry, not polymorphs of the 1:1:1 composition, so neither is recorded in other_polymorphs. Measured window 11-300 K.

basis: Both compositions are on the Mg3Sb2-Mg3Bi2 line with ytterbium on the octahedral cation site: Mg2.725Yb0.4Sb1.5Bi0.5Te0.01 is a Yb-substituted Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 and YbMg2Bi1.58Sb0.4 is the end member YbMg2Bi2. Both are the trigonal CaAl2Si2 type, P-3m1, in which Mg2Pn2 slabs of edge-sharing tetrahedra alternate with a layer of octahedrally coordinated cations, and both papers treat the material as that Zintl phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Te0.01 in Mg2.725Yb0.4Sb1.5Bi0.5Te0.01: tellurium on the pnictogen site is the standard n-type donor for Mg3Sb2-based Zintls, and it is what makes this family work as an n-type leg at all. Its level is tiny by design -- the electron count, not the lattice, is what it changes.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen site of the Mg2Pn2 slab
solid_solution_axis.note: Mg3Sb2 and Mg3Bi2 form a continuous CaAl2Si2 solid solution and the band gap closes towards the bismuth end, so the substitution is isoelectronic band tuning rather than doping. No reference line is offered for this host, so no mp_id is carried per phase.

note: Ytterbium is above the 5 at.% cut in YbMg2Bi1.58Sb0.4, where it is the cation of the end member rather than a dopant, so it carries no dopant_roles entry. Measured window 298-872 K, within which the CaAl2Si2 structure is stable.

basis: SmMg2Bi2 and Sm0.75Yb0.125Eu0.125Mg2Bi1.99 are the trigonal CaAl2Si2-type Zintl phase, Mg2Bi2 slabs of edge-sharing tetrahedra between layers of octahedrally coordinated Sm. The paper is titled for high-performance p-type SmMg2Bi2 and the reference agrees on the structure: Sm(MgBi)2 P-3m1 (164) mp-1068021, one ICSD reference.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm0.75Yb0.125Eu0.125Mg2Bi1.99: ytterbium on the octahedral rare-earth site. YbMg2Bi2 is itself a stable member of this family, so this is alloying on the cation layer to scatter phonons and adjust the gap rather than adding carriers.

The same site as Yb in the same composition, and EuMg2Bi2 is likewise a stable end member. Divalent europium on a site occupied by trivalent samarium can also shift the carrier concentration, which is why the paper pairs the two.

note: The reference entry sits at hull 0.105, which for a rare-earth Zintl in the 2019 dump reflects how poorly these are covered rather than instability -- the compound has an ICSD reference and the paper makes it as a bulk p-type leg. Bi1.99 against Bi2 is a deliberate bismuth deficiency used as the p-type knob, not a parse artefact. Measured window 305-776 K.

basis: Mn55Bi45 and Mn51Fe4Bi45 are both the 1:1 compound MnBi to within the weighing error, and MnBi is the NiAs B8_1 structure, P6_3/mmc, with manganese octahedrally coordinated by bismuth and trigonal-prismatic bismuth. The reference agrees and is well supported: MnBi P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1063902 with 13 ICSD references, by far the best attested entry on the line.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn51Fe4Bi45 is the same MnBi with iron taking manganese sites, which is how the paper on structural, magnetic and electron transport properties of MnBi:Fe films tunes the magnetism. Iron and manganese are neighbours and both sit octahedrally in the NiAs lattice.

note: The hull value of 0.214 for the NiAs phase is a 2019-dump artefact of the magnetic ground state, not a statement that MnBi is unstable; the 13 ICSD references settle it. MnBi decomposes above about 630 K, but the measurement stops at 294 K so nothing is crossed. Mn3Bi, MnBi3 and the Pmma MnBi entry are other compounds or computed cells rather than thermally reached polymorphs of this composition, so other_polymorphs is left empty.

basis: SrMnBi2 single crystals, measured for the large magnetothermopower of the Dirac materials (Sr,Ca)MnBi2. That is the 112 layered pnictide: anti-PbO MnBi slabs alternating with a flat square net of bismuth, and it is the square net that carries the Dirac dispersion the paper is about. The reference agrees on the cell, SrMnBi2 I4/mmm (139) mp-29207, which is the staggered stacking variant of the HfCuSi2 type that strontium and barium members take.
note: The prototype entry gives P4/nmm (129) as the ideal 112 setting, which is what CaMnBi2 takes; SrMnBi2 keeps the same slab-plus-square-net motif but stacks it with a body-centred shift, giving I4/mmm. Same prototype, different stacking, and the reference cell is recorded as such rather than as a disagreement. Measured window 11-320 K; the antiferromagnetic ordering near 290 K is magnetic, not structural, so spans_transition stays false.

basis: MoBi2Te5 is reported only as fibrous nanocrystalline material and thin films in the two papers on this host, and there is no established structure for it: no TEDesignLab entry, no Materials Project line, and no accepted structure type for a molybdenum bismuth telluride at that stoichiometry. Calling it a tetradymite would be an assertion the compositions do not support, so it is parked rather than mislabelled.
note: The two alternatives record what it most plausibly is, without claiming it. A 1:2:5 metal-bismuth-telluride would most naturally be a Bi2Te3 quintuple layer with an inserted MoTe layer, which is the MnBi2Te4 septuple-layer idea and the reason homologous_tetradymite is listed alongside plain tetradymite; the first paper works on MoBi2(Se,Te)5, so the anion site is at least substitutable in the way a tetradymite would be. Against that, molybdenum is not a cation that normally sits in these slabs, and nanocrystalline films are exactly where a metastable or nominal composition can survive. Worth a paper check before stage 2. Measured window 303-497 K.
annotator_note: Low confidence is the finding here, not a gap: this host needs the papers read, not a better guess from the formula.

basis: NdPdBi is the only composition and the first paper is titled for magnetic and transport properties of rare-earth-based half-Heusler phases. The reference agrees: NdBiPd F-43m (216) mp-1008858 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference, the C1b structure of the RPdBi series.
note: One of five RPdBi or RPtBi half-Heusler hosts in this chunk -- La, Lu, Nd, Y with Pd and Yb with Pt -- all assigned the same way and all supported by an F-43m reference entry at hull 0.000. Measured window 11-300 K.

basis: Bi2Rh2O7 is the A2B2O7 pyrochlore composition exactly, and the paper is titled for the impact of an iso-structural template layer on stabilizing pyrochlore Bi2Rh2O7 -- corner-sharing RhO6 octahedra forming the B2O6 network with the Bi2O chains threaded through it.
note: No mp_id is carried and I record why: none of the reference entries is the cubic Fd-3m pyrochlore. Bi12Rh12O41 Imm2 mp-760121 and Bi12Rh12O41 P3m1 mp-686044 are oxygen-deficient cells one oxygen short of the Bi12Rh12O42 that Bi2Rh2O7 expands to, Bi8Rh8O27 R3m is likewise a defect cell, and CeBi2(Rh2O5)3 is a different chemistry altogether. That the snapshot holds only oxygen-deficient variants is itself consistent with the paper, which is about stabilising the stoichiometric pyrochlore on a template layer because it is hard to make. Measured window 30-294 K.

basis: YPdBi is the only composition and both papers are on rare-earth-based Heusler and half-Heusler phases. The reference agrees: YBiPd F-43m (216) mp-1008624 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference, the C1b half-Heusler with yttrium and bismuth on the rocksalt sublattice and palladium in half the tetrahedral holes.
note: full_heusler is listed as an alternative rather than ignored because the reference line also carries YBiPd2 Fm-3m mp-30465 with an ICSD reference, the L2_1 phase that forms when the palladium content doubles. The composition here is 1:1:1, so the half-Heusler is what was measured; the full Heusler is a neighbouring compound and a plausible second phase in an off-stoichiometric ingot, not a polymorph of this composition. Measured window 14-292 K.

basis: YbPtBi and YbBiPt are the same compound written two ways, measured as single crystals for heavy-fermion quantum criticality and semimetallic transport. It is the C1b half-Heusler, and the reference agrees: YbBiPt F-43m (216) mp-1018106 at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references.
note: That YbPtBi is a heavy-fermion system with one of the largest known electronic specific-heat coefficients is a property of its ytterbium f-electrons, not a different structure: it is the same 18-electron half-Heusler lattice as the RPdBi hosts in this chunk. The two composition strings differ only in element order, so the host holds one material and not two. Measured window 12-299 K.

basis: Bi2Te2.3Se0.3S0.4 is Bi2Te3 with part of the tellurium replaced by selenium and sulfur, and the paper studies the Bi2Te3-Bi2Se3-Bi2S3 system for mid-temperature thermoelectrics. The anion count stays at three per two bismuth, so the quintuple-layer tetradymite structure, R-3m, is kept throughout -- this is a solid solution on the chalcogen sublattice, not a new compound.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen sublattice of the quintuple layer, with the substituents preferring the inner site
solid_solution_axis.note: Selenium at 0.3 and sulfur at 0.4 of three anions are 10 and 13 percent of the chalcogen sublattice, which reads as 6 and 8 percent of the whole formula. Both are isoelectronic with tellurium, so they lower the lattice thermal conductivity and widen the gap rather than adding carriers. Bi2S3 is stibnite-structured as an end member, but at this level the sulfur is dissolved in the tetradymite rather than forming it.

note: No reference line is offered for this host, so no mp_id is carried; the R-3m setting is the family structure rather than a database match. Measured window 297-599 K, within which the tetradymite structure is stable.

basis: Both compositions are written (Zn4Sb3)x Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 with x = 0.12 and 0.19, and the paper is titled for the synthesis and thermoelectric properties of Zn4Sb3/Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 bulk nanocomposites. Each sample is therefore two crystalline phases by design -- a tetradymite Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 matrix with beta-Zn4Sb3 dispersed in it -- and no single prototype describes a sample.
note: Both constituents are in the taxonomy and both are named: the matrix is the workhorse p-type tetradymite alloy Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 and the inclusion is the rhombohedral beta-Zn4Sb3 phase with its disordered interstitial zinc. is_mixed is left false because the two phases coexist in every sample rather than separating composition by composition. Zinc and antimony from the inclusion cannot be read as dopants of the matrix, which is why no dopant_roles are recorded. Measured window 310-608 K; beta-Zn4Sb3 converts to the alpha phase near 254 K and to gamma above about 765 K, both outside this window. No reference line is offered for this host.

basis: Yb4Sb2.4Bi0.6 and Yb4Bi0.6Sb2.4 are the same 4:3 composition written twice, and the first paper is titled for antimony-based compounds with the anti-Th3P4 structure as potential high-temperature thermoelectrics. Yb4Sb3 is the anti-Th3P4 phase, I-43d, the same interpenetrating framework as Th3P4 with the cation and anion roles exchanged, and it is the cation-to-anion ratio rather than any dopant that sets the carrier count in this family.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen site of the anti-Th3P4 framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Bismuth replaces one fifth of the antimony in both compositions. It is isoelectronic, so it acts on the mass contrast and the lattice thermal conductivity rather than on the carrier concentration, which in this family is set by the rare-earth to pnictogen ratio instead. The second paper is explicitly on disordered rare-earth pnictide solid solutions, which is the same point.

note: The th3p4 entry covers both the Th3P4 arrangement and its anti type -- La3-xTe4 with cation vacancies is the thermoelectric case the taxonomy notes, and Yb4Sb3 is the anti version where the rare earth occupies the anion positions of the aristotype. Recorded as one prototype rather than split, because the framework topology is identical. No reference line is offered for this host, so no mp_id is carried. Measured window 298-1249 K.

basis: Y0.25Bi1.75Te3 and Y0.3Bi1.7Te3 keep the Bi2Te3 stoichiometry with yttrium taking part of the bismuth site, and the paper is titled for the preparation and thermoelectric properties of yttrium-doped Bi2Te3. The quintuple-layer tetradymite structure, R-3m, is retained; trivalent yttrium on a trivalent bismuth site is a size and mass substitution rather than a structural change.
note: I disagree with the reference and record it rather than matching it. [ref 2] offers YBiTe3 R3m (160) mp-1215930 at hull 0.139 with no ICSD support, which treats the yttrium as a stoichiometric constituent of a line compound. The compositions say otherwise: yttrium is at 0.25-0.3 of two bismuth, about 13-15 percent of the cation site, and the paper calls it doping. No mp_id is carried for that reason. Yttrium sits at exactly the 5 at.% cut of the whole formula so it counts as a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry, but its role in the material is substitutional on the bismuth site. Measured window 307-533 K.

basis: CsSnBr3 single crystals, measured in a paper titled for the thermoelectric properties of the all-inorganic perovskite CsSnBr3. It is the ABX3 halide perovskite with tin in corner-sharing SnBr6 octahedra and caesium in the cuboctahedral cavity, cubic Pm-3m in the measured range, and the reference agrees: CsSnBr3 Pm-3m (221) mp-27214 at hull 0.000.
note: CsSnBr3 has octahedral-tilt transitions to tetragonal and orthorhombic settings below room temperature, near 290 K, but the measurement starts at 332 K so the whole window is in the cubic field and spans_transition stays false. The other two reference entries are different compounds rather than polymorphs: CsSn2Br5 is a layered tin(II) bromide and Cs2SnBr6 is the vacancy-ordered double perovskite with tin(IV), which forms when CsSnBr3 oxidises. That oxidation product is the practical failure mode of this material, which is worth knowing in stage 2, but it is not what was measured.

basis: Ca3Co4O9C1.3 and Ca3Co4O9C2.7 are the misfit cobaltite with carbon added at 1.3 and 2.7 atoms per formula unit, and the paper is titled for the ultralow thermal conductivity and thermoelectric properties of a carbon-added Ca3Co4O9. Carbon does not enter either block of the misfit structure at those levels, so each sample is a cobaltite matrix with a dispersed carbon phase rather than a single crystalline compound.
note: The matrix is named as the alternative: Ca3Co4O9 is the incommensurate misfit cobaltite, a Ca2CoO3 rocksalt block stacked against a CdI2-type CoO2 sheet. Carbon is above the 5 at.% cut in both compositions, so it is a host element with no dopant_roles entry; its role is a dispersed second phase. This follows the same reading as the C-Co-Sb host, where carbon added to a skutterudite was recorded as a composite rather than as a dopant. No reference line is offered. Measured window 31-352 K.

basis: Both compositions are written (Ca3Co4O9)n(SiC)m with the silicon carbide at 48 and 58 percent, and the paper is titled for a significant enhancement in the Seebeck coefficient and power factor of Ca3Co4O9 [with SiC]. At those fractions this is not an additive in a matrix but a two-phase ceramic, an oxide and a carbide that do not react, so no single prototype describes a sample.
note: Both constituents are in the taxonomy and both are named: the misfit cobaltite Ca3Co4O9 and silicon carbide, whose polytype the composition does not fix. is_mixed is left false because both phases are present in every sample by design and the host cannot be split per composition. No reference line is offered for this host. Measured window 324-1066 K; Ca3Co4O9 decomposes above roughly 1200 K, so the window stays inside its stability field.

basis: The two compositions reduce to a sodium cobalt oxide with Na:Co near 0.6 and the paper is titled for the synthesis and electrical properties of gamma-NaxCo2O4 via a citrate sol-gel route. Gamma-NaxCoO2 is the P2-type layered oxide, CdI2-like CoO2 sheets with sodium in prismatic sites between them, and x is a compositional variable of that structure rather than a dopant.
note: The composition strings C13.71O42.95Na15.9Co27.41 and C5.48O48.8Na19.03Co26.69 carry carbon at 5-14 at.% and far more oxygen than a cobaltite needs, and I read both as the citrate precursor showing through the transcription rather than as a carbon composite: the measured material is the fired gamma-NaxCo2O4 the title names. That is a judgement about the transcription, so confidence is medium. The reference line supports nothing here -- NaCo(CO)4, Na4Co2C4SO16, Na5CoCO5 and the rest are carbonyls and carbonates at hulls up to 0.36 with at most one ICSD reference, none of them a layered cobaltite -- so no mp_id is carried. Carbon is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; whatever survives firing is residue, not a lattice species. Measured window 399-901 K, where sodium loss rather than a structural transition is the practical limit.
annotator_note: If the transcription is taken literally this host is a carbon composite instead. The paper would settle it in one figure.

basis: The single composition C3Co4O9 has the Ca3Co4O9 stoichiometry exactly, and the paper is titled for the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of Ca3Co4O9+delta with europium substitution. The calcium has been transcribed as carbon, so the material is the incommensurate misfit cobaltite -- a Ca2CoO3 rocksalt block stacked against a CdI2-type CoO2 sheet -- and not a cobalt carbonate or carbonyl.
note: Confidence is medium because the assignment rests on reading Ca back into a composition string that says C, even though the 3:4:9 ratio and the paper title both point the same way. I reject the whole reference line and say so: Co(CO)4, CoCO3, Co3SnC12ClO12 and the rest are carbonyls and carbonates that exist only because the host key contains carbon. No mp_id is carried, and misfit_cobaltite carries no single mp_id anyway -- it is an incommensurate composite of two subsystems, which stage 2 has to handle as such. The europium of the title does not appear in this composition, so the sample is the undoped member.
annotator_note: Host key C-Co-O is an artefact of the Ca-to-C transcription; the sample belongs with Ca-Co-O. Worth fixing upstream rather than in the ledger.

basis: Sr4Co2O6CO3 is written with a discrete carbonate group, which is what it is: the cobalt member of the layered oxycarbonate family whose best-known member is Sr2CuO2CO3, in which a planar CO3 layer replaces the apical oxide layer of a K2NiF4-like block. No taxonomy entry covers a carbonate as a structural anion, so layered_oxycarbonate is proposed for it rather than forcing the compound into ruddlesden_popper or treating the carbon as residue.
note: Confidence is medium and the space group is left null because the carbonate orientation orders differently across this family and I cannot fix the setting for the cobalt member from the composition alone. The reference line offers only Sr2Co(CO)2 P4/mmm mp-1147608 at hull 0.634 with no ICSD support, which is a carbonyl rather than a carbonate -- the databases confuse the two because both read as carbon next to oxygen next to a metal. No mp_id is carried for that reason. The paper title, on carriers in both a metallic and a semiconducting phase, suggests the sample itself may not be single phase, which is worth checking in stage 2. Measured window 10-300 K.

basis: Both compositions are written (Cr3C2)n(SiC)m at 53-66 percent chromium carbide, and the paper is titled for thermal conduction in a Cr3C2/SiC composite. Two carbides that do not form a solid solution, mixed in comparable amounts, so each sample is two crystalline phases and no single prototype describes it.
note: Both constituents are named as alternatives: Cr3C2 in its orthorhombic Pnma structure and silicon carbide, whose polytype the composition does not fix. I do not follow the reference line, which offers the ternaries Cr2SiC P6_3/mmc mp-1078494 and Cr5Si3C P6_3/mcm mp-1105327: those are compounds that could form if the two carbides reacted, and the paper treats the material as a composite of the two rather than as a reacted ternary. Recorded as a disagreement rather than resolved -- if the sintering did produce a ternary interphase, stage 2 would need the paper to say so. Measured window 295-873 K.

basis: FeC0.1 is an iron-carbon alloy at about 9 at.% carbon and the paper is titled for the effects of precipitation on the thermoelectric power of iron-carbon alloys. Carbon at that level is two orders of magnitude beyond its solubility in ferrite, so the sample is necessarily body-centred iron with cementite precipitated in it, and the precipitation is what the measurement is about. No single crystal structure describes such a sample.
note: This follows the same reading as the C-Cr-Fe-V steel host in chunk 027: an iron matrix with carbides in it is a composite, not a compound. Of the reference entries, Fe3C P6_322 mp-13154 is the one that matters -- cementite is the precipitate expected at this carbon level -- but the orthorhombic Pnma setting is the one cementite actually takes, and neither the carbide nor the ferrite matrix alone describes the sample, so no mp_id is carried. Carbon is a host element at 9 at.% and carries no dopant_roles entry; the small part of it that is genuinely dissolved sits interstitially in the ferrite. Confidence is medium because the carbide identity is inferred from the alloy chemistry rather than reported. Measured window 107-421 K, which is also where the interstitial carbon Snoek relaxation lives.

basis: SnCFe3 is Fe3SnC and the first paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of metallic antiperovskites AXD3. That is the inverse perovskite arrangement: carbon at the body centre in an octahedron of iron, tin at the corners, so the anion and cation roles of a normal ABX3 perovskite are exchanged. The reference agrees: Fe3SnC Pm-3m (221) mp-21850 with an ICSD reference.
note: Carbon here is a structural constituent on the octahedral interstitial site, not residue or an additive, which is the opposite of how carbon reads in the other C-prefixed hosts of this chunk. The hull value of 0.069 is typical for a metallic antiperovskite in the 2019 dump and does not argue against the phase, which has an ICSD reference and is made routinely. The second paper is on the cobalt analogue SnCCo3, the same structure. Measured window 10-325 K; the magnetic ordering in this family is not a structural transition.

basis: Mo5Si3C is the Nowotny phase: the Mn5Si3 D8_8 framework, P6_3/mcm, with carbon filling the octahedral void at the centre of the metal chains. The carbon is written into the composition and is what selects that structure -- carbon-free Mo5Si3 takes a different, tetragonal arrangement -- so the D8_8 entry is the right one for the crystals this paper grew.
note: Confidence is medium for a reason worth recording: the paper is titled for single crystalline Mo5X3, and if the crystal were carbon-free Mo5Si3 it would be the W5Si3 type, I4/mcm, which the taxonomy has no entry for. The composition string carries the carbon, and carbon-stabilised Nowotny phases are common in crystals grown from these melts, so the D8_8 reading is taken -- but a paper check would settle which of the two was actually grown, and if it is the carbon-free phase this host needs a new prototype rather than this one. Carbon is above the 5 at.% cut so it carries no dopant_roles entry; structurally it is interstitial. No reference line is offered for this host. Measured window 13-1064 K.
annotator_note: If the paper reports I4/mcm, propose a w5si3_d8m entry and reassign; the taxonomy has no tetragonal 5-3 silicide.

basis: The curator settles this one: the two compositions written Si3N4C2 and Si3N4C0.5 are recorded in the paper as Si3N4 with 17 vol percent graphene nanoplatelets and Si3N4 with 4 vol percent reduced graphene oxide, and the paper is titled for thermopower and the Hall effect in silicon nitride composites containing [graphene]. Each sample is an insulating nitride matrix with a percolating carbon network in it, two phases that do not react, so no single prototype describes it.
note: The matrix had no taxonomy entry, so beta_si3n4 is proposed in this chunk and named as an alternative here; the carbon phase is graphene, filed under graphite_layered. Essentially all of the measured conduction belongs to the carbon network -- Si3N4 is an insulator -- which is the physical reason the composite label is the honest one rather than either constituent. The reference line reaches neither phase: Si(CN2)2, SiCN and Si2CN4 are carbodiimides and ternary nitrides that exist because the host key contains C, N and Si together. No mp_id is carried. Measured window 97-315 K.

basis: NbC0.96 and NbC0.76 are substoichiometric niobium carbide, the rocksalt structure with carbon vacancies, and the paper is titled for the lattice thermal conductivity of superconducting niobium carbide. The reference is unambiguous and strongly attested: NbC Fm-3m (225) mp-910 with 38 ICSD references, by far the best supported entry on the line.
note: The carbon deficiency is the point of the samples rather than an impurity: it is non-stoichiometry on the anion sublattice, the same case the taxonomy notes for TaN0.89, and it is what the phonon scattering in the paper is attributed to. At NbC0.76 the vacancies can order into the Nb6C5 superstructure, C2/m, which the reference line carries as mp-2760 with four ICSD references; that is an ordered variant of the same rocksalt parent reached by annealing rather than a separate thermal phase, so it is noted here rather than entered in other_polymorphs. Measurement covers 10-76 K only, so nothing is crossed. Carbon is a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry.

basis: The curator records the carbon in SrTiO3C0.31 and SrTiO3C0.63 as graphene oxide, and the paper is titled for grain boundary interfaces controlled by reduced graphene oxide in [a] nonstoichiometric [SrTiO3]. The titanate keeps its own composition and the carbon sits at the grain boundaries as a separate phase, so each sample is a perovskite matrix plus a carbon network rather than a single compound.
note: The matrix is named as the alternative: cubic SrTiO3, Pm-3m. Carbon is above the 5 at.% cut in both compositions so it carries no dopant_roles entry, and it is neither an A-site nor a B-site substituent -- graphene oxide does not dissolve in a titanate. The paper attributes the enhancement to the boundaries the carbon creates, which is exactly a composite mechanism. No reference line is offered for this host. Measured window 295-775 K, entirely above the 105 K antiferrodistortive transition of SrTiO3.

basis: PuC is the rocksalt monocarbide, plutonium and carbon on interpenetrating face-centred sublattices, and the papers are on sintered plutonium carbide and on the electronic structure of the thorium, uranium and plutonium carbides. The reference agrees and is well attested: PuC Fm-3m (225) mp-280 with 8 ICSD references.
note: Worth carrying into stage 2: the plutonium monocarbide is never stoichiometric -- it exists as PuC1-x with roughly 15 percent of the carbon sites vacant and it commonly coexists with Pu2C3, which the reference line carries as mp-19891, I-43d, with 6 ICSD references at hull 0.000. The sintered samples measured here are therefore likely to contain some sesquicarbide, but the monocarbide is what the papers name and the transport they report, so the rocksalt entry is the assignment and the sesquicarbide is recorded as a likely companion phase rather than as a polymorph. PuC2 is a high-temperature phase of a different composition. Measured window 10-1273 K, full span to 1574 K.

basis: SnSeC0.12 and SnSeC0.17 are polycrystalline SnSe with carbon added at 6-8 at.%, from a paper on enhancing the thermoelectric performance of polycrystalline SnSe. Carbon has no site in the orthorhombic SnSe layer structure at that level, so the samples are an SnSe matrix with a dispersed carbon phase, read the same way as the other carbon-added chalcogenide hosts in this set.
note: The matrix is named as the alternative: SnSe in the Pnma GeS structure. Confidence is medium rather than high because the paper title is truncated in the chunk file and does not itself name the carbon phase, so the composite reading rests on the composition and on how carbon behaves in these chalcogenides. One thing to carry forward: the matrix transition matters even though the host record does not. SnSe converts from Pnma to Cmcm near 800 K and the measured window runs to 823 K, so the last points are above it; spans_transition is left false because the assigned prototype is the composite rather than either SnSe phase, but stage 2 should treat the matrix as spanning that transition. No reference line is offered for this host.

basis: Cd6Ca and Cd85Ca15 are the same 1/1 cubic approximant, and the first paper is titled for a novel phase transition in the Cd6M intermetallics. This is a Tsai-type approximant: a periodic Im-3 packing of the same icosahedral clusters that build the i-CdYb quasicrystal, with a disordered Cd4 tetrahedron at the centre of each cluster. As with the Zn6Sc host in chunk 013, this is one of the cases where the prototype names a genuinely periodic structure.
note: The measured window 12-299 K crosses the order-disorder transition the paper is named for, so both sides are recorded even though the prototype does not change: above roughly 100 K the central Cd4 tetrahedra are orientationally disordered and the cell is body-centred cubic Im-3; below it they order and the symmetry drops to a superstructure whose setting is not fixed here, which is why the low-temperature phase carries a null space group at medium confidence. The transition temperature is approximate and shifts between Cd6Ca and Cd6Yb. The reference line describes a different part of the phase diagram -- CaCd2, CaCd, Ca3Cd2 -- and does not reach the 1/1 cell at all, so no mp_id is carried.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [194, 74, 221, 146]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Ca0.6Co0.4Fe2O4 and Ca0.5Co0.5Fe2O4 keep the AB2O4 ratio of a ferrite and the paper is titled for thermoelectric power studies of Ca-Co ferrites, so the intended material is cobalt ferrite with calcium on the divalent A site. CoFe2O4 is the inverse spinel and that is what is assigned, but calcium at half the A site is far beyond what a spinel accommodates, so the assignment is made at low confidence.
note: The low confidence is the finding. Ca2+ is much too large for the tetrahedral A site of a spinel and its solubility there is a few percent, not fifty, so a sample nominally Ca0.5Co0.5Fe2O4 is most likely cobalt ferrite plus orthorhombic CaFe2O4, which is why the post-spinel entry is named as the alternative. I also reject the reference line: it offers Ca2FeCoO5 Pbcm mp-1203339, a brownmillerite, and two computed Ca-Fe-Co oxides, none of which has the 1:2 divalent-to-iron ratio these compositions carry. No mp_id is carried. Measured window 311-658 K, robust range, full span to 735 K.
annotator_note: Needs the paper: whether the samples are single-phase spinel or spinel plus CaFe2O4 decides both the prototype and whether this host should be split.

basis: Ca0.5Y0.5Fe0.5Co0.5O3 and Ca0.3Y0.7Fe0.5Co0.5O3 both keep the ABO3 ratio exactly, and the paper is titled for enhanced oxygen reduction through Ca and Co co-doped YFeO3. The parent is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskite YFeO3, with calcium substituting yttrium on the A site and cobalt substituting iron on the B site.
note: The Pnma setting is the usual one for a small-A-site rare-earth orthoferrite and is recorded at medium confidence on the phase; the prototype itself is not in doubt.
