Cobalt at half the B site is heavy enough that it is alloying rather than doping, and calcium on the A site is the acceptor that creates the mixed iron valence these cathode materials are made for. Both substituents are above the 5 at.% cut, so neither carries a dopant_roles entry. Oxygen non-stoichiometry is likely in a material used as an oxygen reduction cathode but is not written into the compositions. No reference line is offered. Measured window 823-1023 K.

basis: The host holds two different cobaltites. Ca3CoIrO6 is the A3BB-prime-O6 chain compound -- the K4CdCl6 type in which alternating face-sharing CoO6 trigonal prisms and IrO6 octahedra form one-dimensional chains, the same structure as Ca3Co2O6 with iridium on half the chain sites -- and the first paper is titled for quasi-one-dimensional oxides. The second composition is Ca3Co4O9 with a little iridium, a misfit cobaltite, from a paper on Ir doping in a layered cobaltite. Two structures, so the host must be split per composition.
note: The split is clean on the cobalt-to-calcium ratio, the same rule that separates Ca3Co2O6 from Ca3Co4O9 in the Ca-Co-O host: 3:1:1:6 is the chain compound, 3:4:9 is the misfit. The second composition is transcribed Ca3Co3.9Ir40.1O9, where the iridium count is plainly a digitisation artefact for Ir0.1 -- forty iridium atoms per three calcium is not a material, and the paper describes iridium doping of Ca3Co4O9. That artefact is also why iridium sits above the 5 at.% cut for this host and carries no dopant_roles entry, when in the real composition it is a dilute substituent on the cobalt site of the CoO2 sheet. No reference line is offered. Measured window 110-1104 K.
annotator_note: Ir40.1 should be Ir0.1; worth correcting upstream, since it distorts both the host split and the dopant fractions stage 3 will compute.

basis: Both compositions are written in the misfit form itself -- Pb0.7Sr0.5Ca1.5Co0.3O3(CoO2)1.67 and Pb0.75Ca2Co0.3O3(CoO2)1.61 -- and the paper is titled for thermopower enhancement in misfit cobaltites. These are the lead-bearing members of the family: a rocksalt block of (Pb,Ca,Sr)2CoO3 stacked against a CdI2-type CoO2 sheet, with the two subsystems incommensurate along one axis, which is exactly what the 1.6 ratio in the formula records.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb0.7Sr0.5Ca1.5Co0.3O3(CoO2)1.67: strontium sits with lead and calcium in the rocksalt block, not in the CoO2 sheet. It is isovalent with calcium, so it changes the block size and with it the misfit ratio rather than the carrier count.

note: No mp_id is carried and none could be: a misfit cobaltite is an incommensurate composite of two subsystems with their own cells, which the taxonomy flags for special handling in stage 2. The space group is left null for the same reason. No reference line is offered for this host. Measured window 10-789 K.

basis: Sr1.8Ca1.2YCo4O10.5 is the calcium-substituted member of the Sr3YCo4O10.5 family: an A-site ordered, oxygen-vacancy ordered perovskite in which yttrium and the alkaline earths occupy distinct A sites and the missing oxygen orders into a tetragonal superstructure of the simple cubic cell. The paper studies chemical and physical pressure effects on exactly that compound, calcium for strontium being the chemical pressure.
note: Recorded as a perovskite with the layered double perovskite named as the alternative, and the reason for the hedge is worth keeping: the A-site cations here do order, which is what makes the compound interesting, but the ordering is a vacancy-driven superstructure of the ABO3 aristotype rather than the clean alternating stacking that the layered_double_perovskite entry describes for YBaCo2O5+delta. The space group is left null because the superstructure setting is not fixed by the composition. The reference offers Sr10CaY4(CoO3)10 I4/m mp-1218919 at hull 0.025, a computed A-site ordered perovskite with no ICSD support and a different cation ratio and oxygen content from this sample, so its ordering pattern supports the general picture but not this compound; no mp_id is carried. Oxygen at 10.5 per four cobalt is the non-stoichiometry that sets the cobalt valence. Measured window 57-300 K.

basis: La0.7Ca0.3Mn0.4Cr0.6O3 and La0.7Ca0.3Mn0.7Cr0.3O3 hold the ABO3 ratio exactly and are the standard La0.7Ca0.3MnO3 manganite with chromium substituted onto the manganese site, from a paper on spin-cluster and lattice-deformation effects in that system. The structure is the orthorhombically distorted GdFeO3-type perovskite throughout the substitution series; chromium is isostructural on the B site.
note: Both substituents are above the 5 at.% cut and so carry no dopant_roles entries, but their roles differ and are worth stating: calcium on the A site is the acceptor that sets the Mn3+/Mn4+ ratio, while chromium on the B site at 30-60 percent is alloying that breaks the double-exchange network. The reference line offers only two computed supercells, Ca3La5Mn7CrO24 P1 and Ca6La2Mn7CrO24 P-1, which are ordering models of the same perovskite rather than distinct structures; no mp_id is carried. The Pnma setting is recorded at medium confidence on the phase. Measured window 82-301 K, which crosses the ferromagnetic ordering of the parent but that is magnetic rather than structural.

basis: Pr0.5Ca0.5CrO3 and Pr0.7Ca0.3CrO3 are the ABO3 perovskite chromite, orthorhombic GdFeO3-type, with calcium on the praseodymium A site; the paper is titled for the transport and magnetic properties of Pr1-xCaxCrO3. The CrO6 octahedral network is retained across the whole series, and calcium acts by converting Cr3+ to Cr4+ rather than by changing the framework.
note: Calcium is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; at x = 0.3 to 0.5 it is A-site alloying rather than dilute doping in any case. I do not follow the reference, which offers CaPrCrO4 Cmc2_1 mp-1227145 at hull 0.046 with no ICSD support: that is a computed ordered phase with four oxygens, while both compositions here are ABO3 with three. No mp_id is carried. Measured window 37-657 K.

basis: Ca0.6La1.4CuIrO6 is the A2BB-prime-O6 composition exactly, and the paper is titled for iridium valence variation and carrier sign tuning in (Ca,Ba)xLa2-xCuIrO6. Copper and iridium alternate on the B sites of a rock-salt-ordered double perovskite, which is why the iridium valence can be moved by substituting calcium for lanthanum on the A site without touching the framework.
note: The monoclinic P2_1/n setting is the usual one for a double perovskite whose B-site cations differ this much in size and for a Jahn-Teller-active Cu2+, and it is recorded at medium confidence on the phase; the B-site ordering itself is not in doubt given the 1:1 Cu:Ir ratio. Calcium is above the 5 at.% cut so it carries no dopant_roles entry, but it is the tuning variable of the paper: on the A site it changes the total electron count and therefore the iridium valence, which is what flips the sign of the carriers. No reference line is offered for this host. Measured window 322-753 K.

basis: CaCu3Mn4O12 is the AA-prime-3B4O12 ordered perovskite exactly, and the first paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of the AA-prime-3B4O12-type ordered perovskite oxides. The heavy octahedral tilting of that structure forces the A sites to split into one large twelve-coordinate site for calcium and three square-planar sites for copper, with manganese on the B sites; the second composition, CaMn2CuMn4O12, is the same structure with manganese sharing the copper A-prime site.
note: The prototype entry is named for CaCu3Ti4O12 but the family is the same for the manganite member, Im-3 with the same A-site ordering; CaCu3Mn4O12 is its ferrimagnetic, half-metallic representative. The reference offers only Ca3MnCuO6 P2_1/c mp-1214191, a chain compound of a different stoichiometry with no ICSD support, so no mp_id is carried. Measured window 11-537 K; the ferrimagnetic ordering near 355 K is magnetic rather than structural.

basis: CaCuO2 is the infinite-layer cuprate: flat CuO2 sheets with calcium between them and nothing else, the simplest structure that contains a cuprate plane. The papers are on epitaxial CaCuO2 thin films and on superlattices grown by laser ablation, which is how this phase is made. The reference agrees: CaCuO2 P4/mmm (123) mp-4826 at hull 0.001 with 3 ICSD references.
note: The best-supported entry on the reference line is Ca2CuO3 Immm mp-5869 with four ICSD references, but that is the one-dimensional chain cuprate at a different stoichiometry, not a polymorph of CaCuO2; the same goes for CaCu2O3 and Ca5(CuO2)6. This is the case the chunk header warns about -- the reference describes which phases exist in the chemistry, not which one the paper made -- and the compositions are unambiguous at 1:1:2. Measured window 38-196 K robust, full span to 301 K.

basis: TlSr2Ca2Cu3O9.4 is the Tl-1223 cuprate: a single Tl-O charge reservoir layer, two strontium rock-salt layers and three CuO2 planes separated by calcium, which is the n = 3 member of the ABa2Ca(n-1)CunO(2n+2+d) family the prototype covers. The paper is titled for the synthesis and characterization of single-phase TlSr2Ca2Cu3Oy.
note: Two departures from the entry as written are recorded rather than smoothed over. The prototype lists TlBa2Ca2Cu3O9 among its representatives and this compound has strontium in place of barium, which is a smaller rock-salt layer but the same stacking; and the entry is named 1212 while this is the 1223 member, one CuO2 plane further along the same homologous series. tl_2212_cuprate is named as the alternative because the double-TlO-layer family is the other place a Tl-Ca-Cu-O composition can land, and it is ruled out here by the single thallium against three coppers. The reference offers Sr2CaTlCu2O7 P4/mmm mp-20824, which is the 1212 member of this very series with one ICSD reference -- the right family, one plane short of this composition -- so no mp_id is carried. The oxygen excess to 9.4 is the doping variable of the reservoir layer. Measured window 30-293 K.

basis: YBa0.5Ca1.5Cu3O7 and YCa2Cu3O7 are the 123 structure with calcium replacing barium, from a paper on the metal-insulator transition in the YBa2-xCaxCu3O7-delta system. The framework is unchanged: CuO2 bilayers around yttrium, with CuO chains in the charge reservoir, and calcium simply takes the large nine-coordinate site.

dopant_roles.basis: YBa0.5Ca1.5Cu3O7: barium is the parent cation of the 123 structure, not an added impurity. It falls under the 5 at.% cut only because calcium has replaced three quarters of it, so it is the remaining end member of a Ba-Ca solid solution rather than a dopant.

note: Calcium is the substituent that matters and it sits above the cut, so it carries no dopant_roles entry; on the barium site it is isovalent, and what drives the metal-insulator transition in this system is the oxygen content of the chains together with the smaller A-site cation. The Pmmm setting recorded on the phase is the orthorhombic ordered-chain form of fully oxygenated 123, at medium confidence because heavy calcium substitution pushes the structure towards tetragonal. No reference line is offered for this host. Measured window 18-299 K.

basis: Ca0.7Eu0.3MnO3 and Ca0.6Eu0.4MnO3 hold the ABO3 ratio exactly and are CaMnO3 with europium on the A site, from a paper on nanocrystalline Ca1-xEuxMnO3. CaMnO3 is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskite and trivalent europium substituting divalent calcium is the standard n-type donor route in this family -- it reduces Mn4+ to Mn3+ without disturbing the octahedral network.
note: Europium at 30-40 percent of the A site is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry, but its role is substitutional on the calcium site and it is acting as a donor; at that level it is heavy alloying rather than dilute doping, and the paper writes the series as Ca1-xEuxMnO3 for that reason. The oxygen non-stoichiometry the title carries as delta is the other carrier knob and is not written into these two compositions. No reference line is offered for this host. Measured window 299-895 K, within the orthorhombic field of CaMnO3.

basis: Ca0.9Y0.1Mn0.75Fe0.25O3 and CaMn0.7Fe0.3O3 both hold the ABO3 ratio exactly and are CaMnO3 with iron on the manganese site; CaMnO3 is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskite and Fe3+ for Mn4+ is a B-site substitution that keeps the corner-sharing octahedral network intact.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.9Y0.1Mn0.75Fe0.25O3: trivalent yttrium on the divalent calcium A site is the standard n-type donor route for CaMnO3, reducing Mn4+ to Mn3+.

note: I disagree with the reference line here. The MP PRIMARY entries for this chemistry are Ca2MnFeO5 Pnma mp-619355 and Ca4MnFe3O10 mp-1227204, which are the oxygen-deficient brownmillerite and intergrowth phases that form at Fe:Mn ratios of 1:1 and above. Both compositions in this host sit at Fe 0.25-0.3 of the B site, well inside the perovskite field, and are written by their papers as CaMnO3 with dilute iron. No mp_id is carried because none of the listed entries matches these stoichiometries. Fe at 25-30 percent of the B site is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; its role is substitutional on the manganese site.

basis: Nd0.6Ca0.4FeO3 and La0.18Nd0.32Ca0.26Ba0.24FeO3 are both exactly ABO3 with a mixed rare-earth and alkaline-earth A site over a single iron B site, which is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type ferrite perovskite; the second paper is explicitly about A-site size disorder at fixed stoichiometry, which only makes sense in a perovskite.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba at 0.24 of the A site is a quarter of that sublattice and only falls below the 5 at.% cut because the formula has five atoms; it is an A-site end member deliberately chosen to widen the cation size distribution, not a dilute dopant.
La at 0.18 of the A site in the same quaternary A-site mixture, likewise an end member rather than a dopant.

note: The only reference offered, CaNdFeO4 Cmc2_1 mp-1227142, is an A2BO4 layered stoichiometry and does not describe either composition here; both are ABO3. I take the perovskite over the reference. The oxygen deficiency written as delta in the second title is the carrier knob for these ferrites and is not captured in the parsed compositions.

basis: Gd0.3Ca0.7MnO3 is CaMnO3 with gadolinium on the A site, the same trivalent-for-divalent donor substitution as the Y and Eu analogues, and both compositions hold ABO3 exactly; CaMnO3 is orthorhombic GdFeO3-type.
note: The composition string CaGdMnO3 puts gadolinium at half the A site, which is heavy alloying rather than doping, but the first paper writes the series as Ca1-xGdxMnO3-delta with x of 0.00 to 0.05, so that string is more likely a transcription of the series formula than a real 1:1 A-site compound. Flagging it because it affects nothing structurally -- the whole range stays perovskite -- but would matter for a doping level. No reference line is offered for this host. The 41-700 K window covers the charge-ordering and magnetic transitions of this family, which change the electronic and magnetic cell, not the structural prototype.

basis: La2.27Ca0.73S4 and La2.53Ca0.47S4 sit on the La3-xS4 to CaLa2S4 line at a fixed cation-to-sulfur ratio of 3:4, which is the Th3P4 field; gamma-La2S3 is the cation-deficient Th3P4 phase La2.67S4 and divalent calcium fills its vacancies, so the whole series is one cubic I-43d framework with the carrier count set by how many vacancies are left.
note: I disagree with the reference line. Its only entry is Ca(LaS2)2 I-42d mp-35421, a tetragonal 1:2:4 compound; the compositions here are at 3:4 cation to sulfur, which is the Th3P4 stoichiometry and not that of the tetragonal phase. The paper is a phase-relation study of the ternary lanthanum system and the Th3P4 solid solution is the thermoelectric phase in it. No mp_id is carried. Calcium is above the 5 at.% cut and so has no dopant_roles entry; its role is substitutional on the lanthanum site, and it works by filling cation vacancies rather than by adding an impurity level -- the same carrier-concentration knob the taxonomy records for La3-xTe4.

basis: Y0.61Ca0.39TiO3 and Y0.58Ca0.42TiO3 are exactly ABO3 on the YTiO3 to CaTiO3 line; both end members are orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskites and the paper studies the Mott transition that occurs as calcium doping empties the Ti 3d band, which is a purely electronic transition within one structure.
note: The three MP entries offered -- Ca3YTi4O12 Pm mp-1227620, CaY3Ti4O12 Pm mp-1227117 and CaYTi2O6 Pmn2_1 mp-1227099 -- are computed A-site orderings of the same perovskite at particular Ca:Y ratios, carrying no ICSD count. They agree with the assignment at the prototype level; their low space-group symmetry is an artefact of the ordered supercell, not a different structure, so no mp_id is carried for a disordered solid solution at Ca 0.39-0.42. Calcium is above the 5 at.% cut; its role is substitutional on the yttrium A site and it is the hole-doping variable.

basis: Ca3Pt4Sn12 is the R3T4Sn13 Remeika phase written with one tin short; the cubic Pm-3n framework of Sn12 icosahedra around the transition metal is exactly what the paper means by a quasi-skutterudite, and the reference line carries Ca3Sn13Pt4 Pm-3n mp-1214141 for the same chemistry.
note: The 3-4-12 rather than 3-4-13 stoichiometry in the composition string is the tin deficiency these phases are routinely refined with, not a different compound. The two hull-zero MP entries on the line, Ca2Sn5Pt3 and CaSnPt, are other binaries and ternaries in the same system and do not match the 3:4:12 ratio. Single crystals, measured 10-300 K; these phases have a structural superlattice transition well below room temperature in some members (Ca3Ir4Sn13 near 38 K), but it is a superstructure of the same prototype, so spans_transition is left false.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CdCr2S4 is the classic AB2X4 normal thiospinel with tetrahedral Cd2+ and octahedral Cr3+, and TEDesignLab carries Cr2CdS4 Fd-3m mp-4338 at hull zero with 12 ICSD references, the strongest evidence on this host.
note: The MP line offers Cr8Cd3CuS16 R3m mp-1226128, a copper-substituted ordered derivative that does not apply to this undoped composition. The measured window is 11-292 K and covers the ferromagnetic ordering near 85 K and the magnetodielectric response the paper reports; that is magnetic and polaronic, not a change of prototype.

basis: EuCd1.6Mn0.4Sb2 and EuCd1.4Mn0.6Sb2 are EuCd2Sb2 with manganese on the cadmium site; EuCd2Sb2 is the trigonal CaAl2Si2-type 1-2-2 Zintl phase, with Eu2+ layers between [Cd2Sb2]2- slabs of edge-sharing CdSb4 tetrahedra, and Mn2+ substitutes isovalently into that slab.
note: No reference line is offered for this host, so the assignment rests on the chemistry of the AM2X2 Zintl family. Manganese at 0.4-0.6 of the cadmium site is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; it is an isovalent framework substitution that adds local moments and suppresses lattice thermal conductivity rather than changing the carrier count, which is what the paper calls manganese doping. EuMn2Sb2 is itself a CaAl2Si2-type phase, so the whole substitution range stays within one prototype.

basis: The curator records the series as Mn1-xCdxFe2O4, which is the manganese ferrite spinel with cadmium on the tetrahedral A site; both compositions hold the AB2O4 ratio exactly and cadmium is a strong A-site former, so it drives the normal-spinel cation distribution.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Cadmium is above the 5 at.% cut and so has no dopant_roles entry; its role is substitutional on the tetrahedral A site, and because it is a closed-shell d10 ion it displaces Fe3+ from that site into the octahedral sublattice, which is the mechanism behind the conductivity changes the paper reports. The measured window 310-599 K crosses the Curie temperature of these ferrites; that is a magnetic transition, not a structural one.

basis: CdPr2W2O10 is a member of the R2MW2O10 rare-earth double tungstates, built from edge-sharing W2O10 octahedral dimers with the rare earth in high coordination and the divalent metal octahedral; the 2:1:2:10 ratio fixes the family, and the paper describes three new ceramic tungstates.
note: Confidence is low and the space group is left null on purpose. Neither reference offers any entry for this host, and the R2MW2O10 family is reported in more than one monoclinic setting, so naming one from the composition alone would assert more than is known. The new prototype ln2mw2o10_double_tungstate was written to taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl before being used here. This host should be checked against the paper, which reports the structure of all three tungstates it introduces.

basis: Both papers are on Cd2SnO4 thin films prepared as transparent conductors, and sputtered and annealed cadmium stannate films take the cubic inverse-spinel form with Sn4+ octahedral and Cd2+ split between both sites; that is the phase whose degenerate n-type conduction the papers measure.

other_polymorphs.note: The orthorhombic Sr2PbO4-type form, and the bulk equilibrium phase -- TEDesignLab makes it PRIMARY with 3 ICSD references. It is not metastable; it is simply not the phase a sputtered film adopts. Recorded here rather than in phases because it is not reached from the spinel by heating the films.

note: This is a recorded disagreement with the reference. TEDesignLab ranks Cd2SnO4 Pbam mp-5966 (3 ICSD) above Fd-3m mp-1104726 (1 ICSD), and by ICSD weight alone the orthorhombic phase wins. I still assign spinel, because the reference describes which phases exist in the chemistry while both papers here are on thin films, and thin-film cadmium stannate is the spinel. Confidence is medium for exactly that reason and the case is a good candidate for reading the papers, which state the structure they measured. The new prototype sr2pbo4_type was written to taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl before being used above. The reference also lists CdSnO3 in R-3 ilmenite, Pnma perovskite and Pm-3m settings; those are the 1:1 stannate, a different compound from the 2:1 composition in this host.

basis: SnCd0.12Te and SnCd0.15Te are SnTe with cadmium on the tin site, and the paper title states the phase outright -- enhanced thermopower in rock-salt SnTe-CdTe from band convergence, the standard route of raising the light and heavy valence bands into alignment by alloying rocksalt SnTe with a few percent of a second telluride.
note: I disagree with the reference. Its only entry is CdSnTe2 R-3m mp-1226740 at hull 0.094 with no ICSD count, which is a computed ordered 1:1:2 arrangement, not the dilute rocksalt solid solution these samples are. CdTe itself is zincblende, so cadmium is soluble in rocksalt SnTe only to a few percent, which is where these compositions sit. Cadmium at 0.12-0.15 per formula unit is just above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; its role is isovalent substitution on the tin site, a band-structure knob rather than a carrier donor. SnTe also has the rhombohedral distortion below about 100 K, far below the 298-824 K measured window.

basis: The two compositions are different compounds, not a series: TbCd is the equiatomic B2 CsCl-type phase, matching TbCd Pm-3m mp-721 with 5 ICSD references, while Cd6Tb is the cubic 1/1 Tsai-type quasicrystal approximant that the second paper names in its title.
note: Genuinely mixed and separable on stoichiometry alone: Cd:Tb of 1 is b2_cscl, Cd:Tb of 6 is quasicrystal_approximant. One sample each, one paper each -- the first is a survey of RZn and RCd equiatomic compounds, the second is on long-range magnetic order in the quasicrystalline approximant. Cd6Tb is the 1/1 approximant, a periodic Im-3 crystal built from Tsai icosahedral clusters, so unlike a true quasicrystal it does have a structure to resolve in stage 2. The MP line offers TbCd2, Tb11Cd45 and TbCd3, none of which matches the 6:1 ratio, so no mp_id is carried for that half.

basis: Cd0.8Zn0.2Te is the CZT single-crystal detector alloy: CdTe and ZnTe are both zincblende and mix continuously on the cation site, so the whole range is one cubic F-43m tetrahedral structure, and TEDesignLab carries ZnCdTe2 I-42d mp-971837, a cation-ordered variant of the same tetrahedral network.

dopant_roles.basis: Cd0.80Zn0.20TeIn0.0005: indium on the cadmium site is the standard shallow donor used to compensate CZT to semi-insulating behaviour for detector crystals, at 5 parts in ten thousand here.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Zn/(Zn+Cd) is 0.2 in both compositions, well above the dilute limit, so this is the CZT alloy rather than Zn-doped CdTe. Both end members are zincblende, so the axis does not change the prototype.

note: The reference entries are cation-ordered supercells -- I-42d mp-971837 with 1 ICSD reference and R3m mp-1215406 -- while the crystals here are the disordered solid solution, so no mp_id is carried. Neither the 1:1 ordered composition nor the Cc entry at hull 0.258 describes an 80:20 alloy. The 292-1324 K window is wide but CZT stays zincblende up to its melting point.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [216], ICSD-backed references for this host report [122]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The composition string (CeCoIn5)5(CeRhIn5)5 is a molecular-beam-grown superlattice of five unit cells of CeCoIn5 alternating with five of CeRhIn5, and both blocks are the tetragonal HoCoGa5 115 structure -- alternating CeIn3 and TIn2 layers -- which is why they can be grown epitaxially on one another at all.
note: Not a bulk alloy. The paper tunes the pairing interaction of the d-wave superconductor CeCoIn5 by injecting paramagnons across interfaces with the antiferromagnet CeRhIn5, so the 5:5 notation is a layer count. Rhodium and cobalt sit in separate blocks and neither is a dopant for the other. No reference line is offered and no measured range is given for this host. Both constituents are the same prototype, so the record is not marked mixed even though two compounds are present.

basis: Ce3Co4Sn13 is the 3-4-13 Remeika phase outright, and the reference carries Ce3Co4Sn13 Pm-3n mp-21915 with 5 ICSD references for exactly that formula; the paper studies it as a heavy-fermion compound, which is the usual context for these cubic cage stannides.
note: Formula, space group and ICSD evidence all agree; this is the cleanest case in the chunk. Measured 12-296 K. Ce3Co4Sn13 has a structural superlattice anomaly reported near 160 K in some samples, but it is a distortion of the same Pm-3n framework rather than a new prototype, so spans_transition is left false.

basis: RuSr2GdCeCu2O10 is the Ru-1222 ruthenocuprate: RuO2 sheets alternating with a fluorite-like (Gd,Ce)2O2 block and CuO2 bilayers, the n=2 member written RuSr2Gd2-xCexCu2O10+delta in the paper title.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. The Gd:Ce ratio is the doping variable in this family and both are on the same fluorite-block site, which is why neither appears as a dopant here. The oxygen written as 10+delta is the other carrier knob. Ru-1222 is usually refined in a tetragonal I4/mmm-related cell, sometimes with a lower-symmetry RuO6 rotation pattern, so the space group is carried at medium confidence. The 55-250 K window covers the magnetic ordering of the ruthenate sublattice and the superconducting transition of the cuprate one, neither of which is a structural change.

basis: Ce3Cu3-xNixSb4 is the ordered ternary 3-3-4 antimonide, and the paper title revisits the semiconducting behaviour of Ce3Cu3Sb4 -- the narrow-gap state that this cubic I-43d framework produces when the electron count is right; nickel substitutes for copper and tunes it.
note: Taken as y3au3sb4 rather than th3p4 on the taxonomy distinction the two entries already record -- this is the filled ternary ordering of the I-43d framework, not the binary with cation vacancies, and Ce3Cu3Sb4 is isostructural with the Ce3Bi4Pd3 exemplar. No reference line is offered for this host. Nickel is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes for copper and, having one more d electron, moves the Fermi level through the hybridisation gap, which is the point of the series.

basis: Ce0.8Cu0.2Se2 and Ce0.7Cu0.3Se2 are copper-substituted CeSe2, and the rare-earth diselenides take the anti-Fe2As / Cu2Sb arrangement -- CeSe layers alternating with square nets of selenium -- which the taxonomy files under the PbFCl matlockite entry alongside its USbTe and UAsSe exemplars.
note: I disagree with the reference, which offers CeCuSe2 P2_1/c mp-11791 with 3 ICSD references. That is a 1:1:2 line compound; the compositions here are at Cu:Ce of 0.25 and 0.43 against 1.0, so they are the copper-substituted diselenide, not the ternary. Confidence is medium for two reasons: the real LnSe2 phases are usually refined in an orthorhombic distortion of the ideal P4/nmm cell rather than in P4/nmm itself, and whether copper substitutes cerium or sits between the layers is not settled by the composition -- the paper describes f-band control by d-p hybridisation, which would suit either. Worth reading the paper. No mp_id is carried.

basis: Ce5CuSn3 is the Hf5Sn3Cu-type interstitially filled Mn5Si3 structure: the Ce5Sn3 binary is the D8_8 host and copper fills its empty octahedral 2b site along the chain axis, and the reference carries Ce5CuSn3 P6_3/mcm mp-1190264 at exactly that formula and space group.
note: Copper is a framework constituent at the filled interstitial site, not a dopant, and it is above the 5 at.% cut in any case. The reference line also lists CeCuSn, Ce(CuSn)2 and CeCu5Sn with more ICSD references each, but none matches the 5:1:3 ratio of the composition; only mp-1190264 does, at 1 ICSD reference, so the match is weakly attested even though it is exact. Both papers concern the heavy-fermion state in Ce5-xLaxCuSn3 and in Ce5CuSn3 itself.

basis: CeFePO is a 1111 oxypnictide -- alternating [Ce2O2] fluorite-like and [Fe2P2] anti-fluorite layers in the ZrCuSiAs structure, tetragonal P4/nmm -- and is the phosphide member of the same family as LaFeAsO; the paper studies Kondo and spin-glass physics in La-substituted CeFePO, which is a heavy-fermion problem posed on that layered lattice.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.1Ce0.9FePO: non-magnetic lanthanum diluting the cerium sublattice in the oxide layer, the standard way to move from a dense Kondo lattice to the single-ion limit, which is what the paper title describes.

note: I disagree with the reference, whose only entry is Ce2FeP2O P4/mmm mp-1213918 at hull 1.698 -- an energy that far above the hull is a computed structure that does not exist, and the stoichiometry does not match the 1:1:1:1 compositions here either. No mp_id is carried. Both samples are polycrystalline per the curator and measured 11-297 K.

basis: CeFe2Si2 is a textbook ThCr2Si2 122 silicide -- Ce layers alternating with [Fe2Si2] slabs of edge-sharing FeSi4 tetrahedra in I4/mmm -- and the reference carries Ce(FeSi)2 I4/mmm mp-3035 at hull zero with 7 ICSD references, the best-attested entry on the line; the paper compares it across the CeM2Si2 series, which is that family by definition.
note: The other reference entries -- CeFeSi P4/nmm, CeFeSi2 Cmcm, CeFe9Si4 I4/mcm -- are different compounds in the same ternary system, not polymorphs of CeFe2Si2. The measured window reaches 802 K; the intermediate-valence state the papers discuss is a continuous electronic crossover, not a structural transition.

basis: (Gd0.7Ce0.3)2Zr2O7.3 and (Gd0.5Ce0.5)2Zr2O7.5 hold the A2B2O7 ratio on the cation sublattice, which is the pyrochlore stoichiometry; Gd2Zr2O7 is the parent and the paper is on ultralow thermal conductivity in cerium-doped rare-earth zirconates, where the pyrochlore cage and its intrinsic oxygen vacancy are what suppress the lattice conduction.
note: Confidence is medium because Gd2Zr2O7 sits almost exactly on the pyrochlore to defect-fluorite boundary in the radius-ratio criterion, and cerium on the A site pushes it further towards disorder -- the oxygen counts above 7 in both compositions are the sign of that, since Ce4+ on a trivalent site brings extra oxygen into what would be the ordered vacancy. The two structures differ only in whether the cations and the vacancy order, so they are recorded as prototype and alternative rather than as a mixed host. No reference line is offered. An X-ray pattern cannot always tell them apart either, so this is a case where the paper, and preferably its superlattice reflections, would settle it.

basis: CeRhIn is the hexagonal ZrNiAl (ordered Fe2P) type in P-62m, and CeRh1-xGexIn substitutes germanium onto the rhodium site of that framework; the paper follows the evolution from an intermediate-valence state with x, which is a band-filling change on one structure.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Germanium at 0.2-0.3 of the rhodium site is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; its role is substitutional on that site. Note that CeRhIn is the 1:1:1 compound and is distinct from CeRhIn5, the 115 that dominates the Ce-Rh-In literature -- the compositions here are unambiguously 1:1:1 and the paper writes the series as CeRh1-xGexIn.

basis: The paper states the type in its title -- solid solutions based on ThSi2-type CeSi2 -- and CeSi1.6Ge0.4 and CeSiGe are that solid solution with germanium replacing silicon in the three-dimensional three-connected net; the reference agrees at the prototype level, carrying CeSiGe Imma mp-1226579, which is the orthorhombic distortion of alpha-ThSi2 the proposed entry already names.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrel net
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Si+Ge) runs 0.2 to 0.5 across the two compositions. Silicon and germanium are both group 14 and share the three-connected net, so the substitution is isoelectronic and changes the cell size and the degree of orthorhombic distortion rather than the electron count.

note: alpha_thsi2 is a prototype proposed earlier in this project for the Ce-Si host and is reused here rather than re-proposed; proposed_prototype names it because it is not yet in the v3 seed file. The space group is carried as Imma (74) rather than the ideal I4_1/amd (141) because germanium substitution drives the same distortion the silicon-deficient members show, and the reference ranks the Imma entry above the I4_1md one for CeSiGe. Both hull values are modest and neither entry carries an ICSD count, so the match is at the prototype level rather than the polymorph level.

basis: Sr0.7Ce0.3MnO3 holds ABO3 exactly and is SrMnO3 with cerium on the A site; the paper writes the series as Sr1-xCexMnO3-alpha and studies its structural and electrical properties, which is the perovskite manganite problem -- tetravalent cerium on a divalent site is an unusually strong electron donor into the Mn 3d band.
note: The three reference entries -- Sr2CeMn3O9 C2/m mp-1218910, Sr3CeMn4O12 Im-3m mp-1218514 and Sr4CeMn5O15 C2/m mp-1218672 -- are computed A-site orderings of the same perovskite at particular Sr:Ce ratios and carry no ICSD counts, so they support the prototype but none is a structure for a disordered x of 0.3; no mp_id is carried. Cerium is above the 5 at.% cut and so has no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes on the strontium site and is the electron-doping variable, with the oxygen deficiency written as alpha compensating part of it. Note that pure SrMnO3 has a hexagonal 4H polytype as well as the cubic perovskite, but A-site substitution at this level stabilises the perovskite, so it is not recorded as an alternative.

basis: CeNi2P2 is the ThCr2Si2 122 phosphide, cerium layers alternating with [Ni2P2] tetrahedral slabs in I4/mmm, and the paper writes the series as CeNi2-delta(As,P)2 while studying heavy-fermion quantum criticality at the dilute carrier limit -- the 122 pnictides are the standard setting for that.

dopant_roles.basis: CeNi2(As0.1P0.9)2: arsenic is the same group as phosphorus and takes the same pnictogen site in the [Ni2X2] slab, so it expands the lattice and tunes the interlayer X-X bonding rather than adding carriers -- it is the chemical pressure knob used to move this compound towards its quantum critical point. Arsenic is at 0.2 of the pnictogen sublattice, not a dilute level.

note: The reference line lists five other cerium nickel phosphides -- Ce25Ni49P33, Ce6Ni6P17, CeNiP, Ce9(Ni13P6)2 and Ce2Ni12P5 -- each with at most one ICSD reference and none at the 1:2:2 ratio, so none of them applies; no mp_id is carried. The nickel deficiency written as delta in the paper is a non-stoichiometry on the transition-metal site and is what makes the carrier density low.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [139], ICSD-backed references for this host report [187, 194, 217]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CeRh2-xNixSi2 is the ThCr2Si2 122 silicide with nickel substituting rhodium in the [T2Si2] slab; the paper writes the series exactly that way and both compositions hold the 1:2:2 ratio, and the isostructural CeRh2Si2 and CeNi2Si2 end members make the whole range one I4/mmm structure.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Nickel at 0.3-0.4 of the transition-metal site is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes for rhodium and drives the cerium from a magnetically ordered towards a valence-fluctuating state, which is the thermopower behaviour the paper reports. Polycrystalline samples, measured 11-299 K.

basis: Both compositions are written in the two-phase form (Ce3Si2)x(CeO2)1-x and the paper is titled fabrication and thermal conductivity of a CeO2-Ce3Si2 composite, so this host is a deliberate mixture of fluorite ceria and the U3Si2-type silicide, not a single ternary phase.
note: I disagree with the reference, which lists cerium silicates and oxysilicates -- Ce2Si2O7 P4_1 mp-672208 (flagged ambiguous), CeSiO4 I4_1/amd mp-10523, CaCe4Si3O13 -- as though the chemistry were a silicate. It is not: the sample is a mechanical composite of two separate phases and the paper keeps them separate on purpose, because the point is a silicide conduction path through an insulating ceria matrix. If a silicate had formed it would be an unwanted reaction product. The two constituents are named in alt_prototype_ids; per the project README, composite_multiphase hosts are skipped when structures are resolved in stage 2, so no mp_id is carried. The mixture is by volume fraction and both ratios are ceria-rich.

basis: Ce0.7Sm0.3O1.85 and Ce0.5Sm0.5O1.75 are samarium-doped ceria, the standard oxygen-ion conductor: trivalent samarium substitutes Ce4+ in the cubic fluorite lattice and one oxygen vacancy is created for every two substitutions, which is exactly the oxygen stoichiometry written in both formulas.
note: Confidence is medium because of the second composition. At 30 percent samarium the material is unambiguously disordered fluorite, but at 50 percent it is halfway to Sm2O3 and the vacancies begin to order into the C-type bixbyite superstructure, which is a fluorite superlattice with a doubled cell -- hence bixbyite as the alternative rather than a separate phase. The reference line is no help here: every entry it offers (Ce2Sm2O7 Fd-3m mp-752400, Ce4SmO10, Ce4SmO9, Ce5Sm2O13, Ce9SmO20) is a computed ordered vacancy arrangement without an ICSD count, which is a different way of saying the same thing -- ordering is what happens at high substitution. No mp_id is carried for the disordered solid solution. Samarium is far above the 5 at.% cut and has no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes on the cerium site and creates the vacancies.

basis: Both compositions are fluorite-derived zirconia-ceria solid solutions: the curator records the first as ZrO2-50mol percent CeO2, a plasma-sprayed coating in which ceria stabilises the fluorite-derived tetragonal form of zirconia, and the second, (Nd0.2Ce0.8)2Zr2O7.8, is the cerium-rich end of the zirconate line where the cations disorder into defect fluorite rather than ordering into pyrochlore.

dopant_roles.basis: (Nd0.2Ce0.8)2Zr2O7.8: neodymium on the eight-coordinate A site of the zirconate. The paper is on cerium-doped Nd2Zr2O7, so chemically this composition is the cerium-rich member of that series and neodymium is the host cation the series started from -- it appears here as a minor element only because cerium has taken over most of the site.

note: Two rather different samples share this host: a thermal-barrier coating and a zirconate ceramic. Both are fluorite-derived, which is why one prototype covers them, but the first is the tetragonal t-prime form of zirconia (a tetragonal distortion of fluorite, P4_2/nmc, not a separate prototype) and the second is cubic defect fluorite, so confidence is medium and the cubic space group carried in phases is the aristotype rather than a measured setting. Pyrochlore is the alternative for the second composition alone. The reference offers CeZr4-type ordered phases -- CeZrO4 P2_13 mp-4843, Ce3Zr5O16, Ce7ZrO16, Ce5Zr3O16, CeZr3O8 -- each with one to three ICSD references; they are ordered derivatives of the same fluorite framework and do not describe a 50:50 sprayed coating, so no mp_id is carried. The full span reaching 1808 K is a digitisation outlier against a robust range of 290-973 K.

basis: CeOs2 is an AB2 Laves phase and the paper title names both polytypes directly -- evidence of the different valence states in the C14 and C15 phases CeOs2 -- with the reference carrying the cubic C15 at CeOs2 Fd-3m mp-2098, hull zero, 5 ICSD references and the hexagonal C14 at CeOs2 P6_3/mmc mp-1102302 with 2.

other_polymorphs.note: The hexagonal C14 polytype, which the paper measures alongside the C15 and reports a different cerium valence for. It is obtained by how the sample is made rather than by heating through a transition in the 11-297 K window, so it is recorded here rather than in phases. Same prototype entry -- the taxonomy keeps C14, C15 and C36 in one entry and asks that the polytype be recorded when stated, which is what this line does.

note: The host holds one composition and two samples, and the paper compares the two polytypes, so it is likely that one sample is each. That is a polytype difference within one prototype rather than a mixed host, so is_mixed stays false and the C14 form is carried in other_polymorphs. Ce3Os and Ce4Os on the reference line are different binaries.

basis: CePb3 is the cubic AuCu3 L1_2 phase -- cerium at the cube corners, lead at the face centres -- and the reference carries CePb3 Pm-3m mp-20225 at hull zero with 4 ICSD references; both papers treat it as a heavy-fermion compound, and the RPb3 and RSn3 L1_2 series is the standard setting for that.
note: The reference reports the space group as Pm-3m (221) rather than the Pm-3m setting usually written for L1_2 as Pm-3m with the ordered cell; either way it is the ordered AuCu3 arrangement and not a disordered fcc solid solution, and the 4 ICSD references settle it. The first paper is on Ce(Pb1-xSnx)3, so the isostructural stannide is the other end of that line but does not appear in this host. Measured 10-252 K, which covers the antiferromagnetic ordering near 1.1 K only at its lower edge; nothing structural happens in the window.

basis: The two compositions are different compounds: CeRh2 is the cubic C15 Laves phase, confirmed by CeRh2 Fd-3m mp-951 at hull zero with 8 ICSD references, while Ce7Rh3 is the hexagonal Th7Fe3 type that the second paper studies as part of the R7Rh3 series.
note: Mixed and cleanly separable on stoichiometry: Rh:Ce of 2 is the C15 Laves phase, Rh:Ce of 3:7 is th7fe3. One sample and one paper each -- the first is on charge transport in CeM2 compounds, the second on the magnetic and electrical properties of R7Rh3 intermetallics. The reference line covers CeRh3, CeRh, Ce5Rh4 and Ce5Rh3 as well but offers nothing at the 7:3 ratio, so no mp_id is carried for that half.

basis: CeRhSb is the orthorhombic epsilon-TiNiSi type in Pnma, the equiatomic Kondo-insulator structure it shares with CeNiSn, and the reference carries CeSbRh Pnma mp-22249 at hull zero for exactly that formula; both papers measure it as a Kondo alloy with a narrow hybridisation gap.
note: The reference also offers CeSbRh C2/m mp-1226674 at hull 0.157 with no ICSD count, a computed alternative that is not the observed phase, and Ce2Sb4Rh3 and Ce2Sb3Rh4, which are different stoichiometries. The mp-22249 entry rests on a single ICSD reference, so the polymorph match is weakly attested even though formula and space group agree with the structural chemistry. Measured 10-290 K, entirely inside the Kondo-insulating regime; the gap opening is electronic, not structural.

basis: CeTe1.5Sb0.5 and CeTe1.75Sb0.25 sit on the CeTe2 to CeSbTe line, and both ends are the same tetragonal P4/nmm structure -- CeTe layers alternating with a square net of the second pnictogen or chalcogen -- which the taxonomy files under the PbFCl matlockite entry with USbTe as an exemplar; the reference carries CeSbTe P4/nmm mp-917643, the end member itself.
note: Antimony is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes into the square net, which is the whole point of the paper -- the charge density wave that the square net carries changes dimensionality as the net composition is tuned, and CeTe2 itself is usually refined in an orthorhombic or superstructure-modulated distortion of the ideal P4/nmm cell rather than in P4/nmm exactly. The mp-917643 entry carries 2 ICSD references and is the composition at the far end of the substitution, not at either measured point, so the space group is carried at medium confidence. The measured window is 100-300 K and the CDW transition of these compounds lies above it.

basis: Th94Ce6 is dilute cerium in thorium metal, which is face-centred cubic (Cu A1 type) and takes cerium into substitutional solid solution; both papers are on the thermoelectric power of ThCe alloys, the classic dilute-Kondo impurity measurement, and the taxonomy entry already lists Th among its example host systems.
note: I disagree with the reference. All three entries it offers -- Ce3Th I4/mmm mp-1183824, CeTh R-3m mp-1226523, CeTh3 Pm-3m mp-1183732 -- are computed ordered compounds with no ICSD counts, at cerium fractions of 25 to 75 percent. This sample is 6 percent cerium in thorium and is a random substitutional alloy with no ordering, so no mp_id is carried. Cerium is just above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; its role is substitutional on the thorium site and it acts as a magnetic Kondo impurity, which is the whole subject of both papers -- the second is a comment disputing the first.

basis: CrCl3 is named in the taxonomy entry itself: honeycomb CrCl3 layers held by van der Waals forces, and the paper measures spin-phonon scattering in a van der Waals magnet, which is that structure. Below about 240 K the stacking is rhombohedral R-3, and the whole 10-97 K measured window lies in that field.

other_polymorphs.note: The monoclinic C2/m stacking, which is the room-temperature form and the one the reference carries (2 ICSD references). It is a thermal phase, reached from R-3 on warming through about 240 K, but it lies above the 10-97 K measured window, so it is recorded here rather than in phases and spans_transition stays false. Same prototype -- the two differ only in how the honeycomb layers stack.

note: The reference makes CrCl2 Pnnm mp-22857 the PRIMARY entry with 10 ICSD references, above CrCl3 C2/m mp-27630 with 2. That is the reference describing the chemistry rather than this sample: the composition here is unambiguously CrCl3, so the dichloride is not relevant. No mp_id is carried on the measured phase because the reference offers no entry for the low-temperature R-3 stacking. The magnetic ordering near 14 K falls inside the window and is what the paper is about, but it is not a structural transition.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [148], ICSD-backed references for this host report [58, 12]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: FeCl2 is the CdCl2-type layered dihalide: triangular nets of octahedrally coordinated Fe2+ between chlorine layers stacked in the cubic three-layer sequence, R-3m, and the reference carries FeCl2 R-3m mp-23229 at hull zero with 4 ICSD references as its PRIMARY entry for this formula.
note: The new prototype cdcl2_r3m_dihalide was written to taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl before being used here. It is proposed rather than folded into cdi2_1t because the existing entry is specifically the P-3m1 CdI2 stacking of a dichalcogenide, and assigning FeCl2 there would read as a space-group disagreement (164 against 166) on every check. Same paper as the Cl-Cr host, on spin-phonon scattering in van der Waals magnets; the 11-47 K window brackets the antiferromagnetic ordering near 24 K, which changes the magnetic cell and not the prototype. The reference also lists FeCl3 R-3 and several computed iron chlorides, none of which is the 1:2 composition here.

basis: Y0.8Ca0.2Cr0.7Co0.3O3 holds ABO3 exactly and is YCrO3 with calcium on the A site and cobalt on the B site; YCrO3 is an orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskite and the paper is on calcium- and cobalt-doped yttrium chromites as a solid-oxide-fuel-cell interconnect, where the perovskite framework is what the application requires.

dopant_roles.basis: Y0.8Ca0.2Cr0.7Co0.3O3: divalent calcium on the trivalent yttrium A site is the acceptor that makes these chromites p-type conductors, which is exactly what an interconnect needs. At 0.2 of the A site it is heavy doping but it is a genuine aliovalent substitution, not an end member.

note: No reference line is offered for this host. Cobalt at 0.3 of the B site is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes for chromium and is added to improve sinterability and raise the conductivity further. The measured window 893-1259 K is the operating range of the fuel cell rather than a structural probe; YCrO3-based perovskites stay orthorhombic there, though the orthorhombic to rhombohedral crossover in heavily substituted chromites is close enough to be worth checking in the paper.

basis: Cu0.6Co0.4Fe2O4 and Cu0.4Co0.6Fe2O4 hold the AB2O4 ratio exactly and the paper calls them Cu-Co ferrites; both CuFe2O4 and CoFe2O4 are spinel ferrites and they mix continuously on the A site, so the whole series is one Fd-3m framework.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. One caveat worth recording: copper-rich CuFe2O4 undergoes a cooperative Jahn-Teller distortion to a tetragonal spinel in I4_1/amd, and the copper-rich composition here could carry some of it. That is a distortion of the same prototype, not a different one, so it is noted rather than recorded as an alternative, and the cubic space group in phases is carried at medium confidence for that reason. Cobalt and copper are both above the 5 at.% cut and share the tetrahedral A site.

basis: The composition is written as a two-component mixture and the first component, (Hf0.7Ti0.3CoSb0.8Sn0.2)0.75, is the p-type half-Heusler the paper is about -- 1:1:1 (Hf,Ti):Co:(Sb,Sn) in the cubic MgAgAs structure, tin on the antimony site as the acceptor. The second component is a Cu2Te-based phase deliberately added as a 25 percent second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu1.96Ni0.04Te0.97Se0.03: nickel substitutes copper inside the Cu2Te second phase, not in the half-Heusler matrix. It is a dopant of the minority phase.
Same second phase: selenium is the same group as tellurium and takes its site in Cu2Te, tuning that phase rather than the half-Heusler.

note: Marked mixed because the sample is genuinely two-phase by design -- a half-Heusler matrix with a Cu2Te-based inclusion phase used to scatter phonons and modify the grain boundaries. The matrix is the thermoelectric material and carries the prototype; the second phase has no taxonomy entry (Cu2Te has a complex layered structure with several superstructures and none of the existing prototypes describes it), so composite_multiphase stands in for it in alt_prototype_ids rather than a wrong specific label. No reference line is offered for this host. Hafnium, titanium, tin, copper and tellurium are all above the 5 at.% cut; within the matrix, Ti substitutes Hf isovalently on the A site and Sn substitutes Sb as the acceptor.

basis: The same material and paper as the neighbouring host at a different mixing ratio: (Hf0.7Ti0.3CoSb0.8Sn0.2)0.85 is the p-type half-Heusler matrix, 1:1:1 in the cubic MgAgAs structure with tin on the antimony site, and the remaining 0.15 is a Cu2Te-based second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Tellurium is not in the half-Heusler lattice at all; it is a constituent of the deliberate Cu2Te second phase, and it falls below the 5 at.% cut here only because that phase is 15 percent of the mixture rather than 25 percent as in the neighbouring host. Deliberate second phase, not a contaminant.
Cu1.96Ni0.04Te0.97Se0.03: nickel substitutes copper within that second phase.
Selenium on the tellurium site of the same second phase.

note: This host and Co-Cu-Hf-Sb-Sn-Te-Ti are the same composition family from one paper, separated only by where tellurium falls relative to the 5 at.% cut -- at 25 percent second phase tellurium is a host element, at 15 percent it is a minor element. The structural assignment is identical and the two records are kept consistent on purpose. No reference line is offered for this host.

basis: EuCo2P2 is the ThCr2Si2 122 phosphide -- europium layers alternating with [Co2P2] slabs of edge-sharing CoP4 tetrahedra in I4/mmm -- and the reference carries Eu(CoP)2 I4/mmm mp-20038 at hull zero with 2 ICSD references; the paper treats it as a model molecular-field helical antiferromagnet, which is the localised Eu2+ sublattice of that structure.
note: The other reference entry, Eu2Co12P7 P-6 mp-1191681, is a different compound in the same ternary. EuCo2P2 is one of the 122 phosphides that collapses its interlayer P-P bond under pressure, which is a large volume change within the same space group; nothing of the kind happens in the 11-294 K window at ambient pressure, so spans_transition is false. The helical magnetic ordering near 66 K is magnetic, not structural.

basis: Fe0.75Co0.25Ga3 and Fe0.5Co0.5Ga3 are FeGa3 with cobalt on the iron site, and both papers name the parent directly -- TMGa3 thin films for TM of Fe and Co, and the thermoelectric performance of intermetallic FeGa3 with cobalt doping. FeGa3 is the tetragonal P4_2/mnm FeGa3 type, a narrow-gap semiconductor built from Ga-Ga dimers, and CoGa3 is isostructural.
note: I disagree with the reference, which offers only Heusler and Heusler-like entries -- GaFeCo2 Fm-3m mp-30551, GaFe2Co Fm-3m mp-636212, Ga2FeCo P4/mmm mp-1224867. Those are 1:1:2 and 1:2:1 intermetallics at a completely different gallium content; the compositions here are (Fe,Co)Ga3 with three gallium per transition metal, which is the FeGa3 structure. Following the reference would have turned a narrow-gap semiconductor into a metallic Heusler. No mp_id is carried. Cobalt is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes for iron and, with one more d electron, dopes the gap electronically, which is why the series is made at all.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [136], ICSD-backed references for this host report [225]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Fe0.75Co0.25Ga2.65Ge0.35 is the same FeGa3 tetragonal P4_2/mnm structure as the neighbouring Co-Fe-Ga host, doubly substituted -- cobalt on the iron site and germanium on the gallium site -- and the paper is titled improved thermoelectric properties in heavily doped FeGa3.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Both germanium (0.35 of 4 atoms) and cobalt are above the 5 at.% cut and so carry no dopant_roles entries; germanium substitutes gallium and cobalt substitutes iron, and both are electron donors, which is what heavily doped means in the title. The 83-874 K window is wide but the FeGa3 structure is stable across it.

basis: Co1.5Ge0.5Fe1.0O4 and Co1.4Ge0.4Fe1.2O4 hold the AB2O4 ratio exactly and the paper calls them Co-Ge ferrites; this is cobalt ferrite with the coupled substitution of Ge4+ plus Co2+ for two Fe3+, which keeps charge balance inside one spinel framework.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. The coupled Ge4+ and Co2+ substitution for a pair of Fe3+ is the standard way of making the Co2GeO4 to CoFe2O4 join, and Co2GeO4 is itself a spinel, so both ends of the substitution are one prototype. Germanium is above the 5 at.% cut and takes the tetrahedral site preferentially, which is what drives the conductivity changes the paper reports.

basis: Ti0.75Hf0.25Fe0.3Co0.2Ni0.5Sb holds the 1:1:1 half-Heusler ratio exactly -- (Ti,Hf) on one site, (Fe,Co,Ni) summing to one on the second, antimony on the third -- and the paper calls it a Ti(Fe,Co,Ni)Sb pseudo-ternary; mixing the three transition metals sets an average valence electron count near the 18-electron semiconducting condition that the MgAgAs structure needs.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. All five minor-site elements are above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries; hafnium substitutes titanium isovalently for phonon scattering, and the Fe:Co:Ni ratio is the electron-count knob. Worth recording that TiFeSb and TiNiSb on their own are not 18-electron compounds -- only the mixture is -- so the half-Heusler phase here depends on the substitution being homogeneous rather than the sample separating into the binaries, which is the risk the paper is testing. The full Heusler TiNi2Sb is the competing phase if nickel segregates, but the 1:1:1 stoichiometry as written does not support it.

basis: Mn0.5Co0.5Fe2O4 holds the AB2O4 ratio exactly and the paper writes the series as (MnyCo1-y)Fe2O4; MnFe2O4 and CoFe2O4 are both spinel ferrites and mix continuously on the A site, so the composition is one Fd-3m framework.
note: The reference offers only Mn2Fe3Co3O16, Mn3Fe2Co3O16 and Mn3Fe3(CoO8)2, all in Cm (8) at hulls of 0.07 to 0.13 with no ICSD counts. Those are computed low-symmetry cation orderings of the same spinel framework at ratios that do not match this composition, so they support the prototype without supplying a structure; no mp_id is carried. Manganese and cobalt are both above the 5 at.% cut and share the A site. Measured 471-974 K, which is above the Curie temperature for much of the range -- magnetic, not structural.

basis: Pr0.4Sr0.6Co0.3Fe0.6Nb0.1O3 and its cobalt-rich partner hold ABO3 exactly, with (Pr,Sr) on the A site and (Co,Fe,Nb) summing to one on the B site; the paper writes the series as Pr0.4Sr0.6Co0.9-xFexNb0.1O3-delta, which is a cubic or orthorhombic cobaltite-ferrite perovskite of the kind used as a fuel-cell cathode.

dopant_roles.basis: Nb5+ on the B site at a fixed 0.1 across the series. It is there to stabilise the cubic perovskite and raise the average B-site valence, which suppresses the oxygen loss and the phase change these strontium-rich cobaltites otherwise show on heating; it is a structural stabiliser as much as an electronic dopant.

note: The only reference entry, SrPrFeCoO6 P1 mp-1218109, is a computed 1:1:1:1 double-perovskite ordering at hull zero with no ICSD count. It agrees at the prototype level but the compositions here are at Pr:Sr of 0.4:0.6 with a three-element B site and are disordered, so no mp_id is carried and double_perovskite is not recorded as an alternative. The cubic aristotype is carried in phases at medium confidence because the actual setting depends on the tolerance factor and the oxygen deficiency written as delta; measured 360-1169 K, where these cathode materials lose oxygen continuously.

basis: YFe0.5Co0.5O3 and its calcium-substituted partner hold ABO3 exactly, with yttrium on the A site and iron and cobalt sharing the B site; the paper names the parent as YFeO3, which is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskite, and YCoO3 is isostructural, so the B-site mixing does not leave the prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca2+ for Y3+ on the twelve-coordinate A site, which is the standard acceptor doping of a rare-earth orthoferrite. It raises the average B-site valence or creates oxygen vacancies, and since the paper is about oxygen reduction catalysis the vacancies are the point.

note: No reference line is offered for this host. The Pnma setting is the one the orthoferrites take across the whole rare-earth series; the rhombohedral R-3c setting appears only for the larger A cations, and yttrium is small. Cobalt is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry. Measured 823-1023 K, well inside the stability field of the orthorhombic phase, though these cobaltites lose oxygen continuously at those temperatures.

basis: La0.3Ce0.37Fe3CoSb12 is a doubly filled p-type skutterudite -- the Fe3Co ratio sets the electron count that the rare-earth fillers charge-compensate -- and the PbTe written after it is a separate rocksalt phase, which the paper says outright by calling the material binary-phased.

dopant_roles.site: 2a icosahedral void
dopant_roles.basis: Rare-earth filler in the empty void of the CoSb3 framework. It rattles and scatters heat-carrying phonons, and its trivalent charge is what lets iron replace cobalt on the framework site.

dopant_roles.site: 2a icosahedral void
dopant_roles.basis: The second filler in the same void. Two filler species of different mass and size broaden the rattling spectrum, which is why the double filling is made.

note: No reference line is offered for this host. Recorded as mixed because the two compositions are a skutterudite matrix plus a deliberately added PbTe second phase at 1 and 1.5 formula units, not a single structure; a composition-level split will put the PbTe fraction under rocksalt. The 5 at.% filler cut is what puts La and Ce in the dopant list, but a filled skutterudite with 0.67 fillers per formula is heavily filled by the standards of that family, not dilutely doped. Measured 472-773 K, within the stability of both phases.

basis: Co2.5Fe0.5Sn2S2 is Co3Sn2S2 with iron on the cobalt kagome site, and the paper title names the shandite structure directly; Co3Sn2S2 is the R-3m Ni3Pb2S2 shandite that this entry is written for, and both substitutions here stay inside that framework.

dopant_roles.basis: Indium for tin on the main-group site, one electron fewer, which moves the Fermi level down through the flat bands of the cobalt kagome net. That is the double substitution the title refers to: iron on the transition-metal site and indium on the main-group site, tuning carriers from two directions.

note: No reference line is offered for this host, but the neighbouring Co-In-S host in this chunk is the fully substituted end member Co3In2S2 and its Materials Project entry In2Co3S2 R-3m mp-19804 confirms the setting for the same framework. Iron is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes cobalt and suppresses the ferromagnetism of the parent. No structural transition is expected in the measured 297-621 K window.

basis: ZrFe0.2Co0.8Sb holds the 1:1:1 MgAgAs ratio exactly and the paper title calls it Fe-doped ZrCoSb half-Heusler; ZrCoSb is one of the standard 18-electron half-Heusler semiconductors and iron on the cobalt site is p-type doping within that structure.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Iron is at 0.2 of 3 atoms, above the 5 at.% cut, and so carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes cobalt and removes one valence electron per substitution, taking the compound off the 18-electron count and making it degenerately p-type. The competing phase in these samples is the full Heusler ZrCo2Sb, which is what the microstructure work in the title is about, but the stoichiometry as written is 1:1:1.

basis: Fe1-xCoxTe2 across x of 0.2 to 0.4 is the marcasite solid solution: FeTe2 (frohbergite) and CoTe2 (mattagamite) are both orthorhombic Pnnm marcasites built from edge-sharing MTe6 octahedra with Te-Te dimers, and they are miscible, which is why the paper can sinter the whole series.
note: I disagree with the reference. Materials Project offers only FeCoTe2 P-3m1 (164) mp-1224955 at hull 0.193 with no ICSD count, which is a CdI2-type layered arrangement. The ditellurides of iron and cobalt are marcasites, not layered dichalcogenides; the CdI2 type belongs to the group 4 and 5 ditellurides and to the Ni-Te system. The hull value of 0.19 marks that entry as a computed hypothetical rather than an observed phase, so no mp_id is carried and the assignment is made from the chemistry. Confidence is medium rather than high because the Fe-Te system is notoriously non-stoichiometric and the tetragonal PbO-type Fe1+xTe is a competing phase, but that is at 1:1, not at Te2. Cobalt is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes iron and is the carrier-tuning variable of the series.

basis: Co2MnGa is the textbook L2_1 full Heusler -- cobalt on the two tetrahedral sublattices, manganese and gallium ordered on the rocksalt sublattice, Fm-3m -- and both papers study its anomalous Nernst and transverse response, which is the magnetic Weyl physics specific to that ordered cubic structure.
note: The reference agrees: MnGaCo2 Fm-3m mp-21171 at hull zero with 5 ICSD references is the PRIMARY entry and is carried. The other two entries, Mn2GaCo F-43m mp-20160 and MnGa2Co Fm-3m mp-623453, are the inverse Heusler and a gallium-rich variant at different stoichiometries and do not apply. Measured 10-380 K, below the Curie temperature throughout; Co2MnGa also shows a martensitic instability in some off-stoichiometric compositions, but not at the exact 2:1:1 ratio written here.

basis: (Ga0.33Co0.67)2Sr2CoO6 splits exactly into a [(Ga,Co)2O2+delta] bilayer plus a [Sr2CoO4] single perovskite block, which is the 2201 cation and anion count of Bi2Sr2CuO6 and of the known cobaltite Bi2Sr2CoO6; the paper announces it as a new layered cobaltite, and the integer CoO2 count rules out the misfit composites that dominate the rest of the Sr-Co-O chemistry.
note: No reference line is offered for this host and no space group is claimed. The prototype was proposed in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl before use. The reading I am least sure of is the coordination of gallium: if it is tetrahedral the layer is a chain layer of the Ga-1212 cuprate kind rather than a rocksalt bilayer, which would keep the intergrowth description but change the entry. Recorded at medium confidence for that reason. Gallium is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; it shares the bilayer site with cobalt at a fixed 1:2 ratio and is a framework component, not a dopant. The high-spin Co3+ state named in the title is electronic, not a separate phase.

basis: The paper is titled thermoelectric power of Gd4(Co1-xCux)3 compounds, so both samples are the rare-earth-rich R4T3 phase, which takes the hexagonal Ho4Co3 type; Gd4Co3 sits between the R12T7 phases and the Laves phase GdCo2 in that binary and is a distinct line compound, not a solid solution of either.

dopant_roles.basis: Copper for cobalt on the transition-metal sublattice, which is the composition variable x of the series. It fills the 3d band and weakens the cobalt moment, which is what the thermopower measurement is tracking.

note: Two things to flag. First, the second composition string reads Gd(Co0.95Cu0.05)3, a 1:3 ratio, while the first reads Gd4Co3 and the paper title says Gd4(Co1-xCux)3; I take the 4:3 phase for both and treat the missing subscript as a transcription slip, since GdCo3 and Gd4Co3 are different compounds and only one of them is in the title. Second, I disagree with the reference on the setting: Materials Project returns Gd4Co3 P-3 (147) mp-1225806 at hull 0.005 with no ICSD count, while the Ho4Co3 type is hexagonal P6_3mc. The P-3 entry is a computed low-symmetry relaxation with no experimental backing, so no mp_id is carried and confidence is medium. The reference also carries GdCo2 Fd-3m mp-1080387 with 25 ICSD references, which is the Laves phase of the same binary and the phase this host would be wrongly assigned to if the composition were ignored.

basis: Yb3Co4Ge13 is a Remeika phase and the paper says so in its title, naming the Pr3Rh4Sn13 structure type; the 3-4-13 stoichiometry is exact and the cubic Pm-3n cage framework with rare earth inside is what the taxonomy entry is written for.

dopant_roles.site: the cage site
dopant_roles.basis: Lanthanum for ytterbium on the rare-earth site at 0.7 of 3, which is an alloying substitution rather than dilute doping. Trivalent La is a reference point against the intermediate valence of Yb, so the substitution is there to move the valence and the Kondo scale, not to add carriers.

note: The reference agrees at the composition: Yb3Co4Ge13 Pm-3n mp-1203071 at hull zero with 1 ICSD reference, which is carried. The other entries returned for this host, Yb5(Co2Ge5)2, Yb(CoGe)6, YbCoGe2 and Yb7In(CoGe3)4, are different compounds in the same ternary at stoichiometries that do not match. Measured 239-380 K with no structural transition expected; some Remeika phases show a superlattice distortion at low temperature but not in this window.

basis: Both compositions are Co4Sb12 with two filler species in the void, and the paper title is about CoSb3-based skutterudites; the Co4Sb12 framework is written out explicitly, so the structure is not in doubt whatever the filler labels say.

dopant_roles.site: 2a icosahedral void
dopant_roles.basis: Indium in the void of the CoSb3 framework. Indium filling is limited to a few per cent and part of it often ends up as InSb at the grain boundaries, but the filler role is the intended one.

There is no iodine here. The composition string is written TI0.1, which is thallium typed with a capital letter i, and the parser has split it into an element T that it dropped and an iodine. The real filler is Tl at 0.1 per formula, the second half of a Tl and In double filling.

note: No reference line is offered for this host. The hydrogen in the host system name is not real either: it is the residue of the same TI parse failure, so this host should route to Co-Sb with Tl and In as fillers, and the record should be revisited if the composition strings are ever re-parsed. The structural assignment is unaffected because Co4Sb12 is spelled out in both strings. Measured 325-761 K, within the stability of the skutterudite framework.

basis: Ti0.167Zr0.167Hf0.167V0.167Nb0.167Ta0.167CoSb puts six group 4 and group 5 metals in equal amounts on one site, cobalt on the second and antimony on the third, which is the 1:1:1 MgAgAs ratio exactly; the paper title calls it a high-entropy half-Heusler, and the six mixed metals average to a valence electron count that keeps the 18-electron semiconducting condition.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Deliberately not filed under high_entropy_alloy: that entry is for a disordered single-phase solid solution on one lattice, whereas this is an ordered ternary compound whose three sublattices remain distinct and only one of which is mixed. The configurational entropy is a phonon-scattering device inside the half-Heusler structure, not a different structure. Three of the mixed metals are pentavalent and three tetravalent, so the mean electron count is half an electron above the 18-electron point, which is why the paper can make the mixture at all. All six are above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries.

basis: (Zr0.65Hf0.35)(Co0.65Pt0.35)(Sb0.65Sn0.35) is written as three mixed sites in exact 1:1:1 proportion, and both papers are about (Zr,Hf)CoSb half-Heusler phases as p-type thermoelectrics; substituting Pt for Co and Sn for Sb keeps the MgAgAs framework while moving the electron count below 18, which is what makes it p-type.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. All six elements are above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries; hafnium for zirconium is isoelectronic mass contrast, while the platinum and tin substitutions at 0.35 each are heavy enough to be alloying rather than doping. The papers describe the result as semimetallic, which is a consequence of that heavy substitution closing the gap, not of a different structure. Measured 11-301 K.

basis: Co3In2S2 is the indium shandite, isostructural with Co3Sn2S2: a rhombohedral R-3m framework of cobalt kagome layers sandwiching the main-group atoms, with sulfur capping the cobalt triangles. The paper is about metal-atom ordering and Fermi-level tuning in exactly this framework.

dopant_roles.site: the main-group site
dopant_roles.basis: Tin for indium on the main-group site adds one electron per substitution, which is the Fermi-level tuning the paper is doing. In the same framework Co3Sn2S2 is the ferromagnetic Weyl semimetal and Co3In2S2 is not, so this substitution walks between the two.

note: The reference agrees: In2Co3S2 R-3m mp-19804 at hull zero with 3 ICSD references is carried. The second entry, In2CoS4 Fd-3m mp-21173 at hull 0.135, is the thiospinel of the same ternary at a different stoichiometry and does not apply. Measured 313-676 K; the metal-atom ordering the title refers to is a site-occupancy effect inside the shandite framework, not a change of prototype.

basis: LaCo0.75Nb0.25O3 and LaCo0.67Nb0.33O3 hold ABO3 exactly, with lanthanum on the A site and cobalt and niobium sharing the B site; the paper title is about Nb-substituted lanthanum cobaltite, and LaCoO3 is the rhombohedral R-3c perovskite that this substitution starts from.
note: I disagree with the reference. Materials Project returns only La4Nb(CoO4)3 P-1 (2) mp-1223118 at hull 0.032 with no ICSD count, a computed triclinic cation ordering at a composition close to LaCo0.75Nb0.25O3. It supports the prototype but not a structure, so no mp_id is carried. The rhombohedral setting is recorded at medium confidence because a third of the B site being pentavalent niobium is a large perturbation and orthorhombic or even cubic settings are reported across this substitution series; the prototype itself is not in doubt. Niobium is at exactly the 5 at.% cut and appears in the composition rather than the dopant list, so it carries no dopant_roles entry; it is a B-site framework component that raises the average valence and drives cobalt towards Co2+.

basis: LiCo1-xMgxO2 is layered lithium cobaltite: alternating LiO2 and CoO2 sheets of edge-sharing octahedra in the rhombohedral alpha-NaFeO2 ordering of rocksalt, R-3m. The paper compares Cu, Mg, Ni and Zn substitution in LiCoO2, so the parent is named directly and magnesium goes on the cobalt site.
note: The reference offers five computed lithium-magnesium-cobalt oxides -- Li14MgCo13O28 P-1, Li2MgCo13O28 P1, Li2MgCo3O8 C2/m, Li4MgCo3O8 R-3m and Li8MgCo13O28 P1 -- all at hulls between 0.012 and 0.103 with no ICSD counts. These are cation-ordering models of the same layered framework at compositions that do not match, and the one that shares the R-3m setting, Li4MgCo3O8 mp-773461, is at Mg 0.25 rather than 0.2 or 0.3. None is carried. Magnesium is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; Mg2+ for Co3+ is acceptor doping that forces Co4+ and is what raises the conductivity. The 13-1180 K measured range is wide and the upper end is where LiCoO2 begins to lose lithium and oxygen, which is chemical degradation rather than a phase transition, so spans_transition is false. The cubic spinel-like low-temperature LiCoO2 polymorph is a synthesis product, not a thermal phase, and these samples are the layered form.

basis: LuCo2 is a cubic C15 MgCu2 Laves phase, Fd-3m, like the rest of the RCo2 series that both papers study; the papers are about transport in spin-fluctuation systems and in RCo2 compounds, which is the itinerant cobalt sublattice of exactly that structure.
note: The reference agrees: LuCo2 Fd-3m mp-1071554 at hull zero with 11 ICSD references is the PRIMARY entry and is carried. Lu2Co17, LuCo3, Lu2Co7 and Lu4Co3 are the other line compounds of the binary and do not apply at this composition. LuCo2 is an exchange-enhanced Pauli paramagnet with no magnetic ordering and no structural transition; the metamagnetic transition of the RCo2 family is field-induced, not thermal. Measured 12-627 K with outliers to 1000 K, all inside the stability field of the C15 phase.

basis: (Mn0.5Co0.5)3O4 and Cu0.23Mn1.44Co1.32O4 both hold the AB2O4 spinel ratio, and the second paper is explicitly about a sol-gel derived (Cu,Mn,Co)3O4 spinel; Mn3O4 and Co3O4 are both spinels and mix continuously, so the manganese-cobalt oxides at these ratios are one Fd-3m framework with mixed valence on both sites.

dopant_roles.site: tetrahedral A site
dopant_roles.basis: Copper in a manganese-cobalt spinel takes the tetrahedral site as Cu2+ or Cu+ and is the standard way of raising the conductivity of these NTC thermistor oxides by several orders of magnitude. At 0.23 per four oxygens it is a genuine substituent rather than a trace.

note: The reference returns five computed manganese-cobalt oxides -- Mn(CoO2)2 P1, Mn(CoO2)4 C2/m, Mn(CoO3)2 C2/m marked AMBIGUOUS, Mn2Co2O5 P4/mmm and Mn2Co5O12 C2 -- at hulls from 0.025 to 0.52 with no ICSD counts, all of them cation-ordering models rather than observed phases, so none is carried. The cubic setting is recorded at medium confidence for a real reason: manganese-rich members of this series are tetragonal I4_1/amd from cooperative Jahn-Teller distortion of Mn3+, and the cubic-to-tetragonal boundary runs near these compositions, with the cubic form favoured as temperature rises across the measured 309-1067 K. That is a distortion within the spinel prototype rather than a change of prototype, so spans_transition is left false, but a composition close to the boundary should not be asserted as cubic with high confidence. Note also that the first paper listed for this host is about wurtzite (Al,Ti)N and appears to be a linkage error in the source data; it did not inform this assignment.

basis: Co2MnSi is the canonical L2_1 full Heusler and one of the best studied half-metallic ferromagnets; the first paper is titled structural and thermoelectric properties of ternary full-Heusler alloys, so the structure is named in the source.
note: The reference ranks MnCoSi Pnma mp-19809 first on ICSD count (7 references), but that is the equiatomic TiNiSi-type compound, a different phase of the same ternary; the composition here is 2:1:1, so MnCo2Si Fm-3m mp-4492 at hull zero with 6 ICSD references is the entry that matches and is carried. This is the case the chunk header warns about: the reference describes which phases exist in a chemistry, and only the composition says which one was made. The SiC written in the curator detail of one sample is a nanodispersed second phase added for mechanical properties, not a host component, and the sample recorded here is the x equals zero member in any case.
