basis: Co2MnSn is the L2_1 full Heusler of the same series as Co2MnSi and Co2MnGa, and both papers treat it as a ferromagnetic Heusler whose magnetic and transport properties change with phase separation; the 2:1:1 stoichiometry is exact.
note: The reference agrees: MnCo2Sn Fm-3m mp-20840 at hull zero with 9 ICSD references is the PRIMARY entry and is carried. Mn2CoSn F-43m mp-22465 is the inverse Heusler at a different stoichiometry. The flower-like phase separation one paper reports is a microstructural decomposition into Heusler and Co-Sn-rich regions on annealing, which matters for the magnetics but does not change what the majority phase is; it would be worth revisiting at sample level if those papers are ever read. Measured 11-392 K, far below the Curie temperature and with no structural transition.

basis: CoNb1-xMoxSn holds 1:1:1 exactly and the paper title is high temperature thermoelectric properties of CoNb1-xMxSn half-Heuslers; CoNbSn is an 18-electron half-Heusler semiconductor and molybdenum for niobium is n-type doping inside the MgAgAs structure.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Molybdenum is at 0.3 and 0.5 of three atoms, far above the 5 at.% cut, so it carries no dopant_roles entry; at x of 0.5 the material is half way to a hypothetical CoMoSn and is better read as an alloy than as a doped compound. Measured 332-843 K with no structural transition expected in that window.

basis: Na(Co,Ni)2O4 is the way NaCo2O4 is conventionally written, which is Na0.5CoO2: CdI2-type CoO2 sheets of edge-sharing octahedra with sodium partly occupying the interlayer, in P6_3/mmc. The paper title says NaCo2O4 outright and nickel substitutes cobalt in the sheet.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Nickel is at 0.4 to 0.5 of seven atoms, above the 5 at.% cut, and so carries no dopant_roles entry; Ni for Co in the sheet is what the paper varies. The sodium content of these phases is a compositional variable rather than a dopant, as the taxonomy notes record, and it changes during high-temperature measurement because sodium is volatile -- the 721-1073 K window is where that happens, so the sodium stoichiometry at measurement is not necessarily the one written. That is a composition question, not a prototype change.

basis: Ta0.333Nb0.333V0.333CoSb and its 0.25/0.375/0.375 partner hold 1:1:1 exactly with three group 5 metals sharing one site; the paper title is about thermal conductivity reduction by the isoelectronic elements V and Ta, which only makes sense in the NbCoSb half-Heusler they are substituting into.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. All three group 5 metals are above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries; the substitution is isoelectronic by construction, which is the point of the paper -- mass and strain contrast to scatter phonons without touching the carrier count. Worth recording that NbCoSb is a 19-electron half-Heusler and is usually made vacancy-ordered as Nb0.8CoSb; the compositions here are written as full 1:1:1, so any vacancy content is not visible in the data. Measured 20-702 K.

basis: Nd6Co2Sn is a rare-earth-rich R6T2X ternary and the Materials Project entry Nd6Co2Sn Immm mp-1210166 matches both the composition and the Ho6Co2Ga type that family takes. The second composition, Nd12Co6Sn, is a different line compound at 12:6:1 and cannot be the same phase, so the host holds two structures.
note: Two prototypes were proposed in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl before use, ho6co2ga_type for Nd6Co2Sn and r12t6x_sm12ni6in for Nd12Co6Sn, and the host is recorded as mixed with one sample under each. Confidence is low throughout: the paper is a crystal structure and magnetism study of ternary neodymium compounds that I have not read, neither composition has an ICSD-backed space group, and the setting for the 12:6:1 compound is left unstated rather than guessed. The reference also returns Nd3Co4Sn13 Pm-3n mp-1198940, which is the Remeika phase of this ternary and the entry a formula-blind match would have taken; it is at a completely different stoichiometry and does not apply. A composition-level split is needed here and the two structures should be checked against the paper.

basis: PrNi0.4Co0.6O3 and PrNi0.6Co0.4O3 hold ABO3 exactly with praseodymium on the A site and nickel and cobalt sharing the B site; both papers call them perovskites in the title and use them as solid-oxide-fuel-cell cathodes, where PrNiO3 and PrCoO3 are both orthorhombic GdFeO3-type and mix continuously.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Both papers write the formula with a minus delta, so these are oxygen-deficient, and at the 322-1172 K measured range the deficiency grows continuously with temperature -- a defect chemistry effect, not a phase transition, so spans_transition is false. The orthorhombic setting is at medium confidence because rare-earth nickelates commonly show an orthorhombic to rhombohedral change on heating; that is a tilt distortion within the perovskite prototype and would not change the assignment. Both B-site metals are above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries.

basis: SrCo0.6Ni0.4O3 and SrCo0.7Ni0.3O3 hold ABO3 with strontium on the A site and cobalt and nickel on the B site, and the paper title calls them perovskites; SrCoO3 is the cubic end member of this chemistry and nickel substitution stabilises it.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. The real uncertainty is oxygen content, not cation arrangement: strontium cobaltite is written SrCoO3 but is only reached as the fully oxidised cubic perovskite under oxidising conditions, and it readily loses oxygen to SrCoO2.5, which orders its vacancies into the brownmillerite structure. brownmillerite is therefore carried as an alternative rather than ignored. Confidence is medium and a sample-level check of the oxygen stoichiometry would settle it. Both B-site metals are above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries. Measured 298-773 K.

basis: Ti2NiCoSn0.5Sb1.5, which the curator detail spells out as Ti2-x-y-qAlxTayZrqNiCoSn0.5Sb1.5, is a double half-Heusler: two formula units of the MgAgAs structure written together, with (Ni,Co) on one site and (Sn,Sb) on the other, averaging to the 18-electron count that neither TiNiSn nor TiCoSb reaches at this composition alone. The paper title names the Ti2NiCoSn parent directly.

dopant_roles.basis: Aluminium on the group 4 site at a fixed 0.2 per two titaniums. It has three fewer valence electrons than titanium, so it is an acceptor, and together with tantalum it is the entropy engineering the title refers to -- mixing the site while holding the average electron count.
Tantalum on the same group 4 site at a fixed 0.2, one electron more than titanium and much heavier. It compensates the aluminium electronically and adds mass contrast for phonon scattering.

note: No reference line is offered for this host. Recorded as a single half-Heusler rather than mixed: a double half-Heusler is not two phases but one structure with two mixed sublattices, and whether (Ni,Co) and (Sn,Sb) order or stay random is a superstructure question inside the same prototype. Zirconium is above the 5 at.% cut in one composition and carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes titanium isovalently. The off-stoichiometry of the title is the deficiency on the titanium site, written 2-x-y-q, which is a vacancy concentration rather than a second phase.

basis: Pb0.7Sr2Co0.3O3(CoO2)1.79 is written in the misfit notation itself -- a rocksalt-type [Pb,Sr,Co]O3 block with an irrational 1.79 CoO2 layers per formula -- and the paper is titled thermopower enhancement in misfit cobaltites. The irrational ratio is the definition of the incommensurate composite.

dopant_roles.site: rocksalt block
dopant_roles.basis: Calcium for strontium in the rocksalt block of one composition, at 0.5 against 1.5 strontium. That is an alloying substitution, not dilute doping: the size of the rocksalt cation is what sets the misfit ratio between the two subsystems, so replacing a quarter of it changes the 1.75 to 1.79 seen across these two samples.

note: No reference line is offered and none could apply: the README flags misfit_cobaltite as needing special handling in stage 2 because an incommensurate composite has two subsystems and no single Materials Project entry, so spacegroup_number and mp_id are deliberately null rather than filled with one subsystem. The two compositions differ in both the calcium content and the misfit ratio and are the same structural family. Measured 11-699 K.

basis: CoPr2W2O10 is the cobalt member of the R2MW2O10 double tungstates, the same family as the CdPr2W2O10 that this entry was written for in the previous chunk -- a monoclinic framework of edge-sharing W2O10 octahedral dimers with the rare earth and the divalent metal in the cavities. The paper reports three new ceramic tungstates, which is that family.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. The prototype entry lists cobalt explicitly among the divalent metals of the family and names CdPr2W2O10 as its exemplar, so this is the same praseodymium tungstate with cobalt in place of cadmium. No space group is recorded because the family is reported in both P2_1/c and C2/c settings and the composition alone does not fix which; that is stated in the proposed entry and is not resolved here. Cobalt is a framework component, not a dopant. Measured 297-494 K.

basis: Co0.88Ni0.12Sb2.91Sn0.09 is an unfilled CoSb3 skutterudite with nickel and tin as the carrier dopants, and the PbTe written in front of it at 0.24 and 0.48 formula units is a separate rocksalt phase -- the paper is titled the effect of PbTe on the thermoelectric properties of that skutterudite, so the two are deliberately kept as distinct phases.

dopant_roles.site: framework metal site
dopant_roles.basis: Nickel for cobalt on the framework site, one electron more, making the skutterudite n-type. It is a framework substitution, not a void filler.

dopant_roles.site: framework pnictogen site
dopant_roles.basis: Tin on the antimony ring site, one electron fewer, partly compensating the nickel. The pair is how this composition is tuned; neither enters the void.

note: No reference line is offered for this host. Recorded as mixed and as the unfilled skutterudite rather than filled_skutterudite: the 2a void is empty in this composition, lead stays in the PbTe second phase, and the curator detail confirms the PbTe content is quoted as a mass percentage of an added phase. A composition-level split will put the PbTe fraction under rocksalt. Measured 297-803 K, within the stability of both phases.

basis: Co0.2Ti0.8S2 and Co0.3Ti0.7S2 are Co-doped TiS2, which the paper title says directly; TiS2 is the 1T CdI2-type layered dichalcogenide, P-3m1, with S-Ti-S sandwiches separated by a van der Waals gap, and cobalt at these levels sits on or between the titanium layers without leaving that framework.
note: I partly disagree with the reference. Materials Project returns Ti2CoS4 C2/m mp-1025269, Ti4CoS8 C2/m mp-1105097 and two Ti3CoS6 entries, all at hulls below 0.06 and with at most 1 ICSD reference each. Those are ordered cobalt-intercalated superstructures of the same CdI2 layers -- Ti4CoS8 is exactly the Co0.2Ti0.8S2 composition written as a supercell -- so they corroborate the framework but describe a cation ordering the paper does not claim. No mp_id is carried and the parent P-3m1 setting is recorded instead. Cobalt is above the 5 at.% cut and so carries no dopant_roles entry; whether it substitutes titanium in the layer or intercalates into the gap is the open question, and the paper calls it doping. Measured 10-310 K.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [164], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Zn3.5Co0.5Sb3 and Zn3.6Co0.4Sb3 are Zn4-xCoxSb3, which the paper title writes out; beta-Zn4Sb3 is the rhombohedral R-3c structure with a well-ordered antimony framework and heavily disordered interstitial zinc, and cobalt substitution stays inside it.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. The measured 299-600 K window sits between the two transitions of this compound and crosses neither: the beta to alpha ordering transitions are near 254 and 235 K, below the window, and the beta to gamma transition is near 765 K, above it, so spans_transition is false. Cobalt is at 0.4 to 0.5 of about seven atoms, above the 5 at.% cut, and so carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes zinc on the framework site. The disordered interstitial zinc of this structure is a structural feature, not a dopant.

basis: ScCo2 is a cubic C15 MgCu2 Laves phase, Fd-3m, and both papers study the RCo2 series as spin-fluctuation systems, which is the itinerant cobalt sublattice of that structure.
note: The reference agrees: ScCo2 Fd-3m mp-253 at hull zero with 10 ICSD references is the PRIMARY entry and is carried. Sc2Co, ScCo, Sc3Co and Sc4Co are the other line compounds of the binary and do not apply at 1:2. ScCo2 is an exchange-enhanced paramagnet with no magnetic or structural transition in the measured 12-983 K window. This host and Co-Lu in the same chunk are the same structure from the same two papers.

basis: Co2TiSi is an L2_1 full Heusler and both papers treat it as a half-metallic ferromagnet of the Co2TiZ series with Z of Si, Ge and Sn; the 2:1:1 stoichiometry is exact and the cubic Fm-3m ordering is what the half-metallicity depends on.
note: The reference agrees at the composition: TiCo2Si Fm-3m mp-1064854 at hull zero with 5 ICSD references is carried. TiCoSi Pnma mp-21306, Ti6Co16Si7, Ti4Co4Si7 and Ti2CoSi are other phases of the same ternary at different stoichiometries; as with Co-Mn-Si in this chunk, the equiatomic TiNiSi-type compound is a real phase of the system but not the one written here. Measured 11-894 K with no structural transition; the Curie temperature near 380 K falls inside the window but is magnetic.

basis: Sm3Zn2Co3 does not correspond to a structure type I can identify. Read as Sm3T5 with zinc and cobalt sharing the transition-metal sublattice it would sit near the R3T5 compounds, but that reading is a guess from the stoichiometry alone and neither paper gives the structure -- one is a 1954 survey of thermoelectric power in metal alloys and the other a review of rare-earth alloys.
note: Parked in unresolved_crystalline deliberately rather than forced onto a prototype. The only reference entry, SmZnCo2 P6_3/mmc mp-1208993 at hull 0.036 with no ICSD count, is at a 1:1:2 ratio against the 3:2:3 written here and does not match; taking it would have asserted a hexagonal Laves-like phase that the composition does not support. What is needed is the source paper, which should say whether Sm3Zn2Co3 is a line compound or an as-cast multiphase alloy -- a 1954 metals survey is as likely to have measured the latter. Measured 214-376 K.

basis: The paper is about In-doped CdCr2S4, a ferromagnetic thiospinel with colossal magnetocapacitance, so the composition string Cs0.97In0.03Cr2S4 is CdCr2S4 with the cadmium mistranscribed as caesium; ACr2S4 with a tetrahedral divalent A and octahedral Cr3+ is the normal spinel, Fd-3m.

dopant_roles.site: tetrahedral A site
dopant_roles.basis: Indium for cadmium on the tetrahedral site. In3+ against Cd2+ is one extra electron, so it is n-type doping, and the paper is about how the resulting carriers form magnetic polarons that drive the magnetocapacitance.

note: Recorded with the disagreement rather than around it: the host system as stored is Cr-Cs-S and the composition names caesium, but caesium has no chemistry that gives ACr2S4 with A monovalent at 0.97 per formula, and the paper title names CdCr2S4. This host should route to Cd-Cr-S and the record should be revisited if the composition strings are re-parsed. The reference, CsCr5S8 C2/m mp-1021518 at hull 0.041, is what a literal reading of the stored formula pulls up and is a genuine caesium chromium sulfide but at a completely different stoichiometry; it is not carried. Confidence is medium because it rests on that correction. Measured 10-296 K, which spans the Curie temperature near 85 K -- magnetic, not structural.

basis: Fe1-xCuxCr2S4 holds the AB2O4 ratio with iron and copper sharing the tetrahedral site and chromium on the octahedral site; the paper title is electrical transport in FeCr2S4-CuCr2S4 spinels, so both end members are named and both are thiospinels that mix continuously.
note: TEDesignLab returns Cr4FeCuS8 F-43m (216) mp-6685 at hull 0.045 with 2 ICSD references, which is the same spinel framework with iron and copper ordered onto the tetrahedral site, lowering the symmetry from Fd-3m to F-43m. I record the disordered 227 parent because the compositions here are at 0.41 and 0.55 copper rather than the ordered 1:1, and carry no mp_id for the same reason; a reviewer who wants the ordered cell should use mp-6685. The Materials Project entries Cr8Fe3CuS16 in P-4m2 and R3m are further computed orderings at 3:1. Both A-site metals are above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries -- this is an alloy series between two end members, not a doped compound. Measured 19-554 K, spanning the ferrimagnetic ordering near 380 K in the copper-rich member, which is magnetic.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [216]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CuCrTiS4 holds the AB2S4 thiospinel ratio with copper on the tetrahedral site and chromium and titanium sharing the octahedral site; it is the known thiospinel of the CuCr2S4 family with half the chromium replaced by titanium, and the second paper discusses it among spin-entropy thermoelectrics, which is an octahedral-site property.
note: The only reference entry, TiCrCuS4 Imma (74) mp-1216972 at hull zero with no ICSD count, is a computed orthorhombic ordering of chromium and titanium on the octahedral site of the same spinel framework. It agrees at the prototype level and I record the cubic disordered parent instead, since an ordered 1:1 arrangement is a claim the data does not make; no mp_id is carried. Titanium is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry -- Ti4+ against Cr3+ is what sets the copper valence and the carrier count in this compound. Measured 11-322 K.

basis: The compositions are written as two bracketed groups with volume or mass fractions after them -- an yttria-stabilised zirconia (Y0.06Zr0.97O2.03) and an austenitic stainless steel (Ni0.08Cr0.18Fe0.76) -- and the paper is titled thermal conductivities of SUS304/PSZ composite materials. This is a deliberate two-phase ceramic-metal composite, not a compound.

dopant_roles.basis: Yttrium for zirconium in the zirconia phase. Y3+ for Zr4+ creates the oxygen vacancies that stabilise the tetragonal or cubic fluorite structure at room temperature, which is what partially stabilised means in the title; it is a structural stabiliser, not a transport dopant.
Nickel in the steel phase at 8 per cent, the austenite stabiliser of SUS304. It belongs to the metal phase and says nothing about the oxide.

note: Recorded as mixed with fluorite_oxide and solid_solution_alloy as the two constituents, and skipped for structure resolution as the README directs for composite_multiphase. The 5 at.% split has cut this host badly: yttrium and nickel land in the dopant list even though each belongs to a different phase, and chromium and iron are the steel while zirconium and oxygen are the ceramic. Measured 64-1368 K, which crosses the zirconia tetragonal-to-cubic range, but that is one constituent of a composite and no single-phase transition is recorded.

basis: (Fe1-xCrx)Sb2 is chromium-substituted FeSb2, which the paper title says directly; FeSb2 is the orthorhombic Pnnm marcasite, a correlated narrow-gap semiconductor with a colossal low-temperature thermopower, and that is the property both the paper and the 11-303 K measured window are about.
note: I disagree with the reference. Materials Project returns CrFe2Sb Fm-3m mp-1008225 at hull 0.207, and three computed antimonides Cr(Fe2Sb5)2, CrFe3Sb4 and CrFeSb4, none with more than 1 ICSD reference. The first is a Heusler-like 2:1:1 intermetallic at a completely different antimony content, and the others are hypothetical polyantimonides; none is FeSb2 with chromium on the iron site, which is what the paper made. No mp_id is carried. Chromium is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; at x of 0.5 the sample is half way to CrSb2, which is also a marcasite, so the prototype holds across the whole series.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [58], ICSD-backed references for this host report [225]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: GaNCr3-xMnx is written in antiperovskite order in the composition strings themselves and the paper title calls them antiperovskite nitrides: nitrogen at the octahedral centre, the transition metals on the face centres and gallium at the corners, which is the ABX3 perovskite with the anion and cation roles swapped.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Manganese is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; it substitutes chromium on the octahedral metal site and is the composition variable x of the series. Antiperovskite manganese nitrides are the family that shows negative thermal expansion and magnetovolume effects, and the measured 10-325 K window spans whatever magnetic ordering these compositions have, but that is magnetic rather than a change of prototype, so spans_transition is false.

basis: Ni0.90Cr0.10H0.5 and H0.7 are a hydrogenated nickel-chromium alloy, which the paper title says directly; nickel and its chromium solid solutions are face-centred cubic and hydrogen occupies the octahedral interstices of that lattice, giving the Fm-3m interstitial hydride with hydrogen content as a continuous variable.
note: No reference line is offered for this host. Hydrogen and chromium are both above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries; hydrogen is interstitial in the octahedral sites and chromium substitutional on the nickel sites. At x of 0.5 to 0.7 these are close to the saturated beta hydride, which is the same fcc metal lattice with an expanded cell, not a different structure -- the alpha to beta miscibility gap is a composition boundary, not a thermal transition, so spans_transition is false for the 91-227 K window. solid_solution_alloy is carried as an alternative because the metal sublattice alone is exactly that; the hydride entry is the more informative of the two.

basis: La0.75Sr0.25CrO3 and La0.6Sr0.4CrO3 hold ABO3 exactly with lanthanum and strontium sharing the A site and chromium on the B site; both papers are about strontium-doped lanthanum chromite, the standard interconnect and electrode perovskite, which is orthorhombic GdFeO3-type at room temperature.
note: I disagree with the reference. Materials Project returns Sr2LaCrO6 Fm-3m mp-1079391 at hull 0.234 with 1 ICSD reference, SrLa3Cr4O12 P2, SrLa4Cr5O15 C2/m and SrLaCrO4 I4mm; the first is a double-perovskite ordering at a strontium content twice what is written here, and the last is a Ruddlesden-Popper-like 214 phase, a different structure altogether. None matches La0.75Sr0.25CrO3 as a disordered orthorhombic perovskite, so no mp_id is carried. The setting is at medium confidence: LaCrO3 changes from orthorhombic Pnma to rhombohedral R-3c near 540 K and strontium substitution pushes that boundary down, so the room-temperature setting at x of 0.4 may already be rhombohedral. The robust measured range is 151-348 K, below the undoped transition, which is why spans_transition is false -- but the full span reaches 1123 K in one curve and a sample-level look would likely find the rhombohedral form at the top of it. Strontium is above the 5 at.% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry; it is the acceptor that makes these chromites conducting.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62], ICSD-backed references for this host report [225]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions are a magnesium matrix carrying a long list of elements at per-mille to per-cent levels, which is a spectrographic analysis of a commercial alloy rather than a compound -- the paper is a survey of low-temperature transport in commercial metals and alloys. Magnesium is hexagonal close packed and everything else is dissolved in or precipitated from it.

dopant_roles.basis: A deliberate addition in commercial magnesium alloys, added to control the iron content and improve corrosion resistance.
One of the two main strengthening additions to commercial magnesium, soluble in the hcp matrix.
The standard grain refiner for aluminium-free magnesium alloys, present at the tenth-of-a-per-cent level typical of that use.
A minor deliberate addition for creep and ignition resistance, or a residue of the reduction process.
A common impurity in commercial magnesium with very low solid solubility; it forms intermetallic particles rather than staying in solution.
The characteristic magnesium impurity, essentially insoluble and present as separate iron-rich particles.
An impurity that appears as Mg2Si precipitates rather than in the matrix.
A trace of the spectrographic analysis, at the 0.01 level, with no solubility in magnesium.
A trace of the spectrographic analysis at the 0.01 level, insoluble in magnesium.
Present in only one of the two compositions and at trace level; a residue of the feedstock rather than an addition.
Present in one composition at the 0.001 level, which is an impurity reading, not an alloy component.

note: Recorded with a caveat that matters more than the prototype: chromium is at roughly 7 at.% of these formulas, which is why it is in the host system name, but chromium is effectively insoluble in magnesium and no commercial magnesium alloy carries that much. The numbers read like a full analysis whose units were lost in transcription, so the host system name Cr-Mg is probably an artefact and the material is plain commercial magnesium. Confidence is medium for that reason and every dopant role is low. No reference entry applies: Materials Project returns Mg3Cr Pnma mp-1180365 at hull 0.34 and four other Mg-Cr entries at hulls from 0.075 to 0.57, all of them computed hypotheticals in a system with no stable binary compound, which is itself the evidence that chromium does not dissolve here. Measured 10-278 K.

basis: Cr0.9V0.1N is vanadium-substituted chromium nitride and the paper title is thermoelectric properties of stoichiometric and hole-doped CrN; CrN is the rocksalt nitride of the taxonomy entry, made by ammonolysis as the curator detail records, with vanadium on the chromium site.

dopant_roles.basis: Vanadium for chromium on the metal site. V3+ has one d electron fewer than Cr3+, so it is the hole doping of the title, and it also suppresses the antiferromagnetic ordering that drives the structural distortion.

note: This host does cross a transition even though no transition line was printed for it. CrN distorts from cubic Fm-3m to orthorhombic Pnma at its Neel temperature near 280 K, a magnetostructural transition with a discontinuous volume change, and the measured 19-408 K window straddles it; both phases are recorded, both under the same prototype because the orthorhombic form is a distortion of the rocksalt lattice rather than a different structure type. The 280 K value is a default for pure CrN, not a paper value -- vanadium substitution is known to shift and broaden it downwards, which is part of why the paper makes these samples -- so the transition_basis is recorded as knowledge rather than paper and the low-temperature phase is at medium confidence. The reference, VCrN2 R-3m mp-1216389 at hull 0.153 with no ICSD count, is a computed layered ordering of the two metals and is not carried.

basis: NaCr2O4 holds the AM2O4 ratio but sodium is far too large for the tetrahedral site of a spinel, so it takes the CaFe2O4 post-spinel structure instead: double chains of edge-sharing CrO6 octahedra enclosing eight-coordinate tunnels, Pnma. The paper studies it against Ca-substituted members, and CaCr2O4 is the exemplar of this entry.

dopant_roles.site: tunnel site
dopant_roles.basis: Calcium for sodium in the tunnel at a quarter substitution. Ca2+ against Na+ adds an electron per substitution and so changes the chromium valence, which is the carrier tuning the paper is doing; it also moves the compound towards CaCr2O4, which has the same structure, so the substitution is continuous.

note: I disagree with the reference, which returns only sodium chromates and dichromates -- Na2CrO4 Cmcm mp-18779, NaCr3O8 C2/m mp-19280, Na2Cr2O7 P-1, Na2Cr3O9 P2_1/m and a uranium-bearing entry -- all of them hexavalent chromium compounds with discrete CrO4 tetrahedra. Those are what an oxidising synthesis of sodium and chromium oxide gives; NaCr2O4 with trivalent chromium is a high-pressure phase and is absent from the snapshot. No mp_id is carried. Sodium is above the 5 at.% cut and is a framework tunnel cation, not a dopant. Measured 11-371 K, which spans the antiferromagnetic ordering of these chromites but no structural transition.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62], ICSD-backed references for this host report [2, 63, 12, 11]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Cr2Si2Te6 is CrSiTe3 written per two formula units, the van der Waals layered trichalcogenide of the taxonomy entry: honeycomb chromium layers with Si2Te6 units between them, in R-3. The paper is about spin-phonon scattering in a van der Waals magnet, which is that material.
note: TEDesignLab agrees: CrSiTe3 R-3 (148) mp-3779 at hull zero with 4 ICSD references is the PRIMARY entry and is carried. The second TEDesignLab entry is the same compound in space group 146 with no mp_id, which is the polar R3 subgroup and is a refinement choice rather than a separate thermal phase; it is not recorded as a polymorph. Measured 10-139 K, which spans the ferromagnetic ordering near 32 K -- magnetic, and the spin-phonon coupling the paper reports is precisely that ordering acting on thermal conductivity, not a structural change.

basis: Cs2HfI6 is a K2PtCl6-type vacancy-ordered double perovskite: isolated HfI6 octahedra in a cubic array with caesium filling the cavities, Fm-3m. Removing every second octahedral cation from a halide perovskite is what makes these compounds interesting thermoelectrically, and the paper computes exactly that transport.
note: The prototype was proposed in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl before use; the taxonomy had no A2BX6 entry. The reference agrees: Cs2HfI6 Fm-3m mp-29398 at hull zero with 1 ICSD reference is carried, though a single reference is thin evidence by the chunk header standard. The 200-800 K range is a computed grid rather than a measured window -- the paper is a spin-orbit-coupling study of electronic and thermoelectric properties -- so nothing here is confirmed by a sample and the upper end is above where this iodide would be thermally stable in air. Some A2BX6 halides show octahedral rotation transitions to tetragonal or monoclinic settings on cooling; none is recorded because none is reported for this compound.

basis: Cs2ZrI6 is the zirconium analogue of Cs2HfI6 in the same paper, and zirconium and hafnium are the closest chemical pair in the periodic table, so it takes the same K2PtCl6-type vacancy-ordered double perovskite with isolated ZrI6 octahedra in Fm-3m.
note: The reference agrees on the setting: Cs2ZrI6 Fm-3m mp-1206511 at hull zero, but with no ICSD count at all, so it is a computed entry rather than an observed structure. It is carried because the hafnium twin in the previous record is ICSD-backed in the same setting and the two are isostructural. As with that host, the 200-800 K range is a computed grid from a spin-orbit-coupling study, not a measured window, so experimentally_confirmed is false for the ordinary reason and also because no sample exists.

basis: (K,Cs)VO3 is an alkali metavanadate, which is the AVO3 chain structure of this entry: corner-sharing VO4 tetrahedra running in infinite chains with the alkali cations between them. The paper is about the thermoelectric power of ferroelectric potassium vanadate and caesium vanadate, so both end members are named.
note: No reference line is offered and no space group is recorded, deliberately. The taxonomy entry gives C2/c (15) as typical, which is the setting of the small-alkali metavanadates such as LiVO3 where vanadium is five-coordinate in edge-sharing chains; the large-alkali members KVO3 and CsVO3 have isolated tetrahedral chains in orthorhombic settings instead, so the entry value does not transfer. The paper calls these compounds ferroelectric, which requires a polar space group and rules out the centrosymmetric settings usually quoted for KVO3, and the samples here are mixed K and Cs at 0.4 and 0.6, which will have its own setting again. Potassium and caesium are both above the 5 at.% cut and carry no dopant_roles entries; they are alloyed on the alkali site. Measured 611-691 K, a narrow window near where these salts soften. Confidence is medium on the prototype and low on the structure.

basis: The composition string is PbTe NCs, meaning PbTe nanocrystals, and the paper is titled low temperature formation of rectangular PbTe nanocrystals and their thermoelectric properties. PbTe is the rocksalt chalcogenide, Fm-3m, and nanostructuring changes the grain size and the phonon scattering, not the structure.

dopant_roles.basis: There is no nitrogen in this material. The letters NCs after the formula abbreviate nanocrystals and the parser has read them as elements.
There is no caesium either; Cs is the second half of the same NCs abbreviation.

note: The host system name Cs-N-Pb-Te is wrong at the parser level and this host should route to Pb-Te; the two spurious elements are recorded as parse_artifact roles even though the split put them in the host rather than in the dopant list, because that is the only place in the schema to say so. The structural assignment is unaffected, PbTe being spelled out. No reference line is offered, which is itself a consequence of the bad host key -- Pb-Te is one of the best-covered hosts in the whole dataset. Measured 299-476 K, far below any transition in PbTe.

basis: Both compositions are AVO3 alkali metavanadates, CsVO3 and the mixed (K0.2Cs0.8)VO3, and the paper is on the thermoelectric power of potassium and caesium vanadate. AVO3 with A an alkali is the metavanadate entry exactly: corner-sharing VO4 tetrahedra in infinite chains with the alkali between them.

dopant_roles.basis: (K0.20Cs0.80)VO3 sits on the KVO3-CsVO3 join, which is why the paper measures both end members. K and Cs are the same group and the same formal charge, so the substitution changes the cation size and the chain geometry, not the carrier count. It reads as a dopant only because the five-atom formula puts K0.2 at 4 at.%.

note: Space group disagreement worth recording: the taxonomy entry gives C2/c (15), which is the small-alkali setting of LiVO3 and NaVO3. The large alkali metavanadates KVO3 and CsVO3 take the orthorhombic Pbcm variant instead, with the same chain motif, so the prototype is right and the entry space group is not the one to carry into stage 2 for this host. The reference is no help either: Materials Project returns CsV3O8, Cs2V4O9, Cs2V5O13, CsV2O5 and a barium quaternary, every one of them a different Cs:V ratio, and not a single CsVO3 entry. I do not follow it -- the measured compositions are unambiguously 1:1:3.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [15], ICSD-backed references for this host report [11, 107, 122, 161]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions are (Nb,M)Sr2EuCu2O8 and the paper is titled structure and superconductivity in new Nb-based cuprates. Sr2RCu2O8 plus one further cation is the 1212 cation count, and the eighth oxygen forces that cation into octahedral coordination, which is what Nb(V) takes -- the same architecture as RuSr2GdCu2O8 with niobium in the reservoir layer.

dopant_roles.basis: (Nb0.9Ti0.1)Sr2EuCu2O8. Ti(IV) for Nb(V) in the octahedral reservoir layer removes an electron from the block and hole-dopes the CuO2 planes; the parallel composition does the same job with Cu(II) on that site. The paper is about stabilising and doping the phase through this site, so titanium is a reservoir substituent rather than an impurity.

note: Recorded disagreement with the reference. Materials Project offers Sr2EuNb(CuO4)2 in I4/mcm (140), mp-16786, hull 0.022 on a single ICSD reference. A primitive 1212 stack is P4/mmm; a body-centred tetragonal cell is not what that stacking gives, and one ICSD reference is weak, so I take the 1212 architecture from the formula and the paper title and record the reference setting without adopting it. The alternative to a new prototype was to file this under ruthenocuprate, which is genuinely isostructural -- the entry is written around Ru and its magnetism, and the taxonomy already splits 1212 by the reservoir cation, so I proposed the Nb entry and noted that a reviewer may prefer to merge them.

basis: The compositions are GdBaCuFeO5 with the barium written low, and the paper is on conduction in La-substituted GdBaCuFeO5. LnBaB2O5+d with the lanthanide and barium ordered into alternating A-site layers and the oxygen vacancies ordered in the lanthanide layer is the A-site ordered double perovskite entry; here the B site holds the Cu and Fe square pyramids that the O5 stoichiometry implies.

dopant_roles.basis: Barium is not a dopant here at all: in GdBaCuFeO5 it is one of the two ordered A-site cations and should be at 1 per formula. The recorded Gd0.8Ba0.2CuFeO5 and Gd0.7Ba0.3CuFeO5 put it at a fifth to a third of that, which reads as a transcription of a substitution series rather than the real A-site content, and it is that under-statement that pushed barium below the 5 at.% dopant threshold.

note: Two things to flag. The composition strings are internally inconsistent with the paper title -- the parent is GdBaCuFeO5 with Gd:Ba of 1:1, and the recorded Gd0.8Ba0.2 and Gd0.7Ba0.3 do not reach that, so the A-site chemistry should be re-read from the paper before stage 2 uses these fractions. The measured range, 365-2577 K with a full span to 2641 K, is a digitisation artefact: no oxide of this family survives to 2600 K. And the reference returns GdFe4(CuO4)3 in Im-3, a cubic A-site ordered perovskite of quite different stoichiometry on 2 ICSD references, which does not describe the measured 1:1:1:1:5 compound; I do not follow it.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [47, 123], ICSD-backed references for this host report [204]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions are La0.7Sr0.3(Cu,Fe)O3, the ABO3 count exactly, with the A site a La-Sr solid solution and the B site a Cu-Fe solid solution. This is the standard lanthanum strontium ferrite-cuprate cathode chemistry and the paper measures conductivity, thermal expansion and electrochemical properties, which is the SOFC cathode use of the simple perovskite.
note: Disagreement with the reference, stated rather than followed. Materials Project returns only ordered intergrowths for this element set -- Sr2La2FeCu3O10 in Pbam, Sr2La3Fe4CuO15 in R-3m, Sr2La6FeCu7O20 in Pm -- none with ICSD backing. Those are computed orderings of a chemistry that in the laboratory is made as a disordered ABO3 perovskite, and the measured A:B:O ratio here is 1:1:3, not any of theirs. Copper-rich B sites of this kind do usually carry oxygen vacancies, so the real oxygen content is likely below 3; that is a stoichiometry question for the paper, not a change of prototype. The B-site Cu:Fe ratio is also varied across the two samples, which stage 3 should read as a B-site solid solution rather than as doping.

basis: The single composition is Cu10Fe2Sb4S13, which is the tetrahedrite formula Cu12-xMxSb4S13 with x = 2 and M = Fe, and both papers say so in their titles -- mineral tetrahedrites Cu10Tr2Sb4S13 and synthetic tetrahedrites. Iron is a required constituent of the substituted tetrahedrite, not a dopant, and sits on the tetrahedral Cu site.
note: The reference agrees on the compound, Fe2Cu10Sb4S13 mp-1224745, but gives I-42m (121) at hull 0.064 with no ICSD count. Tetrahedrite is cubic I-43m (217); a tetragonal subgroup at a substantial hull distance is a computed ordering of the Fe over the Cu sites rather than the measured phase, so I record 217 in the phase entry and leave the mp_id null rather than attach one I think is the wrong symmetry. Stage 2 should query for the cubic entry directly.

basis: Cu3GaSnS5 and Cu3Al0.25Ga0.75SnS5 are charge-balanced adamantane compositions -- five cations to five anions, with 3(+1) + (+3) + (+4) = 10 matching S5 -- so the framework is certainly the tetrahedral diamond-like one. Which of its ordered variants the cations take cannot be read off the formula: the composition splits as CuGaS2 plus Cu2SnS3, and a nanobulk preparation of that mixture most often gives a cation-disordered zincblende, so sphalerite is the primary call with the ordered variants as alternatives.

dopant_roles.basis: The paper is on the effect of gallium substitution in Cu3Al1-xGaxSnS5, so Al and Ga are the two end members of one trivalent cation site and the series is written from the Al end. Al0.25 falls below 5 at.% only because the formula has ten atoms.

note: Confidence is low and this host needs the paper. Neither reference returns anything at all for this element set, so nothing here is corroborated, and Cu3MSnS5 is not a formula I can match to a named structure type from memory -- the assignment rests entirely on the adamantane electron count. The real risk is that the material is two phases, CuGaS2 plus Cu2SnS3, rather than one quaternary, which a diffraction pattern would settle at once.

basis: The two compositions are different compounds of the Gd-Cu system and do not share a structure. GdCu is the equiatomic B2 CsCl phase, which the reference confirms directly at Pm-3m (221), mp-614455, hull 0.000 on 4 ICSD references. Gd2Cu9 is a separate copper-rich intermetallic, so the host holds two prototypes and the label is decided per composition.
note: The Gd2Cu9 half is the weak one and is why the record is medium rather than high. At Cu:Gd of 4.5 it sits just off GdCu5, which the reference gives as the CaCu5 type in P6/mmm on 5 ICSD references, and R2Cu9 phases are normally described as superstructures or stacking variants of CaCu5; but the reference has no Gd2Cu9 entry of its own, and I am not confident enough in that reading to call it settled. It is recorded as the alternative prototype so stage 2 splits the host rather than forcing both compounds into B2. The first paper is on GdNi1-xCux, so the GdCu sample is the copper end of a substitution series, which is consistent with the equiatomic B2 phase that both GdNi and GdCu take.

basis: The single composition is Gd3Cu3Sb4 and both papers are on the R3Cu3Sb4 series. That is the A3M3X4 archetype of the Y3Au3Sb4 entry, a cation-ordered Th3P4 derivative, and the reference agrees exactly: Gd3Cu3Sb4 in I-43d (220), mp-1189617, hull 0.000.

other_polymorphs.note: GdCuSb2 in P4/nmm, hull 0.000 on 2 ICSD references, is the other Gd-Cu-Sb compound the reference carries. It is a real phase of this chemistry but a different stoichiometry, not a polymorph of Gd3Cu3Sb4 and not what was measured; recorded so the reference entry is not mistaken for an alternative structure for the measured compound. RCuSb2 phases are the HfCuSi2-type square-net layered structure, which is why it carries that prototype id rather than a Th3P4 one.

note: One of the cleanest assignments in the chunk: the compound, the papers and the reference all name the same phase, and the R3Cu3Sb4 series is the thermoelectric context the Y3Au3Sb4 entry exists for.

basis: CuGe2P3 is charge balanced as an adamantane -- Cu(+1) plus two Ge(+4) against three P(-3), three cations to three anions -- so it is a zincblende-derived tetrahedral framework with Cu and Ge sharing the cation sublattice. The reference lists it only as low-symmetry orderings, P3m1, Cm and Pmm2, all at hull 0.115 to 0.324 and none ICSD-backed, which is what a computed search returns when the real phase is a cation-disordered cubic zincblende it cannot represent in a small cell.
note: The second composition, CuGe4P3, is the reason this is medium rather than high. It is not charge balanced as an adamantane -- it leaves a surplus of +8 per formula -- so it cannot be a single phase of this type, and the most likely reading is CuGe2P3 with excess germanium, either dissolved off-stoichiometry or as free Ge. The paper title, on the composition, structure and bonding of these phases, suggests the authors were themselves testing what the real stoichiometry is, so the germanium-rich sample should be read from the paper before stage 3 treats its fractions as a formula. I do not attach an mp_id: every entry offered is an ordered variant at a substantial hull distance and picking one would assert an ordering the composition does not support.

basis: The two compositions are different compounds and the two papers match them one for one. Cu2ZnGeS4 is the A2BCX4 quaternary tetrahedral phase, confirmed by TEDesignLab as ZnCu2GeS4 in I-42m (121), mp-6408, hull 0.000 on 4 ICSD references, which is the stannite setting. Cu22Zn4V2Ge6S32 is the Cu26V2Ge6S32 colusite formula with four of the twenty-six coppers replaced by zinc, and the second paper is on synthetic colusites.

other_polymorphs.note: ZnCu2GeS4 in Pmn2_1 at hull 0.003 with 3 ICSD references is the wurtz-stannite variant, the hexagonal-stacking cousin of the stannite. It is a real and preparable phase rather than a thermal one, which is why it is here rather than in phases; which of the two a given sample holds depends on the synthesis route, not on temperature.

dopant_roles.basis: Vanadium is a required structural cation of colusite, not a dopant. The archetype is Cu26V2Ge6S32 and the V2 per 66 atoms is exactly what the formula demands; it sits on its own tetrahedral site at the centre of the sphalerite-derived framework and fixes the electron count of the whole cluster. It falls under the 5 at.% threshold only because the formula is so large.

note: Genuinely mixed, and the split is clean on composition: one sample per prototype, one paper per prototype. Materials Project adds Zn4FeCu10(GeS4)5 entries in Pm and C2 which carry iron that no measured composition here has; they are ignored.

basis: Both compositions are written as (GeTe)1-x(CuSbSe2)x with x of 0.15 and 0.20, so the host lattice is GeTe and the copper antimony selenide is the alloying addition. The paper is titled thermoelectric performance optimization and phase transition of GeTe, which names both the parent and the behaviour that matters here.
note: The measured window, 301-764 K, straddles the GeTe R3m to Fm-3m transition, so the phases array carries both ends. No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line is printed for this host because it has no seed hypothesis, but the taxonomy entry for gete_rhombohedral does carry the transition at 700 K and the paper title reports one, so it is recorded. The 700 K figure is the taxonomy default and is known to shift with germanium vacancy content and alloying -- here roughly a fifth of the lattice is substituted, which typically pulls the transition down by tens of kelvin, so the boundary between the two phase entries should be read as approximate. Neither reference returns anything for this five-element host, so no mp_id is attached.

basis: Ni0.4Cu0.6H0.08 and H0.15 are a face-centred cubic Ni-Cu solid solution charged with hydrogen, and the paper is on the transport properties of hydrogenated nickel-based alloys. Ni and Cu are completely miscible in the fcc lattice, and hydrogen at 8 to 15 per cent of a formula unit occupies the octahedral interstices of that lattice without changing the metal sublattice, which is the MHx case the metal hydride entry is written for with PdH0.66 as its exemplar.

dopant_roles.basis: Hydrogen enters the octahedral holes of the fcc metal lattice; it is the variable the paper controls and the reason the samples exist, not a contaminant. It is listed here even though the chunk does not offer it as a dopant candidate, because at these levels it is the whole point of the material.

note: Medium rather than high because the two entries are really one material seen two ways: which id is right depends on whether the hydrogen content is high enough to form a distinct hydride phase or is still dissolved in the alloy. At x of 0.08 to 0.15 a Ni-Cu alloy is usually in the dilute alpha solid solution rather than the fcc beta hydride, which would argue for solid_solution_alloy with hydrogen as an interstitial role; I chose the hydride entry because the hydrogen is deliberate and structural in intent, and recorded the alloy as the alternative. Neither reference covers this host. The Ni:Cu ratio is a substitutional solid solution on the metal sublattice and stage 3 should treat it as such rather than as doping.

basis: Hg0.7Cr0.3Sr2CuO4 is the n = 1 member of the mercury single-reservoir cuprate series, HgBa2CuO4 with strontium on the alkaline-earth site -- and HgBa2CuO4 is one of the representative materials of that entry. One CuO2 plane, a Sr-O layer each side and a single Hg-O sheet as the charge reservoir, with the oxygen excess in that sheet as the doping variable.

dopant_roles.basis: Hg0.7Cr0.3Sr2CuO4: chromium takes three tenths of the mercury site in the reservoir sheet. Substituting a higher-valent transition metal there is the standard way to stabilise the strontium-based mercury 1201 phase, which does not form cleanly with mercury alone, and it changes the hole count of the CuO2 plane at the same time. The paper reports X-ray structure alongside resistivity and Hall effect, so the site occupancy is something it should settle.

note: The prototype id says 1212, but the entry is the general A-Ba2-Ca(n-1)-Cun single-reservoir family and explicitly carries HgBa2CuO4, the n = 1 member, in its representative materials. This host is that n = 1 member on strontium rather than barium, so no new prototype is needed. Neither reference returns anything for this element set.

basis: The host holds two different equilibrium compounds. LuInCu4 is the C15b AuBe5 type -- the first paper is titled transport properties of RInCu4 with C15b-type structure, which names it outright -- while LuCuIn is the equiatomic RTX phase, and the second paper on CeCuIn confirms the family. The taxonomy entry for ZrNiAl already lists CeInCu among its representative materials, so the equiatomic half belongs there, not with the 1:1:4.
note: Mixed and cleanly separable by the Cu:Lu ratio, four against one. The reference is unhelpful and mildly misleading here: it returns LuInCu2 in Fm-3m on 2 ICSD references, which is the full Heusler at yet another stoichiometry, and Lu2InCu2 in P4/mbm, neither of which is either measured composition. I state that rather than adopt it. The P-62m assignment for LuCuIn is taken from the RTX family and from the reference entry for the praseodymium analogue in the neighbouring host, which does give PrInCu at P-62m.

basis: PrInCu2 is the RT2X Heusler stoichiometry written with the indium first, and the reference gives PrInCu2 in Fm-3m (225), mp-21148, on 2 ICSD references. Cu2 on the tetrahedral sublattice with Pr and In ordered on the two octahedral sites is the L21 full Heusler arrangement, which is what RCu2In compounds take.
note: The reference also lists PrInCu in P-62m and Pr2InCu2 in P4/mbm, both at hull 0.000, and two computed Pr-In-Cu phases at higher hull. Those are other compounds of the ternary system, not polymorphs of PrInCu2, and neither matches the measured 1:1:2, so they are not recorded as alternatives. The papers are low-temperature specific-heat and thermopower studies of a non-magnetic-doublet ground state, which is Heusler heavy-fermion physics and consistent with the assignment.

basis: Both compositions are K2BaCu8Te10 -- the second, K2.1Ba0.9Cu8Te10, is the same phase with the alkali and alkaline-earth ratio nudged -- and the paper is titled thermoelectric properties and electronic structure of the cage compound K2BaCu8Te10. That compound has no entry in the taxonomy, so a prototype was proposed for it and for its rubidium analogue in the next host but one.

dopant_roles.basis: Barium is a required structural cation of A2BaCu8Te10, one per 21 atoms, which is why it reads as 4.8 at.% and lands under the dopant threshold. The only real variation is K2.1Ba0.9 against K2Ba1, a slight exchange of one guest cation for the other that tunes the electron count of the copper telluride framework; it is not dilute doping.

note: Confidence is medium because the prototype is new and no space group is claimed for it. Both references miss the compound entirely: TEDesignLab offers K4Cu8Te11 in C2/m, KCuTe in P6_3/mmc and KCu3Te2, and Materials Project offers K2(CuTe)5 and K2Cu2Te5 in Cmcm, each on a single ICSD reference and none of them the measured quaternary. I record that disagreement rather than take the closest formula -- K4Cu8Te11 shares the Cu8 unit but has no barium and a different tellurium count.

basis: The compositions are written as ((La,Sr)O)CuS, which is the layered oxysulfide LaCuOS with strontium substituted for lanthanum, and the paper is titled the new conductive oxysulfides [(La1-xSrx)O]CuS containing a Cu-layer. That alternation of a fluorite-type (La,Sr)2O2 layer with an antifluorite-type Cu2S2 layer is the ZrCuSiAs 1111 structure, P4/nmm.
note: Strontium is above the 5 at.% threshold so it is not in the dopant list, but structurally it is the acceptor: Sr(II) for La(III) in the oxide layer hole-dopes the CuS layer, and that is the variable the paper sweeps from x = 0.2 to 0.3. The reference is useless here -- it returns one computed Sr3La21Cu10(SO24)2 in Pm at hull 0.181, a sulfate-like stoichiometry with nothing to do with an oxysulfide, and I disregard it. This host is the sulfur analogue of BiCuSeO-type oxychalcogenide chemistry and the same warning applies: the oxygen belongs to the lanthanide layer and never shares a site with the sulfur.

basis: The composition is almost certainly a commercial 2000-series aluminium alloy with the aluminium balance missing from the transcription: Cu 4.58 and Mg 1.70 with traces of Ga, Fe, Mn, Si, V, Zn, Cr, Sn, Ti, Ca, Ag and Zr is the analysis of a 2024-type Al-Cu-Mg alloy, and the paper is titled low-temperature transport properties of commercial metals and alloys. On that reading the material is an fcc aluminium solid solution with precipitates, which is the A1 entry.

dopant_roles.basis: Trace element in a commercial alloy whose matrix element appears to be missing from the transcribed formula; the role cannot be judged until the host is resolved.

note: This host key is probably wrong and the record should be reviewed before anything downstream uses it. If the formula is taken at face value as a binary, Cu:Mg is 2.7, which lies between MgCu2 and copper-rich fcc and would make the sample two-phase, MgCu2 Laves plus copper -- that is why laves_phase and composite_multiphase are listed as alternatives rather than dismissed. But twelve trace elements at exactly the levels specified for a wrought aluminium alloy, and a paper surveying commercial metals, both point the other way. Neither reference helps: Materials Project returns the Mg-Cu binaries MgCu2 and Mg2Cu, which is what it would return whether or not the aluminium is real. Confidence is low on every field here.

basis: CuMo6Te8 and Cu2Mo6Te8 are the MxMo6X8 Chevrel formula, and the paper is titled thermoelectric properties of MxMo6Te8 with M = Ag and Cu. The Mo6 octahedral cluster capped by eight tellurium atoms, with the copper in the channels between clusters, is the Chevrel entry exactly, and x running from 1 to 2 is the usual filling range.
note: Copper is above the threshold so it is not offered as a dopant candidate, but its role is worth stating for stage 3: it is the channel cation of the Chevrel framework, the x in MxMo6Te8, and the carrier-concentration knob rather than a substituent. Neither reference returns anything for this host, so the R-3 setting comes from the Chevrel family rather than from a database entry.

basis: Cu3PdN is the M3XY antiperovskite count and the paper says so in its title -- epitaxial thin films of the Dirac semimetal antiperovskite Cu3PdN. Nitrogen sits at the centre of a Cu6 octahedron and palladium takes the corner site, the inverse of an ABO3 perovskite, and the reference carries Cu3PdN in Pm-3m (221), mp-1206517.
note: Every Materials Project entry for this chemistry sits far above the hull -- the Cu3PdN one at 0.115 eV, the others from 0.219 to 0.389 -- which is expected for a metastable nitride made as an epitaxial film rather than in equilibrium, and is exactly the case the README warns not to resolve by hull ranking. The ICSD-backed entries at 0.254 and 0.389 are Cu11PdN4 and Cu12PdN4, copper-rich variants of the same anti-perovskite framework with ordered vacancies, not different structure types. Films of this kind are commonly nitrogen-deficient, so the nitrogen content is a stoichiometry question for stage 2.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [123]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions normalise to 1:1:1 -- (Ti,Nb) about 30 at.%, (Ni,Cu) about 33, (Sn,Sb) about 33 -- and the paper is titled thermoelectric behaviour of p- and n-type Ti-Ni-Sn half Heusler alloys. This is TiNiSn with niobium on the titanium site, copper on the nickel site and antimony on the tin site, which is the standard way both carrier types are made in this system.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb1.5 against Sn31.6 puts antimony on a twentieth of the main-group site. One extra valence electron per substitution makes it the n-type donor of the TiNiSn half Heusler, and it is present at the same level in both samples, which is what a fixed donor level looks like.

note: The two samples differ only in the Ti:Nb ratio, 24.3:5.9 against 15.6:12.3, an isoelectronic exchange on the four-valent site that tunes the lattice thermal conductivity; stage 3 should read that as a solid solution on the Ti site, not as doping. Copper sits just above the threshold at 5.1-5.7 at.% and is not offered as a candidate, but it plays the familiar role of the interstitial or excess metal in this system, where a few per cent of copper or excess nickel partially fills the vacant fourth sublattice and shifts the material between half and full Heusler order. Neither reference returns anything for this five-element host.

basis: The matrix is constantan -- the paper says so in its title and the Ni0.47Cu0.53 ratio is exactly that alloy -- which is a face-centred cubic Ni-Cu solid solution, completely miscible across the whole range. The silica is a dispersed second phase, not part of the lattice: the curator records 20 and 30 vol.% SiO2 and the paper is on constantan with spherical SiO2 and Al2O3 particles.

dopant_roles.basis: Silicon is present only as SiO2 particles deliberately dispersed in the metal, at 20 to 30 vol.%. Silica is insoluble in the fcc metal, so no silicon enters the lattice and the prototype is the matrix, not the composite.
The oxygen belongs to the same SiO2 particles and is in the host key only because the particle loading is large.

note: The alternative reading is composite_multiphase, since at 30 vol.% the silica is a major constituent rather than a trace. I keep the matrix as the prototype because that is what the README asks for after the graphene-on-SrTiO3 and CNT-on-MnSi1.75 cases: a dispersed additive should not relabel its host. The point of the paper is the effect of that dispersion on transport, so the composite character is the experiment, not the structure. Neither reference covers this host.

basis: Zr3Ni2.5Cu0.5Sb4 is Zr3Ni3Sb4 with a sixth of the nickel replaced by copper, and the paper is on high thermoelectric performance in a multi-valley electronic system, which is the Zr3Ni3Sb4 story. The Y3Au3Sb4 entry is the A3M3X4 cation-ordered Th3P4 derivative in I-43d, and its example host systems already include Ni-Sb-Zr, the undoped parent of this host.
note: Copper is at exactly 5 at.% of the formula and so is not offered as a dopant candidate, but its role is clear and should carry into stage 3: Cu(I) for Ni(0 or II) on the transition-metal sublattice of the 3-3-4 framework is the acceptor that makes this sample p-type. That the copper level is the only thing distinguishing this host from Ni-Sb-Zr is itself the evidence. No reference line is offered for the host.

basis: (Pb0.75Cu0.25)Sr2(Ca0.5R0.5)Cu2O7 with R = Y or Yb, and the paper is titled superconductivity in Pb-based 1212 cuprates. The formula is the 1212 count exactly: two CuO2 planes about a (Ca,R) spacer, an SrO layer on each side, and a mixed (Pb,Cu)O charge reservoir. The taxonomy carries the Hg and Tl single-reservoir entry and the Ru one but nothing with lead in the reservoir, so a prototype was proposed.

dopant_roles.basis: Calcium is the 1212 spacer cation between the two CuO2 planes, a required site of the structure rather than a dopant; it reads as 3.8 at.% only because the formula has thirteen atoms and the site is shared half and half with the rare earth.

Yttrium takes half the spacer site. Y(III) for Ca(II) there removes holes from the CuO2 planes, which is the under-doping the paper title reports evidence for, so it is the doping variable of this series rather than an impurity.
The second sample swaps ytterbium for yttrium on the same spacer site at the same level -- a smaller rare earth at identical valence, so it changes the plane spacing rather than the hole count.

note: Recorded disagreement with the reference. Materials Project returns five Sr-Ca-R-Cu-Pb-O entries, four of them triclinic P-1 and one C2/m, all near hull 0.02 and none ICSD-backed; one I4/mmm entry appears at hull 0.025. Those are computed cation orderings of a phase that is made and indexed as tetragonal 1212, so the P4/mmm setting here comes from the compound family and the reference is noted rather than followed. Copper appears twice in the formula, in the planes and in the reservoir, which is what distinguishes this from the mercury and thallium members and is the reason for the separate prototype.

basis: La0.5Ca0.5Cu3Ru4O12 is the AA3B4O12 count of the A-site ordered perovskite entry: calcium and lanthanum share the twelve-coordinate A site, copper takes the square-planar A-prime site and ruthenium the octahedral B site. CaCu3Ru4O12 is the metallic member of that family, and the second paper -- on negatively enhanced thermopower near a Van Hove singularity in an electron-doped system -- is what lanthanum substitution on the A site does to it.

dopant_roles.basis: La(III) for Ca(II) on the twelve-coordinate A site of CaCu3Ru4O12 adds an electron per substitution to the ruthenium band; at half the site it is the electron doping the paper is about, not a dilute impurity. It falls below 5 at.% only because the formula has twenty atoms.
Calcium is the parent A-site cation of CaCu3Ru4O12 and a required constituent, under the threshold for the same reason lanthanum is.

note: Flagged mixed because of the second composition, Cu1.82La0.18RuO4, which I cannot place. Its A2BO4 stoichiometry reads as a K2NiF4-type ruthenate with the A site almost entirely copper, which is an unusual site for copper to occupy and not a compound I can name; it is neither a different stoichiometry of the CaCu3Ru4O12 family nor the Cu2Ru2O7 pyrochlore. Rather than force it, the host carries unresolved_crystalline as the alternative and the composition needs the paper -- which of the two papers it comes from is itself unclear, since the review on spin entropy and the Van Hove singularity study could both plausibly supply either sample. Neither reference returns anything for this host at all.

basis: Ru0.9Sr2YCu2.1O7.9 is RuSr2YCu2O8 with a tenth of the ruthenium site taken by copper, and the paper is on the magnetic and thermal behaviour of a magneto-superconductor. That formula is the RuSr2RCu2O8 archetype of the ruthenocuprate entry: two CuO2 planes about an yttrium spacer with a corner-sharing RuO2 octahedral layer as the charge reservoir, the layer that replaces the CuO chain of YBCO.
note: The taxonomy names Cu-Gd-O-Ru-Sr as the example host for this entry; this is the same compound with yttrium in place of gadolinium, so the assignment is a straight family match rather than a judgement call. No element falls below the threshold, but the off-stoichiometry is the doping: Ru0.9Cu2.1 against the ideal Ru1Cu2 means excess copper on the ruthenium site, and O7.9 against O8 a slight oxygen deficiency, both of which shift the hole count of the planes. Stage 3 should read those as non-stoichiometry rather than as separate dopants. The reference returns only two computed quaternary oxides, Sr12Y6CuRu5O36 in P-1 and Sr4CeY3Cu4(RuO10)2 in P4mm, neither of which is the 1212 phase; they are disregarded.

basis: The material is Cu1.8S, digenite, with silica particles dispersed in it -- the composition is written as (Cu1.8S)88.63(SiO2)11.37 and the paper is on the size effect of SiO2 on enhancing the thermoelectric properties of Cu1.8S. Copper-deficient Cu2-xS is the sulfur analogue of the Cu2Se entry: an anion array with a partly disordered, mobile copper sublattice, and the entry already covers Cu-Se and Cu-Te.

dopant_roles.basis: Silicon is present only as the dispersed SiO2 particles whose size the paper varies; silica does not dissolve in copper sulfide, so no silicon enters the lattice.
Oxygen belongs to those same silica particles and is in the host key only because they make up a ninth of the sample.

note: The host key Cu-O-S is misleading -- there is no copper oxysulfide here, only Cu1.8S plus SiO2 -- and the reference line shows the cost of that: every entry it returns is a copper sulfate, CuSO4 and relatives, which have nothing to do with the measured material. I disregard the reference entirely. The two phase entries are both the same prototype: low-temperature digenite is an ordered rhombohedral superstructure that disorders into the cubic superionic form a little above room temperature, near 365 K, so the measured 322-623 K window crosses it while staying within one structural family. That temperature is from general knowledge of the Cu2-xS system and is composition-dependent; it is not from the paper.

basis: ZnCuV2O7 and Zn2CuV2O7 are (Zn,Cu)2V2O7 pyrovanadates -- the paper is titled thermoelectric properties and phase transition of (ZnxCu1-x)2V2O7 -- with M:V:O of 2:2:7, the thortveitite-derived divanadate count of corner-sharing V2O7 groups linking the divalent cations. Zn2V2O7 and Cu2V2O7 are the two end members of the same series and the entry names both.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: divalent cation site
solid_solution_axis.note: Zn:Cu of 1:1 and 2:1 across the two compositions, both on the single divalent site of the M2V2O7 framework. The paper sweeps x across the (ZnxCu1-x)2V2O7 join, so the parent compound is composition-dependent and the transition temperature moves with it.

note: spans_transition is true because the paper title reports a phase transition and the measured window is wide, 375-924 K, but I deliberately leave both transition_K values null. The transition is between two settings of the same pyrovanadate framework -- the alpha and beta forms, blossite Fdd2 and ziesite C2/c -- so the prototype does not change, and the temperature cannot be pinned from composition: the copper end transforms in the neighbourhood of 700 K while the zinc end has its own inversion far lower, near 400 K, and these samples sit between them. Putting a number here would be inventing one. Materials Project returns only computed V-Zn-Cu-O entries in C2, P-1 and P1 with no ICSD backing, so it does not settle the setting either.

basis: Both compositions are written as (PbSe0.998Br0.002)x(Cu2Se)1-x with the copper selenide at 7 to 9 mol.%, and the paper is titled high-performance n-type PbSe-Cu2Se thermoelectrics through conduction band engineering. The host lattice is rocksalt PbSe; the Cu2Se is a second phase deliberately added, and the bromine is the n-type dopant.

dopant_roles.basis: Br for Se at 0.2 mol.% of the anion site is the standard halide donor in lead chalcogenides, one extra electron per substitution, and it is held constant across both samples while the Cu2Se fraction is varied. It is the carrier source, not the variable under study.

note: alt_prototype_ids carries cu2se_superionic but is_mixed is false on purpose: the copper selenide is present in every sample as a dispersed second phase rather than in some compositions and not others, so there is nothing for stage 2 to split -- the host is one composite material, not two structures under one label. Some copper certainly dissolves into the PbSe as well, which is what conduction band engineering in this system means, but that is a solubility question for the paper. Neither reference returns anything for this host.

basis: YbCu4Pd and YbPdCu4 are the same compound written two ways, the RTCu4 stoichiometry of the C15b AuBe5 type, and the entry exemplar is YbAgCu4 -- the same family with silver in place of palladium. The reference confirms it directly: YbCu4Pd in F-43m (216), mp-1077750, hull 0.000. The second paper measures YbMCu4 with M = Ag, Au and Pd together, which is that series.
note: The other two reference entries, Yb2CuPd in Fm-3m and YbCuPd2 in Fm-3m at hull 0.020 and 0.039, are computed compounds at different stoichiometries with no ICSD backing and are not polymorphs of YbCu4Pd. The two composition strings are one compound, so this host needs no split despite looking like two formulas; that the ytterbium valence is the physics being measured, in a heavy-fermion low-temperature study, does not bear on the structure.

basis: Rb2BaCu8Te10 is the rubidium analogue of K2BaCu8Te10, and the paper is the same one -- on the thermoelectric properties and electronic structure of that cage compound -- which measures both alkali members. The prototype was proposed for this chunk because the taxonomy has no A2BaCu8Te10 entry.

dopant_roles.basis: As in the potassium host: barium is a required structural cation of A2BaCu8Te10, one atom in twenty-one, and reads as 4.8 at.% only because the formula is large. It is not a dopant.

note: Same reasoning and same limitation as Cu-K-Te at rank 2166: the compound is named in the paper title but neither reference contains it, so no space group and no mp_id is claimed and stage 2 must read the structure from the paper. The rubidium host has no reference line at all, not even the near-miss formulas the potassium one returned.

basis: The compositions are written as (Cu3SbSe4)x Zn4Sb3 and the paper is titled enhanced thermoelectric performance of beta-Zn4Sb3 based composites incorporating a second phase. The matrix is beta-Zn4Sb3 -- the disordered rhombohedral zinc antimonide with interstitial zinc -- and the copper antimony selenide is the added phase, which is the famatinite-type Cu3SbSe4.
note: Both prototypes are genuinely present but is_mixed is false: every sample is the same two-phase composite, differing only in how much Cu3SbSe4 is in it, so there is nothing for stage 2 to split composition-by-composition. The addition is substantial -- at x = 0.25 the second phase is about a fifth of the atoms -- so a reviewer may prefer composite_multiphase; I keep the matrix as the label because the paper treats it as beta-Zn4Sb3 with inclusions and the transport is the matrix. Note that beta-Zn4Sb3 itself is only stable above about 260 K and orders into the alpha form below that, but the measured window starts at 296 K, so no transition is crossed. Neither reference covers this host.

basis: YCu2.05Si2 is the RT2X2 stoichiometry and the reference gives Y(CuSi)2 in I4/mmm (139), mp-3390, hull 0.000 on 3 ICSD references -- the body-centred tetragonal ThCr2Si2 type, alternating yttrium layers with CuSi4 tetrahedral slabs. The cerium-substituted sample is the same phase, which is the point of the comparison the paper makes.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.1Y0.9Cu2.05Si2: cerium on a tenth of the yttrium site. Y and Ce are close in size and both nominally trivalent, so this is not carrier doping -- it dilutes CeCu2Si2 into a non-magnetic YCu2Si2 host to study isolated 4f moments, which is the standard Kondo-dilution experiment and what a low-temperature transport measurement to 293 K is for.

note: The Cu2.05 excess is a small non-stoichiometry on the transition-metal site rather than a separate element, and stage 3 should read it that way. The other reference entries -- Y3(CuSi)4 in Immm, YCuSi in P6_3/mmc, and two computed phases at higher hull -- are different compounds of the ternary system, not polymorphs of the 122, so they are not recorded as alternatives.

basis: Er0.25Dy0.75PdSb at 1:1:1 and the paper titled antimonides with the half-Heusler structure, new thermoelectric materials. RPdSb compounds are the C1b half Heusler, F-43m, with the rare earth and antimony forming the rocksalt sublattice and palladium in half the tetrahedral holes; the neighbouring DyNiSb host in this same chunk is the nickel member of the identical series.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth site
solid_solution_axis.note: Er:Dy is fixed at 1:3 in both samples, both trivalent heavy rare earths on the same site, so this is isoelectronic alloying that tunes the lattice parameter and the phonon scattering rather than the carrier count. Only one point on the axis is measured here.

note: The two compositions differ only in the palladium excess, Pd1.02 against Pd1.00, both with Sb1.05. Slight excess of the tetrahedral metal is how partial filling of the vacant fourth sublattice is written, the half-to-full Heusler axis, and stage 3 should read both the Pd1.02 and the Sb1.05 as non-stoichiometry rather than as dopants. Neither reference returns anything for this four-element host.

basis: The single composition is Dy2Mo2O7, the A2B2O7 pyrochlore count, and both papers say so -- thermoelectric power of RE2Mo2O7 pyrochlores, and electrical conductivity and thermoelectric power of the same series. The reference agrees: Dy2Mo2O7 in Fd-3m (227), mp-1190424, on an ICSD reference.
note: The reference entry sits at hull 0.014 on a single ICSD reference, which the chunk file would call weak, but the compound is named in both paper titles and the space group is the pyrochlore one, so the agreement is real rather than a coincidence of formula. The other entries returned -- Dy2(MoO4)3, Dy5(MoO6)2, Dy4Mo4O11, Dy2Mo8O33 -- are molybdates at different Mo oxidation states, not polymorphs of the 2-2-7. Dy2Mo2O7 is a spin-ice-adjacent frustrated magnet and the measurement stops at 255 K, so the interest is low-temperature magnetism rather than thermoelectric performance.

basis: DyNiSb at 1:1:1, and both papers are explicitly on half-Heusler RENiSb phases. The reference confirms it directly: DyNiSb in F-43m (216), mp-4510, hull 0.000 on 2 ICSD references -- the C1b structure.
note: One of the few hosts in this chunk where composition, both papers and the reference all point the same way with nothing left over. The other reference entries are DyNiSb2 and Dy(NiSb)2 in P4/nmm and Dy5Ni2Sb in I4/mcm -- other compounds of the ternary system at different stoichiometries, not polymorphs of the equiatomic phase. The measured range runs to 992 K, which is high-temperature power-factor work on a half Heusler and involves no structural change.

basis: Er2Mo2O7 is the A2B2O7 pyrochlore and both papers are on the Ln2Mo2O7 pyrochlore series, one of them the same RE2Mo2O7 study that supplies the neighbouring Dy-Mo-O host. The second composition, written ErMo2O7, is the same compound with the erbium count dropped in transcription -- there is no ErMo2O7 phase and the papers measure only the 2-2-7.
note: The reference misses this one completely. It returns Er5(MoO6)2, Er2Mo4O15, Er6MoO12, ErMoO5 and a potassium lithium erbium molybdate, all Mo(VI) molybdates, and no Er2Mo2O7 entry at all -- whereas the equivalent dysprosium host does have one, in Fd-3m. That is an absence in the 2019 snapshot rather than evidence against the pyrochlore, exactly the weak-primary case the chunk header warns about, so I assign from the paper titles and the isostructural dysprosium neighbour and leave the mp_id null. Er2Mo2O7 sits near the metal-insulator boundary of the Ln2Mo2O7 series, which is why it was measured.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: ErN is a rare-earth mononitride, and the reference is emphatic: ErN in Fm-3m (225), mp-19830, hull 0.000 on 27 ICSD references, the best-attested entry anywhere in this chunk. The rare-earth nitrides are all B1 rocksalt, and the interstitial-nitride entry with CrN as its exemplar is written for exactly that.

other_polymorphs.note: ErN in Pm-3m at hull 0.955 eV on a single ICSD reference. A B1-to-B2 conversion under compression is the normal high-pressure behaviour of the rocksalt nitrides, and an energy that far above the hull cannot be a thermally reached phase; it is recorded here so the reference pair is never read as a thermal sequence.

note: The papers are on specific heat and thermal conductivity at cryogenic temperatures and on the magnetic properties of ErN films, so the measurements are low-temperature magnetism rather than thermoelectrics; the 5th-95th window of 15-72 K against a full span to 255 K reflects that. Rare-earth nitrides are typically nitrogen-deficient and oxidise readily, so the real composition is likely ErN1-x; that is a stoichiometry question, not a structural one.

basis: Both compositions are (Zr,Er)Ni(Sn,Sb) at 1:1:1 and the paper is on the properties and electronic structure of RNiSb compounds. This is the ErNiSb-ZrNiSn half-Heusler join: the two 1:1:1 end members are both C1b, and the samples simply move along it, a quarter and three quarters of the way.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: main-group site
solid_solution_axis.note: Sn and Sb share the main-group sublattice while Zr and Er share the other, and the two ratios move together -- Zr0.25Er0.75 with Sn0.25Sb0.75, and the reverse.
