That pairing is what keeps the valence electron count at 18 across the join, so it is a charge-compensated substitution rather than doping; note that Sn and Sb are NOT isoelectronic, which is precisely why the two sublattices have to move in step.

note: The coupled substitution is the whole design of this sample set and stage 3 should not read Sb as a donor here: every antimony added is matched by an erbium replacing a zirconium, so the electron count is held fixed. No element falls under the threshold, so there are no dopant roles to record. Neither reference covers this five-element host.

basis: The host holds two different compounds of the Er-Se system. ErSe is the rocksalt monoselenide, which the reference gives in Fm-3m (225), mp-2491, hull 0.000 on 5 ICSD references. Er3Se4 is the reduced A3X4 phase, the Th3P4-derived cubic structure that rare-earth sesquichalcogenide-monochalcogenide intermediates take, so the two compositions need separate labels.
note: Mixed and separable on the Se:Er ratio, 1.0 against 1.33. The Er3Se4 half is the less certain one: Th3P4 is the standard structure for R3X4 phases on the La3Te4 pattern that the taxonomy entry is written around, and its A3-xX4 archetype is exactly this composition, but the reference has no Er3Se4 entry to confirm it -- it gives Er2Se3 in Fddd on 6 ICSD references and two ErSe2 phases instead. For the heavy rare earths the sesquiselenide takes the orthorhombic form rather than the cubic Th3P4 one, which raises a real possibility that Er3Se4 is likewise a lower-symmetry defect phase rather than cubic. The paper, on thermoelectric and electrical measurements in the Er-Se system, would settle it; the assignment is medium for that reason.

basis: EuNi2(Si0.05Ge0.95)2 is the RT2X2 stoichiometry and the reference confirms the parent, Eu(NiGe)2 in I4/mmm (139), mp-3333, hull 0.000 on 3 ICSD references -- the ThCr2Si2 type. The first paper, on the thermoelectric power of EuNi2(Si1-xGex)2, is the classic europium valence-transition series in that structure. The second composition, Eu2Ni3Ge5, is a different compound and takes the U2Co3Si5 type.

dopant_roles.basis: The paper sweeps x in EuNi2(Si1-xGex)2; this sample is the germanium-rich end at x = 0.05 silicon. Si and Ge are the same group on the same tetrahedral site, so the substitution acts through chemical pressure on the europium valence rather than by adding carriers -- which is the point of the series.

note: Mixed, and separable on the Ni:Eu ratio, 2 against 1.5. The 2-3-5 half goes to u2co3si5_type, a prototype already proposed in an earlier chunk whose R2M3X5 archetype covers Eu2Ni3Ge5 exactly, and whose entry explains why a 2-3-5 cannot be filed under the 122 -- different symmetry, Ibam rather than I4/mmm, and a different building principle. The reference has no Eu2Ni3Ge5 entry; it returns EuNiGe, EuNiGe2, EuNiGe3 and EuNi9Ge4 instead, other compounds of the same ternary system. The europium valence transition in the 122 is an electronic crossover, not a change of structure type, so spans_transition stays false.

basis: EuPt4Ge12 is the MPt4Ge12 platinum germanide, a filled skutterudite in which the Pt4Ge12 framework of tilted octahedra and Ge12 rings encloses the europium guest. The reference supports it: Eu(Ge3Pt)4 in Im-3 (204), mp-1184807, which is the skutterudite space group and the right formula, and the paper is on superconductivity and antiferromagnetism in these filled cages.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr0.1Eu0.9Pt4Ge12: praseodymium takes a tenth of the guest site inside the Ge12 cage, not a framework site. Substituting one filler for another is how this series is tuned -- PrPt4Ge12 is itself a superconductor and EuPt4Ge12 an antiferromagnet, so the paper is crossing between them.

note: The Im-3 entry sits at hull 0.365 on a single ICSD reference, which looks bad but is the expected signature of a filled cage compound in a computed hull: the filler is far from a convex-hull-stable configuration while being perfectly real. The other entries returned -- EuGe3Pt in I4mm, EuGePt in P2_13, two Eu(GePt)2 phases -- are different stoichiometries of the ternary system, not polymorphs of the 1-4-12. Unlike CoSb3-based skutterudites, MPt4Ge12 has no empty-framework parent, so the europium is a constituent rather than an optional filler even though its role is that of a guest.

basis: EuVO3 is the ABO3 count and the paper names it as a Mott insulator grown as a single-crystal thin film. The RVO3 vanadates are all orthorhombically distorted GdFeO3-type perovskites of corner-sharing VO6 octahedra, and europium at that ionic radius sits squarely in that series.
note: Recorded disagreement with the reference, which returns no EuVO3 at all. Its entries are EuVO4 in I4_1/amd on 5 ICSD references -- a V(V) orthovanadate of isolated tetrahedra, a completely different structure and oxidation state -- plus Eu2VO4, Eu2V2O5, Eu3V2O7 and EuVO2. V(III) perovskite vanadates are harder to make than the V(V) vanadates because they need reducing conditions, which is exactly why the paper grows this one as a strained film, and it is a plausible reason the 2019 snapshot lacks it. I assign from the formula and the paper and leave the mp_id null. The space group is given as 62 for the usual orthorhombic distortion, but a film grown under biaxial strain may hold a different setting, so it is marked medium.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62], ICSD-backed references for this host report [141, 139, 88]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: LaF3 is the tysonite structure -- eleven-coordinate lanthanum in a dense trigonal fluoride framework -- and the reference is strong and in agreement: LaF3 in P-3c1 (165), mp-905, hull 0.000 on 21 ICSD references, by far the best-attested entry for this chemistry. The taxonomy had no fluoride framework entry of any kind, so the prototype was proposed here.

other_polymorphs.note: LaF3 in I4/mmm at hull 0.172 with 6 ICSD references. The tetragonal entry is a high-symmetry idealisation of the tysonite framework rather than a separately preparable phase at ambient conditions, and 0.172 eV above the hull is far too high to be reached by heating; it carries the same prototype id because it is the same structural family, not a different one.

dopant_roles.basis: (LaF3)99.2Eu0.8: europium on a fraction of a per cent of the lanthanum site. At that level in a fluoride crystal it is an optically active or conductivity-modifying substituent on the trivalent cation site, and the second sample is the undoped crystal for comparison.

note: This is a fluoride ionic conductor measured for its thermal conductivity, not a thermoelectric; it is classified for completeness. One caveat on the proposal itself: its structural_class is written as framework halide, which is not among the structural classes declared in prototypes_seed_v3.json, so folding the entry into v4 needs that class added or check_annotations will reject it. The same applies to the NaYF4 entry proposed from this chunk.

basis: NaYF4 has two well-known forms that share this formula exactly -- the hexagonal beta gagarinite-type, which is the thermodynamically stable one, and the cubic alpha form, which is a cation-disordered fluorite with Na and Y sharing one site -- and the composition alone cannot tell them apart. The taxonomy had nothing for either, so a prototype naming both was proposed; the paper measures thermoelectric power on polycrystalline NaYF4 and does not appear in the title to say which form.
note: Low confidence, and the polymorph question is the whole of it -- which form these 1983 polycrystalline samples hold depends on their synthesis and anneal, not on their composition, and the 313-399 K measurement window is far below any transformation, so whatever was made is what was measured. fluorite_oxide is listed as the alternative because the cubic alpha form genuinely is a disordered fluorite; it is not the primary because that entry is scoped to MO2 oxides and cannot carry the hexagonal form. Recorded disagreement with the reference: Materials Project offers NaYF4 in I4_1/amd, mp-34081, flagged AMBIGUOUS -- a scheelite-like setting that matches neither reported polymorph -- alongside Na2YF6, Na3YF6, NaY2F7 and NaY3F10 at other stoichiometries. I do not adopt it.

basis: (SrF)2Ti2Sb2O is the layered titanium oxypnictide: a Ti2O sheet -- titanium on a square lattice with oxygen at the centre of each square, the anti-configuration of a CuO2 plane -- capped above and below by antimony, with the spacer between slabs. The paper is titled structure and physical properties of the layered pnictide-oxides (SrF)2Ti2Sb2O, and the reference agrees, Sr2Ti2Sb2OF2 in I4/mmm (139), mp-1079717, hull 0.000.
note: One extension of the prototype is worth stating: its formula archetype is A2Ti2Pn2O with A = Na or Ba, a single cation layer between the slabs, whereas here the spacer is a fluorite-type SrF sheet. That is the same Ti2OSb2 slab with a thicker, charge-balanced spacer block -- the standard fluoride-layer variant of this family -- so the entry covers it rather than needing a new one, but a reviewer may want the archetype widened to include (SrF)2. The compound is a charge-density-wave system rather than a thermoelectric, measured from 11 K, which is why the interest is low-temperature.

basis: The material is fluorine-doped tin oxide: the first composition is written (SnO2)0.83F0.17 and both papers are on F-doped SnO2 films, one by spray pyrolysis. SnO2 is the rutile-type oxide, and FTO is one of the standard transparent conducting oxides, so the host lattice is rutile with fluorine on the oxygen site.

dopant_roles.basis: Fluorine replaces oxygen in the rutile lattice, one extra electron per substitution, which is the n-type doping that makes FTO conducting. It is above the 5 at.% threshold and so is not offered as a candidate, but it is recorded because it is the entire subject of both papers.

note: The second composition, Sn2OF, is almost certainly a transcription of a fluorine-doped tin oxide film rather than the distinct Sn(II) oxyfluoride phase of that formula -- both papers are on FTO films, neither is on a tin(II) compound, and there is no reason a thermoelectric study would make Sn2OF. Both papers should be checked before stage 3 treats that string as a stoichiometry. The reference offers only genuine Sn(II) oxyfluorides -- Sn2OF2, Sn2OF5, Sn4OF6 and relatives, each on a single ICSD reference -- and no SnO2 entry at all, because F-doped SnO2 is not a distinct compound in a phase database. I disregard it; following it here would turn a transparent conducting oxide into a fluoride salt.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [136], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12, 19]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Fe2V0.8Ti0.2Ga is Fe2VGa with titanium on part of the vanadium site, and the paper is on optimising the thermoelectric properties of Fe2VGa by tuning the electronic structure. Fe2VGa is the L21 full Heusler, isostructural and isoelectronic with Fe2VAl, the pseudogap Heusler thermoelectric.
note: Titanium sits at 5 at.% of the formula in both samples and so is not offered as a dopant candidate, but its role should carry into stage 3: Ti for V on the octahedral site of the Heusler removes one valence electron per substitution and moves the Fermi level across the pseudogap, which is exactly the tuning the paper title describes. Neither reference returns anything for this four-element host, which is unsurprising -- the parent Fe2VGa would be found under Fe-Ga-V. The measured 297-704 K window involves no structural change; Heusler ordering is retained well above it.

basis: The material is GdFeO3 -- the curator records single crystals measured along the a and c axes and the paper is on the magnetic phase transitions and magnetoelectric coupling of GdFeO3 single crystals. GdFeO3 is the orthoferrite that gives its name to the GdFeO3-type tilted perovskite distortion, and the reference confirms it: GdFeO3 in Pnma (62), mp-600862, hull 0.000 on 16 ICSD references.
note: The composition string is recorded as GdFeO, which under-states the oxygen -- the compound is GdFeO3 and there is no 1:1:1 gadolinium iron oxide. The curator detail and the paper title both give the real formula, so this is a transcription problem in the composition column rather than an ambiguity about the material, but stage 3 should not compute anything from these fractions. The two samples are the same crystal measured along two axes, which is anisotropy rather than two materials. The phase transitions in the paper title are magnetic, not structural, so spans_transition stays false.

basis: LaFePO with hydrogen on the oxygen site is the 1111 iron pnictide: a fluorite-type La2O2 layer alternating with an antifluorite-type Fe2P2 layer, P4/nmm. The paper is on three superconducting phases with different pairing categories in hydrogen-doped material, which is the LaFeAsO1-xHx and LaFePO1-xHx chemistry, and the compositions are written exactly that way.

dopant_roles.basis: Hydride replaces oxygen in the La2O2 layer as H-, donating an electron to the FeP layer. It is the doping variable of the whole hydrogen-doped 1111 family and reaches much higher levels than fluorine can, which is why the phase diagram has several superconducting domes. It is above the 5 at.% threshold and so is not offered as a candidate, but it is recorded because it is the subject of the paper.

note: The two composition strings are inconsistent with each other: LaFePO0.75H0.25 has the anion site summing to 1 as it should, while LaFePO0.90H0.30 sums to 1.20, which cannot be right for a fixed site. One of the two is mistranscribed and the paper should settle which, though the structure is unaffected either way. Neither reference covers this five-element host.

basis: FeNbSb is the workhorse p-type half-Heusler: 18 valence electrons from Fe 8 plus Nb 5 plus Sb 5, MgAgAs-type F-43m with one of the two tetrahedral sites empty. Hf substitutes on the Nb site to move the Fermi level into the valence band, which is the FeNb1-xHfxSb series exactly as both compositions are written. Both paper titles name the half-Heusler outright.

dopant_roles.basis: Hf is the acceptor of the FeNb1-xHfxSb series, sitting on the Nb 4b site and removing one electron per substitution from the 18-electron count. At x of 0.16 to 0.2 it is above the 5 at.% threshold and so is not offered as a candidate, but it is the doping variable of both samples and is recorded for that reason.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal 4b site of the half-Heusler cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Hf/(Hf+Nb) across the two compositions. Hf and Nb are neighbours rather than same-group, so this is an aliovalent substitution that dopes as well as alloys; the axis is recorded by judgement, not by the same-group detector.

note: Fe0.89Nb1.10Hf0.16Sb1.00 is written off-stoichiometry on every site at once, which is a refined-composition transcription rather than a second phase; the half-Heusler tolerates a few percent Fe deficiency on the 4c site and that is the usual reading. Neither reference covers this four-element host, so the space group is from the prototype and not from measurement here.

basis: Two unrelated compounds share this host and it has to be split per composition. HfFe4Sb12 is the Hf-filled iron antimonide skutterudite, an Fe4Sb12 framework of corner-linked FeSb6 octahedra with Hf in the icosahedral void; the filling is what makes an Fe-based skutterudite exist at all, since binary FeSb3 is not a stable phase. Hf6FeSb2 is a completely different thing: an R6TX2 filled Fe2P derivative, and [ref 2] puts it in P-62m (189) at hull 0.000, which is the Zr6CoAs2 type.

other_polymorphs.note: Hf6FeSb2, the second composition of this host and not a polymorph of the first. It is the stable phase of its own stoichiometry at hull 0.000 and carries the paper on ternary transition-metal antimonides. Listed here so the split is visible on the record; the real resolution is a composition-level assignment in stage 2.

[ref 2] lists HfFeSb in Pnma (62) at hull 0.056 with no ICSD references. HfFeSb would be a 17-electron half-Heusler, one short of the closed-shell count, which is why it is not the stable 1:1:1 phase and why MP finds an orthorhombic arrangement instead. No sample in this host is at that stoichiometry.

note: The two compositions are one sample each, from two different papers, and there is no composition between them, so this is two compounds filed together rather than a series. Hf plays opposite roles in them: the icosahedral cage guest in HfFe4Sb12 and the majority framework metal in Hf6FeSb2. The 10 to 300 K measured window is low-temperature transport on both. [ref 2] also offers Hf20(FeSb3)3 C222 and Hf5FeSb2 I4/mcm, neither of which matches a composition here.

basis: SrFe0.5Mn0.25Mo0.25O3 is an ABO3 perovskite with Sr alone on the A site and Fe, Mn and Mo sharing the octahedral B site. It belongs to the SrFe1-xMoxO3 family developed as a redox-stable SOFC anode, which is what the paper studies. At Fe:Mn:Mo of 2:1:1 no rock-salt B-site ordering is possible, so this is the simple disordered perovskite rather than an ordered double perovskite.

other_polymorphs.note: Sr2FeMoO6 in the same chemistry is the Fm-3m ordered double perovskite, and partial Fe/Mo ordering is reported in SrFe1-xMoxO3 as x approaches 0.5. At x of 0.25 with Mn also on the B site, long-range ordering is unlikely but a superstructure reflection search in the paper is what would settle it. Recorded as an alternative description of the same sample, not a separate compound.

note: Single composition, and every B-site element is above the 5 at.% threshold, so nothing here is a dopant candidate: Fe, Mn and Mo are all host constituents of one mixed octahedral site. The curator composition detail is a note about how Fig 4a was digitised and says nothing about the structure. The measured window reaches 887 K robustly and 1085 K at the extreme; cubic Pm-3m is recorded as the aristotype, but an oxygen-deficient SOFC anode at that temperature is often orthorhombic or rhombohedral at room temperature and the space group should be taken from the paper in stage 2. Neither reference covers this five-element host.

basis: FeTiNbO6 is a rutile-type oxide in which Fe, Ti and Nb share the single octahedral cation site of the TiO2 rutile framework; the charges balance as Fe3+ plus Ti4+ plus Nb5+ against six oxygens. The paper title states the structure directly, calling these rutile-type FeTiMO6 with M = Ta or Nb.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] gives TiNbFeO6 in P4_2nm (102) at hull 0.040 as the only entry for this host, with no ICSD references. P4_2nm is a cation-ordered superstructure of rutile rather than a different framework, so it is the same prototype at lower symmetry. Whether the real material orders that way or keeps the cations disordered in P4_2/mnm cannot be told from the formula.

note: I considered the trirutile entry and rejected it: trirutile is AM2O6 with a 1:2 cation ratio ordering along a tripled c axis, and this compound is 1:1:1 across three species, which that ordering scheme cannot describe. Filing it as plain rutile asserts the framework, which the paper supports, and leaves the cation ordering open, which is the part no one here has measured. The recorded space group 136 is the disordered rutile aristotype and disagrees with the P4_2nm (102) that [ref 2] asserts; since that MP entry rests on zero ICSD references it is a computed ordering, not evidence.

basis: Nd2Fe2Se2O3 is better written Nd2O2Fe2OSe2: a fluorite-type Nd2O2 layer alternating with an anti-CuO2 Fe2O square net whose apices are selenium. [ref 2] confirms I4/mmm (139) at hull 0.000 with four ICSD references, and the paper is a synthesis-and-structure study of exactly these new layered oxyselenides, so the structure is reported rather than inferred. The sibling host Fe-Mn-Nd-O-Se is already the example host of this prototype.

dopant_roles.site: square-net transition-metal site of the Fe2O layer
dopant_roles.basis: The curator records the series as Nd2(Fe1-xMnx)2Se2O3, so Mn replaces Fe in the anti-CuO2 net. At x of 0.125 it is an alloying step in a deliberate series rather than dilute doping, and its effect is on the magnetic and correlated-electron state of that net rather than on carrier count alone.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: square-net transition-metal site of the anti-CuO2 Fe2O layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Mn/(Mn+Fe) over the two compositions of this host. The full published series runs further; only the x = 0 and x = 0.125 members fall here, the rest sitting in the Fe-Mn-Nd-O-Se host.

note: The 70 to 323 K window is low-temperature transport on a Mott-insulating oxyselenide, and no structural transition is expected in it. experimentally_confirmed stays false by project rule even though the paper reports the structure, since nothing here was read out of the paper itself.

basis: NixZn1-xFe2O4 is the Ni-Zn ferrite series: a cubic spinel Fd-3m with Fe3+ filling the octahedral B sites and Zn2+ and Ni2+ dividing the divalent role, Zn strongly preferring the tetrahedral A site and Ni the octahedral, so these are mixed rather than cleanly normal or inverse spinels. The paper is a Seebeck study of zinc-substituted nickel ferrites and the 1:2 divalent-to-trivalent stoichiometry admits nothing else.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: divalent cation, split between the tetrahedral 8a and octahedral 16d sites of the spinel cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Zn/(Zn+Ni) across the two compositions. Both elements are above the 5 at.% threshold so neither is offered as a dopant candidate; this is an alloy axis, and it also shifts the A/B site distribution rather than only the electron count.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] here and the disagreement is worth recording. Every entry it marks PRIMARY for this host is a P1 or Cm ordered supercell at hull 0.23 to 0.32 resting on a single ICSD reference, and the cubic Fd-3m spinel that these samples certainly are does not appear in the 2019 dump for the quaternary at all. Those low-symmetry cells are how a DFT database represents a disordered cation distribution, not evidence for a monoclinic or triclinic ferrite. The one plausible-looking entry, ZnFe4NiO8 R3m at hull 0.013, is likewise an ordering of the same framework. Stage 2 should resolve this host against NiFe2O4 and ZnFe2O4 end members instead of the quaternary supercells.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [1, 8]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Ti2FeNiSb2 is the double half-Heusler the paper names in its title: two 18-electron half-Heusler formula units, TiFeSb and TiNiSb, combined so that Fe and Ni take the two tetrahedral sites of a doubled MgAgAs cell. If they order, that is the LiMgPdSn-type quaternary Heusler in F-43m; if they do not, it is a disordered half-Heusler alloy on one site. Composition cannot separate the two, which is the same call already made for the Fe-Ni-Sb-Ti host in chunk 4 and this record follows it for consistency.

other_polymorphs.note: The Fe/Ni-disordered description of the same material: one MgAgAs cell with a mixed occupancy on the 4c site. It is not a separate compound but a different answer about ordering, and only a superstructure-reflection or neutron refinement in the paper can choose.

dopant_roles.site: anion 4a site
dopant_roles.basis: Sn for Sb removes one electron per substitution from the 18-electron count and is the p-type doping variable of the double half-Heusler, which is what the paper title means by enhanced p-type properties. At 8 to 10 at.% it sits above the candidate threshold, so it is recorded here rather than offered by the chunk file.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion 4a site of the Heusler cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Sn/(Sn+Sb) across the two compositions. A narrow aliovalent doping range rather than a wide alloy series.

note: This host is the Sn-doped extension of Fe-Ni-Sb-Ti, which was decided at sample_required level in chunk 4 because the Fe/Ni ordering question could not be settled from composition. The same limitation applies here and the two records should be reviewed together.

basis: FeTiTaO6 is the tantalum member of the same rutile-type FeTiMO6 family as FeTiNbO6, from the same paper: Fe3+, Ti4+ and Ta5+ share the single octahedral site of the rutile framework and the charges balance against six oxygens. [ref 2] gives TaTiFeO6 in P4_2nm (102) at hull 0.024, a cation-ordered rutile superstructure.

other_polymorphs.note: The only [ref 2] entry for this host, at hull 0.024 with no ICSD references. Same situation as the niobium analogue: an ordered variant of the rutile framework produced by the calculation, not an independent structure type.

note: Recorded identically to Fe-Nb-O-Ti, deliberately, since it is the same compound family and the same paper. The trirutile entry was rejected for the same reason: three cations in equal amounts is not the AM2O6 1:2 ordering that entry describes. The 538 K start of the measured window is unusually high and reflects how resistive these oxides are below it.

basis: The composition strings are not a compound: (Y0.06Zr0.97O2.03)79.6(Ni0.08Cr0.18Fe0.76)19.9 is a two-part mixture, yttria partially stabilised zirconia in the first bracket and SUS304 austenitic stainless steel in the second, written with the phase fractions attached. The paper measures the thermal conductivity of SUS304/PSZ composite materials. There is no single structure to assign; the two phases do not react and the measurement is of the mixture.

other_polymorphs.note: The zirconia phase of the composite. At 6 mol% yttria it is the partially stabilised material, so it holds tetragonal and cubic fluorite domains together and the tetragonal-to-monoclinic transformation on cooling is what the yttria suppresses. Recorded as the identifiable crystalline constituent, not as a polymorph of the composite.

dopant_roles.site: cation site of the fluorite zirconia lattice
dopant_roles.basis: Yttria is the stabiliser: Y3+ for Zr4+ introduces the oxygen vacancies that hold the cubic and tetragonal forms down to room temperature. It is a deliberate constituent of the PSZ phase, not an impurity, and it belongs to the oxide half of the composite only.
18 wt% chromium in the austenitic stainless steel phase. It is an alloying element of the metal, on the fcc Fe lattice, and has nothing to do with the zirconia.
8 wt% nickel in the same steel phase, the austenite stabiliser of the 18-8 composition. Again a metal-phase constituent rather than a dopant of an oxide.

note: The Y, Cr and Ni candidate list is a good illustration of why roles are decided per host: the three elements fall on opposite sides of a phase boundary and none of them dopes the same lattice. [ref 2] offers only Zr6Fe2O C2/m at hull 0.366, an Fe-Zr-O intermetallic, which is not present in this material at all and should not be used for it. The two samples differ only in the metal-to-oxide ratio, 19.9 against 39.4 percent, so this host is a composition series in phase fraction rather than in chemistry.

basis: FePb4Sb6S14 is jamesonite itself, the chain sulfosalt whose prototype entry was proposed for the neighbouring Pb-S-Sb host: SbS3 pyramidal ribbons cross-linked by lead in irregular seven- and eight-fold sites with iron in a distinct octahedral site. The formula is exact and the paper is an electronic-structure and thermoelectric study of the thioantimonate, so there is nothing else this can be.

dopant_roles.site: octahedral iron site linking the sulfosalt ribbons
dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt for iron on the single octahedral site, at 8 to 12% of that site. It is the only magnetic-and-electronic knob available in jamesonite without touching the ribbon framework, and the two samples differ only in its level.

note: Two disagreements to record. First, the space group: the jamesonite_fepb4sb6s14 taxonomy entry gives P2_1/m (11), while [ref 2] gives P2_1/c (14) with four ICSD references, and 14 is also what I would say, since jamesonite is conventionally reported in P2_1/a, a setting of space group 14. I have recorded 14 and the taxonomy entry should be corrected rather than followed. Second, the composition string: Co0.08Fe0.92FePb4Sb6S14 carries two iron units, as though the substituted site Fe1-xCox had been prefixed to the full parent formula, which would make Fe total 1.92 where jamesonite has one. The intended material is almost certainly Fe1-xCoxPb4Sb6S14 and the parser has taken the prefix at face value.

basis: U2Fe2Sn belongs to the U2T2X family, which is the Mo2FeB2 type: an ordered ternary derivative of U3Si2 in P4/mbm, built from alternating layers of uranium and transition-metal-plus-tin. [ref 2] gives U2Fe2Sn in P4/mbm (127) at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references, which is that type exactly, and the companion compound in the paper, U2Rh2Sn, is a well-known member of the same series.
note: The two samples are the same compound in two states, as cast and annealed at 900 C for 24 h in argon, which the curator records. For a U2T2X intermetallic that difference shows up in the low-temperature resistivity and the Kondo coherence rather than in the structure type, so both samples take the same assignment. [ref 2] also lists UFe5Sn in Pnma at hull 0.063, which is a different compound at a different stoichiometry and not a polymorph of U2Fe2Sn.

basis: RFe2Zn20 is the CeCr2Al20 cage structure in Fd-3m: a Zn framework of Frank-Kasper polyhedra with iron in the small cage and the rare earth in the large one. The seed entry already names YbIr2Zn20 as its exemplar, which is the same YbT2Zn20 series this paper measures. [ref 2] has no Y or Yb member but lists three isostructural analogues at Fd-3m (227) and hull 0.000, TbFe2Zn20, UFe2Zn20 and ZrFe2Zn20, written in the Tb(Zn10Fe)2 form.

dopant_roles.site: 8a rare-earth site of the CeCr2Al20 cage
dopant_roles.basis: Yb is the rare earth of YbFe2Zn20 and sits fully occupied at the centre of the large Zn cage; it is a required host site, not a dilute filler. It falls below the 5 at.% threshold only because the formula has 23 atoms, and it is the whole point of the paper, which is about heavy-fermion behaviour arising from the Yb 4f state being nearly isolated inside that cage.

dopant_roles.site: 8a rare-earth site of the CeCr2Al20 cage
dopant_roles.basis: Y plays the same structural role in YFe2Zn20, which is the non-magnetic reference compound for the Yb member: same structure, no 4f electrons. Also a full host site rather than a dopant.

note: No solid-solution axis is recorded even though Y and Yb share one site, because the two compositions are separate single crystals at the pure end members with nothing in between; calling that a series would overstate it. The host key Fe-Zn is a poor description of this material: the 5 at.% split puts the rare earth, which is the reason these compounds are studied at all, below the threshold and leaves the host named after the framework alone. Both samples are single crystals measured from 11 K, which is what a heavy-fermion thermopower study needs.

basis: Both compositions are Gd(Ni,Ga)4 with nickel and gallium sharing the main-group sublattice, which is the BaAl4 aristotype in I4/mmm: a large electropositive cation between slabs of the tetrel-or-triel network. The paper studies the GdTxGa4-x solid solutions, and that formula is the BaAl4 stoichiometry written out. At a Ni:Ga ratio of 1:3 the two BaAl4 sites cannot order cleanly into the ThCr2Si2 arrangement, which needs 2:2, so the disordered parent is the better label.

dopant_roles.site: 4d and 4e main-group sites of the BaAl4 cell
dopant_roles.basis: Nickel enters the gallium network of the BaAl4 slab, which is what makes the ternary stable where binary GdGa4 is not, and its level is the variable the paper sweeps. At 15 to 25% of that sublattice it is above the candidate threshold and is recorded as the compositional variable rather than as doping.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: main-group sublattice of the BaAl4 slab
solid_solution_axis.note: Ni/(Ni+Ga) across the two compositions, GdNi0.6Ga3.4 and GdNiGa3. Nickel and gallium are not same-group, so this axis both alloys and changes the electron count.

note: Confidence is medium and the reference does not help. [ref 2] offers only Gd3(GaNi3)2 in Im-3m at hull 0.000, a cubic compound at a quite different Gd:Ni:Ga ratio, so it neither confirms nor contradicts a BaAl4-type Gd(Ni,Ga)4; the 1:1:3 composition is simply absent from the dump. The alternative worth checking in the paper is whether the sample at GdNiGa3 has ordered into a ThCr2Si2-type superstructure, which would show as a different diffraction pattern in the same cell.

basis: SrGdGa3O7 is a melilite-group gallate: sheets of corner-sharing GaO4 tetrahedra with strontium and gadolinium sharing the large eight-coordinate site between them, tetragonal P-421m. The ABGa3O7 melilites are a standard laser-host family and this paper grows and characterises Nd-doped SrGdGa3O7 single crystals. I proposed the prototype in taxonomy/prototypes_proposed.jsonl before using it, since the seed carries the neighbouring piezoelectric gallates but not melilite.

dopant_roles.site: eight-coordinate A site shared by Sr and Gd
dopant_roles.basis: Nd3+ replaces Gd3+ on the large interlayer site and is the optically active ion of the laser crystal; the composition puts it at 1% of that site. It is a genuine dilute substitutional dopant, and an isovalent one, so it changes the optical properties without changing carrier count.

note: [ref 2] lists only Sr2GdGaO5 in Fmmm (69) at hull 0.059 for this host, which is a different compound at a different gallium content and not a polymorph of SrGdGa3O7; the melilite is absent from the 2019 dump for this chemistry, so the space group here rests on the prototype and the paper rather than on the reference. This is also a material whose thermoelectric interest is marginal: two samples of a Nd laser crystal, measured over a narrow window, with insulating transport.

basis: Sr7.57Ga15.65Si3.72Ge27.06 is Sr8Ga16SixGe30-x, the strontium-filled type-I clathrate: a Ga-Si-Ge framework of face-sharing dodecahedra and tetrakaidecahedra in Pm-3n with strontium in the two cage sites. The refined guest count of 7.57 against 8 and the framework total of 46.4 against 46 are the usual slight off-stoichiometry of a refined clathrate rather than evidence of another phase, and one of the two papers is on Ba8Ga16SixGe30-x clathrates directly.

dopant_roles.site: 2a and 6d cage sites of the type-I clathrate
dopant_roles.basis: Strontium is the guest atom in both cage types and its rattling is the source of the low lattice thermal conductivity these materials are made for. At 7.57 of 8 sites the cages are very slightly vacant, which is a non-stoichiometry on the guest sublattice; it is above the candidate threshold and recorded here as the defining host constituent.

dopant_roles.site: 6c, 16i and 24k framework sites
dopant_roles.basis: Sixteen gallium atoms per formula substitute into the group-14 framework and set the electron count, each one compensating one guest electron, which is why the composition locks at Ga16 for eight divalent guests. Framework substitution rather than doping.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: group-14 framework sites of the type-I clathrate
solid_solution_axis.note: Si/(Si+Ge) for the single composition of this host. The published series runs over the whole range; only the x near 3.7 member falls here, which is why the axis has no spread.

note: Neither reference covers this four-element host. One paper title names a Ba-filled Si-Ge clathrate and the other Ba8Ga16SixGe30-x, but the composition recorded here is strontium-filled, so these rows are the Sr members measured alongside the Ba ones; the Ba samples route to a different host. The measured window is 19 to 301 K, low-temperature transport rather than the high-temperature range clathrates are usually assessed over.

basis: LaGa2 is the AlB2 type: flat graphite-like gallium honeycomb nets with lanthanum in the hexagonal prisms between them, P6/mmm. [ref 2] gives LaGa2 in P6/mmm (191) at hull 0.000 with six ICSD references, the best-attested entry in the host, and the paper measures transport across RGa2 for R = La, Ce and Sm, a series that is AlB2-type throughout.
note: The other four entries [ref 2] lists for this host, LaGa6, LaGa, La3Ga and La5Ga3, are separate compounds along the La-Ga line rather than polymorphs of LaGa2, so none of them competes here. Both samples are single crystals measured from 15 K.

basis: La(Ni,Ga)5 is LaNi5 with gallium substituted into the nickel sublattice, and LaNi5 is the CaCu5 type in P6/mmm: alternating Ni3 kagome and LaNi2 layers. The paper is about the CeNi5 thermopower and its strong 4f instability, with the La compound as the non-magnetic reference, and both compositions are written as La(Ni1-xGax)5, which keeps the 1:5 CaCu5 stoichiometry exactly.

dopant_roles.site: 3g nickel site of the CaCu5 cell, which is where gallium is known to go preferentially
dopant_roles.basis: Gallium substitutes onto the nickel sublattice and expands the cell while adding electrons, which is how this series tunes the 3d band position; in the sister CeNi5-xGax compounds it is the parameter that drives the 4f instability the paper is about. At 10 to 13.5% of the nickel sites it is above the candidate threshold and is the compositional variable rather than dilute doping.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: 2c and 3g transition-metal sites of the CaCu5 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Ga/(Ga+Ni) across the two compositions. Narrow, and both samples sit in the dilute substitution regime of the LaNi5-xGax line.

note: [ref 2] does not reach this composition. Everything it lists for the host, LaGa2Ni Cmmm, LaGaNi P2_1/c, La2Ga10Ni I4/mmm, La2Ga12Ni P4/nbm and La3(GaNi)2 Pbcm, is a distinct La-Ni-Ga compound at a different ratio, and the CaCu5-type La(Ni,Ga)5 is absent, so the space group rests on LaNi5 itself rather than on a reference entry. The measured range is unusually wide for this family, 16 to 883 K, and the record assumes no structural change across it, which is the normal expectation for a CaCu5 intermetallic.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [191], ICSD-backed references for this host report [65, 14, 57, 125]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Re6Te15 is the octahedral rhenium cluster chalcogenide already in the seed, Re6 cores in a telluride matrix, and these compositions are its gallium-containing derivatives: the paper sweeps Re6GaxSeyTe15-y over x from 0 to 2, so the cluster framework is fixed and gallium is the added variable. The Re6Ch15 stoichiometry is unchanged at 15 chalcogen per six rhenium in both compositions here.

dopant_roles.basis: Gallium is the added component of the Re6GaxTe15 series and the chalcogen count does not change with x, so it cannot be substituting for tellurium; the natural reading is that it occupies voids between the Re6Te8 cluster units, in the way guest atoms enter other cluster chalcogenides. At 6.5 to 8.7 at.% it is above the candidate threshold. The site is a judgement from the stoichiometry alone and the paper should be read before relying on it.

note: Confidence is medium rather than high for two reasons. Neither reference covers this host at all, so the Pbca space group comes from the Re6Te15 prototype rather than from a measured gallium-containing crystal, and inserting up to two gallium atoms per formula could plausibly lower the symmetry. The two compositions differ only in gallium content, 1.5 against 2, which is a filling variable on whatever site gallium takes.

basis: Ga2Se3 is named as a representative material of the ga2te3_defect_zincblende entry, and it is the textbook case for it: a sphalerite lattice in which one third of the cation sites are vacant because gallium is trivalent, with the vacancies ordering into rows and lowering the symmetry to monoclinic Cc. [ref 1], which takes precedence, gives Ga2Se3 in Cc (9) as PRIMARY with six ICSD references, and the paper is specifically about how the vacancy distribution controls thermal conductivity in Ga2Te3 and Ga2Se3.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists a second Ga2Se3 in Imm2 at hull 0.009 with no ICSD references. It is a different ordering of the same cation vacancies rather than a different structure type, and the near-zero energy difference is exactly why the vacancy arrangement is the subject of the paper.

note: The two references disagree about what this host is and the project precedence settles it. [ref 2] marks GaSe P6_3/mmc as PRIMARY and flags it AMBIGUOUS, but GaSe is a layered van der Waals compound at a different stoichiometry, not a polymorph of Ga2Se3, and the samples here are Ga2Se3. [ref 1] covers the actual formula and is ICSD-backed and thermoelectric-specific, so it decides. The GaSe entries in both references, and GaSe2 and Ga3Se, are other compounds along the Ga-Se line.

basis: Sr8Ga16Si30 is the strontium-filled type-I silicon clathrate: a Ga-Si framework of dodecahedral and tetrakaidecahedral cages in Pm-3n with eight strontium guests, and the composition is the ideal one, sixteen gallium exactly compensating eight divalent guests. One paper synthesises silicon clathrates Sr8AlxGa16-xSi30 and the other measures high-temperature thermal conductivity of thermoelectric clathrates, so the structure is not in doubt.

dopant_roles.site: 2a and 6d cage sites of the type-I clathrate
dopant_roles.basis: The guest atom in both cage types, fully occupied at eight per formula, and the rattler responsible for the low lattice thermal conductivity. Above the candidate threshold and recorded as the host constituent it is.

dopant_roles.site: 6c, 16i and 24k framework sites
dopant_roles.basis: Gallium substitutes into the silicon framework and sets the electron count; at Ga16 the compound is charge balanced against eight Sr2+ guests, which is why the composition sits there and not elsewhere.

note: One composition is written Sr8Al0Ga16Si30, with an explicit zero for aluminium. That is the x = 0 member of the paper series Sr8AlxGa16-xSi30 transcribed with the aluminium term left in place, so the two compositions in this host are the same material and aluminium is not present in either; the Al0 term is a transcription artefact and not a constituent. [ref 2] lists only Sr2GaSi, Sr4GaSi3 and SrGaSi for this host, all of them different compounds on the Sr-Ga-Si line, and the type-I clathrate itself is absent from the dump, so the space group comes from the prototype. The robust measured window is 10 to 130 K while the full span reaches 767 K, so the two samples are measured over very different ranges.

basis: TlGaTe2 is the TlSe type in I4/mcm: chains of edge-sharing GaTe4 tetrahedra running along c, with monovalent thallium in eight-coordinate sites between them, so the formula is properly read Tl+[Ga3+Te2]-. [ref 2] gives TlGaTe2 in I4/mcm (140) at hull 0.000 with six ICSD references, and the paper systematically surveys TlMTe2 compounds, which are TlSe-type across M.

dopant_roles.site: tetrahedral trivalent site of the chain
dopant_roles.basis: Indium for gallium on the tetrahedral chain site, isoelectronic since both are group 13, which is why the TlIn1-xGaxTe2 series is continuous: TlInTe2 is the same TlSe structure. It widens the chain rather than changing the carrier count, and the second paper is an X-ray and electrical study of exactly that series.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral trivalent site of the TlSe-type chain
solid_solution_axis.note: In/(In+Ga) across the two compositions. A genuine isoelectronic axis, but sampled only at the gallium-rich end here; the rest of the TlIn1-xGaxTe2 series routes to other hosts.

note: One sample is bulk and the other a single crystal, which matters for a chain compound: the TlSe structure is strongly anisotropic and a polycrystal averages over an anisotropy the crystal resolves. The measured window, 293 to 869 K, is well within the stability range of this structure.

basis: Gd2Ir2O7 is an A2B2O7 pyrochlore, Fd-3m: interpenetrating networks of corner-sharing IrO6 octahedra and eight-coordinate Gd, and the whole RE2Ir2O7 series is pyrochlore. The paper title names the structure, describing the samples as Gd doping of pyrochlore Bi2Ir2O7, so the Bi-containing composition is the Bi2Ir2O7 to Gd2Ir2O7 line rather than a separate phase.

dopant_roles.site: eight-coordinate A site of the pyrochlore
dopant_roles.basis: Bi0.5Gd1.5Ir2O7 puts bismuth on a quarter of the A sites, which makes it an end-member alloying step on the Bi2Ir2O7 to Gd2Ir2O7 line rather than dilute doping; it falls below the 5 at.% threshold only because the formula has eleven atoms. Bismuth on the A site is also not a spectator here, since the Bi 6s states hybridise with the Ir 5d band and are what makes Bi2Ir2O7 metallic where Gd2Ir2O7 is not.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: eight-coordinate A site of the pyrochlore
solid_solution_axis.note: Bi/(Bi+Gd) across the two compositions. Bi3+ and Gd3+ are the same charge but not the same group, so the same-group detector would not find this axis; it is recorded by judgement because the paper treats it as a substitution series.

note: Neither reference covers this host, so the space group rests on the RE2Ir2O7 family rather than on a measured entry. The 11 to 297 K window does cross something, but not a structural transition: Gd2Ir2O7 orders magnetically into the all-in-all-out iridium state near 120 K and is a Mott insulator below it, which is presumably what the paper is measuring. spans_transition is left false because the field is for structural changes and the cubic pyrochlore cell survives the magnetic ordering.

basis: Gd2Mo2O7 is the molybdate pyrochlore, and [ref 2] gives it in Fd-3m (227) at hull 0.000 with five ICSD references, the best-attested entry for this host. Both papers are explicitly on RE2Mo2O7 pyrochlores, one on their thermoelectric power and the other on the electrical properties of the Ln2Mo2O7 series, so the structure is stated in the sources.
note: [ref 2] marks Gd2(MoO4)3 in Pba2 as PRIMARY and flags it AMBIGUOUS, but that is a different compound, the molybdate with isolated MoO4 tetrahedra and Mo6+, not a polymorph of the Mo4+ pyrochlore; the same applies to Gd6Mo10O39, Gd2Mo5O18 and Gd4Mo4O11, all of which are separate phases along the Gd-Mo-O line. Only the Fd-3m entry matches the composition here. Gd2Mo2O7 sits close to the metal-insulator boundary of the RE2Mo2O7 series, which is why its thermopower was of interest, and it orders ferromagnetically below about 70 K, inside the measured window; that is a magnetic transition and does not change the cubic cell.

basis: GdN is a rocksalt nitride, Fm-3m, like every rare-earth mononitride. [ref 2] gives GdN in Fm-3m (225) at hull 0.000 with eleven ICSD references, which is the strongest evidence available anywhere in this chunk, and nothing else is plausible for a 1:1 rare-earth nitride.
note: The provenance is worth noting: the paper is a thermal conductivity study of gadolinium-added uranium mononitride fuel pellets, so these GdN rows are the additive measured on its own rather than a thermoelectric material in its own right. The same paper supplies the Gd-N-O-U host at rank 2225. The measured range runs to 1273 K, which GdN tolerates; it is refractory and stays rocksalt to the melt.

basis: The compositions are written as bracketed phase fractions, (Gd2O3)7.17(UN)92.83, which is a two-phase pellet and not a compound: rocksalt uranium mononitride with gadolinia added as a burnable neutron absorber. The paper measures the thermal conductivity of gadolinium-added UN fuel pellets, where the point is exactly that the additive is a dispersed second phase degrading the conductivity of the matrix.

other_polymorphs.note: The UN matrix, 89 to 93 mol% of the pellet and the phase that carries the heat. Rocksalt Fm-3m, the same structure as the GdN host at rank 2224.

The gadolinia additive. Gd2O3 at ambient conditions is the cubic C-type rare-earth oxide, which is the bixbyite structure in Ia-3; it converts to the monoclinic B-type and then the hexagonal A-type only at much higher temperatures than this measurement reaches. Recorded as the second constituent, not as a polymorph of the composite.

note: No dopant candidates are offered because the parser sees Gd and O as major constituents, which they are of the pellet even though they belong to only one of its two phases. Whether some gadolinium also dissolves into the UN lattice is a real question for a fuel pellet sintered at high temperature and the paper would have to settle it; the composition string treats the two phases as separate and this record follows that. Neither reference covers the host, which is expected for a mixture rather than a compound.

basis: Gd1-xSrxTiO3 is the perovskite solid solution between the Mott insulator GdTiO3 and the band insulator SrTiO3, with Gd3+ and Sr2+ sharing the A site and titanium alone on the octahedral B site; the substitution is what drives the metal-insulator transitions the paper reports in epitaxial films. The ABO3 stoichiometry is exact in both compositions and no other structure type is available at that ratio for these cations.

other_polymorphs.note: The cubic aristotype, which is what SrTiO3 is at room temperature and what the Sr-rich end of this series approaches. These are epitaxial films, so the substrate also imposes a symmetry: a film clamped to a cubic substrate can be tetragonal where the bulk would be orthorhombic. The recorded orthorhombic Pnma is the bulk expectation for the Gd-rich compositions and the film symmetry should be taken from the paper.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: twelve-coordinate A site of the perovskite
solid_solution_axis.note: Gd/(Gd+Sr) across the two compositions. This is the doping variable of the whole study: it sets the d-band filling of titanium and therefore which side of the metal-insulator transition the film is on. Both elements are above the 5 at.% threshold so neither is offered as a dopant candidate.

note: Recorded with a Pnma space group and medium phase confidence because the GdFeO3-type octahedral tilt grows continuously with Gd content, so a single space group cannot be right across the series; at x near 0.285 Gd the material is much closer to cubic than at 0.56. Neither reference covers this four-element host. The composition strings in the chunk file, Gd0.285Sr0.715TiO3 and Gd0.560Sr0.440TiO3, sum correctly on the A site, which is a good sign for the transcription.

basis: This host holds two different compounds and must be split. GdTaO4 is M-fergusonite, the monoclinic scheelite derivative that all the rare-earth tantalates and niobates take, and [ref 2] gives it in P2/c (13) at hull 0.000 with three ICSD references, which is that structure. GdTa3O9 is not a polymorph of it but an A-site-deficient perovskite, Gd1/3TaO3, with two thirds of the A sites empty and corner-sharing TaO6 octahedra; [ref 2] puts it in P2_1/m (11), a tilted and ordered variant of that. I proposed the fergusonite prototype before using it, since the scheelite entry in the taxonomy is explicitly limited to Ca-Sr-Ba-Pb tungstates and molybdates.

other_polymorphs.note: GdTa3O9, the second composition of this host and a separate compound rather than a polymorph. An A-site-deficient perovskite at Gd1/3TaO3; the vacancy ordering on the A site is what lowers the symmetry to P2_1/m and it is sometimes described in the literature as a layered or double perovskite for that reason. Listed here so the split is on the record; the proper fix is a composition-level assignment in stage 2.

note: Confidence is medium because the host label is standing over two compounds at one sample each and the primary choice between them is arbitrary; I made GdTaO4 primary because it is the better-attested composition and the one the taxonomy now has an entry for. One of the two paper titles speaks of a double perovskite rare-earth tantalate and the other of ultralow thermal conductivity in a bismuth-containing compound, so the papers may not both be about the compositions recorded here and should be checked. [ref 2] also lists Gd3TaO7, GdTa4O12 and GdTa7O19 for this host, none of which matches either composition. The ferroelastic monoclinic-to-tetragonal transition of RETaO4 lies far above the 1073 K top of the measured window, so no phase array entry is needed for it.

basis: GdVO4 is a zircon-type orthovanadate, I4_1/amd: isolated VO4 tetrahedra alternating with eight-coordinate Gd along chains, the same structure as YVO4 and ZrSiO4. [ref 2] gives GdVO4 in I4_1/amd (141) at hull 0.000 with seven ICSD references, and the paper characterises mixed Nd:LuxGd1-xVO4 laser crystals, a series that stays zircon-type across x. I proposed the zircon prototype before using it, since the seed taxonomy had only the scheelite side of the ABO4 family.

other_polymorphs.note: Zircon-type orthovanadates convert to a scheelite-type polymorph near 6 GPa. It is a pressure phase, never reached on heating, so it is recorded here rather than in the thermal sequence.

dopant_roles.site: eight-coordinate rare-earth site of the zircon cell
dopant_roles.basis: Nd3+ for Gd3+ is the laser activator, and the curator records the level as 5 at% Nd, matching the composition prefix. Isovalent and dilute, so it is a true substitutional dopant; it changes the optical properties rather than the carrier concentration.

dopant_roles.site: eight-coordinate rare-earth site of the zircon cell
dopant_roles.basis: Lutetium is the other rare earth of the LuxGd1-xVO4 host series and sits on the same site. At 14% of it this is isoelectronic substitution rather than doping: it shrinks the cell and is used to tune the crystal field around the Nd, which is the point of a mixed laser host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: eight-coordinate rare-earth site of the zircon cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Lu/(Lu+Gd) for the single composition here. Both are rare earths on one site, so it is a genuine isoelectronic axis, but the published LuxGd1-xVO4 series is sampled at only this one point in this host.

note: [ref 2] also offers GdVO3 Pnma, Gd3YV4O16, and two Gd2V2O7 entries including a pyrochlore, all of which are different compounds along the Gd-V-O line rather than polymorphs of GdVO4; only the I4_1/amd entry matches the composition. As with the SrGdGa3O7 host, this is a laser crystal rather than a thermoelectric, and the two samples are an optical characterisation that happens to include Seebeck and conductivity data.

basis: GdPdSb belongs to the LnPdSb series, which takes the hexagonal LiGaGe structure in P6_3mc: a puckered honeycomb PdSb net with the rare earth between the layers, the ordered and non-centrosymmetric variant of CaIn2. [ref 2] gives GdSbPd in P6_3mc (186) at hull 0.000, which is that setting exactly, and the prototype entry already names CePdSb as its exemplar. The paper is on LnPdSb for Ln = La and Gd as intermetallics with large carrier mobility.
note: This is the clean case for the hexagonal RTX type: an equiatomic 1:1:1 rare-earth compound that could in principle be the orthorhombic TiNiSi type or the hexagonal ZrNiAl type instead, and the reference space group picks LiGaGe unambiguously. The MP entry rests on a single ICSD reference, which is thin, but it agrees with what the LnPdSb family is known to do. The measured window reaches 922 K robustly and 967 K at the extreme, which is high for an antimonide and is presumably why the second paper is about high-temperature Hall measurements.

basis: Ge38Sb8I8 is a cationic type-I clathrate, and the inversion is the interesting part: the germanium-antimony framework is positively charged and the guests in the cages are iodide anions, the opposite of the usual Ba8Ga16Ge30 arrangement where the guest is a cation. The framework is still the 46-atom type-I cage network, [ref 2] gives Ge19(SbI)4, which is this formula, in P-43n (218) at hull 0.028, and the paper is on sintered iodine-containing germanium clathrates.

dopant_roles.site: 2a and 6d cage sites of the type-I clathrate
dopant_roles.basis: Iodine is the guest, and as an anion rather than a cation it accepts electrons from the framework instead of donating them; eight iodides per formula are what eight antimony substitutions on the framework pay for. Above the candidate threshold and recorded as the defining host constituent.

dopant_roles.site: framework sites of the 46-atom cage network
dopant_roles.basis: Antimony substitutes into the germanium framework and is the electron source that makes the framework cationic; the composition locks at Sb8 for I8 for exactly that reason. Framework substitution, not doping.

note: The recorded space group 218 is the ordered subgroup that [ref 2] asserts rather than the Pm-3n aristotype of the type-I clathrate, and it is plausible here because a cationic clathrate has ordered framework substitution and often framework vacancies; the MP entry carries no ICSD references though, so this is a computed ordering and the aristotype remains the safer general statement. The second paper listed for this host is on Ge30P16Te8, which is the Ge-P-Te host at rank 2236, so the two hosts share a research line: cationic clathrates of germanium with a pnictogen on the framework and a chalcogen or halogen in the cages.

basis: (Yb,Lu)3Ir4Ge13 is an R3T4X13 Remeika phase: a cubic Pm-3n framework of corner-shared IrGe6 trigonal prisms enclosing Ge12 cages, with the rare earth in the large cavities. The 3:4:13 stoichiometry is the signature of the family and admits nothing else, and the paper describes a low-carrier-density Kondo lattice, which is what a Yb-bearing Remeika phase is. The sister host Ge-Ir-Yb at rank 2233 is the pure Yb end member and [ref 2] gives it Pm-3n there.

dopant_roles.site: rare-earth cavity site of the Remeika cage framework
dopant_roles.basis: Lutetium is the non-magnetic diluent of the Yb3-xLuxIr4Ge13 series: it has a filled 4f shell, so replacing Yb thins out the Kondo lattice while barely changing the cell size. That is the point of the paper, which is about magnetism becoming fragile as the lattice is diluted. At 40 to 60% of the rare-earth site this is alloying rather than doping.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth cavity site of the R3T4X13 framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Yb/(Yb+Lu) across the two compositions, both near the middle of the series. Both are rare earths on one site, so this is a genuine isoelectronic axis in size terms, though not in 4f occupancy, which is exactly what is being varied.

note: Neither reference covers this four-element host. One caveat for stage 2: several R3T4X13 Remeika phases undergo a superlattice distortion on cooling, Ca3Ir4Sn13 near 38 K being the best known, which would put a structural change inside the 13 to 124 K measured window. I have not asserted one here because I do not know it for the germanide, and the paper would have to be read; spans_transition is left false on that basis rather than on evidence of no transition.

basis: La0.3Ir4Ge0.9Sb11.1 is a partially La-filled iridium antimonide skutterudite: the Ir4Sb12 framework of corner-linked IrSb6 octahedra with La in the icosahedral void, and germanium substituted onto the pnictogen framework to pay for the filler electrons. The paper is on the effect of partial La filling on high-temperature thermoelectric properties, so the filling is the subject rather than an inference.

dopant_roles.site: 2a icosahedral void of the skutterudite framework
dopant_roles.basis: Lanthanum occupies 30% of the cage sites and rattles there, which is the phonon-scattering mechanism the paper is testing. It is a cage filler and not a substitutional dopant: it takes a site that is empty in binary IrSb3 rather than replacing any framework atom. The partial occupancy is the tuning variable.

dopant_roles.site: 24g pnictogen ring site
dopant_roles.basis: Germanium on the antimony framework removes one electron per substitution and is what charge-compensates the trivalent filler; at Ge0.9 for La0.3 the arithmetic is close to exact. It is above the candidate threshold and is a framework substitution rather than doping.

note: Neither reference covers this host. The recorded Im-3 is the filled skutterudite space group, the same as the unfilled framework since filling the void does not lower the symmetry, only the occupancy. Note the single curve behind the measurement, so the 298 to 954 K range comes from one property rather than from a consistent set.

basis: Yb3Ir4Ge13 is the pure ytterbium member of the R3T4X13 Remeika family, and [ref 2] gives Yb3Ge13Ir4 in Pm-3n (223) at hull 0.000, which is that structure. The seed entry is built on Yb3Rh4Sn13, the same 3:4:13 framework with a different transition metal and tetrel. The paper is the same low-carrier-density Kondo lattice study as the mixed Yb-Lu host at rank 2231.
note: [ref 2] also lists Yb4Ge6Ir7, Yb2Ge2Ir and Yb5(Ge5Ir2)2 for this host, all separate compounds on the Yb-Ir-Ge line rather than polymorphs of the 3:4:13 phase; only the Pm-3n entry matches the composition, and it rests on a single ICSD reference. The robust measured window is 10 to 77 K with the full span reaching 298 K. The same superlattice-distortion caveat noted on the Ge-Ir-Lu-Yb record applies here and is the reason to read the paper before treating the cubic cell as holding down to 10 K.

basis: Both compositions are members of the KxBa8-xZnyGe46-y series the paper names in its title: a type-I clathrate with a Zn-Ge framework of 46 atoms per cell and eight guest sites filled by potassium and barium. K8Zn4Ge42 is the pure potassium end, the framework total 46 exactly, and K6Ba2Zn5Ge41 substitutes two barium for two potassium with one more zinc to keep the electron count. The 8-to-46 guest-to-framework ratio is the type-I signature.

dopant_roles.site: 2a and 6d cage sites of the type-I clathrate
dopant_roles.basis: Barium takes guest sites from potassium, and because it is divalent where potassium is monovalent, each substitution donates one extra electron to the framework, which is why the zinc count rises with it. It is a cage filler on a site that is already occupied rather than an empty one, so it is substitutional within the guest sublattice; at two of eight sites it is an alloying step, not dilute doping.

dopant_roles.site: 6c, 16i and 24k framework sites
dopant_roles.basis: Zinc substitutes into the germanium framework and accepts the guest electrons, setting the charge balance: four zinc for eight potassium, five for six potassium plus two barium. Framework substitution.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: guest cage sites of the type-I clathrate
solid_solution_axis.note: Ba/(Ba+K) across the two compositions. Not same-group and not isovalent, so this axis changes the framework composition with it; it is the electron-count knob of the whole series.

note: [ref 2] lists only K14ZnGe16 in Pmn2_1 for this host, which is a different compound entirely and not a clathrate, so the space group rests on the type-I framework rather than on the reference. The measured window is wide, 93 to 1014 K over ten curves, which is more thorough than most hosts this far down the ranking.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [31]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Mg2(Si,Sn,Ge) is the antifluorite Mg2X structure in Fm-3m: magnesium on the tetrahedral sites of a face-centred group-14 lattice, the CaF2 arrangement with the roles of cation and anion exchanged. Silicon, tin and germanium are mutually substitutional on the single anion site, which is what the Mg2Si-Mg2Sn-Mg2Ge solid solutions are, and the 2:1 stoichiometry holds exactly in both compositions.

dopant_roles.site: anion site of the antifluorite cell
dopant_roles.basis: Bismuth on the group-14 anion site is the standard n-type donor for Mg2(Si,Sn), contributing one extra electron per substitution; the composition pair is the undoped and the Bi0.02 sample, and the difference between them is the carrier concentration. A genuine dilute substitutional dopant, which the composition shows by taking the 0.02 out of the silicon share rather than adding it on top.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion site of the antifluorite cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Reported as the germanium share of the anion site, which is fixed at 0.2 in both compositions; the silicon-to-tin ratio is likewise fixed at 0.4 to 0.4. Three group-14 elements share one site, so this is a ternary isoelectronic axis, and the value of the alloy is the mass and strain disorder it puts on that site rather than any electronic change.

note: Neither reference covers this four-element host. One caveat for stage 2: the Mg2Si-Mg2Sn system has a miscibility gap, so nominally single-phase samples in this composition range are often two antifluorite phases, one silicon-rich and one tin-rich. That does not change the prototype, since both phases are the same structure, but it does mean a single lattice parameter may not describe the sample. The measured window is 19 to 820 K robustly and 986 K at the extreme.

basis: Both compositions are cationic germanium clathrates with phosphorus on the framework and tellurium in the cages, but they are two different clathrate types and the host has to be split. Ge30P16Te8 is the type-I structure, which the first paper names in its title, with 46 framework atoms and 8 guest sites. Ge129.3P42.7Te21.53 is the type-III phase of the second paper, Ge172-xPxTey with y near 21.5, a 172-atom tetragonal framework; the guest-to-framework ratio alone separates them.

other_polymorphs.note: The second composition of this host, Ge172-xPxTey, and a separate compound rather than a polymorph: type III is a 172-atom tetragonal cage framework, not a rearrangement of the 46-atom type-I cell. Recorded here so the split is visible; a composition-level assignment in stage 2 is the proper fix. Note that the clathrate_iii_ix taxonomy entry gives P4132 (213), which is the type-IX space group; type III is P4_2/mnm (136) and that is what I have recorded for this phase.

dopant_roles.site: cage sites of the clathrate framework
dopant_roles.basis: Tellurium is the guest and, like the iodide of Ge38Sb8I8, it is an anionic guest in a cationic framework, accepting electrons rather than donating them. Above the candidate threshold and recorded as a defining constituent.

dopant_roles.site: framework sites of the cage network
dopant_roles.basis: Phosphorus substitutes into the germanium framework and supplies the electrons the tellurium guests take; the composition ratio x near 2y in the type-III phase is the charge-balance condition written out. Framework substitution.

note: Confidence is medium because the host stands over two clathrate types at one sample each and the choice of primary is arbitrary; I made type I primary because its composition is the exact stoichiometric one. Neither reference covers this host. The first paper here is also listed on the Ge-I-Sb host at rank 2230, confirming these are one research line on cationic germanium clathrates.

basis: UPdGe is the equiatomic RTX compound in the orthorhombic TiNiSi type, an ordered Co2Si derivative in Pnma with a three-dimensional PdGe framework and uranium in the channels. [ref 2] gives UGePd in Pnma (62) at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references, which is that structure, and the paper sweeps the URu1-xPdxGe system, continuous across x, so both members share the type.

dopant_roles.site: transition-metal site of the TiNiSi framework
dopant_roles.basis: Ruthenium for palladium is the variable of the URu1-xPdxGe series the paper is about: it changes the 4f-conduction hybridisation and drives the magnetic ground state, which is why the thermopower is worth measuring across it. At 10% of the transition-metal site it is dilute here, but it is an alloying variable in the wider series rather than a dopant in the carrier-count sense.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal site of the TiNiSi framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Ru/(Ru+Pd) across the two compositions. The rest of the series sits in the Ge-Ru-U host at rank 2239, which is the same paper seen from the other end; the two records should be read together.

note: [ref 2] also lists U(GePd)2 in I4/mmm, which is UPd2Ge2, a ThCr2Si2-type compound at a different stoichiometry and not a polymorph of UPdGe. UPdGe orders ferromagnetically near 30 K, inside the 13 to 299 K measured window, but that is magnetic rather than structural and the Pnma cell survives it.

basis: YbPtGe is an equiatomic RTX compound and [ref 2] gives YbGePt in Pnma (62) at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references, which is the TiNiSi type: a three-dimensional PtGe framework with ytterbium in the channels. The paper measures electrical and magnetic properties of YbPdGe and YbPtGe together, and the palladium analogue is the same type.

dopant_roles.site: rare-earth channel site of the TiNiSi framework
dopant_roles.basis: Lanthanum for ytterbium at 10% of the rare-earth site. La3+ has no 4f electrons and is larger than Yb, so it both dilutes the 4f lattice and expands the cell, which shifts the ytterbium valence; in an intermediate-valence Yb compound that is the usual reason to make such a substitution. Dilute and isovalent, so a substitutional dopant rather than an alloying end member.

note: [ref 2] lists four other Yb-Pt-Ge compounds for this host, Yb3Ge13Pt4, Yb2Ge6Pt, YbGe2Pt and Yb2(GePt3)3, none at the 1:1:1 composition, so only the Pnma entry is relevant. One caveat: some Yb-bearing equiatomic RTX compounds take the CeCu2 type in Imma rather than TiNiSi, and the two are closely related orthorhombic structures that a powder pattern can confuse. The reference favours Pnma and I have followed it.

basis: URuGe is the ruthenium end of the URu1-xPdxGe series the paper measures, and a continuous substitution series means both ends share a structure type; the palladium end, UPdGe in the Ge-Pd-U host at rank 2237, is TiNiSi-type Pnma with ICSD backing. The equiatomic UTGe compounds for the late transition metals take that type generally, so the assignment carries across.

dopant_roles.site: transition-metal site of the TiNiSi framework
dopant_roles.basis: The same substitution as in the sister host, seen from the other end: palladium for ruthenium at 10% of the transition-metal site, adding electrons and weakening the 4f-conduction hybridisation. It is the series variable of the paper.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal site of the TiNiSi framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Pd/(Pd+Ru) across the two compositions. The complementary end of the axis recorded on the Ge-Pd-U host; between them the two hosts hold the four samples of one substitution series, split by which element happens to be majority.

note: Confidence is medium rather than high because no reference covers this host at all: the space group is carried over from the palladium analogue and from the family, not measured here. That the same paper spans both hosts is the main support. The 5 at.% split has done something awkward to this series, cutting it in half at x = 0.5 and filing the two halves under different hosts; the Ge-Pd-U and Ge-Ru-U records belong together and stage 3 should treat them as one axis.

basis: Ge25Se65Sb10 is a chalcogenide glass, not a crystal. The Ge-Se-Sb system at 65 at.% selenium is a classical glass-forming region, the composition is written in atomic percent rather than as a formula unit, and no crystalline phase exists at that stoichiometry; the paper proposes Ge-Se-Sb-Cu as a new prospective thermoelectric, which is the bulk-glass line of work. There is no prototype to assign because there is no long-range order.

dopant_roles.basis: The composition pair replaces 2.5 at.% antimony with copper, which the paper title puts in the material name, so copper is a deliberate component of the glass rather than an impurity. In a chalcogenide glass it raises the conductivity by adding states near the mobility edge; site language does not apply since there is no lattice. Recorded as an alloying component rather than a substitutional dopant for that reason.

note: The measured window, 300 to 450 K, is presumably below the glass transition of this composition, which matters because a Ge-Se glass crystallises above it and the material would then no longer be the thing measured. Neither reference covers the host, which is expected for a glass. Stage 2 should skip this host, as the amorphous prototype notes direct.

basis: Ge1-xSnx is a substitutional alloy on the diamond lattice: germanium is diamond cubic and grey tin is too, so the alloy is one random cubic phase across the range with no ordering. The curator records GeSn layers deposited on SiO2/Si substrates and the paper measures carrier and heat transport in polycrystalline GeSn films, which is the group-IV alloy work aimed at direct-gap germanium, not a compound.

other_polymorphs.note: At a nominal 50 at.% tin the film is far beyond the equilibrium solubility of tin in germanium, which is about 1%, so it is metastable and tin tends to segregate as beta-Sn on annealing. That is a decomposition product rather than a polymorph of the alloy, and it is a real risk over a measurement reaching 746 K.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the single site of the diamond lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: Sn/(Sn+Ge) for the one composition here. Both are group 14 on one site, so this is a true isoelectronic alloy axis; at x = 0.5 it is an alloy rather than either end member doped, which is why the host key names both elements.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] on this host and the reason is instructive. Every entry it offers is a hypothetical ordered Ge-Sn compound at a high hull, SnGe P3m1 at 0.489, Sn3Ge I4/mmm at 0.147, SnGe3 at 0.294, and cubic Sn3Ge variants above those; none carries an ICSD reference and none is what the film is. Germanium and tin do not form ordered compounds, and those entries are the database enumerating orderings of a system that has none. The physically correct answer, a disordered diamond-cubic alloy, cannot appear in a database of ordered structures at all. The film flag in the chunk file is doing real work here: this composition is only reachable as a metastable epitaxial or polycrystalline film.

basis: Two different compounds share this host. Tl8GeTe5 belongs with the thallium tetrel tellurides Tl4SnTe3 and Tl4GeTe3, which are Tl5Te3-type: the Tl10Te6 framework in I4/mcm with the tetrel taking cation sites, and they are studied precisely for the very low thermal conductivity the paper title claims. Tl2GeTe3 is a separate compound, which [ref 2] puts in Pnma (62) with one ICSD reference, and I cannot name a prototype for it with any confidence, so it is recorded as unresolved rather than forced into a label.

other_polymorphs.note: Tl2GeTe3, the second composition of this host and not a polymorph of the first. [ref 2] gives it Pnma at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, so it is a real phase, but no taxonomy prototype covers it and I do not know the anion topology well enough to name one; assigning it a structure type from the formula would be a guess. This is the same treatment given to bornite elsewhere in the project. [ref 2] also lists Tl2GeTe5 in P4/mbm and Tl3GeTe3 in P-1 for this host, neither of which matches a composition here.

note: Confidence is low and the composition string is the reason, so this should be flagged for review rather than trusted. Tl8GeTe5 does not balance as written unless germanium is divalent, and it matches none of the known members of the family: the Tl5Te3 derivatives with a tetrel are Tl8M2Te6, written Tl4MTe3, and those with a trivalent or pentavalent substituent are Tl9MTe6. Tl8GeTe5 is one tellurium short of Tl8GeTe6 and one germanium short of Tl8Ge2Te6, so it is most likely a transcription of one of those two, and which one changes nothing about the prototype but does change the stoichiometry stage 3 would compute. The paper is the only thing that can settle it. I am recording the Tl5Te3 reading rather than matching the references because neither reference has an entry at this composition at all.

basis: The compositions are written as two bracketed parts, (Sb2Te3)19.3(CH3NH3I)3.5, which is an inorganic-organic hybrid film rather than a compound: tetradymite Sb2Te3 as the conducting phase with methylammonium iodide incorporated between the grains. The paper is on high-performance p-type inorganic-organic hybrid thermoelectric thin films, so the two-component structure is the design. Sb2Te3 itself is the R-3m tetradymite already in the seed taxonomy.

dopant_roles.basis: Iodine arrives as part of methylammonium iodide, which is added as a discrete second component rather than dissolved into the tetradymite lattice; in these hybrid films the organic salt sits at grain boundaries and scatters phonons while the Sb2Te3 carries the current. Some iodine could in principle dope the Sb2Te3 as an n-type donor on the tellurium site, which would fight the p-type behaviour the paper reports, so the second-phase reading is the consistent one.
The carbon of the methylammonium cation. A deliberate constituent of the organic component, not milling residue and not a dopant of the chalcogenide.
The nitrogen of the same methylammonium cation, with the same reading.

note: Hydrogen is in the host key rather than the candidate list because six hydrogens per methylammonium put it above the 5 at.% threshold, which makes the host name H-Sb-Te and hides the fact that this is a tellurium thermoelectric with an organic additive. is_mixed is set true because every sample really does contain two structures, the tetradymite and the molecular salt, and neither reference covers the host. The two compositions differ only in how much organic is present, 2.5 against 3.5 parts, so this host is a loading series.

basis: YbH1.85 and YbH1.88 are the saline ytterbium dihydride, slightly sub-stoichiometric. YbH2 takes the orthorhombic CaH2 structure, which is the cotunnite PbCl2 type in Pnma with nine-coordinate ytterbium and hydrogen ordered on two distinct anion sites; it is a semiconductor, not a metallic interstitial hydride. [ref 2] supports the setting indirectly, listing YbH2 in Pnma at hull 0.000. I proposed the prototype before using it, since the only hydride entry in the seed describes metallic interstitial solutions.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] marks cubic YbH2 in Fm-3m as PRIMARY on three ICSD references at hull 0.059, above the Pnma entry it puts at 0.000 with two. I have not followed it. Hydrogen scatters X-rays too weakly to locate, so a metal-only refinement of an orthorhombic dihydride can be indexed on a cubic metal sublattice, and the cubic fluorite form belongs to the hydrogen-rich YbH2+x region rather than to YbH1.85. Recorded here so the disagreement is visible; a neutron refinement in the paper is what would settle it.
