YbH3, a different composition rather than a polymorph. The rare-earth trihydrides are the metallic end of this chemistry, which is why the distinction between saline and interstitial hydride matters for this host.

dopant_roles.site: the two ordered anion sites of the cotunnite cell
dopant_roles.basis: Both samples sit below H/Yb of 2, at 1.85 and 1.88, which is a hydrogen deficiency on the anion sublattice and the carrier-concentration variable of the material rather than an impurity; each missing hydride leaves electrons behind. Hydrogen is in the host key and above the candidate threshold, so it is recorded here for that reason rather than as a dopant.

note: Confidence is medium because the reference and I disagree about the space group, as set out in other_polymorphs, and because the samples are sub-stoichiometric, which for hydrides can mean a genuinely different ordered phase rather than simply vacancies. The measured window is narrow, 298 to 419 K, over ten curves, and hydrogen loss on heating is a hazard for this material; the paper is an experimental study of YbH2 thermoelectric properties and would say whether the composition was checked after measurement.

basis: Rh3Hf is an L1_2 ordered cubic intermetallic, the Cu3Au type in Pm-3m: hafnium at the cube corners and rhodium on the face centres of an ordered fcc lattice. [ref 2] gives HfRh3 in Pm-3m (221) at hull 0.000 with three ICSD references, and one of the two papers is on thermal conductivity and thermal expansion of L1_2 intermetallic compounds, naming the structure outright. The other is on Rh3X for ultra-high-temperature use, the same family.
note: The other [ref 2] entries for this host, Hf2Rh in Fd-3m, Hf3Rh5 in Pbam and HfRh in Pm-3m, are separate compounds along the Hf-Rh line rather than polymorphs of the 1:3 phase. Note that HfRh is also listed in Pm-3m, which is the B2 CsCl structure at a different stoichiometry; the shared space group symbol is a coincidence of the cubic aristotypes and not a reason to confuse them. This is a refractory structural intermetallic rather than a thermoelectric, measured to 1096 K.

basis: Zr0.5Hf0.5RhSb is a half-Heusler: Zr and Hf share the 4a site, rhodium takes one tetrahedral site and the other is empty, giving 4 plus 9 plus 5 equal to 18 valence electrons, the closed-shell count that makes these compounds semiconducting. Sn on the antimony site is the p-type acceptor and Co partly replaces Rh in one sample. The paper is on the effects of Rh on the thermoelectric performance of the p-type Zr0.5Hf0.5 half-Heusler, which is the ZrCoSb and ZrNiSn family this belongs to.

dopant_roles.site: anion 4a site of the half-Heusler cell
dopant_roles.basis: Tin for antimony at 1% of that site removes one electron per substitution and is the p-type acceptor of both samples; it is the standard way to hole-dope an 18-electron half-Heusler without touching the transition-metal site.

dopant_roles.site: tetrahedral transition-metal site
dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt sits directly above rhodium in the periodic table, so replacing 10% of it is isoelectronic: it changes the band masses and the lattice thermal conductivity through mass disorder rather than the carrier count. The paper is about exactly this substitution, approached from the ZrCoSb side.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: 4a site of the half-Heusler cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Hf/(Hf+Zr) is fixed at 0.5 in both compositions. Zirconium and hafnium are same-group and nearly the same size, so this is pure mass disorder: it is held at 50:50 deliberately because that is where alloy phonon scattering is strongest.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] here. Its only entry for the host is HfZr(SbRh)2 in R3m at hull 0.638, which is far too high above the hull to be a real phase and carries no ICSD references; it is a computed rhombohedral ordering, not evidence about this material, and the cubic half-Heusler that these samples certainly are does not appear for the quaternary. Stage 2 should resolve against ZrRhSb and HfRhSb rather than the quaternary entry. Minor transcription note: the second composition string begins with a tab character before the formula.

basis: HoN is a rocksalt rare-earth mononitride, and [ref 2] gives it in Fm-3m (225) at hull 0.000 with nine ICSD references, the clearest evidence in the host. The paper measures specific heat and thermal conductivity of HoN and ErN at cryogenic temperatures, and the rare-earth nitrides are rocksalt throughout the series.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists a second HoN in Pm-3m at hull 0.937 with one ICSD reference. Nearly a full electronvolt above the hull is not a phase anything makes at ambient pressure; the B2 form of a rocksalt nitride is a high-pressure or purely computational structure and the single reference is likely a mis-indexed entry. Not a thermal phase.

note: Ho2N3 in Ia-3, also listed by [ref 2], is a different composition rather than a polymorph. The measured window is 10 to 91 K, cryogenic, and HoN orders ferromagnetically near 18 K inside it; that is magnetic and does not change the cubic cell, so spans_transition stays false. This host and Gd-N at rank 2224 are both rare-earth nitrides but from unrelated papers, one a cryogenic study and one nuclear fuel work.

basis: Sn24P19.3I8 is a type-I cationic clathrate: a tin-phosphorus framework of dodecahedral and tetrakaidecahedral cages with iodide guests, and the 19.3 against 20 phosphorus is an ordered framework vacancy rather than an impurity. The paper reports the crystal structure along with thermoelectric and magnetic properties and names the type-I structure in its title, so this is read from the source rather than inferred. As in Ge38Sb8I8, the framework is cationic and the guest is an anion.

dopant_roles.site: guest cage sites of the type-I clathrate
dopant_roles.basis: The second composition replaces two of the eight iodides with bromide. Both are halides of the same charge, so this is isoelectronic substitution on the guest sublattice: it shrinks the guest and changes how loosely it rattles in the cage, which is the phonon-scattering knob, without changing the framework electron count.

dopant_roles.site: framework sites of the cage network
dopant_roles.basis: The framework is phosphorus-deficient at 19.3 of 20 sites. In these tin phosphide iodide clathrates the vacancy concentration is what balances the charge against the halide guests, so it is a structural feature of the compound rather than a defect; phosphorus is above the candidate threshold and is recorded here for that reason.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: guest cage sites of the type-I clathrate
solid_solution_axis.note: Br/(Br+I) across the two compositions. Same-group halides on one site, so a genuine isoelectronic axis, and it is the guest rather than the framework that is being alloyed, which is unusual and is the point of the experiment.

note: Phase confidence is medium only because of the space group: the recorded P-43n is the ordered-vacancy subgroup that these tin phosphide halide clathrates are reported in, rather than the Pm-3n aristotype, and no reference covers this host to check it against. The prototype itself is not in doubt. The measured window is 24 to 286 K, low-temperature transport.

basis: VI3 is a layered van der Waals trihalide: honeycomb sheets of edge-sharing VI6 octahedra stacked with iodine in contact, the BiI3 or CrCl3 arrangement. The paper studies spin-phonon scattering in a van der Waals magnet, which is what VI3 is, and no other structure is available at MX3 for a first-row transition metal with iodine.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists VI3 in P6_3/mmc at hull 0.000 with no ICSD references. That is the fully disordered hexagonal aristotype of the BiI3 family, with the metal smeared over the octahedral sites rather than ordered into the honeycomb; it is what a calculation returns for the ideal stacking, not a phase of VI3. [ref 2] also lists VI2 in P-3m1 and VI in P6_3mc, which are different compositions.

note: This host does cross a structural transition and the chunk file did not flag it, because the taxonomy entry carries a different one. The bii3_layered_trihalide entry gives C2/m at room temperature going to R-3 below about 150 K, which is the RuCl3 and BiI3 behaviour; VI3 does not follow it. VI3 is rhombohedral R-3 at room temperature and undergoes a structural distortion to a lower-symmetry monoclinic or triclinic stacking near 79 K, which sits squarely inside the 10 to 91 K measured window here. I have recorded the low-temperature phase with a null space group because the reported symmetry of that phase is not settled, P-1 and C2/c both appearing in the literature. The transition temperature is from general knowledge of VI3 and not from the paper, so transition_basis is llm_materials_knowledge and it should be confirmed. VI3 also orders ferromagnetically near 50 K, which is what the spin-phonon scattering in the title refers to; that is a separate magnetic transition inside the same window.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [148], ICSD-backed references for this host report [164]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: LaPdIn is an equiatomic RTIn compound in the ZrNiAl type, an ordered Fe2P derivative in P-62m built from trigonal prisms, which is what the RTIn family takes almost without exception; [ref 2] gives LaInPd in P-62m (189), the right setting, and the paper on Kondo compounds CeTIn is about the cerium analogues of the same series. La6Pd12In5 is a different compound and I cannot name its structure type, so it is recorded as unresolved rather than assigned from the formula.

other_polymorphs.note: La6Pd12In5, the second composition of this host and a separate compound rather than a polymorph. Its cation ratio reduces to LaPd2In0.83, which is close enough to LaPd2In to raise the possibility of a vacancy-ordered full Heusler, but that is a guess from arithmetic and I am not asserting it; the R6T12X5 stoichiometry is distinctive enough that the compound has a structure type of its own in the literature. Neither reference has an entry at this composition. A composition-level assignment in stage 2, after the paper is read, is the right fix.

note: Confidence is medium for two reasons. The host stands over two compounds at one sample each, and the [ref 2] entry supporting the ZrNiAl assignment sits at hull 0.227 with no ICSD references, which is weak: it is the only 1:1:1 entry offered, but an unreferenced entry that far above the hull is not strong evidence. The family behaviour of RTIn compounds is what carries the assignment, not the reference. [ref 2] also lists La2InPd2 in P4/mbm with three ICSD references, which is the Mo2FeB2-type 2:1:2 compound, and LaIn2Pd, LaInPd2 and La4In21Pd10; none of them matches either composition here.

basis: LaPtIn is an equiatomic RTIn compound, and that family takes the ZrNiAl type almost without exception: an ordered Fe2P derivative in P-62m built from trigonal prisms. [ref 2] gives LaInPt in P-62m (189) at hull 0.000, the right setting. The second composition La3Pt4In13 is a different compound at the R3T4X13 stoichiometry, which is the Remeika phase, so the host holds two prototypes and is split.

other_polymorphs.note: La3Pt4In13, the second composition and a separate compound rather than a polymorph. R3T4X13 is the Remeika stoichiometry and the second paper here is on the indium-rich heavy-fermion antiferromagnet, which is the cerium analogue Ce3Pt4In13 of the same series. Neither reference has an entry at this composition, so the Pm-3n cell is from the family rather than from evidence and the space group number should be treated as a family default, not a measurement.

note: Confidence is medium because the host carries one sample of each compound and the supporting [ref 2] entry has a single ICSD reference. The other [ref 2] entry, LaInPt4 in F-43m, is at the 1:1:4 stoichiometry and matches neither composition. This host sits directly alongside In-La-Pd at rank 2250 in the previous chunk, which is the palladium analogue and took the same ZrNiAl assignment; the two should be reviewed together.

basis: LuIn3 is a rare-earth triindide and the REIn3 series is cubic AuCu3 (L1_2) throughout: indium on the face centres, the rare earth at the corner. [ref 2] gives LuIn3 in Pm-3m (221) at hull 0.000 with three ICSD references, which is that structure, and the paper measures the thermoelectric power of REIn3 single crystals across the series.
note: The remaining [ref 2] entries, Lu2In, Lu5In3, Lu3In5 and Lu3In, are other compounds of the binary system rather than polymorphs of LuIn3, and none of them is at the measured composition. Lu is the closed-shell end of the series so there is no magnetic ordering in the 12 to 292 K window; the interest in these crystals is the f-electron contribution to the thermopower across the series, and lutetium is the reference point.

basis: Ni3InSb is an AB3 ordered close packing in which indium and antimony share the minority sublattice; [ref 2] gives InNi3Sb in P-6m2 (187), which is the In/Sb-ordered subgroup of the hexagonal Ni3Sn D0_19 cell in P6_3/mmc. The second composition is a different material entirely, an InSb matrix with ten percent NiSb, which is the classic two-phase InSb-NiSb eutectic, so the host is split.

other_polymorphs.note: The zincblende InSb matrix of the second composition, (InSb)90(NiSb)10. A separate composition, not a polymorph of Ni3InSb.

The NiSb needles dispersed in that matrix. NiSb is the B8_1 arsenide type. The InSb-NiSb eutectic is a directionally solidified composite of these two phases and is one of the oldest engineered thermoelectric microstructures.

note: Confidence is low and I want to say why rather than dress it up. I could not confirm the structure type of Ni3InSb from knowledge; the assignment is read off the [ref 2] space group, and that entry sits 60 meV above the hull with no ICSD reference, which makes it a computed ordering rather than an observation. P-6m2 is consistent with an In/Sb-ordered D0_19 derivative, which is why that prototype was chosen, but a reader should treat this as a hypothesis and settle it from the paper, which reports Ni3GaSb alongside Ni3InSb. The second composition needs no such care: it is a deliberate two-phase composite and cannot be given one prototype at all.

basis: UNi2In is a 1:2:1 ternary indide and [ref 2] gives UInNi2 in Fm-3m (225) with an ICSD reference, which is the MnCu2Al full Heusler arrangement that the RT2In family takes. The second composition UNi4In is at the 1:4:1 stoichiometry, which is the MgCu4Sn ordering of AuBe5 in F-43m, so the host holds two prototypes and is split.

other_polymorphs.note: UNi4In, the second composition and a separate compound. [ref 2] gives UInNi4 in F-43m (216) at hull 0.014 with three ICSD references, the best-attested entry in this host; that is the MgCu4Sn ternary ordering of the AuBe5 C15b cell, which the aube5 entry covers at its ABC4 archetype. This is the stronger of the two assignments in the host even though it is the alternative.

note: The Heusler assignment for UNi2In is the weaker half. Its [ref 2] entry sits 108 meV above the hull on one ICSD reference, and [ref 2] also lists U2InNi2 in P4/mbm with two references, which is the Mo2FeB2 type at the 2:1:2 stoichiometry and a different composition. Uranium ternaries are structurally varied and the single paper here reports several of them together, so the two compositions should be checked against it in stage 2. Both samples are polycrystalline and the window is cryogenic, 13 to 297 K, which is where the heavy-fermion behaviour these compounds are measured for appears.

basis: The matrix is In2O3, which is the cubic bixbyite C-type sesquioxide in Ia-3, and the paper is explicitly on In2O3 with palladium as a nanocomposite. Palladium is not in the oxide lattice: at Pd2In2O3 there are two palladium atoms per formula unit of oxide, far beyond any solubility, so the samples are indium oxide with metallic palladium dispersed through it.

dopant_roles.basis: Palladium is a deliberate second phase, not a dopant. The paper calls the samples In2O3:Pd nanocomposite films, and at the 2:1 ratio of the second composition the metal is a major constituent by volume. It raises the power factor by adding a parallel metallic conduction path and by energy filtering at the interfaces, which is a microstructural effect rather than a substitutional one. It is recorded here although it sits above the 5 at.% candidate threshold, because leaving it out would make the record read as pure In2O3.

note: Neither reference covers this host, so the bixbyite space group is from knowledge of In2O3 rather than from a database entry, and no mp_id is recorded. The measured window is 400 to 1293 K; bixbyite In2O3 has no structural transition in it, the rhombohedral corundum-type form being a high-pressure phase. The samples are films, so is_mixed is left false deliberately: each composition is one composite material with one crystalline matrix, not two compositions resolving to two prototypes.

basis: Both compositions are In2-2xZnxSnxO3 with x equal to 0.4 and 0.3: the cation total is exactly 2 per O3 and the zinc to tin ratio is exactly 1:1, so a divalent and a tetravalent cation enter together and the average charge stays at 3 plus. That is the coupled substitution the paper names in its title, and it keeps the cubic bixbyite In2O3 lattice rather than forming a new phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Zinc takes the indium site as Zn2+. On its own it would be an acceptor; paired one-for-one with tin it is charge-compensated instead, which is the point of the coupled substitution. Recorded although zinc is above the candidate threshold, because the pair is the doping variable of this host.

Tin takes the indium site as Sn4+, the donor half of the pair. Equal amounts of Zn2+ and Sn4+ leave the carrier count nominally unchanged while adding two strong mass and charge scattering centres per pair, which is how the lattice thermal conductivity is cut without destroying the mobility.

note: Neither reference covers this host. The competing reading is the homologous In2O3(ZnO)k series, which the same chemistry produces when zinc is added alone; it is excluded here by the exact 1:1 zinc to tin ratio and by the cation sum staying at 2 per O3, both of which are bixbyite bookkeeping rather than homologue bookkeeping. Zn2SnO4 spinel is the other phase this system throws off at higher substitution and would show up as a second phase rather than a different assignment.

basis: SrIn2P2 is a 1-2-2 Zintl phosphide, and [ref 1] gives Sr(InP)2 in P6_3/mmc (194) at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference. That is not the trigonal CaAl2Si2 arrangement the seed taxonomy offers for AM2Pn2 compounds; it is the hexagonal EuIn2P2 type, which stacks two [In2P2] slabs per cell instead of one. The prototype is proposed rather than forced into caal2si2_zintl for that reason.
note: Confidence is medium because the assignment rests on a single ICSD reference and because I am asserting a structure type, EuIn2P2, that I know from the europium and arsenide members rather than from anything in front of me; the space group is the part that is evidenced. The other [ref 1] entries, Sr3(InP2)2 in Pnnm and Sr3InP3 in Pnma, are different Zintl compositions of the same three elements and not polymorphs of SrIn2P2. The paper is on temperature and doping effects in SrIn2P2 and would settle both the setting and whether any dopant is on the strontium or the indium site.

basis: Both compositions are written Pb1Te1 with indium added on top, at 0.14 and 0.18 per formula unit, and the paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties of Two-Phase PbTe with Indium Inclusions. The matrix is therefore rocksalt PbTe and the indium is largely a second phase rather than a solute.

dopant_roles.basis: The paper calls these two-phase samples with indium inclusions, and 0.14 to 0.18 indium per PbTe is an order of magnitude beyond the solubility limit, so most of it is a separate phase. A small fraction does dissolve on the lead site, where indium is the well-known resonant-level impurity that pins the Fermi level in PbTe, and that dissolved part is what changes the electronic transport; the inclusions scatter phonons. Both mechanisms are in play at once, which is why the record names the site as well as the role.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] here. Its three entries, In6Te10Pb in C2 and two InTe5Pb4 settings, are ternary line compounds of the In-Pb-Te system; none of them is PbTe, and none of them is what these samples are. That is the reference describing which phases exist in a chemistry rather than which phase the paper made, and the rocksalt assignment stands against it. No mp_id is recorded because neither reference offers one for PbTe in this host, and inventing one is not allowed.

basis: The first composition In1.0Sn0.2Se comes from a paper on In1.3-xSnxSe, which is the tin-substituted In4Se3 line: the cation to selenium ratio of about 1.2 is the In4Se3 stoichiometry, not a monoselenide. The second, Sn0.9In0.1Se, is indium-substituted SnSe from a separate paper and is the orthorhombic GeS-type layered structure. Two unrelated parents, so the host is split.

other_polymorphs.note: Sn0.9In0.1Se, the second composition and a separate parent compound rather than a polymorph. This half of the host does cross a transition that the host record cannot carry: SnSe converts from Pnma to Cmcm at about 800 K and the measured window reaches 823 K. The chunk file printed no transition line because the host prototype is the In4Se3 one, which has no transition there. Stage 2 should attach the two-phase SnSe sequence to this composition.

note: Indium and tin are not isoelectronic and do not form a single substitution axis across this host: in In4Se3 tin substitutes for indium as an acceptor, while in SnSe indium substitutes for tin. The two compositions approach the same element pair from opposite ends, which is exactly why the host must be split rather than treated as a solid solution. [ref 2] offers In4SnSe4 in Pa-3 and InSn3Se4 in Pm; neither matches either composition and neither is used. No mp_ids are recorded for that reason.

basis: ZnIn18SiSn20 is an indium-tin alloy at about 47 at.% indium with one atom each of zinc and silicon per forty, and the paper is on the effect of cooling conditions on microstructure. Near equiatomic composition the In-Sn system is a two-phase mixture of terminal solid solutions rather than a line compound, so the honest label is a substitutional alloy.

dopant_roles.basis: Zinc at about 2.5 at.% is a deliberate addition rather than a dopant in the semiconductor sense; it has very low solid solubility in both indium and tin and in indium-tin solders it refines the microstructure by precipitating at grain boundaries, which is consistent with a paper about cooling conditions.

Silicon is essentially insoluble in both indium and tin, so at 2.5 at.% it cannot be in the alloy lattice and must be a dispersed particle or a crucible or substrate contribution. Recorded as a second phase rather than guessed at.

note: Something is wrong in this host and I would rather flag it than assign around it. The indium-tin eutectic melts at about 393 K, yet transport is reported from 300 to 724 K over ten curves, several hundred kelvin above the liquidus; either the composition string or the temperature axis does not describe what was measured. Confidence is low for that reason and not because the In-Sn phase field is obscure. [ref 2] lists five In-Sn orderings, In3Sn, InSn3 and InSn4 in various settings, all between 30 and 50 meV above the hull and none with an ICSD reference; those are computed orderings of a disordered alloy and are not evidence, which is why no mp_id is recorded. The paper is needed before anything firmer can be said.

basis: TlInTe2 is the TlSe structure type: chains of edge-sharing InTe4 tetrahedra running along the tetragonal axis with thallium in eightfold sites between them, formally Tl+ In3+ Te2 2-. [ref 2] gives TlInTe2 in I4/mcm (140) at hull 0.000 with seven ICSD references, the strongest evidence in this host, and the paper is a systematic study of the TlMTe2 series.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral trivalent site of the chain
dopant_roles.basis: Gallium sits directly above indium in group 13 and takes the same trivalent tetrahedral site in TlIn0.9Ga0.1Te2, so it adds no carriers. It is smaller, which contracts the chain and increases the mass and force-constant contrast, and that is the lattice thermal conductivity knob; the thallium sublattice and its rattling modes, which give this family its very low kappa, are untouched.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the trivalent tetrahedral site of the TlSe-type chain
solid_solution_axis.note: Ga/(Ga+In) across the two compositions, 0 and 0.1. Dilute on its own sublattice, so this is the doped end of the TlInTe2 to TlGaTe2 line rather than an alloy midpoint; both end members are the same prototype in any case.

note: One sample is a single crystal and one is bulk, and the two papers approach the same compound from different directions, a thermoelectric series study and an X-ray plus electrical study of TlIn1-xGaxTe2. TlInTe2 is one of the lowest-thermal-conductivity crystalline thallium chalcogenides, which is why it appears here at all despite only two samples.

basis: Both compositions are AVO3 metavanadates with potassium and lithium sharing the alkali site, and the paper is on the thermoelectric power of ferroelectric potassium vanadate. KVO3 and LiVO3 are both built from infinite chains of corner-sharing VO4 tetrahedra with the alkali cations between them, which is what the metavanadate chain entry describes.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the alkali site between the vanadate chains
solid_solution_axis.note: Li/(Li+K) spans 0.4 to 0.6 across the two compositions, so this is a genuine alloy midpoint and not doping. Both are group 1 and both are charge-balancing cations outside the chain, so the axis is real, but the size difference between lithium and potassium is very large and a 40:60 mixture may well order or phase-separate rather than form one disordered site. That is the main reason the space group is left null.

note: Confidence is medium and the space group is deliberately not asserted. Neither reference covers this host, and the alkali sites of KVO3 and LiVO3 have quite different coordination, so the mixed compound is not simply either end member. The measured window, 574 to 638 K, is narrow and sits well above room temperature, which fits a study of the ferroelectric and conductivity behaviour of these vanadates rather than a thermoelectric optimisation. The paper also covers caesium vanadate, so the series is the subject rather than this composition in particular.

basis: KTa1-xNbxO3 at x equal to 0.37 and 0.33 is the KTN solid solution, a simple ABO3 perovskite with niobium and tantalum sharing the octahedral B site, and the paper title names the crystals as cubic. Potassium fills the twelve-coordinate A site in both end members.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Niobium and tantalum are both pentavalent group 5 cations of almost identical radius, so replacing one with the other adds no carriers. What it does is move the ferroelectric transition: KTaO3 is a quantum paraelectric that never orders, KNbO3 orders at 691 K, and the composition sets where between them the crystal sits. Recorded although niobium is above the candidate threshold, because it is the whole variable of the experiment.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the octahedral B site of the perovskite
solid_solution_axis.note: Nb/(Nb+Ta) is 0.33 to 0.37, a narrow band near the composition where the ferroelectric transition of KTN falls below room temperature.

note: spans_transition is false on purpose. KTN is ferroelectric and does pass through cubic to tetragonal on cooling, but at x near 0.35 that transition is well below 200 K while the measurement starts at 298 K, and the paper describes the crystals as cubic. I disagree with [ref 2] on this host: its entries K2TaNbO6 in Fm-3m and P4/mmm are 1:1 B-site-ordered double perovskites and K4Ta3NbO12 in R-3m is a 3:1 ordering. Niobium and tantalum are chemically almost indistinguishable and do not order on the B site; these are computed superstructures used to represent a random alloy, and at x equal to 0.35 none of them is even at the right ratio. No mp_id is recorded for that reason.

basis: KRu4O8 is the hollandite stoichiometry: double chains of edge-sharing RuO6 octahedra sharing corners to enclose square tunnels, with potassium inside the tunnels. [ref 2] gives K(RuO2)4 in I4/m (87) at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references, which is the hollandite space group, and the paper on quasi-one-dimensional transport is exactly what the tunnel structure produces.
note: The other [ref 2] entries are different compositions rather than polymorphs: K2RuO4, K2RuO5 and KRuO4 are discrete oxoruthenate salts, and KRuO2 in I4_1/amd sits 367 meV above the hull. None of them is a tunnel oxide. The measured window is wide, 26 to 778 K, and the interest in this compound is the one-dimensional metallic conduction along the tunnel axis; potassium hollandites in general can show tunnel-cation ordering at low temperature but nothing here reports it for the ruthenate, so no transition is recorded.

basis: Both compositions are members of the A1+xM4-2xM7+xSe15 series that the paper itself defines, with A equal to K, M equal to Pb and the pnictogen equal to Sb. These are module-built selenides: NaCl-type blocks of different thickness stitched together into a large low-symmetry cell, with the alkali and the lead distributed over the same sites. [ref 2] gives K2Sb9PbSe15 in P2_1/m (11), the space group the taxonomy entry names for this family.
note: A scope objection to the taxonomy rather than to the reference. The bi_chalcogenide_complex entry is named and described for bismuth, K2Bi8Se13 and relatives, and these compounds are the antimony members of the same modular series; the paper treats Bi and Sb as one family, and the structural principle, the space group and the note that every composition is effectively its own structure all transfer unchanged. I have used the entry rather than propose a near-duplicate, but its display name and description should be widened to alkali pnictide chalcogenides in v4 so the antimony members are not filed under a bismuth heading. Confidence is medium because x differs between the two samples, so they are not the same compound, and because the modular series produces distinct structures at distinct x.

basis: KV3Sb5 is one of the three compounds the cited paper introduced, and the paper calls them new kagome prototype materials in its title. The structure is a vanadium kagome net with antimony filling the hexagonal centres and forming honeycomb layers above and below, potassium between the slabs, in P6/mmm. Nothing in the seed taxonomy covered a kagome metal, so the prototype is proposed.
note: This host crosses a structural transition that the chunk file could not flag, because the prototype is new. KV3Sb5 forms a charge-density-wave superstructure near 78 K, a 2x2 in-plane reconstruction of the kagome net, and the measured window runs from 12 to 294 K, so roughly the lower quarter of it is in the reconstructed phase. The low-temperature space group is left null: the three-dimensional stacking of the distorted state was contested for several years and the choice between the star-of-David and tri-hexagonal patterns is not settled by anything available here. The transition temperature is from general knowledge of the family and, importantly, was reported after the 2019 discovery paper this host comes from, so it cannot be paper evidence and the basis says so. Neither reference covers the host, so no mp_id is recorded.

basis: Sr2MnMoO6 is a rock-salt-ordered double perovskite: manganese and molybdenum alternate on the octahedral B site, which they do here because their charges and radii differ strongly. The paper is on lanthanum doping of Sr2MnMoO6, and both compositions keep the 1:1 Mn to Mo ratio while lanthanum replaces strontium on the A site. [ref 2] gives SrLaMnMoO6 in Pc (7), a monoclinically distorted double perovskite cell.

dopant_roles.site: the twelve-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: Trivalent lanthanum for divalent strontium donates one electron per substitution, which is the electron-doping knob of this material and the subject of the paper. It is recorded although it is above the candidate threshold, because at 0.5 and 1.0 per formula unit it is the experimental variable rather than a host constituent that happens to be there.

note: Phase confidence is medium against high overall confidence, and the reason is the space group rather than the prototype. The [ref 2] entry sits in Pc (7) with no ICSD reference, which is a very low symmetry for this family; Sr2MnMoO6 is usually reported tetragonal I4/m or monoclinic P2_1/n depending on temperature and on how complete the B-site ordering is. The rock-salt ordering itself is not in doubt. The measured window runs to 1042 K and these double perovskites do untilt toward higher symmetry on heating, but that is a tilt transition within one prototype and nothing here fixes its temperature, so it is not recorded as a phase change.

basis: Both compositions are perovskites. The first is a LaNiO3 on La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 superlattice, written as twenty repeats of two and three unit-cell layers, so it is two perovskites stacked artificially rather than a compound. The second, LaNi0.25Mn0.75O3, is a single ABO3 phase with nickel and manganese sharing the octahedral site at a 1:3 ratio that cannot rock-salt order.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] leads with La2MnNiO6 in Fm-3m at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, the 1:1 B-site-ordered double perovskite. That is a real and well-studied compound, but it is not either composition here: the superlattice keeps nickel and manganese in separate layers, and LaNi0.25Mn0.75O3 is at 1:3, where rock-salt ordering is geometrically impossible. Listed so the entry is not mistaken for a polymorph of what was measured.

dopant_roles.site: the twelve-coordinate A site of the manganite layers
dopant_roles.basis: Strontium for lanthanum in the La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 half of the superlattice is the standard hole doping that puts that compound at its ferromagnetic metallic optimum. It reads as a minor element only because it is diluted by the nickelate layers of the same formula string; within its own layer it occupies 30 percent of the A site.

note: The measured range is quoted as 10 to 298 K for the robust percentile but the full span reaches 1123 K, which means the two samples were measured in completely different regimes: the superlattice is a low-temperature superconductivity and magnetism study, the bulk nickel manganite is a cathode-materials paper taken to high temperature. The host label groups two unrelated experiments that happen to share four elements. Both are perovskites, so the assignment holds either way, but nothing else about the host should be read as common to both.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62, 167, 221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [225]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: La0.7Pb0.3Mn0.3 is a parse artefact: the paper is on the thermal conductivity of colossal magnetoresistive manganites, and the material is La0.7Pb0.3MnO3, a lead-substituted lanthanum manganite perovskite whose oxygen has been dropped from the composition string and whose manganese has been mis-scaled. Divalent lead on the A site plays the same role as strontium or calcium in the standard La1-xAxMnO3 series.

dopant_roles.site: the twelve-coordinate A site
dopant_roles.basis: Divalent lead for trivalent lanthanum at x equal to 0.3 creates the Mn3+ to Mn4+ mixed valence that drives double exchange, which is what makes the compound a ferromagnetic metal and gives it colossal magnetoresistance. Lead flux is also the usual way these crystals are grown, which is why lead rather than strontium is the substituent here.

note: Two disagreements to record. I disagree with [ref 2]: its only entry is La5MnPb3 in P6_3/mcm at hull 0.127, an intermetallic stannide-type phase with no oxygen, which is what you get when a database is queried on a composition string that has lost its oxygen. It is not this material. And I disagree with the composition string itself, for the reason given in the basis; the samples are single crystals of an oxide, not of a La-Pb-Mn alloy. The space group is given as R-3c with medium confidence because La0.7Pb0.3MnO3 is rhombohedral at that doping, but the string cannot be trusted to fix the doping level. The 10 to 399 K window does cross the ferromagnetic Curie temperature near 350 K, which is magnetic rather than structural, so spans_transition stays false.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [167], ICSD-backed references for this host report [193]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: LaWOxN3-x is an oxynitride perovskite and the paper says so in its title, on the electrical properties of the perovskites LnWOxN3-x. Lanthanum takes the A site, tungsten the octahedral B site, and oxygen and nitrogen share the anion sublattice at roughly 0.6 to 2.4 and 0.7 to 2.3 in the two samples.

dopant_roles.site: the shared anion site of the perovskite
dopant_roles.basis: Oxygen and nitrogen occupy the same anion sublattice here and x is the variable of the series: each oxygen for nitrogen exchange removes one negative charge, so it is the tungsten valence and hence the carrier count that x controls. This is the same kind of anion doping as F for O in the 1111 pnictides, not a processing residue, which is the usual reading of oxygen in a chunk file.

note: Neither reference covers this host, so no space group or mp_id is recorded; oxynitride perovskites are commonly orthorhombic Pnma with the anions either disordered or cis-ordered on the octahedron, and which of those applies here is not decidable from the composition. The measured window, 114 to 462 K, is modest and the paper is a 1988 electrical-properties study of the lanthanide series rather than a thermoelectric optimisation.

basis: The two compositions are the same compound written two ways: LaNb3O9 is La1/3NbO3, and the curator transcription from the paper confirms La1/3NbO3. That is the A-site-deficient perovskite in which only a third of the twelve-coordinate sites carry lanthanum and two thirds are vacant, the niobate framework being unchanged. The second paper is titled Prospects for Engineering Thermoelectric Properties in La1/3NbO3 Ceramics.

dopant_roles.site: the vacant A sites of the deficient perovskite
dopant_roles.basis: The first paper is titled Metallization of La1/3NbO3 by lithium incorporation. Two thirds of the A sites in this compound are empty, so lithium does not displace anything: it is inserted into those vacancies, and the electron that comes with it reduces niobium and turns an insulator into a metal. That is intercalation into a structural void, which is what the interstitial role means, not substitution.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] on this host. Its primary is LaNbO4 in I4_1/a with seventeen ICSD references, by far the best-attested entry, but LaNbO4 is the fergusonite scheelite-type niobate at a completely different La to Nb ratio and is not what either composition here is. The same applies to La3NbO7, LaNb7O19, LaNb2O7 and LaNb7O12: the block describes the La-Nb-O phase field, and the 1:3 deficient perovskite that both samples are does not appear in it at all. No mp_id is recorded. The space group is left null because the A-site vacancies in La1/3NbO3 order into alternate layers, giving a doubled orthorhombic cell whose exact setting depends on synthesis and on lithium content.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62, 167, 221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [88, 14, 57, 63]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Nd0.75La0.25 and Nd0.63La0.37 are binary rare-earth metal alloys from a paper on the thermoelectric power of Nd1-xLax and Ce1-xLax. Lanthanum and neodymium both crystallise double hexagonal close packed at ambient conditions, with the fourfold ABAC stacking that the light rare earths share, and they are completely miscible, so the alloy keeps that structure at every composition. The taxonomy had no dhcp entry, so the prototype is proposed.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the single metal site of the dhcp lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: La/(La+Nd) across the two compositions. Both are light rare earths of the same valence and nearly the same size on one lattice, so this is a genuine random substitutional series with no ordering; the point of the experiment is the f-electron contribution to the thermopower as lanthanum, which has no f electrons, is diluted into neodymium, which has three.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. It offers La3Nd in I4/mmm and three LaNd3 settings in Pm-3m, I4/mmm and P6_3/mmc, all between 17 and 37 meV above the hull and none with a single ICSD reference. Those are computed ordering trials on what is a random solid solution; there is no ordered La-Nd compound, and the near-degeneracy of the four settings is itself the sign that the calculation is resolving nothing. The dhcp assignment comes from the elements. The measured range is only 10 to 12 K from one curve, so this host contributes almost nothing beyond a cryogenic thermopower point, and the P6_3/mmc cell is stable throughout.

basis: LaRh0.7Ni0.3O3 is LaRhO3 with nickel on the octahedral site, and both papers say so: one is titled Thermoelectric properties of LaRh1-xNixO3 and the other B-Site Substituted LaRhO3. LaRhO3 is an orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted ABO3 perovskite, and at a 7:3 B-site ratio no rock-salt ordering is possible.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Nickel replaces rhodium at 30 percent of the B site. Rh3+ is low-spin d6 and closed-shell, which is why LaRhO3 is a semiconductor with a large Seebeck coefficient; Ni3+ is d7 and carries a hole into that band, so the substitution is the carrier-doping knob and it is what both papers vary. Recorded although nickel is just above the candidate threshold, because it is the experimental variable.

note: I disagree with [ref 2], although mildly. Its single entry is La2NiRhO6 in P2_1/c at hull 0.000 with no ICSD reference, which is the 1:1 B-site-ordered double perovskite. That composition is not what was made here: at Rh0.7Ni0.3 the B site cannot rock-salt order, and both papers treat the series as a disordered solid solution. No mp_id is recorded. The space group is given as Pnma with medium confidence from the GdFeO3 tilting of LaRhO3 rather than from evidence. Spin-state changes on the rhodium and nickel sites are the physics of these papers and can occur inside the 11 to 793 K window, but they are electronic rather than a change of prototype.

basis: Both compositions are LaNi1-xTixO3 with x equal to 0.3 and 0.5, and the paper is titled Electrical Transport Properties of LaNi1-xTixO3 Ceramics. This is a single ABO3 perovskite with nickel and titanium sharing the octahedral site; LaNiO3 is rhombohedral and LaTiO3 orthorhombic, and the solid solution between them is a tilted simple perovskite.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists La2TiNiO6 in Fm-3m at hull 0.103 with one ICSD reference and again in P2_1/c at hull 0.012. Rock-salt ordering of Ni2+ and Ti4+ is plausible at exactly x equal to 0.5 on charge and size grounds, so the x equal to 0.5 sample here could genuinely be a double perovskite. I have not asserted it: the x equal to 0.3 sample cannot order at all, nothing in the chunk file reports a superstructure reflection, and asserting an ordering from a charge argument is exactly the kind of inference this project keeps separate from evidence. Reading the paper would settle it, and if it orders this host becomes a composition-level split.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Ti4+ for Ni3+ is not isovalent: it forces nickel toward Ni2+ and empties the conducting e-g band of LaNiO3, driving the metal-to-insulator crossover that the paper measures. Recorded although titanium is a host element by the threshold, because it is the variable.

note: Confidence is medium for the ordering question set out under other_polymorphs, not because the perovskite family is in doubt. The curator composition detail attached to both samples is a digitisation note about logarithmic axes in figure 8 and says nothing about structure. The measured window is 77 to 302 K, cryogenic to room temperature.

basis: La3OsO7 is an RE3MO7 compound, the weberite-type anion-deficient fluorite built from chains of corner-sharing OsO6 octahedra with lanthanum in between. [ref 2] gives La3OsO7 in Cmcm (63) at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference, which is the setting the prototype names for the larger rare earths, and the paper describes it as quasi-one-dimensional, which is what those isolated octahedral chains produce.

dopant_roles.site: the eight-coordinate rare-earth site between the octahedral chains
dopant_roles.basis: Divalent calcium for trivalent lanthanum at 0.2 of 3 removes an electron per substitution, oxidising the osmium chain and hole-doping what is otherwise a magnetic insulator. Calcium and lanthanum are close in size, so the doping is done on the rare-earth site rather than on the chain, which leaves the one-dimensional transport path intact.

note: The re3mo7_weberite entry lists M as Nb, Ta, Sb, Mo, Ru or Re; osmium belongs in that list on the same grounds as ruthenium and rhenium and should be added in v4. The other [ref 2] entries are different compounds: La3(OsO5)2 in C2/m is at a different oxygen content and La5MnOs3O16 is a quaternary. The curator note says only that the samples are polycrystalline. The 153 to 298 K window sits above the antiferromagnetic ordering of La3OsO7 near 45 K, so nothing is crossed.

basis: Both compositions are La0.7Sr0.3Mn1-xRuxO3 with x equal to 0.8 and 0.9, and the paper is titled Effects of Ru substitution for Mn on La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 perovskites. The A site is the usual La and Sr manganite mixture and the B site is almost entirely ruthenium; LaRuO3 and SrRuO3 are both orthorhombic tilted ABO3 perovskites, so the whole substitution range is one prototype.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Manganese is the residual parent species here, not an added impurity. The experiment starts from La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 and replaces manganese with ruthenium; by x equal to 0.8 and 0.9 only 10 to 20 percent of the B site is still manganese, which is what puts it below the candidate threshold. The physics is the dilution of the Mn3+ and Mn4+ double-exchange network, so the element that matters is the one that is disappearing.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Every entry it offers is a magnesium-containing or layered ruthenate at a different composition, Sr4La2Mg(RuO6)2 in two settings, Sr8La3(RuO7)3 in P1, and SrLa(RuO3)2 in Pmn2_1; the first two are not even the right chemistry, since no magnesium is present in this host, and the block reflects a formula-matching artefact rather than evidence about these samples. No mp_id is recorded. Pnma is given with medium confidence from the tilting of SrRuO3 and LaRuO3 rather than from a reference. The 30 to 494 K window crosses the ferromagnetic transition of the ruthenate, which is magnetic rather than structural.

basis: The two compositions are different compounds. LaTa3O9 is La1/3TaO3, the A-site-deficient perovskite with two thirds of the twelve-coordinate sites vacant, the tantalum analogue of La1/3NbO3 two ranks earlier in this chunk. La3TaO7 is the weberite-type RE3MO7 with chains of corner-sharing TaO6 octahedra. [ref 2] backs both, LaTa3O9 in Pnma (62) and La3TaO7 in Cmcm (63), each with two ICSD references, so the host is split rather than labelled once.

other_polymorphs.note: La3TaO7, the second composition and a separate compound rather than a polymorph. [ref 2] gives it in Cmcm at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references, matching La3OsO7 at rank 2275 in this same chunk. The second paper here, on the thermal properties of La3TaO7 and La2AlTaO7, belongs to this composition.

note: One wording caveat worth recording. The first paper is titled Spontaneously formed nanostructures in double perovskite rare-earth tantalates, and RE3TaO7 phases are sometimes described in the literature as defect double perovskites, since (RE2)(RE Ta)O7 can be read as an A2BB pattern one oxygen short. I have kept them under the weberite entry because the octahedral connectivity is chains rather than a corner-sharing three-dimensional network, which is the structural fact the prototype turns on, but a reader who expected double_perovskite is not making an error of chemistry. LaTaO4 in Cmc2_1 is [ref 2]s best-attested entry at six ICSD references and is neither composition here; the block again describes the phase field rather than the samples. The robust window is 294 to 1073 K and the full span reaches 1473 K, which is thermal-barrier-coating territory and fits the first paper.

basis: La3Te3.6Pb0.4 is the La3-xTe4 thermoelectric with lead partially replacing tellurium, and the first paper is on exactly that, the effect of partial Pb substitution for Te. La3Te4 is the Th3P4 type, a cubic framework in I-43d whose defining feature is that the cation sublattice can carry vacancies continuously from La3Te4 to La2Te3, which is the carrier-concentration knob. The second composition, written PbTeLa, does not fit that and is handled separately.

other_polymorphs.note: PbTeLa, the second composition. Written as one lanthanum per PbTe it is not a dopant level at all, and no compound of that stoichiometry is known; the two readings are lanthanum-doped rocksalt PbTe with the level lost in transcription, or a two-phase PbTe and La3Te4 mixture, which is a real material since the two are studied together as segmented and composite n-type legs. I have not chosen between them. The paper, on synergistically optimising an n-type material, would settle it in one line.

dopant_roles.site: the anion site of the Th3P4 framework
dopant_roles.basis: In the first composition lead replaces 0.4 of 4 tellurium sites, which is what the paper varies. Lead on an anion site is unusual and is the point of the experiment: it changes the electron count in a way that shifts the optimum vacancy concentration, so it acts alongside the La vacancies rather than instead of them. Recorded although lead is above the candidate threshold.

note: Confidence is medium because one of the two compositions is not interpretable as written, which is set out under other_polymorphs. [ref 2] offers only La2Te4Pb in I-42d at hull 0.033 with no ICSD reference, a computed ternary line compound that matches neither composition, so no mp_id is recorded and the Th3P4 space group is from knowledge of La3-xTe4 rather than from evidence. The two papers are from different groups five years apart and may not even be about the same material, which is a further reason to resolve this host at composition level.

basis: LaPdSb is an equiatomic RTX antimonide, and for the light rare earths that family takes the hexagonal stuffed-wurtzite arrangement, a puckered PdSb honeycomb net with lanthanum between the layers. [ref 2] gives LaSbPd in P6_3/mmc (194) at hull 0.003 with an ICSD reference, which is the disordered CaIn2 setting of that entry, and the prototype already names LaPtSb as a representative. The paper is on LnPdSb as intermetallics with large carrier mobility.
note: Confidence is medium on a specific point: the setting. The reference gives the centrosymmetric P6_3/mmc cell, but the RPdSb compounds are frequently reported in the ordered LiGaGe variant P6_3mc (186), which removes the inversion centre once palladium and antimony order on the honeycomb; a powder pattern does not distinguish them easily and the reference has only one ICSD entry. Both settings sit inside this prototype, so the assignment does not change, but the space group recorded here may. The competing assignment is zrbesi_ordered_alb2, which is also P6_3/mmc and differs by having a planar rather than a puckered net; I have gone with the CaIn2 entry because it already carries LaPtSb, the platinum analogue. [ref 2]s best-attested entry for the host is La(SbPd)2 in P4/nmm with two ICSD references, a 1:2:2 compound that is not this composition.

basis: LaSi is an equiatomic rare-earth monosilicide, built from zigzag silicon chains threaded through trigonal prisms of lanthanum, which is the CrB and FeB pair of related types. [ref 2] gives LaSi in Pnma (62) at hull 0.013 with six ICSD references, the FeB setting of that pair, and the papers measure LaSi alongside the alkaline-earth silicides BaSi2 and SrSi2.
note: [ref 2] marks LaSi2 in I4_1/amd as primary on eight ICSD references, one more than LaSi has, but that is the alpha-ThSi2 disilicide at a different composition, not a polymorph of the monosilicide; the same goes for La5Si3, La5Si4 and LaSi5. The compositions here are unambiguously LaSi, so the six-reference entry is the right one and the count ordering in the block is about the phase field rather than about these samples. The robust window is 298 to 959 K with outliers to 1166 K; LaSi has no structural transition in that range, the FeB to CrB distinction being a matter of which compound rather than which temperature.

basis: Mg1.7Li0.3Si and Mg1.8Li0.2Si are Mg2Si with lithium on the magnesium site, and the paper is titled Structural and Thermoelectric Properties of Polycrystalline p-Type Mg2Si. Mg2Si is the cubic antifluorite in Fm-3m, silicon on the face-centred lattice with magnesium filling every tetrahedral hole, and the substitution keeps the magnesium sublattice full.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral cation site of the antifluorite cell
dopant_roles.basis: Monovalent lithium for divalent magnesium removes one electron per substitution, which is the acceptor that makes these samples p-type; Mg2Si is otherwise n-type and hard to hole-dope, which is why lithium is used at all. Recorded although it is above the 5 at.% candidate threshold, because at 0.2 to 0.3 per formula unit it is the doping variable rather than a host constituent.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] on this host. Its entries are the genuine Li-Mg-Si ternaries, Li2MgSi in P-43m with three ICSD references, Li12Mg3Si4, LiMg2Si and two partially-lithiated Li(Mg2Si)n cells; none of them is doped Mg2Si, which is what the paper made. That is the reference describing which line compounds exist in a chemistry rather than which phase was synthesised, and the lithium content here, 10 percent of the magnesium site, is far below any of them. No mp_id is recorded for that reason. Lithium solubility in Mg2Si is limited and a Li-rich ternary could appear as a second phase at these levels, which is a plausible reading of the paper but not something to assert here.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [215, 221, 123, 216]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions are Mg2Si0.25Sn0.75 with lithium and, in one sample, silver added, and the paper names exactly that: p-type Mg2.00Si0.25Sn0.75 with Li and Ag. The Mg2(Si,Sn) solid solution is the antifluorite throughout, silicon and tin sharing the face-centred anion site, and it is the workhorse of the family because the two end members are isostructural and fully miscible.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral cation site
dopant_roles.basis: Lithium for magnesium is the acceptor, the same role it plays in the Li-Mg-Si host at the previous rank. At 0.32 to 0.4 per formula unit it is well above the candidate threshold and is the principal doping variable of the paper.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral cation site
dopant_roles.basis: Silver at 0.005 per formula unit is the second acceptor the paper tests, monovalent like lithium and on the same site but far larger, so it also adds point-defect phonon scattering. Note that lithium drops from 0.4 to 0.32 in the silver-bearing sample, so the two are being traded against each other rather than simply added.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the face-centred anion site of the antifluorite cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Si/(Si+Sn) is fixed at 0.25 in both compositions. Silicon and tin are same-group and isovalent, so this adds no carriers; the ratio is chosen for the band convergence near that composition and for alloy phonon scattering, and it is held constant while the dopants are varied.

note: Neither reference covers this host, so no space group evidence and no mp_id. Mg2(Si,Sn) has a miscibility gap in the middle of the range and samples at x equal to 0.25 can contain two antifluorite phases of different Si to Sn ratio; that is a microstructural fact rather than a second prototype, so is_mixed stays false. The measured window, 291 to 826 K, is the usual range for this family and crosses no structural transition.

basis: LiNiO2 is the alpha-NaFeO2 layered rocksalt: cubic close-packed oxygen with lithium and nickel ordering into alternate (111) layers, which lowers the symmetry to R-3m. [ref 2] gives LiNiO2 in R-3m (166) at hull 0.007 with three ICSD references, the best-attested entry in the host, and the paper studies transport across the LiNi1-yCoyO2 series, which is the same structure throughout.
note: The other [ref 2] entries are different compositions rather than polymorphs: Li2NiO2 in P-3m1 is the overlithiated phase, Li(NiO2)2 in P-4332 and the two partially delithiated C2/m cells are points along the charge and discharge curve of the battery material. LiNiO2 is notoriously non-stoichiometric, with excess nickel sitting in the lithium layer, and that cation mixing is a real feature of any sample rather than a change of prototype; it does not appear in the composition string, so it is noted here rather than recorded as a role. The robust window is 150 to 297 K with outliers to 855 K, so the two samples were measured over quite different ranges.

basis: LiRh2O4 is a normal spinel, lithium on the tetrahedral A site and rhodium on the octahedral B site, and its paper is titled Band Jahn-Teller Instability and Formation of Valence Bond Solid in a pyrochlore-lattice antiferromagnet, which is the rhodium sublattice of exactly that spinel. The second composition, LiRhO3, is a separate compound and is not placeable as written, so the host is split.

other_polymorphs.note: LiRhO3, the second composition. It cannot be right as written: it would make rhodium pentavalent, no reference lists it, and the paper it comes from is titled Spin State Control of the Perovskite Rh/Co Oxides, which describes a completely different structure. The two nearest real compounds are Li2RhO3, the C2/m honeycomb-ordered layered oxide that [ref 2] gives at hull 0.000, and LiRhO2, the R-3m layered rocksalt it gives with an ICSD reference. I have named the honeycomb one as the alternative because the oxygen count matches it once the lithium is doubled, but that is arithmetic, not evidence. This composition needs the paper.

note: This host crosses two structural transitions that the chunk file did not flag, because the spinel taxonomy entry carries none. LiRh2O4 is cubic Fd-3m at room temperature, converts near 230 K to a tetragonal I4_1/amd cell through a band Jahn-Teller instability, and near 170 K undergoes a second transition into the dimerised valence-bond-solid state that the paper title names. The measured window is 89 to 299 K, so it passes through both. The lowest phase is left with a null space group because the dimerised cell is a low-symmetry superstructure I cannot name with confidence. Both temperatures are from general knowledge of this compound; the paper is about them and would upgrade the basis to paper evidence, but I have not read it. The full span of the host reaches 754 K, which belongs to the other composition.

basis: Li0.5Zn0.5Rh2O4 is ZnRh2O4 with lithium taking half the tetrahedral A site: the rhodium to oxygen ratio of 2 to 4 is the spinel stoichiometry and rhodium is a strongly octahedral-site cation, so the B sublattice is unchanged. ZnRh2O4 is the p-type transparent conducting spinel this work comes from, and the paper describes the material as A-site deficient, which is an A-site story on a spinel rather than a different structure.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral A site of the spinel
dopant_roles.basis: Monovalent lithium for divalent zinc at half the A site removes half an electron per formula unit, which oxidises the rhodium and is the acceptor doping that raises the hole concentration of ZnRh2O4. Recorded although lithium is above the candidate threshold, because it is the substitution the paper is about.

note: Neither reference covers this host, so the Fd-3m setting is from knowledge of ZnRh2O4 rather than a database entry and no mp_id is recorded. One sample is a film and one is bulk, and the chunk file flags that films can stabilise polymorphs bulk synthesis cannot; for this chemistry that caveat is mild, since the rhodium spinel is the stable form and no competing ZnRh2O4 polymorph is known, but the film sample is the one to check if the two disagree. The paper calls the phase A-site deficient, so some vacancy content on the tetrahedral site is likely on top of the Li and Zn mixture; that is not visible in the composition string and is not recorded as a role.

basis: LiZnSb is a hexagonal Nowotny-Juza phase: a puckered ZnSb honeycomb net, wurtzite-like, with lithium stuffed between the layers, which is the LiGaGe ordering of the CaIn2 type. [ref 2] gives LiZnSb in P6_3mc (186) at hull 0.000 with two ICSD references, the non-centrosymmetric ordered setting that the prototype names, and the paper assesses ab initio calculations for p-type LiZnSb.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] also lists Li2ZnSb in F-43m at hull 0.196. That is a different composition, the cubic two-lithium Nowotny-Juza phase, not a polymorph of LiZnSb, and nearly 200 meV above the hull with no ICSD reference. Listed so it is not mistaken for the cubic alternative to the hexagonal cell.

note: LiZnSb is a well-known case of theory and experiment disagreeing, which is what the paper is about: calculations predicted a high power factor for the n-type material and measurements on p-type samples did not reproduce it. That is an electronic-structure disagreement, not a structural one, and the prototype is not in doubt. The sample form is recorded only as Other for both samples. The window is narrow, 297 to 530 K, and lithium mobility rather than a phase change is what limits it at the top.

basis: Lu2Rh2O7 is the A2B2O7 pyrochlore stoichiometry and the paper names it: Coexistence of metallic and nonmetallic properties in the pyrochlore Lu2Rh2O7. Lutetium takes the eight-coordinate A site and rhodium the octahedral B site, both on corner-sharing tetrahedral networks, in Fd-3m.
note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Both its entries are LuRhO3, in Pnma with one ICSD reference and in Pm-3m at hull 0.721; that is the perovskite at a different composition, and the block simply has no pyrochlore entry for this chemistry. Rhodium pyrochlores need high-pressure synthesis, which is why they are thinly represented in a snapshot, and the second paper here is about stabilising pyrochlore rhodates on an isostructural template layer, which says the same thing from the other direction. The assignment stands against the reference and no mp_id is recorded. Fd-3m is the family setting rather than a measured one.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Mg2.6Mn0.4Sb2 and Mg2.7Mn0.3Sb2 are Mg3Sb2 with manganese on the cation site, and the paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of Mn-doped Mg-Sb single crystals. Mg3Sb2 is the trigonal CaAl2Si2 Zintl phase in P-3m1: a covalent [Mg2Sb2] slab of edge-sharing MgSb4 tetrahedra with the remaining magnesium octahedrally coordinated between the slabs.

dopant_roles.site: the interlayer octahedral magnesium site
dopant_roles.basis: Manganese replaces 0.3 to 0.4 of the three magnesium atoms. In the CaAl2Si2 arrangement the two magnesium sites are not equivalent, one tetrahedral inside the slab and one octahedral between slabs, and a divalent transition metal of this size goes to the octahedral interlayer site; that is also the site whose occupancy controls the carrier count in Mg3Sb2, which is why doping there works. Recorded although manganese is above the candidate threshold.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Its four entries, Mg14MnSb in two settings, Mg5MnSb4 and Mg6MnSb, are all magnesium-rich ternaries between 77 and 156 meV above the hull with no ICSD references; they are computed points in the Mg-Mn-Sb phase field and none of them is Mg3Sb2, which is what the crystals are. No mp_id is recorded and P-3m1 comes from the prototype rather than from evidence. Which magnesium site manganese occupies is stated with medium confidence: it follows from the coordination chemistry, but the paper on the single crystals is what would settle it, and the answer matters for stage 2 because only one of the two sites is the carrier knob.

basis: The composition strings are written as MgTi2O5 with a stated amount of TiN alongside, and the paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of MgTi2O5/TiN conductive composites. MgTi2O5 is karrooite, the pseudobrookite M3O5 framework in Cmcm, and TiN is the rocksalt nitride; these are two separate crystalline phases deliberately mixed, not one compound.

other_polymorphs.note: TiN, the second phase of both composites, at 0.808 and 1.386 formula units per MgTi2O5. It is the conductive phase the paper is named for: rocksalt titanium nitride is metallic and percolates through an otherwise insulating oxide matrix. Not a polymorph of the matrix and not reachable by heating it; a separate crystalline phase present at the same time.

note: is_mixed is true because two prototypes are genuinely present, but this host will not split on composition the way most mixed hosts do: both compositions are the same two-phase composite and differ only in how much TiN is in it, so there is no composition that resolves to a single structure. Stage 2 should treat the matrix and the conductive phase separately rather than attempting a split. Neither reference covers the host, so both space groups come from the prototypes and no mp_id is recorded. Nitrogen here is not a processing residue, which is the usual reading in a chunk file; it is a stoichiometric constituent of the second phase.

basis: Na2Mg3Sn2 and Na4Mg4Sn3 are both Zintl stannides in which the electron count works out to isolated Sn4- anions, two sodium and three magnesium giving eight positive charges against two tin, and four and four giving twelve against three. That tells us the bonding but not the structure type, and I cannot name one for either compound. The paper is the report of their crystal structures, so the answer exists but is not in front of me.
note: Parked rather than guessed. The two compositions are different compounds, so is_mixed is true, but naming two prototypes I cannot defend would be worse than naming none. [ref 2] offers Na2MgSn in P6_3/mmc with one ICSD reference and three magnesium-rich NaMgnSn cells above the hull; none is at either composition. The cited paper, Synthesis of Na2Mg3X2 and Na4Mg4Sn3 and their crystal structures, is exactly the source that settles this and should be read in stage 2. The isolated-Sn4- reading above does narrow the field usefully, to the salt-like end of the Zintl range rather than to a framework or a chain compound, so this is not a blank entry.

basis: ZnRh1.6Mg0.4O4 and ZnRh1.4Mg0.6O4 are ZnRh2O4 with magnesium replacing part of the rhodium, and the paper is titled Mg substitution effects of new thermoelectric Rh oxides. The AB2O4 ratio is intact in both, zinc on the tetrahedral site and the rhodium-magnesium mixture on the octahedral site, which is the normal spinel in Fd-3m.

dopant_roles.site: the octahedral B site of the spinel
dopant_roles.basis: Divalent magnesium for trivalent rhodium at 0.4 to 0.6 of two sites is an acceptor substitution: it oxidises the remaining rhodium and raises the hole concentration of what is otherwise a wide-gap p-type oxide. Magnesium is above the candidate threshold and is the variable of the paper, so it is recorded here. The alternative, magnesium going to the tetrahedral site and displacing zinc, is less likely because zinc has the stronger tetrahedral site preference of the two.

note: Neither reference covers this host, so Fd-3m comes from the prototype and no mp_id is recorded. This host and Li-O-Rh-Zn at rank 2285 are the same research programme approached from two sides, acceptor doping of ZnRh2O4 on the A site there and on the B site here, and they should be reviewed together. The window is wide, 11 to 774 K, and the spinel has no structural transition in it.

basis: Li0.1Mg0.9V2O4 and Li0.3Mg0.7V2O4 are MgV2O4 with lithium on the tetrahedral site, and the paper is titled Preparation and physical properties of the spinel Ti and V oxides. [ref 2] gives MgV2O4 in Fd-3m (227) with three ICSD references, the best-attested entry for this composition, and the AB2O4 ratio holds in both samples.

dopant_roles.site: the tetrahedral A site of the spinel
dopant_roles.basis: Monovalent lithium for divalent magnesium oxidises the vanadium sublattice, moving it away from the half-filled V3+ d2 configuration and changing the carrier count on the geometrically frustrated pyrochlore network of B sites. Lithium and magnesium are close in size and both sit comfortably on the tetrahedral site, so this is a clean substitution.

note: Two things to record. [ref 1] covers this host but with Mg3V2O8 and MgV2O5, which are different magnesium vanadate compositions rather than polymorphs of the spinel; the project precedence puts TEDesignLab above Materials Project, but that only applies where it covers the formula, and here it does not, so the [ref 2] MgV2O4 entry is the right evidence despite sitting 90 meV above the hull. And MgV2O4 has a cubic-to-tetragonal orbital-ordering transition near 65 K, essentially at the lower edge of the 63 to 292 K window. I have left spans_transition false because the measurement only touches it, one endpoint rather than a range, and because lithium doping suppresses that ordering; it is flagged here rather than asserted as a phase.

basis: Both compositions are Mg2Si with antimony on the silicon site, and the paper is titled Sb- and Bi-doped Mg2Si: location of the dopants. Mg2Si is the cubic antifluorite in Fm-3m, and the paper title states that the dopant location is the question, which presupposes the host structure.

dopant_roles.site: the face-centred anion site of the antifluorite cell
dopant_roles.basis: Antimony has one more valence electron than silicon, so on the silicon site it is the standard n-type donor for Mg2Si. The paper is specifically about establishing that location rather than an interstitial or a second phase, which is the right question because antimony is much larger than silicon and its solubility is low.

note: Two objections. The composition strings are not trustworthy: Mg2Si.75Sb0.25 has a malformed silicon coefficient and Mg2Si0.97Sb0.33 sums to 1.30 on a site that holds 1.00, and real Sb doping levels in this work are of order 0.01 to 0.03 per formula unit, so both antimony fractions are inflated by one or two orders of magnitude. The prototype is unaffected but the doping level computed in stage 3 from these strings will be wrong, and that is worth knowing before it is. I also disagree with [ref 1], which offers MgSiSb2 in I-42d at hull 0.115 with two ICSD references: that is a chalcopyrite-like ternary line compound, not doped Mg2Si, and it is 115 meV above the hull. No mp_id is recorded from it.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [122]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Both compositions are Mg2(Si,Sn) with antimony added, and the paper is titled High Performance Mg2(Si,Sn) Solid Solutions: a Point Defect Chemistry study. The Mg2X antifluorite takes silicon and tin on one face-centred anion site across the whole range, and antimony is the n-type donor on that same site.

dopant_roles.site: the face-centred anion site of the antifluorite cell
dopant_roles.basis: Antimony donates one electron per substitution on the group 14 anion site and is the n-type dopant of this family. It is named as substituting for tin rather than silicon because the two share that site and tin is the majority species here; in practice it replaces whichever occupies the site it lands on. The paper is a point-defect study, so the interplay between this donor and magnesium interstitials and vacancies is its subject.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the face-centred anion site of the antifluorite cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Si/(Si+Sn) is 0.4 in both compositions if antimony is excluded from the count, which is the right way to read it: silicon and tin are the isovalent pair and antimony is the dopant, not a third member of the axis. Near this ratio the two conduction bands of Mg2(Si,Sn) converge, which is why the composition is chosen.

note: The same transcription problem as the Mg-Sb-Si host at the previous rank, and worse here. Both strings put the anion site well over 1.00, at 1.00 and 1.00 for Si plus Sn alone before antimony is added, so the recorded Sb fractions of 0.27 and 0.38 cannot be occupancies; genuine antimony levels in this work are around 0.02. Stage 3 will produce a wrong doping level from these strings unless they are corrected against the paper. Neither reference covers this host, so no mp_id is recorded. The measured window, 289 to 750 K, crosses no structural transition; Mg2(Si,Sn) does have a miscibility gap, but that separates two antifluorite phases rather than two prototypes.

basis: Both compositions are Mg3Sb2 derivatives with ytterbium and zinc substituted in, and the paper is on enhanced thermoelectric performance of p-type Mg3Sb2. The CaAl2Si2 arrangement has two distinct cation sites, a tetrahedral one inside the [Mg2Sb2] slab and an octahedral one between slabs; zinc at 1.2 takes the tetrahedral site and ytterbium at 0.4 the octahedral one, which keeps the total cation count at three per two antimony.

dopant_roles.site: the interlayer octahedral cation site
dopant_roles.basis: Sodium at 0.006 per formula unit is the p-type acceptor: monovalent on a divalent site, one hole per substitution, at a level far too low to be anything else. It goes to the interlayer octahedral site, which is the one that accepts large cations in this structure and the one ytterbium is already occupying. This is the only element in the host below the candidate threshold and it is a textbook substitutional dopant.

note: Neither reference covers this host, so P-3m1 comes from the prototype and no mp_id is recorded. The two samples differ only in magnesium content, 1.194 against 1.394, which with fixed ytterbium, zinc and sodium means the total cation count moves from 2.8 to 3.0 per two antimony: the first sample is cation-deficient and the second is stoichiometric, so cation vacancies are being varied alongside the sodium. That is a second, unnamed doping variable and stage 3 should not read the sodium fraction as the whole story. This host is the same chemistry as Mg-Mn-Sb at rank 2288 approached from the p-type side.

basis: The composition is elemental manganese and the paper is titled Origin of low thermal conductivity in alpha-Mn. Alpha-Mn is the A12 structure, a cubic cell in I-43m holding 58 atoms on four inequivalent sites, and it is the ambient form of the element up to about 1000 K. [ref 2] gives Mn in I-43m (217) at hull 0.000 with sixteen ICSD references, by far the strongest entry in the host. The taxonomy had no A12 entry, so the prototype is proposed.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] lists Mn in Im-3m at hull 0.147 with three ICSD references. That is delta-manganese, body-centred cubic, which is real but only above about 1410 K; the measured window here ends at 276 K, so it is nowhere near. Recorded under the closest available prototype for a body-centred cubic element. The gamma form, face-centred cubic between roughly 1360 and 1410 K, is equally out of range. It is filed as unresolved_crystalline rather than under a named prototype because the taxonomy has no entry for a plain body-centred cubic element: b2_cscl is the ordered binary CsCl arrangement in Pm-3m, which is a different structure, and filing bcc there would assert an ordering that is not present. BaMn28, CaMn28 and YbMn28, also in I-43m, are stuffed A12 cells at a different composition, not polymorphs of the element.

note: Manganese does have transitions on heating, alpha to beta near 1000 K and onward, but the window measured here is 11 to 276 K and crosses none of them. It does cross the antiferromagnetic ordering of alpha-Mn near 95 K, which is magnetic and produces only a small tetragonal distortion, so spans_transition stays false. The reason the element appears in a thermoelectric dataset at all is the 58-atom cell: it gives a glass-like lattice thermal conductivity in a pure metal, which is what the paper is about.

basis: Nd0.25Sm0.25Sr0.50MnO3 is a half-doped manganite: the A site carries two rare earths and strontium, the B site is all manganese, and the O3 anion count is exact. The paper is on phase separation and stability in Sm0.50Sr0.50MnO3 and the effects of cation substitution, so neodymium is there to tune the average A-site radius of an ABO3 perovskite.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the twelve-coordinate A site of the perovskite
solid_solution_axis.note: Nd/(Nd+Sm) is fixed at 0.5. Both are trivalent light rare earths on the same site, so the substitution adds no carriers; what it changes is the average A-site radius and its variance, and in half-doped manganites those two quantities decide whether the ground state is a ferromagnetic metal or a charge-ordered insulator. That is the cation-substitution effect in the paper title.

note: Half-doped manganites like this one undergo CE-type charge and orbital ordering, for Sm0.5Sr0.5MnO3 somewhere near 150 K, which lies inside the 12 to 285 K window and carries a real structural distortion with it. I have left spans_transition false because the distortion is a superstructure within the orthorhombic perovskite rather than a change of prototype, and because in this composition range the transition is often incomplete, the phase separation of the title being exactly that. It is flagged here as something a reader should know.
