It is body-centred cubic A2, and [ref 2] gives V in Im-3m at mp-1056037, hull 0.000, with 22 ICSD references. bcc is the only phase up to the melt. Assigned as Nb was in chunk 008, which comes from the same group VB paper.

other_polymorphs.note: fcc V: 1 ICSD reference at hull 0.252. Not reached by heating bulk vanadium.

note: The full span reaches 1534 K, but bcc vanadium has no transition below its 2183 K melting point, so nothing is crossed.

basis: Ag3AuSe2 is the mineral fischesserite, a cubic chiral structure in I4_132 with gold in linear coordination. The paper is on noble-metal ternary chalcogenides. TEDesignLab gives Ag3AuSe2 in I4_132 at mp-3172, hull 0.000. No existing prototype covers it, so one was proposed.
note: Confidence is medium only because the prototype is newly proposed. The reference and the chemistry agree, although the 2 ICSD references are weak by the chunk convention. ag2se_naumannite was not used: the gold is ordered on its own site and the cell is cubic, not a substituted Ag2Se.

basis: (AgI)0.79(Ag2O)0.21(B2O3)0.21 is a silver-ion-conducting borate glass, and the paper is titled for the thermoelectric power of the vitreous electrolyte. It has no long-range crystalline order.
note: The measured 337-490 K window crosses the 420 K beta-to-alpha transition of crystalline AgI. In a glass that only matters if AgI has crystallised out, which would make the sample a glass-ceramic; the paper would say so. The thermopower here is ionic, carried by Ag+ in the glass network, not electronic.

basis: CdAg2Bi6Se11 comes from a paper titled Six Quaternary Chalcogenides of the Pavonite Homologous Series. It is a selenide member of the series built from NaCl-type slabs of two thicknesses joined across a mirror plane, which is what the proposed pavonite entry was written to cover.
note: A different homologue number from AgBi3S5. That is the case the pavonite proposal anticipated when it suggested filing this as a homologous series at v4. Cd and Ag share the thin-slab cation sites. Neither reference covers the host, so no mp_id is recorded, and the C2/m space group is the family default, not a refinement read for this compound.

basis: The paper is titled for Bi2Sr2Co2Oy/Ag composites, and the curator detail gives 15 wt% Ag2O added. The thermoelectric phase is the misfit-layered cobaltite [Bi2Sr2O4][CoO2], a rocksalt-type Bi-Sr-O block on a CdI2-type CoO2 layer. Silver is a second phase in the grain boundaries, reduced from the oxide. Assigned as Ag-Ca-Co-O was in chunk 026.
note: Silver is in the host key only because the composite loading puts it above 5 atomic per cent. It is not in the cobaltite lattice. The sample is nominally two-phase, but composite_multiphase is not used because the thermoelectric phase is unambiguous. The misfit is incommensurate, so no single MP entry exists and phases is empty.

basis: BiAgOS is the silver member of the BiMOCh layered compounds (M = Cu, Ag; Ch = S, Se, Te), the family the paper title names. It is the BiCuSeO-type 1111 structure: fluorite-like Bi2O2 layers alternating with antifluorite-like Ag2S2 layers, in P4/nmm.
note: O and S are on distinct layers, O in Bi2O2 and S in Ag2S2, so this is not an O/S solid solution despite both being group 16. Neither reference covers the host. Single point near room temperature.

basis: Eu9Cd3.8Ag1.4Sb9 is a coinage-metal-stuffed Eu9Cd4Sb9, as the paper title says: the 9-4-9 Zintl framework with part of the cadmium replaced and extra silver on the interstitial sites that the ideal 9-4-9 formula leaves partly empty.
note: Ag is 6 atomic per cent and so a host element with no dopant entry. It does two things: it replaces some Cd and it stuffs interstitial sites, and together these make the compound metallic, as the paper title says. The total transition-metal count of 5.2 against the ideal 4 shows the stuffing. No reference covers the host, and the space group is left for stage 2 to take from the taxonomy entry.

basis: Ag0.4Cd0.5In2.2Te4 has 3.1 cations per 4 anions, which is cation-deficient relative to chalcopyrite. It is an In-rich AgInTe2-CdIn2Te4 solid solution of the kind in the paper title, silver indium telluride semiconductors and their solid solutions with cadmium indium telluride. Filed as the In-rich Ag0.4Cd0.2In2.4Te4 was under Ag-In-Te in chunk 009.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its three entries, Cd2In3Ag3Te8 P-4, Cd2InAgTe4 I-42m and CdInAgTe3 Cm, are computed orderings at other stoichiometries with no ICSD references, none at this cation deficiency, so no mp_id is recorded. The exact vacancy ordering, a CdIn2Te4-like defect-stannite I-4 or a disordered defect zincblende, needs the paper. chalcopyrite is kept as the alternative.

basis: Ce3Ag4Ge4 is an R3T4X4 compound of the Gd3Cu4Ge4 type, orthorhombic Immm, and the paper covers Ce3Ag4X4 (X = Ge, Sn). [ref 2] ranks Ce3(AgGe)4 in Immm at mp-640597 first, hull 0.000, with 3 ICSD references. No existing prototype covers it, so one was proposed.
note: Confidence is medium only because the prototype is newly proposed; reference and chemistry agree. CeAg2Ge2 I4/mmm and CeAgGe P6_3mc in the same list are the 122 and 111 phases of this ternary, not polymorphs of the 3-4-4 compound.

basis: Ce3Ag4Sn4 is the stannide partner of Ce3Ag4Ge4 in the same paper and the same R3T4X4 Gd3Cu4Ge4-type family, orthorhombic Immm.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. It has no 3-4-4 entry for this chemistry and offers Ce5AgSn3 P6_3/mcm, CeAgSn P6_3mc, Ce2AgSn Fm-3m and a P-3m1 CeAgSn instead, all at other stoichiometries. The type is assigned from the germanide analogue and the paper, and no mp_id is recorded. Stage 2 should confirm the structure from the paper, since a larger Sn atom could favour a different arrangement at this ratio.

basis: AgCr0.8Mg0.2O2 is the delafossite AgCrO2 with a fifth of the chromium replaced by magnesium. The paper is on solution synthesis of p-type Ag-based delafossite transparent conducting films. R-3m, with linear O-Ag-O dumbbells between CrO2 octahedral layers.
note: Mg is exactly 5 atomic per cent and so falls on the host side of the cut. Its role is the p-type acceptor: Mg2+ on the Cr3+ site, as in the classic CuCrO2:Mg delafossite conductors. Stage 3 should treat it as the doping variable. Thin film; neither reference covers the host.

basis: Ag0.32Cu0.43In0.25 is a ternary Ag-Cu-In alloy, the filler studied in the paper on compatibility between Co-metallised PbTe legs and an Ag-Cu-In joint. At 25 per cent indium it lies far beyond the solubility of In in either fcc terminal solution. It will consist of Ag-rich and Cu-rich phases plus Cu-In and Ag-In intermetallics, not a single crystal structure.
note: This is a joining material measured for its own transport, not a thermoelectric. The phase assemblage should be taken from the paper if stage 2 needs it. Neither reference covers the host.

basis: EuAgSb is a hexagonal ZrBeSi-type 111 Zintl compound: planar AgSb honeycomb layers with Eu between them, P6_3/mmc. It appears with SrAgSb in the paper titled Promising Zintl-Phase Thermoelectric Compound SrAgSb. [ref 2] ranks EuAgSb in P6_3/mmc at mp-22707 first, hull 0.000, with 2 ICSD references.
note: Eu(Ag2Sb)2 R-3m and Eu2AgSb Fm-3m in the same list are other stoichiometries. The latter is a computed Heusler-like entry with no ICSD reference.

basis: EuAg2Si2 is a ThCr2Si2-type 122 silicide, and [ref 2] ranks Eu(SiAg)2 in I4/mmm at mp-22653 first, hull 0.000, with 2 ICSD references. The paper is on phase relations in the Ce-Ag-Si and Eu-Ag-Si systems.
note: Eu2Si3Ag Fddd and EuSiAg P-6m2 are other stoichiometries. With 2 ICSD references the entry is weak by the chunk convention, but it matches the composition exactly.

basis: Ag9Ga(S0.85Se0.15)6 is the argyrodite Ag9GaS6 with 15 per cent of the sulfur replaced by selenium. The paper is on the thermoelectric properties of Ag9GaS6 with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity. The structure is an A8BX6-type framework of isolated GaS4 tetrahedra and mobile silver.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen sites of the argyrodite anion framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Isoelectronic Se for S at 15 per cent of the anion site. Se is 5.6 atomic per cent, so it is a host element and not a dopant candidate. It tunes the lattice softness and band gap, not the carrier count.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its four entries, Ga2Ag2Se3S, Ga2Ag2SeS3 and two GaAgSeS cells, are computed AgGa(S,Se)2 orderings, chalcopyrite-derived compounds at a 1:1 Ag:Ga ratio. They are not this 9:1 argyrodite, and none has an ICSD reference, so no mp_id is recorded. Argyrodites order their silver at low temperature and turn cubic F-43m superionic on heating. For Ag9GaS6 that change lies near room temperature, so the space group is left null rather than committed to one side. The chunk printed no crossing line, and stage 2 should read the transition from the paper.

basis: NdAg2Ge2 is a ThCr2Si2-type 122 germanide from a paper on RAg2Ge2 (R = Pr, Nd). [ref 2] ranks Nd(AgGe)2 in I4/mmm at mp-4229 first, hull 0.000, with 4 ICSD references.
note: Nd2AgGe6 and Nd3(AgGe)4 are other stoichiometries. The Nd moments order antiferromagnetically at low temperature; that is magnetic and not recorded as a phase change.

basis: Ge0.77Ag0.11Pb0.12Te is GeTe with about a quarter of the germanium site replaced by lead and silver, from the paper on high figure-of-merit high-entropy GeTe-based thermoelectrics. At room temperature this is the rhombohedral R3m ferroelectric distortion of rocksalt, and it becomes cubic on heating within the measured 299-801 K window.
note: The transition temperature is my estimate, not the taxonomy default. The seed gives about 700 K for pure GeTe. Pb alloying and cation disorder both lower the rhombohedral-to-cubic transition, and pulling it down is the stated aim of the high-entropy approach, so 600 K is recorded with low confidence. The paper reports the real value and should replace it. The chunk printed no crossing line because this host carries no seed hypothesis. Ag at 5.5 and Pb at 6 atomic per cent are host elements with no dopant entries. Ag+ on the Ge2+ site is an acceptor, and Pb is isovalent with Ge and scatters phonons. No reference covers the host.

basis: PrAg2Ge2 is a ThCr2Si2-type 122 germanide, the Pr partner of NdAg2Ge2 in the same paper. [ref 2] ranks Pr(AgGe)2 in I4/mmm at mp-5564 first, hull 0.000, with 2 ICSD references.
note: Pr2AgGe6, Pr3(AgGe)4 and PrAgGe are other stoichiometries. Two ICSD references is weak by the chunk convention, but the entry matches the composition exactly.

basis: The composition string Ag9TITe5 is Ag9TlTe5 with a capital I typed for the lower-case l of thallium. The parser then read TI as tritium plus iodine, which is why H and I appear in the host key. Ag9TlTe5 is the known low-thermal-conductivity silver thallium telluride, and it was filed under tl5te3 in the Ag-Te-Tl host in chunk 004; the same prototype is used here for consistency.

dopant_roles.basis: T of Tl read as tritium.
The letter l of Tl typed as capital I and read as iodine.

note: Two things for review. First, this sample should route to the Ag-Te-Tl host once the formula is corrected; the parse error has put it in a host of its own. Second, I am not confident in the chunk-004 precedent. Ag9TlTe5 is usually described as having its own trigonal cell, not as a Tl5Te3 derivative, and I cannot confirm the structure from memory. That is why confidence is low and unresolved_crystalline is the alternative. There is no measured range, and the paper is about SnTe; the Ag9TlTe5 entry is probably a comparison value from its figure of merit plot.

basis: The paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of molten Bi2Te3, CuI, and AgI, and the measured window is 820-1050 K. AgI melts at about 831 K, so almost the whole window is liquid. Below the melt, AgI is in its alpha phase, the body-centred cubic superionic conductor that is the exemplar of bcc_superionic. The ionic melt is the proposed molten_salt, first used for molten KNO3.

other_polymorphs.note: beta-AgI, the ambient thermal phase, stable below about 420 K. It is part of the heating sequence but lies far below this window, so it is listed here and not in phases.
gamma-AgI, which coexists metastably with beta at room temperature. TEDesignLab lists this one.
Rocksalt AgI, reached only under pressure.

note: Disagrees with both references. TEDesignLab gives zincblende gamma-AgI and [ref 2] ranks wurtzite beta-AgI first; both are ambient solid phases that this measurement never reaches. They are kept as other_polymorphs with their mp_ids. The alpha phase has a disordered cation sublattice and no ordered MP entry; the Pm-3m AgI at mp-22915 is not it. Its phase therefore carries no mp_id. The melt, like CuI from the same paper in chunk 010, gets no crystal structure.

basis: PrInAg2 is a cubic Cu2MnAl-type full Heusler compound, Fm-3m, the RAg2In series. It is the well-known non-Kramers doublet heavy-fermion candidate, and the paper is on the non-enhancement of its low-temperature thermoelectric power.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. It offers only Pr2InAg, in P4/mmm (flagged AMBIGUOUS) and Fm-3m, with no ICSD reference for either. That is a different stoichiometry, a 2:1:1 compound in which Pr takes the Heusler X site. PrInAg2 has Ag on the X sites, so its mp_id is not borrowed and none is recorded.

basis: Ag3K2Mo15Se19 is K2Mo15Se19 with three silver atoms inserted, a single crystal from the paper on the beneficial influence of Ag insertion on its thermoelectric properties. Mo15Se19 compounds hold Mo6Se8 and Mo9Se11 cluster units in equal number. That is neither the Chevrel phase nor the Mo9Se11 entry proposed in chunk 012, so a new prototype was proposed.
note: Ag is 7.7 atomic per cent and so a host element, but its role is interstitial insertion into empty channel sites between the clusters. It adds electrons to the cluster states rather than substituting for K. Stage 3 should read it that way. Neither reference covers the host. Phases is left empty because the space group in the proposal is from memory and marked to be confirmed.

basis: Ag3LiRu2O6 is made from Li2RuO3 by exchanging the interlayer lithium for silver, as in the paper on interlayer tuning in honeycomb-ordered oxides. The honeycomb [LiRu2O6] layer of li2mo3_honeycomb is kept, but the silver sits in linear O-Ag-O dumbbells, a coordination that the li2mo3_honeycomb entry explicitly excludes. A new prototype was therefore proposed rather than stretching that one.
note: Li-O-Ru, the parent Li2RuO3, is under li2mo3_honeycomb from chunk 012. Li2RuO3 dimerises near 540 K; whether the Ag-exchanged compound keeps the Ru-Ru dimers is part of what the paper tests, so no transition is recorded in the 14-300 K window. Neither reference covers the host.

basis: The paper is on Mg2Si-based composites, and the one composition, Mg2SiAg7.5O2.5, is Mg2Si with a silver-and-oxygen additive. Mg2Si is the antifluorite, Fm-3m, and it is the matrix; the Ag and O are the added second phase that gives the composite its name.

dopant_roles.basis: Added as the composite second phase, probably as Ag or Ag2O. Some Ag may also enter Mg2Si as a p-type dopant on the Mg site, but at this loading most of it cannot be in the lattice.
Comes in with the additive, most likely as Ag2O or MgO; oxygen has no site in antifluorite Mg2Si.

note: Read literally, the formula makes Ag about 60 at.%, which cannot describe an Mg2Si-based composite. The indices are almost certainly weight or molar fractions of the additive that were parsed as a formula, so stage 3 should not compute an Ag doping level from them. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: Mn0.90Te0.95(Ag2S)0.05 is MnTe with Ag2S added, from a paper on enhanced thermoelectric performance of MnTe through doping and in-situ phases. MnTe is the hexagonal NiAs type, P6_3/mmc, the only MnTe polymorph stable at ambient pressure.

dopant_roles.basis: S from the Ag2S addition on the Te site is isovalent, so it adds no carriers. Some may instead stay in an Ag2S or Ag2Te in-situ second phase, which is what the paper title suggests.
Ag on the Mn site is the standard acceptor in MnTe. At about 5 at.% it falls just into the host by the split, but it is still acting as a dopant, partly in the lattice and partly as a precipitate.

note: The Mn0.90 index points to deliberate Mn deficiency, which is itself a p-type knob in MnTe. MnTe orders antiferromagnetically near 307 K, just below this 319-871 K window; that is magnetic, not structural. The NiAs-to-wurtzite change sits above 1300 K, well outside the window. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: The paper is on off-stoichiometric silver antimony telluride, and the Ag0.366Sb0.558Te part of the composition is Ag-poor, Sb-rich AgSbTe2. AgSbTe2 is a cation-disordered rocksalt, Fm-3m, with Ag and Sb sharing one site.

dopant_roles.basis: Ni0.02 is listed without explanation and the paper title does not mention it. It could be a dopant on the cation site or a contaminant; left unknown rather than guessed.

note: As parsed, the composition cannot be right. (Na2Se)1.005 makes Na and Se the majority elements, which contradicts a paper about AgSbTe2; the index is probably a misplaced fraction or dopant level. Confidence is low for that reason, not because of the prototype itself: if the sample is AgSbTe2-based, rocksalt is secure. Stage 2 must take the true composition from the paper. The Ag-poor ratio also points to Ag2Te or Sb2Te3 second phases, which are common in AgSbTe2. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: (Ag2O)15(PbO)35(V2O5)50 is a mol-per-cent glass batch, 50 per cent V2O5 with PbO and Ag2O modifiers, from a paper on thermopower in CdO- and Ag2O-containing vanadate glasses. It is a glass, not a crystalline phase.
note: Matches the O-Pb-V host, the PbO-V2O5 glasses, which is also amorphous. Conduction in these glasses is small-polaron hopping between V4+ and V5+, so there is no crystal structure for stage 2 to resolve. The 300-498 K window stays below the glass transition. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: AgRuO3, from a paper describing it as a strongly exchange-coupled honeycomb compound lacking long-range magnetic order. That places it in a layered structure built on honeycomb Ru-O layers with Ag between them. No existing entry matches it, and I cannot state its space group reliably enough to propose a prototype.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its AgRuO3 line is Fd-3m (227) at mp-776168, hull 0.056, with no ICSD reference: a computed cubic cell, and a cubic cell cannot be the honeycomb-layered compound in the paper title. It is therefore not recorded as the structure. Ag3RuO4 and AgRuO4, the other lines, are different compounds. li2mo3_honeycomb and ag3lim2o6_honeycomb both have honeycomb Ru layers but different stoichiometry and interlayer; they are the nearest entries. Once the space group is read from the paper, a prototype can be proposed; the measured window of 13-324 K is magnetic physics.

basis: Ag0.20TiO2 from a paper on Ag nanoparticles embedded in Nb-doped TiO2 nanobulk: TiO2 is the matrix and Ag is dispersed metal, not a lattice species. Rutile is taken for the matrix because a sintered TiO2 bulk measured up to 1042 K should end up as rutile; anatase nanopowder converts irreversibly above roughly 900 K.

dopant_roles.basis: Embedded metallic Ag nanoparticles, as the paper title says. At about 6 at.% Ag falls into the host by the split, but it is a dispersed phase, not in the TiO2 lattice.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. It lists TiAg2O3 in C2/c (mp-29160, 1 ICSD) and Ti4Ag2O9 in C2/m, which are ternary silver titanates, not a TiO2 matrix with metallic Ag, so neither is recorded. The composition carries no Nb, so this sample is probably the undoped Ag-TiO2 reference. If the nanobulk was sintered at low temperature it may still be anatase, and the anatase-to-rutile conversion would then happen during the measurement. That change is irreversible and kinetic, so it is not a thermal phase; it is noted here rather than put in phases. Needs the XRD from the paper.

basis: (AgSbTe2)0.2(Pb0.5Sn0.5Te)0.8 is a pseudobinary of two rocksalt tellurides: AgSbTe2, a cation-disordered rocksalt, and the PbTe-SnTe solid solution. Ag, Sb, Pb and Sn share the cation site of one Fm-3m lattice. The paper studies p-type (AgSbTe2)x(Pb0.5Sn0.5Te)1-x.
note: A LAST-type (lead-antimony-silver-tellurium) system with Sn replacing half the Pb; every element is at host level, so there are no dopant roles. Pb and Sn share the cation site at x = 0.5. The chunk file prints no axis for this host, so solid_solution_axis is left null. Nanoscale Ag-Sb-rich regions are typical of LAST materials but do not change the prototype. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: Ag8SnS6 is canfieldite, the sulfide argyrodite: orthorhombic Pna2_1 at room temperature, disordering to the cubic F-43m superionic phase on heating. [ref 2] gives Ag8SnS6 Pna2_1 at mp-15645, hull 0.000.
note: The cited paper (d0ra10454j) is titled for Ag8SnSe6 and is the same paper filed under the Ag-Se-Sn host; its selenide is also an argyrodite. So either the paper also reports the sulfide, or Se was transcribed as S; stage 2 should check. The prototype is the same either way, but the transition is not: about 330 K for the selenide against roughly 445 K for the sulfide. No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line is printed, because the taxonomy default of 330 K comes from Ag8GeSe6. The 445 K figure is from general knowledge of Ag8SnS6 and is approximate. The mp_id rests on a single ICSD reference, flagged weak. [ref 2] ranks Ag4Sn3S8 in P4_132 (10 ICSD) first, but that is a different compound, so it is not a disagreement. No mp_id is offered for the cubic phase.

basis: Ag2ZnSnSe4 is the silver analogue of Cu2ZnSnSe4, from a paper on nanostructured stannite Cu2ZnSnSe4 and Ag2ZnSnSe4. It is a cation-ordered tetragonal zincblende derivative, and [ref 2] gives it as stannite, I-42m, at mp-1093995, hull 0.010.
note: Stannite (I-42m) and kesterite (I-4) differ only in how the cations order, and both fall under one prototype. Ag2ZnSnSe4 is often reported as kesterite, so the space group should be checked against the paper, but the prototype does not change. The MP entry shows no ICSD count.

basis: Ag8SiTe6, from the paper introducing it as a new thermoelectric with low thermal conductivity. It is the silicon telluride member of the argyrodite family, alongside Ag8GeTe6 and Ag8SnSe6: an SiTe4 tetrahedral framework with mobile Ag.
note: To my knowledge Ag8SiTe6 is already cubic F-43m at room temperature, with its Ag-ordering transition below 300 K, so the 301-799 K window stays in one phase. That should be confirmed from the paper: if the ordering temperature is above 301 K, this host needs a second phase like Ag-Se-Sn. Neither reference printed a line for this host, so no mp_id.

basis: CeAuAl, from a paper on the magnetism of the Kondo compound CeAuAl. The equiatomic rare-earth gold aluminide takes the orthorhombic TiNiSi structure, Pnma, and [ref 2] ranks CeAlAu Pnma first at mp-1102423, hull 0.000, on 2 ICSD references.

other_polymorphs.note: CeAlAu in P6_3/mmc, hull 0.001, 1 ICSD reference. A hexagonal polymorph of the same formula with less support than Pnma; not reached by heating within this window.

note: The Pnma entry rests on 2 ICSD references, which the chunk convention flags as weak, but it is the best-attested line for this formula and matches the expected type. The other Ce-Al-Au lines, CeAl3Au, Ce(AlAu)2 and CeAl7Au3, are different stoichiometries. Any magnetic order in CeAuAl is at a few kelvin, inside the 11-201 K window only at its lower edge, and is not structural.

basis: CeAuAl4Ge2, from a paper on electronic structure and magnetism in the layered triangular-lattice compound. [ref 2] gives exactly this formula in R-3m at mp-12017, hull 0.000. No existing entry has rhombohedral rare-earth triangular planes separated by Au-Al-Ge slabs, so a prototype was proposed.
note: The 5th-95th percentile window is only 11-19 K because two curves are low-temperature only; the full span reaches 305 K. The MP entry shows no ICSD count, but the formula match is exact and there is no competing line.

basis: The paper is on positive ionic conduction in a composite of mayenite cement, Ca12Al14O33, with nano-carbon. The parsed composition, Ca0.078Al0.068C0.024B0.027, has lost the oxygen entirely: Ca and Al are the mayenite, and C is the carbon phase. That is a two-phase composite, not one structure.
note: Two problems with the composition. First, O is missing, so no ratio in it can be trusted. Second, the B is unexplained. The title is cut off at nano-carbon b..., which may read carbon black, in which case the B could be a parsing artefact from that word rather than boron; or boron may be a real additive. Neither can be settled without the paper. Ca and Al map to mayenite, which already has an entry (the Al-Ca-O host), and the carbon to graphite_layered as the nearest entry for a nano-carbon. Measured 295-974 K; the property of interest is ionic conduction, not electronic thermoelectric transport. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: AlMgB14, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of metal borides, is the exemplar of its own entry: B12 icosahedra with Al and Mg partly occupying the voids, orthorhombic Imma.

other_polymorphs.note: Mg(AlB14)2 in Cm, hull 0.031, no ICSD reference: a computed ordering of the partly occupied metal sites into a supercell, not the Imma structure itself.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2] in part. Its closest line, Mg(AlB14)2 in Cm, halves the Mg content to make the partial occupancy periodic. It is the same framework, but it is a model ordering rather than the reported Imma cell, so it is recorded under other_polymorphs rather than as the phase. The other lines, Mg4AlB10, MgAlB4, Mg14AlB and Mg6AlB, are unrelated stoichiometries. Real AlMgB14 is metal-deficient, closer to Al0.75Mg0.78B14, and that deficiency sets its carrier concentration.

basis: BaAl4 single crystal, from a paper on Fermi surfaces and charge density waves in SrAl4 and related compounds. BaAl4 is the aristotype of baal4_type itself, I4/mmm, and [ref 2] ranks it first at mp-1903, hull 0.000, on 3 ICSD references.
note: SrAl4 has a charge-density-wave transition near 243 K; BaAl4, as far as I know, has none and is the comparison compound in the paper, so no phase split is recorded. Consistency issue for review: the Al-Sr host (SrAl4) was filed under thcr2si2_122 before baal4_type was proposed in chunk 035, while the binaries Al-Eu and Eu-Ga use baal4_type. Binary AB4 compounds of this cell should all be in one place. Ba4Al5, Ba3Al5, BaAl2 and Ba7Al13 are other compounds of the chemistry, not polymorphs of BaAl4.

basis: BaCuAlP2 single crystal, from a 2024 paper on the semiconducting BaCuTP2 family (T = Al, Ga, In). I do not know this structure type well enough to assign it, and neither reference covers the host, so it is left unresolved rather than guessed.
note: Charge balance, Ba2+ Cu+ Al3+ and two P3-, makes it a valence-precise Zintl-like phosphide, and tetrahedral Cu and Al coordination is likely. That does not pin down a prototype, though: it could be one of the layered Zintl types or something new. The paper title is truncated at a semiconducting bl..., which may describe the structural motif. Read the paper, then propose a prototype. The measured window is wide, 12-823 K.

basis: BaFe0.7Al0.3O3 is BaFeO3-delta with 30 per cent Al on the Fe site, from a paper on the synthesis and structural characterisation of BaFe1-xAlxO3. BaFeO3-delta made in air is normally a hexagonal perovskite polytype, 6H or 12H, because the large Ba cation favours face-sharing octahedra.

dopant_roles.basis: BaFe1-xAlxO3 at x = 0.3: Al3+ on the B site. At 6 at.% it falls into the host by the split, but it is still a B-site substituent, and it is the variable the paper studies.

note: Confidence is low because B-site substitution can switch BaFeO3-delta between the hexagonal polytypes and a cubic or pseudo-cubic perovskite, and which one forms at x = 0.3 depends on the synthesis atmosphere; the paper title promises the structural answer. perovskite is listed as the alternative. The O3 in the formula is nominal; the real oxygen content is lower and changes with temperature over the 298-773 K window. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: Ba6Gd2Al4O15, from a paper on the thermophysical properties of rare-earth barium aluminates, which are studied as thermal-barrier ceramics. I cannot place the Ba6RE2Al4O15 structure family with confidence, so no prototype is assigned. The same paper supplies the Al-Ba-O-Yb host.
note: [ref 2] has this exact formula, Ba6Gd2Al4O15 in P2/c at mp-1214682, hull 0.000, but shows no ICSD count, so it may be a computed ordering rather than the reported cell. It is recorded as a low-confidence candidate, not adopted as the structure. My recollection is that this family has been reported as hexagonal, which would conflict with a monoclinic P2/c; that is not certain enough to override the reference, so the conflict is flagged here for review rather than resolved. Ba5Gd2ZrAl2O13, the other line, is a Zr-containing compound and not this sample. If the paper confirms one cell for both Ba6Gd2Al4O15 and Ba6Yb2Al4O15, a prototype should be proposed for the pair.

basis: Ba5AlIr2O11 single crystal, from a paper on coexisting charge and magnetic orders in the dimer-chain iridate. Chains of face-sharing Ir2O9 dimers linked by AlO4 tetrahedra match no existing entry, so a prototype was proposed. [ref 2] gives the exact formula in Pnma at mp-21742, hull 0.000.

other_polymorphs.note: Ba4Al(IrO5)2 in Cmc2_1, hull 0.030, no ICSD reference: a computed variant, not the reported cell.

note: Confidence is medium, not high, for two reasons: the Pnma entry rests on a single ICSD reference, and the charge order near 210 K, inside the 79-739 K window, is reported to come with a subtle lattice distortion. If the paper shows a symmetry change there, a low-temperature phase belongs in phases. It is not added now because its space group is not known. The magnetic order is at a few kelvin, below the window.

basis: Ba6Yb2Al4O15, from the same paper on rare-earth barium aluminates as the Al-Ba-Gd-O host, and the Yb member of the same Ba6RE2Al4O15 family. It is left unresolved for the same reason: I cannot place the structure with confidence.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line, Ba5Yb2ZrAl2O13 in P6_3/mmc (mp-1214540), contains Zr and is a different compound, so no mp_id is recorded. The Gd analogue has an exact-formula MP entry in P2/c; if the family is isostructural this host would follow it, but that is an inference, not a reference, so it is not copied here.

basis: [(Bi4Te4Br2)(Al2Cl5.46Br0.54)]Cl2, from a paper on semiconducting cationic bismuth chalcogenide halides with chloroaluminate counter-anions. A cationic Bi-Te-Br framework holds Al2Cl6-type and Cl- anions in large low-symmetry cells, which is the one-compound-one-structure situation bi_chalcogenide_complex exists for. [ref 2] has the same compound, AlBi2Te2BrCl4, which is the formula halved, in C2/c at mp-1200931.
note: The fit to bi_chalcogenide_complex is loose. That entry was written for alkali bismuth chalcogenides such as K2Bi8Se13, and this is a halide salt with a cationic chalcogenide framework, so medium confidence. If more cationic Bi chalcogenide halides turn up, they would deserve their own entry. The MP line is Br/Cl-ordered, whereas the sample has mixed Br/Cl on the aluminate anion; it rests on 1 ICSD reference, flagged weak. The P1 line (mp-1229275) is a computed variant with no ICSD reference.

basis: The curator detail reads 3wt% r-Al2O3/Bi0.4Sb1.6Te3, and the paper is on alumina-dispersed Bi0.4Sb1.6Te3 nanocomposites. The matrix is the p-type Bi-Sb-Te tetradymite alloy, R-3m, and the alumina is a dispersed second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Present as dispersed Al2O3 nanoparticles, which is the point of the paper. The parsed (Al2O3)0.2 lifts Al above 5 at.%, but that comes from treating 3 wt% as a formula index.
Belongs to the Al2O3 dispersoid, not the telluride lattice.

note: Follows the Co-O-Sb precedent, where oxide dispersions in a skutterudite kept the matrix prototype. Bi and Sb share the cation site at Bi/(Bi+Sb) = 0.2, the usual p-type composition. Stage 3 should use the curator weight fraction, not the parsed index, for any Al2O3 content. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: (Al2Te3)0.2(Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3)0.8 is the standard p-type Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 tetradymite alloy, R-3m, with Al2Te3 added. The paper does a crystal-structure analysis of it as a p-type pseudo-ternary, which treats Al2Te3 as a component of the tetradymite rather than a separate phase.

dopant_roles.basis: The pseudo-ternary framing puts Al3+ on the Bi/Sb site. Al is much smaller than Sb, though, and 20 mol per cent Al2Te3 is far beyond what would normally dissolve, so part is probably a separate Al2Te3 phase. Low confidence until the paper structure analysis is read.

note: Medium confidence because the Al solubility is unclear: the matrix is certainly tetradymite, but the sample may be tetradymite plus Al2Te3 rather than a single phase. Al2Te3 is monoclinic, and composite_multiphase would be the alternative if the paper shows it as a separate phase. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: AlCCo3 is the Co3AlC anti-perovskite: C at the octahedral centre, Co at the face centres, Al at the corners, Pm-3m. [ref 2] gives exactly that at mp-10037, hull 0.019. The paper is on good thermoelectric performance in the strongly correlated SnCCo3, and AlCCo3 is its Al analogue.
note: The MP entry rests on one ICSD reference, flagged weak, but it matches formula and type exactly. C occupancy in these antiperovskite carbides is often below 1, and that is the main source of sample-to-sample variation.

basis: Cr2AlC is a 211 MAX phase, M2AX with M = Cr, A = Al and X = C, hexagonal P6_3/mmc. [ref 2] gives exactly that at mp-9956, hull 0.000. The paper is on how Cr7C3 inclusions affect the properties of Cr2AlC.
note: Cr7C3 is a deliberate or incidental second phase in the paper. The composition printed is stoichiometric Cr2AlC, so it is noted here rather than recorded as a role. The MAX phase is stable across the whole 474-1473 K window; it decomposes only well above it. max_phase_mn1axn is still a pending proposal from an earlier chunk.

basis: AlC1.1Fe3 is Fe3AlC, the kappa-carbide anti-perovskite, Pm-3m, with C at the body centre of an Fe6 octahedron. [ref 2] gives AlFe3C at mp-22793, hull 0.000, on 2 ICSD references. The paper is on its structural, magnetic and transport properties.
note: C1.1 is above the single site the structure has for carbon, so the excess is either a nominal starting ratio or free graphite; it is not interstitial carbon in the antiperovskite. Fe3AlC is ferromagnetic well above room temperature, so its magnetic order lies outside the 10-334 K window.

basis: AlCNi3 is Ni3AlC, the anti-perovskite, Pm-3m, from a paper on strong spin fluctuations and possible non-Fermi-liquid behaviour in it. It is the itinerant nearly-ferromagnetic sibling of MgCNi3.
note: Partly disagrees with [ref 2]. Its AlNi3C Pm-3m line, mp-1207084, is the right structure, but it sits at hull 0.168 with no ICSD reference, and [ref 2] ranks two P4/mmm lines, Al3Ni9C and Al4Ni12C, ahead of it. Those are computed carbon-deficient orderings of the same cell, not this composition. The Pm-3m entry is recorded because it matches formula and type, but at medium confidence on the phase since the high hull suggests MP is not describing the real compound well.

basis: YAl3C3 is named as a representative material of zrc_al3c2_homologous, the layered (MC)nAl3C2 aluminium carbides, and the paper is on its crystal structure and thermoelectric properties. [ref 2] gives Y(AlC)3 in P6_3/mmc at mp-1104050, hull 0.000, on 1 ICSD reference.
note: Space-group mismatch with the taxonomy, not with the prototype. The entry gives P6_3mc (186), the space group of the Zr and Hf members, while YAl3C3, the ScAl3C3 type, is P6_3/mmc (194) here. The taxonomy should list both. The MP line rests on one ICSD reference, flagged weak. Y3AlC, Y3AlC3 and Y5Al3C4 are other compounds of the chemistry. No structural transition is known to me inside the 350-1049 K window.

basis: CuAl0.8Ca0.2O2 is delafossite CuAlO2, R-3m, with 20 per cent Ca on the Al site, from a paper on how partial substitution of Ca for Al affects CuAlO2.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca2+ for Al3+ on the octahedral B site is a nominal acceptor and is the variable in the paper. Ca2+ is far larger than Al3+, though, so at x = 0.2 much of it probably ends up as CaAl2O4 or another second phase; the title mentions effects on the microstructure. At 5 at.% it sits on the host boundary.

note: CuAlO2 delafossite is stable across the 540-1141 K window in air. Some papers report the 2H polytype, P6_3/mmc; both are the delafossite prototype. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: Ca4NaAl2Sb6 is Ca5Al2Sb6 with one Ca in five replaced by Na, from the paper that introduced Ca5Al2Sb6 as a low-cost Zintl thermoelectric. Ca5Al2Sb6 is the eponym of zintl_5_2_6, orthorhombic Pbam, with chains of corner-sharing AlSb4 tetrahedra.

dopant_roles.basis: Na+ on the Ca2+ site is the p-type dopant used in Ca5Al2Sb6. At 1 in 13 atoms it falls into the host by the split, but it is still a dopant.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line, Na3Ca3AlSb4 in P6_3mc (mp-1190339), is a different, Na-rich compound and does not describe Na-doped Ca5Al2Sb6, so no mp_id is recorded. Stage 2 should resolve against Ca5Al2Sb6, Pbam. A nominal Na1 is a heavy substitution for this family, so the paper should be checked for a secondary phase, and to confirm that the index is not a transcription of a much smaller x.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [55], ICSD-backed references for this host report [186]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CeFe1.7Ir0.3Al10 is CeFe2Al10 with 15 per cent Ir on the Fe site. CeFe2Al10 is a member of the orthorhombic YbFe2Al10 cage family, Cmcm, alongside CeRu2Al10 and CeOs2Al10. [ref 2] gives Ce(Al5Fe)2, i.e. CeFe2Al10, in Cmcm at mp-1193938, hull 0.000.

dopant_roles.basis: Ir from group 9 on the group-8 Fe site adds one electron per substitution and tunes the Kondo semiconducting gap of CeFe2Al10. The paper combines transport with Moessbauer spectroscopy, which probes the Fe site directly.

note: [ref 2] ranks CeFe2Al8 in Pbam (4 ICSD) and CeFe4Al8 in I4/mmm (3 ICSD) above CeFe2Al10. Those are different compounds of the chemistry, not competing structures for this composition, so there is no disagreement. The CeFe2Al10 line rests on one ICSD reference, flagged weak.

basis: Ce0.5La0.5Al2Ga2 is CeAl2Ga2 with half the Ce replaced by La. It comes from the same paper on antiferromagnetism in Ce1-xLaxAl2Ga2 (PRB 43, 3204) as the Al-Ce-Ga host, which was assigned thcr2si2_122 in chunk 017: the body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm cell with Al and Ga sharing the X2 layers.

dopant_roles.basis: La3+ for Ce3+ with no 4f electron, diluting the Kondo lattice without changing the carrier count. At x = 0.5 it is 10 at.%, which is why this composition split off from Al-Ce-Ga into its own host.

note: No reference printed a line for this host. The Al-Ce-Ga record cites CeAl2Ga2 at mp-3303, but that is the parent compound and is not copied onto this host. Stage 2 can resolve it from there.

basis: Ce0.7Y0.3Al2Ga2 is CeAl2Ga2 with 30 per cent Y on the Ce site. It comes from the same paper on Ce1-yYyAl2Ga2 (PRB 43, 3204) as the Al-Ce-Ga host, which is filed under thcr2si2_122, I4/mmm.

dopant_roles.basis: Y3+ for Ce3+, a non-magnetic and smaller trivalent ion. Unlike La, it compresses the lattice, applying chemical pressure to the Kondo lattice as well as diluting it. At y = 0.3 it is 6 at.%, which puts it in the host.

note: No reference printed a line for this host. The parent CeAl2Ga2 is at mp-3303 on the Al-Ce-Ga record; it is not copied here.

basis: Ce0.5La0.5Al3, from a paper on crystal-field effects on the Kondo effect in cerium alloys. CeAl3, the archetypal heavy fermion, and LaAl3 are both hexagonal Ni3Sn-type D0_19, P6_3/mmc, so the La-Ce solid solution keeps that cell.

dopant_roles.basis: La3+ for Ce3+ at x = 0.5, a Kondo-lattice dilution series.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line, LaCeAl4 in F-43m (mp-1222920, hull 0.015, no ICSD reference), is a computed ordered AB4 cell of a different stoichiometry and not the Ni3Sn-type CeAl3/LaAl3, so no mp_id is recorded. Stage 2 should resolve against CeAl3 P6_3/mmc.

basis: CeOs2Al10 is one of the three CeT2Al10 Kondo semiconductors (T = Fe, Ru, Os), all in the orthorhombic YbFe2Al10 cage structure, Cmcm. The paper covers its transport, thermoelectric and thermal expansion behaviour.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line, Ce3(Al3Os)4 in P6_3/mmc (mp-1213926, no ICSD reference), is a different compound, so no mp_id is recorded. CeOs2Al10 orders antiferromagnetically at about 28.5 K, inside the 10-297 K window, with an anomalously high ordering temperature; a structural component such as dimerisation was once proposed for it. No symmetry change is recorded here; the thermal expansion data in this paper is the place to check.

basis: Co2CrAl is an L2_1 full Heusler, Fm-3m, from a paper on the structural and thermoelectric properties of ternary full-Heusler alloys. [ref 2] gives it at mp-10883, hull 0.071.
note: Co2CrAl is known for Cr-Al antisite disorder, and bulk samples are often partly B2 rather than fully L2_1. That is a degree of order within the same prototype, and the diffraction in the paper would say which. The MP entry rests on one ICSD reference with hull 0.071, consistent with a compound that is only marginally stable when ordered. Its Curie temperature, about 330 K, is inside the window but is magnetic, not structural.

basis: Ho(Co0.9Al0.1)2 is HoCo2 with 10 per cent Al on the Co site, from a paper on static and dynamic disorder in RCo2 compounds. HoCo2 is a cubic C15 MgCu2-type Laves phase, Fd-3m, and Al substitution in RCo2 keeps that cell.

dopant_roles.basis: Al on the Co site of the C15 cell, the classic way to tune itinerant Co magnetism in RCo2. At 6.7 at.% it falls into the host, but it is the variable in the paper.

note: HoCo2 orders ferrimagnetically near 78 K, inside the 16-297 K window, with a small magnetostrictive distortion of the cubic cell. Al substitution raises the ordering temperature and softens the transition. That is a magnetoelastic distortion within the Laves prototype, not a change of structure type, so no second phase is recorded. Disagrees with [ref 2]: Ho2Al3Co14 and HoAlCo are different compounds, so no mp_id.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [194]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The curator detail reads Ti2-x-yAlxTayNiCoSn0.5Sb1.5, from a paper on entropy engineering in the off-stoichiometric Ti2NiCoSnSb double half-Heusler. Ti2NiCoSnSb is TiNiSn and TiCoSb combined on one F-43m half-Heusler lattice, with Al and Ta then put on the Ti site.

dopant_roles.basis: Written as Ti2-x-yAlx in the curator formula, so Al is on the Ti site. As a trivalent ion replacing Ti4+ it also shifts the electron count. It is a host-level component at about 13 at.%.
Written as Ti2-x-yTay, a heavy group-5 metal on the Ti site for mass-disorder phonon scattering, the entropy-engineering lever. Host-level at about 13 at.%.

note: The Ti site is shared by Ti, Al and Ta in roughly equal parts, so this is a high-entropy half-Heusler, but the lattice is still a single half-Heusler phase and high_entropy_alloy, an entry for disordered simple metals, would be the wrong label. Ni and Co share the tetrahedral site and Sn and Sb the anion site. Full-Heusler interstitial filling by excess Ni or Co is common in these off-stoichiometric compositions. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: The curator detail reads Ti2-x-y-qAlxTayZrqNiCoSn0.5Sb1.5, from the same entropy-engineering paper on off-stoichiometric Ti2NiCoSnSb as the Al-Co-Ni-Sb-Sn-Ta-Ti host. This is the four-cation version, with Ti, Al, Ta and Zr sharing the F-43m half-Heusler Ti site.

dopant_roles.basis: Written as Ti2-x-y-qAlx. Trivalent Al on the Ti site, host-level at about 10 at.%.
Written as Ti2-x-y-qTay. Mass disorder on the Ti site, host-level at about 10 at.%.
Zr is isovalent with Ti in group 4. It is the standard half-Heusler Ti-site alloying element and adds strain and mass disorder, not carriers.

note: Filed separately from its sister host only because Zr adds an element. The prototype and the paper are the same, and the reasoning against high_entropy_alloy is the same: the lattice is ordered half-Heusler, and the entropy sits on one sublattice. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: CoSi0.88Al0.12 is CoSi with 12 per cent Al on the Si site, from a paper on the effects of Al doping on the thermoelectric performance of CoSi single crystals. CoSi is the cubic B20 FeSi type, P2_13.

dopant_roles.basis: Al on the Si site is an acceptor in the CoSi semimetal and is the variable in the paper. At 6 at.% it falls into the host by the split.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Every line it prints is a different ternary, Al14Co5Si2, Al(CoSi)2, Al3Co3Si4 and AlCo2Si, none of them CoSi with Al on the Si site, so no mp_id is recorded. Stage 2 should resolve against B20 CoSi.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [198], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62, 164]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: UCu3Cr2Al7, from a paper on specific heat and thermopower in UCu3M2Al7 alloys, is a member of the UT4Al8 family: 1 U to 12 transition-metal and Al atoms, which is the ThMn12 stoichiometry. UCu4Al8 is the ThMn12 type, I4/mmm, with the transition metal on the 8f site and Al on 8i and 8j; here Cr takes part of the Cu share.
note: Here the transition-metal count is 5 (Cu3 plus Cr2) against 7 Al, so one transition-metal atom must sit on an Al site, beyond the usual T4Al8 split. The ThMn12 cell accommodates that; the Fe analogue UCu3.5Fe1.5Al7 is the next host but one and comes from the same paper. Neither reference printed a line for this host.

basis: Al74.5Cr18.2Fe7.3 is from a paper on the magnetic, electrical and thermal transport properties of Al-Cr-Fe approximants. That composition sits in the Al-rich Al-Cr-Fe region where orthorhombic decagonal approximants form, which is what quasicrystal_approximant covers.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its top lines are AlCrFe2 in Fm-3m, a Heusler at 25 per cent Al, and Al119Cr16Fe13 in Cm, neither of which is an approximant at this 74.5 per cent Al composition. Al2CrFe at hull 2.674 is unphysical. So no mp_id is recorded. Medium confidence because the paper title does not say which approximant: the Al-Cr-Fe system has several orthorhombic and monoclinic decagonal approximants, and stage 2 must map to one explicitly and say so.

basis: Al60Cr19.9Fe0.1Ge20 is the subject of a paper titled Physical properties of the icosahedral quasicrystal Al60Cr19.9Fe0.1Ge20. It is an icosahedral phase, aperiodic, which the quasicrystal_approximant entry covers along with its periodic approximants.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.1 against Cr19.9 in the formula, so it is written on the transition-metal share. At 0.1 at.% it is most likely a deliberate trace, possibly a Moessbauer probe, rather than a carrier dopant; a quasicrystal has no crystallographic site for it.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line, AlCrGe in F222 (mp-1228945, no ICSD reference), is a computed periodic equiatomic cell and not the Al-rich icosahedral phase, so no mp_id is recorded. Being aperiodic, it has no MP structure; stage 2 must map it to an approximant and say so.

basis: (Al2O3)90.06(Cr3C2)9.94 is an alumina and chromium carbide composite from a paper on heat conduction of composites and its dependence on the microstructure. That is the same paper as the Al-C-Cr-O host, whose higher-carbide compositions were filed as composite_multiphase in chunk 031. At 10 per cent carbide the parse dropped C below 5 at.%, which is why this composition landed in an oxide-looking host.

dopant_roles.basis: The carbon belongs to the Cr3C2 second phase, not to alumina. It is not a dopant of either constituent.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. It lists Al-Cr mixed oxides, Al2Cr4O19, Al19CrO30, Al2CrO5, Al3CrO6 and AlCr2O4, several flagged ambiguous, and none of them is a two-phase alumina/carbide ceramic. No mp_id is recorded. Stage 2 should send the constituents to corundum and cr3c2_orthorhombic, as for Al-C-Cr-O. This is a thermal-conductivity study, not a thermoelectric one.

basis: Cr(Si0.92Al0.08)2 is CrSi2 with 8 per cent of the Si replaced by Al, from a paper on the effects of Al doping on transport in CrSi2 single crystals. CrSi2 is the hexagonal C40 disilicide, P6_222.

dopant_roles.basis: Al on the Si site is an acceptor in the narrow-gap CrSi2 semiconductor and is the variable in the paper. At 5.3 at.% it falls into the host by the split.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Every line it prints is a different ternary, Al3Cr20Si9, Al8Cr4Si3, Al9Cr3Si and AlCr6Si, none of them CrSi2 with Al on the Si site. No mp_id is recorded, and stage 2 should resolve against C40 CrSi2.

basis: Cs7.9Al7.9Si38.1 is the type-I clathrate Cs8Al8Si38, Pm-3n, from a paper on a combined metal-halide/metal flux route to type-I clathrates. Cs fills the cages and Al replaces Si in the framework, close to the electron-precise Zintl count of 8 Al for 8 Cs.

dopant_roles.basis: Guest in the 20- and 24-atom Si cages. At 7.9 of 8 it is essentially full, and it is host-level.
Al3+ in the tetrahedral framework, each accepting the electron donated by one Cs. At 7.9 per formula unit it nearly balances the Cs count, which sets the carrier concentration.

note: Neither reference printed a line for this host. A slight excess of Cs over Al leaves a small electron surplus, so the sample should be weakly n-type.

basis: UCu3.5Fe1.5Al7, from the same paper on UCu3M2Al7-type alloys as the Al-Cr-Cu-U host. It has 1 U to 12 transition-metal and Al atoms, the ThMn12 I4/mmm stoichiometry of UCu4Al8 and UFe4Al8, both of which take that type.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, UAl7Fe3Cu2 in Cm and UAl8(FeCu)2 in Immm, have no ICSD reference and are computed site orderings of related stoichiometries in low-symmetry supercells, not the disordered ThMn12 cell. No mp_id is recorded. UFe4Al8 orders magnetically, so Fe content can bring magnetic transitions into the 12-299 K window; they are not structural.

basis: Cu3Al0.5Ga0.5SnS5, from a paper on Ga substitution in Cu3Al1-xGaxSnS5 nanobulk. By charge count, Cu+ times 3, a trivalent (Al,Ga) and Sn4+ make 10 positive charges against five S2-, with cations equal to anions. That is an adamantine, tetrahedrally bonded zincblende-derived compound; sphalerite is taken as the parent, with the cations probably disordered in a nanobulk.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga3+ for Al3+, same group and valence, so no carriers are added. It is the variable in the paper, at half the site here, and is host-level at 5 at.%.

note: Low confidence on the specific cell. The charge count and 1:1 cation-to-anion ratio fix a tetrahedral zincblende or wurtzite derivative. Nanocrystal routes to Cu-based multinary sulfides often give wurtzite-derived or cation-disordered cubic phases, and an ordered tetragonal superstructure is also possible. I do not know which the paper reports, and the chunk has no reference to test against, so the alternatives are listed. Stage 2 must take the space group from the XRD.

basis: Al55.0Li35.8Cu9.2 is the icosahedral T2 phase near Al6CuLi3, from a paper on electronic properties of the single-grained icosahedral phase of Al-Li-Cu. It is aperiodic, and quasicrystal_approximant covers it.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, Li4(AlCu2)3, Li6Al13Cu8, LiAl2Cu and LiAlCu2 (all without ICSD references), are periodic computed phases of other stoichiometries and not the icosahedral phase, so no mp_id is recorded. The natural approximant for stage 2 is the cubic R phase, Al5CuLi3 in Im-3, which is close in composition. Measured only at 10-15 K.

basis: Al5Cu6Mg2 is the V phase of the Al-Cu-Mg system, from a paper on the physical properties of the V-Al5Cu6Mg2 complex intermetallic phase. It is the ordered ternary of the cubic Mg2Zn11 type, Pm-3, and [ref 2] gives Mg2Al5Cu6 in exactly Pm-3 at mp-30178, hull 0.000. No existing entry covers the type, so mg2zn11_type was proposed.
note: [ref 2] ranks MgAl2Cu in Cmcm first for the chemistry (mp-3034, 3 ICSD). That is the S phase, a different compound, so it is not a disagreement. The Pm-3 line rests on one ICSD reference, flagged weak, but it matches formula and space group exactly. The paper calls this a complex metallic alloy; it is periodic, not quasicrystalline, which is why it was not filed under quasicrystal_approximant.

basis: CuAl0.8Mg0.2O2 is delafossite CuAlO2 with Mg on the Al site, from a paper on the microstructure and high-temperature thermoelectric properties of polycrystalline CuAlO2 ceramics. The Cu+ O-Cu-O dumbbells between edge-sharing AlO6 layers fix the prototype.

dopant_roles.site: octahedral B site
dopant_roles.basis: Mg2+ for Al3+ is the usual acceptor in CuAlO2, adding holes. At 0.2 per formula unit it is 5 at.% and host-level by the split, but its role is still a dopant.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. All four of its lines, Mg14AlCuO16, Mg30AlCuO32, Mg6AlCuO8, are Mg-rich rocksalt MgO supercells with no ICSD references and describe a different region of the chemistry, not CuAlO2. No mp_id is taken from them. Stage 2 should resolve CuAlO2 R-3m directly. A spinel CuAl2O4 or MgAl2O4 secondary phase is common in Mg-doped CuAlO2 and may be present.

basis: Cu2MnAl is the textbook L21 full-Heusler ferromagnet, from a paper on the transport properties of Heusler alloys as ideal local-moment ferromagnets. [ref 2] agrees: MnAlCu2 in Fm-3m, mp-905565, 12 ICSD references.
note: Cu2MnAl is metastable at room temperature and decomposes on long anneals, but it is retained by quenching and the measurement is below 300 K.

basis: UCu3Mn2Al7 is a member of the U(Cu,M)5Al7 series, from a paper on the low-temperature specific heat and thermopower of UCu3M2Al7 alloys. UCu4Al8 and UCu5Al7 take the ThMn12 type, I4/mmm, with Cu and Al sharing the 8j and 8f sites, and Mn replaces part of the Cu.
note: No structure reference in the chunk. Medium rather than high because the ThMn12 assignment of the Mn-substituted member is inferred from the UCu5Al7 parent and has not been checked against the paper.

basis: Al65Cu20Os15 is an icosahedral quasicrystal, from a paper titled Electrical Transport Properties of Al-Cu-Os Icosahedral Quasicrystal. It is aperiodic and quasicrystal_approximant covers it.
note: Isostructural with the Al65Cu20Fe15 and Al65Cu20Ru15 icosahedral phases. No structure reference in the chunk; stage 2 must map to an approximant and say so.

basis: DyFe5Al7 is a ThMn12-type RFexAl12-x compound, from a paper on the magnetic and magnetotransport behaviour of RFe5Al7 (R = Gd, Dy). [ref 2] gives the Fe4Al8 member of the same type, Dy(Al2Fe)4 in I4/mmm, mp-5091, hull 0.000, 6 ICSD references, as PRIMARY.
note: The mp_id is for DyFe4Al8, the ordered end member, not DyFe5Al7. The extra Fe goes onto the 8j site mixed with Al, which a periodic MP cell cannot represent exactly. The magnetic transitions in this paper are not structural.

basis: ErAl2 is a cubic C15 MgCu2-type Laves phase, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of REAl2 compounds. [ref 2] agrees: ErAl2 in Fd-3m, mp-1208, hull 0.000, 16 ICSD references.
Er3Al5O12 is the erbium aluminium garnet, from a paper on Y3-xErxAl5O12 aluminate ceramics. [ref 2] agrees: Er3Al5O12 in Ia-3d, mp-3384, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD references.
note: A thermal-barrier-type oxide measured for thermal properties. The ErAlO3 perovskite lines in [ref 2] are a different compound. Garnets have no structural transition below the melt.

basis: Fe2V0.8Nb0.2Al0.8Ga0.2 is Fe2VAl with Nb on the V site and Ga on the Al site, from a paper on Nb and Ga double-substituted Fe2VAl. Fe2VAl is the L21 full-Heusler thermoelectric.
note: Nb and Ga are both at 5 at.% and so host-level, with no dopant candidates listed. Both are isoelectronic substitutions, Nb for V and Ga for Al, used to scatter phonons by mass contrast. No structure reference in the chunk; stage 2 should use the Fe2VAl parent.

basis: Fe2VAl0.8Ga0.2 is Fe2VAl with Ga on the Al site, from a paper on Nb and Ga double-substituted Fe2VAl. Fe2VAl is the L21 full-Heusler thermoelectric.
note: Ga for Al is isoelectronic, at 5 at.% and so host-level. No structure reference in the chunk; stage 2 should use the Fe2VAl parent.

basis: GdFe5Al7 is a ThMn12-type RFexAl12-x compound, from a paper on the magnetic and magnetotransport behaviour of RFe5Al7 (R = Gd, Dy). [ref 2] gives the Fe4Al8 member of the same type, Gd(Al2Fe)4 in I4/mmm, mp-1104719, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD references, as PRIMARY.
note: The mp_id is for GdFe4Al8, the ordered end member, not GdFe5Al7; the extra Fe mixes with Al on the 8j site. The primary rests on 2 ICSD references, flagged weak, but the type is well established for the RFe4Al8 series.

basis: Fe2VAl0.80Ge0.20 is Fe2VAl with Ge on the Al site, from a paper on the thermal and transport properties of the Heusler-type Fe2VAl1-xGex. Fe2VAl is the L21 full-Heusler thermoelectric.
note: Ge for Al is aliovalent and adds electrons, making it n-type. It is at 5 at.% and so host-level, with no dopant candidates listed. The full span reaches 996 K on one curve outside the 5th-95th percentile. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: (La0.7Sr0.3)(Al0.7Fe0.3)O3 is an ABO3 perovskite with La and Sr on the A site and Al and Fe on the B site, from a paper on temperature-independent sensors based on perovskite-type oxides.
note: Space group left null. LaAlO3 is rhombohedral R-3c and goes cubic near 800 K, and LaFeO3 is orthorhombic Pnma; which tilt system this mixed composition takes, and whether it reaches cubic inside the 374-1262 K window, is not decidable from composition. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: Mg0.2Al0.4Li0.40Fe2.00O4 is lithium ferrite Li0.5Fe2.5O4 with Al and Mg substituted, from a paper on thermoelectric power of magnesium and aluminium substituted lithium ferrite. Lithium ferrite is an inverse spinel, and the formula keeps the AB2O4 cation-to-oxygen ratio of 3:4.

dopant_roles.site: tetrahedral and octahedral cation sites
dopant_roles.basis: Mg2+ is co-substituted with Al3+ into lithium ferrite as the paper title says; one Mg2+ with one Al3+ replaces a Li+ and an Fe3+ pair, keeping the charge balanced.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, Li2Al2FeO6, Li2AlFeO4, Li3Al(FeO3)2, Li3Al2FeO6, Li3AlFeO4, are Li-rich computed orderings with no ICSD references, not the spinel ferrite; no mp_id is taken from them. Space group left null: Li0.5Fe2.5O4 is P4_332 when Li and Fe order on the octahedral sites and Fd-3m above the order-disorder transition near 1020 K, and the Al and Mg substitution suppresses that ordering. The measurement reaches 1084 K, so this may be crossed, but the transition is ordering within one prototype.

basis: Fe2NiAl has the X2YZ full-Heusler stoichiometry, from a paper on the magnetic and thermoelectric properties of melt-spun ribbons of Fe2XAl alloys. [ref 2] gives AlFe2Ni in Fm-3m, mp-31186, 1 ICSD reference, as PRIMARY.
note: Partly at odds with [ref 2] even though its PRIMARY is the L21 cell: that entry sits at hull 0.233 eV/atom on one ICSD reference, which says ordered L21 Fe2NiAl is not stable. In practice Fe2NiAl is a B2-based bcc alloy, the Alnico base, which decomposes spinodally into Fe-rich bcc and NiAl-rich B2; melt spinning may retain a disordered B2 or A2 state rather than L21. Hence medium, with b2_cscl as the alternative. Stage 2 should take the space group from the ribbon XRD.

basis: Fe2VAl0.9SI0.1 is Fe2VAl0.9Si0.1 with the silicon symbol mis-capitalised, from a paper on a high-strength Fe2VAl thermoelectric module. Si for Al is the standard n-type substitution in the L21 full-Heusler Fe2VAl.

dopant_roles.basis: The I is the second letter of SI, which the parser split into S and I. The sample contains no sulfur or iodine; the element is Si, substituting for Al.

note: The host key Al-Fe-S-V is itself a parse artifact: the real host is Al-Fe-Si-V. The S that the parser counted as host-level is Si, and the I dopant candidate is the rest of the same symbol. The composition string should be corrected upstream so this sample routes with the other Fe2VAl1-xSix records.

basis: Al70Fe20Ta10 is the icosahedral phase from a paper titled A New Icosahedral Al-Fe-Ta Alloy Prepared by Rapid Solidification. It is aperiodic and quasicrystal_approximant covers it.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, Ta3AlFe8, TaAlFe and TaAlFe4, are Fe-rich periodic computed phases with no ICSD references and not the Al-rich icosahedral phase; no mp_id is taken. Medium rather than high because a rapidly solidified icosahedral alloy of this kind is often metastable and may carry crystalline Al13Fe4-type phases; the paper should confirm it is single-phase.

basis: Ce0.2La0.8Al2Ga2 is LaAl2Ga2 with Ce on the La site, from a paper on antiferromagnetism in Ce1-xLaxAl2Ga2 Kondo-lattice systems. CeAl2Ga2 and LaAl2Ga2 take the tetragonal BaAl4 type, I4/mmm, with Al and Ga on the two B sites.

dopant_roles.site: A site (2a)
dopant_roles.basis: Ce is the Kondo ion diluted into the non-magnetic La analogue, which is the axis the paper studies.

note: baal4_type is a previously proposed prototype, not yet in the seed. If Al and Ga fully order onto 4d and 4e the cell is the ThCr2Si2 ordered derivative, hence thcr2si2_122 as the alternative; the reported partial mixing favours the BaAl4 parent. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: Gd2SrAl2O7 has the A3B2O7 stoichiometry of the n = 2 Ruddlesden-Popper phase, from a paper on the thermophysical properties of rare earth barium aluminates. Ln2SrAl2O7 aluminates are reported in the Sr3Ti2O7-type I4/mmm structure.
note: Medium because the small Gd3+ may lower the symmetry from I4/mmm by octahedral tilting, and because the paper title names barium aluminates while this composition has Sr; it is presumably a comparison sample. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: LaAlGe is the non-centrosymmetric Weyl semimetal of the RAlGe family, from a paper on transport in the Weyl semimetal LaAlGe. It takes the LaPtSi-type I4_1md ordering of the alpha-ThSi2 net, and [ref 2] agrees: LaAlGe in I4_1md, mp-11511, hull 0.000. No existing entry covers the ordered type, so laptsi_ordered_thsi2 was proposed.
note: [ref 2] ranks La(AlGe)2 in P-3m1 first for the chemistry (mp-10580, 2 ICSD); that is a different compound of the CaAl2Si2 type, so it is not a disagreement. The chunk gives no measured range for this host, so t_min_K and t_max_K are null. alpha_thsi2 is listed as the alternative for the case where Al and Ge are disordered on the net.

basis: LiAlGe is a Nowotny-Juza filled-tetrahedral compound of the LiAlSi type, F-43m, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of LiAlSi and LiAlGe. [ref 2] agrees: LiAlGe in F-43m, mp-5920, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD references.
note: An 8-electron Nowotny-Juza phase rather than an 18-electron transition-metal half-Heusler, but it is the same C1b MgAgAs cell, which is what half_heusler names. The primary rests on 2 ICSD references, flagged weak, but formula and space group match exactly.

basis: La2Ir3Al9 is the non-magnetic analogue of Ce2Ir3Al9, from a paper on the ground state of Ce2Ir3Al9. The R2T3Al9 aluminides take the orthorhombic Y2Co3Ga9 type, Cmcm, and [ref 2] agrees: La2(Al3Ir)3 in Cmcm, mp-1211311, hull 0.000.
note: The [ref 2] line has no ICSD reference, but it is the only line and matches formula and space group exactly.

basis: Al64.5Ir22Pd13.5 carries the suffix IAC_1_0, a 1/0 icosahedral approximant crystal, from a paper on the synthesis and superstructure of Al-Ir and Al-Ir-Pd crystalline approximants. That is exactly what quasicrystal_approximant names.
note: Unlike most quasicrystal_approximant records this one is periodic, so stage 2 can in principle resolve a real cell; the 1/0 approximant of the Al-Pd-Ir family is cubic, and the paper reports a superstructure of it. The _IAC_1_0 suffix is a sample label in the composition string and should be stripped upstream. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: Yb2Ir3Al9 is an intermediate-valence ytterbium aluminide of the R2T3Al9 family, from a paper on the magnetic, transport and thermal properties of Yb2T3Al9. It takes the Y2Co3Ga9 type, Cmcm, and [ref 2] agrees: Yb2(Al3Ir)3 in Cmcm, mp-1207613, hull 0.000.
note: The [ref 2] line has no ICSD reference, but it is the only line and matches formula and space group exactly.

basis: K8Al8Sn38 is a type-I clathrate A8M8E38, from a paper on sintered n-type K8M8Sn38. K fills the cages and Al replaces Sn in the framework.
note: K (15 at.%) is the cage guest and Al (15 at.%) is framework substitution setting the electron count; both are host-level so no dopant_roles are recorded. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: La4MgAl2TaO12 has four A cations, four B cations and twelve O, i.e. La(Mg0.25Al0.5Ta0.25)O3, a B-site mixed perovskite; it is a comparison material in a paper on ultralow thermal conductivity in a binary Ln-Nb-O oxide system.
note: Low confidence. The formula is not charge-balanced as written: 12 + 2 + 6 + 5 = 25 positive charges against 24 from O12, so either the composition is mis-transcribed or it is a nominal value. The paper title does not name this compound, so the assignment rests on the ABO3 cation count alone; the paper should be checked for what this reference sample actually is. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: La0.5Sr0.5Mn0.75Al0.25O3 is the half-doped manganite perovskite La0.5Sr0.5MnO3 with Al on the Mn site, from a paper on Al doping effects and the high-field phase diagram of La0.5Sr0.5MnO3; the curator records it as polycrystalline.
note: Al (5 at.%) is host-level, a non-magnetic B-site dilution of Mn. Space group left null: La0.5Sr0.5MnO3 is near the rhombohedral R-3c / tetragonal I4/mcm boundary and the magnetic transitions in the measured window are not structural changes of prototype. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: (La0.3Sr0.7)(Al0.65Ta0.35)O3 is LSAT, the standard cubic perovskite substrate, recorded as a thin-film sample from a paper on a ferromagnetic insulating phase in strained La0.8-type films.
note: Two cautions. First, LSAT is an insulating substrate, and the paper studies a strained film grown on it, so this composition may be the substrate recorded in place of the film; the sample should be checked against the paper before it is used. Second, partial agreement with [ref 2]: Sr3LaTaAl3O12 in Cmmm (mp-1232343) and Sr6La2Ta3Al5O24 in R-3m (mp-676456) are ordered perovskite supercells with no ICSD references. Real LSAT is a disordered cubic perovskite, Pm-3m, so neither is taken as its mp_id.

basis: La2AlTaO7 has the A2B2O7 stoichiometry with La on the A site and Al and Ta sharing the B site at an average valence of 4+, from a paper on the thermal properties of La3TaO7 and La2AlTaO7. The large La3+ to B-site radius ratio favours the pyrochlore arrangement.
note: Low confidence. The companion La3TaO7 is a weberite-type Ln3BO7, and a mixed Al/Ta B site with a large size mismatch could instead give a weberite-like or disordered fluorite cell, or a two-phase mixture. The structure was not recalled with confidence and is inferred from stoichiometry; the paper XRD should settle it. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: LiAlSi is the prototype Nowotny-Juza filled-tetrahedral compound, F-43m, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of LiAlSi and LiAlGe. [ref 2] agrees: LiAlSi in F-43m, mp-3161, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD references.
note: An 8-electron Nowotny-Juza phase in the C1b MgAgAs cell, which is what half_heusler names. The primary rests on 4 ICSD references, flagged weak, but formula and space group match exactly.

basis: Mg2SiAl5O7.5 reads as Mg2Si plus 2.5 Al2O3, from a paper on the fabrication and thermoelectric properties of Mg2Si-based composites. The thermoelectric phase is antifluorite Mg2Si and the oxide is a second phase.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, pyrope garnet Mg3Al2(SiO4)3 (mp-6073, 55 ICSD), cordierite Mg2Al4Si5O18 and other aluminosilicates, describe the oxidised chemistry; Mg2Si does not react to a silicate in a thermoelectric composite, so none is taken. The oxide may be Al2O3 as written or MgAl2O4 spinel if the Al2O3 reacted with Mg, which is why both are listed. The composition string mixes the two phases into one formula and should be kept as a composite in stage 2.

basis: Mg36.3Al32.0Zn31.7 is the Bergman phase Mg32(Al,Zn)49, from a paper on the electrical, magnetic, thermal and thermoelectric properties of the Bergman phase. It is the cubic Im-3 1/1 approximant of the Mg-Al-Zn icosahedral quasicrystal.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, Mg19Al4Zn15 Cmcm, Mg2Al4Zn3 P6_3/mmc and several Mg-rich Cm cells, are other compositions and none is the Bergman phase; no mp_id is taken. Being a 1/1 approximant it is periodic (Im-3, about 160 atoms per cell) with Al/Zn site mixing, so stage 2 needs an ordered model of it rather than any of these entries.

basis: Al67.0Pd11.5Mn14.6Si6.9 is an Al-Pd-Mn icosahedral quasicrystal with Si on the Al sites, from a paper on the thermoelectric performance of Al-Pd-Mn quasicrystals compared with approximants; the curator records the composition as measured by EPMA against a nominal Al67Pd11Mn14Si8.
note: The paper compares quasicrystals with approximants and this composition, with Mn at 14.6 at.% and Si added, is closer to the Al-Pd-Mn-Si approximant region than the classic i-Al70Pd21Mn9; it could be either. Both sit under quasicrystal_approximant, so the prototype is unaffected, but stage 2 should check which one this sample is. Si (6.9 at.%) is host-level, substituting for Al. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: YSmSi10.45Al1.55O1.3N14.7 is a Y-Sm-stabilised alpha-SiAlON, which the curator records as Y-Sm/alpha-SiAlON, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of alpha-SiAlON. alpha-SiAlON is the alpha-Si3N4 network, P31c, with Al-O replacing Si-N and Y and Sm in the interstitial cavities; beta_si3n4 covers the alpha form.

dopant_roles.site: anion site of the Si3N4 network
dopant_roles.basis: O for N is paired with Al for Si in the SiAlON network; it is part of the defining m,n substitution, not processing residue.

dopant_roles.site: cavity in the alpha-Si3N4 network
dopant_roles.basis: Y3+ is the classic alpha-SiAlON stabiliser occupying the two large interstices per unit cell and charge-compensating the Al-for-Si substitution.

dopant_roles.site: cavity in the alpha-Si3N4 network
dopant_roles.basis: Sm3+ is a co-stabiliser in the same interstitial site as Y, as the curator label Y-Sm/alpha-SiAlON says.

note: Medium because beta_si3n4 is a proposed prototype named for the beta form; its definition includes the alpha form and SiAlON, but a separate alpha entry may be wanted in v4 since alpha-SiAlON is P31c and not P6_3/m. [ref 2] offers YAl6Si18(N15O)2 and YAl6Si30(N15O)3 in P1, no ICSD references; these are ordered computational models of Y-alpha-SiAlON, not a disagreement, but neither matches this composition and P1 is not the real symmetry, so no mp_id is taken.

basis: Na1.76Al1.76Sn4.24 is a member of Na2+xAl2+xSn4-x, a new Zintl phase from a paper titled Synthesis, Crystal Structure, and Thermoelectric Properties of Na2+xAl2+xSn4-x. The paper reports its own structure, but I do not recall its type, and no existing prototype matches with confidence.
note: Parked rather than guessed. It is a tetrel-rich Na-Al-Sn Zintl phase with an Al/Sn anionic framework and Na counter-cations; it is not a clathrate (that would be Na8Al8Sn38). No structure reference in the chunk. The space group and a prototype, likely a new proposal, should be taken from the paper.

basis: TiAl48Nb6 is the at.% composition Ti-48Al-6Nb, as the curator records it, a high-Nb gamma-TiAl alloy made porous for thermal insulation. gamma-TiAl is the L1_0 tetragonal phase, usually with some lamellar alpha2-Ti3Al.

dopant_roles.basis: Ti is the balance element, 46 at.%, not a dopant. The string was written Ti-48Al-6Nb and parsed as one Ti against 48 Al and 6 Nb.

note: The host key Al-Nb is a parse artifact; the real host is Al-Nb-Ti and the composition should be Ti46Al48Nb6. Disagrees with [ref 2], which answers for the Nb-Al binary (Nb3Al A15, NbAl3 D022, Nb2Al sigma); none of those is the matrix, so no mp_id is taken. is_mixed because gamma-TiAl alloys of this composition are normally gamma plus a few percent alpha2-Ti3Al (D019), listed as the alternative.

basis: YNiAl4 is the prototype of its own orthorhombic Cmcm type and the non-magnetic reference for YbNiAl4 in a paper on intermediate-valence Yb in YbNiAl4. [ref 2] agrees: YAl4Ni in Cmcm, mp-3602, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD references.
note: [ref 2] ranks several Y-Ni-Al phases level on 3 ICSD references; YAl4Ni is the one matching the formula, so it is taken. The primary is flagged weak but matches formula and space group exactly.

basis: (Al2O3)20(MgO)15(TiO2)9(SiO2)56 is a multicomponent aluminosilicate written in oxide mol.%, which is how glasses and glass-ceramics are specified, and it appears as a low-conductivity reference in a paper on ultralow thermal conductivity in an Ln-Nb-O oxide system.

dopant_roles.basis: MgO at 15 mol.% is a network-modifier component of the glass, written into the batch, not a dopant.
TiO2 at 9 mol.% is the usual nucleating agent of a MgO-Al2O3-SiO2 glass-ceramic; it is a batch component, not a dopant.

note: Disagrees with both references. [ref 1] gives Al2Si4O11 and Al2SiO5 polymorphs and [ref 2] gives andalusite Al2SiO5 (27 ICSD) and other crystalline aluminosilicates; these are phases of the Al-Si-O chemistry, not this four-oxide glass, so no mp_id is taken. With 9 mol.% TiO2 this is the classic cordierite glass-ceramic batch, so a crystallised sample would be glass plus cordierite; composite_multiphase is listed for that case. The paper should say whether it is glass or glass-ceramic.

basis: Al72Pd17Os11 carries the suffix IQC, an icosahedral quasicrystal, from a paper on new stable icosahedral phases in the Al-Pd-Ru and Al-Pd-Os systems. It is aperiodic and quasicrystal_approximant covers it.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line, Al2OsPd in Immm, sits at hull 2.981 eV/atom with no ICSD reference, which is not a physical structure; no mp_id is taken. The _IQC suffix is a sample label and should be stripped upstream.

basis: PuPd5Al2 is the plutonium member of the AnPd5Al2 family, from a paper on the magnetic and electronic properties of antiferromagnetic PuPd5Al2. It takes the ZrNi2Al5 type of NpPd5Al2, and [ref 2] agrees: PuAl2Pd5 in I4/mmm, mp-1091385, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The primary rests on one ICSD reference, flagged weak, but formula and space group match exactly. The antiferromagnetic order is magnetic, not structural.

basis: Al70Pd21Tc9 is an icosahedral quasicrystal, from a paper on the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of an icosahedral quasicrystalline Al-Pd-Tc phase. It is the Tc analogue of i-Al70Pd21Mn9 and is aperiodic.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, Al2TcPd in Fm-3m (hull 0.019) and in Immm (hull 2.808), have no ICSD references and are computed Heusler-type cells of another stoichiometry, not the icosahedral phase; no mp_id is taken.

basis: ThPd5Al2 is the non-magnetic 5f-free analogue of NpPd5Al2, from a paper on Kondo behaviour in superconducting NpPd5Al2. It is isostructural with NpPd5Al2 in the ZrNi2Al5 type, I4/mmm.
note: Not matched by [ref 2]. Its only line, ThAlPd in P-62m (mp-1078527, 1 ICSD), is the ZrNiAl-type equiatomic compound, a different stoichiometry. The references have no ThPd5Al2 entry, so no mp_id is recorded.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [139], ICSD-backed references for this host report [189]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: UPd2Al3 is the heavy-fermion superconductor of the hexagonal PrNi2Al3 type, P6/mmm, from a paper on large thermoelectric power in metallic cerium and uranium compounds. [ref 2] agrees: UAl3Pd2 in P6/mmm, mp-4561, 3 ICSD references.
note: The MP entry sits at hull 0.091 eV/atom, which is high for a compound grown routinely as large single crystals; this is a DFT treatment of the 5f electrons, not evidence against the structure. The primary rests on 3 ICSD references, flagged weak, but formula and space group match exactly.

basis: Yb2Pt6Al15 is a heavy-fermion aluminide measured on single crystals, from a paper investigating Yb2Pt6Al15 single crystals. It is reported in the hexagonal Sc0.6Fe2Si4.9 type, P6_3/mmc, with partly occupied Yb-Al layers between Pt-Al slabs. No existing entry covers the type, so sc06fe2si49_type was proposed.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, YbAlPt in Pnma (mp-1102117, 1 ICSD) and Yb4(Al8Pt3)3 in P-1, are other compounds; no mp_id is taken. Medium because the structure type is from memory, and later work on this family reports superstructures and a revised stoichiometry, so the average P6_3/mmc cell may not be the final word.

basis: Rb8Al8Si38 is a type-I clathrate A8M8E38, from a paper on a metal-halide and metal-flux synthetic route towards type-I clathrates. Rb fills the cages and Al replaces Si in the framework.
note: Rb (15 at.%) is the cage guest and Al (15 at.%) is framework substitution setting the electron count; both are host-level so no dopant_roles are recorded. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: Ru0.24Re0.73Si1.5364Al0.1336 lies on the Ru2Si3-ReSi1.75 pseudobinary, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of ternary and Al-containing quaternary Ru1-xRexSiy. Both end members satisfy the 14-electron Nowotny chimney-ladder count (Ru + 1.5 Si, Re + 1.75 Si), and the intermediate compositions are chimney-ladder phases with composition-dependent modulation.
note: Medium because this composition is Re-rich (x = 0.75), near ReSi1.75, which is often described as a defect C11b MoSi2 derivative rather than a chimney-ladder phase; mosi2_c11b is listed for that reading. Al (5.4 at.%) is host-level, substituting for Si as a p-type acceptor. Space group left null: chimney-ladder phases are incommensurate and only approximants exist in MP. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: Yb2Rh3Al9 is an intermediate-valence ytterbium aluminide of the R2T3Al9 family, from a paper on the magnetic, transport and thermal properties of Yb2T3Al9. It takes the orthorhombic Y2Co3Ga9 type, Cmcm, like Yb2Ir3Al9.
