note: Not matched by [ref 2]. Its only line, YbAlRh in Pnma (mp-1207572, no ICSD reference), is the TiNiSi-type equiatomic compound, a different stoichiometry; the references have no Yb2Rh3Al9 entry, so no mp_id is recorded. The Ir analogue in this chunk does have one (mp-1207613).

basis: Yb2Si2Al is an intermediate-valence compound of the tetragonal Mo2FeB2 type, P4/mbm, from a paper on intermediate valence in single-crystalline Yb2Si2Al. [ref 2] agrees: Yb2AlSi2 in P4/mbm, mp-10532, hull 0.028, 1 ICSD reference.
note: [ref 2] ranks Yb(AlSi)2 in P-3m1 level with it on one ICSD reference; that is the CaAl2Si2-type YbAl2Si2, a different compound, so it is not a disagreement. The P4/mbm primary is flagged weak but matches formula and space group exactly.

basis: Al3V0.7Ti0.3 is Al3V with Ti on the V site, from a paper on reducing the lattice thermal conductivity of a pseudogap intermetallic compound. Al3V and Al3Ti are both D0_22, I4/mmm, and form a continuous solid solution.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines, Ti2AlV in F-43m, TiAl2V in P4/mmm and TiAlV2 in Cmm2, are Ti-V-rich cells of other stoichiometries and none is Al3(V,Ti); no mp_id is taken. Ti (7.5 at.%) is host-level, substituting for V on the same D0_22 site, used as mass and strain scattering.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [139], ICSD-backed references for this host report [216]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: TmAl2 is a cubic C15 MgCu2-type Laves phase, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of REAl2 compounds. [ref 2] agrees: TmAl2 in Fd-3m, mp-858, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD references.

(YbAl3)0.95(Y5Sb3)0.05 is YbAl3, the cubic L1_2 Cu3Au-type intermediate-valence thermoelectric, with a 5 mol.% second phase, from a paper on the effects of second-phase Yb5Sb3 on the thermoelectric properties of YbAl3.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb is in the deliberately added second phase, Yb5Sb3, not dissolved in YbAl3.

note: The composition string very likely mis-transcribes Yb5Sb3 as Y5Sb3: the paper title names Yb5Sb3. If so, the sample contains no yttrium and the host key should be Al-Sb-Yb; as parsed, Y reaches about 6 at.% and wrongly becomes a host element. Disagrees with [ref 2], whose lines, YbYAl4 F-43m and YbYAl6 P6_3/mmc, are computed Yb-Y-Al orderings with no ICSD references that exist only because of that Y; no mp_id is taken. Stage 2 should resolve YbAl3 Pm-3m directly.

basis: ZrAl3 is the type compound of the D0_23 long-period tetragonal A3B ordering, I4/mmm, from a paper on tailoring thermal transport by inducing surface oxidation. [ref 2] agrees: ZrAl3 in I4/mmm, mp-395, hull 0.000, 9 ICSD references. No existing entry covers D0_23, so d023_zral3 was proposed.
note: d022_al3ti shares the space group but not the cell, so it was not reused. The other [ref 2] lines, ZrAl2, Zr2Al, Zr5Al3 and Zr3Al, are other compounds of the binary. The paper studies surface oxidation, so an oxide skin on the sample is possible but is not a separate host.

basis: AmN is an actinide mononitride with the NaCl structure, Fm-3m, like UN and PuN, from a paper on the thermal diffusivity of americium mononitride from 373 to 1473 K.
note: No structure reference in the chunk, so no mp_id is recorded. Americium self-irradiation damages the lattice over time, which changes the thermal diffusivity but not the structure type.

basis: CeAuAs2 is one of the CeTAs2 compounds, from a paper on magnetic and electrical transport in novel CeTAs2. These are HfCuSi2-type: [CeAs] slabs alternate with [TAs] layers and a planar As square net. [ref 2] gives CeAs2Au in P4/nmm, mp-1226657, hull 0.000, the tetragonal parent.
note: Inconsistent with an earlier record. CeAgAs2 (Ag-As-Ce, chunk 10) was filed under zrcusias_1111 before hfcusi2_112_square_net was proposed; the two hosts belong in the same entry, and v4 review should move Ag-As-Ce. The proposal lists Sb and Bi as the pnictogen; As extends it. The MP entry has no ICSD reference. Some CeTAs2 members distort to orthorhombic when the As net dimerises, so the tetragonal cell is medium confidence.

basis: (BTBT)2AsF6 is a 2:1 radical-cation salt of the organic donor benzothienobenzothiophene with the closed-shell AsF6 anion, from a paper on low-temperature thermoelectric generators using molecular conductors. It has the same layered donor-sheet and anion-sheet arrangement as the BEDT-TTF salts.
note: Used at one remove: BTBT is not a TTF derivative, so this salt is filed under the only organic charge-transfer-salt entry the taxonomy has. A broader organic radical-cation salt entry may be better at v4. The host key is a parse artefact: B was read from the BTBT abbreviation, C and S from the molecule are missing, and H cannot be traced to the string. Only As and F, in AsF6, are genuine. No structure reference and no mp_id.

basis: The paper is on transport and superconductivity in Ba1-xMxFe2As2 (M = La and K), so the composition Ba0.85La0.15As2 has lost its Fe2 in transcription and the sample is Ba0.85La0.15Fe2As2, the ThCr2Si2-type 122 iron arsenide, I4/mmm, with La on the Ba site.

dopant_roles.basis: La3+ for Ba2+ is the electron-doping variable in Ba1-xLaxFe2As2, x = 0.15 here.

note: Disagrees with [ref 1] and [ref 2]. [ref 1] gives BaAs2 in Pc (mp-31243, 1 ICSD) and [ref 2] other Ba-As binaries; these exist only because Fe was dropped from the string, so no mp_id is taken and the host key should read As-Ba-Fe-La. Undoped BaFe2As2 distorts to orthorhombic Fmmm near 140 K; at 15% La that distortion may be suppressed or only lowered, so no second phase is recorded, but the 14-269 K window could cross it.

basis: Ba2Ti2Cr2As4O is the Cr analogue of the self-doped superconductor Ba2Ti2Fe2As4O, from a paper on the synthesis and crystal structure of a new oxypnictide. The structure is an intergrowth of one BaTi2As2O block and one BaCr2As2 block. No existing entry covers this intergrowth, so ba2ti2fe2as4o_22241 was proposed.
note: alt_prototype_ids name the two component blocks, not other phases in the sample; is_mixed stays false. The I4/mmm space group is recalled for the Fe member, not the Cr one. BaTi2As2O has a density-wave transition near 200 K that may carry over into the Ti2As2O layer here with a small distortion; this is not recorded as a phase. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: As5.26Bi31.57Se2.63Te55.26Tl5.26 is from a paper on diphasal systems combining As2Te3 and Tl2-based phases, and decomposes exactly into Bi2Te3 (about 79 at.%), As2Te3 (about 13 at.%) and Tl2Se (about 8 at.%). This is a deliberately phase-mixed sample, not one crystal structure.

dopant_roles.basis: Se is accounted for exactly by the Tl2Se component, Tl:Se = 2:1, so it sits in the second phase rather than in the Bi2Te3 matrix.

note: The majority phase is Bi2Te3, tetradymite, listed as the alternative. Some As may dissolve in Bi2Te3 rather than stay as As2Te3. The decomposition is arithmetic on the composition string and the paper title, and should be checked against the paper. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: (Fe2As2)Ca5(Sc0.5Ti0.5)4O11 is an iron arsenide in which the anti-PbO Fe2As2 layers are separated by thick Ca-(Sc,Ti)-O perovskite-type blocks, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of FeAs based superconductors with thick perovskite-type blocks.
note: Sc and Ti share the octahedral site of the block in equal amounts and are both host-level. This is a thicker-block member than the 21113 exemplar, so the space group is left null for stage 2. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: Eu11Cd6Sb10As2 is Eu11Cd6Sb12 with As on the Sb sites, from a paper on the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of the Eu11Cd6Sb12-xAsx solid-solution Zintl phases.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: pnictogen
solid_solution_axis.note: As/(As+Sb) = 2/12 for the one composition. As is isoelectronic with Sb and substitutes on the pnictogen sites, which the paper reports as site-preferential rather than random.

note: The taxonomy gives Pbam (55) as the typical space group for zintl_11_6_12, but Sr11Cd6Sb12 and Eu11Cd6Sb12 are monoclinic C2/m (12), which is what is recorded here; the taxonomy entry should be checked at v4. No structure reference in the chunk.

basis: NaCd4As3 is an AM4As3 Zintl arsenide, the Cd analogue of NaZn4As3, from a paper on eight-coordinated arsenic in the Zintl phases RbCd4As3 and RbZn4As3. [ref 2] gives NaCd4As3 in R-3m, mp-1078578, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference, matching the rhombohedral nazn4as3_type.
note: Medium because the paper title names only the Rb compounds; NaCd4As3 may be a comparison sample in that paper, or the composition may be mis-transcribed. The primary rests on 1 ICSD reference, flagged weak. The NaCdAs Pnma line is the 1:1:1 compound, a different stoichiometry.

The space group stays Pnma on both sides, so the two phases share a prototype and an mp_id, but transport jumps at the transition, which is why it is recorded. The transition temperature is recalled, not read from the paper. The other [ref 2] lines, Cr2As, CrAs2, Cr4As3 and Cr15As7, are other compounds.

note: PrFeAsO distorts from tetragonal P4/nmm to orthorhombic Cmme near 153 K, just above its spin-density-wave order; the 78-307 K window crosses it. basis: Sr4Sc2O6Fe2As2 is Sr2ScO3FeAs written per two formula units, the 21113 perovskite-blocked iron arsenide, from a paper on the structure and physical properties of the new layered oxypnictides Sr4Sc2O6M2As2. basis: Ni4As9.1Ge2.9 is a ternary skutterudite in which Ge replaces part of the As in the pnictogen rings, balancing the extra electron of Ni against Co, from a paper on the crystal structure and thermoelectric properties of novel skutterudites.

Medium because the composition is As-rich of the charge-balanced NiGeAs2-type ratio and the paper structure was not seen.

basis: Gd14.34Au67.16Ge18.5 is the Tsai-type 1/1 approximant composition, about RE14Au86-xGex, and the paper is titled for the synthesis optimization, structure and thermoelectric properties of 1/1 approximants. These are the body-centred cubic Im-3 approximants of the Tsai icosahedral quasicrystals.
note: One of three hosts from the same paper, with Au-Gd-Si and Au-Ge-Yb. No structure reference. The approximant is periodic, so stage 2 can map it to an Im-3 cell if MP holds one, but the Au/Ge mixing on the shell sites will not be in any ordered entry.

basis: Gd14.4Au69.9Si15.7 is the Si analogue of the Gd-Au-Ge approximant from the same paper on 1/1 approximants: the Tsai-type cubic Im-3 approximant at about RE14Au86-xSix.
note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Its only entry is Gd(SiAu)2, GdAu2Si2 in the ThCr2Si2 type, I4/mmm, mp-22615, with 3 ICSD references. That is a real compound of this chemistry but at 20 per cent Gd and 40 per cent Si it is far from the sample, which is 70 per cent Au. The reference describes what exists in the chemistry, not what this paper made, so its mp_id is not taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [139]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Si0.5Ge0.5Au0.07 is an equiatomic SiGe alloy film with gold added, from a paper on the nanostructure and thermoelectric properties of SiGeAu thin films. SiGe is the diamond-cubic Fd-3m solid solution; gold does not dissolve in it to 6 per cent and in such films sits as nanoprecipitates or drives metal-induced crystallization.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: diamond lattice
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Ge+Si) = 0.5 for the one composition, the middle of the continuous Si-Ge solid solution.

note: Au is 6.5 atomic per cent and so a host element with no dopant entry. Its likely state is a second phase of Au nanoparticles in the SiGe matrix, hence composite_multiphase as the alternate. As-deposited films of this kind can be amorphous; the measurement from 326 K upward is consistent with an annealed, crystallized film, but the paper should settle it. No structure reference.

basis: Yb15.78Au65.22Ge19 is the Yb member of the same paper on 1/1 approximants: the Tsai-type cubic Im-3 approximant at about RE14-16Au86-xGex, where Yb takes the rare-earth site of the icosahedral cluster.
note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Its entries are Yb2GeAu in Fm-3m, Yb4Ge3Au5 in Cm and YbGeAu in P-6m2 and C2/m, none with an ICSD reference and all far richer in Yb and Ge than the sample, which is 65 per cent Au. They are other compounds of the chemistry, so no mp_id is taken.

basis: YbInAu2, from a paper on the thermopower of Yb heavy-fermion compounds at high pressure, is the cubic L2_1 Heusler compound YbAu2In, Fm-3m, with Au on the 8c site and Yb and In on the rocksalt-like 4a and 4b sites.
note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Its entries, Yb(In2Au)2 in P2_1/m, Yb2In5Au3 in Cmc2_1 and YbIn2Au in Cmcm, are In-rich compounds of the chemistry at other stoichiometries; none is YbAu2In, so no mp_id is taken. The sample was measured under pressure, but the pressure is not expected to change the Heusler structure in this range.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [11, 36, 63]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: AuTlSb is a crystalline equiatomic ternary with a paper on its crystal structure, electronic structure and thermoelectric properties, but I cannot place its structure type with any confidence. An equiatomic 1-1-1 composition suggests a half-Heusler or a ZrBeSi or TiNiSi variant, but thallium and gold are not the usual half-Heusler components and I do not recall the reported structure.
note: Parked rather than guessed. The paper itself reports the structure and should settle it in one reading. No structure reference and no mp_id.

basis: Tl2Au4Sn2Se6 is one of the seventeen new thallium chalcogenides of the paper Exploring Thallium Compounds as Thermoelectric Materials. It is a crystalline quaternary selenide with a structure of its own, and I do not recall its type; no seed prototype covers a Tl-Au-Sn selenide.
note: Parked rather than given an invented type. The source paper reports the structures of all seventeen compounds, so this can be resolved by reading it. No structure reference and no mp_id.

basis: AuTe2, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of gold telluride, is calaverite: a CdI2-derived layered ditelluride whose Te layers are incommensurately modulated, giving a monoclinic C2/m average cell. It is a distorted 1T structure, so it is filed under cdi2_1t with the monoclinic cell recorded for this phase.

other_polymorphs.note: Undistorted CdI2-type AuTe2, P-3m1, the [ref 2] PRIMARY with 22 ICSD references and hull 0.011. The modulation of calaverite is suppressed under a few GPa, giving this trigonal cell. The high ICSD count probably also covers calaverite indexed on its trigonal subcell.
Te2Au in Pma2, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD references: krennerite, a separate natural orthorhombic AuTe2 mineral. Not reached by heating calaverite.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] on the ambient phase. Its PRIMARY is the trigonal P-3m1 cell, but bulk AuTe2 at 319-609 K is monoclinic modulated calaverite, and there is no C2/m entry on the reference line, so the phase mp_id is left null. Stage 2 should take mp-1662 only as the high-symmetry parent cell and say so. Te3Au2 and Te3Au on the same line are other compounds.

basis: Ca0.5Ba0.5B6 is a solid solution of two CaB6-type hexaborides, from a paper on high-pressure densified solid solutions of alkaline-earth hexaborides: the cubic Pm-3m framework of B6 octahedra with the alkaline-earth cation in the cube-centre cavity.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Ba/(Ba+Ca) = 0.5 for the one composition, between the CaB6 and BaB6 end members. Both are the same prototype, so the end member does not change the assignment.

note: No structure reference. Stage 2 can take CaB6 or BaB6 as the parent cell; the solid solution is disordered on the cation site.

basis: The host string is a parsing artefact. The composition reads Ba0.92Ni4SB6.7Sn5.3, which is Ba0.92Ni4Sb6.7Sn5.3 with the antimony symbol split into sulphur and boron, and the paper confirms it: Ba-filled Ni-Sb-Sn based skutterudites. Ni4(Sb,Sn)12 is the Sn-compensated nickel skutterudite framework, Im-3, with Ba in the icosahedral cage.
note: Recorded under the host key the pipeline produced, as B-Co-S was in chunk 039; the real element set is Ba-Ni-Sb-Sn. Ba at 5.1 atomic per cent is a host element and so has no dopant entry, but its role is cage filler. Sn shares the pnictogen ring site with Sb and sets the framework electron count. No structure reference.

basis: Sr0.5Ba0.5B6 is a solid solution of the CaB6-type hexaborides SrB6 and BaB6, from the same paper on high-pressure densified alkaline-earth hexaboride solid solutions: cubic Pm-3m, B6 octahedra with a disordered Sr/Ba cation.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: Ba/(Ba+Sr) = 0.5 for the one composition.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Its only entry, Ba2SrB18 in P4/mmm, mp-1228370, is a computed ordered supercell of the hexaboride with no ICSD reference and a 2:1 ratio that is not the sample. It stands for the same B6 framework with an imposed cation order, so it is not a different prototype, but it is not the disordered cubic solid solution either, and its mp_id is not taken.

basis: Fe41.6Cr17.5Mo2.4W2.5C7.6Mn4.2Si3.2B21.1 is an iron-based amorphous-alloy composition of the Fe-Cr-Mo-W-C-B family, with over 28 per cent metalloid, sprayed as a coating in a paper on intermetallic thermal-barrier coatings. At that composition the as-sprayed coating is mostly glassy.

dopant_roles.basis: A designed constituent of the multicomponent glass-forming alloy, not a dopant; there is no lattice site to substitute on in an amorphous phase.
A metalloid glass former alongside B and C.
A refractory addition that raises the crystallization temperature of iron-based glasses.
Added with Cr for corrosion resistance and glass-forming ability in this alloy family.

note: The measurement runs from 573 to 873 K, and iron-based glasses of this kind crystallize to borides and carbides somewhere near the top of that window, while thermal-sprayed coatings are rarely fully amorphous to begin with. Hence composite_multiphase as the alternate. The host key has dropped Mn, Si, W and Mo as sub-5 per cent constituents. No structure reference.

basis: (B4C)40.48(Cu)59.52 is a boron carbide/copper cermet, as the paper title says: rhombohedral B4C particles in an fcc copper matrix, two phases that do not react, not a ternary compound.
note: The copper matrix is fcc metal and has no separate taxonomy entry, so only boron_carbide is listed as an alternate. The numbers are mole or volume fractions of two components, not atomic percentages. A single mp_id would be wrong in principle; no structure reference.

basis: Fe37.5Ni37.5C5Mo2Si10B8 is an Fe-Ni-based metal-metalloid glass, and the paper is on the thermopower of amorphous Fe-Ni-Cr-Mo-Si-B from 40 K upward. Equal Fe and Ni with 23 per cent metalloids is a classic melt-spun glass composition.

dopant_roles.basis: A designed minor constituent of the glass, named in the paper title; there is no lattice site in an amorphous alloy.

note: The paper title lists Cr, and the composition lists C5 instead. That may be a transcription of Cr as C; either way the sample is the same amorphous alloy, but if it is Cr, the host key is wrong and should be B-Cr-Fe-Ni-Si. The measurement to 579 K stays below the usual crystallization temperature of such glasses. No structure reference.

basis: (La2O3)0.012(SiC)0.5HfB2 is an HfB2-SiC ultra-high-temperature ceramic with a small La2O3 addition, from a paper on the thermal properties of La2O3-doped ZrB2- and HfB2-based ceramics. HfB2 is the AlB2 type and SiC a tetrahedral polytype, two sintered phases rather than a quaternary compound, in the same way as the NbB2-SiC host B-C-Nb-Si in chunk 017.

dopant_roles.basis: Added as La2O3, a sintering aid that reacts with the surface oxides of the boride and SiC to form a grain-boundary phase. It does not go into the HfB2 or SiC lattice.
The oxygen of the La2O3 addition, in the same grain-boundary oxide phase.

note: Mixed by construction; a single mp_id would be wrong in principle. The measurement runs to 2173 K, where neither HfB2 nor SiC changes structure, although the grain-boundary oxide may soften. No structure reference.

basis: HoNi2B2C, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of RNi2B2C single crystals, is the quaternary borocarbide itself: the LuNi2B2C type, I4/mmm, with Ni2B2 layers separated by HoC rocksalt layers. [ref 2] agrees: HoNi2B2C in I4/mmm (139), mp-6646, hull 0.000, 6 ICSD references.
note: The chunk file shows no measured range for this host, so the phase bounds are null.

basis: Y0.74B21.5C2.12N1.5 is the rare-earth boron carbonitride YB22C2N with yttrium deficiency and C/N off stoichiometry, from a paper on the structural and thermoelectric properties of Y1-xB22+yC2-yN. That is the B22C2N member of the REB17CN / REB22C2N homologous series already proposed as reb17cn_boron_carbonitride.

dopant_roles.basis: Yttrium is a structural constituent of YB22C2N, not a dopant; it falls below 5 atomic per cent only because the boron framework is so large. The x in Y1-x is a vacancy fraction on the Y site, which the paper varies.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Every entry on its line, BC2N, B2CN, B3C10N3, B2(CN2)3 and B2CN2, is a computed yttrium-free B-C-N phase at hull 0.17 to 0.58, none relevant to an icosahedral rare-earth boride. The host key has also dropped Y, the defining metal. No mp_id is taken.

basis: C82.3B6.11N5.52O6 is a film of carbon nanotubes with a BCN shell, as the paper title says: C/BCN core/shell nanotube films. Both the carbon core and the B-C-N shell are sp2 graphitic sheets rolled into tubes, the nearest crystalline description being the layered graphite / h-BN family.
note: Used at one remove: a nanotube film has no periodic 3D cell, and graphite_layered is the nearest entry for sp2 carbon. B and N substitute into the graphitic shell, which is what the paper engineers. O at 6 per cent is a host element, most likely surface oxygen groups from processing rather than a lattice constituent. No mp_id should be assigned.

basis: Ce0.5La0.5B6 is the Ce1-xLaxB6 Kondo solid solution, from a paper on its thermoelectric power: the cubic CaB6-type Pm-3m hexaboride with Ce and La disordered on the cation site, a single crystal here.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation
solid_solution_axis.note: La/(Ce+La) = 0.5 for the one composition, on the continuous CeB6-LaB6 solid solution.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. LaCeB12 in Fm-3m and La(CeB8)3 in Pmmm, and their P4/mmm variants, are computed cation-ordered supercells of the same hexaboride, with no ICSD reference. They are not the disordered cubic crystal, so no mp_id is taken; stage 2 should use CeB6 or LaB6 as the parent cell. The measured window ends at 96 K and does not reach any structural change.

basis: Ce3Ni2B2N3, from a paper on the Anderson lattice in intermediate-valence Ce3Ni2B2N3-delta, is the La3Ni2B2N3 type: the same Ni2B2 layers as the LuNi2B2C borocarbide, but separated by a triple R-N rocksalt block instead of a single R-C layer. [ref 2] gives Ce3Ni2B2N3 in I4/mmm (139), mp-21136, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: Used at one remove: this is the n = 3 member of the (RX)n Ni2B2 homologous series of which RNi2B2C is n = 1, in the way that Ruddlesden-Popper members share one entry. A separate La3Ni2B2N3 entry was not proposed for one sample; v4 may want one. Stage 2 must take the mp-21136 cell, not an RNi2B2C cell. The delta in the paper title is nitrogen non-stoichiometry.

basis: Ce2NiB9.7 is Ce2NiB10-delta, from a paper on its magnetic and thermoelectric properties. [ref 2] lists Ce2NiB10 in Pbam (55), mp-21169, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference. No seed prototype covers a boron-rich rare-earth nickel boride of this stoichiometry, so a compound-named entry was proposed.
note: The space group rests on one ICSD reference and was not recalled independently. The other [ref 2] lines, Ce(Ni2B)6, Ce2Ni5B4, Ce3Ni13B2 and CeNi4B, are metal-rich compounds at the other end of the system, not this sample. The boron deficit is non-stoichiometry of the same structure.

basis: CeReB4, from a paper on the crystal structure and magnetic, electronic and thermal transport properties of RReB4, is an RTB4 boride of the YCrB4 type: planar boron nets of fused five- and seven-membered rings between R and T layers, orthorhombic Pbam. [ref 2] agrees: CeReB4 in Pbam (55), mp-22361, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The other [ref 2] lines, Ce2(ReB2)3 and Ce8Re13B12, are other compounds. Same paper as B-Ho-Re in this chunk.

basis: The paper is on the thermoelectric power of amorphous Co100-xBx alloys and the sample is a melt-spun ribbon of Co-Cr-B at 25 per cent boron. That is a Co-metalloid glass with some Co replaced by Cr, as B-Co-Mn is with Mn.
note: The composition string reads Co37.5Cr7.5B25, which sums to 70, while its sister sample in B-Co-Mn reads Co67.5Mn7.5B25; this one is almost certainly Co67.5Cr7.5B25 with a transcription slip. I disagree with [ref 2]: its only entry, CrCoB in Fmmm, mp-1226217, is a computed crystalline compound at hull 0.084 with no ICSD reference, and an amorphous ribbon has no mp_id.

basis: Fe74Co5Cr5B16 is a melt-spun Fe-B metallic-glass ribbon from a paper on the resistivity and thermopower of Fe74Co10-xCrxB16 amorphous alloys: Fe84B16-type glass with Co and Cr on the metal side.
note: Co and Cr are each exactly 5 atomic per cent and so host elements with no dopant entry; in the series they trade off against each other at a fixed total of 10. The measurement to 579 K stays below the crystallization of Fe-B glasses. No structure reference.

basis: Co67.5Mn7.5B25 is a melt-spun ribbon from the paper on the thermoelectric power of amorphous Co100-xBx alloys: a Co75B25 glass with 7.5 per cent of the cobalt replaced by manganese.
note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Its entries, the Co-Mn borides Mn2(Co7B2)3 and Mn3(Co10B3)2 in Fm-3m, MnCoB in Fmmm and MnCoB2 in Pmc2_1, are the crystalline compounds the glass would devitrify into, not the as-spun ribbon. An amorphous sample has no mp_id. The measurement to 397 K stays well below crystallization.

basis: N0.7Co0.5B0.5O2 is Na0.7Co0.5B0.5O2 with the Na symbol mis-transcribed as N: the paper is on the magnetic and thermoelectric properties of B-substituted NaCoO2, the same paper whose other three compositions sit in the B-Co-Na-O host filed under naxcoo2_layered in chunk 032. The parent is the layered sodium cobaltate, CoO2 sheets of edge-sharing octahedra with partial Na between them.
note: The host key is a transcription artefact and should be B-Co-Na-O; nitrogen is not in the sample. B at x = 0.5 on the cobalt site is the paper nominal composition. Whether that much boron really enters the CoO2 sheet rather than forming a borate second phase is doubtful and is the same question noted for the sister host; the assignment follows the paper parent. No structure reference.

basis: Ti9Co2Ru18B8, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of pseudogap Ti10Ru19B8 and Ti9TM2Ru18B8, is the Co member of the Ti9M2Ru18B8 series of the Zn11Rh18B8 type, tetragonal P4/mbm. [ref 2] agrees on the space group: Ti9Co2(B4Ru9)2 in P4/mbm (127), mp-1200174, hull 0.033, 1 ICSD reference.
note: One of four hosts from the same paper, with B-Cr-Ru-Ti, B-Cu-Ru-Ti and B-Fe-Ru-Ti; the new entry was proposed for all four together. The type name is recalled, not checked; the space group rests on one ICSD reference.

basis: CoSi0.9B0.1 is CoSi with a tenth of the silicon nominally replaced by boron, from a paper on the role of boron segregation in the enhanced power factor of CoSi. CoSi is the cubic B20 FeSi type, P2_13.
note: B is exactly 5 atomic per cent and so a host element with no dopant entry, but the paper title says it segregates, so most of it is at grain boundaries rather than on the Si site. I disagree with [ref 2]: its only entry, Co19(Si2B)4 in C2, mp-1226660, is a computed Co-rich phase at hull 0.028 with no ICSD reference, not CoSi. No mp_id is taken.

basis: GdCrB4, from a paper applying an electron-counting rule to screen prospective thermoelectric borides, is an RCrB4 compound of the YCrB4 type itself: orthorhombic Pbam with planar five- and seven-membered boron rings. The paper covers the same family as HoCrB4 in this chunk.
note: No structure reference. Stage 2 can take the HoCrB4 cell, mp-1191543, as a template.

basis: HoCrB4, from the same paper on electron counting in prospective thermoelectric borides, is the YCrB4 type. [ref 2] agrees: HoCrB4 in Pbam (55), mp-1191543, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD references.
note: Ho3CrB7 in Cmcm on the same [ref 2] line is another compound.

basis: Ni69.8Cr6.7Si7.2B13.7Fe2.7 is the composition of a nickel-based self-fluxing NiCrSiB alloy, sprayed as a coating in a paper on intermetallic thermal-barrier coatings. Such coatings solidify as fcc Ni solid solution with Ni3B, nickel silicides and chromium borides, a multiphase alloy rather than one compound.

dopant_roles.basis: A standard minor constituent of NiCrSiB self-fluxing powders, dissolved mainly in the fcc nickel phase. It is part of the alloy specification, not a deliberate dopant.

note: With 21 per cent metalloid, rapid-quench spraying can leave part of the coating amorphous, hence metallic_glass as the alternate; the measurement from 573 to 873 K would crystallize much of any glassy fraction. A single mp_id would be wrong. No structure reference.

basis: Ti9Cr2Ru18B8, from the paper on pseudogap Ti10Ru19B8 and Ti9TM2Ru18B8, is the Cr member of the Ti9M2Ru18B8 series of the Zn11Rh18B8 type, tetragonal P4/mbm.
note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Its only entry is Ti8Cr3(B4Ru9)2 in Cmmm, mp-1217552, a computed ordered cell at hull 0.006 with no ICSD reference and a Ti8Cr3 rather than Ti9Cr2 metal count. It is a relative of this structure, not this compound, so its mp_id is not taken; stage 2 can use the Fe, Co or Cu member cells of the series as a template.

basis: SrCu2(BO3)2, from a paper on the damping of phonon heat current by magnetic excitations in SrCu2(BO3)2, is the Shastry-Sutherland quantum magnet: layers of orthogonal Cu2 dimers linked by planar BO3 groups, separated by Sr, tetragonal I-42m at low temperature. [ref 2] agrees: SrCu2(BO3)2 in I-42m (121), mp-6602, hull 0.051, 10 ICSD references. No seed prototype covers it, so an entry was proposed.

other_polymorphs.note: SrCu2(BO3)2 in I4cm, hull 0.052, 1 ICSD reference. This is not the known high-temperature I4/mcm phase above about 395 K, and the measurement ends at 275 K in any case.

note: A thermal-conductivity sample of a quantum magnet, not a thermoelectric. The recalled I-42m to I4/mcm transition near 395 K lies above the measured window, so there is one phase. Sr2Cu(BO3)2 and BaSr3Cu8(BO3)8 on the [ref 2] line are other compounds.

basis: Ti9Cu2Ru18B8, from the paper on pseudogap Ti10Ru19B8 and Ti9TM2Ru18B8, is the Cu member of the Ti9M2Ru18B8 series of the Zn11Rh18B8 type. [ref 2] agrees on the space group: Ti9Cu2(B4Ru9)2 in P4/mbm (127), mp-1201135, hull 0.033, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The space group rests on one ICSD reference; the type name is recalled, not checked.

basis: (BTBT)2PF6 is a 2:1 radical-cation salt of the organic donor benzothienobenzothiophene with the PF6 anion, from a paper on low-temperature thermoelectric generators using molecular conductors. It is the PF6 sister of (BTBT)2AsF6, filed under bedt_ttf_salt in chunk 051, with the same donor-sheet and anion-sheet arrangement.
note: Used at one remove, as for the AsF6 salt: BTBT is not a TTF derivative, and a broader organic radical-cation salt entry may be better at v4. The host key is a parse artefact: B was read from the BTBT abbreviation, C and S of the molecule are missing, and H cannot be traced to the string. Only P and F, in PF6, are genuine. No structure reference and no mp_id.

basis: The host string is a parsing artefact. Pr0.42Fe3NiSB12 is the filled skutterudite Pr0.42Fe3NiSb12 with the antimony symbol split into sulphur and boron, and the paper confirms it: ground-state properties and thermoelectric behaviour of PrFe4-xTMxSb12. The 1-4-12 formula with Pr in the cage is the filled skutterudite, Im-3.

dopant_roles.basis: Rare-earth guest in the icosahedral void of the Sb12 framework. It sits below 5 atomic per cent only because the filling is partial, 0.42 of the available cages.

note: Recorded under the host key the pipeline produced; the real element set is Fe-Ni-Pr-Sb. Ni at one of four framework sites is a host element with no dopant entry, but its role is framework substitution for Fe, which adds electrons against the holes of the Fe4Sb12 framework and so lowers the filler content the structure needs. No structure reference.

basis: Ti9Fe2Ru18B8, from the paper on pseudogap Ti10Ru19B8 and Ti9TM2Ru18B8, is the Fe member and the best-known compound of the Ti9M2Ru18B8 series of the Zn11Rh18B8 type, with chains of Fe atoms running through a Ti-Ru-B framework. [ref 2] agrees on the space group: Ti9Fe2(B4Ru9)2 in P4/mbm (127), mp-684003, hull 0.010, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The Fe-chain description and the type name are recalled, not checked; the space group rests on one ICSD reference.

basis: The host string is a parsing artefact. Ce0.32Yb0.36Fe3.32Ni0.68SB12 is the double-filled skutterudite (Ce,Yb)0.68Fe3.32Ni0.68Sb12 with Sb12 split into a sulphur and a B12, and the paper confirms it: thermoelectric properties of the new skutterudites (Ce-Yb)yFe4-xNixSb12. This is the Ni-compensated sister of the B-Co-S host of chunk 039.

dopant_roles.basis: Ni-for-Fe on the skutterudite framework site adds electrons against the holes of Fe4Sb12; the Ni content and the filling fraction are one tied variable in this family, not two separate dopants.
Divalent rare-earth guest in the icosahedral void, one of the two fillers the paper mixes.
Trivalent rare-earth guest in the same cage; mixing two fillers of different mass and valence is the point of the (Ce-Yb)y series.

note: Recorded under the host key the pipeline produced; the real element set is Ce-Fe-Ni-Sb-Yb. No structure reference.

basis: The composition reads FeBSb, but the paper is on the mechanical and thermoelectric properties of FeVSb-based half-Heusler alloys, and no FeBSb compound of any structure is known. The most likely reading is FeVSb with the V symbol transcribed as B, which is the cubic C1_b half-Heusler, F-43m.
note: Low confidence because the assignment rests on reading the composition string as a transcription error. If it is, the host key should be Fe-Sb-V. The other possibility is a boron-containing FeVSb whose V was dropped from the string; either way the matrix is the FeVSb half-Heusler, but the paper must be checked before stage 2. No structure reference.

basis: GdB6, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of RB6 single crystals (R = Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd), is the cubic CaB6-type hexaboride, Pm-3m. [ref 2] agrees: GdB6 in Pm-3m (221), mp-22266, hull 0.000, 9 ICSD references.
note: The other [ref 2] lines, GdB2, Gd2B5, GdB4 and GdB12, are other borides of the binary, not polymorphs of GdB6. GdB6 orders antiferromagnetically near 15 K with a small lattice distortion; that sits inside the measured window but is magnetic, and is not recorded as a change of prototype.

basis: NiSi2Ge0.6B0.4P4 is NiSi3P4 with 0.6 of the three silicons replaced by germanium and 0.4 by boron, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of polycrystalline NiSi3P4. That is the NiSi3P4 type already proposed as nisi3p4_type, with substitution on the Si site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: Si
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Ge+Si) = 0.6/2.6 = 0.23 for the one composition. Ge is isoelectronic with Si and tunes the lattice; B on the same site is the aliovalent part.

note: B is 5 atomic per cent and Ge 7.5, so both are host elements with no dopant entry. Boron on a Si site of this tetrahedral phosphide is an acceptor, which is presumably why it is combined with Ge here. No structure reference; the space group is left for stage 2 to take from the proposed entry.

basis: HoReB4, from the same paper on RReB4 as CeReB4 in this chunk, is the YCrB4 type, orthorhombic Pbam. [ref 2] agrees: HoReB4 in Pbam (55), mp-975064, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD references.
note: Ho2ReB6 in Pbam and Ho3ReB7 in Cmcm on the same [ref 2] line are other compounds.

basis: The host string is a parsing artefact. BI0.905Sb0.095 is Bi0.905Sb0.095 with bismuth read as boron plus iodine, and the paper confirms it: transport properties of Bi-rich Bi-Sb alloys. Bi-Sb is the A7 rhombohedral semimetal solid solution, R-3m.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb replaces Bi on the single A7 site. The Bi-Sb join is one continuous solid solution, and 9.5 per cent Sb is in the semiconducting window of the alloy, which is why it is studied; it tunes the band overlap rather than adding carriers.

note: Recorded under the host key the pipeline produced; the real element set is Bi-Sb. I disagree with [ref 2], which matched the artefact literally: BI3 in P6_3/m and B5I in C2/c are boron iodides and have nothing to do with the sample. No mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [166], ICSD-backed references for this host report [176]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The host string is a parsing artefact. BI2Te3 is Bi2Te3 with bismuth read as boron plus iodine, and the paper is on hydrothermally synthesized Bi2Te3-xSex nanostructures, of which this is the x = 0 member. Bi2Te3 is the tetradymite, R-3m.
note: Recorded under the host key the pipeline produced; the real element set is Bi-Te, and this sample belongs with the Bi-Te host. No structure reference was matched to the artefact key, so no mp_id is taken here.

basis: La3Ni2B2N3, from a paper on the Anderson lattice in intermediate-valence Ce3Ni2B2N3-delta, where the lanthanum compound is the non-magnetic reference. It is the La3Ni2B2N3 type: Ni2B2 layers as in LuNi2B2C, separated by a triple La-N rocksalt block instead of a single R-C layer. [ref 2] gives La3Ni2B2N3 in I4/mmm (139), mp-6114, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD references.
note: Filed under borocarbide_1221 at one remove, as the n = 3 member of the (RX)n Ni2B2 series, matching the B-Ce-N-Ni record from chunk 052. Stage 2 must take the mp-6114 cell, not an RNi2B2C cell. The LaNiBN entry in [ref 2] (P4/nmm, mp-20881) is the n = 2 member and a different composition. One curve runs out to 759 K; the robust window is 13-284 K.

basis: LiB, from a paper titled for LiBx (0.82 < x <= 1.0) as an incommensurate composite structure below 150 K. Lithium forms a hexagonal framework and boron sits in linear chains in its channels, with the two sublattices repeating at different periods along c. None of the seed entries has this motif, so libx_boron_chain was proposed first. [ref 2] gives LiB in P6_3/mmc (194), mp-1001835, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD references, which is the average hexagonal cell.
note: The 150 K comes from the paper title. The low-temperature phase is an incommensurate composite with no space-group cell, so its spacegroup_number is null. The paper only places the composite below 150 K; I have not confirmed that the average P6_3/mmc cell describes the sample above it, so the second phase is low confidence. mp-1001835 is at best a commensurate approximant. The other B-Li entries in [ref 2] (LiB11, Li5B4, LiB9, Li2B) are different compositions and are not relevant.

basis: LuB12, from a paper on transition and rare-earth dodecaborides. It is the UB12-type cubic dodecaboride: Lu in the cuboctahedral B24 cages of a boron framework, Fm-3m. [ref 2] agrees: LuB12 Fm-3m (225), mp-1104289, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD references.

Lu0.66Yb0.34Ni2B2 single crystals, from a paper on the physical properties of Lu1-xYbxNi2B2C. The carbon is in the material and missing from the parsed composition, exactly as in the B-Lu-Ni and B-Ni-Yb hosts from the same series. This is the rare-earth nickel borocarbide, I4/mmm, with Lu and Yb sharing the rare-earth site at 34 per cent Yb.
note: The true host key is B-C-Lu-Ni-Yb. Yb is above 5 at.% here, so it has no dopant role; it is a Lu-Yb solid solution on the rare-earth site. No structure reference was matched, so no mp_id is taken.

basis: Ti9Mn2Ru18B8, from the paper on thermoelectric properties of pseudogap Ti10Ru19B8 and Ti9TM2Ru18B8. It is the Mn member of the Ti9M2Ru18B8 series of the Zn11Rh18B8 type, tetragonal P4/mbm, like the Co, Cr, Cu and Fe members annotated in chunk 052. [ref 2] agrees on the space group: Ti9Mn2(B4Ru9)2 P4/mbm (127), mp-1197511, hull 0.014, 1 ICSD reference.
note: Mn is 5.4 at.%, so it is a host element and has no dopant role. It sits on the M site of the Ti9M2Ru18B8 series. The Cmmm entry Ti8Mn3(B4Ru9)2 (mp-1217647) is a computed ordering with no ICSD reference and is not used.

basis: (TiB2)18Si3N4, from a paper on the fabrication and contact resistivity of W-Si3N4 / TiB2-Si3N4 electrodes. This is a two-phase ceramic, AlB2-type TiB2 with a Si3N4 second phase, written as a molar mixture. It is not a single Ti-B-N compound.

dopant_roles.basis: Si comes in as Si3N4, the insulating second phase of the composite. It is not in the TiB2 lattice.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. It matched Ti4B2N3 (R3m, mp-1217108), a computed ternary at hull 0.805 with no ICSD reference, which has nothing to do with this sample. No mp_id is taken. The N in the host key belongs to the Si3N4, and the conducting phase is TiB2 (alb2), listed as the alternative. This matches the B-N-Si-Ti record from an earlier chunk.

basis: Nb2SB, from a paper on the synthesis and characterization of ternary layered Nb2SB ceramics. It is a MAX phase with boron as the X element: NbB-like Nb2B slabs interleaved with planes of S, in the Ti2AlC-type P6_3/mmc arrangement reported for Nb2SB and Nb2SC.
note: The pending max_phase_mn1axn proposal names X = C or N only. Boride MAX phases such as Nb2SB are a recent extension, so v4 should widen the formula archetype rather than add a separate entry. No structure reference was matched, so no mp_id is taken.

basis: Nb5SiB2, the T2 phase of the Nb-Si-B system, from a paper on the electrical and thermal properties of single-crystalline Mo5X3-type silicides and borosilicides. The T2 phase is the Cr5B3 type, I4/mcm, as in Mo5SiB2. [ref 2] has the matching formula: Nb5SiB2 I4/mcm (140), mp-1209930, hull 0.000, with no ICSD reference.
note: The ICSD-ranked entry at the top of [ref 2] is Nb5Si3B in P6_3/mcm (193, mp-1106165), a boron-stabilised D8_8 phase of a different composition. I did not follow it; the sample is written Nb5SiB2. mp-1209930 is taken because it matches the formula, but it has no ICSD reference behind it.

basis: NdB6 single crystal, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of RB6 (R = Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd). It is the CaB6-type cubic hexaboride, Pm-3m. [ref 2] agrees: NdB6 Pm-3m (221), mp-1929, hull 0.000, 9 ICSD references.
note: NdB6 orders antiferromagnetically near 8 K, below this window. That is a magnetic transition, not a structural one.

basis: NiB, from a paper on Seebeck coefficients of iron-group borides. NiB is the CrB type, orthorhombic Cmcm, with zigzag boron chains. [ref 2] has it: NiB Cmcm (63), mp-14019, hull 0.005, 2 ICSD references.
note: Ni2B and Ni3B top the ICSD ranking in [ref 2], but they are other compositions in the same binary. The sample is written NiB, so the NiB entry is taken.

basis: Ni80P14B6, from a paper on transport properties of Fe-Ni glasses. M80(P,B)20 is the classic melt-spun transition-metal-metalloid glass composition, near the deep eutectic, and the paper names the samples glasses.
note: This is the Ni end member of the series filed under B-Fe-Ni-P in an earlier chunk. It is amorphous, so there is no mp_id; stage 2 skips it.

basis: Ti9Ni2Ru18B8, from the paper on thermoelectric properties of pseudogap Ti10Ru19B8 and Ti9TM2Ru18B8. It is the Ni member of the Ti9M2Ru18B8 series of the Zn11Rh18B8 type, P4/mbm. [ref 2] agrees: Ti9Ni2(B4Ru9)2 P4/mbm (127), mp-1199093, hull 0.033, 1 ICSD reference.
note: Ni is 5.4 at.%, a host element on the M site, so it has no dopant role. Same paper as B-Mn-Ru-Ti and B-Ru-Ti in this chunk.

basis: PrRh4.8B2, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of PrRh4.8B2, described as a layered boride. The formula fits none of the rare-earth rhodium borides I can place with confidence: it is not CeCo3B2-type PrRh3B2, not antiperovskite PrRh3B, and it has too much boron for the CeCo4B-type RM4B. It is crystalline and layered by the paper title, but I cannot name the structure type from recall. It is left unresolved rather than forced into a near miss.
note: None of the four [ref 2] entries (PrB2Rh3 P6/mmm mp-5369, PrBRh3 Pm-3m mp-5200, Pr(BRh)4 P4_2/nmc mp-1179918, Pr4(BRh4)3 P4/mmm mp-1219901) has this composition, so no mp_id is taken. The fractional Rh count suggests partial occupancy in a structure of its own; the paper should be read before a prototype is proposed. The CeCo4B-type alternative is the nearest intergrowth family, not a claim.

basis: TbReB4, from a paper on its crystal structure, magnetism and thermal transport. It is an RMB4 of the YCrB4 type, Pbam, with a planar boron net of five- and seven-membered rings, like the B-Ho-Re and B-Ce-Re hosts already filed. [ref 2] agrees: TbReB4 Pbam (55), mp-1192121, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: Tb2ReB6 (Pbam) and Tb3ReB7 (Cmcm) in [ref 2] are other compositions in the same ternary.

basis: TaRuB, from a paper on the synthesis, crystal structure and properties of the new superconductors TaRuB and NbRuB. It is a crystalline equiatomic ternary boride whose structure the paper itself determines. [ref 2] offers two orthorhombic TaRuB cells with one ICSD reference each, Pbam (55, mp-1195237, hull 0.000) and Pmma (51, mp-1205358, hull 0.013), and I cannot tell from recall which one the paper reports for the tantalum compound. Neither matches a type in the taxonomy.
note: No mp_id is taken because the reference offers two TaRuB cells with equal ICSD support. The PRIMARY mark on Pbam comes only from hull order. The paper settles this and should be read before a TaRuB-type entry is proposed. The Ta3B2Ru5 and Ta7(B4Ru3)2 entries are other compositions.

basis: Ti10Ru19B8, the parent compound of the paper on pseudogap Ti10Ru19B8 and Ti9TM2Ru18B8. The substituted members (Co, Cr, Cu, Fe, Mn, Ni) are Ti9M2Ru18B8 with M on the extra site, so the parent is the same tetragonal Zn11Rh18B8-derived P4/mbm framework, with Ti and Ru filling that site.
note: No structure reference was matched to this host, so no mp_id is taken. The space group is inferred from the substituted members, whose MP entries are P4/mbm.

basis: V5SiB2, the T2 phase of V-Si-B, from the same paper on single-crystalline Mo5X3-type silicides and borosilicides as the Nb5SiB2 host. It is the Cr5B3 type, I4/mcm. [ref 2] agrees: V5SiB2 I4/mcm (140), mp-10126, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD references.
note: V5Si2B, V5Si3B and V10Si6B in [ref 2] are other compositions. The full span runs to 1070 K.

basis: TbB12, from a paper on transition and rare-earth dodecaborides. It is the UB12-type cubic dodecaboride, Fm-3m. [ref 2] has it: TbB12 Fm-3m (225), mp-1104066, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: TbB6 tops the ICSD ranking in [ref 2] with 4 references, but it is the hexaboride, a different composition. Tb is the largest rare earth that forms the UB12 type, so TbB12 is hard to make as a single phase, and a TbB6 or TbB4 impurity would not be surprising. The sample is written TbB12 and is taken as such.

basis: YWB4, from a paper applying an electron-counting rule to screen prospective thermoelectric borides. It is an RMB4 of the YCrB4 type, Pbam. [ref 2] agrees: YB4W Pbam (55), mp-1190755, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: Y3B7W (Cmcm) and YB4W3 (Pmm2) in [ref 2] are other compositions.

basis: YB12, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of metal dodecaborides with the UB12 structure. The paper names the type. [ref 2] has it: YB12 Fm-3m (225), mp-7817, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD references.
note: YB6 has more ICSD references (9) in [ref 2], but it is a different composition. The sample and the paper are both YB12.

basis: Bi1.975Na0.025Ba2Co2O8 with C0.8, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of CNT-dispersed, Na-doped Bi2Ba2Co2Oy. The oxide is the Bi-Ba misfit cobaltite, a rocksalt [Bi2Ba2O4] block on a CdI2-type CoO2 layer. The carbon is dispersed carbon nanotubes, a second phase.

dopant_roles.site: the Bi site of the rocksalt block
dopant_roles.basis: The formula takes Na from the Bi count, Bi1.975Na0.025. Monovalent Na for trivalent Bi in the charge-reservoir block adds holes to the CoO2 layer.

note: C is 5.5 at.% in the parsed formula, so it counts as a host element, but it is CNT and not part of the oxide lattice. Stage 2 should treat this sample as a misfit cobaltite with a carbon second phase. Incommensurate, so no single mp_id.

basis: (Ca0.5Ba0.5)0.995Na0.005Mg2Bi1.98, from a paper on high thermoelectric performance in rare-earth-free Ca-Ba-Mg-Bi Zintl compounds. It is AMg2Bi2 in the CaAl2Si2 type, P-3m1, with Ca and Ba sharing the A site.

dopant_roles.site: the A site shared by Ca and Ba
dopant_roles.basis: The formula scales the whole (Ca,Ba) site by 0.995 and adds Na0.005 there. Monovalent Na on the divalent A site is the usual p-type acceptor in AMg2Bi2.

note: No structure reference was matched to this host, so no mp_id is taken. The Bi1.98 is a deliberate small Bi deficiency, not a dopant. Na substitutes for Ca and Ba together; substitutes_for names Ca only because the field holds one element.

basis: [(Bi0.8Pb0.8)2Ba2O4]0.5CoO2, from a paper on Pb-for-Bi substitution for enhancing the thermoelectric characteristics of the Bi-Ba-Co-O misfit. The formula is written in the misfit form: a rocksalt [(Bi,Pb)2Ba2O4] block with incommensurate ratio 0.5 to the CoO2 layer.
note: Pb is well above 5 at.% and shares the Bi site of the rocksalt block, so it has no dopant role. The parsed Bi0.8Pb0.8 sums to 1.6 on a site of 2. That is probably a transcription of Bi2-xPbx; the parsed fractions should be checked before stage 3. Incommensurate, so no single mp_id.

basis: Bi2SrBaCo2O8, from a paper on anisotropic electrical and thermal conductivity in Bi2AE2Co2O8+delta. This is the Bi-AE misfit cobaltite with Sr and Ba sharing the alkaline-earth site of the rocksalt block over the CoO2 layer.
note: Incommensurate composite, so there is no single mp_id. Same family as the Bi-Co-O-Sr and Ba-Bi-Co-O hosts.

basis: BaFe0.5Sn0.2Bi0.3O3, from a paper on the electrocatalytic activity of cobalt-free barium ferrite-based cathodes. It is an ABO3 perovskite with Ba on A and Fe, Bi and Sn sharing B, the BaFeO3-delta cathode family stabilised in cubic form by B-site substitution.

dopant_roles.site: B site
dopant_roles.basis: Sn0.2 of the B site in BaFe0.5Sn0.2Bi0.3O3. It is below 5 at.% only because the B site is a fifth of the formula. Tetravalent Sn is added to stabilise the cubic oxygen-deficient perovskite, so at 20 per cent of the site it is closer to an alloying component than to dilute doping.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. It offers Ba2Fe4Bi2O11 (P4mm) and BaFe5Bi4O15 (Cc), computed cells of other compositions with no ICSD reference, so no mp_id is taken. Cubic Pm-3m is inferred from the cathode family, not from the paper.

basis: (Ca0.25Ba0.75)0.995Na0.005Mg2Bi1.98, from the same paper as Ba-Bi-Ca-Mg on rare-earth-free Ca-Ba-Mg-Bi Zintls. It is BaMg2Bi2 in the CaAl2Si2 type, P-3m1. [ref 1] TEDesignLab agrees: Ba(MgBi)2 P-3m1 (164), mp-29209, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: Ca is 25 per cent of the divalent A site, just under 5 at.% of the formula. Ca2+ for Ba2+ is isovalent. It tunes the lattice and band structure along the CaMg2Bi2-BaMg2Bi2 join, and the paper varies it as an alloy fraction, not as a dopant.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: Na0.005 is added on the A site, which the formula scales by 0.995. Monovalent Na on a divalent site is the p-type acceptor.

note: The BaMg14Bi and BaMg6Bi entries in [ref 2] are computed magnesium-rich cells at hull 0.13 to 0.23 with no ICSD reference, and they are irrelevant. mp-29209 is the BaMg2Bi2 parent, so the Ca-substituted sample inherits its cell.

basis: BaMn2Bi2 single crystals, from a paper on large thermopower in the antiferromagnetic semiconductor BaMn2Bi2. It is the ThCr2Si2 type, I4/mmm, the Bi analogue of BaMn2As2. [ref 2] has the formula: Ba(MnBi)2 I4/mmm (139), mp-1068010, 1 ICSD reference.
note: mp-1068010 sits at hull 0.278, which is high for a compound grown as single crystals. That is a DFT artefact of the magnetic Mn; the space group is not in doubt. BaMnBi2 (I4/mmm, mp-1079799) is a different composition, a 112 square-net compound.

basis: Sr0.7Ba0.3Pb0.75Bi0.25O3, from a paper on the effect of Bi doping on the thermoelectric properties of perovskite-type SrPbO3. It is an ABO3 perovskite with Sr and Ba on A and Pb and Bi on B, and the paper names the type. SrPbO3 is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted variant.
note: Ba (6 at.%) and Bi (5 at.%) are both at or above the host threshold, so neither has a dopant role. Bi on the Pb site is the donor the paper studies, and Ba on the Sr site expands the lattice. The exact tilt setting depends on composition and is not recorded; no structure reference was matched.

basis: (Rb0.45Ba0.55)Bi0.58, from a paper on superconducting (Rb,Ba)BiO3 thin films grown by MBE. The oxygen is in the material and missing from the parsed composition. This is Ba1-xRbxBiO3, the Rb analogue of the Ba1-xKxBiO3 superconductor, a cubic perovskite at superconducting compositions.
note: The true host key is Ba-Bi-O-Rb, the same chemistry as Ba-Bi-K-O filed under perovskite. The Bi0.58 also looks like a parse error for BiO3. The film is an MBE film, so the cell may be strained; cubic is from the bulk family.

basis: (CaBa)Co2O5, which is CaBaCo2O5+delta, from a paper on anomalous redox properties and ultrafast chemical sensing. That is the epitaxial LnBaCo2O5+delta double-perovskite sensing work, with Ca in place of the rare earth. Co2 per AA pair with O5 is the A-site-ordered double perovskite with oxygen vacancies ordered into the Ca layer.
note: The paper title is truncated, and my reading of it as the double-perovskite film work is an inference. Whether Ca and Ba actually order into layers, rather than disorder on one A site, is not settled, which is why perovskite is the alternative. It is not the CaBaCo4O7 swedenborgite: the Co to A ratio is 1, not 2. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba3CaIr2O9, from a paper on Ba3MIr2O9 hexagonal perovskites and spin-orbit coupling. It is the 6H hexagonal perovskite with face-sharing Ir2O9 dimers and Ca on the corner-sharing site. For the large Ca ion it is monoclinically distorted, and [ref 2] agrees: Ba3CaIr2O9 C2/c (15), mp-17448, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.

other_polymorphs.note: A trigonal P-3m1 cell of the same formula at hull 0.021, also with 1 ICSD reference. It may be an older or higher-symmetry refinement of the same 6H stacking rather than a separate phase; nothing in the chunk places it on heating.

note: Both [ref 2] cells have a single ICSD reference, so C2/c is PRIMARY only on hull order. I agree with it from the chemistry, since Ca is the large-M end of the Ba3MIr2O9 series, but that is weak evidence. Ba2CaIrO6 (Fm-3m) is a different composition, the cubic double perovskite.

basis: YBa2Cu2.2(CdS)0.8O7, from a paper on the thermopower of YBa2Cu3-z(CdS)zO7-delta. The matrix is YBCO-123 with nominal CdS substitution for Cu.
note: At z = 0.8, over a quarter of the Cu, I would not expect Cd and S to go into the 123 lattice as written. A large part likely stays as CdS or forms Cd-containing impurity phases, which is why composite_multiphase is the alternative. Cd and S are both above 5 at.%, so neither gets a dopant role. Orthorhombic Pmmm is the fully oxygenated 123 cell; the actual symmetry depends on oxygen content and is not established. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba8Cd7Si39, from a paper on the clathrates Ba8{Zn,Cd}xSi46-x with x near 7. It is a type-I clathrate, Pm-3n: Ba guests in a Si framework with Cd substituted into the framework to reach charge balance.
note: Cd is 13 at.%, a host element on the framework, so it has no dopant role here. Stage 3 should record it as framework_substitution for Si. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba(CeCo)0.4(FeZr)0.1O3, that is BaCe0.4Co0.4Fe0.1Zr0.1O3, from a paper on the triple ionic and electronic conductivity of a new cathode material. It is an ABO3 perovskite formula with Ba on A and Ce, Co, Fe and Zr on B, from the BaCeO3 proton-conductor and BaCoO3 cathode families.

dopant_roles.site: B site
dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.1 on the B site of a Ba cobaltite-cerate. It is an iron-for-cobalt substitution that stabilises the oxygen-deficient perovskite and moderates thermal expansion. At 10 per cent of the site it is an alloying level, below 5 at.% only because B is a fifth of the formula.

dopant_roles.site: B site
dopant_roles.basis: Zr0.1 on the B site. Tetravalent Zr for tetravalent Ce is the standard way to improve chemical stability of BaCeO3-based proton conductors.

note: Ce-rich and Co-rich Ba perovskites are usually immiscible at 40:40. Compositions like this one often self-assemble into a two-phase nanocomposite of a Ce-rich proton-conducting perovskite and a Co-rich electronic-conducting one, which is why composite_multiphase is the alternative. The truncated title does not say which. No structure reference was matched and no space group is recorded.

basis: BaZr0.4Ce0.4Y0.2O3, the BZCY442 proton conductor, from a paper on an in-situ formed core-shell triple-conducting oxygen-reduction electrode. BaZr1-x-yCexYyO3 is an ABO3 perovskite with Zr, Ce and Y on B.

dopant_roles.site: B site
dopant_roles.basis: Y0.2 of the B site. Trivalent Y for tetravalent Zr and Ce is the acceptor that creates the oxygen vacancies, which hydrate into the protonic carriers. This is its deliberate function, at 20 per cent of the site.

note: I disagree with [ref 2]. Its entries, Ba2CeZrO6 and Ba5Ce4ZrO15, are computed orderings with no ICSD reference and no Y, and they are not taken. The distortion of BZCY442, cubic, rhombohedral or orthorhombic, depends on composition and temperature, so no space group is recorded.

basis: Ba2HoCu2CoO6+y, from a paper on thermoelectric and structural characterization of Ba2Ho(Cu3-xCox)O6+y at x = 1. It is HoBa2Cu3O6+y (123) with Co on the Cu sites, where Co is known to take the Cu1 chain site preferentially. [ref 2] has the formula as Ba2HoCoCu2O7 Pmmm (47), mp-1214661, hull 0.034, with no ICSD reference.
note: I disagree with [ref 2] on symmetry. Co on the chain site cross-links the Cu-O chains and makes 123 tetragonal already at a few per cent Co, so at a third of the Cu I expect P4/mmm (123), not orthorhombic Pmmm. The Pmmm cell of mp-1214661 is a computed ordered arrangement with no ICSD reference, so its mp_id is not taken. Co is 9 at.%, so it has no dopant role.

basis: EuBaCo2O5.5, from a paper on a new method to control oxygen stoichiometry and thermoelectric properties. It is the LnBaCo2O5+delta A-site-ordered double perovskite: Eu and Ba in alternating layers, with the O5.5 vacancy ordering giving the orthorhombic Pmmm cell with alternating octahedra and pyramids.
note: No space group is recorded. At 673-873 K the oxygen content, and with it the vacancy order, depends on atmosphere, and the paper is precisely about controlling that. Pmmm at O5.5 may give way to a tetragonal P4/mmm cell with disordered vacancies inside this window. No structure reference was matched.

basis: PrBaCoFeO5+delta, bulk pressed and sintered per the curator detail, from a paper on electrochemical performance and thermal-expansion compatibility of a cathode. It is the PrBaCo2O5+delta A-site-ordered double perovskite with half the Co replaced by Fe, typically tetragonal P4/mmm.
note: Fe is 10 at.%, a host element sharing the B site with Co, so it has no dopant role. Same family as the Ba-Co-O-Pr host. No structure reference was matched.

basis: LaBa0.5Sr0.5Co2O5+delta, a bulk sintered pellet, from a paper on oxygen permeation, thermal expansion and electrochemistry. The formula is written as a double perovskite, but La is the rare earth for which LnBaCo2O5+delta A-site ordering is hardest to get. La is close in size to Ba and Sr, and conventionally sintered La-Ba-Sr cobaltites usually come out A-site-disordered, as a simple cubic perovskite La0.5(Ba,Sr)0.5CoO3-delta.
note: This departs from the SmBa0.5Sr0.5Co2O5 and PrBa0.5Sr0.5Co2O5 hosts, which are filed layered. The ordered versus disordered question for the La member is what the paper settles, so confidence is low and the layered entry is the alternative. I disagree with [ref 2]: its only entry is Ba4Sr2La2Co4O15 (Cc, mp-1228696), a computed cell with no ICSD reference and a different oxygen count. It is not taken.

basis: SmBa0.5Sr0.5Co2O5+delta, bulk, from a paper on the electrical, thermal and electrochemical properties of SmBa1-xSrxCo2O5+delta. It is the A-site-ordered layered double perovskite with Sr replacing half the Ba in the Ba layer. For small Sm, the size contrast keeps the Sm/(Ba,Sr) layering, and the series is reported tetragonal P4/mmm.
note: I disagree with [ref 2]: its only entry is Ba4Sr2Sm2Co4O15 in P1 (mp-1228582), a computed cell with no ICSD reference and a different oxygen count. It is not taken.

basis: La0.2Ba0.7988Sb0.0012Co0.4Ti0.6O3, from a paper on resistivity control by solid-state reaction of perovskite-type oxides. It is a BaTiO3-based ABO3 perovskite with Co sharing the B site and La and Sb on the A site.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: La0.2 is written with the A-site cations. Trivalent La for Ba is the standard donor in BaTiO3-based resistive ceramics. At 20 per cent of the site it is heavy substitution, below 5 at.% only because A is a fifth of the formula.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: Sb0.0012 is written with the A-site cations, which implies Sb3+ for Ba. Sb is also a common donor on the Ti site as Sb5+ in BaTiO3 PTC ceramics, so the site is taken from the formula and is not certain.

note: With 40 per cent Co on the B site, the ferroelectric tetragonal distortion of BaTiO3 is likely suppressed toward cubic, but no space group is recorded. No structure reference was matched.

basis: BaTmCo4O7, from a paper on the structural and thermoelectric properties of BaRCo4O7 (R = Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, Yb, Lu). It is the swedenborgite framework: CoO4 tetrahedra in alternating kagome and triangular layers, with Ba and Tm in the cavities. The high-temperature cell is hexagonal P6_3mc. On cooling, these compounds distort to an orthorhombic Pbn2_1 cell, the Pna2_1 (33) entry of [ref 2].

other_polymorphs.note: Orthorhombic BaTmCo4O7 at hull 0.002 with 1 ICSD reference, marked AMBIGUOUS in [ref 2]. It is most likely the low-temperature distorted phase. For the heavy rare earths I place that transition near or below room temperature, but I have not established its temperature for Tm, so it is not entered as a thermal phase.
Monoclinic Cc cell of the same formula at hull 0.005 with 1 ICSD reference, as seen for BaYbCo4O7. Possibly a further low-temperature distortion; not placed.

note: I disagree with [ref 2] on which cell applies to the measurement. It offers only the orthorhombic and monoclinic low-temperature cells, while this 299-853 K window should be mostly or entirely in the hexagonal phase. The hexagonal cell has no mp_id in the reference, so none is taken. If the Tm transition is above 299 K, the bottom of the window would sit in the Pna2_1 phase.

basis: BaCo0.6Zr0.4O3, from a paper titled for a self-assembled cubic-hexagonal perovskite nanocomposite cathode. At this composition the Ba-Co-Zr-O system separates into a cubic Zr-rich BaZr(Co)O3 perovskite and a hexagonal Co-rich BaCoO3-type polytype. The single nominal formula stands over a two-phase material.
note: Not flagged is_mixed because a per-composition split cannot separate the two phases: there is one composition and both phases are in every sample. The two constituent prototypes are given as alternatives. The phase split is taken from the paper title, not measured. No structure reference was matched.

basis: DyBaCuFeO5, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. It is the YBaCuFeO5-type A-site-ordered double perovskite: Dy and Ba layers, Cu and Fe in corner-sharing square pyramids, with the oxygen vacancy in the Dy layer. It is tetragonal P4mm. [ref 2] has the formula: BaDyFeCuO5 P4mm (99), mp-1207068, hull 0.000, with no ICSD reference.
note: mp-1207068 matches formula and expected space group, but it is a computed cell with no ICSD reference behind it. One of five LnBaCuFeO5 hosts from the same paper in this chunk (Dy, Er, Ho, Lu, Nd); the same paper also fed the Ba-Cu-Fe-O-Sm host in chunk 020.

basis: ErBaCuFeO5, from the paper on layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. It is the YBaCuFeO5-type A-site-ordered double perovskite, tetragonal P4mm, with Cu and Fe in square pyramids.
note: No structure reference was matched, so no mp_id is taken. The space group follows the Dy and Lu members, which [ref 2] gives as P4mm.

basis: HoBaCuFeO5, from the paper on layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. It is the YBaCuFeO5-type A-site-ordered double perovskite, tetragonal P4mm.
note: No structure reference was matched, so no mp_id is taken. The space group follows the Dy and Lu members.

basis: La0.5Pr0.5BaCuFeO5+delta, a member of the La1-xPrxBaCuFeO5+delta series per the curator detail, from a paper on the structure and properties of those solid solutions. It is the LnBaCuFeO5 layered ferrocuprate with La and Pr sharing the rare-earth layer.
note: This follows the Ba-Cu-Fe-La-O and Ba-Cu-Fe-O-Pr hosts, both filed layered. But La is large enough that LaBaCuFeO5 is often reported with a disordered, near-cubic A site, and the paper is about how structure changes along the La-Pr series. So at x = 0.5 the A-site order is not certain, and perovskite is the alternative. Pr is 12.5 at.%, a host element, so it has no dopant role. No structure reference was matched and no space group is recorded.

basis: Sm0.5La0.5BaCuFeO5, bulk, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of Sm1-xLaxBaCuFeO5 ceramics, the same series as the Ba-Cu-Fe-O-Sm host. It is the layered LnBaCuFeO5 ferrocuprate with Sm and La sharing the rare-earth layer.
note: La is 12.5 at.%, a host element. The Ba-Cu-Fe-O-Sm record already covered x = 0.2 to 0.4 of this series; at x = 0.5 the growing La share weakens the A-site ordering, so perovskite is the alternative, as for the La-Pr host. No structure reference was matched.

basis: LuBaCuFeO5, from the paper on layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. It is the YBaCuFeO5-type A-site-ordered double perovskite, tetragonal P4mm. [ref 2] agrees: BaLuFeCuO5 P4mm (99), mp-611393, hull 0.013, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The only member of the LnBaCuFeO5 series in this chunk with an ICSD-backed reference.

basis: NdBaCuFeO5, from the paper on layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. It is the A-site-ordered LnBaCuFeO5 double perovskite with Nd and Ba in alternating layers and Cu and Fe in square pyramids.
note: No structure reference was matched, so no mp_id is taken. Nd is larger than the Dy to Lu members, and the tilt setting may differ from P4mm, hence medium on the phase.

basis: TbBaCuFeO5, from the paper on layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. It is the YBaCuFeO5-type A-site-ordered double perovskite: Tb and Ba layers alternate, and Cu and Fe sit in corner-sharing square pyramids.
note: No structure reference was matched, so no mp_id is taken. P4mm is carried over from the Tm and Lu members of the same paper, which do have [ref 2] entries.

basis: TmBaCuFeO5, from the paper on layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. It is the A-site-ordered LnBaCuFeO5 double perovskite. [ref 2] agrees: BaTmFeCuO5 P4mm (99), mp-1205946, hull 0.006.
note: The [ref 2] entry shows no ICSD count, so it is a computed cell of the right formula rather than an ICSD-backed one.

basis: YbBaCuFeO5, from the paper on layered ferrocuprates LnBaCuFeO5+delta. It is the A-site-ordered LnBaCuFeO5 double perovskite, like the Tm and Lu members of the same series.
note: No structure reference was matched, so no mp_id is taken. Its neighbours Tm and Lu both resolve to P4mm.

basis: BaCuGaP2 single crystal, from the 2024 paper on the semiconducting BaCuTP2 family (T = Al, Ga, In). This matches the Al-Ba-Cu-P record from chunk 49: I do not know this structure type well enough to assign it, and neither reference covers the host.
note: It charge-balances as Ba2+ Cu+ Ga3+ and two P3-, a valence-precise Zintl-like phosphide. The Al, Ga and In members come from one paper and should get one prototype. So when that paper is read, propose it once and re-file Al-Ba-Cu-P, Ba-Cu-Ga-P and Ba-Cu-In-P together.

basis: Ba8Cu14Ge6P26, from a review of unconventional clathrates with transition-metal and phosphorus frameworks. There are 8 Ba guests and a 46-atom Cu-Ge-P framework, the type-I clathrate count, and Ge substitution makes it the cubic type-I clathrate. It is not the orthorhombic Ba8Cu16P30 superstructure filed under ba8cu16p30_clathrate.
note: Cubic Pm-3n for Ba8Cu14Ge6P26 is recalled, not checked. If the paper reports a lower-symmetry ordered cell like Ba8Cu16P30, move it to ba8cu16p30_clathrate. No structure reference was matched.

basis: BaCu2GeSe4, from a paper on ultralow thermal conductivity in 1-2-1-4 quaternary selenides, which is the AM2MQ4 family this proposed prototype covers. [ref 2] gives BaCu2GeSe4 P3_121 (152), mp-17252, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference. That is one of the trigonal settings the proposal says the family also takes.
note: The PRIMARY cell rests on a single ICSD reference, so it is flagged weak. The Sn analogue is orthorhombic, so the setting really does vary across the family. That supports keeping one family prototype with a per-compound space group.

basis: BaCuInP2 single crystal, from the same 2024 BaCuTP2 (T = Al, Ga, In) paper as Ba-Cu-Ga-P and Al-Ba-Cu-P. It is left unresolved for the same reason: the structure type is not one I can assign from memory, and no reference covers the host.
note: In is much larger than Al or Ga, so the In member could take a different structure from the other two. Check that when the paper is read, and do not assume one prototype for all three.

basis: YBa2Cu3La0.7Sr0.3MnO10 is the sum formula of a YBa2Cu3O7 / La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 bilayer, as the paper title says. The sample is two phases: a YBCO cuprate and a manganite perovskite. It is not a single compound.

dopant_roles.basis: La is a major constituent of the La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 layer, not a dopant in YBCO. It falls under 5 at.% only because the formula sums both layers.
Sr is the divalent A-site component of the La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 layer, at 30% of its A site. It belongs to the second phase, not the cuprate.

note: Neither role in the vocabulary fits a heterostructure constituent exactly. secondary_phase_or_contaminant is used because both elements sit in a separate phase, not because they are impurities. Stage 3 must not compute a doping level for them.

basis: BaCu5.9STe6, from a paper on the quaternary chalcogenides BaCu5.9STe6 and BaCu5.9SeTe6. The Se analogue is the exemplar of this proposed prototype, and this is its S member.
note: [ref 2] has two PRIMARY cells, neither ICSD-backed. BaCu6Te6S P2 (3), mp-1228010, matches the formula and is used, but only as a computed ordered cell of a Cu-deficient compound, so the phase is low. Ba4Cu11(Te4S)2 Pm (6), mp-1228217, is a different stoichiometry and is not a polymorph of this one.

basis: The composition reads GaBaFeNiO5, but the paper title is about the cobalt-free double perovskite cathode GdBaFeNiO5+delta. Ga is almost certainly a transcription of Gd, and GdBaFeNiO5 is an A-site-ordered LnBaM2O5+d layered double perovskite.
note: PARSE ISSUE: the host is probably wrong, and should be Ba-Fe-Gd-Ni-O. Ga on the lanthanide A site of this structure makes no chemical sense, because Ga3+ is far too small. The composition string should be corrected upstream. Confidence is low only because the assignment rests on that reading. As written, the composition does not correspond to a known compound.

basis: Ba3Fe1.56Ir1.44O9 single crystal, described in its paper title as a polar semiconducting triple perovskite. It is a Ba3MM2O9 hexagonal stacking with face-sharing octahedral dimers, the same family as the Ba3MIr2O9 iridates.
note: Polar means a non-centrosymmetric setting, not the usual P6_3/mmc 6H cell, so the space group is left null for the paper to fix. No structure reference was matched. Fe and Ir both sit above 5 at.% and share the octahedral sites, so neither is a dopant.

basis: LaBa0.5Sr0.5Fe1.8Cu0.2O6 is (La0.5Ba0.25Sr0.25)(Fe0.9Cu0.1)O3 written on a doubled cell. The paper is an SOFC-style XRD, XANES and conductivity study of doped Ba-Sr ferrites, and a mixed La-Ba-Sr A site in these cathode ferrites is normally disordered cubic perovskite.

dopant_roles.site: B
dopant_roles.basis: Cu replaces Fe on the octahedral B site, the usual cathode doping in these ferrites.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives Ba5SrLa2Fe4O15 Cc (9), mp-698793. It has no ICSD count and a different, oxygen-deficient stoichiometry, so it is a computed vacancy-ordered cell, not evidence for this composition. I did not follow it. The formula written as LaBa...O6 could suggest an A-site-ordered LaBaFe2O6 layered double perovskite. That is kept as an alternative, but La and Ba ordering usually needs reducing synthesis.

basis: Ba2FeMoO6 is the rock-salt B-site-ordered double perovskite, the Ba analogue of the half-metal Sr2FeMoO6. [ref 2] agrees: Ba2FeMoO6 Fm-3m (225), mp-18995, hull 0.000, 12 ICSD references.
note: Ba2FeMoO6 stays cubic because the large Ba removes octahedral tilts, unlike tetragonal Sr2FeMoO6. The full measured span reaches 849 K, but the robust range ends at 310 K.

basis: BaFe0.75Ni0.25O3-delta, from a paper describing Ni-doped BaFeO3-delta as a perovskite oxide cathode electrocatalyst. Oxygen-deficient cathode-grade BaFeO3-delta with B-site substitution is normally stabilised in the cubic perovskite. This matches the Ba-Fe-O record.
note: Undoped BaFeO3-delta readily forms hexagonal 6H or other polytypes, depending on oxygen content and synthesis. Whether 25% Ni gives cubic or hexagonal stacking should be checked in the paper. Ni is above 5 at.% and is a host element, so it has no dopant role.

basis: Ba0.96Fe3NiSb12, from a paper on RyFe3NiSb12 (R = Ba, Nd, Yb). It is a (Fe,Ni)4Sb12 skutterudite framework with Ba filling the icosahedral voids. This matches the Fe-Ni-Sb-Yb and Ba-Fe-Sb records.
note: Ba, at 0.96 per 17 atoms, is just above the 5 at.% cut, so it is counted as a host element and not listed in dopant_roles. It is still the cage filler, and stage 3 should treat its fraction as the filling fraction. Ni substitutes for Fe on the framework and supplies electrons that offset the holes of Fe4Sb12. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba2Fe1.12Os0.88O6, from a paper on high-temperature ferrimagnetism with large coercivity and exchange bias. As I recall, this compound is reported as a partially ordered 6H hexagonal perovskite with face-sharing (Fe,Os)2O9 dimers, not a cubic rock-salt double perovskite. The Fe-rich off-stoichiometry fits partial ordering over hexagonal sites. This matches the Ba-O-Os record.
note: The hexagonal assignment comes from my recollection of the full paper title, which is truncated in the chunk. The A2BBO6 formula alone would suggest double_perovskite, so this is the first thing to check against the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba0.5Sr0.5Fe0.5Sb0.5O3, from a paper on antimony-doped barium strontium ferrite perovskite cathodes. The Ba0.5Sr0.5FeO3 parent is cubic perovskite, and Sb substitutes on the B site.
note: At 50% Sb, Fe3+ and Sb5+ differ strongly in charge and size, which usually drives rock-salt B-site ordering, as in Sr2FeSbO6. So this member may be a double perovskite rather than disordered cubic, hence the alternative. The title calls Sb a dopant, which suggests the series mostly sits at low x. Check whether x = 0.5 really belongs to it or is a transcription of a smaller x. No structure reference was matched.

basis: BaFe0.7Ti0.3O3-delta, from a paper on high-temperature thermoelectric properties of BaFexTi1-xO3-delta. Fe substitution in BaTiO3 is known to stabilise the 6H hexagonal polytype over a wide range of x, and oxygen-deficient Fe-rich BaFeO3-delta also tends to hexagonal stacking.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: none of the five [ref 2] PRIMARY cells is this composition. They are computed Ba-Ti-Fe-O orderings with no ICSD count: Ba2Ti4Fe2O13, Ba2TiFeO6, Ba3Ti(FeO4)2, Ba3TiFe2O9 and BaTi2Fe4O11. None is taken. Ba3TiFe2O9 P6_3mc (186) is at least a hexagonal stacking, which is weakly consistent with this call. Cubic versus 6H at x = 0.7 is genuinely uncertain and depends on oxygen content, so the cubic perovskite alternative is kept.

basis: BaFe0.6Zn0.3Nb0.1O3-delta, from a paper on BaFe0.8Zn0.1Nb0.1O3-delta-type cathodes. It is a B-site-substituted BaFeO3-delta, where Nb5+ is the classic cubic-perovskite stabiliser, and it is cubic Pm-3m in this materials class.

dopant_roles.site: B
dopant_roles.basis: Nb5+ replaces Fe on the octahedral B site and stabilises the cubic perovskite against hexagonal stacking.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives BaZnFe6O11 Cm (8), mp-1227632, at hull 0.196 and with no ICSD count. It is a different, hexaferrite-like stoichiometry that is far above the hull, so it is not evidence about this sample and I did not take it. Zn, at 0.3 per formula, is above 5 at.% and counts as a host element sharing the B site.

basis: BaGa4 single crystal, from a paper on Fermi surfaces and charge-density waves in SrAl4 and related compounds. BaGa4 is isostructural with BaAl4, the body-centred tetragonal parent of ThCr2Si2. [ref 2] agrees: BaGa4 I4/mmm (139), mp-335, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD references.
note: The other [ref 2] entries are separate Ba-Ga compounds, not polymorphs of BaGa4: BaGa2 P6/mmm, Ba10Ga, Ba8Ga7 and Ba5Ga6. The CDW in the title belongs to SrAl4. Whether BaGa4 itself distorts below 284 K is not stated in the chunk, so no transition is recorded.

basis: Ba8Na2.97Ga3.94Ge38.91, from a paper on designing high-efficiency clathrates by systematic cross-substitution of framework elements. There are 8 Ba guests and 45.8 framework atoms of Na, Ga and Ge, which is the type-I Ba8(M,Ga,Ge)46 count.
note: Na is written as a framework cross-substituent in the Ba8M3Ga4Ge39 series of that paper, where M runs over Ni, Pt and others. Na on a tetrahedral framework site is chemically unusual, so it may partly occupy guest sites instead. That is a stage-2 site question, not a prototype one. Na, at 5.5 at.%, is a host element here. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba8Ni2.97Ga3.94Ge39.09, from the same cross-substitution clathrate paper. It is a type-I Ba8(Ni,Ga,Ge)46 clathrate, with Ni and Ga substituting in the Ge framework. This matches the Ba-Ga-Ge and Ba-Ge-Ni records.
