note: Ni and Ga are both above 5 at.% and are framework host elements, so there are no dopant roles. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba8Pt3Ga4Ge39, from a paper on transition-element substitution in clathrates. It is a type-I Ba8(Pt,Ga,Ge)46 clathrate, with Pt and Ga on the Ge framework.
note: No structure reference was matched.

basis: Gd2BaNiO5, from a paper on multiferroicity and magneto-electric effect in Gd2BaNiO5. It is a member of the R2BaNiO5 family, which has chains of apex-sharing NiO6 octahedra, and nothing in the seed taxonomy covers it, so a prototype is proposed. [ref 2] agrees: BaGd2NiO5 Immm (71), mp-19332, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD references.
note: Proposed in prototypes_proposed.jsonl as r2banio5_haldane_chain. Gd2BaNiO5 orders antiferromagnetically near 55 K, below the measured window, and the multiferroic behaviour is magnetic, not structural, so no phases split is needed.

basis: K4Ba4Zn6Ge40, from a paper on the crystal structure and thermoelectric properties of KxBa8-xZnyGe46-y clathrates. There are 8 K and Ba guests over a 46-atom Zn-Ge framework, which is type I. It matches the Ba-Ge-Zn record.
note: K replaces Ba on the guest sites. That lowers the electron count, so less Zn is needed on the framework for charge balance. Both are host elements here. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba8Ni3.4Si9.0Ge33.6, from a paper on crystal chemistry and thermoelectric properties of type-I clathrates. It is a Ba8(Ni,Si,Ge)46 type-I clathrate with a mixed Si-Ge framework.
note: Si and Ge are isoelectronic framework partners in this composition, with Si/(Si+Ge) near 0.21. There is only one composition, so no solid_solution_axis is recorded at host level. No structure reference was matched.

basis: BaRhGe3, from a paper on cage-forming compounds in the Ba-Rh-Ge system. It is a non-centrosymmetric BaNiSn3-type compound, the ordered BaAl4 derivative. [ref 2] has the exact formula: BaGe3Rh I4mm (107), mp-1070247, hull 0.038, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The other two [ref 2] cells are different compounds, not polymorphs: Ba(GeRh)2, a ThCr2Si2-type BaRh2Ge2, and Ba3(Ge4Rh)4, the Ba3Rh4Ge16 cage compound the title refers to. The chunk ranks them PRIMARY only because each formula is ranked separately.

basis: Ba3MgIr2O9, from a paper on Ba3MIr2O9 hexagonal perovskites and spin-orbit coupling. It is the 6H hexagonal perovskite with face-sharing Ir2O9 dimers and Mg on the corner-sharing octahedral site. This matches Ba-Ca-Ir-O from the same paper.
note: Mg is the small-M end of the series, so the undistorted P6_3/mmc 6H cell is expected. Ca, the large-M end, went monoclinic C2/c. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ba3SrIr2O9, from the same paper on Ba3MIr2O9 hexagonal perovskites. It is the 6H Ba3MIr2O9 stacking, with Sr as the M cation on the corner-sharing site.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: neither [ref 2] cell is this formula. Ba2SrIrO6 Fm-3m (225), mp-9115, is the cubic rock-salt double perovskite at a 2:1:1 ratio. Ba2Sr(IrO3)3 P-6m2, mp-1229074, is a computed cell at a different ratio. No mp_id is taken. Sr is very large for the M site of a 6H stacking, and that site is octahedral. So a monoclinic distortion, or even a sample that is partly Ba2SrIrO6, is possible, and the double perovskite is kept as an alternative.

basis: Ba0.35K0.65SbO3, from a paper on superconductivity in (Ba,K)SbO3. It is the antimonate analogue of Ba1-xKxBiO3, a cubic perovskite with K on the A site suppressing the Sb3+/Sb5+ charge-density wave. This matches the Ba-Bi-K-O record.
note: My recollection is that this phase is made under high pressure and is cubic at this K content. K, at 0.65 on the A site, is the doping variable rather than a dilute dopant, and it is a host element here. No structure reference was matched.

basis: BaLaNiOsO6, from a paper on crystal structures and magnetism of double perovskites. It is an A2BBO6 rock-salt B-site-ordered double perovskite with Ni2+ and Os5+ ordered on the B sites and a mixed Ba/La A site.
note: La reduces the average A-site size relative to Ba2NiOsO6, so a tilted monoclinic P2_1/n setting is likely, but the space group is left null. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Y0.5Ba0.5MnO3, from a paper on A-site randomness effects on the structure and physics of these manganites. The half-and-half formula without doubling is the A-site-disordered cubic perovskite form, which that paper sets against the A-site-ordered layered YBaMn2O6.

other_polymorphs.note: BaYMn2O6 P2/c at hull 0.075, [ref 2] PRIMARY for that formula, is the A-site-ordered form of the same composition. It is reached by a different, reducing-then-reoxidising synthesis, not by heating.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: the best-attested [ref 2] cell is BaYMn2O5 P4/mmm (123), mp-18850, with 5 ICSD references. That is the oxygen-deficient O5 ordered phase, a different composition, and it is not taken. Ordered versus disordered cannot be read from the formula. The paper studies both, so this sample could be the ordered one written on a half cell. Check against the paper.

basis: BaSrTiMoO6, from a paper on Ba doping of Sr2TiMoO6. It is the x = 1 member of (Sr,Ba)2TiMoO6, and it follows the Mo-O-Sr-Ti record, which filed Sr2TiMoO6 as the B-site double perovskite on the paper wording and an I4/m (87) [ref 2] cell.
note: Ti4+ and Mo4+ are similar in charge and size, so real B-site order in this system is weak and a disordered cubic perovskite is plausible. The perovskite alternative is kept for that reason. Ba substitution enlarges the A site and pushes towards cubic. No structure reference was matched.

basis: BaTiMoO6, from the same paper on Ba doping of Sr2TiMoO6. The formula as written is not charge- or site-balanced for a perovskite, since it has one A cation for two B cations. It is most likely Ba2TiMoO6, the full-Ba end member of the (Sr,Ba)2TiMoO6 series, with a subscript lost.
note: PARSE ISSUE: check the composition string against the paper. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: the [ref 2] cells are computed compounds of other Ba-Ti-Mo-O stoichiometries, Ba3TiMoO8 R3m and Ba5Ti4MoO15 Cmmm, with no ICSD count. They describe neither BaTiMoO6 nor Ba2TiMoO6 and are not taken. A large all-Ba A site could also favour hexagonal stacking, which is not ruled out.

basis: (Ba6O)(OsN3)2 = Ba6Os2N6O, from a paper on its synthesis, crystal structure and bonding. It is a nitridoosmate with trigonal-planar OsN3 units and O-centred Ba6 octahedra, a structure type of its own with no seed prototype. [ref 2] has the exact formula: Ba6Os2N6O R-3 (148), mp-1104257, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: I did not propose a prototype, because this is a one-compound structure type unlikely to recur. The mp_id is kept on the phase so stage 2 has the structure anyway. The OsN3 unit geometry is recalled, not checked. Ba5Os3NO18 in [ref 2] is a different compound.

basis: Ba3NiTa2O9, from a paper on high-temperature thermal properties of Ba(Ni1/3Ta2/3)O3 ceramic. It is the 1:2 B-site-ordered trigonal perovskite of the Ba(M2+1/3M5+2/3)O3 microwave-ceramic family, like Ba(Zn1/3Ta2/3)O3. [ref 2] agrees: Ba3Ta2NiO9 P-3m1 (164), mp-32310, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: In these ceramics the degree of 1:2 order depends on sintering and annealing, and a disordered cubic form exists. The measured window reaches 1473 K, where order-disorder may begin, so the cubic perovskite is kept as an alternative. The chunk prints no transition line. Ba4Ta10NiO30 in [ref 2] is a different compound.

basis: BaNi2P4, from a paper on twisted Kelvin cells and truncated octahedral cages in unconventional phosphide clathrates. It is a Ni-P framework with Ba in cages, a clathrate-like structure that does not match any seed or proposed prototype. [ref 2] has the exact formula: Ba(NiP2)2 I4/mmm (139), mp-28927, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The I4/mmm cell may be the older average structure. The paper title suggests a re-determination, possibly with a lower-symmetry twisted-cage cell, so the phase is low. It is not ThCr2Si2-type BaNi2P2, which is the separate Ba(NiP)2 entry. The other [ref 2] cells, BaNi9P5 and Ba(Ni5P3)2, are also different compounds. Once the paper is read, a single AM2P4 cage prototype should be proposed.

basis: Ba2RhO4, from a paper on its high-pressure synthesis. It is the n = 1 K2NiF4-type Ruddlesden-Popper rhodate, the Ba analogue of Sr2RhO4 and a structural relative of Ba2IrO4. This matches the O-Rh-Sr record.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: every [ref 2] cell is a different compound. BaRhO3 P6_3/mmc, with 1 ICSD reference, is a hexagonal perovskite. Ba3(RhO2)14 and Ba9Rh8O27 are computed cells with no ICSD count. BaRhO3 Pm-3m is at hull 0.112. None describes Ba2RhO4, so no mp_id is taken. Ba2RhO4 is metastable at ambient pressure, which is why it needs high-pressure synthesis, and it is absent from the snapshot.

basis: Ba0.5Sr0.5SbO3, from the same paper on antimony-doped barium strontium ferrite perovskite cathodes as Ba-Fe-O-Sb-Sr. Taken at face value, it is the Fe-free end of a Ba0.5Sr0.5Fe1-xSbxO3 perovskite series.
note: PARSE ISSUE: Ba0.5Sr0.5SbO3 needs Sb4+, which does not exist as such. It would have to be a Sb3+/Sb5+ mixed-valence perovskite like BaSbO3, which is not a plausible SOFC cathode composition. The paper is about ferrites, so the Fe term was probably lost when the composition was parsed, for example from Ba0.5Sr0.5Fe1-xSbxO3. Correct it upstream, then re-file it with Ba-Fe-O-Sb-Sr. The measured window of 673-1073 K is identical to that host.

basis: Ba2Si3P6, from a paper presenting it as a one-dimensional nonlinear optical material with thermal-barrier chains. It is a chain Zintl phosphide of its own structure type, with no seed or proposed prototype.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: neither reference describes this compound. [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives Ba3(Si2P3)2 = Ba3Si4P6, P2_1/m (11), mp-27887, and [ref 2] gives Ba4SiP4 P-43n, mp-14214. These are neighbouring Ba-Si-P phases with different Si:P ratios, not polymorphs of Ba2Si3P6. So neither mp_id is taken, although [ref 1] outranks [ref 2] by project precedence. Ba2Si3P6 is a 2019 compound, probably later than both snapshots. If a sample were actually Ba3Si4P6, [ref 1] would apply, so check the composition against the paper.

basis: Ba8Pt5Si41, from a paper on high-temperature thermoelectric properties of polycrystalline silicon clathrates. There are 8 Ba guests over a 46-atom Pt-Si framework, the type-I Ba8PtxSi46-x clathrate. This matches the Au-Ba-Si and Ba-Ni-Si records.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: none of the [ref 2] cells is a clathrate. They are BaSi3Pt I4mm, BaSiPt P2_13 and BaSi12Pt5 C2/m, which are separate Ba-Pt-Si compounds, so no mp_id is taken. The clathrate is absent from the snapshot, but the 8:46 count is unambiguous.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [107, 198]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Ba2Sb2Se5, from a paper on the synthesis, crystal structure and thermoelectric properties of two new barium antimony selenides. It is a new compound, and I do not know its structure type. No seed prototype covers the Ba-Sb-Se selenoantimonates.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: every [ref 2] cell is a different stoichiometry: Ba(SbSe2)2 = BaSb2Se4 P2_1/c, Ba3Sb2Se7 C2/c and Ba4Sb4Se11 Pnnm. These are sibling compounds, not polymorphs, so no mp_id is taken. Ba2Sb2Se5 = 2BaSe + Sb2Se3 is charge-balanced with Sb3+, so it is likely a SbSe3 or Sb2Se5 chain selenoantimonate. The paper will give the setting.

basis: BaSc2Te4 single crystal, from a paper on the new tellurides SrSc2Te4 and BaSc2Te4. As I recall, AM2Q4 compounds with a large A2+ cation and octahedral M3+ adopt the orthorhombic CaFe2O4 type, with double chains of edge-sharing MTe6 octahedra around A-filled tunnels. [ref 1] TEDesignLab agrees on the setting: Ba(ScTe2)2 Pnma (62), mp-17501, hull 0.002, 1 ICSD reference.
note: TAXONOMY SCOPE: cafe2o4_postspinel is written for oxides, and its formula_archetype says AM2O4. Using it for a telluride stretches the definition. The reviewer should either widen it to chalcogenides or split out a chalcogenide variant. That the telluride is CaFe2O4-type is my recollection, and it rests only on Pnma matching, which is weak on its own because many AM2Q4 types are Pnma.

basis: Sr0.81Ba0.19Si2, from a paper on thermoelectric properties of cubic Ba-substituted strontium disilicide. It is the cubic chiral SrSi2 (P4_332) structure with Ba on the Sr site. This matches the Si-Sr record.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives only BaSrSi4 C222_1 (20), mp-1227347, and Pnma, mp-1227506. Both are computed 1:1 Ba:Sr orderings with no ICSD count, at a different composition. The paper title says cubic, so neither is taken. Ba, at 0.19/3 = 6.3 at.%, is just above the cut and is a host element. It is an isovalent A-site substituent for Sr.

basis: Ba2SnTe5, from an exploratory-synthesis paper on new heavy main-group chalcogenides. It is a Ba telluro-stannate that is Te-rich relative to charge balance, so it must contain Te-Te bonds, for example Te2 dumbbells alongside SnTe4 tetrahedra. I do not know its structure type, and no reference covers it.
note: With Ba2+ and Sn4+, five Te would need a total charge of -8, so at least one Te-Te bond per formula is required. That makes it a Zintl polytelluride, but the arrangement is unknown and the paper should be read.

basis: BaY2Te4 single crystal, measured in the same paper as BaSc2Te4. It is the Y analogue in the same orthorhombic AM2Te4 family. [ref 1] TEDesignLab agrees on the setting: Ba(YTe2)2 Pnma (62), mp-17872, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: TAXONOMY SCOPE: this has the same oxide-only definition problem as Ba-Sc-Te, and the two should be moved together. The chunk titles the paper for SrSc2Te4 and BaSc2Te4, but the sample here is BaY2Te4. That may be a truncated title covering more compounds, or a paper-linkage error.

basis: The composition reads CeBe2, but I know of no CeBe2 compound. The only Ce-Be binary I recall, and the only one in [ref 2], is CeBe13, NaZn13-type Fm-3c (226), mp-457 with 6 ICSD references. The paper is titled for zirconium copper as a low-temperature material, which matches neither.
note: PARSE ISSUE: CeBe2 may be a truncation of CeBe13, which would make this nazn13_type like Be-Th and Be-U. The paper link may also be wrong. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] points to CeBe13, but I have not matched to it, because the composition says otherwise and a Be:Ce ratio of 2 against 13 is not a doping difference. Check the curve source before re-filing.

basis: CePd3Be0.4, from a paper on the Kondo effect and thermoelectric transport in CePd3Bex. It is the L12 Cu3Au-type intermediate-valence CePd3 with Be in the body-centre octahedral hole, the same arrangement as the CePd3Bx record (B-Ce-Pd).
note: Be, at 0.4/4.4 = 9 at.%, is above the cut and counts as a host element, so it has no dopant role. Physically it is an interstitial filler of the 1b octahedral site. Stage 3 should treat x as the filling fraction, as for B in CePd3Bx. No structure reference was matched.

basis: ThBe13, from a paper on the Seebeck coefficient of heavy-fermion compounds, where it serves as the non-magnetic reference for UBe13. It is the cubic NaZn13 type. [ref 2] agrees: ThBe13 Fm-3c (226), mp-1562, hull 0.000, 7 ICSD references. This matches the Be-U record.
note: Th3Be Pm-3m, at hull 0.338, is a computed cell of a different formula, not a polymorph, and is not listed.

basis: VBe12, from a paper on beryllides for fusion reactors. MBe12 beryllides of V, Cr, Mo, W and Ti are ThMn12-type tetragonal I4/mmm, which matches the Be-Ti record.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives only Be2V P6_3/mmc (194), mp-11281, a C14 Laves phase of a different composition. VBe12 is absent from the snapshot, so no mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [139], ICSD-backed references for this host report [194]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: BiOBr single crystal, from a paper on reduced dimensionality in the bismuth oxyhalides. BiOX is the PbFCl (matlockite) type, P4/nmm, with fluorite-like Bi2O2 layers separated by double halide layers. [ref 2] agrees: BiBrO P4/nmm (129), mp-23072, hull 0.000, 5 ICSD references.
note: The other [ref 2] entries (Bi4Br2O5, Bi3BrO4, Bi12Br5O16, Bi2Br2O) are different formulas in the same chemistry, not polymorphs of BiOBr, and are not listed.

basis: (Bi2Te3)88.56(C14H14O5S2)11.44, and the curator detail names the second component as PEDOT:PSS. This is an inorganic-organic composite of tetradymite Bi2Te3 with a conducting polymer, filed the same way as the Bi-C-H-Te and Bi-C-Te composites.

dopant_roles.basis: The sulfur is the sulfonate group of PSS in the polymer phase, not a substituent in the Bi2Te3 lattice.

note: The phases entry describes the inorganic Bi2Te3 component only; the polymer has no crystal structure to record. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3CeBi3 single crystal, from a paper on disordered rare-earth compounds of the Ca3REPn3 family. (Ca3RE)Bi3 is an M4Pn3 composition, the anti-Th3P4 type (I-43d) with Ca and the rare earth disordered on the cation site, the same arrangement as Yb4Sb3 in the Bi-Sb-Yb record.
note: Anti-Th3P4: the pnictogen takes the Th site. Ce at 1/7 of the formula is a host element sharing the cation site with Ca, so it has no dopant role. The paper title is truncated, so the structure type is inferred from the 4:3 ratio. Confidence is medium for that reason. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi2Ca1.99Co1.44Al0.28O7I0.98, from a paper on iodine-intercalated misfit layered cobalt oxides. This is the Bi2Ca2Co2Oy misfit cobaltite (a Bi2Ca2O4 rocksalt block on a CdI2-type CoO2 layer) with iodine inserted between the BiO layers, as in iodine-intercalated Bi-2212.

dopant_roles.site: CoO2 layer
dopant_roles.basis: Al3+ at 0.28 alongside Co 1.44 sums to about 1.7 on the cobalt site. It is small and trivalent, so it goes on the octahedral CoO2 layer.

note: Iodine at 0.98 is about 7 at.%, so it is a host element, and it is an intercalant rather than a substituent. Stage 2 needs the misfit handling: two subsystems, no single MP entry. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi1.1Pb1.1Sr1.4Ca1.4Co2O9, from a paper on magneto-thermoelectric effects in layered cobalt oxides. It is the (Bi,Pb)2(Sr,Ca)2Co2Oy misfit cobaltite, the same family as the Bi-Co-O-Sr, Bi-Ca-Co-O-Sr and Bi-Ca-Co-O-Pb records.
note: Pb shares the Bi site of the rocksalt block and Ca shares the Sr site. Both are host elements here. Incommensurate composite, so there is no single MP entry. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu2ErO10, from a paper on Er-substituted Bi-2223 glass-ceramic superconductors. The host is the BSCCO homologous series. With Er in the formula and only two Cu, the product is more likely Bi-2212-like than true 2223.
note: Er is a full formula unit (about 6 at.%), so it is a host element. The nominal composition is written as if one Cu were replaced by Er; Er3+ normally goes on the Ca site in BSCCO, and a glass-ceramic route often leaves secondary phases. Which n-member forms has to be taken from the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (Bi1.6Pb0.4)Sr2Ca3(Cu0.965Si0.35)4O12, from a paper on the thermoelectric power of Si-doped (Bi,Pb)SrCaCuO superconductors. The nominal cation ratio is Bi-2234 on the Pb-stabilised 2223 route, which is the BSCCO homologous series.

dopant_roles.site: BiO layer
dopant_roles.basis: Pb at 0.4 of the Bi site is the standard phase stabiliser for Bi-2223.

note: The Si fraction as written (0.35 x 4 = 1.4 Si against 3.86 Cu) is far above what Si4+ can put on a square-planar Cu site. It likely means 0.035 or a Si-rich secondary phase such as Ca2SiO4. Si is therefore a host element here only because of how the composition is written. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca2Dy7Bi5O5, from a paper on the transport properties and compositions of Ca2RE7Pn5O5 phases. These rare-earth pnictide oxides belong to the (RE,Ca)mPnnOm family that also contains RE2O2Pn, but the 9:5:5 member is a separate structure type, and I cannot give its space group with confidence. It is not the I4/mmm square-net RE2O2Pn, so it is left unresolved rather than forced into re2o2pn_square_net.
note: A candidate for a new prototype (RE9Pn5O5 / Ca2RE7Pn5O5), not proposed here because the space group would have to come from memory. Resolve from the paper; same for Bi-Ca-Gd-O. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Er2O1.4Bi1.3(CaO)0.5, from the paper titled Superconductivity in Anti-ThCr2Si2-type Er2O2Bi. The host is Er2O2Bi with Ca added: fluorite-like Er2O2 layers alternating with a bonded Bi square net, I4/mmm.
note: LEDGER INCONSISTENCY: the Bi-Er-O record (chunk 20, same paper) was filed under bi2o2se_layered, before re2o2pn_square_net was proposed in chunk 40 for exactly this compound class. I use the newer, more specific id; Bi-Er-O should be moved to match. Ca at about 9 at.% is a host element. As written, (CaO)0.5 suggests CaO is a second phase or flux residue rather than Ca on the Er site. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3ErBi1.5Sb1.5, from the same paper on disordered Ca3REPn3 compounds as the Ca3REBi3 hosts. It is an anti-Th3P4 M4Pn3 phase (I-43d) with Ca/Er disordered on the cation site and Bi/Sb on the pnictogen site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen site of the anti-Th3P4 framework
solid_solution_axis.note: An equimolar Bi/Sb mix, isoelectronic, used for disorder and mass contrast.

note: No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi0.7Ca0.3FeO3, from a paper on calcium doping of BiFeO3. It is Ca-substituted BiFeO3, a rhombohedrally distorted perovskite (R3c), the same as the Bi-Fe-O record. At 30 percent Ca the distortion may relax toward a pseudocubic or orthorhombic cell, but it stays perovskite.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only CaFe2BiO6 I4mm (107), mp-1227229, a computed ordered cell at hull 0.506 with no ICSD support and a different formula. It is not taken. Ca at 6 at.% is a host element on the A site. BiFeO3 has its Neel point near 640 K and its ferroelectric Curie point near 1100 K, and both shift with Ca. The measurement runs to 1074 K, so the R3c phase may not be the only one; the space group is given at medium confidence.

basis: Ca2Gd7Bi5O5, from the same paper on Ca2RE7Pn5O5 phases as Bi-Ca-Dy-O. This is a rare-earth pnictide oxide of the (RE,Ca)mPnnOm family, not the I4/mmm RE2O2Pn member. I cannot assign its space group with confidence, so it is left unresolved rather than forced into an existing id.
note: Resolve with Bi-Ca-Dy-O from the paper; both should move together if a Ca2RE7Pn5O5 prototype is proposed. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3HoBi1.5Sb1.5, from the paper on disordered Ca3REPn3 compounds. It is an anti-Th3P4 M4Pn3 phase (I-43d) with Ca/Ho disordered on the cation site and Bi/Sb on the pnictogen site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen site of the anti-Th3P4 framework
solid_solution_axis.note: An equimolar Bi/Sb mix on the pnictogen site.

note: Same series as Bi-Ca-Er-Sb, Bi-Ca-La-Sb and Bi-Ca-Lu-Sb. No structure reference was matched.

basis: IBi2Sr2CaO8, from a paper on iodine-intercalated Bi2Sr2CaCu2Oy. The host is Bi-2212 with iodine inserted between the double BiO layers.
note: The composition has no copper, which cannot be right for the superconductor the paper studies. The Cu2 of IBi2Sr2CaCu2O8 was almost certainly dropped in transcription, so the host key itself is wrong. Iodine is a host-level intercalant. Same paper as Bi-Ca-O-Sr, which has the same missing Cu. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3LaBi3 single crystal, from the paper on disordered Ca3REPn3 compounds. (Ca3La)Bi3 is an anti-Th3P4 M4Pn3 phase (I-43d) with Ca and La disordered on the cation site.
note: Same series as Bi-Ca-Ce, Bi-Ca-Nd, Bi-Ca-Pr and Bi-Ca-Sm. No structure reference was matched for La.

basis: Ca3LaBi1.5Sb1.5, from the paper on disordered Ca3REPn3 compounds. It is an anti-Th3P4 M4Pn3 phase (I-43d) with Ca/La on the cation site and Bi/Sb on the pnictogen site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen site of the anti-Th3P4 framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Equimolar Bi and Sb on the pnictogen site, the same as the Er, Ho and Lu members.

note: No structure reference was matched for the La member.

basis: Ca3LuBi1.5Sb1.5, from the paper on disordered Ca3REPn3 compounds. It is an anti-Th3P4 M4Pn3 phase (I-43d) with Ca/Lu on the cation site and Bi/Sb on the pnictogen site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen site of the anti-Th3P4 framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Equimolar Bi and Sb on the pnictogen site. Lu is the smallest rare earth in the series.

note: Lu3+ is much smaller than Ca2+, so the cation site is the most strained in this series. Single-phase formation is worth checking in the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3NdBi3 single crystal, from the paper on disordered Ca3REPn3 compounds. (Ca3Nd)Bi3 is an anti-Th3P4 M4Pn3 phase (I-43d) with Ca and Nd disordered on the cation site.
note: Same series as Bi-Ca-Ce. No structure reference was matched for Nd.

basis: Bi2Sr2CaO8, from the same paper on iodine-intercalated Bi2Sr2CaCu2Oy as Bi-Ca-I-O-Sr. It is the pristine Bi-2212 reference sample, with the Cu2 missing from the transcribed formula.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] matches the Cu-free formula literally and returns Sr8Ca3(Bi3O11)2 P2_1/c (14), mp-1208822, a Bi-Sr-Ca oxide with no ICSD count shown. That is what the transcription error points to, not what the paper made. No mp_id is taken. The host key is wrong because Cu was dropped; this should be corrected upstream to Bi-Ca-Cu-O-Sr.

basis: Ca3PrBi3 single crystal, from the paper on disordered Ca3REPn3 compounds. (Ca3Pr)Bi3 is an anti-Th3P4 M4Pn3 phase (I-43d) with Ca and Pr disordered on the cation site.
note: Same series as Bi-Ca-Ce. No structure reference was matched for Pr.

basis: Ca3SmBi3 single crystal, from the paper on disordered Ca3REPn3 compounds. (Ca3Sm)Bi3 is an anti-Th3P4 M4Pn3 phase (I-43d) with Ca and Sm disordered on the cation site.
note: Same series as Bi-Ca-Ce. No structure reference was matched for Sm.

basis: CsCdBi3Se6, from a paper on the homologous series A2[M5+nSe9+n] with A = Rb, Cs and M = Bi plus a divalent metal. These are alkali bismuth selenides built from NaCl-type and Bi2Te3-type rod fragments, each member its own structure. That is what bi_chalcogenide_complex covers, the same as the Bi-K-Se and Bi-Pb-Se records.
note: Cd shares the octahedral M sites with Bi. It is a host element at 1/11 of the formula. Oriented bulk sample. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CdPb2Bi4S9, from a paper titled Six Quaternary Chalcogenides of the Pavonite Homologous Series. The paper places it in that series by name, and pavonite_agbi3s5 was proposed for the homologous series and not just AgBi3S5.
note: A higher pavonite homologue (N greater than 3) in which Cd and Pb replace Ag. The monoclinic C2/m setting is the one usual for the series, and the paper should confirm the member and cell. Confidence is medium because this is a quaternary member rather than AgBi3S5 itself. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Cd4Bi2Te7, from a paper on CdTe nanoparticles self-reorganising into two-dimensional Bi2Te3/CdTe structures. The formula is 4 CdTe + Bi2Te3 added together, not a ternary compound. The sample is a Bi2Te3 (tetradymite) and CdTe (sphalerite) nanocomposite.
note: The two phases coexist over the whole range; they are not a thermal sequence. The EDX ratio in the curator detail is what the formula was derived from. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ce2O2Bi, from a paper on magnetic and magnetotransport properties of anti-ThCr2Si2-type RE2O2Bi. It is fluorite-like Ce2O2 layers alternating with a bonded Bi square net, I4/mmm, which is the entry re2o2pn_square_net was proposed for. [ref 2] agrees: Ce2BiO2 I4/mmm (139), mp-23003, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD references.
note: The primary rests on 2 ICSD references, which the chunk flags as weak, but the paper names the structure type. As with Bi-Ca-Er-O, the earlier Bi-Er-O record uses bi2o2se_layered for the same compound class and should be aligned.

basis: Ce0.3Bi1.7Se0.3Te2.7, from a paper on Ce-doped n-type CexBi2-xTe2.7Se0.3. The host is the n-type Bi2(Te,Se)3 tetradymite with Ce on the Bi site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen sites of the tetradymite quintuple layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Se is 0.3 of 3 chalcogens, the standard n-type Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 alloy.

note: Ce at 0.3 per formula is 6 at.%, just over the cut, so it is a host element, although the paper treats it as a dopant on the Bi site. Stage 3 should treat it as Bi-site substitution. At 15 percent of the Bi site it may partly form a secondary phase. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ce0.3Bi1.7Te3, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of flower-like nanoparticles. This is Ce-substituted Bi2Te3, tetradymite R-3m.
note: Ce at 6 at.% is a host element by the cut but is physically a Bi-site substituent, as in Bi-Ce-Se-Te. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (K2Bi8Se13)68.33(BiCl3)31.67, and the curator detail says K2Bi8Se13 + 5% BiCl3. The paper is on multiple converged conduction bands in K2Bi8Se13. The host is K2Bi8Se13 (P2_1/m), filed under bi_chalcogenide_complex as in the Bi-K-Se record, with BiCl3 added as an n-type Cl dopant.
note: The parsed coefficients (68.33 : 31.67) do not match the curator 5% BiCl3, so the parse has inflated Cl above the cut and made it a host element. Physically Cl is a substitutional donor on the Se site at a few percent, and stage 3 should use the curator value. No structure reference was matched.

basis: BiOCl single crystal, from the same paper on reduced dimensionality in bismuth oxyhalides as Bi-Br-O. BiOCl is the PbFCl (matlockite) type P4/nmm. [ref 2] agrees: BiClO P4/nmm (129), mp-22939, hull 0.000, 5 ICSD references.
note: The other [ref 2] Bi-Cl-O entries are different formulas, not BiOCl polymorphs.

basis: (Bi2S3)0.99(BiCl3), from the paper titled Tellurium-Free Thermoelectric: The Anisotropic n-Type Semiconductor Bi2S3. This is Bi2S3 (stibnite type, Pnma) with BiCl3 added as a Cl donor, the same host as the Bi-S record.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives BiSCl Pnma (62), mp-23318, as primary on 2 ICSD references. That is the ternary chalcohalide, which is not what the paper made, so its mp_id is not taken even though the space group number matches. The BiCl3 coefficient was almost certainly 0.01 in the paper and lost its decimal, which puts Cl above the cut. Physically Cl is a substitutional donor on the S site.

basis: BiTeCl, from a paper on its low-temperature thermoelectric properties. BiTeCl is the polar layered BiTeX family, P6_3mc for the chloride, the same entry as the Bi-I-Te and Bi-Br-Te records. [ref 2] lists BiTeCl P6_3mc (186), mp-28944, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The chunk ranks the host references by ICSD count, which puts Bi2Te4Cl7 P2_12_12_1 (2 refs) first. That is a different formula and is not taken. For BiTeCl itself the single entry is mp-28944. The chloride stacks differently from BiTeI (P3m1), which is why the space group differs within the same prototype.

basis: Bi2Mg2CoO6, from a paper on thermoelectric properties of layered Bi2A2Co2Oy compounds. The paper places it in the Bi-based misfit cobaltite series with Mg on the A site. Mg2+ is much smaller than Ca2+ or Sr2+, and the formula carries one Co where the series has two, so whether a single misfit phase forms is doubtful.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] returns only computed MgO-rich rocksalt supercells (Mg14CoBiO16, Mg30CoBiO32, Mg6CoBiO8, all P4/mmm, no ICSD support, one flagged AMBIGUOUS). They describe Co/Bi-substituted MgO, not a layered cobaltite. None is taken. A MgO-based secondary phase alongside a Bi-Co oxide is a real possibility, which is why composite_multiphase is the alternative. Check the XRD in the paper.

basis: Bi1.4Pb0.8Sr2Co2O9, from a paper on the Bi2.2-xPbxSr2Co2Oy system. This is the Pb-substituted Bi2Sr2Co2Oy misfit cobaltite, the same as the Bi-Co-O-Sr record.
note: Pb at 0.8 shares the Bi site of the rocksalt block and is a host element. This is an incommensurate composite, so there is no single MP entry. No structure reference was matched.

basis: ZrCoBi0.60Sb0.20Sn0.20, from a paper on ZrCoBi-based half-Heuslers. The host is ZrCoBi (F-43m), with Sb alloyed and Sn as the p-type acceptor on the Bi site, the same series as the Bi-Co-Zr and Bi-Co-Sn-Zr records.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the 4b pnictogen site of the half-Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: Sb is 0.2 of the 0.8 pnictogen on this site. Sn, at 0.2, takes the rest of the site as an acceptor. At 6.7 at.% it is a host element by the cut, but physically it is the p-type dopant.

note: No structure reference was matched.

basis: Cs4Cu3Bi9S17, from the paper titled The New Semiconductor Cs4Cu3Bi9S17. It is a new alkali copper bismuth sulfide with its own structure type, which is what bi_chalcogenide_complex covers, the same as the Bi-Cu-S record.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives Cs3Cu2(BiS2)5 = Cs3Cu2Bi5S10 Pnnm (58), mp-669419, on 1 ICSD reference. That is a related compound but a different formula. The paper reports Cs4Cu3Bi9S17 as new, so it is unlikely to be in the 2019 snapshot. No mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [11], ICSD-backed references for this host report [58]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CsBiNb2O7 epitaxial layers, from a paper on their low thermal conductivity. CsBiNb2O7 is the n = 2 Dion-Jacobson layered perovskite, Cs[BiNb2O7], with a single Cs layer between double NbO6 perovskite slabs. It is polar orthorhombic, P2_1am.
note: The sample is an epitaxial film, so the symmetry may be substrate-constrained. The prototype is secure but the space group is medium confidence. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CsBi3Se5, from a paper on the homologous series A2[M5+nSe9+n] (A = Rb, Cs; M = Bi and a divalent metal). CsBi3Se5 = Cs2Bi6Se10 is the n = 1 member. Each member is its own structure, which is what bi_chalcogenide_complex covers.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: none of the five [ref 2] Cs-Bi-Se entries (Cs2Bi8Se13, Cs3Bi7Se12, Cs2Bi4Se7, Cs3Bi11Se18, CsBi4Se7) is CsBi3Se5. They are other phases in the same chemistry, several with no ICSD support, so no mp_id is taken. The paper describes the series as having a divalent metal on M, so the ternary member may be nominal. Same paper as Bi-Cd-Cs-Se.

basis: CsBi4Te5.0Se1.0, from a paper on Sb and Se substitution in CsBi4Te6, where the resulting semiconductors are written CsM4Q6. It is Se-substituted CsBi4Te6 (C2/m), the same entry as the Bi-Cs-Te record.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen sites of CsBi4Te6
solid_solution_axis.note: One of six chalcogens is Se. The paper reports CsBi4Q6 as keeping the CsBi4Te6 structure under this substitution.

note: No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi2Sr1.4La0.6CuO6, from a paper on transport in Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+d. This is La-substituted Bi-2201, the n = 1 member of the BSCCO series, with La3+ on the Sr site to underdope it.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: the three [ref 2] entries (Sr2LaCu2(BiO4)2 Cccm, Sr3LaCu2(BiO3)4 P1, Sr7LaCu4(BiO3)8 P1) are computed ordered cells with no ICSD support and different formulas. None is Bi-2201, so no mp_id is taken. La at 6 at.% is a host element; its doping role is the Sr-site hole-count knob, as the paper intends.

basis: Bi0.8Mg0.2CuSeO, from a paper on doping for higher thermoelectric properties in p-type BiCuSeO. This is BiCuSeO (ZrCuSiAs 1111 type, P4/nmm) with Mg on the Bi site, the same as the Bi-Cu-O-Se record.
note: Mg at 0.2 of 4 atoms sits at exactly 5 at.%, so it lands on the host side of the cut. It is physically a Bi-site acceptor in the Bi2O2 layer. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi0.875Ba0.125Cu0.8Ni0.2SeO, from a paper on raising the Seebeck coefficient of BiCuSeO. This is BiCuSeO (ZrCuSiAs 1111, P4/nmm) with Ni on the Cu site of the Cu2Se2 layer and Ba on the Bi site.

dopant_roles.site: Bi2O2 layer
dopant_roles.basis: Ba2+ on the Bi3+ site is the standard hole dopant in BiCuSeO and also lowers the lattice thermal conductivity.

note: Ni at 0.2 of the Cu site sits at 5 at.% and falls on the host side of the cut. It substitutes for Cu in the conducting Cu2Se2 layer. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi0.70Yb0.30CuSeO, from a paper on optimising BiCuSeO by doping. This is BiCuSeO (ZrCuSiAs 1111, P4/nmm) with Yb on the Bi site of the Bi2O2 layer.
note: Yb at 0.3 of the Bi site (7.5 at.%) is a host element. Whether it is Yb3+ (isovalent) or partly Yb2+ (acceptor) is a question for the paper. 30 percent is high enough that a Yb2O3 secondary phase is possible. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (EuF)2Ti2Bi2O, from a paper on layered titanium-based pnictide oxides. It carries the same anti-CuO2 Ti2O sheet capped by Bi as Na2Ti2Sb2O, with a fluorite-type (EuF)2 block in place of the alkali layer. It is the Eu member of the (SrF)2Ti2Pn2O family, I4/mmm.
note: The Ti2Pn2O slab is the same as in the proposed entry, but the spacer is a fluorite (EuF)2 double layer rather than a single alkali layer. That makes it an intergrowth variant. If the reviewers want the spacer to define the prototype, this needs its own entry. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Sm0.5Eu0.5Mg2Bi1.99, from a paper on p-type SmMg2Bi2. This is the CaAl2Si2-type 122 Zintl (P-3m1) with Sm and Eu sharing the cation site, the same as the Bi-Mg-Sm and Bi-Eu-Mg-Sm-Yb records.
note: Bi1.99 is a deliberate slight Bi deficiency, a non-stoichiometry knob for the carrier count. It is not a dopant. No structure reference was matched.

basis: EuMnBi2, from a paper on a magnetopiezoelectric effect in this antiferromagnetic Dirac semimetal. EuMnBi2 is an AMnBi2 112 compound: MnBi4 tetrahedral layers alternating with Eu-sandwiched Bi square nets. That is the same entry as the Bi-Mn-Sr and Bi-Ca-Mn records. [ref 2] gives EuMnBi2 I4/mmm (139), mp-1078314, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The mp entry sits at hull 0.186, which is high for a compound that is routinely grown as single crystals. That is probably the usual magnetic or DFT artefact for Eu 4f states and not a reason to doubt the phase. The primary rests on 1 ICSD reference and is flagged weak.

basis: EuBiSe3, from a paper on single-crystal EuBiSe3 fibres. I do not know a settled structure type for EuBiSe3, so it is filed under the catch-all for bismuth chalcogenides that are each their own structure.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives Eu(BiSe2)2 = EuBi2Se4 Pnma (62), mp-1193071, on 2 ICSD references. That is a different Eu:Bi ratio from the composition. The fibre may be EuBi2Se4 with a mis-stated formula, or a separate phase. I record the disagreement rather than adopting the reference, and no mp_id is taken. Resolve from the paper.

basis: EuZnBi2, from the same magnetopiezoelectric paper as EuMnBi2. The paper appears to use it as a Zn analogue of EuMnBi2. AZnPn2 compounds (for example EuZnSb2 and SrZnSb2) are 112 square-net structures, so this entry is the best fit.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only Eu2ZnBi2 P-6m2 (187), mp-1225393, a computed cell at hull 0.090 with no ICSD support and a different formula. It is not taken. The space group is left null because which 112 variant (P4/nmm, I4/mmm or I4/mcm) EuZnBi2 adopts has to come from the paper.

basis: La0.6Bi0.4Mn0.6Fe0.4O3.1, from a paper on Fe and Ni substitution in a ferromagnetic-insulating manganite. This is an ABO3 perovskite with La/Bi on A and Mn/Fe on B, the same entry as the Bi-La-Mn-O record.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives LaMnFe3(BiO4)3 Cm (8), mp-1223013, a computed ordered cell at hull 0.060 with no ICSD support and a different cation ratio. It is not taken. O3.1 is oxygen excess, which in manganites is accommodated as cation vacancies. The distortion (orthorhombic or rhombohedral) is left null for the paper to settle.

basis: La22.3Bi35.3Te37.2Fe5.2, from a paper on solvothermal synthesis of lanthanum-containing Bi2Te3. The intended host is Bi2Te3 (tetradymite). But La at 22 at.% cannot sit on the Bi site of a single tetradymite phase, and Fe at 5 at.% is not a deliberate addition. The measured sample is almost certainly multiphase.
note: This looks like an EDX analysis in at.% rather than a nominal formula. The La excess would most plausibly go into a La telluride such as La2Te3 or La3Te4 (th3p4), and the Fe is probably steel-autoclave contamination. Both La and Fe are host elements by the cut. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Fe60Ni20Bi10Si10, from a paper on thermoelectric power singularities of FeNiBSi amorphous alloys. The paper is about Fe-Ni-B-Si metallic glasses, so Bi here is a transcription or parse error for B (boron). The sample is an amorphous Fe60Ni20B10Si10 ribbon.
note: HOST KEY WRONG: Bi should be B, which would make the host B-Fe-Ni-Si. Bismuth has no place in an FeNiBSi glass and would not form one. This should be corrected upstream. The measurement reaches 946 K, above typical Fe-based glass crystallisation temperatures (about 700-800 K), so the upper part of the curve may be from a partly crystallised ribbon. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi0.50Sr0.50FeO3, from a paper on Sr-doped BiMO3 (M = Mn, Fe, Y) perovskites. This is the BiFeO3-SrFeO3 perovskite solid solution with Bi and Sr sharing the A site. At 50% Sr the R3c polar distortion of BiFeO3 is suppressed, leaving a pseudo-cubic perovskite.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks Sr15Fe10(Bi5O23)2 C222 (mp-617430, 2 ICSD references) first. None of the five listed phases is an A(Bi,Sr)FeO3 perovskite at a 1:1:1 A:Fe:O3 ratio, and the paper title says perovskite, so the reference is not followed and no mp_id is taken. The cubic Pm-3m space group assumes the Sr has fully suppressed the rhombohedral distortion. A slight rhombohedral or orthorhombic distortion may survive at x = 0.5, so confirm from the XRD.

basis: FeBi4S7, from a paper on XBi4S7 (X = Mn, Fe) compounds. This is the Fe member of the MnBi4S7 structure type, filed with the Bi-Mn-S host.
note: [ref 2] FeBi4S7 C2/m (mp-1095303) matches the formula and the space group of the MnBi4S7 type. It rests on 1 ICSD reference and sits at hull 0.126, so it is a weak primary but the formula match is exact.

basis: Bi1.7Fe0.3Te3 single crystal, from a paper on doped Bi2Te3 single crystals. This is Bi2Te3 with Fe on the Bi site.
note: Fe at 0.3 per formula is 6 at.%, so it counts as a host element by the 5% cut, although it is a dopant on the Bi site (Fe for Bi). At that level in a grown crystal some Fe may end up in FeTe or FeTe2 inclusions. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Zr6FeBi2 is a member of the Zr6CoAs2 family (ordered Fe2P type, P-62m), like the Zr6MSb2 and Zr6MBi2 phases in the paper on ternary transition metal antimonides.
note: [ref 2] Zr6FeBi2 P-62m (mp-1205897, hull 0.000) matches both the formula and the prototype space group.

basis: BiGdIr2O7, from a paper on Gd doping of pyrochlore Bi2Ir2O7. Gd replaces half the Bi on the A site of the cubic pyrochlore.
note: Gd is a host element here (Gd for Bi, 50% of the A site). This is consistent with the Bi-Ir-O and Gd-Ir-O pyrochlore assignments. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Gd8Bi3O8, from a paper on the synthesis and crystal structure of Gd3BiO3 and a related phase. These are rare-earth-rich suboxide bismuthides: Gd-O slabs with Bi anions, not a Bi3+ oxide. The taxonomy has no prototype for them.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks Gd2BiO2 I4/mmm (mp-1070662, the La2O2Bi square-net type) and Gd3BiO3 C2/m (mp-1103896) first, on 1 ICSD reference each. Neither has the Gd8Bi3O8 stoichiometry, so no mp_id is taken. I recall that Gd8Bi3O8 is monoclinic and related to Gd3BiO3, but I have not checked this, so no space group is recorded. A dedicated prototype should be proposed once the structure is read from the paper.

basis: Mg2Si0.7Ge0.3Bi0.2, from a paper on Bi-doped Mg2Si0.7Ge0.3 made by a solid-state route. This is an antifluorite Mg2(Si,Ge) solid solution with Bi as the n-type dopant on the Si/Ge site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion (4a)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Ge/(Si+Ge), a single composition.

note: Bi at 0.2 per formula is 6 at.%, so it counts as a host element by the cut. That is well above the solubility of Bi in Mg2Si (about 0.03), so most of the Bi probably sits in a secondary Mg3Bi2 phase. This is consistent with the Ge-Mg-Si and Bi-Mg-Si antifluorite assignments. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (Ge0.87Pb0.13Te)0.93(Bi2Te3)0.07, from a paper on stacking faults in a GeTe-based alloy. This is rhombohedral GeTe alloyed with PbTe and Bi2Te3.
note: The chunk file shows no MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line, because no taxonomy hypothesis is attached to this host. But GeTe goes from R3m to cubic Fm-3m near 700 K, and both Pb and Bi lower that temperature. The 600 K value is an estimate for this composition, not taken from the paper. Bi2Te3 at 7 mol% also introduces the Ge vacancies and stacking faults that the title refers to. No structure reference was matched.

basis: BiOI single crystal. This is the bismuth oxyiodide member of the BiOX family (PbFCl/matlockite type, P4/nmm), filed like the Bi-Cl-O and Bi-Br-O hosts.
note: [ref 2] BiIO P4/nmm (mp-22987, hull 0.000, 5 ICSD references) matches the formula and the prototype.

basis: IBi2Sr2Ca0.6Y0.4O8, from a paper on iodine-intercalated Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8. The Bi2Sr2(Ca,Y)O8 formula is exactly Bi-2212 with the Cu2 missing, so Cu was lost when the composition was transcribed. The sample is Y-doped Bi-2212 with iodine between the BiO double layers.

dopant_roles.site: Ca site between the CuO2 planes
dopant_roles.basis: Ca is the Ca-site host element of Bi-2212 and is partly replaced by Y. It falls below 5 at.% only because of the formula normalisation.

dopant_roles.site: Ca site between the CuO2 planes
dopant_roles.basis: Y3+ for Ca2+ is the standard underdoping substitution in Bi-2212. It removes holes from the CuO2 planes.

note: HOST KEY WRONG: Cu is missing from the composition, so the host should be Bi-Ca-Cu-I-O-Sr (or Bi-Cu-I-O-Sr under the 5% cut). This should be corrected upstream. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] SrBi3I3O4 I4mm (mp-1218434) is a Cu-free oxyiodide. It matches only because Cu is missing from the key, so it is not followed. Iodine intercalation expands the c axis, and the incommensurate modulation of Bi-2212 means no single space group is recorded.

basis: Bi2NaIrO6 single crystal, from a paper on a Jeff = 0 ground state. With Na+ and 2 Bi3+ this charge-balances to Ir5+ (5d4), which is the Jeff = 0 case. I cannot place this sodium bismuth iridate in a known structure type with confidence.
note: The A2BB-prime O6 ratio suggests a double perovskite, but Bi3+ with Na+ on a large site is also common in defect pyrochlores. Read the structure from the paper before assigning. No structure reference was matched.

basis: K0.5Bi0.5VO3, from a paper titled Na1/2Bi1/2VO3 and K1/2Bi1/2VO3: new lead-free tetragonal perovskites. This is an A-site-disordered (K,Bi)VO3 perovskite with a polar tetragonal distortion.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives K3V3(BiO6)2 C2/c (mp-622115, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference), a different ambient-pressure phase with V5+. The perovskite has V4+ and is almost certainly a high-pressure product quenched to ambient, so it is not the hull ground state. The reference is not followed and no mp_id is taken. The P4mm (99) space group follows the tetragonal-polar description in the title and is not confirmed.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [99], ICSD-backed references for this host report [15]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: K1.46Sn3.09Bi7.45Se15, from a paper on the modular A1+xM4-2xM-prime7+xSe15 family (A = K, Rb; M = Pb, Sn). This is a complex alkali bismuth selenide built from NaCl- and Bi2Te3-type blocks, filed with Bi-K-Se.
note: The x = 0.46 member is fractional, with Sn/Bi mixing on shared sites. Each composition is effectively its own structure (stage 2 handling for bi_chalcogenide_complex). No structure reference was matched.

basis: LaBiMn1.33Ni0.67O5.96, from a paper on ferromagnetism enhanced by Co and Ni substitution in a perovskite. This is (La,Bi)(Mn,Ni)O3 with Ni replacing a third of the Mn, filed like La-Mn-Ni-O and Bi-La-Mn-O.
note: Ni is a host element (Ni for Mn, a third of the B site). Near Mn:Ni = 2:1 the B site can partly order as in La2NiMnO6, so double_perovskite is an alternative. The distortion (monoclinic or orthorhombic) is not recorded. No structure reference was matched.

basis: LaPbBiS3O, from a paper on the design of a new layered thermoelectric, LaPbBiS3O. It stacks fluorite-type La2O2 layers with a thicker NaCl-type (Pb,Bi)S slab, extending the LaOBiS2 series filed under bis2_layered.
note: This is a thicker-block homologue, not LaOBiS2 itself: (LaO)2(M4S6) rather than (LaO)(BiS2). If more of these homologues appear, they may deserve their own prototype. The space group is not recorded. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Li1.1Bi2Se0.3Te2.7, from a paper on structural modifications and carrier concentration in Bi2(Te,Se)3 under reversible electrochemical lithiation. This is n-type Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 with Li inserted into the van der Waals gaps, filed like Bi-Li-Se-Te.

dopant_roles.site: Te(1) outer layer
dopant_roles.basis: Se0.3 in Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 is the standard n-type alloy end member, not dilute doping. It sits below 5 at.% only because of the Li added to the formula.

note: Li at 1.1 per formula (18 at.%) is an intercalant. At this loading it can partly convert the host, and the title mentions structural modifications. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives LiBiTe2 P4/mmm (mp-1222394), but at hull 0.278 with no ICSD references it is a computed phase. It is not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: Li2TlBi, from a paper on designing chemical analogs to PbTe with intrinsic high band degeneracy. This is a cubic Li2AB compound of the full-Heusler (L21, Fm-3m) kind, with Li on the 8c tetrahedral sites.
note: [ref 2] Li2TlBi Fm-3m (mp-865713, hull 0.000) matches the formula. It carries no ICSD reference, so it is a computed entry. This is a Zintl-like Li2TlBi with a filled BiF3/Li3Bi-derived lattice, not a transition-metal Heusler. If the Heusler label proves misleading for stage 2, it should be revisited.

basis: Mg2SiBi5O7.5, from a paper on Mg2Si-based composites made by a reduction reaction with additives. The formula is Mg2Si plus 2.5 Bi2O3. Reacted with Mg, this gives antifluorite Mg2Si with MgO and Bi (or Mg3Bi2), not a single quaternary oxide.
note: The phases entry describes the Mg2Si matrix only. The formula as parsed may be a misreading of a small wt% Bi2O3 addition, because 2.5 Bi2O3 per Mg2Si would swamp the matrix. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists only computed Mg-Si-Bi-O rocksalt supercells (Mg14SiBiO16 and similar, hull 0.16-0.67, no ICSD references). None corresponds to the composite, and they are not followed.

basis: Mg3Bi1.5P0.5, from a paper on Zintl compounds Mg3Bi2-xPnx (Pn = P, Sb). This is trigonal CaAl2Si2-type Mg3Bi2 with a quarter of the Bi replaced by P, filed like Bi-Mg.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion (2d)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is P/(Bi+P), a single composition. Mg3P2 is cubic anti-bixbyite, so at the P-rich end this axis leaves the CaAl2Si2 type. At x = 0.25 the Mg3Bi2 structure is kept, but P solubility is limited and a secondary Mg3P2 phase is possible.

note: No structure reference was matched.

basis: Sm0.5Yb0.5Mg2Bi1.99, from a paper on high-performance p-type SmMg2Bi2. This is a CaAl2Si2-type AMg2Bi2 Zintl with Sm and Yb sharing the A site, filed like Bi-Mg-Sm and Bi-Mg-Yb.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site (1a)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Yb/(Sm+Yb). Both are nominally divalent on the A site.

note: Bi1.99 is a slight Bi deficiency (non-stoichiometry), used to tune the hole concentration. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi2Mn4O10 is BiMn2O5 written doubled. It is the Bi member of the RMn2O5 family (Pbam, with Mn4+O6 octahedral chains linked by Mn3+O5 pyramids), and the paper on local distortions studies it as a polycrystal.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks MnBiO3 C2/c (mp-25035, 9 ICSD references) first. That is the high-pressure BiMnO3 perovskite, with a 1:1 Bi:Mn ratio, not the 1:2 of this sample. BiMn2O5 does not appear in the five listed phases at all, so the reference is not followed and no mp_id is taken. New prototype rmn2o5_pbam was proposed in prototypes_proposed.jsonl for this host.

basis: (La0.7Sr0.3MnO3)72(SrBi4Ti4O15)28, from a paper on a colossal Seebeck coefficient in an Aurivillius phase-perovskite oxide composite. This is a two-phase ceramic of perovskite LSMO and the four-layer Aurivillius SrBi4Ti4O15.

dopant_roles.site: A site of the LSMO perovskite
dopant_roles.basis: La is the A-site host cation of the La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 component. It falls below 5 at.% only because the composite formula is normalised over both phases.

dopant_roles.site: A site of LSMO, and the perovskite-block A site of SrBi4Ti4O15
dopant_roles.basis: Sr is a constituent of both phases: the hole dopant in LSMO and the A cation in the Aurivillius block. It is not a dopant of the composite.

note: The phases entry follows the majority LSMO phase (R-3c). The Aurivillius SrBi4Ti4O15 phase (A21am) is recorded in alt_prototype_ids. Filed like Bi-La-Mn-O-Sr-Ti. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Mn3.2Sb1.5Bi0.49Se0.01, from a paper titled Realizing a high ZT of 1.6 in n-type Mg3Sb2-based Zintl compounds. This is the standard n-type Mg3.2Sb1.5Bi0.49Se0.01 composition with Mg transcribed as Mn, a trigonal CaAl2Si2-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2.

dopant_roles.site: anion (2d)
dopant_roles.basis: Se on the Sb/Bi site is the donor that makes Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 n-type.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion (2d)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Bi/(Sb+Bi).

note: HOST KEY WRONG: Mn should be Mg, which would make the host Bi-Mg-Sb (already assigned caal2si2_zintl). This should be corrected upstream. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] Mn4BiSb3 Pmm2 (mp-1221739) is a computed Mn pnictide. It matches only because of the Mg/Mn error, so it is not followed.

basis: Bi2Mo2O9, from a paper on the low thermal conductivity of Bi2Mo2O9 ceramics. This is beta-bismuth molybdate, the monoclinic member of the Bi2O3-MoO3 catalyst family between alpha-Bi2Mo3O12 and gamma-Bi2MoO6. It is scheelite-related, but the taxonomy has no entry that fits it.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists alpha-Bi2(MoO4)3 (mp-32039), gamma-Bi2MoO6 (mp-25708) and others, but not Bi2Mo2O9. No listed phase matches the composition, so no mp_id is taken. I recall beta-Bi2Mo2O9 as monoclinic P2_1/n, but I am not sure enough to record it, or to decide whether it should join scheelite_awo4 or get its own prototype. beta-Bi2Mo2O9 is metastable below about 820 K and can decompose to alpha + gamma, which the upper end of this measurement approaches.

basis: MoBi2Se5, from a paper on fibrous reticulate nanocrystalline n-type MoBi2(Se1-xTex)5. There is no established MoBi2Se5 phase. At 12.5 at.% Mo, the likely product is Bi2Se3 tetradymite with Mo incorporated or with a MoSe2 second phase, filed like Bi-Mo-Se-Te.
note: Whether this is a single phase or Bi2Se3 + MoSe2 has to be read from the XRD in the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (Bi0.4Sb1.6Te3)93.24(C3N4)6.76, from a paper on graphitic carbon nitride-bismuth antimony telluride nanocomposites. This is p-type tetradymite (Bi,Sb)2Te3 with a g-C3N4 second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: C belongs to the g-C3N4 inclusions, not the telluride lattice.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation (6c)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Bi/(Bi+Sb) in the telluride matrix.

note: The phases entry describes the telluride matrix. N is a host element only because of the C3N4 second phase. Filed like other tetradymite composites. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Na0.5Bi0.5VO3, from a paper titled Na1/2Bi1/2VO3 and K1/2Bi1/2VO3: new lead-free tetragonal perovskites. This is an A-site-disordered (Na,Bi)VO3 perovskite, the sodium analogue of the Bi-K-O-V host.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists only computed Na-V-Bi-O phases (Na3V4(Bi10O21)2, NaV2Bi3O10, NaV4Bi13O30, none with ICSD references), all V5+ compositions. The V4+ perovskite is a high-pressure product, so the reference is not followed and no mp_id is taken. The P4mm (99) space group follows the tetragonal description in the title and is not confirmed.

basis: NaSn5BiTe7 is SnTe alloyed with NaBiTe2 (5 SnTe + NaBiTe2), from a paper contrasting SnTe-NaSbTe2 and SnTe-NaBiTe2 alloys. It is a cation-disordered rocksalt solid solution, filed like Na-Sb-Sn-Te.
note: Na and Bi are host elements (7 at.% each) and share the Sn cation site as an aliovalent Na+ + Bi3+ pair. No structure reference was matched.

basis: YNiBi, from a paper on the synthesis and thermoelectric properties of the half-Heusler alloy YNiBi.
note: [ref 2] YNiBi F-43m (mp-30460, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference) matches. The other listed phase, Y5Ni2Bi I4/mcm, is a different stoichiometry and a possible Y-rich impurity.

basis: Bi6Pb2O11 (3Bi2O3 plus 2PbO), from a paper on the electrical and thermal properties of Bi2O3, PbO and mixed oxides. The Bi2O3-PbO system at this ratio holds tetragonal beta-Bi2O3-type and fluorite-derived Pb-stabilised phases. Which one this ceramic is cannot be read from the formula.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks sillenite Bi12PbO20 I23 (mp-667342, 1 ICSD reference) first. That is a Bi:Pb ratio of 12:1, against 3:1 here, so the reference is not followed and no mp_id is taken. Pb-Bi-O mixed oxides also show oxide-ion-conducting fluorite-type high-temperature phases, so a phase change inside 289-660 K cannot be ruled out.

basis: BiYRu2O7 is the (Bi,Y)2Ru2O7 pyrochlore solid solution between metallic Bi2Ru2O7 and insulating Y2Ru2O7, with Bi and Y sharing the A site. Filed like Bi-O-Ru and O-Ru-Y.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site (16c/16d)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Y/(Bi+Y). Both are trivalent, so this is isovalent A-site mixing that drives a metal-insulator crossover.

note: The linked paper title (CuO-added AgSbO3 ceramics) does not match this composition, so the paper link may be wrong. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists only computed A-site-ordered supercells (Y3Bi(Ru2O7)2 R-3m, YBi3(Ru2O7)2 R-3m, YBiRu2O7 Imma, none with ICSD references). These are ordering models of the cubic pyrochlore, not distinct phases, so they are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: (Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3)84.08(Y2O3)15.92, from a paper on the Seebeck coefficient enhanced by energy filtering in Bi-Sb-Te based composites. This is p-type tetradymite Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 with Y2O3 nanoinclusions.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation (6c)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Bi/(Bi+Sb) in the telluride matrix.

note: The phases entry describes the telluride matrix. Y2O3 is a cubic bixbyite (Ia-3) second phase. The molar fraction as parsed is large, so the paper probably specified a small vol% or wt%. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3)69.78(ZnO)30.22, from a paper on carrier tailoring and phonon scattering from n-type zinc oxide in a telluride. This is p-type tetradymite Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 with wurtzite ZnO inclusions.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation (6c)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Bi/(Bi+Sb) in the telluride matrix.

note: The phases entry describes the telluride matrix. This is the same paper as Bi-O-Te-Zn (the n-type Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 counterpart). No structure reference was matched.

basis: ((Bi2Te3)0.25(Sb2Te3)0.75)74.24(ZrO2)25.76. The curator detail records BiSbTe alloy powder plus 6 wt% ZrO2, so this is p-type tetradymite with ZrO2 nanoparticles.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation (6c)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Bi/(Bi+Sb) in the telluride matrix.

note: The phases entry describes the telluride matrix. The ZrO2 polymorph (monoclinic baddeleyite, or a stabilised tetragonal/cubic form in nanoparticles) is not stated. The parsed molar fraction (26% ZrO2) is much larger than 6 wt% implies, so the parsed formula overstates the oxide. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Bi1.25Sn0.75O2Se, from a paper on the high-temperature thermoelectric behaviour of Sn-doped n-type Bi2O2Se. This is tetragonal Bi2O2Se with Sn on the Bi site of the Bi2O2 layer.
note: Sn at 0.75 per formula (15 at.%) counts as a host element. That is far beyond a dilute donor level, so an SnO2 or SnSe second phase is likely. The parsed value may be a mis-stated x. Filed like Bi-O-Se. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (Bi2Te2.7Se0.3)90.28(Y2O3)9.72, from a paper on n-type Bi2Te2.7Se0.3/Y2O3 nanocomposites. This is tetradymite Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 with Y2O3 inclusions.

dopant_roles.basis: Y is in the Y2O3 nanoinclusions, not on a lattice site of the telluride.

note: The phases entry describes the telluride matrix. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives Bi2Te2SeO10 C2/c (mp-1192658), an oxidised tellurite-selenite that the key matches only because of the O from Y2O3. It is not followed and no mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [166], ICSD-backed references for this host report [15]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Bi2Sr2Ca0.6Y0.4O8, the undoped reference from the same paper as Bi-I-O-Sr (iodine-intercalated Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8). The formula is Y-doped Bi-2212 with Cu2 lost in transcription, filed like Bi-Ca-O-Sr.

dopant_roles.site: Ca site between the CuO2 planes
dopant_roles.basis: Ca is the Ca-site host element of Bi-2212, partly replaced by Y.

dopant_roles.site: Ca site between the CuO2 planes
dopant_roles.basis: Y3+ for Ca2+ underdopes the CuO2 planes.

note: HOST KEY WRONG: Cu is missing from the composition, so the host should contain Cu. This should be corrected upstream. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks Sr2Bi2O5 Pnma (mp-23357, 2 ICSD references) first. That and the other listed phases are Cu-free Sr-Bi oxides, matched only because Cu is missing from the key, so they are not followed.

basis: Bi2O2Te, from a paper on the synthesis, characterisation and thermoelectric properties of this oxytelluride. It is the telluride analogue of Bi2O2Se: [Bi2O2] fluorite layers with Te square nets, I4/mmm.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT on ranking only: [ref 2] ranks Bi2TeO5 Aem2 (mp-23334, 2 ICSD references) above Bi2TeO2 I4/mmm (mp-849872, 1 ICSD reference). Bi2TeO5 is a Te4+ tellurite, a different compound. The formula-matching entry mp-849872 is taken instead of the reference primary.

basis: (Bi2Te2.7Se0.3)66.3(ZnO)33.7, from the same paper as Bi-O-Sb-Te-Zn, on n-type zinc oxide in a telluride. This is n-type tetradymite Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 with wurtzite ZnO inclusions.

dopant_roles.site: Te(1) outer layer
dopant_roles.basis: Se0.3 in Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 is the n-type alloy end member, diluted below 5 at.% by the ZnO in the formula.

note: The phases entry describes the telluride matrix. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Sn0.6Pb0.4Bi2Te4, from a paper on transport in the SnBi2Te4-PbBi2Te4 solid solution. This is the septuple-layer MBi2Te4 member of the homologous (MTe)n(Bi2Te3)m series, R-3m, filed like Bi-Sn-Te.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: central M site of the septuple layer
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Pb/(Sn+Pb). Both are divalent group-14 cations.

note: No structure reference was matched.

basis: (Ce0.09La0.01)3Bi4Pt3 single crystal, from a paper on substitutional effects on transport in the Kondo semiconductor Ce3Bi4Pt3. This is cubic Y3Au3Sb4-type Ce3Bi4Pt3 with La on the Ce site, filed like Bi-Ce-Pt.

dopant_roles.site: rare-earth site (12a)
dopant_roles.basis: Ce is the host rare earth of Ce3Bi4Pt3. Its recorded fraction (0.27 per formula) is about ten times too small, almost certainly a transcription of (Ce0.9La0.1)3 as (Ce0.09La0.01)3. The Y3Au3Sb4 structure cannot exist with 90% of the rare-earth site empty.

dopant_roles.site: rare-earth site (12a)
dopant_roles.basis: La3+ (4f0) replaces Ce to dilute the Kondo lattice. This is the substitution studied in the paper.

note: HOST KEY WRONG: because the Ce fraction was mis-scaled, Ce and La fall below the cut and the host collapses to Bi-Pt. The host should be Bi-Ce-Pt, or Bi-Ce-La-Pt (compare the earlier Bi-Ce-La-Pt record). This should be corrected upstream. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks Bi2Pt Pa-3 (mp-22864, 4 ICSD references) first. That and the other listed phases are binary Pt bismuthides, matched only because of the collapsed key, so they are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: Bi1.6Sb0.4Te2.4Se0.3S0.3, from a paper on multicomponent solid solutions based on bismuth telluride. This is tetradymite (Bi,Sb)2(Te,Se,S)3, filed like Bi-S-Sb-Te and Bi-Sb-Se-Te.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: anion; S and Se prefer the central Te(2) site
solid_solution_axis.note: x is (Se+S)/(Te+Se+S) on the anion sublattice. Bi/(Bi+Sb) = 0.8 on the cation sublattice. This is a two-sublattice solid solution.

note: All five elements are above the 5% cut. No structure reference was matched.

basis: TlBiS2 is the rhombohedral cation-ordered rocksalt superstructure (alpha-NaFeO2 type, R-3m) shared by TlBiTe2, TlBiSe2 and AgBiSe2. It comes from a paper on TlBiS2-PbS alloys, and is filed like Ag-Bi-Se.
note: [ref 1] TEDesignLab lists TlBiS2 at space group 166, which agrees with this assignment, but gives no mp_id for it, so mp_id stays null. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] Materials Project ranks TlBiS2 I4_1/amd (mp-36946, hull 0.124, no ICSD references) first. That is a computed structure without experimental support, and it is not taken. The [ref 1] primary Tl4Bi2S5 Pnma is a different, Tl-rich compound. In the TlBiS2-PbS alloys of the paper, Pb dilution drives the structure toward disordered cubic rocksalt.

basis: (Zn2Sb3)75.9Bi24.1, from a paper on p-n conduction-type conversion by spinodal decomposition in Zn-Sb-Bi. With 24 at.% Bi added to a zinc antimonide, the sample decomposes into Zn4Sb3/ZnSb plus Bi-rich regions, not a single phase.
note: The Zn:Sb ratio of 2:3 lies between ZnSb (1:1) and Zn4Sb3 (4:3). It is written as Zn2Sb3 with Bi. Which zinc antimonide dominates, and how Bi partitions between Sb substitution and elemental Bi (A7) regions, must be read from the paper. The phases entry records beta-Zn4Sb3 as a low-confidence placeholder for the matrix. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Sn0.95Bi0.05 as recorded is white tin (beta-Sn, I41/amd) with Bi on the Sn site at its solubility limit. The paper title speaks of chemical doping enhancing thermoelectric performance, which suggests a compound host. It is possible that a chalcogen was dropped from the formula, such as Bi-doped SnSe or SnTe.

other_polymorphs.note: alpha-Sn (grey tin) is the equilibrium phase below 286 K, but the transformation is kinetically very slow, and Bi additions suppress it. A measurement from 12 K is taken on retained beta-Sn, so alpha-Sn is not recorded as a thermal phase.

note: Bi at exactly 5 at.% counts as a host element by the cut. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists only computed Sn-Bi ordered cells (Sn3Bi Fm-3m, SnBi I-4m2 and others, all above hull, none with ICSD references). The Sn-Bi system has no intermediate compounds, so these are not followed. Confirm from the paper whether this is really a Sn-Bi alloy.

basis: (BrC6H4NH2)2CuBr2 film, from a paper on the giant power factor and air stability of an n-type metal-organic material. This is a copper(II) bromide complex with two 4-bromoaniline ligands, a molecular coordination compound, filed like C-Cl-Cu-H-O-S.

dopant_roles.site: metal centre of the complex
dopant_roles.basis: Cu is the coordinating metal of the complex, a stoichiometric constituent. It falls below 5 at.% only because the H and C atoms of the ligands dominate the atom count.

note: The sample is a film, so the packing may differ from a bulk crystal. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks CuH12C6(Br3N2)2 P-1 (mp-1200376, 2 ICSD references) first. That is a different copper bromide amine complex, not this one, so it is not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: Sn24P19.3Br4I4, from a paper on the crystal structure and properties of a type-I clathrate. This is a cationic clathrate: a Sn24P19.3 framework with halide guests in the cages, filed like I-P-Sn (Sn24P19.3I8) with half the iodine replaced by bromine.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cage guest sites (2a and 6d)
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Br/(Br+I). The smaller Br may prefer the small dodecahedral cage (2a).

note: P19.3 is a non-stoichiometric framework: P vacancies balance the charge of the cationic framework. Br and I are cage guests, not framework substituents. No structure reference was matched.

basis: La3Zn4P6.6Br0.8 single crystal, from a paper on the enclathration of X@La4 tetrahedra in channels of Zn-P frameworks. This is a Zn-P framework compound with halide-centred La4 tetrahedra in its channels, a specific new structure type not in the taxonomy.
note: Confidence is medium that the structure is unique and crystalline. I do not know its space group, so no prototype is proposed from recall. It should get a dedicated prototype once the structure is read from the paper. Br is a host element (6 at.%), sitting at the centre of the La4 tetrahedra. P6.6 indicates partial P occupancy. No structure reference was matched.

basis: LiBr, from a paper on the thermal conductivity and heat capacity of solid LiBr and RbF under pressure. Bulk LiBr is the rocksalt alkali halide.

other_polymorphs.note: Hexagonal LiBr sits at hull 0.000 in MP, 0.025 eV/atom below rocksalt, but carries no ICSD references. It is known only as a metastable low-temperature deposit or a DFT artefact, and is never reached on heating bulk LiBr.

note: [ref 2] ranks LiBr Fm-3m (mp-23259, 4 ICSD references) PRIMARY, and that is taken, even though the wurtzite entry is lower on the hull. The paper applies pressure, but LiBr stays rocksalt over the ranges usually studied.

basis: (CH3Cl)27.88(C)72.12 film. The curator detail names polyvinyl chloride with C:PVC = 8:13, and the paper is on three-component hybrid organic thermoelectric films. So this is a carbon filler (nanotube or graphite) dispersed in a PVC matrix, and CH3Cl is the parse of the PVC repeat unit, not chloromethane.
note: The PVC repeat unit is C2H3Cl, not CH3Cl, so the parsed formula mis-states the polymer. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks CH3Cl Cmc2_1 (mp-1078233, solid chloromethane, 4 ICSD references) first. That is a molecular crystal of the monomer-like formula, not PVC, so it is not followed. The other listed entries are unrelated metal-organic chlorides.

basis: C6H7NCl pellets. The curator detail names polyaniline (PANI), and the paper is on doped polyaniline nanowires. C6H7N is the aniline repeat unit, and Cl is the HCl dopant that turns the emeraldine base into the conducting emeraldine salt.
note: Cl is above the 5% cut (one per 15 atoms), so it is a host element here, even though physically it is the protonic-acid dopant of the polymer. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks FeH12C2(NCl2)2 P4_2/ncm (mp-1194613, 19 ICSD references) first. That and the other listed entries are metal-organic chloride salts, not polyaniline, so they are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: GaCCo3, from a paper on thermoelectric performance in the strongly correlated antiperovskite SnCCo3 and its relatives. This is the cubic ACM3 antiperovskite: C at the body centre inside a Co6 octahedron, Ga at the corners, filed like C-Co-Sn.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only Ga2Co6C P4/mmm (mp-1224829, hull 0.039, no ICSD references). That is a computed cell with half the carbon sites filled (Ga:Co:C = 2:6:1), not the 1:3:1 compound measured, so it is not followed and no mp_id is taken. Stage 2 should query MP for GaCCo3 at Pm-3m directly.

basis: GeCCo3, from the same paper on the antiperovskite SnCCo3 and its relatives. This is written as the ACM3 antiperovskite, with Ge at the corners, C in the Co6 octahedron, Pm-3m, filed like C-Co-Ga and C-Co-Sn.
note: Confidence is medium because GeCCo3 is less established than the Ga and Sn members, and the carbon site in these antiperovskites is often partly empty. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only Co12Ge4C P4/mmm (mp-1226575, hull 0.068, no ICSD references), a computed carbon-poor cell at a different stoichiometry. It is not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: GeCCr3, from a paper on the synthesis and characterisation of Ge-Cr intermetallics (GeCr3 and its carbide and nitride). GeCCr3 is read as the cubic antiperovskite, C inside a Cr6 octahedron with Ge at the corners, like GeNCr3 and the Co and Mn carbides of this chunk.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks Cr2GeC P6_3/mmc (mp-922991, 3 ICSD references) first. That is the 211 MAX phase, a different stoichiometry (Cr:Ge:C = 2:1:1), and it is recorded only as the alternative in case the sample is really a MAX-phase mixture. [ref 2] also lists Cr3GeC at Cmcm (mp-1079343, 2 ICSD references), not cubic. The antiperovskite reading follows the paper context, not the references, and should be checked against its XRD. No mp_id is taken.

basis: Cu3(CO3)2(OH)2 single crystal, from a paper on thermal conductivity and spin state of the spin diamond-chain system azurite. The formula is the mineral azurite, a basic copper carbonate with Cu2+ diamond chains. The taxonomy has no entry for it, so one is proposed.
note: [ref 2] ranks Cu3H2(CO4)2 P2_1/c (mp-23733, hull 0.007, 5 ICSD references) PRIMARY. That formula is azurite, so it is taken. This is a magnetic insulator measured for phonon and magnon heat transport, not a thermoelectric.

basis: CuOC0.7, from a paper on CuO/SWCNT nanocomposites as thermoelectric materials. This is tenorite CuO with single-walled carbon nanotubes dispersed in it. Carbon takes no lattice site in CuO, so the matrix is recorded as the alternative.
note: C is 26 at.% by atom count, so it is a host element, but it is a dispersed nanotube phase. The CuO matrix is monoclinic tenorite, C2/c. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks Cu2CO5 P2_1/c (mp-1198809, 9 ICSD references) first, and all five listed entries are copper carbonates or oxalates. None is CuO plus carbon, so they are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: C0.33Cu2SnSe3 bulk, from a paper on Cu2SnSe3-based composites that incorporate a carbon phase. The matrix is Cu2SnSe3, filed under cu2gese3 as the Cu-Se-Sn host is. The carbon is a dispersed second phase, not a lattice constituent.
note: C is 5.2 at.%, just above the cut, so it is a host element. Cu2SnSe3 is usually reported as monoclinic Cc or as disordered cubic sphalerite, depending on how it was processed. The cu2gese3 filing follows the Cu-Se-Sn precedent, and stage 2 should settle the polymorph. Measured 300-700 K. No structure reference was matched.

basis: EuC2, from a paper on structural phase transitions in EuC2. This is a europium acetylide with C2 dumbbells, in the CaC2 / ThC2 dicarbide family. The taxonomy has no entry for it, so one is proposed.

other_polymorphs.note: Tetragonal CaC2-type EuC2. As I recall, this is the phase reached on heating well above room temperature, so it is outside the 10-299 K window rather than metastable. The enum has no value for a high-temperature phase that is not crossed, so occurrence is unknown.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks EuC2 I4/mmm (mp-1018177, 2 ICSD references) PRIMARY over EuC2 C2/c (mp-1077301, 1 ICSD reference). My reading is that EuC2 is monoclinic (ThC2 type) at ambient and below, and tetragonal only at high temperature, so the C2/c entry is taken for the measured window. That is recalled, not read from the paper, and the paper itself is about these transitions, so it should settle this directly. EuC6 P6_3/mmc is a graphite intercalation compound, not this sample.

basis: C13H7BF4NS6 is beta-double-prime (CNB-EDT-TTF)4BF4, from a paper on anion disorder in bilayer molecular metals. This is a TTF-derivative radical-cation salt with BF4- counter-anions, filed with the BEDT-TTF salts.

dopant_roles.site: centre of the BF4- counter-anion
dopant_roles.basis: B is a stoichiometric constituent of the BF4- anion. It falls below 5 at.% only because the organic donor dominates the atom count.

dopant_roles.site: nitrile group of the CNB-EDT-TTF donor
dopant_roles.basis: N belongs to the cyanobenzene substituent of the donor molecule. It is a constituent, not a dopant.

note: The beta-double-prime packing sets the space group, which is not recorded here from recall. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists two Pt phosphine complexes (mp-1204443 and mp-1202301). These are unrelated molecular crystals, so they are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: Fe0.95Co0.05Si2C0.58, from a paper on optimising the properties of Fe1-xCoxSi2+z for energy conversion. The matrix is Co-doped beta-FeSi2, the standard n-type iron disilicide. The carbon is best read as an added second phase (such as SiC or graphite), not a lattice constituent.

dopant_roles.site: Fe sites of beta-FeSi2
dopant_roles.basis: Co on the Fe site is the standard n-type donor in beta-FeSi2. This is the x of Fe1-xCoxSi2 in the paper title.

note: C is 16 at.%, so it is a host element. The title gives Si2+z, and C0.58 is not explained by it: it may be a carbon or SiC addition, or a mis-parse of the excess-Si term. The paper should settle this. The measurement stays below the beta to alpha transition near 1210 K. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only Fe5SiC Cmc2_1 (mp-1212719, no ICSD references), an Fe-rich carbosilicide unrelated to FeSi2, so it is not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: PCDIPT film. The curator detail names a cyclopentadithiophene-alt-thiadiazolopyridine donor-acceptor copolymer, and the paper is on doping high-mobility donor-acceptor copolymer semiconductors. This is a conjugated polymer film.
note: HOST KEY WRONG: the composition string is the acronym PCDIPT, and the parser read its letters as element symbols (P, C, D taken as H, I, P, T taken as H). The real polymer contains C, H, N and S, and it is doped with a molecular dopant. The host key C-H-I-P is a parse artifact and should be corrected upstream. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists P2H19C6I7N P-1 (mp-1196394), an unrelated iodide salt matched only through the false key. It is not followed.

basis: (C6H7N)37(Te)63, from a paper on flexible low-grade energy devices based on a high-performance material. This is a polyaniline/tellurium hybrid: Te nanorods or nanowires coated with or embedded in PANI (C6H7N is the aniline repeat unit).
note: The inorganic phase is trigonal Te, P3_121. The polymer is amorphous or semicrystalline PANI. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists BaTe3H15(CN)3 and MnTe2H20(CN)4, which are unrelated coordination salts, so they are not followed and no mp_id is taken.
