basis: (C4H2Se)(C6H4O2S) film. The curator detail names polyselenophene and PEDOT, and the paper is on poly(selenophene-co-3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene). This is a conjugated copolymer film at a 1:1 selenophene:EDOT ratio.
note: The same paper supplies C-H-O-Se, the 2:1 copolymer, where S falls below the cut. Any counter-ion used for doping is not in the formula. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (C4H2Se)2(C6H4O2S) film, the 2:1 selenophene:EDOT member of the poly(selenophene-co-EDOT) series. It is filed like C-H-O-S-Se, from the same paper.

dopant_roles.site: thiophene ring of the EDOT unit
dopant_roles.basis: S is the ring heteroatom of the EDOT comonomer, a stoichiometric part of the copolymer. It falls below 5% only because the selenophene units outnumber EDOT two to one.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists H6C2SeO P-1 and a uranyl selenite, which are unrelated small-molecule crystals. They are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: (HSC6H4OH)39.14(Sb2Te3)60.86 multilayer film. The curator detail names a 4-mercaptophenol (0.7 nm) / Sb2Te3 (6 nm) superlattice, and the paper is on an organic-inorganic superlattice with a nanocrystal-amorphous composite. The inorganic layers are Sb2Te3, which is tetradymite.

dopant_roles.site: thiol group of 4-mercaptophenol
dopant_roles.basis: S is the thiol anchor of the organic layer, a stoichiometric part of the molecule, bonded to the Sb2Te3 surface. It does not substitute into the telluride.

dopant_roles.site: hydroxyl group of 4-mercaptophenol
dopant_roles.basis: O is the phenol oxygen of the organic layer, a molecular constituent, not an oxide impurity in Sb2Te3.

note: Per the title, the Sb2Te3 layers are partly nanocrystalline and partly amorphous, so amorphous is recorded as an alternative. Measured 298-499 K. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Mg2SiLi5C2.5O7.5 is Mg2Si plus 2.5 Li2CO3 written as one formula. The paper is on Mg2Si-based composites. So this is an antifluorite Mg2Si matrix with a lithium carbonate additive or its reaction products, not a single phase.
note: Confidence is medium because the formula decomposes exactly into Mg2Si + 2.5 Li2CO3, but the paper may use Li2CO3 only as a Li-doping source. It may also leave Li2O or MgO after sintering. Only the paper can say how much Li enters Mg2Si. Mg2Si is antifluorite, Fm-3m. Measured 305-862 K. No structure reference was matched.

basis: SnCMn3, from the paper on the antiperovskite SnCCo3 and its relatives. Mn3SnC is a well-known cubic antiperovskite carbide: C inside a Mn6 octahedron, Sn at the corners, filed like C-Co-Sn.
note: [ref 2] ranks Mn3SnC Pm-3m (mp-991257, 4 ICSD references) PRIMARY, which agrees, so it is taken. Mn3SnC has a first-order magnetic transition near room temperature, inside this window, with a volume jump. As I recall the lattice stays cubic, so it is not recorded as a structural phase change. The paper should confirm this.

basis: (TiC)89.86(Ni3Al)10.14, from a paper on the densification and thermal properties of TiC-Ni3Al composites. This is a cermet: TiC particles bonded by a Ni3Al binder, filed like Al-C-Ni-Ti. Here the carbide makes up 90%.

dopant_roles.basis: Al belongs to the Ni3Al binder phase, not to the TiC lattice. It falls below 5% only because the binder is 10% of the formula.

note: This host differs from Al-C-Ni-Ti only because Al drops below the cut at 90% TiC. TiC is rocksalt, Fm-3m, and usually carbon-deficient. Ni3Al is L1_2, Pm-3m. Measured 292-1311 K. Neither constituent transforms in that window. No structure reference was matched.

basis: TiO2SC, from a paper on the concentration of electrons at grain boundaries in rutile TiO2. The matrix is rutile. S and C are read as co-dopants or surface species that the formula lists at full stoichiometric weight, not as lattice constituents in a 1:2:1:1 compound.
note: No Ti-O-S-C compound exists at this stoichiometry. The formula almost certainly marks TiO2 with S and C present, perhaps as dopants or as the gas-phase or grain-boundary species the paper studies. At 20 at.% each, the cut makes them host elements. The paper should say how much actually enters the lattice. Rutile is stable to the melt, so the 1223-1323 K window crosses nothing. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Y0.06ZrO2C0.3, from a paper on mechanically reliable thermoelectric nanocomposites made by dispersing a carbon phase. The matrix is yttria-stabilised zirconia at about 3 mol% Y2O3. The carbon (nanotubes or similar) is the dispersed conducting phase that makes the ceramic thermoelectric.

dopant_roles.site: cation site of the fluorite-derived lattice
dopant_roles.basis: Y3+ on the Zr site, compensated by oxygen vacancies, stabilises tetragonal zirconia. It is the standard 3Y-TZP stabiliser.

note: At about 3 mol% Y2O3 the zirconia is tetragonal (P4_2/nmc), a distortion of fluorite, which is why fluorite_oxide is the alternative, as for O-Y-Zr. The exact carbon form is not visible from the formula. Confidence is medium because I am inferring the dispersed phase from a truncated title. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (U)81.14(PuC)18.86, from a paper on U-PuO2, U-PuC and U-PuN cermet fuels for fast reactors. This is a cermet: PuC particles in a uranium metal matrix, two phases by design.
note: The phases array follows the uranium matrix only. Pure U goes alpha (Cmcm) to beta (P4_2/mnm) near 941 K, then beta to gamma (bcc, Im-3m) near 1049 K. The 750-1309 K window crosses both, although the chunk file shows no transition line for this host. There is no bcc element prototype in the taxonomy, so gamma-U is filed under solid_solution_alloy. Pu dissolved from the carbide would shift these temperatures. The PuC dispersoid is rocksalt, Fm-3m, and does not transform here. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks PuU4C5, PuUC2 and PuUC3 (all computed, no ICSD references), mixed-actinide carbides that are not this cermet. They are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: WS2C0.2 bulk, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of WS2/single-walled carbon nanohorn composites. The matrix is 2H-WS2, and the carbon nanohorns are a dispersed second phase.
note: C is 6 at.%, so it is a host element. 2H-WS2 is P6_3/mmc. Measured 290-780 K. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CSn3, from a paper on the thermoelectric power of Ce(Pb1-xSnx)3. The formula is CeSn3 with the e dropped, so Ce was parsed as C. CeSn3 is the cubic AuCu3-type intermediate-valence compound, filed like Ce-Pb-Sn.
note: HOST KEY WRONG: this sample is the x = 1 end member of the Ce-Pb-Sn series and should be keyed Ce-Sn. This should be corrected upstream. Confidence is medium only because of the parse. The structure is not in doubt once the formula is read as CeSn3. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives SnC F-43m (mp-1009820, hull 0.815) and [ref 2] gives SnC Fm-3m (mp-1009822, hull 1.293). Both are far above the hull, hypothetical tin carbides matched only through the false key. They are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: C90W10, from a paper on the thermal diffusivity and conductivity of doped graphites. The matrix is graphite. The W addition is at a level far beyond its solubility, so it is present mainly as tungsten carbide particles.
note: W is 10 at.%, so it is a host element. Doped graphites for plasma-facing use are usually graphite with carbide dispersoids, which is why composite_multiphase is the alternative. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks WC P-6m2 (mp-1894, 20 ICSD references) first. That is the likely W-bearing second phase, not the host, so its mp_id is not attached to the graphite phase. Stage 2 can use it for the dispersoid.

basis: CaCeO3 bulk. As written, this is an ABO3 perovskite with Ce4+ on the B site. The linked paper title is about BaUO3, part of the same nuclear-materials perovskite work, so the sample is taken to be the perovskite, not checked.
note: Confidence is low for two reasons. First, the paper title does not match the composition. Second, Ce4+ is small for the perovskite B site next to Ca, and a CaO-CeO2 mixture tends to form a Ca-doped fluorite ceria plus CaO, not a single perovskite. That is why fluorite_oxide is the alternative. [ref 2] lists CaCeO3 Pnma (mp-756365, hull 0.059) with no ICSD references. It is taken as the formula-matched perovskite candidate, but it is a computed entry. The 580-1460 K window may cross orthorhombic-to-higher-symmetry perovskite transitions, which are not recorded without data.

basis: Ca3CeSb3, from a paper on the Ca3RESb3 family of Zintl phases. Ca3RESb3 is the 4:3 cation:anion stoichiometry of the anti-Th3P4 structure, with Ca and Ce sharing one cation site, the same framework as Yb4Sb3 (filed under th3p4 for Bi-Sb-Yb).
note: Confidence is medium because the anti-Th3P4 (I-43d) assignment is recalled for this family, not read from the paper. The mixed Ca/RE occupancy, and so the charge count (3 Ca2+ + RE3+ = 3 Sb3-), makes the ideal compound valence-precise. Deviations set the carrier concentration. Filed identically for Ca-Gd-Sb and Ca-La-Sb. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Sr2.4Ca1.6Fe4.5Co1.5O13, from a paper on the synthesis, crystal chemistry and electrical properties of an intergrowth oxide. The 4:6:13 cation:oxygen stoichiometry is the Sr4Fe6O13 intergrowth of perovskite and double iron-oxide layers, with Ca on the Sr site and Co on the Fe site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site of the perovskite block
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Ca/(Sr+Ca). Co/(Fe+Co) = 0.25 on the iron sites is a second, non-isoelectronic substitution.

note: The taxonomy space group (Iba2, modulated) is itself marked to be confirmed. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists five computed Sr-Ca-Fe-Co-O supercells (for example Sr2Ca2Fe(CoO4)3 Pm, mp-1099605), all without ICSD references and none at the 4:6:13 stoichiometry. They are not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: Ca3Co3.9I40.1O9, from a paper on Ir doping in layered Ca3Co4O9. The intended formula is Ca3Co3.9Ir0.1O9, which is misfit Ca3Co4O9 with 0.1 Ir on the Co site. The parser read Ir0.1 as I40.1.
note: HOST KEY WRONG: as parsed, iodine is 72 at.% of the formula, which is impossible. The host should be Ca-Co-O with Ir as a dilute dopant substituting for Co. This should be corrected upstream. When it is, Ir is the substitutional dopant on the Co site (most likely the CoO2 layer). Confidence is medium only because of the parse. The prototype is not in doubt. No measured range and no structure reference are given.

basis: Ca2.2Mg0.8Co4O9 epitaxial film, from a paper on cation-substituted (Ca2CoO3)xCoO2 films. This is misfit Ca3Co4O9 with Mg on the Ca site of the rocksalt block, filed like Ca-Co-O.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site of the Ca2CoO3 rocksalt block
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Mg/(Ca+Mg). This is a single film composition. How much Mg actually sits on the Ca site, and how much on the Co site of the block, needs the paper.

note: Epitaxial film. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] lists computed Ca-Mg-Co-O supercells (for example Ca7Mg(Co2O5)4 P1, mp-1076526), none with ICSD references and none a misfit composite. They are not followed and no mp_id is taken. As an incommensurate composite, this host has no single MP entry.

basis: Pb0.7SrCaCo0.3O3(CoO2)1.71, from a paper on thermopower enhancement in misfit cobaltites. This is a misfit layered cobaltite with a [Pb0.7Co0.3 / Sr / Ca] rocksalt block and a CdI2-type CoO2 layer at an incommensurate ratio of 1.71, filed like Ca-Co-O-Pb.
note: This is an incommensurate composite with two subsystems, so there is no single MP entry. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3CoRhO6, from a paper on the magnetic and thermoelectric properties of quasi-one-dimensional oxides. This is the Ca3Co2O6 structure with Rh on the octahedral chain site: chains of alternating face-sharing CoO6 prisms and RhO6 octahedra, R-3c.
note: [ref 2] ranks Ca3CoRhO6 R-3c (mp-1191540, hull 0.051) PRIMARY. That is the formula match and the expected space group, so it is taken, although it carries no ICSD reference count. The other listed entry, Ca6Co3RhO12 R-3, is a computed ordering at a different Co:Rh ratio.

basis: Ca2SbCo4O9, from a paper on low-temperature electrical and thermal transport in Ca3Co4O9 with a substitution. This is the Ca3Co4O9 misfit formula with one of the three Ca replaced by Sb.
note: Sb at 6 at.% is just above the cut, so it is a host element. Replacing one Ca in three with Sb is far beyond what the Ca2CoO3 block normally takes. It may be a mis-scaled x (for example Ca2.9Sb0.1 written as Ca2Sb) or a nominal composition with Sb-rich secondary phases. Confidence is medium for that reason. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Sm0.6Ca0.4CoO3 rods, from a paper comparing dual-phase oxygen-transport membranes that contain cobalt. This is the A-site-substituted SmCoO3 perovskite, the mixed-conducting cobaltite used in such membranes.
note: SmCoO3 is orthorhombic Pnma. Ca doping and the high-temperature window may drive it toward higher symmetry, and the oxygen content moves with temperature in a membrane material. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only CaSmCoO4 Cmc2_1 (mp-1227147, no ICSD references), a computed A2BO4 Ruddlesden-Popper-type composition, not the 1:1 ABO3 measured. It is not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: Ca2YCo4O9 bulk, from a paper on thermoelectric properties enhanced by chemical pressure in Ca3Co4O9. This is misfit Ca3Co4O9 with Y on the Ca site of the rocksalt block.
note: Y at one in three Ca sites is heavy, but Y3+ for Ca2+ is the usual electron-doping substitution in the rocksalt block. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only Ca9Y3(CoO6)4 P1 (mp-1227804, no ICSD references), a computed cell, not the misfit composite. It is not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: Gd0.70Ca0.30CrO3 bulk, from a paper on magnetic and transport properties of Gd1-xCaxCrO3. This is the orthorhombic GdCrO3 perovskite with Ca on the Gd site, filed like Ca-Cr-O-Y and Ca-Cr-O-Pr.
note: Ca2+ on the Gd3+ site hole-dopes the Cr3+ sublattice toward Cr4+. No structure reference was matched.

basis: La0.7Ca0.3Cr0.97O3, from a paper evaluating a simple, easily sintered La0.7Ca0.3Cr0.97O3-delta perovskite. This is the Ca-doped lanthanum chromite interconnect perovskite with a small B-site deficiency.
note: LaCrO3 goes from orthorhombic to rhombohedral near 530 K, and Ca doping shifts that temperature. The 773-1123 K window may therefore be entirely in a rhombohedral (R-3c) phase. The space group is left at the ambient Pnma with medium confidence, and the paper should settle it. Cr0.97 is deliberate B-site deficiency to aid sintering. It is a non-stoichiometry, not a dopant. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Na0.5Ca0.5Cr2O4 bulk, from the paper on the electronic, thermoelectric and magneto-dielectric properties of Ca1-xNaxCr2O4. This is the CaFe2O4-type post-spinel with Na on the tunnel site, filed like Ca-Cr-O.
note: At x = 0.5, Na is 7 at.%, so it is a host element here. At x = 0.25 in Ca-Cr-O it fell below the cut. Na+ for Ca2+ drives Cr toward 3.25+. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca0.7Na0.3Pd2.5Cu0.5O4, from a paper on the logarithmic temperature dependence of resistivity in hole-doped CaPd3O4. This is the cubic NaPt3O4-type palladate with Na on the Ca site and Cu on the square-planar Pd site. The taxonomy has no entry for it, so one is proposed.

dopant_roles.site: A site (cube-coordinated)
dopant_roles.basis: Na+ for Ca2+ adds holes to the Pd-O network and turns semiconducting CaPd3O4 metallic. This is the substitution the paper is built on.

note: Cu at 6 at.% is a host element, on the Pd site. Confidence is medium because the Pm-3n structure is recalled and the chunk offers no reference line. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CaZn0.25Cu0.5Sb bulk, from a paper on the structure transition and thermoelectric properties of AZn1-xCuxSb-type compounds. Ca2+ + 0.25 Zn2+ + 0.5 Cu+ exactly balances Sb3-, the signature of a valence-precise ABX Zintl phase with a partly empty honeycomb site. That is filed under ZrBeSi like Ag-Ca-Sb-Zn.
note: The title speaks of a structure transition across the series. Zn-rich members are more likely CaAl2Si2-type (as CaZn2Sb2, filed under Ca-Sb-Zn), and Cu-rich members hexagonal ZrBeSi-type. Where this x sits is not certain, so caal2si2_zintl is the alternative. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca2Dy7Sb5O5 bulk, from a paper on the transport properties and compositions of the Ca2RE7Pn5O5 family. This is a Ca-substituted RE9Sb5O5 rare-earth antimonide oxide, a specific layered structure type with a reduced-Sb substructure that the taxonomy does not hold.
note: It is related to the RE2O2Sb compounds filed under bi2o2se_layered (Gd-O-Sb and others), but at a different cation:Sb:O ratio (9:5:5). I do not know the space group reliably, so no prototype is proposed from recall. It should get a dedicated prototype once the structure is read from the paper, together with Ca-Gd-O-Sb. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only Ca2Dy3Sb3O14 C2/c (mp-1227760, no ICSD references). That is an Sb5+ antimonate, a different chemistry, so it is not followed and no mp_id is taken.

basis: La0.6Ca0.4Fe0.7Ni0.3O3 rods, from a paper on the synthesis and electrochemical performance of La0.6Ca0.4Fe1-xNixO3 cathodes. This is the A-site Ca-doped LaFeO3 perovskite with Ni on the Fe site.
note: Pnma is the LaFeO3 parent. At 40% Ca and 30% Ni, and at 773-1073 K, the symmetry may be higher (rhombohedral or cubic), and the oxygen content shifts with temperature. The paper should settle the setting. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca2FeRuO6 polycrystal, from a paper on reentrant magnetism at the borderline between long-range antiferromagnetism and spin glass. This is an A2BB-prime-O6 perovskite with Fe and Ru on the B site. Fe3+/Ru5+ order on it is only partial, so the simple perovskite is the alternative.
note: The borderline magnetism in the paper title is itself a sign of B-site disorder. If Fe and Ru are fully disordered, the cell is simple orthorhombic Pnma perovskite. If they are rock-salt ordered, it is monoclinic P2_1/n (14). The paper should say which. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CaSrFeRuO6 polycrystal, from the same paper as Ca2FeRuO6. It is the same A2FeRuO6 perovskite with half the Ca replaced by Sr, filed like Ca-Fe-O-Ru.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site
solid_solution_axis.note: x is Sr/(Ca+Sr). Larger Sr reduces the octahedral tilt.

note: B-site order is as uncertain as for Ca2FeRuO6. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CaGa4 single crystal, from a paper on Fermi surfaces and charge-density waves in SrAl4 and related BaAl4-type compounds. CaGa4 belongs to the BaAl4 family. As I recall, though, it is a monoclinic distortion of it (C2/m), not the tetragonal aristotype.

other_polymorphs.note: The undistorted tetragonal I4/mmm cell, as listed by [ref 2]. It is recorded here in case the monoclinic reading is wrong, or in case this is a higher-temperature form.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] ranks CaGa4 I4/mmm (mp-1976, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD references) PRIMARY. My recollection is that CaGa4 is monoclinic C2/m, a sheared BaAl4 cell, so the I4/mmm entry is not taken for the measured phase. This recollection has not been checked against the paper, and the reference may well be right. Either way the prototype is the BaAl4 family. Stage 2 should confirm which cell applies before attaching mp-1976.

basis: Ca2Gd7Sb5O5 bulk, from the same Ca2RE7Pn5O5 paper as Ca-Dy-O-Sb. It is the gadolinium member of that family and filed identically.
note: It should get the same dedicated prototype as Ca-Dy-O-Sb once the structure is read from the paper. It is distinct from Gd2O2Sb (Gd-O-Sb, bi2o2se_layered). No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3GdSb3, from the paper on the Ca3RESb3 Zintl family. It is the gadolinium member, read as anti-Th3P4 with Ca and Gd sharing the cation site, and filed like Ca-Ce-Sb.
note: The structure type is recalled for this family, not read from the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3GeO bulk, from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of the inverse perovskites A3TtO (A = Mg, Ca; Tt = Si, Ge, Sn, Pb). This is the antiperovskite: O at the octahedral centre of Ca6, Ge4- at the corners, filed like Ca-O-Pb.
note: [ref 2] ranks Ca3GeO Pm-3m (mp-9721, hull 0.001, 2 ICSD references) PRIMARY. It is taken, but with medium phase confidence. The smaller tetrels (Si, Ge) in Ca3TtO have been reported with octahedral tilting that lowers the symmetry to tetragonal (I4/mcm), and the paper should settle this. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 1] TEDesignLab lists only calcium germanates (CaGeO3 Pnma mp-8130 with 19 ICSD references, CaGe2O5, Ca2GeO4). Those are Ge4+ oxides, a different compound class from this Ge4- antiperovskite. They are not followed.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [221], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62, 15, 2, 139]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CaHf0.7Sc0.3O3, from a paper on the influence of Sc concentration on transport in CaHf1-xScxO3-alpha. This is the orthorhombic CaHfO3 perovskite with acceptor Sc3+ on the Hf site, compensated by oxygen vacancies. It is an ionic (oxide and proton) conductor.
note: Sc at 6 at.% is a host element. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca0.9Gd0.1MnO3(K2CO3)0.2. The curator detail gives Ca0.9Gd0.1MnO3 + 15 wt% K2CO3, from a paper on improving the thermoelectric properties of Ca0.9Gd0.1MnO3 by powder engineering. The matrix is the electron-doped CaMnO3 perovskite, and K2CO3 is a processing additive.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: Gd3+ on the Ca2+ site is the electron donor of the Ca0.9Gd0.1MnO3 base composition.
C comes from the K2CO3 additive, which decomposes on sintering and releases CO2. Carbon does not enter the manganite.

note: K is above the cut only because the additive was written into the formula. Some K may enter the A site. The rest forms a K-rich grain-boundary phase or evaporates. That is why composite_multiphase is the alternative and confidence is medium. CaMnO3 is orthorhombic Pnma. Its high-temperature transitions (to tetragonal near 1170 K) are above this window. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3LaSb3, from the paper on the Ca3RESb3 Zintl family. It is the lanthanum member, read as anti-Th3P4 with Ca and La sharing the cation site, and filed like Ca-Ce-Sb.
note: The structure type is recalled for this family, not read from the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CaLuSb3, from the paper on the Ca3RESb3 Zintl family. As written the formula does not charge-balance (Ca2+ plus Lu3+ gives +5 against -9 for three Sb3-) and is not a member of that family, so it is read as Ca3LuSb3 with a lost subscript. On that reading it is the lutetium member, anti-Th3P4 with Ca and Lu sharing the cation site, filed like Ca-La-Sb and Ca-Ce-Sb.
note: Confidence is low for two reasons. The composition string is probably a transcription error and should be checked against the paper. Lu is also the smallest rare earth in the series, and whether it keeps the same structure as the La and Ce members is recalled, not checked. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca2MnMoO6, from an early paper on the effect of alkaline-earth and transition metals on electrical transport in these oxides. A2BB-prime-O6 with Mn2+ and Mo6+ is the B-site rock-salt-ordered double perovskite; the large charge difference between the two B cations drives the ordering. It is filed like Sr2MnMoO6 in Mn-Mo-O-Sr.
note: The small Ca cation tilts the octahedra, so the monoclinic P2_1/n cell is taken rather than the cubic Fm-3m aristotype. That is recalled for Ca-based double perovskites in general, not read from this paper. The degree of Mn/Mo order in a 1960s ceramic is unknown, which is why perovskite is the alternative. Full measured span reaches 819 K. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca0.75Sm0.25MnO3 bulk, from a paper on Ca1-xSmxMn1-yWyO3 for power generation. This is electron-doped CaMnO3 with Sm3+ on the Ca site: the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type Pnma perovskite.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. It lists CaSmMn2O6 Pmn2_1 (mp-1227151) and Ca3SmMn4O12 Pm (mp-1227761) as PRIMARY. Both are A-site-ordered supercells computed for these stoichiometries, with no ICSD support. In a sintered ceramic Ca and Sm are disordered on the A site, so neither mp_id is taken. Sm is 5 at.% of the formula and so a host element, and the W from the paper title is absent from this composition. The Pnma-to-tetragonal transition of CaMnO3 lies above 1073 K, so none is crossed here.

basis: La0.1Ca0.9Mn0.7Ti0.3O3, from a paper on the role of the tetravalent ion in the metal-insulator transition of (La0.1Ca0.9)(Mn,M)O3. This is La-doped CaMnO3 with Ti4+ replacing 30 per cent of Mn on the B site. It is the orthorhombic Pnma perovskite with Mn and Ti disordered on the B site.

dopant_roles.site: A site
dopant_roles.basis: La3+ on the Ca2+ site is the electron donor, and the (La0.1Ca0.9) A-site block is fixed across the paper series while the B site is varied.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its PRIMARY entries are Ca2TiMnO6 I4/m (mp-1080507) and CaTi2MnO6 P4_2mc (mp-1194928). These are B-site-ordered cells at 1:1 or 2:1 Ti:Mn with one ICSD reference each. At Mn0.7Ti0.3 there is no stoichiometry for rock-salt ordering, and Ti4+ and Mn3+/4+ are too close in charge and size to order. The disordered Pnma cell is taken and no mp_id is assigned.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62], ICSD-backed references for this host report [87, 105]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CaOsO3, from the paper on high-pressure synthesis of the cubic 5d perovskite BaOsO3, which places it in the AOsO3 series. CaOsO3 is the small-A-cation member, the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type tilted perovskite, and [ref 2] carries CaOsO3 Pnma (62) mp-1213970.

other_polymorphs.note: Untilted cubic cell at hull 0.253 with no ICSD reference; the Ca cation is too small to stabilise it.

note: Disagrees with [ref 2] PRIMARY by ICSD count. That entry is Ca2Os2O7 Imma (mp-2923, 4 ICSD references), a different compound: an Os5+ weberite-type oxide, not the Os4+ perovskite measured here. The perovskite entry mp-1213970 has no ICSD reference in the 2019 dump and sits at hull 0.088, which reflects a high-pressure phase, not a doubtful one.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62], ICSD-backed references for this host report [74]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Ca2Pr7Sb5O5 bulk, from the paper on the transport properties and compositions of the Ca2RE7Pn5O5 family. It is the praseodymium member of that family and is filed identically to Ca-Dy-O-Sb and Ca-Gd-O-Sb.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2], and its entry is not used. The only line is Ca3Pr2Sb3O14 C2/m (mp-1214039), a fully oxidised Sb5+ antimonate. Ca2Pr7Sb5O5 is a reduced antimonide oxide with Sb as an anion, so it is a different compound, not a polymorph. Three members of this family now sit in unresolved_crystalline, which is the case for a family prototype at v4 review.

basis: Ca2Re2O7, from a paper on the structural and electronic properties of pyrochlore-type A2Re2O7. The paper title names the structure: A2B2O7 with corner-sharing ReO6 octahedra, filed like Cd2Re2O7 in Cd-O-Re.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. None of its entries is Ca2Re2O7. Ca(ReO5)2, Ca11(ReO6)4 and Ca3ReO6 are other calcium rhenates at different oxidation states, so no mp_id is taken. Cd2Re2O7 has low-temperature structural transitions (near 200 K and 120 K) inside a window like this one. Whether Ca2Re2O7 has comparable transitions is not recalled, so none is recorded and the paper should be checked.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [15, 9, 14, 80]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Ca2Sm7Sb5O5 bulk, from the same Ca2RE7Pn5O5 paper as Ca-O-Pr-Sb. It is the samarium member of that family and is filed identically.
note: No structure reference was matched. See Ca-O-Pr-Sb for the case for a family prototype.

basis: Ca3SnO bulk, from the paper on thermoelectric properties of the antiperovskite calcium oxides Ca3PbO and Ca3SnO. The title names the structure: O at the octahedral centre, Ca at the octahedron corners and Sn4- at the A site. [ref 2] confirms it as Ca3SnO Pm-3m (221) mp-29241 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references. Filed like Ca3PbO in Ca-O-Pb.
note: Disagrees with [ref 1]. TEDesignLab has no Ca3SnO entry, and its PRIMARY is CaSnO3 Pnma (mp-4438, 11 ICSD references). That is the ordinary Sn4+ stannate perovskite, a different compound in the same chemistry. Following it would invert the anion and cation roles. The [ref 2] Ca3SnO entry matches the composition exactly and is taken.

basis: CaSrO3, from a thin-film paper on separated transport relaxation scales and interband scattering (title truncated). As written this is not a known compound: CaO and SrO form a rock-salt solid solution, and an ABO3 formula needs a B-site cation. The ABO3 formula and the thin-film transport study suggest a perovskite whose B-site element (plausibly Ru) was lost in transcription, so perovskite is assigned at low confidence.
note: The composition string needs checking against the paper before this record means anything. Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its SrCaO3 Pm-3m (mp-978842, hull 0.456, no ICSD) is a computed hypothetical, and the Sr3CaO4, SrCa3O4 and SrCaO2 lines are orderings of the rock-salt oxide solid solution, so no mp_id is taken. If the film is (Ca,Sr)RuO3, it would be orthorhombic Pnma.

basis: PbS0.9Cl0.1CaS, from a paper on enhancing the figure of merit of PbS with second-phase nanostructures. The matrix is Cl-doped n-type PbS and CaS is the nanostructured second phase; both are rock-salt sulfides. The fraction of CaS was lost from the string, which is why Ca reaches host level.

dopant_roles.site: anion site
dopant_roles.basis: PbS0.9Cl0.1 writes Cl against S. A halide on the chalcogen site is the standard n-type donor for PbS.

note: Both phases are Fm-3m rock salt, so the prototype holds whether Ca dissolves into PbS or stays as CaS precipitates. Only the multiphase character is uncertain, which is why composite_multiphase is the alternative. The written Ca:Pb of 1:1 is an artefact of how the composite was transcribed; a few per cent CaS is the likely real content. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3SmSb3, from the paper on the Ca3RESb3 Zintl family. It is the samarium member, read as anti-Th3P4 with Ca and Sm sharing the cation site, and filed like Ca-La-Sb and Ca-Ce-Sb.
note: The structure type is recalled for this family, not read from the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ca3TbSb3, from the paper on the Ca3RESb3 Zintl family. It is the terbium member, read as anti-Th3P4 with Ca and Tb sharing the cation site, and filed like Ca-Sb-Sm.
note: The structure type is recalled for this family, not read from the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ag0.15Cd2.9Ca0.1Co4O9, from a paper on filiform silver nanoinclusions to enhance the thermoelectric performance of p-type Ca3Co4O9. The 3:4:9 stoichiometry and the paper title identify the Ca3Co4O9 misfit layered cobaltite. The Cd2.9Ca0.1 in the string is read as Ca2.9Cd0.1 with the two symbols swapped: no Cd3Co4O9 misfit is known, while a small Cd substitution on the Ca site of Ca3Co4O9 is plausible.

dopant_roles.basis: The paper title says the silver is present as filiform metal nanoinclusions, a second phase, not a lattice substituent. Some Ag may still enter the Ca site; that is not separable from the composition.
As written Ca is a 0.1 minor element, but on the swapped reading it is the majority rock-salt-layer cation of Ca3Co4O9, not a dopant. Left unknown until the composition is checked against the paper.

note: The composition string should be corrected before stage 3; as it stands, the host key Cd-Co-O is itself an artefact. Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its lines are Cd-Co spinel, ilmenite and related oxides (CdCo2O4 Fd-3m mp-771736 and others), none of which is a misfit layered compound. They describe the chemistry as written, not this sample. Misfit cobaltites are incommensurate, so no single space group or mp_id applies.

basis: Eu9Cd3.8Cu1.5Sb9 is a coinage-metal-stuffed Eu9Cd4Sb9, as the paper title says. It is the Cu member of the series whose Ag and Au members are filed under zintl_9_4_9: the 9-4-9 Zintl framework with some Cd replaced and extra Cu on the interstitial sites the ideal formula leaves partly empty.
note: Cu is 6.4 atomic per cent and so a host element with no dopant entry. The transition-metal total of 5.3 against the ideal 4 shows the stuffing, which is what makes the compound metallic. No reference covers the host.

basis: Cu2Cd0.5Mn0.5SnSe4, from a paper on enhanced thermoelectric performance of Cu2CdSnSe4 by Mn doping; the curator gives the series as Cu2Cd1-xMnxSnSe4. Cu2CdSnSe4 is the stannite-type quaternary diamond-like selenide, and Cu2MnSnSe4 is isostructural, so the whole series is one prototype. Filed like Cd-Cu-Se-Sn.
note: Partly disagrees with [ref 2]. MnCdCu4(SnSe4)2 C2 (mp-1221832) is this exact formula, but in a supercell that orders Mn and Cd, which lowers the symmetry to C2. The paper treats Mn as substituting randomly on the Cd site, so the stannite I-42m cell is kept and that mp_id is not taken. At x = 0.5 Mn is a host element, not a dopant.

basis: YbCdCu4 single crystal, from a paper revisiting the heavy-fermion compound. YbXCu4 is the cubic MgCu4Sn (C15b) ordered variant of AuBe5, the family YbAgCu4 exemplifies. [ref 2] confirms it as YbCdCu4 F-43m (216) mp-12009 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference.
note: The Yb5CdCu2 I4/mcm line, which [ref 2] also marks PRIMARY, is a different compound in the same chemistry. Full measured span reaches 291 K.

basis: Cd83.7Er16.3, from the paper on the low-temperature structural stability of the Cd6M (M = Ho, Er, Tm, Lu) cubic approximants. The composition is the Cd6Er 1/1 Tsai-type approximant, a periodic Im-3 packing of the icosahedral clusters that build the i-CdYb quasicrystal. Filed like Cd-Yb and Ca-Cd.
note: Cd6M approximants undergo a low-temperature ordering of the central Cd4 tetrahedra, which lowers the cubic symmetry. That ordering is the subject of the paper and probably falls inside this 17-295 K window. Its temperature for M = Er is not recalled, so only the cubic phase is recorded and the transition should be taken from the paper. Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its PRIMARY ErCd Pm-3m (mp-867) is the equiatomic B2 compound, and ErCd6 Immm (mp-1227922, no ICSD) is not the approximant cell, so neither mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 12, 63, 191]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Cd0.89Ga0.11Te single crystal, from a paper on the structural analysis, growth and characterization of cadmium gallium telluride. At Ga0.11 on the Cd site this is Ga-alloyed zincblende CdTe, not the defect-chalcopyrite CdGa2Te4. Filed like CdTe in Cd-Te.
note: Disagrees with [ref 1]. Its only entry is CdGa2Te4 I-4 (mp-13949, 4 ICSD references), the vacancy-ordered defect chalcopyrite at Cd:Ga 1:2. This crystal is Cd:Ga 8:1, far on the CdTe side. Ga3+ on Cd2+ at this level leaves cation vacancies, and some local vacancy ordering is possible, which is why defect_chalcopyrite_ovc is the alternative and confidence is medium. Ga is 5.5 at.% and a host element. Full measured span reaches 390 K.

basis: GdCd, from a paper on transport in the RZn and RCd compounds. The equiatomic RCd compounds are the B2 CsCl type, and [ref 2] confirms it as GdCd Pm-3m (221) mp-1031 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references, its best-attested entry. Filed like TbCd in Cd-Tb.
note: GdCd orders ferromagnetically in the measured range, which is a magnetic transition, not a structural one.

basis: Tl2CdGeTe4, from the paper Tl2AXTe4 (A = Cd, Hg, Mn; X = Ge, Sn): Crystal Structure, Electronic Structure and Thermoelectric Properties. It is the Cd-Ge member of the family filed under tl2axte4_type for Ge-Hg-Te-Tl and Hg-Sn-Te-Tl. The A2BCX4 stoichiometry is that of stannite, but Tl(I) is a 6s2 lone-pair cation that cannot occupy a sphalerite cation site.
note: The proposed prototype still carries an unverified space group. It should be read from the crystal-structure section of this paper before v4 review. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Cd83.7Ho16.3, from the paper on the low-temperature structural stability of the Cd6M (M = Ho, Er, Tm, Lu) cubic approximants. It is the Cd6Ho 1/1 Tsai-type approximant, filed like Cd-Er.
note: Same low-temperature Cd4-tetrahedron ordering caveat as Cd-Er: probably inside the window, temperature not recalled, so it should be taken from the paper. Disagrees with [ref 2]. HoCd Pm-3m (mp-170) is the B2 equiatomic compound and HoCd6 Immm (mp-1225485, no ICSD) is not the approximant cell, so no mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 63, 164, 191]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CdIn2O4, the transparent-conducting cadmium indate, from a paper on preparation, electrical properties and optical characterization of cadmium-based oxide films (title truncated). AB2O4 with Cd2+ and In3+ is the cubic spinel, and [ref 1] confirms it: TEDesignLab CdIn2O4 Fd-3m (227) mp-19803 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references.

other_polymorphs.note: TEDesignLab also lists a tetragonal I4_1/amd CdIn2O4 with no Materials Project counterpart. It is a distorted spinel cell, not reached by heating in this window.
Imma cell at hull 0.078 with no ICSD reference. Its prototype is not identified, and post-spinel is a guess from the formula.

note: The degree of Cd/In inversion is not set by the composition and depends on preparation.

basis: Cd83.7Lu16.3, from the paper on the low-temperature structural stability of the Cd6M (M = Ho, Er, Tm, Lu) cubic approximants. It is the Cd6Lu 1/1 Tsai-type approximant, filed like Cd-Er.
note: Same low-temperature ordering caveat as Cd-Er. Disagrees with [ref 2]. LuCd Pm-3m (mp-2217) is the B2 compound and no Cd6Lu entry exists, so no mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 63, 164, 216]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Cd0.89Mg0.11O polycrystal, from a paper on tuning the microstructure and thermoelectric properties of CdO ceramics. CdO and MgO are both rock-salt oxides, so Mg on the Cd site keeps the Fm-3m structure. Filed like CdO in Cd-O.
note: Mg is 5.5 at.% and so a host element. Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line, Mg3CdO4 Pm-3m (mp-1099255, hull 0.129, no ICSD), is a computed cation ordering of the rock-salt lattice at the wrong ratio, so it is not taken.

basis: NdCd, from the paper on transport in the RZn and RCd compounds. It is the equiatomic B2 CsCl-type phase, confirmed by NdCd Pm-3m (221) mp-991061 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, the best-attested entry. Filed like Cd-Gd.
note: The other [ref 2] PRIMARY lines are different Nd-Cd compounds at other ratios.

basis: Cd2Ru2O7, measured alongside Cd2Re2O7 in a paper on fluctuation effects in the physical properties of that pyrochlore. A2B2O7 with Cd2+ and Ru5+ is the cubic pyrochlore, filed like Cd-O-Re and the Tl2Ru2O7 pyrochlore in O-Ru-Tl.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line is CdRuO3 Pm-3m (mp-1016849), a computed perovskite at hull 0.336 with no ICSD reference and a different stoichiometry, so it is not taken.

basis: PrCd, from the paper on transport in the RZn and RCd compounds. It is the equiatomic B2 CsCl-type phase, confirmed by PrCd Pm-3m (221) mp-646 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references, the best-attested entry. Filed like Cd-Gd.
note: Full measured span reaches 241 K.

basis: Undoped CdSe single crystal, from a paper on DC galvanomagnetic and thermoelectric effects in it. Bulk CdSe grown from the melt or vapour is hexagonal wurtzite, and [ref 1] confirms it: TEDesignLab CdSe P6_3mc (186) mp-1070 at hull 0.001 with 25 ICSD references, its best-attested entry.

other_polymorphs.note: Zincblende CdSe, 10 ICSD references. It is found in nanocrystals and epitaxial films on cubic substrates, not reached by heating a wurtzite crystal.
Rock-salt CdSe at hull 0.146, 4 ICSD references. It is the pressure-induced phase near 3 GPa.

note: MP places zincblende 0.001 eV below wurtzite. That is inside DFT error, and it does not override the ICSD evidence or the known growth habit.

basis: Cd6Sm, marked IAC (icosahedral approximant crystal) in the string itself, from the paper on structural and magnetic transitions in the crystalline approximant Cd6Sm. It is the 1/1 Tsai-type approximant, filed like Cd-Yb and Cd-Er.
note: The paper title reports a structural transition, and the full measured span of 10-298 K will cross it. Its temperature is not recalled, so the cubic Im-3 cell is recorded alone and the low-temperature phase should be added from the paper. The _IAC suffix is a label, not an element. Disagrees with [ref 2]. SmCd Pm-3m (mp-572) is the B2 compound and no Cd6Sm entry exists, so no mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 191]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Tl2CdSnTe4, the Cd-Sn member of the Tl2AXTe4 family, from the same paper as Cd-Ge-Te-Tl and filed identically.
note: Unverified space group on the proposed prototype, as for Cd-Ge-Te-Tl. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Cd83.7Tm16.3, from the paper on the low-temperature structural stability of the Cd6M (M = Ho, Er, Tm, Lu) cubic approximants. It is the Cd6Tm 1/1 Tsai-type approximant, filed like Cd-Er.
note: Same low-temperature ordering caveat as Cd-Er. Disagrees with [ref 2]. TmCd Pm-3m (mp-2502) is the B2 compound and no Cd6Tm entry exists, so no mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221, 63, 164, 191]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Cd6Y, from the paper on a novel phase transition in the Cd6M intermetallics. It is the 1/1 Tsai-type cubic approximant, filed like Ca-Cd, which comes from the same paper.
note: The phase transition named in the paper title is the Cd4-tetrahedron ordering, and it lies inside this window. Its temperature for Cd6Y is not recalled, so it is not recorded. Disagrees with [ref 2]. YCd Pm-3m (mp-915) is the B2 compound and no Cd6Y entry exists, so no mp_id is taken.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [191, 221, 63, 216]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CeCo2 single crystal, from a paper on its transport properties. CeCo2 is the cubic C15 Laves phase, confirmed by [ref 2] as CeCo2 Fd-3m (227) mp-1112 at hull 0.000 with 15 ICSD references. Filed like CeRh2 in Ce-Rh.
note: [ref 2] ranks CeCo5 P6/mmm (19 ICSD) above CeCo2 by ICSD count. That is a different compound, the CaCu5 phase, and not a polymorph of this one; the CeCo2 entry matches the composition and is taken.

basis: CeCo0.8Cu0.2Si rod, from a paper on thermoelectric properties of rare-earth alloys. Equiatomic CeCoSi is the tetragonal CeFeSi type, P4/nmm, which is the PbFCl type with Ce and Si on the two 2c sites and Co on 2a. Cu is taken to substitute on the Co site.
note: Cu is 6.7 at.% and so a host element. CeCuSi itself is a different (AlB2-derived hexagonal) type, so enough Cu could change the structure; at 20 per cent of the T site the CeCoSi type is assumed. The CeFeSi type for CeCoSi is recalled, not read from this paper. Disagrees with [ref 2]. Its only line, CeCoCuSi2 I-4m2 (mp-1226624, hull 0.053, no ICSD), is a different stoichiometry, so it is not taken.

basis: Ce0.4Sr0.6Co0.7Fe0.3O3-delta pellets, from a paper on highly conducting perovskite-structured (M-SrCoFe-O3-delta, M = Ce, Ba) cathodes. The title names the structure. It is the SrCo0.7Fe0.3O3 cobaltite-ferrite perovskite with Ce on the A site, filed like Co-Fe-O-Sr.
note: Ce is 8 at.% and a host element. The solubility of Ce on the A site of SrCoO3-based perovskites is limited, and at Ce0.4 a CeO2 fluorite second phase is likely. That is why composite_multiphase is the alternative. The space group of the main phase depends on Ce content and oxygen stoichiometry, so it is left null. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeCoGeH bulk, from the paper on the influence of Ce-H bonding on the physical properties of the hydrides CeCoSiH and CeCoGeH. Hydrogen enters the Ce4 tetrahedra of the CeFeSi-type parent. This gives the filled PbFCl type, ZrCuSiAs, with H on the site oxygen takes in LaFeAsO. [ref 2] confirms it as CeCoGeH P4/nmm (129) mp-644499 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference.
note: H is 25 at.% and a host element. Its content is the variable that sets the Ce valence, so stage 3 should treat it as a compositional variable, not a dopant.

basis: Yb2CeCo4Ge13 bulk, from a paper on thermoelectric properties of Pr3Rh4Sn13-type Yb3Co4Ge13 and Yb3Co4Sn13. It is Yb3Co4Ge13 with one Yb in three replaced by Ce, the cubic Remeika 3-4-13 phase, filed like Co-Ge-Yb.
note: Ce is 5 at.% and a host element on the rare-earth site. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeCoSiH bulk, from the same paper as Ce-Co-Ge-H, on the hydrides CeCoSiH and CeCoGeH. It is the silicide partner of CeCoGeH: the CeFeSi-type CeCoSi with H filling the Ce4 tetrahedra, which gives the ZrCuSiAs type.
note: Medium rather than high because no reference covers CeCoSiH directly. The type is carried over from the germanide, which [ref 2] does confirm.

basis: Ce2Ni2.5Co0.5Si, from a paper on thermoelectric properties of intermediate-valent cerium intermetallics. As written, Ce2(Ni,Co)3Si matches no Ce-Ni-Si compound I can place. Ce2Ni3Si5 and Ce2Co3Si5, however, are both well-known intermediate-valent U2Co3Si5-type compounds with exactly this Ni/Co split on the transition-metal site. The string is read as Ce2Ni2.5Co0.5Si5 with the Si subscript lost.
note: Low confidence because the assignment rests on correcting the composition string. It must be checked against the paper. If the Si1 stoichiometry is real, the host belongs in unresolved_crystalline. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeRh0.75Co0.25Sn bulk, from a paper on thermoelectric and magnetic properties of CeRh1-xMxSn (M = Co, Ni, ...). CeRhSn is the equiatomic hexagonal ZrNiAl-type RTX compound, P-62m, filed under zrnial_fe2p for Ce-Rh-Sn. Co substitutes on the Rh site.
note: Co is 8 at.% and a host element. The tinisi_co2si entry advises medium confidence for either RTX ordering until diffraction is read. CeCoSn is not ZrNiAl-type, so the structure at this x depends on the solubility limit in the paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ce3CoRu3Sn13 polycrystal, from a paper on the doping effect on the electronic structure and thermodynamic properties of Ce3Ru4Sn13-type compounds (title truncated). It is Ce3Ru4Sn13 with one Ru in four replaced by Co, the cubic Remeika 3-4-13 phase, filed like Ce-Ru-Sn and Ce-Co-Sn.
note: Co is exactly 5 at.% and a host element on the transition-metal site. Some 3-4-13 stannides have a superlattice distortion (I4_132 or similar) below room temperature. None is recorded here because the chunk shows no transition line and it is not recalled for this composition. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeCrGe3 bulk, from a paper on heavy-fermion and Kondo-lattice behaviour in this itinerant ferromagnet. It is the cerium partner of LaCrGe3, filed under hexagonal_perovskite_polytype for Cr-Ge-La: the BaNiO3 2H structure with face-sharing CrGe6 octahedral chains. [ref 2] confirms it as CeCrGe3 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-20650 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference.
note: The ferromagnetic order near 70 K is magnetic, not structural. Full measured span reaches 400 K.

basis: CeNi4Cr bulk, from a paper on thermal transport in this intermetallic compound. RNi4X compounds of this kind take the cubic MgCu4Sn (C15b) ordered-AuBe5 type, with Ce and Cr on the two distinct large and small sites and Ni forming the tetrahedral network. Filed alongside YbCdCu4 in this chunk.
note: The alternative is a Cr-substituted CeNi5, the hexagonal CaCu5 type: the 1:5 overall ratio of Ce to transition metal allows both. The cubic assignment is recalled for CeNi4Cr and CeNi4Mn, not read from the paper, and should be confirmed. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Cs0.772Ce2Cu5.232Te6 bulk, from the Chem. Mater. paper on syntheses, structures, and magnetic and thermoelectric properties of double-tunnel tellurides. It is the Cs-Ce member of the AxRE2Cu6-xTe6 family. The Cs and Cu contents sum to 6.0, which is the charge balance of that family with Ce3+ and Te2-. No seed prototype has an alkali in the tunnels of a rare-earth copper telluride framework, so axre2cu6te6_double_tunnel was proposed.
note: The proposed prototype carries a recalled, unverified space group, so it is left null here. Cs at 0.772 is partial tunnel occupancy and the Cu deficiency compensates it; both are compositional variables, not dopants. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeCu4Ga bulk, from a paper on thermoelectric power in (Ce,Ni; Cu,Ga) compounds. CeCu5 is the hexagonal CaCu5 type, and Ga substitutes on the Cu sites across a range that includes CeCu4Ga, which stays in P6/mmm.
note: Disagrees with [ref 2]. None of its entries is CeCu4Ga. Ce2Ga12Cu, Ce2Ga3Cu, Ce2Ga5Cu3, CeGa2Cu3 and CeGa3Cu are other Ce-Cu-Ga compounds, most with no ICSD support, so no mp_id is taken. The CaCu5 type at this composition is recalled, not read from the paper.

basis: CeLa4CuSn3, from a paper on the formation of the heavy-fermion state in Ce5-xLaxCuSn3. It is Ce5CuSn3 with four Ce in five replaced by La: the Hf5CuSn3-type interstitially filled Mn5Si3 structure, filed like Ce5CuSn3 in Ce-Cu-Sn.
note: Ce and La are a continuous rare-earth-site series here, so Ce is a host element, not a dopant. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeIrGaH1.8 bulk, from a paper on hydrogenation of the Ce(Rh1-xIrx)Ga system and the resulting antiferromagnetism. The parent CeIrGa is taken to be the orthorhombic TiNiSi-type RTX compound, and the hydride is recorded under the parent framework with H in its interstices.
note: Low confidence on two counts. The parent type is recalled, not read. More importantly, at 1.8 H per formula unit hydrogenation of an RTX compound can rebuild the metal framework (hexagonal AlB2-derived hydrides are known for some CeTX). So the hydride may not keep the parent structure, and the paper must be read. H is 36 at.% and a host element. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ce(Rh0.46Ir0.54)GaH1.8 bulk, from the same paper as Ce-Ga-H-Ir on hydrogenation of the Ce(Rh1-xIrx)Ga system. It is the mixed Rh/Ir member of that hydride series and is filed identically.
note: Rh and Ir are an isoelectronic series on the T site, so both are host elements. Same caveats as Ce-Ga-H-Ir. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeNiGaH1.1 bulk, from a paper on the change from intermediate valence to magnetic behaviour without long-range order on hydrogenation. The Ce-Ga-Ni record notes that [ref 2] placed equiatomic CeNiGa in the hexagonal P-62m ZrNiAl type. The hydride is recorded under that parent framework with H in its interstices.
note: Low confidence. CeNiGa is reported in more than one RTX ordering, and hydrogenation can rebuild the framework. So both the parent type and whether the hydride keeps it need the paper. H is 26 at.% and a host element. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeRhGaH1.8 bulk, from the same paper as Ce-Ga-H-Ir and Ce-Ga-H-Ir-Rh on hydrogenation of the Ce(Rh1-xIrx)Ga system. It is the Rh end member of that hydride series. It is filed like its siblings, under the orthorhombic TiNiSi-type parent CeRhGa, with H in its interstices.
note: Same caveats as Ce-Ga-H-Ir: the parent type is recalled, and at 1.8 H per formula unit the hydride may have rebuilt the metal framework into a hexagonal AlB2-derived cell. H is 36 at.% and a host element. The Ce-Ga-Rh host record is filed under thcr2si2_122, which covers a different composition (a 1-2-2 phase), not equiatomic CeRhGa. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ce2Ir3Ga9 polycrystal, from the paper on new ternary Ce2T3X9 compounds. The R2T3X9 compounds are the Y2Co3Ga9 type, orthorhombic Cmcm. [ref 2] agrees: Ce2(Ga3Ir)3 Cmcm (63) mp-1213877 at hull 0.000.
note: The MP entry carries no ICSD reference count, so the agreement is with a computed structure. The CeGaIr Pnma entry on the same ref line is a different compound and does not apply.

basis: CePtGa, from the paper on thermoelectric power of Ce-based Kondo alloys. Equiatomic CePtGa is an orthorhombic TiNiSi-type RTX compound. [ref 2] agrees: CeGaPt Pnma (62) mp-1103487 at hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: Medium rather than high: the reference rests on a single ICSD entry, and RTX compounds can switch between TiNiSi and ZrNiAl types with small changes in stoichiometry. CeGa3Pt and CeGaPt4 on the ref line are other compounds.

basis: Ce2Ru3Ga9 polycrystal, from a paper revisiting the intermediate-valence physics of Ce2Ru3Ga9. Like Ce2Ir3Ga9 it is an R2T3X9 compound of the Y2Co3Ga9 type. [ref 2] agrees: Ce2(Ga3Ru)3 Cmcm (63) mp-1214327 at hull 0.000.
note: The MP entry has no ICSD reference count. The full measured span is 11-390 K.

basis: CeSiGa bulk, from the paper on thermoelectric properties of solid solutions based on ThSi2-type CeSi2. The paper title places this Ga-substituted disilicide in the tetragonal alpha-ThSi2 type, I4_1/amd, the same entry as the Ce-Si host.

other_polymorphs.note: The [ref 2] PRIMARY, CeGaSi Imma, hull 0.000, no ICSD refs. Imma is the orthorhombic GdSi2-type distortion of alpha-ThSi2.
CeGaSi I4_1md, hull 0.017: the Si/Ga-ordered LaPtSi-type variant of alpha-ThSi2.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] prefers orthorhombic Imma (74) for CeGaSi, not the tetragonal I4_1/amd aristotype that I record from the paper title. Neither MP entry has an ICSD reference. At Si:Ga = 1:1 an ordered I4_1md or a distorted Imma cell is possible, and AlB2-type disorder is also known for RGaSi. So no mp_id is attached to the phase, and the space group must come from the paper.

basis: CeGe2 is the alpha-ThSi2-type digermanide, I4_1/amd. [ref 2] agrees: CeGe2 I4_1/amd (141) mp-21055 at hull 0.000, 5 ICSD references, the best-attested entry on the ref line.
note: The linked paper is titled on CexY1-xInCu2 and CeInCuyAg2-y, not on CeGe2, so this sample may be a reference compound in that paper or a misattribution; worth checking. CeGe2-x is often germanium deficient and may then distort to orthorhombic Imma. Robust range 10-17 K, full span 10-298 K.

basis: CeRuGeH bulk, from the paper on the antiferromagnetic behaviour of the hydride CeRuGeH. This is the same chemistry as Ce-Co-Ge-H. H enters the Ce4 tetrahedra of the CeFeSi-type parent CeRuGe, which gives the filled PbFCl type, ZrCuSiAs.
note: H is 25 at.% and a host element; its content sets the Ce valence and is a compositional variable, not a dopant. No structure reference was matched, so the P4/nmm cell is from the analogy with CeCoGeH (mp-644499 on that host ref line), not from a reference for this formula.

basis: Ce2MnGe6 bulk, from the paper on electric transport in R2MGe6 ternary compounds (R = La, Ce, Gd, Tb, Dy). R2TGe6 is the Ce2CuGe6 type, and the paper treats the whole rare-earth series as one structure family.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] returns Ce(MnGe)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-21089 (7 ICSD refs) and CeMnGe P4/nmm (129) mp-21399. Both are different compounds (CeMn2Ge2 and CeMnGe), and neither is Ce2MnGe6. I do not take their mp_ids. CeMn2Ge2 is the obvious secondary phase to look for in the paper. Medium because Mn is not a typical T for this type, and the space group (Amm2 or Cmce) must come from the paper.

basis: Ce4Sb1.5Ge1.5, from a paper on ferromagnetism and transport in this Kondo system. At R4X3 this is the anti-Th3P4 stoichiometry that Ce4Sb3 adopts (I-43d), with Ge substituted onto the Sb site.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives only Ce5GeSb2 Pnma (62) mp-1213986, a Sm5Ge4-type R5X3 compound at a different stoichiometry. I do not take that mp_id for an R4X3 sample. Sb and Ge are not isoelectronic, so the 1:1 mixing needs charge compensation. The anti-Th3P4 assignment is recalled, not confirmed, and the paper should be checked.

basis: CePdInH bulk, from the paper on the Doniach diagram and hydrogenation of CePdIn and CePdSn. The parent CePdIn is the hexagonal ZrNiAl type (the Ce-In-Pd host record). The monohydrides of ZrNiAl-type RTIn compounds keep that framework, with H in the R3T tetrahedra.
note: H is 25 at.% and a host element. Retention of the ZrNiAl framework is recalled from the LaNiInH/CeNiInH hydrides, not read from this paper. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CePdSnH bulk, from the same paper as Ce-H-In-Pd on the Doniach diagram and hydrogenation of CePdIn and CePdSn. The parent CePdSn is the orthorhombic TiNiSi type (the Ce-Pd-Sn host record). The hydride is filed under that parent framework with H in its interstices.
note: Low confidence. At one H per formula unit, TiNiSi-type stannides can transform on hydrogenation to a hexagonal ZrBeSi-type (ordered AlB2) cell, so the hydride may not keep the parent structure. H is 25 at.% and a host element. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeRhSbH0.2 bulk, from the paper on inducing magnetism in the Kondo semiconductor CeRhSb through hydrogenation. CeRhSb is the orthorhombic TiNiSi type (the Ce-Rh-Sb host record). At only 0.2 H per formula unit the hydrogen is a dilute interstitial and the framework is expected to be kept.
note: H is 6 at.%, just above the 5% cut, so it counts as a host element. Structurally it is an interstitial and should be treated in stage 3 as the hydrogenation variable. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ce1.5Ho1.5SbO3, from an Inorg. Chem. paper on the synthesis, crystal structure and electronic properties of tetragonal mixed rare-earth RE3SbO3 phases. Ho3SbO3 itself is monoclinic C2/m (the Ho-O-Sb host record). The title says that mixing a large and a small rare earth gives a tetragonal variant, and the taxonomy has no entry for that variant.
note: Parked rather than proposed: one sample, and the tetragonal cell is known here only from the title. If more RE3PnO3 members appear, the monoclinic and tetragonal RE3SbO3 types need their own entry. Ce and Ho share the rare-earth sites 1:1, but site ordering between them is likely and is what stabilises the tetragonal cell. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeIrSn, from a paper on large thermopower in several metallic cerium compounds. Equiatomic CeIrSn is the hexagonal ZrNiAl type, as CeRhSn is (the Ce-Rh-Sn host record). [ref 2] lists the matching formula as CeSnIr P-62m (189) mp-20835 at hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: [ref 2] ranks Ce(SnIr)2 P4/nmm and Ce3Ir4Sn13 Pm-3n above CeSnIr (2 ICSD refs each against 1), but those are different compounds, CeIr2Sn2 and a Remeika phase, not the equiatomic sample. The 1-ICSD-ref match is weak, hence medium. Full measured span 13-488 K.

basis: Ce0.5La0.5NiSn, from the paper on gap formation in CeNiSn at low temperatures. It is the CeNiSn-LaNiSn solid solution, and both end members are the orthorhombic epsilon-TiNiSi type, Pnma.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth site
solid_solution_axis.note: La is 4f-empty and dilutes the Kondo lattice; one composition only.

note: CONSISTENCY FLAG: the Ce-Ni-Sn (chunk 7) and Ce-La-Ni (chunk 8) host records file CeNiSn under crb_feb_chain, from before tinisi_co2si existed. TiNiSi is the more specific entry and is what later RTX records (Ce-Pd-Sn, Ce-Rh-Sb) use, so I use it here. The two older records should be moved to tinisi_co2si at v4 review. No structure reference was matched. Full span 11-258 K.

basis: (Ce0.75La0.25)Ru2 polycrystal, from the paper on transport in (Ce1-xRx)Ru2 (R = La, Nd). CeRu2 is the cubic C15 MgCu2-type Laves phase (the Ce-Ru host record), and La substitutes on the Ce site.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] LaCeRu4 F-43m, hull 0.000, no ICSD refs: a computed 1:1 La/Ce ordering of the C15 cell. The real sample is a disordered 3:1 solid solution in Fd-3m.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth (8a) site
solid_solution_axis.note: x = La/(Ce+La).

note: The only ref line is an ordered model, so it agrees on the prototype but not on the space group, and its mp_id is not attached to the phase.

basis: Ce7Li3 bulk, from a paper on electrical resistivity and thermopower of a heavy-fermion system. Ce and Li are essentially immiscible and form no established binary compound, so a Ce7Li3 composition is most likely a two-phase Ce plus Li alloy, or a nominal label. There is no single structure to assign from the composition.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] Li3Ce Fm-3m, hull 0.344: a hypothetical ordered compound far above the hull.
[ref 2] LiCe3 Pm-3m, hull 0.270: hypothetical.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: the only [ref 2] entries are computed compounds 0.27-0.34 eV/atom above the hull, which I read as evidence that no stable Ce-Li phase exists, not as candidate structures. The paper title is truncated; the sample may be a Ce-based compound with Li that was mis-parsed. Needs the paper.

basis: Ce0.6Pr0.4Mn2Si2, from a paper on thermopower in intermediate-valence Ce compounds. CeMn2Si2 and PrMn2Si2 are both body-centred tetragonal ThCr2Si2 type, and Pr substitutes on the Ce site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth (2a) site
solid_solution_axis.note: x = Pr/(Ce+Pr); one composition.

note: No ref line for this host. The Ce-Mn-Si ref line in the same chunk gives CeMn2Si2 as mp-2965; that mp_id belongs to the parent, not this alloy, so it is not attached.

basis: CeMn2Si2 is the body-centred tetragonal ThCr2Si2 type. [ref 2] agrees: Ce(MnSi)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-2965 at hull 0.000, 8 ICSD references, the best-attested entry.
note: CeMnSi2 Cmcm (mp-5901) on the same ref line is a different compound.

basis: (Ce2S2)2NbS2, from a paper on crystal structure and thermoelectric properties of misfit-layered sulfides. The curator detail says the paper assigns the NbS2 slab to subsystem 1 and the Ln2S2 block to subsystem 2. This is the (LnS)1+xNbS2 misfit family, as in the La-Nb-S host.
note: Incommensurate composite: two subsystems, no single MP entry. Stage 2 should not try to resolve an mp_id. The curator detail is the paper describing its own refinement, not a proof of phase purity, so experimentally_confirmed stays false. No structure reference was matched.

basis: (Nd0.5Ce0.5)2Zr2O7.5 bulk, from a paper on ultralow thermal conductivity of cerium-doped Nd2Zr2O7 over a wide doping range. The parent Nd2Zr2O7 is the ordered pyrochlore (the Nd-O-Zr host record). Ce4+ on the Nd site brings extra oxygen, O7.5, into the vacant 8a anion site, which pushes the structure toward defect fluorite.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] CeNd4Zr3O14 R-3m, hull 0.022, no ICSD refs: a computed ordered cell at a different stoichiometry.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only a computed R-3m CeNd4Zr3O14 cell. It is neither this composition nor a phase reported for Ce-doped Nd2Zr2O7, so I do not follow it. Medium because at half Ce on the A site the sample may have crossed from pyrochlore to disordered fluorite. The XRD in the paper decides this, and the alternative is recorded.

basis: CeRh0.75Ni0.25Sn bulk, from the paper on thermoelectric and magnetic properties of CeRh1-xMxSn (M = Co, Ni, ...). CeRhSn is the hexagonal ZrNiAl type (the Ce-Rh-Sn host record). Ni substitutes on the Rh site. This is the same series as the Ce-Co-Rh-Sn host.
note: Ni is 8 at.% and a host element. Medium because CeNiSn, the Ni end member, is TiNiSi type, so a large enough Ni content would change the structure; at x = 0.25 the ZrNiAl framework is expected to hold. No structure reference was matched.

basis: CeNiSb2 bulk, from the paper on Kondo-lattice behaviour in CeTSb2 (T = Ni, Cu, Ag). The CeTSb2 compounds are the HfCuSi2 type, with Sb square nets. [ref 2] lists the matching formula as CeNiSb2 P4/nmm (129) mp-22539 at hull 0.000, 3 ICSD references.
note: The top-ranked entry on the ref line, Ce(NiSb)2 P4/nmm mp-1078924 (4 ICSD refs), is CeNi2Sb2, a CaBe2Ge2-type 1-2-2 compound, not this sample. I take the matching-formula entry instead of the PRIMARY one.

basis: CeRuPO, from the PRB paper on the avoided ferromagnetic quantum critical point in CeRuPO. It is a LaFeAsO-type 1111 oxypnictide. [ref 2] agrees: CePRuO P4/nmm (129) mp-21372 at hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: Ce2P2RuO P4/mmm on the ref line is 1.7 eV/atom above the hull and irrelevant. Measured range is only 11-15 K.

basis: Sm2(Zr0.7Ce0.3)2O7, from a paper on the preparation and thermophysical properties of Sm2(Ce0.3Zr0.7)2O7 ceramic, a thermal-barrier candidate. Sm2Zr2O7 is an ordered pyrochlore, and here Ce4+ replaces 30% of the Zr on the B site.
note: Ce is 5.5 at.%, just above the cut, so it counts as a host element. The large Ce4+ on the B site lowers rA/rB toward the pyrochlore-fluorite boundary, and Sm2Ce2O7 is fluorite. At 30% the pyrochlore is expected to survive, hence medium, with fluorite recorded as the alternative. The order-disorder transition of Sm2Zr2O7 lies near 2000 K or above, beyond the 1672 K window. No structure reference was matched.

basis: U0.80Ce0.20O2, from a paper on CeO2 as a surrogate for PuO2 in MOX fuel development. UO2 and CeO2 are both fluorite oxides and form a continuous fluorite solid solution, with Ce on the U site.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation (4a) site
solid_solution_axis.note: Not isoelectronic in general, but both cations are tetravalent in the dioxide, so this is a cation-site solid solution rather than doping. x = Ce/(U+Ce).

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: all five [ref 2] entries (Ce2U2O9, Ce2U3O10, Ce2UO6, Ce3UO8, Ce4UO10) are computed ordered cells with no ICSD references, and two are flagged AMBIGUOUS. They describe hypothetical orderings, not the disordered fluorite solid solution the paper makes. None of their mp_ids is attached.

basis: Ce2P3Si, from a paper on thermoelectric properties of intermediate-valent cerium intermetallics. No established structure type matches a Ce2SiP3 stoichiometry. The only reference, CeSiP3, is a different composition.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] CeSiP3 Pna2_1, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD refs. If the recorded formula is a transcription slip for CeSiP3, this is the structure.

note: Either an unfamiliar compound or a mis-transcribed CeSiP3; the paper decides. Parked rather than proposed.

basis: Ce0.75Sc0.25Pd3, from a paper on thermoelectric properties of Ce1-xScxPd3. CePd3 is the cubic Cu3Au (L12) type (the Ce-Pd host record), and Sc substitutes on the Ce corner site, as Y does in Ce-Pd-Y.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] CeScPd6 P4/mmm, hull 0.000, no ICSD refs: a computed 1:1 Ce/Sc ordering of the L12 cell.

note: Sc is 6 at.% and a host element. The only ref line is an ordered model, so it agrees on the prototype but not on the space group or the stoichiometry. Its mp_id is not attached to the phase.

basis: CeRh0.75Ru0.25Sn bulk, from the same CeRh1-xMxSn paper as Ce-Ni-Rh-Sn. CeRhSn is the hexagonal ZrNiAl type, and Ru substitutes on the Rh site.
note: Ru is 8 at.% and a host element. CeRuSn itself is a different, monoclinic CeCoAl-derived superstructure, so the ZrNiAl framework holds only while Rh dominates. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ce3Ru4Sn11.05Sb1.95 polycrystal, from the PRB paper on doping effects on the electronic structure of Ce3Ru4Sn13. Ce3Ru4Sn13 is a cubic Remeika phase, Pm-3n (the Ce-Ru-Sn host record), and Sb substitutes on the Sn sites.
note: Sb is 10 at.% and a host element, but structurally it is an electron-donating substitution for Sn (one extra electron per Sb). Stage 3 should treat Sn/Sb as the doping variable. No structure reference was matched.

basis: Ce1.47(SrS)0.4, from a paper on thermoelectric properties of cerium sulfide semiconductors from 4 to 1300 K. This is a gamma-Ce2S3/Ce3S4-based sulfide with SrS dissolved into it. The cerium sulfides between Ce2S3 and Ce3S4 are the Th3P4 type, and SrCe2S4 sits on the same Th3P4 cation-vacancy line, as in the Ce-S and Ce-Eu-S host records.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] Sr(CeS2)2 I-42d, hull 0.033, no ICSD refs: a computed cation-ordered subgroup of the Th3P4 cell (I-43d, 220).

note: The parsed formula carries only the SrS sulfur, so it is almost certainly a CeSx(SrS)0.4 composition with the cerium-sulfide sulfur dropped in transcription; read as written it is not charge balanced. Medium for that reason, not for the structure. [ref 2] agrees on the family but offers an ordered model, so its mp_id is not attached. Full span 317-1178 K.

basis: CeSbSe, from the PRB paper on a possible devil staircase in the Kondo lattice CeSbSe. The RSbX (X = S, Se, Te) compounds are ZrSiS-type square-net relatives of PbFCl, and CeSbTe is filed here (the Ce-Sb-Te host record).

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] PRIMARY CeSbSe Pnma, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD ref. If the reference is right, this and not the tetragonal cell is the sample structure.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives CeSbSe as orthorhombic Pnma (1 ICSD reference), whereas I recall the tetragonal P4/nmm ZrSiS-type cell for this compound. In the RSbX series the Sb square net distorts as the chalcogen gets smaller, so a lower-symmetry cell for the selenide is plausible. I have not overridden the reference on the space group: no mp_id is attached, and the paper decides. Robust range 10-20 K, full span 10-297 K.

basis: (Zn0.7Ce0.3)4Sb3, from a paper on dislocation-induced ultra-low lattice thermal conductivity in rare-earth-doped Zn4Sb3. The paper is about rare-earth doping of beta-Zn4Sb3, so the host framework is Zn4Sb3.

dopant_roles.basis: As parsed, Ce is 17 at.% and a host element. That is not credible as substitution in Zn4Sb3, and the paper title says doping. The composition is most likely a dilute (Zn1-xCex)4Sb3 with x mis-transcribed, and any excess Ce would go to a Ce-Sb secondary phase.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] returns Ce2ZnSb4 and Ce4Zn3Sb8, P-4m2 ternary compounds with no ICSD refs. They describe the Ce-rich corner of the chemistry, not a doped Zn4Sb3. At 30% Ce on the Zn site as written, one of them could well be the majority phase, so the composition should be checked against the paper. The window 301-674 K stays within beta-Zn4Sb3 (alpha below ~250 K, gamma above ~765 K).

basis: CeSe1.8Sn0.2 bulk, from the paper on low-temperature thermoelectric properties of CeSe2-xSnx. CeSe2 is filed under pbfcl_matlockite (the Ce-Se host record): it is a ZrSSi/Cu2Sb-type layered diselenide with a Se square net, commonly monoclinically distorted, and Sn replaces Se in that net.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] gives only Ce2SnSe4 Pnma (1 ICSD ref, hull 0.077), a different compound at a much higher Sn content. It could be a secondary phase but is not the host structure, and its mp_id is not attached. Sn is 7 at.% and a host element; stage 3 should treat Sn-for-Se as the doping variable. The space group is left null because CeSe2 has a monoclinic superstructure of the tetragonal parent.

basis: Y0.5Ce0.5Si2 bulk, from the same paper as Ce-Ga-Si on thermoelectric solid solutions based on ThSi2-type CeSi2. The title places this Y-substituted disilicide on the CeSi2 alpha-ThSi2 framework.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth site
solid_solution_axis.note: x = Y/(Ce+Y). The Y end member is not ThSi2 type (YSi2-x is AlB2 derived), so the structure itself changes along this axis.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] returns Ce(YSi)4 P2_12_12_1 and Ce2YSi2 P4/mbm. Both are computed cells at other stoichiometries with no ICSD refs, and neither is a disilicide. I do not follow them. Medium because at half Y the solid solution may sit near the ThSi2/AlB2 boundary.

basis: CeSn3, from a paper on thermopower and resistivity of Ce(In1-xSnx)3. CeSn3 is the cubic Cu3Au (L12) type. [ref 2] agrees: CeSn3 Pm-3m (221) mp-1911 at hull 0.000, 10 ICSD references, the best-attested entry.
note: The other ref-line entries (Ce5Sn3, Ce3Sn, Ce5Sn4, Ce3Sn5) are different compounds. This is the Sn end member of the Ce(In,Sn)3 series filed under Ce-In-Sn.

basis: Tl9CeTe6 bulk, from the paper on hot-pressed Tl9LnTe6 (Ln = La, Ce, Pr, Nd, ...). Tl9LnTe6 is the Tl5Te3 type, with Ln sharing the 4c site with Tl, as for La-Te-Tl. [ref 2] lists the matching formula as Ce(Tl3Te2)3 I4/m (87) mp-1106203 at hull 0.000, 1 ICSD reference.
note: The MP cell is I4/m (87), a Tl/Ce-ordered subgroup of the Tl5Te3 aristotype I4/mcm (140). Experimentally the 4c site is usually refined as a disordered Tl/Ln mixture in I4/mcm, so stage 2 should confirm which cell to use. CeTlTe2 on the ref line is a different compound.

basis: CeZn11 single crystal, from the PRB paper on anisotropic transport, magnetism and a field-tuned transition in CeZn11. CeZn11 is the tetragonal BaCd11 type. [ref 2] agrees: CeZn11 I4_1/amd (141) mp-640370 at hull 0.004, 4 ICSD references.
note: New prototype bacd11_type proposed in prototypes_proposed.jsonl for this host. [ref 2] ranks CeZn and CeZn5 above CeZn11 (5 ICSD refs each against 4), but those are different compounds; I take the matching-formula entry, not the PRIMARY.

basis: CsTmCl3, from a theoretical (DFT) study of the structural, thermoelectric and spin-orbit properties of this compound. CsTmCl3 is an ABX3 halide with divalent Tm, and such studies model it as the cubic Pm-3m perovskite.
note: This is a computed curve, not a measured sample; the structure is whatever the paper assumed. REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] has no CsTmCl3 entry, only Tm3+ chlorides (Cs2TmCl4, Cs2TmCl5, Cs3TmCl6, CsTm2Cl7). That is a real hint that CsTmCl3 with Tm2+ may not be stable in bulk, so none of those mp_ids is attached. Medium because heavy-alkali ABCl3 halides can also take the hexagonal CsNiCl3 polytype.

basis: CuCl measured at 1103-1273 K, from the paper on electrical properties of molten CuCl-Cu2Se mixtures; this is the pure-CuCl end member. CuCl melts near 700 K, so the whole window is the ionic melt and no crystal structure applies.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 1] TEDesignLab CuCl F-43m, 4 ICSD refs: the ambient gamma-CuCl solid. It lies entirely below the measured window, which it never reaches (there is a brief wurtzite beta phase just below the melt). Recorded for completeness, not as a measured phase.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives zincblende CuCl, which is correct for the solid but not for this measurement, which is entirely liquid. I follow the measurement temperature, not the reference. CONSISTENCY FLAG: the sibling Cl-Cu-Se host (same paper, chunk 21) is filed under liquid_metal from before molten_salt was proposed. Pure CuCl is an ionic melt and fits molten_salt better. For the Cu2Se-rich mixtures, which conduct electronically, liquid_metal may still be the better fit, so that record needs a decision at v4 review.

basis: Li3InCl6, from the Small paper arguing that good solid-state electrolytes have low, glass-like thermal conductivity. Li3InCl6 is a superionic Li3MCl6 halide: a cubic close-packed Cl array with Li, In and vacancies ordered over the octahedral sites. The taxonomy has no entry for it, so one is proposed.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] Li3InCl6 Fm-3m, hull 0.231: a cation-disordered rocksalt model.

note: [ref 2] PRIMARY is Li3InCl6 C2 (5) mp-676109, hull 0.000, no ICSD refs. I recall the refined structure as C2/m (12), so the MP cell may be a lower-symmetry setting of it. The mp_id is attached but the space group is left null for stage 2 to settle. New prototype li3mx6_halide_electrolyte proposed in prototypes_proposed.jsonl.

basis: La3Zn4P6Cl single crystal, from the Chem. Mater. paper on enclathration of Cl@La4 tetrahedra in channels of Zn-P frameworks. From the title, this is a Zn-P framework whose channels hold La4 tetrahedra centred on a halide. No taxonomy entry describes that.
note: Parked rather than proposed: one sample, and the structure is known here only from the title (the paper title mentions X@La4, so other halides or chalcogenides probably occupy the same site in sister compounds). If more members of this family appear, it deserves its own entry. No structure reference was matched.

basis: LiCl, measured alongside Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6 and Li6PS5Cl in the Small paper on glass-like thermal conductivity of solid electrolytes. LiCl is rocksalt. [ref 2] agrees: LiCl Fm-3m (225) mp-22905 at hull 0.000, 5 ICSD references.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] LiCl P6_3mc, no ICSD refs: a computed wurtzite polymorph, reported only as a metastable thin-film or low-temperature-deposition form.

note: Same filing as the F-Li and Br-Li hosts.

basis: Li6PS5Cl, the lithium argyrodite solid electrolyte, from the same Small paper as Cl-Li. [ref 2] lists the matching formula as Li6PS5Cl F-43m (216) mp-985592 at hull 0.080.
note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: the [ref 2] PRIMARY is Li5P(S2Cl)2 Amm2 (38) at hull 0.008. That is a different stoichiometry (Li5PS4Cl2) and a computed ordering, so I take the matching-formula F-43m entry instead. Its 0.080 eV/atom hull energy reflects the Li and S/Cl site disorder that MP has to order, not instability of the real cubic phase.

basis: Li3YCl6, from the same Small paper as Cl-In-Li. Li3YCl6 is the hexagonal close-packed member of the Li3MCl6 halide-electrolyte family (trigonal P-3m1, recalled), with Li and Y ordered over octahedral sites.
note: Uses the li3mx6_halide_electrolyte entry proposed for Cl-In-Li in this chunk. The trigonal cell is recalled and there is no structure reference, so the space group is left null.

basis: SnSe0.95(NbCl5)0.03 bulk, from a paper on the thermoelectric performance of n-type SnSe with NbCl5. This is SnSe doped with NbCl5, and SnSe is the orthorhombic Pnma layered GeS type, as in the Se-Sn host.

dopant_roles.basis: NbCl5 is added as a donor. Nb on the Sn site is the usual reading, but Nb solubility in SnSe is low and some may sit in a secondary phase.

note: The chunk file prints no MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line for this host, but its 95th-percentile end, 816 K, is above the ~800 K Pnma-to-Cmcm transition of SnSe. So I record both phases; the Cmcm segment is only the top ~16 K. No ref line was given, so no mp_id is attached. The Se-Sn host carries mp-691 (Pnma) and mp-2168 (Cmcm) for stage 2. Cl is 7 at.% and a host element by the cut, but it is the donor half of the NbCl5 dopant, substituting for Se. Se0.95 means about 5% Se deficiency, which is non_stoichiometry for stage 3.

basis: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi bulk, from the paper on high-entropy alloys as high-temperature thermoelectric materials. CoCrFeNi is the standard single-phase fcc (Fm-3m) high-entropy alloy.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] CrFeCoNi Pm, hull 0.060, no ICSD refs: a computed chemically ordered cell.
[ref 2] CrFeCoNi P1, hull 0.132: a computed ordering.

note: REFERENCE DISAGREEMENT: [ref 2] offers only computed ordered cells, Pm and P1. The real alloy is a random fcc solid solution, so neither mp_id is attached, and stage 2 should represent it as disordered fcc rather than as an MP entry.

basis: Co0.5Zn0.5Cr0.4Fe1.6O4 polycrystal, from a paper on structural and electromagnetic properties of a substituted ferrite. It is a Cr-substituted Co-Zn ferrite, AB2O4 cubic spinel, as for the Co-Fe-O-Zn and Co-Cr-Fe-O hosts.
note: Co and Zn share the A (tetrahedral) site, with some inversion, and Cr and Fe share the B site. All four cations are host elements. No structure reference was matched.

basis: A Co-based Co-Cr-Ni-Si coating with B, C and W (Co 44.6, Cr 18.9, Ni 15.0, Si 14.8 at.%), from a paper on intermetallic Al-, Fe-, Co- and Ni-based thermal barrier coatings. With about 15% Si plus B and C, a sprayed coating of this kind is a Co/Ni solid solution mixed with silicide, boride and carbide phases, not one structure.

dopant_roles.basis: A deliberate alloy addition (boride former and melting-point depressant in Co/Ni hardfacing alloys), not dilute doping.
Carbide former in the alloy design. It is listed in the analysed composition, so it is not treated as processing residue.
Solid-solution strengthener and carbide former in Co-based alloys.

note: Skip in stage 2 (composite). The phase assemblage should come from the paper; plausible constituents are fcc Co/Ni solid solution, Co/Ni silicides, CrB-type borides and M7C3/M23C6 carbides. No structure reference was matched.

basis: FeCoNiCuGe thin films, from a paper on films made by reactive sputtering of the high-entropy alloy FeCoNiCuGe. The composition is the equiatomic HEA target. FeCoNiCu is an fcc base, but 20% Ge is likely to cause intermetallic precipitation.
note: Low on three counts. First, reactive sputtering implies a reactive gas (N2 or O2), so the films may be nitrides or oxides of the HEA even though the recorded composition lists only the metals. Second, sputtered films of this kind are often amorphous or nanocrystalline. Third, Ge at 20 at.% may form intermetallics. The chunk file gives no measured range. No structure reference was matched.
